doc:
Flip to non-streaming for failures streaming itself cannot survive, or that
re-streaming can only repeat: the provider rejecting streams outright,
AnthropicBedrock IAM lacking InvokeModelWithResponseStream, a custom anthropic_messages
provider emitting SSE events out of order (#72833), or a gateway answering
with contentless SSE keepalive frames (a degraded gateway answers every
streaming request that way, so the retry must change channel to make progress).
llama-server stays on streaming: the router can't cancel a non-streamed request.

significant_calls.expression:
self.agent._emit_warning(
                "⚠️ Provider stream returned an empty keepalive frame — retrying this turn "
                "without streaming (streaming stays off for this session).")

name: _handle_stream_error
arguments: self, e: Exception, attempt: int, max_retries: int
doc:
Classify a failed attempt: True = retry; False = stop with
``result["error"]`` set (unless our own interrupt force-closed the
socket). Runs inside the ``except`` so ``logger.exception`` works.

name: _unmask_server_error_with_nonstreaming
doc:
One non-streaming re-issue when a 5xx killed the stream before any delta.

Some gateways validate the request only on their non-streaming path and crash
opaquely ("500 something went wrong") when streaming — the real 4xx, with its
actionable message, never reaches the user through stream retries. One
non-streaming probe per 60s window (timestamped on the agent: each outer retry
builds a fresh _StreamingCall, so an instance flag would re-probe every attempt)
surfaces it: on success the response is delivered for this turn WITHOUT latching
non-streaming (a transient gateway 500 must not permanently disable streaming);
on a probe 4xx that error REPLACES the opaque 5xx; any other probe failure keeps
the original error. The successful delivery is bracketed by its own stream
start/end pair (the failed attempt already emitted a terminal end), and a response
that cannot be replayed propagates ``e``. The probe runs on this worker thread while
the stream monitor still polls, so its stale check is suspended for the probe's
duration (the probe has its own non-streaming watchdog). Interrupts re-raise (the outer handler routes them), and a /stop that arrived before
this point suppresses the probe entirely — the loop's pre-retry interrupt check owns
that decision, so a pending stop must not buy one more request.
True = handled (caller must not overwrite result); False = propagate ``e``.

name: _shutdown_stale_attempt_socket
doc:
Best-effort ``shutdown()`` on the killed attempt's socket (monitor thread).

The pool sweep in ``close_once`` can miss a connection that is checked
out for the in-flight body read. ``shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)`` is FD-safe
from any thread — it wakes the owner's ``recv`` without releasing the
descriptor — so the worker unwinds and releases its own response on
the owner thread (``_call``'s ``except``/``finally``). Never
``close()`` here: releasing a live TLS descriptor from a stranger
thread lets the kernel recycle it under the owner's SSL BIO, which is
exactly what the shutdown-only rule in ``_abort_request_slot_client``
forbids (it covers request-local clients too, #30858).

name: _uncounted_stale_attempt
doc:
The started attempt the circuit breaker (see ``_stale_streak()``) has not counted
yet, else 0. Like the non-streaming and inline watchdogs, each attempt counts once:
the stale timer re-fires every window while the worker has not dispatched yet or is
still unwinding a kill, and none of those re-kills is another unresponsive attempt.

name: _kill_stale_stream
doc:
SSE pings but no chunks: cancel the attempt and abort the request-local
client so the retry loop opens a fresh one. The shared client is never
closed from this (stranger) thread — earlier stale-killed workers may
still be unwinding SSL BIOs (FD-recycle corruption); the OpenAI primary
is replaced lazily.

significant_calls.expression: self.agent._emit_diagnostic_wait(f"⚠ no output from provider for {int(elapsed)}s — reconnecting...")

name: _abort_for_interrupt
doc:
/stop seen by the monitor: mark cancelled, abort the request-local
socket, wait for the worker, flag the interrupt.

name: _resolve_stale_timeout
doc:
Set ``_stream_stale_timeout``. Local endpoints (unless the env is set) get
long but FINITE patience — 900s / ``agent.local_stream_stale_timeout`` /
HERMES_LOCAL_STREAM_STALE_TIMEOUT — an infinite one stalled sessions on a
crashed endpoint forever. Cloud values scale with context size and are
floored for known reasoning models (else BrokenPipeError from the gateway).

name: _partial_stream_stub
doc:
Tokens already reached the platform: a finish_reason="length" stub fires the
continuation machinery; tool_calls=None blocks executing incomplete calls.
Content may be EMPTY (dropped tool call, overflow) — the loop skips appending an
empty stub and only sends the nudge (placeholder text leaked into the stitched
response). A text-only death with 0 visible chars never gets here: the error
handler reclassifies it as undelivered (#112419).

name: run
doc:
Resolve the stale timeout, run the request (worker thread or inline),
drive the heartbeat/stale/interrupt monitor, then translate the outcome.

name: _tool_call_delta_view
doc:
Attribute view of a JSON tool-call delta for ``_ToolCallAccumulator.feed`` (written
against SDK objects). Only ``function`` is wrapped: ``feed`` passes ``extra_content``
(a dict) straight through ``_dump_if_model``, so a recursive view would corrupt it.

name: materialize
doc: Join buffered argument deltas into each entry's ``arguments``; idempotent. Returns ``acc``.

name: _starts_new_call
doc:
Whether a fresh id at a reused raw index opens a new call (Ollama parallel batch) or
continues the current one. LM Studio and Kimi send a fresh id on every argument fragment
with no name, and some MiniMax routes resend the same name on each fragment too: only a
named delta can start a call, and a same-name one only once the current call's arguments
have closed (two parallel calls of one tool must still split).

name: _arguments_closed
doc:
Structural completion (brackets balanced outside strings), not strict JSON validity, so a
repairable call with a trailing comma still ends its slot. Scans only fragments added since
the last check: linear over the call, and free for providers that never reach here.

name: feed
doc: Merge one delta; return the tool name the first time it is complete.

name: _streams_llamacpp
doc:
True when this agent's chat requests go to llama-server: the managed server, or a
``llamacpp`` provider endpoint. These requests always stream and ask for prompt progress
(unless the user turned streaming off in config). A non-streamed request can't be cancelled
through the router, so it would keep the server busy after Hermes gives up on it.

name: stale_giveup
doc: Consecutive stale attempts after which calls fail at once; 0 turns the breaker off.

name: _local_server_answers
doc: True when the llama-server behind *agent* answers ``/health`` within a few seconds.

name: retry_recovered_local_server
doc:
Turn start: when the stale breaker is open, the agent talks to llama-server, and the
server answers its health check, let one attempt through. Within a turn the breaker stops
endless retries; across turns, a local server that crashed or fell behind and has since
recovered gets the user's next message instead of an instant error. The router answers
``/health`` even while its model is stuck, so one more stale attempt shuts the breaker again.

name: _managed_local_load_notice
_abort_request
doc:
Watchdog/interrupt kill: abort the request client (kind-aware, #67142)
and retire the codex token; the worker sees its own forced close via
the cancel flags.

name: _codex_watchdog_snapshot
doc:
``(last_event_ts, last_progress_ts, retry_started_ts, attempt_started_ts)`` under one lock.

``attempt_started_ts`` is the physical attempt's origin (the reconnect marker, else
``call_start``); the notice and the kill loop must anchor to the same value.

name: _pre_progress
doc: Stream open on this attempt, but no substantive model progress yet.

name: _ttfb_kill
doc:
No parsed Codex event past the first-event cutoff — kill so the retry loop
reconnects instead of waiting out the stale timeout.

significant_calls.expression: agent._emit_diagnostic_wait(f"⚠ no response from provider in {int(elapsed)}s — reconnecting...")

name: _progress_kill
doc: The stream opened, but this physical attempt never made model progress.

name: _idle_kill
doc:
SSE events stopped after the phase-specific idle arm point.

Only the implicit official OpenAI Codex policy arms on substantive model
progress; compatible providers and explicit operator timeouts arm on first
parsed event. Once armed, any parsed SSE event refreshes transport activity.

name: _stale_kill
doc:
No response within the stale timeout: kill and count toward the
circuit breaker (#58962, see ``_stale_streak``).

name: _poll_local_load_notice
doc:
Managed local server: surface a cold model's weight-load progress
instead of the 60s neutral "waiting on <model>" notice. Polled ~1s only while no
REAL chunk arrived for 2s+ (never during healthy token flow); in-memory,
no network. True while loading = heartbeat liveness, skip the rest of
this iteration (the stale detector's local floor dwarfs any load).

name: _show_prompt_progress
doc:
Prompt progress straight from the stream's own progress chunks (llama-server with
``return_progress``), at most once a second until the first token. Clears the line
when the first token arrives. True when it showed progress.

significant_calls.expression:
self.agent._emit_wait_notice(
            f"⚙ processing prompt — {percent}%" if percent is not None else "⚙ processing prompt")

name: _skip_sleep
doc:
The computer slept and froze this request with a server on the same machine: move the
stall clock past the sleep, so the request gets its full patience again after wake. Never
past now: a chunk can land between the sleep reading and this write.

name: _heartbeat
doc:
Gateway inactivity heartbeat: the start-to-first-chunk gap (thinking,
local prefill) can exceed the gateway timeout.

name: wait_notice_text
arguments: model: str, silence_secs: float, phase: str, watchdog: Optional[tuple[str, float]]=None
doc: One neutral status line. ``watchdog`` is ``(label, seconds_until_it_fires)``.

name: codex_watchdog_deadline
arguments: *, stale_timeout: float, ttfb_enabled: bool, ttfb_timeout: float, last_event_ts: Optional[float], last_progress_ts: Optional[float], retry_started_ts: Optional[float], call_start: float, idle_enabled: bool, idle_timeout: float, idle_requires_progress: bool, elapsed: float, progress_timeout: float=0.0
doc:
Earliest enabled Codex watchdog as ``(label, seconds_until_it_fires)``; None when
none applies (disabled/infinite, or its deadline already passed).

name: should_emit
arguments: self, phase: str, watchdog: Optional[tuple[str, float]]

name: _routermint_headers
doc: User-Agent RouterMint needs to avoid Cloudflare 1010 blocks.

name: _swap_fallback_clients
arguments: agent, fb_client, fb_provider: str, fb_model: str, fb_base_url: str, fb_api_mode: str
doc: Install the fallback client(s) in place, honoring request_timeout_seconds (None = SDK default).

name: _close_task_resources
doc: Release task resources without treating a shared environment as process ownership.

name: _is_openai_client_closed
doc:
Check if an OpenAI client is closed.

Handles both property and method forms of is_closed:
- httpx.Client.is_closed is a bool property
- openai.OpenAI.is_closed is a method returning bool

Prior bug: getattr(client, "is_closed", False) returned the bound method,
which is always truthy, causing unnecessary client recreation on every call.

name: _build_keepalive_http_client
doc: Build the shared OpenAI httpx client used by main and aux paths.

name: _close_openai_client
arguments: self, client: Any, *, reason: str, shared: bool

name: _retire_shared_openai_client
doc:
Ownership-safe retirement of a replaced shared OpenAI client: ``shutdown()`` sockets only, FDs to GC.

``close()`` releases FDs from the calling thread while other threads may still hold the fd in an SSL BIO;
a recycled fd then gets a TLS record written into an unrelated file (SQLite-header corruption).

The shared primary client has no single owning thread — worker threads from stale-killed attempts
may still be unwinding their SSL BIOs, and the codex-direct / MoA paths stream on the shared client
itself. If we release an FD while another thread's SSL layer still caches the raw integer fd, the
kernel can recycle it into an unrelated ``open()`` (e.g. ``kanban.db``) and the unwinding TLS flush
then writes an application-data record into that file — the SQLite-header corruption documented in
#29507/#70773.

name: _drain_transports_after_abandonment
doc:
FD-safe transport drain for an abandoned (timed-out) worker; returns sockets shut down.

The worker may be blocked in an OpenSSL read; hard-closing from the timeout thread releases FDs under a
live BIO (native corruption / SIGSEGV). Only ``shutdown()`` so the read sees EOF and the worker closes itself.

See #94248.
A delegation deadline abandons this agent's daemon worker while it may still be blocked inside an
in-flight OpenSSL ``read`` (Codex Responses stream, httpx request). This helper only ``shutdown()``s
pooled sockets (safe from any thread), settling blocked reads with EOF/EPIPE so the worker can
unwind and run the real close from its own thread. See #70773, #94248.

name: _api_kwargs_have_image_parts
doc: True when the outbound request still has native image parts (Chat ``messages`` / Responses ``input``).

name: _checkout_request_slot
doc: Return ``(reusable_client, stale_client)``; at most one is non-None.

name: _store_request_slot
arguments: self, slot_attr: str, client: Any, key: Any

name: _release_request_slot
arguments: self, slot_attr: str, client: Any, reason: str
doc: Owner-thread release; True when the client stays cached (clean finish, not poisoned).

name: _take_request_slot
doc: Teardown: empty the slot and return ``(client, was_in_use)``.

name: _abort_request_slot_client
arguments: self, slot_attr: str, client: Any, *, reason: str
doc:
Cross-thread abort (interrupt loop, stale detector): ``shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)`` without releasing FDs.

``close()`` from a non-owning thread races the live SSL BIO and corrupts unrelated FDs; shutdown unblocks
the owner's recv/send so it closes from its own context. The slot is poisoned so the pool is never reused.

name: _close_cached_request_openai_client
doc: Teardown hook: really close the cached per-request wire client.

name: _request_anthropic_client_key
doc: Cache key over everything forcing a fresh client: credential, base URL/region, timeout, 1M-beta flag.

name: _build_direct_anthropic_client
doc: Native Anthropic client for ``token``/``base_url`` with the provider/model request timeout.

name: _anthropic_oauth_flag
doc: OAuth flag only on native Anthropic routes; third-party Anthropic-protocol endpoints must not trip OAuth paths.

name: _create_request_anthropic_client
doc:
Build (or reuse) a request-local Anthropic client for one in-flight call.

The watchdog must never ``close()`` a client a worker is still reading (fd recycled under a live SSL BIO →
TLS record in a SQLite header); per-request clients let the stranger ``shutdown()`` while the owner closes.

name: _close_request_anthropic_client
doc: Owner-thread close: clean finish keeps the pool warm; otherwise force-close sockets (CLOSE-WAIT) + SDK close.

name: _close_cached_request_anthropic_client
doc: Teardown hook: really close the cached per-request Anthropic client.

name: _sync_client_kwargs_credentials
doc: Mirror ``self.api_key`` / ``self.base_url`` into the OpenAI-style client kwargs.

name: _adopt_openai_credentials
arguments: self, api_key: str, base_url: str, *, reason: str
doc: Apply a fresh key/base_url to the OpenAI-style kwargs and rebuild the shared client.

name: _try_refresh_nous_client_credentials
arguments: self, *, force: bool=True, require_account: str | None=None

name: _adopt_nous_key_before_expiry
doc:
Swap in a fresh Nous agent key BEFORE the one in hand expires, so the request never 401s.

The agent key is a JWT; its ``exp`` is read locally (no network). Inside the skew the store
is re-read under the auth-store lock: the keepalive thread normally holds a fresh key already
(adopt, no POST), otherwise ONE refresh runs and every peer adopts its result. Before this,
every agent in a process learned about the hourly expiry from its own 401, all in the same
minute (620 in one 200-subagent run), and the pool benched the sole credential for all of
them. Returns True when a new key was adopted.

Identity guard: the replacement must belong to the SAME account (``sub`` claim) as the key
in hand. The store holds the logged-in singleton; an agent running on an explicitly supplied
or pool-selected key for a different account must never be silently moved onto it (that
changes who is billed). When either side lacks a ``sub`` nothing is adopted here; the
reactive 401 path is unchanged.

name: _resolve_env_credentials
doc:
Current ``.env``-sourced ``(api_key, base_url, default_base)`` for this provider, or ``None``.

Covers registry api-key providers and named custom providers with ``key_env``.

name: _should_adopt_env_credentials
arguments: self, api_key: str, base_url: str, default_base: str
doc:
Adopt only env *edits* (resolved value changed since last look), never drift from ``self.*``:
pool rotation/failover and a config ``model.base_url`` legitimately move the session.

name: _try_refresh_env_client_credentials
doc:
Adopt ``~/.hermes/.env`` credential/base-url edits at the turn boundary (a Settings save updates ``.env``
but a live worker keeps init-time values). Adoption rule: ``_should_adopt_env_credentials``.

Covers api-key registry providers and named custom providers with a ``key_env`` (#67935) — the
latter resolve to ``provider="custom"`` with no registry entry, so they are matched through the
runtime provider's config lookup instead.

name: _try_refresh_vertex_client_credentials
doc: Re-mint the Vertex OAuth2 token (~1h TTL; long sessions 401 on the expired bearer) and rebuild the client.

name: _apply_copilot_token
arguments: self, token: str, enterprise_base_url: Any, *, reason: str

name: _try_refresh_copilot_client_credentials
doc:
Refresh Copilot credentials and rebuild the shared OpenAI client (caller enforces the single-shot guard).

The raw GitHub token is stable; the short-TTL *exchanged* IDE token is what expires mid-turn (``401 IDE
token expired``), so force a fresh exchange rather than re-resolving the raw token.

name: _try_recover_stale_copilot_credential
doc:
Force a fresh Copilot token exchange + client rebuild after a 400 (single-shot, caller-guarded).

Copilot surfaces a stale credential as ``400 model_not_available_for_integrator`` / ``model_not_supported``
— typically a raw ``ghu_`` token cached when the startup exchange degraded (restricted integrator allowlist).

name: _apply_user_default_headers
doc:
Merge config ``model.default_headers`` onto the OpenAI client (user wins; WAFs rejecting SDK headers).
Delegates to ``agent.auxiliary_client`` so main and aux clients cannot drift. No-op for Anthropic/Bedrock.

name: _swap_credential
doc:
Adopt *entry* as the live credential. Returns False, changing nothing, when the entry's
route cannot serve this conversation's model (a conversation's model is never rewritten by a
rotation; the caller treats a refused swap as "no entry").

name: _reapply_route_client_config
doc:
Recompute route-derived client kwargs (TLS material, default headers) for ``self.base_url``.

Any rebuild that may have moved ``base_url`` must call this or the new endpoint inherits the old config.

name: _rebuild_anthropic_client
doc: Rebuild the Anthropic client after an interrupt/stale call (Bedrock SDK for bedrock; honors 1M-beta flag).

name: is_official_codex_base_url
doc: Identify OpenAI's Codex endpoint without matching custom proxies.

name: codex_cloudflare_headers
doc:
Identity and account headers for chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex.

OpenAI requires third-party harnesses to identify themselves: the official
endpoint gets Hermes' originator and version, custom endpoints keep the
codex_cli_rs compatibility identity. The account headers come from the
OAuth JWT (see :func:`codex_account_headers`).

name: codex_account_headers
doc:
Workspace headers the Codex backend derives from the OAuth JWT.

``ChatGPT-Account-ID`` (canonical casing, from codex-rs ``auth.rs``) comes from
``chatgpt_account_id``; ``x-openai-internal-codex-residency`` from
``chatgpt_data_residency`` (fallback ``chatgpt_compute_residency``) — without
it residency-enforced workspaces answer 401 "Workspace is not authorized in
this region". A malformed token drops the headers rather than raising, so it
surfaces as a 401 instead of a crash at client construction.

name: codex_request_compression_hooks
doc:
httpx ``event_hooks`` that zstd-compress Responses request bodies for the official Codex backend.

Parity with the official Codex client (zstd on ``/responses`` with ChatGPT auth, default since
openai/codex#10102). Lossless transport encoding: tokens and prompt caching are unchanged. Uses the
stdlib codec (Python 3.14+); without it, or for any other endpoint/proxy, bodies stay raw JSON.

name: apply_required_codex_headers
arguments: client_kwargs: dict[str, Any], *, access_token: str, base_url: str
doc: Keep required Codex identity after user/provider header overrides.

name: _classify_responses_issuer
arguments: *, is_xai_responses: bool=False, is_github_responses: bool=False, is_codex_backend: bool=False, base_url: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Stable identifier for the endpoint that mints ``reasoning.encrypted_content``. Blobs are sealed to their
issuer (HTTP 400 ``invalid_encrypted_content``), so stamping lets replay drop foreign blobs after a model switch.

name: _canonical_issuer_kind
doc:
Canonicalise a persisted ``other:<url>`` issuer stamp. Items stamped before canonicalisation carry the raw
``agent.base_url`` (trailing slash / host case) and must still replay on the same endpoint.

name: _wire_model_identity
doc:
Canonical Responses wire model stamped on encrypted reasoning: blobs are sealed to the issuing
model too, so a same-endpoint model switch must not replay them (HTTP 400).

name: openai_reasoning_family
doc: ``_OPENAI_ALL_TURNS_FAMILIES`` entry ``model`` belongs to (``gpt-6.1-sol`` -> ``gpt-6``), else None.

name: _model_can_read_blob
arguments: issuer_kind: Optional[str], item_model: Any, current_model: Optional[str]
doc: Exact model everywhere; same all_turns family on api.openai.com, which accepts sibling-variant blobs.

name: strip_unverified_reasoning_items
arguments: messages: Any, *, issuer_kind: Optional[str], issuer_model: Optional[str]
doc:
First ``invalid_encrypted_content`` rung: drop the items the failing request REPLAYED without an exact
issuer+model stamp (unstamped legacy blobs, sibling-variant blobs). Items another issuer or model minted
were never sent (``_replay_reasoning_items`` skips them) and stay in history for a switch back.
Consumes its own precondition (a second call removes nothing), so recovery cannot loop.
Rebinds the filtered list, never mutates a shared one; returns the number of items removed.

name: _leaked_tool_call_text
doc: True when assistant text carries a tool call the model failed to emit as a structured ``function_call``.

name: _field
arguments: obj: Any, name: str, default: Any=None
doc: Read ``name`` from a dict or an attribute-style (SDK/SimpleNamespace) object.

name: _coerce_arguments
doc: Normalize replayed tool-call arguments to a non-empty JSON string.

name: _neutralize_harmony_tokens
doc: Keep Harmony source readable without emitting reserved wire tokens.

name: _neutralize_harmony_structure
doc:
Neutralize JSON-like values (tuples → lists). A reserved token in an object *key* is
rejected, not rewritten — renaming could desync a tool schema from the executor contract.

name: _iter_content_parts
doc: Yield ``("text", str)`` / ``("image", part)`` for recognized chat parts.

name: _input_image_part
arguments: part: dict[str, Any], role: str='user', *, keep_empty_url: bool
doc:
Responses image part from a chat/Responses image part (``image_url`` may be a str or
``{url, detail}``). Assistant → text placeholder (an assistant ``input_image`` 400s every
replay); user → ``input_image``, None for an empty url unless ``keep_empty_url``; an inline
SVG is rasterized to PNG when a rasterizer is installed, any other unsupported inline
subtype (or an SVG with no rasterizer) → text placeholder.

name: _chat_content_to_responses_parts
doc:
Chat-style multimodal content → Responses API input parts ([] if not a list). Text is
``input_text`` (user) / ``output_text`` (assistant) — the API rejects the wrong type per role;
``input_image`` is only legal on user messages (see :func:`_input_image_part`). Unsupported
video parts fail closed instead of silently turning a video request into a text-only request.

name: _summarize_user_message_for_log
doc:
Flatten message content to plain text: text parts joined with ``sep`` (``" "`` for logs; ``"\n"`` for memory
providers feeding regexes), images → ``[N image(s)]`` marker, ``""`` for None, ``str(content)`` for other scalars.

name: _clamp_responses_call_id
doc:
Keep ``call_id`` within the API's 64-char cap (the codex app-server namespaces MCP call ids past it). The
surrogate is a pure function of the original so a ``function_call`` and its ``function_call_output`` agree.

name: _canonical_call_id_from_fc
doc:
Map an ``fc_…`` item id to its canonical ``call_<suffix>``. Both sides of a replayed
pair must derive the SAME call_id, or an oversized pair clamps to two surrogates.

name: _split_responses_tool_id
doc: Split a stored tool id into (call_id, response_item_id).

name: _resolve_call_id
arguments: raw_call_id: Any, raw_item_id: Any, fn_name: str, arguments: Any, index: int, *, canonicalize_fc: bool
doc:
Pick a non-blank call_id: explicit -> embedded in ``call|fc`` id -> (replay only)
canonical ``call_<fc suffix>`` -> deterministic hash of name/arguments/index.

name: _derive_responses_function_call_id
doc: Build a valid Responses `function_call.id` (must start with `fc_`).

name: _responses_tools
doc: Convert chat-completions tool schemas to Responses function-tool schemas.

name: _normalize_responses_message_status
doc:
Normalize a replayed assistant message status, modulo case/hyphen spelling, so incomplete Codex
continuation turns are not falsely marked completed.

name: _message_item
arguments: content: list[dict[str, Any]], *, status: str, item_id: Optional[str]=None, phase: Optional[str]=None
doc: Assistant ``message`` item; ``id``/``phase`` are added only when non-empty.

name: _role_message_item
arguments: role: str, content: Any, phase: Any=None
doc:
Plain ``message`` input item for ``role``. ``type`` is required: llama.cpp's ``/v1/responses``
parser rejects a typeless assistant item ("Cannot determine type of 'item'"). Assistant ``phase``
is forwarded only for values the API accepts on input messages; others would 400.

name: _assistant_message_item
arguments: raw: dict[str, Any], content: list[dict[str, Any]], *, is_github_responses: bool, current_issuer_kind: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Replayable assistant ``message`` item from a stored one. ``id`` is kept only when short enough and never for
GitHub Copilot (ids bind to a backend connection; stale → 401); ``phase`` is preserved per OpenAI's cache guidance.
The ChatGPT Codex backend additionally rejects ids that do not begin with ``msg`` (foreign Responses issuers
mint short UUIDs), so those are dropped there while other issuers' policies are unchanged.

name: _replay_reasoning_items
arguments: msg: dict[str, Any], *, seen_item_ids: set, current_issuer_kind: Optional[str], current_issuer_model: Optional[str]=None, native_compaction_eligible: bool
doc:
Replay persisted encrypted reasoning/compaction items for one assistant turn. Skips duplicate
ids, ``compaction`` checkpoints unless THIS request carries ``context_management`` (else a persisted
checkpoint erases pre-checkpoint history on a model that cannot decrypt it), and items stamped by
another issuer or model (HTTP 400). Items without a model stamp (legacy or unstamped) replay on a
matching issuer. ``id`` (store=False lookups 404) and the Hermes provenance fields are stripped.

name: _replay_message_items
arguments: msg: dict[str, Any], *, is_github_responses: bool, current_issuer_kind: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Replay exact assistant message items (id/phase) for prefix-cache hits.

A ``msg_*`` id minted in the same response as a ``reasoning`` item is bound to that item's ``rs_*`` id,
which ``_replay_reasoning_items`` always strips (store=False). Replaying the message id alone is a
deterministic HTTP 400 ("provided without its required 'reasoning' item", #97427/#97442), so the message
id is dropped whenever its turn carried encrypted reasoning — replayed, suppressed, foreign-issuer or
trimmed by the transport (``codex_reasoning_trimmed``) — and the message goes out as content/status/phase
only. Reasoning-free turns keep their id.

name: _replay_tool_call_items
arguments: msg: dict[str, Any], *, start_index: int, wire_ids: Optional[_WireCallIds]=None
doc: Convert an assistant message's ``tool_calls`` into ``function_call`` items.

name: _tool_output_items
doc: Convert a tool-role message to ``[function_call_output]`` (``[]`` if unpairable).

name: _chat_messages_to_responses_input
arguments: messages: list[dict[str, Any]], *, is_xai_responses: bool=False, is_github_responses: bool=False, replay_encrypted_reasoning: bool=True, current_issuer_kind: Optional[str]=None, current_issuer_model: Optional[str]=None, native_compaction_eligible: bool=False
doc:
Convert internal chat-style messages to Responses input items.

``is_xai_responses``: signature compatibility only (xAI DOES replay encrypted reasoning).
``replay_encrypted_reasoning``: per-session kill switch, threaded False by
``AIAgent._disable_codex_reasoning_replay`` after a repeat ``invalid_encrypted_content`` 400.
``is_github_responses``: drops ``id`` from replayed message items (Copilot 401s on stale ids).
``current_issuer_kind`` / ``current_issuer_model``: provenance guard; items stamped by another issuer or
model drop. Legacy items carrying only an endpoint stamp replay on a matching issuer.
``native_compaction_eligible``: THIS request carries ``context_management``; gates both replaying ``compaction``
checkpoints and ``prune_pre_checkpoint_items``. Checkpoints persist across model swaps / compression flips / resume,
so without the gate one checkpoint would erase pre-checkpoint history on a model that cannot decrypt it (lossless:
local history is never truncated).

Earlier (PR #26644, May 2026) we believed xAI's OAuth/SuperGrok ``/v1/responses`` surface rejected
replayed ``encrypted_content`` reasoning items minted by prior turns, and we stripped them. That
decision was wrong — xAI explicitly relies on Hermes threading encrypted reasoning back across turns for
cross-turn coherence (the whole point of their partnership integration). We now replay encrypted
reasoning on every Responses transport (xAI, native Codex, custom relays) and let xAI tell us explicitly
if a specific surface ever rejects a payload.
The Copilot backend (api.githubcopilot.com/responses) binds these ids to a specific backend "connection"
— credential-pool rotation, a gateway restart, or routine load-balancer churn between turns all
invalidate it — and rejects a stale id with HTTP 401 "input item ID does not belong to this connection"
even for short ids (see #32716). ``phase``/ ``status``/``content`` are still replayed; only ``id`` is
unsafe to reuse across a Copilot connection.
``native_compaction_eligible`` mirrors, for THIS request, the decision made by
``native_compaction.native_compaction_context_management`` — it is True only when that gate returned a
payload, i.e. when the request actually carries ``context_management``. It controls two things that must
never outlive the gate: replaying ``type: "compaction"`` checkpoint items, and restructuring the wire
around them (``prune_pre_checkpoint_items``). Checkpoints are persisted in the ``codex_reasoning_items``
sidecar and survive a mid-session model swap, a ``compression.enabled: false`` flip, the rejection kill
switch and a resumed session; without this flag a single captured checkpoint would keep deleting every
pre-checkpoint item from every later request, on a model that cannot decrypt the blob (#85914). Default
False = pre-feature wire, which is also correct for every caller that never sends ``context_management``
(auxiliary/compression client, ad-hoc ``convert_messages``). Dropping the checkpoint costs nothing:
Hermes' local history is never truncated by native compaction, so the full conversation is still on the
wire.

name: classify_responses_route
doc:
Classify the agent's Responses route from provider + base URL. Host checks are
exact-host-or-subdomain, never substring (``evil.com/models.github.ai`` is not GitHub).

name: _native_responses_replay_items
doc: Build the native-compaction-eligible wire items, or ``None`` when ineligible.

name: has_replayable_native_compaction_checkpoint
doc: Whether the current route would replay a persisted native checkpoint.

name: estimate_native_responses_preflight_tokens
arguments: agent: Any, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], *, system_prompt: str='', tools: Optional[list[dict[str, Any]]]=None
doc:
Estimate tokens for the checkpoint-pruned Responses payload (the full transcript overstates a natively compacted
session and fires local compression needlessly). None when native compaction is not proven eligible or conversion fails.

Automatic preflight previously counted the full durable transcript. On a natively compacted Codex
session that overstates the wire by several times and fires local compression against history the main
request will never send (#96155).

name: _preflight_function_call
arguments: item: dict[str, Any], idx: int, ctx: _PreflightCtx

name: _preflight_function_call_output
arguments: item: dict[str, Any], idx: int, ctx: _PreflightCtx

name: _preflight_encrypted
arguments: item: dict[str, Any], idx: int, ctx: _PreflightCtx
doc: ``reasoning`` / ``compaction`` items: opaque, issuer-sealed; forward only API-defined fields.

name: _preflight_message
arguments: item: dict[str, Any], idx: int, ctx: _PreflightCtx

name: _preflight_role_message
arguments: item: dict[str, Any], idx: int, ctx: _PreflightCtx
doc: ``user``/``assistant`` role message, typed or untyped; string content or Responses parts.

name: _preflight_codex_input_items
arguments: raw_items: Any, *, is_github_responses: bool=False, sanitize_harmony_tokens: bool=False

name: _extract_responses_message_text
doc:
Assistant text from a Responses message output item. A ``refusal`` part carries the
model's explanation in ``refusal`` instead of ``text``; it is message text too, otherwise a
refusal-only turn reads as an empty response (sibling of chat_completions ``message.refusal``).

name: _extract_responses_reasoning_text
doc: Compact reasoning text from a Responses reasoning item (summary, else ``text``).

name: _format_responses_error
doc:
``"<code>: <message>"`` for a ``response.error`` payload (dict or object), else whichever
is present, else ``str(error_obj)``, else a status-based default.

name: _response_tool_call
arguments: item: Any, item_type: str, index: int
doc: Build a chat-style tool_call from a ``function_call``/``custom_tool_call`` item.

name: _capture_encrypted_item
arguments: item: Any, item_type: str, issuer_kind: Optional[str], issuer_model: Optional[str]=None
doc:
``{type, encrypted_content[, _issuer_kind, _issuer_model]}`` for replay, or None without a blob. Reasoning
items also carry ``id`` + ``summary`` (required by the API on replay); transient ``rs_tmp_`` skip.

name: _normalize_codex_response
arguments: response: Any, *, issuer_kind: Optional[str]=None, issuer_model: Optional[str]=None, recover_leaked_tool_call: bool=True
doc:
Normalize a Responses API object to ``(assistant_message, finish_reason)``.
``issuer_kind`` / ``issuer_model`` are stamped onto captured reasoning items for provenance replay drops.
``recover_leaked_tool_call=False`` is for callers with no continuation (aux): tool-call-shaped text is
then kept as ordinary content and judged by the same phase/completion gates as any other answer.

name: emit
arguments: new_items: list[dict[str, Any]], msg: dict[str, Any]

name: scan
arguments: self, output: list[Any], issuer_kind: Optional[str], issuer_model: Optional[str]=None

name: _stream_drain_timeout
doc:
``agent.stream_drain_timeout`` (seconds) — how long the post-terminal SSE drain may block.

The drain is a courtesy to Relay's finalizer, never a correctness requirement: ``final`` is fully
assembled before it starts. A relay that never closes the socket after ``response.completed`` would
otherwise wedge the turn until the idle watchdog discards the already-billed response (#103864).
``0`` skips the drain entirely.

name: _call_guarded
arguments: fn: Callable | None, fail_msg: str, *fail_args: Any, args: tuple=(), kwargs: dict | None=None
doc: Invoke an optional display/debug callback; a buggy hook must never tear down the turn.

name: _codex_request_failure_details
doc:
(serialized request bytes, exception class chain); the buffered ``httpx.Request`` content
on OpenAI connection errors gives the exact byte count without logging payloads or URLs.

name: _prune_zero_event_retry_payload
arguments: api_kwargs: dict, attempt: int, attempts: int
doc:
#95429 criterion 3: a reconnect after an attempt that produced no stream event must not resend
a pathological payload unchanged. Inline ``function_call_output`` strings over the per-result
threshold (results that escaped commit-time persistence) are spilled through the standard
policy -- bounded preview + recoverable ``<persisted-output>`` reference -- and ONE log line
records the size delta. When nothing is prunable the resend is logged as unchanged. The
caller's kwargs are never mutated; only the retried wire payload changes.

name: _queue_token_counts
arguments: agent, fail_msg: str, *fail_extra: Any, counts: Callable[[], dict]
doc:
Enqueue per-call accounting for the SessionDB background writer. ``counts`` is built
lazily inside the guarded try so a stub agent without a session DB is never touched.

name: _record_codex_app_server_usage
doc:
Translate Codex app-server token usage into Hermes accounting. Prompt bucket = uncached + cached
input (the protocol exposes no cache-write tokens); a turn with no usage still counts as one API call.
``messages`` (the transcript mirror) lets real usage anchor the next preflight: this runtime bypasses
the main loop's capture, and the mirror is never compacted natively, so without an anchor the rough
estimate grows monotonically and hermes-mode fires thread compaction on tiny threads (#100381).

name: _record_codex_app_server_compaction
arguments: agent, turn, *, approx_tokens: int | None=None, force: bool=False
doc:
Record a Codex-native compaction boundary: the app-server owns the compacted thread,
so local transcript rows are NOT rewritten — only session event/usage counters.

name: _delta_text
doc: Non-empty text carried by an app-server delta notification, else "".

name: _codex_item_to_tool_name
doc: Synthetic Hermes tool name for a codex item (mirrors CodexEventProjector).

name: _codex_item_to_args
doc: Args dict for tool_progress_callback("tool.started"); mirrors the projector shapes.

name: _codex_item_to_preview
doc: Short preview for the tool.started bubble; None when nothing useful (UI tolerates None).

name: _codex_item_completion_payload
doc:
(result_text, is_error) for a completed tool item — display-facing text for live tool cards (the
persisted history keeps the projector's ``{exit_code, output}`` envelope instead).

name: _stable_call_id
doc: Deterministic tool_call id mirroring CodexEventProjector (live TUI card correlates with projected history).

name: make_codex_app_server_event_bridge
doc:
Build the ``on_event`` callback for ``CodexAppServerSession(on_event=...)``.

Tool items fire ``tool_progress_callback`` plus the stable-ID ``tool_start_callback`` /
``tool_complete_callback`` card hooks; deltas go to ``_fire_stream_delta`` / ``_fire_reasoning_delta``;
a completed agentMessage goes to ``_emit_interim_assistant_message`` (the gateway's ``already_streamed``
check dedupes against streamed deltas). Current-turn progress refreshes the activity clock even
without display hooks. Every callback is guarded so a buggy display hook cannot tear down the turn loop.

name: _close_codex_session
doc: Drop the session so the next turn respawns codex instead of reusing a dead client.

name: _consume_user_interrupt
doc:
(user_interrupted, interrupt_message); clears the agent-level interrupt so a hard
stop cannot poison the next turn (mirrors the conversation-loop finalizer).

name: _codex_developer_instructions
doc: The prompt composition the standard loop sends as its system message (turn_context order).

name: _store_codex_thread_id
doc: Merge (``None`` clears) the binding into the session row; a failed write only logs — the turn is done.

name: _start_codex_thread
doc:
``ensure_started`` with the fail-closed resume policy: a stored thread that codex cannot hand back
(unknown id, rollout locked by a killed app-server, different thread) is dropped from the session row,
the user is told once on the status rail, and a fresh thread starts on the same client.

name: _codex_model_provider
doc:
codex's ``[model_providers.<id>]`` for a named custom provider (``providers.<name>``); None means codex's
own provider. Only the stable id is sent and codex resolves base_url/env_key itself, so Hermes' credential
never enters the JSON-RPC payload (#75186).

name: _codex_wire_model
doc:
The slug codex should run. ``-900k`` picker variants are Hermes-side aliases the backend rejects
("not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account"); codex applies the catalog's extended window
to the base slug itself. On codex's own provider the slug is bare (``openai/gpt-5.5`` -> ``gpt-5.5``),
as for openai-codex; a named custom provider's model ids are its own and pass through.

name: _codex_turn_effort
doc:
``turn/start.effort``: only an explicit Hermes reasoning setting overrides codex's own default, clamped
to the route's vocabulary like the Responses path (a level the model lacks fails the turn with 400
"Unsupported value"). ``ultra`` stays ``ultra`` where the model reaches ``max``: codex runs it as its
harness mode. Disabled reasoning goes out as ``none`` where the route accepts it.

name: _codex_turn_service_tier
doc:
``turn/start.serviceTier``: the tier Hermes' own Responses path would request this turn (a static
``/fast`` tier pinned in request_overrides, or an open ``auto``/``cold`` window), in codex's words: the
OpenAI ``priority`` tier is codex's ``fast``. A tier codex has no word for (``ultrafast``) is not sent.

name: _ensure_codex_session
doc:
Lazily spawn one CodexAppServerSession per AIAgent (reused across turns, closed by the _cleanup hook).
A live session whose thread was started with a different prompt composition (TUI/Desktop ``/personality``
or a prompt mirror mutate the agent in place) is retired first so the new thread carries the current one.
Only the FIRST session of an AIAgent resumes the stored codex thread: a retired/recreated one keeps
today's fresh-thread behaviour and overwrites the binding once its turn is committed. ``messages`` is the
turn's transcript (current user row last); a thread started from scratch is seeded with the prior turns.

name: _persist_projected_messages
doc:
Splice the projected messages into ``messages`` and flush them to the session DB; True when the
rows are durable in the session DB (the codex thread binding may then be published).

Bypasses conversation_loop's per-step _persist_session(); the flush dedups via _DB_PERSISTED_MARKER so
only the new codex rows are written. The agent stays the sole persister (agent_persisted=True): a
gateway re-write would re-INSERT the user turn.

name: _finish_codex_turn
arguments: agent, turn, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], *, original_user_message: Any, should_review_memory: bool
doc: Post-turn bookkeeping mirroring the chat_completions loop; returns usage fields.

name: run_codex_app_server_turn
arguments: agent, *, user_message: str, original_user_message: Any, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], effective_task_id: str, should_review_memory: bool=False
doc:
Hand the turn to a ``codex app-server`` subprocess and project its events into ``messages``.
Returns the chat_completions result shape. The user message is ALREADY in ``messages`` — never append it again.

name: _turn_result
arguments: interrupt: tuple[bool, Any], messages: list[dict[str, Any]], *, api_calls: int, completed: bool, error: Any, final_response: Any, **extra: Any
doc: Result shape shared with the chat_completions path (``partial`` == ``not completed``).

name: _event_field
arguments: event: Any, name: str, default: Any=None
doc: Field access for attr-style (SDK objects) and dict (raw JSON) events/items.

name: _codex_event_has_content
doc:
Whether a Codex Responses event carries substantive forward progress.

Lifecycle/keepalive frames and empty structural deltas prove transport
liveness, but do not mean the model has begun producing its response.

name: _raise_stream_error
doc:
Raise ``_StreamErrorEvent`` from a ``type=error`` SSE frame. The spec puts code/message/param at the
top level, but the SDK and several proxies nest them under ``error``; read top-level first, then the envelope.

significant_calls.callee: (str(raw_message) if raw_message is not None else "stream emitted error event").strip
significant_calls.expression: (str(raw_message) if raw_message is not None else "stream emitted error event").strip()

name: _output_text_of
doc: Concatenated ``output_text`` parts of a message item ("" if content is not a list).

name: _consume_codex_event_stream
arguments: event_iter: Any, *, model: str, on_text_delta=None, on_reasoning_delta=None, on_commentary_message=None, on_first_delta=None, on_event=None, interrupt_check=None
doc:
Consume a Codex Responses SSE stream into a Response-shaped ``SimpleNamespace`` (see
:class:`_CodexResponseAssembler`; ``status`` is ``completed`` when the stream ended with content but no
terminal frame; ``model`` comes from kwargs).

Callbacks: ``on_text_delta`` per output_text delta, suppressed once a function_call is seen;
``on_reasoning_delta`` for reasoning and ``phase=analysis`` deltas (also commentary without a commentary
callback); ``on_commentary_message`` once per completed ``phase=commentary`` message, before any following
tool item; ``on_first_delta`` one-shot; ``on_event`` every event before any processing; ``interrupt_check()``
True breaks the loop and may raise ``TimeoutError`` / ``InterruptedError`` for request retirement that
must not become a partial final response.

name: _sanitize_consumer_codex_request
doc:
Drop fields the ChatGPT OAuth Codex endpoint rejects, at the final wire boundary (after Relay /
middleware / ``request_overrides``): a late ``prompt_cache_retention``, top-level or nested in
``extra_body``, would otherwise HTTP 400 a valid follow-up.

name: run_codex_stream
arguments: agent, api_kwargs: dict, client: Any=None, on_first_delta=None
doc: One streaming Responses API request over raw ``responses.create(stream=True)`` events.

name: agent_cb
arguments: attr: str, fail_msg: str, *fail_args: Any, args: tuple=(), kwargs: dict | None=None

name: __init__
arguments: self, *, model, on_text_delta, on_reasoning_delta, on_commentary_message, on_first_delta

name: _safe
arguments: self, cb: Callable | None, label: str, *args: Any

name: feed
doc: Process one event; True when the stream hit a terminal frame.

name: _settled_output
doc: Merge .done items with settled pending calls, keeping stream order.

name: _fenced
doc: Wrap a callback so a retired request's late frames never reach the agent.

name: _live
doc: Wrap a live-display callback so a superseded writer's frames never reach the sink (retired ones neither).

name: render_history_seed
doc:
Prior turns as one text block, newest last; empty when there is nothing before the current
user message. The trailing user row is the turn being submitted and is never included.

name: remember_catalog
doc: Retain only speed metadata, even when a model omits its context window.

name: _tiers_for_model
arguments: access_token: str, base_url: str, model: str

name: codex_account_offers_tier
arguments: model: Any, tier: str, *, base_url: Any=None, access_token: Any=None
doc:
Whether the signed-in ChatGPT account's Codex catalog lists ``tier`` for ``model``.

``None`` when unknown (no usable token, catalog unreachable, model absent) so callers never refuse
on a failed lookup. ``access_token`` defaults to the profile's stored Codex OAuth token.

name: ultrafast_offered
arguments: model: Any, *, provider: Any=None, base_url: Any=None, access_token: Any=None
doc:
Whether ``/fast ultrafast`` (and the Ultrafast picker row) is offered on this route: the route
gate plus, on the ChatGPT/Codex subscription, the account's own Codex catalog. That backend accepts
``service_tier: "ultrafast"`` from a plan without the entitlement and silently serves the default
tier, so the catalog the official client reads is the authority. An unreadable catalog never
blocks (request-time negotiation still clamps per credential).

name: ultrafast_offered_for
doc: :func:`ultrafast_offered` on a CLI shell's resolved route (attributes absent before setup).

name: negotiate_request_tier
doc: Resolve the current credential on each build without mutating user preference.

name: _model_family
doc: Edit-format family key for a model id, or ``None`` (neutral wording applies).

name: _agent_config_value
arguments: config: Optional[dict[str, Any]], key: str, default: Any, *, readonly: bool
doc: ``config["agent"][key]``, loading config when none was passed.

name: _coding_mode
doc: Normalized ``agent.coding_context`` mode (auto/focus/on/off).

name: _marker_root
doc:
Nearest ancestor (≤6 levels) that looks like a project root, or ``None``. ``$HOME``
and the shared temp root are skipped: a Makefile/AGENTS.md in the home dir is global
config, and a stray manifest in /tmp must not flip every session under it.

name: _has_code_files
doc: Bounded check for source files in the root and its immediate subdirs.

name: _detect_profile
arguments: mode: str, platform: str, cwd: Path
doc:
``auto``/``focus``: coding when the surface is interactive AND the cwd is a code
workspace (project root, or a git repo that actually holds code; a repo rooted at
``$HOME`` is NOT a signal). ``on``/``off`` force. Not memoized: one gateway serves many cwds.

name: _enabled_mcp_servers
doc:
Names of MCP servers the user has enabled — kept in the coding posture. The profile default's
resolver, so plugin-provided servers stay too; *config* None reads the user's config.

name: _posture_toolsets
doc: The coding posture's toolset list; callers own the ``focus`` check.

name: focus_toolsets
doc:
The coding posture's toolsets when ``agent.coding_context`` is ``focus``, else None, for a
session whose workspace decision is already made (no cwd probe).

name: resolve_runtime_mode
arguments: *, platform: Optional[str]=None, cwd: Optional[str | Path]=None, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, model: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Resolve the operating posture once (a handful of ``stat`` calls) — the single entry
point every domain should call; the result is safe to hold for the session. ``model``
only steers edit-format guidance; ``agent.coding_instructions`` (str or list) becomes
the trailing block so a user can pin workflow rules without editing the shipped brief.

name: is_coding_context
arguments: *, platform: Optional[str]=None, cwd: Optional[str | Path]=None, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Whether Hermes should operate in its coding posture right now.

name: in_focus_workspace
arguments: *, platform: Optional[str]=None, cwd: Optional[str | Path]=None, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Whether *cwd* selects the coding posture's toolsets (``focus`` and a code workspace), without
building them; ``focus_toolsets`` builds them once the decision is made.

name: coding_selection
arguments: *, platform: Optional[str]=None, cwd: Optional[str | Path]=None, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Toolset selection for the coding posture (``None`` unless ``focus`` and active).

name: coding_system_prompt_parts
arguments: *, platform: Optional[str]=None, cwd: Optional[str | Path]=None, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, model: Optional[str]=None, valid_tool_names=None, workspace_block: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Return coding prefix, workspace snapshot, and trailing guidance.  ``workspace_block``
replays the caller's pinned session-start snapshot instead of probing git again.

name: coding_compact_skill_categories
arguments: *, platform: Optional[str]=None, cwd: Optional[str | Path]=None, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Skill categories the active posture demotes to names-only (empty outside ``focus``).

name: _git
doc:
``git -C <cwd> <args>`` → stripped stdout, or ``""`` on any failure. bounded_git_probe
bounds post-kill cleanup on Windows — plain ``subprocess.run(timeout=...)`` deadlocked
when a killed git left a suspended descendant holding the pipe handles.

See #66037.

name: _parse_status
doc: Parse ``git status --porcelain=2 --branch`` into branch + counts.

name: _read_small
doc: Read a small text file, or ``""`` — never raises, never reads huge files.

name: detect_project_facts
doc: Detect manifests, package manager(s), verify commands, context files (single source of truth).

name: _workspace_roots
doc: (git_root, workspace_root) for *cwd*; workspace root is git root else marker root.

name: project_facts_for
doc: Structured project facts for ``cwd`` (desktop verify UI) — ``None`` outside a workspace.

name: build_coding_workspace_block
doc:
Workspace snapshot for the system prompt (empty outside a workspace): git state when
in a repo, plus project facts — so marker-only (non-git) projects still get one.

name: toolset_selection
doc:
Toolset list (only under ``focus``), or ``None`` to keep the platform default. Callers
apply it only when the user hasn't pinned a selection (``--toolsets``, ``HERMES_TUI_TOOLSETS``).
*config* None lists MCP servers from the user's config.

name: system_prompt_parts
doc:
Return (prefix, workspace, trailing) posture blocks in the historical flat order —
brief, snapshot, operator instructions — so prompt assembly can put a cache boundary
before the snapshot without changing persisted bytes. The brief carries the model-family
edit-format nudge (one cached string); ``valid_tool_names`` drops the ``todo_list``
sentence when that tool isn't loaded; operator instructions ride their own block so
the brief stays byte-stable. ``workspace_block`` replays a snapshot the caller already
pinned at session start (``""`` = no workspace) instead of re-running the git probe;
``None`` probes.

name: system_blocks
doc: Posture blocks as one flat list in historical order.

name: compact_skill_categories
doc:
Skill categories to demote to names-only in the skill index. Gated on ``focus``
like the toolset collapse (index changes under ``auto`` proved too surprising).
Demoted, never hidden: pruning caused silent capability loss.

name: materialize_probe_api_key
doc: Best-effort probe credential; never send a callable's repr or log mint errors.

name: _mint
doc:
Run *command*, returning ``(token, ttl_seconds_or_None)``. The helper runs FOR the profile whose
provider is being minted: it gets that profile's own env (secrets + HERMES_HOME), never the multiplexer's
launch environ — an ``op read`` / ``vault kv get`` helper must sign in as the served profile.

name: build_command_token_provider
doc: A per-request token provider for *key_cmd*, or ``None`` when unset.

name: cache_identity
doc: Stable catalog identity; token rotation must not mint on cache reads.

name: project_compaction_message_for_display
doc:
Return authentic transcript content, or ``None`` for a pure handoff.

Model-facing recovery history retains the complete carrier. Display
projections instead remove the handoff, inherited tool state, and internal
reasoning while preserving any real prior-tail content or live user ask
embedded in the carrier.

name: _closed
arguments: value: Any, allowed: frozenset[str], default: str | None='other'

name: failure_class
doc:
Closed failure class: ``exception:<Type>`` / ``rollback:<Type>`` keep only the prefix (the type name
may be a plugin's); a missing class reads ``none``.

name: event_name
doc: ``compaction`` only for a committed history or provider rewrite; ``compaction.attempt`` otherwise.

name: _attempt_outcome
arguments: commit_status: Any, failure: str, history_rewritten: Any

name: _attempt_trigger
doc:
``(trigger, trigger_class)``. ``auto`` is what an unlabelled automatic caller records: the reason is
unknown, but the attempt is still known to be automatic.

name: attempt_payload
doc: Map one attempt telemetry record (the attempt log line's dict) onto the v1 schema.

name: micro_payload
doc: Map one micro-compaction telemetry record onto the v1 schema.

name: prune_payload
arguments: *, session_id: str, tokens_before: int, tokens_after: int, messages: int, tool_results_pruned: int
doc: A committed proactive tool-result prune: deterministic, no LLM, message count unchanged.

name: provider_native_payload
doc: A compaction the provider ran on its own thread and Hermes only observed.

name: fire_post_compaction
arguments: *, session_id: str, old_session_id: str='', kind: str | None, reason: str | None, before_tokens: int | None, after_tokens: int | None, messages_removed: int | None
doc: The ``post_compaction`` plugin hook, gated on a listener. Callbacks are isolated by the dispatcher.

name: _publish
arguments: build: Any, *args: Any, turn_session_id: str | None=None, require_target_session_id: str | None=None, live_session_id: str | None=None, **kwargs: Any
doc:
Build one record, fire ``post_compaction`` for a committed one, and fan it out to the built-in Relay
integration. ``live_session_id`` is the session holding the compacted transcript now (a rotating commit
moved it off the record's session). Never raises into compaction: the first failure logs at WARNING with
its traceback, later ones at DEBUG.

name: _publishes_for
doc: A persistence-detached fork (background review) rewrites only its own throwaway transcript.

name: _turn_session_id
doc:
The session the agent's current turn started in; a rotating commit moves ``agent.session_id`` off it
mid-turn. ``None`` outside a turn.

name: publish_attempt
doc: Publish one ``compress_context`` attempt record (the attempt telemetry seam calls this).

name: publish_micro
arguments: record: dict[str, Any], *, turn_session_id: str | None=None
doc:
Publish one micro-compaction pass record. The finalizer never runs micro-compaction for a fork, and passes
the session its turn started in (``_turn_session_id``) because the pass may run in a rotated child.

name: publish_prune
arguments: agent: Any, messages: list, pruned: list, tool_results_pruned: int
doc:
Publish one committed proactive tool-result prune, measured like the attempt record (rough estimate of
the message list the model sees next).

significant_calls.expression:
_publish(lambda: prune_payload(
            session_id=session_id, tokens_before=estimate_messages_tokens_rough(messages),
            tokens_after=estimate_messages_tokens_rough(pruned), messages=len(pruned),
            tool_results_pruned=tool_results_pruned,
        ), turn_session_id=turn_session_id, require_target_session_id=session_id)

name: publish_provider_native
doc: Publish one provider-native compaction Hermes observed but did not run.

significant_calls.expression:
_publish(
            provider_native_payload, session_id=getattr(agent, "session_id", None) or "",
            compression_count=getattr(getattr(agent, "context_compressor", None), "compression_count", None),
            turn_session_id=_turn_session_id(agent),
        )

name: _timeout_fallback_prompt
doc:
Cached prompt, else a fresh build, else the raw ``system_message`` (never raises).
Resolved lazily by the timeout wrapper: an eager rebuild would raise before compress_context runs when
``_cached_system_prompt`` is unset and the builder fails.

name: _report_compression_timeout
arguments: agent, *, idle: float, waited: float, since_progress: float, total_ceiling: float, total_exhausted: bool, progress_observed: bool
doc: Host-side timeout bookkeeping: log, activity stamp, cooldown ladder, user warning.

significant_calls.expression:
emit(
            "⚠ Context compression reached its total ceiling "
            f"after {waited:.1f}s{progress}. No messages were "
            "dropped — continuing without compression. Run /compress to retry or /new for a clean session."
        )

emit(
            f"⚠ Context compression timed out after {idle:.1f}s with no output from the summary "
            "model. No messages were dropped — continuing without compression. Run /compress to retry, /new "
            "for a clean session, or check auxiliary.compression."
        )

name: _warn_commit_overrun
doc: Commit-phase ceiling breach: the SessionDB mutation must complete, so only surface it.

significant_calls.expression:
emit(
            f"⚠ Context compression commit is taking unusually long ({waited:.0f}s, ceiling {ceiling:.0f}s). "
            "Waiting for it to finish safely — if this persists, check SessionDB health (disk / lock contention)."
        )

name: _sync_persisted_markers
doc:
Mirror ``_DB_PERSISTED_MARKER`` stamps from the worker's snapshot onto a live list.
Matched by scoped identity; timestamp-less repeated content is ambiguous, so every scoped match is
stamped. Imported UNCONDITIONALLY: a silent fallback literal would split the stamping key from the flush's
and resurrect the duplicate-row bug.

name: _run_under_progress_timeout
arguments: agent, run, messages, system_message, *, active_fence, registration, fence_registration_lock, idle_timeout, total_ceiling, approx_tokens=None
doc:
Run ``run(fence, target_messages=snapshot)`` on the pool under the progress-aware timeout.
The pooled worker must NEVER share the caller's live transcript — a late engine after a host timeout could
rewrite it. It deep-snapshots on the worker and publishes only via an ADMITTED commit; a no-op/abort
returns the snapshot unchanged, so the ORIGINAL list is handed back to keep identity semantics.

name: _mirror_result_onto_live_lists
doc: Mirror persisted-marker stamps from the result list onto the live list(s).

name: _rebind_caller_session_context
doc:
Propagate a rotated session id to the CALLER's thread/ContextVar (idempotent otherwise).
The worker thread rotated hermes_logging's thread-local id; post-compression tools must resolve
HERMES_SESSION_ID to the child id.

name: _compress_context
arguments: self, messages: list, system_message: str, *, approx_tokens: int | None=None, task_id: str='default', focus_topic: str | None=None, force: bool=False, bypass_cooldown: bool=False, defer_context_engine_notification: bool=False, commit_fence=None, verbatim_tail: list | None=None, trigger: str | None=None, snapshot_is_current=None, overflow_reason: str | None=None
doc:
Forwarder — see ``agent.conversation_compression.compress_context``.
``force=True`` (manual /compress) bypasses the summary-failure cooldown; ``bypass_cooldown=True``
(provider-proven overflow recovery) runs one real attempt while the cooldown stays armed.

``force=True`` is passed by the manual ``/compress`` slash command so users can bypass the
summary-failure cooldown after an auto-compress abort. Auto-compress callers use the default
``force=False``. See #100661.

name: _elision_marker
doc: Render the non-imitable elision marker with per-instance byte counts.

name: elide
doc:
Cap ``text`` at ``limit`` chars, marking the elision with ``_elision_marker``.

Every model-visible renderer must truncate through here (#121548). ``text`` is
returned unchanged when it already fits. Otherwise the result is ``head + marker``
with accurate omitted/total counts and never exceeds ``limit`` (sized against the
widest rendering the counts can take), unless ``limit`` cannot hold the marker at
all, in which case the marker alone is returned.

name: elide_middle
arguments: text: str, head: int, tail: int
doc: Keep ``head`` chars from the start and ``tail`` from the end, eliding the middle.

name: _skills_block
doc: The live ``<available_skills>`` block inside the stable tier, or ''.

name: context_display_source
doc:
Distinguish the built-in preflight display seed from a provider reading.

Engines without the built-in real-usage ledger own their occupancy figure.
A seed never updates that ledger, even if its number later matches real usage.

name: context_usage_fields
doc: Current occupancy only; lifetime throughput is never a context fallback.

name: compute_session_context_breakdown
doc: Return a Cursor-style context usage breakdown for one live agent.

name: compute_context_details
doc:
Expanded per-skill / per-toolset cost listing for ``/context all``.

Reuses the ``hermes prompt-size`` attribution (index-line bytes from the
live skills block; schema bytes via the registry's tool→toolset map).

name: render_context_grid
doc:
Glyph grid: 100 cells, one per percent of the context window; categories
fill in declaration order, the remainder is free space.

name: render_context_category_lines
doc: Render the 'Estimated usage by category' table as plain-text lines.

name: _table
arguments: lines: list[str], title: str, rows: list[dict[str, Any]], fmt
doc: Append a titled, display-capped table (blank-separated from a preceding one).

name: render_context_details_lines
doc: Render the expanded ``/context all`` per-skill / per-toolset tables.

name: render_context_breakdown_lines
arguments: payload: dict[str, Any], *, details: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, grid: bool=True
doc:
Full /context view. ``grid`` prepends the glyph grid (CLI; the gateway
keeps its own gauge); ``details`` appends the expanded listings.

name: pin_summary_route
doc: Pin the next summary LLM call to an explicit route; ``None`` is a no-op. Re-entrant: restores the prior pin.

name: take_pinned_summary_route
doc: Read and consume the pinned summary route (single use: the main-model retry must not re-issue it).

name: take_deterministic_summary_pin
doc: Consume the pin when it is the deterministic sentinel; a real route (or no pin) is left in place.

name: _pinned_summary_call_kwargs
doc: Consume the pinned route as explicit ``call_llm`` keyword arguments.

name: _is_hygiene_preagent_only_cooldown
doc:
Return True for a cooldown that belongs only to pre-agent hygiene.
Hygiene watchdog timeouts / turn-hold deferrals are not evidence of an auxiliary-model failure and
must never block the in-agent compressor.

See #74136, #86972.

name: _response_finish_reason
doc: Lowercased ``choices[0].finish_reason`` of a dict- or object-shaped response; ``""`` when unreadable.

name: _is_summary_refusal
doc: Return whether a complete response is a refusal instead of a summary.

name: _response_refusal_text
doc:
Explicit provider ``choices[0].message.refusal`` (str, or dict with message/reason/text); ``""`` when absent.

OpenAI-style structured-output refusals put the refusal here and leave ``content`` as filler or
empty, so the prose detector never sees it.

name: _is_refusal_response
doc:
Single refusal predicate for both summarizer paths.

An explicit provider ``message.refusal`` wins even when ``content`` looks like a
summary; otherwise fall back to the prose detector on the extracted content.

name: _is_summary_access_or_quota_error
doc: Return True for non-retryable summary auth, permission, or quota errors.

name: _exc_status_code
doc: HTTP status carried on the exception itself or on its ``response``.

name: _fresh_compaction_message_copy
doc: Copy a message for compaction assembly without persistence markers (``_strip_persistence_markers`` is authoritative).

name: _template_visible_role
doc:
Role as counted by strict chat-template alternation checks.
Mistral-family templates exempt ``tool`` rows and assistant rows with ``tool_calls`` from
alternation. Returns ``None`` for messages the check skips.

name: _last_template_visible_role
doc:
Last role a strict alternation template would count in *messages*.

``None`` when every row is template-exempt (tool flow only).

name: _strip_persistence_markers
doc:
Enforce the invariant: no assembled message carries a persistence marker.
A leaked ``_db_persisted`` makes the child-session rotation flush skip the row, losing it from state.db.
Per-copy-site strips are positional and re-leak when a copy site is added; this terminal sweep makes the
guarantee structural. Run once on the fully assembled list; mutates in place (compaction-local copies).

name: _archive_watermark_for
arguments: session_db: Any, session_id: str, held: list[dict[str, Any]], start_watermark: Optional[int]=None
doc:
The archive watermark for a commit that rewrites the history this process holds.

Without one, ``archive_and_compact`` archives every active row, including turns another surface appended
to the same session since this process loaded it (a Desktop session continued from Telegram) and rows
that arrived while the commit was being built. Those never reached this process, so they would be marked
summarized away with no summary holding them: still displayed and searchable, but gone from the model's
history. Capping at the newest row the process held sends them down the
concurrent-append path instead (cloned after the new set), the same rule the in-place compaction commit
applies. *start_watermark* is the store's watermark from before any slow step; it defaults to now.
A store without the watermark API keeps today's archive-everything commit.

Raises :class:`StaleHeldHistory` when the newest held exact row is no longer active. The in-place commit
falls back to the lease watermark there because its lease rules out an overlapping compaction; prune and
micro-compaction hold no lease, so for them that fallback would publish a stale generation beside the one
that won.

name: stamp_db_persisted_markers
doc:
Fulfil the post-commit contract of ``SessionDB.archive_and_compact()``.
Single stamp site for all callers. Call ONLY after the commit succeeded, on the dict instances the
caller keeps live. Needed because compress() output is marker-swept for the ROTATION flush; an
in-place commit returned unstamped is re-INSERTed as new by the next persist walk and the transcript
doubles on every compaction.

name: _newest_checkpoint_carrier
doc:
Index of the last assistant message carrying a ``type: "compaction"`` item under *key*, or -1.
Transcript-side mirror of ``native_compaction.prune_pre_checkpoint_items``' newest-run-wins rule:
the wire builder drops every checkpoint before the last one, so this is the only carrier whose
checkpoint can still reach a request.

name: _set_sidecar
arguments: msg: dict[str, Any], key: str, kept: list[Any]
doc: Filter items, never leave an empty sidecar behind.

name: drop_shadowed_checkpoints
arguments: messages: list[dict[str, Any]], key: str='codex_reasoning_items', *, before: Optional[int]=None
doc:
Drop ``type: "compaction"`` items from every assistant row older than the newest carrier (rows at
index >= *before* are left alone). A checkpoint a newer carrier shadows has no reader on any wire:
``prune_pre_checkpoint_items`` rebuilds each request around the newest checkpoint run and the replay
gate drops checkpoints wholesale once native compaction is ineligible. Non-checkpoint items stay.
In place; returns the indices rewritten.

name: _prune_stale_reasoning_replay
doc:
Drop shadowed ``type: "compaction"`` checkpoints from assistant turns older than the active one; only the
NEWEST survives (``drop_shadowed_checkpoints``): a shadowed one was still copied into the compacted transcript
and every child session built from it (#102374). Per-turn ``codex_reasoning_items`` are never pruned: the
compacted list becomes canonical history, the wire builder already filters per issuer/model, and a later
switch to a route that reads earlier-turn reasoning needs them. In place; returns pruned message count.

name: _salvage_reduce_todo_snapshot
doc: Last-resort shrink: drop the synthetic todo snapshot, keeping only a pruned-skill reload notice if present.

name: salvage_grown_transcript
arguments: original: list[dict[str, Any]], candidate: list[dict[str, Any]], budget: Optional[int]=None
doc:
Mechanically shrink a compression candidate (copies, cheapest loss first); ``None`` unless strictly smaller.
Never strips reasoning (text or encrypted items): the result becomes canonical history replay reads.

name: _short_error_text
doc: Error text (or class name) capped for durable cooldown rows and telemetry.

name: _classify_summary_failure
doc:
Classify a summary-call exception by status code / message shape.

A "refusal content" RuntimeError (prose or provider ``refusal`` field) deliberately rides the
``empty_content`` class — cooldown + main-model fallback + abort — so the "returned empty content"
fallback log line is expected for refusals.

name: _next_timeout_cooldown
doc:
Bump ``compressor.<counter>`` and return the ladder rung for it.
Module-level (not a method) so callers that bind a single real method onto a stub still exercise the ladder.
``counter`` stays separate per failure class: the timeout streak also arms the deterministic stall fallback
(``_prior_timeout_failures``), which a truncation must not trigger.

name: _is_summary_stub
doc: True for a tool result already replaced by a 1-line ``[tool] ... (N chars)`` summary or a lean-tail demotion stub.

name: _skill_pruned_marker
doc: Return the canonical prune marker for *skill_name* (shared by emit and check sites).

name: _extract_pruned_skill_names
doc: Return skill names referenced by prune markers in *text*, in order.

name: _skill_view_failed
doc: True for a ``skill_view`` that loaded nothing: the raw failure payload or its ``[skill_view] … FAILED`` stub.

name: _collect_ghosted_skill_names
doc:
Skills about to be lost in compaction, whatever their size: marked or plain ``skill_view`` stubs, raw
``skill_view`` bodies, and skills a ``/skill``, bundle or auto-load turn carried inline.

name: _reinject_pruned_skill_markers
doc:
Deterministically restore prune markers the summarizer dropped.
Presence is checked against the canonical marker string; the appended block is plain body text (no
handoff prefix/scaffolding) and is redacted like all others.

name: _synthetic_user_row
doc: True for scaffolding user rows that carry no real user words.

name: _typed_user_text
doc:
A ``/skill``, bundle or auto-load turn as the user typed it (``/skill do X``); other text unchanged.
Its inline skill body is not the user's words — it is carried by a ``[SKILL_PRUNED: ...]`` marker instead.

name: _build_verbatim_user_section
doc: Compacted region's REAL user messages verbatim, newest-first under a char budget (straddler truncated); "" if none.

name: _build_recovery_footer
doc:
Deterministic pointer to the compacted region in session history.
state.db keeps every pre-compaction message; naming the session_search re-access path lets the model
treat compaction as deferred retrieval, not loss.

name: _build_anchor_index
doc: Regex-harvest exact identifiers from the compacted region (LLM-free); per-category caps, most-frequent first.

name: _skill_view_call_sites
doc: Yield ``(message_index, skill_name)`` for every skill_view tool call.

name: _collect_protected_skill_names
doc:
Skill names (lower-cased) whose skill_view bodies must survive Phase-1 demotion.
Recently loaded, loaded inside the protected tail, or named by a tail user message. Applies to
Phase-1/2 only; the Pass-4 pressure demotion ignores it.

name: _redact_compaction_text
doc:
Redact text that crosses a compaction summary boundary (strict mode).
``force=True`` overrides ``security.redact_secrets: false``; URL credentials are redacted too, since
summaries persist and re-enter every later prompt.

name: _dedupe_append
arguments: items: list[str], value: str, *, limit: int

name: _tc_get
arguments: obj: Any, key: str, default: Any=''
doc: Field of a dict- or object-shaped tool call (or its ``function`` sub-object).

name: _extract_tool_call_name_and_args
doc: Return a best-effort ``(name, arguments)`` pair for dict/object tool calls.

name: _tool_calls_by_id
doc: Map ``tool_call_id -> (tool_name, raw_arguments)`` over every assistant tool call.

name: _collect_path_mentions
arguments: text: str, relevant_files: list[str], *, limit: int=12

name: _collect_paths_from_jsonish
doc: Harvest path-like values (known keys + inline mentions) from parsed tool arguments.

name: _compact_fallback_turn
doc: One-line, redacted, length-capped rendering of a turn's content for the static fallback.

name: _bullets
doc: Markdown bullets of the first ``limit`` distinct non-blank items, or ``None.``.

name: _content_length_for_budget
doc:
Effective char-length of message content for budgeting: text by length plus the learned
per-image price (``agent.image_token_cost``, same figure the trigger estimator uses) per image.

name: _serialized_length_for_budget
doc: Return a stable char-length for non-content replay/metadata fields.

name: _reasoning_details_text_chars
doc: Thinking-text chars inside a ``reasoning_details`` envelope (never the signed/base64 envelope blobs).

name: _estimate_msg_budget_tokens
doc:
Token estimate for one message in the tail-protection budget walks.
Counts content, the full ``tool_call`` envelope (arguments-only undercounted parallel-call turns by 2-15x),
and always-replayed provider fields. Always-replayed fields are charged because the preflight estimator sees
the full shape; a mismatched size class protects blob-heavy rows as "small" and compaction re-fires.
``charge_stale_thinking=False`` skips newest-turn-only thinking keys. Accounting only; never mutates.

name: _last_index_with_role
doc: Index of the newest dict message with ``role``, or -1.

name: _last_assistant_index
doc: Newest assistant message index, or -1 (the one turn whose thinking may replay; see ``_NEWEST_TURN_ONLY_BUDGET_KEYS``).

name: _pending_tool_round
doc:
Indices of the tool results the transcript ends with — a round the model has not answered yet; empty when
the transcript ends in any other row. /steer rows after the round do not answer it: a steer is delivered
after the newest tool result before the next API call, and two can land in one iteration (one when the tool
batch ends, one before the request), so every contiguous trailing steer row is skipped.

name: _part_text
doc: Text of a content part: the string itself, a dict's ``text``, else None.

name: _with_part_text
doc: Copy of a content part carrying ``text`` (string parts become the text itself).

name: _content_text_for_contains
doc: Return a best-effort text view of message content (for substring checks only).

name: _restated_request_text
doc:
A user turn's text, stripped, after the last in-flight replay header if present.

A request restated by an earlier compaction carries the replay header (and possibly the
