arguments: method: str, params: dict[str, Any], *, text_parts: list[str] | None=None, reasoning_parts: list[str] | None=None

name: is_borrowed_credential_source
doc: Return True when ``source`` points at a borrowed/reference-only secret.

name: fingerprint_secret_value
doc:
Non-reversible ``sha256:<16 hex>`` fingerprint of one secret value.

Callers comparing a live secret against the ``secret_fingerprint`` left on
a sanitized (borrowed) pool row need exactly the digest this module writes.

name: sanitize_borrowed_credential_payload
doc:
Return a disk-safe credential-pool payload.

Owned sources pass through unchanged.  Borrowed sources keep labels,
source refs, status/cooldown metadata, counters and a fingerprint, but
every raw secret value field is removed.

name: _load_config_safe
doc:
Read-only config (``load_config_readonly`` skips the per-row deepcopy), None on any error.
Inside ``frozen_runtime_config`` it is the session's frozen config: a key rotated in config.yaml
must never seed a frozen session's pool.

name: _is_source_suppressed_fn
doc: ``hermes_cli.auth.is_source_suppressed`` (late-bound), or an always-False stub.

name: _normalize_pool_auth_type
arguments: provider: str, token: Any, auth_type: Any
doc: Infer pool auth metadata for token formats with one unambiguous meaning.

name: _codex_principal_identity
doc:
``(chatgpt_account_id, sub)`` of a Codex access token, or None when either claim is missing.

Decoded without signature verification: this only decides whether two credentials Hermes
already holds belong to the same principal, never whether a token is valid. Both claims are
required because members of one ChatGPT workspace share ``chatgpt_account_id`` yet have their
own subjects and quotas.

name: _codex_entry_tracks_singleton
doc:
Whether a Codex pool entry may adopt the auth.json singleton's token pair.

``device_code`` IS the singleton. ``manual:device_code`` is ambiguous: a legacy alias of the
singleton (same account, must follow its rotations) or an independent account added with
``hermes auth add openai-codex`` (must never be overwritten — adopting turned two logins into
one account, both hitting the same usage limit). Same principal proves the alias; unknown
identity fails closed.

name: _exhausted_ttl
arguments: error_code: Optional[int], *, sole_credential: bool=False, failure_reason: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Return cooldown seconds based on the HTTP status that caused exhaustion.

*sole_credential*: the pool has nothing to rotate to, so transient
throttles (429 and the catch-all default covering 403/5xx/unknown) are
capped to a brief cooldown; 401 keeps its own already-short TTL.

*failure_reason* is the classifier verdict: an OpenRouter ``key limit
exceeded`` and an xAI spending block both arrive as 403 but are billing,
and a 60s retry on a spent account just re-fails. Billing keeps the full
bench regardless of status; 402 is billing by definition.
Unverified billing (#82154) gets the short cooldown regardless of pool
size (the credential may be healthy), unless the status is a true 402.

name: _singleton_predates_entry
doc:
True only when the auth.json singleton is PROVABLY older than *entry*.

Both sides stamp ``last_refresh`` on every successful rotation. When
either side lacks a parseable stamp this returns False (cannot prove),
which keeps the historical adopt-on-difference behavior (#70111) intact
for legacy writers.

name: _normalize_custom_pool_name
doc: Normalize a custom provider name for use as a pool key suffix.

name: _iter_custom_providers
doc: Yield ``(normalized_name, entry)`` from the merged custom-provider config view.

name: _pool_keys_for_custom_entry
doc: Durable ``providers.<key>`` slug first, then legacy ``custom:<name>``.

name: custom_provider_pool_key_candidates
arguments: base_url: Optional[str], provider_name: Optional[str]=None, config: Optional[dict]=None
doc:
Return pool keys to try for a custom endpoint: the durable ``providers.<key>`` slug
(``hermes auth add <key>``), then legacy ``custom:<display-name>``, so a populated pool is not
skipped for the ``no-key-required`` placeholder. ``config`` is a frozen route's config: ITS
entry owns the endpoint, so a live edit of that entry's URL neither drops nor redirects the pool.

name: get_custom_provider_pool_key
doc:
Preferred pool key for a custom provider: durable slug, else ``custom:<name>``.

When provider_name is given, match by name first so two custom providers
sharing a base_url keep separate keys.

name: list_custom_pool_providers
doc: Return all 'custom:*' pool keys that have entries in auth.json.

name: _get_custom_provider_config
doc: Return the custom_providers config entry matching a pool key like 'custom:together.ai'.

name: get_pool_strategy
doc: Return the configured selection strategy for a provider.

name: _keyed_custom_pool_matches
arguments: pool_provider: str, provider_norm: str, base_url: Optional[str]
doc: Match a durable ``providers.<key>`` pool against runtime identities.

name: _legacy_custom_pool_matches
arguments: pool_provider: str, provider_norm: str, runtime_url: str
doc: Match a legacy ``custom:<name>`` pool against a named runtime identity.

name: credential_pool_entry_serves_endpoint
doc:
Whether a pooled credential may be bound to a session running at ``base_url``. ``_swap_credential``
adopts the entry's base_url too, so a same-provider entry for another endpoint (public OpenAI vs. an
Azure resource) would send the session's requests — and the entry's key — to the wrong host (#68237).
Entries or sessions without endpoint metadata (legacy adapters, test doubles) cannot rebind and are accepted.

name: credential_pool_matches_provider
arguments: pool_or_provider: Any, provider: Optional[str], *, base_url: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Return whether a pool belongs to the requested runtime provider.

Named custom endpoints may use three identities: the live agent can retain
the configured name/provider key, newer runtime paths normalize it to
``custom``, and the pool may be keyed as the durable ``providers.<key>``
slug or as legacy ``custom:<name>``. Accept those aliases only when the
runtime endpoint belongs to the same configured custom provider. Empty
identities fail closed. Legacy pool adapters without a ``provider``
attribute remain compatible; production pools are scoped.

name: resolve_runtime_pool_key
doc:
Resolve the credential-pool key for a runtime provider identity.

Named custom runtimes retain their configured alias while their pool may
be stored under the durable ``providers.<key>`` slug or legacy
``custom:<name>``. Return that scoped key only when the canonical
provider/endpoint boundary accepts it; otherwise preserve the normalized
runtime identity so callers fail closed.

name: _guarded_global_root
doc:
Apply the pytest seat belt to a resolved global-root auth.json path.

``None`` means classic mode (profile == root) or "refuse": under pytest,
never write the real user's ``~/.hermes/auth.json`` even when HERMES_HOME
points at a profile path (mirrors the read-side guard in
``_load_global_auth_store``). Uses the unmodified HOME env, not
``Path.home()`` which fixtures may monkeypatch.

name: _write_through_provider_state_to_global_root
doc:
Persist a rotated OAuth ``state`` into the global-root auth.json.

Best-effort write-through for the multi-profile rotation hazard: nous,
openai-codex, and xai-oauth rotate the refresh_token on refresh, so when
a profile pool refresh rotates a grant it resolved from the root fallback,
the rotated chain must land back in root. Otherwise root keeps a revoked
refresh token and every other profile dies with ``refresh_token_reused``
/ ``invalid_grant`` once its access token expires.

Only updates ``providers.<provider_id>`` in the root store; never touches
the profile store (the caller already saved that). Swallows all errors —
a failed write-through degrades to root-stale and must never break the
profile's own successful save. Mirrors
``hermes_cli.auth._write_through_xai_oauth_to_global_root``.

See #48415.

name: _singleton_target_for_entry
doc: Root ``.anthropic_oauth.json`` when *entry* is a borrowed hermes_pkce row, else None.

name: _store_owns_pool_provider
doc: True when an already-loaded *auth_store* has its own rows for *provider*.

name: _profile_owns_pool_provider
doc:
True when the ACTIVE auth.json has its own rows for *provider*.

Named profiles with no local rows read the provider through the
``read_credential_pool`` global-root fallback ("borrowing").

name: _borrowed_single_use_pool_root
doc:
Global-root auth.json when persisting a BORROWED single-use pool, else None.

``None`` means "persist to the active store as usual": classic mode
(profile == root), or the profile owns its own rows for this provider.

name: _update_root_pool_rows
arguments: provider: str, payloads: list[dict[str, Any]], global_path: Path, *, status_cleared_ids: Optional[Iterable[str]]=None, token_bases: Optional[dict[str, tuple[Any, Any]]]=None
doc:
UPDATE-ONLY merge of *payloads* into the root store's rows for *provider*.

A borrower may refresh the root's rows (rotation, cooldown state) but
never add or delete them — the root owns their lifecycle. In particular a
profile's singleton-prune (it has no ``.anthropic_oauth.json`` of its own)
must not delete the root grant, so ``removed_ids`` is ignored by callers.

name: persist_pool_entries
arguments: provider: str, payloads: list[dict[str, Any]], *, removed_ids: Optional[Iterable[str]]=None, status_cleared_ids: Optional[Iterable[str]]=None, token_bases: Optional[dict[str, tuple[Any, Any]]]=None
doc:
Persist a provider's pool rows to the store that OWNS them.

A named profile that sees a single-use-refresh provider (see
``SINGLE_USE_REFRESH_POOL_PROVIDERS``) only through the global-root fallback must not
materialize a local ``credential_pool.<provider>`` copy: that copy forks
the single-use refresh token, the first profile to rotate commits the new
pair only to its own file, and root plus every sibling die with
``invalid_grant`` (#100339). Such rows are written back to the root store
(under the root lock); everything else goes to the active store.

name: _upsert_entry
arguments: entries: list[PooledCredential], provider: str, source: str, payload: dict[str, Any]

name: _retain_sources_not_in
doc: Remove entries whose source is in *drop*; True if anything was removed.

name: _warn_copilot_raw_degradation_once
doc: WARN once per token per process when Copilot exchange degrades to raw token (#114740).

name: _reset_copilot_raw_degradation_warned
doc: Clear the degradation warning cache (for test isolation).

name: _seed_tokens_singleton
doc:
Codex / xAI: surface the auth.json ``providers.<id>.tokens`` singleton as ``device_code``.

Hermes owns its own Codex auth state and does NOT auto-import
~/.codex/auth.json: refresh tokens are single-use, so sharing them with
Codex CLI / VS Code causes refresh_token_reused races. Adoption is an
explicit one-time prompt via `hermes auth openai-codex`.

name: get_env_prefer_dotenv
doc:
Resolve a credential env var, preferring ~/.hermes/.env over os.environ.

The user's config file is authoritative; stale env vars from parent
processes (Codex CLI, test scripts) must not override deliberate .env
changes. load_env() memoizes on mtime, so per-call reads cost a stat().
An unresolved ``op://`` reference in .env yields to the already-resolved
value from the active secret scope (set by apply_onepassword_secrets());
otherwise every provider auth attempt would receive a URL instead of a key.

name: _warn_env_ingestion_once
doc:
WARN once per process per provider when an env credential is ingested into a paid pool.

Auto-ingesting OPENROUTER_API_KEY is what ARMS silent OpenRouter spend —
every downstream auto-detect keys off the pool having credentials.
Ingestion stays allowed (an exported key is arguable intent) but must
never be silent.

name: _env_payload
arguments: *, env_var: str, token: str, base_url: str

name: _env_key_var_candidates
doc:
*env_vars*, their numbered siblings, and the ``env:VAR`` names already persisted.

``VAR_2``, ``VAR_3``, ... are tried for every declared VAR until the first
one that does not resolve, so a `.env` or secret-manager project can back a
whole rotation pool with no config: setting ``NVIDIA_API_KEY_2`` is the
whole opt-in (#76593).

Env-backed rows are written to auth.json without their secret and
re-hydrated on every load; a row whose VAR the registry does not
declare would otherwise stay empty forever and be silently dropped
from rotation by ``_available_entries``.

name: _prune_stale_seeded_entries
arguments: entries: list[PooledCredential], active_sources: set[str], *, prune_env_sources: bool=True

name: _seed_custom_pool
doc: Seed a custom endpoint pool from custom_providers config and model config.

name: from_dict
arguments: cls, provider: str, payload: dict[str, Any]

name: has_available
doc:
True if at least one entry is not currently in exhaustion cooldown.

``_available_entries`` is not read-only (it prunes aged-out DEAD
manual entries and persists), so it must run under ``self._lock``
like every other caller or a probe can race a concurrent rotation.

name: lift_reopened_cooldowns
doc:
Clear cooldowns that have elapsed or (Codex) reopened early, then report availability.

The lift ``select()`` performs, without leasing an entry. ``has_available`` and
``next_available_at`` never run the early-reopen probe.

name: next_available_at
doc:
Earliest epoch time (seconds) any entry re-enters rotation.

``None`` when an entry is available now, or when no exhausted entry
carries a usable recovery time (empty pool, or only ``STATUS_DEAD``
entries). Callers must treat ``None`` as "no wait information".
Runs under ``self._lock`` for the same reason as ``has_available``.

name: _is_sole_credential
doc: DEAD entries never re-enter rotation, so <=1 non-DEAD entry means nothing to rotate to.

name: entry_id_for_api_key
_replace_entry
doc:
Swap an entry in-place by id, preserving sort order.

Self-locking (RLock) so the deferred refresh path — which runs outside
the pool lock — cannot tear ``self._entries`` against a concurrent
select()/rotation.

name: _adopt
arguments: self, entry: PooledCredential, *, persist: bool=True, **updates: Any
doc: ``replace(entry, **updates)``, swap it into the pool, optionally persist.

name: _quarantine_sources
doc:
Drop every entry seeded from *sources* and persist the removal.

Atomic read-modify-write of ``self._entries``: this runs on the
DEFERRED refresh path (outside the pool lock), so take the RLock here;
still-locked callers re-enter safely.

name: _is_terminal_auth_failure
arguments: self, status_code: Optional[int], normalized_error: dict[str, Any]
doc:
Detect upstream-permanent OAuth failures that won't recover on TTL.

Only 401s whose reason is a known terminal OAuth state count;
token_expired (refreshable) and reason-less 401s (possible glitch)
stay transient, as do 429/402. The one status-independent case is
``CREDENTIAL_PERSIST_FAILED_REASON``: no upstream response is involved,
the rotated pair never became durable and only a re-auth recovers it.

name: _mark_exhausted
arguments: self, entry: PooledCredential, status_code: Optional[int], error_context: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, *, persist: bool=True, failure_reason: Optional[str]=None

name: _sync_anthropic_entry_from_credentials_file
doc: Sync a claude_code entry from ~/.claude/.credentials.json if tokens differ.

name: _sync_entry_from_pool_store
doc:
Adopt a token pair rotated by another pool instance (anthropic, xai-oauth).

Re-reads the exact persisted row from the credential-pool store while
the shared cross-process auth-store lock is held. Direct integrations
load a fresh ``CredentialPool`` per request, so in-memory locks cannot
protect a single-use refresh token across requests or processes.

Anthropic borrowed sources (``claude_code``) are excluded: they are
reference-only rows whose secrets are stripped before reaching
auth.json, so re-reading yields empty tokens that would be adopted as
a "rotation" — blanking a usable credential. The singleton file, not
the pool store, is token authority for those sources; a row with no
token material at all is refused for the same reason.

name: _sync_entry_from_auth_store
doc:
Sync a Codex / xAI device_code entry from auth.json ``providers.<id>.tokens``.

A fresh ``hermes model`` / ``hermes auth`` login writes new tokens
under ``_auth_store_lock`` while the pool entry may sit frozen behind
a ``last_error_reset_at`` hours in the future; without this sync every
request fails with "no available entries" despite fresh credentials on
disk. Only singleton-seeded entries apply — env/API-key rows have no
auth.json shadow.

name: _sync_nous_entry_from_auth_store
doc:
Sync a Nous device_code entry from auth.json ``providers.nous`` if state differs.

Another process refreshing via ``resolve_nous_runtime_credentials``
writes fresh tokens under ``_auth_store_lock``; adopting them avoids a
"refresh token reuse" revocation on the Nous Portal.

name: _sync_device_code_entry_to_auth_store
doc:
Write refreshed pool entry tokens back to auth.json ``providers.<id>``.

Otherwise the next ``load_pool()`` re-seeds the stale singleton state
over the fresh entry — potentially a consumed single-use refresh
token. Applies to Nous, OpenAI Codex and xAI OAuth singletons.

``set_active=False`` everywhere: a sync-back is a token-rotation side
effect, not the user choosing a provider; ``_save_provider_state``
would flip ``active_provider`` to whichever provider refreshed last.

#74339: decide the root write-through on WHERE the state resolved
from (``_load_provider_state_with_source``), not on whether the
profile has a ``providers.<id>`` key — ``_store_provider_state``
creates that key unconditionally, which self-sealed the check after
the first refresh. When the grant came from the global root, write
back to root ONLY and skip the profile store so it never accrues a
shadowing key that blocks both the fallback and the write-through.

name: _apply_entry_to_singleton_state
arguments: self, entry: PooledCredential, state: dict[str, Any]
doc: Copy *entry*'s tokens into the provider's auth.json ``state`` in place.

name: _claude_code_credentials_lock
doc:
Cross-process lock keyed to the shared claude_code credentials file.

Unlike the per-profile ``_auth_store_lock()`` this serializes every
profile and process that might refresh a ``claude_code`` entry.

name: _fail_closed_unpersisted_rotation
arguments: self, entry: PooledCredential, exc: BaseException, *, store: str
doc:
Quarantine an entry whose rotated pair never reached its store.

For ``claude_code`` / ``hermes_pkce`` the singleton file — not
auth.json — is authoritative: ``_seed_from_singletons()`` re-reads it
on every ``load_pool()``. When the refresh POST succeeded but the
singleton write failed, the replacement pair exists only in memory
while the consumed pair survives on disk and would be re-seeded over
any row we persisted; the next refresh would replay the spent token.
So never expose or persist the rotated pair; mark the entry terminally
so it surfaces as an explicit re-auth requirement.

name: _single_use_refresh_lock_timeout
doc: Configured refresh POST timeout plus margin, so a slow token endpoint cannot starve the flock.

name: _commit_anthropic_rotation
arguments: self, entry: PooledCredential, refreshed: dict[str, Any]
doc:
Write a rotated Anthropic pair to its authoritative singleton, or fail closed.

claude_code -> ~/.claude/.credentials.json (so the fallback resolver
and other profiles see it). hermes_pkce -> ~/.hermes/.anthropic_oauth.json
(``_seed_from_singletons`` re-seeds it every load; a borrowed row commits
to the ROOT's file, never a new profile-local copy, #100339). Not
``endswith``: manual:hermes_pkce is pool-owned and a singleton for it
would be a second authority for the same refresh-token family.

name: _refresh_anthropic
doc: POST the Anthropic refresh, commit to the singleton, return the rotated (unpersisted) entry.

name: _post_tokens_refresh
doc: Codex / xAI: POST the refresh and return the rotated (unpersisted) entry.

name: _recover_failed_refresh
doc:
After a failed refresh POST: adopt a peer's rotation, quarantine a dead grant, or bench.

Another process may have consumed the refresh token between our
pre-POST sync and the HTTP call; re-read the provider's token
authority once more and adopt fresher tokens before giving up.

name: _mark_dead_refresh_grant
doc:
Mark a row whose refresh token was terminally rejected DEAD, if the quarantine kept it.

``_quarantine_sources`` drops only singleton-seeded rows; an independent ``manual:*`` login
(``hermes auth add``) survives, and an unmarked survivor re-enters rotation and re-fires the
terminal WARNING on every later refresh attempt. DEAD leaves rotation until a write-side
re-auth sync clears it (never via TTL).

name: _clear_terminal_tokens_state
doc: Drop the dead Codex/xAI token pair from auth.json unless a peer already rotated it.

name: _codex_quota_restored_upstream
doc:
Live-check whether an exhausted Codex entry's quota reset early.

A Codex 429 persists a ``last_error_reset_at`` that can be days out
(weekly windows), but the window can reopen before then (redeemed
reset, plan upgrade, OpenAI reset) — issue #43747. Only fires for
429/quota-shaped errors; the probe is throttled per token (5 min) so
it is safe on the hot selection path.

name: _refresh_pending_entries
doc:
Refresh deferred single-use-token entries OUTSIDE the pool lock.

Each refresh takes the cross-process ``_auth_store_lock`` (20+ s
possible) and merges into the pool through the self-locking mutation
primitives; failures are silently skipped.

Entries are refreshed one at a time with a lock-free spacing window
between consecutive holds: ``_refresh_entry`` legitimately keeps the
store lock across its POST (single-use-token safety — sync -> POST ->
write-back must be atomic across processes), so a back-to-back chain
of N holds can starve a waiter on the same profile's auth.json whose
timeout is shorter (a Desktop assistant start, AUTH_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
= 15s, vs the holder's max(15s, refresh_timeout + 5s)) for the whole
sweep (#124533). A short window between holds lets the waiter's
50ms poll cadence interleave; the chain still finishes promptly.

name: _reset_cleared_after
doc: Epoch of a ``hermes auth reset`` persisted by another process AFTER *entry*'s status, else None.

name: _resync_stale_entry
doc:
Re-read an exhausted/DEAD singleton-seeded entry from its token authority.

The user may have re-authed (``hermes model`` / ``hermes auth``, the
Claude Code CLI, another profile) leaving fresh tokens on disk while
the pool entry is frozen behind ``last_error_reset_at``. A ``hermes auth
reset`` run from another process while this pool is live is honoured the
same way (#89415): the in-memory cooldown would otherwise outlive it.

name: _available_entries
arguments: self, *, clear_expired: bool=False, refresh: bool=False, model: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Return (available, pending_refresh) for entries not in cooldown.

*clear_expired* resets elapsed cooldowns to STATUS_OK and persists.
*refresh* refreshes entries needing a token refresh (skipped on
failure) — except single-use-token providers (openai-codex,
xai-oauth), which are returned as *pending_refresh* so the caller
refreshes them outside the lock instead of stalling every pool
consumer during cross-process flock acquisition + OAuth network I/O.

name: _log_no_available_entries
doc: Emit the empty-pool INFO line at most once per throttle window.

name: _select_unlocked
arguments: self, *, refresh: bool=True, count: bool=True, model: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Select the best available entry; returns ``(entry, pending_refresh)``.

``count=False`` skips the ``request_count`` bump for selections that are
not going to serve a request (a forced-refresh target lookup).

name: reclaim
doc:
Entry *credential_id* once its cooldown has lifted (cleared and token-refreshed the way
``select`` would), else ``None``. Never bumps ``request_count`` or round-robin order: a
live session asking "may I go back?" every turn is not a request.

name: _identify_failed_entry
doc: Resolve the entry that issued a failed request from its supplied identity.

name: _rotate_unmatched
doc:
Rotate without marking anything when the failed identity matches no entry.

Falling through to current()/_select_unlocked() would bench an
innocent healthy key for the full TTL. But this must be BOUNDED
(#70401): with OAuth-token auth the 401's key hint never matches any
``runtime_api_key``, so every retry lands here, nothing is marked, and
the caller retries the same dead token forever (~6/sec, starving the
event loop). Cap consecutive no-mark rotations at one lap of the
available entries, then surface the error; no cooldown is written.

name: mark_exhausted_and_rotate
arguments: self, *, status_code: Optional[int], error_context: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, api_key_hint: Optional[str]=None, credential_id: Optional[str]=None, failure_reason: Optional[str]=None, model: Optional[str]=None

name: acquire_lease
doc:
Acquire a soft lease on a credential.

With *credential_id*, lease that entry directly. Otherwise prefer the
least-leased available credential (priority as tie-breaker); when
every credential is at the soft cap, still return the least-leased
one instead of blocking.

name: try_refresh_matching
doc:
Force-refresh the entry that supplied the failed request.

Direct integrations may reload the pool after a request failed, so
``current_id`` cannot identify the issuing credential. With no hint,
select WITHOUT the normal proactive refresh: the forced refresh below
must consume a rotating refresh token exactly once.

name: upsert
arguments: self, source: str, payload: dict[str, Any]
doc: Upsert unless suppressed (``hermes auth remove`` must stay stable across loads).

name: reset_status
doc: Clear only the target's local error state, preserving sibling cooldowns.

name: reset_statuses
doc:
Clear exhaustion state on every entry. Returns how many were cleared.

``failure_reason`` lives in ``extra``, not a dataclass field, so it is
stripped explicitly. The persist declares the cleared ids because the
disk-recency merge reads a cleared ``last_status_at`` (None -> epoch 0)
as a stale snapshot and would copy a still-binding cooldown back.

name: move_entry
doc: Place an entry at a clamped zero-based position and persist contiguous priorities.

name: pool_failure_reason
arguments: reason: Any, error_context: Optional[dict[str, Any]], billing_unverified: bool
doc:
The pool's failure reason for a rotation (*reason* is a ``FailoverReason``). A usage-window 402
benches only the refused model; an ambiguous billing body is sized as transient, not a 1-hour bench.

name: model_cooldown_until
doc:
Active cooldown blocking *entry* for *model*, or ``None``.

Callers that do not know the model stay conservative: any active model
cooldown blocks them, so an unscoped route cannot reuse the credential.

name: merge_model_cooldowns
doc: Latest reset per model across snapshots — each writer only observed its own model.

name: token_is_blocked
doc:
Whether a pool cooldown blocks *token* for *model*.

Closes the paths that hand out a native Anthropic token without
selecting it from the pool (env / borrowed credentials). Tokens the
pool does not know fail open: no row can attribute a cooldown to them.

name: _is_model_scoped_failure
arguments: self, status_code: Optional[int], model: Optional[str], failure_reason: Optional[str]
doc:
Anthropic per-model 429s, and a Codex ChatGPT-account model entitlement 400: the
account cannot use *model*, but the credential stays valid for every other model (#71970).

name: _cool_down_model
arguments: self, entry: PooledCredential, model: str, error_context: Optional[dict[str, Any]], failure_reason: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Record a cooldown for *model* on *entry* and every sibling sharing its key.

Same TTL policy as a credential-wide 429 (provider ``reset_at`` wins, a
sole credential keeps its short bench), except a ``model_entitlement``
rejection, which stays benched until the explicit reset path clears it.
Siblings matter because a ``model_config`` twin seeded from the same key
would otherwise be re-selected for the very model that just failed.
Caller holds the lock.

name: limit_state
doc:
What a picker should say about this pool's rate limits, or ``None`` when nothing is limited.

``{"scope": "account", "resets_at": epoch}`` when every live entry is benched credential-wide
(the whole login is out; another model won't help), else ``{"scope": "models", "models":
{model: epoch}}`` for the given *models* no usable entry can serve until a model cooldown
ends. Entitlement benches (a year: the plan lacks the model) aren't windows that reset, so
they're left out. Read-only: never clears or persists a cooldown.

name: plugin_row_is_expiring
doc:
An expiry-stamped OAuth row (a plugin's, or Anthropic's) is due within the skew of ``expires_at_ms``.

The token endpoint's ``expires_in`` is the only clock: many providers issue opaque bearers (Google's
``ya29.*``) with no JWT ``exp`` to decode, so without this a long session sends the dead bearer.

name: apply_plugin_refresh_result
doc:
Merge a ``refresh_credential`` return value into *entry*.

Field names go through ``dataclasses.replace``; everything else is merged into ``extra``
(mirroring ``PooledCredential.from_dict``). Before this split a token-endpoint-shaped mapping
with ``expires_in`` raised ``TypeError`` inside ``replace`` and the pool benched a row whose
single-use refresh token the server had already rotated — the login was lost.

name: is_terminal_plugin_refresh_error
doc:
True when retrying the same plugin refresh token cannot succeed.

Plugins have no per-provider code table, so the predicate is the structural one every built-in
flow shares: a structured ``AuthError`` that asks for a re-login, or one carrying a grant-dead
OAuth code. Transport errors, 429/5xx-shaped ``RuntimeError`` and plain ``AuthError`` without
that signal stay transient (EXHAUSTED for one cooldown).

name: recover_failed_plugin_refresh
arguments: pool: CredentialPool, entry: PooledCredential, exc: Exception
doc:
Recovery for a plugin hook that raised: adopt a peer's rotation, or quarantine a dead grant.

Returns ``(handled, result)``; ``handled=False`` means the caller should bench the row as a
transient failure. A peer process may have rotated the single-use token between our in-lock
sync and the hook's POST — adopt that pair before classifying the failure.

name: _parse_absolute_timestamp
doc: Best-effort parse of epoch seconds / epoch ms / ISO-8601 into epoch seconds.

name: tag_credential_source
doc: Record *source* on *provider* and return it (a no-op for objects that refuse attributes).

name: credential_source
doc: The source tag of a callable key, or None (string keys and untagged callables).

name: credential_label
doc: Translated label for a callable key's source (neutral when untagged); None for a non-callable.

name: adopt_external_logins_enabled
doc:
``auth.adopt_external_logins`` (default True).

Codex and Claude OAuth refresh tokens are single-use and rotate, so once Hermes borrows a CLI's
token pair the two programs hold one token family and whichever refreshes first logs the other
out. When the user opts out, Hermes never reads or refreshes those files and says so once per
process (INFO) the first time it would have.

name: find_removal_step
doc: First matching RemovalStep, or None (``manual``: nothing external to clean).

name: _remove_env_source
doc: env:<VAR> — clear from ~/.hermes/.env; hint when the shell exports it.

name: _remove_hermes_pkce
doc: ~/.hermes/.anthropic_oauth.json is ours — delete it outright.

name: _remove_auth_store_oauth
doc:
Clear auth.json ``providers.<provider>`` (nous, minimax-oauth, xai-oauth, openai-codex).

Suppression by the dispatcher is still required — otherwise
``_seed_from_singletons`` re-seeds from any path that rewrites the block.

name: _remove_codex_device_code
doc:
Codex tokens also live in ~/.codex/auth.json (Codex CLI's file, kept).

Suppress the canonical ``device_code`` key — not just ``removed.source`` —
so a ``manual:device_code`` removal still blocks the re-seed path.

name: _remove_copilot_gh
doc:
The same Copilot token is seeded as gh_cli AND env:<VAR> rows, so suppress
every variant or the duplicates resurrect the entry. gh CLI and shell state
are left untouched.

name: _suppress_only
doc:
remove_fn for sources whose backing file/config belongs to another tool
(Claude Code, Qwen CLI, config.yaml): never delete it, just suppress and
explain. ``{source}`` in a hint is the removed entry's source string.

name: _safe_int
doc:
Exact int (money-safe) or ``_SENTINEL``. ``int()`` directly, NOT ``int(float())``
(precision loss above 2**53 corrupts money); float-shaped strings fail.

name: new_credits_latch
doc: Fresh notice latch for :func:`evaluate_credits_notices`; every producer builds it here so a new gate key lands everywhere.

name: format_window_reset
doc:
Local-time reset for notices: ``HH:MM`` within 24h, ``Tue HH:MM`` within a week, ``Nov 3`` beyond (the
monthly large-model allowance), ``shortly`` once passed (the server rolls the clock on the next request, so a stale
stamp is never contradicted).

name: _resets
doc: `` · resets 15:56``; empty when the instant is unknown.

name: _spent_window
doc: The binding allowance's limit name (``daily``; an unknown id: the server's label) and its reset.

name: window_approach_key
doc: ``credits.window.<gauge id>``: one key per allowance, so a client replaces it in place.

name: _window_approach_text
doc: ``⚠ 90% of your weekly limit used · resets Thu 09:00``.

name: _stop_gauge
doc:
The full allowance behind the limit line, by :func:`agent.plan_limits.blocking_gauge` (the rule
``limit_hit`` reads, so the line, the retry time and the card agree). A full top-tier allowance counts only on
a refusal: the API stamps ``spend-source`` on every admitted request and never on a 402, so header-sourced
+ no source = this model was refused; an ``included`` source means the model is not top-tier and a seed
cannot know the model. A refusal no all-scope allowance explains is the top-tier one (a cold catalog).
``model_is_top_tier=None`` (tier unknown) counts the top-tier allowance as one that may stop the model, so
of several full ones the later reset wins and no retry is promised before the model can run.

name: _window_hard_stop
arguments: state: CreditsState, *, model_is_free: bool, model_is_top_tier: Optional[bool]=False
doc:
Blocking copy for a usage-window account, or None. ``paid_access`` is the portal's word (dunning);
then: payment paused with no credits (credits keep a paused plan going whatever the setting says; a
card update restores included usage), the large-model allowance used with no pay path, the window used with no
pay path. A free model keeps inferencing, so only the payment-paused line survives it.
The credits step comes from :func:`agent.plan_limits.credits_action`, the rule every limit surface reads.

name: window_stop_resets_at_ms
doc: When the allowance behind :func:`_window_hard_stop`'s limit line frees up (the same gauge).

name: _window_payg_text
doc: The one-shot PAYG line: the last request drew on top-up credits instead of the window. None otherwise.

name: _reconcile_sticky
arguments: key: str, text: Optional[str], level: str, latch: dict, to_show: list, to_clear: list
doc: Show / replace / clear one sticky line by key: a text change re-emits (clear first), None clears.

name: _evaluate_window_notices
arguments: state: CreditsState, latch: dict, *, model_is_free: bool, model_is_top_tier: bool=False
doc:
Notice policy for a usage-window account (see :func:`evaluate_credits_notices` for the contract).

Approach: each allowance warns once at 90% per reset (``credits.window.<id>``, a TTL heads-up; the
limit line takes over when it runs out). The top-tier allowance warns only while the session is on a
top-tier model (no other model moves it); a free model warns about nothing. grant_spent never fires (no
grant); a payment pause / depleted account reuses ``credits.depleted`` and its ``credits.restored``.

name: _sticky_notice
arguments: text: str, level: str, key: str

name: _is_nous_welcome_route
is_free_tier_model
doc:
True when *model* is a Nous free-tier model, using ONLY local data: (1) ``:free`` suffix — canonical
Nous free SKU marker; (2) ``stealth/`` prefix — stealth-preview SKUs are free without the suffix
(naming-convention trust: a PAID ``stealth/`` model would wrongly suppress the banner); (3) a PEEK into
``hermes_cli.models``' pricing cache (filled by the model picker; a miss never fetches). Fail-open to
False (depleted notice still shows): a wrong warning is recoverable noise; hiding it masks a real block.

name: evaluate_credits_notices
arguments: state: CreditsState, latch: dict, *, model_is_free: bool=False, model_is_top_tier: bool=False
doc:
Reconcile credits notices against the latch (see :func:`new_credits_latch`); mutates ``latch`` IN
PLACE. Pure — no I/O, no agent/run_agent imports. ``model_is_free`` suppresses ``credits.depleted`` (a
depleted account on a free model keeps inferencing) WITHOUT emitting "restored" — that fires only on a
genuine ``paid_access`` flip back to True. Returns ``(to_show, to_clear)``; caller emits to_clear FIRST.
A usage-window state (day/week percents, no grant) takes the window policy; everything else is unchanged.

name: _parse_window_fields
doc:
Usage-window fields from lowercased headers; None when the gauge list is absent or unreadable.
``spend_source`` outside its vocabulary reads as absent (fail-open).

name: _parse_field
arguments: kind: str, raw: Optional[str], default: Any=_SENTINEL
doc: One header value → field value; ``default`` when absent, ``_SENTINEL`` on a contract violation.

name: parse_credits_headers
response_is_usage_window
doc:
True iff *http_response* carries complete usage-window ``x-nous-credits-*`` headers (the same
test as ``CreditsState.is_usage_window``). Lets the window-only header captures leave every other
account untouched. Never raises.

name: _fixture
arguments: remaining: str, subscription: str, limit: Optional[str]=None, purchased: Optional[str]=None, *, paid: bool=True, reason: Optional[str]=None
doc: Fixture spec from *_usd strings; micros derived exactly (Decimal).

name: dev_fixture_credits_state
doc:
Fixture CreditsState for HERMES_DEV_CREDITS_FIXTURE, or None (unknown name / unset). Prod-leak guard:
applies ONLY when HERMES_DEV_CREDITS is also on, so a stray fixture env var never surfaces fabricated balances.

name: _credits_state_from_account
doc:
Map a NousPortalAccountInfo into a header-shaped CreditsState for the seed. Float account dollars →
micros plus a DISPLAY *_usd (formatting account floats is allowed; parsing a server *_usd is not). Fail-open → None.

name: _window_seed_fields
doc:
Portal ``usage_window`` (NousUsageWindowInfo or dict) → CreditsState window fields; None unless it
carries a readable gauge list with an all-scope allowance (same requirement as the header parser).

name: _remember_shown_band
doc:
Remember the usage band last evaluated for ``session_id`` (process-lifetime).

Desktop reap/resume rebuilds the AIAgent per turn, so the in-memory ``_credits_latch``
(and its ``usage_band``) never survives across messages — every rebuild re-announces the
current band as a fresh crossing (#101578). ``agent.session_id`` IS stable across those
rebuilds, so this map lets ``_hydrate_seed_state`` restore the band the user already saw.
Deliberately NOT durable: a real process restart is a real ``session open`` and the
cold-start seed should still warn immediately. Bounded (MRU eviction) so a long-lived
gateway juggling many sessions cannot grow it without limit.

name: restore_window_notices
doc: Load what this session already showed into a fresh latch (once per latch). Never raises.

name: apply_keep_going_change
doc:
The user just changed "Keep going on credits": the agent's state takes the new value now (the next
reply's headers confirm it) and the notice policy re-runs, so a "turn on Keep going" line clears at once.
The account snapshot the pickers read is refreshed in the background. Never raises.

name: forget_window_notices
doc: The session is no longer on a window plan: drop its saved lines. Never raises.

name: remember_window_notices
doc: Record the window notices this session shows now (process lifetime, bounded MRU). Never raises.

name: _hydrate_seed_state
doc:
Install a seed CreditsState on the agent and fire the notice policy once. Primes the crossing gate:
the cold-start snapshot IS the first observation, so a session opening in a band warns immediately.

name: _warm_nous_pricing_cache
doc:
Fill the in-process Nous pricing catalog so :func:`is_free_tier_model`'s peek can answer.
The peek never fetches and nothing else warms it during session start, so a cold process reads
an EMPTY catalog and a subscription-billed model — which spends no credits — still draws the
depleted banner. Fail-open: a miss leaves the peek exactly as it was.

name: rewarm_pricing_before_depleted_notice
doc:
Depleted account, model the peek cannot vouch for, Nous catalog cold: start a background warm
whose completion re-runs the policy and return True so the caller defers the depleted decision
to it — the session-start warm is one-shot but the catalog expires after
``_NOUS_CATALOG_TTL_SECONDS``, and a cold peek would bring the banner back for a
subscription-billed model. False = decide now: peek warm, not on Nous, a warm in flight (the
warm's own re-run included — fail-open, a failed fetch leaves the peek cold and the banner
shows), or a fetch already failed and the cache is still refusing to dial. May raise; the notice
path that calls it catches.

name: seed_credits_at_session_start
doc:
Hydrate agent._credits_state from the portal account (or a dev fixture) and fire the notice policy so
warnings show at session OPEN (TUI/desktop "ready" and plain-CLI first-turn setup). Idempotent once a seed
or real header populated _credits_state. Returns True iff it seeded this call. Never raises.

name: credits_pay
doc: Top-up credits will cover Hermes usage once the included allowance is used up.

name: depleted
doc:
``paid_access == False`` ONLY — ``remaining_micros == 0`` is a false positive
when the balance is zero but access is live (renewal pending).

name: is_usage_window
doc: A usage-window plan with at least one allowance that stops every paid model.

name: binding_gauge
doc: The all-scope allowance that binds (see :func:`usage_gauges.binding_gauge`). Usage window only.

name: used_fraction
doc:
Fraction of the cap consumed in [0.0, 1.0]; None without a computable denominator.
Credit-grant: guarded on the LIMIT FIELD (the real denominator), not ``denominator_kind``.
Usage window: the binding all-scope allowance (whichever stops every model first).

name: window_resets_at_ms
doc: Reset instant of the binding allowance.

name: window_exhausted
doc: An allowance that stops every paid model is full. Paused (payment) is NOT exhausted: nothing was spent.

name: top_tier_exhausted
doc: The top-tier allowance is full (a percent, like the others — not a blocked flag).

name: _subdict
doc: Walk nested dict keys; {} if any level is missing or not a dict.

name: _read_config_section
doc: Read a nested section of ~/.hermes/config.yaml. Tolerates missing file.

name: _bounded_count
doc:
*key* (a ``curator.<key>`` day/hour count), floored at 1 like ``curator prune --days`` already
refuses (hermes_cli/curator.py::_cmd_prune). A value < 1 collapses stale_cutoff/archive_cutoff
onto or past "now" in apply_automatic_transitions(), mass-transitioning every skill with any
past activity on the next automatic pass — unlike the manual prune path this runs unconfirmed,
so it falls back to the default instead of acting on the bad value.

name: get_consolidate
doc: LLM consolidation pass — OFF by default (prune only, no aux-model fork); ``hermes curator run --consolidate`` overrides per invocation.

name: should_run_now
doc:
Gates: curator.enabled, not paused, ``last_run_at`` present AND older than interval_hours. First observation seeds
``last_run_at`` to now and defers one interval, so a fresh install/update never mutates the library on its first tick.
``hermes curator run`` bypasses this; the idle check is the caller's.

name: _cron_referenced_skills
doc: Skill names referenced by any cron job (incl. paused/disabled). Best-effort: a cron import error or corrupt jobs store yields an empty set, never a crash.

name: _archive_as_curator
doc: Archive via skill_usage with the ledger actor tagged 'curator', so the ledger entry reads as an autonomous transition, not a foreground call.

name: apply_automatic_transitions
doc:
Move every curator-managed skill between active/stale/archived based on its latest real activity; pinned skills are
never touched. Built-ins are seeded with a baseline record on first sight so their inactivity clock starts NOW, not at epoch.
Returns a counter dict.

name: _reports_root
doc: ``~/.hermes/logs/curator/`` (telemetry next to agent.log, not under skills/). mkdir'd here too so gateway-only / bare-library entry paths work.

name: _needle_in_path_component
doc:
True if *needle* equals a complete filename stem or directory name in *path* — so "api" does not match
"references/api-design.md". Hyphens and underscores are normalised ("open-webui-setup" matches "open_webui_setup.md").

name: _skill_manage_args
doc:
Parsed arguments of a ``skill_manage`` tool call (JSON string or dict), or None to skip. With *raw_fallback*,
a malformed string yields ``{"_raw": raw}`` so substring matching still catches the common case.

name: _find_reference
doc:
First argument value (file_path, file_content, content, new_string, _raw — in that order) that references one of
*needles*. ``file_path`` must match a whole path component; content fields match on word boundaries so "test" does not match "latest".

name: _classify_removed_skills
arguments: removed: list[str], added: list[str], after_names: set[str], tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]]
doc:
Split ``removed`` into consolidated vs pruned. Heuristic: a ``skill_manage`` call on a DIFFERENT, surviving-or-new
skill whose file_path/content arguments reference the removed name is the "absorbed" signal; earliest match wins.
Returns ``{"consolidated": [{name, into, evidence}], "pruned": [{name}]}``.

name: _parse_structured_summary
doc:
Extract the required fenced ```yaml block (``consolidations:`` / ``prunings:`` lists) from the curator's final
response. Tolerant: missing block or malformed YAML → empty lists (caller falls back to the tool-call heuristic); a partial
block returns what parsed. Returns ``{"consolidations": [{from, into, reason}], "prunings": [{name, reason}]}``.

name: _extract_absorbed_into_declarations
_reconcile_classification
arguments: removed: list[str], heuristic: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], model_block: dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]], destinations: set[str], absorbed_declarations: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]=None
doc:
Merge heuristic (tool-call evidence) with the model's structured block.
First match wins; every removed skill lands in exactly one bucket:
- ``absorbed_into`` declared at delete is authoritative: existing target → consolidated; ``""`` → pruned; missing target → fall through.
- Model-declared consolidation wins when its ``into`` is in ``destinations``.
- Model named a missing umbrella → heuristic's finding, else pruned.
- Heuristic-only consolidation kept, marked ``source="tool-call audit"``.
- Otherwise pruned (model-declared, or no-evidence fallback).

name: _diff_and_classify
arguments: before_names: set[str], after_names: set[str], tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]], model_final: str
doc:
Diff the before/after skill sets and classify every removal: the model's YAML block carries intent + rationale,
the tool-call heuristic audits for hallucinated umbrellas/omissions, per-delete ``absorbed_into`` beats both.

name: _build_rename_summary
arguments: *, before_names: set[str], after_report: list[dict[str, Any]], tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]], model_final: str
doc:
The "where did my skills go?" lines appended to the user-visible ``final_summary``; "" when nothing was archived.
Capped at 10 entries so a big consolidation doesn't flood agent.log (full list is in REPORT.md); the pin hint
appears only when a consolidation produced an umbrella.

name: _rewrite_cron_refs
arguments: consolidated: list[dict[str, Any]], pruned: list[dict[str, Any]]
doc:
Point cron jobs at the umbrella when the curator consolidated a skill they list — otherwise the scheduler fails to
load it and the job runs without its instructions. Best-effort: a cron-module issue never breaks the curator.

name: _write_file
arguments: path: Path, label: str, render: Any
doc:
Best-effort write of *render()* (or the JSON dump of a non-callable payload);
rendering runs inside the guard so a serialisation error is logged, not raised.

name: _write_run_report
arguments: *, started_at: datetime, elapsed_seconds: float, auto_counts: dict[str, int], auto_summary: str, before_report: list[dict[str, Any]], before_names: set[str], after_report: list[dict[str, Any]], llm_meta: dict[str, Any]
doc:
Write run.json + REPORT.md under logs/curator/{YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS}[-N]/ (N disambiguates a crash-rerun in the same
second). Returns the report dir, or None if it couldn't be created (reporting is best-effort).

name: _render_report_markdown
doc: Render the human-readable REPORT.md.

name: _render_candidate_list
doc:
Human/agent-readable list of LLM consolidation candidates.

Bundled built-ins are excluded even when ``curator.prune_builtins`` is
on. That flag makes them eligible for *deterministic archival*
(``apply_automatic_transitions`` → ``archive_skill``), not for the
rewrite/umbrella pass. Listing them here invites umbrella deletes
that ``_background_review_delete_guard`` unconditionally refuses,
burning tool calls until the loop guard aborts the run.

Skills in ``skills.disabled`` (global or platform list) are excluded for
the same reason on the read side: ``skill_view`` — the pass's only read
path — refuses them, so the fork retries the same refused read until
the same-tool-failure halt ends the run with zero findings.

name: _llm_meta
doc: Structured result of an LLM pass that did not run (skipped or failed).

name: _consolidation_pass
arguments: prefix: str, auto_summary: str, dry_run: bool, before_names: set[str]
doc:
The LLM half of a run: fork (unless no candidates), then append the rename map (`old-name → umbrella`) so users
needn't dig into REPORT.md. Returns ``(final_summary, llm_meta)``; never raises.

name: run_curator_review
arguments: on_summary: Optional[Callable[[str], None]]=None, synchronous: bool=False, dry_run: bool=False, consolidate: Optional[bool]=None, trigger: str='manual'
doc:
Execute a single curator review pass: (1) automatic state transitions (no LLM); (2) if *consolidate* and there are
candidates, fork an AIAgent on the review prompt; (3) update .curator_state; (4) call *on_summary*.
*synchronous* runs the LLM review in the calling thread (default: daemon thread). *consolidate* ``None`` reads
``curator.consolidate`` (OFF by default); when off only the deterministic prune runs — no fork, no aux cost.
*dry_run* SKIPS the stale/archive transitions and instructs the fork to report only; REPORT.md is still written and
recorded in ``state.last_report_path`` so users can read what WOULD have happened.

name: _record_run_metric
arguments: trigger, dry_run, counts, before_report, after_report, llm_meta, hermes_home

name: _merge_request_overrides
doc: Merge resolver metadata with task-local request body fields.

name: _resolve_review_runtime
doc:
Curator is a regular auxiliary task slot (``auxiliary.curator.*``), so it rides the canonical aux-model plumbing. Precedence:
  1. ``auxiliary.curator.{provider,model}`` when both are set non-auto
  2. Legacy ``curator.auxiliary.{provider,model}`` (deprecated) when both set
  3. Main ``model.{provider,default/model}`` pair ("auto" + "" = main chat model)
Non-empty slot ``api_key``/``base_url`` are returned as explicit overrides so ``resolve_runtime_provider`` doesn't reuse the main chat credential chain.

name: _resolve_review_provider
doc:
``(runtime_provider, model_name, provider_name, request_overrides)`` resolved the way the CLI does: AIAgent() without
explicit provider/model hits an auto-resolution path that fails for OAuth-only providers and pooled credentials
(HTTP 400 "No models provided"). Never raises.

name: _run_llm_review
doc:
Spawn an AIAgent fork on the review prompt. Returns ``final`` (untruncated response), ``summary`` (240-char cap),
``model``/``provider`` (what ran), ``tool_calls`` ([{name, arguments}], truncated) and ``error``. Never raises.

name: _claim_run
doc:
One automatic pass per home across processes: two CLIs launched seconds apart both saw the
weekly interval elapsed and both pruned the tree. O_EXCL create wins the claim; a claim older than
an hour is a crashed holder and is taken over. When the lock dir cannot be created, run anyway.

name: maybe_run_curator
doc: Best-effort: run a curator pass if all gates pass. Returns the result dict if a pass was started, else None. Never raises.

name: _set
arguments: name: str, state: str, key: str

name: _slot
arguments: provider: str, model: str, slot: dict[str, Any]

name: _cons
arguments: into: str, source: str, reason: str='', **extra: Any

name: _excluded_member
doc:
Skip excluded names anywhere in the path, plus regeneratable DIRECTORIES (venv, node_modules,
caches — a 1.3 GB torch venv inside one skill made every snapshot 349 MB, #107539). Directory
parts only: a plain file that happens to be called ``venv`` is skill content.

name: _jobs_list
doc: jobs.json is ``{"jobs": [...], "updated_at": ...}``; also accept a bare list for forward compat. None otherwise.

name: _backup_cron_jobs_into
doc:
Copy the live ``~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json`` into ``dest`` as ``cron-jobs.json``. Never raises: a missing/unreadable
file yields ``backed_up=False`` plus a reason, and the snapshot proceeds.

name: _utc_id
doc: UTC ISO-ish filesystem-safe timestamp: ``2026-05-01T13-05-42Z``.

name: is_enabled
doc: Default ON — the whole point of the backup is safety by default.

name: _write_manifest
arguments: dest: Path, reason: str, archive_path: Path, skills_counted: int, cron_info: dict[str, Any]

name: _mkdir
arguments: path: Path, what: str, *, exist_ok: bool

name: snapshot_skills
doc:
Create a tar.gz snapshot of ``~/.hermes/skills/`` and prune old ones. Returns the snapshot dir, or None when
skipped (disabled, skills dir missing, IO error) — logged at debug so the curator never aborts a pass over a
backup failure. ``protect_ids`` survive the prune step (rollback protects its target).

name: prune_old_snapshots
doc: Apply ``curator.backup.keep`` without taking a new snapshot (the prune-only curator pass).

name: _prune_old
doc:
Delete regular snapshots beyond the newest *keep*; returns deleted ids. Ids in *protect* are never deleted —
rollback() uses this so the mandatory pre-rollback safety snapshot cannot evict the snapshot being restored.
Stale ``.rollback-staging-*`` dirs (crashed rollback) are cleaned up on every call; ``.rollback-unrestored-*`` is kept on purpose.

name: _is_restorable
doc: A real snapshot dir with a tarball (excludes ``.rollback-staging-*`` and retained ``.rollback-unrestored-*``).

name: _restorable_snapshots
doc: Restorable snapshot dirs, newest first.

name: list_backups
doc: All restorable snapshots (manifest dicts), newest first.

name: _resolve_backup
doc: Path of the requested backup (newest if *backup_id* is None); None if no match.

name: _restore_cron_skill_links
doc:
Reconcile backed-up cron skill links into the live ``cron/jobs.json``. Only ``skills``/``skill`` are restored,
and only on jobs that still exist live (by ``id``) — everything else is live state. Backup-only jobs are skipped
and reported; live-only jobs untouched. Never raises; writes through ``cron.jobs`` under the scheduler's lock so
we don't race tick().

name: _restore_excluded_subtrees
doc:
Move excluded entries (nested ``.git``/``.hub``/...) from *staged* back under *skills* after a successful extract.
Snapshots never contain these, so the staged copy of the live tree is the only source. ``.git`` may be a dir or a file
(submodule / worktree ``gitdir:`` pointer) — both are moved. Best-effort and conditional: an entry is carried only when
its parent skill dir was restored and nothing sits at the target. If the target snapshot predates the skill, the entry
is dropped with the staging dir rather than left orphaned; the safety snapshot excludes these paths too, so not undoable.
Returns entries whose move failed, so their only surviving copies stay staged for recovery.

name: _retain_staging
arguments: staged: Path, unrestored: list[str], reason: str
doc:
Keep a staging dir that still holds the only copy of *unrestored* entries and build rollback()'s failure result.
The dir is renamed out of the prunable prefix (unique suffix on a same-second collision). If the rename fails, the
original path is reported so recovery never raises out of rollback().

name: _unstage
doc:
Move staged entries back to their original paths; returns names that could not be restored. ``shutil.move``
moves *into* an existing destination dir, so partial-extract debris would bury the real skill
(``skills/foo/foo/``) — clear each original path first. The staged copy is authoritative.

name: rollback
doc:
Restore ``~/.hermes/skills/`` from a snapshot (explicit id or newest): safety-snapshot the CURRENT tree; stage
current top-level entries; extract; on failure move staged entries back. Returns ``(ok, message, snapshot_path)``.

name: entry_declares_credential
doc:
Whether a custom entry names its own credential (``api_key`` / ``key_env`` / ``key_cmd``). A
snapshot's provenance carries the verdict itself, since it never copies an inline secret.

name: row_owned_by_entry
doc:
Ownership by provenance: ``hermes auth add`` (manual) rows, and rows seeded from the entry's
own ``key_env``. Rows the built-in seeded from its registry env vars or auth files are foreign.

name: entry_scoped_pool
arguments: pool: Any, pool_key: str, entry: Optional[dict[str, Any]]
doc:
The rows of ``pool`` the custom ``entry`` owns: the pool itself when it owns them all, else a
view of them, or None when it owns none. ``custom:<name>`` pools are seeded from the entry's own
config and stay whole; so does any pool for an entry that declares no credential (as before).

The view shares the loaded rows and token baselines, so persisting it merges into the stored
pool under its lock and leaves the built-in's omitted rows on disk.

name: custom_entry_for_endpoint
arguments: base_url: Optional[str], provider_name: Optional[str]=None, config: Optional[dict]=None
doc:
``(normalized_name, entry)`` of the configured custom entry that owns ``base_url``: by name
first (a named entry's pool never serves another URL), else by URL. ``config`` is a frozen
route's config, whose entry owns the endpoint even after a live edit.

name: named_custom_entry
doc: ``(normalized_name, entry)`` of the configured custom entry ``provider_name`` names, else None.

name: pool_for_aux_provider
arguments: provider: Optional[str], pool_key: str, load: Callable[[str], Any]
doc:
``load(pool_key)`` for an auxiliary pool read (the key peek, credential recovery). A pinned
``custom:<name>`` normalizes to its entry's slug, which may also be a same-named built-in's pool,
so it gets the entry-scoped view; a bare built-in name keeps its whole pool.

name: _custom_identity
doc: ``(is_custom, custom:<name> or None)`` for a runtime's provider / requested_provider pair.

name: runtime_entry_owner
arguments: provider: Optional[str], requested_provider: Optional[str], base_url: Optional[str]
doc:
Credential provenance of the entry that owns a custom runtime, for its ``_primary_runtime``
snapshot: matched in the config the route runs on (the frozen scope, else the profile's), the way
resolution matched it. Names only, never a secret. None for a built-in or an unowned endpoint.

name: load_runtime_pool
arguments: provider: Optional[str], base_url: Optional[str], requested_provider: Optional[str]=None, snapshot: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
The pool for a runtime snapshot's identity. A custom runtime (``custom`` or ``custom:<name>``)
is the entry's, so it gets the entry-scoped view; a built-in identity loads its whole pool.
Ownership and the pool key come from the runtime identity, never from the pool slug, which both
share: a ``custom:<name>`` identity keys on its own entry, not the first entry on its URL.

``snapshot`` is the ``_primary_runtime`` being restored: the owner it recorded wins over live
config, so an edit can't reassign the endpoint or drop the entry's declared credential. A named
identity whose snapshot recorded no owner gets None and keeps the snapshot's own credential.

name: _mark_backend_suspect
arguments: backend: object | None, label: str, timeout_s: float
doc: Best-effort ``mark_suspect``; never raises, non-adopting backends tolerated.

name: _result
arguments: start: float, timeout_s: Optional[float], label: str, *, value: Any=None, timed_out: bool=False

name: clamp_timeout
doc: Normalize a timeout: None/non-positive/non-numeric/NaN -> None (unbounded), else capped.

name: _timeouts_section
doc: Read the ``timeouts:`` root section from config.yaml (read-only, fail-open).

name: _lookup_dotted
doc: Walk ``a.b.c`` through nested dicts; return None when absent.

name: resolve_timeout
arguments: key: str, *, default: Optional[float], env_var: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Resolve a timeout (seconds): dotted ``timeouts.<key>`` > ``env_var`` > ``default``; the winner
goes through :func:`clamp_timeout`, invalid config/env values fall through with a warning.

name: _consume_abandoned
doc: Observe an abandoned task's outcome so it never logs 'never retrieved'.

name: _abandon
doc: Cancel ``task`` and never await it; its outcome is consumed so it stays unobserved-safe.

name: _run_abandon_cleanup
doc: Run abandonment cleanup fire-and-forget (its failures swallowed).

name: run_bounded_async
arguments: awaitable: Awaitable[Any], timeout: Optional[float], *, label: str='operation', on_abandon: Optional[Callable[[], Awaitable[Any]]]=None, dump_on_blocked_loop: bool=True, backend: object | None=None
doc:
Await ``awaitable`` under a wall-clock deadline independent of loop timers.

Operation exceptions (incl. ``CancelledError`` from a caller cancelling *us*) propagate
unchanged. On timeout the task is cancelled and **abandoned** (never awaited —
cancellation-shielded scopes are exactly the paths that wedge); ``on_abandon`` runs detached.

name: run_bounded_sync
arguments: fn: Callable[[], Any], timeout: Optional[float], *, label: str='operation', on_timeout: Optional[Callable[[], None]]=None, backend: object | None=None
doc:
Run ``fn`` in a daemon worker thread under a wall-clock deadline; exceptions re-raise in
the caller. On expiry the worker is **abandoned** (every timeout leaks one daemon thread, so
do NOT use per-item in hot loops) and ``on_timeout`` runs best-effort in the caller's thread.
The worker runs under ``contextvars.copy_context()`` so secret scope / session id survive.

See #94285.

name: _process_tree_snapshot
doc:
Stop each hard-kill target before discovering its children: a running
parent can fork after psutil builds its PID map and escape the final signal.
Resume anything we stopped if signalling fails. Graceful signals never stop
their recipients, since their handlers must remain able to run.

name: kill_process_tree
doc:
Terminate ``pid`` and all its descendants, portably; True when anything was signalled.

Windows: ``taskkill /F /T`` (``sig`` ignored). POSIX: snapshot descendants via
psutil; for SIGKILL, stop and rescan the live tree so a concurrent fork cannot
escape a stale snapshot. Signal identity-checked descendants before their
parent, then its group when ``pid`` leads one. Stopping is best-effort with a
bounded wait; unavailable psutil still leaves process-group cleanup. Other
signals do not suspend recipients. ``sig`` defaults to ``SIGKILL``.

name: list_backends
doc: ``default`` first, then every registered backend (unavailable ones included, with their reason).

name: get_session_backend
doc: The session's override, ``None`` when it follows config.yaml.

name: set_session_backend
doc:
Switch one session's backend; ``None``/blank clears the override. Raises ``ValueError`` (with the
reason) for a backend that cannot run here, so a typo never leaves the session broken.

name: set_global_backend
doc:
Persist ``delegation.backend`` to the active profile's config.yaml (raw user config, never merged
defaults) and drop ``session_key``'s override, which would otherwise shadow it. Raises ``PermissionError``
on a package-manager-managed install (its config.yaml is not ours to write) and ``ValueError`` for a backend
that cannot run.

name: session_delegation_config
doc: ``config`` (the ``delegation`` section) with the calling session's backend override applied.

name: delegated_child_context
doc:
Mark child execution and isolate its task-local session identity. Even a context
entered without an id must restore the parent's session ContextVar (child
construction calls ``set_current_session_id``).

name: is_delegated_child_context
doc: Return True while code is running for a delegate_task child.

name: enter_non_dispatcher_owned_context
doc: Token form of :func:`non_dispatcher_owned_context` for long try/finally scopes.

name: exit_non_dispatcher_owned_context
doc: Restore the flag saved by :func:`enter_non_dispatcher_owned_context`.

name: non_dispatcher_owned_context
doc:
Mark in-process execution that does NOT own the dispatcher's Kanban task; without it
a cron agent run inside a worker is misread as that worker (kanban toolset force-added,
``kanban_complete`` defaulting to its task). ContextVar-scoped rather than clearing
os.environ, which the worker's claim heartbeat and concurrent readers share.

name: is_dispatcher_owned_worker_context
doc: The single predicate every ``HERMES_KANBAN_*`` identity gate should use.

name: explicit_board_intent_is_pinned
doc:
Whether an explicit kanban ``board=`` argument must still resolve through
the dispatcher-injected env pins (``HERMES_KANBAN_DB`` & friends) rather than
its own board directory.

True for in-process delegate children, descendants carrying
:data:`DELEGATED_CHILD_ENV_MARKER`, and dispatched workers
(``HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`` set). The pins are the "workers physically cannot
see other boards" isolation, and :func:`kanban_path_is_fenced` checks the
pinned path / fenced root — an explicit board that resolved elsewhere would
also escape that fence. Outside these fences an explicit board is the
caller's own intent and wins.

name: owned_kanban_task
doc:
The board task this execution OWNS: ``HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`` for the dispatcher-owned
worker, ``""`` otherwise. Tool access is not worker identity — a profile can expose the
kanban toolset interactively, and children/cron runs inherit the env var — so every
reader that turns the task id into worker behaviour (guidance, stop nudge, terminal
outcomes) goes through this one helper.

name: is_delegated_child_process_context
doc: Return True in this process or a subprocess spawned by a child.

name: _fenced_kanban_root
doc:
The board root this process's Kanban lineage lives under (``kanban_home()``); ``"1"`` when it
cannot be resolved, which readers treat as "fence every board" (the pre-path marker).

name: scrub_kanban_env
doc:
Remove worker identity, retaining board/location and an inherited write fence.

TASK absence alone would promote a descendant to an orchestrator. The marker
survives later execs, including scripts that remove TASK themselves. This is
cooperative runtime scoping, not confinement of code with direct SQLite access.

The marker's value is the fenced board ROOT, so the fence applies to the lineage's
board and not to every Kanban DB the descendant touches: a child running a repro
against a temp ``HERMES_HOME`` got a silently read-only board there. An inherited
path-valued marker is kept (a grandchild that moved HERMES_HOME must not re-fence
onto its scratch root and unfence the real one).

name: kanban_path_is_fenced
doc:
Whether Kanban mutations at *path* (a board DB or board-metadata root) are denied for this
process: always for an in-process delegate child (the parent's own board); for a spawned
descendant only when *path* is the dispatcher-pinned ``HERMES_KANBAN_DB`` or lies under the
fenced root the marker carries. A legacy ``"1"`` marker fences everything.

name: delegated_child_subprocess_env
arguments: env: Mapping[str, str] | MutableMapping[str, str] | None=None
doc:
Carry worker/delegate descendant denial across a real process spawn.

Location and credentials are untouched; callers retain their existing secret policy.
Dispatcher workers and supervised tool transports grant their own explicit scope.

name: settings
doc: This backend's settings: ``delegation.backends.<name>`` (empty when unset or not a mapping).

name: summary
doc: One user-facing line for backend pickers (``/delegation``); never shown to the model.

name: is_available
doc:
Whether this provider can run here. MUST NOT make network calls. False fails delegation closed: a
``delegate_task`` call under this backend is a tool error naming it, never a run on another route.

name: task_parameters
doc:
Extra per-task JSON-schema properties, ``{name: schema}``, merged into
``delegate_task``'s ``tasks.items.properties``.

Called when the tool definitions are built for a session, never mid-conversation, and the
result must be deterministic for a given ``config`` (same input, same bytes): the schema
is part of the cached prompt prefix. Names in :data:`RESERVED_TASK_PARAMETERS` are
refused. An ``enum`` here is enforced by core before :meth:`route_task` runs, and a task
carrying a parameter this method did not declare is refused before it reaches you.

name: description
doc:
Optional guidance appended to the ``delegate_task`` description (same caching rule
as :meth:`task_parameters`).

name: route_task
arguments: self, task: Mapping[str, Any], config: Mapping[str, Any]
doc:
Return the route for one task (vocabulary in the module docstring).

``task`` carries ``goal``, ``context``, ``index`` and the values the model supplied for
this provider's :meth:`task_parameters` (absent when omitted). Raise
:class:`DelegationRouteError` to refuse the task.

name: configured_backend
doc: ``delegation.backend`` normalized; blank/non-string means ``default``.

name: _load_bundled
doc:
The bundled strategy ``plugins/delegation/<name>/`` on first use when the plugin sweep has not
registered it (a runtime that never ran discovery, or pinned it with zero plugins): delegation is a
core tool and must not depend on the sweep. ``plugins.disabled`` wins on every call, so a later
disable takes effect without a restart.

name: _usable
doc:
The available provider for ``name``: the registered one, else a bundled strategy of that name
(also when the registered one reports unavailable), else one plugin discovery sweep (a caller
that never imported ``model_tools``).

name: backend_status
doc:
``(provider, "")`` when backend ``name`` can run here, else ``(provider or None, reason)``; the reason is
the user-facing fix (it becomes the ``delegate_task`` tool error).

name: get_active_provider
doc:
The provider ``config`` (the ``delegation`` section) selects; ``default`` when unset. Raises
:class:`DelegationRouteError` naming the backend and the fix when it is not registered or unavailable.

name: _display_url
doc: Extract a display-only URL without assuming model argument types.

name: _http_url
doc: ``candidate`` when it parses as an absolute http(s) URL, else None.

name: _get_skin
doc: Active skin config, or None when unavailable (lazy import avoids cycles).

name: _fg
arguments: r: int, g: int, b: int

name: _tinted_bg
arguments: rgb: tuple[int, int, int], dominant: int

name: _diff_ansi
doc: Return ANSI escapes for diff display, resolved from the active skin.

name: set_tool_preview_max_len
doc: Set the global max length for tool call previews. 0 = no limit.

name: get_tool_preview_max_len
doc: Return the configured max preview length (0 = unlimited).

name: verbose_tool_args_text
arguments: args: dict, max_len: int, code_block: bool
doc:
Verbose tool-progress args: compact JSON (capped at ``max_len``; 0 = no cap). On markdown
platforms it goes in a code block so the formatter keeps it verbatim (``**x**``/``a_b`` are
otherwise rendered as markup), with JSON's ``\n``/``\t`` shown as real line breaks. Args
holding ``` stay plain: Slack and Discord end a code block at any ``` inside it.

name: set_friendly_tool_labels
doc: Toggle friendly human-phrased tool labels (display.friendly_tool_labels).

name: get_skin_tool_prefix
doc: Get tool output prefix character from active skin.

name: get_tool_emoji
doc: Display emoji for a tool: skin ``tool_emojis`` override, then registry, then *default*.

name: _oneline
doc: Collapse whitespace (including newlines) to single spaces.

name: _tail_trunc
doc:
Tail-truncate to ``limit`` chars with ``...`` (0/None = unlimited). The result never
exceeds ``limit``: for 1-3 the ellipsis itself is clipped (``text[:limit - 3]`` would go
negative and hand back almost the whole string, #9439).

name: _clip
doc: ``text[:n]`` plus ``...`` when longer (used inside quoted previews).

name: _scan_quoted
doc: Yield ``(index, char, inside_quotes)``; a quote closes unless backslash-escaped.

name: _strip_shell_pipe_tail
doc: Drop a trailing ``| head/tail/wc/sort/uniq ...`` pipeline stage.

name: _split_shell_compound
doc: Split on unquoted ``&&`` / ``||`` / ``;`` / newline, dropping pipe tails per segment.

name: _shell_head_word
doc: Command name of a segment, skipping leading ``VAR=value`` assignments.

name: _clean_shell_segment
doc: Drop redirections (``> file``, ``2>&1``) from a segment.

name: summarize_shell_command
doc: Compact shell wrapper/plumbing for display while preserving raw command elsewhere.

name: redact_browser_typed_text_for_display
doc:
Replace every occurrence of a secret-looking browser_type value with its redacted form.

Backends echo the attempted input in error strings/metadata, so it is swapped before
reaching logs, callbacks, the model, or chat history. Forced regardless of
``security.redact_secrets``: a leaked typed credential is a security boundary.

name: redact_tool_args_for_display
doc: Return a copy of tool args safe for logs/progress UI (masks ``browser_type`` secrets).

name: _delegate_task_goals
doc: One truncated goal string per dict task (``?`` when missing).

name: _browser_exec_step_label
doc: User-friendly step label from browser_exec code's leading comment.

name: _delegate_action_preview
doc: Shared ``list/steer/stop <id>`` preview for delegate_task, or None for spawn calls.

name: build_tool_preview
arguments: tool_name: str, args: dict, max_len: int | None=None
doc:
Build a short preview of a tool call's primary argument for display.

*max_len* ``None`` defers to the global ``_tool_preview_max_len``; ``0`` means unlimited.

name: _primary_arg_preview
arguments: tool_name: str, args: dict, max_len: int

name: prepare_tool_preview
arguments: tool_name: str, args: dict | None, *, fallback: str, max_len: int
doc:
Compact preview plus explicit truncation/URL facts (the uncapped preview is
rebuilt from the arguments so an upstream display cap cannot drop its link target).

name: tool_row_emoji
arguments: tool_name: str, args: dict | None=None, default: str='⚡'

name: get_tool_verb
doc:
Friendly verb for a built-in tool, or None (labels disabled / no curated verb);
callers compose ``f"{verb}{tool_verb_connector(tool)}{preview}"`` themselves.

name: tool_verb_connector
doc: Return the connector between a verb and its preview (" for " or " ").

name: verb_drops_preview
doc: Whether the verb should render alone, without the argument preview.

name: build_status_phrase
arguments: tool_name: str, args: dict | None, max_len: int=49
doc:
Lowercase "is <verb> <preview>…" phrase following the bot's display name (Slack setStatus).

``args=None`` gives a verb-only phrase (``display.live_status: verb`` keeps previews out
of shared channels). None for ``_thinking`` or disabled labels so callers use their
static default. Default ``max_len`` stays under Slack's ~50-char status truncation.

name: build_tool_label
arguments: tool_name: str, args: dict, max_len: int | None=None

name: _resolved_path
doc: Resolve a possibly-relative filesystem path against the current cwd.

name: _snapshot_text
doc: Return UTF-8 file content, or None for missing/unreadable files.

name: _display_diff_path
doc: Prefer cwd-relative paths in diffs when available.

name: _resolve_skill_manage_paths
doc: Resolve skill_manage write targets to filesystem paths.

name: _resolve_local_edit_paths
