doc: Canonical usage for ``response`` or None (no usage / normalization failed).

name: _estimate_attempt_cost
doc: Best-effort USD estimate for one attempt. None when unknown.

name: _zero_output
doc: Return (usage_present, zero_output) for a response, failing open.

name: record_empty_attempt
arguments: agent: Any, *, finish_reason: str, response: Any, observed_generation: bool=True
doc:
Record one empty completion in the current streak.

Call BEFORE ``_empty_content_retries`` is incremented: a counter of 0 marks a new
streak and clears prior history.

name: deterministic_empty
doc:
True when the current streak looks deterministic.

Requires >= 2 consecutive attempts with an identical (model, provider,
finish_reason) signature. Usage-backed attempts must all prove zero output.
Usage-absent attempts must all have no observed content or reasoning. Mixed
evidence fails open so ambiguous transients keep their retries.

name: empty_retry_budget
doc:
Empty-retry budget for the current streak (3, or 1 when a single attempt is
estimated to cost more than the configured threshold).

name: streak_cost_usd
doc: Accumulated estimated cost of the current empty streak, if known.

name: is_reasoning_level_rejection
doc:
Provider 400 rejecting the *value* of a reasoning wire control against the endpoint's closed
level set ("'reasoning_effort' must be one of: 'minimal', 'low', …", Alibaba token-plan /
DashScope routes, code ``invalid_parameter_error``). The reasoning-field token must be present
next to the wording — a 400 enum complaint about some other field is not this class. The field is
understood and has to stay on the wire; only the disabled level ("none") is invalid, so the
recovery is the floor step-up in the auxiliary ladder and the disable-drop in the main loop, not
the strip rung and not an abort to the fallback chain.

name: is_reasoning_required_rejection
doc:
Provider 400 saying the model's reasoning cannot be switched OFF ("Reasoning is mandatory for
this endpoint and cannot be disabled", the Nous Portal on gpt-6-astra) — or refusing the OFF
*level* because the endpoint's closed set starts at ``minimal``
(``is_reasoning_level_rejection``). The opposite of ``is_reasoning_field_rejection``: the field is
understood, the *disable* is refused, so the right reaction is to step the effort up to the
lowest level rather than drop the field (a dropped field also works, but tells the caller nothing
about the next call).

name: is_reasoning_field_rejection
doc:
Provider 400 rejecting a reasoning wire control by name (``reasoning_effort``, ``reasoning``,
``thinking``/``think``): the field token plus either a generic unsupported marker ("Unrecognized
request argument supplied: reasoning_effort", #112781) or a standalone "unsupported" next to the
field in either word order ("unsupported reasoning_effort"; "reasoning_effort 'none' unsupported;
use minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh", #114460). The route default is the right answer for such a
model, so both the main loop and the auxiliary ladder retry once without the disable. A body
whose structured ``param``/code names the reasoning field (``'param': 'reasoning.effort'``,
``invalid_reasoning_effort``, #100536) is a rejection whatever the message says — even none.

Known trade-off: a 400 about a thinking *state* ("Function calling is not supported when
thinking is enabled") also matches — the marker sits right next to the token, so no proximity
rule separates it from the forward wordings. Cost is one dropped-disable retry before the
spent path takes the fallback chain; the auxiliary ladder already treated it this way.

name: _billing_hints
doc: Billing verdict carrying the #82154 ambiguity marker when applicable.

name: _first_match
doc: Verdict of the first rule whose pattern list hits ``error_msg``.

name: _plugin_verdict
doc:
First valid plugin classification (runs before the built-in pipeline so a
provider plugin can add or correct verdicts). invoke_hook isolates callback
failures; this guard only covers import/dispatch failure.

name: _profile_verdict
doc:
The current provider's own ``ProviderProfile.classify_api_error`` verdict, or None.

A ``kind: model-provider`` plugin never enters the PluginManager hook lifecycle, so without this a
vendor-specific body (a 403 ``quota_exhausted`` that is billing, not auth) could only be corrected by
shipping a second plugin component. Scoped to the provider that produced the error; no name table.

name: _nous_welcome_tier
doc:
The Nous inference gateway's welcome-tier (free tier) refusals, read from the structured body.

A 429 carrying a fairshare ``reason`` is either a tier gate (``model_not_free`` /
``feature_not_free``: the model or feature is never served on the free tier, so retrying is
pointless — abort this route and fall back) or capacity (``at_capacity`` / ``admission_closed``
/ ``rate_limited``: honour ``retry_after``, never rotate the free tier's only credential). A
400/403 whose message names the wrong host or a dark tier is deterministic for the request.
The parsed refusal rides ``error_context`` so the terminal copy can say what happened.

name: _provider_special_cases
doc: Highest-priority provider-specific shapes that a status code would misroute.

name: _by_error_code
doc: Structured error codes from the response body.

name: _by_message
doc:
Message patterns when no status code settled it; status-less usage
limits get the same disambiguation as 402.

name: _by_transport
doc: SSL, disconnect, circuit-breaker and transport-type heuristics, in that order.

name: _by_status
doc: HTTP status code with message-aware refinement (unlisted 4xx/5xx → generic).

name: classify_api_error
arguments: error: Exception, *, provider: str='', model: str='', approx_tokens: int=0, context_length: int=200000, num_messages: int=0, base_url: str='', api_key: Any=None
doc:
Classify an API error into a structured recovery recommendation (see ``_STAGES``).

``base_url`` (optional) is the route the call went to; the Nous welcome tier keys its
dark-tier 403 on it because that refusal carries no distinguishing message.
``api_key`` identifies an anonymous request; a host or fairshare reason alone does not.
The credential is never included in the returned context.

name: _off_route_host
doc: The contacted host when ``base_url`` is set and is not the provider's own endpoint; ``""`` otherwise.

name: _is_nous_route
doc: The usage-window 402 code is Nous's: any other upstream sending it keeps main's text rules.

name: _classify_402
arguments: error_msg: str, result_fn: Callable[..., Any], code: str='', body: Any=None
doc:
Disambiguate 402: "usage limit, try again in 5 minutes" is a periodic quota, not billing.
The Nous usage-window code is decisive (its prose names the reset time, which must not
demote it to a transient rate limit); every other 402 keeps the text rules. A usage-window 402's
optional ``display_message`` (server-set wording) rides in ``error_context`` for the refusal line.

name: _usage_window_display_message
doc:
The server's optional wording for a usage-window 402 (top level or under ``error``), trimmed and
capped; "" when absent.

name: _has_large_inline_image
doc:
True when a rejected ``content`` list carries a ``data:image/`` part the shrink pass would rewrite
(over ``conversation_compression._IMAGE_SHRINK_TARGET_BYTES``; below it a shrink retry is a no-op).

name: _oversized_message_content_rejection
doc:
400 rejecting a *message* ``content`` field whose rejected value carries a large inline image.

Nebius Token Factory caps a single image at 10 MiB and reports the violation through the field that
failed to coerce — pydantic ``{"type": "string_type", "loc": ["body","messages",N,"content","str"],
"msg": "Input should be a valid string", "input": [...]}`` — naming no size vocabulary, so the
keyword multimodal *tool*-content rule (#104731) claimed it and spent its retry stripping tool images
that were never there (#112473). The same list-shaped content with a small image succeeds, so the
image bytes are the trigger. Tool-scoped locs (``messages.N.tool.content.str``) stay with #104731.

name: _classify_400
doc: 400 Bad Request — image/tool shapes, request-shape rejections, overflow, or generic.

name: _classify_image_tool_422
doc: 422: pydantic relays report the same content-field shapes as 400 (#104731, #112473).

name: _has_usage_limit_transient_signal
doc: Whether a usage-limit response identifies a reset window (message, body fields, or headers).

name: _rate_limit_reset_seconds
doc:
Seconds until a 429's window reopens, from the body's reset fields, ``Retry-After`` or the
message grammar (``retry after Ns`` / ``resets in 4hr``); None when the response names none.

name: _model_id_missing_known_prefix
doc:
True when a bare model id is only known to the provider as ``vendor/id``.

Never guesses: an id absent from the curated catalogue returns False so real
endpoint problems keep their retryable ``unknown`` classification.

name: _is_server_injected_param_rejection
doc:
True when a 400 blames a one-route-only parameter this route never sends.

Conservative: known parameters only, and only when ``provider`` is not a
sender, so a genuine bad parameter (``max_tokens`` on GPT-5) stays format_error.

name: _is_codex_masked_replay_rejection
doc:
HTTP 400 / status-less ``{code: invalid_prompt, message: "Request blocked."}`` from
``openai-codex`` — as an SDK error body, a Responses ``error`` SSE frame, or the
``response.failed`` text ``"invalid_prompt: Request blocked."`` — or the bare
``{"detail": "Unsupported content type"}`` envelope the same backend returns for a rejected
encrypted-reasoning replay (#51512). Both are exact envelopes, provider-gated.

name: _error_obj
doc: ``body["error"]`` when it is a dict, else ``{}``.

name: _json_dict
doc: Parse a JSON object string; None for non-strings, blanks, invalid JSON or non-objects.

name: _openrouter_wrapped_message
doc: Lowercased inner message from OpenRouter's ``error.metadata.raw`` JSON wrapper.

name: _build_error_msg
doc:
Lowercased str(error) + body message + OpenRouter-wrapped upstream message
(OpenAI SDK's APIStatusError.__str__ omits the body, so it is appended).

name: _body_message_candidates
doc: Body message fields in priority order (OpenAI, flat, litellm/Bedrock proxy, FastAPI shapes).

name: _from_cause_chain
arguments: error: Exception, pick: Callable[[Any], Any], default: Any
doc: First non-None ``pick(exc)`` over the error and its __cause__/__context__ chain (max 5 deep).

name: _status_code_from_body
doc:
Numeric HTTP error status (400-599) from ``error.code``/``code`` in a structured body.
An aggregator/relay can deliver the upstream failure only this way — as an
error object inside an HTTP-200 SSE stream — leaving the SDK to raise a
status-less ``APIError`` whose ``body`` carries the status (#121270). String
codes stay symbolic (``_code_from_payload``'s ``"400" is not a code``), unlike the
string-parsing text-SSE sibling ``chat_completion_helpers._status_code_from_payload``.

name: _extract_status_code
doc:
HTTP status code from the error or its cause chain; a body-carried numeric
``code`` counts when the exception itself carries no status (#121270).

name: _extract_error_body
doc: Structured error body from an SDK exception or its cause chain.

name: _code_from_payload
arguments: payload: Any, top_keys: Sequence[str], peek_message: bool
doc:
Code/type from ``payload.error`` or a top-level key; ``"400"`` is not a code.
``peek_message`` also parses a JSON ``error.message`` for a nested code
(Responses API surfaces ``invalid_encrypted_content`` this way). Gemini
puts the HTTP status in ``error.code`` and the symbolic code
(``UNAVAILABLE``) in ``error.status``, so a numeric code defers to it.

name: _extract_error_code
doc: Extract an error code string from the response body.

name: _extract_message
doc: Extract the most informative error message (structured body first).

name: _is_openrouter_upstream_error
doc:
OpenRouter's "Provider returned error" wrapper: the key is healthy, the
upstream failed, so credential rotation is the wrong recovery.

name: _extract_upstream_provider_name
doc: Pull the upstream provider name out of OpenRouter's error metadata.

name: billing_unverified
doc: True when a ``billing`` verdict rests on an ambiguous body (#82154).

name: large_session
arguments: self, frac: float, tokens: int, messages: int
doc: Absolute thresholds only proxy for smaller context windows.

name: _surface
arguments: layer: str, code: str, retryable: bool, provider: str='', model: str=''

name: _api_key_env
doc: The env var holding ``provider``'s API key, so the client can open that row.

name: auth_kind
doc:
``"oauth"`` for providers whose credential is an OAuth/subscription grant
(desktop Accounts tab), ``"api_key"`` for everything else.

name: _result_layer
arguments: reason: str, error_text: str, provider: str

name: build_error_surface_from_result
arguments: result: Any, provider: str='', model: str=''
doc:
Descriptor for a returned-error turn result (``failed=True`` dicts).

Uses the stamped ``failure_reason`` plus error text. None when the result
carries no failure signal.

name: build_error_surface_from_exception
arguments: exc: BaseException, provider: str='', model: str='', api_key: Any=None
doc:
Descriptor for an exception that escaped the turn dispatcher.

API/transport exceptions go through ``classify_api_error`` (same taxonomy
as the retry loop); anything else is a gateway-layer failure.

name: sentinel_path
doc: Path of the ESTOP sentinel this process would write on `hermes pause`.

name: _candidate_sentinel_paths
doc:
Profile home first, then the fleet root if it is a different directory: a profile
gateway (HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes/profiles/<n>) must still honor an operator's ~/.hermes/ESTOP.

name: is_engaged
doc: True if ANY candidate sentinel exists; fail SAFE (True) on stat errors.

name: engage
doc: Create the ESTOP sentinel. Idempotent; re-engaging updates the file.

name: disengage
doc: Remove every visible sentinel (process-local and fleet-root).

name: get_state
doc:
Return ``{"reason", "engaged_at"}`` or None when not engaged; an unreadable/corrupt
body still reports engaged with both fields None.

name: paused_reply
doc: Short user-facing notice for new gateway turns, or None if not paused.

name: check_paused
doc: Return True when engaged, logging once per engagement per component (re-armed after a resume).

name: _provider_reset_delay
doc: Seconds until the provider-declared reset, or None when missing/invalid/expired.

name: switch_deferred_by_reset
doc:
Opt-in ``fallback.min_switch_reset_seconds`` (default 0 = off, #117484): when the primary's
rate limit reopens sooner than N seconds, switching model mid-task costs more than waiting, so
the fallback walk is skipped and the retry loop's own backoff rides out the window. Only for
rate-limit failovers leaving the primary with a valid future ``reset_at``.

name: _arm_rate_limit_cooldown
doc:
Arm the primary cooldown until the provider reset, or use exponential backoff.

``reset_at`` is an absolute wall-clock timestamp while ``_rate_limited_until`` is monotonic;
convert through a duration so wall-clock epoch values never enter the monotonic comparison.
Missing, invalid, or expired provider resets retain the 60s → 2m → ... → 4h fallback.
Only arm when leaving the primary: chain-switching from an active fallback means the primary
was not the failing source. Return the armed cooldown in seconds, or None when not armed.

name: _mark_entitlement_rejected_model
doc:
Record a Codex ChatGPT-account 400 that rejects the current model for this account.

Pool rotation runs first (recover_with_credential_pool benches (credential, model) and
moves to the next entitled entry, #71970); this runs only once no pool entry is left for
the model, so the (provider, model) pair is treated as dead for the session: the fallback
walk skips it and restore_primary_runtime stops switching back — otherwise every turn
re-fails on the primary, announces an unverified "Primary model restored", and oscillates
forever (#106475).

name: _is_entitlement_rejected
doc:
True when (provider, model) — as configured or normalized — was rejected as unentitled
for this account (see _mark_entitlement_rejected_model).

name: parse_service_tier
doc: ``agent.service_tier`` for a user/config word; None for normal and for unknown words.

name: parse_exact_service_tier
doc:
Strict :func:`parse_service_tier` for an explicit client pick: ``""`` pins normal, an unknown
word raises ``ValueError`` instead of silently reading as normal.

name: service_tier_word
doc: The user-facing word for a stored tier (``priority`` -> ``fast``, None/"" -> ``normal``).

name: begin_turn
doc: Open (or refuse) the fast window at a user-turn boundary.

name: effective_request_overrides
doc:
``agent.request_overrides`` plus the fast override while the window is open, minus
``speed`` for a model this session learned has no fast capacity.

name: fast_mode_unprovisioned
doc:
True for a 429 on a ``speed: "fast"`` request whose fast-mode limit header is 0. The
organization has no fast capacity for the model, so waiting or rotating keys cannot help.

name: mark_fast_mode_unavailable
doc:
Stop sending ``speed`` for the current model for the rest of the session. False when the
model was already marked, so the caller retries at most once per model.

name: _constants_path
doc: Call ``hermes_constants.<getter_name>()`` (local import avoids cycles); ``~/.hermes`` on any failure.

name: _hermes_home_path
doc: Active HERMES_HOME (profile-aware). Tests monkeypatch this name.

name: _hermes_root_path
doc: Hermes root dir (parent of any profile, never per-profile).

name: _hermes_dirs
doc:
Resolved active HERMES_HOME and global root, deduplicated.

Both are checked so credential stores at <root>/... stay guarded when
running under a profile (HERMES_HOME = <root>/profiles/<name>).

name: _resolve_each
doc: ``p.resolve()`` for each path, skipping ones that fail to resolve.

name: _is_under
arguments: resolved: str | Path, base: str | Path
doc:
True when ``resolved`` equals ``base`` or lies below it (both already resolved);
``Path`` inputs use ``relative_to`` (platform semantics), ``str`` a realpath prefix test.

name: _resolve_target
doc: ``Path(expanduser(path)).resolve()``, or None when resolution fails.

name: _guard_homes
doc:
Every home the write guards must cover. Process ``~`` alone is wrong whenever the
process HOME is not the OS user's real home — ``TERMINAL_HOME_MODE=profile``,
containers, and spawned workers pin ``HOME`` to ``{HERMES_HOME}/home``, which leaves
the real home's credential paths unguarded against absolute-path writes while file
tools happily write there (and ``_expand_tilde`` may route ``~`` to yet another
home). Deny/approval lists are built over the union: process home, real home,
subprocess home, and the profile home. A ``~name/...`` input resolves to a named
account's home, which joins the set so ``~root/.ssh/authorized_keys`` stays denied.

name: _homes_and_resolved
doc: ``(guard homes, realpath(expanduser(path)))`` — the write-guard coordinate pair.

name: is_nt_namespace_path
doc:
Return True if ``path`` is a Windows NT-/device-namespace path.

Checks the raw string only — never resolves the path (resolving is the
credential-leak trigger this guard exists to prevent).

name: get_nt_namespace_error
doc: Return an error message when ``path`` uses the NT/device namespace.

name: build_write_denied_paths
doc: Return exact sensitive paths that must never be written.

name: build_write_denied_prefixes
doc: Return sensitive directory prefixes that must never be written.

name: get_safe_write_roots
doc: Resolved HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT paths (``os.pathsep``-separated list).

name: build_write_approval_paths
doc:
Paths that need human APPROVAL to write but are not hard-denied credentials.

``~/.ssh/config`` is routine to edit and holds no key bytes, but can carry
``ProxyCommand`` / ``Match exec``. Interactive file tools prompt
(approve-once/session/always, like the terminal tool's ``~/.ssh`` gate);
non-interactive callers (ACP shims, background jobs) fail closed.

name: _classify_write_denial
doc:
Return ``'credential'``, ``'safe_root'``, ``'nt_namespace'``, or ``None`` if writes are allowed.

``entry=True`` is for ops that unlink/rename the directory entry itself (a
symlink, not its target): the entry — parent realpath'd, final component
kept — is vetted as well as the target it resolves to.

name: _classify_resolved_write_denial
doc: Credential / protected-subpath / safe-root verdict for an already-resolved path.

name: is_write_denied
doc: Return True if path is blocked by the write denylist or safe root.

name: get_write_denied_error
arguments: path: str, *, verb: str='Write', entry: bool=False
doc:
Return a user/model-facing error when writes to ``path`` are blocked
(``entry``: see :func:`_classify_write_denial`).

name: is_write_approval_required
doc:
True if ``path`` is approval-gated (``~/.ssh/config``): interactive callers
prompt, callers without a channel treat it as a block (fail closed).

name: get_read_block_error
doc:
Return an error message when a read targets a denied Hermes path.

Blocked: internal skill-hub caches (prompt-injection carriers), credential
stores under HERMES_HOME and the global root (exact files, plus anything
under ``mcp-tokens/`` and ``browser-profile/``), and project-local ``.env``
files anywhere on disk (``.env.example`` is the documented-shape substitute).

Callers that resolve relative paths against a non-process cwd (e.g.
``TERMINAL_CWD``) MUST pass an absolute path: ``resolve()`` here anchors at
the process cwd, so a relative ``"auth.json"`` would miss the denylist.

name: raise_if_read_blocked
doc:
Raise ``ValueError`` if ``path`` is a denied Hermes read (see ``get_read_block_error``).

Shared chokepoint for provider input-loading sites (e.g. image-gen local
paths). Best-effort: unexpected internal errors no-op rather than break
local-file loading; a real block still propagates.

name: _resolve_active_profile_name
doc:
Active profile name from HERMES_HOME: ``~/.hermes`` -> ``"default"``,
``~/.hermes/profiles/X`` -> ``"X"``; ``"default"`` on any resolution failure.

name: _mirror_info
arguments: target: Path, mirror_root: Path, inner_path: str
doc: Common ``classify_*_mirror_target`` result shape.

name: classify_sandbox_mirror_target
doc:
Classify a write target as a sandbox-mirror of authoritative Hermes state: ``None``
for non-mirror paths, else ``target_path`` (resolved), ``mirror_root`` (the
``…/home/.hermes`` prefix) and ``inner_path`` (what the agent meant on the host).

name: _mirror_warning
arguments: info: Optional[dict], body: str, bypass: str
doc: Render ``_SANDBOX_MIRROR_WARNING`` for a classify_* result (``body`` may use ``{inner_path}``).

name: get_sandbox_mirror_warning
doc:
Model-facing soft-guard warning when ``path`` lands in a sandbox mirror, else ``None``;
the caller surfaces it as a tool-result error and ``cross_profile=True`` bypasses.

name: classify_container_mirror_target
doc:
Classify a write target as a container-side sandbox mirror. Inside the container
the bind mount strips the ``sandboxes/`` prefix (the agent sees plain ``/root/.hermes/…``),
so the caller supplies ``mirror_prefix`` once it knows file tools run in a docker sandbox.
``None`` without a prefix or outside it, else ``target_path``/``mirror_root``/``inner_path``.

name: get_container_mirror_warning
doc: Model-facing soft-guard warning when ``path`` lands in the container's mirror, else ``None``.

name: long_decode_max_output_tokens
doc: Total output budget a Gemini 4 request gets for its reasoning effort, or None (per-request cap).

name: long_decode_hops
doc:
Most hops a request with this total budget can take; 1 when it fits one request. The stale
watchdog scales by it (one timer spans every unary hop) and the hop loops stop one past it, so a
server that keeps answering CONTINUATION can't bill forever.

name: long_decode_stale_multiplier
doc:
Non-streaming stale budgets are one timer around every unary hop of a long decode: scale it by
the hop count so a healthy multi-hop answer isn't killed and re-billed from hop 1. The run-budget
cap still applies afterwards; streaming re-arms on every chunk and needs no scaling.

name: continuation_token
doc: The token to resend with when this hop ended on CONTINUATION; None on any other finish.

name: merge_hop_usage
doc: Sum every count across hops; ``initialPromptTokenCount`` (the google-genai name) is hop 1's prompt.

name: merge_hop_responses
doc: One generateContent response whose model turn joins every hop's parts, ending as the last hop did.

name: split_stream_continuation
arguments: event: dict[str, Any], hop_usage: list[dict[str, Any]]
doc:
``(event to translate, token to resend with if the stream ends here)`` for one SSE event.

A CONTINUATION finish is not the end: its finish reason and (per-stream cumulative) usage are
held back in ``hop_usage`` and the token returned for the next hop. The real final event gets
the usage summed over every hop. A token on an event with no finish is a mid-stream checkpoint
(every ~5K tokens past 32K): it commits that event and everything before it, so the caller resumes
a dropped stream by resending the request with it; a drop with no clean checkpoint restarts.

name: bare_gemini_model_id
doc: Strip Gemini's own provider prefix from an aggregator-style model id.

name: gemini_requires_tool_call_ids
doc:
Gemini 3+ needs explicit functionCall/functionResponse ids so replayed parallel tool calls
pair with their responses; 2.x rejects the field.

Gemini 3+ models require explicit tool call IDs in replayed history — without them, multi-tool turns can
be rejected or mismatched. Older Gemini models (2.x) reject unexpected ``id`` fields, so this is gated
on the major version. Mirrors earendil-works/pi#7494 (their fix for the same class of bug in the
google-shared converter).

name: _gemini_version
doc:
(major, minor) of a Gemini model id: ``gemini-4-argon`` -> (4, 0), ``google/gemini-3.8-flash`` ->
(3, 8); (0, 0) for non-Gemini and unversioned ids (``gemini-flash-latest``, ``gemini-exp-1206``).

name: gemini_uses_thinking_level
doc:
Gemini 3 and every later generation steer thinking with the ``thinkingLevel`` enum (``thinkingBudget``
is deprecated there), as do the ``gemini-*-latest`` aliases, which Google hot-swaps to the newest
release of each variant. A version-number gate, not a ``gemini-3`` prefix, so a new generation
(``gemini-4-argon``) isn't silently treated as legacy.

name: gemini_sampling_deprecated
doc:
Gemini 3.6+ (Gemini 4 Argon included) ignores ``temperature``/``top_p``/``top_k`` and Google
slated them for removal; older families (2.x, 3.0-3.5) keep them.

name: is_vertex_express_base_url
doc:
An aiplatform host speaking the native API with an API key: the bare express surface, or its
``…/projects/{p}/locations/{l}`` form, which reaches models served only in ``global`` (Gemini 4).
The OAuth Vertex provider's ``…/endpoints/openapi`` base is OpenAI-compatible and must stay off
the native adapter.

name: normalize_gemini_base_url
doc:
Gemini native base URL with the API version segment guaranteed. Google's own client treats the
base as a host root and appends the version itself, so users configure ``GEMINI_BASE_URL`` (or a
proxy root like ``http://localhost:4000/gemini``) that way; our request builders expect
``{base}/models/{model}:generateContent`` — without ``/v1beta`` that is a guaranteed 404. Trailing
slashes and an ``/openai`` suffix are stripped; an existing version segment (``v1``, ``v1beta``,
``v1alpha``, ...) is kept; empty input returns ``DEFAULT_GEMINI_BASE_URL``. Only the LAST path
segment is inspected, so ``.../v1beta/extra`` still gets ``/v1beta`` appended; this does not
decide routing (see ``is_native_gemini_base_url``).

A Vertex express base (``aiplatform.googleapis.com``, ``…/v1beta1`` or the full
``…/v1beta1/publishers/google``) is completed to the ``publishers/google`` form. The key never
decides routing: Google issues ``AQ.…`` keys for both AI Studio and Vertex express mode
(#115306), so an express key reaches aiplatform only through this explicit base configuration.

name: is_native_gemini_base_url
doc: True when the endpoint speaks Gemini's native REST API (not ``/openai``).

name: gemini_accepts_parameters_json_schema
doc:
``FunctionDeclaration.parametersJsonSchema`` exists only in the ``v1beta`` surface of
generativelanguage (absent from ``v1`` / ``v1alpha`` content.proto); other versions and
unknown proxies get the legacy ``parameters`` subset.

name: probe_gemini_tier
arguments: api_key: str, base_url: str=DEFAULT_GEMINI_BASE_URL, *, model: str='gemini-3.7-flash', timeout: float=10.0
doc: Probe a Google AI Studio key → ``"free"`` | ``"paid"`` | ``"unknown"`` (probe failed; callers proceed without blocking).

name: is_free_tier_quota_error
doc: True when a Gemini 429 message indicates free-tier exhaustion.

name: wrong_gemini_surface_guidance
arguments: base_url: str, api_key: str, err_status: str
doc:
Guidance text for the 403 PERMISSION_DENIED key/host mismatches Google's AQ. rollout created.

Google issues ``AQ.…`` keys for both AI Studio and Vertex express mode, so neither the key prefix
nor the host alone proves the pairing; on a PERMISSION_DENIED, point the user at the surface their
key likely belongs to: an AQ. key rejected by the Studio host may be an express key (the explicit
aiplatform base_url is that key's only route there), and any key rejected by an explicitly
configured aiplatform base may be an AI Studio key (#115306). Empty string when the shape matches
neither.

name: is_standard_key_auth_error
arguments: status: int, error_message: str, reason: str='', *, api_key: str=''
doc:
True when Google rejected a legacy "Standard" (AIza) Cloud key.

Original shape (June 2026): 401 + ``ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED`` / "expected OAuth 2
access token". After the September 2026 cutoff the same leftover AIza key often comes
back as 400 ``API_KEY_INVALID`` ("API key not valid") — attach migration guidance on
that 400 only when the presented key is still AIza-shaped, so a mistyped Auth (``AQ.``)
key keeps the raw invalid-key message.

name: _text_of
doc: Text of an OpenAI content item (plain str or ``{"type": "text"}`` dict), else None.

name: _inline_data_part
doc: ``inlineData`` part for an ``image_url`` item carrying a ``data:`` URL; None otherwise.

name: _tool_call_extra_signature
doc: Replayed Gemini thoughtSignature from ``extra_content`` (``google.thought_signature`` or flat).

name: _looks_like_json_schema
doc:
True if a parsed value contains a JSON-Schema ``$ref`` pointer (``#/...``): Gemini 3 resolves
``$ref``/``$defs`` inside functionResponse.response and rejects unknown pointers with HTTP 400, so a
tool result that is itself a JSON Schema (e.g. ``tool_describe`` output) is forwarded as opaque text.
False positives only lose the structured shape, never the content.

name: _translate_tool_result_to_gemini
arguments: message: dict[str, Any], tool_name_by_call_id: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None, include_ids: bool=False, *, is_gemini3: bool=False

name: _merge_alternating
doc:
Alternation contract for generateContent: 1) adjacent same-role contents merge (else HTTP 400
"multiturn requests [must] alternate"); 2) EXCEPT never fuse a human user text turn into a preceding
user content that only carries functionResponse parts (or vice versa) — Gemini 3 accepts the fold but
reads the text as a continuation of the tool result and returns an empty candidate (parallel
functionResponse + functionResponse still merge); 3) the split pair stays API-valid via an interposed
placeholder model turn.

name: _build_gemini_contents
arguments: messages: list[dict[str, Any]], include_tool_call_ids: bool=False, *, is_gemini3: bool=False

name: _thinking_requests_output_headroom
doc:
True when Gemini will spend output tokens on thinking: thought tokens bill against ``maxOutputTokens``,
so a global 4096/16384 cap can be consumed entirely by high thinking (``finishReason=MAX_TOKENS``, no answer).

name: _effective_gemini_max_output_tokens
doc:
Native ``maxOutputTokens``: an omitted/invalid cap becomes the published ceiling (Gemini
truncates on its low internal default); an explicit cap is raised to the ceiling when
thinking is enabled so thoughts don't starve the answer.

name: _translate_response_format
doc:
OpenAI ``response_format`` → Gemini ``generationConfig`` JSON-output keys.

Full-JSON-Schema ``responseJsonSchema`` exists only on the generativelanguage ``v1beta``
surface (same gate as ``parametersJsonSchema``); ``v1`` / ``v1alpha``, Vertex express
``v1beta1`` and unknown proxies take the OpenAPI-subset ``responseSchema`` path.

name: build_gemini_request
arguments: *, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], tools: Any=None, tool_choice: Any=None, temperature: Optional[float]=None, max_tokens: Optional[int]=None, top_p: Optional[float]=None, stop: Any=None, thinking_config: Any=None, response_format: Any=None, model: str='', tools_as_json_schema: bool=False

name: _new_call_id
doc: Echo the functionCall/delta ``id`` when present, else mint an OpenAI-style one.

name: _usage_from_metadata
doc:
Gemini ``usageMetadata`` → OpenAI-shaped usage.

Hidden thinking is reported separately in ``thoughtsTokenCount``:
``candidatesTokenCount`` counts visible output only, while ``totalTokenCount``
already includes thoughts. OpenAI's ``completion_tokens`` covers reasoning, so
thoughts are folded in (otherwise a thinking turn bills a few percent of its
real output and ``prompt + completion != total``) and also surfaced under
``completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens``, where ``normalize_usage`` reads
them. Absent on non-thinking/older responses, which keeps their numbers as-is.

name: _envelope
arguments: model: str, object_: str, choice: SimpleNamespace, usage: Any, cls: type=SimpleNamespace
doc: OpenAI chat.completion / chat.completion.chunk envelope around one choice.

name: _tool_call_ns
arguments: name: str, arguments: str, index: int, call_id: str, extra_content: Any
doc: OpenAI-shaped tool call; ``extra_content`` attached only when it is a dict.

name: _part_text
doc: ``(text, is_thought)`` for a candidate part; ``(None, False)`` when it carries no text.

name: _text_part_signature
doc:
``thoughtSignature`` on a non-functionCall part (a text turn's last part; in streams an empty-text
part). Replay is optional, but the server rehydrates the turn's thoughts from it (live: 31 -> 237
prompt tokens), so it is kept as the message-level ``extra_content`` signature.

name: _make_stream_chunk
arguments: *, model: str, content: str='', tool_call_delta: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, finish_reason: Optional[str]=None, reasoning: str='', text_signature: Optional[str]=None

name: _parse_sse_line
doc: One SSE line → payload dict, ``_SSE_DONE`` for the terminal frame, or None.

name: _tool_call_slot
arguments: fc: dict[str, Any], part: dict[str, Any], part_index: int, args_str: str, tool_call_indices: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
doc:
``(key, existing slot or None)`` for a streamed functionCall.

Gemini 3 ids each tool call, so the id is the slot identity (``part_index`` and the thought
signature drift across events of one call). Gemini 2.5 sends no id and ``part_index`` restarts
at 0 per event, so two different calls to one tool in separate events would share a slot and
have their arguments concatenated into unparseable JSON: Gemini re-sends full arguments, so a
payload that is not a prefix-extension (or resend) of the slot's accumulated arguments is a
different call and gets its own ``key#N`` slot, kept reachable so its own resend lands on it.

name: translate_stream_event
arguments: event: dict[str, Any], model: str, tool_call_indices: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]

name: _error_info
doc: ``(reason, metadata)`` from the first google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail (later ones fill gaps until reason is set).

name: _error_object
doc: The ``error`` object of a Google JSON error body, or ``{}``.

name: gemini_http_error
arguments: response: httpx.Response, *, body_text: Optional[str]=None, api_key: str='', base_url: str='', key_guidance: bool=True
doc:
``key_guidance=False`` for OAuth-bearer callers: the API-key fixes (free tier, Standard key, wrong
key surface) are wrong advice when the credential is a user's OAuth access token.

name: __init__
arguments: self, message: str, *, code: str='gemini_api_error', status_code: Optional[int]=None, response: Optional[httpx.Response]=None, retry_after: Optional[float]=None, details: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None

name: __init__
arguments: self, *, api_key: str, base_url: Optional[str]=None, default_headers: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None, timeout: Any=None, http_client: Optional[httpx.Client]=None, **_: Any

name: _create_chat_completion
arguments: self, *, model: str='gemini-3.7-flash', messages: Optional[list[dict[str, Any]]]=None, stream: bool=False, tools: Any=None, tool_choice: Any=None, temperature: Optional[float]=None, max_tokens: Optional[int]=None, top_p: Optional[float]=None, stop: Any=None, response_format: Any=None, extra_body: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, timeout: Any=None, **_: Any

significant_calls.expression:
build_gemini_request(
            messages=messages or [], tools=tools, tool_choice=tool_choice, temperature=temperature, max_tokens=max_tokens,
            top_p=top_p, stop=stop, thinking_config=extra.get("thinking_config") or extra.get("thinkingConfig"),
            response_format=response_format or extra.get("response_format"), model=model,
            tools_as_json_schema=gemini_accepts_parameters_json_schema(self.base_url),
        )

name: _generate
arguments: self, url: str, request: dict[str, Any], timeout: Any

name: _stream_completion
arguments: self, model: str, url: str, request: dict[str, Any], timeout: Any

name: _stringify_enum_value
doc: Gemini-safe string for a scalar enum entry, or None to drop it.

name: _normalize_gemini_type_array
doc: Keep union alternatives and their branch-local structural constraints.

name: sanitize_gemini_schema
doc:
Gemini-compatible copy of a tool parameter schema: keeps only the documented subset
(drops e.g. ``$schema`` / ``additionalProperties``) and recursively sanitizes nested
``properties`` / ``items`` / ``anyOf``.

name: sanitize_gemini_tool_parameters
doc: Normalize tool parameters to a valid Gemini object schema.

name: _resolve_local_ref
doc: Resolve a same-document JSON pointer (``#/$defs/Foo``) against *root*.

name: _inline_refs
arguments: node: Any, root: dict[str, Any], budget: list[int], stack: tuple=()
doc:
Recursively inline same-document ``$ref`` nodes; ``ValueError`` on an unresolvable
or circular reference or an exhausted budget (the caller then keeps the original).

name: prepare_gemini_tool_parameters
doc:
Full JSON Schema for ``parametersJsonSchema``: deep-copied, root ``$schema`` dropped,
same-document ``$ref`` inlined, object root guaranteed. A schema whose references
cannot all be resolved is sent untouched so the provider names the real problem.

name: visible_commentary
doc: Use the same think stripping and secret redaction as live delivery.

name: _without_flattened_commentary
doc:
Omit exact whole-line public segments from a display copy, not source data.

Current normalization separates parts with two newlines; older rows may
have one. If a private segment happens to be identical, origin is ambiguous:
omit both occurrences rather than leaking the public text or choosing the
wrong one. Surrounding reasoning is retained in its original line style.

name: project_history_commentary
doc: Project a batch inside the owning profile's config and redaction scope.

name: _locales_dir
doc:
Locale dir: ``HERMES_BUNDLED_LOCALES`` (sealed packaging, e.g. Nix) if it exists, else ``<repo-root>/locales``.

The source path is returned even when missing so ``_load_bundled`` can log
the path it looked at rather than raise.

name: supported_languages
doc:
Every language some layer supplies for the current profile home: bundled ∪ user overlay ∪ plugin
packs, ``en`` first then sorted. Cached until :func:`reset_language_cache`.

name: resolve_language_id
doc:
Canonical supported id for a user-supplied value (code, alias, regional tag), or ``None`` when no
layer supplies it — the validation ``hermes config set display.language`` runs.

name: _normalize_lang
doc: Map a user-supplied value to a supported code (any layer), else the default.

name: _load_bundled
doc: One bundled locale YAML flattened to dotted keys (empty dict on any failure — never crashes).

name: _flatten_into
arguments: node: Any, prefix: str, out: dict[str, str]
doc: Flatten a nested mapping into ``out`` (text leaves only).

name: _load_catalog
doc: Merged catalog for ``lang`` in ``home`` (packs > overlay > bundled); cached per (home, lang).

name: surface_catalog
doc:
What ``i18n.catalog`` serves for one surface: packs > overlay > bundled ``locales/<lang>.<surface>.yaml``.

The core surface omits the bundled layer (the Python renderer already has it); the TUI ships only an
English catalog in-tree, so its bundled translations live in ``locales/<lang>.tui.yaml`` and ride
along here.

name: _config_language_cached
doc:
``display.language`` from config.yaml, read once per profile home (``t()`` is a hot path).
Keyed by home so a multiplexed gateway serving several profiles doesn't freeze the first
profile's language for every other profile.

name: reset_language_cache
doc:
Invalidate cached language resolution, merged catalogs and every layer view (call after
``save_config`` changes ``display.language``, after a pack registers/unregisters, or after editing
an overlay file).

name: get_language
doc:
Resolve the active language using env > config > default order. ``HERMES_LANGUAGE`` is a
per-profile ``.env`` value, so it is read through the secret scope: under multiplexing a raw
environ read would impose the default profile's language on every other profile.

name: t
arguments: key: str, lang: str | None=None, **format_kwargs: Any
doc:
Translate a dotted catalog key to the active (or explicit ``lang``) language.

``format_kwargs`` are applied with ``str.format``. Falls back to English,
then to the bare key; a format failure returns the unformatted string.

name: describe_language
arguments: lang: str, *, pack: dict | None, overlay: bool
doc:
One picker row. Precedence for endonym/rtl: bundled table → pack metadata → bare id / LTR.
``source`` names the highest layer that supplies the language (``plugin:<name>`` > ``overlay`` >
``bundled``) so a picker can say where a language came from.

name: language_options
doc:
``[{"id", "endonym", "rtl", "source"}, ...]`` for every supported language, ``en`` first then sorted
by id — the list ``i18n.languages`` serves and every switcher renders (endonym only, no flags).

name: normalize_language_id
doc: Canonical spelling of a language id: lowercase, ``_`` -> ``-``, surrounding whitespace dropped.

name: flatten
arguments: node: Any, prefix: str='', out: dict[str, str] | None=None
doc:
Nested mapping -> ``{dotted.key: text}``. Non-string, non-mapping leaves are dropped (catalogs are
text-only); :func:`non_text_leaves` reports them for the validator.

name: non_text_leaves
doc: Dotted paths of leaves that are neither text nor a mapping (numbers, lists, booleans, nulls).

name: parse_locale_file
doc:
Parse one locale YAML into a flat catalog. Raises on unreadable/unparseable input or a non-mapping
document — the strict form for registration and validation.

name: load_locale_source
doc:
``register_locale`` input -> flat catalog: a mapping (nested or already flat) is flattened; a path
is parsed with :func:`parse_locale_file`.

name: scan_locale_dir
doc:
``(lang, surface, path)`` for every ``<lang>[.<surface>].yaml`` under *directory* (sorted; empty when
the directory is missing). Unknown surfaces are reported so a typo like ``pl.tiu.yaml`` is visible.

name: register_pack
arguments: lang: str, surface: str, messages: Mapping[str, str], *, source: str, endonym: str | None=None, rtl: bool=False
doc: Add a pack layer for ``(lang, surface)``; later registrations shadow earlier ones key by key.

name: unregister_pack
doc: Drop one registration (``PluginRegistration`` release). ``False`` when it was already gone.

name: pack_layer
doc: Merged pack messages for ``(lang, surface)`` in registration order (last wins); cached.

name: pack_info
doc:
``{endonym, rtl, source}`` of the newest pack registration for *lang* (``None`` when no pack has
it). ``endonym``/``rtl`` come from the newest registration that declared them.

name: overlay_layer
arguments: home: Path | str, lang: str, surface: str=CORE_SURFACE
doc:
``<home>/locales/<lang>[.<surface>].yaml`` flattened; ``{}`` (logged) when missing or broken. Cached
per home so a multiplexed process serving profile A then B then A never mixes overlays.

name: overlay_languages
doc: Language ids that have at least one overlay file (any surface) under *home*.

name: surface_catalog
arguments: home: Path | str, lang: str, surface: str=CORE_SURFACE
doc:
Overlay + packs (packs win) for one surface — the layer ``i18n.catalog`` ships to a renderer, which
merges it over its own bundled catalog. Bundled Python locales are NOT included.

name: layered_languages
doc: Languages supplied by any layer above bundled (overlay of *home* ∪ packs).

name: clear_cache
doc: Drop merged views (not the registrations); the facade's ``reset_language_cache`` calls this.

name: image_dimensions_from_bytes
doc:
(width, height) for PNG / JPEG bytes, or None when unreadable. PNG: IHDR. JPEG: walk
segments (skipping 0xFF fill bytes) to the first SOF marker; stop at SOS. Lives here so both
the send-path passes and the tool layer share one header-only reader.

name: image_max_side_from_data
doc:
Longest side (px) of a data-URL / bare-base64 image, or None when it cannot be read.

Decodes only the leading base64 prefix (``_DIMENSION_PROBE_CHARS``), so classifying a request
with dozens of images costs a few header reads, not a full decode of every payload. Accepts
both ``data:image/...;base64,....`` and a bare base64 string; anything else (a remote URL, an
unrecognized container) yields None.

name: image_within_many_image_limit
doc:
True only when the image's longest side is known and within ``MANY_IMAGE_DIMENSION_LIMIT``.

Unknown dimensions are NOT safe: the stricter per-request cap would still be live, so the
caller keeps the strict trigger. See :func:`images_all_within_many_image_limit`.

name: images_all_within_many_image_limit
doc:
True when EVERY image in the request is a readable image within the many-image limit.

The Anthropic rule is per request: one oversized image holds every image in the request to the
stricter cap, so a single unreadable or over-limit image must keep the strict block ceiling.
Short-circuits on the first offender, which is what keeps this cheap on image-heavy turns.

name: outbound_image_block_limit
doc: Block ceiling for a request: the strict 20 unless every image is within the many-image cap.

name: outbound_image_retire_count
arguments: carrier_blocks_newest_first: Sequence[int], reserved_blocks: int, *, carrier_bytes_newest_first: Optional[Sequence[int]]=None, reserved_bytes: int=0, many_image_safe: bool=False, limit: Optional[int]=None, budget: int=OUTBOUND_IMAGE_BUDGET_BYTES, batch: int=IMAGE_EVICTION_BATCH, floor: int=OUTBOUND_IMAGE_FLOOR
doc:
How many of the OLDEST image-bearing tool results to retire.

``carrier_blocks_newest_first`` is the image-block count per image-bearing tool result,
newest first; ``reserved_blocks`` counts images the pass must never rewrite (user
uploads). The byte dimension is active only when ``carrier_bytes_newest_first`` is
given. ``limit`` defaults to :func:`outbound_image_block_limit` of ``many_image_safe``,
so both passes pick the same ceiling from the same per-request classification.

The retire count must be a STEP FUNCTION of the overshoot, because the pass is recomputed
on every request: an exact ``count - limit`` target moves the frontier on every new image,
and a fixed one-batch retire stops enforcing the limit after the first batch. So the count
advances in quanta until the request fits.

The quantum is ``batch`` capped at ``window - floor``, where ``window`` is how many newest
carriers fit under the ceiling. A quantum wider than that would step past the newest frames
on every advance; cutting each step back to exactly ``total - floor`` instead makes the
retire count track ``total`` again — the per-image frontier this policy exists to avoid,
visible whenever a tool result carries several images or uploads fill most of the ceiling.
Holding for ``window - floor`` turns per advance is the most the floor allows.

The floor is a SATISFIABILITY floor: it shelters the newest frames only when reserved
uploads alone breach the block ceiling (no retirement can fix that), and never under byte
pressure — the request-size limit is hard and the provider answers 413. Even then the
count stays a step function: it retires whole quanta down toward the floor (keeping
``floor`` to ``floor + batch - 1`` carriers, fewer when the byte budget binds), so the
cached prefix is rewritten once per quantum rather than on every new image.

significant_calls.expression:
_retire_count_for_request(
                carrier_blocks_newest_first[total - m:],
                reserved_blocks,
                None if sizes is None else sizes[total - m:],
                reserved_bytes,
                limit,
                budget,
                batch,
                floor,
            )

name: outbound_retired_image_ids
doc:
The session's latched set of tool-call ids whose images the send path has retired.

Keyed on ``agent.session_id`` so a new session (or a compaction rotation, which rewrites the
prefix anyway) starts clean and a reused provider call id cannot retire a fresh screenshot.

name: latched_retire_count
arguments: retire: int, carrier_ids_newest_first: Sequence[Optional[str]], retired_ids: Optional[set[str]]
doc:
Widen ``retire`` so every carrier up to the newest previously retired one stays retired,
then record the carriers being retired into ``retired_ids``.

The per-request decision cannot see history: a request that drops an upload (once it leaves
the replay window) relaxes the ceiling, and re-deciding from scratch would restore
screenshots an earlier request already retired, rewriting the cached prefix back.

name: _retire_count_for_request
arguments: carrier_blocks_newest_first: Sequence[int], reserved_blocks: int, sizes: Optional[Sequence[int]], reserved_bytes: int, limit: int, budget: int, batch: int, floor: int
doc: Retire count for one request in isolation; see :func:`outbound_image_retire_count`.

name: resolve_aspect_ratio
doc:
Clamp to :data:`VALID_ASPECT_RATIOS`; invalid values coerce to landscape so
the tool surface forgives agent mistakes instead of rejecting them.

name: normalize_reference_images
doc:
Coerce a str or list into a clean list of non-blank strings; ``None`` when
nothing usable remains so providers treat "no refs" as one sentinel.

name: save_b64_image
arguments: b64_data: str, *, prefix: str='image', extension: str='png'
doc: Decode base64 image data into ``$HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/images/``; return the path.

name: save_url_image
arguments: url: str, *, prefix: str='image', timeout: float=60.0, max_bytes: int=25 * 1024 * 1024
doc:
Download an (often ephemeral) image URL into ``$HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/images/``. Raises on
network / HTTP / oversize / empty errors so callers can fall back to the bare URL.

name: success_response
arguments: *, image: str, model: str, prompt: str, aspect_ratio: str, provider: str, modality: str='text', extra: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Uniform success dict; ``extra`` keys are added without overriding standard ones.

name: error_response
arguments: *, error: str, error_type: str='provider_error', provider: str='', model: str='', prompt: str='', aspect_ratio: str=DEFAULT_ASPECT_RATIO
doc: Build a uniform error response dict.

name: capabilities
doc:
``modalities`` (``"text"`` and/or ``"image"``) and ``max_reference_images``; optionally
``supports_upscale`` (bool), ``creative_controls`` (names from the tool's creative-control
vocabulary: ``creativity``, ``intensity``, ``complexity``, ``movement``, ``thinking``,
``resolution``) and
``source_image_role`` (``"style"`` when image inputs set the look and are not edited). Surfaced in the
dynamic tool schema so the model knows when ``image_url`` / ``upscale`` / each control is
honored, and only declared controls are passed to :meth:`generate`; the text-only default
keeps non-overriding providers backward compatible.

name: generate
arguments: self, prompt: str, aspect_ratio: str=DEFAULT_ASPECT_RATIO, *, image_url: Optional[str]=None, reference_image_urls: Optional[list[str]]=None, **kwargs: Any
doc:
Generate an image, or edit ``image_url`` (``reference_image_urls`` are extra
style/composition refs, clamped to ``max_reference_images``); any source image
routes to the edit endpoint. Return :func:`success_response` / :func:`error_response`.
Unknown ``kwargs`` MUST be ignored (forward compat); ``upscale`` (bool) is a
post-generation high-res pass, reported as ``upscaled: True`` in ``extra``.

name: get_active_provider
doc:
Resolve the currently-active provider. Availability semantics (mirrors
:mod:`agent.web_search_registry`): an explicitly configured provider is returned
even if ``is_available()`` is False, so the dispatcher surfaces a precise
"X_API_KEY is not set" error instead of silently switching backends; only the
unconfigured fallback path is filtered by availability.

name: resolve_replay_recent_images
doc: ``vision.replay_recent_images`` as an int >= 0; an unusable value warns and disables replay.

name: _split_rebuilt_row
doc:
A DB-rebuilt user row as its original parts, in order: ``("text", str)`` for each text run and
``("image", (ref, detail, marker_line))`` per ``[screenshot]`` line, the markers pairing 1:1 in order
with the row's ``[Image attached…]`` hints wherever the image sat (API callers put it first;
turn-time memory/hook context follows it). ``None`` when the counts disagree (a typed marker).

name: _retained_data_url
doc: Data URL for a retained local image this profile still holds unchanged, else ``None``.

name: replay_frontier
doc:
Oldest image slot still replayed when the request holds ``total`` images.

The frontier moves forward only in whole batches of ``keep``: the newest ``keep`` to
``2 * keep - 1`` images replay, and an image that drops out stays dropped as the session
grows. A strict newest-``keep`` window would turn one early row back into ``[screenshot]``
text on every new photo, rewriting the cached prefix each time; this rewrites it at most once
per ``keep`` new images. Counted by slot position (missing or changed files hold their slot),
so a swept file never moves the frontier.

name: replay_recent_images
doc:
Rebuild retained images at or after ``replay_frontier`` in place on ``api_messages`` (wire
copies); images still live in the conversation hold slots too. Returns the number re-attached.

name: _turn_replay_window
doc:
Images to replay this turn: 0 unless the model takes images natively. Resolved once per turn
(keyed on the turn's frozen admission clock and the model), not per tool-loop request.

name: replay_for_agent
doc: ``build_api_messages`` hook: replay only when this turn's model takes images natively.

name: _matches_outside_code
doc: Yield ``pattern`` matches whose start is not inside a fenced block or inline backticks.

name: _existing_file
doc:
Normalized path when it is a regular file; None otherwise (incl. OSError on pathological input).
The return value is the OS-canonical spelling of the real file (same norm class as
``str(Path(...))``), so callers can compare it against actual paths — ``~`` expansion
alone would leave the textual ``/`` separators of the source text in place on Windows.

name: extract_image_refs
doc:
Scan free-form text for image references → ``(local_paths, urls)``, each
ordered and deduplicated. Local paths must exist as files; URLs are not
validated (the provider fetches them). Code spans are skipped so pasted
snippets aren't live attachments (mirrors ``BaseAdapter.extract_local_files``).

name: _coerce_capability_bool
doc:
Strict boolean coercion for capability overrides: real bools, 0/1 and YAML
boolean tokens only; anything else is None so the caller falls through to
models.dev. ``bool("false")`` is True, so a quoted ``supports_vision: "false"``
would otherwise silently enable native routing on a model that can't handle it.

name: _runtime_main
doc: Context-local credential source or stripped runtime text; "" when unavailable.

name: _model_supports_vision_override
doc: Per-model ``supports_vision`` (or ``vision`` alias) from a ``models`` mapping.

name: _custom_provider_entries
doc:
Yield legacy ``custom_providers`` entries matching ``names`` (case-insensitive);
``names`` is the outer loop so list order cannot let a persisted default shadow the live route.

name: _custom_provider_list
doc: Dict entries of the legacy ``custom_providers`` list (empty when absent/malformed).

name: _supports_vision_override
arguments: cfg: Optional[dict[str, Any]], provider: str, model: str, *, requested_provider: str=''
doc:
Resolve user-declared vision capability from config.yaml; None when unset. First hit wins: ``model.supports_vision`` → ``providers.

.models.`` → legacy ``custom_providers[].models.``. Named custom providers are rewritten to ``provider="custom"`` at runtime while config keeps the user's name under ``model.provider``, so the requested, runtime and config identities are all tried, plus the bare ```` of any ``custom:``.

name: _resolve_inference_value
arguments: cfg: Optional[dict[str, Any]], provider: str, key: str, *, runtime_ok: Callable[[str], bool]
doc:
``base_url`` / ``api_key`` of the active inference provider. Order: runtime
value (when ``runtime_ok`` accepts it) → ``model.<key>`` → ``providers.<name>.<key>``
→ ``custom_providers[].<key>``, ``<name>`` covering the provider and
``model.provider`` in both bare and ``custom:``-prefixed forms.

name: _resolve_inference_base_url
doc:
Best-effort base URL for the active inference provider; the runtime value is
only trusted when it belongs to the requested provider (or none was requested).

name: _resolve_inference_api_key
doc:
Best-effort API key, resolved like :func:`_resolve_inference_base_url` so it
matches the base URL actually probed; otherwise the local server-type probe hits
a keyed remote endpoint without Authorization and sprays 401s on every image turn.

Mirrors :func:`_resolve_inference_base_url`'s resolution order (runtime value, then ``model.api_key``,
then the providers blocks) so the key matches the base URL actually being probed. See #89863.

name: _should_probe_ollama_vision
arguments: provider: str, base_url: str, api_key: str=''
doc:
True when the active provider likely fronts a local Ollama server. Fingerprint
probing is only valid for LOCAL endpoints: remote OpenAI-compatible APIs (sglang,
vLLM) expose Ollama-compat routes that can misidentify, and probing them without
an api_key returns 401 on every leg.

name: _coerce_mode
doc: Normalize a config value into one of the valid modes (default ``auto``).

name: _explicit_aux_vision_override
doc:
True when the user configured a specific ``auxiliary.vision`` backend — the
de-facto image route in ``auto`` mode even when the main model has native vision.
``auto``/empty provider with no model and no base_url is not explicit.

name: _probe_managed_runtime
arguments: provider: str, model: str, cfg: Optional[dict[str, Any]]
doc:
Managed local runtime verdict: the server receiving the image is the authority
on whether it can see (its /props reports modalities). Cloud catalogs have never
heard of a local GGUF, so without this every local model reads as text-only and
screenshots detour to a cloud auxiliary.

name: _probe_models_dev
arguments: provider: str, model: str, cfg: Optional[dict[str, Any]]
doc:
models.dev catalog verdict. ``allow_network=True`` on purpose: this runs only
when an image needs routing, and the text-only-main guard depends on catalog
data — a cold cache returning "unknown" would reintroduce attempting the call.
The fetch is cached (4h TTL) and backoff-limited.

name: _probe_ollama
arguments: provider: str, model: str, cfg: Optional[dict[str, Any]]
doc: Ollama ``/api/show`` verdict for local endpoints (see :func:`_should_probe_ollama_vision`).

name: _lookup_supports_vision
arguments: provider: str, model: str, cfg: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, *, requested_provider: str=''
doc:
Return True/False if vision capability can be resolved, None if unknown.

Order: config ``supports_vision`` override → :data:`_VISION_PROBES`
(managed local runtime → models.dev catalog → Ollama probe). A plugin's
per-model ``ProviderProfile.model_capabilities`` reaches this through the
catalog probe. The provider-wide ``ProviderProfile.supports_vision`` flag is
deliberately NOT consulted: it declares that tool-result messages may carry
images (``tools.vision_tools``), not that every model on the provider can see
user attachments — relays such as ``router`` set it for mixed catalogs.

name: decide_image_input_mode
arguments: provider: str, model: str, cfg: Optional[dict[str, Any]], *, requested_provider: str=''
doc:
Return ``"native"`` or ``"text"`` for the given turn (``cfg`` None behaves as
auto; ``requested_provider`` is the identity before runtime canonicalization).

name: _sniff_mime_from_bytes
doc: Detect image MIME from magic bytes; None if unrecognised.

name: _transcode_to_png
doc:
Decode with Pillow and re-encode as PNG; None when impossible. HEIC/HEIF and
AVIF need optional Pillow plugins, registered on demand; a missing plugin just
looks like "can't decode" so the caller skips the image and the turn proceeds.

name: _guess_mime
doc: Image MIME for *path*: magic bytes (authoritative) → ``mimetypes`` → suffix → jpeg.

name: _accepted_mimes
doc:
Provider-accepted MIME set for the current main runtime. The managed local
server decodes fewer formats (no WebP — and a WebP part fails SILENTLY: the model
confabulates a description), so its narrower set transcodes those here.

name: _file_to_data_url
doc:
Encode a local image as a base64 data URL at native size (the agent retry
loop shrinks on rejection, so lenient providers pay no silent quality tax);
MIMEs outside the accepted set are transcoded to PNG. None when unreadable,
blocked by the read guard, or untranscodable — the caller reports ``skipped``.

name: build_native_content_parts
arguments: user_text: str, image_paths: list[str], image_urls: Optional[list[str]]=None
doc:
Build an OpenAI-style ``content`` list for a user turn.

Local paths become base64 ``data:`` URLs; remote URLs pass through verbatim.
When any image attaches, one text part combines the caption (or a neutral
default) with a ``[Image attached at: <path>]`` / ``[Image attached: <url>]``
hint per image — a string handle for tools taking an image path/URL, mirroring
``Runner._enrich_message_with_vision``. Returns ``(content_parts, skipped)``;
``skipped`` holds unreadable local paths (URLs are never skipped).

name: _table
doc: The active profile's learned table, loaded lazily from its cache file.

name: learned_image_token_cost
doc: Learned per-image cost for ``model@host``, else the flat default.

name: current_image_token_cost
doc: Per-image cost bound for the running turn (see :func:`image_cost_context`), else the default.

name: bind_image_token_cost
doc: Bind the agent's learned per-image cost to the current context for the rest of the turn.

name: calibrate_from_usage
arguments: agent: Any, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], prompt_tokens: Any
doc:
Learn the per-image cost from the response that just priced ``messages``.

Requires the PREVIOUS anchor (real count of the prior request) to still match: the residual
``prompt_tokens - (anchor + text-only delta)`` is then the provider's price for the images the
delta introduced. Returns the new learned cost, or None when this response teaches nothing
(no anchor, no new images, implausible residual).

name: tool_hook_ids
doc: Identity kwargs every tool hook/middleware call carries (all coerced to ``""``).

name: emit_terminal_post_tool_call
arguments: agent, *, function_name: str, function_args: dict, result: Any, effective_task_id: str, tool_call_id: Optional[str], duration_ms: int=0, status: Optional[str]=None, error_type: Optional[str]=None, error_message: Optional[str]=None, middleware_trace: Optional[list]=None
doc: Emit the one terminal ``post_tool_call`` hook for a tool_call_id (best-effort).

significant_calls.expression:
_emit_post_tool_call_hook(
            function_name=function_name,
            function_args=function_args,
            result=result,
            **tool_hook_ids(agent, effective_task_id, tool_call_id),
            duration_ms=duration_ms,
            status=status,
            error_type=error_type,
            error_message=error_message,
            middleware_trace=list(middleware_trace or []),
        )

name: apply_transform_tool_result
arguments: agent, *, function_name: str, function_args: dict, result: Any, effective_task_id: str, tool_call_id: Optional[str], duration_ms: int=0
doc:
Apply ``transform_tool_result`` to an inline-dispatched tool's result.

Registry tools get this inside ``handle_function_call``; inline executors never
reach it, so the agent paths call the same helper (after the terminal
``post_tool_call``) to keep the hook's "every tool" contract. Fail-open.

name: _call_tool
arguments: module: str, func: str, args: dict, arg_specs: tuple[_ArgSpec, ...], **fixed: Any
doc: Import ``module.func`` lazily and call it with args mapped per ``arg_specs`` plus ``fixed``.

name: _tool
arguments: module: str, func: str, *arg_specs: _ArgSpec, **fixed: Callable[[Any, InlineToolContext], Any]
doc: Executor calling ``module.func`` with mapped args plus ``fixed`` kwargs computed from ``(agent, ctx)``.

name: _callback_tool
arguments: module: str, func: str, callback_attr: str, *arg_specs: _ArgSpec
doc: Executor for a GUI-callback tool: mapped args plus ``callback=getattr(agent, callback_attr, None)``.

significant_calls.expression:
agent._memory_manager.notify_memory_tool_write(
            result,
            args,
            build_metadata=lambda: agent._build_memory_write_metadata(
                task_id=ctx.effective_task_id,
                tool_call_id=ctx.tool_call_id,
            ),
        )

name: _scope_in_connected_mcp_servers
doc:
Add the MCP servers this call connected to the agent's toolset selection.

``tool_describe``/``tool_call`` resolve names inside that selection, and it was fixed when the
agent was built, so a server registered a moment ago is otherwise "not found" for the rest of
the turn the result calls it available in. Only the selection changes; ``agent.tools`` does
not, so the sent tool schema bytes stay the same.

name: resolve_invoke_tool_executor
doc:
Inline executor for ``invoke_tool`` (concurrent path), or None for registry dispatch.

Precedence: todo_list/session_search/memory, then memory-manager tools, then the
remaining inline tools (``message_agent`` excluded).

name: _fmt_est_cost
doc:
Shared label helper so sub-cent totals render at 4dp, not "~$0.00".

Routes through ``format_cost_label`` so sub-cent aggregates render at 4dp instead of collapsing to
"~$0.00" (#79220 bug class — the same dishonesty this module's cost buckets exist to fix, #77223).

name: _estimate_cost
arguments: session_or_model: dict[str, Any] | str, input_tokens: int=0, output_tokens: int=0, *, cache_read_tokens: int=0, cache_write_tokens: int=0, provider: Optional[str]=None, base_url: Optional[str]=None
doc: Estimate the USD cost for a session row or a model/token tuple.

name: _short_model
doc: Display name: strip the provider prefix; empty → "unknown".

name: _parse_json
doc: JSON-decode *raw* when it is a string; the value if it is a *kind*, else None.

name: _iter_functions
doc: Yield the ``function`` dict of every well-formed entry in a tool_calls column.

name: _scoped
arguments: before: str, after: str='', *, alias: str='s.'
doc:
(unfiltered, source-filtered) query pair sharing one body. Built once at class definition,
so no runtime value can alter query structure.

significant_calls.callee:
self._conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='index' AND name=?", (self._MESSAGES_ASSISTANT_CALLS_INDEX,)).fetchone
significant_calls.expression:
self._conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='index' AND name=?", (self._MESSAGES_ASSISTANT_CALLS_INDEX,)).fetchone()
