force-aborts healthy, still-streaming advisor turns at ``agent.turn_liveness.timeout_s``
(default 600s) even though the aux stream layer deliberately permits
``max(600, 4 × timeout)``. ``call_llm`` preserves a thread-local hook across its
dispatch/protected-daemon paths and ticks it per substantive stream chunk, so each
chunk re-arms the watchdog. A failed touch must never break the advisor call.

name: _touch_fanout_progress
doc:
Best-effort activity stamp for fan-out milestones; never raises (display of
progress must not decide turn liveness on its own, it only supports it).

name: _maybe_apply_moa_cache_control
arguments: messages: list[dict[str, Any]], runtime: dict[str, Any], *, cache_disabled: bool | None=None, cache_ttl: str | None=None
doc:
Apply cache_control to an advisor/aggregator request when its route honors it.

Same policy/marker helpers as the main loop; MoA has no static prefix so the
legacy system-and-3 fallback is used. ``cache_disabled`` is stamped onto the
stub so ``cache_ttl: off`` is honored; ``cache_ttl`` is clamped per destination.
Returns the messages unchanged on any error.

``cache_disabled`` (or the live config when omitted) is stamped onto the policy stub so
``prompt_caching.cache_ttl: off`` is not bypassed by the blank-agent pattern (#76085).

name: _price_reference_response
arguments: response: Any, slot: dict[str, Any], runtime: dict[str, Any]
returns: tuple[Any, Any, str | None, str | None]
doc:
Normalize a reference's usage with the slot's OWN provider/api_mode and price it
at its own rate (hence fan-out cost is summed in dollars). Never raises.

name: _run_reference
arguments: slot: dict[str, Any], ref_messages: list[dict[str, Any]], *, temperature: float | None=None, max_tokens: int | None=None, reference_timeout: float | None=None, context_length_cache: Any=None, cache_disabled: bool | None=None, cache_ttl: str | None=None, agent: Any=None
doc:
Call one reference model; return ``(label, text, accounting)``. Never raises:
a failed reference becomes a labelled ``[failed: …]`` note. Runs in a thread pool.

name: _reference_context_length
arguments: slot: dict[str, Any], runtime: dict[str, Any], cache: Any
doc:
Context window for a slot, memoized in ``cache`` per (provider, model) when given.

Failures are cached too so a flaky metadata source is not re-probed per reference.

name: _trim_messages_for_reference
arguments: messages: list[dict[str, Any]], slot: dict[str, str], runtime: dict[str, Any], *, reserve_output_tokens: int | None=None, context_length_cache: Any=None
doc:
Trim an advisory request to fit a reference model's context window.

Budget = window − ``reserve_output_tokens`` (or a default) − a safety fraction.
Drops the OLDEST frames after the system prompt, always keeping a user-first
body and the trailing user turn plus one preceding turn (even if still over
budget). ``context_length_cache`` memoizes the window per (provider, model);
unresolvable windows leave messages unchanged.

Reference models may have a smaller context window than the aggregator or the main conversation. Without
this trim, a reference whose window is exceeded gets a hard HTTP 400 from the provider, which
``_run_reference``'s try/except silently converts to a ``[failed: …]`` note — the MoA turn silently
degrades to fewer references (issue #60345).

name: _placeholder_output
doc: A reference-output tuple for a slot that was not (fully) run: zero accounting.

name: _settle_interrupted
arguments: futures: dict[Any, int], results: list, reference_models: list[dict[str, Any]], late_accounting_sink: Any
doc:
Fill every unfinished slot after a user interrupt: cancel never-dispatched
futures (nothing billed), keep real output of ones that just finished, and hand
running ones (cannot be killed, WILL bill) to ``late_accounting_sink``.

name: _record_late
arguments: sink: Any, label: str, future: Any
doc: Done-callback for an abandoned reference future: forward its real accounting.

name: _run_references_parallel
arguments: reference_models: list[dict[str, Any]], ref_messages: list[dict[str, Any]], *, temperature: float | None=None, max_tokens: int | None=None, progress_callback: Any=None, reference_timeout: float | None=None, agent: Any=None, late_accounting_sink: Any=None
doc:
Fan out all reference models in parallel; ``(label, text, _RefAccounting)`` per
slot in ``reference_models`` order.

``provider == "moa"`` slots are skipped with a note (recursion guard).
``progress_callback(refs_done, refs_total, label)`` fires per completion. With
*agent*, the wait polls every ``_REFERENCE_POLL_INTERVAL_S`` so a user interrupt
can abort it; in-flight calls cannot be killed and bill via ``late_accounting_sink``.

name: _truncate_tool_result
doc: Head+tail preview of a tool result with an ``[... N chars omitted ...]`` marker.

name: _field
doc: Read ``name`` from a dict or an attribute object (tool calls arrive as either).

name: _render_tool_calls
doc:
Render an assistant turn's tool_calls as ``[called tool: name(args)]`` lines.

Tolerates dict- and SimpleNamespace-shaped entries (and nested ``function``).

name: _tool_activity_since_last_user
doc:
Whether the acting model has already called tools since the last real user turn.
Guidance cached from the start of the turn predates those results, so replaying a
tool call it suggests can repeat work the transcript already shows as done.

name: _reference_messages
doc:
Build the advisory (reference-model) view of the conversation.

Plain user/assistant TEXT turns only: system prompt dropped, tool_calls rendered
inline, tool results folded into the preceding assistant turn as previews (no
tool-role messages / tool_calls arrays, so strict providers do not 400). Always
ends on a ``user`` turn (Anthropic treats a trailing assistant turn as prefill)
by APPENDING a synthetic request. The aggregator always gets the full transcript.

name: _extract_text
doc: Assistant text of a completed response: transport-normalized, else ``choices[0]``.

name: _preset_temperature
doc: Read an optional preset temperature; None (absent/empty/null) = provider default.

name: _is_failed_reference
doc: Whether a reference output is a ``[failed: …]`` / ``[skipped: …]`` sentinel.

name: _join_reference_outputs
arguments: outputs: list[tuple[str, str, Any]], degraded: str=''
doc: Render numbered reference blocks for the aggregator, appending any degraded notice.

name: _sum_reference_accounting
doc: Sum fan-out usage AND cost in dollars (each advisor priced at its OWN rate).

name: _guidance_inputs
arguments: reference_outputs: list[tuple[str, str, Any]], privacy_full: bool, policy: str
doc:
``(advisor outputs for the aggregator, degraded notice, all_failed)``.

'full' privacy mode redacts advisor text reaching the aggregator (applied to a
per-call copy — caches hold raw text). Failed refs are filtered out first.

name: aggregate_moa_context
arguments: *, user_prompt: str, api_messages: list[dict[str, Any]], reference_models: list[dict[str, Any]], aggregator: dict[str, Any], temperature: float | None=None, aggregator_temperature: float | None=None, reference_max_tokens: int | None=None, reference_timeout: float | None=None, degraded_reference_policy: str='loud', agent: Any=None
doc:
Run configured reference models and synthesize their advice (one-shot /moa).

Failures become model-specific notes instead of aborting the loop.
``reference_max_tokens`` caps ONLY the fan-out (capping the aggregator truncated
long syntheses). ``agent`` makes the fan-out interruptible.

``reference_max_tokens`` applies ONLY to the reference fan-out — the aggregator's own synthesis call is
not given an advisor budget. Omission uses provider-specific defaults; native protocols may
still require an internal wire limit.
A hardcoded cap on the aggregator call previously truncated long aggregator syntheses (#53580) — passing
``reference_max_tokens`` to both calls here would silently reintroduce that regression.

name: _completed_response_as_stream_chunk
doc: Adapt a completed response into one delta stream chunk (facade boundary only).

name: _attach_reference_guidance
doc:
Attach the per-turn reference block as its OWN trailing user message.

The block varies per turn; appending keeps ``[system][task][tool-history]``
cache-stable. It is never merged into a trailing user turn: iteration 1 of a
tool loop ends on ``user(task)``, and a merged ``user(task + guidance)`` byte-differs
from the ``user(task)`` every later iteration replays, so the provider prefix cache
collapsed to the system prompt on iteration 2 of every turn (#112358). Converters
that require strict alternation (Anthropic Messages, Converse, native Gemini) merge
the two user turns as SEPARATE content blocks, so the task block stays byte-stable
there too; on the OpenAI-compatible wire the request ends ``user(task), user(guidance)``,
which a chat template that enforces strict user/assistant alternation rejects.

name: peel_reference_guidance
doc:
Exact inverse of ``_attach_reference_guidance`` (plain string, or its cache-decorated
single-text-part form), so a cache breakpoint never lands on the turn-varying guidance.
Inputs are not mutated.

name: build_moa_facade
doc:
Single construction point for ``MoAClient``: a bare ``MoAClient(preset)`` would
drop the ``reference_callback`` relay and silence display events for the session.
The relay reads ``agent.tool_progress_callback`` at emit time.

name: bind_moa_runtime
doc:
Make ``agent`` act as the MoA preset: pin the virtual runtime fields and install the facade.

Every site that puts an agent onto ``provider: moa`` (init, ``/model`` switch, fallback
activation) must pin the same fields — the facade speaks only chat.completions, has no HTTP
endpoint and no OpenAI client kwargs — or the next dispatch/rebuild reaches a real wire with a
virtual identity (``moa://local`` 404, or the preset name sent as a model id).

name: __init__
arguments: self, preset_name: str, reference_callback: Any=None, agent: Any=None

name: consume_reference_usage
doc:
Pop pending fan-out ``(CanonicalUsage, cost_usd_or_None)`` and reset both
(so a streaming retry re-entering accounting cannot double-count).

name: last_reference_metrics
doc: Per-advisor metrics from the most recent fan-out, or None (read-only).

name: _record_late_reference_accounting
doc: Done-callback for abandoned (still billing) futures: fold their real spend in.

name: _fold_pending_accounting
doc: Add (never overwrite) fan-out spend so late interrupted-reference deposits survive.

name: consume_and_save_trace
doc:
Flush the pending full-turn trace to disk (no-op when nothing is pending).

``aggregator_output_fallback`` is the caller's resolved acting text for the
streaming path (not capturable at ``create()`` time). Never raises.

name: prepare
doc:
Run the advisor fan-out and return the exact aggregator request, which the
loop measures before its compression gate and hands back to ``create()``.

name: rebase_prepared_request
arguments: self, prepared: dict[str, Any], messages: list[dict[str, Any]]
doc: Re-attach already-generated guidance to a rebuilt (compressed) transcript.

name: _plan_aggregator_cache
arguments: self, agg_messages: list[dict[str, Any]], tools: Any, guidance: Any, agg_runtime: dict[str, Any]
doc:
Cache-breakpoint the aggregator request for its destination.

Guidance is peeled before planning and re-attached after so a breakpoint never
lands on the turn-varying block. Any error → undecorated request (warning, not
debug: this is the aggregator's ONLY decoration path).

name: _call_prepared_aggregator
arguments: self, prepared: dict[str, Any], api_kwargs: dict[str, Any]
doc: Send an already prepared MoA aggregator request exactly once.

name: _fanout_cache_key
arguments: self, preset: dict[str, Any], ref_messages: list[dict[str, Any]], reference_models: list[dict[str, Any]]
doc:
Turn-scoped reference cache key per the preset's fan-out cadence.

"user_turn" (default) hashes only the prefix up to the LAST USER message, so
later tool iterations are HITs. "per_iteration" re-runs whenever the advisory
view changes. "every_n:<N>": iteration 1 of a turn, then every Nth; in-between
iterations return the pinned last on-cadence key (HIT: no calls, no re-emit).

name: _run_fanout
arguments: self, preset: dict[str, Any], ref_messages: list[dict[str, Any]], reference_models: list[dict[str, Any]], aggregator: dict[str, Any], aggregator_temperature: Any, cache_key: tuple
doc:
Cache-MISS path of ``create``: run the advisors, account, trace and emit.

A preset MAY cap ADVISOR output (dominant MoA latency); the acting aggregator
is never capped. None timeout = inherit auxiliary.moa_reference.timeout.

significant_calls.expression:
self._emit(
                "moa.reference", index=idx, count=ref_count, label=label,
                text=_redact_reference_text(text) if privacy_mode else text,
            )

name: _build_guidance
arguments: self, reference_outputs: list[tuple[str, str, Any]], aggregator: dict[str, Any], degraded_reference_policy: str, stale: bool=False
doc: Render the reference block attached to the aggregator prompt (None = nothing).

name: __init__
arguments: self, preset_name: str, reference_callback: Any=None, agent: Any=None

name: _traces_enabled_and_dir
doc:
Trace directory if ``moa.save_traces`` is on, else None. Reads config per
call (once per cache-MISS turn); ``moa.trace_dir`` overrides the default.

name: _slot_trace
doc:
One reference's _RefAccounting as a full trace dict, including the FULL
input messages and output (not the truncated display preview).

name: slot_metrics
arguments: acct: Any, label: str, output: Any=None
doc:
``_slot_trace`` minus ``input_messages`` (the bulk of a record) for
observability hooks. ``output`` comes from the caller because the
privacy-redacted advisor text lives alongside the accounting, not on it.

name: save_moa_turn
arguments: *, session_id: Optional[str], preset_name: str, reference_outputs: list[tuple[str, str, Any]], aggregator_label: str, aggregator_model: Optional[str], aggregator_provider: Optional[str], aggregator_temperature: Any, aggregator_input_messages: Any, aggregator_output: Optional[str], aggregator_streamed: bool
doc:
Append one full MoA turn record to the session's trace JSONL, if enabled.

Best-effort: failures are logged at debug and swallowed. ``aggregator_output``
is captured inline on the non-streaming path and after the fact from the
resolved assistant text on the streaming path; if unavailable it is None and
``output_location`` points at the session store.

name: _models_dev_to_hermes_ids
doc: Return the Hermes provider ids that map to *mdev_id* (may be []).

name: _configured_catalog_provider
doc:
``catalog_provider`` declared on a custom provider's ``providers.<name>`` row (or legacy
``custom_providers[]`` entry): the catalogued vendor whose models it resells. None when unset.

name: _models_dev_id
doc:
models.dev provider id for a Hermes provider id, or None. A custom provider reaches the
catalog only through its configured ``catalog_provider`` alias (#112649).

name: _cfg_get
arguments: *keys: str, default: Any, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: ``cfg_get`` over the read-only config; *default* on any failure.

name: _quietly
doc: Run *fn*; on any exception log ``"Failed to <what>: %s"`` at debug and return *default*.

name: _load_etag
doc: Last-known ETag from disk, or "" if missing.

name: _clear_etag
doc:
Delete the ETag sidecar so the next fetch is unconditional: an If-None-Match without a
servable cache invites a 304 that leaves the process with no data at all.

name: _get_models_dev_url
doc: The models.dev API URL, honoring the ``models_dev.url`` config override.

name: _validate_registry
doc: True if *data* is a non-empty dict suitable for serving.

name: _load_disk_cache
doc:
Load the disk cache; a corrupt/empty one is quarantined with a warning so it never
masquerades as ``{}`` and breaks provider/model resolution.

name: _quarantine_corrupt_cache
doc:
Rename a rejected cache aside and drop its ETag sidecar. Renaming makes the rejection a
one-time event — otherwise every hot-path call that finds the in-memory cache empty re-parses
and re-warns until a network fetch succeeds. The sidecar vouches for a registry we no longer hold.

name: _disk_cache_age_seconds
doc:
Age of the disk cache file in seconds, or None if missing/unreadable. An mtime in the future
(clock skew) is also None — unknown freshness — so callers fall through to the network.

name: _save_disk_cache
doc: Save the registry atomically, plus the ETag sidecar when non-empty.

name: _fetch_models_dev_from_network
doc:
Fetch the live registry; returns ``(registry, etag)`` (etag "" if none). Raises on network
errors and on an empty/invalid payload. ``conditional`` sends ``If-None-Match`` with the sidecar's
ETag and raises ``_NotModified`` on 304 — pass True ONLY while holding ``_models_dev_fetch_lock``
AND a servable registry, or a 304 leaves the process with no data.

name: _mark_stale_cache_grace
doc:
Give stale cache data a 5-minute in-memory grace before retrying refresh. Only ever moves the
timestamp forward, so a background refresh that completed meanwhile keeps its fresh stamp.

name: _serve_stale
doc: Arm the grace window, kick off a background refresh, return the held cache.

name: _commit_registry
arguments: data: dict[str, Any], *, etag: str='', where: str
doc:
Persist a fetched registry: disk + in-mem + clear backoff. Callers hold ``_models_dev_fetch_lock``
so a failing refresh on one path can never stomp state a succeeding refresh just committed.

name: _confirm_cache_not_modified
doc:
After a 304: clear backoff and re-mark the held cache fresh (disk is untouched — only the
freshness marker advances). Caller holds the lock.

name: _note_refresh_failure
doc: Arm the process-wide 5-minute backoff. Caller holds the lock.

name: _refresh_locked
doc:
One conditional fetch + state update; caller holds ``_models_dev_fetch_lock``. Returns the
registry to serve, or None when the fetch failed (backoff armed).

name: _background_refresh_models_dev
doc: Best-effort refresh after serving stale cache data.

name: _start_background_refresh_models_dev
doc: Start one daemon refresh worker if none is running and the failure backoff has elapsed.

name: fetch_models_dev
doc:
Fetch the models.dev registry (dict keyed by provider ID; {} on failure). Cache hierarchy:
fresh in-memory → stale in-memory (served now, refreshed in one background daemon thread — stale
beats a foreground timeout) → disk of any age (stale triggers the same background refresh) →
singleflight foreground fetch. A failed refresh suppresses automatic refreshes for 5 minutes.
``force_refresh=True`` bypasses the cache fast paths and the backoff, falling back to cached data
only if the call fails. ``allow_network=False`` returns any memory/disk cache and never makes a request.

name: _registry_provider
doc: The raw models.dev provider entry, or None.

name: _registry_models
doc: The ``models`` dict of a models.dev provider entry, or None.

name: _get_provider_models
arguments: provider: str, *, allow_network: bool=False, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Resolve a Hermes provider ID to its models dict, or None if unknown.
``allow_network`` defaults to False — hot-path callers must never block.

name: _openrouter_catalog_lookup_base
doc:
Return the base id to retry a catalog lookup with, or ``None``.

OpenRouter's ``:nitro`` / ``:floor`` / ``:exacto`` / ``:online`` are
request-time routing modifiers: they change which endpoint serves the
request, never which model runs. ``/models`` and models.dev list only the
base id, so a routed id must resolve to the base model's metadata.

Scoped to OpenRouter so a genuine ``model:tag`` on another provider (an
Ollama tag, a ``:cloud`` catalog key) is never rewritten.

Deliberately excludes ``:free``, ``:batch``, ``:extended``, and
``:thinking``: those are REAL catalog SKUs with their own entries and
their own — sometimes different — context windows. Stripping them would
report a window LARGER than the model actually has. Their real entries
are found by the exact/case-insensitive passes above, and a genuinely
absent SKU must miss so ``model_overrides`` ``_default`` fill-gap
semantics still apply.

name: _iter_model_entries
arguments: models: dict[str, Any], model: str, *, suffix_fallback: bool=True, provider: str=''
doc:
Yield ``(model_id, entry)`` candidates: exact, case-insensitive, then (optionally)
``:cloud``/``-cloud`` suffixed forms. Suffix fallback: some providers (ollama-cloud) store
``kimi-k2.6:cloud`` while the live API returns the bare name; without it context lookup falls to
stale OpenRouter metadata and trips the 64k minimum-context guard. Every consumer shares this
order so a suffix-keyed catalog model counts as KNOWN for ``model_overrides`` fill-gap ``_default``.

``provider`` enables the OpenRouter routing-variant fallback as a LAST
resort — after exact, case-insensitive, and ``:cloud`` matching — so a
real catalog SKU always wins over its base.

name: _find_model_entry
arguments: models: dict[str, Any], model: str, provider: str=''
doc: First catalog entry for *model* (exact, case-insensitive, suffix), or None.

name: _extract_limit
doc: Positive int ``entry.limit[key]`` or None (audio/image models have context=0).

name: _extract_context
doc: Context length from a models.dev model entry, or None if invalid/zero.

name: lookup_models_dev_context
arguments: provider: str, model: str, *, allow_network: bool=False
doc:
Context window in tokens for provider+model, or None if not found. An EXPLICIT ``model_overrides``
entry wins over the catalog; ``_default`` fills the gap only when the catalog has no answer (the
self-unblock path for wrong/missing context in models.dev). Catalog entries with context=0 are
skipped in favour of later candidates. ``allow_network`` defaults to False — runs every turn.

See #84482.

name: _load_model_overrides
doc:
The ``model_overrides`` config section ({} on any failure). Deliberately not memoized:
``load_config_readonly()`` is already (mtime, size)-cached upstream, and an ``id(cfg)``-keyed
layer can serve stale overrides after a reload when CPython reuses the dict address.

name: _provider_override_section
doc: Override section for *provider* (keyed by Hermes OR models.dev id), or None.

name: _explicit_model_override
arguments: provider: str, model: str, *, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Explicit per-provider+model override dict (exact, then case-insensitive skipping the ``_default`` sentinel), or None.

name: _default_model_override
doc: Fill-gap ``_default`` override: per-provider first, then global; or None.

name: _override_for
arguments: provider: str, model: str, *, catalog_hit: bool, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Explicit override if any; else the ``_default`` only on a catalog miss.

name: _override_int
doc: Coerce an override field to a positive int, warning once on garbage.

name: _override_context_window
doc:
EXPLICITLY overridden context_window, or None. Explicit-only on purpose: this runs early in the
resolution chain (agent/model_metadata.py, before custom_providers and live probes) where a
``_default`` must not preempt more specific sources; fill-gap defaults apply in ``lookup_models_dev_context``.

name: _default_override_context
doc: Fill-gap context from a ``_default`` override, for catalog misses.

name: _override_to_catalog_shape
doc:
Translate canonical override keys into a models.dev-shaped patch. Returns ``(patch, vision)`` —
vision is out-of-band because it maps onto the ``modalities.input`` list rather than a scalar field.

name: _merge_catalog_entry_with_override
arguments: raw: dict[str, Any], override: dict[str, Any]
doc:
Patch a catalog entry with a canonical-schema override. Sub-dicts (``limit``, ``modalities``) are
merged, not clobbered — setting only ``context_window`` must not wipe the catalog's ``limit.output``.

name: _builtin_model_metadata
arguments: provider: str, model: str, *, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Built-in metadata for a provider/model pair, if Hermes has a vendor-specific entry.

name: _relay_vision_marker_metadata
doc:
Fill-gap base for an OpenCode Zen/Go ``*-vision*`` model id the catalog does not know. The relays
resell vendor previews (``deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp``) before models.dev indexes them, and the id's
``-vision`` token is the vendor's own capability marker; without it ``image_input_mode: auto`` treats
the model as text-only and detours images through the lossy describe path (#96066). Every other field
keeps the unknown-model defaults, so only vision is claimed.

name: _provider_model_capabilities
doc:
Exact-model declaration from the registered ``ProviderProfile.model_capabilities`` (canonical
``model_overrides`` schema). The ONE plugin seam: every consumer that reads models.dev through this
module (picker badges, image routing, ``/api/model/info``, context lookup) sees it (#102115).

name: _apply_overrides
arguments: provider: str, model: str, entry: Optional[dict[str, Any]], *, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Catalog/builtin metadata, patched by the plugin's declaration, then by the explicit user override.
``_UNKNOWN_MODEL_BASE`` is the base on a catalog miss; a fill-gap ``_default`` applies only when no
source knows the model. None when nothing knows it.

name: _entry_supports_vision
doc:
Prefer explicit ``modalities.input`` (the older ``attachment`` flag can be stale or too broad
for image routing); fall back to it only when the input modalities are absent/invalid.

name: get_model_capabilities
arguments: provider: str, model: str, *, allow_network: bool=False, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Capability metadata from the models.dev cache, or None if unresolvable. EXPLICIT ``model_overrides``
patch catalog fields; ``_default`` fills the gap only for models the catalog does not know. Unspecified
fields fall through to the catalog, or to safe defaults. ``allow_network`` defaults to False (hot path).

EXPLICIT ``model_overrides`` entries (per-provider+model) win over catalog values for the fields they
set. ``_default`` entries fill the gap only for models the catalog does not know — the supported
self-unblock path for custom/local models (#8731) and for models with wrong metadata in models.dev
(#84482).

name: list_provider_models
doc:
All model IDs for a provider ([] if unknown). ``allow_network`` defaults to True: the model
picker is interactive and a fresh catalog is worth a short wait.

name: list_agentic_models
doc:
Model IDs suitable for agentic use: tool_call=True, minus hidden and noise models. [] on any
failure. ``allow_network`` defaults to True (called from interactive model selection).

name: _parse_model_info
arguments: model_id: str, raw: dict[str, Any], provider_id: str
doc: Convert a raw models.dev model entry dict into a ModelInfo dataclass.

name: _parse_provider_info
doc: Convert a raw models.dev provider entry dict into a ProviderInfo.

name: get_provider_info
arguments: provider_id: str, *, allow_network: bool=True, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Provider metadata by Hermes or models.dev ID, or None if not cataloged. ``allow_network`` defaults to True (interactive setup).

name: get_model_info
arguments: provider_id: str, model_id: str, *, allow_network: bool=False, config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Full model metadata by Hermes or models.dev provider ID (exact match, then case-insensitive), or
None if not found. EXPLICIT ``model_overrides`` patch known catalog models; ``_default`` fills the gap
only for unknown ones. ``allow_network`` defaults to False — cost guard and inventory are hot paths.

``model_overrides`` entries use the SAME canonical schema as every other consumer (``context_window``,
``supports_*``, ``model_family``) — they are translated into the catalog shape at
this boundary, and sub-dicts (``limit``, ``modalities``) are merged rather than clobbered. See #84482,
#8731.

name: format_capabilities
doc: Human-readable capabilities, e.g. 'reasoning, tools, vision, PDF'.

name: _strip_provider_prefix
doc:
Strip a registry-known provider prefix: ``"local:m"`` -> ``"m"``. Ollama ``model:tag``
ids are preserved even when the model half is a provider name (``qwen:0.5b``).

name: _parse_base_url
doc: ``urlparse`` of the normalized URL (``scheme`` prepended when absent); None when empty.

name: _endpoint_host_key
doc: ``host:port`` key (None without a host) so every probe path for one server shares an entry.

name: _note_endpoint_blackholed
doc: Record that a probe to ``base_url`` timed out during TCP connect.

name: _endpoint_blackholed
doc: True if a recent probe to ``base_url`` timed out during TCP connect (cache lookup only).

name: _note_if_connect_timeout
doc: Blackhole ``base_url`` when ``exc`` is a connect-phase timeout.

name: _is_connect_timeout
doc: Read timeouts prove the server accepted a connection, not a blackhole.

name: _load_json_dict
doc: JSON object at ``path``, or {} when missing/invalid.

name: _ttl_memo_get
arguments: path: Path, key: str, ttl: float, *, ts_key: str, value_key: str
doc: Fresh (< ``ttl`` seconds) ``value_key`` of the ``key`` entry in a TTL memo file, else None.

name: _ttl_memo_put
arguments: path: Path, key: str, value: Any, ttl: float, *, ts_key: str, value_key: str, what: str, ts_first: bool=False
doc: Write ``key`` into a TTL memo file, dropping expired siblings. Best-effort.

name: _local_probe_disk_get
doc: Return a fresh cached value for ``kind:key``, else None.

name: _local_probe_disk_put
arguments: kind: str, key: str, value: Any
doc: Persist a successful probe result. Best-effort; prunes stale entries.

name: _get_model_metadata_cache_path
doc: Path to the OpenRouter model metadata disk cache.

name: _model_metadata_disk_cache_age_seconds
doc: Disk-cache age in seconds, or None if freshness is unknown.

name: _load_model_metadata_disk_cache
doc: Processed OpenRouter metadata cache from disk ({} on any failure).

name: _get_endpoint_metadata_cache_path
doc: On-disk memo of remote ``/models`` probes (see ``_endpoint_disk_cache_get``).

name: _endpoint_disk_cache_get
doc:
Fresh cross-process memo of a remote ``/models`` probe (same TTL as in-memory): one-shot
runs (``hermes -q``, cron) start cold and Nous bypasses the persistent context cache, so
without this every launch paid the live probe. Local endpoints are never memoized.

name: _endpoint_disk_cache_put
arguments: normalized: str, cache: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
doc: Memoize a successful remote ``/models`` probe; expired siblings are dropped.

name: _warn_context_length_fallback
doc:
Warn once per model+endpoint that detection failed and the hard default is used,
so small-context models (8K, 32K) don't silently get 256K and fail at the API.

name: grok_supports_reasoning_effort
doc: Allowlist check (aggregator prefixes like ``x-ai/`` stripped); unknown Grok models get no effort dial.

name: openai_model_rejects_reasoning
doc:
True for an OpenAI model id (aggregator ``openai/`` prefix stripped) that rejects the
Responses ``reasoning`` parameter outright, so callers send no ``reasoning`` key at all.

name: is_grok_46_family
doc: Whether *model* is a Grok 4.6 family identifier.

name: is_anthropic_fast_mode_model
doc:
Whether *model* accepts Anthropic fast mode. Accepts vendor-prefixed, dotted, variant and
dated spellings (``anthropic/claude-opus-5.5``, ``claude-opus-4-8-20260601``). Dedicated
``...-fast`` ids select fast inference through the model field and are not in the list.

name: _infer_provider_from_url
doc: models.dev provider name for a base URL (custom endpoints need no explicit provider).

name: _strip_openrouter_routing_variant
arguments: model: str, base_url: str='', provider: str=''
doc:
Strip an OpenRouter routing-variant suffix for catalog lookup.

``:nitro`` / ``:floor`` / ``:exacto`` / ``:online`` are request-time
routing modifiers, NOT catalog entries — OpenRouter's ``/models`` lists
only the base id, and a variant shares the base model's context window.
Without this, every lookup below misses and the resolver falls through to
a generic family default (``x-ai/grok-4.6:nitro`` → the 131K ``grok``
catch-all instead of its real 2M window).

Only the id used for LOOKUP is rewritten. The suffixed id the caller holds
stays on the wire, so the routing opt-in is preserved — the same rule
:func:`hermes_cli.models.validate_requested_model` applies. Sharing the
base's cache key is intentional: the window is identical, so a variant and
its base must never disagree.

Narrow by design: only applied when the request actually routes through
OpenRouter, so a local ``model:tag`` that happens to end in one of these
words is untouched.

name: _lmstudio_server_root
doc: LM Studio server root for native ``/api/v1`` endpoints.

name: _server_root
doc: Probe root for a local server: IPv4-resolved, ``/v1`` suffix stripped.

name: _catalog_key_matches
doc:
Substring match with version separators normalised on both sides, so a relay slug like
``z-ai-glm-5-3`` still hits the ``glm-5.3`` entry instead of the ``glm`` catch-all (#97398).
Boundary-matched families: a key must be followed by ``-:.@`` or the end, and a key ending in
``-`` is the family default for bare names (``org/`` allowed) continuing with a lineup letter.

name: _longest_key_match
doc:
First ``(key, value)`` whose key is a substring of ``model_lower``, longest key first so
specific entries (``gpt-5.4-mini``) beat their family catch-all (``gpt-5``); ties keep table order.

name: _ollama_show_context
arguments: data: dict[str, Any], *, gguf_first: bool, minimum: Optional[int]=None
doc:
Context length from an Ollama ``/api/show`` payload. ``parameters.num_ctx`` is the RUNTIME
window (Modelfile override), ``model_info.*.context_length`` the GGUF training max. Local users
control num_ctx (prefer it); hosted operators may cap it arbitrarily (``gguf_first``).

name: _endpoint_scoped_context_length
doc:
Context confirmed for one provider endpoint only (see _ENDPOINT_SCOPED_CONTEXT): Kimi Coding
serves K3 at 1 Mi only on the canonical ``api.kimi.com/coding`` host (legacy Moonshot keys do
not); NVIDIA NIM serves deepseek-v4-pro at 262,144 while DeepSeek's native endpoint is 1M.

name: _skip_persistent_context_cache
doc:
Providers whose disk context cache must not short-circuit probing: LM Studio (loaded
context is transient), Codex OAuth (entitlement-specific window; a persisted fallback would suppress revalidation).

name: _is_codex_route
arguments: provider: str, base_url: str, custom_providers: list | None
doc:
True when the request travels the Codex Responses wire regardless of host: the native
``openai-codex`` provider (also behind a ``HERMES_CODEX_BASE_URL`` / ``model.base_url`` proxy)
or a custom entry declaring ``api_mode: codex_responses``. The transport, not the hostname,
decides which window the model actually gets (#116191).

name: _save_unless_skipped
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, ctx: int, provider: str
doc: Persist ``ctx`` unless the provider opts out of the disk cache.

name: _maybe_cache_local_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, length: int
doc:
Persist a probed local window only at/above MINIMUM_CONTEXT_LENGTH: sub-minimum windows are
still returned so agent_init can reject them, but must not be blessed into the disk cache.

name: _probe_local_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: str, provider: str
doc: Live local probe; persists a positive result unless the provider opts out of the disk cache.

name: _reconcile_local_cached_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, cached: int, api_key: str=''
doc:
*cached* unless a live local probe reports a different limit (operators restart
vLLM/Ollama with a new --max-model-len / num_ctx under the same id). A failed
probe keeps the disk entry; sub-minimum live windows invalidate but are not persisted.

name: is_local_endpoint
doc:
True for loopback, container-internal DNS, unqualified hosts, RFC-1918,
link-local and Tailscale CGNAT (so a trusted Ollama box over Tailscale gets
the same timeout auto-bumps as localhost).

name: _localhost_to_ipv4
doc:
``localhost`` HOST -> ``127.0.0.1`` (Windows dual-stack resolves ::1 first and pays a ~2s IPv6
connect timeout on IPv4-only servers). Scheme-anchored so ``?upstream=http://localhost`` is untouched.

name: detect_local_server_type
doc: Probe known endpoints: "ollama", "lm-studio", "vllm", "llamacpp", or None (TTL-cached).

name: _coerce_reasonable_int
arguments: value: Any, minimum: int=1024, maximum: int=10000000

name: _extract_flat_context_length
doc:
Top-level-only context WINDOW read (no nested walk, so an unrelated nested section can't leak
a same-named key). ``max_tokens`` is NOT a window key: on OpenAI-compatible passthroughs it is the max OUTPUT.

name: _context_length_from_model_payload
doc:
Context window from a ``/v1/models`` object: window keys first, ``max_tokens`` last (Anthropic
payloads carry ``max_input_tokens`` = 1M window AND ``max_tokens`` = 128k OUTPUT cap).

name: _normalize_token_rates
doc:
Rescale the generic path's token rates to per-token strings (the contract usage_pricing
multiplies by 1e6), the way the Novita/DeepInfra branches already do for their known units.

name: _add_model_aliases
arguments: cache: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], model_id: str, entry: dict[str, Any]

name: fetch_model_metadata
doc: Fetch model metadata from OpenRouter (cached for 1 hour).

name: _endpoint_model_entry
arguments: model: dict[str, Any], model_id: str, context_length: Optional[int]
doc: Cache entry for one ``/models`` item; optional keys are set only when known.

name: _lmstudio_loaded_context
doc: Context of the first loaded LM Studio instance (the runtime value), else None.

name: _lmstudio_native_models
doc: LM Studio ``/api/v1/models`` → cache; context comes from the first loaded instance.

name: _apply_llamacpp_props
arguments: cache: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], request_candidate: str, headers: dict[str, str], verify
doc:
Overwrite ``context_length`` with llama.cpp's allocated ``n_ctx`` from /props (``/v1/props``, then
``/props`` for older builds). In router mode the bare endpoint 400s, so each LOADED child is read
via ``/props?model=``; unloaded children are skipped — probing could autoload them.

name: _remember_endpoint_models
arguments: memo_key: tuple[str, str], cache: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]

name: fetch_endpoint_model_metadata
arguments: base_url: str, api_key: str='', force_refresh: bool=False
doc: Model metadata from an OpenAI-compatible ``/models`` endpoint (cached per base URL).

name: _resolve_endpoint_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: str=''
doc: Resolve context length from an endpoint's live ``/models`` metadata.

name: _get_context_cache_path
doc: Path to the persistent context length cache file.

name: _load_context_cache_document
doc: Read scalar lengths and their provenance from the same atomic document.

name: _load_context_cache
doc: Load scalar lengths, preserving the legacy reader contract.

name: _context_cache_key
doc: Canonical ``model@base_url`` key; trailing slashes stripped so ``/v1`` and ``/v1/`` share one entry.

name: save_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, length: int, *, source: str=''
doc: Persist a discovered context length under ``model@base_url`` (same model, different providers, different limits).

name: save_provider_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, length: int, provider: str=''
doc: Persist a provider-confirmed window, distinguishing it from legacy Bedrock fallbacks.

name: get_cached_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, *, bedrock_confirmed: bool=False
doc: Look up a previously discovered context length for model+provider.

name: _invalidate_cached_context_length
doc:
Drop a stale entry and its probe cooldown using the persisted cache URL.

Bedrock callers without a runtime endpoint must pass ``bedrock://``, as
the resolver does; a blank URL addresses the distinct generic cache key.
In-process caches are dropped unconditionally; only the file update takes the cache lock.

name: get_next_probe_tier
doc: Next lower probe tier, or None if already at minimum.

name: parse_context_limit_from_error
get_context_length_from_provider_error
doc:
Provider-reported limit LOWER than the current window, else None. Overflow recovery must
not invent a window: when the provider only says the input is too long, callers keep the
configured length and compress rather than stepping down guessed probe tiers.

name: _completion_split_budget
doc:
window - measured prompt from the OpenAI-style parenthetical split, or None when the wording
is absent or the prompt alone fills the window (a genuine input overflow -> compress).

name: parse_available_output_tokens_from_error
doc:
Available OUTPUT tokens from a "max_tokens too large" error, or None. Distinct from "prompt
too long" (-> compress): here input + requested_output > window, so the fix is a smaller
max_tokens for this call and context_length must NOT be touched.

name: _sglang_window_and_input
doc: ``(window, input_tokens)`` from SGLang's wording, else None; both figures are explicit there.

name: is_output_cap_error
doc:
Yes/no sibling of :func:`parse_available_output_tokens_from_error` for unparseable wordings. An
output-cap 400 misclassified as context overflow death-loops the compressor (same max_tokens, same
rejection). Signal: talks about max_tokens as a cap/range/limit and NOT about an oversized input.

name: _model_id_matches
doc: Exact match, or ``publisher/slug`` (LM Studio native ids) whose slug equals the configured name.

name: _ollama_show
arguments: server_url: str, api_key: str, bare_model: str, timeout: float=3.0, *, note_blackhole: bool=False
doc: Ollama ``/api/show`` JSON for ``bare_model``, or None on any failure (``note_blackhole``: connect timeouts condemn the host).

arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: str=''
doc: Ollama ``/api/show`` context (Modelfile num_ctx, else GGUF max); the value to send as ``num_ctx``.

name: query_ollama_supports_vision
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: str=''
doc:
True/False when Ollama ``/api/show`` reports vision support (``capabilities`` on 0.6.0+, else
``model_info.*.vision.block_count``); None when unreachable, not Ollama, or model unknown.

name: _memo_local_probe
doc:
Short-TTL, positive-only memo of a local probe (see _LOCAL_CTX_PROBE_CACHE): a failure during
a startup race must not suppress the retry once the server is up, so only truthy results memoize.

arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: str=''

Provider-agnostic Ollama ``/api/show`` probe (any hostname; non-Ollama servers 404 fast).
GGUF-first (hosted users can't set num_ctx) — the reverse of query_ollama_num_ctx(), hence the namespaced memo key.

name: _query_ollama_api_show_uncached
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: str=''
doc: Uncached body of ``_query_ollama_api_show`` — one POST to ``/api/show``.

name: _model_name_suggests_kimi
doc: Kimi family (``kimi-*``, ``moonshotai/*``) — guard against stale 32K underreports.

name: _model_name_suggests_minimax_m3
doc: MiniMax M3 on any surface — models.dev underreport guard and agent_runtime_helpers cache-control gating.

name: _stale_pre_catalog_cache_entry
doc:
True when a persisted window is a pre-catalog leftover: the model resolves (longest-key-first) to a
_PRE_CATALOG_STALE_KEYS key and the cached value is <= the largest shorter matching catch-all (or 256K).

name: _model_name_suggests_minimax
doc: MiniMax family (``minimax*``, ``minimaxai/*``) — guard against stale 32K underreports (real: 204.8K).

doc: Local-server context probe, short-TTL cached (see _LOCAL_CTX_PROBE_CACHE).

LM Studio native /api/v1/models (the OpenAI-compat list omits context);
loaded-instance config is the runtime value.

name: _openai_models_list_context
doc: /v1/models list: match by id, else the sole model on single-model servers (llama.cpp reports a GGUF path as id).

name: _query_local_context_length_uncached
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: str=''
doc: Query a local server for the model's context length.
