doc: Dots -> dashes so Nous ids (claude-opus-4-6) compare with OpenRouter's (claude-opus-4.6).

name: _query_anthropic_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: Any
doc:
Anthropic /v1/models max_input_tokens; OAuth tokens (sk-ant-oat*) 401 and are skipped.

``api_key`` may be a ``key_cmd`` callable token source; the metadata probe never mints — a
callable is not a Console key, so the lookup is skipped like an OAuth token (#114967).

name: _bare_codex_slug
doc:
Lowercased slug without ``vendor/`` (display/auxiliary callers pass ``openai/gpt-5.6-sol-900k``).

Display/auxiliary callers pass ids like ``openai/gpt-5.6-sol-900k``; the main-agent path normalizes the
namespace away earlier, but this resolver must accept both shapes (#92797 review).

name: is_codex_900k_base
doc: Single source of truth for ``-900k`` eligibility (picker, resolution, /model validation, wire stripping).

name: _codex_variant_base
doc: Lowercased eligible base of a VALID ``-900k`` variant, else None (``gpt-5.5-900k`` is an invalid alias).

name: is_codex_context_variant
doc: Suffix AND eligible base — ``gpt-5.5-900k`` is an invalid alias, not a variant.

name: strip_codex_context_variant_suffix
doc:
Wire-safe slug with a VALID ``-900k`` suffix removed (vendor prefix kept); an ineligible alias is
returned unchanged so it fails honestly at the API instead of running as another model.

name: has_codex_context_variant
doc: Picker-side alias of :func:`is_codex_900k_base`.

name: _verified_codex_ctx_for_slug
doc: Live-verified cap for a VALID ``-900k`` variant only; base slugs and ineligible aliases -> None.

name: _codex_catalog_urls
doc:
Catalog URLs against ``base_url`` when it names a Codex-compatible gateway, else the
hard-coded endpoint. A custom base's credential belongs to that service — sending it to
chatgpt.com (or fetching the direct catalog behind a gateway's back) is wrong (#121486).

name: _codex_catalog_probe_allowed
doc:
Whether a catalog probe may carry ``access_token`` to ``base_url``'s ``/models``.

The caller binds ``base_url`` to the credential's own route, so a custom gateway is asked with
its own key (opaque or JWT). chatgpt.com only accepts ChatGPT OAuth access tokens — JWTs — so a
non-JWT credential aimed there is a gateway key composed with the wrong host: refuse it
(defense in depth, mirroring ``_probe_codex_quota_restored``'s gate; #121486).

name: fetch_codex_catalog_entries
doc:
``(models, last_status)`` from the first catalog URL that answers HTTP 200 with a non-empty
``models`` list; ``get(url)`` is any client returning an object with ``status_code``/``json()``.
An empty or non-200 answer on the newest-client URL falls through to the ``0.0.0`` sentinel.

name: _codex_oauth_token_fingerprint
doc:
Non-secret cache key for a Codex OAuth access token (plus the base it was probed against —
a gateway's catalog can differ from chatgpt.com's for the same forwarded token).

name: _remember_no_codex_catalog
doc:
A probe that found no catalog (down, non-200, not Codex-shaped) is remembered briefly: context
resolution runs on init, /status, aux and @-reference turns, and each miss can block ~30s. The entry is
stamped as if cached ``TTL - NEGATIVE_TTL`` ago, so the shared freshness check expires it after
``_CODEX_OAUTH_CONTEXT_NEGATIVE_TTL``. A fresh catalog a concurrent probe just stored is kept, and the
max cache is left alone so an observed cap survives.

name: _fetch_codex_oauth_context_lengths_with_source
doc:
Account-scoped catalogue context lengths and HTTP freshness; also retain max-context and
speed metadata. In-process hits report False and must not drive persistent writes.

name: _codex_catalog_key
doc: The catalog key for ``slug``: exact, then case-insensitive in case casing drifts.

name: _cached_codex_catalog_max
arguments: access_token: str, base_url: str, slug: str
doc: ``max_context_window`` the catalog behind ``(access_token, base_url)`` last published for ``slug``.

name: _resolve_codex_oauth_context_length_with_source
arguments: model: str, access_token: str='', base_url: str=''
doc:
``(context_length, source)`` for a Codex OAuth slug. source: "live" (fresh authenticated probe —
the only one eligible for persistent writes), "memory" (same-token in-process hit), "fallback"
(static table), or "" when unresolved.

name: _resolve_nous_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str='', api_key: str=''
doc:
``(context_length, source)`` for a Nous Portal model: portal /v1/models is authoritative
("portal"). Fallback matches OR's prefixed ids against the bare Nous id with dot/dash
normalisation ("openrouter" — callers must NOT persist it, or a portal blip freezes the wrong value).

name: _validate_cached_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, cached: int, *, api_key: str=''
doc:
Step 1 of get_model_context_length: accept, repair, or drop a persisted entry. Returns the
value to use, or None to fall through to live resolution. Order matters: a value must be
rejected as bogus before any provider-specific handling.

name: _bedrock_probe_failed_recently
doc: Prune expired failures and check this home/endpoint/model/region's cooldown.

name: _resolve_bedrock_context_length
doc:
Step 1b: Bedrock static table + one cached live probe (Bedrock exposes no context window via
metadata APIs); None when boto3 is absent. Only provider-confirmed windows from a probe
or runtime error are reused. The table answers a call, never the cache. Keys use base_url,
or synthetic bedrock:// when absent, consistently with provider-error writers.

name: _resolve_custom_endpoint_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: str, provider: str
doc: Steps 2-3 for a truly custom endpoint: /models, local probes, Ollama /api/show, catalog, default.

name: _resolve_custom_codex_route_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: str, provider: str
doc:
Step 2 for a custom ``api_mode: codex_responses`` route — a Codex proxy on a generic URL.
The Codex OAuth table (with the opted-in ``-900k`` bump) answers first: the proxy's own /models
and the direct-API catalog both advertise the 1.05M direct window that Codex does not honour.
The proxy's context_window is never trusted; only an opted-in ``-900k`` variant asks the route's own
catalog (with the route's own key), and only for its max_context_window cap. Slugs the table does
not know take the ordinary endpoint probes.

name: _resolve_moa_context_length
doc:
Step 0a: MoA virtual provider — ``model`` is a preset name, so every probe would miss. Resolve
the aggregator's real provider+model (references are advisory). None on any failure.

name: _config_override_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, provider: str, custom_providers: list | None
doc:
Steps 0b-0c: config-only overrides (never touch the network). 0b: EXPLICIT model_overrides
only — fill-gap _default entries apply inside lookup_models_dev_context once the catalog has
missed, so a _default can never preempt custom_providers or live probes. 0c: custom_providers.

name: _resolve_provider_aware_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str, api_key: str, provider: str, effective_provider: str
doc: Step 5: provider-specific sources, tried in order; None when all miss.

name: get_model_context_length
arguments: model: str, base_url: str='', api_key: str='', config_context_length: int | None=None, provider: str='', custom_providers: list | None=None
doc:
Context length for a model. Resolution order: 0 config override / MoA aggregator /
model_overrides / custom_providers / endpoint-scoped; 1 persistent cache (Nous, LM
Studio, Codex OAuth bypass it) and Bedrock; 2-3 custom endpoints (/models, local
probe, Ollama); 4 Anthropic /v1/models (API keys only); 5 provider-aware (Copilot,
Nous, Codex OAuth, GMI, Ollama, OpenRouter live, models.dev); 6 OpenRouter for
unknown providers; 7 local server; 8 hardcoded defaults; 9 256K fallback.

name: get_model_context_length_async
arguments: model: str, base_url: str='', api_key: str='', config_context_length: int | None=None, provider: str='', custom_providers: list | None=None
doc: get_model_context_length on a worker thread (its blocking HTTP would stall the event loop).

name: estimate_tokens_rough
doc:
Rough token estimate: CJK/Hangul/Kana codepoints ~1 token each; everything else ceil(UTF-8 bytes/4).
Ceiling keeps short texts from estimating 0. Runs on every preflight walk, so all-ASCII stays O(1).

Byte-counting (not chars) is the corrective for non-CJK, non-ASCII text: Cyrillic/Greek/Arabic are 2
bytes/char so count ~chars/2, matching real BPE cost (~2-3 chars/token) where chars/4 under-counted
~2x and let sessions ride the provider ceiling below the compaction threshold. Calibrated vs
cl100k/o200k/Qwen2.5 (estimate/real): Russian 0.67->1.24, Arabic 0.53->0.96, Hindi 0.34->0.90,
Greek 0.37->0.68; accented Latin barely moves (French 1.02->1.03). errors="replace": lone surrogates
(routine in tool output; see message_sanitization) must not turn an estimate into a raise.

name: estimate_messages_tokens_rough
doc:
Rough token estimate for a message list (pre-flight only). Images cost the per-image price
learned from provider usage (``agent.image_token_cost``; flat default before calibration)
rather than their base64 length. ``charge_stale_thinking=False`` mirrors the tail-budget
walk (``context_compressor._estimate_msg_budget_tokens``): on non-echo routes stale reasoning
rides the wire only for the NEWEST assistant turn, so excluding it keeps the compaction TRIGGER
in the same size class as the walk — otherwise reasoning-heavy sessions fire preflight forever.

name: estimate_native_anthropic_messages_tokens_rough
doc: Estimate native Anthropic messages with replayed readable thinking charged exactly once.

name: estimate_native_anthropic_request_tokens_rough
arguments: messages: list[dict[str, Any]], *, system_prompt: str='', tools: Optional[list[dict[str, Any]]]=None
doc: Request estimate for native Anthropic; opaque replay bytes never enter text accounting.

name: _strip_stale_thinking_for_estimate
doc:
Copy of ``messages`` with stale thinking keys removed (newest kept). Shallow stripped copies
share the original value objects, so the per-message memo still hits for the stripped shape.

name: _estimate_message_tokens_cached
doc:
Text tokens + images x ``image_cost``; the memo holds text and image COUNT so a recalibrated
per-image price re-prices cached rows without invalidating them.

name: _count_image_tokens
doc: Count image-like content parts in a message; return their token cost.

name: strip_opaque_replay_items
doc:
``codex_reasoning_items`` with ``encrypted_content`` blanked for local token estimation.
The ciphertext is priced by the provider's own count, never by its bytes (a compaction
checkpoint alone can be 5M chars, #100611); only real usage prices it.

name: _wire_message_shadow
doc:
Shadow of a message holding only what the provider actually receives.
* ``api_content`` SUBSTITUTES ``content`` (mirrors ``turn_context.substitute_api_content`` exactly):
  only a non-empty STRING sidecar on a user/assistant row displaces content; substituting any
  other shape would UNDERcount — the dangerous direction.
* Base64 images become a placeholder; ``_count_image_tokens`` charges them flat.
* ``reasoning`` never ships as-is (request builds pop it after optionally promoting it into
  ``reasoning_content``); counting both inflated estimates up to +53%.
* Opaque provider blobs (``encrypted_content`` on codex reasoning / compaction items) are
  ciphertext the provider prices by its OWN token count, never by bytes; a native compaction
  checkpoint alone can be 5M chars (#100611). They contribute 0 here: only real usage ever
  prices them, and the usage anchor carries that price forward.

name: _estimate_message_tokens_without_images
doc: Token estimate for a message shadow with image payloads stripped.

name: estimate_request_tokens_rough
arguments: messages: list[dict[str, Any]], *, system_prompt: str='', tools: Optional[list[dict[str, Any]]]=None, charge_stale_thinking: bool=True
doc:
Rough token estimate for a full request: system prompt + messages + tool schemas (50+ tools
add 20-30K on their own). ``charge_stale_thinking`` is forwarded — pass False when the route
provably strips stale thinking (``message_sanitization.stale_thinking_reaches_wire``).

name: _per_token
arguments: source: dict[str, Any], fields: dict[str, str], scale

name: _apply_verified_bump
arguments: ctx: int, source: str, catalog_max: Optional[int]=None
doc:
Lift an EXACT stale 272K advertisement to the verified cap for opted-in ``-900k`` variants only,
never above the catalog's own ``max_context_window`` when it publishes one (#105443).

name: _safe_ctx
doc: Context length minus the known stale 32K underreports (same guard as step 6).

name: _write_context_cache
arguments: cache: dict[str, int], bedrock_confirmed: dict | None=None
doc:
Atomic write (a truncating write killed mid-dump leaves a partial file that
_load_context_cache() swallows as {}, wiping EVERY cached length). Raises on failure.

name: locked_context_cache
doc:
Run ``fn``'s load -> mutate -> write cycle under the cache file's cross-process lock.

The cache is best-effort: when the lock cannot be taken in time the update is skipped, never raised.

name: drop_context_cache_rows
doc:
Remove every key shape of one cached entry (and its Bedrock provenance) under the cache lock.

Only the file update is locked: callers evict their in-process probe caches unconditionally.

name: stream
arguments: url: str, *, headers=None, params=None, timeout=10.0, verify=None

name: get
arguments: url: str, *, headers=None, params=None, timeout=10.0, verify=None

name: _json_object
doc: The response body when it is a JSON object, else an empty dict.

name: llamacpp_context
doc:
llama.cpp's RUNTIME n_ctx: /props for a loaded model, else the ``--ctx-size`` the router will
launch it with (its /models entry), so a lazily-loaded model doesn't fall to a family catch-all.
The /props read passes autoload=false: the router loads any model a request names, and a context
probe must not undo an Eject or an idle unload.

name: router_launch_ctx
doc: ``--ctx-size`` from the router's launch args for *model* (GET /models), or None.

name: forget_message_token_memo
_repair_schema
doc: Recursively apply the Moonshot repairs to a schema node.

name: _ensure_required_array
doc:
Guarantee an object schema carries a ``required`` list, pruning names not in
``properties`` (Moonshot also rejects dangling names). Mutates and returns ``node``.

name: _fill_missing_type
doc:
Infer a ``type`` if this schema node has none.

A type list collapses to its first concrete member; otherwise
``properties``/``required``/``additionalProperties`` → object,
``items``/``prefixItems`` → array, ``enum`` → type of its first value,
else ``string`` (safest scalar). A bare ``if``/``then``/``else`` node
constrains whatever instance it is attached to rather than describing
its own type, so it is left untyped instead of defaulting to ``string``.

name: sanitize_moonshot_tool_parameters
doc: Deep-copied, Moonshot-compatible object schema; input is not mutated.

name: sanitize_moonshot_tools
doc:
Apply ``sanitize_moonshot_tool_parameters`` to every tool's parameters.

Returns the input list object itself when nothing needed repairing.

name: is_moonshot_model
doc:
True for any Kimi / Moonshot model slug, regardless of aggregator prefix.

Matches bare names (``kimi-k2.6``, ``moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6``) and
aggregator-prefixed slugs (``nous/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6``), since aggregators
route to Moonshot inference under their own base URL.

name: is_native_compaction_model
arguments: model: Optional[str], *, provider: Optional[str]=None, base_url: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Preserve gpt-5.6 eligibility; Astra (``-900k`` is a picker alias of the same wire slug)
additionally requires official Codex OAuth.

name: resolve_native_compaction_capabilities
arguments: *, model: Optional[str], base_url: Optional[str], provider: Optional[str]=None, is_codex_backend: bool=False
doc:
Resolve the native-compaction capability for a runtime destination (a resolved ``False``
is distinct from "unresolved" and must survive model switches unchanged).

name: is_direct_openai_route
doc: True for api.openai.com or the ChatGPT Codex backend — nothing else.

name: _positive_int
doc: ``int(value)`` when it is a positive integer-like (never a bool), else None.

name: resolve_compact_threshold
doc:
Resolve automatic mode or clamp an explicit native threshold.

Omitted/invalid follows the local compressor trigger minus the safety margin. An
explicit positive integer is absolute unless it must be clamped so native compaction
fires first. Booleans are never thresholds.

name: _warn_native_compaction_suppressed_by_checkpoint_gate
doc: Log once per process; the suppression itself is re-evaluated per request.

name: native_compaction_context_management
arguments: agent: Any, *, is_codex_backend: bool, is_xai_responses: bool=False, is_github_responses: bool=False
doc:
Return the ``context_management`` payload for this request, or None ("do not send").

Every gate is re-checked per request so a mid-session model switch or the in-session
kill switch (``agent.codex_responses_native_compaction = False``) takes effect next call.

name: _approx_tokens
doc: Retention cost of one carried-over text; never 0 so an empty item still consumes budget.

name: _head_within_budget
doc:
Longest prefix of ``text`` whose ``_approx_tokens`` fits ``budget``. A plain ``budget * CHARS_PER_TOKEN``
char slice would keep ~2x the budget of Cyrillic and ~4x of CJK; ASCII still gets that many chars.

name: _extract_item_text
doc: Measurable text from a Responses item (string/multipart/metadata), or None.

name: _input_text_parts_cost
doc: Measure only the adapter-owned text-only shape, including whitespace and empty parts.

name: _truncate_input_text_parts
doc: Copy the head of validated input_text parts without flattening their metadata.

name: _has_retainable_image_content
doc:
True for a converted Responses message with a valid ``input_image`` part (only the
adapter-owned shape counts, so empty multipart placeholders never become durable history).

name: prune_pre_checkpoint_items
arguments: items: list[dict[str, Any]], retained_user_token_budget: int=RETAINED_USER_MESSAGE_TOKEN_BUDGET, retained_summary_token_budget: int=RETAINED_SUMMARY_TOKEN_BUDGET, enable_summary_retention: bool=True, item_sources: Optional[list[Any]]=None
doc:
Restructure Responses input around the newest compaction checkpoint.

The server drops every input item preceding a replayed ``compaction`` item, erasing the
user's plaintext asks and any local-compression summary. Rebuild as::

    [checkpoint run] + [retained user & summary messages (newest-first budget)] + [post]

- The NEWEST contiguous run of checkpoints wins; relative order is preserved.
- User messages are kept verbatim within ``retained_user_token_budget``; the boundary
  message is head-truncated when it only partially fits (strings or text-only typed
  ``input_text`` parts, preserving part metadata). An oversized unsupported/mixed-content
  boundary stops older user retention rather than substituting an older ask. A recognized
  image-only user message is retained whole at one-token cost.
- Summaries are retained whole within ``retained_summary_token_budget``, never sliced
  (framing would corrupt) and never duplicated.
- ``item_sources`` (parallel to ``items``) is the raw chat message each item came from.
  Conversion can be lossy for summaries (merge-into-tail carrier → typed
  ``function_call_output``; assistant carrier shadowed by a stale replay), so a source
  that is itself a canonical summary carrier is read from the SOURCE and retained as a
  synthesized ``role="assistant"`` message.
- ``enable_summary_retention`` is a test override, not a config surface.

The server drops every input item that precedes a replayed ``compaction`` item (live-verified Aug 2026),
so sending pre-checkpoint history is dead weight AND silently erases the user's plaintext asks —
including any local-compression summary the agent already produced, which previously vanished here
because it carries ``role="assistant"``, not ``"user"`` (#90975).
A summary is never byte/character-sliced: Hermes summaries carry structural framing (handoff prefix, end
marker, merge-into-tail delimiters) that a blind slice can corrupt, so one that doesn't fit whole is
dropped instead. A summary already retained once (identical text) is never duplicated, so repeated
checkpoints stay idempotent. - ``enable_summary_retention`` is a function-level override (used by tests
and callers that need the pre-#90975 behavior back); it is not wired to a user-facing config surface.
Without ``item_sources`` (default), retention only sees what survived conversion, matching pre-#90976
behavior (#90976).

name: is_native_compaction_rejection
doc:
True when a provider error is a STRUCTURED rejection of ``context_management``.

Drives one-shot recovery (strip, disable for the session, retry), so matching is narrow:
a transient 5xx that merely ECHOES the request must not downgrade native compaction.
Requires ``status_code`` 400 (or unknown) AND the field name with rejection language.

See #82777.
* ``status_code`` is 400 (or unknown/None — some transports surface only a message string; field-name
matching alone is then the best available signal, preserving pre-#82777 behavior for them), and * the
error text names ``context_management`` / ``compact_threshold`` alongside rejection language ("unknown",
"unsupported", "invalid", "unexpected", "not permitted"...). A bare field-name echo without rejection
language does not match.

name: has_compaction_checkpoint
doc:
Does this ``codex_reasoning_items`` sidecar carry a compaction checkpoint? A checkpoint is
cumulative context living in exactly one place: rewrite/discard the sidecar only after asking.

name: merge_interim_reasoning_items
doc:
Merge ``codex_reasoning_items`` across Codex incomplete-continuation dedup.

A checkpoint on the EARLIER response is not re-emitted by the continuation, so a blind
overwrite drops the only copy: newer items win, prior checkpoints are prepended unless
the newer payload has its own.

name: _retain_summary
doc: Retain a summary whole when it fits the budget and is not a duplicate (never sliced).

name: diagnostic_process_event
doc: Early failure/monitor diagnostics, not the explicitly requested final result.

name: notification_config_snapshot
doc: Read the owning effective config once per turn (the loader already returns a fresh copy).

name: notification_policy_snapshot
doc: Bind one foreground policy for callbacks, including worker threads. ``config`` is read-only.

name: notification_turn
doc: Freeze the current turn's presentation without touching prompts or tool schemas.

name: _state_path
doc: Path to the Nous rate limit state file.

name: _parse_reset_seconds
doc: Best reset estimate (seconds from now) from hourly, per-minute, then retry-after headers.

name: record_nous_rate_limit
arguments: *, headers: Optional[Mapping[str, str]]=None, error_context: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, default_cooldown: float=300.0, anonymous: bool=False
doc:
Record that Nous Portal is rate-limited in the shared state file.

Reset time comes from ``error_context["reset_at"]`` (the 429 body's own wait), then headers, then
``default_cooldown``. The body wins: a welcome-tier refusal says when to retry (410 s), while the
hourly bucket's reset header is that window's end (about an hour) even with requests left in it.

name: nous_rate_limit_remaining
doc: Seconds remaining until reset, or None if not rate-limited (expired state is removed).

name: clear_nous_rate_limit
doc: Clear the rate limit state (e.g., after a successful Nous request).

name: _is_exhausted
doc: remaining == 0 AND a reset window long enough to be a real quota exhaustion.

name: is_genuine_nous_rate_limit
doc:
Decide whether a 429 from Nous Portal is a real account rate limit.

Nous multiplexes upstream providers behind one key, so a 429 may be one
upstream model out of capacity (clears in seconds) rather than our quota;
tripping the breaker on that would block every Nous model for minutes.
Only an exhausted bucket (remaining == 0 with reset >= 60s) in the 429's
own headers, or in the last-known-good ``RateLimitState``, is genuine.

name: is_long_welcome_rate_limit
doc:
True for a Nous welcome-tier ``rate_limited`` refusal whose reset is long enough to be an
exhausted allowance (``WELCOME_LONG_WAIT_SECONDS``), as parsed into ``error_context``
(``welcome_refusal`` from ``hermes_cli.anon_auth.parse_welcome_refusal``). Capacity refusals
(``at_capacity`` / ``admission_closed``) are never this: they are retried in place.

name: welcome_refusal_from_headers
doc:
A free-tier 429 that carried no structured ``reason``, read from its headers (else the wait
its body named) into the ``parse_welcome_refusal`` shape. Long wait or an empty bucket =
``rate_limited``; a short or unexplained one = ``at_capacity``. A missing wait stays 0 so the
breaker never trips on a guess.

name: _parse_buckets_from_headers
doc: (remaining, reset_seconds) per bucket from x-ratelimit-* headers ({} if none).

name: _has_exhausted_bucket_in_object
doc: Check a RateLimitState-like object (duck-typed; missing attrs are skipped).

name: classify_upstream
doc:
``"openrouter"`` / ``"gmi"`` / ``None`` (unknown) from a Portal response object.

Works on both wires: the OpenAI SDK object exposes ``.provider`` (OpenRouter's upstream name,
e.g. ``"Anthropic"``, ``"Amazon Bedrock"``) and an OpenRouter-minted ``.id``; the Anthropic SDK
object has ``.id`` only. GMI/Vertex responses have Anthropic-native ``msg_…`` ids and no
``provider``. Anything else is unknown, and unknown never triggers a switch.

name: wire_for_upstream
doc: The api_mode ``auto`` wants once the upstream is known. Chat unless GMI and cleared.

name: maybe_switch_wire_after_first_response
arguments: agent: Any, response: Any, api_call_count: int
doc:
Decide the session's wire from its first response; the switch itself is applied at the
start of the next iteration (``apply_pending_wire_switch``), never while a response is being
consumed. Returns True when a switch was scheduled.

Only for provider=nous, anthropic/* models, ``nous.anthropic_wire: auto``, and only on the
session's first API call.

name: apply_pending_wire_switch
doc:
At iteration start, with no response in flight: perform the switch scheduled by
``maybe_switch_wire_after_first_response``. Reuses ``switch_model`` (same model/provider, new
api_mode) so client rebuild, cache policy and ``_primary_runtime`` stay consistent. A failure
is logged and the session stays on its current wire.

name: busy_input_hint_gateway
doc: Hint shown the first time a user messages while the agent is busy (markdown).

name: busy_input_hint_cli
doc: CLI version of the busy-input hint (plain text, no markdown).

name: openclaw_residue_hint_cli
doc: Banner shown the first time Hermes finds ``~/.openclaw/``: migrate first, cleanup (which breaks OpenClaw) after.

name: detect_openclaw_residue
doc: True if ``$HOME/.openclaw`` is a directory (``home`` override for tests).

name: profile_build_mode
doc:
``config.onboarding.profile_build``: ``"off"`` never offers; anything else -> ``"ask"``.

Only governs whether the offer is made; lookups inside the flow are
consented to separately in conversation.

name: first_contact_turn_note
arguments: config: Mapping[str, Any], config_path: Path, *, session_history_empty: bool, install_has_prior_sessions: bool, onboarding_run_active: bool=False
doc:
Return a one-shot sidecar note for the install's first-ever message.

Matches the gateway first-contact path: when ``profile_build`` is ``ask``
and the offer has not been latched yet, return the opt-in profile-build
directive and persist ``onboarding.seen.profile_build_offered``. Otherwise
return the plain intro note. Returns ``None`` when this is not the first
contact (non-empty session history or prior sessions exist on the install).
``onboarding_run_active``: the chat is running first-run onboarding, whose opening replaces this note.

name: profile_build_directive
doc:
System-note directive appended to the very first message ever.

Short opt-in profile-build flow persisting to the user-profile memory store;
phrased so the agent ASKS before any lookup and never silently reads
connected accounts.

name: is_seen
doc: True if the user has already been shown this first-touch hint.

name: mark_seen
doc: Persist ``onboarding.seen.<flag> = True`` atomically; False on any error (best-effort).

name: read_facts
doc: ``locale``: the desktop's UI language, preferred over the backend OS locale for wording.

name: suggested_name
doc:
The OS account's real name for the name card. It goes to the card only: the model sees it
when the user picks it.

name: eligible_tasks
doc: The rows the model may pick from on this machine and run, in catalog order.

name: card_options
doc: The build card: the model's picks as given, then the fixed row.

name: _option_error
arguments: option: Any, eligible: set[str], seen: set[str]

name: pick_error
arguments: options: Any, facts: Facts, picks: Mapping[str, Any]
doc: Why the model's build picks are refused, naming the eligible ids; None when they are valid.

name: task_skills
arguments: option: str, resolve_skill: Callable[[str], str | None]
doc:
The skills a task loads first, humanizer last, each by the name ``skill_view`` loads it with here:
``resolve_skill`` maps a written name to that name (a plugin skill's registered name differs from
its ``<plugin>:<skill>`` form), or to None for a skill missing here, which is dropped.

name: build_values
doc: Ids the build beat accepts: what its card showed, plus a task they named in words.

name: new_record
arguments: facts: Facts, *, now: float=0.0, run_id: str=''

name: next_beat
doc: The first beat still pending or shown; None when every beat is settled.

name: _settle
arguments: record: dict, beat: str, patch: Mapping[str, Any]

name: _build_picks_error
arguments: record: dict, event: Shown, facts: Facts
doc: Stores the model's build picks; a bring-back without picks reuses the ones already on the card.

name: _shown
arguments: record: dict, event: Shown, facts: Facts, now: float

name: valid_answer
arguments: beat: str, answer: Mapping[str, Any], facts: Facts, picks: Mapping[str, Any]
doc:
A card answer carries only its beat's pick keys, with ids from the card's own options. ``label``
is the text the card showed, kept for the transcript and never recorded.

name: _answered
arguments: record: dict, event: Answered, facts: Facts, now: float

name: _note_present
arguments: record: dict, event: Wrote | TimedOut | Recorded | Skipped
doc: Record the beat's picks as the machine has them now; returns them for the result.

name: _wrote
arguments: record: dict, event: Wrote, facts: Facts, now: float

name: _timed_out
arguments: record: dict, event: TimedOut, facts: Facts, now: float

name: _recorded
arguments: record: dict, event: Recorded, facts: Facts, now: float

name: _skipped
arguments: record: dict, event: Skipped, facts: Facts, now: float

name: _end
arguments: record: dict, event: End, facts: Facts, now: float

name: _done
arguments: record: dict, event: Done, facts: Facts, now: float

name: _applied_beats
doc: The beats a general tool's result settles, with the picks it recorded.

name: _applied
arguments: record: dict, event: Applied, facts: Facts, now: float
doc:
The reminder names the last beat this result newly settled, so the model moves on instead of
recording it again with setup_beat. ``after_<beat>``, not ``Beat.after``: the tour already started.
A repeat apply of a theme or layout already settled gets ``already_<beat>``, so it stops re-applying.

name: _ended
doc:
An ended run ignores general tool results and refuses setup_beat, except a repeat of its own
end: done on a completed run and any end on an ended run answer as if they had ended it.

name: apply
arguments: record: Mapping[str, Any], event: Event, facts: Facts, *, now: float=0.0
doc:
The record after ``event``, the model-facing result, and the reminder key. The run completes
when the build beat settles: the answer to the first-task card ends onboarding.

name: applies_to
doc: Whether a general tool's result can settle a beat (the hook's cheap pre-check).

name: after
doc: Reminder key for the result that settles this beat.

name: _announce
arguments: run_id: str | None, session_id: str, outcome: str

name: _transition
doc:
Apply *event* and write the result in one database transaction at the compression tip, so Skip
setup pressed while a card answer is being applied is never overwritten by the older copy, and an id
read before a rotation published still lands on the copy the chat reads. An ended run then closes the
install flag (a Skip or Done retried after a failed config write repairs it), unless another run
is still open: the flag belongs to that run, and an old chat must not end it.

name: start
doc:
Write a fresh run record (the row must exist) and mark the install as mid-onboarding, so a
crash or a quit before the end runs onboarding again on the next launch (which starts over:
``onboarding.start`` with ``fresh_launch``).

name: advance
doc: Apply one event to the stored run; LookupError when this session has no run.

name: open_session_ids
doc:
The chats whose run is still in progress, newest first. Rotation leaves the active copy on the
compression parent, so each id is read at its compression tip.

name: delete_chat
arguments: db, session_id: str, delete: Callable[[], bool]
doc:
Run *delete*; when it removed the chat holding the live run, end that run (``deleted``) on every
compression copy and tell windows once. Only the compression tip holds the live run, so deleting an
older copy ends nothing. The install flag closes before the delete when no other run is open: a
failed flag write keeps the chat for a retry, and a refused delete sets the flag again.

name: observe_tool_result
arguments: agent, name: str, args: Mapping[str, Any], result: Any
doc:
Settle a beat from a general tool's result (``set_theme``, ``manage_connections`` display,
``gui_tour``). Runs for every tool result; only an onboarding chat (one whose agent carries
``setup_beat``) reads its record. Returns *result*, with the next-step reminder added when it
settled a beat.

name: keeps_toolsets
doc: An explicit empty list is a zero-tool chat; None is unrestricted and still gets the fold-in.

name: with_onboarding
doc:
*enabled* plus onboarding. None (every toolset outside the session-gated ones, which onboarding
is) is spelled out by name: the agent's other toolset gates read the names, as they read None.

name: onboarding_toolsets
doc:
*enabled* plus ``onboarding`` for a chat whose run is in progress. Decided once, at agent build:
the tool array is part of the cached prefix, so a finished run keeps setup_beat (as a refusal)
until the session is rebuilt.

name: onboarding_chat_toolsets
doc:
The session authority's per-turn fold-in: *enabled* plus ``onboarding`` for a chat that is or was
an onboarding chat. Keyed on the record existing, never on the run being open, because the
authority resolves toolsets every turn and the tool array is part of the cached prefix: a run that
ends must not change it mid-conversation (setup_beat answers a finished run with a refusal).

name: carry_onboarding_toolset
doc: A tool refresh keeps the onboarding toolset the agent was built with.

name: onboarding_prelude
doc:
The opening's scripted step, greeting and name card, while the name beat was never shown. A
greeting already in the chat (a relaunch) is not said twice.

name: onboarding_turn_note
doc:
Before a user turn in the onboarding chat, while no card waits: which card is closed and how to
bring it back.

name: ui_language
doc:
A locale (``zh-hant``, ``de-DE``, ``zh_TW``) as the desktop language it reads in; English when
none fits.

name: question
doc: The card's own question; the name card asks in the user's language.

name: opening_prompt
doc: The hidden first turn of the onboarding chat: every rule of the run.

name: _preview_line
doc: Every host shows results in the app's preview pane, which watches a local file but not a remote one.

name: _task_prompt
arguments: option: str, label: str, resolve_skill: Callable[[str], str | None]

name: build_guidance
arguments: option: str, facts: Facts, resolve_skill: Callable[[str], str | None]=lambda name: name, label: str=''
doc:
The prompt once a first task is picked; ``label`` is the card text they clicked, ``resolve_skill``
names a skill as this install loads it (None: missing here).

name: _build_menu
doc: The rows the model picks the build card from.

name: _already
doc: A repeat apply of a settled beat: steer the model forward instead of drawing another receipt.

name: reminder
arguments: key: str, record: Mapping[str, Any], facts: Facts, beat: str | None=None, resolve_skill: Callable[[str], str | None]=lambda name: name
doc:
The text for a reminder key; ``beat`` names the card a ``wrote`` / ``timed_out`` result is about;
``resolve_skill`` names a first task's skill as this install loads it, None dropping a missing one.

name: turn_note
doc:
The note on a user turn while no card waits: which card is closed, how their message applies it
when it answers it, and how to bring it back. Empty once every card is settled: the build is under
way and nothing is left to reopen.

name: render_template
doc: Resolve a registered template into (instructions, user_input); KeyError if unknown.

name: run_oneshot
arguments: *, instructions: str='', user_input: str='', template: Optional[str]=None, variables: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, task: str='title_generation', max_tokens: int=1024, temperature: Optional[float]=0.3, timeout: float=60.0, main_runtime: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Run a single stateless LLM request and return its text (fence-stripped).

Raises RuntimeError when no provider is configured (from :func:`call_llm`),
KeyError for an unknown template, ValueError when the prompt is empty.

name: _strip_code_fence
doc: Drop a single wrapping ``` fence the model may have added.

name: is_single_query_session
doc:
The finite ``-q`` marker, read through the session env so gateway-bound sessions never see it.

A gateway-owned ``chat -q`` / ``-z`` session never has that env (only the client process set it): its
one-shot fact is the frozen launch policy's ``oneshot`` source, a property of the SESSION, not of one
admission, so the cached agent's tools[] and system prompt stay byte-stable across its turns.

name: prune_oneshot_tools
doc: *tools* minus ``ONESHOT_HIDDEN_TOOLS``; identity when the session is not one-shot.

name: opencode_transport
arguments: provider: Optional[str], model: Optional[str], base_url: Optional[str]
doc:
``(api_mode, base_url)`` re-derived per model for an OpenCode relay target; ``(None, base_url)`` otherwise.

OpenCode Zen/Go serve Responses-only (``gpt-*``, ``grok-*``, ``muse-spark``), Anthropic-wire
(``minimax-*``, ``qwen*``, ``claude-*``) and chat/completions models behind one provider, so a
provider-level or persisted ``api_mode`` is wrong for every model but the one it was saved for.
The main runtime (``hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py``) always re-derives from the effective model;
auxiliary resolution must agree or ``gpt-5.6-luna`` compression 500s on /chat/completions (#98799).
Built-in families, custom entries named after one (``opencode-go-bridge``, #85589) and opencode.ai
hosts all count.

name: is_opencode_target
doc:
True when *provider* or *base_url* addresses the OpenCode relay.

Matches the built-in opencode-zen/go providers, custom
``opencode-<family>-*`` providers, and any base_url hosted on opencode.ai.

name: resolve_affinity_key
doc: Return the normalized rotation-stable conversation affinity key ("" when unknown).

name: opencode_session_headers
arguments: provider: Optional[str], base_url: Optional[str], session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Return ``{"x-opencode-session": <key>}`` for OpenCode targets, else ``{}``.

OpenCode targets always get a key: when no conversation/session key resolves, an
ephemeral ``oneshot-<hex>`` value is generated (OpenCode Go rejects requests without
the header, #105841).

name: custom_provider_session_affinity_headers
doc: Return ``{<session_affinity_header>: <key>}`` when the route's provider entry declares one, else ``{}``.

name: merge_session_affinity_headers
arguments: kwargs: dict[str, Any], provider: Optional[str], base_url: Optional[str], session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Merge the affinity header(s) into ``kwargs["extra_headers"]`` (in place).

Existing per-request headers win, so a caller-pinned value is preserved.
Targets with neither source configured are left untouched.

name: register_from_config
doc:
Register every configured outbound webhook on the plugin manager.  Malformed ``hooks.outbound``
means zero targets — never raises.  Returns the targets that ended up wired (deduplicated).

name: iter_configured_targets
doc: Parse ``hooks.outbound`` without registering anything (``hermes hooks list``).

name: flush
doc: Block until all queued deliveries are done (or *timeout* elapses); True if drained.

name: re_register_config_hooks
doc:
Re-register outbound webhooks after a plugin force-reload cleared ``_hooks``.  Only the
current home's idempotence keys are cleared so a force-reload in one profile cannot
invalidate another profile's still-live registration.

Mirrors ``agent.shell_hooks.re_register_config_hooks``: config-owned outbound-webhook callbacks live in
the same ``_hooks`` dict that ``PluginManager.discover_and_load(force=True)`` clears via ``unload()``,
so without this the force-reloaded profile's outbound webhooks go silently inert (#92682 review).

name: reset_for_tests
doc: Clear the idempotence set and drain the queue.  Test-only helper.

name: _make_callback
doc: Build the notify-only closure ``invoke_hook()`` calls per firing.

name: _serialize_payload
arguments: event: str, kwargs: dict[str, Any], delivery_id: str
doc:
Render the POST body: shell-hooks stdin shape plus delivery metadata.  ``delivery_id``
(also the ``X-Hermes-Delivery`` header) and ``timestamp`` live inside the HMAC-signed
body, so they double as replay protection.

name: _build_delivery
arguments: event: str, target: WebhookTarget, body: bytes, delivery_id: str

name: _deliver
doc: POST with bounded retries: retry on connection errors and 5xx; 4xx and 3xx are final.

name: redirect_request
arguments: self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl

name: schedule
doc: Run ``fn()`` every ``interval`` seconds via the shared scheduler.

name: __init__
arguments: self, scheduler: PeriodicScheduler, fn: Callable[[], object], interval: float

name: cancel
doc:
Stop future runs.  ``wait`` (seconds) additionally blocks until an
in-flight run of this callback finishes — the analogue of
``thread.join(timeout=wait)`` on the old per-child thread.

name: schedule
arguments: self, fn: Callable[[], object], interval: float

name: _dispatch
doc:
Start ``handle``'s body on its own worker.  Called with ``_cond`` held
so ``cancel`` can never observe a half-set runner.

name: _requeue
doc: Push ``handle``'s next due time (``_cond`` held).

name: persisted_turn_receipt
arguments: messages: Any, start: Any, history: list, raw: Any, status: str, *, compression_unchanged: bool, prefix_row_matches: Callable[[Any, Any], bool]
doc:
Report committed row addresses, never a text/timestamp search for a matching turn.

``start`` is the agent's persistence cursor (``_persist_user_message_idx``), re-anchored during
compaction. A partial receipt can address its surviving rows, but cannot retire a client's
entire streamed turn. Full coverage additionally requires the unchanged pre-turn prefix
(``prefix_row_matches(history_row, turn_row)`` for every row before ``start``), no compaction
and no redirected user boundary.

name: cached_pricing
doc:
The calling profile's own cached Nous catalog (never fetches); ``base_url`` is not needed for it. Only
the profile-keyed read: a process serving several profiles holds their catalogs side by side, and a
usage level (Large / Free) is per plan, so another profile's catalog must never answer.

name: is_free
doc: $0 to the plan: a ``:free`` id or a row the catalog lists as free.

name: is_top_tier
doc:
The gateway marks the model top tier (``usage_level: top_tier``, or an older gateway's ``top_tier:
true``), read by the same rule as the picker tags. Unmarked or no catalog: not top tier.

name: blocking_gauge
arguments: model: str, gauges: Iterable[Any], *, free: bool, top_tier: bool
doc:
The full gauge that stops *model*, or None while it still has included room. Free models are
never blocked. Of several full gauges, the one that frees up last (that is when the model works).

name: current_model_is_top_tier
doc:
*agent*'s current model is top tier, by its own profile's cached catalog (see :func:`is_top_tier`), or
None when the catalog has no row for it (cold, or its 300 s cache lapsed): the tier is unknown.

name: is_blocked
arguments: model: str, gauges: Iterable[Any], pricing: Optional[dict]

name: _portal_free_models
doc:
The Portal's free picks, from what this profile already holds for its own Portal (in-process,
else its last copy on disk). Never fetches: this runs mid-turn.

name: _fits_context
arguments: model: str, needed_tokens: Optional[int], base_url: str

name: suggest_models
arguments: current_model: str, gauges: Iterable[Any], *, pricing: Optional[dict]=None, featured: Iterable[str]=(), needed_tokens: Optional[int]=None, base_url: str='', limit: int=_MAX_SUGGESTIONS
doc:
The plan's recommended models (in order) that the full gauges do not block, then the Portal's free picks.
Never the current model, only a model whose context window holds the conversation.

name: credits_action
doc:
The credits step past a limit; every surface's copy reads this one rule. With Keep going on credits
off, the gateway refuses whatever the balance, so a balance alone is not enough and neither is the
setting alone: off with no balance needs both steps. An unknown balance counts as none.

name: credits_option
doc:
How credits could carry on past the limit (see :func:`credits_action`). None while paused (a card
update restores included usage; the paused copy says so).

name: limit_hit
arguments: agent: Any, *, message: str, needed_tokens: Optional[int]=None
doc:
After a usage-window 402: which limit stopped *agent*'s current model, when it resets, and what to
offer. None when the state names no full gauge for this model (a paused plan, a stale snapshot).

name: portal_wording
doc: A refusal line for a surface without ``/topup`` (messaging): point its credits steps at the Portal.

name: chat_refusal_wording
doc:
A refusal sent to a chat: credits steps point at the Portal (:func:`portal_wording`), and the reset
reads as a duration ("resets in 3h"), since the gateway's clock is not the reader's time zone.

name: suggestion_phrase
doc: ``Model A (free)``.

name: next_steps_text
arguments: hit: LimitHit, *, model_command: str='/model', topup_command: Optional[str]='/topup', portal: bool=False
doc:
One line on how to keep going, for a surface without buttons. ``model_command`` is the platform's
own spelling (e.g. ``!model``). ``portal``: point at the Portal for credits (messaging),
instead of a command that would spend from the chat.

name: limit_next_steps_from_payload
arguments: limit: dict, *, model_command: str='/model', topup_command: Optional[str]='/topup', portal: bool=False, markup: bool=False
doc:
:func:`next_steps_text` for a :meth:`LimitHit.to_payload` dict (what the result carries). ``markup``
bolds the commands for a Rich panel.

name: build_plan_prompt
doc:
Build the plan-mode prompt; empty *task* asks the agent to infer it from conversation context.

See #36821.

name: _snapshot_full_ids
doc: Ids of the full allowances in the cached snapshot; None when it has no window plan.

name: plan_snapshot_is_stale
doc:
True when a reply's credits state contradicts the cached snapshot in a way a picker shows:
window headers but a non-window snapshot (upgrade), the reverse (downgrade or cancel), or a
different set of full allowances (a limit filled or reset). No snapshot yet: nothing to fix (the
session-start seed is fetching it).

name: sync_plan_snapshot
doc:
Start one background refresh when *state* (a fresh ``CreditsState`` from reply headers) says the
cached plan is out of date. Returns True iff a refresh started. Never raises, never blocks.

name: queue_plugin_notice
arguments: agent: Any, plugin_key: str, note: str
doc: Queue ``note`` for ``agent``'s next tool result or user turn; it replaces this plugin's older one.

name: pop_plugin_notices
doc: Every queued notice, oldest plugin first, and clear the queue.

name: attach_to_tool_message
doc:
Append every queued notice to ``message``, the tool result about to be appended and flushed. It
goes after the content, so a result wrapped as untrusted data keeps the notice outside the wrapper.

name: keep_after_turn_budget
doc:
Put a notice back on a batch row whose content the turn budget spilled to a file: the inline
preview keeps only the head, and the notice sits at the tail. The flushed row already holds it.

name: _coerce_allowlist
doc:
YAML list → ``(frozenset_or_None, allow_any)``. A ``"*"`` entry sets
``allow_any``; missing / non-list → ``(None, False)`` = no allowlist.

name: _resolve_trust_policy
doc:
Read ``plugins.entries.<plugin_id>.llm`` from config.yaml (missing → fully
restrictive). Resolved per call so config edits apply without a restart.

name: _denied
arguments: plugin_id: str, what: str, flag: str

name: _gate_ref_override
doc: Gate a ``provider`` / ``model`` override: trust flag, then optional allowlist.

name: _check_overrides
arguments: policy: _TrustPolicy, *, requested_provider: Optional[str], requested_model: Optional[str], requested_agent_id: Optional[str], requested_profile: Optional[str]
doc:
Gate each override independently, in the order provider, model, agent_id,
profile. Returns ``(provider, model, agent_id, profile)`` (agent_id unstripped).

name: _resolve_task_ownership
doc:
``(owned_keys, builtin_keys)`` for the task trust gate.

Imports are lazy (circular import at plugin discovery); an unreadable registry
yields empty sets, failing the gate closed. Ownership matches on the canonical id
``ctx.llm`` is bound to (``manifest.key or manifest.name``), which is what
``register_auxiliary_task`` stores as the entry's ``plugin``.

name: _check_task
doc:
Validate a plugin's requested auxiliary ``task`` key.

unset / ``""`` / ``"auto"`` → ``None`` (main-model path); a key the plugin
registered itself → allowed; a built-in key → only with ``allow_task_override``;
anything else raises + logs. Never silently downgraded to ``auto``: that would
mask the misconfiguration and could route to a main model the user steered
elsewhere on purpose.

A foreign/unknown key raises :class:`PluginLlmTrustError` and logs a warning naming the offending plugin
and key. See #64174, #64182.

Publish the active conversation id for ambient Portal tagging; returns the token.

doc:
``conversation=<session_id>`` — high-cardinality, so only appended when a

Fresh list of the canonical Nous Portal tags.

The ambient conversation context (lineage ROOT id) wins over the explicit
``session_id``, a fallback for callers outside any agent turn.

name: _build_primary_runtime_snapshot
doc: The ``_primary_runtime`` record that persists a switch across turns.

name: _enable_happy_eyeballs
doc:
Install the racing backend on one httpx transport.

Reaches into private ``transport._pool._network_backend`` (httpcore pinned
1.0.x); hasattr-guarded so an incompatible httpcore degrades to the default
serial backend. Pools of ``skip_pool_types`` (proxies) are left alone.

name: enable_happy_eyeballs_on_client
doc:
Install the racing backend on every direct transport of a ready-built httpx.Client.

For callers that build clients inline (Codex OAuth/device-login). Proxy-backed
pools are skipped (TCP connect goes to the proxy host); async clients need
nothing (anyio already races per RFC 8305). Best-effort.

Proxy-backed transports (``httpcore.HTTPProxy`` / SOCKS pools) are left untouched: with a proxy in play
the TCP connect goes to the proxy host, which is out of scope for the direct-transport racing added in
#94388. Async clients are also left untouched — httpcore's async backend already performs RFC 8305
racing natively via ``anyio.connect_tcp(happy_eyeballs_delay=0.25)``.

name: _load_openai_cls
doc: Import and cache ``openai.OpenAI``.

name: _get_proxy_from_env
doc: First configured proxy URL from HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / ALL_PROXY (any case), or None.

name: _get_proxy_for_base_url
doc:
Env-configured proxy unless NO_PROXY excludes this base URL (same matcher as the
gateway adapters: CIDR, ``*.`` wildcards and host:port entries all count).

name: _shared_transport_cls
doc: Lazily define the per-client transport view (httpx import is deferred).

name: _shared_transport_key
arguments: base_url: str, verify: Any, proxy: Optional[str]
doc: Identity under which sync direct transports are pooled process-wide.

name: close_shared_transports
doc: Really close every process-shared transport (test teardown / atexit).

name: build_keepalive_http_client
arguments: base_url: str='', *, async_mode: bool=False, verify: Any=True
doc:
httpx client for OpenAI SDK calls with env-only proxy policy (None on failure).

Explicit no-proxy mounts disable httpx's ``trust_env`` path so macOS system
proxies (which omit the ExceptionsList) are never applied. ``keepalive_expiry``
reaps idle connections before reverse proxies' 30-60 s timeouts (a custom
socket_options transport broke streaming and stripped TCP_NODELAY). ``verify``
goes on the client AND the mounts, since a mounted transport owns its SSL context.

Every call returns a NEW ``httpx.Client`` (per-client close semantics), but sync clients
with the same (verify, proxy, happy-eyeballs) identity mount the SAME underlying
``HTTPTransport`` through a ``_SharedTransport`` view, so N delegated children share one
connection pool + SSL context. Async clients are never shared: an httpcore async pool is
bound to the event loop that first used it. Proxy-backed clients keep httpx's own transport.

See #12952, #54049.
See #10933.

name: _install_safe_stdio
doc: Wrap stdout/stderr so best-effort console output cannot crash the agent.

name: connect_tcp
arguments: self, host: str, port: int, timeout: Optional[float]=None, local_address: Optional[str]=None, socket_options=None

name: _get_context_file_read_timeout
doc: ``context_file_read_timeout`` from config.yaml, else the 5s default.

name: _read_text_with_timeout
arguments: path: Path, timeout: Optional[float]=None, encoding: str='utf-8-sig'
doc:
``path.read_text()`` on a daemon thread so a slow file can't stall startup.

Returns the text, or ``None`` after *timeout* seconds (logged at WARNING;
the orphaned reader thread finishes on its own). Read errors propagate to
the caller exactly as a direct ``read_text`` would, so existing
``try/except`` handling at each site is unchanged.

name: _scan_context_content
arguments: content: str, filename: str, *, user_authored: bool=False
doc:
Scan a context file (AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, SOUL.md) for injection; matches are BLOCKED.

"context" scope only (strict-scope SSH-backdoor/persistence/exfil patterns are too aggressive for a
cloned repo's docs); blocking, not warning, because the file would otherwise enter the prompt verbatim.

*user_authored* (SOUL.md in the user's own HERMES_HOME): a hit is WARNED and the file still loads.
SOUL.md sits in the same trust class as config.yaml — file-tool writes to it go through the
protected-instruction approval gate (``tools/file_tools_write_guards.py``) and project checkouts never
supply it — so a user who *documents* "ignore previous instructions" in their security guidance
must not lose their whole identity file to a one-line log entry (#112570). Project-dir files
(repo AGENTS.md / .cursorrules / .hermes.md) arrive with the checkout and keep blocking, and so does
a SOUL.md owned by a profile distribution (``hermes profile install <git-url>`` copies it in unscanned;
``load_soul_md`` passes ``user_authored=False`` when ``distribution.yaml`` owns the file).

name: _find_git_root
doc: Nearest ancestor (or *start* itself) containing ``.git``, else None.

name: _find_hermes_md
doc: Nearest ``.hermes.md`` / ``HERMES.md`` from *cwd* up to the git root, else None.

doc: Drop optional ``---`` YAML frontmatter so only the markdown body is injected.

name: build_memory_guidance
arguments: memory_enabled: bool=True, profile_enabled: bool=True, *, skill_manage_available: bool=True
doc: Adapt store and skill-write guidance without widening what belongs in memory.

name: execution_guidance_text
doc:
OPENAI_MODEL_EXECUTION_GUIDANCE for the session's toolset (cache-safe: the toolset is fixed per session).

Lines that tell the model to reach for a tool absent from the session's toolset would dangle, so they are
dropped.

name: format_steer_marker
doc: Wrap a mid-turn steer in the self-describing marker (see note above).

name: steer_user_row
doc:
The standalone ``role:user`` row a mid-turn /steer is delivered as (after the newest tool
result). Its own row — never smeared onto the already-persisted tool row, which append-only
persistence would leave divergent from the live request — and typed so the alternation repair
never merges the next real prompt into it and history renderers can label it.

name: hud_surface_note
arguments: valid_tool_names: set[str] | None=None, deferred_tool_names: frozenset[str] | set[str]=frozenset()
doc:
Per-turn note for a message typed into the desktop's floating HUD ("this"/"here" = the app behind it).

A per-turn fact, not a platform (one session alternates between app window and HUD), so it rides the
model-bound message, never the byte-stable system prompt. Each sentence is gated on the tool it names (an
unknown tool name invites a hallucinated call); without read_window_below the whole note is withheld.
``deferred_tool_names`` are tools this session reaches only through the tool_call bridge (the default
tool_search defer list holds the desktop tools): they count as available, and the note says to invoke
them via tool_call, since a direct call to a deferred name is rejected as an unknown tool.

name: _plugin_backend_attr
doc: *attr* of a plugin-registered terminal backend, fail-soft (unknown backend / raising plugin -> *default*).

name: _plugin_backend_is_remote
doc: Whether a plugin-registered terminal backend runs commands remotely (unknown names are local).

name: _windows_marketing_version
doc:
"10"/"11" (``platform.release()`` says 10 for both; 11 is build >= 22000).

``platform.release()`` reports the kernel version, which is ``10`` for BOTH Windows 10 and Windows 11 —
the prompt then claims "Windows (10)" on Windows 11 hosts and misleads the model about the OS (#51755).
Windows 11 is distinguished by build number: >= 22000 is 11. Falls back to ``platform.release()`` on any
lookup failure.

name: _tenv_read
doc:
Scope-aware TERMINAL_* read: the multiplexing gateway's per-turn scope carries
the active profile's settings (raw os.getenv could read a previous profile's value).
Only an import failure falls back — an active refusal scope must raise.

name: _format_backend_probe

name: _clear_backend_probe_cache
doc: Test helper — drop the backend probe cache so monkeypatched backends take effect.

name: _local_host_hints
doc: Host OS / home / cwd block for a local terminal backend (tools run on this host).

arguments: running: bool, display: str | None, holder: str

The one-line Bot Screen status the model sees — the prompt's ``_bot_screen_hint`` body,
parameterised so the display watcher can stage the same sentence as a per-turn note when a
screen starts or stops mid-session (#125830; the byte-stable prompt only converges at
compaction). ``holder`` is ``lease.AGENT``/``lease.HUMAN``; "" when there is nothing to say
(a stop with no display known, or an unknown holder on a running screen).

name: _bot_screen_hint
doc:
One line naming this profile's running Bot Screen (#125830): the display, and who holds it.

Pure reads (``published_env`` + the lease file); never raises — a missing/unimportable
bot_desktop module or an unreadable lease must not break prompt construction. ``""`` when
no screen is running, so the block simply drops out of the environment hints.

doc: Backend-only block for remote/sandbox backends (host info deliberately suppressed).

name: _config_readonly

name: _embedder_environment_hint

Embedder-supplied environment description: HERMES_ENVIRONMENT_HINT (container ENV)
wins over config.yaml ``agent.environment_hint``. Read once at prompt-build time.

doc:
Execution-environment block: local backends get host OS/home/cwd; remote/sandbox
backends get ONLY the backend's own state (the agent's tools cannot touch the host).
WSL and embedder hints are appended.

doc: Context-file truncation limit: explicit config.yaml ``context_file_max_chars`` wins, else the dynamic cap.

doc: Serialisable metadata dict for one skill.

doc: Read a SKILL.md once -> (is_compatible, frontmatter, description); errors yield (True, {}, "").

name: _skill_should_show
arguments: conditions: dict, available_tools: set[str] | None, available_toolsets: set[str] | None, session_platform: str | None=None
doc: False if the skill's conditional activation rules exclude it.

name: _plugin_skill_prompt_rows
arguments: disabled: set[str], available_tools: set[str] | None, available_toolsets: set[str] | None, session_platform: str | None
doc:
``(qualified_name, description)`` for every skill registered by an ENABLED plugin
(``ctx.register_skill``), filtered through the same offer-time gates as on-disk skills.
Plugin skills live in the plugin-manager registry — never under the profile skills tree —
so the disk scans above cannot see them; this is their one path into ``<available_skills>``.
The qualified ``plugin:skill`` name is exactly what ``skill_view`` resolves, and disabling
or unloading a plugin removes its registry entries, so enablement gating is inherent.

name: _current_session_platform_hint
doc: Active platform without importing the gateway package on CLI startup.

Compact skill index for the system prompt.

Same-named skills resolve like skill_view: project > local > create_dir > external_dirs, and a
same-tier duplicate is listed under its exact relative path (``agent.skill_utils.resolve_skill_catalog``).
``compact_categories`` (coding posture) demotes categories to a names-only line — nothing is ever hidden.
``skills_dir_override`` makes home resolution EXPLICIT: a build thread that never bound the HERMES_HOME
ContextVar would otherwise leak the default profile's skills into a bot's prompt.
