thread costs it nothing; the context is copied so session-scoped state survives the hop, and errors
re-raise here. Async code awaits ``asyncio.to_thread`` instead.

name: __init__
arguments: self, rpc, scope, outbox_dir, adopted=None, *, max_bytes=4 * 1024 * 1024

name: _reconcile_adopted
doc:
Carry a retained outbox across verified owner replacement.

``adopted`` is the separately authenticated ``worker.adopt`` result for the requested
scope; never self-adopt. Only the owner epoch (forward) and the physical target may
differ from the journal (a same-epoch restart can still find the target rotated).
Pending entries replay under the journal's own target with the adopted epoch, so an
exact lost-ACK retry resolves its original receipt instead of creating a second one;
the constructor then requires the replayed scope to equal the adopted one.

name: adopt
doc: Install only a separately verified worker.adopt result; never self-adopt.

name: append_messages_batch
arguments: self, session_id, messages, compression_lock_holder=None, turn_lease_holder=None, chunk_rows=None, turn_lease_ttl_seconds=300.0

name: acquire_session_turn_lease
arguments: self, session_id, holder, *, ttl_seconds=300.0, wait_seconds=1800.0, poll_interval_seconds=1.0, on_wait=None, wait_notice_interval_seconds=15.0, should_abort=None, acquire_patience_s=0.5, on_contended=None

name: _bind_safe_worker_policy
arguments: *, safe_mode: bool, ignore_user_config: bool, config: dict
doc: Called by the private worker bootstrap, never by the owner or public CLI.

name: _bind_worker_config
doc:
An ordinary managed worker's frozen session config: every config reader returns it (the
session never follows later profile edits), while plugins, MCP, hooks and providers load as
usual — ``safe_worker_enabled()`` stays False. Same one-shot, pre-import rules as bypass.

name: _bind
arguments: safe_mode: bool, ignore_user_config: bool, config: dict

name: worker_config_snapshot
doc: Return detached explicit config; None means the ordinary loader owns it.

name: _is_plain_json_data
doc: True when ``value`` is purely JSON wire types; pydantic models / generators must keep the typed SDK path.

name: bypass_sdk_request_transform
arguments: request_kwargs: dict, fields: tuple[str, ...]=RESPONSES_BYPASS_FIELDS, *, keep_slots: bool=False
doc:
Move wire-format bulk ``fields`` into ``extra_body``.

Returns ``request_kwargs`` itself when nothing is safe to move, so callers use
the result unconditionally. ``keep_slots`` leaves an empty-list placeholder in
the typed kwargs for each moved field: it satisfies ``@required_args``
(``messages`` on chat.completions) and keeps the field's position in the JSON
body, so the bytes — and therefore any byte-keyed prompt cache — are unchanged.

name: bypass_chat_sdk_request_transform
doc:
Chat-completions bypass, gated on the real OpenAI SDK.

Only the SDK performs the transform and only the SDK merges ``extra_body``
afterwards. Hermes also drives chat-shaped facades that are NOT the SDK (the
in-process MoA aggregator, test stand-ins); handing those an ``extra_body`` they
never merge would silently send an empty conversation.

name: set_multiplex_active
doc:
Mark whether the process is a profile multiplexer (get_secret fails closed).

Activation also pins the launch home for routed-profile decisions
(``hermes_constants.pin_process_hermes_home``) unless an embedding host already pinned one:
from here on "is this task routed" compares the override against the home the process was
launched with, not against whatever a host later mirrors into ``os.environ["HERMES_HOME"]``.
Deactivation releases only the pin activation itself created — a transient toggle
(``gateway_migrate._multiplex_read_mode``, a cron worker restoring the caller's mode) must not
drop the host's explicit pin (#119242).

name: set_multiplex_context
doc:
Run the current task under multiplex semantics regardless of the process flag.
Returns a reset token; pair with :func:`reset_multiplex_context` in a ``finally``.

name: is_multiplex_active
doc: True in a multiplexing process, or for a task running under multiplex semantics.

name: serves_routed_profile
doc:
True when the current task runs for a profile other than the process's own: always under
multiplexing, else when a HERMES_HOME override names another home (dashboard/desktop backend,
per-profile cron ticker) or a secret scope stamped with a foreign home is bound. The MCP
registry scope and the check_fn cache key both follow this predicate so a served profile's
view never aliases the launch profile's (#111151). A host that mirrors the turn's profile into
``HERMES_HOME`` pins its own home with ``hermes_constants.pin_process_hermes_home`` so the
mirror cannot flip this predicate.

name: set_secret_scope
doc:
Install the active profile's secret mapping; ``None`` clears. Returns a reset token.

``profile_home`` stamps the home the mapping was built for so
``serves_routed_profile`` detects a foreign-home scope even when the binder
deliberately skips the HERMES_HOME override.

name: current_secret_scope
doc: The active secret mapping, or None when no scope is installed.

name: current_secret_scope_home
doc: The home the active scope was stamped with, or None when unstamped/unbound.

name: _is_global_env
doc: True for genuinely process-global (non-profile-secret) env vars.

name: get_secret
doc:
Resolve a credential by env-var name, honoring the active profile scope.

Global vars always read ``os.environ``. With a scope installed, a miss returns
``default`` under multiplexing (never another profile's ``os.environ`` value)
but falls through to ``os.environ`` otherwise — single-profile deployments
inject credentials via the process env (systemd, ``op run``), so the scope
must stay a ``.env`` overlay, not a blindfold (otherwise cron 401s). With no
scope: multiplex INACTIVE reads ``os.environ``; ACTIVE raises (fail closed).

name: get_secret_str
doc:
``get_secret`` for callers that want a ``str``: ``default`` only when the secret is genuinely
unset. Still raises ``UnscopedSecretError`` — swallowing it hides a spawn-site bug.

name: _strip_inline_comment
doc:
Strip a dotenv-style inline comment (python-dotenv semantics): quoted values
scan to the matching close quote (backslash-aware for double quotes) and drop a
trailing ``# ...``, else stay untouched; unquoted values truncate only at a
``#`` PRECEDED BY WHITESPACE (``foo#bar`` survives, ``value # c`` → ``value``).

name: _parse_env_value
doc:
Parse the small .env value subset Hermes writes itself (bare, 'single', or "double" with
``\"`` / ``\\`` escapes).

name: invalidate_env_file_cache
doc: Drop one path from the ``load_env_file()`` memo, or all of them.

name: _decode_env_bytes
doc:
BOM stripped; invalid UTF-8 falls back to latin-1 exactly as
``env_loader._load_dotenv_with_fallback`` installs it into ``os.environ``.

name: _parse_env_text
doc: Tokenize already-read ``.env`` text. See :func:`load_env_file`.

name: load_env_file
doc:
THE ``.env`` tokenizer: every reader (profile scope, ``hermes_cli.config.load_env``, the dashboard
scrub, skill secret capture, managed .env, setup prompts) parses through here so no two boundaries
disagree on which keys/values a file defines. Dict only — never touches ``os.environ``. ``export``
prefix, ``#`` comments, quote escapes reversed; a BOM is stripped so it doesn't prefix the first key.
Invalid UTF-8 decodes as latin-1, exactly like ``env_loader._load_dotenv_with_fallback`` installs it
into ``os.environ``. Absent/unreadable → ``{}``.

Memoised per path on the file's exact bytes (see the cache comment above). Always
returns a fresh dict: callers mutate what they get back (``build_profile_secret_scope`` layers
external secrets over it).

name: build_profile_secret_scope
doc:
Build a profile's secret mapping from ``<home>/.env`` plus its external
secret sources. Global vars are NOT copied in — ``get_secret`` reads those
from ``os.environ`` — so the scope holds only profile secrets.

name: _is_process_home
doc:
Is *hermes_home* the profile this process serves as its own? Same launch-home identity as
``serves_routed_profile()``: a host that mirrors a served profile into ``HERMES_HOME`` would
otherwise seed the launch profile's bridged allow-all grant into that profile's scope.

name: refresh_installed_secret_scope
doc:
Fold a fresh build of *hermes_home*'s secrets into the INSTALLED scope, in place.

A scope is frozen when installed, but a fire can learn of new values afterwards: a routed cron
fire's first agent build discovers plugin secret sources, and under multiplex semantics the
reload that follows is hydrate-only (never ``os.environ``), so nothing else would carry those
values into the scope this fire already holds. The caller names the home the installed scope
was built for. True when a scope was updated; False when none is installed.

name: served_model_from_headers
doc: First non-empty served-model header, or ``None``.

name: install_served_model_capture
doc: Register the response hook on *client*'s ``httpx`` transport (idempotent per client).

name: result_model_fields
doc:
``requested_model`` / ``served_model`` for the turn result: the proxy header when the
last response carried one, else Hermes' own fallback route (primary → active model).

name: is_terminal_compression_provenance
doc: True when this stamp ends a compression phase and must bypass the persist rate limit.

name: bound_activity_description
doc: Clamp free-form activity text to the shared description budget.

name: normalize_activity_provenance
doc: Return a known provenance, or ``UNKNOWN`` when unset/unrecognized.

name: format_iteration_progress
doc:
``iteration N/M`` for user-facing status lines, or ``iteration N`` when the cap is unbounded.

``AIAgent.max_iterations`` defaults to ``sys.maxsize`` (unlimited), so printing the pair verbatim
shows ``iteration 3/9223372036854775807`` in busy acks, heartbeats and timeout diagnostics (#102806).

name: reset_session_activity_persist_window
doc: Clear the persist rate-limit so the next stamp writes through (terminal compression labels must not stick on mid-compress text).

name: build_activity_snapshot
arguments: *, last_activity_at: Optional[float], last_activity_description: Optional[str], last_activity_provenance: Optional[ActivityProvenance | str]=None, now: Optional[float]=None, extra: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]]=None
doc: Build the shared activity snapshot (plus optional caller extras).

name: measure
doc: Return *idle_s* minus the sleep observed since the agent's last activity.

name: configured_names
doc: The profile's extra tool names (``terminal.client_env_passthrough``).

name: _travels
doc:
A toolchain name may travel unless it is a credential by execute_code's secret policy (even when
listed: ``NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`` matches ``NODE_``; secrets reach tools through ``terminal.env_passthrough``)
or a Hermes control name (a delegated child's markers, Kanban pins). ``secret``: a session's frozen
copy of that policy's substrings.

name: client_env_rules
doc:
The normalisation rules (plain data) a session's map is filtered by, frozen with it: an exact retry
is judged by these, never by the profile's allowlist or the secret policy as they are later. A client
not proven ``local`` keeps only the values that name nothing on this host (prompt, provider request).

name: collect_client_env
doc: Client side: this shell's allowlisted values (the profile's extra names included).

name: normalise_client_env
doc:
The validated map filtered by ``rules`` (``None``: unfiltered, for a map frozen before rules were).
Raises ``ValueError`` for anything but a bounded flat string-to-string map.

name: accept_client_env
doc: Gateway side: the map filtered by the session profile's own current rules.

name: retry_matches
doc:
Whether a retried ``session.create`` (``request``: its params) carries the client environment the
committed session (``committed``: its stored policy) froze. The complete retried map, normalised by
the rules frozen with the session, must equal the stored one: an added name those rules keep, a
missing stored name or a changed value is a different request; one they drop never counts. Staging
and the transactional commit both judge by this. A session committed without a map (Desktop, one
from before the field) still matches only a retry that sends none.

name: client_env_scope
session_env
doc:
A behaviour value for the session executing here: its client's (an unexported name is unset,
as it was for main's process), else the gateway's own environment, which a client not attached
locally also keeps for the values that name this host.

name: tool_env
doc: The toolchain values this session's tool subprocesses start with (empty when unbound or remote).

name: toolchain_environ
doc:
The environment this session's tool subprocesses start from (``base``: the gateway's). Unbound
(messaging, cron, Desktop): unchanged. Every client's session drops the gateway's own behaviour
values it reads from its client (:func:`session_env`), so tools never see the daemon's ephemeral
prompt or provider request in place of the session's. A client not attached locally keeps the
host values (``HOST_BEHAVIOUR``) and the rest of the gateway's environment. A local shell client's
session: its toolchain replaces the gateway's, and every toolchain name it did not export (built-in,
or configured for its profile when the session was created) is unset, as in main's process: one
client's venv or GEM_HOME never reaches another's session through the daemon it started. PATH is
the exception: a client that sent none runs with the gateway's.

name: _is_ephemeral_scaffolding
doc: True when ``msg`` is internal recovery scaffolding that must never reach the durable transcript.

name: _safe_session_filename_component
doc:
Path-safe component for a (possibly untrusted ``X-Hermes-Session-Id``) ID: non ``[A-Za-z0-9_-]`` → ``_``,
capped, plus a content hash when changed so distinct IDs cannot collide.

name: _override_replaces_content
arguments: msg: dict, content: Any, override: Any
doc:
May the persist override replace ``content``? A plain-text override must not replace native image/audio
blocks (a list override is the clean multimodal payload and does), nor a message MERGED with a compaction
summary (overwriting would drop the summary).

name: _content_with_turn_override
arguments: msg: dict, content: Any, override: Any
doc:
Replace only the absorbed current turn, leaving unanswered history intact. The join matches
``_merge_consecutive_users``; a row that no longer holds the prefix takes the plain override.

name: durable_user_row_content
arguments: agent, msg: dict, content: Any, api_content: Any
doc:
``(content, api_content)`` as the current turn's user row is written: the persist override is the
clean transcript, the live content is what the wire sent — so when they differ and nothing else was
injected, the live bytes ARE the sidecar. Shared by the flush and the turn-start stamp so the stamp
matches the row the flush wrote.

name: _summary_display_kind
doc:
Standalone handoffs are hidden so they never occupy the active user slot in retry/undo dispatch;
merge-into-tail carriers keep their prior visibility.

name: _durable_content
doc: Text-only DB projection: multimodal envelopes → summary; part lists keep text, images → ``[screenshot]``.

name: _image_marker
doc:
``[screenshot]`` at the image's position; a caller-chosen ``detail`` rides along so a replay
(``agent.image_replay``) rebuilds the part the live turn sent.

name: _persist_lock
doc:
Close and turn-start persistence can run on separate CLI threads: one critical section.

``__init__`` always creates ``_session_persist_lock``; only ``object.__new__``-built test stubs lack it
(they run unlocked, matching the historical ``if persist_lock is None`` branch).

name: adopt_unanswered_turn
arguments: history: list[dict[str, Any]], query: Any, agent: Any
doc:
Re-stage the transcript's unanswered tail row as THIS turn's user message; True when adopted.

A dispatcher's re-run of a failed delivery turn resumes the DM its first attempt already persisted
instead of appending it again. Rows loaded from the store are born durable (``_rows_to_conversation``),
so handing the tail row back as ``agent._pending_cli_user_message`` makes ``_stage_turn_user_message``
reuse it as this turn's user dict and the flush writes no second row. The one user is the peer-DM
lane's re-run (``resume_unanswered_turn`` in ``gateway.platforms.api_server``, #115325): in process it
calls this on the agent it just built for the re-run; under the session authority the admission
carries ``resume_unanswered`` and ``gateway.run_turn_runner`` calls it on the admitted history
when its tail is that bare user row (a tool suffix there keeps the completed work in view).
The owner-side Bot Chat retry (``gateway.session_bot._maybe_retry``) does not adopt: its failed
turn is already closed by the durable failed-turn boundary, which this function declines by design.

The DM is not always the literal tail: a turn that died mid-way persisted its tool scaffolding — assistant
``tool_calls`` rows and their ``tool`` results — behind the DM before the failure text was built, and the
dispatcher retries that too. The DM is still unanswered while nothing after it is a plain assistant reply,
so it is adopted and the failed attempt's scaffolding leaves the in-memory transcript: the re-run starts
the turn over from the DM (the rows stay in the DB as the record of the failed attempt; the re-run's
answer lands after them as a valid continuation). Anything else declines — no user row at the tail, or a
different text there — so a person's deliberate re-send of the same text is never swallowed.

name: _db_flush_seed_ids
doc:
One-shot ``_flushed_db_message_ids`` seed (same session, after a non-empty flush); the scan translates
it to markers and the flush clears it.

name: _db_flush_scan_start
doc: Skip the identity-matched, still-marked prefix of the previous flush's snapshot.

name: _db_flush_row
doc: Build the session-db row for ``msg``, applying the persist override to THIS row only.

name: _db_flush_collect
arguments: agent, messages: list[dict], conversation_history: Optional[list[dict]], replay_history: bool=False
doc:
Scan for un-flushed messages; returns ``(rows, msgs)`` to write in one transaction. ``replay_history``
(session-row heal) writes the history prefix again instead of stamping it as already durable.

name: _db_flush_write
arguments: agent, batch_rows: list[dict[str, Any]], batch_msgs: list[dict], messages: list[dict]
doc: One transaction for the turn's new rows: on failure nothing lands and no markers are stamped.

name: _db_flush_adopt_compression_tip
doc:
Adopt the live continuation of a compression-closed session. Same-id tip = no continuation; a tip
whose row is missing or already ended is not adopted either.

name: _db_flush_session_row_gone
doc: True only when ``session_id``'s row is confirmed absent; a failed lookup is not proof.

name: _db_flush_failed
arguments: agent, e: Exception, batch_rows: list[dict[str, Any]], adoption_budget: int, messages: list[dict]
doc:
Classify a failed flush and name the one retry the caller should take, or None to fail closed.

``"adopted"``: a compression-closed session moved onto its live tip. ``"healed"``: the session row was
deleted under the live agent and has been recreated (unparented for a delegate child whose parent went
with it); flush markers are reset so the caller replays the full in-memory transcript. Either retry is
taken at most once (``adoption_budget``).

name: _apply_persist_user_message_override
doc:
Rewrite the current-turn user message in place: some paths send an API-only variant that must not
leak into transcripts or resumed history.

name: _persist_session
arguments: self, messages: list[dict], conversation_history: list[dict] | None=None
doc:
Save to SQLite on any exit path. Trailing empty-response scaffolding is dropped from
the live list; the persist override is applied to the DB row only.

The persist user-message *override* is NOT applied here — it is resolved inside
``_flush_messages_to_session_db`` and written only to the DB row, never mutating the live message
list used by the API call (#48677 is thus closed for every persist caller, not just this one).

name: _drop_trailing_empty_response_scaffolding
doc:
Pop empty-response retry scaffolding from the tail. The
assistant(tool_calls) / tool rows before it stay: they were saved before the tools ran, so
dropping them from the live history only makes the model repeat a side effect the durable
transcript already records.

name: _flush_messages_to_session_db
doc: Serialize direct and turn-boundary session flushes per agent.

name: _flush_messages_to_session_db_unlocked
arguments: self, messages: list[dict], conversation_history: Optional[list[dict]]=None, _adoption_budget: int=1
doc:
Persist un-flushed messages to SQLite. Dedup is the intrinsic ``_DB_PERSISTED_MARKER`` on each written
dict — not positional slices (drift after sequence repair) nor an ``id(msg)`` set (address reuse). The
persist override touches the written row only. A compression-closed session adopts its live tip and
retries exactly once.

Deduplicates via an intrinsic ``_DB_PERSISTED_MARKER`` stamped on each written message dict, so
repeated calls (from multiple exit paths) only write truly new messages — preventing the
duplicate-write bug (#860) without relying on positional slices that can drift after
message-sequence repair, and without a retained ``id(msg)`` set that CPython could alias onto a
freed-then-reused address (#50372). The ``_flushed_db_message_ids`` attribute is now only a one-shot
seed (translated to markers, then cleared each flush), not a persisted set.

name: _get_messages_up_to_last_assistant
doc: Messages before the last assistant turn (rollback point for a malformed final answer); all if none.

name: _save_trajectory
arguments: self, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], user_query: str, completed: bool
doc: Save conversation trajectory to JSONL file.

name: is_attended
doc:
A delegated child answers its parent, not a person, though its copied context still carries
the parent's source; a library caller (no platform) has no one reading either.

name: _forget_home_registrations
doc: Drop the current home's keys only (shared with outbound webhooks): profile A's reload must not drop B.

name: _entry_matches
arguments: e: Any, event: Optional[str], command: str

name: _payload_fields
doc: Common stdin/POST payload fields (shared with outbound webhooks); key order is wire order.

name: register_from_config
arguments: cfg: Optional[dict[str, Any]], *, accept_hooks: bool=False, interactive: bool=False
doc:
Register every configured shell hook (idempotent); returns the newly wired specs. Skipped
entries (unknown, malformed, not allowlisted, already registered) are logged only.

``interactive=True`` lets a hook that is not yet allowlisted ask at the terminal; only a
foreground CLI command passes it. Every other caller (gateway startup and profile loads, cron
and managed workers, tui_gateway, force-reload re-registration) never prompts: ``isatty()``
cannot tell a hidden console or ``NUL`` from a person, and a prompt there blocks the event loop
until the liveness watchdog kills the gateway (#120356, #127822).

name: sync_from_config
doc:
Bring this home's registered shell hooks in step with its config (``load_cfg()``) and
consent, for a long-lived process (the gateway) that must behave as a new process would: hooks
configured and consented since start register, hooks removed from config or revoked are
unregistered. Consent is the allowlist, an opt-in in force (``hooks_auto_accept`` /
``HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS`` / this process's own ``--accept-hooks``), or a launch's ``--accept-hooks``
whose allowlist write failed (``accept_for_launch``). Never prompts or writes. An empty config
(a loader that failed open), a malformed ``hooks:`` entry or an unreadable allowlist must never
disarm a ``fail_closed`` guard, so each adds but never removes. Config and allowlist are read
under the same lock as the apply, so the last sync to run always applies the newest state.

name: record_consent_from_config
doc:
First-use consent without registering anything, for a client whose turns run in a gateway that
has no TTY: the prompt (or an opt-in) for each configured hook not yet allowlisted. The gateway
registers from the same allowlist when the client opens its session. Returns the consented specs.

name: accept_for_launch
doc:
A launch's ``--accept-hooks`` on the gateway: record every configured hook in the allowlist,
and keep the consent in memory when that write fails, so it still registers
the hook at the next ``sync_from_config`` (main registered it in memory). Only an unsaved approval
is held, so a later ``hermes hooks revoke`` of a saved one takes effect.

name: accept_for_process
doc:
This process's own ``--accept-hooks`` (``hermes gateway run --accept-hooks``): an opt-in in
force for its lifetime, as ``HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS`` would be, without exporting that variable to
every tool subprocess.

name: _hook_specs
_wire
arguments: manager: Any, home_key: str, specs: list[ShellHookSpec]
doc: Register ``specs`` not yet wired for this home; caller holds ``_registered_lock``.

name: _consented
arguments: spec: ShellHookSpec, accept: bool, allowed: set[tuple[str, str]], *, prompt: bool
doc:
Allowlisted, or approved now (opt-in, or a TTY prompt when ``prompt``; recorded); ``allowed``
caches one read.

name: iter_configured_hooks
doc: Parse config hooks without registering (``hermes hooks list`` / doctor).

name: re_register_config_hooks
doc:
Re-register after a plugin force-reload cleared the manager's hooks; only this home's keys
are cleared (profile A's reload never drops B), never re-prompts.

``PluginManager.discover_and_load(force=True)`` unloads via the ownership ledger and clears the
manager's ``_hooks`` dict, which silently drops shell hooks that were registered from ``config.yaml`` at
startup (they are config-owned, not plugin-owned, so the ledger cannot restore them). Clear the
idempotence set and re-run ``register_from_config()`` so hooks are wired again (#60036 / PR #60267;
tracking #64178 — salvaged from PR #64188).
Only the idempotence keys for the *current* Hermes home are cleared — ``discover_and_load(force=True)``
only unloads the manager scoped to that one home, so clearing every home's keys would make a
force-reload in profile A drop profile B's still-live registration from the ledger and duplicate it on
B's next registration call (#92682 review).

name: reset_for_tests
doc: Test-only: clear the idempotence set.

name: _parse_hooks_block
doc: Normalise ``hooks:`` into specs; malformed entries warn-and-skip, never raise.

name: _parse_hooks
doc:
``(specs, complete)``: ``complete`` is False when an entry was dropped as malformed (a typo
must not read as a deliberate removal); an absent or empty ``hooks:`` is complete.

name: _parse_single_entry
arguments: event: str, index: int, raw: Any

name: _windows_script_argv
doc:
``argv`` with the interpreter prepended when element 0 is an existing script we can name an
interpreter for; unchanged otherwise, including on POSIX, where the shebang already works.

name: _spawn
doc: The single subprocess site: run ``spec.command`` with ``stdin_json`` on stdin. Same result keys for every outcome.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(argv, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                                text=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', shell=False,
                                env=build_subprocess_env(scrub_secrets=is_multiplex_active()), **popen_kwargs)

name: _make_callback
doc: Build the closure that ``invoke_hook()`` will call per firing.

name: _evaluate_result
doc:
Turn a :func:`_spawn` diagnostic dict into the hook's contribution.

Single place that encodes the failure semantics:

* spawn error / timeout — fail open (log + ``None``) unless the spec
  is ``fail_closed`` on a blocking-capable event, in which case a
  canonical block shape is returned;
* exit code 2 on a blocking-capable event — block, with the message
  taken from stdout block JSON, then stderr, then a default
  (Claude-Code / Cursor compatible);
* other non-zero exits — warn, then parse stdout normally; a
  ``fail_closed`` hook blocks if no directive was produced;
* non-JSON / unparseable stdout on a ``fail_closed`` blocking hook —
  block instead of silently contributing nothing.

Shared by the live callback path (:func:`_make_callback`) and the CLI
test helper (:func:`run_once`) so ``hermes hooks test`` reflects
production behaviour exactly.

name: _serialize_payload
doc: Render the stdin JSON payload; unserialisable values are stringified.

name: _block_message
doc: Validated string block message (primary wins), falling back to the default.

name: _parse_response
doc: Translate stdout JSON into a Hermes wire-shape dict, or ``None``.

name: allowlist_path
doc: Path to the per-user shell-hook allowlist file.

name: _read_allowlist
doc:
``(allowlist, readable)``: the parsed allowlist (an empty skeleton when absent or broken) and
whether it could be trusted; a missing file is readable (nothing approved yet), an unreadable or
malformed one is not.

name: load_allowlist
doc: Return the parsed allowlist, or an empty skeleton if absent.

name: save_allowlist
doc: Atomic write; on OSError log and carry on (the approval is not saved).

name: _locked_update_approvals
doc: Serialise allowlist read-modify-write across processes via a sibling flock file.

name: _prompt_and_record
arguments: event: str, command: str, *, accept_hooks: bool
doc: Approve an unseen ``(event, command)`` pair; True iff granted and recorded.

name: revoke
doc:
Remove every allowlist entry for ``command``; returns the count. A gateway unregisters it at its
next allowlist check (``sync_from_config``, about every 30 s) unless an opt-in approves every hook; other live
processes keep it until restart.

name: _command_script_path
doc: First token with a script extension, else the first path-like token, else the first token.

name: _resolve_effective_accept
doc:
Any truthy opt-in channel wins: explicit arg, this process's --accept-hooks, HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS,
hooks_auto_accept.

name: allowlist_entry_for
doc: Return the allowlist record for this pair, if any.

name: script_mtime_iso
doc: ISO-8601 mtime of the resolved script path, or ``None`` if missing.

name: script_is_executable
doc: Runnable as configured: a bare script needs X_OK, an interpreter-prefixed one only R_OK (as ``_spawn`` does).

name: run_once
doc: Fire one hook with a synthetic payload (``hermes hooks test`` / doctor) through the production path.

name: trim_snapshot_for_fork
doc:
Drop trailing messages until the snapshot ends with a completed assistant text.

A mid-turn tail (unresolved ``tool_calls``, tool result, in-flight user message) breaks
role alternation on strict providers; trimming only the TAIL keeps the warm prefix cache.

name: render_history_for_side_question
doc:
Plain-text transcript for the fallback path: newest-biased fit to ``char_budget``,
tool calls summarized by name, tool results truncated, system prompt skipped.

name: _side_question_task_config
doc: Return ``auxiliary.side_question`` from config (or ``{}``).

name: _answer_via_fork
arguments: parent_agent: Any, question: str, history: Optional[list[dict[str, Any]]], on_fork: Optional[Callable[[Any], None]]=None
doc:
Answer via a cache-parity fork of ``parent_agent`` on the calling thread.

An empty thread-scoped tool whitelist denies every tool call at dispatch: ``tools[]``
stays byte-identical for cache parity, but the side question can never mutate anything.
``on_fork(fork)`` publishes the built fork so an owner can interrupt it, and
``on_fork(None)`` follows its teardown.

name: _answer_via_oneshot
arguments: question: str, history: Optional[list[dict[str, Any]]], **run_kwargs: Any
doc: Fallback: answer from a rendered transcript digest in one aux call.

name: answer_side_question
arguments: question: str, history: Optional[list[dict[str, Any]]], *, parent_agent: Any=None, main_runtime: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, max_tokens: int=2048, temperature: Optional[float]=0.3, timeout: float=180.0, on_fork: Optional[Callable[[Any], None]]=None, should_stop: Optional[Callable[[], bool]]=None
doc:
Fork when ``parent_agent`` is live, else (or on empty answer / failure) the one-shot
digest. Raises on failure — callers surface the error on their own UI.

``on_fork`` receives the fork once built (and ``None`` after its teardown) so the caller can
interrupt it; ``should_stop()`` true after the fork skips the one-shot fallback.

name: _row_name
doc:
Skill name of an index row (``    - name: description`` / ``    - name``). Split on ``": "``:
plugin skills are qualified (``plugin:skill``), so a bare ``":"`` is part of the name.

name: index_entries
doc:
``{name: index row}`` for every skill in ``prompt``'s ``<available_skills>`` block; names-only
category rows (focus mode) map to ``""``. ``{}`` without a block.

name: _parse
doc: Inverse of :func:`_render` for the text that follows ``_NOTE_PREFIX``.

name: _announced
doc:
The difference named by the newest skills note anywhere in the transcript: a note far back
still describes the current state when nothing changed since it was sent.

name: stage_skills_index_note
arguments: agent: Any, prompt: Any, conversation_history: Any
doc:
Stage a one-shot note when the skills this session can load differ from ``prompt``'s index
by something the model has not been told yet. Returns whether it staged.

A prompt without an index is never compared: it has no baseline (skills tools off, a seeded or
embedder-supplied prompt), and announcing the whole catalog there would only add noise. MoA and
codex_app_server turns never stamp the ``api_content`` sidecar, so the note could not be read
back from the transcript; those modes skip it, like the surface-switch note.

name: _bundles_dir
doc: Bundles directory: ``HERMES_BUNDLES_DIR`` override (tests) or ``<HERMES_HOME>/skill-bundles``.

name: _bundles_sig
doc:
Sorted ``(path, content digest)`` of the bundle files. Content, not timestamps: a same-size
rewrite within one coarse mtime/ctime tick, or under host/filesystem clock skew, still moves it.
Bundles are a handful of small YAML files, so reading them per check is cheap.

name: _load_bundle_file
doc: Parse one bundle YAML; ``None`` (logged) on any error so a broken bundle can't break discovery.

name: scan_bundles
doc: Rebuild the ``"/slug"`` -> bundle info cache; duplicate slugs keep the first (alphabetical).

name: get_skill_bundles
doc: Current bundle mapping; rescans only when the set of bundle files or their content changed.

name: resolve_bundle_command_key
doc: Resolve a user-typed command to its ``/slug`` key (``_`` ≡ ``-``, as Telegram rewrites hyphens).

name: reload_bundles
doc: Re-scan and return an ``added``/``removed``/``unchanged``/``total`` diff (same shape as reload_skills).

name: list_bundles
doc: Return a sorted list of bundle info dicts for display.

name: build_bundle_invocation_message
arguments: cmd_key: str, user_instruction: str='', task_id: str | None=None, platform: str | None=None
doc:
Build the user message for a bundle invocation: ``(message,
loaded_skill_names, missing_skill_names)`` or ``None`` if the bundle wasn't
found. Uninstalled members are skipped with a note; disabled ones too, since
``_load_skill_payload`` bypasses the scan-time filter (``platform`` scopes
that check — gateway passes it, None resolves from env).

Disabled skills are also skipped: bundles load members via ``_load_skill_payload`` directly, bypassing
the scan-time disabled filter in ``get_skill_commands()``, so the disabled list must be re-applied here.
``platform`` scopes the check to a specific platform's ``skills.platform_disabled`` config (gateway
dispatch passes it explicitly because the gateway handles multiple platforms in one process); when
*None*, the platform resolves from session env vars and the global disabled list still applies. Mirrors
the stacked-skill gate in gateway dispatch (#58888).

name: bundle_path_for
doc: Return the canonical filesystem path for a bundle name.

name: save_bundle
arguments: name: str, skills: list[str], description: str='', instruction: str='', overwrite: bool=False
doc:
Write a bundle to disk and refresh the cache. Raises ``FileExistsError``
if the target exists and not ``overwrite``; ``ValueError`` for unusable inputs.

name: delete_bundle
doc: Delete a bundle by name and return its path; ``FileNotFoundError`` if absent.

name: get_bundle
doc: Look up a bundle by name (slug-normalized).

name: slugify_skill_name
doc:
Normalize a skill/bundle name to a ``/command`` slug (``Foo Bar`` -> ``foo-bar``);
strips chars (``+``, ``/``) that would make invalid Telegram command names.

name: append_user_instruction
doc:
Append the instruction line to ``parts``; return the stable prefix, which
ends exactly at the instruction marker so (registered with
``agent.prompt_cache_boundary``) the cache planner can break on the scaffold.
Single construction site guarantees the prefix is a byte-prefix of the message.

Shared by every builder that ends a static skill scaffold with the caller-supplied volatile instruction
(single-skill invocations, cron job prompts). Keeping construction in one place guarantees the
registered prefix stays a byte-prefix of the built message — the invariant the request-time split
depends on. See #81867.

name: extract_user_instruction_from_skill_message
doc:
Recover the user's instruction from a slash-skill-expanded turn: the
string unchanged when it is NOT scaffolding, the extracted instruction when
the scaffolding carried one, or ``None`` for a bare ``/skill`` invocation.

name: _describe_auto_loaded_skill_turn
doc:
``[IMPORTANT: The "X" skill is auto-loaded. …]`` + payload(s) + typed text
-> the typed text.

``_hmwa_auto_load_skills`` builds each payload with ``_build_skill_message``
(activation header, body, then the skill-directory footer note) and appends the
user's text as the final block. The footer's closing sentence is the reliable
payload-end marker: the user's text is what follows the LAST footer. A header
quoted inside a body (a skill embedding the scaffold in an example) carries no
footer, so it cannot end the payload early. ``/<skill>`` renders when no user
text follows, matching the single-skill describer's bare-invocation shape.

name: describe_skill_invocation
doc:
Render a slash-skill-expanded turn the way the user typed it:
``"/work — fix the title leak"``, ``"/work"`` for a bare invocation, or
``None`` when *content* is not scaffolding. ``separator=" "`` gives the
literal invocation as typed (chat transcripts).

A gateway auto-load scaffold (channel-bound skill on a new session) is also
scaffolding: the typed request follows the skill payload, so it renders as
that request — the header/body never reaches a preview or a title (#48359).

name: skills_loaded_by_scaffold
doc:
Skill names a slash-skill, bundle/stacked or gateway auto-load turn carries inline; ``[]`` for any
other text. Only a complete activation header counts, so typed text that merely starts like one
(``[IMPORTANT: The "config" file is broken]``) is not mistaken for a skill load.

name: _cut_after
arguments: message: str, marker: str, stop_marker: str, find
doc: Text between *marker* (located with ``find``) and *stop_marker*, stripped; None if absent/empty.

name: _resolve_skill_commands_platform
doc:
Current platform scope for disabled-skill filtering, or None (CLI, RL,
scripts). A change invalidates the scan cache so each platform sees its
own ``skills.platform_disabled`` view.

Used to detect when the active platform has shifted so :func:`get_skill_commands` can drop a stale cache
that was populated for a different platform's ``skills.platform_disabled`` view (#14536).

name: _resolve_skill_commands_home
doc:
Effective Hermes home the scan is scoped to (profiles carry their own
``skills.external_dirs``, so a profile switch must invalidate the cache).

A gateway session can switch between profiles that each carry their own ``skills.external_dirs`` (via
``set_hermes_home_override``), but the module-level scan only tracked
``_resolve_skill_commands_platform()``. Switching profiles without a platform change left the previous
profile's skill list cached, so ``get_skill_commands()`` reported a cache miss for skills that only
exist under the new profile (#88023).

name: _resolve_skill_commands_project
doc:
The project root the scan's project skills resolve from (None outside a repo). One multi-session
host serves sessions in different repos; without this tag the first session's project skills stayed
published for every other session's ``get_skill_commands`` lookup (#114359).

name: _load_skill_payload
returns: tuple[dict[str, Any], Path | None, str] | None
doc: Load a skill by name/path and return (loaded_payload, skill_dir, display_name).

name: ambiguous_skill_label
doc:
``Ambiguous skill name X: use one of <paths>`` when a failed skill_view *payload* is a same-tier
name collision, else None — so preload/cron say why instead of "Unknown"/"not found".

name: _missing_skill_label
doc: Display form of an identifier that failed to load (failure path only: re-asks skill_view).

name: format_missing_skills
doc:
One error line for unresolved preload identifiers: ambiguous ones keep their own wording,
the rest are reported as ``Unknown skill(s): ...``.

name: _inject_skill_config
doc:
Append a ``[Skill config: ...]`` block with resolved ``metadata.hermes.config``
values so the agent needn't read config.yaml. Any failure leaves the message without it.

name: _supporting_files
arguments: loaded_skill: dict[str, Any], skill_dir: Path | None
doc: Skill-relative support file paths: from ``linked_files`` or a disk walk.

name: _build_skill_message
arguments: loaded_skill: dict[str, Any], skill_dir: Path | None, activation_note: str, user_instruction: str='', runtime_note: str='', session_id: str | None=None
doc: Format a loaded skill into a user/system message payload.

name: _render_skill_block
arguments: loaded: tuple[dict[str, Any], Path | None, str], activation_note: str, task_id: str | None, **message_kwargs: str
doc: Bump Curator usage tracking (never fatal) and build the message block for one loaded skill.

name: _scaffold_header
arguments: subject: str, loaded_names: list[str], *, lead_lines: list[str] | None=None, missing: list[str] | None=None, disabled: list[str] | None=None, extra_instruction: str='', user_instruction: str=''
doc:
Header for multi-skill messages (bundles and stacked invocations).
``subject`` must end in " skill bundle" so the bundle-format extractor applies.

name: skill_command_collision_note
doc:
User-facing note when *name*'s slash slug is a core command (name or alias), else None.

The single source of the collision predicate: ``scan_skill_commands`` uses it to skip
auto-registration (the shadowing guard from 370ebf2d3 — the skill map is consulted before
built-in handlers), and the ``/skills`` listing plus the command palette render the note so
the skipped skill is explained where the user looks, not only in the log.

name: _scan_skill_md
arguments: skill_md: Path, disabled: set, seen_names: set, commands: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
doc: Register one SKILL.md in *commands* (no-op when filtered or colliding).

name: scan_skill_commands
doc:
Scan skill dirs and return {"/skill-name": {name, description, skill_md_path, skill_dir}}.
Builds a local map and publishes once at the end: writing straight into the
global exposed partial results to overlapping scans, which then logged
bogus "already claimed" collisions against their own incumbents.

name: published_scopes_signature
doc:
Signature of every skill scope a session has resolved commands for, plus the ambient one.

One gateway serves sessions in several profiles and repos; each published ``(platform, home,
project)`` key names a scope whose roots (that profile's skills/external dirs, that repo's trusted
project skills) a viewer is looking at. The change watcher (``skills.changed``) compares this, so
an install in a session's repo B notifies viewers even when the gateway was launched in repo A.
Only command maps/catalogs refetch; a conversation's stored system prompt is never rebuilt.

name: _skill_dirs_signature
doc:
Stat-cheap change signature of every skill root (the catalog's own: the mtime and child names of
every directory the catalog walks, depth-bounded, plus the disabled set and the platform). None when
it cannot be computed (a root that cannot be stat'ed), which keeps the published map rather than
rescanning on every lookup. Any other error raises: the catalog scan itself takes the same signature
unguarded (``tools.skills_tool._skill_catalog``), and a swallowed bug would pin a stale map silently.

name: get_skill_commands
doc:
Return the current skill commands mapping (scan first if empty). Rescans
when the platform scope (one gateway serving Telegram and Discord) or the
active profile's home (Desktop profile switch) or the session's project root (two sessions in two
repos) changes, so each sees its own ``platform_disabled`` / ``external_dirs`` / project-skill view.

See #14536, #88023, #114359, #104849.

name: invalidate_plugin_skill_commands
doc: Drop the cached plugin skill projection.

name: get_plugin_skill_commands
doc:
Project enabled plugin skills into the interactive-only slash namespace (``/plugin:skill``).

Config disable lists (``skills.disabled``, ``plugins.disabled``) are applied on EVERY call, so a
config-only disable takes effect without a rescan.

name: _scan_plugin_skill_commands
doc: Build the plugin skill projection and publish it with its tag atomically.

name: _merge_interactive_skill_commands
arguments: filesystem_commands: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], plugin_commands: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
doc: Merge interactive sources with filesystem commands winning collisions.

name: get_interactive_skill_commands
doc:
Filesystem skills plus profile-scoped plugin skills; never use for
messaging/native command menus (plugin skills are CLI/TUI/desktop only).

name: diff_command_snapshots
arguments: before: dict[str, str], after: dict[str, str]
doc:
Diff two {name: description} snapshots into added/removed/unchanged/total.
Removed entries carry the pre-rescan description (the file may be gone).

name: command_snapshot
doc: ``{"/slug": info}`` -> ``{"slug": description}`` for diff_command_snapshots.

name: reload_skills
doc:
Re-scan skill dirs and return a diff of the slash-command map (``added``
/ ``removed`` / ``unchanged`` / ``total`` / ``commands``; descriptions are the
full frontmatter field). Does NOT invalidate the skills system-prompt cache:
skills are called by name, so ``/reload-skills`` costs no cache reset. The
plugin projection is rebuilt too, so a plugin enabled/disabled/installed
since the last scan shows up without a restart.

name: resolve_skill_command_key
doc:
Resolve a user-typed slash command, or return None.

Try the exact qualified spelling before the filesystem skill slug fallback,
where underscores and hyphens are interchangeable for Telegram. Native
callers retain the filesystem-only lookup; plugin skills are interactive.

name: resolve_slash_key
doc: ``command`` -> ``"/slug"`` when present in *table* (``_`` normalized to ``-``), else None.

name: build_skill_invocation_message
arguments: cmd_key: str, user_instruction: str='', task_id: str | None=None, runtime_note: str=''
doc: Build the user message for a skill slash command, or None if not found.

name: split_stacked_skill_commands
doc:
Consume further leading ``/skill`` tokens from *rest* (text after the first
matched command); stops at the first non-skill (or repeated) token, which
starts the user instruction. Returns ``(extra_cmd_keys, remaining_instruction)``.
Native callers (messaging gateway) must pass ``interactive=False``: plugin
skills are interactive-only and must not resolve here.

name: build_stacked_skill_invocation_message
arguments: cmd_keys: list[str], user_instruction: str='', task_id: str | None=None
doc:
Build the user message for a stacked multi-skill slash invocation:
``(message, loaded_skill_names, missing_skill_names)``, or ``None`` when no skill loaded.
Keys come from ``split_stacked_skill_commands``; native callers only ever pass filesystem keys.

name: _disabled_skill_names
doc: Operator-disabled skill names (empty set when config is unreadable).

name: _load_skill_blocks
arguments: identifiers: list[str], load, activation_note, task_id: str | None, *, missing_label=lambda ident: ident, disabled_names: set | None=None, disabled_as_missing: bool=False, already_loaded: set | None=None
doc:
Load each distinct identifier via *load* and render its block; returns
``(loaded_names, missing, disabled, blocks)``. With *disabled_names*, members
whose canonical (LOADED — identifiers may be paths) name or identifier is
disabled go to ``disabled`` (or ``missing`` when *disabled_as_missing*).
Canonical names in *already_loaded* (e.g. skills.auto_load) count as resolved
but render no block, so one skill never lands in the prompt twice.

name: build_preloaded_skills_prompt
arguments: skill_identifiers: list[str], task_id: str | None=None, excluded_loaded_names: set[str] | None=None
doc:
Load skills for session-wide CLI/TUI preloading; returns (prompt_text,
loaded_skill_names, missing_identifiers). Disabled skills count as missing:
this path bypasses the scan-time filter, and ``hermes -s <skill>`` must not
force-load an operator-disabled skill. *excluded_loaded_names* are canonical
names the session already carries (skills.auto_load): they resolve as loaded
but are not rendered again.

Disabled skills are treated the same as missing ones: this loads via a raw identifier straight into
``_load_skill_payload``, bypassing ``get_skill_commands()``'s scan-time disabled filter — mirrors the
bundle-invocation gate (#59156).

name: resolve_auto_load_skills
doc:
``skills.auto_load`` from *user_config* (else the active profile config), deduplicated;
empty when unset, malformed, or the config is unreadable.

name: build_auto_load_prompt
arguments: task_id: str | None=None, user_config: dict | None=None, home_override: Path | None=None
doc:
Render ``skills.auto_load`` as fully loaded skill blocks for a new session; returns
``(prompt_text, loaded_names, missing)``. Missing and operator-disabled names are reported,
never raised: a typo in config must not block session start on any surface.

*home_override* makes home resolution EXPLICIT (same seam as ``build_skills_system_prompt``): the config,
the disabled list and the ``<home>/skills`` lookup all resolve under that home, so a gateway build thread
that lost the HERMES_HOME ContextVar cannot pin the launch profile's skills into another profile's prompt.

name: load_skills_config
doc: Load the ``skills`` section of config.yaml (best-effort).

name: substitute_template_vars
arguments: content: str, skill_dir: Path | None, session_id: str | None
doc: Replace ${HERMES_SKILL_DIR} / ${HERMES_SESSION_ID}; tokens without a value stay in place.

name: run_inline_shell
arguments: command: str, cwd: Path | None, timeout: int
doc:
Run one inline-shell snippet and return its stdout (trimmed; stderr when
stdout is empty). Failures return an ``[inline-shell ...]`` marker instead
of raising, so one bad snippet can't wreck the whole skill message.

name: expand_inline_shell
arguments: content: str, skill_dir: Path | None, timeout: int
doc: Replace every !`cmd` snippet with its stdout, run with the skill dir as CWD.

name: _is_community_hub_skill
doc:
Whether *skill_dir* is a hub-installed skill the scan gate classifies as community trust.

The hub's INSTALL_POLICY blocks a community install on a caution/dangerous verdict — but
``--force`` (or a pre-scanner install) puts that skill on disk anyway, and the inline-shell
DSL scans as high severity, so auto-executing it on view would re-arm exactly what the
gate refused (#63307). Provenance is the hub lock entry (trusted/builtin entries expand;
anything without one — bundled-synced, user-created, project/external — keeps the flag's
contract). It covers every SKILL.md nested inside a community install and is read from
the lock that owns the skills tree the dir lives in, not only the active profile's
(``external_dirs`` can expose another profile's installs). A lock that exists but cannot
be read fails closed for skills in its tree; no lock means no hub installs.

name: preprocess_skill_content
arguments: content: str, skill_dir: Path | None, session_id: str | None=None, skills_cfg: dict | None=None
doc: Apply configured SKILL.md template and inline-shell preprocessing.

name: is_excluded_skill_path
doc:
True if *path* should be skipped by skill scanners (VCS/dependency/cache
dirs + support packages). Apply to every SKILL.md from a direct ``rglob``.

name: is_skill_support_path
doc:
True if *path* is under a support dir sitting directly inside a skill root
(``skills/scripts/foo`` stays discoverable: no ``SKILL.md`` above ``scripts``).

name: yaml_load
doc: Parse YAML with the shared safe loader, imported lazily.

name: parse_frontmatter
doc:
Parse YAML frontmatter from markdown; returns (frontmatter_dict, body).
Malformed YAML falls back to key:value line splitting. A leading UTF-8 BOM
(Windows editors) is stripped first or it would defeat the ``---`` fence check.

name: skill_matches_platform_list
doc: Return True when *platforms* is compatible with the current OS.

name: skill_matches_platform
doc: True when the skill's ``platforms:`` list (absent = all) matches this OS.

name: _detect_environment
doc:
True when the named runtime environment is active (unknown => True).
Cached per process EXCEPT ``kanban``: that verdict is context-dependent
(delegate children / in-process cron see the worker's vars), so a
process-wide cache would leak the first asker's answer to the others.

name: skill_matches_environment
doc:
True when ANY declared ``environments:`` tag is active (absent = all;
unknown tags fail open). Offer-time filter only.

name: skill_matches_apps
doc:
True when every app named in ``requires_apps:`` has a registered declaration this host satisfies.

Names resolve through ``hermes_platform.declaration`` (registered by whoever owns the server,
e.g. the plugin loader); the check is the same ``availability()`` the MCP check_fn uses. An
unknown name hides the skill (fail closed). Offer-time filter, like ``environments:``.

name: _raw_config_cache_clear
doc: Test hook — drop the shared raw config cache.

name: _config_cache_key
doc: ``(path, *file_signature)`` identity of config.yaml, or None when unreadable/absent.

name: _load_raw_config
doc: Read config.yaml with an mtime+size keyed cache (no hermes_cli.config import).

name: _skills_cfg
doc: The ``skills:`` mapping from config.yaml, or None when absent/malformed.

name: _skills_cfg_get
doc: ``skills.<key>`` from config.yaml, or None when the section is absent/malformed.

name: _expand_path
doc: Expand ``~`` and ``${VAR}`` in a config path entry.

name: _home_relative
doc: Anchor a relative config path at HERMES_HOME; absolute paths pass through.

name: get_disabled_skill_names
doc:
Disabled skill names from config.yaml: global list ∪ platform list
(*platform* defaults to ``HERMES_PLATFORM`` / ``HERMES_SESSION_PLATFORM``).

name: parse_config_string_list
doc:
Normalize a config value that may hold a JSON-array string into a list.
``hermes config set`` stores lists as quoted JSON/Python-literal strings;
treating one as a single name would silently filter nothing. A scalar
string still means one name.

See #13026, #86661.

name: _external_dirs_cache_clear
doc: Test hook — drop the in-process cache.

name: _config_str_list
doc: A scalar-or-list config entry as a list of stripped non-empty strings.

name: get_external_skills_dirs
doc:
Validated, deduplicated ``skills.external_dirs`` (existing dirs only). Entries
are ``~``/``${VAR}`` expanded, relative to HERMES_HOME; the local skills dir is skipped.

name: get_skill_create_dir
doc:
Configured ``skills.create_dir`` (need not exist yet), or None when unset;
relative to HERMES_HOME; a value equal to the local skills dir counts as unset.

name: display_skill_create_dir
doc:
User-facing path where new skills are created (``~/`` shorthand when
possible); tool schema descriptions and prompts follow ``skills.create_dir``.

name: get_skill_search_roots
doc:
``(tier, dir)`` for every skill root in precedence order — the ONE ordering the skills list,
prompt index, slash commands, skill_view, preload and cron share. *local* overrides the profile
skills dir (skills_tool passes its live root); that entry is kept even when missing.

name: get_all_skills_dirs
doc:
Skill dirs: local ``~/.hermes/skills/`` first, then create_dir, then external.
Trusted project dirs are NOT included (higher precedence; see get_project_skills_dirs).

name: provably_same_skill
doc:
True only when every path is the SAME skill: one resolved file (symlink view) or byte-identical
content (copy). Anything else is two different skills sharing a name, and picking one by depth
would let ``<root>/evil`` (``name: github``) shadow the real one.

name: skill_candidate_rank
doc:
Same-root order of identical copies: a real SKILL.md beats a legacy flat ``<name>.md``,
then the shallower path wins (shared by skill_view and :func:`resolve_skill_catalog`).

name: pick_skill_candidate
doc:
Winner index among one identifier's ``(tier, root, rank, skill_md)`` candidates, plus the
winning tier's contender indexes. The lowest tier wins; inside it a lone candidate wins, identical
copies under one root resolve to the strictly best ``rank``, anything else is ambiguous (None).

name: is_disabled_entry
doc:
``skills.disabled`` matches a resolved catalog entry by its declared name OR its ``load_name`` —
the exact path a same-tier duplicate's list/config/web row shows (``a/one``) and saves. A unique
copy elsewhere that merely sits at the same relative path is not matched.

name: resolve_skill_catalog
doc:
Copies of scanned skills (each with ``name``, ``tier``, ``root`` and ``path`` = its SKILL.md)
annotated with what skill_view() resolves, using its aliases (declared name, directory name, path
relative to the root) and :func:`pick_skill_candidate`. Adds ``relative_path`` and ``status``:
``unique`` (``load_name`` = name), ``ambiguous`` (``load_name`` = the exact relative path, or None
when even that is shared) or ``shadowed`` (a higher tier owns the name: hidden, warned once).

name: find_project_root
doc:
Nearest ancestor containing ``.git`` (dir or worktree file), or None.
Without *start*, the surface's effective working directory wins over the process cwd — the same
ladder every other cwd consumer reads (``resolve_agent_cwd``: session-bound cwd, then the scope's
``TERMINAL_CWD``, then the process cwd). The session cwd comes first because a multi-session host
(TUI/desktop gateway) pins each session's workspace there while its terminal scope resolves a
placeholder ``terminal.cwd`` to ``$HOME``; reading only the scope made every project skill invisible
on those surfaces (#114359). ``TERMINAL_CWD`` is the per-surface workdir the terminal tool and cron
jobs use (a cron job sets it from its per-job ``workdir`` without chdir'ing the scheduler process),
which lets non-interactive surfaces inherit a prior interactive trust decision by project identity —
and a surface with no workdir in a trusted repo simply resolves no project and loads nothing (#48975).

name: _project_trusted_dirs_from_config
doc: Resolved set of trusted project roots from ``skills.trusted_project_dirs``.

name: is_project_root_trusted
doc: True when *root* is listed in ``skills.trusted_project_dirs``.

name: _candidate_project_skills_dirs
doc:
Existing skill dirs under *root*, excluding the profile's own skills dir
(HERMES_HOME itself may live inside a git checkout).

name: _current_project_root
doc: cwd's project root when discovery is on and its trust state == *trusted*.

name: get_project_skills_dirs
doc: Trusted project-local skill dirs for the current cwd (may be empty).

name: get_untrusted_project_skills_root
doc: (root, skill_count) when cwd's project has skills but is NOT trusted, else None.

name: is_quarantined_project_skill
doc:
True when a project skill's scan verdict is ``dangerous``. Fail-closed: a
scanner crash or missing scanner quarantines the skill. Scans
unconditionally — non-project callers should not call this.

name: iter_project_skill_files
doc:
Yield non-quarantined SKILL.md files under a trusted project dir — the
single iteration chokepoint for the project tier, so the quarantine cannot
be bypassed by a call site forgetting the check.

name: normalize_skill_lookup_name
doc:
Translate a trusted absolute skill path (slash commands / cron may store
them) to the relative form ``skill_view()`` accepts.

name: is_external_skill_path
doc:
True when ``path`` lives under an external or trusted project skills dir.
Those are externally owned: autonomous lifecycle maintenance treats them as
read-only (user-directed tool calls may still edit them).

name: _hermes_metadata
doc: ``metadata.hermes`` mapping from frontmatter, or ``{}`` when malformed.

name: extract_skill_conditions
doc: Extract conditional activation fields from parsed frontmatter (absent = ``[]``).

name: extract_skill_config_vars
doc:
Extract ``metadata.hermes.config`` declarations (key/description/default/prompt).
Entries missing ``key`` or ``description`` are skipped; ``prompt`` defaults to the description.

name: discover_all_skill_config_vars
doc:
Config var declarations across all enabled, platform-compatible skills,
deduplicated by key; each dict carries a ``skill`` attribution key.

name: _resolve_dotpath
doc: Walk a nested dict following a dotted key; None if any part is missing.

name: _expand_skill_config_path
doc:
Expand ``~`` / ``$HOME`` against the HOME Hermes injects into tool subprocesses.

Skill config defaults describe paths the agent hands to tools, so in a container where the
control process HOME (``/opt/data``) differs from the tool HOME (``{HERMES_HOME}/home``) a
plain ``expanduser`` pointed the prompt at a path no tool would ever read (#12260).

name: resolve_skill_config_values
doc:
Map logical skill config keys to current values (or declared defaults);
path-like string values are ``~``/``$HOME``/``${VAR}`` expanded against the tool HOME.

name: _normalize_skill_description
doc: Normalize a skill's description field for comparison/truncation.

name: extract_skill_description
doc: Extract a system-prompt-length description from parsed frontmatter.

name: is_skill_description_truncated_for_prompt
doc: True when the description will be truncated in the system prompt skill index.

name: iter_skill_index_files
doc:
Walk skills_dir yielding sorted paths matching *filename*; prunes
EXCLUDED_SKILL_DIRS and support dirs of skill roots.

name: parse_qualified_name
doc: Split ``'namespace:skill-name'`` into ``(namespace, bare_name)``; ``(None, name)`` without ``':'``.

name: is_valid_namespace
doc: Check whether *candidate* is a valid namespace (``[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+``).

name: _windows_unbiased_clock
doc: The unbiased interrupt time in seconds, or None where kernel32 lacks it.

name: slept
doc: Seconds stopped since the previous call, or 0.0.

name: install_truststore
doc:
Point every default SSLContext at the OS trust store. Idempotent.

Returns True when the platform verifier is in force. A False return
means truststore could not load (an unsupported platform, or a
stripped payload); TLS still works off OpenSSL's compiled-in paths,
it just won't see certificates the OS trusts.

Call before the first HTTPS client is constructed.

name: _stdlib_ssl_context_class
doc:
The un-injected stdlib ``ssl.SSLContext``.

An explicit bundle must REPLACE OS trust, and truststore's context falls
back to the OS verifier whenever the loaded bundle rejects a chain — so
the bundle context has to be built from the stdlib class. Once injected
(here, or by pm.launch/pm.worker before this module loads) the only
handle on it is truststore's own saved reference; when nothing is
injected — truststore absent or not installed — ``ssl.SSLContext`` is
already the stdlib class and truststore must not be imported at all.

name: _shared_context
doc:
A stable context identity lets clients reuse the existing transport pool.

``union`` adds ``ca_path`` to the platform store (the ``SSL_CERT_FILE``
contract) instead of replacing it (a provider ``ssl_ca_cert``).

name: platform_ssl_context
doc:
The process-wide client context (cheap after the first call).

An existing ``SSL_CERT_FILE`` bundle is trusted ON TOP of the platform store,
as it was for httpx ``verify=True``; a missing or stale path falls back to
the platform store alone.

name: certifi_bundle_path
doc:
certifi's CA bundle path, re-derived when a rotation invalidated it.

``certifi.where()`` resolves its path once, against the ``certifi`` package on the
``sys.path`` of the moment it was first called, and caches it in ``certifi.core``:
a process that outlives an install-environment rotation — the package manager
creates a new environment directory and deletes the old one — keeps pointing into
the deleted directory for the rest of its life, and every TLS client it builds
afterwards fails. Re-importing the package against the live ``sys.path`` repairs it
process-wide; when even that finds nothing, the platform store is the answer and
never an exception.

The repair, and its warning, happen ONCE per dead path: a gateway builds clients
per turn, per cron run and per model-metadata fetch, so an un-cached reload here
would re-execute third-party module code and re-log on every client it builds.

Returns a bundle path that exists on disk, else ``None``.

name: _recover_bundle_once
doc:
Re-derive ``stale`` at most once, and report it at most once.

A cached outcome is reused while it still holds (a re-derived path that exists, or
an unrecoverable one); a later rotation dead-path is a new key and is repaired on
its own.

name: _reload_certifi_bundle
doc:
Re-import certifi from the live ``sys.path`` so its ``where()`` follows it.

``importlib.reload`` on its own does NOT re-derive the path with the real package:
``certifi.where`` is ``certifi.core.where`` re-exported by ``__init__``, and ``core``
caches the resolved path in a module global, so re-executing ``__init__`` re-binds
``where`` from the still-loaded ``core`` — the replaced directory, cached a second
time. Only dropping the package and its submodules from ``sys.modules`` makes both
files re-execute against the live ``sys.path``. They are put back when the import
fails, so the process is never left without the ``certifi`` it already had.

``None`` when certifi was never imported or its package is gone from every
``sys.path`` entry — the caller then falls back to the platform store.

name: requests_verify
doc:
``verify`` for a ``requests`` call in this process.

``requests`` resolves ``verify=True`` through ``DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH``, a string
frozen when ``requests`` was imported — the one certifi consumer a module reload
cannot reach, so a rotated environment leaves every ``requests`` call raising
``OSError: Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle``. The live bundle
(certifi's, re-derived; else OpenSSL's own default) keeps those calls working;
``True`` only when nothing resolves, which is requests' own default. A healthy
install keeps ``True`` too: requests reads ``REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE``/``CURL_CA_BUNDLE``
only for ``verify=True``, and an explicit path would silently bypass a user's
proxy CA.

name: _platform_store_bundle
doc: The OS store's CA certificates written once to a PEM file under HERMES_HOME.

name: _default_verify
doc:
``verify`` for the platform default path.

httpx resolves ``verify=True`` through ``certifi.where()`` at client construction,
which raises ``FileNotFoundError`` on a bundle path a rotation deleted. Hand the
platform context over instead when no bundle can be found; a re-derivable bundle
keeps ``True`` — the module reload already repaired certifi process-wide.

name: resolve_httpx_verify
arguments: *, ca_bundle: Optional[str]=None, ssl_verify: Any=None, base_url: str=''
doc:
Resolve ``verify`` for an HTTP client.

1. ``ssl_verify: false`` — verification off (local development only)
2. explicit ``ca_bundle`` (the provider's ``ssl_ca_cert``) — that
   bundle INSTEAD of the platform store, for an endpoint whose chain
   the machine has no reason to trust
3. ``True`` — the platform store, via the process-wide install, or the
   platform context when the certifi bundle this process resolved at
   import no longer exists (a replaced install environment)

``base_url`` only labels the insecure-mode warning.

name: _safe_print
doc:
Print that swallows broken pipes / closed stdout (headless stdout can vanish mid-session);
routes through ``self._print_fn`` so the CLI can inject an ANSI-aware renderer.

name: _vprint
doc:
Verbose print — suppressed while tokens are streaming (allowed during tool execution) and after
the main response; ``force=True`` bypasses both. ``suppress_status_output`` (``hermes chat -q``) wins.

name: _should_start_quiet_spinner
doc:
True when quiet-mode spinner output has a safe sink (``_print_fn`` or a real TTY); a raw spinner
on a non-TTY stdout can corrupt protocol streams (ACP JSON-RPC).

name: _should_emit_quiet_tool_messages
doc:
True when quiet-mode tool summaries should print directly (CLI, no callback owns rendering);
``suppress_status_output`` always wins so ``[tool]``/``[done]`` never land in captured stdout.

``suppress_status_output`` (the strict machine-readable mode used by ``hermes chat -Q``) always
wins: those flows neutralize the rendering callbacks, and without this gate the "no callback owns
rendering" fallback would print ``[tool]``/``[done]`` spinner lines into the captured stdout it
exists to keep clean (#93220).

name: _call_callback
doc: Invoke ``self.<name>(*args)`` if set, swallowing errors — a driver callback must never break the loop.

name: _emit_status_kind
arguments: self, kind: str, message: str, *, origin: str
doc: Print to the CLI (``_vprint(force=True)``) and forward to ``status_callback(kind, message)``. Never raises.

name: _emit_diagnostic_status
doc: A diagnostic on the lifecycle rail, without changing legacy formatting.

name: _emit_status
doc: Emit a lifecycle status message (CLI + gateway ``status_callback``).

name: _emit_warning
doc: Emit a user-visible warning for degraded side paths where the turn continues but the user must know.

name: _emit_startup_warning
doc:
A warning raised during ``__init__`` that the user must see (e.g. a memory provider that
could not be recovered). The CLI prints it. Other drivers get a sticky warn ``AgentNotice``:
Desktop renders notices but no warn-kind ``status.update``, and the messaging gateway wires
its callbacks per turn, after init, so a notice raised before then waits for
:meth:`_replay_startup_warnings` on the first turn.

name: _warn_context_overflow_blocked
arguments: self, reason: str, preflight_tokens: int, threshold_tokens: int
doc:
Warn (deduped on the block *kind* — ``cooldown`` / ``ineffective`` — not the countdown string;
cleared by ``_clear_context_overflow_warn``) when context is over the threshold but compression is blocked.

name: _warn_uncompressed_context_overflow
doc:
Deduped warning when uncompressed context exceeds the model limit; points the user at /compact.

When compression is explicitly disabled (compression.enabled: false), long sessions can grow past
the model context window with no compression to shrink them (#89297). Surface an actionable warning
so the user knows to run /compact or enable compression.

name: _clear_context_overflow_warn
doc: Reset the blocked-overflow warning dedup so it can re-fire on the next blocked turn.

name: _emit_notice
doc: Fire a structured ``AgentNotice`` to the active driver (TUI / CLI).

name: _emit_notice_clear
doc: Clear a previously-fired sticky notice by ``key`` (e.g. on recovery).

name: _emit_wait_notice
doc:
Rewrite the live status line (CLI spinner, TUI ``thinking.delta``, gateway activity)
so long provider waits are not an anonymous spinner.

name: _buffer_retry_message
doc:
Buffer a retry/fallback line as ``(kind, text)`` until we know whether the turn recovered.

``kind`` is ``"status"`` (replays via ``_emit_status``), ``"vprint"`` (``_vprint(force=True)``) or
``"warn"`` (``_emit_warning``).

name: _clear_status_buffer
doc: Drop buffered retry messages — call on successful recovery.

name: _emit_pending_fallback_notice
doc:
Surface the one-shot fallback-switch notice on successful recovery: a provider switch is durable
state operators must see, unlike the retry chatter ``_clear_status_buffer`` drops. Emitted once, then
cleared; on terminal failure the buffered switch line is flushed instead (``_flush_status_buffer``).

name: _flush_status_buffer
doc: Emit buffered retry messages — call on terminal failure so the user sees what was tried.

name: _call_quietly
doc: Call ``cb(*args)`` if set, swallowing errors; True when it ran without raising.

name: _deliver_to_stream_callbacks
doc: Send ``text`` to the display + TTS delta callbacks; True if at least one accepted it.

name: _enqueue_stream_hook
arguments: self, event: str, *, label: str | None=None, **fields: Any
doc: Best-effort plugin stream hook enqueue; never raises into the stream path.

name: _reset_stream_delivery_tracking
doc:
Reset tracking for text delivered during the current model response.

Flushes the think scrubber's benign tail first, routed through the context scrubber (a span
straddling the boundary must still be caught), then the context scrubber's own tail.

name: _current_streamed_assistant_text
doc:
Visible assistant text streamed so far this turn. Backed by a list of pieces: ``+=`` on a string
attribute copies the whole reply on every delta (quadratic). Hot-path emptiness checks look at
``_streamed_assistant_text_parts`` so they do not join per token.

name: _record_streamed_assistant_text
doc: Accumulate visible assistant text emitted through stream callbacks (superseded writers excluded).

name: _interim_visible_and_streamed
doc: (visible content, streamed text), both think-stripped and whitespace-normalized.

name: _interim_content_fully_streamed
doc:
Exact-match variant for the gateway interim path: a True verdict finalizes the bubble
as-is, so a truncated prefix must fall through to a full-text resend (#88954).

name: _extract_codex_interim_visible_parts
doc:
Visible Codex commentary (``phase=commentary`` items), one string per message item.

``phase=analysis`` stays hidden (scratchpad); with ``display.show_commentary=false``
commentary stays on the reasoning channel.

name: _visible_commentary
doc: Think-stripped, redacted commentary text ("" when nothing visible remains).

name: _extract_codex_interim_visible_text
doc: All visible Codex commentary joined, for comparison/fallback.

name: _interim_assistant_visible_text
doc:
Assistant text eligible for interim delivery: structured Codex commentary first — a response can
hold commentary AND a partial final answer while tools are pending, and treating content as
progress leaks the answer early — else top-level content (may be a parts list).

name: _deliver_interim
arguments: self, visible: str, *, already_streamed: bool, record: list[str]
doc: Hand ``visible`` to ``interim_assistant_callback`` and mark ``record`` delivered; swallows callback errors.

name: _fire_streamed_codex_commentary
doc: Deliver a completed live Codex commentary message immediately.

name: _emit_interim_assistant_message
doc:
Surface a real mid-turn assistant commentary message to the UI layer. Does NOT set
``_response_was_previewed`` ("the final response was shown") — the CLI would then suppress a
different final summary.

name: _ensure_stream_writer_state
doc:
Lazily create the single-writer guard fields (#65991).

The fields are normally set unconditionally in ``agent_init`` (``_STREAM_STATE``), so every
``__init__``-built agent shares ONE lock from birth and the lazy path below is never taken by
two threads. Only agents constructed via ``AIAgent.__new__`` (test doubles, legacy/partially-
initialized instances) skip that path; claiming/checking the writer must not crash those, so
initialize the fields on first use.

name: _claim_stream_writer
doc:
Claim exclusive ownership of the delta sink for this stream attempt; returns its writer token.

Every attempt (each provider path, each retry) claims right before consuming; claiming bumps
the shared token, so an earlier attempt still alive on another thread is superseded and its
late chunks fenced out. Stored per-thread: a thread that never claimed can never be fenced.

See #65991.

name: _stream_writer_is_current
doc:
True when ``token`` is still the active writer, so a stream loop can bail the instant it is superseded.

active writer — i.e. no newer stream attempt has claimed the sink since (#65991).

name: _stream_writer_superseded
doc:
True when this thread claimed the sink but a newer attempt has since claimed it (never for a non-claimer).

stream attempt has since claimed it — i.e. this thread is a stale writer whose chunks must be
dropped (#65991).

name: _note_dropped_stream_writer
doc: Record + log that a superseded stream's delta was discarded.

name: _emit_stream_end
arguments: self, *, final_text: str, finished: bool, error: str | None

name: _fire_stream_delta
doc: Fire all registered stream delta callbacks (display + TTS).

name: _fire_reasoning_delta
doc:
Fire reasoning callback if registered; superseded writers are fenced like content deltas.

``inline`` marks text recovered from ``<think>`` blocks in content; any other call is a native
provider reasoning delta and stops inline forwarding for the rest of this model response.

name: _fire_tool_gen_started
doc: Notify the display layer that the model is generating tool call arguments (spinner for large payloads).

name: _has_stream_consumers
doc: Return True if any streaming consumer is registered.

name: stream_diag_init
doc: Fresh per-attempt diagnostic dict; mutated in place by the streaming functions and read by the retry block.

name: stream_diag_capture_response
arguments: agent: Any, diag: dict[str, Any], http_response: Any
doc: Snapshot headers + HTTP status at stream open (so they survive a drop before the first chunk). Best-effort.

name: flatten_exception_chain
doc:
Compact ``Outer(msg) <- Inner(msg) <- ...`` rendering, walking ``__cause__`` then ``__context__``
(deduped, max 4 deep): the OpenAI SDK wraps httpx errors so only the wrapper class is visible at
the catch site; the inner RemoteProtocolError/ConnectError/ReadError says WHY the stream died.

name: _diag_fields
doc:
(http_status, bytes, chunks, elapsed, ttfb, serving_provider, finish_reason_seen, upstream)
for the retry log line; ``-`` when unknown.

name: log_stream_retry
arguments: agent: Any, *, kind: str, error: BaseException, attempt: int, max_attempts: int, mid_tool_call: bool, diag: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Structured WARNING to ``agent.log`` for a transient stream drop + retry, always logged regardless of
UI verbosity. With *diag*, also records upstream headers, HTTP status, bytes/chunks, elapsed and TTFB on
the dying attempt — enough to tell "one CF edge / downstream provider" from "random across runs".

The ``serving_provider`` field names the downstream that actually served the attempt (relays re-roll it
per request and report it only in the chunk body), so a drop can be attributed to a provider even when
