route keyed users onto a higher-priority backend's free tier. Cheap, no network.

name: supports_extract
doc:
True if this provider implements :meth:`extract` (sync or ``async def`` —
the dispatcher awaits coroutine functions).

name: search
doc: Execute a web search. Callers gate on :meth:`supports_search`.

name: extract
doc:
Extract content from URLs (callers gate on :meth:`supports_extract`); may be ``async def``.
Returns ``[{"url", "title", "content", "raw_content", "metadata"?, "error"?}, ...]`` (``error``
only on per-URL failure). Ignore unknown ``kwargs`` (``format``, ``include_raw``, ``max_chars``).

name: _read_config_key
doc: Resolve a dotted config key from ``config.yaml``. Returns None on miss.

name: _configured_backend
doc:
``web.<capability>_backend`` (preferred) or ``web.backend`` (shared fallback). The managed ``nous``
selection names no provider: it is served by Perplexity (search) and Firecrawl (extract).

name: _keyless_preference
doc:
Keyless walk order, starting at the ring cursor in
:mod:`plugins.web.keyless_mcp` so resolution and dispatch agree on which
vendor a fresh install starts at; the rest follow in ring order.

name: _resolve
doc:
Resolve the active provider for a capability ("search" | "extract").

Rules, in order (see module docstring): explicit config wins even when
``is_available()`` is False (the dispatcher surfaces a precise
"X_API_KEY is not set" error instead of a silent switch); then the single
available capable provider; then the availability-filtered legacy walk;
then the keyless free-tier walk; else None.

name: _keyless_tier_enabled
doc: Read ``web.keyless_fallback`` from config.yaml (default: enabled).

name: _disabled_web_plugin_for
doc:
Plugin key of a *disabled* bundled web plugin that would have provided
the configured backend (``web.<capability>_backend`` → ``web.backend``), or None.

Lets the dispatcher say "re-enable web-firecrawl" instead of "No web extract
provider configured". Resolved from config.yaml rather than the resolved
backend because a disabled provider fails the availability gate and silently
drops to the default. Bundled web plugins live under ``web/<vendor>`` with
the provider name differing only by hyphen/underscore, so both are normalized.

When a user sets ``web.extract_backend: firecrawl`` (or the search equivalent) but also lists
``web-firecrawl`` in ``plugins.disabled``, the provider never registers and the dispatcher would
otherwise emit a misleading "No web extract provider configured. Set web.extract_backend to ..." error —
even though the backend IS configured correctly. This helper detects that case so the dispatcher can
point the user at the actual cause (issue #40190 follow-up: pi314's disabled-plugin symptom).

name: get_active_search_provider
doc: Resolve the currently-active web search provider.

name: get_active_extract_provider
doc: Resolve the currently-active web extract provider.

name: register_subparser
doc: Wire the ``hermes lsp`` subcommand tree into the main argparse.

name: run_lsp_command
doc: Top-level dispatcher for ``hermes lsp <subcommand>``.

name: _all_servers
doc: Config-declared servers (``lsp.servers.<id>.extensions``) ahead of the built-in registry.

name: _recipe_pkg_for
doc: Map a registry ``server_id`` to its install-recipe package key.

name: _backend_warnings
doc: Notes about missing sidecar tools that make a server spawn fine but emit nothing (e.g. shellcheck).

name: file_uri
doc: Return a ``file://`` URI for a path (handles spaces, unicode, Windows drive letters).

name: _folder
doc: Build an LSP ``WorkspaceFolder`` for ``root``.

name: uri_to_path
doc: Inverse of :func:`file_uri`.

name: _end_position
doc: LSP Position at the end of ``text`` (for a whole-document replace range).

name: as_disk_read
doc: ``text`` as ``Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig", errors="replace")`` returns the file holding it.

name: _diagnostic_key
doc:
Content-equality key: severity + code + source + message + range.  Shared with the manager's
cross-edit delta filter (``_diag_key``) so both layers agree on identity.  Range is included so an
identical error at a second site still surfaces as new (the manager line-shifts its baseline first).

name: __init__
arguments: self, *, server_id: str, workspace_root: str, command: list[str], env: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None, cwd: Optional[str]=None, initialization_options: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, seed_diagnostics_on_first_push: bool=False

name: start
doc: Spawn + initialize handshake.  On failure the process is killed and state is ``"error"``; re-call to retry.

name: _describe_exit
doc: Human rendering of the server exit status; empty when the process is still live.

name: failure_details
doc: Exit status + last stderr lines for a failed spawn/initialize; empty for a live server.

name: add_workspace_folder
doc:
Attach another root to a running multi-root server.  Idempotent; the folder is recorded
before the notification is sent so concurrent callers for the same root only announce once.

name: remove_workspace_folder
doc:
Detach ``root`` from a running multi-root server (a removed worktree) so the process keeps
serving its sibling roots instead of being torn down with them.  Idempotent.

name: shutdown
doc:
Best-effort graceful shutdown: ``shutdown`` + ``exit``, wait ``SHUTDOWN_GRACE`` for the
server to honour ``exit``, then SIGTERM/SIGKILL.  Idempotent.

name: _send_request_with_retry
arguments: self, method: str, params: Any, *, timeout: float
doc: Send a request, retrying ``ContentModified`` (-32801) with backoff; other errors propagate.

name: _send_reply
doc: Send a response to a server→client request; silently no-ops when the pipe is gone.

name: _handle_workspace_configuration
doc: Walk dotted ``section`` paths through initializationOptions; null when missing.

name: open_file
arguments: self, path: str, *, language_id: str='plaintext', text: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Send didOpen (first time) or didChange (subsequent); return the new document version.
``text`` is the document content to sync (default: the file on disk) — the deferred write check
syncs the exact pre-/post-edit snapshots of the edit it checks, whatever the disk holds by then.
A supplied text is normalized as the disk read would decode it (BOM, newlines, undecodable bytes),
so a snapshot and the file it was written to sync identically.

name: _evict_lru_docs
doc:
Drop least-recently-touched documents beyond MAX_TRACKED_FILES; didClose the ones the server
has open so it releases its mirror too (version -1 entries were never opened).

name: save_file
doc: Send didSave for ``path``.  Some linters re-scan only on save.

name: _pull_document_diagnostics
doc:
Send ``textDocument/diagnostic`` for one file into the pull store.  Results are tagged with the
version captured at send time, so a didChange racing past the request makes them stale
automatically.  Silently no-ops on errors (server may not support pull).

name: wait_for_diagnostics
arguments: self, path: str, version: int, *, mode: str='document', timeout: Optional[float]=None
doc:
Wait for fresh diagnostics for ``path`` at ``version``; True iff fresh data arrived in budget.

``mode`` is ``"document"`` (5s) or ``"full"`` (10s); ``timeout`` overrides the budget (how
``lsp.wait_timeout`` reaches the loop).  Callers must treat False as "no data", NOT "no errors" —
the stores may still hold stale entries.  Never throws for servers lacking pull support.

name: _await_push
doc: Block until the next publishDiagnostics or ``timeout``; True iff a push woke us.

name: _wait_for_fresh_push
arguments: self, path: str, version: int, timeout: float
doc: Wait until a fresh publishDiagnostics arrives for ``path`` at ``version``+.

name: wait_for_seed
doc:
For a server whose first push per document is a seed (never fresh): wait up to ``timeout``
for that push and return what it carried (the verdict on the text sent with didOpen), or None.
``path`` must be absolute (the key ``open_file`` stored it under).

name: document_text
doc: The text last synced to the server for ``path`` (None when never opened).

name: diagnostics_for
doc:
Merged + deduped push/pull diagnostics for one file.  With ``fresh_only=True`` a store only
contributes once its version tag has caught up to the document's — report paths must use this
so "stale" and "clean" aren't conflated.

name: bind_owner
doc: Attribute writes in this block to ``owner`` (the session id, else the task id).

name: post
arguments: owner: str, path: str, text: str, baseline_text: Optional[str]
doc:
Queue ``text`` (a formatted diagnostics block) for ``owner``.  A note still queued for ``path``
(an older check finished while a newer one was starting) is kept in front, with its baseline.

name: take
doc:
Withdraw ``owner``'s undelivered note for ``path``: a newer edit of the file supersedes it and
diffs against its ``baseline_text``.  The newer check carries it and hands it back to
:func:`restore` only if it ends with no verdict, so the older errors are not lost.

name: restore
doc: Queue ``notes`` (oldest first) withdrawn by :func:`take` again.

name: pop_notes
doc: Every queued ``(path, text)`` for ``owners``, oldest first, and clear them.

name: track_pending
doc:
Record a check of ``owner``'s still running; pass the token to :func:`settled` once its verdict
has been posted (or dropped).

name: settle_for_agent
doc:
Turn end: wait up to ``timeout`` for ``agent``'s running checks, then pop every undelivered
``(path, text)`` verdict.  Returns at once when nothing is running.

name: forward_to_agent
doc:
Move ``agent``'s finished verdicts onto its live-notes queue, which rides the next tool result
(or the next user turn).  Called right before that tool result is built.

name: inline_wait
doc: Seconds the write may still wait for its verdict inline.

name: start
arguments: svc: LSPService, path: str, *, pre_text: Optional[str], post_text: Optional[str]=None, owner: Optional[str]=None, carry: tuple=()
doc:
Schedule the check of ``path`` (already written) on the service loop; the Future resolves to a
:class:`CheckResult`.  ``pre_text`` None = the file is new; ``post_text`` = the content this edit
wrote (None: read the file when the check runs).  ``owner`` = the editing session (None:
no later delivery, nothing to take over); ``carry`` = that session's undelivered notes for this
file (``agent.lsp.deferred``) this edit supersedes: the oldest one's baseline becomes ours.

name: _serialized
arguments: svc: LSPService, abs_path: str, pre_text: Optional[str], post_text: Optional[str], owner: Optional[str], carry: tuple
doc:
Run after any unfinished check of the same file; take over the same session's unfinished check:
its baseline and carried notes become ours, and its result is ours to report when we get no
verdict.  Never cancelled: cancelling mid-spawn would restart a cold server on every rapid edit.

name: _check
arguments: svc: LSPService, abs_path: str, baseline_text: Optional[str], post_text: Optional[str], budget: float
doc:
Verdict on ``post_text`` (the bytes this edit wrote) first; only when it has diagnostics, the
verdict on ``baseline_text`` (cached from an earlier check when that text was checked before) to drop
the pre-existing ones.  The server is left holding the file's current disk content afterwards.
A clean edit costs one round trip, and push-only servers answer the baseline fast in the common
case (errors -> fewer errors is a change they publish).

name: _resync_disk
arguments: svc: LSPService, client: Any, abs_path: str, language_id: str
doc:
Leave the server holding the newest content written to the file (a newer edit, or this check's
baseline sync, may differ from the snapshot just diagnosed); no-op when it already does.  Unknown
newest content (a caller without a snapshot) re-reads the file, as every sync used to.

name: _verdict
arguments: svc: LSPService, client: Any, abs_path: str, version: int, budget: float, use_sync: bool
doc:
Diagnostics on the text synced at ``version``: a synchronous request where the server has one
(``agent.lsp.sync_diagnostics``, ~10ms, so the write can report it inline), else the push/pull
wait.  None = no verdict within ``budget``.

name: _report
arguments: server_id: str, abs_path: str, diags: Optional[_Diags]

name: remember
arguments: self, abs_path: str, text: str, diags: _Diags

name: _short_path
doc: Render *file_path* relative to cwd when it's inside it, else absolute (no ``../..`` chains).

name: _emit
arguments: server_id: str, level: int, message: str

name: _emit_once
arguments: bucket: set, key: tuple, server_id: str, level: int, first: str, repeat: str
doc: Log *first* at *level* the first time *key* is seen, *repeat* at DEBUG thereafter.

significant_calls.expression: _emit(server_id, level if is_first else logging.DEBUG, first if is_first else repeat)

name: log_clean
doc: No diagnostics emitted for *file_path*.  DEBUG.

name: log_disabled
arguments: server_id: str, file_path: str, reason: str
doc: LSP intentionally skipped for this file (feature off, ext unmapped, ...).  DEBUG.

name: log_active
doc: A client started for (server_id, workspace_root).  INFO once per pair, DEBUG thereafter.

significant_calls.expression:
_emit_once(_announced_active, (server_id, workspace_root), server_id, logging.INFO,
               f"active for {workspace_root}", f"reused client for {workspace_root}")

name: log_diagnostics
arguments: server_id: str, file_path: str, count: int
doc: Diagnostics arrived for a file.  INFO every time — rare per edit and what users grep for.

name: log_no_project_root
doc: File had no recognised project marker.  INFO once per file, DEBUG thereafter.

name: log_server_unavailable
doc: Server binary unresolved.  WARNING once per (server_id, binary), DEBUG thereafter.

significant_calls.expression:
_emit_once(
        _announced_unavailable, (server_id, binary_or_pkg), server_id, logging.WARNING,
        f"server unavailable: {binary_or_pkg} not found "
        "(install via `hermes lsp install <id>` or set lsp.servers.<id>.command)",
        f"server still unavailable: {binary_or_pkg}",
    )

name: log_timeout
arguments: server_id: str, file_path: str, kind: str='diagnostics'
doc: A request to the server timed out.  WARNING every time.

name: log_server_error
arguments: server_id: str, file_path: str, exc: BaseException
doc: An unexpected exception bubbled out of the LSP layer.  WARNING.

name: log_spawn_failed
arguments: server_id: str, workspace_root: str, exc: BaseException
doc: The LSP server failed to spawn or initialize.  WARNING.

name: log_skipped_broken
arguments: server_id: str, workspace_root: str, file_path: str, retry_in: Optional[float]=None
doc:
A request was skipped because ``(server_id, root)`` is marked broken.  INFO once per root, then DEBUG:
at default log levels a skipped file and a clean file otherwise look identical (``log_clean`` is DEBUG).
``retry_in`` (seconds, from ``lsp.broken_retry_seconds``) names when the pair gets another try.

significant_calls.expression:
_emit_once(_announced_skipped, (server_id, workspace_root), server_id, logging.INFO,
               f"skipping {_short_path(file_path)}: {workspace_root} marked broken after an earlier failure ({until})",
               f"skipping {_short_path(file_path)}: {workspace_root} marked broken")

name: log_root_excluded
arguments: server_id: str, workspace_root: str, file_path: str, *, invalid: bool=False
doc:
``workspace_root`` matches ``lsp.exclude_roots`` (or the key is malformed and every root is skipped).
INFO once per root — a deliberate gate must still be visible, or an excluded file looks like a clean one —
DEBUG thereafter.

significant_calls.expression:
_emit_once(_announced_excluded, (server_id, workspace_root), server_id, logging.INFO,
               f"skipping {_short_path(file_path)}: {workspace_root} {why}",
               f"skipping {_short_path(file_path)}: {workspace_root} excluded")

name: log_untrusted_skipped
arguments: server_id: str, workspace_root: str, file_path: str
doc:
``server_id`` is not safe in an untrusted workspace and ``workspace_root`` is not trusted.
INFO once per root (a deliberate gate must not look like a clean file), DEBUG thereafter.

significant_calls.expression:
_emit_once(_announced_untrusted, (server_id, workspace_root), server_id, logging.INFO,
               f"skipped: untrusted workspace {workspace_root} ({_short_path(file_path)}); "
               "add it to lsp.trusted_workspaces to run this server there",
               f"skipped: untrusted workspace {workspace_root}")

name: log_reaped
doc:
Idle clients were reaped.  INFO, one line per sweep.

Also forgets the ``log_active`` announcement for those keys so a respawn
re-announces at INFO instead of a misleading DEBUG "reused client".

name: log_released
doc:
Clients were shut down because their workspace went away (worktree released or root deleted).
INFO, one line per event; forgets the ``log_active`` announcement like :func:`log_reaped`.

name: reset_announce_caches
doc: Test-only: clear the dedup caches.  Production code never calls this.

name: _recipe
arguments: strategy: str, pkg: str, bin_name: str, **extra: Any

name: hermes_lsp_bin_dir
doc: Return the Hermes-owned bin staging dir for LSP servers.

name: _native_binary_candidates
doc:
Return platform-native executable candidates for a staged binary, most runnable first.

On Windows the ``.cmd``/``.exe``/``.bat`` wrappers come BEFORE the bare name: npm writes a
POSIX ``#!/bin/sh`` shim under the bare name next to its ``.cmd``, ``os.access(X_OK)`` is
always true there, and ``CreateProcess`` on the shim fails with WinError 193.  The bare name
stays as a last resort for genuinely extension-less executables.

name: _first_existing
doc: First platform-native candidate of any ``base`` that exists on disk.

name: _npm_bin_dir
doc: npm's own ``node_modules/.bin`` under the staging tree, where its ``%~dp0``-relative wrappers work.

name: _existing_binary
doc:
Probe the staging dir (+ npm's bin dir on Windows) then PATH for a binary named ``name``.

``is_windows`` overrides the host check so the Windows resolution is testable as data on every lane.

name: try_install
doc:
Try to install ``pkg``; return the binary path or ``None``.

Only ``"auto"`` installs; ``"manual"``/``"off"`` just probe for an existing
binary.  Results are cached per package and concurrent calls are serialized.

name: _run_installer
arguments: tool: str, pkg: str, cmd: list, *, timeout: int, env: Optional[dict]=None
doc: Run one install subprocess; log and return False on non-zero exit or error.

name: _link_into_bin
doc: Symlink (or copy, where symlinks fail) ``target`` into ``lsp/bin/`` and return the path to use.

name: _node_package_manager
doc: ``lsp.package_manager`` from config (npm default); an unknown value fails closed (``None``).

name: _install_npm
arguments: pkg: str, bin_name: str, extra_pkgs: Optional[list]=None
doc:
Install with the configured Node package manager into ``<staging>`` and link
``node_modules/.bin/<bin_name>`` into ``lsp/bin/``.

name: _install_go
doc: Install a Go module to GOBIN=<staging>.

name: _install_pip
doc: Provision a Python server in its own PM-managed environment.

name: detect_status
doc: Return ``installed``, ``missing``, or ``manual-only`` (for ``hermes lsp status``; spawns nothing).

name: _path_list
doc: A config list of paths, ``~``-expanded; ``None`` when the value is not a list of strings.

name: _parse_exclude_roots
doc: ``lsp.exclude_roots``; ``None`` (fail closed: every root excluded) for a malformed value.

name: parse_trusted_workspaces
doc: ``lsp.trusted_workspaces``; a malformed value trusts nothing extra.

name: _client_key
arguments: srv: ServerDef, root: str, trusted: bool
doc:
Cache key for the client serving ``root``: multi-root servers share one process per
``server_id`` across trusted roots; everything else, untrusted roots included, is keyed per
resolved project root (a shared process keeps the trust its first root spawned it with).

name: run
doc: Submit a coroutine to the loop and block for its result (or raise).

name: __init__
arguments: self, *, enabled: bool, wait_mode: str, wait_timeout: float, install_strategy: str, binary_overrides: Optional[dict[str, list[str]]]=None, env_overrides: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, str]]]=None, init_overrides: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]=None, disabled_servers: Optional[list[str]]=None, idle_timeout: float=DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT, extra_servers: Optional[list[ServerDef]]=None, broken_retry_seconds: float=0.0, warmup_timeout: float=0.0, exclude_roots: Any=None, trusted_workspaces: Any=None

name: create_from_config
doc: Build a service from ``hermes_cli.config``; ``None`` if config can't load.

name: _server_for
doc: Config-declared servers first (they may claim an extension ahead of a built-in), then the registry.

name: handles_extension
doc: True iff a config-declared or built-in server claims ``ext`` (pre-write capture decision).

name: is_active
doc: Return True iff this service should be consulted at all.

name: _broken_key
doc:
``(server_id, per-server root)`` broken-set key, or ``None`` when the file isn't gated in.

Falls back to the workspace root when the per-server resolver fails —
the same key ``_get_or_spawn`` would have used when it failed.

name: enabled_for
doc:
True iff LSP should run for this file: registered non-disabled server, git workspace,
and pair not broken (a failed server costs nothing until ``hermes lsp restart`` / exit).

name: _note_operator_roots
doc:
Remember this thread's ``operator_workspace_roots``.  Called where a tool thread enters (it sees
the session's cwd; the loop thread that spawns servers does not), so trust is per process: a
workspace any session was opened in stays trusted until shutdown.

name: _live_key
doc:
The client key for ``root`` (under ``_state_lock``): a multi-root server started while
``root`` was untrusted keeps its own client after ``root`` becomes trusted, so it is found and
released rather than orphaned.

name: _untrusted_denied
arguments: self, srv: ServerDef, root: str, file_path: str, trusted: bool
doc:
True iff ``srv`` may run project code and ``root`` is not a trusted workspace (deny by default:
only ``UNTRUSTED_SAFE_SERVERS`` start in a checkout the operator has not trusted).

name: _root_excluded
doc: True iff ``root`` matches an ``lsp.exclude_roots`` glob (or the key is misconfigured).

name: _is_broken
doc: Broken-set membership; an entry whose retry deadline passed is dropped so the pair gets one more try.

name: _wait_budget
doc:
``wait_timeout`` for a root with a running client; ``max(wait_timeout, warmup_timeout)`` for a
cold root, whose first request also pays the spawn/initialize and the server's initial program build.

name: snapshot_baseline
doc:
Snapshot current diagnostics for ``file_path`` as the delta baseline (call BEFORE a write).
Best-effort: failures are swallowed so a flaky server can't break a write, but they mark the pair broken.

name: start_edit_check
arguments: self, file_path: str, *, pre_text: Optional[str], post_text: Optional[str]=None, owner: Optional[str]=None, carry: tuple=()
doc:
Non-blocking post-write check (``agent.lsp.edit_check``): a Future of the diagnostics the edit
introduced, or None when LSP doesn't handle the file.  Replaces snapshot_baseline +
get_diagnostics_sync on the write path, which blocked the write on both waits.  ``owner`` = the
editing session; ``carry`` = its undelivered notes for the file this check takes over.
``pre_text`` / ``post_text`` = the edit's own before/after content: the check diagnoses these
snapshots, never whatever another session has written to the file since.

name: _set_delta_baseline
doc:
Store a baseline, refreshing recency (pop + reinsert) so eviction tracks write order.
Callers run on arbitrary threads; the multi-step mutation needs the lock (callers don't hold it).

name: get_diagnostics_sync
arguments: self, file_path: str, *, delta: bool=True, timeout: Optional[float]=None, line_shift: Optional[Callable[[int], Optional[int]]]=None
doc:
Synchronously open ``file_path``, wait for diagnostics, return them.  Never raises.

With ``delta`` (default) the result excludes the :meth:`snapshot_baseline`; ``line_shift`` (from
:func:`agent.lsp.range_shift.build_line_shift`) remaps that baseline into post-edit coordinates
first, so pre-existing diagnostics that merely moved don't look introduced by this edit.
``[]`` when LSP is disabled, nothing matches, or the server can't be spawned.

name: _apply_delta
arguments: self, file_path: str, diags: _Diags, line_shift: Optional[Callable[[int], Optional[int]]]
doc: Drop diagnostics present in the pre-write baseline, then roll the baseline forward.

name: _detach_broken
doc:
Mark the file's ``(server_id, root)`` pair broken after an outer timeout/error, drop its
client from the live maps and log the failure once; returns the dropped client for the caller
to shut down.  The outer timeout cancels the in-flight spawn before ``_get_or_spawn`` could
record the failure; without this every later write would re-pay the full timeout.  The one
owner of this cleanup: ``_mark_broken_for_file`` (tool threads) and
``_mark_broken_for_file_async`` (the loop) only differ in how they await the shutdown.

name: _mark_broken_for_file
doc: Tool-thread bridge of :meth:`_detach_broken`: shuts the client down through the loop.

name: _mark_broken_for_file_async
doc: Loop-side :meth:`_detach_broken` (``_mark_broken_for_file`` would block on the loop it runs on).

name: shutdown
doc: Tear down all clients and stop the background loop.

name: get_status
doc: Return a snapshot of the service for ``hermes lsp status``.

name: _open_and_wait_async
arguments: self, file_path: str, *, snapshot: bool=False, budget: Optional[float]=None
doc:
Open + wait for FRESH diagnostics: ``[]`` = checked clean, ``None`` = no verdict in budget.

Callers must not substitute stale data for either.  ``snapshot`` mode (pre-write baseline)
skips didSave; both modes wait at most ``budget`` (``lsp.wait_timeout`` unless the caller
computed a cold-root warm-up budget via :meth:`_wait_budget`).

name: _attach_root
arguments: srv: ServerDef, client: LSPClient, root: str
doc: Multi-root servers: announce ``root`` to the shared process instead of spawning another.

name: _spawn_client
arguments: self, srv: ServerDef, root: str, trusted: bool
doc: Resolve the binary and start a client; ``None`` (after logging) when either fails.

name: _touch
doc: Refresh last-used; guarded on membership so a client reaped mid-operation can't resurrect its entry.

name: release_workspace
doc:
Shut down the clients serving ``workspace_root`` or any root beneath it; returns how many.

Called by the worktree cleanup paths BEFORE ``git worktree remove`` so a gateway that outlives the
session does not keep the language server (and its stdio pipes) alive for a tree that no longer
exists.  Multi-root servers only drop the folder.  Idempotent; best-effort — never blocks removal.

name: _detach_roots
arguments: self, is_gone: Callable[[str], bool], *, reason: str
doc:

Resolve the animation state from coarse activity signals.

Priority (highest first) — only one row can show at a time, so the most
salient signal wins:

1. ``error``          → ``FAILED``  (a tool/turn just failed)
2. ``celebrate``      → ``JUMP``    (explicit success beat, e.g. todos done)
3. ``just_completed`` → ``WAVE``    (turn finished cleanly / greeting)
4. ``awaiting_input`` → ``WAITING`` (blocked on the user — outranks the in-flight
   signals below because the turn is paused on *you*, even mid tool call)
5. ``tool_running``   → ``RUN``
6. ``reasoning``      → ``REVIEW``
7. ``busy``           → ``RUN``     (turn in flight, unspecified work)
8. otherwise          → ``IDLE``

name: _load_rgba
doc: Open a path (or take an image) as RGBA.

name: _flood
arguments: w: int, h: int, visited: bytearray, seeds, accept
doc: 4-connected BFS from *seeds* over pixels passing *accept*; returns the visited pixels.

name: _border_flood
arguments: w: int, h: int, visited: bytearray, accept
doc: Flood from every border pixel passing *accept* (edge-connected region only).

name: _unvisited_components
arguments: w: int, h: int, visited: bytearray, accept
doc: Yield each 4-connected component of not-yet-visited pixels passing *accept*, in scan order.

name: _near_key_mask
arguments: image, key: tuple[int, int, int], tol: int=48
doc:
``L`` mask, 255 where a pixel is within *tol* per-channel of *key*.

Tight on purpose: marks only near-pure backdrop so trapped chroma pockets seed the flood while chroma-tinted character pixels stay outside it.

name: _remove_masked
doc:
Clear the pixels *mask* (``L``, 255 = remove) selects, then erode alpha by 1px (3x3 min).

The erosion drops the antialiased key/sprite blend ring (too far from the key to match); the sprite's thick outline keeps the silhouette.

name: remove_background
arguments: image, *, chroma_key: tuple[int, int, int] | None=None, threshold: float=90.0
doc:
Return *image* (RGBA) with its flat background keyed out to transparent.

Strips already carrying a real alpha background (>5% of pixels at/below the floor)
are left alone (holes repaired). Otherwise key out *chroma_key* (or the most common
opaque corner color) from the border inward: a global color match punched holes
wherever an interior highlight matched the backdrop.

name: _repair_internal_alpha_holes
doc:
Fill transparent islands fully enclosed by opaque sprite pixels.

Some providers return "transparent" PNGs with swiss-cheese alpha inside the character; enclosed holes take the average opaque-neighbour color.

name: _fit_to_cell
doc: Crop to content, scale to fit a padded cell, and center on transparent.

name: _drop_side_bleed
doc:
Remove tiny separated left/right lobes (neighbour-pose slivers) before fitting.

Component extraction may group a near sliver with the subject; the column profile still shows it as a low-mass lobe. Only those go (wide poses survive).

name: _thin_groups
doc: ``(start, end)`` for each run of consecutive *indices* at most 4 long.

name: _erase_long_axis_lines
doc: Remove thin slot-spanning guide/floor/divider lines (they survive keying and bridge clean poses).

name: _component_boxes
doc: Connected opaque components as ``[(bbox, mass)]``.

name: _isolate_slot_subject
doc: Keep the slot's real subject; drop detached effects/noise.

name: _has_margin
arguments: size: tuple[int, int], box: tuple[int, int, int, int], fx: float, fy: float
doc: True when *box* leaves empty room on all four edges of an image of *size* (≥4px, ≤12/16px).

name: _group_component_rows
doc: Group component boxes into visual rows, then sort left→right.

name: _merge_related_boxes
doc:
Merge disconnected parts of one subject (capes, tails, props) on the same row.

Merges when vertical spans overlap and the horizontal gap is tiny relative to component size; never bridges the larger gaps between separate poses.

name: _component_crops
doc: Frames as connected subjects in reading order (robust to 2D grids); ``None`` when *frame_count* can't be met.

name: _sever_expected_gutters
doc: Cut narrow transparent bands at expected frame boundaries (shared shadows/1px bridges merge poses).

name: _slot_crops
doc: Slice *strip* into *frame_count* equal, independently cleaned columns (one shared coordinate frame).

name: _content_runs
doc: ``[((left, right), mass)]`` column spans whose alpha exceeds *threshold* (candidate frames).

name: _frame_x_ranges
doc:
Per-frame ``(left, right)`` column ranges from the row's empty gutters.

Extra spans merge across the smallest gaps (a detached halo sits closer to its body than to the next pose); fewer spans than frames → ``None``.

name: _significant_subject_boxes
doc: Merged boxes of components carrying meaningful mass (≥12% of the largest).

name: _is_multi_pose_outlier
arguments: width: int, height: int, med_w: int, med_h: int
doc: A frame several times wider than the median but not proportionally taller.

name: _validate_extracted_frames
doc: Reject rows where one "frame" is really multiple poses (normalization would shrink the whole pet).

name: extract_strip_frames
arguments: strip, frame_count: int, *, chroma_key: tuple[int, int, int] | None=None, method: str='auto', fit: bool=True
doc:
Turn one generated row strip into *frame_count* frames.

Keys out the background, then isolates padded subjects (components, then equal slots). When that fails ``components``
raises while ``auto`` salvages leniently. *fit* centers each frame into a cell; hatching passes ``fit=False`` so
:func:`normalize_cells` can register the whole pet with one shared scale.

name: _salvage_frames
doc: Lenient last resort: gutter ranges (severing expected gutters if needed), else raw slots.

name: _column_profile
doc: Per-column alpha mass — collapse to a 1px-tall strip (fast in C).

name: _best_shift
arguments: ref: list[int], prof: list[int], window: int
doc: Integer dx that best aligns *prof* onto *ref* (1-D cross-correlation; the body dominates, limbs barely move it).

name: normalize_cells
doc:
Register every frame into a 192x208 cell — the deterministic anti-jitter math.

Per-frame crop→scale→center jitters. Instead: align each frame's column profile
to the state's median (locks the body), union-crop through one shared window,
then scale all states by one global factor keyed to median pose height.

name: single_frame
doc: One frame from a standalone image (idle fallback); ``fit=False`` yields the raw keyed sprite for :func:`normalize_cells`.

name: _clear_transparent_rgb
doc: Zero the RGB of fully-transparent pixels (no colored-halo residue).

name: mirror_frames
doc: Flip each frame horizontally (``running-left`` from ``running-right``; per-frame, NOT a strip reverse).

name: compose_atlas
doc: Pack per-state frame lists into the atlas; short states leave trailing cells transparent.

name: validate_atlas
doc: Geometry/occupancy/transparency checks → ``{ok, width, height, errors, warnings, filled_states}``.

name: _check_atlas_cells
doc: Occupancy/collapse/residue checks for a correctly-sized atlas → ``(errors, warnings, filled_states)``.

name: _available
doc: The registered provider *name* if it exists and has credentials, else ``None``.

name: resolve_provider
doc:
Pick the image provider for sprite work.

Preference: ``HERMES_PET_IMAGE_PROVIDER`` (QA override, unknown values ignored),
then *prefer* (desktop picker), then the active provider, then the first available
— each only if ref-capable and configured. With *require_references* off, any
available active provider is accepted (prompt-only base drafts).

name: list_sprite_providers
doc: ``[{name, label, default}]`` per configured ref-capable provider, in preference order; empty hides the picker.

name: _save_local
doc: Return a local path for *image_ref*, downloading it if it's a URL.

name: _rejected_background
doc: True when a provider error is specifically about ``background=transparent`` (a per-model capability; we retry without it).

name: generate
arguments: prompt: str, *, n: int=1, reference_images: list[Path] | None=None, provider: SpriteProvider | None=None, prefix: str='pet_gen', aspect_ratio: str='square'
doc:
Generate *n* sprite images and return their local paths.

*reference_images* grounds the output on a base image (required for rows).
*aspect_ratio* ``"landscape"`` (row strips) gives every frame horizontal room so
winged poses needn't shrink. We *ask* for a transparent background but fall
back to opaque on models that reject the flag. Raises :class:`GenerationError`
if nothing usable comes back.

name: _harden_transparency
doc:
Key out any solid backdrop the provider painted; save as an RGBA PNG.

``background=transparent`` is honored inconsistently, so every base draft gets
the chroma-key pass. Best-effort: a decode failure leaves the original untouched.

name: _run_parallel
doc:
Fan *fn* over *items* in a pool, yielding results in completion order.

``as_completed`` runs on the caller's thread, so result callbacks inherit the
request's bound transport (workers don't). Once *cancelled* trips, queued work
is cancelled and in-flight results dropped.

name: generate_base_drafts
arguments: concept: str, *, n: int=4, style: str='auto', reference_images: list[Path] | None=None, provider: SpriteProvider | None=None, on_draft: Callable[[int, Path], None] | None=None, is_cancelled: Callable[[], bool] | None=None
doc:
Generate *n* candidate base looks for *concept* concurrently; returns image paths.

Drafts are hardened to transparent cutouts; *on_draft(index, path)* fires as each
finishes so UIs can stream previews. *is_cancelled* is polled cooperatively.

name: _humanize_image_error
doc: Turn a raw provider error into a friendly, actionable sentence.

name: _generate_row
arguments: spec: tuple[str, int, int], *, base: Path, label: str, style: str, slug: str, sprite, cancelled
doc:
Generate + slice one animation row, retrying up to ``_ROW_GEN_ATTEMPTS`` times.

Self-healing: a roll whose poses touch (no gutters) slices badly, so
``components`` (raises on touching poses) drives regeneration and only the
final attempt uses lenient ``auto`` slicing. Returns ``(state, None)`` when
cancelled or every attempt failed.

name: hatch_pet
arguments: *, base_image: str | Path, slug: str, display_name: str='', description: str='', concept: str='', style: str='auto', on_progress: ProgressFn | None=None, provider: SpriteProvider | None=None, is_cancelled: Callable[[], bool] | None=None
doc:
Turn an approved base image into a full, installed Hermes pet.

Idle falls back to the base look so the pet always renders. Raises
:class:`GenerationError` on failure. Once *is_cancelled* trips, aborts before
composing/saving so a stopped hatch never writes a half-built pet.

name: _spacing_spec
doc:
(per-pose width px, gap px) for a row of *frame_count* poses.

Pixel counts alone don't hold — the model fills each slot edge-to-edge. The lever
that works is proportional containment: equal cells, whole silhouette inside,
~70% occupancy (still a generous gutter on 1536px, no shrinking).

name: build_base_prompt
arguments: concept: str, *, style: str | None='auto', variation: str=''
doc: The base look: a single, clean, centered full-body mascot; *variation* differentiates drafts.

name: build_row_prompt
arguments: state: str, frame_count: int, concept: str, *, style: str | None='auto'
doc: A row strip: *frame_count* poses of the SAME character, left→right, identity locked to the attached base image.

name: _proxy_state_dir
doc: Proxy state dir (CA key, pidfile, logs), created 0o700; unconditional chmod tightens a pre-existing slack-umask dir.

name: find_iron_proxy
doc: External tools do not require PM platform support; acquire only on a miss.

name: install_iron_proxy
doc: Explicit setup/repair; PM verifies and repairs existing entries too.

name: _verify_checksums_signature
doc:
Best-effort GPG check of checksums.txt in an ephemeral keyring.  False (with a warning) when gpg or the signature
assets are unavailable — SHA-256 stays enforced, gpg is never a hard dependency.  Raises ONLY on a present-but-bad signature.

name: allowlisted_env
doc: Infrastructure-only env (PATH, HOME, locale) — never the operator's secrets.

name: _run
arguments: argv: list[str], *, timeout: int, text: bool=False, **kwargs

name: iron_proxy_version
doc: ``iron-proxy --version`` output, stripped and cached by path.  Empty on failure.

name: _write_private_file
doc:
Create/truncate ``path`` 0o600 from the first byte (no chmod-after TOCTOU), O_NOFOLLOW against a planted
symlink, fchmod to tighten a pre-existing file.

name: _fd_owned_by_us
doc: False iff the open file is owned by another uid (same threat model as the pidfile).

name: ensure_ca_cert
doc: Generate (or return existing) 10-year CA cert + key via the host ``openssl``.

name: mint_proxy_token
doc: Opaque token: recognizable prefix + 128-bit random hex suffix (iron-proxy matches exactly).

name: _read_text_or_none
doc: Stripped file contents, or None when missing/unreadable/empty.

name: _management_token_path
doc: Management-token location; resolving it never creates or changes state.

name: ensure_management_token
doc:
Return the management-API bearer key, minting it on first call.

Stored at the path from :func:`_management_token_path` with 0600 perms.
The daemon receives it via the ``HERMES_IRON_PROXY_MGMT_KEY`` env var
(named in the generated config's ``management.api_key_env``);
``hermes egress reload`` reads the same file to authenticate.

name: _yaml
doc: Shared YAML helpers or None (not a hard requirement for proxy discovery).

name: _parse_listen
doc: ``"host:port"`` -> ``(host, port)``; empty host means loopback.

name: _config_listen
doc: ``(host, port)`` from the first truthy ``proxy.yaml[section][key]``, or None (also when file/ruamel.yaml is missing).

name: _probe_target
doc:
Configured bind host/port to probe — on Linux the docker bridge, where a loopback connect would report a healthy
daemon as down.  ``tunnel_listen`` (CONNECT/MITM) falls back to ``http_listen`` for pre-listener-role-split configs.

name: reload_proxy
doc: ``POST /v1/reload`` (validation failures leave the running config untouched); actionable RuntimeError on any failure.

name: _default_http_listen
doc:
Single bind (v0.39 allows one): docker bridge on Linux (what ``host.docker.internal`` resolves to; loopback is
unreachable from containers), loopback on Docker Desktop (VPNkit).  NEVER 0.0.0.0: a LAN peer with a leaked
sandbox token could spend the operator's API quota.

name: _detect_docker_bridge_ip
doc:
docker0 IPv4 via ``ip -4 addr show docker0``, or None.  SECURITY: validated through
:mod:`ipaddress` so a hostile ``ip`` shim can't inject 0.0.0.0/loopback/multicast/link-local/public.

name: build_proxy_config
arguments: *, mappings: list[TokenMapping], ca_cert: Path, ca_key: Path, tunnel_port: int=_DEFAULT_TUNNEL_PORT, audit_log: Optional[Path]=None, allowed_hosts: Optional[list[str]]=None, upstream_deny_cidrs: Optional[list[str]]=None, http_listen: Optional[list[str]]=None

name: _open_private_append
doc:
O_APPEND|O_CREAT 0o600 + O_NOFOLLOW (planted symlinks refused); fchmod tightens a pre-existing
file (failure fatal iff ``strict_chmod``).  Raises OSError; caller owns the fd.

name: ensure_audit_log
doc: Pre-create the audit log 0o600 (forward-compat: v0.39 never writes it); RuntimeError on any OSError.

name: write_proxy_config
doc:
Serialize the config dict to ``<hermes_home>/proxy/proxy.yaml`` (safe_dump, no Python tags).

The file holds proxy tokens: written 0600 from creation, never at process umask.

name: write_mappings
doc: Persist sandbox-visible tokens to ``mappings.json`` (read by the Docker backend, not iron-proxy).

name: load_mappings
doc: Read mappings.json, if it exists.  Empty list on any error.

name: discover_provider_mappings
doc:
One TokenMapping per known provider whose env var is set (bearer providers first).  Canonical OR any alias
present -> ONE mapping on the canonical name (the subprocess-env builder mirrors aliases).
``available_env_names`` (Bitwarden adapter) overrides the non-empty names in the host env.

name: discover_uncovered_providers
doc: Env names of recognized providers the proxy can't swap (SigV4 / SDK-minted OAuth).

name: merge_mappings
arguments: *, existing: list[TokenMapping], discovered: list[TokenMapping], rotate: bool=False
doc:
Existing tokens are preserved (containers baked with them keep working), hosts/headers/aliases refresh
from ``discovered``; ``rotate=True`` re-mints; undiscovered providers drop.

name: _pid_proc_starttime
doc: /proc/<pid>/stat starttime (field 22) on Linux, else None — cheap PID-recycling detector.

name: _persisted_nonce_path
doc: On-disk nonce sibling of the pidfile, so stop/status in a later CLI process can still defeat PID recycling.

name: _read_persisted_nonce
doc:
Nonce from disk, or None if missing/unreadable/empty/not owned by us (callers fall back to argv0
matching).  O_NOFOLLOW: this read decides whether stop_proxy SIGKILLs a PID.

name: _pid_alive
doc:
True iff ``pid`` is alive AND an iron-proxy process.  PID-reuse defense, in priority order: nonce in
/proc/<pid>/environ, argv[0] basename in /proc/<pid>/cmdline, ``ps -o comm=`` basename (a loose
``"iron-proxy" in cmdline`` would hit ``tail iron-proxy.log``).

name: start_proxy
arguments: *, binary: Optional[Path]=None, config_path: Optional[Path]=None, extra_env: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None, install_if_missing: bool=True, refresh_secrets_from_bitwarden: bool=False, bitwarden_config: Optional[dict]=None
doc:
Spawn iron-proxy as a managed background subprocess (idempotent if already running).  ``refresh_secrets_from_bitwarden``
re-fetches secrets from BWS — the ``credential_source: bitwarden`` rotation promise.

name: _interrupt_guard
doc: Route SIGINT/SIGTERM to ``handler`` for the block (POSIX main thread only); previous handlers restored after.

name: _spawn_daemon
arguments: bin_path: Path, cfg: Path, env: dict[str, str], log_path: Path
doc:
Popen with stdout/stderr appended to ``log_path`` (0o600 from the first byte, O_NOFOLLOW so a planted
symlink e.g. to authorized_keys can't receive output, owner-checked).  Our log fd closes after Popen — the child has its dup.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(
            [str(bin_path), "-config", str(cfg)], env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=log_fd, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            **({} if platform.system() == "Windows" else {"start_new_session": True}),
        )

name: _await_listening
arguments: proc: subprocess.Popen, host: str, port: int, *, on_exit
doc: Poll until ``host:port`` accepts or the grace window lapses (do-while: >=1 check even at 0s); raises ``on_exit()`` if the child dies.

name: _write_pidfile_safely
doc:
O_EXCL + O_NOFOLLOW + ownership check, then persist the nonce.  An existing pidfile is either a concurrent
start (fail cleanly) or a stale crash leftover (unlink and retry once).

name: _build_proxy_subprocess_env
arguments: *, extra_env: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None, refresh_from_bitwarden: bool=False, bitwarden_config: Optional[dict]=None
doc:
Allowlisted infra vars + the secrets named in mappings.  With ``refresh_from_bitwarden`` and a populated
``bitwarden_config`` secrets come from BWS (the rotation guarantee); without ``allow_env_fallback`` any BWS
shortfall fails closed instead of keeping stale host-env values.

name: _bitwarden_shortfall
arguments: allow_env_fallback: bool, error: str, warning: str, *args, cause: Optional[BaseException]=None
doc: Raise ``error`` (chained to ``cause`` when given) unless the operator opted into the legacy host-env fallback (then log ``warning``).

name: _refresh_secrets_from_bitwarden
arguments: env: dict[str, str], needed: set, bitwarden_config: dict, allow_env_fallback: bool
doc: Overwrite ``env[needed]`` with fresh (uncached) BWS values; only mapped names are injected so unrelated BWS secrets never leak.

name: stop_proxy
doc: Returns True if it was running.

name: get_status
doc: Snapshot the proxy state without side effects (called per Docker container create).

name: set_source_environment
doc: Install a per-fetch environment view without changing ``os.environ``.

name: get_source_environment
doc: Return the active per-fetch environment, or the process environment.

name: source_child_env
classify_cli_error
doc: Best-effort mapping of helper-CLI failure text onto the taxonomy.

name: coerce_float
doc: ``float(value)`` with ``default`` for malformed config values.

name: is_valid_env_name
doc: True when ``name`` is a legal environment-variable name.

name: scrub_ansi
doc: Strip ANSI escape sequences (whole CSI/OSC sequences, not just ESC).

name: run_cli
arguments: argv: Sequence[str], *, env: dict[str, str], timeout: float, label: str, timeout_message: str, stdin: Any=subprocess.DEVNULL
doc:
``subprocess.run`` an argv list (never a shell), capturing utf-8 text; timeout
and spawn failure become ``RuntimeError``. Callers own returncode interpretation.

name: run_secret_cli
arguments: argv: Sequence[str], *, allow_env: Sequence[str]=(), extra_env: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None, timeout: float=DEFAULT_CLI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
doc:
Run a secret-manager helper CLI with a minimal, allowlisted env (never the
full post-dotenv ``os.environ``): PATH/HOME/locale basics plus ``allow_env``
and ``extra_env``. ``NO_COLOR=1`` + ANSI-scrubbed stderr; stdin is /dev/null so
a prompting helper fails fast. Pass user refs AFTER a ``--`` terminator.

name: fetch
doc:
Resolve this source's secrets. MUST NOT raise or prompt; ``cfg`` is the
raw ``secrets.<name>`` section and may be malformed.

name: override_existing
doc:
May this source overwrite vars .env / the shell already set? Never extends
to vars claimed by another source (a config error the orchestrator warns about).

name: token_env
doc: Name of the env var holding this source's bootstrap credential.

name: protected_env_vars
doc: Env vars the orchestrator must never let ANY source overwrite.

name: fetch_timeout_seconds
doc: Wall-clock budget the orchestrator enforces around fetch().

name: config_schema
doc: Informational ``{key: {"description": str, "default": Any}}`` for setup UIs.

name: remediation
doc: One-line actionable next step for a failed fetch (pure); "" suppresses the hint.

name: find_bws
doc: External tools do not require PM platform support; acquire only on a miss.

name: install_bws
doc: Explicit setup/repair; PM re-verifies even a warm entry (including force).

name: _derive_encrypted_cache_key
doc:
HKDF the local cache key from the bootstrap BWS token. cryptography is imported
lazily: eagerly mapping ``_rust.pyd`` on Windows blocks the updater replacing it.

name: _write_encrypted_disk_cache
arguments: *, cache_key: _CacheKey, access_token: str, entry: _CachedFetch, home_path: Optional[Path]=None
doc:
Persist an AES-GCM encrypted last-good entry atomically (best-effort). The raw
token only derives the key; a successful write removes the legacy plaintext cache.

name: _read_encrypted_disk_cache
arguments: *, cache_key: _CacheKey, access_token: str, max_age_seconds: float, home_path: Optional[Path]=None
doc: Decrypted encrypted-cache entry if it matches ``cache_key`` and is in-window.

name: fetch_bitwarden_secrets
arguments: *, access_token: str, project_id: str, binary: Optional[Path]=None, cache_ttl_seconds: float=300, use_cache: bool=True, server_url: str='', home_path: Optional[Path]=None, encrypted_cache_enabled: bool=False, encrypted_cache_max_stale_seconds: float=0
doc:
Pull the secrets for ``project_id`` from BSM → ``(secrets, warnings)``.

``server_url``: region / self-hosted instance (empty = US Cloud). With
``encrypted_cache_enabled`` fresh entries are written AES-GCM encrypted and a
last-good entry may be served after NETWORK/TIMEOUT failures for up to
``encrypted_cache_max_stale_seconds`` — independent of the fresh TTL, so
``cache_ttl_seconds: 0`` can coexist with a break-glass offline cache.
Raises ``RuntimeError`` on fatal conditions (missing binary, auth failure,
unparseable output); env_loader catches, the setup wizard lets it propagate.

name: _summarize_bws_stderr
doc:
Reduce a bws (color-eyre) error dump to its numbered cause lines joined with
``; `` (dropping ``Location:``/``Backtrace`` on); raw text if unrecognized.

name: _run_bws_list
arguments: bws: Path, access_token: str, project_id: str, server_url: str=''

name: clear_caches
doc: Drop in-process AND disk caches (plaintext and encrypted), e.g. after a token rotation.

name: unquote_dotenv_value
doc:
Strip one layer of matching surrounding quotes from a dotenv value.

Requires length >= 2 so a lone ``"`` stays intact while ``""``/``''``
correctly yield an empty string.

name: _run_helper
arguments: command: str, secret_key: str, timeout_seconds: float, max_output_bytes: int
doc:
Run the helper via ``/bin/sh -c`` and return its stdout, or None.

The key travels as DATA in ``HERMES_SECRET_KEY``. stdout/stderr are piped
(never inherited); stderr is discarded. Any failure logs structured fields
only and returns None — never raises.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(
            ["/bin/sh", "-c", command], env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,  # stderr captured and DISCARDED — never inherited
            start_new_session=True,  # so the hard timeout can kill the whole group
        )

name: _parse_dotenv_map
doc: Parse a KEY=VALUE blob; comments and non-env-shaped lines are skipped.

name: _validate_references
doc: ``(valid_refs, warnings)``: keep valid env names bound to stripped ``op://`` strings.

name: _auth_fingerprint
doc:
SHA-256 prefix over everything `op` would authenticate with (token, account,
Connect host/token, ``OP_SESSION_*``), so a new identity never sees old cached values.

name: find_op
doc:
Resolve a usable ``op`` binary, or None. A pinned ``binary_path`` is used
verbatim — pinned-but-missing returns None rather than falling back to PATH.

name: _scrub
doc: Full ECMA-48 ANSI strip (so a control sequence can't hide text after a redaction marker) + trim.

name: _run_op_read
arguments: op: Path, reference: str, *, account: str='', token_value: str=''
doc:
Resolve one ``op://`` reference; raises ``RuntimeError`` on any failure, including
an exit-0 empty value (applying it would clobber a good credential with ``""``).

name: fetch_onepassword_secrets
arguments: *, references: dict[str, str], account: str='', token_env: str=_DEFAULT_TOKEN_ENV, binary: Optional[Path]=None, binary_path: str='', use_cache: bool=True, cache_ttl_seconds: float=300, home_path: Optional[Path]=None
doc:
Resolve ``references`` (name → ``op://…``) to ``(secrets, warnings)``.

Raises ``RuntimeError`` only when no ``op`` binary is available; per-ref
failures become warnings. Only a complete, error-free pull is cached, so a
transient auth failure isn't frozen in for the whole TTL window.

name: apply_onepassword_secrets
arguments: *, enabled: bool, env: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None, account: str='', service_account_token_env: str=_DEFAULT_TOKEN_ENV, binary_path: str='', override_existing: bool=True, cache_ttl_seconds: float=300, home_path: Optional[Path]=None
doc:
Resolve configured ``op://`` references and set them on ``os.environ``
(``hermes secrets onepassword sync --apply``). Never raises. Refs already
satisfied by the env (when ``override_existing`` is false) and the token var

arguments: secrets_cfg: dict, home_path: Path, environ: Optional[MutableMapping[str, str]]=None
doc:
Fetch from every enabled source and apply the merged result to ``environ``
(default ``os.environ``).

Precedence per env var, most-specific intent first: (1) ``secrets.preserve_existing``
names always keep a pre-existing value, even against ``override_existing: true``;
(2) pre-existing .env/shell value, unless the winning source has
``override_existing: true``; (3) mapped sources in configured order; (4) bulk
sources in configured order. First claim wins: a later source carrying the same
var gets ``skipped_claimed`` plus a conflict warning — never a silent clobber,
and ``override_existing`` never applies across sources.

Profile aliasing: under a named profile an applied ``FOO_<PROFILE>``
(credential-shaped suffixes only) also hydrates canonical ``FOO``, under the
same guards; disabled with ``secrets.profile_alias: false``.

1. 2. 3. 4. See #58073.
See #51447.

doc:
Alias the client ``tool_search`` declaration for xAI; returns ``(tools, {alias: "tool_search"})``.

If a real tool already holds ``hermes_tool_search``, the bridge takes a ``_2``/``_3`` suffix.

name: _static_prompt_instructions
doc: Stable leading system/developer prefix used for cache routing (later messages are conversation state).

name: _add_prompt_cache_key
arguments: api_kwargs: dict[str, Any], *, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], tools: list[dict[str, Any]] | None, supports_prompt_cache_key: bool, session_id: str | None=None, cache_scope_id: str | None=None
doc:
Add a content-addressed ``prompt_cache_key`` only for a capable endpoint.

``cache_scope_id`` (compression-lineage root) beats ``session_id`` so the key
survives compression rotation. A caller-supplied key is authoritative but is
bounded to OpenAI's 64-char cap in place. Shares the Responses transport's hash
so equivalent prefixes hit one bucket across modes.

``cache_scope_id``, when provided, is the rotation-stable logical scope (compression-lineage root —
agent/prompt_cache_scope.py) and takes precedence over the physical ``session_id`` so the key survives
context-compression session rotation (#79017).

name: _has_positive_completion_tokens
doc: Return whether a response usage object proves text was generated.

name: router_timeout_shim_may_follow
doc: True while streamed text is still a prefix of the shim sentinel (hold it back until judged).

name: is_router_timeout_shim
doc:
Recognize a router failure encoded as a successful ChatCompletion (#68396).

Some OpenAI-compatible routers answer an upstream connect timeout with HTTP 200 and the
sentinel as the sole assistant message. Only the exact sentinel, with no tool calls and no
positive ``completion_tokens``/``output_tokens`` proof of generation, is a shim — a model
that really produced those words keeps its usage evidence. Shared by every consumer of an
OpenAI-compatible response: ``validate_response``, the stream assembler, the
iteration-limit summary and the auxiliary ``_validate_llm_response``.

name: _reasoning_config_for_model
doc:
Clamp Hermes' extended effort set (``ultra``) to the OpenAI-compat wire vocabulary.

Hermes' internal effort set extends the wire vocabulary with ``ultra`` (the /reasoning command documents
none..xhigh|max|ultra). OpenAI- compatible wires — OpenRouter chief among them — accept exactly
max|xhigh|high|medium|low|minimal|none and reject the extension with HTTP 400 (#89503). Clamp against
the declared wire vocabulary via the shared policy in ``agent.reasoning_effort``; provider profiles with
narrower sets clamp again downstream.

name: _build_gemini_thinking_config
doc: Translate Hermes/OpenRouter-style reasoning config to Gemini thinkingConfig.

name: _snake_case_gemini_thinking_config
doc: Convert Gemini thinking config keys to the OpenAI-compat field names.

name: _raise_gemini_thinking_max_tokens
arguments: model: str, reasoning_config: dict | None, requested: Any
doc: Raise Gemini output caps that thinking tokens (billed against max_tokens) would otherwise exhaust.

name: _is_openai_api_base_url
doc:
True only for the exact api.openai.com host (implies ``prompt_cache_key`` support).

Not a substring match: Azure / strict compat endpoints stay opt-in via ``supports_prompt_cache_key``.

arguments: model: Any, base_url: Any=None, provider: Any=None

name: _wire_reasoning_carriers
doc:
Reasoning keys an assistant message may carry on this route; the rest are stripped.

``message_sanitization.route_reasoning_carriers`` owns the table; keys the route rejected
this session were already removed upstream by ``reapply_reasoning_echo``. The table replays
``reasoning_details`` to OpenRouter-format gateways (OpenRouter, Kilo, Vercel AI Gateway,
Nous Portal) and to vendors documenting it (Novita, MiniMax /v1, TokenHub), never to strict
schemas (Groq, Mistral, Cerebras, opencode relays: ``property 'reasoning_details' is
unsupported`` / ``Extra inputs are not permitted`` / ``no such field``, #70233).
The Portal is back on the list: the "cumulative replayed-reasoning budget" blamed for #118182
does not exist in the Portal code and ~440 live replay requests (up to 32 KB of reasoning)
returned no 400; the observed failures were an upstream content filter surfaced as
"Provider returned error". Portal lanes that reject a carrier are handled by the
per-(provider, host, model) reactive strip. Stored history always keeps every carrier.

name: _has_replayable_thought_signature
doc:
Whether OpenRouter's Gemini sidecar contains a usable thought signature.

Gemini accepts the signature either directly or under its ``google``
namespace.  Replaying an empty or non-string value makes a multimodal
request fail with ``Corrupted thought signature``; omit that sidecar while
leaving the stored history untouched.

arguments: msg: Any, strip_extra_content: bool, strip_reasoning: frozenset=frozenset(), native_reasoning_details_type: str | None=None, *, mistral_tool_ids: bool=False
doc:
Sanitized copy of ``msg``, or None when nothing needs stripping.

Drops persistence sidecars, ``_``-prefixed scaffolding markers, tool-call ``call_id`` /
``response_item_id`` (and ``extra_content`` unless Gemini), an assistant
``tool_calls: []`` / ``null`` (strict providers reject both), ``name``
on tool results (schema-valid only on user/assistant messages; strict
providers reject it with ``contains item with unknown key name``), and the reasoning
keys in ``strip_reasoning`` (carriers the route does not read, ``_wire_reasoning_carriers``).
On a route that reads ``reasoning_details``, private ``<provider>.native_assistant`` carriers still go only to the
profile that declared that exact type: another provider's signed replay is meaningless (or
rejected) elsewhere, and stored history keeps it for a return to the original provider.
``mistral_tool_ids`` maps the call ``id`` and the result ``tool_call_id`` through
``_mistral_tool_id`` from the pairing key the result writers use (``coalesce_tool_call_id``:
``call_id`` first, call half of a composite ``call|item`` id), so each pair stays matched.

doc:
Alias provider-reserved function names on the wire; returns ``(tools, {alias: original_name})``.

An alias already taken by a real tool gets a ``_2``/``_3`` suffix. ``name_of``/``rename``
adapt the tool shape (Responses ``{name}`` by default; chat_completions passes ``function.name``).

name: _xai_prefers_native_web_search
doc:
True when xAI Responses should use Grok's native ``web_search`` built-in.

Web-search registry first, then the legacy ``_get_search_backend`` probe; fails closed to native (True).

Delegates to the web-search registry's provider resolution (which reads ``web.search_backend`` /
``web.backend`` from config) and checks whether the resolved provider is xAI. On any resolution failure,
returns True (fail-closed to native — preserves the #48108 incomplete-hang fix rather than risk
reintroducing it).

name: _reserves_tool_search
doc: True when the Responses endpoint owns the ``tool_search`` namespace (xAI, OpenAI, ChatGPT Codex).

name: _openai_prefers_native_web_search
doc:
True when the active web-search backend selects OpenAI's server-side ``web_search``.

Same contract as :func:`_xai_prefers_native_web_search` with one deliberate
difference: it fails CLOSED (False). A resolution failure must leave the client-side
Hermes tool in place rather than swap in a built-in the endpoint might reject.

Only consulted for the Codex backend (``chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex``); a custom
OpenAI-compatible endpoint does not implement the server-side tool.

name: _alias_wire_tools
arguments: response_tools: Any, params: dict[str, Any], is_xai_responses: bool, is_codex_backend: bool=False
doc:
Apply provider-reserved tool-name aliasing; returns ``(tools, {alias: original})`` for THIS request.

xAI: a client ``web_search`` collides with Grok's native search — native mode
swaps it 1:1 for the built-in, client mode keeps Hermes dispatch under an alias.

OpenAI Codex: the Responses endpoint carries the same collision, so the backend
selection drives the same 1:1 swap (``web.search_backend: openai-native``).

name: _resolve_reasoning
doc:
``(effort, enabled)`` for the request, effort clamped (never escalated) to the endpoint's vocabulary.

A profile-declared ``()`` (or a model that takes no ``reasoning`` field on its route) means "no
reasoning parameters accepted" (400 on any reasoning field) and disables reasoning outright:
``(None, False)``. An explicit ``reasoning_effort: none`` on a route whose vocabulary has ``none``
resolves to ``("none", False)`` so the disable goes on the wire instead of being omitted — omitting
it re-enables the model's default effort (gpt-5.6 defaults to ``medium``, #75227).

name: _default_prompt_cache_retention_for_request
doc: Return ``24h`` for supported hosts/models (Bedrock Mantle, Meta).

name: _is_openai_api_origin
doc: Exact host, so a Responses-compatible proxy or a lookalike subdomain keeps the generic contract.

name: _is_official_openai_responses_route
doc: Astra on the canonical API origin only.

name: _codex_efforts_for_route
arguments: model: Any, base_url: Any, *, is_codex_backend: bool=False
doc:
Effort vocabulary for a Responses route; ``()`` when the model takes no ``reasoning`` field at all.

Keeps Astra's new vocabulary off unrelated Responses-compatible endpoints, and sends nothing for the
chat-era OpenAI families (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, ...) on api.openai.com, which 400 on any ``reasoning``
key (#76255). Only the exact OpenAI origin is judged: a relay serving those ids may translate.

name: _sanitize_astra_request_kwargs
arguments: kwargs: dict[str, Any], model: Any, base_url: Any
doc:
Astra's official-API contract, applied AFTER ``request_overrides`` so an override can't put a
rejected field back on the wire: ``reasoning.effort`` is ``low..max`` only (``none``/``minimal``
400), sampling and logprob knobs are rejected, and cache lifetime is fixed server-side (the
pre-5.6 ``prompt_cache_retention`` knob is dropped here; ``prompt_cache_options`` is already
stripped on every route by ``build_kwargs``).

name: _content_cache_key
arguments: instructions: str, tools: Optional[list[dict[str, Any]]], scope_id: str=''
doc:
``pck_<sha256[:24]>`` of (scope_id, instructions, name-sorted tools), or None if nothing static.

Routing hint only; ``scope_id`` keeps unrelated sessions off one bucket.

``scope_id`` (pass ``_cache_scope_from_session_id(session_id)``) keeps unrelated sessions — independent
conversations, main vs. child/subagent, sibling children — from concentrating onto the same bucket
merely because their static prefix matches (see #78941), while still letting recurring cron fires of one
job share a stable key across their timestamped session_ids (the original #51395/#52295 fix this built
on). Sorting tools by name keeps the hash insertion-order independent.

name: _profile_declared_efforts
arguments: provider: Any, model: Optional[str], base_url: Any=None
doc:
Provider-profile-declared reasoning-effort vocabulary, or None (fail-open).

Resolves by endpoint host first, then by provider name: a ``custom:<name>`` entry pointed
at a host with a registered profile must follow that host's vocabulary, not the generic
custom declaration. Lazy import: provider plugins import this transport during registry
discovery.

name: _is_azure_foundry_responses
doc: True for Microsoft Foundry's Responses API (provider id, else host match — not substring).

name: _is_post_tool_replay
doc:
True when ``messages`` end on a tool-result run issued by the preceding assistant turn.

Azure Foundry rejects only this post-tool shape when encrypted reasoning is
replayed, so only the *trailing* messages are checked (a whole-history scan
would make suppression sticky). Call ids resolve like ``_chat_messages_to_responses_input``.

name: _is_azure_responses
doc:
True for any Azure-hosted Responses endpoint: the ``azure-foundry`` provider, a resource-level
``*.openai.azure.com`` host, or the project-scoped ``*.services.ai.azure.com`` gateway.

name: _newest_reasoning_only
doc:
Copy of ``messages`` keeping ``codex_reasoning_items`` only on the newest assistant row that has any.
Foundry rejects a request that replays encrypted reasoning from more than one prior response (HTTP 400
"Conflicting authenticated continuation identities", #105369). ``compaction`` checkpoints stay everywhere.
A trimmed row is marked ``codex_reasoning_trimmed`` so the converter still drops its ``msg_*`` id (#97427).

name: _native_compaction_active
doc:
True only when the caller's eligibility gate produced a non-empty payload.

Every native-compaction wire effect hangs off this predicate, so a persisted
checkpoint cannot keep reshaping requests after the gate closes.

name: _coerce_timeout
doc: Finite positive number -> float; anything else (None, bool, str, inf) -> None.

name: _sends_all_turns
_reasoning_fields
arguments: model: str, params: dict[str, Any], *, effort: Any, enabled: bool, replay_encrypted_reasoning: bool, is_xai_responses: bool, is_github_responses: bool, all_turns: bool=False
doc:
``reasoning`` / ``include`` request fields for the endpoint family.

xAI 400s on ``reasoning.effort`` outside its allowlist; GitHub Models takes a
verbatim ``github_reasoning_extra`` and never ``include``. A disabled ask resolved to
``effort="none"`` is sent as ``{"effort": "none"}`` — the wire has no other way to switch
a reasoning model's default effort off (#75227). ``all_turns`` adds ``context: "all_turns"``
so the model renders replayed reasoning from earlier user turns (``_sends_all_turns``).

name: reject_all_turns
doc:
400 naming ``reasoning.context``/``all_turns`` on a request that carried the opt-in: omit it for that
model for the rest of the session. False otherwise, so it buys at most one retry per model.

name: drop_unverified_replay
doc:
First ``invalid_encrypted_content`` rung: drop the replayed blobs the failing request could not vouch
for (not stamped by exactly its endpoint + model), keeping the session's own continuity. Returns the
count removed from the first list; 0 means only the route's own blobs were sent.

name: _resolve_issuer_kind
doc: Classify the current Responses endpoint from transport params (stashed for normalize_response).

name: convert_messages
doc: Convert OpenAI chat messages to Responses API input items.

name: convert_tools
doc: Convert OpenAI tool schemas to Responses API function definitions.

name: build_kwargs
arguments: self, model: str, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], tools: Optional[list[dict[str, Any]]]=None, **params
doc:
Build Responses API kwargs (calls convert_messages/convert_tools internally).

the proven identities (PID + create time) are swept afterwards.

exactly the #103567 loss window.

arguments: root: Path, recipe: Recipe, phases: tuple[str, ...] | list[str] | None=None, phase_timeout: float=DEFAULT_PHASE_TIMEOUT, ready_timeout: float=DEFAULT_READY_TIMEOUT, skip_start: bool=False, port_override: int | None=None, stop_on_failure: bool=True, on_output: Callable[[str], None] | None=None

phase failed) boot ``recipe.start``, poll readiness, and tear the process group down.

A ``compose`` recipe refuses outright when the project already has running
containers: ``docker compose build`` + ``up`` replaces them on an image-hash
change, destroying any container-local state they carry -- this has caused a
real state-loss incident (#103567). The check is best-effort and read-only
(``docker compose ps``); when it cannot run at all, verify proceeds rather than
blocking on an unrelated environment gap, matching every other recipe kind's
behavior when its own tooling is unavailable.

doc:
Record one attempt as ``unknown`` with a cause this process actually observed.

``recover_interrupted_executions`` sweeps every attempt whose owner is provably
dead, and knows nothing but that absence — so all it can write is
``_OWNER_GONE_REASON``, which asserts a scheduler restart. A waiter that held the
worker's ``Popen`` knows more: the owner was that external worker, and it exited
with a known status. Without this, a manual run whose worker dies is filed as
"Scheduler restarted ..." (a restart that never happened) and, because the sweep
leaves the row terminal, the waiter reports success and never records the run —
the job's ``fire_claim`` then blocks the next manual fire for the whole lease
(#128509).

unknown. Only the CAUSE becomes truthful. Returns False — leaving the caller to
fall back to the generic sweep — when the row is absent, already terminal, owned by
this process, inside the handoff adoption grace, or owned by a live process: a
