which case the store is marked degraded and the MCP orphan sweep still runs.

name: _advance_or_drop_recurring
doc:
Persist the recurring jobs' advance before any runs; when the store refuses it, drop them
(no durable advance -> a crash mid-run would re-fire them, so skipping is the at-most-once
side). One-shots still go through their own fire claim.

name: _pre_dispatch_housekeeping
doc:
Admission reconcile, legacy upgrade drain and dead-owner reap, run under the tick lock
before due jobs are read.

name: _tick_admitted
arguments: verbose: bool=True, adapters=None, loop=None, sync: bool=True, *, can_dispatch=None, headless: bool=False
doc:
Check and run all due jobs. File-locked so only one tick runs at a time (gateway ticker vs
standalone daemon / manual tick). ``can_dispatch``: optional gate; false leaves due jobs for the
next allowed tick. ``headless``: the tick runs outside any gateway (system crontab, ``hermes
cron tick``) and must refuse agent jobs rather than spawn one. Returns the number of jobs
executed (0 if another tick holds the lock).

name: _committed_dependency_site_packages
doc:
The dependency ``site-packages`` PM committed for this install, or ``None``.

Asked of PM's own committed selection -- the record ``activate_dependencies`` resolves
at process boot -- rather than re-derived from this process's ``sys.path``: the record
belongs to this install (``install_state_dir``, shared by every profile it serves). A
runner that owns its dependencies (wheel / pipx / developer venv / Nix: no committed
generation) has nothing to restore, so ``None`` means "pin the tree only" and nothing
is invented.

name: pin_hermes_tree_on_pythonpath
doc:
Prepend ``repo_root`` -- and, when this runner has one, the committed dependency
generation's ``site-packages`` -- to the worker env's own PYTHONPATH (never
``os.environ``'s).

Skipped when ``repo_root`` is the interpreter's ``purelib``: under a wheel / pipx /
uv-tool install ``cron/`` lives in site-packages itself, which is already importable,
and pinning it would move site-packages ahead of the stdlib on ``sys.path``.

Order (checkout, generation, sanitizer-kept) mirrors ``activate_dependencies``' own
``sys.path``. For the cron worker, its boot (``cron/worker_bootstrap.py``) then re-selects
and leases the committed generation before any third-party import, and exits the worker
if it cannot.

name: record_unknown_worker_outcome
doc:
Project only this fire's uncertain outcome, without retrying its side effects.

A terminal ledger row alone does not retire the job claim or notify its owner.
Fence the notice and bookkeeping together so recovery cannot overwrite a newer
fire or duplicate a failure the worker already recorded.

name: external_worker_exited_reason
doc:
Cause for an attempt whose restart-safe worker this process watched exit.

The generic dead-owner sweep can only say the owner vanished, so it names a
scheduler restart — but this waiter never lost its scheduler: it handed the
attempt to the external worker and then saw that worker exit with this status.
The run is still ``unknown`` rather than ``failed`` (whether side effects ran is
still unknown); only the cause becomes truthful (#128509).

name: _report_fields
arguments: store: str, error: str, since: Optional[float]
doc: The fields `cron status`, doctor and the home-channel notices print for an unwritable store.

name: _key
doc:
Record key for a store: its resolved path (default: the active store). Callers pass both
resolved (cron store) and unresolved (tick-lock dir, profile homes) paths for one store.

name: note_unwritable
arguments: exc: OSError, consequence: str, site: str, skipped_jobs: Iterable[dict]=(), cron_dir: Optional[Path]=None
doc:
Record a failed write to ``cron_dir`` (default: the active store); WARN once, when the store
enters the degraded state. Callers skip the dispatch that needed the write: no job runs
without a durable advance/fire claim.

name: note_writable
doc: A jobs.json save landed: clear the degraded state for that store.

name: outage_covers
arguments: cron_dir: Path, due_at: float, grace: float
doc: Whether a run due at ``due_at`` fell inside this store's current or just-ended outage.

name: store_key
doc: Record key of a profile home's cron store (a symlinked cron/ resolves elsewhere).

name: forget_stores
doc:
Drop the state of ``stores`` (``store_key`` values, resolved while each home existed) whose
profile this process no longer ticks, so a profile that left this gateway cannot keep the
host-wide gauges at writable=0.

name: dispatch_blocked
doc:
Whether this tick skips advance/claim for ``due_jobs``: the active store is known
unwritable and the minute-throttled re-probe has not seen it accept a write. Skipped runs are
recorded; once the probe passes, the dispatch's own save confirms recovery (or re-degrades).

name: end_recovery_window
doc: A due scan's save landed after the outage ended: normal grace applies again.

name: recheck_idle
doc:
Idle tick (nothing due, so no save will land): re-probe a degraded store at most once a
minute. The probe only creates an empty file, so a passing probe is confirmed by a real
jobs.json save, whose ``note_writable`` ends the outage; metrics, notices and the one-shot
grace gate then stop treating a recovered store as degraded.

name: probe_report
free_bytes
doc:
Bytes this process can still write. Root may also fill the reserved blocks that
``disk_usage().free`` leaves out, so a 'full' disk is not full for root.

name: probe_store
doc:
Write probe mirroring a jobs.json save: ``None`` when it would land (or the store does not
exist yet), else the OSError it would hit. Stages a payload the size of the current jobs.json
(plus a page) where the save stages it (beside a symlinked file's real target), so a full,
over-quota or read-only target fails here the way the save would.

name: load_suggestions
doc: Return all suggestion records (any status).

name: list_pending
doc: Return pending suggestions in creation order (oldest first).

name: add_suggestion
arguments: *, title: str, description: str, source: str, job_spec: dict[str, Any], dedup_key: str
doc:
Register a pending suggestion. Returns the record, or None when skipped: the same
``dedup_key`` was already decided on or is still pending (never re-offer, never duplicate), or
the pending list is full (``MAX_PENDING``). ``job_spec`` is passed straight to
``cron.jobs.create_job`` on accept.

name: get_suggestion
doc: Resolve a suggestion by id, 1-based pending index, or exact (case-insensitive) title.

name: dismiss_suggestion
doc: Dismiss a suggestion (latched — never re-offered for its dedup_key).

name: accept_suggestion
doc:
Accept a suggestion: create the real cron job from its ``job_spec``. Returns the job dict, or
None if not found / not pending. ``origin`` (platform/chat) is merged so "origin" delivery
routes back to the chat where the user accepted.

name: clear_resolved
doc:
Drop ACCEPTED records from disk (they served their purpose once the job exists); dismissed
records are RETAINED for their dedup_key. Returns the count removed.

name: classify_items_script_path
doc: Absolute path to the urgency classifier script shipped with cron/.

name: seed_catalog_suggestions
arguments: *, add_fn: Optional[Callable[..., Optional[dict[str, Any]]]]=None, keys: Optional[list[str]]=None
doc:
Register catalog entries as pending suggestions.

``add_fn`` defaults to ``cron.suggestions.add_suggestion`` (injectable for tests). ``keys``
restricts to specific catalog entries; omit to seed all. Entries already dismissed/accepted (by
dedup key) or beyond the pending cap are skipped by the store, so re-seeding is safe and
idempotent. Returns the list of suggestion records actually created.

name: retry_enabled
doc:
``cron.retry_unreachable`` — default ON (spend-neutral: only fires when zero
model calls were made).

name: is_model_unreachable_failure
doc:
True when *exc* is a transient network/DNS failure and *agent* (may be ``None``)
never completed a model call — the run consumed nothing and executed nothing.

name: _ladder_applies
doc: The ladder's applicability gate: recurring, not paused, and enabled in config.

name: _ladder_instant
arguments: job: dict[str, Any], natural_next: Optional[datetime], now: datetime
doc:
The ladder instant ``plan_retry`` parks for this flagged failure, or None when it
parks nothing: not recurring, paused, disabled, ladder exhausted, or the schedule's
own *natural_next* fires at or before the rung. The single source of that decision
for ``plan_retry`` and ``will_retry``.

name: will_retry
doc:
True iff ``plan_retry`` will park a re-run for this flagged failure, so the scheduler
may hold the interim notice. Called before ``mark_job_run``.

name: clear_state
doc: A run reached the model (any outcome): the ladder resets.

name: is_retry_fire
doc:
True for the exact ladder instant parked by ``plan_retry`` (off the cron lattice).

The expression fingerprint keeps a direct ``jobs.json`` schedule edit from inheriting the
exception, as in ``cron.quota_hold.is_recovery_fire``.

name: is_retry_run
doc:
True when this dispatch snapshot fired the ladder instant parked by ``plan_retry``: a
re-run of an occurrence that already counted toward ``repeat``, so it must not count again.
Manual runs carry no ``_scheduled_instant`` and always count.

name: plan_retry
doc:
Called under the jobs lock AFTER ``_advance_after_run`` computed the schedule's
natural ``next_run_at`` for a failed, flagged run. Pulls ``next_run_at`` earlier to
the ladder instant when that is sooner than the natural occurrence; exhausted or
inapplicable cycles clear state and leave the schedule untouched. Returns True when
a retry was scheduled.

name: worker_bootstrap
doc: Run PM's dependency boot in the marked external worker (again after a relaunch).

name: finish_worker_boot
doc:
Run ``hermes_bootstrap`` before the worker reads its payload; may relaunch the worker.

Not from ``worker_bootstrap()``: while ``-m cron.scheduler`` executes ``cron/__init__.py``,
``sys.argv[0]`` is still ``-m`` and ``__main__`` has no spec, so the relaunch command could
not name the module to re-run. In ``__main__`` both are set.

name: _positive
doc: ``cast(value)`` if it is a positive number (bools rejected), else None.

name: _finite_limit
doc:
A cgroup memory limit file's value when it is a real cap; None for unreadable, empty,
``max``, or the v1 near-2^63 sentinel (all mean unlimited).

name: _cgroup_limit_bytes
doc:
Memory limit this process runs under, if cgroup-capped.

Prefers v2 ``memory.high`` (the throttling point) over ``memory.max``, then v1.
Own cgroup first (where a systemd unit's ``MemoryHigh=``/``MemoryMax=`` lands —
root reads ``max`` there), then root for container-style limits.

name: resolve_memory_high_mb
doc:
Absolute MB budget: ``"auto"`` derives from the cgroup limit (or total RAM when
uncapped); a positive number is literal; anything falsy/off disables the pass.

name: resolve_agent_cache_bounds
doc:
Read ``agent.agent_cache`` from the *raw* config: the gateway loader does not
deep-merge ``DEFAULT_CONFIG``, so callers can tell "operator chose 128" from "unset".

name: _cgroup_anon_bytes
doc:
Anonymous memory charged to this process's own cgroup v2 (``memory.stat`` ``anon``), or None.

The budget is derived from the same cgroup's ``memory.high``/``memory.max``, and the kernel
charges every process in the unit against it — execute_code kernels, terminal children — so a
self-only reading under-counts by exactly the children's share (#110549).  Anon, not
``memory.current``: the module's signal is heap, and reclaimable page cache is noise.
Only for a *capped* cgroup: an uncapped one (a plain login session) is the whole user
slice, and its budget is total RAM — self RSS stays the right scope there.

name: read_anon_rss_mb
doc:
Anonymous memory in MB (where cached transcripts live; file-backed pages are noise),
or None.  Own cgroup's ``memory.stat`` anon first — the scope the budget is charged
against, so same-unit child processes count; then ``/proc/self/status``; psutil covers
other platforms (total RSS only).

name: transcript_persistence_caught_up
doc:
True when the live transcript is fully on disk.

Soft eviction rebuilds from the persisted session, so it is only safe once
``_last_flushed_db_idx`` (advanced only on a fully successful write) has caught
up.  Unknown shapes are *not* caught up: a skipped eviction costs memory, a
wrong one costs the conversation.

name: plan_pressure_evictions
arguments: ordered_entries: Iterable[tuple[str, Any]], *, is_evictable: Callable[[str, Any], bool], max_evictions: int, protect_recent: int=0
doc:
Choose which cached sessions to shed, least-recently-used first.

``ordered_entries`` must be LRU→MRU (the cache OrderedDict ``move_to_end``s on
every hit).  The batch is capped so one pass cannot stall the gateway.
``protect_recent`` is clamped to half the cache: a few huge transcripts can
exhaust the budget alone, and a fixed guard would leave nothing to shed.

name: authz_field
doc: Late-bound :func:`gateway.platform_env.authz_field` (entry field, else the bundled declaration).

name: _group_chat_env
doc: The platform's group-chat allowlist env name (``PlatformEntry.group_allowed_chats_env``), or "".

name: _registry_entry
doc:
Platform-registry entry for a (plugin) platform, or None. Discovers first (idempotent): the
allowlist env names live only on the entry, so an undiscovered process must not read "no list".

name: _coerce_allow_set
doc: Parse an allowlist (YAML list, JSON list literal string, or comma-separated scalar) into a set of strings.

name: _convertbits
arguments: data, frombits: int, tobits: int, pad: bool=True

name: _npub_to_hex
doc: Decode an ``npub1…`` bech32 string to a 64-char hex pubkey, else None.

name: _normalize_nostr_allow_entries
doc:
Add the hex form of every valid ``npub1…`` entry; invalid entries are kept as-is.

Hex entries pass through unchanged; each valid ``npub1…`` entry is decoded and its 64-char hex form
added, so either form authorizes the same identity (#78428). Invalid entries are kept as-is (they simply
never match an inbound hex pubkey).

name: _principal_matches_allowlist
doc: Whether *user_id* (under any platform-specific alias) is in *allowed_ids*.

name: _authorization_adapter
doc:
Live adapter whose intake policy gates authorization (``_adapters_for_profile`` for the
profile rule). ``None`` when the profile has no adapter for *platform*.

name: _adapters_for_profile
doc:
The live adapter map *profile* may deliver through: ``_profile_adapters[p]`` for a
secondary, ``self.adapters`` only for the primary/default. ``_profile_adapters`` is consulted
BEFORE the active profile name: multiplex turns override ``HERMES_HOME`` so
``_active_profile_name()`` reports the secondary profile mid-turn, and treating it as primary
would hand it the default bot. A named profile with no map gets ``{}`` — fail closed: a
secondary whose adapter failed to connect must NOT fall back to the default profile's adapter
(replies, tool sends, marker-file notices out the wrong bot).

name: _is_shared_bot_satellite
doc:
A served profile with NO adapter of its own that a ``profile_routes`` entry targets through the
default profile's bot: it drains through the primary's adapters (gateway/AGENTS.md). Its
``_profile_adapters`` entry is the ``{}`` startup placeholder; a secondary connected on ANY
platform is its own credential boundary and never borrows the primary. Restored/cached sources
carry no transport ref, so this is what keeps heartbeats, completions and goal notices for such a
profile deliverable after a restart (the same rule ``kanban_watchers_notifier`` and cron apply).

name: _intake_adapter_for
doc:
The adapter that RECEIVED *source*'s event — the only one whose intake policy (ignored
channels, relay fronting, re-dispatch of a still-live event) may act on it.

Live provenance only: the registered transport that built the source, the process-level
RelayAdapter for relay-delivered events, or the receiving bot named by a pinned
``RoutingIdentity`` (``transport_profile``) when its adapter reconnected. A source with none
of these (restored row, hand-built) fails closed under multiplexing — nothing can say which
bot admitted it, and guessing the runtime profile's bot is exactly the shared-bot /
route-override confusion the identity exists to end. A standalone gateway owns one adapter
per platform, so that adapter is the receiver by construction.

name: _delivery_adapter_for
doc:
The adapter that ANSWERS *source*: sends, edits, typing, progress, pickers, pending slots.

The receiving bot whenever it is known (:meth:`_intake_adapter_for` — a routed event replies
through the bot that received it, whether the runtime is a shared-bot satellite or a profile
with a bot of its own). With no live provenance the unique owner of ``(platform,
runtime_profile)`` delivers — ``_adapters_for_profile`` holds one adapter per platform per
profile, a shared-bot satellite drains through the primary, and a disconnected secondary
fails closed to ``{}`` rather than borrowing the default bot. Restored sessions, cron,
kanban and completion notices all rely on this row. Matrix: gateway/AGENTS.md § Profile scope.

name: _owning_profile
doc: Return (registered, profile) for a live adapter: profile is None for primary.

name: _transport_owner
doc:
``(adapter, profile)`` of the registered adapter that created *source*, if retained; else None.

``source.profile`` may differ from the adapter profile when one shared credential serves
several routed runtimes; ``build_source`` keeps the receiving adapter as provenance so replies
stay on that transport. Restored/hand-built sources fall back (fail-closed) to profile lookup.

name: _authorization_home_for_source
doc:
HERMES_HOME whose allowlist admits *source*: the identity's transport home (or the
ingress-stamped one), else the home of the profile owning the adapter that delivers it.
``None`` = authorize in the ambient scope (multiplex off, or no live adapter — the check then
fails closed on its own).

Inside a routed satellite's turn the ambient scope is the satellite's, whose ``.env`` has no
token/allowlist; every authorization decision made mid-turn (``/topic``, sibling ``/stop``, plugin
injection, voice, auto-resume) must read the admitting bot's allowlist instead.

name: _adapter_profile_for_source
doc: Resolve the transport-owning profile for adapter policy lookups.

name: _restored_source
doc:
``entry.origin`` with its identity re-pinned from the routing entry's persisted
``transport_profile`` (no live adapter: the restored row of the transport matrix). Every path
that revives a session from durable state — auto-resume, heartbeat restore, plugin injection,
background-process events — reads the origin through here, so the receiving bot decides
delivery and authorization after a restart, not the runtime profile's heuristics.

name: _adapter_flag
doc:
Adapter-declared boolean, False when unknown. ``authorization_is_upstream`` (relay: a trusted
authenticated upstream decides) is honored directly; ``enforces_own_access_policy`` (WeCom, Weixin,
Yuanbao, QQBot, WhatsApp gate at intake) is NOT "already authorized" — those adapters default to
``open``, so ``_is_user_authorized`` only trusts them under an actual ``allowlist`` policy.

name: _config_extra
doc: ``config.platforms[platform].extra`` as a dict ({} when absent).

name: _adapter_setting
arguments: self, platform, attr: str, extra_key: str, profile
doc:
Live adapter's resolved ``attr`` (folds in the ``<PLATFORM>_*`` env override),
else ``config.extra[extra_key]`` for bare runners with no adapter.

name: _adapter_policy
doc:
Lowercased effective ``dm_policy`` (open/allowlist/disabled/pairing) or ``group_policy``
(open/allowlist/disabled) for *kind* in {"dm", "group"}; ``""`` if unknown.

name: _adapter_group_has_sender_allowlist
arguments: self, platform: Optional[Platform], chat_id: Optional[str], *, profile: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Whether a per-group sender allowlist (WeCom ``groups.<id>.allow_from``) gated this message:
a group may be open at the chat level while restricting senders, so reaching the gateway
means the adapter already checked that list.

name: _pairing_store_for
doc: Per-profile PairingStore for a source, else the global ``self.pairing_store``.

name: _own_policy_authorizes
doc:
Own-policy adapter verdict when no env allowlist exists; None = no verdict.

Trusted only when the effective policy for THIS chat type is ``allowlist``: ``open`` forwards
EVERY sender (the fail-open SECURITY.md §2.6 forbids), ``disabled`` never forwards, ``pairing``
forwards unpaired DMs for the handshake (already denied by the pairing-store check).
Anything else → default-deny.

name: _adapter_extra_allowlist_authorizes
doc:
Adapters (e.g. Telegram) that gate via config.extra.allow_from / group_allow_from
without setting enforces_own_access_policy.

name: _adapter_resolved_allowlist_ids
doc:
IDs an adapter resolved from username-shaped allowlist entries at connect time (Discord).

The per-turn .env hot-reload restores RAW usernames, so from the second turn on the env
allowlist holds usernames while user_id is numeric. Never a widening: the empty-allowlist
branch already returned and adapters only resolve operator-written entries. Only called with
a non-empty platform allowlist so group/global-only configs never consult adapter memory;
type-checked so mocks cannot auto-truthy in.

name: _chat_scoped_grant
arguments: self, source, adapter_profile, is_group: bool, allow_adapter_delegation: bool
doc: Grants that need no ``user_id`` (checked before the no-user-id guard).

name: _legacy_telegram_chat_grant
doc:
TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_USERS was once (mis)used as a chat-ID allowlist; "-"-prefixed
values are chat IDs, honor them and warn once.

name: _admit_bot_message
doc:
Count one authorized bot-authored inbound message. False when it trips the budget or the chat is cooling down.
The inbound handler calls this once per message; ``_is_user_authorized`` only peeks because it is asked several times.

name: _is_user_authorized
doc:
Whether a user may use the bot.

Order: trusted-upstream delegation, chat-scoped group allowlists, ``{PLATFORM}_ALLOW_BOTS``,
per-platform allow-all, adapter role auth, pairing store, env/config allowlists,
``GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS``, default deny. A bot-authored message that any of these admits
is still refused while its chat's loop guard is cooling down.

name: _principal_authorized
doc: The allowlist verdict alone, before the bot loop guard.

name: _get_unauthorized_dm_behavior
doc:
How unauthorized DMs are handled ("pair" / "ignore" / "decline") for a platform.

Order: explicit per-platform config; Email → "ignore" (inboxes hold arbitrary mail); explicit
non-default global; adapter dm_policy (pairing → "pair", allowlist/disabled → "ignore"); any
configured allowlist → "ignore" (spamming unknown contacts with codes is noisy and leaks); else "pair".

1. 2. Email defaults to ``"ignore"`` unless explicitly opted into pairing. 3. Explicit global
``unauthorized_dm_behavior`` in config — wins for chat-shaped platforms when no per-platform
override is set. 4. When an adapter-level DM policy opts into pairing or silent drop, honor it. 5.
When an allowlist (``PLATFORM_ALLOWED_USERS``, ``PLATFORM_GROUP_ALLOWED_USERS`` /
``PLATFORM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS``, or ``GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS``) is configured, default to
``"ignore"`` — the allowlist signals that the owner has deliberately restricted access; spamming
unknown contacts with pairing codes is both noisy and a potential info-leak. (#9337) 6.

name: settings_from_config
doc: Read ``gateway.bot_loop_guard`` from a loaded config dict. Unusable values keep the default.

name: load_settings
doc: Settings from the live config.yaml. Defaults when the config cannot be read.

name: __init__
arguments: self, settings: Callable[[], BotLoopGuardSettings]=load_settings, clock: Callable[[], float]=time.monotonic

name: blocked
doc: True while ``conversation`` is cooling down. Reads only, so callers may ask as often as they like.

name: admit
doc:
Count one admitted bot-authored message for ``conversation``.
Returns ``(allowed, state)``; state is ``disabled``, ``ok``, ``tripped`` (this message started the cooldown) or ``cooldown``.

name: _sweep
doc: Drop idle conversations at most once per window so memory stays bounded.

name: artifact_scope_key
doc:
Derive the stable scope key an artifact is bound to.

Only principal (mandatory) + transport family participate. ``session_id`` is deliberately EXCLUDED: HTTP
artifact routes authenticate by API key and can't resolve a session while broker dispatch always carries
one, so hashing it would make upload and dispatch never compose (ids are unguessable and downloads
one-shot). Capabilities/optional ids are excluded so a reconnect keeps its artifacts.

name: _normalize_content_type
doc: Return the canonical MIME type, or ``""`` for malformed input.

name: _bounded_filename
doc: Sanitize a display-only filename; never used as a filesystem path.

name: to_dict
doc: Serialize to the wire receipt (never contains file paths).

name: __init__
arguments: self, root: Path, *, ttl_seconds: float=DEFAULT_ARTIFACT_TTL_SECONDS, max_bytes: int=DEFAULT_MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES, allowed_mime_types: frozenset=DEFAULT_ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES, clock: Optional[Callable[[], float]]=None

name: _sweep_orphan_files
doc:
Delete on-disk files with no live index entry; only minted-id-shaped and ``*.tmp`` names are
touched. Returns the number removed.

name: root
doc: Controlled artifact root (never exposed to callers by default).

name: store
arguments: self, data: bytes, *, filename: str, content_type: str, scope: Any
doc: Validate and store one artifact, returning its receipt; size/MIME rejections fire before any disk write.

name: validate
doc: Receipt when the artifact is live for ``scope`` (existence, TTL, scope), without consuming.

name: load
doc: One-shot download: verify, read, checksum, then consume (a checksum mismatch does not consume).

name: prune_expired
doc: Delete every artifact past its TTL (and stale temp files); return the count removed.

name: count
doc: Number of live (unconsumed, not-yet-pruned) artifacts.

name: _discard_locked
doc: Drop the index entry and best-effort unlink its file.

name: _artifact_path
doc: Resolve a minted id strictly inside the controlled root.

name: __init__
arguments: self, *, window_seconds: float=60.0, max_requests: int=30, clock: Optional[Callable[[], float]]=None

name: allow
doc: Return True when ``key`` is under the window cap; else False.

name: reset
doc: Drop the recorded hits for ``key`` (tests/diagnostics).

name: browser_control_protocol_supported
doc: Return whether ``value`` names the exact supported wire version.

name: _extension_control_flag
doc: Read ``browser.extension_control.<key>`` as a literal ``True`` (default off).

name: browser_control_developer_mode
doc: Explicit Developer Mode flag; gates ``browser_evaluate``/raw CDP only.

name: browser_control_enabled
doc: Return the explicit browser-control feature flag (disabled by default).

name: filter_browser_control_capabilities
doc: Permitted subset of a capability list (non-list -> empty); developer caps only in Developer Mode.

name: get_browser_control_broker
doc: Process-local broker shared by API and dashboard Gateway transports.

name: __init__
arguments: self, *, ticket_ttl: float=DEFAULT_TICKET_TTL, command_timeout: float=DEFAULT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT, clock: Optional[Callable[[], float]]=None, developer_mode: Optional[bool]=None

name: developer_mode
doc: Whether privileged capabilities may be selected/dispatched (live config unless pinned).

name: attach_artifact_store
doc:
Attach a store exposing ``validate(artifact_id, *, scope) -> receipt`` for one profile
(``None`` = default slot); ``store=None`` clears the slot. Artifact actions fail closed without one.

name: mint_ticket
doc: Mint a short-lived, single-use ticket bound to ``scope``.

name: consume_ticket
doc: Exchange a ticket for its scope exactly once; unknown/consumed/expired -> ControllerTicketInvalid.

name: _controller_for_identity_locked
doc: Attached controller sharing ``scope``'s stable identity (any capabilities).

name: attach
arguments: self, scope: ControllerScope, send: Callable[[dict], None], *, owner: Any=None
doc:
Attach or refresh the controller for one stable identity: a same-identity reconnect refreshes send
and capabilities without cancelling pending work; a different controller/browser profile in the same
authenticated session lane hard-replaces it.

name: select
doc:
Connected controller matching identity whose *current* negotiated set holds ``capability`` (the
caller's set is not authoritative); developer capabilities are also gated on LIVE Developer Mode.

name: is_owner
doc: Whether ``owner`` is the exact live transport for ``scope`` (capability-independent).

name: disconnect
doc: Mark one exact controller transport offline without cancelling work.

name: detach
arguments: self, scope: ControllerScope, *, owner: Any=_OWNER_UNSET, notify_controller: bool=True
doc: Remove the controller for ``scope`` and fail its pending work closed (ControllerCancelled).

name: dispatch
arguments: self, scope: ControllerScope, *, action: str, arguments: Optional[dict]=None, tool_call_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Send one controller command and block for completion; raises ControllerUnavailable/Cancelled/Timeout/
Rejected. Artifact actions also need an attached store and an approved ``artifact_id`` (only the id travels).

name: complete
arguments: self, command_id: str, *, scope: Optional[ControllerScope]=None, ok: bool, result: Any=None
doc: Resolve a pending command by id; ``False`` when none is pending. Safe from inside the send callback.

name: cancel
doc: Cancel the pending command matching ``scope`` + tool_call_id (one cancel frame); ``False`` if none.

name: _validate_artifact_reference
arguments: self, scope: ControllerScope, action: str, arguments: dict
doc: Fail closed unless ``arguments`` carries a store-approved artifact id (failures -> ControllerRejected).

name: _emit_cancel_frames
doc: Send cancel frames (caller holds ``send_lock``, never the broker lock).

name: _lane_scopes
doc: Attached scopes bound to one session lane (session + principal + transport).

name: scope_for_session
arguments: self, *, session_id: Optional[str]=None, task_id: Optional[str]=None, principal_id: Optional[str]=None, transport_family: Optional[str]=None
doc:
One unambiguous attached scope for a server-owned session (session id is only a hint; the caller
supplies its server-derived principal + transport family). Missing/ambiguous identity fails closed.

name: lane_registered
arguments: self, *, session_id: Optional[str]=None, task_id: Optional[str]=None, principal_id: Optional[str]=None, transport_family: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Whether ANY controller (even offline) registered for this lane: "bound but unavailable" fails closed
vs "never registered" (caller keeps the legacy backend). Ambiguous lanes report True.

name: disconnect_owner
doc: Mark every controller owned by one lost transport offline.

name: reset
doc: Fail all live work closed and clear tickets (tests/shutdown).

name: ticket_ttl_seconds
doc: Configured lifetime for newly minted one-shot tickets.

name: pending_count
doc: Number of commands awaiting completion (diagnostics/tests).

name: _own_cgroup_path
doc: Return the cgroup v2 path for the calling process, or None.

name: _parent_is_systemd
doc:
True when this process was spawned by a systemd manager (ExecStopPost etc.).

Any other parent (an agent terminal tool, a shell) shares a *live*
process's cgroup, so reaping there would SIGKILL that process. No PID-1
shortcut: in a container the gateway itself can be PID 1 (or init can be
``tini``), so PID 1 must present as systemd too; an unreadable
``/proc/<ppid>/comm`` fails closed.

name: _live_gateway_among
doc:
True when one of ``pids`` is a live Hermes gateway runtime.

A PID whose command line can't be read has already exited (or is a
zombie) — exactly what the reaper clears — so only a readable,
gateway-shaped command line blocks. Uses the *runtime* matcher (``run``
or ``restart``): without a service manager, ``gateway restart`` runs the
gateway in-process and is itself the live runtime.

name: reap_cgroup
doc:
SIGKILL every PID in the cgroup other than the caller. Returns the count killed.

Returns None (no signals) when a live gateway process is still in the
cgroup — the reaper must never signal the live gateway, however invoked.

name: _load_json_dict
doc: Read a JSON object from *path*; {} when missing, unreadable, or not a dict.

name: _apply_channel_aliases
doc:
Overlay friendly names onto directory entries by chat_id, in place.

An aliased id not yet discovered gets a placeholder entry so a freshly-created
group is addressable by name before its first message.

name: _channel_target_name
doc: Human-facing target label for a channel entry.

name: _report_slack_failure
arguments: team_id: str, error_code: Optional[str], detail: str
doc: missing_scope is expected (session-history fallback); anything else warns once per interval.

name: build_channel_directory
doc: Build the directory from connected adapters + session data and persist it.

name: _build_discord
doc: Enumerate text + forum channels the Discord bot can see, plus session DMs.

name: _slack_api_error_code
doc: Slack Web API error code from SlackApiError-like exceptions.

name: _normalize_adapter_channels
doc: Validate and dedupe entries returned by an adapter's ``list_channels()`` hook.

name: _slack_base_id
doc: Thread-qualified IDs (``C0xxx:ts``) are internal routing keys, not Slack API IDs.

name: _slack_team_channels
doc: ``users.conversations`` for one workspace (public + private member channels), paginated.

name: _slack_resolve_raw_names
doc:
Name remaining raw-ID entries (DMs, channels outside bot scope) via
conversations.info + users.info once per base conversation, concurrently.

name: _build_slack
doc:
List Slack channels the bot has joined across all workspaces, merged with
session-history DMs. Missing channels:read falls back to session history quietly.

name: _build_from_sessions
doc:
Known channels/contacts from session origins: state.db first, sessions.json fallback (pre-migration).

state.db is the primary source (#9006): gateway session rows persist origin_json.

name: _entries_from_origins
doc:
Deduped entries for the (origin, chat_type) pairs from ``origins_fn()``; a mid-iteration
failure keeps entries read so far.

name: _build_from_sessions_db
doc: Pull channels/contacts from state.db gateway session rows.

name: _build_from_sessions_json
doc: Legacy fallback: pull channels/contacts from sessions.json origin data.

name: load_directory
doc: Load the cached directory from disk, with aliases re-applied on read.

name: lookup_channel_type
doc: Channel ``type`` string (e.g. ``"channel"``, ``"forum"``) for *chat_id*, or None if unknown.

name: resolve_channel_name
doc:
Resolve a friendly channel name (e.g. "bot-home", "#bot-home", "GuildName/bot-home",
Slack "#engineering") to an ID; case-insensitive, first match wins.

name: format_directory_for_display
doc:
Format the channel directory as a human-readable list for the model.

``platforms`` overrides the on-disk directory (``hermes send --list`` merges in
configured-but-undiscovered platforms); an empty channel list renders a "(no channels
discovered yet)" hint because the platform is still a valid send target.

name: _fingerprint
doc:
Current checkout fingerprint via the CLI's worktree-aware git-rev reader
(``hermes_cli.main`` is always already imported in a gateway process).

name: record_boot_fingerprint
doc: Snapshot the checkout revision at gateway startup (idempotent).

name: _short
doc: Render a ``git:<ref>:<sha>`` fingerprint as a compact label.

name: current_code_sha
doc: Full SHA for the checkout currently on disk, or None when unresolved.

name: detect_code_skew
doc: ``(boot_rev, disk_rev)`` short labels if the checkout drifted since boot, else ``None``.

name: _bool_token
doc: True/False for a recognized truthy/falsy token, else None.

name: _coerce_bool
doc: Coerce bool-ish config values, preserving a caller-provided default.

name: _env_multiplex_profiles_override
doc:
GATEWAY_MULTIPLEX_PROFILES operator override: True/False for a recognized token.

``None`` when unset, blank, or unrecognized so the caller keeps the config.yaml
value (env > config > default). Blank is deliberately ``None``, not ``False``:
a provisioned-but-unpopulated Fly secret arrives as ``""`` and must NOT shadow
a config.yaml opt-in.

name: _env_on_all_adapters_down_override
doc:
GATEWAY_ON_ALL_ADAPTERS_DOWN operator override: 'exit'/'stay_alive' for a recognized token.

``None`` when unset, blank, or unrecognized so the caller keeps the config.yaml value
(env > config > default). Launchers without a supervising service manager (the desktop app
spawns ``hermes serve`` directly) set ``stay_alive``: a failure exit there only severs the
UI's websocket connections and drops in-flight assistant messages (#118080).

name: _normalize_transport_token
doc:
Canonical streaming transport token. YAML 1.1 parses bare ``on``/``off`` as
booleans (``mode: off`` → ``False`` → ``"false"`` would ENABLE streaming), so
booleans map to ``"auto"``/``"off"``; anything else lower-cases, default ``"auto"``.

name: _coerce_optional_positive_int
doc: ``None``/0/negative disable; malformed values are ignored with a warning so a typo never blocks startup.

name: coerce_systemd_watchdog_seconds
doc:
Bounded positive watchdog interval, or zero when disabled/invalid. Shared by runtime
and service generation so a value can never enable ``Type=notify`` without heartbeats.

name: _normalize_choice
arguments: value: Any, choices: set, default: str
doc: Lower-cased *value* when it is one of *choices*, else *default*.

name: _dict_slot
doc: Get-or-create ``container[key]`` as a dict, replacing a non-dict value with ``{}``.

name: _getenv
doc:
Env read through the active profile secret scope when present (multiplexed
per-profile secrets must win); otherwise legacy ``os.getenv``.

name: _bundled_platform_manifest_name
doc: Lowercased ``name:`` from a bundled platform's plugin manifest (None when absent/unreadable).

name: platform_binds_port
doc: True when *platform_value* actually binds a port for *extra* config.

name: discord_channel_id_from_link
doc:
Channel id from a pasted Discord channel link (``https://discord.com/channels/<guild>/<channel>``),
else None. Message links (a third path segment) and anything that is not a channel link are
left alone so callers keep their own error path.

name: persist_home_channel
doc: Persist a logical home without falsely enabling a Relay-fronted adapter.

name: _has_usable_api_server_key
doc:
True when API_SERVER_KEY is strong enough for the adapter to start (mirrors the
``has_usable_secret(min_length=16)`` guard in ``gateway/platforms/api_server.py``).

name: _discovered_registry_entry
doc:
Registry entry for *platform* after (idempotent) plugin discovery, so a directly-constructed
config sees plugin platforms; None when absent or the registry is not initialised yet (early import).

Enablement gate (#31116): a plugin's ``is_connected`` ("has the user actually configured
credentials for this?") is consulted before treating it as connected; ``check_fn`` alone — a
passive "is the SDK importable?" probe — must never make a platform the user never opted into
look connected (``_platform_status`` was fixed for the same bug class in commit 7849a3d73).

name: load_gateway_config
doc: Load gateway configuration. Priority: env > ~/.hermes/config.yaml > legacy gateway.json > defaults.

name: _validate_gateway_config
doc: Validate and sanitize a loaded GatewayConfig in place (after all sources are merged).

name: _apply_env_overrides
doc: Apply environment variable overrides to config (see ``gateway.config_env``).

name: _missing_
doc: Accept unknown names only for bundled or runtime-registered plugin adapters (no enum pollution).

name: _scan_bundled_plugin_platforms
doc:
Directory names of bundled platform plugins under ``plugins/platforms/``, plus a map of
manifest ``name:`` keys that differ from their directory (alias -> directory name). Aliases
never shadow a directory name, so the directory stays the canonical platform value.

name: globally_enabled
doc: The ``streaming.enabled`` master switch (``transport: off`` also disables).

name: enabled_for
doc:
Effective streaming for one platform.

``platform_override`` is ``display.platforms.<plat>.streaming`` (``None`` = follow global).
A per-platform value can only narrow the global switch, never enable streaming on its own.

name: get_connected_platforms
doc:
Enabled + configured platforms, sorted by value so the rendered "Connected
Platforms" prompt block is byte-stable (a reorder busts the prompt cache).

name: _extra_choice
arguments: self, platform: Optional[Platform], key: str, choices: set, default: str
doc: Normalized ``platforms[platform].extra[key]`` when the key is present, else None.

name: get_unauthorized_dm_behavior
doc:
Effective unauthorized-DM behavior. Email is inbox-shaped so it defaults to ``"ignore"``
unless its own ``unauthorized_dm_behavior`` opts in (a global default does not).

name: get_notice_delivery
doc: Effective notice-delivery mode ("public"/"private") for a platform.

name: pick
doc: Top-level key wins by presence; else the nested ``gateway.<key>`` form.

name: key_label
doc: Warning key prefix: "gateway." when the nested form was the one consulted.

name: by_platform
doc: ``{Platform(name): parse(block)}`` for a platform-keyed mapping; unknown platforms skipped.

name: bounded_float
arguments: key: str, default: float, lo: float, hi: float

name: _enable_credential_names
doc:
WARNING credential names: the core row, else the platform entry's declaration. The entry is
already materialized (its own env step is what is warning), so the lookup never imports.

name: _warn_explicit_disable_beats_env
doc:
One-time WARNING: ``platforms.<x>.enabled: false`` wins over env creds (which
used to force-enable), so users relying on "creds in .env = on" learn why it went dark.

name: _loading_secondary_under_multiplexer
doc:
True while a multiplexer loads a NON-default profile's config (``_profile_runtime_scope`` sets the
home override; the runner sets the multiplex flag). Same signal ``gateway.config`` uses for scoped reads.

name: _enable_from_env
arguments: config: GatewayConfig, platform: Platform, *, pop_marker: bool=False, warn: bool=True
doc:
Enable *platform* on env credentials unless config.yaml explicitly disabled it.

A multiplex secondary profile may pin ``enabled: false`` yet inherit the process env; without
this guard env presence would force-enable it. By default the ``_enabled_explicit`` marker is
READ (the plugin-enable and relay passes still need it) and the disable is warned once;
api_server/webhook POP it (terminal branch) and stay silent.

name: _api_server
doc: Require a usable key: an unauthenticated adapter refuses to start and the reconnect watcher would spin.

name: _plugin_probe_seed
doc: ``env_enablement_fn()`` result as a non-empty dict, else None.

name: _plugin_is_configured
doc: ``entry.is_connected`` on a transient ``enabled=True`` view seeded with env extras (never the real config).

name: _configured_plugin_entries
doc:
Plugin entries with activation evidence (config block, env/.env, credential pool); only those
are imported — an unconfigured adapter has nothing to enable. See gateway.platform_activation.
config.yaml blocks already materialized their adapters in load_yaml_layer (and every merged
block is in config.platforms), so the YAML is not parsed a second time here.

name: _bundled_env_fallbacks
doc:
Env rows of bundled platforms with activation evidence but no registry entry (discovery
suppressed or the plugin disabled), read from their ``gateway_env`` files; see
``gateway.platform_env.bundled_env_rows``. They only run the env steps, never the enable pass.

name: _apply_plugin_env_overrides
doc:
Run each plugin platform's declared ``env_overrides`` steps (credential enable, home channel,
reply mode, ...). Every step touches only its own platform, so only the order WITHIN an entry is
significant (e.g. Telegram's reply mode may create the entry its home channel then attaches to).

name: _enable_plugin_platforms_from_env
doc:
Registry-driven enable for plugin platforms whose ``env_overrides`` did not already enable them.

Enabled when credentials are configured (``is_connected`` MUST gate: ``check_fn`` alone would
enable unconfigured platforms that retry-connect forever) and deps are present (``check_fn``) or
installable later by ``create_adapter()`` — never here: installing in this sweep boot-looped the app.

name: _relay
doc:
Relay (connector-fronted, EXPERIMENTAL): enabled by GATEWAY_RELAY_URL or gateway.relay_url;
the URL is mirrored into extra["relay_url"] for the connected-checker.

Relay-exclusive: the GATEWAY_RELAY_URL env stamp means the connector owns every platform
connection; a directly-connected adapter would be a second unmanaged ingress (duplicate
deliveries, split sessions, a socket disarming scale-to-zero). So the env stamp disables all
other messaging platforms — even explicitly enabled ones — except non-messaging surfaces (local,
api_server, webhook; same set as the scale-to-zero arm gate). relay_url from YAML only keeps the
additive behavior. Opt out with GATEWAY_RELAY_ALLOW_DIRECT_PLATFORMS=true.

name: _apply_env_overrides
doc:
Apply environment variable overrides to *config*.

Order: plugin platforms' declared env rows, then the core-only rows (api_server, webhook,
msgraph_webhook; each touches only its own platform), then the registry enable pass, relay
disabling (needs every platform's final ``enabled``), and the marker scrub, which must be last.

name: load_legacy_gateway_json
doc: Legacy ``gateway.json`` base layer (config.yaml keys always win). Malformed → ``{}`` + warning.

name: bridged_allow_all_users
doc: ``os.environ['GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS']`` when it is the bridge's own write, else None.

name: drop_bridged_env
doc: Remove the bridge-owned ``GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`` from a child-process env (operator-set stays).

name: _bridge_lookup
arguments: yaml_cfg: dict, gateway_section: Any, gw_data: dict, key: str, mode: str
doc: Return ``(found, value)`` for *key* under the given fallback *mode*.

name: bridge_toplevel_keys
arguments: yaml_cfg: dict, gateway_section: Any, gw_data: dict

name: merge_platform_sections
arguments: yaml_cfg: dict, gateway_cfg: Any, gw_data: dict, *, also: frozenset=frozenset()
doc:
Merge every place a platform block may live into ``gw_data["platforms"]`` and return it.

Order (later wins on shared keys, ``extra`` deep-merged so gateway.json defaults survive):
``gateway.platforms.*`` → top-level ``platforms.*`` → ``gateway.<platform>`` subsections (nested
first so top-level config keeps precedence, matching the gateway.streaming fallback). An
``enabled`` key in any block sets the ``_enabled_explicit`` marker consumed by the env pass.
Top-level adapter keys (``gateway.api_server.port: 8642``) reach ``extra`` in
``PlatformConfig.from_dict``. *also* names platforms whose ``gateway.<platform>`` shorthand counts
even while no adapter is registered (a platform that left core, read before its plugin loads).

name: platform_section
arguments: yaml_cfg: dict, name: str, gateway_platforms: Any
doc:
``(section, is_toplevel)`` for platform *name*: a top-level ``<name>:`` block wins; otherwise
the block under ``gateway.platforms`` / ``platforms`` so shared-key bridging and adapter hooks
still run for nested-only configs.

name: _plain
doc: Keys copied verbatim into ``extra`` for every platform.

name: _bridged_keys
arguments: plat: Platform, platform_cfg: dict, gw_data: dict, *, root_block: bool=False
doc:
Shared-key bridge; a ROOT-level ``<platform>:`` block (which ``merge_platform_sections``
never copies into ``platforms_data``) also gets its adapter keys promoted into ``extra``, with
the same typed-key exclusion and explicit-``extra`` precedence as ``PlatformConfig.from_dict``.

name: shared_loop_targets
doc:
Built-in platforms plus registered plugin platforms (so plugin authors get shared-key bridging).

*entries* are the plugin entries to bridge (``load_yaml_layer`` passes only the configured
ones, see ``gateway.platform_activation``); None means every registered plugin platform.

name: snapshot_authored_extra
doc:
``{plat_name: extra}`` as the user authored it under ``platforms.<plat>.extra``, captured
right after ``merge_platform_sections`` and BEFORE either copy site runs. Reading
``platforms_data`` live at a copy site would mistake values the earlier site bridged from the
block's own ``extra:`` sub-dict for authored ones (``telegram: {reply_to_mode: all, extra:
{reply_to_mode: off}}`` must still resolve to ``all``). Copies, never creates slots.

name: _apply_managed_extra
arguments: authored: dict, managed: dict, platforms_data: dict
doc:
Remove from *authored* (in place) every key the administrator pinned in a managed ``<plat>:``
block: the user's ``platforms.<plat>.extra`` must not outrank it. A key the managed layer itself
sets under ``platforms.<plat>.extra`` stays authored.

name: _authored_wins
arguments: extra: dict, block: dict, plat_name: str, *, toplevel: bool, warned: Optional[set]=None
doc:
Effective ``<plat>:`` block for YAML→extra/env bridging: *block* (top-level or
nested) overlaid with the keys the user authored in ``platforms.<plat>.extra``.

Returns a NEW dict and never mutates *block* or *extra*. For every key present in
both with DIFFERENT values, ONE warning logs that the authored extra took precedence
(equal values are silent). *warned* dedupes across both copy sites within one
``load_yaml_layer`` pass; ``None`` gives the caller a fresh local set.

name: bridge_platform_shared_keys
arguments: yaml_cfg: dict, gateway_platforms: Any, gw_data: dict, platforms_data: dict, targets: list, warned: Optional[set]=None, authored: Optional[dict]=None
doc:
Copy shared keys (allow_from, require_mention, …) from each platform's YAML section into ``extra``.

``enabled`` is only written from a TOP-LEVEL block: for nested-only configs ``merge_platform_sections``
already merged it with the correct precedence. An explicit top-level enable/disable sets
``_enabled_explicit`` so the env pass honors ``enabled: false`` for migrated plugin platforms
instead of re-enabling them on token/SDK presence.

name: apply_plugin_yaml_hooks
arguments: yaml_cfg: dict, gateway_platforms: Any, platforms_data: dict, registry, warned: Optional[set]=None, authored: Optional[dict]=None, managed_extra: Optional[dict]=None, entries: Optional[list]=None
doc:
Plugin-owned YAML→env config bridges (``PlatformEntry.apply_yaml_config_fn``). Order: shared-key
loop → this dispatch → core-only bridges (require_mention/signal) → ``_apply_env_overrides()``.
*entries* limits the dispatch to those platforms (None = every registered entry).

name: bridge_core_env_settings
doc:
The YAML→env bridges that stay in core (per-platform ones live in plugin hooks).

Top-level ``require_mention`` → Telegram when the ``telegram:`` section has none: users write it
alongside ``group_sessions_per_user`` expecting it to work, and the telegram plugin's hook only
runs when a telegram block exists. Signal ``require_mention`` → ``SIGNAL_REQUIRE_MENTION`` (env wins).
``allow_all_users`` (top-level or ``gateway.allow_all_users``) → ``GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS``: every
allow-all reader (authz mixin, startup access check, own-policy adapters, plugin gates) consults
that env var, so the bridge is the one seam that makes the YAML key reach all of them (#110690).

Platform values are ALWAYS seeded into the owning platform's ``extra`` (the adapters read extra
first); the process-env write is skipped while a multiplexed secondary profile's scope is active —
the loader runs inside ``_profile_runtime_scope`` for every secondary, and a first-writer-wins write
there would make the secondary's policy the DEFAULT profile's (#80099 class). A secondary profile
sets ``GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`` in its own ``.env`` like every other scoped authorization gate.

name: read_yaml_layers
doc:
User ``config.yaml`` with the managed overlay applied — the YAML the gateway loader sees.

Raises on a malformed user file (the loader then falls back to env + gateway.json WITHOUT the
managed layer). An ABSENT user file is an empty layer, not a reason to skip the administrator's
values: a fleet host with no ``config.yaml`` must still honor them. Any pre-activation predicate
(``gateway.relay.relay_explicitly_disabled``) reads through here so it cannot disagree with
``load_gateway_config()`` on which files count.

name: load_yaml_layer
doc: Overlay ``read_yaml_layers`` onto *gw_data* in place. Raises on any failure (caller warns + falls back).

name: windows_pipe_name
doc: Per-HERMES_HOME named pipe path (Windows transport).

name: _private_runtime_dir
doc:
``$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`` when it is what the spec promises: an absolute directory owned by this
user with no group/other access. Other users cannot pre-create names inside it.

name: _fallback_socket_path
doc:
Short path for homes whose direct socket path exceeds sun_path: the private
``$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`` first, then ``tempfile.gettempdir()`` and ``/tmp`` (POSIX); if nothing fits
the first candidate is returned anyway. A squatted shared-temp name is handled at bind time
(``_squat_proof_fallback``).

name: _squat_proof_fallback
doc:
Same ``hermes-gw-<hash>/control.sock`` leaf (what clients authenticate through the private
pointer), under a fresh ``mkdtemp`` root no other user can predict or pre-create.

name: _publish_pointer
doc:
Replace ``pointer_file`` with one naming ``bind_path``, atomically: the listener is already
accepting, so a client polling for it may read the pointer at any instant, and an empty or
partial pointer is ``invalid_control_pointer`` to it, a refusal rather than "still starting".
The fresh mkstemp inode is 0600 and the rename replaces a symlink rather than following it,
which also heals an older gateway's leftover 0644 pointer.

name: resolve_server_socket_path
doc: Return ``(bind_path, pointer_file)``; pointer_file is set only for the temp-dir fallback.

name: resolve_client_socket_path
doc: Where a client should connect for ``home``, or None when nothing exists.

name: _detect_supervisor
doc:
Supervisor kind for THIS process from its own launch env (not inferred outside-in).

Unlike the outside-in `_detect_supervisor_for_pid` scan, this answers from the process's own launch
context — which is exactly the provenance the 92091 design wants declared rather than inferred. See
#92091.

name: _structured_login_subject
doc:
Whether ``value`` is ``authenticated_subject``'s namespaced login form
``auth:v1:[provider, issuer, user]`` (gateway.session_identity) — the only identity
a same-user peer may forward a ticket for. Bare labels (``admin``, ``uid:501``) fail:
they can collide with another stored owner representation.

name: launch_supervisor
doc:
What launched the gateway behind an ``identify`` answer (``manual``, ``desktop``, ``systemd``, ...).

The session runtime protocol folds ``manual`` and ``desktop`` into ``supervisor: "none"``, so the
launch value rides in ``launch_supervisor``. A gateway that predates that field and answers
``"none"`` is ambiguous: None (unknown), never ``manual``.

name: build_identify_payload
doc: Default ``identify`` answer, built from gateway.status primitives.

name: build_status_payload
doc: Default ``status`` answer — current runtime status, answered live.

name: query_gateway_control
arguments: home: Path, verb: str, *, params: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, timeout: float=_DEFAULT_CLIENT_TIMEOUT
doc:
Ask the gateway serving ``home`` a control verb; returns its ``result`` payload. Any failure (no/stale
socket, timeout, malformed answer, ``ok: false``) returns None so callers fall back to the scan layer.
``params`` carries verb arguments (e.g. ``{"old": ..., "new": ...}``). Never raises.

name: _read_response_line
doc: Read chunks until a newline, EOF, deadline, or the size cap (-> None).

name: _query_unix_socket
arguments: home: Path, request: bytes, timeout: float

name: _query_windows_pipe
arguments: home: Path, request: bytes, timeout: float
doc:
The native overlapped client checks its deadline per I/O step, but SID verification and the
connect/peer handshake are still synchronous calls into the pipe. Run the exchange on an
abandoned-at-deadline worker so a peer that never answers costs ``timeout``, never forever —
the bound ``_query_unix_socket`` already gets from ``sock.settimeout`` (#132547).

name: _windows_pipe_exchange
arguments: home: Path, request: bytes, timeout: float

name: identify_gateway
doc: Convenience wrapper: ``identify`` the gateway serving ``home``.

name: pause_gateway_for_update
doc:
Ask the gateway serving ``home`` to drain and exit for an update. Returns the ACK ``{"pausing",
"already_stopping", "pid", "drain_timeout"}`` or None when no gateway answers (old gateway without
the verb, no/dead socket) — the caller then uses the legacy signal/tree-kill pause path.

Step 2 of the socket migration (#92091).

name: rescan_gateway_profiles
doc:
Ask the multiplexer serving ``home`` to reconcile ``profiles/`` now (hot-serve a created profile,
unroute a deleted one). Returns its ``{"served_profiles", "added", "removed", ...}`` answer, or None
when no gateway answers / the gateway predates the verb — callers then rely on the periodic rescan
(or the restart reminder).

name: migrate_gateway_profile_identity
arguments: home: Path, old_name: str, new_name: str, *, timeout: float=8.0
doc:
Ask the multiplexer serving ``home`` to rekey a renamed profile's in-memory + on-disk routing
from ``agent:<old>:`` to ``agent:<new>:`` now. Returns its ``{"rekeyed": N, ...}`` answer, or None
when no gateway answers / the gateway predates the verb — the CLI's durable DB rewrite still lands,
and a restart reconciles the in-memory copy.

name: purge_gateway_profile_identity
arguments: home: Path, name: str, *, timeout: float=8.0
doc:
Ask the multiplexer serving ``home`` to drop a deleted profile's routing identity now — the
in-memory index AND the durable rows, neither of which a CLI-side delete can settle: this process
writes its in-memory copy back, so it re-creates what the CLI removed. Returns its
``{"ok": True, "dropped": N, ...}`` answer, or None when no gateway answers / the gateway predates
the verb.

name: reload_gateway_plugins
arguments: home: Path, *, profile_home: Optional[Path]=None, timeout: float=30.0
doc:
Ask the gateway serving ``home`` to force plugin re-discovery for ``profile_home`` (default: ``home``)
and re-wire its live adapters' plugin handlers now (#87770). Returns ``{"reloaded", "plugins",
"adapters_rewired", ...}`` or None when no gateway answers / it predates the verb — callers then
fall back to the restart hint. Tools and prompt sections of the reloaded plugin still apply next
session; only handlers go live.

name: __init__
arguments: self, home: Optional[Path]=None, *, verb_handlers: Optional[dict[str, Callable[..., dict[str, Any]]]]=None

name: start
doc: Bind and start serving. Returns True on success, False otherwise.

name: stop
doc: Stop serving and remove the socket/pointer files.

name: cleanup_files
doc: Best-effort removal of socket + pointer files (atexit-safe).

name: handle_request_line
doc: One JSON request line -> one JSON response line. Never raises (shared by POSIX + pipe).

name: install_cron_store_notices
doc:
Route store transitions from the ticker thread onto the gateway loop. Installed once the
adapters are connected, so a store that degraded during boot is announced then. The last

name: default_db_path
doc:
Return the hosted-room coordination database for the active install.

Profile gateways (``~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/``) resolve to the shared
ROOT ``shared-state.db`` instead of the master ``state.db``: hosted-room
coordination is the only thing this module owns, and pointing profile
gateways at the master session store makes every profile process a
long-lived writer on state.db — the recurring multi-writer corruption
vector observed across a 6-gateway fleet (state.db WAL/FTS collisions
during bot-gateway restart storms, 2026-09-03). Keeping the hosted_room*
tables in a dedicated file means profile gateways never open the master
session store writable.

rewritten, and read-only projections use validate_stored instead.
