name: profile_name_for_home
doc: Profile a home belongs to; the root/default home is ``'default'`` (not ``None``).

name: record_home
doc:
Home the owner was launched from. Records written before the field existed fall back to the
default root — the home every pre-record multiplexer ran under.

name: launched_by_other_tenant
arguments: owner_home: Path | str, our_home: Path | str
doc:
Was the owner launched from ANOTHER Hermes root (a second tenant on this host)?

The host record and lock are per OS user, and two tenants (separate ``HERMES_HOME`` roots)
each expose a profile named ``default``: tenant A's multiplexer "serving default" is a name
collision for tenant B, never coverage, so it is not this tenant's host gateway (#121352).
A legacy record with no ``home`` proves nothing and counts as ours.

name: _served_from_identity
doc:
Served set from a live ``identify``. A STANDALONE gateway publishes no ``served_profiles``;
it serves its own profile and nothing else, which is not the same as "unknown".

The unified runtime publishes each served profile as ``{"profile_id", "home"}`` (what
``hermes_cli.gateway_runtime`` matches homes against); older gateways published bare names.
Both spell the same roster, so a dict entry is reduced to its profile name here.

name: _identity_matches
doc:
Is this ``identify`` answer really the record's owner?

PID alone is not enough: a record naming an arbitrary home makes us dial whatever listens
there, so the answer must also agree about the home it was launched from.

name: invalidate_host_gateway_cache
doc: Forget the memoized probe (called by ``host_rendezvous`` on every record write).

name: host_gateway
doc:
The one live host gateway, or ``None``.

The served set comes from the owner's control socket and nowhere else; a record with no live
answer behind it yields ``served_known=False`` — an owner whose served set nobody knows yet.

name: host_gateway_serving
doc: The host gateway when it is live AND serves ``profile`` — true for ``default`` too.

name: request_serve_profile
arguments: profile: str, *, timeout: float=8.0, owner: Optional[HostGateway]=None
doc:
Ask the live host gateway to reconcile ``profiles/`` now; return it once it serves
``profile``. ``None`` when nobody answered or a multiplexer's roster still excludes the profile.
An owner that answers ``multiplex: False`` comes back flagged ``standalone``: it cannot take the
profile, and it is not a multiplexer that refused — the caller runs beside it, as before.

name: _coexisting_gateways
doc:
A standalone lock owner can hide a multiplexer launched beside it.

Use the existing per-home liveness and control channels, not the single host
record, to ask every running profile gateway what it actually serves.

name: standalone_attach_decision
doc:
An opt-out permits coexistence only after every live gateway confirms we are unserved.

Shared by the initial attach check and the lock-losing race check.

name: decide
doc:
Attach, rescan-then-attach, replace or refuse; configured standalone profiles may coexist.

Never raises: a broken probe degrades to ``START``, i.e. exactly the pre-rendezvous behaviour.

name: host_state_dir
doc: Per-OS-USER rendezvous dir (shared by every profile of this user).

name: ensure_host_state_dir
doc:
The rendezvous dir, created owner-only (``0o700``) and tightened if it is not.

A bare ``mkdir`` under the common ``umask 002`` leaves the dir group-writable, and the record
inside it is what every lifecycle verb believes: a same-group process could unlink+replace it
and choose this host's ATTACH answers (which home to dial, which profiles are "served").
Ownership of the dir is ours, so widening is repaired rather than refused.

name: _record_is_own
doc:
True when ``path`` was written by THIS OS user inside a dir this user owns.

``read_record`` hands its result straight to :mod:`gateway.host_attach`, which dials the home
it names and believes the served set it carries. A hand-written record therefore buys an
attacker the lifecycle verdict for every profile on the host, so the file's ``st_uid`` — not
its contents — is what makes it a record at all. Windows sets no ACLs from mode bits; there
the dir already lives under the user's own state root.

name: token_fingerprint
doc: Short, non-reversible handle for a session token (safe to publish in the record).

name: process_create_time
doc: Creation time of ``pid`` (default: this process); ``None`` when unknowable.

name: _pid_incarnation_matches
doc: Reuse the spawn ledger's proof: True/False when provable, ``None`` when it cannot say.

name: _host_lock_is_free
doc:
True when no process holds the host lock for ``role``; ``None`` when it cannot be probed.

Read-only callers (status, dashboard) reach this, so it never creates the lock dir or file: a
missing lock file means nobody holds the lock. The probe takes the lock for an instant, so a
gateway claiming it in that instant gets HELD_BY_OTHER and its supervisor retries.

name: _current_boot_epoch
doc: Identity of this boot. Empty when /proc is unreadable — a recorded epoch is then unprovable.

name: _record_incarnation_matches
doc:
Whether the record still names the same live process incarnation.

New records prefer the canonical start fingerprint: on Linux/WSL it comes from /proc start
ticks and is immune to wall-clock shifts that move psutil.create_time(). Those ticks are
NOT unique across reboots — they reset, and an early-boot PID reused within the drift
tolerance looks like the dead owner. A published boot epoch that differs from this boot's is a
mismatch; one that cannot be compared (this boot's epoch is unreadable) is unprovable, ``None``.

A gateway record with no epoch (published before ``bootEpoch`` existed, or on any platform
without /proc, where the epoch is always empty) whose create_time predates this boot is a
mismatch only while nobody holds the host lock. A record with neither create_time nor
start_time proves nothing about its pid, so it never vouches for one. Legacy records without
a start fingerprint keep the create-time check. Do not infer identity from argv.

name: record_is_stale
doc:
A record nobody may attach to: absent, unknown protocol, dead PID, or PID reuse.

``None`` from the liveness probe (no psutil, permission denied, an unexpected psutil error)
means UNPROVABLE, and an unprovable record is a CANDIDATE, never an owner: it survives this
predicate only to be handed to :func:`probe_owner`, which dials the recorded port and makes
the owner prove itself. Treating unprovable as dead would let a second process bind a second
port; treating it as alive *without the probe* made a record for a long-dead PID a permanent
silent outage (attach exited 0 forever, with nothing listening).

name: liveness_is_proven
doc:
True only when the record's process-incarnation probe positively matched (never on ``None``).

A record with neither ``createTime`` nor ``startTime`` cannot prove incarnation:
``_same_incarnation`` treats a missing create_time as a match, so a recycled pid would
otherwise look alive forever. Topology already refused that shape; attach did not.

name: dial_host
doc: Address to dial for ``record``: a wildcard bind is reached over loopback.

name: probe_owner
doc:
Make the recorded endpoint prove it is this record's owner; ``None`` when it does not.

Two gates, both required: a bounded TCP connect (nothing listening → the owner is gone, even
though its record and PID may still look alive during a graceful-shutdown window) and an
identity GET authenticated with the 0600 token (a foreign listener that inherited the port
answers the connect but cannot answer as PID N of role R).

Returns the owner's identity payload (``pid``/``role``/``servesSpa``) on success.

name: read_record
doc: Published record for ``role``; ``None`` when absent, foreign, corrupt or (by default) stale.

name: read_token
doc:
Owner-written session token for ``role`` (``""`` when absent/unreadable).

This is the handle an attaching client uses when the backend is auth-gated and therefore
withholds its token from an unauthenticated ``GET /``. Confidentiality is enforced at WRITE
time by :func:`_write_private_text` (POSIX ``0o600``; an owner+SYSTEM-only protected DACL on
Windows, where mode bits set no ACLs at all). Reading it is therefore evidence of, not proof
of, same-OS-user authority — the authority boundary the host lock is scoped to.

name: record_token_is_consistent
doc:
Does the on-disk token still hash to the record's fingerprint?

A record published without a token (the gateway) has an empty fingerprint and is consistent
by definition. A mismatch means the record and the token file come from different
incarnations (a torn restart) — discovery must not attach with a token the owner rejects.

name: _write_private_text
doc:
Create/replace ``path`` with owner-only content.

POSIX: ``0o600`` via tmp + atomic replace. Windows: mode bits set NO ACLs, so the same
``os.open`` would leave a live session token readable by whatever the inherited DACL grants;
the SSH runtime's protected owner+SYSTEM DACL writer is the repo's primitive for exactly this
credential class and is reused here. It also replaces in place, because ``os.replace`` onto a
token file another process still holds open fails on Windows.

name: claim_host_lock
doc:
Take the host-wide lock for ``role``. Idempotent per (role, lock path).

Returns the outcome and, for ``COULD_NOT_OPEN``, the OSError that explains it.

name: release_host_lock
doc: Release the host lock for ``role`` when this process holds it.

name: owns_host_lock
doc: True when THIS process holds the host lock for ``role`` (re-probing our own flock lies).

name: host_lock_is_held
doc:
Whether any process currently holds the host lock for ``role``.

``True`` / ``False`` when the flock can be observed; ``None`` when the lock file cannot
be opened. Never retains a lock. This process's handle is authoritative: re-probing our
own flock succeeds on POSIX, so a second open would lie.

name: record_names_live_owner
doc:
True when ``record``'s incarnation is proven AND its host lock is not observed free.

The publisher holds the host lock for its whole life and the OS drops it on death, so a free
flock falsifies a record whose pid merely looks alive (recycle, start-tick collision after a
reboot — #138343, #133744). Every reader that trusts a record as a running owner uses this.

name: publish_record
arguments: role: str, *, host: str='', port: Optional[int]=None, profiles: Sequence[str]=(), token: Optional[str]=None, home: str=''
doc:
Publish this process as the host owner of ``role``. ``None`` when the write failed.

``token`` (serve) is persisted 0600 next to the record and only its fingerprint is published.
``home`` is the launch HERMES_HOME — the key an attaching client needs to reach this owner's
control socket.

name: _invalidate_attach_cache
doc: Drop :mod:`gateway.host_attach`'s memo: the record it summarises just changed.

name: discard_dead_record
doc:
Retract the record for ``role`` when its owner is provably gone; True when one was removed.

A confirmed stop must retract the record too. Leaving it made ``gateway restart --all`` a
silent no-op: the re-entered ``gateway run`` read the corpse's record, decided ATTACH and
exited 0, so the host ended up with no gateway at all.

name: _hold_lock_briefly
doc: Open and flock ``role``'s host lock without registering it; ``None`` when not won.

name: clear_record
doc: Remove this process's record + token on exit (never another owner's).

name: _handle_terminating_signal
doc: Drop the record + token, then hand off to the handler we prepended to.

name: cleanup_on_exit
doc:
Clear ``role``'s record + token and release its lock on exit — SIGTERM included.

``atexit`` alone is false advertising for the NORMAL stop: systemd stop, ``docker stop`` and
the update relaunch all send SIGTERM, and every terminating SIGTERM path here ends in the
default disposition (uvicorn's ``capture_signals`` re-raises it after its graceful shutdown),
which kills the process without running ``atexit``. The record then outlived its process and
the 0600 token kept a LIVE session token on disk indefinitely.

The handler only PREPENDS cleanup: whatever handler was installed before (uvicorn's graceful
shutdown, the exit-flush chain, a supervisor's) still runs, so the shutdown sequence is
unchanged.

name: _multiplex_profiles_enabled
doc:
Will THIS process multiplex? An explicit ``true`` and an unset key both say yes, and an
explicit ``false`` is RETIRED (``hermes_cli.gateway_multiplex_mode``) — it is warned about and
ignored at boot, so it must not make the claim-time record advertise a narrower roster than
the process actually serves. Reading it here was the last place the retired flag still decided
topology, and it made CLI/dashboard report "standalone, serving default" while the runtime
multiplexed. The RUNTIME verdict (a boot-time guard refusal) narrows the record afterwards, in
``gateway.run._refresh_host_gateway_record``, which republishes the SETTLED set.

name: served_profiles
doc:
Profiles this process multiplexes; ``()`` when the roster cannot be read.

``multiplex`` defaults to what this process's own config says. Hard-coding ``True`` here
published a record claiming EVERY profile from a gateway that would only ever serve its own,
and a second profile's supervised unit then stood down against a set nobody serves.

name: describe
doc: One-line human description used by attach messages and conflict logs.

name: _from_served_record
doc:
A gateway started before the host record existed still publishes ``served_profiles`` into
the default home's ``gateway_state.json``; that plus a proven-live PID is the same fact.

name: host_gateway_topology
doc: The one live host gateway and its served profiles, or None when no gateway owns the role.

name: host_gateway_serving
doc: The host gateway when it serves ``profile_name`` (default: the active profile), else None.

name: serves
doc: True when this host process ticks/serves ``profile_name`` (``default`` included).

name: describe
doc:
``the host gateway (PID 42) serving profiles default, coder`` — one shared phrasing so
doctor, cron status and the state.db holder lines cannot drift apart.

name: _release_kanban_dispatcher_lock
doc: Clear notifier-visible ownership before releasing the OS lock.

name: _sleep_between_ticks
doc: Sleep *interval* (floored to 1s) in 1s slices so stop() never waits a full interval.

name: _kanban_notifier_watcher
doc:
Poll ``kanban_notify_subs`` and deliver terminal events to users.

Per subscription, claims ``task_events`` newer than the stored cursor
(kinds in TERMINAL_KINDS), sends one message per event, then advances
the cursor. The subscription is removed only when the task is
``archived``: ``done`` is reversible, so the cursor — not unsubscribing
— is the dedup mechanism (unsub-on-terminal dropped users when the
dispatcher respawned a crashed task). All SQLite work runs in a thread;
one tick's failure never stops the next.

name: _kanban_sub_op
arguments: self, board: Optional[str], op: str, sub: dict, **extra: Any
doc: Sync helper (runs in to_thread): call ``kanban_db_notify.<op>`` for one subscription on its board.

name: _kanban_advance
arguments: self, sub: dict, cursor: int, board: Optional[str]=None

name: _kanban_rewind
arguments: self, sub: dict, claimed_cursor: int, old_cursor: int, board: Optional[str]=None
doc: Undo a claimed notification cursor after send failure.

name: _deliver_kanban_artifacts
arguments: self, *, adapter, chat_id: str, metadata: dict, event_payload: Optional[dict], task
doc:
Upload artifact files referenced by a completed kanban task.

Sources, in priority order: ``event_payload['artifacts']``,
``event_payload['summary']``, then ``task.result`` (legacy). Paths are
deduplicated, missing files are skipped (may be mentioned for
reference only), and upload errors are logged, never raised.

name: _kanban_dispatcher_boot
doc:
Resolve config, kanban_db and the singleton lock; None when the dispatcher must not run.

Config is read once at boot (restart to apply), except the auto-decompose
toggle which is re-read every tick. The env var is an escape hatch to
disable without editing YAML.

name: _kanban_dispatcher_watcher
doc:
Embedded kanban dispatcher — one tick every `dispatch_interval_seconds`.

Gated by `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway` (default True); when false the
loop exits and an external `hermes kanban daemon` is expected. Each
tick runs :func:`kanban_db_dispatch.dispatch_once` in a thread; one tick's
failure never stops the next. Shutdown: ``self._running`` is checked
between ticks and the in-flight ``to_thread`` returns on its own.

name: _run_in_fresh_context
doc:
Run *func* in an empty ``Context`` so request-local ContextVars stay behind.

``asyncio.to_thread`` copies the caller's context; a lingering
``delegate_task`` child marker would make ``write_txn`` false-trip for
these process-owned writers. An empty Context keeps the DB guard intact
for real children without exempting dispatcher writes.

name: _to_thread_process_service
doc: Offload blocking process-service work without inheriting request ContextVars.

name: _list_boards
doc: Enumerate live boards; fall back to the default board when listing fails.

name: _positive_int_setting
doc: Parse an optional ``kanban.<key>`` int cap; None when unset or invalid (< 1 is invalid).

name: _resolve_auto_decompose_settings
doc:
Live (enabled, per_tick) auto-decompose settings, re-read every dispatcher tick.

Fails safe: a config read error returns ``(False, 3)`` rather than
re-enabling a feature the user turned off. ``per_tick`` is clamped to ``>= 1``.

Read fresh from config on every dispatcher tick (#49638) so that flipping ``kanban.auto_decompose:
false`` to STOP runaway fan-out takes effect on the next tick instead of requiring a gateway restart.
Auto-decompose is a safety toggle — a user who sees it create and launch tasks they didn't intend
reaches for this flag to halt it, and a stale boot-captured value silently ignoring that change is the
bug reported in #49638.

name: _gc_retention_days
doc: ``kanban.done_sub_retention_days`` (default 30; 0 disables), re-read per sweep; fails safe to 30.

name: _kanban_dispatch_allowed
_acquire_singleton_lock
doc:
Take the exclusive, non-blocking advisory lock for the sole dispatcher.

Only one gateway machine-wide may run the embedded dispatcher: concurrent
dispatchers double reclaim frequency and claim events, and with
``wal_autocheckpoint=0`` concurrent manual checkpoints can corrupt index
pages. ``dispatch_in_gateway`` is the primary control; this is the backstop.

Returns ``(handle, "held")`` (release via :func:`_release_singleton_lock`),
``(None, "contended")`` when another process holds it (caller must NOT
dispatch), or ``(None, "unavailable")`` when locking cannot be performed
(caller falls back to config control).

name: _release_singleton_lock
doc: Release a lock acquired via :func:`_acquire_singleton_lock`.

name: _resolve_dispatcher_settings
doc: Parse and log the dispatcher settings in their established order.

name: _default_profile_secret_scope
doc:
Install the gateway launch profile's secret scope while multiplexing is on.

The tick runs via ``_to_thread_process_service`` in a fresh context, so no
per-turn scope exists and ``get_secret`` fails closed. The decomposer's aux
LLM reads ``auxiliary.*`` from ``get_hermes_home()``, so its credentials come
from that same home. No-op for single-profile gateways.

name: _log_spawn_results
doc: Log per-board spawn summaries; returns whether any board spawned.

name: _quarantine_lifted
doc: Return False while *slug* stays quarantined; lift (and log) otherwise.

name: tick_once_for_board
doc:
Run one dispatch_once for a specific board.

The per-board DB is opened explicitly so boards never share a
connection or claim across each other.

name: tick_once
doc: Run one dispatch_once per board. Returns (slug, result) pairs.

name: ready_nonempty
doc:
Is there a ready+assigned+unclaimed task on ANY board the dispatcher would spawn for?

Control-plane lanes (e.g. ``orion-cc``) are pulled by terminals via
``claim_task`` and never spawnable — a queue full of those is
"correctly idle", not "stuck". The review column is probed only when
review dispatch is on (same gate as the dispatcher): a task waiting
for a human reviewer is idle, not stuck.

name: auto_decompose_tick
doc:
Auto-decompose up to N triage tasks across all boards into ready workgraphs.

Runs before dispatch fans out; the per-tick cap keeps a bulk triage
load from burst-spending the aux LLM. Returns the number decomposed.

name: _decompose_one
doc: Decompose one triage task; returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

name: _pin_first
doc:
Machine-flow board resolution: env pins outrank the enumerated slug.

The slug here came from ``list_boards()``, not from a user — on a box whose
env pins ``HERMES_KANBAN_DB`` every board must resolve to the pinned file
or the notifier reads per-slug DBs nobody writes (see
``kanban_db.pin_first_board_resolution``).

name: diagnostic_event
doc: Infrastructure attention is distinct from an explicit owner decision.

name: _safe_review_reason
doc: Return a mobile-friendly review reason safe for external delivery.

name: _wake_scope_id
doc:
Return the tenant scope (Slack workspace) a subscription's wake keys to.

``build_session_key()`` includes ``scope_id`` on multi-tenant platforms,
so the wake must carry the same scope as inbound messages. Persisted
``delivery_metadata`` wins (it records the creating scope); the adapter's
live chat → scope map only covers rows without metadata. ``None`` means
unscoped, matching an unscoped platform's key.

name: _warn_anchorless_thread_sub_once
doc:
A thread-shaped subscription without ``parent_chat_id`` cannot match a channel-level
``profile_routes`` entry, so the fail-closed route gate skips it on every tick. Say so ONCE per
row at WARNING — a subscription that can never deliver was invisible below DEBUG (#110919).

name: _warn_unroutable_sub_once
arguments: sub: dict, platform: Any, message: str, *extra_args: Any
doc:
A routed subscription the credential gate fail-closes is a permanent dead-end: delivery
rewinds every tick with only a DEBUG line. Say so ONCE per row at WARNING, mirroring
``_warn_anchorless_thread_sub_once`` (#115460).

name: _platform_names
doc: Lower-cased platform names of an adapters mapping (Platform enums or strings).

name: _adapter_for_subscription
arguments: runner: Any, platform: Any, sub: dict, owner_profile: Optional[str]
doc: Resolve a durable route without turning a missing secondary bot into primary authority.

name: _notifier_collect
arguments: runner: Any, kb: Any, *, notifier_profile: Optional[str], gc_due: bool, gc_retention_days: int
doc:
Claim unseen terminal events for every owned subscription on every board.

Each gateway polls only subscriptions owned by profiles whose adapters it
hosts; legacy rows without a profile stamp are visible only to the process
holding the singleton dispatcher lock.

name: _payload
doc: Shared "payload present and truthy" read.

name: _clip
arguments: ev: Any, key: str, msg_key: str, limit: int
doc:
Catalog message ``msg_key`` (``{value}`` placeholder) rendered with the truncated payload
value, or ``""`` when absent.

name: _fmt_block_loop_detected
doc:
Re-blocked for the same cause past the limit and routed to `triage`.

It emits no blocked/status event, so ping loudly here. A repeated-block
circuit breaker establishes that orchestration attention is needed; it
does NOT establish that a human decision or owner input exists. Use
neutral orchestration wording unless the block was typed as a genuine
owner-input request (`needs_input`, the only kind that carries a concrete
question for the owner).

arguments: self, runner: Any, kb: Any, *, notifier_profile: Optional[str], gc_due: bool, gc_retention_days: int

doc:
Cheap read-only probe before the writable connect() (schema init, WAL
sidecars, checkpoints); a probe failure falls back to the writable open.

name: _gc_stale_subs
doc: Best-effort stale-sub sweep: a failed sweep never blocks delivery; the next hourly gate retries.

name: _claim_for_sub

doc: Claim one subscription's unseen events; None when skipped or nothing new.

name: collect_board

arguments: self, runner: Any, d: dict, *, platform_cls: Any, sub_fail_counts: dict

arguments: self, fmt: str, prefix: tuple, drop_fmt: str, exc: Exception, exc_info: bool
doc: Bump the failure counter; drop the sub past the limit, else rewind the claim so the next tick retries.

name: format_event
doc: Render one event; accumulates wake handoff/review detail. None → silent kind.

name: build_wake_text
doc: Set ``wake_kinds`` / ``session_key`` / ``synth`` for the wake paths.

name: _served_wake_profile
doc:
The subscription's profile when THIS gateway is a multiplexer serving it, else ``None``.

``None`` keeps the historical path: a standalone ``hermes -p <name>`` gateway owns its own
listener and key, so its api_server wakes keep using the HTTP self-post.

name: _owner_scope
doc: Runtime scope of the subscription's profile under multiplex, else a no-op context.

name: wake
doc: Wake the creator session (raises on failure): push adapters get a full SessionSource, non-push a raw self-post.

name: _send_event
doc: Send one text ping; raises on adapter exception or SendResult(success=False).

name: _send_pings
doc: Send every text ping; False when a send failed (claim already rewound/dropped).

name: _process_hermes_home
doc: HERMES_HOME for process-level identity files (ignore task overrides).

name: get_lifecycle_sentinel_path
doc: Return ``<HERMES_HOME>/state/gateway.lifecycle.json``.

name: _proc_fields
doc: ``{dst: int}`` for each ``src: dst`` key found in a ``Key: value`` /proc file.

name: sample_memory
doc:
Cheap /proc snapshot (KiB): own RSS + MemTotal/MemAvailable + swap used.  Linux-only
(``{}`` elsewhere), never raises; the 30s heartbeat embeds it so OOM cycles are classifiable.

name: _append_exit_diag
doc: Append a JSON line to gateway-exit-diag.log (same format as the CLI's ``_exit_diag``).

name: _pid_is_sentinel_owner
arguments: pid: Any, start_time: Any, create_time: Any
doc:
True when ``pid`` is a live process that is the sentinel's incarnation — guards the
``--replace`` race: a live matching owner mid-teardown is a handover, not a death.

Identity is the psutil ``create_time`` the sentinel stamps at claim (epoch seconds, same
producer on both sides). The sentinel's ``start_time`` is the ledger claim time and is NOT
comparable with ``gateway.status.get_process_start_time`` (proc ticks on Linux, centiseconds
elsewhere) — the old comparison never matched, so every ``--replace`` handover read as an
unclean death. A pre-stamp sentinel (no ``create_time``) still has ``start_time`` in epoch
seconds: the owner was born BEFORE it claimed, a PID reuser AFTER the owner died, so a birth
later than the claim is a reuser.

name: _suspected_oom
doc:
Heuristic only (classification stays with the reader); thresholds are
memory_status' "critical" tier so a live warning and a post-mortem verdict agree.

name: detect_unclean_exit
doc: Evidence dict when the previous life died uncleanly, else ``None``. Read-only.

name: _install_integrity_check_lease
doc:
Claim the integrity-check lease and renew it from a SQLite progress handler.

``report_startup_progress`` is a no-op when no watchdog is armed and never raises.
Without ``deadline_at`` the handler always returns 0 -- it must never abort the verdict
PRAGMA.  With ``deadline_at`` (a ``time.monotonic`` timestamp) it returns non-zero once
that instant is reached, so SQLite raises ``OperationalError: interrupted`` and the
caller can bound the scan.  Synchronous by design: no checker worker thread can outlive
the check.

name: check_state_db_integrity
doc:
``"ok"``, ``"absent"``, or the first ``quick_check`` complaint.  Never raises.

Only after an unclean death — SIGKILL mid-WAL-checkpoint can leave half-written
b-tree pages.  ``quick_check(1)`` stops at the first problem (~2s on a healthy
500MB store): cheap once per unclean boot, too costly every boot.  Opened
normally: a WAL store needs its -shm sidecar for read-only, and the PRAGMA writes nothing.

Holds a phase-owned startup-watchdog lease for the check duration
(renewed from a SQLite progress handler, #115542) so a long healthy check
on a huge store is not mistaken for a parked deadlock.

``deadline_s`` (optional): abort the scan once that many seconds elapse and
return ``"check-incomplete: exceeded <N>s"``.  ``deadline_s=None`` (default) is the
historic unbounded behaviour -- the progress handler never aborts the PRAGMA.

name: _state_db_journal_mode
doc:
On-disk journal mode of ``path`` via one ``PRAGMA journal_mode`` read on a short-lived
connection (no lock outlives it); ``None`` when undeterminable.  Never raises.

name: _report_unclean_exit
arguments: evidence: dict[str, Any], home: Optional[Path], *, defer_integrity_check: bool=False
doc:
Persist the exit-diag record and log at WARNING.

When ``defer_integrity_check`` is set, the forensic store scan is NOT run here (it would
gate platform startup); the record carries ``state_db_integrity: "deferred"`` and
:func:`run_deferred_integrity_check` runs the scan post-connect.

name: record_startup
doc:
Boot entry point: report any unclean previous exit (evidence dict, also persisted
to ``gateway-exit-diag.log`` and logged at WARNING) then claim the sentinel.  Never raises.

``defer_integrity_check`` defaults to True: the state.db integrity scan is forensic and
must NOT gate platform startup (a large store's ``quick_check`` blocked the ``:8644`` fleet
peer-DM transport for minutes).  In deferred mode the exit-diag record is written
immediately with ``state_db_integrity: "deferred"`` and the scan runs post-connect via
:func:`run_deferred_integrity_check`.  Pass False for the historic INLINE scan.

name: run_deferred_integrity_check
arguments: evidence: Optional[dict[str, Any]], *, home: Optional[Path]=None, deadline_s: float=STATE_DB_INTEGRITY_DEADLINE_S
doc:
Run the deferred post-connect state.db scan and append a second diag record.

Companion to :func:`record_startup` with ``defer_integrity_check=True``: the forensic scan
is moved off the startup path (where, on a multi-GB store, it gated every platform adapter
— including the ``:8644`` fleet peer-DM transport — for minutes) into a daemon thread
started only after platforms connected.  ``deadline_s`` bounds a pathological store so the
thread cannot be pinned forever.

Appends ``{"tag": "gateway.state_db_integrity", "deferred": true, "state_db_integrity":
<verdict>, "prior_pid": ...}`` and logs the existing ERROR text on a bad verdict.  NEVER
raises -- a forensic scan must not disturb a running gateway (the alerting path is the
bounded per-poll readiness probe ``gateway/readiness.py::_probe_state_db``).

Only a WAL store is scanned: in rollback-journal mode (``database.journal_mode: delete``,
or a silent WAL fallback) the scan's SHARED lock would block every live commit for its
whole run, so the scan is skipped with a ``skipped: ...`` verdict and one WARNING.  The
on-disk mode decides, not config; an undeterminable mode is skipped too.

name: mark_exited
arguments: exit_code: Optional[int]=None, reason: str='graceful_shutdown', home: Optional[Path]=None
doc:
Mark the current life as cleanly exited.  Idempotent, never raises.

Only rewrites a sentinel provably owned by this process: during ``--replace``
the replacement claims it before the old process finishes teardown and must not
be clobbered.  ``pid=None`` / malformed sentinels have unknown ownership → left alone.

name: read_prior_exit_label
doc:
``clean``/``unclean``/``unknown`` for the profile's last gateway life; annotates
``container-boot.log``.  ``running`` is unclean: the old PID namespace is gone at container boot.

name: _emit
doc: ``desktop_ui`` sink: publish *event* on the stream of the turn that raised it.

name: _publish_process
doc: Publish a process event on the stream of the session that owns the process.

name: _install_process_sinks
doc: main's ``_wire_desktop_sinks``: live output and tab close for background processes (once).

name: _install_connection_hook
doc: ``connection.update`` for an operation opened by one of our turns, on the session that owns it (same session key and profile, as the sidecar matches its own); any other operation goes to the hook this one wraps (the sidecar's, for its own sessions). Re-wraps whenever another hook replaced it, so install order does not matter.

name: _ask_result
doc: One structured server request; the viewer's ``result`` dict, or None when none answered.

name: _theme
doc: main's ``theme_request``: ``theme.apply`` for values, or a ``theme.pick`` card that waits.

name: _tour
doc: main's ``_tour_request``: probe once per session, then the full deadline or fail fast.

name: _ask
doc: One ``ValueResult`` server request to the session's attached viewers; "" when none answered.

name: _preview_action
doc:
main's ``_preview_action_request`` ladder: a short probe until the renderer has answered once,
then the full deadline; an unanswered probe fails fast for a cooldown instead of stacking waits.

name: wire
doc: Install the window bridges for one local-viewer turn; returns the registry key to release.

name: release
doc: Drop this turn's routing entry, unless a newer turn of the same session already replaced it.

name: wire
doc: Install this turn's local-viewer sinks on ``agent``; returns what ``restore`` needs.

significant_calls.expression: publish("agent.print", {"text": str(kwargs.get("sep", " ")).join(str(a) for a in args)})

name: show_reasoning
doc:
The session's ``show_reasoning`` display flag (``config.set``, ``/reasoning show|hide``); unset on an
Ink or Desktop launch, its ``display.show_reasoning`` (default on), as main's TUI gateway resolved it.

name: launch_shows_reasoning
doc: An unset session flag: ``display.show_reasoning`` for an Ink or Desktop launch, else off.

name: publish_progress
doc: ``subagent.*``, ``reasoning.available`` and the MoA facade events from the agent's progress callback; a classic CLI renders MoA references whatever its reasoning display (main's ``_on_tool_progress``), while other viewers get them only with reasoning shown.

significant_calls.expression:
_publish_subagent(turn, event_type, _subagent_payload(
            event_type, name, preview, kwargs, show_reasoning=show_reasoning(turn)))

name: publish_control_if_changed
doc:
Agent thread, after each tool: a tool (a plugin adding goal criteria, parking the goal) can move
automation state mid-turn, so viewers' cards repaint now instead of at turn end. The snapshot is read,
compared and published on the gateway loop, in order with the slash commands' publishes (a snapshot
read here could land after a newer one); revision-gated, so other tools publish nothing.

name: note_tool_start
doc:
Monotonic start time of one call (``tool.complete.duration_s``) and, for a write-capable
tool, the before-state of its local files: the agent fires the start callback BEFORE the tool
writes, so the gateway owns the snapshot the classic CLI used to take in process.

name: complete_fields
doc:
``duration_s``, ``inline_diff`` (the rendered edit diff main's CLI printed after a write,
``None`` when there is none) and, for the todo tool, the full ``todos`` snapshot.

name: todo_state
doc: The client-safe ``{todos, revision}`` snapshot a todo tool's result carries, else None.

name: prompt_timeout_s
doc:
``timeout_s`` of a local viewer's approval / clarify prompt: the window the gateway's own wait
enforces (``approvals.timeout`` / the clarify timeout), so the classic CLI's modal shows the
same countdown and gives up when the gateway does. ``None`` on a messaging turn (frame
unchanged) and for an unlimited clarify wait.

significant_calls.expression: publish("agent.print", {"text": str(kwargs.get("sep", " ")).join(str(a) for a in args)})

name: remote_path_is_denied
doc:
Pure string check (the remote fs can't be stat'd from here) applying the host denylist to a
sandbox path. Unknown home ⇒ home-relative entries match ANY path component (conservative).

name: _active_remote_env
doc:
The live remote BaseEnvironment for the current session, or None (local backend / no env yet).
Keyed by the session id the turn registered its sandbox under (falls back to the session key).

name: fetch_remote_media
doc:
Host path of a validated copy of sandbox file ``path``, or None (never raises). Only fires
when a remote backend is active; the caller has already failed local validation.

name: _routed_gateway_cfg
doc:
``gateway`` section of the ROUTED profile's config when a HERMES_HOME override is active
(multiplexed turn), else None. The env bridge is one process-wide copy of the launch profile's
policy, so a secondary's deliveries must read their own config instead of ``os.environ``.

name: media_delivery_allow_dirs
doc: Operator allowlist as the ``os.pathsep``-joined string the validator splits.

name: media_delivery_trust_recent_seconds
doc: Raw recency window (``""`` = validator default); the caller parses/floors it.

name: _set_env_default
doc: Set ``env`` only when unset/empty and ``value`` is non-empty (env wins).

name: apply_media_policy_env
doc:
Bridge gateway media-policy settings from config.yaml into the env.  Idempotent,
env-wins, never raises — a bridge failure must not break delivery (validator defaults apply).

No-op under a HERMES_HOME override, the same gate the readers use: there they take the
profile's own config (``_routed_gateway_cfg``), and ``os.environ`` is shared — a routed cron
fire would hand its allowlist and strictness to the launch profile and its children.

name: tool_name_by_call_id
doc: Map assistant tool-call ids to tool names for the given messages.

name: _computer_use_capture_basename
doc: Canonical (lowercased) capture basename for either separator style, or ''.

name: _iter_computer_use_capture_paths
doc:
Yield persisted screenshot paths from computer_use result content (JSON, a
multimodal list, or text; the latter two keep the canonical path in the summary
line since the envelope's ``meta`` is not stored in the tool message).

name: repair_explicit_computer_use_media_paths
arguments: response: str, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], history_offset: int=0
doc:
Recover model-mangled paths in explicit ``MEDIA:`` directives whose basename
matches (case-insensitively) a canonical screenshot path from this turn.
Fail-open: the repair is cosmetic, so any error returns the response unchanged.

name: _canonical_capture_paths
doc: ``{lowercase basename: absolute canonical path}`` from this turn's computer_use results.

name: _repair_explicit_computer_use_media_paths_inner
arguments: response: str, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], history_offset: int=0

name: _get_rss_mb
doc: Return process RSS high-water mark in MB, or None if unavailable.

name: log_memory_usage
doc: Log ``[MEMORY] [<prefix> ]rss=... gc=... threads=... uptime=...``; safe from any thread.

name: _monitor_loop
doc: Background thread body — log every ``interval`` seconds until stopped.

name: start_memory_monitoring
doc:
Start periodic logging in a daemon thread (baseline logged immediately).  False if
already running or RSS introspection is unavailable (warned once).

name: stop_memory_monitoring
doc: Stop the monitor thread and log a final ``shutdown`` snapshot. No-op if never started.

name: is_running
doc: True if the background monitor thread is alive.

name: _nonneg_int
doc: Return *value* if it is a non-negative int (bools rejected), else None.

name: classify_pressure
doc:
``ok``/``elevated``/``critical`` from MemAvailable/MemTotal; ``unknown`` when the
sample is missing/malformed — "could not read it" must never read as "fine".

name: _read_state_files
doc: ``(heartbeat, sentinel)`` dicts, each ``None`` when unreadable.

name: collect_memory_status
doc:
``memory`` block for ``/api/status``; ``home`` scopes to a profile (``None`` =
active), ``now`` is injectable.  Never raises — a down gateway or corrupt files
yield ``pressure="unknown"`` plus whatever fields could be recovered.

name: _localize
doc: Epoch for ``dt`` in ``tz`` or the local zone; None outside platform limits.

name: _parse_iso
doc: Parse an ISO-8601 string (incl. ``+0200`` offsets fromisoformat rejects).

name: coerce_message_timestamp
doc:
Epoch seconds from a number, datetime, ISO string, or the gateway's bracketed
format; ``None`` when uninterpretable.

name: format_message_timestamp
doc: Format a timestamp value as ``[Tue 2026-04-28 13:40:53 CEST]``.

name: strip_leading_message_timestamps
doc:
Strip leading gateway timestamp prefixes → ``(clean_content, embedded_epoch)``.
With several prefixes the one closest to the text wins, preserving the platform-send
time of legacy rows like ``[processing time] [platform time] [sender] message``.

name: render_user_content_with_timestamp
doc:
Render a user message for LLM context with exactly one timestamp prefix; an
existing prefix is stripped and its parsed time wins over ``ts_value``.

name: _resolve_sessions_index
doc:
Active profile's ``sessions.json`` at call time: the patched ``_SESSIONS_INDEX`` when a test
changed it, else live profile-scoped HERMES_HOME — under the multiplexed gateway one process
serves every profile, so the import-time constant would resolve every profile's pre-migration
session lookup against the launch profile's index.

name: mirror_to_session
arguments: platform: str, chat_id: str, message_text: str, source_label: str='cli', thread_id: Optional[str]=None, user_id: Optional[str]=None, role: str='assistant', session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Append a delivery-mirror message to the target session's SQLite transcript.

Pass ``session_id`` when the caller already holds the exact session (e.g. the
cron in_channel seed) to skip the origin scan, which refuses to guess on a
populated chat (flat + N thread sessions per chat_id) and would drop the mirror.
Text that is NOT the agent speaking (e.g. a cron brief) must pass
``role="user"``: ``mirror`` metadata is dropped at the SQLite boundary, so an
assistant-role mirror replays as a real turn and yields assistant→assistant
pairs that break strict-alternation providers, while a user-role mirror
collapses safely via the consecutive-user merge.
Returns True if mirrored, False if no matching session or error. Never raises.

``role`` defaults to ``"assistant"`` — correct for the interactive ``send_message`` mirror, where the
mirrored text is the agent's own outgoing reply (a genuine assistant turn). See #2221.

name: _find_session_id
arguments: platform: str, chat_id: str, thread_id: Optional[str]=None, user_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Active session_id for a platform + chat_id pair.

state.db is primary; sessions.json is the pre-migration fallback.  DM keys
don't embed the chat_id ("agent:main:telegram:dm"), so match on the persisted
origin.  With *user_id*, exact sender matches win; several same-chat candidates
with no user match → None rather than contaminate another participant's session.

Queries state.db gateway session rows (primary source since #9006); falls back to scanning sessions.json
for pre-migration databases.

name: _append_to_sqlite
doc:
Append a message to the SQLite session database.

Raises on failure: ``mirror_to_session`` reports ``False`` (and warns) only when the
exception reaches it — swallowing it here made every failed write look mirrored (#10130).

name: _allowlist_env_for_platform
doc:
Allowlist env var name for ``platform`` (its ``PlatformEntry.allowed_users_env``), or None.

Approving a code also writes the user into an already-configured allowlist (revoke removes
them) so the operator's list stays the visible source of truth. Platforms without one (or with
no allowlist configured) keep the pairing store as the sole grant record (authz union). See
#23778. Discovers plugins first: ``hermes pairing approve`` runs in a CLI process that may not
have loaded them yet.

name: _platform_uses_whatsapp_identity
doc: True for Baileys WhatsApp and Meta Cloud — same phone/JID identity rules.

name: _normalize_user_id
doc: Normalize platform-specific user IDs before persisting / comparing them.

name: _user_id_aliases
doc: All known equivalent user IDs for auth / allowlist matching.

name: _user_ids_match
arguments: platform: str, left: str, right: str
doc: True when two user IDs represent the same principal.

name: _matching_ids
arguments: platform: str, approved: dict, user_id: str

name: _read_allowlist_env
doc:
Read a platform allowlist env var through the profile secret scope.

Under multiplexing the process env may hold ANOTHER profile's allowlist, so a
scoped miss must return empty rather than borrow it. The shared reader owns the
contract: a bound-scope failure propagates (never silently borrows the env),
while the unscoped default-profile path keeps the legacy ``os.getenv`` read.
Writes (``save_env_value``/``remove_env_value``) target the active profile's
``.env`` / installed scope, not ``os.environ``.

See #88441.

name: _configured_allowlist
doc:
``(env_var, ids)`` for a platform whose allowlist is configured, else None.

An unconfigured allowlist means an open gateway: the pairing store stays the
sole grant record and we must never lock the gateway by materializing one.

name: _write_allowlist_env
doc: Best-effort persist (empty list removes the key); the pairing store grant still authorizes via the union.

name: _sync_allowlist_add
doc: Add ``user_id`` to the platform allowlist env var IF one is configured.

name: _iter_live_gateway_adapters
doc: Yield adapters from the in-process GatewayRunner, if one is running.

name: _purge_allowlist_entries
doc: Drop alias-equivalent allowlist entries while preserving ``*``.

name: _sync_live_adapter_allowlist_remove
doc:
Clear revoked principals from in-process adapter allowlist snapshots,
so intake and adapter-owned controls do not keep authorizing until restart.

name: _sync_allowlist_remove
doc:
Remove ``user_id`` (and WhatsApp alias equivalents) from the allowlist.

Approve mirrors a normalized phone while revoke is often given a JID/device
form, so matching uses alias rules -- exact delete would leave the sender authorized.
An unconfigured allowlist is left alone (config-only snapshots are not touched).

name: _load_json_file
doc:
Read a JSON object; {} when missing, malformed, unreadable, or not a dict.

PermissionError is logged loudly: a 0600 file owned by another uid (Docker:
``docker exec`` as root wrote it, the gosu-dropped gateway can't read it)
would otherwise silently leave the user unauthorized.

name: _migrate_split_pairing_dirs
doc:
Merge split legacy (``pairing``) / new (``platforms/pairing``) data into the active dir.

If both exist, approved users in the inactive location must not be silently
ignored (they would be asked for a fresh code). Active data wins on key conflict.

name: _dir_lock_holder
doc: Per-directory reentrancy holder for ``_file_lock`` (shared by every store on that dir).

name: _entry_created_at
doc: Numeric ``created_at`` of a pending entry, or None for malformed/legacy entries.

name: profile
doc: Profile name this store is scoped to, or None for the global store.

name: _cleanup_expired
doc: Remove expired pending codes; malformed/legacy entries (no numeric ``created_at``) count as expired.

name: _locked
doc:
Serialize load->mutate->save across stores and processes: the dashboard builds a
store per request and the CLI runs in its own process, so ``self._lock`` alone is not enough.
The file lock is taken FIRST: ``is_approved`` runs on the gateway event loop under
``self._lock``, so holding it while waiting (up to 10 s) on another process would stall
every chat on that loop. ``is_approved`` never takes the file lock, so the order is safe.

name: is_approved
doc: Check if a user is approved (paired) on a platform.

name: list_approved
doc: List approved users, optionally filtered by platform.

name: _approve_user
arguments: self, platform: str, user_id: str, user_name: str=''
doc: Add a user to the approved list. Must be called under self._locked().

name: revoke
doc: Remove a user from the approved list. Returns True if found.

name: _finish_approval
arguments: self, platform: str, pending: dict, matched_key: str, matched_entry: dict
doc: Remove a pending request and approve its user. Must hold self._locked().

name: generate_code
arguments: self, platform: str, user_id: str, user_name: str=''
doc:
Generate a pairing code for a new user.

Returns None if the user is rate-limited, the platform hit MAX_PENDING_PER_PLATFORM,
or the platform is locked out. Only a salted SHA-256 hash of the code is persisted.

name: approve_code
doc:
Approve a pairing code and add its user to the approved list.

Returns ``{user_id, user_name}``, or ``None`` if the code is invalid/expired OR the
platform is locked out (disambiguate with ``_is_locked_out``). Constant-time
salted-hash compare; legacy plaintext entries are ignored and pruned at TTL.

See #10195.

name: looks_like_request_id
doc:
True when ``value`` is shaped like a ``list_pending`` request id (16 hex chars);
pairing codes are 8 uppercase chars, so callers accepting either can dispatch on this.

name: approve_request
doc:
Approve a pending request by its server-side request id (admin surfaces that
must never reveal the DM'd code). Returns ``{user_id, user_name}`` or ``None``.

Neither counts toward nor is gated by the brute-force lockout: a request id is only
obtainable by an authenticated admin, so a stale id is "the row expired", not an
attack -- counting it would let a few GUI clicks lock the operator out.

name: list_pending
doc:
List pending requests (codes are never returned; each exposes a ``request_id``
for :meth:`approve_request`; legacy pre-hash entries report an empty id).

name: clear_pending
doc: Clear all pending requests. Returns count removed.

name: _is_rate_limited
doc: Whether a user (under any alias) has requested a code too recently.

name: has_recent_decline
doc: Whether this sender (under any alias) was sent a polite decline within DECLINE_DEDUPE_SECONDS.

name: record_decline
doc:
Stamp the sender (all aliases) and prune expired stamps. Callers stamp BEFORE sending so a
delivery failure cannot become a decline storm on the sender's next message.

name: _record_failed_attempt
doc: Record a failed approval attempt; triggers lockout after MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS.

name: _reset_failed_attempts
doc: Clear the failed-approval counter after a success (it tracks *consecutive* failures).

name: _all_platforms
doc: Platforms that have a ``-<suffix>.json`` data file (``_``-prefixed files are shared state).

name: retryable_ingress
doc:
Scope an awaited dispatch its transport has not acknowledged. A parked route inside it is only
recorded (``scope.refused``) for the caller to raise :class:`ParkedRouteRefused`; no in-chat notice.
Closed on exit, so a task that outlives the dispatch still refuses in-channel.

name: _notice_due
doc: True (and the window restarts) when this chat was not told about *profile* in the window.

name: drop_rejected_route
doc:
Log an inbound event dropped because its explicit profile route targets a profile this
gateway does not serve; when that profile is parked, also refuse it to the sender in-channel.

name: refuse_parked_route
doc:
Refuse an event routed to the parked *profile*, nothing admitted: answered retryably inside
:func:`retryable_ingress`, else told to the sender in-channel, in reply to *reply_to* (default:
the source's message), off the caller, which may be the transport reader a relay send waits on.

significant_calls.expression:
asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(
            _send_refusal(adapter, source, reply_to or getattr(source, 'message_id', None)))

name: _send_refusal
doc:
Reply in the sender's chat and thread, as the runner's own notices do. Marked interim: it is no
turn's answer, so it never seals another turn's open stream (relay Slack) or fills a pending
answer slot (LINE's postback cache).

name: _yaml_block_names
doc:
Keys of every mapping a platform block may live in (``platform_section`` /
``merge_platform_sections`` read the same places): ``<name>:``, ``platforms.<name>``,
``gateway.<name>``, ``gateway.platforms.<name>``.

name: activation_predicate
arguments: *, yaml_cfg: Any=None, platform_names: Iterable[str]=(), home: Optional[Path]=None, registry: Any=None
doc:
``name -> bool``: does this profile show evidence of configuring platform *name*?

*yaml_cfg* is the loaded config.yaml layer (read from *home* when omitted), *platform_names*
any already-merged platform keys (``GatewayConfig.platforms``). *home* defaults to the active
Hermes home.

name: configured_plugin_entries
doc:
Plugin entries for platforms this profile configures (see module docstring); already-loaded
entries are always included. Never imports an adapter with no activation evidence.

name: int_or
doc: ``int(raw.strip(), 10)`` with *default* on malformed/blank input.

name: mention_patterns
doc: JSON list, else comma/newline separated.

name: csv_extras
doc: ``extra[key] = csv_list(raw)`` for each ``(key, raw)`` whose list is non-empty.

name: env_first
doc: First truthy value among *envs* (a single name or a tuple of alternatives).

name: env_extras
arguments: extra: dict[str, Any], spec, *, strip: bool=False
doc:
``extra[key] = fn(value)`` for each ``(key, env[, fn])`` whose env value is truthy.

``strip=True`` strips BEFORE the truthiness check. ``fn=INT`` parses an int
and silently ignores a non-integer value.

name: env_home_channel
arguments: config: GatewayConfig, platform: Platform, env_base: str, *, strip: bool=False
doc: Set ``home_channel`` from ``<env_base>`` (+``_NAME``/``_THREAD_ID``) when the platform is configured.

name: env_reply_mode
arguments: config: GatewayConfig, platform: Platform, env: str

name: home_step
arguments: platform: Platform, env_base: str, *, strip: bool=False

name: enable_from_env
doc:
Enable *platform* on env credentials unless config.yaml explicitly disabled it (warns once).
Delegates to the core gate, which owns the explicit-disable marker and the one-time WARNING.

name: bundled_sibling
doc:
``plugins/platforms/<directory>/<stem>.py`` (a light declaration module importing only core)
executed from its file under a private name: the plugin package (``__init__``, adapter,
``register()``) is never imported. None when absent or *directory* is not a bundled plugin.

name: bundled_env_rows
doc:
``(env_overrides, env_enable_credentials)`` a BUNDLED platform plugin declares, read without
the plugin. For when its registry entry is absent: discovery suppressed (a parked profile's
config read, ``HERMES_SAFE_MODE``) or the plugin disabled. These rows were core's own table, and
the duplicate-credential guard and the explicit-disable warning still need them then.

name: bundled_authz
doc:
``AUTHZ`` (allowlist / allow-all / allow-bots / own-policy env names) a bundled platform
plugin declares in its ``gateway_env.py``, read without the plugin; {} for other names.

name: authz_field
arguments: name: str, field: str, entry: Any=None
doc:
*entry*'s authorization env field, else the bundled plugin's declaration. A user plugin
overriding a bundled platform, safe mode or a disabled plugin then still gate on the names core
always enforced for it; never looser than the bundled adapter.

name: _plugin_scope_from_callable
doc: Infer a plugin profile from code registered outside PluginContext.

name: core_ships_platform
doc:
*name* is a platform core ships an adapter for: a static ``Platform`` member or a bundled
``plugins/platforms/`` plugin. A user plugin may replace such an adapter but never mark it
``trusted_inbound``: its senders are people, and that flag waives allowlists and pairing.

name: _registration_state
arguments: self, scope: Optional[str], name: str, *, create: bool=False
doc: (entry, loader) for *name*; the loader falls back to in-flight, then consumed.

name: register_deferred
arguments: self, name: str, loader: _Loader, *, scope: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Register a lazy loader (imports the plugin module, which must call :meth:`register`);
runs at most once, on first lookup; a concrete registration drops it.

name: note_activation_env
doc: Record the env names a deferred platform's manifest declares (see ``_activation_env``).

name: snapshot_registration
doc:
Concrete and deferred state for *name* without resolving it, so the plugin ledger can
restore a deferred loader displaced by a concrete registration without importing it.

name: restore_registration
arguments: self, name: str, current: tuple[Optional[PlatformEntry], Optional[_Loader]], previous: tuple[Optional[PlatformEntry], Optional[_Loader]], *, scope: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Restore a registration if its full state is still *current* (CAS): a later
registration is never removed, and deferred loaders are part of the state.

name: _resolve
doc: Run the deferred loader for *name* if one is pending.

name: is_deferred_load_cancelled
doc: Whether ownership teardown cancelled an in-flight loader.

name: _pending_names
doc: Deferred (or in-flight) names for *active_scope*, scoped first, without loading them.

name: _resolve_all
doc:
Run every pending deferred loader, or only those *wanted* accepts (``all_entries`` /
``plugin_entries`` / ``configured_entries``; CLI chat never iterates the full set).

name: pending_names
doc: Names registered as deferred loaders that have not been imported yet (current scope).

name: configured_entries
doc:
Loaded entries, after materializing only the deferred platforms *wanted* accepts.

The gateway's config/env passes need each platform's hooks only for platforms the profile
actually configures; importing every bundled adapter (~20 SDKs) just to read metadata cost
every cold start ~0.5 s. *wanted* is :func:`gateway.platform_activation.has_activation_evidence`
(or a test stub); entries that are already loaded are always returned.

name: loaded_entries
doc: Entries already materialized (never imports a deferred adapter).

name: register
doc: Register a platform adapter entry (last writer wins on name clash).

name: unregister
doc: Remove a platform entry. Returns True if it existed.

name: _load_pending
doc: True when a lookup of *name* must run/await a deferred loader (lock held).

name: get
doc: Look up a platform entry by name.

name: all_entries
doc: Return all registered platform entries.

name: plugin_entries
doc: Return only plugin-registered platform entries.

name: registered_names
doc:
Concrete and deferred names (current profile scope AND process-global, like
``is_registered``) without loading adapters.

name: required_env_names
doc:
``required_env`` of every loaded entry (current profile scope AND process-global) without
loading deferred adapters; the child-env scrub reads this on every spawn.

name: create_adapter
doc:
Create an adapter instance for *name*; None when no entry exists, deps are missing
and cannot be installed, ``validate_config`` fails, or the factory raises.

name: chat_choices
doc:
Bind the messaging asker for a command *source* sent, unless the caller bound one already (a
local viewer's ``slash.exec``) or the source is a local session (it has no chat to post in).

name: _ask_chat
arguments: runner, source, session_key, loop, question, labels

name: viewer_choices
doc: Bind the local-session asker: the ``clarify`` server request to *live*'s attached viewers.

name: _refuse
arguments: plugin_id: str, kind: str, detail: str

name: resolve
arguments: runner, *, plugin_home, calling_session_key: str, plugin_id: str
doc:
``(authority, live session)`` the key-less inject goes to, or ``None`` (logged). Runs on the
plugin's calling thread so a refusal is the plugin's own ``False``; it only reads the authority's
live map, never the store.

name: admit
arguments: runner, authority, live, *, content: str, plugin_id: str
doc:
Commit the text to *live*'s durable FIFO through the keyed path's producer admission, under the
plugin's profile (whose authority resolved it).

name: _fit
arguments: adapter: Any, chat_id: str, text: str
doc: Clamp *text* to the adapter's per-chat message limit (ellipsis), never split it.

name: bound_route
doc:
The live source bound in THIS context (read on the caller's thread: the gateway loop runs the
send in its own context), or ``None``.

name: resolve
arguments: runner, *, session_key: str, route, plugin_home, plugin_id: str
doc:
``(PostTarget, None)`` for the session *session_key* names, or ``(None, error dict)``. *route*
is the live source the gateway bound for this call, used only while the session is not stored.

name: post
arguments: target: PostTarget, text: str, *, plugin_id: str
doc: First message of a handle.

name: edit
arguments: target: PostTarget, message_id: Optional[str], text: str, *, plugin_id: str
doc: Edit *message_id* in place; a surface that cannot edit gets a fresh message (``fallback``).

name: _is_whatsapp_non_user_chat
doc: True for group / broadcast / newsletter JIDs — not a sender identity.

name: _whatsapp_user_chat_ids_match
arguments: platform: str, left: Optional[str], right: Optional[str]
doc:
True when two WhatsApp *user* chat_ids refer to the same person.

Uses ``expand_whatsapp_aliases`` (same helper as session keys and adapter allowlists) so a bare
number, JID and LID collapse to one identity. Group/broadcast JIDs are chats, not senders;
non-WhatsApp platforms → False.

name: _bot_profile_key
doc: ``None`` for the default profile, else the profile name (mirrors ``set_owner_profile``).

name: _coerce_route_id
doc:
Normalize a route discriminator to str for strict equality matching.

YAML loads unquoted numeric IDs as ``int`` while ``SessionSource`` fields are ``str``. Only
``int`` (not ``bool``) is coerced; floats stringify to something (``"123.0"``) that can never
match, so they get a load-time warning instead.

``bool`` is an ``int`` subclass but never a valid id; floats and other types stringify to something
(``"123.0"``) that can never equal an inbound id — recreating the silent no-match this exists to fix —
so they are passed through with a load-time warning instead of being silently "fixed" (#86470).

name: parse_profile_routes
doc: Parse profile_routes from config.yaml, sorted most-specific-first.

name: match_profile_route
arguments: routes: list[ProfileRoute], platform: str, guild_id: Optional[str]=None, chat_id: Optional[str]=None, thread_id: Optional[str]=None, parent_chat_id: Optional[str]=None, adapter_profile: Optional[str]=None, user_id: Optional[str]=None
doc: Return the first (most specific) matching route, or None.

name: specificity
doc: Higher value = more specific match.

name: matches
arguments: self, platform: str, guild_id: Optional[str]=None, chat_id: Optional[str]=None, thread_id: Optional[str]=None, parent_chat_id: Optional[str]=None, adapter_profile: Optional[str]=None, user_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
True if every discriminator the route declares holds (AND).

``chat_id`` matches the channel directly or as the parent of a thread/forum post; WhatsApp
``chat_id`` also matches across number/JID/LID after the exact check (groups/broadcasts stay exact-only).
``adapter_profile`` is the profile owning the receiving bot (``None`` = default); it must equal
the route's ``bot_profile``.

name: _check
arguments: status: str, detail: str | None=None, **extra: Any

name: _probe_state_db
doc:
Read-only schema probe plus the process-wide corruption latch (``hermes_state_health``).

The schema read only catches an unreadable header or schema; damage deeper in the file
surfaces when a reader or writer touches it, and those publish into the latch. Reporting
the latch here is what makes readiness and ``/api/status`` agree with the session list
(#72046). ``detail="corrupt"`` is the one reason string consumers key off.

name: _probe_session_store
arguments: runtime_status: dict[str, Any], state_db_probe: dict[str, Any]
doc:
Report the running gateway cache state, not an independent reopen.  A corrupt store is
unavailable whatever the cache says: an open handle on a damaged file is not a working one.

name: collect_runtime_readiness
arguments: *, configured_model: str, runtime_status: dict[str, Any] | None, active_api_runs: int=0, process_completion_queue_depth: int=0, active_delegations: int=0
doc:
Bounded readiness diagnostics, no runtime mutation.  Even authenticated, probes
expose status and counts only: never config values, credentials, paths, payloads.

name: _strip_edge_silence_punctuation
doc: Strip stray edge punctuation (``.NO_REPLY``, ``*NO_REPLY*``) without erasing marker structure.

name: _canonical_silence_candidates
doc: Canonical forms of a short marker-sized response; ``()`` when not a candidate at all.

name: is_intentional_silence_response
doc:
True only when ``response`` is exactly a silence marker.

Prose that merely mentions ``NO_REPLY`` must be delivered normally. A blank
response is not silence either — that is the empty-response failure path.

name: is_autonomous_silence_response
doc:
Loose silence matcher for autonomous lanes (cron, webhook).

Models reliably bracket ``[SILENT]`` with a short note, so unlike the
interactive EXACT rule this also suppresses when a marker sits on its own
first/last line or the bracketed sentinel opens the response (``[SILENT] No
changes detected``).  A token buried mid-sentence is still delivered.
Shares :data:`LIVE_GATEWAY_SILENT_MARKERS` so the two sets cannot drift.

name: is_intentional_silence_agent_result
doc: Silence markers suppress delivery only for successful agent turns.

name: display_kind_for_event
doc:
The persisted user-row kind for a gateway turn: only self-injected events are machinery.

A scheduled heartbeat prompt is self-injected too (``_heartbeat_session_id`` is stamped only
by the gateway poller, never inferred from inbound text), but it deliberately stays
non-internal so authorization and the emergency stop still apply to it.

name: display_metadata_for_event
doc:
``{"display_text": ...}`` for an internal event whose producer named an async-result card, plus the
``title_preview`` (titler-only) a canonical admission committed for this exact event.

name: is_machinery_display_kind
doc:
Only a machinery turn may vanish on a bare silence marker; a human turn gets a visible fallback.

The caller passes the current turn's persisted display kind instead of inferring it from the
transcript: the inbound user row is not persisted yet, and a previous internal row must never
authorize silence on a human turn.

name: silence_allowed
doc: Whether a successful bare silence marker may remain silent for this turn.

name: reply_expected_metadata
doc:
The persisted user row's ``reply_expected`` key, only when the adapter knew; crash recovery
reads it back to judge a silence marker as the live turn did.

name: is_partial_silence_marker
doc:
True while streamed ``text`` could still resolve to a silence marker.

A buffer whose canonical form is a non-empty *prefix* of a marker (``"NO"`` on
the way to ``"NO_REPLY"``, or an exact marker not yet terminated by stream-end)
is held back so a raw marker is never shown and then retracted.  Divergence
from every marker, or exceeding the cap, resumes normal streaming.

name: map_fatal_config_exit_for_launchd
doc:
Translate gateway EX_CONFIG so launchd can park the job.

systemd uses ``RestartPreventExitStatus=78``; s6 maps 78→125. launchd cannot
gate on a specific status, and unconditional ``KeepAlive=true`` respawns 78
forever (#89477). The generated plist uses ``KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false``;
mapping 78→0 is a deliberate stop. Exit 75 (please restart) and other
failures pass through so KeepAlive still relaunches them. Negative ``wait()``
codes (signals) are left to the caller.

name: parse_launchd_exit_timeout
doc: Extract ``exit timeout = N`` from ``launchctl print`` output.

name: launchd_job_label
doc:
The ``ai.hermes.*`` launchd job label in *environ*, or ``None`` (no darwin gate).

launchd stamps ``XPC_SERVICE_NAME`` only on the job process it spawns. The generated plist
runs the stderr-timestamp wrapper there, so the gateway grandchild reads ``XPC_SERVICE_NAME=0``
and finds its label only in the wrapper's re-export, ``HERMES_LAUNCHD_LABEL``. Both go through
the same ``ai.hermes`` predicate: app-coalition labels (``application.<bundle>…``, exported
into IDE integrated terminals) are not our job. ONE seam for every reader of launchd identity
(drain cap, restart route, control-socket supervisor declaration).

name: launchd_service_label
arguments: environ: Mapping[str, str] | None=None, *, platform: str=sys.platform
doc:
Return this process's ``ai.hermes.*`` launchd job label, or ``None`` off darwin.

``launchctl print`` reports ``exit timeout = 1`` for app-coalition labels — treating those as
a budget would cap the drain to 0 for a gateway Ctrl+C'd in an IDE terminal, hence the
predicate in :func:`launchd_job_label`. ``platform`` is data so the mapping logic is testable
on any host.

name: read_launchd_exit_timeout_s
arguments: label: str | None=None, *, environ: Mapping[str, str] | None=None, uid: int | None=None, run: Callable[..., subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]]=subprocess.run, platform: str=sys.platform
doc:
Live ``ExitTimeOut`` (seconds) launchd enforces for this gateway's job.

Returns ``None`` — meaning "no launchd budget applies" — when the process
is not launchd-owned (non-darwin, or no ``ai.hermes`` job label — see :func:`launchd_job_label`), ``launchctl`` is missing
or fails, or the print output carries no ``exit timeout`` line. Callers
must treat ``None`` as fail-open: the configured drain stands unchanged.

name: resolve_launchd_capped_drain
arguments: drain_timeout: float, launchd_exit_timeout_s: float | None, *, cleanup_reserve_s: float=LAUNCHD_STOP_CLEANUP_RESERVE_S
doc:
Clamp a SIGTERM-driven stop drain to what launchd will actually allow.

``launchd_exit_timeout_s`` is the live ``exit timeout`` for this job (see
:func:`read_launchd_exit_timeout_s`); ``None`` means no launchd budget
applies and the configured drain is returned untouched. Otherwise the
drain may use at most ``exit_timeout - cleanup_reserve_s`` so the
post-drain teardown (interrupt agents, disconnect adapters, checkpoint
and close SQLite) still completes before launchd escalates to SIGKILL.
Never *extends* the drain — an operator who configured a short one
keeps it.

name: effective_stop_drain_timeout
doc:
Drain budget for the stop in progress on ``runner``.

Signal-driven stops under launchd are timed by launchd's live
``ExitTimeOut`` (``runner._launchd_exit_timeout_s``, set at boot);
everything else — in-band SIGUSR1 restart after the turn, ``--replace``
takeover, tests — keeps the configured drain. Duck-typed and
getattr-guarded on purpose: shutdown-path tests drive ``_stop_impl``
from bare doubles that are not ``GatewayRunner`` instances.

name: effective_stop_watchdog_delay
doc:
Thread-watchdog leash for the stop in progress on ``runner``.

``watchdog_delay`` is the supervisor-agnostic leash (effective drain +
grace). Under launchd a signal-driven stop is SIGKILLed at the live
``ExitTimeOut`` — with a 60s budget the default leash (50 + 60 = 110s)
can never fire, so the forensic stack dump and ``os._exit`` the watchdog
exists for are lost. Clamp the leash to ``ExitTimeOut -
LAUNCHD_WATCHDOG_DUMP_MARGIN_S`` so the dump lands before SIGKILL. Same
duck-typing / fail-open rules as :func:`effective_stop_drain_timeout`.

name: is_global_startup_conflict
doc:
True when an adapter's fatal error is a single-writer ownership conflict.

Adapters emit ``{scope}_lock`` with ``retryable=True`` so a *mid-run* reconnect can
recover; at startup a live foreign holder is a configuration conflict (two gateways
cannot poll one token), not a transient blip.  Matches by error CODE only, never text.

``BasePlatformAdapter._acquire_platform_lock`` emits ``{scope}_lock`` with ``retryable=True`` on
purpose: a *mid-run* reconnect must be able to recover once the live holder exits or a stale record is
cleared (#54167). This matches by error CODE only (the ``{scope}_lock`` / ``lock_conflict`` families
every adapter emits for scoped-lock and identity conflicts), never by message text.

name: is_gateway_supervisor_process
doc:
Return whether this gateway process is owned by a supervisor that RESTARTS it.

Selects the exit-75 restart route, so only markers of a manager with a restart policy count:
systemd ``INVOCATION_ID``, launchd ``XPC_SERVICE_NAME`` (or the wrapper-forwarded
``HERMES_LAUNCHD_LABEL`` the grandchild sees), the s6 sentinel, or the explicit
``--external-supervisor`` opt-in. The generalized ``HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD`` launcher marker is
deliberately NOT read here: the Windows Scheduled-Task launcher sets it without a restart policy
(#113670), and routing its ``/restart`` through exit 75 would leave the gateway dead.

name: is_supervised_gateway_launch
doc:
Return whether this gateway was launched by a generated service/launcher rather than a shell.

Superset of :func:`is_gateway_supervisor_process` that also honours ``HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD``,
the marker every generated launcher exports (systemd unit, launchd plist, s6 run script, Windows
Scheduled Task — see ``hermes_cli.main._apply_profile_override``). This is the identity the
self-targeting guards key on: a kill or lifecycle command issued from inside such a gateway takes
down the process hosting the caller with nobody at a terminal to bring it back (#113667).

name: is_container_restart_context
doc:
In a container (Docker/Podman) the detached setsid restart path dies with the cgroup,
so exit-75 service restart is the only viable path.  Own function so tests can mock it.

name: _seconds
doc: Non-negative float, or ``fallback`` on non-numeric input.

name: _parse_timeout_keeping_zero
arguments: raw: object, default: float, *, finite: bool=False
doc:
Parse a timeout where ``0`` is a deliberate disable (must NOT fall through
to ``default``), unlike None / blank / non-numeric (/ non-finite) input.

name: parse_restart_drain_timeout
doc: Parse a configured drain timeout; falsy (incl. ``0``) falls back to the shared default.

name: parse_restart_after_turn_timeout
doc: Parse the after-turn wait cap for in-band restart (``0`` = legacy immediate drain).

name: parse_cron_drain_timeout
doc:
Parse the cron/api_server drain floor (``0`` = opt out; both interrupted on the chat budget).

``0`` is a deliberate opt-out — cron and api_server (/v1) work is then interrupted on the same budget as chat work, the
pre-#82161 behaviour — and must not fall through to the default, unlike empty/missing input.

name: parse_signal_interrupt_grace_timeout
doc: Parse the unexpected-signal post-interrupt grace timeout.

name: resolve_cron_drain_budget
arguments: drain_timeout: float, cron_drain_timeout: float, *, watchdog_delay: float, elapsed: float=0.0, cleanup_reserve_s: float=CRON_DRAIN_CLEANUP_RESERVE_S
doc:
Seconds the stop drain may wait on in-flight cron and api_server (/v1) work.

Clamped to what this process can honour: the watchdog hard-exits at ``watchdog_delay``,
so waiting past that leash minus ``cleanup_reserve_s`` swaps a cleanly-interrupted job
for a SIGKILL that leaves it wedged.  Never less than ``drain_timeout`` (only extends).

name: resolve_systemd_timeout_stop_sec
arguments: drain_timeout: float, cron_drain_timeout: float=DEFAULT_GATEWAY_CRON_DRAIN_TIMEOUT, *, cleanup_reserve_s: float=CRON_DRAIN_CLEANUP_RESERVE_S, headroom_s: float=SYSTEMD_STOP_HEADROOM_S, floor_s: float=SYSTEMD_TIMEOUT_STOP_SEC_FLOOR
doc:
Seconds systemd ``TimeoutStopSec`` must cover: the stop path may first wait
``cron_drain_timeout`` + ``cleanup_reserve_s`` for cron and api_server work, so sizing from the chat drain
alone lets systemd SIGKILL an in-budget drain.  A zero cron timeout is an opt-out.

``restart_drain_timeout`` is only the chat-turn interrupt budget (default 0). See #94759.

name: resolve_restart_exit_wait_budget
arguments: drain_timeout: float, after_turn_timeout: float, cron_drain_timeout: float, *, headroom: float=15.0
doc:
Seconds a CLI waits for the gateway PID to exit after SIGUSR1: the in-band after-turn
deferral, then the longest supervisor stop envelope — the one systemd's ``TimeoutStopSec`` is
sized from (cron drain + cleanup reserve, supervisor headroom, floor; #94759) — then
observer ``headroom``.

A non-finite drain means "wait indefinitely", not a crash in the integer envelope.

name: _chain_gap
doc:
Inter-boot gap that still links two boots; floored by ``window_seconds`` so
widening the window never makes the breaker *less* sensitive.

name: _chain_ending_at
arguments: boots: list[float], ts: float, gap: float
doc:
Unbroken chain of boots leading up to ``ts`` (oldest first): walks backwards
while each gap stays within ``gap``; the first wider gap ends the chain (older
boots are a resolved episode).  Empty when nothing is recent — how a healthy
gateway forgets a loop.

name: record_restart_interrupted_boot
arguments: window_seconds: int=DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS, *, now: Optional[float]=None, max_gap_seconds: int=DEFAULT_MAX_GAP_SECONDS
doc:
Record a restart-interrupted boot; return the pruned chain + now (most recent
last).  A persistence failure returns the in-memory list without raising.

name: clear
doc: Remove the persisted boot log (used on clean shutdown / by tests).

name: check_and_record
arguments: max_restarts: int=DEFAULT_MAX_RESTARTS, window_seconds: int=DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS, *, now: Optional[float]=None, max_gap_seconds: int=DEFAULT_MAX_GAP_SECONDS
doc:
Gateway entry point: record this boot; True when the chain reached
``max_restarts`` and auto-resume should be SKIPPED.

name: _update
doc: Merge ``fields`` into the ``(chat_id, message_id)`` entry. No-op on any failure.

name: record
doc: Persist ``text`` for ``(chat_id, message_id)``. No-op on any failure.

name: record_media
doc: Persist local attachment ``(path, mime)`` pairs for ``(chat_id, message_id)``.

name: record_async
doc:
``record`` for coroutine callers: the read-modify-write + ``os.replace``
runs on a worker thread so the event loop is not stalled by the filesystem.

name: record_media_async
doc: ``record_media`` for coroutine callers; see ``record_async``.

name: lookup
doc: Return stored text for ``(chat_id, message_id)`` or ``None``.

name: lookup_media
doc: Return stored ``(path, mime)`` pairs whose file still exists (attachments may be temp files).

name: _gateway_session_db_inner
doc: The raw SessionDB behind ``gateway._session_db`` (unwrapping the async facade), or None.

name: _hygiene_cooldown_for_failure
doc:
Bump the hygiene failure streak and return the escalated cooldown (x1/x3/x9 over base, clamped).

Hygiene's per-run ``AIAgent`` is fresh, so the streak lives in SQLite keyed by rotation-stable session_key.

It exists because the in-agent equivalent is unreachable from here:
``ContextCompressor.record_timeout_failure`` escalates on an absolute 60 -> 300 -> 900s ladder driven by
the in-memory ``_consecutive_timeout_failures`` counter, which ``bind_session_state`` zeroes. Session
hygiene constructs a FRESH ``AIAgent`` per run and re-binds state every time, so from the gateway that
streak is structurally always 0 and only the flat ``hygiene_failure_cooldown_seconds`` could ever be
recorded — a session whose summary model always times out retried on that same fixed interval forever
(#79624). The streak is mirrored to SQLite by rotation-stable ``session_key`` so it outlives both the
per-run agent and gateway restarts; ``PersistentState`` keeps the hot in-process view.

name: _reset_hygiene_failure_streak
doc:
Clear the hygiene failure streak after a compression that reduced context.
