(preserve the queue so messages sent during the outage are delivered rather than silently dropped —
#46621).
``initial`` selects the capped cold-start budget for platforms whose full connect budget is too long
to spend before the gateway reaches ``running`` (#85993 — Telegram's 180s).

name: _connect_adapter_bounded
arguments: self, adapter, platform, *, is_reconnect: bool, initial: bool

name: _connect_initial_adapter_with_timeout
doc:
Cold-start connect with replace intent visible ONLY during this await, so a later
network recovery can never evict a healthy token holder.

name: _handle_reaction_event
doc: Fan a normalised reaction event out to the HookRegistry; errors never block the adapter.

name: _handle_adapter_fatal_error
doc:
React to an adapter failure after startup (retryable → background reconnect queue). Runs
detached: the notification arrives on the failing adapter's own polling task, which the
handler's disconnect can cancel mid-flight, stranding the platform half-handled.

name: _reconnect_queue_entry
arguments: self, platform, adapter, platform_config, *, attempts: int, delay: float, queued: bool=True
doc: Build a ``_failed_platforms`` entry (startup failures and runtime fatals share the shape).

name: _queue_retryable_fatal_platform
doc:
Queue a retryable fatal adapter for background reconnection (True when newly queued).

Must not await: callers run this BEFORE any disconnect so a wedged close can't strand it.

Idempotent if already queued. See #80598.

name: _on_all_adapters_down
doc:
Normalized ``GatewayConfig.on_all_adapters_down``: ``"exit"`` (default — a supervising
service manager restarts the process) or ``"stay_alive"`` (launchers with no supervisor,
e.g. the desktop app's direct ``hermes serve`` child, where a failure exit only severs the
UI's websockets and drops in-flight assistant messages; #118080).

name: _handle_adapter_fatal_error_detached
doc:
Run the fatal handler; a platform left stranded (not reconnected, not queued, not
intentionally disabled) exits the gateway with failure so the service manager restarts it.

name: _retain_background_task
doc: Register ``task`` in ``_background_tasks`` (created lazily for bare test runners).

name: _track_task_in
doc: Register ``task`` in an arbitrary lifecycle set with self-removal on completion.

name: _supervised_backoff
doc: Capped exponential respawn delay (a method so tests can collapse the schedule).

name: _spawn_supervised
arguments: self, coro_factory, name, *, restart=True, _attempt=0, on_spawn=None, on_give_up=None
doc:
Launch a long-lived supervised background task: exceptions a bare ``create_task`` drops
are logged, and it respawns with capped backoff up to ``_MAX_SUPERVISED_RESTARTS`` rapid
failures (counter resets after ``_SUPERVISED_HEALTHY_SECS`` healthy). Fresh ``Context`` per
spawn (an inherited delegated-child marker would make the Kanban dispatcher reject its own
writes). ``on_spawn`` fires on EVERY spawn incl. respawns — handle trackers MUST pass it or a
respawn leaves a stale handle and a SECOND watcher; ``on_give_up(name)`` fires at budget end.

``on_give_up`` (optional) is invoked with ``name`` when supervision is abandoned — the restart
budget is spent and this task will never be respawned by the supervisor again. Supervision being
finite is correct; having no owner of the invariant afterwards is not. A task that still has queued
work depending on it needs somewhere to hand that fact to, and before this hook existed the only
thing standing between budget exhaustion and a permanent silent outage was a *later, unrelated
event* happening to call ``_ensure_...`` (#90386). This is the supervisor telling its caller "I am
done; the invariant is yours now", which is a thing only the supervisor knows.

                        coro_factory, name, restart=restart, _attempt=effective_attempt + 1,
                        on_spawn=on_spawn, on_give_up=on_give_up,  # only the LAST give-up matters
                    )

name: _handoff_watcher
doc:
Process pending CLI→gateway session handoffs from ``state.db``: claim atomically (pending
→ running), re-bind the home channel to the CLI session_id, dispatch a synthetic event, mark
``completed``/``failed``.

name: _on_reconnect_watcher_gave_up
doc:
Own the reconnect invariant once supervision gives up: while running with queued
platforms, a watcher is live or a bounded respawn is scheduled (no later event can notice
a dead watcher). Slow-tier exhaustion logs loudly; deliberately NOT a process restart.

Before this, the only thing that noticed a dead watcher was a *later fatal error from some other
platform* reaching ``_queue_retryable_fatal_platform``. That is event-coupled recovery: it needs an
event that, by construction, may never come. #81036 moved queue publication ahead of disconnect and
drops the failed adapter from the live map, so once the watcher's budget is spent there may be no
adapter left that can emit the event recovery was waiting on. The platform stays queued, nothing
retries it, and the stranded check in ``_handle_adapter_fatal_error_detached`` treats a queued
platform as safe — so the process is never restarted either.

name: _schedule_slow_reconnect_watcher_respawn
doc: Bounded slow-tier respawn of the reconnect watcher.

name: _spawn_reconnect_watcher
doc:
Launch the reconnect watcher. ``on_spawn`` is load-bearing: without it a supervised
respawn leaves ``_reconnect_watcher_task`` dead and ``_ensure_...`` spawns a second one.

significant_calls.expression:
self._spawn_supervised(
            self._platform_reconnect_watcher, "platform_reconnect_watcher",
            on_spawn=lambda t: setattr(self, "_reconnect_watcher_task", t),
            on_give_up=on_give_up or self._on_reconnect_watcher_gave_up,
        )

name: _ensure_reconnect_watcher_running
doc:
Respawn a dead reconnect watcher (called on BOTH _queue_retryable_fatal_platform paths:
the re-fatal of an already-queued platform is the only case that exhausts the budget).

If the tracked reconnect watcher task has died (e.g. from exhausting its restart budget, or a
terminal exception that _spawn_supervised could not recover), respawns it so platforms queued for
reconnection are not permanently stranded. Called from _queue_retryable_fatal_platform on BOTH paths
(#70344, #90386): after a new enqueue, and after a re-fatal for a platform that is already queued --
the latter being the only case in which the watcher can have been retrying long enough to exhaust
its supervised restart budget.

name: _platform_reconnect_watcher
doc:
Periodically retry failed platforms: backoff 30s → 300s cap, retryable failures retry
forever (self-heal), non-retryable drop out. Pausing is manual only (``/platform pause``).

name: _flag_reconnect_needs_attention
arguments: self, platform, info: dict, now: float, *, status_key: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Flag NEEDS_ATTENTION (once) past the threshold — a signal, NOT a circuit breaker. The threshold
is the bound profile's ``agent.reconnect_attention_after``: secondaries call this inside their
``_profile_runtime_scope`` with their ``<profile>:<platform>`` status key.

name: _mark_platform_fatal
doc: Record an adapter's fatal error code/message as ``fatal`` runtime status.

name: _bump_reconnect_backoff
arguments: self, platform, info: dict, attempt: int, error_code, error_message: str
doc: Mark the platform retrying and record the failed attempt; returns the backoff applied.

name: _adapter_may_heal
doc:
Whether a platform whose ``_create_adapter`` returned None can heal without a config change.

Only an unregistered plugin can (a plugin load can fail transiently). A builtin whose probe fails
(missing deps/creds), a registered plugin returning None, or an empty bot credential needs a config
change: retrying it re-warns forever at the backoff cap (#5196 fleet nodes). Shared by startup and
the reconnect watcher so both classify the same platform the same way.

name: _reconnect_failed_platform
doc: One watcher pass for a queued platform: gate, attempt, and record the outcome.

name: _publish_primary_adapter
doc: Register a connected primary adapter and wire voice mode/input (transcription without /voice join).

name: _schedule_planned_restart_replay
doc:
Replay the owed planned-restart notice after a reconnect, in the background: notification delivery
must not hold up adapter recovery or other platforms' reconnects.

name: _install_reconnected_adapter
doc: Publish a freshly reconnected primary adapter and replay what it missed while down.

name: _cancel_secondary_profile_reconnect_tasks
doc:
Cancel profile-scoped reconnects before tearing down their registry, so a reconnect
mid-setup cannot republish an adapter after the registry drains (bounded wait).

name: _start_secondary_profile_adapters
doc:
Bring up adapters for every non-active profile (multiplex only); returns connected count.
Each profile connects under its own HERMES_HOME + secret scope; credential/listener collisions
are refused here — the only point seeing every profile's credentials together.

name: _primary_resource_claims
doc:
Resource claim -> owning profile for every live or queued primary adapter (credential:
one account polled once; listener: one bind+port). A queued retryable primary owns both.

name: _record_served_profiles
doc:
Record the served set (eligible for routing/HTTP prefixes/cron/runtime scope — broader
than "has a connected adapter") for `hermes status`; seed per-profile PairingStores.

name: _load_secondary_profile_config
doc:
Hydrate + enter ``profile_home``'s scope once; return its gateway config. Raises
``MultiplexConfigError`` (open dm/group policy). Port-binding platforms are NOT refused: the
default profile owns the single shared listener and a secondary's port-binders are built in
shared-listener mode (``/p/<profile>/...``) by ``_start_one_profile_adapters``.

name: _credential_claim_origin
arguments: profile_name: str, profile_home, platform: Platform, token: str
doc:
Where *token* was configured for *profile_name*: that profile's ``.env``, or ambient env.

``None`` when the value is not in either place (yaml-only, or unknown). An env label
is only returned when the profile's own ``.env`` does not contain the value — a shell
export that merely echoes the file is the file.

name: _duplicate_credential_origins
arguments: self, owner: str, profile_name: str, profile_home, platform: Platform, adapter: Any
doc: ``(owner_origin, incoming_origin)`` for a same-credential refusal; either may be None.

name: _refuse_duplicate_claim
arguments: self, claim, claimed: dict[tuple, str], profile_name: str, platform: Platform, kind: str, *, owner_origin: Optional[str]=None, incoming_origin: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Log + park a secondary adapter whose credential/listener another profile owns (True when
refused). NOT disconnected: it never connected, and for a same-credential Photon adapter
disconnect() would shut down the primary profile's live sidecar.

name: _note_unserved_secondary_platform
doc:
Report unpaired WhatsApp or secondary-only Relay. Log the reason and remedy and stamp a
``<profile>:<platform>`` status entry so ``hermes gateway status --profile X`` and the
dashboard show *why* the channel is dead instead of nothing at all.

name: _unserved_shared_ingress_warnings
doc:
Loud ``not being served`` lines for shared-ingress platforms secondaries enabled while
NO profile (default included) actually runs them; empty when the default serves the platform.

name: _start_one_profile_adapters
arguments: self, profile_name: str, profile_home: Path, claimed: dict[tuple, str]
doc: Create+connect one profile's adapters under its runtime scope.

name: _wire_adapter_handlers
arguments: self, adapter: BasePlatformAdapter, *, message_handler=None, fatal_error_handler=None, busy_session_handler=None, authorization_check=None, platform_event_handler=None, busy_text_mode: Optional[str]=None, busy_text_timing: Optional[tuple[float, float]]=None, human_delay: Optional[tuple[int, int]] | object=_UNSET
doc:
Install the runner callbacks every adapter needs (defaults = primary handlers;
secondary wiring passes profile-scoped variants). ``set_reaction_handler`` is optional.

name: _configure_profile_adapter
arguments: self, adapter: BasePlatformAdapter, profile_name: str, platform: Platform
doc: Install the profile-scoped handlers shared by startup and reconnect.

name: _secondary_reconnect_attempt
arguments: self, profile_name: str, platform: Platform, predecessor=None

arguments: self, profile_name: str, platform: Platform, predecessor=None
doc: Reconnect a retryable secondary adapter under its own profile scope.

name: _schedule_secondary_profile_startup_reconnect
arguments: self, profile_name: str, platform: Platform, adapter: BasePlatformAdapter
doc:
Queue a cold-start reconnect: startup failures happen BEFORE ``_running`` flips True (the
regular scheduler would drop them), so park a task and hand off once live.

name: _schedule_secondary_profile_reconnect
arguments: self, profile_name: str, platform: Platform, adapter: BasePlatformAdapter
doc: Schedule one runner-owned reconnect without sharing primary secrets.

name: _make_profile_fatal_error_handler
doc: Route a secondary-profile fatal error to that profile's reconnect slot.

name: _handle_profile_adapter_fatal_error
arguments: self, profile_name: str, platform: Platform, adapter: BasePlatformAdapter
doc: Remove a failed multiplexed adapter (the primary-only fatal handler ignores them).

name: _routed_profile_home
doc:
A named routed profile's home, or :data:`UNRESOLVED_PROFILE_HOME` when it does not
resolve (deleted or renamed mid-run, invalid name, transient OSError).

Never ``None``: ``None`` is reserved for "this body is the launch profile's own work", and
answering it for an unresolvable NAMED profile is what made a secondary's inbound message
run on the launch profile's credentials.

name: _scope_or_null
doc:
The runtime scope for one body, by what ``profile_home`` IS:

* a home — that profile's scope;
* ``None`` — no routed profile: the LAUNCH profile's own work, so bind the launch profile
  explicitly once this process multiplexes. A bare ``nullcontext()`` made the launch
  profile the one tenant running on ambient ``os.environ`` and the process home, which a
  secondary's context may have poisoned; under the one-process-per-host ruling it is a
  tenant like any other. Single-profile hosts are unchanged (no-op until activation);
* :data:`UNRESOLVED_PROFILE_HOME` — a NAMED profile whose home is gone: bind nothing, so an
  unscoped ``get_secret`` raises ``UnscopedSecretError`` under multiplexing. A profile never
  borrows another profile's value, and "we cannot tell whose this is" must fail closed.

name: _async_scope_or_null
doc: ``async with`` twin of :meth:`_scope_or_null` (for ``_async_profile_runtime_scope``).

name: _canonicalize
arguments: self, source, *, transport_profile: Optional[str]=None, primary_home: Optional[Path]=None
doc:
Runner-side identity seam: the pinned :class:`RoutingIdentity` of *source*, resolving it
once when absent. ``transport_profile`` names a secondary's own bot (its handlers know it by
construction); ``None`` = the primary/shared bot. ``None`` result = rejected route under
multiplexing (the caller drops; the ingress gate warns once) or a source that cannot resolve
(bare test rigs) — the legacy readers then stay in force.

name: _make_profile_message_handler
doc:
Message handler that canonicalizes the event's identity FIRST, then delegates under the
profile scope (auth runs BEFORE the agent-turn scope, so the profile's ``.env`` must be
visible here).

name: _make_profile_busy_session_handler
doc:
Busy-path twin: canonicalize FIRST, then resolve busy policy under the profile scope
(auth runs against the profile's own allowlist, same as the cold-path message handler).

name: _make_default_profile_message_handler
doc:
Scope primary-adapter messages to their routed multiplex profile. Authorization stays
with the transport profile (a routed profile may have no credential/allowlist).

name: _make_default_profile_busy_session_handler
doc:
Busy-path twin of ``_make_default_profile_message_handler``: busy callbacks bypass the message
handler, so the routed scope and transport-home authorization must be re-established here or the
follow-up is authorized in whatever scope is ambient (#103717).

name: _admit_primary_source
doc:
Canonicalize a primary-adapter source (transport home for authorization, routed profile
for the runtime) and return the runtime home to scope the turn under; ``None`` when the
route targets an unserved profile. Route ≠ admitting bot.

name: _primary_message_handler
doc: Return the correctly scoped handler for a primary adapter.

name: _primary_busy_session_handler
doc: Return the correctly scoped busy-session handler for a primary adapter.

name: _standalone_scoped
doc:
Standalone twin of the ``_make_default_profile_*`` wrappers: run ``handler`` under
``_standalone_launch_scope`` so slash commands and turns keep resolving the launch profile's
credentials after a hosted room flipped the process-wide guard (#112878). The credential
body is marked at entry (``launch_body``): a turn already running when a second profile
switches this gateway to multiplexing keeps resolving its launch credentials.

name: _handle_gateway_platform_event
doc: Authorize and publish one normalized adapter event to plugin hooks.

name: _make_profile_platform_event_handler
doc: Bind platform-event auth and hook dispatch to one multiplex profile.

name: _make_default_profile_platform_event_handler
doc: Scope primary-transport events to their routed multiplex profile.

name: _adapter_credential_claim
doc: Return the exclusive credential resource claimed by an adapter.

name: _adapter_listener_claim
doc:
Exclusive listener claim (Photon sidecar bind+port): distinct credentials still cannot
share a port, so the later adapter is rejected before connect() disturbs the first.

name: _adapter_credential_fingerprint
doc:
Salted, log-safe hash of an adapter's credential; None when none is discoverable
(conflict detection is then skipped).

name: _create_adapter
doc:
Create an adapter bound to this runner (every lifecycle path goes through here so
adapters can resolve inbound profile routes before handlers or connect()).

name: _instantiate_adapter
doc: Instantiate the adapter for a platform: plugin registry first, then built-ins.

name: _make_adapter_auth_check
doc:
Platform-bound auth callback for adapters (prompt-injection mitigation for fetched
context); delegates to :meth:`_is_user_authorized`. ``profile_name`` binds a secondary to
its scope; for the shared primary (None) the routed profile is stamped so its pairing store
is consulted while allowlist reads stay under the transport home.

Without this an inline-button caller approved only in the routed profile's pairing store was denied
(#86296), because the adapter's callback source was never route-stamped. A secondary-owned bot's
callback fires outside the profile runtime scope (straight off the adapter's event loop), so the
check re-enters the owning profile's scope per call — the gate's scoped env read otherwise falls
back to os.environ (the default profile's env) and denies the secondary's own allowlisted
callers (#120639).

One poll of the CURRENTLY-SCOPED store; ``profile_name`` (None = root) routes delivery
to that profile's OWN adapter. A closure, not a method: tests bind ``_handoff_watcher`` onto
a ``SimpleNamespace`` with only ``_session_db``/``_running``/``_process_handoff``.

name: _first_agent
doc: Unwrap a cache entry (``(agent, sig, ...)`` tuple or bare agent) to its agent.

name: _tuple_agent
doc: Agent of a ``(agent, sig, ...)`` cache tuple; None for any other entry shape.

name: _extract_cache_busting_config
doc:
Values that must bust the cached agent, as a flat dict keyed by 'section.key'. ``user_config``
is the raw file (no DEFAULT_CONFIG merge), so absent keys and non-dict sections take the
DEFAULT_CONFIG value — what the agent was actually built with — while an explicit ``null`` stays
None so opting out of a non-None default still rebuilds. Includes the live tool registry
generation: MCP reloads mutate the registry without touching config.yaml.

name: _memory_provider_identity_signature
doc:
The active memory provider's ``identity_signature()``. ``{}`` when there is no provider,
it fails to load, or the hook raises.

name: _agent_config_signature
arguments: model: str, runtime: dict, enabled_toolsets: list, ephemeral_prompt: str, cache_keys: dict | None=None, user_id: str | None=None, user_id_alt: str | None=None, skip_context_files: bool=False
doc:
Stable key from agent config: change → cached AIAgent rebuilt; unchanged → reused (frozen
prompt + schemas for cache hits). ``user_id`` / ``user_id_alt`` participate because Honcho
freezes them at init; omitting them in shared-thread keys would cross-attribute messages.

``user_id`` and ``user_id_alt`` are the runtime user identities carried by the current message's
gateway source. They participate in the cache key because memory providers freeze them at
first-message init (the Honcho plugin resolves its user peer from them once). Without them in the signature, a
shared-thread session_key (one in which ``build_session_key`` intentionally omits the participant
ID, e.g. ``thread_sessions_per_user=False``) would reuse the cached AIAgent across distinct users,
causing the second user's messages to be attributed to the first user's resolved Honcho peer. This
broke #27371's per-user-peer contract in multi-user gateways. Per-user agent rebuilds in shared
threads trade prompt-cache warmth for correct memory attribution.

name: _session_model_override
doc: Current in-memory /model override for ``session_key`` (None when absent).

name: _rehydrate_session_model_override
doc:
Lazily restore a persisted /model override after a gateway restart: non-secret parts
(model/provider/base_url) are written through on /model and read back on first use; api_key
is never persisted and is re-resolved. No-op when an in-memory override or nothing exists.

name: _apply_session_model_override
arguments: self, session_key: str, model: str, runtime_kwargs: dict
doc:
Apply /model session overrides (precedence over config.yaml defaults; ``None`` fields skipped
so partial overrides don't clobber defaults), returning (model, runtime_kwargs).

name: _snapshot_session_model_override
doc: Capture a gateway session override before a one-turn switch.

name: _claim_one_turn_restore
doc:
Arm the one-shot restore snapshot for ``/model --once`` / ``/moa``. A repeated one-shot
command before the turn runs keeps the EARLIEST snapshot: the later command's snapshot is
the first temporary model, not the user's standing override. Pass *snapshot* when the
caller captured the pre-switch state earlier (``/model --once`` applies its override before
arming); omit it to snapshot now.

name: _restore_session_model_override
doc: Restore the session override captured before a one-turn switch.

name: _is_intentional_model_switch
arguments: self, session_key: str, agent: Any, config_model: str
doc:
True when *agent* running a model other than *config_model* is deliberate: a /model session
override names that model, or the Nous gateway moved the session off the ``nous/welcome``
alias that *config_model* still carries (``anon_auth.apply_model_switch``).

name: _fallback_baseline_model
arguments: self, session_key: str, source: Optional[SessionSource], agent: Any, *, policy_model: Optional[str]=None
doc:
The model *agent* was built to run, for the post-turn fallback check: what
``_resolve_session_agent_runtime`` chose (session /model, then a LOCAL session's frozen launch
policy model, then channel_overrides on the chat, thread or parent, then the global model),
canonicalized as ``AIAgent.__init__`` did on the agent's PRIMARY route. The route a fallback
moved it to would make that fallback look primary.

name: _release_running_agent_state
doc:
Pop ALL per-running-agent state for ``session_key`` (call at every site that ends a running
turn); True when cleared. Persistent state (model overrides, voice mode, approvals) is NOT
touched. With ``run_generation``, only clear if still current — a stale async unwind bumped
by /stop or /new must not clobber a newer run (returns False).

name: _drop_turn_slot
doc:
Release the running-agent slot and evict the cached instance (/stop, eviction, reaper).
``_interrupt_requested`` is cleared only by the turn finalizer, so on a hung/still-draining
run the flag would survive and silently kill the session's NEXT message (interrupted=True,
api_calls=0, empty response); the next message rebuilds from history while the old agent
keeps its flag so a hung drain still dies (#44212). With ``run_generation`` (the post-bump
value ``_interrupt_running_turn`` returns), the release is generation-guarded: an async
path awaits between bump and release, so a successor claiming the slot in that window must
not have its sentinel/lease wiped by the displaced path's tail. Then sweep lease tokens
from generations OLDER than the current one: a hung evicted turn's finalizer may never run,
and each such generation would otherwise pin its token (and its ``_SessionLease``) forever.
Identity-checked + idempotent, so a live successor's token is never affected.

name: _held_turn_lease
doc:
Return ``(registry, lease_tokens)`` when ``session_key`` holds a lease token for
``run_generation``, else None. Callers ``get``/``pop`` the token from the map themselves.

name: _release_turn_lease
doc:
Release the turn lease acquired by (``session_key``, ``run_generation``). Keyed by (routing
key, run generation) so a stale unwind pops only ITS token; the registry's identity check
refuses it if a newer turn holds the lease. Idempotent.

name: _rebind_turn_lease
arguments: self, session_key: str, run_generation: int, new_session_id: str
doc:
Follow a mid-turn session_id rotation (compression) with the held turn lease, or an alias
key resolving the new id could start a concurrent turn the lease never sees. Call at every
mid-turn reassignment; no-op if no token.

name: _clear_conversation_scope
doc:
THE single conversation-boundary funnel (/new, /resume, suspension replacement,
compression-exhausted reset). New conversation-scoped dicts go in _CONVERSATION_SCOPED_STATE
so every boundary picks them up. Turn-scoped state (_running_agents/_ts, slot leases, turn-
lease tokens) is owned by _release_running_agent_state and NOT cleared. Idle agent-cache
eviction is NOT a boundary (a resumed turn rebuilds from these). getattr-guarded.

Why a funnel: these boundaries used to each carry a hand-copied pop-list of the per-session dicts,
and the lists drifted every time a new dict was added (#48031, #58403, #10702, #35809 were all
"boundary X forgot dict Y" bugs — e.g. /new cleared the /model override but not the /model --once
restore snapshot). Adding a new conversation-scoped dict now means adding its attribute name to
_CONVERSATION_SCOPED_STATE below; every boundary picks it up automatically.

name: _clear_session_boundary_security_state
doc: Clear per-session control state that must not survive a boundary switch.

name: _begin_session_run_generation
doc:
Claim a fresh, monotonically increasing run generation token (NEVER reset): a late result
from a worker /stop or /new invalidated is recognized and dropped.

name: _invalidate_session_run_generation
doc:
Invalidate any in-flight run token for ``session_key``.

Settles a pending one-shot model override first: the displaced turn's finalizer is
generation-guarded and would otherwise leave ``/moa`` / ``/model --once`` in force.

name: _current_session_run_generation
doc: Current run generation for ``session_key`` (0 when the key tracks no run).

name: _is_session_run_current
doc: Return True when ``generation`` is still current for ``session_key``.

name: _bind_adapter_run_generation
arguments: self, adapter: Any, session_key: str, generation: int | None
doc: Bind a gateway run generation to the adapter's active-session event.

name: _interrupt_running_turn
arguments: self, session_key: str, *, interrupt_reason: str, invalidation_reason: str, tool_reason: str | None=None
doc:
Sync core shared by /stop, /new and eviction: request a hard interrupt on the in-flight
agent, invalidate its run generation, and reap the tool processes that turn spawned.
``tool_reason`` names a system issuer (eviction); ``None`` keeps the user attribution of /stop and /new.
Returns the post-bump generation.

name: _interrupt_and_clear_session
arguments: self, session_key: str, source: SessionSource, *, interrupt_reason: str, invalidation_reason: str, release_running_state: bool=True
doc: Interrupt the current run and clear queued session state consistently.

name: _refresh_agent_cache_message_count
doc:
Re-baseline a cached agent's stored message_count after THIS turn — the coherence guard
rebuilds on mismatch, so without this every turn would rebuild and destroy prompt caching.
Only the count is refreshed, only if the same agent is still cached. DB errors leave the
snapshot as-is (one spare rebuild).

But the snapshot is taken at agent-BUILD time — before this turn writes its own user + assistant (+
tool) rows — and the cache entry is never rewritten on a reuse. See #45966.

name: _set_pending_turn_sidecar_notes
doc: Stage per-turn must-deliver notes for the next agent run (one-shot).

name: _voice_channel_sidecar_note
arguments: self, event, source: SessionSource, session_key: str
doc:
``[Voice channel now: ...]`` note when VC state changed; ``None`` when unchanged so per-turn
member/speaking churn can't touch the prompt.

name: _rehydrate_prompt_pins
doc:
Adopt the durable pin snapshot for an internal turn when this process holds no context pin
for *session_key*: a restart, or an eviction (/stop, /undo, /model), which clears only
``ephemeral_pin``. Without it the wake renders from its origin-only source (no chat or user
names) and the next human turn re-keys back, rewriting the system bytes twice. Human turns
never call this, so an evicted agent's next human turn still re-renders.

name: _persist_prompt_pins
doc:
Persist this conversation's pins before the agent runs; the store no-ops an unchanged
snapshot and refuses a session that has moved on.

name: _pinned_session_context_prompt
arguments: self, context, redact_pii: bool, session_key: Optional[str], *, internal: bool=False
doc:
Session-context prompt pinned per session: key hit → pinned bytes reused VERBATIM (immune
to renderer nondeterminism); key miss → re-render and re-pin (rename, topic edit, /sethome).

``internal`` events (kanban wakes, delegation completions, watch notifications) carry a
source rebuilt from the persisted origin, without chat_name/user_name/message_id. Rendering
from it re-keyed the pin, and the next human turn re-keyed it back (A→B→A), rewriting
already-sent system bytes each time. An internal event is never a real metadata change, so
it reuses an existing pin verbatim (restored by ``_rehydrate_prompt_pins`` after a restart or an eviction); with
no pin yet it renders and pins as usual. The pin records the ``privacy.redact_pii`` it was
rendered under: bytes from another privacy policy are never reused, even by an internal
event. Callers pass ``event.internal or event.inherit_channel_pin`` (synthetic
goal/heartbeat/resume turns strip ``message_id``) so this pin and ``_pinned_channel_inputs``
reuse on the same decision.

name: _pinned_channel_inputs
arguments: self, session_key: Optional[str], channel_prompt: Optional[str], source: SessionSource, *, internal: bool
doc:
``(channel_prompt, source)`` for this turn's agent run.

The ephemeral system prompt also appends ``channel_prompt`` and the ``channel_overrides``
prompt (looked up by chat/thread/``parent_chat_id``). Events with no channel inputs of
their own (internal events, and synthetic goal/heartbeat/resume turns — see
``MessageEvent.inherit_channel_pin``) carry ``channel_prompt=None`` and a source without
``parent_chat_id``, so they dropped both and toggled the system prompt like the context pin
did. Human turns record their inputs; turns that ask to reuse the pin get them back
(``_rehydrate_prompt_pins`` restores both after a restart).

name: _ephemeral_change_key
doc:
Hash the exact inputs ``build_session_context_prompt`` renders. Invariant
(test_prompt_tail_freeze.py): any input whose change alters the rendered bytes MUST appear
here — omission means a stale pinned prompt; extras only re-render.

name: _evict_cached_agent
arguments: self, session_key: str, *, commit_memory: bool=False, release_after_turn: bool=False
doc:
Remove a cached agent (/new, /model, ...) and soft-release its LLM client pool (AIAgent
holds reference cycles; without it RSS grows across /new). Soft = frees clients and child
subagents but PRESERVES terminal sandbox / browser / bg processes since the session may
resume; true boundaries call ``_cleanup_agent_resources`` first. Cleanup runs on a daemon
thread so ``_agent_cache_lock`` never spans slow socket teardown.

Pops the entry AND soft-releases the evicted agent's LLM client pool so the httpx connection
(sockets + held buffers) is freed promptly rather than waiting on CPython GC — AIAgent holds
reference cycles (callbacks, tool state) that delay refcount collection, so a manual release is
required to keep gateway RSS flat across many /new, /model, undo and reset operations (#29298, same
leak class as #25315).

``release_after_turn``: an agent still mid-turn is released when that turn's running slot
clears (``_release_running_agent_state``) instead of being left to the garbage collector.

name: _evict_cached_agent_at_boundary
doc:
Reset and compress end the conversation the provider was tracking, so the old agent's
transcript is committed (``on_session_end``) before its clients go; a plain evict is not.

name: _spawn_release_thread
arguments: self, target, args: tuple, name: str, *, inline_fallback: bool, session_key: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Run a release on a daemon thread. ``inline_fallback`` runs it inline (best-effort) when no
thread can start (interpreter shutdown); otherwise a spawn failure propagates, as on main.
The thread runs inside the owning profile's scope (see ``_run_release_in_profile_scope``).

name: _run_release_in_profile_scope
arguments: self, target, args: tuple, session_key: Optional[str]
doc:
Call ``target(*args)`` under the profile that OWNS ``session_key``.

Threads start with an EMPTY context, so a bare thread would commit end-of-session memory
(provider ``on_session_end`` reads credentials/home at call time) under the launch profile.
And the LRU-cap eviction runs inside the REQUESTING turn, whose agent may belong to another
profile — so "some scope is present" is not enough either. The owner comes from the session
key: a named profile's home, else the DEFAULT profile (``agent:main:`` keys), which is the
root Hermes dir even when the gateway was launched under a named profile. Its scope is
entered unless the current one already is the owner's.

name: _commit_memory_before_soft_evict
arguments: self, agent: Any, key: str, boundary: bool=False
doc:
Commit the live transcript to memory providers before resource-only eviction. A session
boundary (reset, compress) also ends the context engine's session; that engine can run without a provider.

name: _commit_then_release_soft
arguments: self, agent: Any, key: str, boundary: bool=False
doc:
Commit end-of-session memory (if warranted), then soft-release — on the daemon eviction
thread. Order matters: commit needs the live memory manager before ``release_clients``.

name: _release_evicted_agent_soft
doc:
Soft cleanup for cache-evicted agents: unlike _cleanup_agent_resources, the session may
resume, so terminal sandbox, browser daemon and bg processes outlive the AIAgent instance.

name: _agent_cache_bounds
doc:
Operator-configured agent-cache bounds, resolved once per process (lazily, not in
``__init__``, so ``__new__``-constructed test / slash-command runners work too).

name: _agent_cache_cap
doc: Effective LRU cap — the configured override, else the default.

name: _agent_cache_idle_ttl
doc: Effective idle TTL in seconds — configured override, else default.

name: _sweep_agent_cache_under_pressure
doc:
Shed cached transcripts once the gateway heap nears its budget; returns count evicted.

The LRU cap counts entries and the idle sweep counts seconds; neither knows one cached agent
pins a full ``_session_messages`` transcript (tens of MB), so RSS climbs until the cgroup
throttles. Above the anonymous-RSS budget this soft-evicts LRU agents (transcript rebuilt
from the persisted session next turn). Never touched: agents mid-turn, the most recently
used sessions, and transcripts not yet on disk.

A gateway serving many chats can hold every warm transcript for the TTL window.
Pressure eviction bounds that heap before the cgroup throttles and SIGTERM can
no longer flush inside systemd's stop timeout (#80764).

name: _release_pressure_batch
doc:
Release a pressure-evicted batch sequentially on one daemon thread, then ``malloc_trim`` so
RSS actually falls. The plan is drained (``pop`` + ``del``), not iterated, so no local
reference pins evicted agents during ``gc.collect`` + trim (else the valve over-evicts).

name: _enforce_agent_cache_cap
doc:
Evict oldest cached agents past the LRU cap (requires _agent_cache_lock); cleanup on a
daemon thread. Mid-turn agents are SKIPPED, so the cache may stay over cap until the next
insert.

name: _sweep_idle_cached_agents
doc:
Evict cached agents idle past the idle TTL (lock acquired internally; cleanup on daemon
threads; mid-turn agents SKIPPED); returns the number evicted.

name: warm_gateway_dashboard
doc:
Mount the dashboard in the background once the gateway is READY (supervised gateways, whose
clients — Desktop, the dashboard SPA — call its routes right away). Never raises.

name: stop_gateway_api
doc: Drain sockets without stopping the session authority or taking signals.

name: _embedded_chat_enabled
doc:
``web_server._DASHBOARD_EMBEDDED_CHAT_ENABLED`` without importing the dashboard (always True
unless a loaded dashboard says otherwise).

name: state
doc:
Boundary state: the dashboard app's own state once mounted (operators and tests may
change it there), the listener's pre-mount snapshot before.

name: ensure
doc: Import (off the loop), bind and start the dashboard app once; returns ``web_server``.

name: _start_deferred_state_db_integrity_check
doc:
Run the store scan an unclean-exit report deferred, once the runner is live.

On the event loop it held every local listener open but unanswered for the whole
``quick_check`` (minutes on a multi-GB ``state.db``), so local clients hung instead of being
refused. A daemon thread nothing waits on; it only appends the forensic exit-diag record.

significant_calls.callee:
spawn_context_thread(
        run_deferred_integrity_check, args=(evidence,),
        kwargs={"deadline_s": STATE_DB_INTEGRITY_DEADLINE_S}, name="state-db-integrity-check").start
significant_calls.expression:
spawn_context_thread(
        run_deferred_integrity_check, args=(evidence,),
        kwargs={"deadline_s": STATE_DB_INTEGRITY_DEADLINE_S}, name="state-db-integrity-check").start()

spawn_context_thread(
        run_deferred_integrity_check, args=(evidence,),
        kwargs={"deadline_s": STATE_DB_INTEGRITY_DEADLINE_S}, name="state-db-integrity-check")

name: _start_gateway_replace_existing_instance
doc:
Handle a live gateway PID under this HERMES_HOME: replace it (``--replace``) or refuse.
Returns False when startup must abort (refused, permission denied, target still alive).

name: _start_gateway_configure_logging
doc: Sync bundled skills, set up file logging + startup security audit, and the -v/-q stderr handler.

name: _start_gateway_make_shutdown_signal_handler
doc: Build the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler; ``_signal_initiated_shutdown[0]`` records an unplanned signal.

name: _start_gateway_claim_pid_file
doc: Claim the runtime lock + PID file (O_EXCL winner is the authoritative gateway). False = lost.

name: _start_gateway_start_control_socket
doc: Start the gateway control socket (identify/status/pause-for-update); None when unavailable.

name: _start_gateway_start_cron_and_housekeeping
doc:
Start the cron scheduler thread + gateway housekeeping thread; returns
``(cron_stop, cron_provider, cron_thread, housekeeping_thread)``.

name: _start_gateway_shutdown_tail
arguments: runner, _control_server, cron_stop: threading.Event, cron_provider, cron_thread: Any, housekeeping_thread: threading.Thread, _planned_stop_watcher_stop: threading.Event, _planned_stop_watcher_thread: threading.Thread, _signal_initiated_shutdown: list
doc: Post-``wait_for_shutdown`` teardown; returns the process exit verdict (True = exit 0).

name: _launch_home_may_multiplex
doc:
A named profile serving ``default`` as a secondary splits default's local sessions between
the two stores (routing rows follow the launch home, receipts follow the authority), so the
multiplexer is the default profile's job.

An EXPLICIT ``gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`` (config.yaml or ``GATEWAY_MULTIPLEX_PROFILES``)
on a named launch home exits EX_CONFIG: a config verdict, never a retry. The implicit default
(unset key, or the retired ``false`` that ``resolve_multiplex_mode`` settles like unset) is not
the operator's choice, so it is downgraded the way every other implicit-multiplex blocker is:
this process comes up standalone, says why, and *config* is flipped in place so the boot below
reserves and serves only the launch profile.

name: _start_gateway_resolve_terminal_cwd
doc: Messaging-only defaults belong to startup, not incidental imports by the TUI.

name: _conflicting_homes
doc:
The homes whose gateway.lock another holder has right now: each probed alone with its own open
file description and released at once (the all-or-nothing reserve does not say which failed).
A home freed meanwhile is simply not listed; the next reserve attempt takes it.

name: _reserve_waiting_out_browse_reconcile
doc:
Reserve *homes*, waiting (bounded) while a contender is a browse reconcile or has not yet
published its lock record (flock taken, record unwritten). Only a positively identified holder
that is not browse maintenance refuses at once; the flock exclusion itself is never weakened.

name: _start_gateway_reserve_profiles
doc: Reserve the launch home plus every served profile home; False when startup must abort.

name: _start_gateway_install_signal_handlers
doc: SIGINT/SIGTERM drain, SIGUSR1 restart; main thread only.

name: _start_gateway_run_runner
doc:
MCP discovery, then ``runner.start()``. Returns the exit verdict when the process must end
before running mode (start failed, clean exit, aborted startup); None to continue into cron.

name: _start_gateway_early_environment_probe
doc:
Background-start the host toolchain probe the warm-up and first prompt read (idempotent;
honours ``agent.environment_probe: false``). Never raises: the warm-up still runs it lazily.

name: start_gateway
arguments: config: Optional[GatewayConfig]=None, replace: bool=False, verbosity: Optional[int]=0, force: bool=False, idle_exit: bool=False
doc:
Start the gateway and run until interrupted; False if it failed to start (non-zero exit so
systemd can auto-restart). ``replace`` kills any existing instance first (avoids restart-loop
deadlocks); ``force`` starts without consulting the host owner at all; ``idle_exit`` arms the
unmanaged idle exit (``gateway.run_idle_exit``) for a client-started daemon.

name: _rescan_profiles_handler
doc:
``hermes profile create/delete`` asks the multiplexer to reconcile ``profiles/`` now
(the watcher also rescans periodically). Runs on the socket executor: marshal onto the loop
and wait briefly so the caller learns whether the profile is served. A gateway standalone
only because the host had one profile starts multiplexing in place on this rescan.

name: approval_input_words
doc:
Typed-reply synonyms for ``approval.inputs.<input_key>`` (comma-lists): the English words
ALWAYS match, plus the active language's list, so a Polish pack can add "tak" without losing
"yes". Lower-cased, de-duplicated, order preserved (English first).

name: _strip_slot
doc:
Remainder after ``slot`` when ``text`` starts with it as a WHOLE slot, else None.

The ``:``-delimited slot layout is ``build_session_key``'s: an id that merely starts with another
must never match, so a whole-slot comparison is what every caller here uses. A text that IS the
slot yields ``""``.

name: _tail_has_slot
doc:
True when ``tail``'s FIRST slot is ``slot`` (``tail`` is ``""`` when the key ends at the
chat id).

name: _same_chat_key_slots
arguments: key: str, *, prefix: str, chat_id: str, scope_id: Optional[str]
doc:
``(chat_type, tail)`` when ``key`` names the SAME chat as ``prefix`` + ``chat_id``, else None.

``prefix`` is the key's fixed-shape head, ``agent:<profile>:<platform>:``. Everything after it is
matched as TEXT, because ids may themselves contain ``:`` (Matrix ``!room:example.org``).
``scope_id`` is Slack's workspace slot — ``build_session_key`` emits it there alone — and a key
without it still names the same chat; a key carrying a DIFFERENT known scope is another
workspace's chat. ``tail`` is ``""`` when the key ends at the chat id.

name: _overflow_queue
doc: The session's FIFO overflow list, or None when no session state exists yet.

name: _enqueue_fifo
arguments: self, session_key: str, queued_event: MessageEvent, adapter: Any
doc: Append a /queue event to the FIFO chain for a session.

name: _promote_queued_event
arguments: self, session_key: str, adapter: Any, pending_event: Optional[MessageEvent]
doc:
Promote the next overflow item after the slot drained.

``pending_event`` None → the overflow head becomes the pending event; otherwise the head is
staged into the slot for the NEXT recursion. Returns the (possibly updated) pending_event.

name: _defer_past_exhaustion_reset
arguments: self, result: Any, adapter: Any, source: SessionSource, session_key: str, pending_event: MessageEvent
doc:
Leave the post-turn drain to the fresh session after a compression-exhausted turn.

The outer handler owns the reset: the exact queued event goes back in the head slot so the
adapter's post-handler drain starts it on the fresh session (never promoted or prepared on the
exhausted one). An accepted leftover /steer was already taken out of the agent's buffer, so it
keeps its usual place ahead of that event instead of vanishing.

name: _merge_leftover_steer
arguments: self, result: Any, adapter: Any, source: SessionSource, session_key: Optional[str], pending_event: Optional[MessageEvent], pending: Optional[str]
doc:
Fold a leftover /steer (arrived after the last tool batch) into the post-turn drain:
the next user turn when nothing else is pending, otherwise ahead of / behind it in the FIFO.

name: _queue_depth
doc: Total pending /queue items for a session — slot + overflow.

name: _rescue_orphaned_overflow
doc:
Pop the oldest orphaned FIFO overflow event for an idle session (None if nothing to rescue).

``queued_events`` drains only at the post-turn promotion site; a busy window ending without
it (early exit, exception/interrupt/generation-bump) orphans the overflow. On a NEW event for
a NON-busy session the oldest orphan runs as THIS turn, the next is staged into the slot so
arrival order holds, and the caller enqueues the incoming event behind it. The returned
event is REMOVED from both stores, else the post-turn dequeue would run it twice.

See #28503.

name: _is_goal_continuation_event
doc: True for synthetic /goal continuation turns (so pause/clear can spare real /queue items).

name: _clear_goal_pending_continuations
doc: Remove queued synthetic /goal continuations for one session; real /queue items are kept.

name: _goal_still_active_for_session
doc: Best-effort fresh DB check before running a queued continuation.

name: _get_max_concurrent_sessions
doc: Return the configured active chat session cap, if enabled.

name: _active_session_limit_message
doc: Return a user-facing rejection when starting a new session exceeds the cap.

name: _claim_active_session_slot
doc: Claim a cross-process active-session slot for a new gateway turn.

name: _agent_has_active_subagents
doc:
True when *running_agent* is driving subagents (callers demote interrupt → queue;
``interrupt()`` would cascade through ``_active_children``). Fail-safe False on any error.

name: _steer_active_subagents
doc:
Queue *text* into every live child of *running_agent*; returns how many accepted it.

A parent blocked inside ``delegate_task`` only drains its own steer queue after the tool
returns, i.e. after the child finishes — so a steer aimed at a looping child would sit
unread for the whole delegation (#112095, Telegram). Children are the parent's own
``_active_children`` (identity-scoped, same snapshot ``interrupt()`` fans out to).

name: _steer_running_agent
doc:
``running_agent.steer(text)`` plus fan-out to its active subagents (see
:meth:`_steer_active_subagents`); True when the parent or any child queued it.

name: _session_has_compression_in_flight
doc:
True when a compression lock is held for this session's id (callers demote interrupt →
queue, else a follow-up against the pre-rotation parent orphans compression siblings).
Both blocking reads run in a worker thread so a large state.db never freezes the loop.

Context compression is interrupt-protected (#23975) but gateway ``interrupt`` busy-input mode can
still start a follow-up turn against the pre-rotation parent while compression is mid-flight,
producing orphaned compression siblings (#56391).

name: _lookup_session_id_under_store_lock
doc: Sync helper run in the thread pool: read session_id under the store lock.

name: _prepare_busy_steer_text
doc:
Steerable text for a busy follow-up, transcribing voice-message media first.

Steer bypasses the inbound STT queue, so a media-only voice follow-up would otherwise
silently degrade to queue mode. Uses the single out-of-band STT choke point, so STT runs at
most once per message; on failure the caption (if any) is kept.

name: _steer_text_with_origin
doc: Keep event origin in this injection, never in the cached system prompt.

name: _send_busy_reply
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, adapter, content: str, *, plain_anchor: bool=False
doc: Send a busy-path reply anchored to the event (thread metadata included).

significant_calls.expression:
adapter._send_with_retry(
            chat_id=event.source.chat_id, content=content,
            reply_to=reply_anchor if plain_anchor else self._busy_reply_to(event, reply_anchor),
            metadata=self._thread_metadata_for_source(event.source, reply_anchor),
        )

name: _send_busy_drain_notice
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, effective_mode: str
doc: Busy path while the gateway is restarting/stopping: queue (if allowed) and tell the user.

name: _plaintext_approval_words
doc: Word → (verb, args) for the active language: the English list ∪ ``t("approval.inputs.<k>")``.

name: _route_plaintext_approval_while_busy
doc:
Route a bare "yes"/"no" to the approval handlers while a dangerous-command approval blocks.

Returns True when the message was consumed as an approval response.

name: _resolve_busy_steer_or_redirect
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, effective_mode: str, running_agent: Any
doc: Apply interrupt->queue demotions, then attempt steer (steer mode) or redirect (interrupt mode).

name: _try_agent_verb
arguments: self, running_agent, verb: str, text: str, session_key: str, *, event: Optional[MessageEvent]=None
doc: Call ``running_agent.<verb>(text)`` (steer/redirect); False + warning on failure.

name: _redirect_active_turn
arguments: self, running_agent, text: str, session_key: str, event: MessageEvent
doc:
``redirect()`` the running turn onto *event* and re-anchor its delivery to that message.

The turn's reply anchor and ledger identity were bound to the message that OPENED it, and
the final send is bracketed against that event; after a successful redirect the answer is
to *event*, so the reply must quote it (#115001). Both redirect entry points (busy
interrupt mode and the priority path) go through here.

name: _fold_into_running_turn
arguments: self, running_agent, session_key: str, event: MessageEvent
doc:
The running turn now answers *event* too (steer, redirect): if *event* was addressed to
the bot, a bare silence marker must not end the turn. Returns the turn, or None when a newer
turn already owns the slot.

name: _interrupt_running_agent_for_busy_event
doc: Interrupt mode: abort in-flight tool calls; the agent loop exits at its next check point.

name: _compose_busy_ack_message
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, now: float, _busy_state, running_agent: Any, *, is_steer_mode: bool, is_queue_mode: bool, is_redirect_mode: bool, demoted_for_subagents: bool, demoted_for_compression: bool

name: _send_busy_ack_reply
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, adapter, message: str

name: _busy_interrupt_and_ack
doc:
Interrupt-mode abort (voice transcribed) and the busy ack, after the steer/redirect resolution.
Shared by the in-process busy handler and the session authority's busy preempt.

name: _gateway_plain_command_handlers
doc: Return ordinary slash handlers shared by idle and busy dispatch.

name: _send_command_ack
arguments: self, source, text: str, label: str
doc: Best-effort acknowledgment for a slash command that falls through to agent processing.

name: _gateway_idle_command_handlers
doc: Slash handlers dispatched only on the idle path (busy dispatch has its own allowlist).

name: _dispatch_busy_slash_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, cmd_def, quick_key: str, source
doc:
Dispatch a recognized slash command while an agent is running.

Order: ``busy_handler`` (mid-run variant) → ``busy_policy == "dispatch"`` (normal handler)
→ catch-all reject text. Rejecting is required rather than falling through to
interrupt + discard: commands like /model, /reasoning, /voice, /insights, /title,
/resume, /retry, /undo, /compress, /usage, /reload-mcp, /sethome, /reset (all
registered as Discord slash commands) would interrupt the agent AND get silently
discarded by the slash-command safety net, producing a zero-char response.
See #5057, #6252, #10370.

1. ``busy_handler`` — special mid-run variant (e.g. /goal's control-verb whitelist, /queue's FIFO
enqueue, /model's custom reject text). 2. 3. See #5057, #6252, #10370.

name: _busy_slash_route
doc:
``(kind, target)`` :meth:`_dispatch_busy_slash_command` takes mid-run: ``special`` (the
variant's method name), ``plain`` (the normal handler) or ``reject`` (its text key, None for the
catch-all). A ``special`` variant may still refuse its arguments: it awaits ``_busy_accepted``
only once it accepts.

name: _handle_pause_command
doc:
`/pause [reason]` engages the global emergency stop; `/pause off` lifts it (the estop gate
lets slash commands through while paused so messaging-only operators are never locked out).

name: _busy_start_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, quick_key: str, source

name: _busy_egress_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, quick_key: str, source

name: _busy_stop_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, quick_key: str, source

name: _busy_new_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, quick_key: str, source

name: _busy_queue_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, quick_key: str, source

name: _busy_steer_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, quick_key: str, source

name: _command_turn_admitted
doc:
Whether *event*, a turn a slash command produced, goes to the authority's FIFO. Text that is
still a command, an internal event, an executing admission and a turn carrying a one-turn
model (``/moa``, which would otherwise land on whichever admitted turn runs next) stay
in-process, as without an authority.

name: _route_stop_epoch
doc:
How many messaging /stop and /new fenced *session_key*: the authority's one per-route epoch
(``fence_route``, bumped by ``_hm_stop_owner_turn``), shared with inputs still capturing.

name: _admit_command_turn
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source, session_key: str, stop_epoch: int
doc:
Inline admission (the idle path, a mid-run skill reaching the runner): ``(True, reply)``
like ``_hm_authority_admission``, else ``(False, None)`` to stay in-process. *stop_epoch* is
the route's /stop and /new epoch read when the command arrived, before any rewrite.

name: _queue_command_turn
arguments: self, session_key: str, command: MessageEvent, event: MessageEvent, adapter, ack: Optional[str]=None, stop_epoch: Optional[int]=None
doc:
A turn of its own after the current run. True: committed in the background like a busy
text follow-up (``dispatch_shared_busy``), and ``ack`` is sent once the row commits, never
on the transport's earlier release or a refusal. False: the in-process slot (no authority),
and the caller answers with ``ack`` itself.

name: _send_after_commit
arguments: self, adapter, event: MessageEvent, text: str

name: _busy_skill_turn
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source, session_key: str, adapter=None
doc:
A mid-run ``/<skill>`` or ``/<bundle>`` under a session authority, rewritten as on the idle
path and queued as a turn: ``(True, reply)`` when handled (``reply`` refuses it, or is the
turn's reply when admitted inline; with ``adapter``, the busy handler's, it is committed in
the background). ``(False, None)`` leaves a plugin, quick or unknown command to the busy path.
It keeps the /stop and /new epoch it arrived under across the (slow) rewrite.

name: _busy_goal_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, quick_key: str, source

name: _busy_loop_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, quick_key: str, source

name: _check_slash_access
doc:
Denial message if ``source`` cannot run ``canonical_cmd``, else None (both dispatch paths
use it so an in-flight agent can't bypass admin gating; no ``allow_admin_from`` → None).

name: _same_chat_runs
doc:
``(key, chat_type, tail)`` for every OTHER running turn in the caller's chat (``tail`` is
the key text after the chat id, ``""`` when the key ends there).

The namespace comes from ``own_key`` — the session store's own answer, so a named-profile
stop matches that profile's runs and never a literal. ``_snapshot_running_agents`` already
drops the pending sentinel (a session still being set up has no agent). Callers gate on
authorization; ``own_key`` is excluded. Both tiers share one call.

name: _sibling_thread_run_keys

doc:
Keys from ``runs`` belonging to OTHER participants in the caller's own thread (per-user
thread mode keys are ``...:{thread_id}:{user_id}``, so another user's run is invisible to the
caller's own ``/stop``). Callers still gate on authz.

name: _chat_scoped_run_keys
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, runs: list[tuple[str, str, str]]
doc:
Keys from ``runs`` for ANY session of the same chat, whatever the chat_type/thread/
participant slots. Two supported shapes make a /stop key miss a run in the same chat (found
via Slack's native stop button, gateway-gateway#286): a top-level channel turn keys
``channel`` while an in-thread /stop normalizes to ``thread``, and rolling-DM configs key
without the thread slot the stop carries. "/stop" means "stop what's running in THIS chat",
which is also what lets a human stop a peer's per-sender group run (see ``_same_chat_runs``).

A stop sent from INSIDE a thread only reaches runs whose own thread slot is that thread (or
that carry no thread slot at all — the rolling-DM shape). Anything else in the channel is a
different conversation: another reply thread, or a peer's top-level run. Callers gate on
authz.

name: _is_stale_restart_redelivery

The previous gateway wrote ``.restart_last_processed.json`` (platform + update_id). A
/restart with update_id <= that value is a redelivery when this process booted from that
restart; otherwise the marker must be < 5 minutes old. Telegram only (numeric ordering).

when ``launchctl print`` is unavailable. Logs a WARNING when the configured drain exceeds
the live budget so the misconfiguration is visible at boot, not at the next SIGKILL.

Re-read fallback_providers from disk for the next agent create/reuse.

Lets a chain edited after startup reach messaging sessions (cron already re-reads per job).
A TRANSIENT read/parse failure (user mid-edit, non-atomic write) keeps the last known-good
chain; only a successful read that genuinely lacks the key clears it.

Cron already does this per job via ``get_fallback_chain``; the gateway previously froze
``self._fallback_model`` at process start, so a chain configured (or changed) after ``hermes
gateway`` was running never reached messaging sessions even though the same process's cron jobs fell
back correctly. Fixes #60955.

Reads the ACTIVE gateway home (the routed profile under multiplexing, else the launch home)
and keeps one last-known-good chain per home: a single runner-wide slot filled from the launch
home handed every secondary profile the default profile's fallback chain.

Skips the rewrite while a cooldown holds the agent on an activated fallback provider
(``restore_primary_runtime`` owns that lifecycle); otherwise replaces the chain so
mid-uptime ``fallback_providers`` edits apply without a restart.

When primary is active (or cooldown expired), replace the chain so mid-uptime ``fallback_providers``

a demotion, or an interrupt — the ended turn lets the FIFO run the follow-up next).

name: _hm_handle_running_session_message
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, _quick_key: str
doc:
Fast-path while this session's agent is running: interrupt by default (minimal latency);
busy_input_mode queue/steer, subagent and compression protection demote to queue.

name: _hm_resolve_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, _quick_key: str
doc:
Resolve the slash command (aliases, access gate, hooks) → ``(handled, result, command,
canonical)``; when ``handled`` the caller returns ``result`` as-is (may be None).

name: _hm_confirm_destructive
arguments: self, event, command: str, detail: str, handler

name: _hm_rewrite_turn_to_prompt
arguments: self, event, source, name: str, ack: str, build
doc:
Ack, then rewrite the turn to ``build()`` and fall through to the agent (keeps role
alternation; works on any backend). A failing builder replies with a retry hint.

name: _hm_dispatch_canonical_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, _quick_key: str, canonical: Optional[str]
doc:
Dispatch built-in idle-path commands → ``(handled, result)``; prompt-rewriting commands
mutate ``event.text`` and return ``(False, None)`` to fall through to the agent.

name: _hm_bundle_slash_rewrite
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, _quick_key: str, command: str
doc:
Rewrite ``/<bundle>`` to the bundle invocation message; True when handled.
Skill bundles take precedence over individual skill commands (mirrors CLI dispatch).

name: _hm_unknown_slash_reply
doc: Reply for a /command that is not built-in/plugin/skill; None when it is known.

name: _hm_skill_slash_rewrite
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, _quick_key: str, command: Optional[str]

name: _hm_pending_reply_intercepts
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, _quick_key: str
doc:
Replies owned by in-flight work: pending /update prompt, clarify, slash-confirm.
Only events that may control the gateway (``allow_gateway_control``) can answer them, never
an admitted turn: it was offered here before its commit, or a slash command queued it.

name: _hm_dispatch_idle_commands
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, _quick_key: str
doc:
Idle path: resolve + dispatch slash commands; rewriting commands fall through to the agent.
A command rewritten into a turn keeps the /stop and /new epoch it arrived under, read before
the (slow, off-loop) rewrite, so a reset during it drops the command, as on the busy path.

name: _hm_rescue_orphaned_fifo
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, is_internal: bool, _quick_key: str
doc:
FIFO orphan rescue: a session that went idle with a populated overflow (post-turn drain
never promoted, e.g. a compression-demoted follow-up) silently orphaned those events. The
oldest orphan runs as THIS turn and the incoming event is parked behind the chain. Skipped
for control commands and internal events.

name: _hm_authority_admission
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, _quick_key: str, is_internal: bool
doc:
``(True, reply)`` when the routed profile's session authority owned this message
(preempted, plugin-consumed or admitted to its durable FIFO); ``(False, None)`` to continue
on the in-process path. Raises ``RuntimeStoreError('profile_mismatch')`` for a scope this
process does not serve.

name: _handle_message
doc:
Handle an incoming message from any platform: auth → command check → running-agent
interrupt → get/create session → build context → run agent → return response.

name: _restore_pending_one_turn_model_override
arguments: self, session_key: str, run_generation: int | None=None
doc:
Restore the per-session model override captured by ``/model --once`` or ``/moa``.

With ``run_generation`` (the turn finalizer) the restore happens only while that generation
is still current; a stop/reset/eviction has already settled the snapshot itself (see
``_invalidate_session_run_generation``), so the displaced finalizer finds nothing to do.
Without it (the settlement paths) the restore is unconditional.

name: _prefix_inbound_sender_context
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, message_text: str
doc: Attribute the sender in shared multi-user sessions and prepend history-backfill channel context.

name: _classify_inbound_media
doc:
Split ``event.media_urls`` into (image, STT-voice, audio-file, video) paths. Per-attachment
MIME wins over the message-level type (a document sent alongside an image must not be routed
as an image). MessageType.AUDIO / mixed DOCUMENT audio is a file attachment, never STT.

name: _enrich_inbound_images
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, session_key: str, message_text: str, image_paths: list[str]
doc: Route images natively (attach pixels at run_conversation) or pre-analyze them into text.

name: _echo_stt_transcripts
arguments: self, adapter, source: SessionSource, transcripts: list[str], *, metadata=None, log_context: str='Transcript'
doc: Send each transcript back as ``🎙️ "…"`` (best-effort; failures are logged, never raised).

name: _enrich_inbound_voice
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, message_text: str, audio_paths: list[str]

name: _inbound_attachment_display_name
doc:
``(display_name, agent_visible_path)``: cache filename is ``<id>_<id>_<original>``; the
path is translated to the in-container mount under a Docker backend.

name: _prepend_inbound_media_file_notes
arguments: cls, message_text: str, audio_file_paths: list[str], video_paths: list[str]
doc: Prepend a path-pointing note per audio-file / video attachment (content is not inlined).

name: _prepend_inbound_document_notes
doc: Prepend a context note per non-media attachment (anything not routed as image/audio/video).

name: _prepend_inbound_reply_context
arguments: event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, message_text: str
doc: Prepend the reply-to pointer, then the Discord triggering-message note (outermost).

name: _inbound_model_context_length
doc:
Context length of the model this turn runs on. A global ``model.context_length`` pin
belongs to the configured model, not a /model or channel override; custom-provider limits win.

name: _expand_inbound_context_references
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, session_key: str, message_text: str
doc: Expand ``@`` context references; returns None when the injection was refused (user notified).

name: _prepare_inbound_message_text
arguments: self, *, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, history: list[dict[str, Any]], session_key: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Prepare inbound event text for the agent. Shared by the normal inbound and queued
follow-up paths so attribution, image enrichment, STT, document notes, reply context and
@ references behave the same. Side effect: buffers per-session native image paths when the
model supports native vision; the caller consumes that buffer at ``run_conversation``.

name: _prepare_profile_scoped_inbound_message_text
arguments: self, *, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, history: list[dict[str, Any]], session_key: Optional[str]=None
doc: Run inbound preprocessing under the routed profile when multiplexed.

name: _prepare_clarify_reply_text
doc: Return raw text or successful voice transcripts for a clarify reply.

name: _mark_durable_active_turn
doc: Persist the exact resolved routing key for this running turn.

name: _clear_durable_active_turn
doc:
Best-effort CAS clear of the marker owned by *event* (3 attempts; never blocks agent/lease
release — a stale marker is bounded by the agent timeout and clean-start discard).

name: _decide_image_input_mode
arguments: self, *, source: Optional[SessionSource]=None, session_key: Optional[str]=None, user_config: Optional[dict]=None, provider: Optional[str]=None, model: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Resolve image-input routing (``"native"`` / ``"text"``) for the effective model this turn
(see agent/image_routing.py). Sessions can carry /model overrides and this runs before AIAgent
sets the auxiliary_client runtime globals, so resolve the per-session runtime bundle the
upcoming turn will use, not just the persisted default.

name: _enrich_message_with_vision
doc:
Auto-analyze user-attached images with the vision tool and prepend the descriptions.
Description *and* local cache path are injected so the model understands the image without
a tool call and can re-examine it with vision_analyze.

name: run_post_admission_hook
arguments: runner: Any, event: Any, source: Any, session_key: str
doc: Return ``(handled, reply)``; ``handled=False`` means run the ordinary agent turn.

name: _stop_exec_tree
doc:
Kill an exec quick command's shell and everything it started, then reap the shell (bounded).

Killing only the shell leaves ``sleep 120 & wait``'s sleep running. ``kill_process_tree`` reaches
descendants (``taskkill /T`` on Windows); on POSIX the group the shell led also catches members
that already outlived it.

name: _hm_post_admission_consume
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, session_key: str
doc:
``post_gateway_admission`` exactly once per inbound message: ``(consumed, reply)``.

Never while an admitted row EXECUTES (first run or restart replay): the authority path
already offered the message at ingress, before its commit, so a consumed message is never
admitted and an admitted one is never offered twice.

name: _hm_pre_gateway_dispatch_hook
doc:
Run the ``pre_gateway_dispatch`` plugin hook; None = drop, else the (maybe rewritten) event.
Results: ``{"action": "skip"}`` → drop; ``{"action": "rewrite", "text"}`` → replace ``event.text``;
``allow``/None → normal dispatch. On the messaging path it runs BEFORE auth so plugins can handle
unauthorized senders; on the producer path (webhook/relay, ``admit_producer``) it runs AFTER the
delivery's authorization, which preparing its payload performs, so it never sees a refused sender.

Once per inbound message, at ingress (here, or ``admit_producer`` for webhook/relay), never
while an admitted row EXECUTES: a messaging turn already passed it before its commit, and a
local CLI/TUI/Desktop turn never fired it on main, so a skip must not drop committed input.

name: _hm_quick_commands
doc: User-defined ``quick_commands`` mapping from config (empty dict when unset/malformed).

name: _hm_expand_alias_quick_command
doc: Rewrite ``event.text`` to an alias quick command's target; returns the new command name.

name: _hm_command_hooks
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, _quick_key: str, command: str, canonical: str
doc:
Fire ``pre_command`` (observer) and ``command:<canonical>`` (interceptor) hooks →
``(handled, result, new_command)`` (``new_command`` set when a handler rewrote the command).
The running-agent path deliberately does NOT fire these — a slow or hostile plugin must not
interfere with the operator's escape hatches for a live agent.

name: _hm_run_exec_quick_command
arguments: self, command: str, exec_cmd: str, cwd: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Run a ``type: exec`` quick command as a host shell of the gateway process: sanitized env
(the gateway process has every API key in os.environ), redacted output, its process tree
killed after 30 s or when the awaiting task is cancelled (gateway shutdown).
``cwd`` is a local session's folder; None keeps the gateway's own (messaging).

name: _hm_dispatch_quick_and_plugin_commands
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, command: Optional[str]
doc:
Drain gate, user-defined quick commands (exec/alias) and plugin slash commands →
``(handled, result, command)``; an alias quick command rewrites ``command``.

name: _hm_dispatch_plugin_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, command: str
doc:
Plugin-registered slash command *command* → ``(handled, result, command)``. No quick
commands: a local session resolves those in its own profile before calling this.

name: _hm_run_plugin_handler
arguments: self, plugin_handler, event: MessageEvent, source: SessionSource, session_entry=None, args=None
doc:
Run a resolved plugin command handler for *source* → its reply text or None; raises what
the handler raises (``gateway/session_commands.py`` resolves the exact registered name).
*args* is the argument as typed (a local session's command); otherwise the message's
command arguments, with the messaging dash repair of ``get_command_args``.

name: rehome_inbound_media
doc:
Move adapter-cached attachments into the ACTIVE profile's ``cache/`` and repoint the event.

Adapters download and cache an attachment BEFORE the gateway routes the event to a profile, so
on a multiplexed gateway the file lands under the launch home while the routed turn's sandbox
mounts (``get_cache_directory_mounts``) and vision's ``_media_cache_roots`` resolve the routed
profile's ``cache/`` — the agent is handed a mounted, empty directory (#101134). Runs inside the
routed scope at the shared preprocessing choke point (every adapter, every media kind); a no-op
when the active home is the launch home, and idempotent (a moved entry is no longer under it).

name: _enrich_message_with_transcription
arguments: self, user_text: str, audio_paths: list[str], clip_memo: Optional[dict]=None
doc:
Transcribe voice clips with the configured STT provider and prepend the transcripts →
``(enriched_text, successful_transcripts)``; the transcripts (input order; empty if every clip
failed or STT is disabled) let callers echo them back before the agent loop. ``clip_memo``
(path → ``_transcribe_one_clip`` result) skips clips an earlier pass already transcribed.

name: _pending_event_audio_paths
doc: Return STT-eligible paths from a pending voice message.

name: _transcribe_pending_audio_event_once
doc:
Transcribe a pending audio event once and cache the result on the event: the interrupt
monitor and the pending-drain path both need it — one STT call and one echo per message.
``user_text`` is a deliberate override of the caption; ``None`` reads ``event.text`` live.

name: _echo_pending_stt_transcripts_once
arguments: self, event, adapter, source, transcripts: list[str], *, metadata=None, log_context: str='Transcript'
doc:
Echo pending-event STT transcripts to the chat at most once. Tracked as a COUNT (not a
set — identical transcripts are distinct deliveries): ``merge_pending_message_event`` can
append a second voice note and invalidate the cache; the re-run returns earlier transcripts
as a prefix, so only the unsent tail is echoed.

name: _transcribe_and_echo_pending_voice
arguments: self, event, adapter, source, text: str, *, log_context: str, metadata=_UNSET
doc:
Transcribe a pending voice event and echo transcripts once → ``(enriched_text,
transcripts)`` for ``agent.interrupt()`` or the pending-drain flow; ``(text, [])`` when there
is no STT-eligible media (caller owns the ``_build_media_placeholder`` fallback). ``text`` is
only that fallback: the caption is read live from ``event.text`` so one merged in during
the STT await is kept.

name: _prepend_media_prefix
doc: ``prefix`` + the user's text; the Discord empty-content placeholder is dropped as redundant.

name: _untranscribed_audio_note
doc:
One minimal neutral marker for every STT failure. Never mention "no STT provider" or setup
steps — persisted in history they make the model keep volunteering STT-setup advice.

name: _transcribe_one_clip
doc: ``(transcript_or_None, note)`` for one clip via configured STT with local fallback.

name: pairing_profile_arg
doc: ``-p <profile> `` when the store belongs to a non-default profile, else ``""``.

name: pairing_code_reply
arguments: platform_name: str, code: str, profile_arg: str=''
doc:
The DM a first-time sender receives: what happened, how long the code lives, what to do
whether they are the owner or a guest, and that they must message again after approval.

name: unauthorized_owner_hint
arguments: platform_name: str, user_id: str, user_name: str='', *, hermes_home: str
doc:
One-line hint for the owner (log + home channel): who was dropped and how to let them in.
No pairing request is minted for an ignored sender (a configured allowlist means the owner chose
to restrict access), so the ways in are the allowlist itself or switching the platform to
pairing mode.

name: notify
doc: Best-effort post to the source platform's home channel; silent when none is configured.

name: _served_notice_target_key
arguments: profile: Optional[str], platform_value: str, chat_id, thread_id
doc:
Notice-dedupe key for one SERVED profile's home channel.

A secondary uses the ``<profile>:<platform>`` key convention the runtime status already
stamps in ``gateway_state.json``; the launch profile keeps the bare platform value so a
marker written before this change still matches its delivered targets.

name: _safe_delivery_transport
doc:
``resolve_delivery_transport`` isolated to one target: ``None`` (logged) on failure.

The fan-out spans every served profile, so one profile's broken adapter must not abort the
pass and starve every profile after it in dict order.

name: _refusal_retry_at
doc: When a refused queued notice is next offered: exponential from the drain base, capped.

name: _mark_internal_notification
doc:
Append unambiguous machine provenance to model-facing notification text (#52694).

A process notification re-enters the conversation as a role=user turn on every wake path
(push ``handle_message`` and the api_server self-post alike); without this footer the model
has read it as something the human said — including "replying" to the message the watch
was armed from. Appended, not prepended, so start-anchored consumers (session timeline,
memory gating, desktop notification detection, the SYSTEM prefix) keep matching.
Idempotent so a retried delivery never stacks footers.

name: _raw_process_event_session_id
doc: Recognize API routes, not malformed structured or partial messaging routes.

name: _local_completion_card
doc:
The card of a local process notice: the async-result card the in-process TUI wrote for a
completion or async delegation (a gateway-side ``/review`` reports as one), and a liveness tick's
one-line receipt. The claim's ``message.start`` carries it, and an idle classic CLI only opens a
turn that has one. ``{}`` for a watch match.
