name: _watch_notification_metadata
doc:
Synthetic-event metadata for a watch/completion notification: routing pins, proof ids,
automation identities, and the local async-result card.

name: _deliver_platform_notice
doc: Deliver a setup/operational notice using platform-specific privacy rules.

name: _deliver_media_from_response
arguments: self, response: str, event: MessageEvent, adapter, thread_metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Deliver explicit MEDIA: tags from an already-streamed response (text already delivered).
EXPLICIT-ONLY, unlike the non-streaming path in ``gateway/platforms/base.py``: a bare local
path in a streamed reply is shown text or stale inspected content, and promoting it sent
files the model never asked for. MEDIA tags are NOT deduped against prior turns (a final-reply
directive is a deliberate attach); stale auto-appended tags are deduped upstream.

Only ``MEDIA:`` directives — the explicit attachment contract — trigger post-stream uploads. See
#20834.

name: _deliver_queued_first_response
arguments: self, response: str, source: SessionSource, adapter, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, event_message_id: Optional[str]=None, text_already_delivered: bool=False, deliver_media: bool=True, stream_consumer=None, session_key: Optional[str]=None, inbound_message_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Deliver a queued response using the normal text+attachment split.

``session_key`` lets the text send record a delivery-ledger obligation like the normal final
send does, keyed on ``inbound_message_id`` (the raw inbound id, distinct from the
``event_message_id`` reply anchor); see ``_send_queued_final_text``. Without a key the send
stays unledgered.

Returns whether the caller may treat this turn's final as delivered. True: the stream had
already delivered it, the reconcile edit landed, the send succeeded, or there was nothing
textual to send. False: the send was REFUSED (flood control, dead transport) — the caller
must leave the normal completion send as the fallback, or the user gets nothing. A connector
DECLINE returns True: that destination is not approved and must not be re-sent.

significant_calls.expression:
self._send_queued_final_text(
                        adapter, source, text_content, metadata, event_message_id, session_key,
                        inbound_message_id)

name: _send_queued_final_text
arguments: self, adapter, source: SessionSource, text_content: str, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]], event_message_id: Optional[str], session_key: Optional[str], inbound_message_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Send a queued-lane final through the same ledger bracket as the normal final
(``send_final_ledgered``). This lane used to call ``adapter.send`` bare and discard the
result, so a final refused here (flood control, a transport that had just died) left no
ledger row and was gone for good. The ledger identity is the raw inbound message id;
``event_message_id`` is only the reply anchor, which is None wherever replies are not used
(Telegram forum topics, Slack reaction handoffs) and so cannot identify the turn; with no
inbound id the ledger falls back to the event's own (empty) message id. Adapters without
the base contract and sends without a session key keep the plain send.

significant_calls.expression:
adapter.send_final_ledgered(
                MessageEvent(text="", source=source, ledger_message_id=inbound_message_id),
                session_key, text_content, _mark_notify_metadata(metadata), reply_to=event_message_id)

name: _send_restart_notification
doc: Notify the chat that initiated /restart that the gateway is back.

name: _home_channel_transports
doc: Yield ``(platform, platform_cfg, home, transport)`` for every home channel with a live transport.

name: _served_home_channel_configs
doc:
``(profile, platform, platform_cfg)`` for every SERVED profile's configured home channel.

``self.config`` is the launch profile's alone, but one host process multiplexes every
profile, so a host-wide notice built from it silently skips the others' channels. The
secondary configs are the ones ``_load_secondary_profile_config`` already cached at
adapter start; ``profile`` is ``None`` for the launch profile.

name: _served_home_channel_transports
doc:
``(profile, platform, platform_cfg, home, transport)`` for every served profile's home
channel with a live transport — the launch profile's (``profile`` ``None``) first.

name: _send_home_channel_message
arguments: self, platform, home, transport, message: str, failure_fmt: str
doc: Best-effort send to one home channel; True on success, failures logged with ``failure_fmt``.

name: _replay_pending_planned_restart_notification
doc:
Send the planned-restart online notice to every home channel still owed one; clear
``.restart_pending.json`` only once all of them were reached.

Runs from the boot pass and again from ``_install_reconnected_adapter``, so a home whose
platform was down at boot gets its notice when the platform comes back (#112109). Delivered
targets are recorded in the marker so neither a later replay nor the next process (if this
one restarts first) notifies a home twice. The lock serializes a boot pass that outlived the
restore gate against a concurrent reconnect replay.

name: _send_home_channel_startup_notifications
doc:
Notify EVERY served profile's configured home channels that the gateway is back online.

Best-effort, once per home CHAT — several served profiles can share one chat (a single
Telegram group for the whole host), and one host process restarting once owes that chat
one notice. Accounting stays per profile so the marker's owed set still discharges.
``skip_targets`` lets startup avoid duplicate messages when a more specific restart
notification is queued for the same chat.

name: _send_session_db_warning_notifications
doc:
Broadcast a state.db failure warning to all home channels.

When SessionDB init fails at gateway startup, messages may flow but nothing is persisted
— /resume, /history, and session_search all silently break. Best-effort: failures are
logged, not raised.

See #88235.

significant_calls.expression:
self._send_home_channel_message(
                    platform, home, transport, message, "state.db warning notification failed for %s:%s: %s")

name: _build_process_event_source
doc:
Resolve the canonical source for a synthetic background-process event.

Prefer the persisted session-store origin; the active foreground event causes cross-topic bleed.

name: _drain_watch_notifications
doc:
Consume queued watch events and inject them when notifications are enabled.

The queue is ALWAYS drained (so watch events don't rot or requeue-spin) but injection is
skipped when the OWNING profile's ``display.background_process_notifications`` is ``off``
— one shared queue carries every served profile's events, so the gate is evaluated per
event inside its profile scope, never once for the ambient (launch) profile.

See #9290.

name: _requeue_refused_watch_event
doc:
Retry a refused watch event on a bounded backoff, never on every 2 s tick (#140899).

Only a refusal proven permanent (``WakeNotAccepted.permanent``: the route has no session,
or the payload is invalid) counts toward the cap that drops it. A transient one (a restart's
after-turn wait, a parked profile, a full owner FIFO) or one whose owner may still appear (an
unowned or foreign-pinned notice) waits it out however long it lasts.

name: _adapter_by_platform_value
doc: Literal ``p.value == platform_name`` scan over connected adapters (native adapters only).

name: _self_post_api_server
arguments: self, adapter, synth_text: str, raw_sid: str, evt: dict
doc:
Deliver to a non-push (api_server) session by raw session id.

Async-delegation completions are persisted as a durable delivery row — after the parent
turn's event.complete the CLIENT owns the next turn on this stateless surface, so never
self-post them as a new role=user prompt. Other watch events wake the session via self-post.

name: _served_api_server_wake_profile
doc:
The served (non-primary) profile whose own session store holds *raw_sid*, else ``None``
(the default profile's HTTP self-post). Blocking: reads served ``state.db`` files.

A served profile's ``api_server`` turn binds the RAW session id as its session key, so its
completion event names no profile: the only ownership proof is the served profile's own
store, exactly the rung the Kanban notifier applies. An event whose source DOES name a
served profile (structured key / persisted origin) must be owned by that profile or it
raises ``LookupError`` — never a wake in the default profile's store.

name: _resolve_injection_adapter
doc:
Adapter for a synthetic-event platform: alias-aware transport resolver first (one
Platform.RELAY adapter fronts N logical platforms; native wins), literal ``p.value`` scan as
fallback for minimal runner stubs / exotic platform strings when the resolver can't run.

name: _inject_watch_notification
arguments: self, synth_text: str, evt: dict, *, raise_not_accepted: bool=False
doc:
Inject a watch/completion notification as a synthetic message event.

Routing comes from the queued event, never the active foreground message. Returns
``True`` on adapter acceptance, ``False`` on retryable adapter failure, ``None`` with no
gateway route or a refused notice pinned to a permanently-gone session (``_watch_pin_gone``).
Not transactional: a crash after acceptance can replay (at-least-once).

name: _completion_delivery_identity
doc:
Return a producer-stable identity when one is available.

Delegation UUIDs identify one producer completion. Process session IDs include the
persisted spawn epoch so a reused ID is a distinct incarnation; legacy events without
``started_at`` are delivered undeduplicated rather than risk suppressing a real completion.

name: _mark_completions_delivered_locked
doc: Move identities inflight -> delivered and trim retention. Caller holds ``_completion_delivery_lock``.

name: _completion_identity_seen
doc:
True when ``identity`` is inflight or already delivered this gateway lifecycle.

With ``claim`` an unseen identity is atomically marked inflight (same lock hold).

name: _classify_completion_target
doc:
Classify an async-completion target before adapter acceptance: ``"deliver"`` (spawning
session live or compression-rotated with a live continuation; the resolver still retargets),
``"terminal"`` (parent gone for good — unknown / user boundary like /new; drop the durable row
rather than falsely ack), ``"retry"`` (DB unavailable / rotation mid-flight; defer the claim).

name: _classify_completion_owner
doc:
``_classify_completion_target``'s verdict and, on ``"deliver"``, the owning session it proved
(a delegate child's pin resolved through ``model_config._delegate_from``) and the session delivery
reaches (the owner, or its compression tip).

name: _settle_durable_claim
arguments: kind: str, delegation_id: str, claim_id: str
doc: Best-effort ``drop``/``release`` of a durable completion claim.

name: _completion_delivery_ready
doc: Unavailable owners/transports must not spend a durable delivery attempt.

name: _preflight_completion_delivery
doc:
Claim the durable row (async delegations) and verify the target before adapter acceptance.

Adapter acceptance is not proof of delivery: the inner resolver can still fail closed inside
the pipeline after acceptance, falsely acking the durable row. Verifying first gives drops an
honest durable disposition.

name: _completion_event_scope
doc:
Profile runtime scope of the session a completion event targets (a no-op context when the
event is the default profile's or the scope is already installed).

The pre-flight (``_classify_completion_target`` → ``_session_db``) and every durable-ledger op
(``tools.async_delegation`` → ``get_hermes_home()/state.db``) resolve from the ambient scope.
The supervised ``_async_delegation_watcher`` and startup-recovered process watchers run under
the ROOT scope, so a secondary profile's completion was looked up in the DEFAULT profile's
state.db — classified ``terminal`` and dropped, its ledger row stranded ``pending`` forever.

name: _served_api_server_event_scope
doc:
Scope of the served profile whose own store holds a raw api_server session (its events name no
profile), else the launch profile's, as for any unrouted event.

name: _deliver_completion_notification
arguments: self, synth_text: str, evt: dict, *, sibling_claims=()
doc:
Acknowledge one admitted batch, refund refusals, or release failed deliveries.

True means adapter admission, not model execution; None means deduplicated or
terminal. False remains retryable. Claims are settled together for every sibling.

name: _deliver_completion_notification_scoped
arguments: self, synth_text: str, evt: dict, *, sibling_claims=()

name: _format_coalesced_process_completions
doc: Build one bounded synthetic event from several redacted completions.

name: _record_coalesced_completion_siblings
doc: Extend a successful primary delivery claim to its batched siblings.

name: _flush_process_completion_batch
doc: Deliver one short-window completion batch and resolve its waiters.

name: _cancel_process_completion_batch_tasks
doc: Settle pending completion batches before adapter teardown.

name: _enqueue_process_completion_notification
doc: Fan in policy-admitted process completions with compatible pinned owners.

name: _enrich_async_delegation_routing
doc:
Fill platform/chat_id/thread_id/chat_type on an async-delegation event.

Such events only carry ``session_key`` (the daemon worker lacks per-message routing
metadata). Best-effort: a CLI-origin event (empty session_key) is left as-is and won't route.

name: _deliver_async_delegation_group
doc:
Deliver a same-session batch of async completions as ONE turn: the primary carries the
consolidated text of every sibling THIS runner claimed (siblings owned elsewhere are excluded;
their claims are acked only after adapter acceptance). True after acceptance, False to requeue
the group, None when nothing is deliverable here (retry siblings requeued).

name: _restore_secondary_completion_ledgers
doc:
Re-queue undelivered async completions from every SECONDARY profile's ledger. The process
registry's ``restore_completions()`` covers only the launch profile's ``state.db``; a
secondary's rows would otherwise never be replayed after a restart.

name: _sweep_orphaned_completion_ledgers
doc:
Offer completions whose owner process died while this gateway runs (#97202): the launch
ledger in the launch scope, each served secondary under its own. Startup replay only covers
owners that were already gone when the gateway started.

name: _each_secondary_ledger
doc: Run ``fn`` (returns a completion count) once per SECONDARY profile, bound to that profile.

name: _async_delegation_watcher
doc:
Drain async completions and pattern notifications even while sessions are idle.

Background subagents and process pattern events have no per-process notification
consumer; both must progress without a later foreground turn.

name: _back_off_refused_completions
doc:
Space out an undelivered async group's retries instead of re-offering it every 2 s pass.
The backoff only paces; the durable ledger decides when a row gives up (a permanent refusal
spends a delivery attempt there, so the count survives restarts) (#141153).

name: _redacted_output_tail
doc: Last ``limit`` chars of process output through the secret redactors (unconditional floor).

name: _launching_turn_active
doc:
Whether the session that launched *watcher*'s process is still inside a turn on its
adapter (``_active_sessions`` is the base adapter's busy guard).

name: _send_watcher_message
arguments: self, platform_name: str, chat_id, thread_id, message_text: str, watcher: dict

name: _build_process_completion_event
doc: Build the synthetic ``completion`` event for an agent-notify watcher.

name: _format_process_final_message
arguments: self, session_id: str, session, notify_mode: str
doc:
Human-facing completion message. Every mode shares the one-line status header; the
raw-output modes (all/result/error) append the bounded output tail under it instead of the
old bracketed ``[Background process proc_… finished~ …]`` debug wrapper (#54266).

name: arm_process_watcher
doc:
Start ``_run_process_watcher`` for a watcher registered mid-turn, from the agent's
tool thread. Waiting for the post-turn drain leaves a process that finishes while its
launching turn is still running with no watcher at all (#112033). False = the gateway
is not serving (startup, shutdown): the caller keeps the descriptor in
``pending_watchers`` for the startup / post-turn drain.

name: _run_process_watcher
doc:
Poll a background process and push updates until it exits. Mode
(``display.background_process_notifications``): concise (default one-liner; failures append
the output tail) / all (running updates + final raw) / result (final raw) / error (final raw
if exit != 0) / off.

name: _resolve_compression_lineage_target
arguments: self, session_db: Any, session_entry: Optional[SessionEntry], pinned_session_id: str
doc: Distinguish uncertain compression ownership from a proven foreign route.

name: _closed_local_target
arguments: self, session_db: Any, entry: Optional[SessionEntry], pinned_session_id: str, pinned_row: Optional[dict]
doc:
The closed (/new, exit) physical session of a local conversation a completion is noted on
(#134889 LC-7, ``session_completion_notes``), else ``""``. The pinned session, or the compression
tip it rotated to, must be the one the conversation's route still names: a local /new opens a new
route, so the replacement never matches, and messaging routes never qualify. Only a close ends a
local tip (``session.detach {end_reason}`` stamps the client's own reason: ``cli_close``,
``tui_close``, ``tui_shutdown``...), so any end but compression is one.

name: _lookup_completion_owner
doc:
Nonmutating delegation proof shared by preflight and route resolution.

A current route is an explicit ownership boundary, not a route to repair.
Generic parent pointers also describe compression and branches; only
``_delegate_from`` authorizes walking out of an execution transcript.

name: _watch_pin_gone
arguments: self, evt: dict, refusal: str, *, log: bool=True
doc:
True (logged once with ``log``) when a refused notice is pinned to a permanently-gone session.

The session authority admits a notice only into its pinned session or that session's
compression continuation, so after /new it refuses the notice on every retry and the drain
would spin on it (#141562). This is the completion pre-flight's verdict, applied after the
refusal. A dropped notice is gone for good; a /resume reopens the pinned session, so the
process's later notices are admitted again.

name: _resolve_async_delegation_session
arguments: self, session_entry: SessionEntry, pinned_session_id: str, proven_session_id: str='', completion_ids: Sequence[str]=()
doc:
Resolve an async completion to its verified owning gateway session.

Follow compression-rotation lineage (parent row ended, child continues), but never let a
late completion override an unrelated /new or restored route. Unknown ownership fails
closed; the result stays in the delegation records. An owner that cannot be confirmed right
now (``retry``) sends the completions admitted with the event back to the delivery queue.

A pinned *delegate* row is likewise canonicalized to its human-facing parent through
``model_config._delegate_from`` before any route check or mutation (#92611). Unresolvable
provenance — a cycle, a missing parent, a malformed config, or a chain longer than
``_MAX_DELEGATE_PROVENANCE_HOPS`` — drops the injection rather than falling back to the
current route entry. That is deliberate: routing an internal child's output into a session
whose ownership was never verified is the same class of defect this canonicalization fixes,
and the completion remains readable in the delegation records either way.

name: _requeue_uncertain_completion
doc:
Offer admitted completions again when the turn could not confirm their owner (``retry``),
so the next delivery re-runs the pre-flight; boundary verdicts stay dropped.

name: _update_output_tail
doc: Last ``limit`` chars of an update log, prefixed with an ellipsis when cut.

name: _schedule_update_notification_watch
doc: Ensure a background task is watching for update completion.

name: _marker_profile
doc:
Owning profile of a persisted restart/update marker: explicit ``profile``, else the
``agent:<profile>:`` lane of its ``session_key`` (markers written before ``profile`` was
persisted); ``None`` = default profile.

name: _marker_age_seconds
doc:
Age of a persisted update marker, from the ``timestamp`` stamped by its writer.

``None`` when the marker carries no parseable stamp — the field is absent on markers
written before it existed, and callers keep the old retry behavior rather than guess.

name: _resolve_update_target
doc: Resolve adapter/chat/session for update watcher messages from the pending marker.

name: _pending_marker_metadata
arguments: self, platform, chat_id, data: dict, adapter
doc: Thread metadata for a persisted update/restart marker (thread_id/chat_type/message_id keys).

name: _watch_update_completion_only
arguments: self, paths: _UpdatePaths, deadline: float, poll_interval: float
doc: Fallback when no adapter/chat can be resolved: wait for the exit code, then notify.

name: _read_update_output_since
doc: Read update output defensively; logs may contain invalid UTF-8.

name: _send_update_output
doc: Send buffered update output as fenced chunks that fit message limits (Telegram: 4096).

name: _forward_update_prompt
arguments: self, target: _UpdateTarget, prompt_text: str, default: str
doc: Forward an update prompt: platform-native buttons first (Discord, Telegram), else text.

significant_calls.expression:
adapter.send_update_prompt(
                    chat_id=target.chat_id, prompt=prompt_text, default=default,
                    session_key=target.session_key, metadata=target.send_metadata(),
                )

name: _watch_update_progress
arguments: self, poll_interval: float=2.0, stream_interval: float=4.0, timeout: float=1800.0

name: _send_update_notification
doc:
If an update finished, notify the user.

False while the update is still running (caller may retry); True after a definitive send/skip.

name: _install_plugin_message_injector
doc: Publish this live gateway's plugin message scheduler process-wide.

name: _clear_plugin_message_injector
doc: Remove this runner's scheduler without clobbering a newer owner.

name: _schedule_plugin_message_injection
arguments: self, *, content: str, plugin_id: str, session_key: Optional[str]=None, origin: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]]=None, plugin_home: Optional[Path]=None, keyless: bool=False, calling_session_key: str=''
doc:
Schedule a plugin-triggered turn on the live gateway loop (thread-safe).

With ``origin`` the profile, origin and adapter checks run here, synchronously, so the plugin
gets ``False`` for a chat it may not start; authorization is rechecked at dispatch. ``keyless``
(neither given) picks the target here too (``gateway/plugin_keyless_inject.py``).

name: _plugin_injection_scope
doc:
Multiplex: enter the source's profile runtime scope (or *home*'s, when the owner is known)
around ``handle_message`` so the background task it spawns — the turn AND the reply send after
the handler returns — inherits that profile's home and secrets (this coroutine runs from the
default loop context, not from the profile adapter's own intake task).

name: _plugin_injection_authorized
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, *, plugin_id: str, target: str
doc:
Current gateway authorization for the route the injected turn will run as. Host-side
plugin code is trusted to ask, never to widen access: a stored or supplied route must pass
today's allowlists / pairing / allow-all, and adapter-time grants (Discord roles) do not count.

name: _plugin_session_key_admissible
arguments: self, session_key: str, *, plugin_home: Optional[Path], plugin_id: str
doc:
Synchronous refusal of a keyed injection into another profile's session (local or
messaging), so the plugin gets ``False``; an unknown key is decided at dispatch, as before.
Dispatch rechecks.

name: _plugin_messaging_session_owned
arguments: self, session_key: str, *, plugin_home: Optional[Path], plugin_id: str
doc:
A messaging session belongs to the profile its key names (``agent:<profile>:...``) under
multiplexing, and to the one served profile of a standalone gateway; it must be the plugin's
own, as on the origin path. A caller with no plugin home is left to dispatch, as before.

name: _plugin_local_session
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, session_key: str, *, plugin_home: Optional[Path], plugin_id: str
doc:
A local session's own source passes no chat allowlist, so the plugin's profile boundary is
the only check: the session authority registered for the plugin's immutable home must hold
the live session under this key. Its ``LiveSession``, or ``None`` (logged). Never resolved
through the source's profile, whose fallback is the ambient scope (a default-profile local
source carries none, so under beta's scope it would read as beta's).

name: _dispatch_plugin_message_injection
arguments: self, *, session_key: str, content: str, plugin_id: str, plugin_home: Optional[Path]=None
doc: Route a plugin-triggered turn through the session's live adapter.

name: _dispatch_plugin_local_injection
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, entry, *, content: str, plugin_id: str, plugin_home: Optional[Path]
doc:
A local (CLI/TUI/Desktop) session has no messaging adapter or chat allowlist: the plugin
turn is committed to its FIFO on the live session's own source and adapter, as a bot delivery
is, only when the plugin's own profile's authority holds the session (checked before entering
that scope). Main queued key-less CLI injections into the REPL; this is where they land now.

name: _served_profile_for_home
doc:
Name of the profile this gateway serves at *home* (a plugin manager's immutable home), or
``None`` when this gateway does not serve it.

name: _plugin_origin_source
arguments: self, origin: Mapping[str, Any], *, plugin_home: Optional[Path], plugin_id: str
doc:
The canonicalized source for a plugin-supplied *origin*, or ``None`` (logged) when the
plugin may not start a turn there: its profile is not served, the origin is malformed or
names another profile, that profile has no live adapter for the platform, or the gateway's
own routing for the chat lands in a different profile.

name: _plugin_origin_admissible
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, *, plugin_home: Optional[Path], plugin_id: str
doc:
Under the session authority a plugin turn borrows the connector provenance of a human
message already committed in that chat, and the gateway never mints it for a chat the
platform did not deliver: refuse such an origin here, so the plugin gets ``False`` instead of
a ``True`` for a turn the dispatch then drops. Dispatch rechecks.

name: _dispatch_plugin_origin_injection
arguments: self, *, source: SessionSource, content: str, plugin_id: str
doc:
Start (or continue) the session at a plugin-supplied origin through the adapter's normal
message path: ``get_or_create_session`` creates it, the reply goes back to that chat.

name: _admit_plugin_injection
arguments: self, adapter, source: SessionSource, *, session_key: str, session_id: str, content: str, plugin_id: str
doc:
Under a session authority, commit the plugin turn into the session's durable FIFO as a
trusted producer admission (the heartbeat / completion seam) instead of running it on the
in-process lane beside an admitted turn. ``None`` means no authority serves this scope and
the caller keeps the standalone adapter path; a refused admission is ``False``, logged.

name: reload_plugins_verb
doc:
Control-socket ``reload-plugins``: force re-discovery under the requested home's scope so a plugin
installed/enabled by another process (CLI, Desktop, ``plugins.manage``) loads now; the loaded event
then re-wires that profile's adapters. Only the gateway home and served profile homes are accepted.
Answer: ``{"reloaded", "home", "plugins", "activations", "adapters_rewired"}``. Runs on the socket executor thread
(discovery is blocking); the count is read on the loop AFTER the re-wire callback (FIFO), so a
truthful "active now" reaches the caller.

name: _count_adapters
doc: Live adapters for the profile; scheduled after the loaded-event callback, so they are re-wired.

name: _subscribe_plugin_rewire
arguments: self, manager: Any, profile_name: Optional[str]=None, profile_home: Optional[Path]=None
doc:
Idempotent per manager scope: a served-profile rescan re-enters ``_load_secondary_profile_config``
and must not stack a second listener (two listeners = two re-wire passes, still deduped, but noise).

name: _rewire_plugin_handlers
doc:
Call ``rewire_plugin_handlers()`` on every live adapter of one profile (``None`` = the launch
profile's ``self.adapters``); a secondary's adapters read their own manager, so bind its scope.
Returns the number of adapters re-wired.

name: profile_serve_signature
doc: Cheap change detector for a served profile's credentials/config: file signature per file.

name: _added_profile_blocker
doc:
Why a single-profile boot must not start multiplexing now that a second profile exists: the
``gateway.auto_multiplex_migration: false`` opt-out on the default profile, else boot's preflight.

name: _profile_lifecycle_verb
doc: Build on the owning loop; socket handlers themselves run on executor threads.

name: _mcp_config_reconciler
doc:
Housekeeping chore keeping live MCP servers in step with ``mcp_servers`` on disk, every tick
after the first (startup discovery owns that one). Reconciling on DRIFT rather than only on a
config EDIT is what brings back a server whose FIRST connect failed (#112445): it never reached
``_servers``, so the parked self-probe — a property of a task that connected once — cannot revive
it, and its config never changes. The reconcile is a cached config read plus set compares when
nothing moved; a server dropped from config is torn down (a parked one otherwise self-probes
every ``_PARKED_RETRY_INTERVAL`` for the life of the process) and a missing one is reconnected
only once its per-server connect cooldown (30s→600s backoff) has lapsed, so a chronically failing
server is retried on that schedule, not every tick. Interactive OAuth is suppressed — this runs
on a housekeeping thread nobody is watching.

name: _for_each_served_profile
doc:
Run ``body(profile_label)`` once per served profile, inside that profile's runtime scope.

Housekeeping runs on a bare thread with no turn on the stack, so nothing binds a profile for it:
``get_hermes_home()`` and ``get_secret()`` see the LAUNCH profile's values, and under
``gateway.multiplex_profiles`` a fail-closed credential read logs ``no profile secret scope on a
multiplexed call`` on every tick (the skills-sync pulls resolved Nous credentials this way, four
WARNINGs per hourly tick per chore). A single-profile gateway runs ``body`` once, unscoped:
there the process env IS the profile's own value — unless a hosted room already flipped the
process-wide guard (#112878), in which case the launch profile's OWN scope is bound, as
``run_turn.py::_standalone_launch_scope`` does for turns.

name: profile_scoped_chore
doc:
Wrap a zero-arg housekeeping chore that reads the profile's home, config or credentials so it
runs once per served profile under that profile's scope (see ``_for_each_served_profile``).

name: migrate_profile_identity_verb
doc:
Build the ``migrate-profile-identity`` control-verb handler for ``hermes profile rename``
(#111926). The live multiplexer owns the routing index in memory and writes it back
periodically, so a CLI-side rewrite of ``agent:<old>:*`` would be clobbered on the next save;
the CLI therefore asks this process to rekey both durable stores AND ``SessionStore._entries``.
Runs on the control-socket executor thread; ``rekey_profile_routing`` takes the store lock.

name: purge_profile_identity_verb
doc:
Build the ``purge-profile-identity`` control-verb handler for ``hermes profile delete``
(#111926, delete side). The live multiplexer owns the routing index in memory and writes it back
periodically, so a CLI-side DELETE of ``agent:<name>:*`` rows would be undone by its next save;
the CLI therefore asks this process to drop the durable rows AND ``SessionStore._entries``.

Deliberately NOT part of ``_unserve_profile()``: that path also unserves names that are still
alive elsewhere in the identity story — a rename's old name leaves the served set exactly like a
delete does (its directory is gone either way) — and purging there would race the rekey it is
supposed to leave intact. Only the delete path invokes this verb. Runs on the control-socket
executor thread; ``purge_profile_routing`` takes the store lock.

name: served_profile_names
doc: Profiles this multiplexer currently serves (active first), from the live bookkeeping.

name: _note_served_profiles
doc: Called by ``_record_served_profiles``: remember the served set and each home's signature.

name: _profile_reconcile_watcher
doc:
Supervised safety net, every ``interval`` seconds: re-sync shell hooks whose consent changed
(every gateway), then rescan ``profiles/`` when multiplexing (creators signal the control
socket for an immediate rescan); a gateway standalone only because the host had one profile
starts multiplexing here once a second one exists.

name: _sync_hooks_on_consent_change
doc:
Re-sync the shell hooks of each home (launch + served) whose consent allowlist or config
changed since the last tick, under that home's scope: hooks consented since start register, revoked ones stop
firing. A home seen for the first time syncs once (consent may have landed after startup
registered). Hook registration only: adapters and sessions are never touched.

name: _resync_changed_hook_consent
doc:
Blocking half of ``_sync_hooks_on_consent_change``; returns the signatures it applied. The
key covers ``config.yaml`` too: a sync that read an empty/unreadable config applied nothing,
so its recovery must re-run it. A failed sync is left unrecorded and retried next tick.

name: reconcile_served_profiles
doc:
Diff ``profiles/`` (what exists now) against the served set (the process reservation):
reserve + build the runtime and start adapters for new profiles, tear down, unroute and
unreserve deleted ones, (re)build adapters for served profiles whose config/.env changed.
Other profiles' adapters are never touched. A new profile whose home another gateway owns or
whose store is unusable is parked (logged, not served) and left for an explicit rescan.
Returns ``{"added", "removed", "rescanned", "parked", "served_profiles"}``.

name: _apply_profile_changes
arguments: self, current, added, removed, changed, *, reason, live=None, result=None
doc:
Apply a selected diff under the reconcile lock, shared by the watcher and the
serve/unserve control verbs. New profiles first get a runtime (reservation + store); one
whose home another gateway owns or whose store is unusable is parked, not served.

name: _parked_profile_names
doc:
Profiles that exist but could not be served (unusable store, home owned elsewhere); boot's
``initialize_gateway_runtime`` parks into the same published ``name -> reason`` map.

name: _multiplex_for_added_profile
doc:
Start multiplexing in place when this gateway booted standalone ONLY because the host had
one profile and a second now exists (#141623). Boot settles the mode once, so without this a
profile created afterwards (Desktop's New Agent, ``hermes profile create``) was never served:
every ticket, session and delete for it was refused until a manual restart.

No restart and no drain: the launch env is frozen and unscoped secret reads fail closed
(``activate_multi_profile_hosting``, the hosted-room precedent), the launch home becomes the
first entry of the reservation, and the caller's ordinary hot-serve reconcile serves the new
profile. Turns already running keep their bound scope; the launch profile's later work binds
its own scope through ``_standalone_launch_scope`` and the re-wired primary handlers. Any
other standalone verdict, or a preflight blocker now, leaves the gateway as it is; nothing is
latched, so the next rescan or watcher tick retries once the blocker clears. The switch is an
automatic migration, so ``gateway.auto_multiplex_migration: false`` holds it back the same way
(re-read on every rescan: setting it back to true converges without a restart). True when armed.

name: _serve_profile_runtime
doc:
Grow the reservation by *home* and build its session authority (boot's per-secondary
steps). Returns the park reason — reservation released — when another gateway owns the home
(a stray per-profile daemon) or its store cannot be opened; None when served. An
adapters-only runner (no authority registry) grows the reservation alone.

name: _live_resource_claims
doc:
Startup's ``claimed`` map rebuilt from what is live now: primary claims plus every connected
secondary's credential/listener, so a hot-added profile reusing a token is parked, never a
second poller.

name: _after_profiles_added
doc: Per-profile startup side effects for hot-added profiles: log routing + scoped MCP discovery.

name: _unserve_profile
doc:
Stop and unroute one profile: cancel its reconnects, tear down its adapters, drop its
bookkeeping and release this process's handles into its home so the deleter's rmtree succeeds.
The releasing process is not always the deleter (#130244): under multiplexing THIS gateway
process routes the profile's logs and owns its scoped MCP servers, so both must be released
here too or the deleter's rmtree still fails on ``logs/.__agent.lock`` / ``mcp-stderr.log``.

The whole teardown runs inside the removed profile's own runtime scope: adapter disconnect
hooks, the agent-cache eviction (provider/memory shutdown) and the state/memory handle
release all read config and credentials at call time, and this coroutine runs on the
reconcile task with no profile bound — unscoped they resolved against the LAUNCH home, so a
teardown hook needing this profile's credential failed closed (or, worse, borrowed the launch
profile's). Secrets are not re-hydrated: teardown must not block the loop on a source fetch.

name: reserved_profile_homes
doc: ``(name, home)`` pairs this process reserved: launch home first, then served secondaries.

name: _build_profile_authority
doc: One profile's authority against its own ``state.db``; raises when that store is unusable.

name: _store_open_failure
doc:
Why *home*'s ``state.db`` has no handle: the scoped handle caches answer None for a failed open
(and while they back off), so the park reason named an ownership mismatch over the real cause, a
legacy store that crashed its migration on every open (#141467). The reason is the exception the
failed open recorded; reopening here to learn it could create or migrate the store, and would skip
the caches' backoff.

name: _park_reserved_profile
doc:
A secondary whose store is unusable is parked: logged, unreserved, left out of
``served_profiles`` and named under ``parked_profiles`` in the runtime descriptor. Boot
continues for every other profile (a runtime hot-add parks the same way).

name: park_profile
doc:
Publish *name* under ``parked_profiles`` (name -> reason) in the runtime descriptor and the
root's ``gateway_state.json``: a client of that profile then gets a terminal ``profile_parked``
verdict from ``ensure`` instead of waiting its whole deadline for a service that never comes.

name: profile_parked
doc:
True when *name* is parked: not served now, but a rescan serves it again, so its ingress is
temporarily unavailable (retry it), never an invalid route (refuse it for good).

name: refuse_parked_scope
doc:
An API request under a parked profile's ``/p/<profile>/`` prefix finds no authority: refuse it
retryably (``runtime_draining``, a 503 with ``Retry-After``), not with the final
``profile_mismatch`` of a profile this gateway does not serve.

name: release_unknown_turn_markers
doc:
Before the unclean-start pass reads crash-left turn markers: a marked turn whose canonical
admission recovered ``unknown`` (the owner died before its terminal commit) owes no reply, so
its marker is cleared rather than ledgered as a delivery the FIFO never committed. A terminal
admission keeps its marker: its persisted reply is ledgered and sent once, never re-run.

name: reserve_profile_home
doc:
Grow the process reservation by one profile (hot-serve): take its ``gateway.lock`` and add it
to the frozen boot set, so every reader of the reservation — and the next restart's
all-or-nothing reserve — sees it. ``OwnershipConflict`` when another gateway owns the home.

name: release_profile_home
doc: Shrink the reservation by one profile (deleted, or parked because it cannot be served).

name: _withdraw_profile_home
doc:
Drop *home* from the served set every startup consumer reads (adapters, served status, cron
ticks, ingress, spool recovery) without releasing its ``gateway.lock``.

name: _authority_tasks
doc: Snapshot every async task family owned directly by one session authority.

name: managed_turn_count
doc: Unmapped claims, managed workers and owner mutations across the served authorities.

name: stop_authority_turns
doc:
Cooperative Stop for every turn *authority* is executing: the control a user's Stop sends to a
managed worker (acknowledged, or terminated within STOP_ACK_SECONDS, and the admission settles
through its own fenced path). ``in_process`` also hard-interrupts the running agent of each
executing in-process turn, or latches the generation ``adopt_agent`` consumes before it exists.
``reason`` (a gateway restart/shutdown) is recorded on each worker it signals, so the turn settles
with that cause; a worker already stopped (the user's Stop came first) keeps none. A worker
still being spawned gets the same Stop and cause through latches (``_stop_spawning_managed``).

name: _stop_spawning_managed
doc:
A managed turn whose worker is still being spawned has nothing to signal yet: latch the
Stop for its generation (``adopt_agent`` delivers it to the worker, which is never
bootstrapped) and, for a gateway restart/shutdown, the cause its pre-bootstrap interrupted
result carries (#134889 GW-22). A user's Stop latched first keeps no cause.

name: stop_managed_turns
doc: ``stop_authority_turns`` across every served authority (whole-runtime shutdown).

name: interrupt_side_agents
doc: Whole-runtime shutdown: interrupt every counted side agent (``session_runtime_workers``).

name: _retire_profile_authority
doc:
Stop profile-local services and turns before its ownership is released.

Claims are refused from here on; every executing turn gets a cooperative Stop, and its session
task is joined (an in-process turn's task ends only after its executor thread returned and the
admission settled). The hosted-room stop runs alongside that join under the same deadline: it
never interrupts accepted turns and its room threads wait for the member turns they observe, so
those turns must be signalled first or the room stop cannot finish. False when a turn or room
thread misses *timeout* (default TURN_SETTLE_SECONDS): it may still call tools and write
history, so the caller must keep the profile's reservation and store handles.

name: serve_profile_runtime
doc:
Hot-serve one reserved profile's runtime: build its authority, recover its durable state and
publish it in the descriptor/ticket store — the steps boot performs per secondary. Raises when
the profile's store is unusable; the caller parks it (and releases the reservation). Its
queued native rows are recovered once its adapters connect (``recover_served_native_rows``).

name: _drop_retired_local_adapter
doc:
A LOCAL adapter still bound to this profile's previous authority, once that authority fully
retired, gives way to *authority*'s own: restore and create otherwise refuse every local session
of the served profile as ``runtime_draining``. A retained writer never gets here (the serve is
refused while the previous authority is still retiring).

name: _recover_published_api_turns
doc:
Boot recovers queued API turns when the launch API adapter is published
(``recover_api_turns``); a profile served after that runs the same pass on its own store.

name: recover_served_native_rows
doc:
Boot's native-row recovery once hot-served profiles' adapters connected (boot runs it after
every adapter connects), in every serving ledger: a ``bot_profile`` route runs a bot's messages
on another profile, so the new bots can carry rows queued in any ledger. A session already
draining keeps its one drain. A store that cannot answer leaves its rows queued for the next
start and never stops the other ledgers or the reconcile.

name: unserve_profile_runtime
doc:
Retire one profile's authority (deleted while running) and shrink the published set.
False when one of its turns outlived the Stop deadline (keep the reservation); True otherwise,
including for a profile this process never served.

name: recover_bot_mailbox
doc:
Owner-startup Bot Chat recovery, skipped when this token cannot use the mailbox dir.

An elevated install/update can leave ``runtime/bot_live_delivery`` owned by Administrators with
no entry for the user (#139485, #138872): the gateway cannot even open its ``.lock``. Bot Chat
deliveries pause (``_locked`` already logged the dir, its owner and the remedy); every other
client keeps working instead of the whole gateway refusing to start. Any other failure still
aborts startup.

name: _recover_profile_bot_mailbox
doc:
Startup Bot Chat recovery of one served profile. A secondary whose durable leftovers cannot
be recovered is parked like one whose store cannot be opened (retired, unreserved, named under
``parked_profiles``): under multiplex it would otherwise take every other profile down with it,
on every restart (#140018). The launch profile's failure still aborts the start.

name: recover_gateway_native_sessions
doc:
Recover against the published routing index and currently connected adapters.

Stored envelopes are input, not authority to create a route or reconnect a
transport. The authority preflights every queued sender before any claim.

name: recover_profile_native_sessions
doc: Bind one authority's queued native rows to the adapters connected now.

name: wait_gateway_runtime
doc: A vanished interactive listener is fatal, not a healthy headless runtime.

name: drain_gateway_runtime
doc: Withdraw admission before any await; close sockets before DB teardown.

name: settle_gateway_runtime
doc:
Keep authority tasks alive until their last durable settlement write, within a bound.

A managed turn still running here gets its Stop first (its worker acknowledges or is
terminated, and the admission settles interrupted or ``unknown``); a task that still misses
TURN_SETTLE_SECONDS (clamped to ``budget``, what the stop's watchdog leash has left, minus
STOP_TAIL_RESERVE_SECONDS) is logged and left running for recovery. The stop sequence continues:
the executor quiesce skips the DB close while a writer is live, and process exit releases
the ownership lock, so raising here would only skip teardown and disarm the watchdog.

name: _init_runtime_settings
doc: Load ephemeral per-call config (prefill, reasoning, busy modes, timeouts, routing).

name: _init_session_store
doc: Build the SessionStore (with process-registry reset guard), its async facade and the router.

name: _init_lifecycle_state
doc: Initialise run/exit/restart flags, per-session state, and completion-delivery bookkeeping.

name: _init_runtime_caches
doc: Agent cache, profile identity, Teams runtime, failed-platform tracking, slash-confirm counter.

name: _init_session_db
doc: Open the session DB for the active scope and run opportunistic state.db / checkpoint maintenance.

name: _init_registries_and_clocks
doc: Pairing stores, hook registry, voice modes, background-task set, liveness and idle clocks.

name: _exit_with_failure_verdict
doc: True (after logging the reason) when the runner asked for a failure exit.

name: _resolve_gateway_exit_verdict
doc: Resolve the process verdict after either startup abort or normal shutdown.

name: _log_suppressed
arguments: level: int, msg: str, *args, exc_info: bool=False
doc:
``suppress(Exception)`` that logs the swallowed exception on ``gateway.run``.

Without ``exc_info`` the exception is appended as the last ``%s`` argument (``msg % (*args, exc)``);
with it the traceback is attached instead. Best-effort seams use this everywhere a failure must be
visible in the log but must never propagate.

name: _send_failed
doc: True when an adapter ``send()`` result explicitly reports failure.

name: _send_error
doc: Error text of a failed ``send()`` result (adapters may omit it).

name: _notice_target_key
doc: Dedup key for one notice destination: thread/topic platforms share a chat but route apart.

name: _delivery_target_key
arguments: platform_value: str, chat_id, thread_id, *, profile: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Dedupe key for one DELIVERED chat: profile-independent, except Telegram private chats.

Two served profiles can share one home chat (one Telegram group for the whole host) and owe it
ONE notice per host restart. A positive Telegram chat id names the USER, though: the same id
under two bot tokens is two conversations, so those stay keyed per served profile (#118233).

name: _effective_watchdog_leash
doc:
Thread-watchdog leash for the stop in progress: effective drain + grace, clamped under
launchd's live ``ExitTimeOut`` minus the dump margin. Lives here (not in gateway.restart)
because restart.py cannot import shutdown_watchdog without a cycle.

name: _active_work_count
doc: All agent work the gateway must expose and drain as one total.

name: _active_cron_job_count
doc:
Cron jobs currently executing — they run outside ``_running_agents``; 0 if cron can't import.

Cron jobs run through a standalone ``AIAgent`` on the scheduler's own thread pool
(``cron/scheduler.py::run_job``), entirely outside ``self._running_agents`` — the dict every OTHER
active-work check on this class (``_running_agent_count``, ``_drain_active_agents``) reads. Without
this, the shutdown drain is structurally blind to in-flight cron work: it can report
``active_at_start=0`` and proceed straight to killing tool subprocesses while a cron job's terminal
command is still running (#60432). Best-effort: returns 0 if the cron module can't be imported (e.g.
a minimal test double for this class).

name: _api_server_hook
doc:
Call the primary API-server adapter's ``name`` hook, clamped >= 0 (0 when the hook is absent).

Only the primary API server owns the HTTP listener, so only it is a source of this work.

name: _active_api_run_count
doc: API-server work that is outside ``_running_agents``.

name: _active_api_worker_count
doc:
API-server executor threads still inside an agent turn (#116535).

Module-level, like the cron registry above: the handler-side adapter count is already
unreachable here (``adapters`` was cleared a phase earlier) and, worse, drops on handler
cancellation while the worker thread lives on. Read live at the close gate instead of
snapshotting.

name: _interrupt_api_server_runs
doc: Interrupt API-server agents not in ``_running_agents`` (same set ``_active_api_run_count`` counts).

name: _mark_api_runs_shutdown_requested
doc: Persist the shutdown boundary on API runs before the drain can await.

name: _active_deferred_agent_worker_count
doc: Executor workers that outlived their gateway turn (e.g. a timed-out hygiene compression).

name: _track_deferred_agent_worker
doc: Expose an executor worker to drain/interrupt until it really exits.

name: _interrupt_deferred_agent_workers
doc: Request cancellation of detached executor-backed agent work.

name: _scale_to_zero_has_live_background_work
doc:
Live background work (delegations, processes, pending watchers) that must block a suspend.

PERMANENT supervised watchers (_hermes_supervised_watcher, incl. the scale-to-zero watcher
itself) are excluded, else this would be True forever and the gateway could never go dormant.

name: _gateway_cfg_section
doc: ``gateway.<name>`` from the user config when it is a dict, else None (never raises).

name: _restart_loop_guard_config
doc:
``(max_restarts, window_seconds, max_gap_seconds)`` for the restart-loop breaker.

``max_restarts <= 0`` disables it; ``max_gap_seconds`` is the longest spacing between
restart-interrupted boots that still counts as one loop.

name: _scale_to_zero_active_messaging_platforms
doc:
Return every enabled or live messaging platform across served profiles.

``self.config`` belongs to the launch profile, while ``_profile_adapters`` holds
live adapters for multiplexed secondary profiles. A direct secondary connection
must block suspension just like a direct primary connection. A secondary adapter
parked in ``_profile_failed_platforms`` (popped from ``_profile_adapters`` while a
retryable fatal reconnects) is still served: suspending mid-reconnect would leave
that reconnect unable to complete, so pending reconnects count as active too.

config.platforms is pre-seeded with disabled placeholders, and the api_server is
force-enabled on every hosted container (counting it silently disarmed the feature).

name: _scale_to_zero_should_arm
doc: Whether to start the idle watcher (D1/D11/§3.4(1)).

name: _log_scale_to_zero_not_armed_reason
doc: One INFO line on why the idle watcher did NOT arm — only for an OPTED-IN instance.

name: _scale_to_zero_note_real_inbound
doc:
Stamp real inbound and flip status back to running after a dormant wake.

Internal completion/replay events deliberately do not call this (they must not keep an idle
gateway awake).

name: _scale_to_zero_status
doc: Best-effort runtime status write; failures are debug-logged with ``fail_msg``.

name: _relay_adapter_for_dormancy
doc: Return the connected RELAY adapter, if any (the one go_dormant targets).

name: _scale_to_zero_watcher
doc:
Watch for idle, drive the relay dormant, then self-suspend. On sustained idle: status
`draining` (NOT _running=False), relay go_dormant() (socket close, NOT disconnect()), no
mark_resume_pending (suspend preserves RAM), THEN suspend via the flaps socket — Fly autostop
sees only INBOUND connections and would freeze mid-job. Without a flaps socket NAS brokers
the stop through the stamped GATEWAY_RELAY_SLEEP_URL; with no lever at all the watcher
abstains.

name: _scale_to_zero_self_suspend
doc:
Suspend this machine, in-guest where possible and via NAS otherwise (fail-awake).

Called ONLY after a clean, acked go_dormant(), with the re-dial already held.

name: _scale_to_zero_await_freeze_gap
doc:
Hold the re-dial fence across the flaps-2xx -> kernel-freeze gap.

Sliced on the WALL clock rather than one ``asyncio.sleep`` because a Fly suspend stops
CLOCK_MONOTONIC while CLOCK_REALTIME keeps tracking host time. Measured on a Fly machine
(gru, 2026-09-03) across a 252.219s freeze: ``time.monotonic()`` advanced 0.501s,
``time.time()`` advanced 252.219s. ``asyncio.sleep`` runs on ``loop.time()`` (monotonic),
so a single sleep would resume with its REMAINDER after the wake and delay the drain
re-dial by exactly that much, on every wake of every Fly agent.

On the wall clock the deadline is already past by the time we resume, so the fence costs
nothing after a freeze while still spanning the full gap before one. That decoupling is
what lets FLY_FREEZE_GRACE_S be sized for the slowest (largest-RAM) machine.

name: _scale_to_zero_abandon_suspend
doc:
Undo a quiesce we are not going to follow with a suspend.

All three together: a released supervisor still advertising `draining` reads as
mid-shutdown until the next real inbound event, and an abort that skips the cooldown
re-runs on every tick.

name: _scale_to_zero_hold_redial
doc:
Hold or release the relay's reconnect supervisor. Returns whether the transport actually
took it, so the caller can refuse to suspend without the protection rather than fail open.

name: _enter_external_drain
doc: Begin external drain: refuse NEW turns (in-flight ones are NOT interrupted). Idempotent.

name: _exit_external_drain
doc: Cancel external drain: re-accept new turns. Idempotent; never resurrects a stopping gateway.

name: _drain_control_watcher
doc: Poll ``.drain_request.json`` at 1s: present -> enter drain, absent -> exit; a stale epoch = absent.

name: _update_platform_runtime_status
arguments: self, platform: str, *, platform_state: Optional[str]=None, error_code: Optional[str]=None, error_message: Optional[str]=None, needs_attention: Optional[bool]=None, retrying_since: Any=_UNSET

name: _pause_failed_platform
doc: Pause a queued platform (manual ``/platform pause`` only — the watcher never auto-pauses).

name: _resume_paused_platform
doc: Unpause a platform (reset attempts, retry on the next watcher tick). True iff it was paused.

name: _drain_work_counts
doc: ``(agents, cron, api, deferred)`` the drain waits on; a managed-worker turn is a chat turn.

name: _mark_running_sessions_resume_pending
doc: Mark every non-pending running session resume_pending; returns the keys marked.

name: _restart_notification_allowed
doc: False when the platform config sets ``gateway_restart_notification=false``.

name: _notice_allowed
arguments: self, platform: Platform, what: str, platform_cfg=None
doc:
``_restart_notification_allowed`` with the INFO suppression line for shutdown notices.
``platform_cfg`` is a SERVED profile's own platform entry; ``self.config`` is the launch profile's.

name: _notify_interrupted_cron_jobs
doc:
Tell the owner of each just-interrupted cron job that its run died; returns notices sent.

The cron worker can't (its thread reaches ``_deliver_result`` after teardown closed the
transport), so this runs post-interrupt while adapters are still connected. Best-effort.

Its thread reaches ``_deliver_result`` asynchronously, and by then ``_bounded_adapter_teardown`` has
closed the transport — so the notice never leaves the process, and ``_consume_interrupted_flag``
discards the resulting ``delivery_error`` along with it. The run's only trace is a line in jobs.json
nobody reads (#82232).
Must therefore be called from the post-interrupt phase, while adapters are still connected — the
same window ``_notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown`` relies on for chat sessions, which is blind to
cron work because cron runs on the scheduler's own thread pool rather than ``self._running_agents``
(#60432).

significant_calls.expression:
self._send_notice_logged(
                            adapter, chat_id, msg, platform.value, "Cron interrupt notice to %s:%s failed: %s",
                            "Cron interrupt notice to %s:%s raised: %s", metadata=metadata,
                        )

name: _shutdown_notification_target
doc:
``(source, platform_str, chat_id, thread_id, profile)``: persisted origin > cached source >
parsed key. ``profile`` is the owning profile from the source or the ``agent:<profile>:`` key
namespace (``None`` = default) so the notice leaves through that profile's bot.

name: _send_shutdown_notice
arguments: self, adapter, chat_id: str, msg: str, kind: str, platform_str: str, **send_kwargs
doc: Send one shutdown notice; True when delivered. Failures are debug-logged, never raised.

name: _send_notice_logged
arguments: adapter, chat_id: str, msg: str, platform_str: str, fail_fmt: str, raise_fmt: Optional[str]=None, **kw
doc:
``adapter.send`` whose failure is debug-logged as ``fmt % (platform, chat, error)`` — ``fail_fmt``
for success=False, ``raise_fmt`` (default ``fail_fmt``) for a raise; True only on a delivered send.
Every shutdown notice races live turns, so it always carries the interim marker (#98432).

name: _notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown
doc:
Send shutdown/restart notifications to active chats and home channels.

Called at the start of stop() while adapters are connected; send failures never block shutdown.

name: _flush_agent_transcript_at_shutdown
doc:
Persist an in-flight transcript before teardown.

A force-interrupted agent may never reach finalize_turn (the only mid-turn flush), so its
tool rounds would vanish on resume. Idempotent; gracefully finished agents re-flush nothing.

name: _should_emit_long_running_notification
arguments: self, session_key: Optional[str], agent: Any, executor_task: Optional[Any]
doc:
Emit the heartbeat only while this task still owns the live run (not after ``/new`` rebinds).

Guards against a stale ``running: delegate_task`` heartbeat outliving the run that started it: stop
once the executor finishes, the agent is gone, or the session key has been rebound to a different
live agent (e.g. the user sent ``/new`` and a fresh agent took the slot mid-run, #12029).

name: _defer_agent_cleanup_until_future_done
arguments: self, future: asyncio.Future, agent: Any, *, context: str
doc: Clean up ``agent`` only after its executor future finishes (it may still use the agent's clients).

name: _cleanup_agent_resources_off_loop
arguments: self, agent: Any, *, context: str='', session_key: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Run _cleanup_agent_resources in a worker thread, bounded; on timeout the worker is left alone.

The teardown fires the memory-provider lifecycle hooks (``flush_pending`` → ``on_session_end`` →
``shutdown`` → ``close``), which read credentials/home at call time. In-turn callers carry the
profile scope through ``_run_housekeeping_in_executor``; shutdown does not (it runs on the main
loop, outside any adapter handler), so under multiplexing ``on_session_end`` failed closed and the
session tail was never committed (#110622). ``_run_release_in_profile_scope`` enters the OWNING
profile's scope from ``session_key`` when the caller has none, exactly like cache eviction.

name: _cleanup_agent_resources
doc: Best-effort cleanup for temporary or cached agent instances.

name: _read_json_counts
doc: Parsed counter dict, or None when the file is missing/unreadable (no exists() pre-check needed).

name: _increment_restart_failure_counts
doc: Increment persisted restart-failure counters for active sessions; drop the rest (loop broken).

name: _suspend_stuck_loop_sessions
doc: Suspend sessions active across too many restarts (startup, AFTER crash-turn recovery).

name: _clear_restart_failure_count
doc: Clear a completed session's restart-failure counter off-loop (atomic_json_write fsyncs).

name: _restart_watcher_env
doc:
Watcher env minus ``_HERMES_GATEWAY`` (else the CLI's self-restart guard refuses; gateway stays down).

The host multiplexer is respawned with ``host_gateway_child_env`` (default-root
secrets via ``served_profile_child_env``, not ``os.environ.copy()``). A standalone
named-profile gateway keeps that profile's home — only a multiplexer, or a process
already on the default root, is the host.

name: _spawn_windows_restart_watcher
arguments: hermes_cmd: list, current_pid: int, restart_after_s: float
doc: Spawn the detached Windows watcher (``python -c``), retrying once without job breakaway.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(  # noqa: ASYNC220 -- fire-and-forget spawn; Popen returns immediately and callers need the Popen object
            argv, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            env=GatewayShutdownMixin._restart_watcher_env(), start_new_session=True,
        )

name: _wedged_agent_count
doc:
Work units the restart wait may skip: chat agents idle past ``agent.gateway_timeout`` and
cron runs older than the scheduler's stale-inflight allowance (#115469).

API work has no activity clock and pending sentinels are brand-new, so neither counts.

name: _restart_wait_cron_counts
doc:
``cron.scheduler.get_restart_wait_cron_counts``, counted per profile-scoped run.

Fail-soft toward waiting: if the split can't be read, every active cron run stays
awaitable and nothing is excluded.

name: _wedged_cron_job_count
doc: Cron runs past ``cron.scheduler.get_wedged_job_ids``'s allowance; 0 if cron can't import.

name: _restart_safe_cron_count
doc:
Cron runs whose worker owns a restart-safe systemd scope; 0 if cron can't import.

Such a worker runs outside the gateway cgroup, so neither the tool-process sweep nor
``mark_running_jobs_interrupted`` reaches it, and its final send rides the durable delivery
queue for whichever gateway is live next. The restart after-turn wait must therefore not
hold the gateway in ``draining`` for it: waiting buys the run nothing and refuses new turns
for up to the whole cap (observed live: a 100-minute job held the gateway ~30 minutes).
Degraded (no user bus) workers are NOT in this set — they share the cgroup and die with a
systemd stop, so they keep holding the wait.

name: _wedged_chat_agent_count
doc:
Running chat agents with no activity for ``agent.gateway_timeout`` (0 when disabled);
an unreadable activity summary means "not wedged".

name: _awaitable_work_count
doc:
Active work minus the units the restart wait must not hold for.

Two disjoint exclusions: wedged turns (idle past ``agent.gateway_timeout`` / past the cron
in-flight allowance — restart is their remedy, #115469) and cron runs executing in a
restart-safe external worker (``_restart_safe_cron_count``), which outlives this process
either way. Cron runs are counted per profile-scoped run by the scheduler, not by
subtracting from the bare-ID active count: two profiles can run the same job ID, and one
excluded run must not hide the other.

name: _describe_active_work
doc:
One dict per in-flight work unit the restart wait is holding for, so an observer
(``hermes update``, ``hermes gateway status``) can name it instead of printing a bare count.

``kind`` ∈ ``chat`` (session turn), ``cron`` (job id + external worker pid when the run was
handed to a restart-safe scope), ``managed`` / ``api`` / ``deferred`` (count only — those sources expose
no identity). Best-effort: a source that can't be read is omitted, never raises.

name: _await_active_work_before_restart
doc:
Wait for in-flight work before ``stop()`` so the requesting turn isn't force-interrupted.

Wedged turns are excluded (restart is their remedy). True when drained to zero, False when the
cap elapsed or only wedged work remains (caller proceeds to ``stop()``).

name: _start_systemd_watchdog
doc: Start sd_notify only after a configured gateway is truly running.

name: _stop_systemd_watchdog
doc: Stop heartbeats before any potentially long shutdown drain.

name: _quiet_step
doc: Run one best-effort teardown step; a failure is debug-logged as ``"<label>: <exc>"``.

name: _stop_kill_tool_subprocesses
doc:
Kill tool subprocesses + terminal envs + browsers; returns cron job IDs marked interrupted.

Called twice: after a drain timeout (reclaim children before systemd SIGKILLs) and as a final
catch-all. Best-effort; one failing subsystem cannot block the rest.

name: _stop_kill_tool_subprocesses_off_loop
doc:
Run _stop_kill_tool_subprocesses in a worker thread; returns cron job IDs marked interrupted.

``kill_all`` fans out into per-target ``kill_process`` calls that do blocking work
(registry checkpoint disk I/O, ``subprocess.run`` for systemd scopes, sandbox exec),
so running the sweep inline would monopolize the gateway event loop (#116327).
Offloaded with ``asyncio.to_thread`` — the loop's default executor, deliberately NOT
the gateway-owned ``self._executor``, which ``_stop_quiesce_and_close_session_dbs``
drains right after this phase. Phase order is preserved: callers await this before
cron notices / adapter teardown. If the surrounding stop task is cancelled while the
worker runs, the thread is left to finish on its own; the thread-based shutdown
watchdog remains the hard backstop.

name: _stop_begin_teardown
doc: Flag teardown, stop room worker/watchdog, notify sessions.

name: _stop_drain_active_work
doc: Pre-mark resume_pending, drain agents/cron/API work into ``ctx``.

name: _stop_interrupt_remaining_work
doc: Drain timed out: mark resume_pending, interrupt, settle, kill tool subprocesses, notify cron.

name: _stop_finalize_agents_and_adapters
doc: Detached restart launch, agent finalization, idle-cache cleanup, adapter teardown.

name: _stop_release_runtime_state
doc: Cancel background tasks, flush pending messages, clear per-session state, final tool kill.

name: _stop_quiesce_and_close_session_dbs
doc: Quiesce the executor, then close SessionDB handles only if no worker is still live.

name: _stop_persist_exit_state
doc:
Clean-shutdown marker, restart markers, terminal runtime status; process bootstrap
releases PID/lock ownership after the writer drain.

name: _shutdown_watchdog_snapshot
doc: State dumped by the thread-based shutdown watchdog when teardown hangs.

name: _stop_impl
doc: Run every ``_stop_*`` phase under the thread-based shutdown watchdog.

name: stop
arguments: self, *, restart: bool=False, detached_restart: bool=False, service_restart: bool=False
doc: Stop the gateway and disconnect all adapters.

name: wait_for_shutdown
doc: Wait for shutdown signal.

arguments: label: str, fn: Callable[[], Any], busy_sentinel: Any

self._send_notice_logged(
                            adapter, chat_id, msg, platform.value, "Cron interrupt notice to %s:%s failed: %s",
                            "Cron interrupt notice to %s:%s raised: %s", metadata=metadata,
                        )

name: _deliver_session_end_messages
arguments: self, messages: list[str], *, source: Any=None, session_key: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Send plugin ``on_session_finalize`` text to the chat that owns the session — a plain adapter send,
never an agent turn. No resolvable chat (or no adapter) → logged and dropped.
