name: _reset_session_off_loop
doc:
Plugin ``on_session_reset`` off-loop under the profile owning ``session_key``, bounded like
finalize: a viewer's ``/new`` resets its conversation on the owner (gateway/session_viewer_close).

name: _finalize_session_off_loop
arguments: self, *, session_id: Any, platform: str, reason: str, session_key: Optional[str]=None, **extra: Any
doc:
Run hermes_cli.lifecycle.finalize_session off-loop, bounded; on timeout the worker is left alone.
``session_key`` lets an unscoped caller (shutdown) enter the owning profile's scope: plugin
``on_session_finalize`` observers and the Relay coordinator (``current_profile_key``) resolve
profile state at call time. Returns the plugins' user-facing messages (empty on timeout/error).

name: recover_left_core_in
doc:
Install the catalog plugin of every feature that left core (Home Assistant) *home* uses, in
*home*'s runtime scope (its config, secrets and allow_lazy_installs); once per process per home.
Blocking: call it off the event loop.

name: recover_left_core_at_gateway_start
doc:
Left-core migration for the homes whose platform config the runner loads first: the launch
home and the default root (the multiplex primary; a named launcher is then served as a
secondary). Every secondary runs :func:`recover_left_core_in` before its plugins are discovered,
so a platform plugin it gets starts its adapter in the same gateway start.

name: _own_policy_envs
doc:
``(dm_policy_env, group_policy_env, allow_all_env)`` for a platform that declares
``own_policy_env``, else None. The live entry wins; a bundled platform whose entry is absent
(plugin disabled, safe mode) or lacks the field (a user plugin overriding it) falls back to the
names its ``gateway_env.AUTHZ`` declares, so the startup refusal never weakens.

name: _log_agent_budget
doc:
Report the ENFORCED per-turn budget: ``agent.max_turns`` is bridged into
``HERMES_MAX_ITERATIONS`` before this runs, so the env slot already carries the config value;
resolve it the same way the turn loop does (``none``/``unlimited`` spellings included) instead of
``int()`` on the raw string with an invented ``500`` default (#116888).

name: _run_startup_resume_event
arguments: self, adapter: BasePlatformAdapter, event: MessageEvent, session_key: str
doc:
Dispatch one synthetic startup resume and wait for its agent turn (inbound stays queued
until it finishes, else a user message can race it).

name: _drain_startup_restore_queue
doc: Replay inbound messages queued while startup auto-resume ran.

name: _start_startup_warmup
doc:
Kick off the boot turn-machinery warm-up so it overlaps the network-bound platform
connects; ``_finish_startup_restore`` awaits it (bounded).

name: _run_boot_probe_in_launch_scope
doc:
Run a boot-time probe on the default executor under the LAUNCH profile's scope when
multiplexing (the ``_discover_gateway_mcp_tools`` shape). Boot probes (``check_fn``s) read profile-scoped secrets; an unscoped read under multiplex fails
closed, so routing overrides resolve as absent and default routing applies. ``copy_context``
carries the contextvars across the executor hop; single-profile keeps environ semantics.

name: _warm_turn_prerequisites
doc:
Initialize turn machinery on an executor thread before the gate opens. Never raises: a
failed warm-up degrades to lazy init and must not block startup.

name: _await_startup_warmup
doc:
Bounded wait for the boot warm-up. On timeout the gate opens anyway (availability outranks
prompt completeness for a WEDGED init); the warm-up continues and a late failure is logged.

name: _wait_bounded_or_release
arguments: self, tasks: set, timeout: float, warn_fmt: str, late_msg: str, *, level: int=logging.WARNING, track: bool=False
doc:
``asyncio.wait`` (which, unlike wait_for/gather+timeout, does NOT cancel on timeout) with
the gate-release warning + late-failure callback every boot gate uses. Returns ``done``.
``warn_fmt`` takes ``%.0fs`` (timeout) and optionally ``%d`` (pending count). A non-positive
``timeout`` opts out of the bound ("wait forever").

name: _finish_startup_restore
doc:
Wait (BOUNDED by ``_startup_restore_drain_timeout_secs``) for startup auto-resume, then
release + drain inbound. On timeout the gate opens and resume turns finish in the background
(NOT cancelled) — safe because ``_schedule_resume_pending_sessions`` claims each
``_running_agents`` slot SYNCHRONOUSLY first, so drained inbound queues behind.

name: _late_failure_callback
doc:
Done-callback for boot-path tasks that outlive the startup-restore gate: surface a late
failure otherwise swallowed once the task leaves ``_background_tasks``. Cancellation is
expected (shutdown), not an error.

name: _await_startup_boot_sends
doc:
Run boot-path sends without letting them pin the inbound restore gate (one Telegram
flood-control sleep must not freeze inbound on every platform): same bounded wait as the
resume gate, sends finish in the background on timeout. The ledger claim + ``resume_pending``
clear run INLINE before the send task exists — deferring it let a hung notification expire the
gate with zero rows claimed, so answered turns were replayed AND redelivered.

``_send_restart_notification`` and ``_redeliver_pending_obligations`` used to be awaited inline
*before* ``_finish_startup_restore`` released the gate. See #91969.

name: _clear_resume_pending_for_claimed_obligations
_claim_pending_obligations
doc:
Claim recoverable delivery-ledger rows and clear their ``resume_pending`` flags (pure DB
work, no sends). Must run INLINE BEFORE ``_schedule_resume_pending_sessions`` and the
abandonable boot-send task: these sessions already produced their answer, so the resume path
must not re-run (re-pay for) the turn however long the sends take. Mid-send / rejected rows
carry a visible recovered-reply marker (gateway/delivery_ledger.py). Returns the rows.

A session with a recoverable obligation already produced its answer — the turn completed and only
delivery is owed — so clearing ``resume_pending`` here prevents the resume path from re-running (and
re-paying for) a turn whose output we hold, regardless of how long the sends ahead of redelivery
take (#91969). Flood-refused rows adopted inside their wait come back flagged ``adopted``: their
flags are cleared here too, and ``_redeliver_claimed_obligations`` leaves them to the timer.

name: _release_runtime_claim_quiet
doc:
Release an unsent runtime delivery-ledger claim; log-only on failure. ``error`` is what the row
goes back to ``failed`` with: the claim's own pre-claim error when the caller knows it, so a
flood-refused row keeps its ``flood_control:<seconds>`` and stays on the flood timer's list (the
release re-stamps ``updated_at``, so it waits the platform's figure once more); else
``send_path_degraded``.

name: _schedule_flood_redelivery
doc: Wake one deadline-driven ledger worker per bot identity, never sleep in a send.

name: _arm_flood_timers_for_waiting_rows
doc: Recover adopted, newly refused/rejected and unsent released rows without blocking the loop.

name: _redeliver_claimed_obligations
doc:
Redeliver final responses for claimed rows (network half of the split): runs inside the
bounded boot-send task, so a flood-limited send can be abandoned by the restore gate without
reopening the turn-replay window. Returns the redelivered count.

name: _obligation_adapter
doc: Resolve the adapter for a claimed ledger row, or None when it cannot be delivered now.

name: _redeliver_pending_obligations
doc:
Claim + redeliver in one call. Stable shape for tests/external callers; the startup path
calls the halves separately so the DB half runs inline before the abandonable send task.

name: _redeliver_failed_obligations_for_platform
doc:
Replay one adapter identity's transient failures after reconnect: the startup sweep cannot
claim live-owner rows, so ``send_path_degraded`` responses would otherwise stay failed until
the next restart. Best-effort; reuses the startup redelivery contract.

name: _resume_pending_candidates
doc:
Snapshot resume-pending entries (optionally scoped to ``platform``); None when
enumeration failed or the restart-loop breaker tripped for this boot.

name: _resume_owner_authorized
doc:
Validate the session owner against the CURRENT allowlist: a session created before the
allowlist existed (or whose owner was since removed) must not silently receive a full agent
response just because it carries a resume marker.

name: _schedule_resume_pending_sessions
doc:
Auto-continue fresh restart-interrupted sessions: synthesize an empty-text turn (the
``_is_resume_pending`` injection path owns the wording). Sessions whose adapter is offline stay
``resume_pending`` for the reconnect watcher, which re-calls this scoped to that ``platform``;
sessions with a running agent are skipped so none is resumed twice.

name: _startup_teardown_adapter
doc: Cancel an adapter's background tasks (best-effort) then disconnect it.

name: _startup_retry_entry
arguments: self, platform, adapter, platform_config, *, queued: bool=True
doc: ``_failed_platforms`` entry for a platform that failed at startup (first retry in 30s).

name: _abort_startup_if_shutdown_requested
doc: Clean up and exit startup when restart/shutdown begins mid-startup.

name: _start_loop_liveness_guards
doc:
Arm the selector floor and out-of-loop watchdog before adapters. Disabled entirely with
``gateway.loop_watchdog: false`` in config.yaml (config-only knob).

See #69089.

name: _stop_loop_liveness_guards
doc:
Disarm lifetime liveness guards before shutdown can load the loop — including the
heartbeat writer, which would otherwise make a draining gateway look healthy to probes.

name: _consume_clean_shutdown_marker
doc:
Discard orphan turn markers before consuming a clean-exit receipt. Raises (fail closed):
continuing with the old receipt would let a later unclean exit masquerade as clean.

name: _recover_unclean_sessions
doc:
Recover only the turns the dead process left marked: one whose reply is already in the
transcript is owed delivery, not a new answer; any other resumes once. An unmarked session
finished its turn (the marker is held until the reply is ledgered), so nothing re-runs it —
the old 120 s recency sweep re-answered every recently active chat. Returns (resumed,
ledgered).

name: _ledger_crash_left_replies
doc:
Settle every marked turn whose final reply was persisted and clear its marker, so
auto-resume does not regenerate it: a reply live delivery would have suppressed is owed
nothing, any other goes to the delivery ledger for the boot sweep. Without the ledger a
presentable reply stays marked and resumes.

name: _crash_left_reply
arguments: self, history: list, started: float, origin
doc:
What a crash-left turn owes, judged as live delivery would have: ``None`` when it never
persisted a final reply after *started*; ``""`` when nothing would have been presented (a
silence marker on a machinery turn or on a turn the adapter reported as not addressed to the
bot, a muted diagnostic wake); else the text to send, with any other bare silence marker
replaced by the same notice the live path sends.

name: _start_hosted_room_worker_sync
doc: Start the local Group Chat worker without importing the dashboard.

name: _hosted_room_worker_watcher
doc: Keep the room worker alive for the messaging gateway lifetime.

name: _stop_hosted_room_worker
doc: Pause room execution durably without interrupting accepted turns.

name: _start_loop_heartbeat_task
doc:
Start the loop-liveness heartbeat task (idempotent, best-effort). An asyncio task so a
frozen loop stops refreshing ``state/gateway.heartbeat``; cancelled with the others in stop().

See #66892.

name: _open_faulthandler_log
doc: Open (append) ``<log_dir>/gateway_faulthandler.log``, creating the directory.

name: _start_install_faulthandler
doc: Enable faulthandler (stderr or a log file) plus the SIGUSR2 stack-dump hook.

name: _start_log_startup_environment
doc: Bind the gateway loop, disarm the startup watchdog, and log the startup environment.

name: _start_log_retired_session_reset
doc:
Warn per served profile whose config still declares an idle/daily ``session_reset``,
unless the plugin that honours it is enabled. Never raises.

name: _start_log_systemd_timing_alignment
doc:
Warn when systemd's TimeoutStopSec does not cover the drain window (a unit file from before
an upgrade may encode the old default, so SIGKILL hits mid-drain). Never raises.

name: _start_check_access_policy
doc: Warn about missing allowlists; return True when startup must be refused.

name: _start_register_plugins_relay_hooks
doc: Plugin discovery, relay registration and shell-hook/webhook registration. Never raises.

name: _register_launch_profile_config_hooks
doc:
The launch profile's ``hooks:`` block, registered under ITS runtime scope when multiplexing.

Startup runs before any turn scope exists and ``get_secret`` fails closed outside a scope
while multiplexing is on, so the launch profile needs the scope secondaries already get
(``_start_secondary_profile_adapters``) or its ``secret_env`` targets cannot resolve.

name: _register_config_hooks
doc:
Register declarative shell hooks + outbound webhooks from the CURRENT scope's config.

The gateway never prompts (register_from_config defaults to ``interactive=False``), even
when a hidden console makes stdin look like a TTY, so consent must come from the allowlist,
--accept-hooks, HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS, or hooks_auto_accept: true; ``accept_hooks=False`` lets
register_from_config resolve env + config.
Never raises (logged at ``level``).

name: _recover_secondary_process_checkpoints
doc:
Replay every SERVED secondary profile's ``processes.json`` under its own scope.
The launch profile's file was already read by ``recover_from_checkpoint`` above.

name: _start_recover_previous_run
doc: Plugins, relay, hooks, then crash/clean-exit recovery of processes and sessions.

name: _start_prefilter_platforms
doc:
Create + wire an adapter per enabled platform (no connects). Returns
(aborted, enabled_platform_count, multiplex_skipped_platforms, pending_connects).

name: _start_connect_pending
doc:
Connect the pre-filtered adapters concurrently. Returns the raw per-platform results, or
None when a restart/shutdown aborted startup mid-connect (adapters already torn down).

name: _startup_queue_transient_failure
arguments: self, platform, adapter, platform_config, message: str, startup_retryable_errors: list
doc: Mark a platform ``retrying`` with ``message`` and queue it in ``_failed_platforms``.

name: _start_aggregate_connect_results
arguments: self, _raw: list, startup_retryable_errors: list, startup_nonretryable_errors: list
doc:
Apply connect outcomes to shared state single-threaded (exactly as the original serial
loop did); returns the connected adapter count.

name: _startup_fail_fatal_config
doc: Record a fatal-config startup failure (exit 78) and request a clean exit.

name: _start_secondary_profiles
doc: Bring up multiplexed secondary-profile adapters. Returns (aborted, connected_count).

name: _start_handle_no_connections
arguments: self, connected_count: int, enabled_platform_count: int, startup_retryable_errors: list, startup_nonretryable_errors: list
doc:
Log/degrade when a configured platform failed to start; return True when startup must exit.

The SHARED gate for every platform, not the api_server path: a configured platform that never
came up must leave a loud, observable trace (ERROR + a ``degraded`` runtime state) even while
sibling platforms serve normally. One WARNING next to "Gateway running with N platform(s)" let
a gateway with no API server at all look healthy for half an hour (api_server lost the bind
race against the gateway it was replacing, and nothing retried).

name: _start_post_connect_services
doc: Room worker, heartbeat, gateway:startup hook, channel directory, /update notice.

name: _start_finish_wiring
doc: Post-connect wiring: services, boot notifications, startup restore, recovered watchers.

name: _start_spawn_background_watchers
doc: Spawn the long-lived supervised background watchers.

name: _start_flush_runtime_status
doc: Bound startup on the latest diagnostic snapshot, never on filesystem health.

name: start
doc: Start the gateway and all configured platform adapters.

name: _handoff_resolve_scope
doc:
Return (config, adapters) for the profile that queued the handoff. For a secondary
profile the watcher already entered _profile_runtime_scope, so a fresh load resolves THAT
profile's config; fail closed — self.config would deliver to the WRONG chat.

name: _handoff_resolve_destination
arguments: self, row: dict[str, Any], profile_name: Optional[str]
doc: Resolve platform, transport, home channel, thread and destination source for a row.

name: _handoff_home_is_dm
doc:
Whether the home chat is a DM by the adapter's own ``get_chat_info`` (``type: "dm"``);
unknown/failed → not a DM, the common handoff target.

name: _handoff_session_key
doc:
Destination session_key by the adapters' own rules. Thread keys omit user_id so the next
message shares it. Namespaced to the queuing profile (else a multiplexed gateway builds
``agent:main:...`` while the profile's adapter routes on ``agent:<profile>:...``); the store
resolver is only the root fallback. The isinstance check is load-bearing: a Mock store returns
a truthy MagicMock.

name: _process_handoff
arguments: self, row: dict[str, Any], profile_name: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Execute one handoff row; raises on failure (caller marks failed). ``profile_name`` (None =
root) is the profile whose store queued it — load-bearing under multiplex: secondaries live in
``_profile_adapters`` and the key must be namespaced ``agent:<profile>:...`` or nobody reads it.

name: _connect_one_startup
doc: Connect a single platform; never let one block the others (#83791).

name: _telegram_topic_profile_name
doc:
Profile namespace for topic-mode rows: the profile stamped on the routed event, never the
process-global one (under multiplex that mis-attributes state across bots sharing state.db).

See #76423.

name: _sync_session_db
doc: The sync SessionDB handle, or None. Only for callers that provably run off-loop.

name: _telegram_topic_mode_enabled
doc: Return whether Telegram DM topic mode is active for this chat.

name: _is_telegram_topic_root_lobby
doc: True for the main Telegram DM (or General topic) when topic mode has made it a lobby.

name: _is_telegram_topic_lane
doc: True for a user-created Telegram private-chat topic lane.

name: _telegram_topic_cooldown_key
doc:
Cooldown key (profile, chat_id): profiles sharing a Telegram private chat_id under
multiplex must not suppress each other's lobby reminders / capability hints.

See #76423.

name: _telegram_cooldown_elapsed
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, attr: str, cooldown_s: float
doc: Per-(profile, chat) debounce: True (and stamp now) when the window has elapsed.

name: _should_send_telegram_lobby_reminder
doc: Rate-limit root-DM lobby reminders to one per cooldown window, not one per prompt typed.

name: _should_send_telegram_capability_hint
doc: Rate-limit the BotFather Threads Settings screenshot (repeated /topic must not re-upload it).

name: _record_telegram_topic_binding
doc: Persist the Telegram topic -> Hermes session binding for topic lanes (off-loop).

name: _sync_telegram_topic_binding
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, session_entry, *, reason: str
doc:
Update the topic binding to ``session_entry.session_id``: a stale binding after a mid-turn
compression rotation reloads the oversized parent next message, retriggering compression.

Telegram topic lanes persist a (chat_id, thread_id) -> session_id row so reopening a topic in a
fresh process resumes the right Hermes session. See #20470, #29712, #33414.

name: _recover_telegram_topic_thread_id
doc:
Adapter-ingress recovery hook (sync, called off-loop before session keying): lobby recovery,
except when ``dm_topic_auto_transfer`` is on — then the root-DM source is left alone so
``_transfer_telegram_root_dm`` can open a fresh topic (and fall back to this recovery itself).

name: _recover_telegram_lobby_thread_id
doc:
Pin lobby-shaped topic-mode DM replies (missing ``message_thread_id`` or General) to the
user's most-recent bound topic. Never rewrite a non-lobby, unbound thread id: a brand-new DM
topic is also "unknown" until its first message is recorded. None = leave the source alone.

name: _telegram_dm_topic_auto_transfer_configured
doc:
The RECEIVING bot's ``extra.dm_topic_auto_transfer`` (default False): under multiplexing each
bot owns its opt-in. Off keeps the v0.22 lobby recovery (#136567). No state.db read.

name: _telegram_topic_auto_transfer_enabled
doc: The key is on and ``source`` is a ``/topic``-mode root DM (reads state.db: call off-loop).

name: _transfer_telegram_root_dm
doc:
Adapter-ingress transfer hook for an opted-in root-DM message (#139136).

``(thread_id, True)``: a fresh topic was created and the turn runs there. ``(thread_id, False)``:
creating it failed, so the message falls back to lobby recovery (the last bound topic).
``None``: not applicable (key off, not a topic-mode root DM) or nothing to recover to.

name: _get_telegram_topic_capabilities
doc: Read Telegram private-topic capability flags via Bot API getMe.

name: _ensure_telegram_system_topic
doc: Create/pin the managed System topic after /topic activation when possible.

name: _send_telegram_topic_setup_image
doc: Send the bundled BotFather Threads Settings screenshot when available.

significant_calls.expression:
adapter.send_image_file(
                chat_id=source.chat_id, image_path=str(image_path), caption=t("gateway.topic.setup_image_caption"),
                metadata={"thread_id": str(source.thread_id)} if source.thread_id else None,
            )

name: _sanitize_telegram_topic_title
doc: Bot API-safe forum topic name: names are 1-128 chars; keep room for multi-byte titles.

name: _sanitize_discord_thread_title
doc:
Discord-safe thread title: the 100-char cap is measured in UTF-16 code units (emoji count
double), so truncate with the UTF-16 helpers rather than Python code-point slices.

name: _is_discord_auto_thread_lane
doc: Return True only for Discord threads Hermes just auto-created.

name: _recover_discord_auto_thread_source
doc:
*source* with the auto-thread markers of the session's opening event, when that event
created this same native Discord thread.

Native Discord stamps the markers only on the opening event, so a later title retry on a
rebuilt agent arrives unmarked. The routing entry's ``origin`` is that opening source and
survives restarts. ``replace_source`` keeps the live transport owner and message id.

name: _is_relay_discord_channel_lane
doc:
Shape-only check: a relay-delivered Discord CHANNEL event whose reply the connector MAY
auto-thread (title-turn registration gate). Deliberately does NOT consult the send-result
cache — before delivery the feedback can't exist; the rename lane polls it at fire time.

name: _relay_auto_thread_info
doc:
(thread_id, initial_name) when the RELAY connector auto-threaded our reply — the title-turn
sibling of _is_discord_auto_thread_lane (whose markers only exist from turn 2 on; the title
turn's source is the PARENT channel event).

Preferred: the connector's per-message ``prospective_thread_id`` stamp (anchor message id ==
the thread it will create), exact even when several auto-threads spawn from one channel;
the connector's created-name guard enforces no-clobber. Fallback: the per-chat send-result
cache (older connectors), which only ever renamed the FIRST thread.

name: _await_relay_auto_thread_info
doc:
``_relay_auto_thread_info``, waited out until this turn delivers (the legacy send-result
path can only answer once the reply is sent; the caller asks at title time, one turn early).
The timeout is only a backstop for a turn that never sends: the turn's own inactivity limit.

name: _rename_discord_auto_thread_for_session_title
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, session_id: str, title: str, relay_info: Optional[tuple[str, str]]=None
doc:
Best-effort semantic rename of a newly auto-created Discord thread. ``relay_info`` is the
connector's (thread_id, initial_name) feedback, supplied on the title turn where the source
is the parent-channel event without auto-thread markers (see _relay_auto_thread_info).

name: _schedule_rename_from_title_thread
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, make_coro, label: str
doc:
Schedule a best-effort rename coroutine onto the gateway loop from the auto-title thread.
The source is copied so the thread never shares the live dataclass with the loop; failures
are logged at debug and never propagate.

name: _schedule_discord_semantic_thread_rename
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, session_id: str, title: str
doc: Schedule Discord auto-thread rename from the auto-title background thread.

name: _schedule_telegram_topic_title_rename
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, session_id: str, title: str
doc: Schedule a topic rename from the auto-title background thread.

name: _telegram_topic_auto_rename_disabled
doc: ``gateway.platforms.telegram.extra.disable_topic_auto_rename``; default False (auto-rename on).

name: _rename_telegram_topic_for_session_title
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, session_id: str, title: str
doc: Best-effort rename of a Telegram DM topic when Hermes auto-titles a session.

name: _disable_telegram_topic_mode_for_chat
doc: Cleanly disable topic mode for a chat via /topic off.

name: _restore_telegram_topic_session
doc: Restore an existing Telegram-owned Hermes session into this topic.

name: _tool_call_logger
doc:
Process-wide ``hermes.tool_calls`` Logger + one RotatingFileHandler on logs/tool_calls.log.
Named Loggers live in ``logging.Logger.manager.loggerDict`` forever, so the former per-turn name
(``hermes.tool_calls.<id(log_queue)>``) leaked one Logger per logged turn (#62950); a single
shared handler also keeps concurrent turns from double-writing lines.

name: _unexpected_silence_reply
doc: Reply when the model returned only a silence marker for a message that needed an answer.

name: _bg_prompt_preview
doc: Short single-line quote of a /bg prompt for its failure notice (the task id means nothing to the user).

name: is_context_overflow_failure_result
doc:
One verdict for "this failed turn is a context overflow", shared by transcript persistence
(#1630 skip) and the user-facing reply so the two can never disagree.

Multi-word phrases (not bare "exceed"/"token") avoid matching "rate limit exceeded" or
"invalid authentication token"; a bare 400 only counts on a long session.

name: bound_model_input_without_hygiene
doc:
Fail-closed in-context bound for a turn where hygiene has not landed (#111988).

Keeps the leading ``system``/``session_meta`` setup rows plus the newest tail, total <= ``limit``.
Deterministic (the same transcript always yields the same cut) and payload-only: the stored
transcript is never touched, so the agent's durable-prefix slice (``history_offset``) is
unaffected. Returns ``history`` unchanged — same object — when nothing needs dropping, so the
landed-compression and below-the-limit paths stay byte-identical.

name: hygiene_no_commit_reason
doc:
Name WHY a hygiene compression left the session id unchanged with no in-place commit.
The terminal ``else`` used to blame "no session_db on the hygiene agent" for every route into it,
but that is one of several causes (#71097): an attempt that ABORTED before any commit boundary
(lock skip, transient cooldown, summary timeout, codex thread interrupted) leaves
``_last_compression_attempt_in_place`` at ``None``; a DB-less agent is only the case when
``_session_db`` really is missing. Read the per-attempt signals the compressor sets, in that order.

name: _event_thread_metadata
doc: Thread metadata for a send that replies to ``event`` on ``source``.

name: _pop_post_delivery_callback
doc: Pop the adapter's deferred post-delivery callback for ``key`` (legacy dict fallback).

name: _hmwa_stop_typing_for_turn
doc:
Stop the typing indicator (never raises). Slack AI status is scoped to a thread/
workspace, so preserve the routing metadata used by the response delivery path.

name: _handle_message_with_agent
arguments: self, event, source, _quick_key: str, run_generation: int
doc: Inner handler that runs under the _running_agents sentinel guard.

name: _profile_scope_for_source
doc:
``_profile_runtime_scope`` for ``source``'s profile when a secret scope is required.

Under multiplexing config/skills/memory resolve to the source profile's home AND credentials
come from its secret scope (never process-global ``os.environ``). A standalone gateway
(``multiplex_profiles`` off) still binds once a hosted room has flipped the process-wide
credential guard — see ``_standalone_launch_scope``.

name: _profile_scope_key_for_source
doc:
Profile home ``_profile_scope_for_source`` binds for ``source``, or ``None`` when it falls
back to the standalone launch scope. The single owner of that branch condition: callers that
group work per scope (heartbeat restore) key on this so they cannot drift from the scope
actually entered.

name: _async_profile_scope_for_source
doc:
``async with`` twin of :meth:`_profile_scope_for_source` (secret hydration off-loop).

Slash dispatch runs under the RECEIVING bot's scope (auth needs its ``.env``), which is not
the routed runtime when a bot serves another profile's chat; every handler reading
home-relative state (pending writes, memory store, config) binds the runtime here (#119915).

name: _standalone_launch_scope
doc:
Scope for a standalone gateway's own (launch-profile) work: a no-op until the process hosts
another profile home, then the launch profile's OWN runtime scope.

A native hosted room running a second profile calls
``tui_gateway.launch_profile_policy.activate_multi_profile_hosting`` inside the gateway process,
so ``get_secret`` fails closed for every unscoped read afterwards — including the standalone
gateway's ordinary turns, which never bound a scope because ``multiplex_profiles`` is off
(#112878). The launch profile is a profile too: bind its ``.env`` over the env frozen at
activation (a key injected by systemd / ``op run`` has no file to rebuild it from), never a
secondary's scope and never live ``os.environ``.

name: _media_delivery_scope_for_source
doc:
Home + terminal-policy scope for validating a turn's MEDIA / local-file paths on the
adapter's delivery side, which runs after the routed turn scope was reset.

Docker path translation (``platforms/base.py::_translate_docker_container_media_path``)
infers the producing container from the ACTIVE profile (``get_active_profile_name``) and the
scope-aware ``TERMINAL_DOCKER_VOLUMES``; without this a secondary's ``MEDIA:/output/x.png``
resolves against the default profile's sandbox and mounts (#109024). No secret hydration:
path validation reads no credentials and this runs on the event loop.

name: _reset_notice_session_info
doc:
Session-info block for the auto-reset notice, resolved inside the profile serving ``source``.

Call via ``asyncio.to_thread``: resolution can block (credential refresh, context-length
probes), and the scope is entered here so contextvars behave in the worker thread.

name: _format_session_info
doc: Model / provider / context-length / endpoint block so users can spot bad context detection.

doc: Profile-scoping wrapper around the background agent task (mirrors ``_run_agent``).

name: _resolve_enabled_toolsets_for_source
arguments: self, user_config: dict, source: SessionSource, platform_key: str
doc:
Enabled toolsets for an agent run, honoring an adapter ``toolsets_for_source()`` override
validated through the SAME ``_get_platform_tools`` path (unknown / platform-restricted
toolsets dropped, not trusted).

name: _resolve_turn_toolsets
arguments: self, user_config: dict, source: SessionSource, platform_key: str
doc: ``(enabled_toolsets, disabled_toolsets)`` for an agent run on ``source``.

name: _run_background_task_inner
arguments: self, prompt: str, source: SessionSource, task_id: str, event_message_id: Optional[str]=None, media_urls: Optional[list[str]]=None, media_types: Optional[list[str]]=None
doc: Execute a background agent task and deliver the result to the chat.

adapter.emit_warning(
                    source.chat_id,
                    t("gateway.background.failed", preview=_bg_prompt_preview(prompt)),
                    metadata=_thread_metadata, logical_platform=source.platform,
                )

name: _mcp_reload_refresh_cached_agents
doc:
Refresh cached agents so existing sessions see new MCP tools on their next turn without
a history-destroying ``/new``. Each agent keeps its build-time toolset selection EXACTLY: a
session built with restricted enabled_toolsets (e.g. ["safe"]) must NOT silently gain tools.

name: _execute_mcp_reload
doc:
Disconnect, reconnect, and notify MCP tool changes (shared by button / text / no-confirm paths).

Under multiplex the reload runs inside the requesting profile's runtime scope (entered here
when the caller did not) and only that profile's servers are torn down and rediscovered.

See #95518.

name: _get_proxy_url
doc:
Proxy URL if proxy mode is configured (GATEWAY_PROXY_URL env wins over ``gateway.proxy_url``).
Per-profile like GATEWAY_PROXY_KEY: under multiplex a raw environ read would ship a secondary's
turns (authenticated with ITS scoped key) to the default profile's proxy. Same fallback shape as
the key — only ``UnscopedSecretError`` (the unscoped default-profile path) reads the env.

name: _build_stream_consumer_config
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, scfg: Any, adapter: Any, *, on_missing_cursor: str

name: _run_still_current_fn
doc: Predicate: does this run's generation still own ``session_key``? (always True when untracked).

name: _proxy_stream_consumer
doc: Platform stream consumer for the proxy path when streaming is enabled, else ``None``.

name: _run_agent_via_proxy
arguments: self, message: str, context_prompt: str, history: list[dict[str, Any]], source: SessionSource, session_id: str, session_key: str | None=None, run_generation: Optional[int]=None, event_message_id: Optional[str]=None, scheduled_heartbeat: bool=False
doc:
Forward the message to a remote Hermes API server instead of running a local AIAgent.

Lets a Docker container handle Matrix E2EE while the agent runs on the host with full
access to local files, memory, skills, and a unified session store.

Profile-scoping wrapper around ``_run_agent_inner`` (same keyword parameters; pass-through
when multiplexing is off).

name: _run_agent_display_settings
doc: Resolve per-platform display, progress, status and streaming-surface settings for a turn.

name: _run_agent_build_turn_context
arguments: self, disp: GatewayRunner._RunAgentDisplay, AIAgent: Any, *, message: str, source: SessionSource, session_key: Optional[str], run_generation: Optional[int], **turn_params
doc:
Build the ``TurnContext`` and its ``TurnRunner``; ``turn_params`` (history, context_prompt,
session_id, persist_user_*, …) are stored verbatim. Returns ``(turn_ctx, turn_runner,
cleanup_adapter)``.

name: _thread_metadata_for_progress
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, event_message_id: Optional[str], _progress_thread_id: Any, _relay_prospective_thread_id: Optional[str]
doc:
Thread metadata for a progress-lane send; relay Discord auto-thread lane falls back to the reply anchor.

The connector will auto-thread on the reply anchor (thread is born on its FIRST send), so
carrying it routes progress / status bubbles into the same thread as the final reply.

name: _run_agent_progress_threading
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, event_message_id: Optional[str], _native_slack_task_cards: bool
doc:
Resolve where progress bubbles are threaded (platform-specific).

Returns ``(progress_metadata, progress_reply_to, status_thread_metadata)``; the latter is
for status / approval / stream sends (Feishu topics need the triggering message id via the
reply API, so carry it as a fallback). Slack and Buzz honour the user's reply_in_thread
opt-out: never synthesise a thread for progress, or every later reply inherits it.

name: _run_agent_write_tool_log
doc:
Drain log_queue and append tool-call lines to tool_calls.log (tool_progress=log).

RotatingFileHandler (5MB × 3) bounds the log; RedactingFormatter keeps secrets off disk.

name: _run_agent_start_streaming_tts
arguments: self, source: SessionSource, message_type: Optional[str], _status_thread_metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]], streaming_tts_consumer_holder: list
doc:
Start the streaming-TTS consumer for a voice-input turn on an auto-TTS chat.

Created on the gateway loop thread (not run_sync's executor); an inactive consumer leaves
the holder None so the whole-file fallback path runs.

name: _run_agent_stream_consumer_task
doc: Wait (up to 10s) for the stream consumer to be created inside run_sync, then run it.

name: _await_stream_task
doc: Give the stream consumer task 5s to flush, then cancel it.

name: _run_agent_track_agent
doc:
Track this agent as running for the session (interrupt support) once it is created — only
if this run is still current, else leave the newer run's slot alone.

name: _run_agent_fire_pending_interrupt
arguments: self, adapter: Any, agent: Any, source: SessionSource, session_key: str, _interrupt_detected: asyncio.Event, streaming_tts_consumer_holder: list, *, log_context: str, log: Callable[[], None]
doc:
Peek the adapter's pending event, transcribe voice, then signal the agent + abort streaming TTS.

Peek WITHOUT consuming: the event must stay for the post-run ``_dequeue_pending_event()``
(popping races the agent finishing). Transcribe BEFORE signaling so voice interrupts carry
the real transcript.

name: _run_agent_monitor_for_interrupt
doc:
Poll the adapter for interrupts (new messages) every 200ms and signal the agent.

Level 1 (base.py) catches regular text before _handle_message(); the inactivity poll loop
has a BACKUP check in case this task dies. Keyed by session_key, NOT source.chat_id.

name: _run_agent_backup_interrupt_check
arguments: self, turn_ctx: TurnContext, _interrupt_detected: asyncio.Event, interrupt_monitor: asyncio.Task
doc: Backup interrupt check: if the monitor task died or missed the interrupt, catch it here.

name: _run_agent_stream_confirmed_final_delivery
doc:
True only when the actual final reply reached the user: a finalize call may carry only the
last preview snapshot, so reconcile against the recorded payload — a demonstrable mismatch
(False) overrides the flag; None keeps legacy trust.

name: _run_agent_start_turn_worker
arguments: self, turn_ctx: TurnContext, run_sync: Callable[[], Any]
doc:
Schedule ``run_sync`` on the executor plus the inactivity watchdog thread.

*Inactivity* timeout (agent.gateway_timeout / HERMES_AGENT_TIMEOUT, env wins; 0 = unlimited),
not wall-clock. The daemon watchdog is independent of asyncio: cgroup memory reclaim can
starve the loop that runs the normal timeout poll.

name: _reaper_kwargs
doc: Shared kwargs of the watchdog + timeout-reaper threads.

name: _agent_activity_summary
doc: ``agent.get_activity_summary()`` or ``{}`` when unavailable / failing.

name: _run_agent_inactivity_warning
doc: Staged one-shot warning before the inactivity timeout escalates.

_warn_adapter.emit_warning(
                source.chat_id, t(
                    "gateway.progress.stuck_warning",
                    minutes=int(worker.agent_warning // 60) or 1,
                    remaining=int((worker.agent_timeout - worker.agent_warning) // 60) or 1),

doc:
Synthetic failed run dict for an inactivity timeout, with the activity-tracker diagnostic;
interrupts the agent if it is still running so the thread pool worker is freed.

name: _run_agent_await_turn_worker
arguments: self, worker: GatewayRunner._RunAgentWorker, turn_ctx: TurnContext, _interrupt_detected: asyncio.Event, interrupt_monitor: asyncio.Task
doc:
Poll the executor future (inactivity timeout + backup interrupt checks); return its result,
or a synthetic failed run dict on inactivity timeout. Polls even with an unlimited timeout
so the backup interrupt check runs if monitor_for_interrupt() silently died.

name: _run_agent_evict_on_fallback
doc:
Evict the cached agent when a fallback model activated on a SUCCESSFUL run (so /model shows
the active model and the next message retries the primary). Skip failed runs: evicting
would loop bad model → fallback → evict → recreate.

name: _run_agent_finalize_streaming_tts
doc:
Finalize the streaming-TTS consumer on the outer event-loop thread (covers early returns
from run_sync). On drain timeout abort to free the task — audible streams keep whole-file
suppression, silent streams stay eligible for the whole-file fallback.

name: _run_agent_drain_pending
arguments: self, result: Any, adapter: Any, source: SessionSource, session_key: Optional[str]
doc:
Dequeue the adapter's pending / interrupt / leftover-steer follow-up as ``(pending_event, pending)``.

Keyed by session_key (not source.chat_id) to match the adapter's storage keys.

name: _run_agent_deliver_first_response
arguments: self, turn_ctx: TurnContext, adapter: Any, response: Any, result: Any, stream_task: Any
doc: Deliver the first response before a queued follow-up runs, unless streaming already did.

doc: Run the queued / interrupting follow-up as the next turn (recursive ``_run_agent``).

arguments: self, turn_ctx: TurnContext, *, progress_task: Any, log_task: Any, interrupt_monitor: asyncio.Task, _notify_task: asyncio.Task, tracking_task: asyncio.Task, stream_task: Any
doc: ``finally`` half of a turn: cancel background tasks, flush stream, release the session slot.

name: _run_agent_edit_streamed_message
arguments: self, _sc, source, response, content, *, _sk, ok, fail_result: str, fail_exc: str
doc:
Edit the stream consumer's message in place with ``content``; on success mark
``response["already_sent"]`` and log ``ok``. A returned failure logs ``fail_result`` as
``(session, error)`` and an exception logs ``fail_exc`` as ``(session, exc)``; either way
``already_sent`` stays unset so the normal final send delivers the content.

name: _run_agent_mark_streamed_delivery
doc:
Set ``response["already_sent"]`` when streaming already delivered the final reply.

Never when the agent failed (unseen error), on "(empty)", or on a finite (`-z`, `chat -q`) turn:
its viewer prints only the completion text, never the deltas (#139666). Both flags reflect call
success, not content: a mismatch with the recorded turn-final payload never suppresses.

name: _run_agent_schedule_bubble_cleanup
arguments: self, response: Any, _cleanup_adapter: Any, turn_ctx: TurnContext
doc:
Schedule deletion of tracked temporary progress bubbles after the final response lands.

Failed runs keep them as breadcrumbs. Only on adapters with ``delete_message``; failures swallowed.

name: _run_agent_bind_turn_wiring
arguments: self, turn_ctx: TurnContext, turn_runner: TurnRunner, source: SessionSource, event_message_id: Optional[str], _native_slack_task_cards: bool
doc:
Resolve progress threading, then publish progress metadata and the sync→async bridges onto
``turn_ctx`` (the one-slot holders shared with run_sync's executor thread are TurnContext
defaults). Returns ``_status_thread_metadata``.

arguments: self, disp: GatewayRunner._RunAgentDisplay, turn_ctx: TurnContext, _executor_task_holder: list
doc:
Periodic "still working" heartbeat, edited in place where supported. Stops once this run
no longer owns the session slot or the executor finished. ``_executor_task_holder[0]`` is
bound just after this task is scheduled (reads as None until then).

Interval: agent.gateway_notify_interval / HERMES_AGENT_NOTIFY_INTERVAL (default 180s; 0 or
long_running_notifications=off disables).

doc:
Run the agent; returns the full run_conversation result dict.

Keys: "final_response", "messages", "api_calls", "completed".

doc:
Parse one SSE line into full_response; True when the terminal ``[DONE]`` was seen.

Malformed frames (bad JSON, ``choices: [null]``, non-dict deltas) are skipped —
one bad chunk must not abort the whole stream.

name: _display_surface_mode
arguments: setting: str, *, default: bool=False, require_platform_override_for: set[Any] | None=None, allow_generic: bool=False
doc: Return off|raw|generic for a gateway visibility surface.

name: _generic_status_phrase
arguments: kind: str, *, tool_name: str | None=None, preview: str | None=None, args: Any=None

name: _followup_processing_hooks_apply
doc:
Both conditions are necessary: a real inbound platform message to acknowledge (adapters key their
marker off ``message_id`` — Slack/Telegram/Feishu/Matrix/Photon — or off ``raw_message`` — Signal,
Discord; synthetic drains such as ``/goal`` continuations, wake-ups and startup auto-resume carry
neither and must stay silent), and an adapter that overrides ``on_processing_start``. We bracket, so
both halves must belong to us: a complete-only adapter (Google Chat reaps its typing card there,
webhook ends its per-delivery session) would otherwise be handed a completion for a turn whose reply
is delivered only after the drain chain unwinds back into ``_process_message_background``.

name: _followup_cancel_outcome
doc:
Classify a cancelled follow-up exactly as ``_process_message_background`` does: only cancels the
adapter itself routed (``/stop``, ``/new``, ``/reset``, cleanup) are CANCELLED, anything else is a
failure. Signal and Matrix leave the in-progress marker in place on CANCELLED, so reporting an
unexpected cancellation as CANCELLED would strand it.

name: _run_followup_processing_hook
arguments: adapter, event: MessageEvent | None, hook_name: str, *args
doc: Fire one lifecycle hook for a runner-drained follow-up; no-op per ``_followup_processing_hooks_apply``.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_read_config
doc: Apply model / compression knobs from the gateway config onto ``hs`` (invalid values keep the defaults).

name: _hmwa_hygiene_settings
doc:
Resolve model/provider/context-length + hygiene knobs (fail-soft: errors keep defaults).

The 0.85 threshold is deliberately HIGHER than the agent's compressor (0.50): a safety net
for sessions that grew between turns. ``max_turn_hold_seconds`` bounds the TURN wait
(compressor keeps running detached, commit fenced); kept below transport idle-timeouts.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_plan
doc:
Decide whether hygiene compression fires this turn (token/message thresholds, DB-backed
failure cooldown, in-flight compression).

name: _hmwa_hygiene_wait_for_summary
doc:
Progress-aware inline wait for the detached hygiene compressor. Returns the compressed
transcript; raises ``HygieneTurnHoldExceeded`` (turn-hold budget) or
``asyncio.TimeoutError`` (idle/ceiling/fence cancel) for the caller's handlers. Idle timeout
(fence ticks per streamed token) + hard ceiling (moved back by prompt reading) + turn-hold cap.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_cancel_or_adopt
doc:
Cancel the worker at the commit fence; on success release its lease and defer agent
cleanup, returning ``None``. When the worker already crossed into its commit, consume and
return the compressed transcript instead (a successful compaction is never a timeout; the
turn may be held past the budget by up to the commit duration — by design). The lock-free
``commit_in_flight`` marker keeps the poll from spinning on a hung commit.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_defer_cleanup
doc: Hand the agent's cleanup to the still-running worker future and mark it deferred.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_notify
doc: Best-effort user notice on the hygiene thread; failure is logged, never raised.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_record_failure_cooldown
doc: Escalate the failure streak (off-loop) and persist the cooldown, when enabled.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_on_turn_hold
arguments: self, attempt, hs, session_entry, session_key, source
doc:
``except HygieneTurnHoldExceeded`` body: keep or cancel the worker's commit admission,
notify the user, and re-raise; returns the compressed transcript only when the worker
was already committing.

Turn-hold expiry is an availability boundary, not a failure: the streak must NOT advance,
only flat retry spacing is recorded. A watermark-fenced commit (rows appended after
compression start survive as cloned tail) KEEPS admission: the turn proceeds uncompressed
now and the summary is adopted at the worker's fenced commit — always cancelling burned
every attempt for thinking summary models. Without the fence a late commit could clobber
newer turns, so cancel.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_on_timeout
arguments: self, attempt, hs, session_entry, session_key, source
doc:
``except asyncio.TimeoutError`` body: cancel at the commit fence, record the failure
cooldown, warn the user, and re-raise; returns the compressed transcript only when the
worker crossed the commit boundary first.

significant_calls.expression:
self._hmwa_hygiene_notify(
            source, attempt.meta,
            _hygiene_compression_timeout_message(
                total_exhausted=_hyg_total_exhausted, elapsed=_hyg_elapsed,
                idle_timeout=hs.timeout_seconds, progress_observed=fence.progress_observed,
            ),
            "compression-timeout warning",
        )

name: _hmwa_hygiene_on_unwind
doc:
``except BaseException`` body (caller re-raises): revoke commit admission BEFORE the host
unwinds so the detached worker can never commit later, and record a cooldown — otherwise
the next turn re-arms hygiene and waits up to 600s behind a fence that refuses again.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_adopt_transcript
arguments: self, attempt, _compressed, history, plan, *, session_entry, source, _quick_key, run_generation
doc:
Adopt a finished compression (rotation / in-place / refused); publishes the transcript to
continue with on ``attempt.history``. Returns ``(rotated, in_place, new_count, new_tokens)``.

Rewrite only on rotation (NEW session id): in-place compaction already soft-archived the
old rows and rewrite_transcript() would DELETE them; neither rotation nor in-place signals
FAILURE and an unconditional rewrite would leave only the summary. Write-before-repoint:
a repoint-then-failed-rewrite would point the live entry at an empty session.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_apply_result
arguments: self, attempt, hs, _compressed, history, plan, *, session_entry, session_key, source, _quick_key, run_generation
doc:
Adopt a finished hygiene compression, rebind the session + turn lease, record
streak/cooldown, and warn the user on abort.

significant_calls.expression:
self._hmwa_hygiene_notify(
                source, attempt.meta, t("gateway.compress.aux_failed", model=_aux_model, error=_aux_err),
                "aux-model-fallback notice",
            )

name: _hmwa_hygiene_codex_compaction
arguments: self, hs, plan, history, session_entry, session_key, _hyg_runtime
doc:
codex app-server runtime: the real context is the server-side thread, not the transcript
mirror. The detached-agent path would only rewrite the mirror and its finally-eviction
would destroy the live thread (next turn starts blank), so use the cached agent's
thread/compact/start and KEEP it cached.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_build_agent

Build the detached hygiene ``AIAgent`` with the live session's system prompt. Returns
``(agent, sync_session_db)``.

name: _hmwa_hygiene_detached_attempt
arguments: self, attempt, hs, plan, history, _hyg_msgs, _hyg_model, _hyg_runtime, source, session_entry, session_key, _quick_key, run_generation
doc:
Run one detached hygiene compression attempt end to end; publishes the transcript to
continue with (compressed or original) on ``attempt.history``.

name: _hmwa_run_session_hygiene
arguments: self, event, source, session_entry, session_key, history, _quick_key, run_generation
doc:
Auto-compress pathologically large transcripts before the agent starts so oversized
histories don't cause repeated truncation/context failures. Token source: the API's
prompt_tokens from the last turn, else a char/4 estimate.

Prepend the last reasoning block when show_reasoning is on for this platform. Mattermost

name: _hmwa_runtime_footer_line

Runtime-metadata footer for the FINAL message of the turn; off by default
