name: _hmwa_post_turn_hooks
doc: agent:end hook, process-watcher scheduling, and watch-notification drain.

name: _hmwa_add_failed_turn_notice
doc: Make failed-turn delivery explicit without replacing the provider-specific guidance.

name: _hmwa_failed_turn_notice
doc: Choose retry guidance without assuming completed tool effects can be repeated safely.

name: _hmwa_close_failed_turn
doc:
Append the gateway-owned assistant boundary iff the durable tail is open (a user row, or the
tool row of a call that ran before the failure).

The tail, not "did the gateway write the user row", is the key: on the primary path the
agent's turn-start flush already persisted the row (so the platform-id dedupe skips the
gateway write), and a platform redelivery of an already-closed turn must not stack a
second assistant row.

name: _hmwa_classify_turn_failure
doc:
Classify a finished turn for transcript persistence. Returns
``(agent_failed_early, hidden_reasoning_incomplete, is_context_overflow_failure)``.

Context-overflow failures must NOT persist the user message (session would grow and
reproduce the failure forever); transient failures (429/timeout/5xx) DO.

name: _hmwa_compression_exhaustion_reset
arguments: self, agent_result, response, session_entry, session_key, source
doc:
Auto-reset a permanently oversized session so the next message starts fresh instead of
replaying the oversized context forever. Never on a lock-contended defer — that is the
OPPOSITE case (a concurrent path holds the lock and is shrinking it). Returns
``(response, session_entry)``.

name: _hmwa_defer_exhaustion_reset
doc:
True when the reset was handed to the authority drain. A LOCAL session (the Bot Chat a
``hermes peer dm`` lands in) resets its target in the store, which refuses while an admission
on it is started (``session_busy``): this turn's own. The drain runs the reset right after it
settles this admission, before it claims any successor (the Bot Chat's retry included).

name: _hmwa_rotate_exhausted_session
doc: The compression-exhaustion auto-reset itself; returns the route's (fresh) entry.

name: _hmwa_user_transcript_entry
doc: Transcript row for the inbound user turn (clean text + event time when captured).

name: _hmwa_persist_turn_transcript
arguments: self, *, event, source, session_entry, session_key, agent_result, agent_messages, prepared, response, agent_failed_early, hidden_reasoning_incomplete, is_context_overflow_failure
doc:
Persist this turn to the transcript (session_meta on first turn, user-only on transient
failure, nothing on context overflow), update last_prompt_tokens, and re-baseline the
cached agent's message count.

name: _usage_window_chat_wording
doc:
A usage-window refusal sent to a chat: credits steps point at the Portal (a chat's /topup has no
Keep going control) and the reset reads as a duration (the gateway's clock is not the reader's).
Every other reply is returned unchanged.

name: _deliver_turn_response_then_limit_offer
arguments: self, event, source, session_entry, session_key, run_generation, agent_result, agent_messages, response, footer_line, intentional_silence
doc:
``_hmwa_deliver_turn_response``, then, for a usage-window refusal, the limit offer: the limit
sentence is the reply, and the button follows it once it lands.

name: _hmwa_deliver_turn_response
arguments: self, event, source, session_entry, session_key, run_generation, agent_result, agent_messages, response, _footer_line, _intentional_silence
doc:
Final delivery decisions: intentional silence, voice reply, streamed-turn media/footer.
Returns the text for the adapter to send, or ``None`` when already delivered.

name: _hmwa_agent_error_reply
arguments: self, e, event, source, session_entry, session_key, prepared
doc:
``except Exception`` body of the agent turn: stop typing, log, persist the inbound user
turn once, and build the sanitized user-facing error reply.

name: _hmwa_discard_stale_result
doc: A newer run generation superseded this turn: drop its deferred post-delivery callback.

name: _resolve_policy_agent_runtime
doc:
``_resolve_session_agent_runtime`` for a session bound to a launch policy: the route's FROZEN
config and launch credential, walking its own fallback chain on an AuthError unless
``fallback=False`` (a session control asking which route the session itself runs). Module-level
so tests that bind the method onto bare namespaces still reach it.

name: _recover_or_remember_model
doc: Last step of ``_resolve_session_agent_runtime``: remember a good model, recover an empty one.

name: _resolve_session_agent_runtime
arguments: self, *, source: Optional[SessionSource]=None, session_key: Optional[str]=None, user_config: Optional[dict]=None, fallback: bool=True
doc:
Resolve model/runtime for a session.

Priority (highest first): session ``/model`` → ``channel_overrides`` → global config/env
(``_resolve_gateway_model(user_config)`` and default provider resolution). ``fallback=False``
keeps a launch-policy session on its own route (see ``_resolve_policy_agent_runtime``).

name: _resolve_turn_agent_config
arguments: self, user_message: str, model: str, runtime_kwargs: dict
doc:
Effective model/runtime config for one turn. With `/fast` priority on, fast-mode
``request_overrides`` are deep-merged OVER the per-provider ones so both reach the model.

name: _sync_session_model_from_agent
doc:
Persist the runtime model/provider a gateway turn actually used (provider fallback can
switch them after the row was created). Runs in the ``run_sync`` executor thread, so it
uses the sync ``SessionDB`` (``_db``), not the AsyncSessionDB forwarder.

name: _hmwa_resolve_session
doc:
Resolve ``source`` to its session entry (topic recovery, internal-route guards, Telegram
topic-binding heal). Returns ``(source, session_entry, session_key)`` or ``None`` to drop
the event.

name: _hmwa_heal_telegram_topic_binding
doc:
Follow the (chat_id, thread_id) topic binding — healed to its compression tip — or record
a fresh one. Returns the (possibly switched) session entry.

name: _hmwa_open_session
doc:
Consume auto-reset / fresh-reset flags and emit ``session:start`` for new sessions.
Returns ``(_was_auto_reset, _is_new_session)``.

name: _hmwa_deliver_auto_reset_notice
doc: Stage the auto-reset sidecar note for the agent and notify the user (policy-gated).

name: _hmwa_auto_load_skills
doc: Prepend topic/channel-bound skill payload(s) to ``event.text`` on a new session.

name: _hmwa_acquire_turn_lease
doc:
Serialize [load history → run → flush] per resolved SESSION_ID so another routing key on
the same session waits for the prior flush. Fail-closed on timeout (outer dispatch returns
a resend notice). Released in _handle_message's finally, granted per (routing key, run
generation) so a stale unwind can't release a newer turn's.

name: _hmwa_first_contact_notes
doc:
First-ever-message onboarding note + one-time 'no home channel' prompt (both only when
the session has no history). Delivered on the user message (sidecar), NOT the ephemeral
system prompt: present-on-turn-1/absent-on-turn-2 was a guaranteed prompt diff + rebuild.

name: _hmwa_apply_message_timestamp
doc:
Capture the platform event time as message metadata and keep the persisted transcript
clean — strip any leading timestamp prefix and the Discord triggering-message note (a
model instruction, not authored text) — regardless of the toggle; only the in-context
RENDER is gated behind gateway.message_timestamps.enabled (default OFF).

name: _hmwa_prepare_turn
arguments: self, event, source, session_entry, session_key, _quick_key, run_generation
doc:
Everything between session resolution and the agent run: session open, task-local env,
context prompt, sidecar notes, turn lease, transcript load + hygiene, inbound text. Returns
``(_PreparedTurn, env_tokens)``; a ``str`` first element is a reply to send instead of
running (history unreadable, a local turn's refused ``@`` references); ``None`` drops the turn
(inbound text rejected).

name: _append_progress_repeat_count
doc:
Put a repeat counter after a closing code fence on its own line: ```` ``` (×N) ```` is not a
valid closing fence, so Telegram/Markdown renderers would leave the block open.

name: _tool_lifecycle_payload
doc:
The ``ToolStartPayload`` contract every client reads (``tool_id``/``name``/``context``),
plus the ``tool_call_id``/``tool_name`` the gateway's own consumers were built on.

name: _tool_complete_payload
arguments: call_id, tool_name, args, result, *, is_error=None, verbose=False
doc:
``tool.complete`` as every viewer reads it: the start contract plus the executor's verdict and
the result (ACP renders paths/output and failure from it), and ``result_text`` under /verbose.

name: publish_worker_tool_event
doc:
A managed worker's tool frame, published exactly as an in-process turn publishes its own
(the shared viewer stream and this admission's API observers). False for any other frame.

significant_calls.expression: publish_api_tool_event(authority, session_id, generation, kind, call_id, name, args, result)

publish_api_tool_progress(authority, session_id, generation, "tool.started", name,
                                  build_tool_preview(name, args), args)

publish_api_tool_progress(authority, session_id, generation, "tool.completed", name, None, None,
                                  is_error=frame["is_error"], result=result)

name: local_viewer_turn
doc:
A local route's viewers read the canonical event stream; ``LocalSessionAdapter.send``
publishes nothing, so status and notices go to that stream instead.

name: _viewer_status_kind
doc: The TUI's ``status.update`` kind: auto-compaction progress is re-tagged ``compacting``.

name: _schedule
doc: Hop a coroutine from the agent's sync worker thread onto the gateway loop.

name: _agent_interrupted
doc: True once the user sent `stop` (agent_holder[0] is the shared agent handle).

name: _track_progress_result
doc: Remember a delivered progress/status message id for end-of-turn cleanup.

name: progress_callback
arguments: self, event_type: str, tool_name: str | None=None, preview: str | None=None, args: dict | None=None, **kwargs
doc: Callback invoked by agent on tool lifecycle events.

name: _progress_subagent_notice
doc: Only terminal failure statuses render (same notice rail as credit warnings).

name: _progress_live_status
doc:
Live status line (Slack assistant status): stash the tool phrase on the adapter; the
_keep_typing refresh renders it. Plain dict write, safe from the sync worker thread.

name: _progress_onboarding_hint
doc:
First-touch onboarding: the first time a tool exceeds _LONG_TOOL_THRESHOLD_S while
streaming every tool (progress_mode == "all"), append a one-time /verbose hint.

name: _preview_cap
doc: tool_preview_length (default 40): the one-line preview budget for "all"/"new" modes.

name: _progress_terminal_blocks
doc:
(full, short) fenced blocks for a terminal command on markdown platforms, else (None, None).

No language tag: Slack mrkdwn renders it as a literal first code line. Verbose shows the FULL
command; "all"/"new" truncate to one line capped at ``tool_preview_length``. Consecutive
terminal calls drop the repeated header so back-to-back commands render as adjacent blocks.

name: _progress_build_message
doc: Render the progress line. Verbose mode queues directly (no dedup) and returns None.

name: _progress_emit
doc:
Dedup consecutive identical lines (execute_code boilerplate), then route to the native
stream bubble when the consumer accepts tool progress, else the progress queue.

name: _task_card_uncardable_destination
arguments: self, st, reason: str='no thread anchor'
doc:
The chat cannot host a card (flat DM: no thread anchor) — a property of the destination,
not a transient outage. The text fallback exists to keep a WORKING card lane live through a
transient failure, not to invent text bubbles the operator never asked for: with Slack's tier
default (``tool_progress: off``) the lane goes silent for the turn. An operator who WROTE
``new``/``all`` asked for text progress, so the editable fallback carries it instead.

name: _send_native_task_card_progress
doc:
Drain progress into native cards; supported destinations retain editable fallback.
Unsupported destinations and egress refusals suppress publication, never finalization.

See #29483.

name: _edit_progress_message
arguments: self, st, message_id: str, content: str

name: _split_progress_groups
doc: Partition progress lines into platform-sized editable bubbles.

name: _roll_progress_overflow_if_needed
doc:
Start fresh editable progress bubbles before a bubble exceeds limit.

Returns True when it delivered/split the buffer or a transient edit failure left it
intact for retry — either way the caller skips the normal send/edit path this tick.

name: _reset_progress_bubble
doc:
Content bubble landed — close the tool-progress bubble so the next tool starts fresh
below it; else tool edits hit the ORIGINAL message above (out of order).

name: _progress_absorb
doc: Fold a queue item into the bubble buffer; returns the line to render this tick.

name: _progress_send_or_edit
doc:
Deliver this tick's bubble. Returns False on a transient edit failure (retry next tick).

Transient network errors (ConnectError, timeouts) must not disable editing; only permanent
failures (not found, permissions) set can_edit=False. Flood control backs off but keeps editing.

name: voice_ack_callback
doc: tool_start_callback: speak a one-time ack in the voice channel.

name: native_tool_start_callback
doc: Queue an ID-correlated native progress start from the agent thread.

name: native_tool_complete_callback
doc: Queue the matching native completion using the real tool-call ID.

name: combined_tool_start_callback
doc: Compose the voice ack + native task-card start consumers.

name: _local_notice_callback_sync
doc: ``AgentNotice`` -> ``notification.show`` for local viewers (the TUI's payload).

name: _local_notice_clear_callback_sync
doc: Recovery -> ``notification.clear`` for local viewers (main's TUI payload).

name: _status_live
doc: Status adapter present and this run is still the current generation.

name: _send_status_text
arguments: self, text: str, metadata, log_message: str

name: _attach_session_title_callback
doc:
Wire the platform thread-rename lane onto the agent as `_on_session_title`.

The titler runs in the turn prologue, so attach before the run, not after it.

name: _renders_exec_approval_buttons
doc:
True when the adapter class renders native approval buttons. BasePlatformAdapter subclasses
say so through ``supports_exec_approval_buttons``; anything else (test doubles, relay-style
duck types) counts when it defines ``send_exec_approval`` itself.

name: _persisted_turn
doc:
``message.complete.persisted_turn`` for this turn, the receipt the TUI gateway's own turns
publish: clients bind the streamed reply to its stored row instead of comparing words. The
agent copies ``conversation_history`` into its message list, so an untouched pre-turn prefix
is the same dicts (transcript rows here carry no ``_row_id`` to compare).

name: _settle_api_runtime_lock
doc:
A confirmed API model lock settles only on the runtime it named (main's
``_finish_turn_result``): the served runtime rides the usage, a mismatch fails the turn.

name: _resolution_failure_reply
doc: ``(chat text, failure_reason, retryable)`` for a model/credential resolution failure before the turn.

name: _publish_api_tool
arguments: self, event_type, call_id, tool_name, args, result=None
doc:
The retained tool payload reaches the API observers of this exact admission only;
the shared viewer stream keeps its ID-correlated frames.

significant_calls.expression:
publish_api_tool_event(authority, session_id, generation, event_type,
                                   str(call_id or ""), str(tool_name or "tool"), args, result)

name: _notice_callback_sync
doc:
Credits / out-of-band notices (usage bands, depletion, restored) fire from the agent's
sync worker thread; hop onto the gateway loop. Fired-once latch lives on the cached agent.

name: _make_bg_review_callbacks
doc:
(send, release): background-review messages ("💾 Memory updated") are held until the
adapter's post-delivery hook releases them after the main response lands.

name: _merge_turn_request_overrides
doc:
Merge, never overwrite: init-time request overrides (e.g. a custom provider's extra_body)
must survive every reused-agent turn. Drop only the PREVIOUS turn's routing overrides before
layering this turn's, so stale per-turn values never linger.

name: _wire_turn_agent_callbacks
arguments: self, agent, turn_route, reasoning_config, stream_delta_cb, interim_assistant_cb, want_interim_messages
doc: Per-message state (callbacks, reasoning, voice route) — never baked into the cached agent.

name: _close_native_stream_boundary
arguments: self, reason: str, placeholder: str | None=None, reopen: bool=False
doc:
Native-streaming platforms (e.g. WeCom): an interrupting interaction (approval or clarify
prompt) must finalize the current stream first, or post-interaction output keeps updating the
OLD bubble above the prompt. Runs on the agent thread; the consumer serializes via its queue.

name: _clarify_callback_sync
doc:
Answer the clarify tool's questions (clarify_tool's synchronous contract): one card per
question, stop at the first the user never answers. The stream/typing re-arm waits for the
last question — between two cards it only opens a bubble the next boundary closes.

name: _ask_clarify_question
arguments: self, question, choices, multi_select, rearm: bool=True
doc:
One card: register, send, wait, then retire it (no answer) or re-arm (answer).
Returns ``(response, answered)``; the caller decides what "no answer" means.

name: _render_approval_sync
doc:
Send the approval request from the agent thread: the adapter's interactive button
approvals (``send_exec_approval``) when available, else plain text with ``/approve`` steps.

significant_calls.expression:
adapter.send_exec_approval(
                        chat_id=ctx._status_chat_id, command=cmd, session_key=ctx.session_key or "",
                        description=desc, metadata=ctx._status_thread_metadata, **flags,
                    )

name: _prepend_pending_note
doc:
Consume a one-shot per-session note (model switch, /reload-skills) into the NEXT user
message. Nothing hits the transcript out-of-band, so alternation stays intact.

name: _resume_note_interactive
doc:
Interactive platforms report the restore and ask what next; event platforms (webhook,
API server) continue the work — nobody is present to answer.

name: _prepare_turn_message
doc:
Prepend recovery/notice guidance to ``ctx.message``.

Returns (persist_user_message_override, persist_user_timestamp_override): real user text is
kept separate from API-only recovery guidance so stale guidance never replays as user text.

name: _native_image_run_message
doc:
Wrap the user turn as an OpenAI-style multimodal content list when
_prepare_inbound_message_text buffered image paths; consume-and-clear so later turns on the
same runner never re-attach stale images. Falls back to plain text when nothing is readable.

name: _run_conversation_with_approval
arguments: self, agent, agent_history, observed_group_context, persist_user_message_override, persist_user_timestamp_override
doc:
Run the turn with the per-session gateway approval callback registered: dangerous-command
approval blocks the agent thread (mirrors CLI input()); the callback bridges sync→async.

name: _restore_telegram_thread_id_after_split
doc:
Telegram DM whose source.thread_id was lost in the session split (synthetic/recovered
event): restore it from the binding so _thread_metadata_for_source yields the right
message_thread_id instead of the General thread (non-fatal).

name: _sync_session_after_run
doc:
Sync session_id right after run_conversation(): compression can rotate before a follow-up
model call fails, and the failure return must still point at the compressed child.
Returns (compacted_in_place, effective_session_id, effective_history_offset).

name: _combined_ephemeral_prompt
doc:
Platform context + YAML channel_prompts hint + channel_overrides system_prompt (or global
ephemeral) + the gateway ephemeral prompt.

name: _append_auto_media_tags
arguments: self, final_response: str, result, agent_history, history_media_paths
doc:
Append MEDIA:<path> tags from tool results (e.g. TTS) that the model's final text omits, so
extract_media() delivers each file once. Scoped to THIS turn (slice at len(agent_history)) so
a stale MEDIA: path from an earlier turn never rides a later reply; the history-path dedup is
the secondary guard — and the sole one when mid-run compression shrank the list.

name: _run_sync_scoped
doc:
Executor-thread body of the turn; returns the gateway result dict.

The turn message lives on the shared TurnContext (``ctx.message``) so ``_run_agent_inner`` sees
every rebind. session_key propagates via contextvars (_set_session_env / set_current_session_key)
— never os.environ["HERMES_SESSION_KEY"], which would misroute approvals across sessions.

name: _text_fallback
doc: Schedule the plain-text prompt when the native card cannot render; None = no such path.

name: register_timeout_notice
arguments: runner, approval_data: dict, *, command: str, card_message_id: Optional[str]
doc:
Arm a settle hook that posts the timed-out notice for ``approval_data['request_id']``.

``runner`` is the ``TurnRunner`` (for ``_ctx`` and ``_schedule``); ``card_message_id`` is the
delivered BUTTON card's id when the adapter returned one, so the card itself is edited in place
(which also drops its buttons). The plain-text prompt passes ``None``: it has no buttons to
drop and rewriting it would erase the record of what was asked. ``command`` is the
already-redacted command shown to the user. The notice is skipped when the run is no longer
current (``ctx._run_still_current``).

name: _post_timeout_notice
arguments: ctx, command: str, card_message_id: Optional[str], timeout_s: int

name: _edit_card
arguments: adapter, chat_id: str, message_id: str, content: str
doc: Edit the card in place (drops the buttons on platforms whose edit replaces the markup).

name: text_fallback_coro
doc:
The base numbered-text ``send_clarify`` as a fresh coroutine, or ``None`` when the adapter has
no native override — its ``send_clarify`` already IS the text path, so retrying it would only
repeat the failure.

name: _abort_for_outcome
doc:
Map a send outcome to the abort sentinel (registration torn down) or ``None`` (proceed to wait).

Only a DEFINITIVE failure tears down the registration; ``ambiguous`` (card may have posted) stays armed
and proceeds to the bounded wait, whose response timeout covers a lost card.

name: _clarify_send_disposition
doc: Decide whether a clarify prompt send aborts the wait; returns the abort sentinel or ``None``.

name: _clarify_send_then_wait
arguments: fut, *, clarify_id: str, session_key: str, clarify_mod, fallback: Optional[Callable[[], Any]]=None
doc:
Resolve a clarify prompt: send disposition, plain-text fallback, then the bounded wait.

``fallback()`` schedules the plain-text ``send_clarify`` and returns its future (or ``None``);
it runs when the native card failed definitively — at once, or late, after the ack window —
and never on a connector DECLINE (re-sending refused content as text is the exfiltration the
egress guard exists to stop). A card that fails after the window releases the wait with the
delivery notice, not the inactivity one.

Returns ``(response, answered)``. ``answered`` is the only signal that a user reply arrived;
callers must not infer it from the text (a real answer may start with '[' like a sentinel).

name: __init__
arguments: self, fut, *, clarify_id: str, session_key: str, clarify_mod, fallback

name: _voice_key
arguments: self, platform: Platform, chat_id: str, profile: Optional[str]=None
doc:
``<profile>:<platform>:<chat_id>`` under multiplexing (else two bots in one channel
share a key and one ``/voice`` flips the other's); default keeps ``<platform>:<chat>``.

Under multiplexing the key is additionally namespaced by the profile whose bot speaks in the chat
(``<profile>:<platform>:<chat_id>``); the default profile keeps the historical
``<platform>:<chat_id>`` shape so persisted state stays valid. See #75198.

name: _voice_key_for_source
doc:
Voice mode belongs to the (bot, chat) pair: namespace is the profile that OWNS the
receiving adapter, not the routed profile.

name: _bind_voice_input_callback
doc: Route voice transcripts back through the adapter that captured them.

name: _toggle_adapter_auto_tts_set
arguments: adapter, chat_id: str, on: bool, *, enable: bool
doc:
Add/discard ``chat_id`` in the adapter's enabled (``enable=True``) or disabled set;
adding also clears the other set (``/voice off`` and ``/voice on``/``tts`` override).

name: _set_adapter_auto_tts_disabled
arguments: self, adapter, chat_id: str, disabled: bool

name: _set_adapter_auto_tts_enabled
arguments: self, adapter, chat_id: str, enabled: bool

name: _apply_voice_mode
arguments: self, adapter, voice_key: str, chat_id: str, mode: str
doc: Record+persist ``mode``; mirror into adapter sets (``off`` -> disabled, else enabled).

name: _sync_voice_mode_state_to_adapter
doc:
Restore persisted /voice state into a live adapter: ``_auto_tts_default`` from
``voice.auto_tts``; enabled (voice_only/all) / disabled (off) sets from ``_voice_mode``.

name: _voice_ack_guild_for
doc:
Guild whose voice call is bound to *source*'s text channel on the bot that ANSWERS it.
Under multiplexing a secondary profile's call lives on its own adapter, never the default's
(#139345): reading ``self.adapters`` would miss its call or borrow the primary bot's.

name: _handle_voice_timeout_cleanup
doc:
Adapter callback on voice-channel timeout: clear runner-side voice_mode state.
``adapter`` (bound at join) is that profile's bot, not always ``self.adapters[DISCORD]``.

name: _is_duplicate_voice_transcript
arguments: self, binding: tuple, user_id: int, transcript: str
doc:
Suppress repeated STT outputs for one recent utterance (voice capture can emit it twice a
few seconds apart -> a second queued run and overlapping spoken replies). ``binding`` is
(receiving bot's profile, guild, bound text channel): the store is runner-wide, and another
bot's copy of the utterance, or a new binding, is a separate turn.

name: _cached_user_display_name
doc:
``get_member`` is cache-only; a speaker it misses may still be a cached user, whose display
name (global name or username, no server nickname) beats a bare id.

name: _voice_input_source
arguments: adapter, guild_id: int, user_id: int, text_ch_id
doc:
Bound text channel's own source when available (voice shares the text conversation's
session), else a synthetic one.

name: _handle_voice_channel_input
arguments: self, guild_id: int, user_id: int, transcript: str, *, adapter=None
doc:
Handle transcribed voice from a voice channel. ``adapter`` captured the audio; under
multiplexing each profile's bot dispatches through its own adapter, never the default's.

name: _should_send_voice_reply
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, response: str, agent_messages: list, already_sent: bool=False
doc:
False when voice_mode is off for this chat, the response is empty/an error, the agent
already called text_to_speech this turn, or voice input + base adapter auto-TTS handled it
— UNLESS streaming consumed the response (already_sent): then the runner must do it.

name: _send_voice_reply
doc:
Generate TTS audio and send as a voice message before the text reply. The TTS tool
may return one combined file or several separately valid ones (combination unavailable /
over a platform limit); legacy single-file results keep working.

name: _deliver_voice_reply
doc: Play the files in the connected voice channel, else send them as voice messages.

name: _interruptible_sleep
doc: Sleep in 1s increments so the watcher stops quickly when ``runner._running`` flips.

name: _session_housekeeping_watcher
doc: Reclaim resources without ending durable conversations.

name: _session_housekeeping
doc: Idle/pressure agent-cache sweeps plus the hourly SessionStore prune.

name: _session_stall_timeout_seconds
doc: Return configured stall timeout (seconds); 0 disables the watchdog.

name: _session_activity_for_stall
doc:
Stall-progress snapshot from ``AIAgent.get_activity_summary()`` only; no other clocks.

See #72039.

session_key -> (adapter, pending event) from every live adapter's pending slot (default
+ multiplex profiles, deduped by identity), then the overflow queues; first one wins.

Log one stall episode and deliver the notice. True only when sent (latched);

doc:
Refresh the /model picker's remote catalogs every TTL window. The picker itself only
refreshes on a cold/stale open, so if nobody opens ``/model`` the cache never updates.

doc:
Pending-inbound + stale-activity stall watchdog. Progress comes only from
``get_activity_summary()``; pending inbound is a notify policy gate, not a progress clock.
Notify-only: never kills the turn (contrast ``gateway_timeout`` / ``shutdown_watchdog``).

See #72016.
See #72039.

name: scale_to_zero_enabled
doc: Whether the Labs toggle stamp is set. Absent/blank/falsey -> disabled.

name: parse_idle_timeout_seconds
doc:
Coerce ``scale_to_zero.idle_timeout_minutes`` to seconds. Non-numeric / non-positive
degrades to the default (never <= 0: instant dormancy).

name: messaging_is_relay_only_or_absent
doc:
True iff the only connected platform is RELAY, or there is none. A directly-connected
platform holds a live socket and cannot scale to zero. Compared by ``.value``/name so this
module stays enum-import-free.

name: should_arm
arguments: *, enabled: bool, relay_only_or_absent: bool, wake_url: Optional[str]
doc:
Arm only if ALL hold: flag on, relay-only/absent messaging, wakeUrl registered
(a suspended instance with no wake target is a black hole). Otherwise the watcher
never starts, so a non-opted instance behaves exactly as before.

name: is_idle
arguments: *, active_work_count: int, seconds_since_last_inbound: float, idle_timeout_seconds: float, has_live_background_work: bool
doc:
Pure idle predicate: no active work, no inbound within the window, no live background work.
``active_work_count`` is the BROAD aggregate (agent turns + cron + API runs) — passing only
``len(_running_agents)`` reopens the mid-cron-job suspend hole. Callers that cannot read a
work source must fail AWAKE (pass a positive sentinel), never fail to 0.

name: dashboard_client_heartbeat_path
doc: Path of the dashboard-client liveness marker under HERMES_HOME.

name: touch_dashboard_client_heartbeat
doc: Mark "a dashboard client is attached right now". Best-effort, never raises.

name: dashboard_client_last_seen
doc:
Epoch seconds a dashboard client last sent a WS frame, or None if never. Missing marker ->
None (steady state when nobody has the dashboard open — NOT fail-awake, or no instance would
ever sleep). Unreadable marker -> ``now`` (fail-awake, as in ``is_idle``). Clamped to now: an
NTP step-back can leave the mtime in the future.

name: self_suspend_available
doc:
True iff Fly machine identity is present AND the local Machines API socket exists.
Off-Fly this is False; see ``suspend_available`` for whether some OTHER lever exists
before concluding the watcher must abstain.

name: brokered_sleep_url
doc:
The NAS sleep endpoint to POST, or None when this backend has no broker.

Validated here rather than at POST time: a malformed value would otherwise let
the watcher mark draining, hold the re-dial and flip the connector before
urllib rejected it, quiescing for a suspend that could never happen.

name: suspend_available
doc:
Whether ANY suspend lever exists, in-guest or brokered.

Quiescing without one is worse than not quiescing: the re-dial clears the flip.

name: request_brokered_suspend
arguments: url: str, *, timeout: float=BROKERED_SUSPEND_TIMEOUT_S, opener: Any=None
doc:
POST the NAS sleep URL so NAS stops this machine on our behalf.

Same contract as ``suspend_self``: never raises, True only on 2xx, fail-awake.

name: suspend_self
arguments: environ: Optional[dict]=None, *, socket_path: str=FLY_API_SOCKET, timeout: float=10.0
doc:
POST /v1/apps/{app}/machines/{id}/suspend on the local flaps socket (the socket is the
credential). Returns True when flaps accepted (2xx); the kernel then freezes this process
shortly after, so treat as fire-and-forget. Never raises: a failed suspend leaves the machine
running (fail-awake). stdlib-only on purpose — a plain unix-socket HTTP/1.1 request, no async
plumbing to freeze mid-await.

name: _hash_id
doc: Deterministic 12-char hex hash of an identifier.

name: _hash_sender_id
doc: Hash a sender ID to ``user_<12hex>``.

name: _hash_chat_id
doc: Hash the numeric portion of a chat ID, preserving a ``platform:`` prefix.

name: _is_path_unsafe
doc:
True if ``value`` could traverse outside the sessions dir.

Session ids become filenames, so the strict form rejects ``..``, ANY path separator, and a
leading Windows drive letter. ``strict=False`` is for *logical* session keys, where interior
``/`` is legitimate (Google Chat ``spaces/<id>/threads/<id>``): only a *leading* one is refused.

name: _should_redact_pii
doc: Keep model-visible identifiers usable on platforms requiring raw mentions.

name: _slack_tools_loaded
doc:
True iff the agent will actually have Slack tools this session.

Either the native `slack` toolset is enabled AND `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` is set (the tool's
`check_fn` gates on it), or an MCP server whose name suggests Slack has ACTUALLY registered
tools (configured-but-unconnected does not count; MCP servers are process-wide, so this is
intentionally not per-session). False on any error so a bad config never promises tools.

name: _discord_tools_loaded
doc:
True iff the agent will actually have Discord tools this session: `discord`/`discord_admin`
toolset enabled AND `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` set (the tool's `check_fn` gates on it).

name: _format_untrusted_prompt_value
doc: Render untrusted gateway metadata as an inert quoted string.

name: neutralize_untrusted_inline_text
doc:
Collapse untrusted text to a single inert line, unquoted.

For inline call sites (e.g. a ``[Name]`` turn prefix) where JSON-quoting would visibly change
rendering. Embedded newlines are the injection vector (a display name masquerading as a new
markdown section); collapsing them keeps a normal value byte-identical, a hostile one inert.

name: build_session_context_prompt
doc:
Build the "Current Session Context" system prompt section.

With *redact_pii* on a PII-safe platform (builtin set or plugin registry ``pii_safe``),
user/chat IDs become deterministic hashes for the LLM only; routing keeps the originals.

name: sanitize_model_override
doc: Copy of *override* with only persistable, non-secret keys, or ``None`` when empty.

name: build_channel_continuity_note
doc:
One-line continuity hint for long-lived Slack/Discord channels/threads.

After an auto-reset the agent could bind a new request to an unrelated recent session; this
points it at the prior session in *this* channel (via ``session_search``). ``None`` unless the
platform is Slack/Discord, the auto-reset had real activity, and prev_session_id is set.

name: is_shared_multi_user_session
arguments: source: SessionSource, *, group_sessions_per_user: bool=True, thread_sessions_per_user: bool=False
doc:
True when a non-DM session is shared across participants (mirrors the
isolation rules in :func:`build_session_key`).

name: _session_key_namespace
doc:
``agent:<ns>`` prefix for a session key: default/None profile → ``agent:main``
(BYTE-IDENTICAL to every historical key); named profile → ``agent:<name>`` so two
profiles serving the same chat never collide. A profile literally named ``main`` would
otherwise produce the default's namespace and share every session (routing index, agent
cache, store) with it, so it is marked ``main~``: ``~`` is outside the profile-id alphabet,
so the marked form can never be another profile's id.

name: _canonical_participant
doc:
Sender id for key isolation; WhatsApp JID/LID aliases are canonicalized so alias flips
cannot split one member into two sessions.

name: build_session_key
arguments: source: SessionSource, group_sessions_per_user: bool=True, thread_sessions_per_user: bool=False, profile: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Build a deterministic session key from a message source (single source of truth).

Layout: ``<ns>:<platform>:<chat_type>[:<slack scope_id>][:<chat_id>][:<thread_id>][:<user>]``.
Slack ``scope_id`` precedes chat ids (Discord guild scope is deliberately NOT added, for key
compatibility). DMs are isolated per chat_id, falling back to the sender id, then to one
session per platform. Groups add the participant id only when ``group_sessions_per_user`` and
not in a thread (threads are shared unless ``thread_sessions_per_user``).

created. ``touch_activity=False`` (internal events) preserves the user-activity clock.

name: _get_or_create_session_impl

only ``_entries`` / ``_loaded`` mutations.

the entry during the lock-free window the snapshot no longer applies: route is healthy.

returns ``create_session`` kwargs when the candidate won.

Persist a small JSON-serializable metadata value. Deliberately does NOT advance

Internal bookkeeping must not advance the user-activity clock used by housekeeping
and restart recovery.

name: set_model_override

doc: Persist (or clear, with ``None``) the /model override; non-secret keys only.

name: set_session_yolo

entry yet or it is unchanged.

name: _replace_route_locked
doc: Publish a fresh entry (inheriting origin/platform/chat_type) and save. Lock held.

name: rekey_profile_routing
doc: Rekey the live routing index and reject target collisions before mutation.

name: purge_profile_routing
doc:
Drop a deleted profile's live routing entries and persist the drop (#111926, delete side).

The mirror of :meth:`rekey_profile_routing`, and it has to happen here for the same reason:
this index is written back by the owning process, so a durable DB delete made elsewhere is
undone by the next save of this in-memory copy — which is how a deleted profile kept
resolving. Idempotent; returns the number of entries dropped.

name: remove_by_session_id
doc:
Drop every routing entry pointing at *session_id* (hard delete) and persist the drop.

The routing index is written back by THIS process, so removing only the state.db rows
elsewhere in a delete flow is undone by the next whole-index save: the surviving entry
hands the same id to the next inbound message and run_agent's INSERT OR IGNORE
re-creates the row — the deleted conversation comes back (#42422). Idempotent; returns
the number of entries dropped.

name: switch_session
arguments: self, session_key: str, target_session_id: str, *, expected_session_id: Optional[str]=None, preserve_prompt_pin: bool=True
doc:
Point a session key at an existing session ID (``/resume``): ends the current row and
reopens the target so resume matches the CLI.

``expected_session_id`` makes the repoint a compare-and-swap: ``None`` is returned when
the key no longer points at that session, so a caller that resolved against a snapshot
across an await (async-delegation re-pin) cannot overwrite a concurrent /new or /resume.
Prompt pins follow non-boundary repoints by default; /resume opts out explicitly because it
starts a different conversation on the same routing key.

name: lookup_by_session_id

name: lookup_by_session_key

``session.detach {end_reason}`` from the last viewer: end *session_id*'s idle local row with the

ACP rows keep their own reason; a busy FIFO keeps the row open, as for ACP.

On the owner loop after the close committed: a viewer attached meanwhile, so the session
it watches is live again (the stamp would make active work prune/archive eligible).

name: subagent_control
doc:
Desktop's per-child Steer / Stop: only a child of THIS session's live agent (the
``subagent.list`` rule). The sidecar handler never held an authority session.

name: show_tools
doc:
``/tools``: the session's catalog as main's CLI listed it (``get_tool_definitions`` with the
session's toolsets, pre tool_search assembly), resolved in the owner, where the MCP and plugin
tools live. Rows carry the first description sentence, grouped by toolset.

name: reload_skills
doc:
``/reload-skills`` (and the CLI's ``/skills install``): rescan the skill dirs in the owner,
whose skill-command map serves this session's skill and bundle invocations. The CLI renders
main's lines from ``result`` and queues main's next-turn note itself.

name: attach_file
doc:
Desktop's non-image attachment: stage the file for this session (its frozen launch cwd and
the owner profile's ``attachments/``) and hand back the ``@file:`` ref its next submit carries.
The sidecar handler looked the session up in its own table, which never holds an authority
session, so every file drop failed with ``session not found``.

name: approvals
doc:
The Desktop's approval replay (``approval.pending``) and card ack (``approval.received``)
over the owner's generation-bound prompt projection. Left to the legacy sidecar they answered
``session not found`` for every authority session, which the renderer reads as a reaped
runtime and answers with a mid-turn re-resume.

name: _owned_targets
doc:
``(registry, ids)``: the session's own processes (what ``process.list`` shows) that
``select(process)`` keeps; ``(None, [])`` when no process was ever registered here.

name: kill_process
doc:
Desktop's per-process Stop: one process THIS session owns (the ``process.list`` rule); any
other id, another chat's included, is ``process_not_found``. The legacy sidecar handler looked the
session up in its own table, which never holds an authority session.

name: reload_mcp
doc:
Desktop's MCP add / toggle / repair: bring THIS profile's live MCP servers in step with its
config (the owner's housekeeping reconcile, run now) and refresh this profile's cached agents.
Never the sidecar's teardown of every server, which cut every chat's in-flight MCP calls. The calling
session's MCP servers then change as a new policy generation when it is idle (``session``: applied,
unchanged or busy); other sessions take theirs when next attached. A configured server that did not
connect is named: a refusal when nothing took effect (no server registered or removed, no session
generation), else ``unavailable`` beside the success. A call naming ``rev``, the revision the session
already holds, is that same nothing-left-to-load, answered as success with ``loaded_rev``.

name: _held_mcp_rev
doc:
The ``mcp_rev`` this session's committed policy already holds — the value ``config.get mtime`` shipped
the client — or ``''`` when the call names no live local session. The policy is read on the loop (it
walks ``authority.sessions`` and the adapter's maps, which only the loop mutates); only the config read
and hash go to a worker thread.

name: _session_servers
doc:
The profile MCP servers the session's committed policy runs (its toolsets name them) that are *ready*
(live or lazy): a server connected for the profile is not one a chat with ``no_mcp``, an explicit pick or
a platform allowlist enabled, and one the policy names but that parked serves the chat nothing.

name: _commit_session_mcp
doc:
The calling local session's MCP servers as a gateway-committed generation (``commit_refresh``):
never a running or queued turn's, never another session's.

name: stop_processes
doc:
Ink ``/stop``: kill the background processes this session owns (what ``process.list``
shows), never the registry-wide ``kill_all`` the legacy sidecar ran, which on the shared owner
reached every chat, Desktop window and served profile (dokterdok N2). An explicit stop, so a
``persist_on_release`` job of THIS session is still reached (#41225).

name: _interrupt_delegations
doc:
Main's ``/stop`` also interrupted the background (async) delegations; here only the ones this
session dispatched (its route or its durable id), never another chat's.

name: _require_current_route
doc: The route still serves this conversation (a reused route must not lend its objects).

name: _owner_objects
doc:
``(agent, subagent records)`` of this in-process session. Process-local registries cannot
describe (or stop) another interpreter's live objects: a managed worker is refused rather than
answered with an empty success.

name: _owned_by_lineage
doc:
The read-only roster follows the conversation, as ``delegate_task(action="list")`` does: a
child whose durable owner id is in this session's compression lineage, written to the same
session database file. Without it every cached-agent rebuild (``/reasoning``, ``/model``, a
policy refresh, idle eviction) hid still-running children from the dock while the status bar
kept counting them. Control and tail stay pinned to the resident parent.

name: _compression_lineage
doc: *session_id* plus the sessions it continues by compression, walked backward so a closed sibling under a compressed parent cannot divert the walk.

name: _ownership
doc:
``(routing keys, owners)`` a registry process must match to belong to this session: its
routing key AND an owner among the session, its agent and its subagents.

name: _owned_locked
doc:
Matching process objects; the caller holds ``registry._lock``. Read directly:
``list_sessions`` refreshes recovered processes and writes checkpoints.

doc:
The session a header-less Chat Completions turn lands on. Its id is derived from the
conversation's opening, and a deleted id stays retired for good, so a NEW conversation that
opens like a deleted one moves to the next generation of that opening, the way a deleted Bot
Chat is replaced: the first ``api-<digest(id, n)>`` that is not retired. Read from durable rows
only, so every later turn of that conversation (same opening) lands on the same session. An
exact retry stays on the generation holding its request id's terminal identity; explicit ids
never come here.

The session a new turn on a retained chain (``previous_response_id``, a named conversation)

comes from the response store). An exact retry stays on the generation holding its identity.

name: room_session_id

``room_<digest>`` of a hosted room member's identity (home install, room, member, target
profile); a later generation folds its number into the digest.

name: hosted_member_session

``(generation, session_id)`` of the hidden session a hosted room member's dispatches land on:
a deleted one stays retired, so the room's next task moves to the next generation. A room
retry is replayed by the run's Idempotency-Key, never by this id, so nothing pins it.

name: _served_profile

Name of the profile *authority* serves; None for the launch profile (and for bare runners
without a registry), which is what ``SessionSource.profile`` means on the wire.

name: _pin_api_identity
doc:
Pin the shared-listener identity on an API source: transport = the launch profile whose
listener received ``/p/<name>/``, runtime = ``source.profile``. Returns the transport profile to
persist; None outside multiplexing, where the launch adapter is the only one by construction.

doc: Drive a write-step generator (see ``run_steps_off_loop``) inline: tests and sync callers.

name: run_steps_off_loop
doc:
Drive a write-step generator on the owner loop, each yielded SQLite write in a worker thread
in admission order (``tracked_write(ordered=True)``): a held writer must not freeze every session.
The whole drive is one tracked, shielded task, so a cancelled caller cannot separate a commit
from the steps after it; ``orphaned(result)`` then runs when the drive completes.

doc:
``bind_api_session`` as write steps (``run_steps``): the binding transaction is yielded.

``caller_key`` is this request's validated ``X-Hermes-Session-Key`` even when an explicit
session id selected the conversation (``declared_key`` is set only when the key selected it).
It is used only to adopt a row an earlier release stamped with that same key, and is then
registered as that session's declared key (and stamped into its binding receipt).

``walked_from`` is the stored session a Responses/Runs chain continued from when the chain moved
past it to *session_id* (``continued_api_session``): the fences it passed stay for good. If one
aged out since that lookup, the bind refuses with the retryable ``chain_moved``.

name: require_active_authority
doc:

profile is parked, else ``profile_mismatch``. With *store* (a callable returning the caller's
SessionDB, called only once an authority exists), that store must be the authority's: an API
adapter bound to another profile's SessionDB never admits here.

name: serving_authorities
doc:
The authorities that accept work (``SessionAuthorities.serving``: no reserved-but-unbuilt slot,
none retiring): what startup recovery, service creation and cross-ledger reads cover. Shutdown
keeps ``all_authorities``, so a retained authority's live writer is still settled.

name: require_serving
doc:
Refuse a verb reached through a stale connection to a retired authority: its ownership is
released, and until a successor bumps the epoch its own epoch still passes the store fence.

name: admission_owner
doc:
The admission identity a physical store row answers to: its compression root, then the
local creation id a canonical reset forks under (a reset child is not a compression child, so
``logical_owner`` alone stops at the child and misses the conversation's admissions).

name: holds_admission
doc:
Whether *authority*'s store holds a canonical admission for *session_id*. A parked profile's
retained (retiring) store that cannot answer counts as holding one: startup auto-resume fails
closed for that entry instead of stopping the boot or resuming a turn that FIFO may own.

name: owner_scope
doc:
Runtime scope of the profile that owns *authority* — under multiplex only.

Owner-side handlers (RPC dispatch, cron submit, admitted execution) must read config, jobs
and policy for the OWNING profile, never the launch profile's ambient scope. A
single-profile gateway keeps its ambient scope byte-for-byte: entering a scope there
would read the profile's config/.env for every handler, including bypass (--safe-mode)
launches that must never touch the profile YAML. Test peers with symbolic ids ('fixture')
likewise keep the ambient scope.

A standalone gateway that already hosts a second home (a profile created over the wire froze
the launch env and made unscoped secret reads fail closed) binds the launch profile's own scope
instead: unbound, every launch-profile session.create raised UnscopedSecretError (#141623).

name: remove
doc:
Drop *home*'s slot (a parked boot, a hot-unserved profile); returns the authority or None.
The launch slot is never removed.

name: profile_name
doc:
Served profile name for *authority*; None for the launch profile (its adapters are
``runner.adapters``, its session keys the historical ``agent:main`` namespace).

name: for_home
doc: Authority owning *home*, or None when this process does not serve it.

name: active
doc:
Authority for the active runtime scope.

Unscoped code (startup, shutdown, background watchers) belongs to the launch profile.
Scoped code that names a home this process does not serve gets ``None``: a routed
profile must never fall back to the launch profile's ledger — including once a removed
secondary leaves only the launch slot (a late callback of that profile). Only a runtime
that never multiplexed is a map of one that answers every scope with the launch authority.

name: serving
doc:
Authorities that accept work: not a reserved-but-unbuilt slot, not one retiring (a
failed serve or an unserve whose turn outlived Stop keeps its slot but refuses admissions).

name: keyed_turn
doc:
One FIFO turn per *key*: ``table[key]`` is ``[asyncio.Lock(), holder + waiters]``, created on
first use and deleted when the last one leaves. asyncio's Lock is FIFO and a cancelled waiter gives
up only its own place. *queued* runs (before waiting) when an earlier turn holds or awaits the key.

refused for as long as it runs; doing it here is what migrates an upgraded install. Idempotent
and never overwrites an owner, so every start runs it. A store outside the profile tree has
no derivable owner and keeps NULL.

name: _pause
doc:
The FIFO stopped without claiming its head. Committed rows stay queued for a later
drain; process-local delivery/HTTP/producer waiters on this session are released,
with the reason instead of a reply, so an adapter loop is never parked on a turn that
will not run. The ingress turns that refusal into one user-facing notice per episode.
``session_busy`` is transient (a registered worker finishes and wakes the FIFO), so only
the messaging delivery waiters are released for it; an API/webhook/Bot observer keeps
waiting for the answer instead of reporting accepted work as a conflict.

earlier one still in flight. Other routes never wait; an unroutable event (refused by
``prepare_native``) is not held. Yields the messaging input's fence check (else None).

kanban, hosted rooms) keep the plain ``runtime_draining`` refusal and retry against the next
owner with their own stable request id; none of them reads a released waiter as queued.

``_kanban_card`` is the Kanban dispatcher's trusted producer marker (``session_kanban.run_task``
only): committed as ``kanban_card_v1``, it lets a card attempt lost across an owner restart
settle interrupted (#134889 KB-8). Never a payload field: a client cannot supply it.

name: _release_refused_capture
doc:
A refused submission's captured bytes have no owner unless another admission holds the
same bytes. They become durable retirement candidates (collected again by delete/prune if
this pass fails), then a holder-aware release runs. Its failure is logged and never replaces
the refusal the client must see (e.g. ``admission_conflict``).

name: cancel_or_claimed
doc:
Cancel a row the caller read ``queued``: None once cancelled, else the started row the
drain claimed between that read and the cancel commit (``stale_generation``), which the
caller must stop instead of refusing a live execution.

name: resolve_unknown

Operator acknowledgement that an ``unknown`` turn will not finish; the paused FIFO behind
it resumes. Never requeues the input. A turn that finished in THIS owner but whose
settlement write failed (its exact result is still in ``pending_results``) commits that
result instead of discarding it: the answer was produced, only its receipt was lost.

closed a session whose turn recovered ``unknown`` (gateway/session_viewer_close), or when an
unattended automation turn settles itself (``notice``: its transcript copy, GW-10).

name: _classic_turn_holds
doc:
The route's running slot is held by a turn this FIFO did not claim (the drain is serial:
its own previous turn released the slot before this claim). Leaked and reaped slots are
evicted first, so they never block the FIFO; the reaped check reads state.db at most 1/s.

name: _runs_own_agent
doc:
The route's running slot holds a real agent (not the claim's pending sentinel), so the
Stop above reached the turn's own agent, not a cached one it may still replace.

name: steer_agent
doc:
The agent a steer for this running generation reaches; the caller holds the session's
event_stream.lock after check_approval_generation. Before the turn adopts its agent the
resident one is the previous turn's cached agent, which this turn may replace, so *text* is
latched for the agent this generation adopts (adopt_agent, under the same lock):
``(None, True)``. A claim with no steer seam (cron, managed worker) latches nothing.

name: adopt_agent
doc:
The turn installs its agent for the running claim; a Stop latched while there
was no agent to deliver it to fires now, never against a later generation. A Stop
delivered to the cached agent for an earlier generation may have landed after that
turn's finalizer cleared it, so it is dropped rather than cancelling this turn. A managed
worker is a fresh process per turn and carries no earlier flag to drop.

name: publish_execution
doc: Worker callbacks never outlive their exact running claim.

retirement's join) ever sees a committed claim that no execution stamp names.

name: _drain_stopping
doc:
A drain about to wait (storage retry, classic slot) exits instead when the runtime drains,
the profile retires or the live entry was replaced; committed rows stay queued.

waiter wakes: a delivery retry or the next DM then reads the fresh target.

name: _resolve_settled_waiter
doc:
Hand the settled reply to its waiter. The adapter sending it adopted the turn's crash marker
and releases it once the reply is ledgered (seconds with auto-TTS); a follower claimed before
that replaces the one-slot marker, so a kill in between would lose the persisted reply: the
drain waits for that release (bounded; never while draining or retiring).

name: deliver_heartbeat
doc:
Prepare, format and admit one liveness tick as one critical section with a completion's
admit-and-withdraw (``admit_process_notice``): a completion that lands while this tick is on its
way in withdraws it once it is in, and a tick checked after it sees it. True when admitted, None
to drop it, False to requeue the original event.

name: admit_process_notice
doc:
Admit a process notice. A completion and the withdrawal of its process's waiting ticks hold
the heartbeat lock together; a tick already holds it (``deliver_heartbeat``).

name: prepare_heartbeat
doc:
The liveness tick to admit for ``event``, or None to drop it because its process's completion
is already in the session: a later tick would be a stale "still running" turn. The caller holds
the heartbeat lock.

Otherwise a tick of the same process still queued is replaced: this one carries its stored
output, and ``_replaces`` names it, so its cancellation commits in this tick's own admission
(``admit_automation``) and a refused replacement leaves it queued. A tick's output is never sent
again, so a busy session gets one waiting turn holding every tick's output instead of one turn
per tick. A queued tick that started or settled first ran with its own output, and this one
queues behind it. A retry of a tick already admitted is dropped.

name: _tick_metadata
doc: A liveness tick's stored output (``heartbeat_tick``): what a later tick folds in.

name: _replace_queued

Write guard: cancel the replaced queued tick in the replacement's own transaction; refuse the
replacement when that tick was claimed or settled first (its output already ran).

stale "still running" turns, and the completion carries the final output, so they are cancelled.
A tick that already started is left alone. Never raises: the completion is already admitted, and
a retry of it takes the lost-acknowledgement path, not this one. The caller holds the heartbeat
lock (``admit_process_notice``).

surface would. ``{}`` for every other input.

name: committed_route_envelope
doc:
The route's last committed native envelope with connector provenance (what a producer turn
borrows), or ``None`` while no human message was admitted there.

name: admit_automation
doc:
``replaces``: a queued automation row of the same session this input supersedes (a liveness
tick carrying the output of the one still waiting). Its cancellation commits in this admission's
own transaction, so neither lands without the other.

name: move_route_wakes
doc:
After the route rotated (/new, /reset, compression-exhaustion reset), carry the old owner's
still-queued route wakes to the fresh session, as main's #114456 kept a parked internal wake
across /new. Left behind, the old drain refuses them (``admission_conflict``) and they stay
queued forever. Completions pinned to the closed conversation are not moved (they fail closed,
#55578), nor anything behind an ``unknown`` head (the operator's to resume).

name: _local_owner
doc: The LOCAL FIFO serving ``session_key`` (its owner is the receipt id, which a reset keeps).

name: _reset_and_retarget_local
doc:
A LOCAL route (the Bot Chat ``hermes peer dm`` lands in) keeps its FIFO owner across the
reset, so nothing moves between FIFOs. Its queued automation rows (a DM that arrived while the
exhausted turn ran) still name the pre-reset transcript and are retargeted at the fresh one,
in the same ordered worker step as the rotation; left stale, the drain refuses them
(``admission_conflict``) and the Bot Chat's FIFO pauses for good, across restarts.

name: reset_and_rehome_messages
doc:
The compression-exhaustion auto-reset: rotate the route to a fresh session and move the old
owner's still-queued native ``messaging:*`` rows onto it, same order and request ids. Left
behind they pause the old FIFO (``admission_conflict``) and never run, while a later message
runs ahead of them. /new and /stop cancel these rows instead (the user asked for a clean break);
the exhausted turn itself is started, so it is never moved.

The rotation (sessions.json) and the move (one SQLite transaction) run in one worker step
ordered with native admissions, not atomically across the two stores: a redelivery that
resolves the route to the fresh session commits after the move and dedupes onto the moved row,
and one that reserved the old route before the rotation is retargeted at commit
(``_admit_native_write``). Returns ``(entry, release)``. Until the caller runs ``release()``
(once, after its conversation cleanup and topic binding sync, also on failure) the fresh
session's ``claim_gate`` is held, so no scheduler (a redelivery, a moved route wake, this
move) starts a turn there against stale state; ``release()`` then schedules its FIFO.

Commit a producer wake (Kanban push wake, /loop tick) for ``source``'s route into the
authority FIFO, like heartbeats and process completions, instead of a classic turn that
interrupts or races the admitted one. ``False`` when no authority serves the scope or the
route holds no committed human turn to borrow provenance from: the caller keeps the adapter
path (nothing is queued there either). Raises ``RuntimeStoreError`` on a refusal.

An owner scan passes ``pins``: pre-admission pins land there with their mtime, unwarned, since

name: _scan_owner_receipts
doc:
The owner's bulk scan, under the mailbox lock ``_admit`` holds. A pre-admission pin past the
grace window whose ``bot:<key>`` never committed (refused by an older build, a death before the
commit, a transient refusal on the legacy migration path) is withdrawn as ``_admit`` withdraws
one: the scan stops warning and a same-id resend admits once. A pin laid over a legacy ticket
(``owner``) is that never-run message's only copy: it is requeued instead, for ``_migrate`` to
admit once under the same id. A pin whose admission committed stays the explicit unknown record
and keeps its warning.

Also returns the FIFO barrier: the lowest ``_legacy_order`` of a legacy pin of this home that is
still unresolved (inside the grace window, or its requeue lost to a concurrent change). No
legacy ticket ordered after it may be admitted by this pass. It holds for one scan only: past
the grace window the pin is requeued and released, and a failed requeue is re-read by the next
scan (gone, admitted or a ticket again), so the barrier never outlives the pin.

The delivery's receipt. Once the one transient-failure retry was admitted, the sender's
outcome is the retry's: ``status``/``reply`` follow it (``retry_admission_id``).

A ``failed`` receipt carries ``error`` + a typed ``reason`` (``tools.bot_failure_reasons``):
the relay's Desktop forwards ``res.reason`` to the sender, which cannot re-derive it from a
reply that lacks the provider text.

name: _failure

An original that failed while its one retry is still eligible is ``interim``: pending, never

the receipt file is re-read for that, the caller's in-memory record is stale).

name: _retry_eligible

context overflow). queued/started/unknown admissions never qualify — unknown execution is never
replayed — and the retry itself is never retried.

doc:

repeated deliver(), an owner restart or a second settle re-reads that admission instead of
minting another. The identity is written before the admission: a death in that two-store window

boundary. A failure that left the DM as an OPEN tail (the context-pressure classes skip the closer)
is not retried: the owner execution has no adoption seam, and the retry's DM would merge into it.

name: _receipt_answer
arguments: authority, actor, home, record, identity, retry_path=None
doc:

published result (after its one retry when ``retry_path`` is given), or a terminal refusal
(``refuse_pin``, ``settle``), which is the id's answer for good. Both check the identity.

name: _settle
doc:
Finalize a delivery the sender was told may not have been admitted: under the mailbox lock
every ``_admit`` holds, either settle the id as never sent or answer with what it already is.

A ``deliver`` refusal marked ``admitted=False`` proves absence only while that request held
the lock; a same-id attempt may admit right after. The sender calls this before it says "NOT
sent": with no receipt and no admission row for ``bot:<id>``, a terminal ``refused`` receipt
bound to the full identity is written, and every later ``deliver`` of the id answers with it
instead of admitting. An admitted id gets its receipt; an in-flight pin stays unknown. Only the
Bot DM tool calls this, so cron's same-id retries of a refusal are unchanged.

The writer is not re-checked: it may release between the refusal and this call, and "nothing
was admitted" is all that is serialized here. So the receipt claims only that, and any
``session:submit`` principal of the profile can settle an id it never delivered: the trust
``deliver`` already grants it over that id.
