Session-scoped ``/fast`` (the classic CLI's tier pick, ``normal`` clears to normal): the
session's service-tier override the next turn's agent reads (``current_service_tier``), never a
settings write. ``--global`` persistence stays the client's own config.yaml write.

name: yolo_config
doc:
Session-scoped /yolo (TUI slash + Shift+Tab, Desktop toggle): this session's approval bypass,
never HERMES_YOLO_MODE or approvals.mode. A ``--yolo`` launch is seeded first, so revoking it
here is not re-enabled by the next turn's launch seeding. The write goes through the shared
``tools.approval_yolo.toggle_session_yolo`` contract on the route's persisted copy
(``SessionEntry.yolo``, restored by ``restore_gateway_yolo``), like the messaging
``/yolo``: persisted before the live flip, so an OFF here is not revived by the next turn.

name: adopts_owner_agent
doc:
The claimed turn runs an in-process owner agent, which adopt_agent hands latched steers to;
a cron job or a managed worker has no steer seam, so a latch there would be acknowledged and lost.

name: submit_cli_turn_fields
doc: The raw per-turn CLI fields of a ``prompt.submit`` request, forwarded to admission.

name: admit_cli_turn
doc: Wire fields -> committed ``cli_turn_v1`` (``{}`` when absent); malformed values are refused.

name: cli_turn
doc:
The committed CLI turn fields of the admission whose event id is ``message_id``; ``{}`` for
any other turn, so a follow-up drained on the same task never inherits them.

name: rebind_api_text
doc:
This admission's ``api_text`` with its ``@`` references expanded, for the rest of this execution
(``session_context_refs.turn_references``). The committed row keeps what the CLI sent, so a retry
expands it afresh rather than twice.

name: one_turn_runtime
doc:
``(model, runtime_kwargs)`` of a committed ``model_override`` for this one turn, resolved by the
same ``switch_model`` pipeline ``/model`` uses against the session's current route. Nothing is
written: the session's route, policy and cached agent are untouched, so the next turn runs its own
route again (main's ``/model --once`` restore). Raises ``RuntimeError`` with the switch's own
sentence when the target cannot be resolved; the caller fails the turn with it.

name: classic_cli_turn
doc:
A local-viewer turn on a classic-CLI surface session (``cli`` / ``oneshot`` / ``tool``): the
viewer is main's HermesCLI, which reads the run_conversation-shaped result itself.

name: clarify_batch_turn
doc:
The clarify tool's batch goes to main's batch panel as one request: a local-viewer turn whose
submitter declared it answers the whole set (``clarify_batch`` committed with its admission).
Main's classic CLI, Ink TUI and Desktop all showed every question at once (TUI-18); a viewer that
never asks (an ACP editor, a raw WebSocket client) keeps one ``clarify.request`` card per question.

name: take_cli_result_fields
doc:
The receipt-only fields of a classic CLI turn, taken from the agent's raw result.

``pending_steer`` is REMOVED from ``result``: main's CLI queues a leftover /steer as its own
next turn (``delivering leftover steer``), so the gateway must not also run it as a follow-up
inside this admission. ``final_response`` is the agent's raw text: main renders its own
``chat_error_copy`` for an empty failed turn instead of the gateway's chat copy.

name: one_turn_route
doc: The executing admission's ``model_override`` applied to the resolved route (unchanged without one).

name: one_turn_reasoning
doc:
The executing admission's one-turn reasoning level (``model_override.reasoning``), else
*reasoning_config* (the session's).

name: run_classic_cli_turn
doc:
``run()`` (the turn's run_conversation) for any turn; on a classic CLI turn the receipt-only
fields are taken from its raw result and kept on ``turn`` for the committed receipt.

name: _split
doc:
``arg`` as a shlex-splitting handler parses it: an unclosed quote can't run there either, so it is
refused by name (before ``pre_command`` fires) instead of failing as an internal error.

name: _first_token
doc: /kanban's verb as its handler parses it (shlex, hermes_cli/kanban.py ``run_slash``).

name: _first_word
doc:
The first whitespace-separated word, as main's CLI and the messaging /memory and /skills
handlers split it: a quote later in the line belongs to the argument (`/memory pending it's`).

name: command_verdict
doc: ``read`` / ``control`` / ``refused`` for a canonical registry command on a local session.

name: _runner_command
doc:
``('exec', shell)`` for a ``type: exec`` quick command, ``('plugin', registered)`` for a plugin
slash command, else None (read in the owning profile's scope). The exact registered name wins over
Telegram's ``_`` -> ``-`` form, as main's CLI looked it up: ``foo_bar`` is its own command.

name: _run_runner_command
arguments: runner, live, name, arg, kind, shell
doc:
The messaging gateway's own quick-command / plugin-command dispatch for this session
(``run_inbound_hooks``): the operator's slash access policy, the 30 s sanitized-env exec with
redacted output, the plugin handler under this session's env scope.

name: _skill_directive
doc:
A local session's ``/skill`` (its plugin skills included, as on main's interactive surfaces),
stacked ``/skill-a /skill-b do X`` too: built here, so no client loads plugins to resolve one.

name: _tui_read
arguments: authority, actor, ref, name, arg, before
doc:
Main's TUI sidecar text for a TUI session's /status or /context read, else None;
``before`` (its ``pre_command``) runs once the read is accepted.

name: _on_own_thread
doc:
``fn()`` on a daemon thread of its own (under the caller's contextvars), awaited on the loop: never
the loop's shared executor, and no shared worker a callback waiting out its bound
(``plugins.hook_callback_timeout``, enforced by the hook dispatcher: abandoned worker, suppression,
cap) holds from another session. One session runs one delivery at a time, so this is at most one
thread per session with a delivery in flight.

name: _pre_command
doc:
Queue main's ``pre_command`` observer for a recognized command typed in a local session, fired
here for every surface (classic CLI, Ink, Desktop), so no client loads plugin code to fire it; the
delivery task, or None when not fired. One session's deliveries fire in arrival order; the hook
dispatcher bounds each callback, and one still running for this session (hung) is skipped for its
later commands, never run out of order, while other sessions' deliveries go on. ``surface`` and
``platform`` keep main's ``cli`` on every local surface (Ink and Desktop fired it through the CLI
slash worker). During a turn every command that still runs fires, as main's CLI did, except the
escape hatches.

name: _pre_command_before
doc: ``pre_command`` before the gateway runs the command itself (``slash.exec``/``command.dispatch``).

name: observe_command
doc:
``command.observe``: a recognized command the classic CLI or Ink runs itself on this session.
``pre_command`` fires here, in the session's profile, after the reply: the client never waits on a
plugin and never loads one. Plain data only (the command name as typed and its arguments).

name: _accepting
doc:
``before`` as the busy dispatcher's acceptance hook: a mid-run variant that refuses its arguments
(``/goal <new text>``) never reaches it, so a refused command fires no ``pre_command``.

name: _session_workspace
doc:
The session's frozen terminal policy (``TERMINAL_CWD`` = its launch cwd), so ``/diff``
reads the caller's checkout instead of the gateway process's configured directory.

name: _text
doc: A handler reply as text: ``/blueprint``'s result object carries it in ``.text``.

name: noted_completion
doc: *row* is a local completion admission: a note when it runs with no viewer attached.

name: note_if_unviewed
doc:
The claimed *row*'s response when it was written as a note instead of running, else None.
It is the FIFO head, so the note lands after every input committed before it and before every
input committed after; the viewer check and the decision share one loop step.

name: mcp_revision
doc:
``mcp_rev``: the MCP-relevant sections a client polls (``config.get mtime``) and names back on
``reload.mcp``. Read from the session's frozen policy when it has one — a live config edit is not an
MCP reload request, it reaches a chat as a committed generation — so the value a client is told to load
is the value the session already holds.

name: session_voice_mode
doc: ``off`` / ``voice_only`` / ``all``: the session's ``/voice`` mode as the messaging handler stored it.

name: local_voice_enabled
doc:
True/False for a local session the running owner holds (its gateway ``/voice`` mode), else
None (no owner in this process, or not one of its sessions: the sidecar's env flag applies).

name: set_local_voice_mode
doc:
The one writer for a local session's voice mode outside ``/voice`` (wake, spoken stop): sets
and persists the owner's per-session mode. True when the running owner holds the session, else
None (the sidecar's env flag applies).

name: local_voice_transition
doc:
A local session's voice mode went ``off``: end the push-to-talk capture it started in this
process (and drop its late callbacks), as the sidecar's ``voice.toggle off`` did. Another
session's capture is left alone.

name: _voice
doc:
The session's own ``/voice`` mode, so Ink mirrors the gateway's per-session state instead of
the sidecar's process-global ``HERMES_VOICE`` (T9).

name: pending_connection
doc: The open operation of a live session as its ``connection.request`` payload, or None.

name: _request
doc: The validated envelope and, for ``connection.respond``, the answer validated on its own as the legacy handler does: a bad answer is ``INVALID_ANSWER``, not a bad envelope.

name: _retry
doc: The card's Try again, under the session's own context, as the sidecar ran it for its session.

name: _require_connectors
doc: The sidecar's ``_session_connector_gate``: connectors on, and ``manage_connections`` in the session's tools.

name: _session_context
doc: The session vars a turn of this session binds (``GatewayRunner._session_env_scope``), so a re-mint carries the turn's caller identity and session key.

name: session_context_engaged
doc: True if any session has been bound via set_session_vars in this process.

name: _runtime_cwd
doc: Best-effort call of ``agent.runtime_cwd.<func>``; import/runtime failures are ignored.

name: set_current_session_id
doc:
Synchronize ``HERMES_SESSION_ID`` across ContextVar and ``os.environ`` (tools read it
with an os.environ fallback).  Delegated subagent children (built in the parent process)
get ONLY the task-local write, or they would clobber the parent's id.

name: scoped_current_session_id
doc:
Bind a task-local session id and restore the prior value on exit; never touches
``os.environ``.  ``session_id=None`` is a pure save/restore boundary.

name: scoped_session_key
doc:
Bind only the route key of the session a call works for (a hook fired for it outside its
turn) and restore the prior value on exit; never touches ``os.environ``.

name: bound_session_key
doc:
The route key bound in THIS context, ``""`` when none is: no ``os.environ`` fallback, so a
thread that inherited no context never borrows another session's key.

name: source_route_metadata
doc: Keep inbound route anchors for durable deliveries after the source is gone.

name: set_session_vars
arguments: platform: str='', source: str='', chat_id: str='', chat_type: str='', chat_name: str='', thread_id: str='', user_id: str='', user_id_alt: str='', user_name: str='', scope_id: str='', session_key: str='', session_id: str='', message_id: str='', profile: str='', browser_control_principal: str='', browser_control_transport_family: str='', cwd: str='', async_delivery: bool=True, ui_session_id: str='', cron_session: Any=_UNSET, parent_chat_id: str='', session_history_delivery: str | None=None
doc:
Set all session context variables and return reset tokens.  Call
``clear_session_vars(tokens)`` in a ``finally``; not nestable, clearing resets every var
to ``""`` rather than restoring prior values (tokens are accepted only for API compat).

``session_history_delivery`` declares whether the bound chat id is one the client can address again:
``"1"`` (audited producers — explicit session-id header, native API sessions, /v1/runs) or
``""`` / omitted (default-deny, #98619).  ``None`` leaves the var at ``_UNSET`` ("never
declared"), which ``session_history_delivery_supported()`` treats as NOT capable — an omitted declaration
cannot grant wake authority.

name: clear_session_vars
doc:
Mark session context variables as explicitly cleared (``""``, not ``_UNSET``), so
``get_session_env`` returns empty instead of stale ``os.environ`` values.  Async-delivery
goes back to ``_UNSET``: a cleared context is default-supported, not opted-out.  Wake
capability goes back to ``_UNSET`` too — but for the opposite reason: a cleared context has
declared nothing, and an undeclared capability FAILS CLOSED (#98619).

name: reset_session_vars
doc:
Reset every session var to ``_UNSET`` ("never bound here") for THIS context.  Call at
the top of a fresh task *before* it binds: ``create_task`` snapshots the context, so B's
task inherits A's already-set vars and a subprocess spawned before B binds would read A's
identity.  ``_SESSION_ASYNC_DELIVERY`` and ``_SESSION_HISTORY_DELIVERY`` (outside ``_VAR_MAP``)
are reset explicitly too.

name: get_session_env
doc:
Read a session var by legacy ``HERMES_SESSION_*`` name; drop-in for os.getenv.  The
ContextVar wins if ever set here (even to ``""``); else ``os.environ``; else *default*.

name: session_is_messaging_surface
doc:
Whether this turn is delivered over a human messaging channel (checks
``HERMES_PLATFORM``, then the session platform, then the session source).

name: declare_stateless_channel
doc:
Declare that this session cannot receive an async background completion.  Unlike
``set_session_vars(async_delivery=False)`` this does NOT latch ``_session_context_engaged``
(flipping the subprocess env bridge), which a one-shot CLI must not do as a side effect.

See NousResearch/hermes-agent#53027 and #63142.

name: async_delivery_supported
doc:
Whether the current session can deliver a background completion later.  False for
stateless channels (:func:`declare_stateless_channel`), Kanban workers
(``HERMES_KANBAN_TASK``: one-shot subprocesses whose parent disappears after the turn) and
registered worker processes: a managed worker exits at its turn boundary, so detached work
it scheduled would be lost (recovered ``unknown``) and its completion queue has no reader.

name: session_history_delivery_supported
doc:
Whether this request declares a server-history consumer for detached results.

Fail closed on omitted bindings; never borrow authority from the environment.

name: expand_references
doc:
``(text, refusal)``: the expanded text, or the refusal when the injection was refused. A failed
expansion leaves the text as typed.

name: inbound_references
doc: ``expand_references`` for an inbound turn: a local session's policy cwd, else the terminal cwd.

name: turn_references
doc:
An inbound turn's text with the references of the text the model reads expanded; None when
refused. The classic CLI's committed ``api_text`` replaces ``text`` at the turn
(``TurnRunner._prepare_turn_message``), so ITS references are expanded and rebound for this
execution, and the returned text, the stored user row, is ``text`` with the same attached
context, as a typed turn stores it: later turns still read the content. A refused local turn
leaves its refusal on ``event`` for the prepare step to answer with.

name: managed_turn_text
doc:
``(text, refusal)`` for a managed worker's admitted text, expanded against the session's
workspace. Built-in kinds only for a bypass session, which loads no plugins; the context length
is the frozen policy's, never the profile file a bypass session must not read. ``None`` text means
the admitted text as committed.

name: refused_turn_result
doc:
A turn that never ran because its references were refused: the refusal is its answer, and a
finite (``chat -q`` / ``-z``) prompt fails with it, as ``execute_admission`` settles a notice.

name: detach
arguments: self, actor: Principal, subscription_id: str, *, end_reason: str | None=None

name: receipt
arguments: self, actor: Principal, ref: SessionRef, admission_id: str

name: cancel_queued
arguments: self, actor: Principal, ref: SessionRef, admission_id: str

name: interrupt
arguments: self, actor: Principal, ref: SessionRef, generation: int

name: respond
arguments: self, actor: Principal, ref: SessionRef, generation: int, prompt_id: str, response: JsonObject

name: mutate
arguments: self, actor: Principal, ref: SessionRef, revision: int, request_id: str, action: str, arguments: JsonObject

name: _refusal_data
doc:
The ``error.data`` for one ``RuntimeStoreError``: always the reason, plus the field and the
detail when the raiser named them.

name: _profile_label
doc:
The profile as a log line should carry it: a named profile by name, a root profile (keyed by its
home path) by its name, never the path itself.

name: _log_refusal
doc:
One line per refusal, at the level its audience deserves.

A refusal that names the check that fired is a launch diagnostic (warning). A bare reason code is
the client's own state: ``permission_denied`` on a submit, ``not_found``, ``session_busy`` are
routine, and a retrying client must not be able to flood the gateway log, so those stay at debug
where they were silent before. The shape follows the gateway's own refusal log lines
(``gateway/run_notifications.py``): what was refused, for which profile, and why.

name: _log_storage_failure
doc:
Keep SQLite's diagnostic at the gateway while its wire error stays retryable.

Clients retry on ``storage_unavailable``, so, like ``_log_refusal``, a retrying client must not
flood the log: every failure keeps one line with its cause, the traceback comes once per method
and error class, and the client-supplied ``session_id`` is capped.

name: display_projection
doc:
Main's TUI display rows for a snapshot's stored rows: the sidecar's own
``_history_to_messages`` (compaction handoffs stripped, ``/steer`` unwrapped, tool rows
labelled from the paired assistant ``tool_calls``), never a re-implementation.

name: model_only
doc: A live row the model reads but nobody typed as one message (a micro-compaction merge): never rendered.

name: host_scoped
doc:
A host-scoped grant (the Desktop's shared-primary socket, the dashboard gate) acts for
every profile this process serves; any other grant is bound to its own profile.

name: _sibling_for
doc:
Connection bound to the sibling authority a ``profile`` param names, or None for our own
home. Only a host-scoped grant (the Desktop's shared-primary socket, the dashboard gate)
reaches a sibling; a profile-bound ticket naming any other profile is a mismatch, exactly
like a profile nobody here serves. Never a fallback, never a rewritten profile_id.

name: handlers
doc:
Method → handler for every verb ``dispatch`` serves outside the group controls; each
name is declared in ``tui_gateway/contracts`` (``METHODS`` or ``CANONICAL_METHODS``).

name: _spawn_notice
doc: Low-disk auto-prune question for this viewer, off the resume reply's path.

name: _voice_stop_replay
doc:
A retry of a stop this owner already consumed (its reply was lost; Ink offers Alt+K on the
same submission id). Voice is off by then, so the phrase check alone would admit ``stop`` as a
turn: the request identity answers it again, as an admission's replay would.

name: _typed_voice_stop
doc:
TUI-26: a bare stop phrase typed while the session's voice chat is on ends the chat
(the sidecar's ``methods_prompt._consume_typed_stop_phrase``, its typed twin of the spoken
stop) and is never admitted. Only a submitter attached to the session may end it, and only
on a LOCAL session: a messaging lane's own ``/voice`` mode belongs to that chat, so a
viewer's typed text there is admitted untouched.

name: submission
doc: The admission a ``prompt.submit``-shaped request asks for (``prompt.replace_queued`` too).

name: _subgoal
doc: A criterion button on the session's goal manager. A goal that is gone or an index that no longer exists is a refusal the card shows; the typed /subgoal command reports the same cases as text.

name: publish
doc:
Push one live session's control snapshot to every viewer as ``session.control.update``.

Desktop, Ink and the classic CLI paint the goal/loop/heartbeat cards from this event and run the loop
countdown off its ``next_due_at``, so every place that moves that state on the owner publishes: the
slash commands, a fired or settled loop wakeup, a judged turn, a tool that changed it mid-turn.
``only_if_present`` skips a session with no automation state (a plain turn's event stream stays
unchanged); ``only_if_changed`` also skips one whose snapshot matches the last one published.

name: bind_execution
doc:
Bind this context's cron admission ``(authority, session_id, job_id, execution_id)``, the
layout ``current_execution()`` readers index; returns the ``ContextVar`` reset token.

name: scheduler_execution_id
doc:
The scheduler's execution id this admission carries: ``_create`` admits under
``cron:<job>:<request_id>`` and the ticker's ``request_id`` IS its ``cron/executions`` row id.

name: _run_identified
doc:
``run_job`` inside this fire's cron identity (``ctx.current_cron_execution()``).

The scheduler binds it in the FIRING thread, but the owner executes on its own loop, whose
context never saw that binding; re-bind it here from the same ledger row, in the profile scope
the caller entered (so the row and the profile name are this profile's).

name: cron_read
doc:
``'overview'`` / ``'list'`` / ``'list-all'`` for the read forms of the shlex-split ``/cron`` argument;
None for a write.

name: run_cron
doc: ``/cron <arg>`` off the owner loop in the owning profile: the store is written here, never by a client.

name: _publish_health
doc: Publish one privacy-safe aggregate (no paths, no errors) across all live caches.

name: _registry_owned
doc:
True while the process-wide registry owns *handle*; an ``AsyncSessionDB`` (the only handle
type with a ``_db``) is judged by the SessionDB it wraps. ``close_all`` / ``close_all_under``
clear the flag when they tear the generation down.

name: last_error
doc: The exception the latest failed open of *path* raised (``''`` when none is recorded).

name: close_all
doc: Drain cached handles under the lock and close them outside it.

name: list_plugins
doc:
``plugins.list`` for this profile's own plugin manager: what the gateway loaded, with each
plugin's tool/hook/command counts and load error (the classic CLI's ``/plugins`` reads it, so the
CLI process imports no plugin code). Plain data only.

name: submit_display_fields
doc: The raw per-turn presentation fields of a ``prompt.submit`` request, forwarded to admission.

name: admit_display
doc:
Wire ``display_kind`` / ``title_preview`` -> committed ``display_v1`` (``{}`` when absent).

Only ``hidden`` is a client-authorable kind; anything else is refused rather than rendered,
so a typo can never turn machine text into a visible user row.

name: restore_display

name: _hand_over_turn_marker
doc:
The executed turn's durable active-turn marker outlives the handler, as the in-process
turn's does on main, and is released only once its reply is in the delivery ledger (or nothing
is owed). A kill between the terminal commit and that ledger write then leaves a marked turn
whose persisted reply the next unclean boot ledgers and sends once, without new inference,
instead of a settled answer nobody owes. The waiting adapter lifecycle adopts it; a recovered
no-waiter reply keeps it until ``deliver_settled``; any other turn releases it here.

name: waiter_replies
doc:
admission -> the reply a live native waiter is about to send, kept only until the drain
settles the turn, so a turn fenced ``unknown`` can still owe it to the chat.

name: retain_unsettled_delivery
doc:
Settlement could not commit and the turn is fenced ``unknown``, but this owner keeps its
captured answer for Discard (``resolve_unknown``). The reply stays owed to its destination,
and so does the turn's crash marker: the live waiter is released with a pause notice, so the
marker is taken back from it. Restart while unknown clears the marker (no answer is owed,
``release_unknown_turn_markers``); a Discard that commits the captured answer makes it owed,
sent once by ``deliver_resolved`` or, after a kill before that send, by the boot ledger.

name: deliver_resolved
doc:
After a Discard committed: send the retained reply when its captured answer committed with
the resolution (``owed``), else release its marker and drop it. Popped first, so a repeated
resolution never sends twice; a turn the drain still owns is delivered by the drain.

name: pause_notice
doc:
The committed input stays queued behind a paused FIFO (a turn lost across an owner
restart, or a head the preflight refused). Tell the platform user once per pause episode
through the ordinary reply path; later messages onto the same pause are admitted silently.

name: row_turn_author
doc:
Who wrote the admitted input, for memory attribution only: the producer's stamp when it
left one, else the forwarded peer bound into the session policy; never grants anything.

name: _launch_body_if_launch_owner
doc:
A standalone owner's turn binds nothing, but the launch profile's is marked at entry: a second
profile switching this gateway to multiplexing mid-turn must not fail its later credential reads
closed. Any other owner (a hosted named profile) stays unmarked, never reading the launch env.

name: _execution_scope
doc:
Under multiplex, owner-side execution runs under the OWNING profile's home (agent build,
config, secrets, state.db), never the launch profile's ambient scope; native provenance
(``home``) refines it. A single-profile gateway keeps its ambient scope byte-for-byte.
Secret sources (external CLIs) hydrate off the loop, as main's per-message scope does (#99519).

name: deliver_settled
doc:
Send a recovered no-waiter turn's reply after its terminal outcome committed. A send
failure cannot rewrite that outcome; it is logged, and inference never runs again.

name: dispatch_shared_busy
doc:
Serial receive loops (IRC, Signal) await this before reading their next frame, so return
once the follow-up is committed to the FIFO, or queued behind an earlier input of its chat still
capturing (its position is then fixed; acceptance still waits for the commit); a tracked
observer delivers its one reply. *durable*: return only once the row is committed (or the input
was refused, fenced or answered), never on the earlier position release: a busy burst's commit
task, which a command barrier (``/restart`` closing admission) waits on. Otherwise an input
released before its commit is held until it commits or its handler ends, and a serial reader's
next command waits for that too (``burst_gate``): a non-burst busy input (a second video, a voice
note, text outside queue mode) has no burst commit task to wait on.

name: _hold_until_committed
doc:
Released before its commit: the reader reads on, but this input is not durable yet. A serial
reader's next command waits for its commit or its handler's end (``burst_gate``), so /restart never
closes admission, and /new never cancels the chat's rows, before it lands.

name: holds_busy_burst
doc: A burst is held or committing: later input for the route must queue behind it.

name: burst_gate
doc:
``handle_message``'s entry check. True: a held or committing burst owns the route, so this
shared-runtime input must queue behind it. A command on a serial reader first waits for every
input that reader already returned on, as main's reader reached it only after their commits:
/stop, /new and /reset drop their own chat's held burst (main dropped the debounce buffer),
every other held burst commits now, and every pending commit lands before the command runs.

name: dispatch_busy_burst
doc:
``dispatch_shared_busy`` for one busy input, merging a same-sender PHOTO+PHOTO or
queue-mode TEXT+TEXT burst first.

name: _flush
doc: Start committing ``burst`` (once), after any earlier commit for the route.

name: _settle
doc: Every absorbed caller sees the merged admission's outcome, refusal or cancellation.

name: _undurable
doc:
Inputs the reader already returned on that are not committed yet: held bursts, burst commits
and busy inputs released before their commit (``session_ingress._hold_until_committed``).

name: when_returned_inputs_durable
doc:
Run ``persist()`` once every input a serial reader returned on is committed: a reader that
saves its own receive cursor after the call returns (Buzz) must not advance it past a held burst,
or a restart in the hold window loses it. Inline when nothing is pending; otherwise one tracked
task per adapter, so the reader reads on (a lost cursor write only replays inputs admission
already holds). ``persist`` carries the cursor as of this call; while that task waits, a newer
call replaces it, and the task picks the newest in the same step that saw nothing pending, so
an input that arrives during the write's I/O is never in it.

name: discard_busy_burst
doc: ``/stop`` / ``/new`` drop a held burst as main dropped its debounce buffer; nothing was ACKed.

name: register_transport_home
doc: Called when the server creates a callback, never from event home fields.

name: carry_callback

Gateway code that rebuilds a callback's event (a ``pre_gateway_dispatch`` rewrite, the
``/retry`` re-send) keeps the callback's provenance, but only on the source object the callback
authenticated: a new event with a swapped source carries nothing (#139045, #139040).

name: reauthorize_roles

name: capture_lease
doc:
Hold every path captured inside this block (capture through admission commit or refusal)
against a concurrent release: an older turn's settlement or cancellation that names the same
content-addressed bytes would otherwise unlink them before the new admission holds them.

name: drop_capture_lease
doc:
End this scope's lease on *paths* (default: all) early, e.g. before a refused admission
releases its own fresh capture, which its lease would otherwise keep from collection.

name: abandon_capture
doc:
Mark *scope*'s capture abandoned and release it, once: no row can own these bytes. A no-op for no
scope, a scope without an authority, or one already abandoned (its release ran or is arranged).

name: release_abandoned_capture

name: native_inputs_store

and an elevated grant on the resolved path would land outside the home with no home fence.

name: admit_attachments
doc:
Wire ``attachments: [{path, mime}]`` -> committed payload fields (``{}`` when absent).

``admitted()`` returns the durable admission already holding this request's identity (or
``None``): a lost-ACK retry whose disposable staging file is gone reconciles against it.

name: ingress_fingerprint
doc:
SHA-256 of a delivery as received: its prepared payload and the provider payload the hook also
sees (``raw_message``: a webhook's parsed, route-script-transformed body; None on relay, whose
wire fields are all in the payload). Transport headers (delivery id, signature, attempt counters,
timestamps) never reach the hook and are not hashed. Media count by bytes: a redelivery
re-captures them under a fresh staging name (``reconcile_native_retry``).

name: reconcile_native_retry
arguments: db, *, principal_id, session_id, request_id, payload, raw=None
doc:
A redelivered native message (lost provider ACK, Relay buffer replay) re-downloads its media
under a fresh disposable staging name, so its captured path differs from the committed one.
Retry identity is the committed bytes, not that name: when this exact identity already holds
the same digests and sizes in the same order, the committed references stand in for the fresh
capture (whose now-unowned copy is collected) and the admission digest decides the rest, so
changed bytes or any other changed field still conflict. A delivery committed in
``pre_gateway_dispatch``-rewritten form resolves to its committed payload when the resend matches
the fingerprint recorded at ingress (``ingress_fingerprint``); a changed resend, or a row
committed before fingerprints, is compared exactly as above.

name: _parse_iso
doc: ``datetime.fromisoformat`` that returns None for empty/malformed input.

name: auto_continue_freshness_window
doc: Resume-scheduler freshness window; stale automation never discards the transcript.

name: _is_session_ended_in_db
doc:
True iff state.db says the session is gone: ended (non-null end_reason) or hard-deleted
(no row in a readable owning DB). No DB or a DB error -> False (same failure mode as
``_prune_stale_sessions_locked``). Lets routing self-heal a session finalized or deleted
while the gateway stays alive. Store resolved from the owning profile.

Used by ``get_or_create_session`` to self-heal at routing time: ``_prune_stale_sessions_locked``
only runs at startup, so a session ended in the DB while the gateway stays alive (any path that
finalizes the row without clearing sessions.json) would otherwise be reused as a live routing key
and silently swallow every subsequent message until the next restart (#54878 — the live-gateway
variant of #52804/FM9). A hard delete is the same shape one step further: the row is GONE, not
merely ended, and reusing the route makes run_agent's INSERT OR IGNORE resurrect the deleted
session with its old id (#42422) — so a missing row is treated exactly like an ended one. DB
errors are non-fatal — never block routing on a failed lookup.
The store is resolved from the row's owning profile rather than the ambient scope: an unscoped
background writer keeps its own copy of the same session, and comparing against that copy reports a
live session as ended (#66887).

Pass *session_key* when the owning key is known but the id may have left the routing index:
after the self-heal re-homes the key, the id has no owner and would resolve to the launch
store, which never holds a routed profile's rows (#118862).

name: _local_receipt_target
doc:
The physical target the authority's receipt names for *entry*'s local route, else None
(not a local route, no receipt, or the receipt belongs to another route).

Such a route moves only through the authority (compression and reset advance the receipt
and the route in one transaction), and its first admitted turn reopens a stamped row
(``reopen_local_session``). A row stamped ended (a viewer's ``ws_orphan_reap``) is
therefore never a stale route: dropping it minted a replacement id the authority refuses
(``admission_conflict``) and stranded the conversation (#140642).

name: _route_reset_reason

name: _update_entry

name: _update_all_entries_locked

name: suspend_session

Mark a session suspended so it auto-resets on next access (/stop). True if it existed.

Used by ``/stop`` to prevent stuck sessions from being resumed after a gateway restart (#7536).

Drop routing entries idle (by ``updated_at``) for more than max_age_days; suspended
entries and entries with active background processes are kept. Only the key -> session_id

conn.execute(
            "SELECT target_session_id, admission_id, seq, status FROM session_admissions "
            "WHERE target_session_id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?)) "
            "AND status IN ('queued','started','unknown') ORDER BY seq", (ids,))

name: _masked_pending
doc: ``SessionAuthority._pending_rows``: a settlement not yet published still reads as its started claim.

name: live_entries
doc: Every live session *actor* may read, with its handle, picker row and closed-and-unviewed verdict.

name: forget
doc:
The socket closed: drop its queued calls and answers. A call already running in its thread
cannot be interrupted; it finishes, keeps its slot until then, and its reply is discarded.

name: stop
doc:
Owner shutdown (whole runtime or one profile's unserve), on the loop: refuse new calls, cancel
every queued call, and answer each outstanding request once with ``runtime_draining``. One
profile's unserve leaves the host socket open for the others, so unlike ``forget`` its requests
still get a reply. Running calls finish on their own (no SessionDB writes, only the model reply)
and that reply is dropped.

name: _answer
doc:
Write the request's one reply: the call's result or failure, or ``runtime_draining`` once the
owner stops first. Its socket closing cancels this task instead, and then no frame goes out.

name: _session_runtime
doc:
``main_runtime`` for the auxiliary client: the resident agent's live route (main's sidecar),
snapshotted here on the loop, else the session's own frozen launch route as its next turn
resolves it (read from config in the worker).

name: submit
doc: Admit ``work`` (or refuse it: ``runtime_draining``, ``oneshot_busy``) and return its Future.

name: release
doc: The call finished, or was cancelled while queued: its slot and its queued work go now.

name: start
doc:
Admit the call (or refuse it: ``oneshot_busy``, ``runtime_draining``) and answer it later;
``check`` is the contract's result check, run before the reply is written.

name: authorize_local_source
doc: None for legacy/nonlocal routes; registered local adapters fail closed.

name: _bypass_policy
doc:
Frozen snapshot for --safe-mode / --ignore-user-config: code defaults plus the explicit
launch options. The profile's config.yaml/.env are never read, so a malformed profile cannot
block or shape the session; there is no default model to inherit, so one must be explicit.

name: load_profile_config
doc:
The profile's effective config.yaml for a NEW session's policy, ``${VAR}`` refs expanded against
the profile's CURRENT ``.env`` (the source tool env refreshes from), not the env this daemon
started with: a single-profile owner binds no secret scope and never reloads ``.env`` for local
turns. A bound scope (a served profile's owner scope) already is that source and is kept; a miss
on the launch profile still falls to the process env (systemd / ``op run`` injection).

name: profile_env_scope
doc: Bind the profile's current ``.env`` (see ``load_profile_config``) unless a scope is bound.

name: project_plugins_warning
doc:
The plain notice for a session whose client opted into project plugins (its forwarded
``HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS``) in a folder that has some: the gateway never loads them.

name: create_local_session
arguments: authority, actor, params, *, trusted_policy=None, trusted_secrets=None, skills_prompt=None, client_local=False
doc: Stage, commit and publish a local session inline (synchronous callers).

name: staged_creation_follows
doc:
Whether a retry of *request_id* may ask to follow the profile.

True when nothing is staged under that identity, or the staged request already follows.
False only when an older build committed the session without ``follow_profile_config`` and
stopped before its title. The next attempt reuses the identity, and a different request is
refused for good. The retry then carries the frozen request.

name: stage_local_session
arguments: authority, actor, params, *, trusted_policy=None, trusted_secrets=None, skills_prompt=None, client_local=False, desktop_local=False
doc:
Everything before the creation commit: the existing session's ref on an exact retry, else the
receipt ``commit_local_session`` writes (the async RPC commits it off the owner loop).
``client_local``: the gateway's own proof that the client is on this host (its connection redeemed a
ticket minted over the private control socket), never a value the client sends. ``desktop_local``:
that client is also the Desktop app (``process_identity.local_desktop_client``); a Desktop chat
records it so its turns run as work for the local Desktop (``session_policy.local_desktop_turn``).

name: _lazy_model
doc:
The model a not-yet-built session will run: with no provider pinned, the free tier's agent
build pins ``nous/welcome`` (``pin_model_for_route``), so the configured default is not it.

name: _reasoning_fields
doc:
Main's session-info effort/tier fields, from the built agent or (lazy) what the policy's next turn
resolves (a following session's current profile): a resumed Desktop slice holds its reasoning pill
pending until ``reasoning_effort`` arrives.

name: effort_fields
arguments: config, tier, model, provider, base_url, api_mode=None
doc: Session-info ``reasoning_effort`` / ``_wire`` / ``service_tier`` / ``fast`` for one resolved route.

name: _classic_cli_fields
doc:
What main's HermesCLI read off itself for /status, the status bar and the exit summary: the
stored title and times, the session's yolo, api_mode, the loaded tool count and a masked
credential hint (never the key). Lazy sessions report what is known without building an agent.

name: send_clarify
arguments: self, chat_id, question, choices, clarify_id, session_key, metadata=None

significant_calls.expression: super().send_clarify(chat_id, question, choices, clarify_id, session_key, metadata)

name: _unanswerable_clarify
doc:
Why no one can answer a question asked in this chat now, or None to ask it.

Hosted rooms (controls expose approvals only) and forwarded A2A conversations (the
author is a remote peer with no prompt surface) never have an answering viewer. Any
other chat can be answered by an attached viewer holding ``session:respond``; with none
attached, a producer turn (Bot Chat DM, plugin/heartbeat injection) declines, while a
viewer's own turn keeps waiting so its author can re-attach and answer.

name: _due
doc: *sid*'s stored receipt when a catch-up would commit for it on this owner, else None. Read-only.

name: adopt_before_restore
doc:
Commit *sid*'s due catch-up in a worker, so the restore that follows only reads.

``tracked=False``: an authority still being built, not yet published for retirement to join.

name: adopt_local_compressions
doc: Boot and hot-profile recovery: every receipt's due catch-up, before ``recover_local_sessions``.

name: schedule_adoption
doc:
A sync restore on the owner loop found *receipt*'s catch-up due: commit it in a tracked worker,
then publish the session on the loop. One worker per session at a time.

name: closed_idle_unviewed
doc:
The verdict on facts already read: the live listings read ``target_ended_at`` for a whole batch
in one off-loop query (``gateway/session_live_listing``).

name: closed_and_unviewed
doc: A live-feed row main would list as resumable: closed, idle and with no viewer left.

name: validate_editor
doc:
The launch's editor policy, or a refusal that names the key it read (create path totality).

An ACP connection is a viewer; the policy itself lives with execution. Every branch below refuses
with its own field, so a rejected editor launch says which key was wrong instead of a bare code.

name: _policy_requester
doc:
The session's edit approval policy in front of the editor's consent (main's ACP modes): Accept
Edits / Don't Ask let an edit run unasked; sensitive paths and everything else still ask.

name: _start_update_prefetch
doc:
Main's TUI gateway started the passive update check at import; the owner starts it once,
on the first snapshot, so ``update_behind`` reports like main's banner instead of staying null.

name: _grouped
doc: ``{toolset: [tool names]}`` exactly as main's ``_session_info`` grouped ``agent.tools``.

name: _policy_tools
doc:
The tool list the session's next agent build loads (``agent/agent_init.py`` tool snapshot):
the policy's toolsets minus the configured and platform-gated disabled ones, one-shot pruned.

name: _project
doc: ``tui_gateway/server.py::_project_info_for_cwd``: the named project owning *cwd*, or None.

name: _cli_startup_notices
doc:
The lines main's HermesCLI printed under its banner, computed where the tools run: the toolset
availability warning (``cli.py::_show_tool_availability_warnings``) and the Browser Use downgrade
notice (``_show_browser_backend_notice``). The classic CLI renders them with its own console.

name: _unknown_toolsets
doc:
Main's "Unknown toolsets" startup warning (``HermesCLI._init_toolsets``), judged where the plugins
load: the session's toolset names the profile's registry, MCP servers, plugin toolsets and platform
bundles cannot place (an uninstalled plugin's stale ``platform_toolsets`` entry).

name: _cli_skills
doc:
``hermes_cli.banner.get_available_skills`` as main's classic CLI computed it: ``cmd_chat`` pins
``HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD`` before HermesCLI starts, so ``environments: [kanban]`` skills are offered.
The owner never sets that env; the kanban relevance is scoped to this scan (a ContextVar) and the
catalog cache entry it would poison is restored, so other surfaces keep their own view.

name: session_inventory
doc:
Main's banner/status fields for one session. Each section degrades to main's empty value on
its own, so one failing builder never blanks the others (main wrapped each in ``suppress``).

name: snapshot_info
doc: ``local_session_info`` plus main's inventory, the builders run off the owner loop.

name: agent_inventory
doc:
The banner fields only a built agent knows (main's ``_session_info`` read them off it): the
tools it loaded, its cached system prompt (the ``▸ System Prompt`` row), provider and context
length. Cheap attribute reads, safe on the agent thread at turn end.

name: publish_settled_info
doc:
Main's end-of-turn ``session.info`` (``session_workdir._emit_settled_session_info``) for a local
viewer: the first turn builds the agent, so this is when the banner's ``▸ System Prompt`` row, the
agent's tool list and provider first become known. Never breaks the turn.

A ``model_override`` admission (``/model --once``, ``/moa``) built its agent on the one-turn
route. That agent must not become the route Desktop, the TUI, and resume read. Drop it from
the cache (released once this turn's running slot clears) and publish the model and provider
of the policy route, both from one read of the profile.

name: private_mutation_payload
doc:
``(store payload, servers)`` of an ``editor_mcp`` or a ``branch`` naming servers: the list
stays in owner memory; the receipt digest and every store write see only its fingerprint.

name: session_scope
doc: A session's own ledger scope: never shared with another session (a fork included) or profile.

name: _server_names
doc:
Index -> ledger name: the editor's own server name (the model sees ``mcp__editor_github_<tag>__x``)
plus a per-session tag, so two sessions borrowing same-named servers never adopt one connection.

name: _frozen_names
doc: The names a session's manifest was frozen under; manifests without ``names`` predate them.

name: _frozen_toolset
doc: Whether *toolset* is one of the editor toolsets frozen in *data* (a manifest or None).

name: _borrowed
arguments: authority, scope, servers, names, cwd, *, partial=False
doc:
Yield ``(schemas, connected indexes)`` inside the session's tool scope. Only ``partial`` (a
selection being frozen) may leave a server out; an execution needs every server its manifest
was frozen with. A held connection is reused; the last borrower closes it unless a viewer remains.

name: release_editor_mcp
doc:
The last viewer left (or the sessions retired): close their held editor connections. One an
execution still borrows is closed by that execution when it ends.

name: rebind_editor_mcp
doc:
``(policy, manifest changed)``: *policy* with its editor selection freshly discovered from
*servers* under *sid*'s own scope (blocking). A broken server is left out of the frozen selection
(main skipped it too), so no later execution respawns it.

name: resume_editor_mcp
doc:
Call after ordinary resume authorization, before attaching the viewer. An empty or omitted
list keeps the session's servers: ACP load always carries one, so a second editor without MCP
config must not strip the first one's tools for every viewer. Removal is only the fenced
``editor_mcp`` change with ``[]``.

name: retire_editor_mcp
doc: An empty selection committed: *sid*'s held editor connections close now (blocking), viewer or not.

name: install_editor_mcp
doc: After a committed change: *sid*'s borrowed credentials follow its committed policy (memory only).

name: announce_tools_changed
doc:
One ``session.tools_changed`` on the session's stream when a change altered the manifest:
server names and the generation only, never a transport specification.

name: prepare_editor_mcp
_live_tools_changed
doc:
Whether a held server's live ``tools/list`` differs from the tools its connection was
discovered with. Editor servers ignore ``tools/list_changed`` (the manifest is frozen), so
the admission start asks; an unanswered list (bounded) counts as unchanged.

name: refreeze_editor_mcp
doc:
The drain, once the FIFO head is authorized and before it is claimed (claim gate and mutation
lock held, nothing executing), re-checks the editor schemas; a drifted manifest is re-frozen through the
``editor_mcp`` writer path, so the turn runs on it instead of failing ``acp_mcp_schema_changed``.
Best-effort: the FIFO must not pause on it, so a failed re-check only logs and the turn then
reports real drift as before.

name: _commit_refreeze
doc:
The ``editor_mcp`` change on the owning principal's behalf, through ``session.mutate``'s own
writer (the drain holds the session's locks, and a schema re-check needs no capability).

name: _child_secret_ref
doc:
A durable config-secret reference names the policy identity, which the child's own editor
selection changed; the frozen secrets themselves are the parent's.

name: prepare_branch_editor
doc:
``(prepared, servers)`` for a fork of an editor session: the child's selection under its OWN
scope, from the fork's list or else a copy of the parent's borrowed servers. The child never
shares the parent's scope or connections. ``(None, None)`` when no editor servers are involved.

Discovery starts every server, so *gate* (the branch's prepare-only fences: receipt, revision,
generation, idle) runs first; an exact retry's durable receipt comes back as ``prepared``.

name: require_history_claim
doc: Import receipts confer ownership; merely knowing an old ID does not.

name: legacy_launch_params
doc:
``(create params, api_mode)`` a legacy row resumes on.

The old local surfaces persisted their effective route and runtime choices in
``model_config``. Preserve those choices while adopting them, rather than
combining their model with a later profile default. Older ACP rows also hold
their workspace only there. ``api_mode`` is no create field, so it is
returned apart.

name: bot_chat_row
doc:
Main's Bot Chat rule for a stored row: the ``follow_profile_config`` marker, or, for a row
written before the marker existed, the exact title ``Bot Chat``.

name: composer_pick_holds
doc: Whether *row*'s composer pick still holds: the profile (*config*) targets what it diverged from.

name: legacy_bot_chat_launch
doc:
``(params, api_mode)`` for adoption. A Bot Chat (``bot_chat_row``) follows its profile.

A composer pick is kept only while the profile still targets what the pick diverged from, and
is adopted the way a create records one: held until the next profile edit. Otherwise only the
workspace and source carry over, so the route last run is not frozen and its wire mode is not
either. Any other row is unchanged.

name: follow_bot_chat
doc:
*policy* following its profile when the session is a Bot Chat an earlier build committed
frozen (its delivery door, a CLI titled create, an adoption), else *policy* itself.

The caller is a client opening the chat (``session.resume``), which adopts it on the same rule
and composer pick as adoption above; *live* is the profile's config the open read. A request
that names ``follow_profile_config`` (``false`` included) is the client's own choice, and a
bypass launch never reads the profile. The request is not rewritten. A committed ``/model``
(*picked*, the session's policy edits) holds like a composer pick, and a committed ``/reasoning``
stays the session's level, recorded as its session pin.
The caller re-binds the private values without the followed sections, so a frozen key never
reaches the profile's route.

name: _route_is_usage_stamp
doc:
True when the row's only route record is the ``billing_provider='custom'`` + ``billing_base_url``
usage stamp: no ``gateway_runtime`` and no top-level ``provider``/``base_url`` in ``model_config``.
That stamp records which endpoint billed the last turn (the profile's route at the time), not a
route the user picked for this session.

name: _configured_owner
doc: The configured named entry (``providers:``/``custom_providers:``) serving the saved URL, or None.

name: _endpoint_owner
doc:
The provider whose credential may serve the saved endpoint. A named entry that now points
elsewhere owns a credential for THAT host: rebind to the entry still serving the saved URL, or
refuse by name rather than send the moved entry's key to the old host.

name: local_adapter_map
doc:
The adapter map a LOCAL session of *authority* lives in: ``runner.adapters`` for the launch
profile, ``runner._profile_adapters[name]`` for a served secondary (its routed home, so
``_adapter_for_source`` / ``_adapters_for_profile`` resolve the right transport).

name: local_source
doc:
LOCAL SessionSource for a session owned by *authority*. A served secondary's local sessions
carry its profile so ``build_session_key`` namespaces them (``agent:<name>:local:...``) and the
SessionStore writes their rows to that profile's ``state.db``, not the launch store.

name: _refused_check
doc:
``<reason or error> at <function>:<line>``: where a receipt check raised, and why, followed
through every chained ``__cause__`` (``restore_policy`` and ``local_receipt`` wrap the check
that failed into a bare ``storage_unavailable``).

name: _with_untracked_compression
doc:
*receipt*, after recording compression steps an older build published past its tip (#140060).

The catch-up writes, so it never runs on the owner loop: a contended writer there would stall every
profile the loop serves. The async restore paths commit it in a worker first
(``session_local_adoption``); a sync restore on the loop that still finds it hands it to a tracked
worker, which publishes the session once it commits, and refuses this read.

name: _checked_entry
doc: *receipt*'s entry, once its route, origin and stored identity are this authority's.

name: owned_receipt
doc: *sid*'s stored receipt with its LOCAL source, route and entry, once all are this owner's.

name: _stray_route_target
doc:
*session_id* is a replacement the SessionStore's stale-route self-heal minted on this local
route before #140642: outside the receipt's lineage, never admitted, no transcript. The receipt
is the route's truth, so restoring it drops that entry instead of refusing the conversation
forever (``admission_conflict`` on every resume). Anything with history or ledger rows still
refuses: it is not provably a stray.

name: transcript_target
doc: The current physical transcript of logical *ref* (a local receipt's entry, else the tip).

name: display_rows
doc:
``(live row ids, display rows, truncated)`` of physical *target*, the live ids read first
(``local_history``'s fence). The display rows are the compression lineage as main's resume and the
REST transcript show it: every live row, and the newest compaction-archived rows that fit what the
live rows leave of ``RESUME_HISTORY_BYTES`` (``truncated`` when older ones were left out). A lineage
over the resume cap shows only the live rows.

name: _fit_archive
doc:
``(display rows kept, truncated)``: every live row of *display*, and its newest archived rows that fit
what *live_rows* leave of ``RESUME_HISTORY_BYTES``.

name: prepare_history
doc: ``local_history``'s lineage read, off the owner loop; the locked part re-reads only the live tip.

name: _merge_live_in_stored_order
doc:
The live rows in stored (``row_id``) order, each archived display row placed before the live
row it preceded in display order.

Display deduplication keeps a carried message at its FIRST copy's position, so after a rotated
compression the copied tail sits before the new summary. Clients take the live rows of a resume
as the transcript (the CLI's ``conversation_history``, ``/undo``'s prefix, rollback, ACP replay),
so the live subsequence must be the stored one; archived rows only anchor between live rows.

name: local_history
doc:
Display history of logical *ref*: every stored row the user saw, in display order.

A row outside the current physical transcript's active set (summarized away by a compression)
carries ``archived: true``: it is shown, never live, so no undo, retry or rewind may target it.
The rows without it are exactly the live transcript's, so a client choosing among live rows sees
what it saw before. That includes a micro-compaction merge (``display_metadata.model_only``): its
originals are the archived rows renderers show, so renderers skip the merge itself.

Each row carries its durable ``messages.id`` as ``row_id`` (the ``TranscriptMessage`` field
Desktop hydration and the legacy ``session.history`` already use): a ``session.mutate`` rewind
addresses its ``target_message_id`` by it, so a snapshot without it leaves no way to undo/retry.
*prepared* (``prepare_history``) is kept while every row it read as live still is; a rewind or
compaction since then re-reads the lineage here. When the byte budget left older archived rows out
(``display_rows``), the first row carries ``archived_truncated: true``.

name: reopen_local_session
doc:
The first admitted turn makes a finalized local session live again (#85303).

Mounting (``session.resume``) is a read and leaves ``ended_at``/``end_reason`` alone; the drain
calls this after the turn's local preflight, before execution routes it. A TUI shutdown / WS
disconnect / idle eviction stamps ``end_reason`` on the physical row. ``SessionStore`` reads any
stamped row as a stale route (#54878) and, since those reasons are not recoverable, answers the
turn with a FRESH session — the client keeps waiting on an id that never emits again. The classic
surfaces clear the stamp on the first real turn (tui_gateway ``_reopen_if_finalized``); the
authority must too. Only the lineage tip is reopened: a
compression parent or reset predecessor is never the physical target.

conn.execute(
