name: resolve_launch_route
doc:
Return ``params`` with an explicit launch model decoded the way every other startup path does.

The client sends the raw ``-m`` string; the authority owns the profile whose ``model_aliases:``
/ ``providers:`` define it. Unresolved, the alias name becomes the model sent to the profile
DEFAULT provider, and the alias's own endpoint/key are never used (#103933/#107191/#109440).
Same owner as HermesCLI / oneshot / the TUI factory: ``resolve_startup_model_route``. A plain
model id (no alias, no qualifier) is returned untouched; explicit ``--base-url``/``--api-key``
launches already carry their route.

name: resolve_titled_session
doc:
Exact session id first, then title (latest ``"<title> #N"`` continuation wins over
the bare title), projected forward to the compression tip. Only a local session the
actor may read is returned; a foreign or non-local match is ``not_found`` so another
principal's titles are never confirmed.

name: resolve_latest_session
doc:
The most recently active session of a surface family (``cli`` = classic CLI incl. its finite
one-shot runs, ``tui``), scoped to ``workspace`` (git root / cwd) first and then global: the
classic ``hermes -c`` / ``--resume latest`` rule (``hermes_cli.main._resolve_last_session``),
applied by the owner so the client opens no database. Only a local session the actor may read
counts; another principal's sessions are skipped, never confirmed.

name: title_new_session
doc:
User-provenance title on a just-created local session (auto-titling never overwrites it).
A concurrent creator that won the unique title is a conflict, not a silent orphan.

name: managed_policy
doc:
Bypass (safe / config-only) sessions always execute out of process; other local
sessions only under the explicit custom-provider opt-in.

The frozen creation snapshot, not current profile config, chooses execution.

name: _bootstrap
arguments: authority, ref, row, policy, scope, text=None

name: _worker_config
doc:
The frozen session config the child binds as its only config (``bind_worker_policy``).
``command_allowlist`` is approval state rather than launch policy: an ``always`` grant an
earlier worker of an ordinary session persisted, or one the operator removed by hand, comes
from the live profile file, as it did before the child's config was frozen. Bypass sessions
never read the profile.

name: _session_yolo
doc:
The route's bypass as the in-process turn arms it on the owner, the one place a revocation
is recorded: a ``--yolo`` launch seeded once per boundary, then the persisted ``/yolo`` copy.

name: worker_turn_scope
doc:
Child side of ``turn_v1``: bind what the in-process turn binds on the owner
(execute_finite_admission, the route's YOLO, the committed surface), so ``chat -q``/``-z``
never park a prompt, the session's current YOLO governs this child and a HUD / live-voice /
voice turn reaches the model as it does in process. Frames without it bind nothing.

name: _worker_env
doc:
Child env for the OWNING profile under multiplex: its HERMES_HOME plus its ``.env``
secrets over a scrubbed base, never the launch profile's process environment (the same
rule MCP stdio children and shell hooks follow) — except for the launch profile's own
worker, whose scope legitimately includes its frozen launch env. Single-profile gateways
inherit the process env byte-for-byte, exactly as before.

name: _launch_env_only_credentials
doc:
Credentials the LAUNCH profile's owner resolves from its frozen launch env
(``launch_secret_scope``: systemd ``Environment=`` / ``op run`` keys with no ``.env`` line) that
the scrub removed from *env* — the same mapping the owner's own ``get_secret`` reads for this
profile. Credential names only: non-credential names the constructor removed on purpose
(unbound session context, venv markers) stay removed, and Hermes-internal secrets
(``AUXILIARY_*_API_KEY``, relay auth) never reach a child. Only the launch home's worker calls
this; a routed home's worker sees its own files only.

name: _latched_stop_cause
doc:
The gateway restart/shutdown cause latched for this generation before its worker existed
(``run_runtime._stop_spawning_managed``), consumed once; None for a user's Stop.

name: _with_stop_cause
doc: The wire result carries no interruption cause; the owner recorded which stop it sent.

name: _settled_session_usage
doc: A managed turn's ``message.complete.usage``: the worker exits with its turn, so the session-cumulative counters come from the rows its usage writes committed. A worker that compresses mid-turn ends on a child of this reservation's session; the owner's execution row records that tip (compression moves it in the same transaction), so the path from the tip back to the reservation plus the reservation's own compression ancestors is summed, and stale siblings or the conversation a branch came from never count.

name: _execution_tip
doc: The session this worker execution last wrote to, as the owner's ledger records it.

significant_calls.callee: conn.execute('SELECT session_id FROM worker_executions WHERE execution_id=?', (execution_id,)).fetchone
significant_calls.expression: conn.execute('SELECT session_id FROM worker_executions WHERE execution_id=?', (execution_id,)).fetchone()
conn.execute('SELECT session_id FROM worker_executions WHERE execution_id=?', (execution_id,))

name: _continuation_path
doc: Ids from *start* to *tip* when *tip* reaches *start* through compression continuations only, else None.

name: _compression_ancestors
doc: Root-first ids of the sessions *session_id* continues by compression, excluding itself.

name: _mark_spawning
doc:
Mark the generation pre-worker: until the worker registers, a gateway stop has nothing to
signal, so it latches for this generation instead (#134889 GW-22). Set before ``@`` expansion,
which may await the network, so a Stop there is never lost.

name: _stopped_before_spawn
doc:
A Stop latched for this generation while it had no worker (a gateway stop during ``@``
expansion, or a user's Stop): consume it and record the interrupted result, never spawning.

name: _spawn_registered_worker
doc:
Spawn the turn's child and register it for Stops: ``(worker, process)``, or None when the spawn was cancelled (the
interrupted result is already recorded). The generation stays marked spawning until registration.

name: admit_managed
doc:
The ingress route into a managed worker. A removed folder is refused before a worker exists,
like the in-process runner: a worker failing in its policy scope reads as a LOST execution
(``unknown``) and parks every follower behind it.

significant_calls.expression:
live.event_stream.publish(ref.session_id, {'text': 'Worker execution is unknown.',
                'content': 'Worker execution is unknown.', 'admission_id': row['admission_id'], 'outcome': 'unknown',
                'status': 'error'})

name: _read_frames
doc: Reader thread body. It owns ``stdout``: no other thread closes it under a blocked read.

name: drain_stderr
doc:
Route the child's stderr (its tracebacks and redirected prints) into the profile's
bounded, redacted, private log instead of discarding it.

significant_calls.expression:
spawn_context_thread(drain_worker_stderr, name='managed-stderr-drain',
                                                 args=(self.process.stderr, path, self.process.pid, lambda: self.secrets))

name: _stop_budget
doc:
Seconds left of the ``ack`` window that opened at the first Stop. Pure: only
``control`` stamps ``stopped_at``, so a read before any Stop (the hello) never starts
the window a later Stop must receive in full.

name: next_frame
doc:
Read one frame. A requested Stop bounds supervision to ``ack`` seconds TOTAL from the
first Stop: a child that keeps emitting valid frames is escalated on the same deadline as a
silent one, instead of leaving the turn started behind it.

name: _signal_worker
doc:
Signal the verified interpreter, not only the handle: a launcher that exec-chained
or exited leaves the real worker outside the Popen's reach.

name: _signal_group
doc:
POSIX: signal the worker's whole process group (it leads one, WORKER_POPEN), so the tool
children a killed worker never reaps with _die_with_owner go too. Only while the leader is
unreaped and still leads its group; otherwise (Windows, gone) the handle alone.

name: worker_log_path
doc: The owning profile's sink, or None when the authority has no home path (test doubles).

name: _append
doc: Append under the per-file lock; rotate once the cap would be exceeded. 0600 always.

name: drain_worker_stderr
doc:
Thread body: read ``stream`` to EOF; ``scrub()`` returns this worker's exact secrets
(launch key, assignment secret) known so far. Never stops reading on a write failure.

name: _apply_reasoning
doc: ``/reasoning <level>`` (``None``: ``/reasoning reset``) as the chat would run it.

name: _pick_model
doc:
The chat's ``/model <name> [--provider p]`` resolution, guarded like a LOCAL pick, then committed
as its session override. Returns the receipt fields, or the guard's confirmation request.

name: apply_chat_pick
arguments: authority, ref, owner, live, params, *, principal_id
doc:
Apply a ``model`` / ``reasoning`` mutation to the messaging chat *live* mounted on *owner* (the
caller authorized control and holds its mutation lock). The fences are the mount's, the ones
``session.resume`` handed the viewer; comparing them with a compression segment's row refused a
pick on a compressed chat with ``stale_generation``. The receipt is keyed on that mount too: an
exact retry answers its stored receipt without re-applying the override, and the commit bumps the
mount's revision, so a retry of an older pick refuses ``revision_conflict``.

name: messaging_route_info
doc:
``model`` and the effort fields a messaging chat's next turn resolves, without building an agent
or resolving credentials: session ``/model`` > ``channel_overrides`` > config.yaml, and the session
``/reasoning`` > per-model > global level (``_resolve_session_reasoning_config``).

name: _authorize_import
doc: Import authorization; returns the imported session ids the write must claim.

name: _authorize_control
doc:
Control authorization; True when the session is cold history the write must claim. *owner* is
``_owner_ref``'s answer when the caller already resolved it (one read per mutation, not two).

name: _owner_ref
doc:
A metadata control (rename, archive, pin) or a delete names the listed row, which may be a
later reset or compression segment of a local conversation; the conversation's creation id owns
its live session, so control and the session gate are checked on that owner. The write itself
still names the listed row (a title or archive flag belongs to it; delete takes the lineage).
Gating only ``delete`` answered rename/archive of a compressed conversation with
``storage_unavailable`` (#134889 LC-22, as LC-12 on resume).

A transcript- or policy-changing operation (rewind, reset, compress, a policy pick) keeps the
listed id: its busy gate, generation fence and eviction are keyed by the session it writes, so
authorizing it on the owner while writing the segment would bypass the owner's FIFO. A segment
of a live owner therefore stays a named refusal for those, as on main. A delete of a messaging
conversation's later compression segment, or a model/reasoning pick on it, resolves to its
lineage root, where its lane's session lives (``messaging_owner_ref``, as resume does).

name: _mutate_session
arguments: authority, actor, ref, params, *, commit_lock=None, owner=None

name: _runtime_owns_authority
doc:
Whether *authority* is one of its own runner's authorities, so one process coordinates
both writes of a delete: the receipt commit to ``authority.db`` and the routing retire
through the runner store's routing index. Raw ``db_path`` equality only ever holds for the
launch home — the routing index is pinned to the launch home for every profile (#66887) —
so a multiplexed secondary profile's store never compares equal and each of its deletes
was refused with ``runtime_coordination_required`` (#138826).

name: write_mutation
arguments: authority, ref, params, editor_servers, *, principal_id, authorize_write=None, commit_lock=None
doc:
The writer phase of ``session.mutate``, and of the admission-start editor MCP re-freeze
(``refreeze_editor_mcp``): fenced prepare, the receipt commit, then its runtime projections.
The caller authorized the change and holds the session's locks; this takes neither.

name: _project_result
arguments: authority, ref, live, params, result, editor_servers, *, applied
doc:
A committed receipt's projections, under the writer's commit lock. They are idempotent reads
of the committed receipt, so exact retries repeat them (like delete's retirement); only the
one-shot event is fenced.

name: _project_committed
doc: Publish a committed receipt's runtime projections (safe to repeat on exact retry).

name: retire_live_sessions
doc:
Drop committed deletions from this owner's memory: routes, launch secrets, live sessions
and their cached agents. Shared by canonical delete and the owner-run bulk prune.
``require_fence``: refuse ``storage_unavailable`` when the shared routing fence could not be
written (canonical delete, whose exact retry replays the receipt and repeats this call).

name: compress_request
doc:
``session.mutate(compress)`` payload → the shared ``CompressRequest``.

A ``focus``-only payload is the raw ``/compress`` argument string (Ink/Desktop send it that
way, like ``session.compress`` always has), so it goes through the parser every native surface
uses: ``--preview`` stays read-only and ``here [N]`` stays a boundary instead of becoming a
focus topic. ``--aggressive`` has no canonical implementation and is refused before any write.

name: fire_post_compaction_hook
doc:
``post_compaction`` for a committed ``/compress``: this path summarizes outside the agent's
``compress_context``, so it fires here, after the commit, in the session's profile.

name: _request_tokens
doc:
Main's /compress request estimate: the agent's system prompt and tool schemas plus the messages.
No resident agent (a cold session): the prompt and tools[] pin the session row stores, which the
next agent restores and sends, so the figure matches what main's resident agent reported.

name: _current_route
doc:
``(config, route)`` the session runs now, both from ONE read of the owning profile.

A following session runs the profile's current route, so its frozen creation endpoint beside
the current key would send that key to a host the profile left. Main switched from the live
runtime's whole tuple (``tui_gateway.model_switch._current_model_runtime``). The provider is
the configured name: a named ``providers:`` entry resolves to the bare ``custom`` class, and a
pick on the same entry must not read as a route change. Only the session's own route counts:
a fallback is where a turn lands, not what the user switches from. A route that cannot
authenticate here must not block leaving it: like main's agent-less ``--provider`` path, the
pick then switches from the configured provider alone and resolves its own target.

name: _provider_resolution_config
doc:
*config* with the owning profile's CURRENT named providers over its frozen ones, used only to
resolve and freeze a pick. Reads this owner's own config.yaml (never another profile's); a
frozen entry the profile no longer declares stays resolvable. A session that bypasses the
profile (``ignore_user_config``, implied by safe mode) resolves only its own frozen config.
``${VAR}`` refs expand against the profile's CURRENT ``.env``, not the daemon's start env.

name: _custom_provider_name
doc: The runtime's canonical identity: ``My Provider`` and ``my-provider`` are one provider.

name: _selected_provider_key_env
doc: Return a selected ``providers.<slug>`` credential pointer, never its secret value.

name: _freeze_selected_provider
doc:
Copy only the picked named provider's declaration into the frozen session route.

The next turn resolves from the session's own configuration, not a later profile edit. Private
fields move to the policy's secret store, as policy creation does; nothing else moves. Returns
``(secrets, retired)``: the entry's private values and every ``(section, key)`` whose previous
private subtree they replace, plus ``moved``: ``{old (section, index): new}`` for an unrelated entry
the pick displaced. A legacy entry from the profile is frozen at its profile index (the path cold
recovery re-reads); an equivalent earlier spelling is blanked, never left to win.

name: _provider_key_slug
doc: A ``providers:`` key's canonical identity: ``Review Prov`` and ``review-prov`` are one.

name: _alias_credential
doc:
``(key_env, source_path, literal_key)`` the direct alias a switch resolved declares for its own
endpoint, read from THIS owner's config.yaml: the file a restarted owner re-reads, never the
process-global alias cache another served profile may refill after the switch. A raw
``api_key: "${VAR}"`` is the pointer ``VAR``; ``(None, None, None)`` when it declares none.

name: _selection_guard_refusal
arguments: authority, live, payload, snapshot, current, result
doc:
The shared selection-guard registry (cost, data-policy, large-context switch) runs before the
commit. A flagged target is refused with ``status: confirmation_required`` and a ``confirm``
token bound to the resolved target, the selection it replaces and the session revision; nothing
is written. Only that exact token in ``payload['confirm']`` applies it: a stale or foreign
token (target re-resolved elsewhere, another switch landed, a turn settled) gets a fresh
refusal, never a silent apply.

name: prepare_reasoning
doc:
``/reasoning <level>`` for this session: the level ``build_policy`` freezes at creation. ``None``
(``/reasoning reset``) gives the level back to the profile.

name: prepare_workspace
doc: Move to project: execution cwd and TERMINAL_CWD move together (restore_policy's invariant).

name: prepare_edit_policy
doc:
Main's ACP modes (Default / Accept Edits / Don't Ask) as the session's frozen edit approval
policy. Only an ACP session's edits ask an editor; selecting the current policy writes nothing.

name: _choose_run
doc:
A refused claim (5079) or a blocked one with nothing else to run on (5080) leaves no chat, so
the install stays due.

name: _claim_before_run
doc:
``onboarding.run: true`` on disk before the welcome-trial claim, so a crash after the claim still
opens onboarding next launch.

name: keep_from_discard
doc:
``attach``, after its last other await: a chat a fresh launch was about to delete is kept. The
take-back itself never yields, so the viewer joins in the same loop step and a later start sees it
watched; a start claims only on the loop. A delete in flight holds the lock across its write, so
that wait runs off the loop and the take-back is retried after it.

name: _settle_runs
doc:
The new chat's record and title, and the end of every other open run; returns the chats it
deleted. One open run at a time: the kept run is open before the others end, so the install flag
never closes in between.

name: _discard_unfinished_runs
doc:
A new launch's start: the runs the app was closed on never count as done. A chat no window
watches (still in *discards*) is deleted the way ``session.delete`` deletes it, which ends its run
(``deleted``) and tells every window; the caller retires the deleted ids from the authority. A chat a
window reopened, or one a turn still writes (the delete refuses it), is kept, and its run ends as
``replaced`` so it is never resumed.

name: ending_run_on_delete
doc:
*commit* (the canonical delete's receipt transaction) wrapped so deleting the chat that holds
the live run ends that run (``deleted``) and tells every window, as the sidecar's
``session.delete`` did. Returns the receipt.

name: _withdraw_setup_cards
doc: Close the card still waiting in a chat whose run just ended; its answer would be refused.

name: skip
doc:
Skip setup: end the chat's run and close the card that waits. The card's asker reads the
skipped record when it wakes (``setup_beat``).

name: arm_onboarding_turn
doc:
The onboarding chat's per-turn inputs on an authority-owned local turn: the turn note (which
card is closed and how to bring it back) appended to the API-only notes, and the scripted opening
returned for ``run_conversation(prelude=...)``. Nothing for a chat without ``setup_beat``.

name: is_viewer_input
doc:
A row a session viewer submitted through ``session.submit`` (a client's own prompt), not a producer
admission: ``local_automation_v1`` (plugin injection, delegation completions, process and watch notices,
/loop, heartbeat), a hosted-room task (``hosted:`` request id) or any other envelope.

name: register
arguments: self, session_id, route, generation, data, *, timeout_s=None

name: respond
arguments: self, session_id, generation, prompt_id, response, *, kind='approval'

name: _is_live_system_guard
doc: Test-isolation guard: must stay a loud failure and is never cached.

name: retire_runtime_sessions
doc: Publish committed retirement; durable fences reject delayed saves.

name: fence_retired_routes
doc:
Durably retire *session_ids* in the routing index's own database (fences + route
drop in one transaction). A delete committed in another profile's store fences only that
store; the shared index lives in the launch home, so its saves need the fence here too,
keyed by the deleting profile's routing *namespace* (``retire_gateway_routes``).
Raises when the routing store cannot take the fence: the delete must not report success.

name: strip_retired_mirror_routes
doc:
Drop from an existing sessions.json every route a routing save now skips as retired
(``route_retired``, the check ``replace_gateway_routing_entries`` applies), only those naming
*session_ids* when given. Runs whatever ``write_sessions_json`` says and never creates the
file: the mirror is derived, and a retired route left in it would come back through the
next start's legacy import once a prune's fence ages out.

name: _open_session_db_for_active_scope
doc:
SessionDB for the active profile scope. ``db_path`` pins the store; otherwise
``_default_db_path()`` follows the context-local HERMES_HOME (resolved per call so
multiplexed profiles reach their own store). Handles are cached per path; failed opens enter
a bounded backoff during which callers keep using the JSONL fallback.

Resolving here rather than once in ``__init__`` is the whole fix for #88532: it lets the scoping
that the multiplexed inbound path already performs actually reach session storage.

name: _pinned_db
doc: Return the explicitly pinned DB (``store._db = x``), else ``_DB_UNPINNED``.

name: _db
doc:
The SessionDB for the active profile scope, or a pinned override. Assigning ``store._db``
pins that value for every subsequent read (tests install a fake or disable the DB with
``store._db = None``); unpinned, each read resolves the scope so a multiplexed profile's
writes reach its own store.

name: _routing_db
doc:
The one store that owns the routing index, whatever scope is active. ``_entries`` is one
flat dict holding every profile's keys, so it must persist to ONE file (``_routing_home``),
not whichever profile is scoped — otherwise a mid-turn rewrite and the unscoped startup
load see different copies and crash markers under a secondary profile go unrecovered. A
pinned handle still wins; bare test instances lacking the handle cache report no DB.

Reading it through ``_db`` made that file whichever profile happened to be scoped at the time: a
whole-index rewrite during one profile's turn copied every other profile's routing rows into that
profile's store, and startup — which runs unscoped — then loaded a different copy than the one the
last writer produced. See #66887.

name: _named_profile_for_key
doc:
The non-default profile that owns *session_key*, or None (ambient store is authoritative:
multiplexing off, or legacy ``agent:main``). Deliberately does NOT cover "that profile has
no directory" — ownership and resolvability are separate questions for ``_db_for_key``.

name: _profile_home_for_key
doc:
HERMES_HOME of the profile owning *session_key*, or None (no named owner or
unresolvable).

name: _db_for_key
doc:
The SessionDB holding *session_key*'s rows, whatever scope is active (the owning profile
is encoded in the key). ``_db`` follows the ambient HERMES_HOME that only the inbound message
path installs; unscoped background work (expiry watcher) would otherwise write profile rows
into the ROOT store until the stale-route self-heal drops a live conversation.

Background work runs unscoped while operating on every profile's keys out of the single process-wide
``_entries`` dict — ``_session_housekeeping_watcher`` is the clearest case — so it reads and writes the
ROOT store for rows that actually live under ``profiles/<name>/state.db``. The two writers then
drift apart on the same logical session until the routing index disagrees with the row and the
#54878 self-heal drops a live conversation (#66887).

name: _owner_key_for_session_id
_db_for_session_id
doc:
The SessionDB holding *session_id*'s row (owner from the index or a pre-published hint;
unknown ids fall back to the ambient store).

name: close_all_db_handles
doc:
Close every SessionDB handle this store opened (one per path). Closing only ``store._db``
would strand secondary profiles' handles with their WAL lock held ('database is locked' on
restart). Drained under the lock, closed outside it; a pinned handle is the pinner's.

name: _ensure_loaded
doc: Load sessions index from disk if not already loaded.

name: _entry_locked
doc: Load the index and return the entry for *session_key*. Lock held.

name: _routing_scope
doc:
Namespace for this store's gateway_routing rows: the resolved sessions_dir, so stores
with different dirs never share entries.

name: _routing_db_method
doc: Bound ``_routing_db.<name>`` if the handle exists and has it, else None.

name: record_chat_labels
doc:
Persist *source*'s ``chat_name`` / ``chat_topic`` as the chat's current labels, at the
moment they are observed; True once written. A session origin cannot answer "what is this
chat called now": it is written when its session is created, which can be after a newer
observation (a delayed first turn), and a reset inherits it under a fresh ``created_at``.

False when there is no database handle right now (open failed, backoff, JSONL fallback):
nothing was written, so the caller must not treat these labels as recorded.

name: chat_labels
doc:
The ``(chat_name, chat_topic)`` last recorded for a chat, or None when none was. Raises
when the store cannot be read, including when there is no database handle right now:
"unreadable now" is not "never labelled".

name: _load_routing_rows_locked
doc:
Load state.db routing entries into ``_entries``; False when there is no loader or the
load failed (warned). Lock held.

name: _routing_entry_from_json
doc: Parse one gateway_routing row; None (with a warning) when invalid.

name: _ensure_loaded_locked
_import_legacy_sessions_json
doc:
Legacy import: sessions.json fills only keys the DB lacks. Lock held. Returns how many
mirror entries it skipped as retired routes.

name: _prune_stale_sessions_locked
doc:
Remove routing entries whose session has ended in state.db (startup, lock held). Stale ==
``end_reason IS NOT NULL``; rows absent from the DB are kept; a ``None`` DB handle is a
no-op; DB errors are non-fatal.

name: _stale_entry_verdict
doc:
For a routing entry whose row has ended: ``"prune"``, a replacement entry (repoint), or
None (keep as-is).

name: _entries_as_dicts
doc: Serializable snapshot of ``_entries``. Lock held.

name: _save
doc: Persist the routing index while the caller holds ``_lock``.

name: _next_routing_generation_locked
doc:
Bump and return the shared routing counter (lock held). Full snapshots AND single-entry
fast saves MUST allocate from this one counter: the stale-write protection is a total order
over serialization times and silently breaks otherwise.

name: _reconcile_recovered_routing_locked
doc: Merge authoritative rows after a fallback-only startup load.

name: _snapshot_routing_locked
doc: Capture immutable routing data and a monotonic generation.

name: _persist_routing_data
arguments: self, data: dict[str, Any], generation: int
doc: Serialize all whole-index writers through one durable write lock.

name: _save_sessions_json
doc: Write the legacy sessions.json mirror of the routing index (atomic + fsync).

name: _save_entries
doc: Snapshot latest state under ``_lock`` and persist after releasing it.

name: _save_entry
arguments: self, session_key: str, *, entry_data: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, lock_held: bool=False
doc:
Persist ONE routing entry via UPSERT — the per-turn fast path (a full rewrite fsyncs a
multi-MB sessions.json). The key -> session_id mapping never changes here: structural
transitions use the full rewrite (which also refreshes the sessions.json mirror; it may lag
in metadata only). The revision comes from the shared routing generation counter; under
``_save_lock`` the upsert is skipped if a full snapshot or a newer fast save of this key
already persisted (the reverse case lives in ``_persist_routing_data``). No DB or a failed
upsert falls back to the full rewrite. ``entry_data`` persists a candidate BEFORE it is
published to the live entry (failure-atomic transitions); the fallback carries it too.

name: session_pinned
doc: Whether *field* is the session's own choice: its last committed session edit, else *launched*.

name: pin_reasoning_effort
doc:
Write an explicit session reasoning level into *config*: it wins over a per-model default
(``reasoning_overrides``), at creation, on ``/reasoning`` and on a model pick that carries one.
A *session* edit also records the pin.

name: profile_config
doc: The owning profile's current ``config.yaml`` (its present sections), read fresh.

name: unpin_reasoning
doc:
``/reasoning reset``: the level is *profile*'s (its current config) again, re-read every turn by a
following session and on each resume by any other; a create-time ``reasoning`` included.

name: created_surface
doc:
``created_source`` for a policy or live label.

``local`` and ``unknown`` are not surfaces. A label stored as ``local`` maps
through ``SURFACES`` (``gui`` is ``desktop``). Any other label, including
``tool`` and ``oneshot``, is kept as itself: created_source is provenance.

name: _refuse
doc:
One named refusal: the launch field the check read, and why it failed.

``reason`` stays the bounded wire code every caller compares as a string; ``field`` and
``detail`` are what tells ~20 different create checks apart, in the client and in the
gateway log, without a second run to find out which one fired (``RuntimeStoreError`` bounds
and flattens both).

name: profile_target
doc: (model, provider) a profile config selects; 'auto' is no provider (main's _config_model_target).

name: model_route
doc: ``(provider, endpoint)`` identity of a ``model:`` block: what an endpoint-bound credential belongs to.

name: bound_route_holds
doc:
True when *block* (resolved in *config*) is the route *bound* was bound to, *bound* resolved in
the config it was bound in: a respelled provider on one endpoint is one route, and a named entry
whose ``base_url`` moved is another. An ``auto``/unset side keeps the literal comparison: a
credential never follows a route the resolver picks later.

name: entry_serves
doc:
False when *block* pins a ``base_url`` that the config entry its credential comes from no longer
serves in *config*: its named provider (``providers:`` / ``custom_providers:``), or the alias its
``api_key_from`` points into. That entry's key (inline, ``key_env``, ``key_cmd``) authenticates the
entry's own endpoint, so a pick held on the old one ends rather than carry the new key there.

name: _held_pick
doc:
A pick that still holds keeps its selection; on the profile's own endpoint the rest of the
``model:`` block (a rotated key included) is the profile's. Another endpoint never gets it.

name: present_sections
doc:
A bare ``gateway:`` key parses as YAML null; like load_config's merge (#58277), treat it as absent so
``cfg.get('gateway', {}).get(...)`` reads the default instead of crashing a fresh install's first turn.

name: build_policy
arguments: params, config, *, private_secrets=None, profile_terminal=True, workspace_posture=False, client_local=False

name: terminal_uses_host_cwd
doc:
Whether the terminal works in the session's host cwd: the local backend, or docker mounting it at
``/workspace``. ssh, modal and the other sandboxes resolve their own cwd.

name: _profile_workspace_cwd
doc:
A NAMED profile's configured ``terminal.cwd``, which beats a client cwd the Desktop only inherited
(``cwd_explicit: false``; main's ``_completion_cwd``). Placeholders and missing dirs are unset.

name: _without_auto_pick
doc: `provider: auto` is the thin client's "no pick" sentinel: the profile's route stands as configured.

name: _keeps_profile_route
doc:
Whether a provider pick resolves to the profile's own route, so its endpoint and key pins stay.

The same resolved provider under another spelling (`vllm` for `custom`, `deep-infra` for
`deepinfra`, `custom:<name>` for a named entry) is the same route. A block with an endpoint
and no provider (or `auto`) already routes to `custom` there.

name: _with_entry_pick
doc:
*params* with a provider pick of the held entry's bare config key spelled as its ``custom:<key>``.

A configured entry keyed like a canonical built-in (`providers: deepseek`) is shadowed by the
built-in in raw provider resolution, so the bare spelling would route, and be frozen, as a
different provider than the entry the profile runs (#140107). Only the held entry's bare key
is that entry (Desktop's guard). A keyed entry's display name is not; a keyless legacy
``custom_providers:`` entry's is (``configured_entry_key``). Other picks stay as they came.

name: _apply_launch_overrides
doc: Validate the explicit model/agent launch overrides and fold them into *config*.

name: _resolve_toolsets
arguments: params, config, source, safe_mode, coding_posture=False, bypass=False
doc:
Validate explicit toolsets and return the session's enabled toolset set. Without a pick, a
*coding_posture* session runs ``focus_toolsets`` instead of the profile default while the profile
stays on ``focus``; the gateway decides it, never the client.

name: _in_coding_workspace
doc:
Whether *cwd* selects the coding posture (``agent.coding_context: focus`` in a code workspace).
A detection failure keeps the profile default rather than refusing the session.

name: launch_skills
doc:
The validated `-s/--skills` identifiers of a create request (empty when absent). Skills
live in the profile, which a bypass launch must never read: refused there, not dropped.

name: render_launch_skills
doc:
`-s/--skills` preload blocks for a new session, rendered ONCE at creation and frozen in its
policy (the CLI's startup preload). Blocking skill-tree reads: callers run it off the owner
loop. A typo among good names is logged and skipped, like the CLI; none resolving refuses.

name: accept_launch_hooks
doc:
`--accept-hooks` / `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1` on a launch: consent to the profile's configured
shell hooks in the per-user allowlist (no prompt; kept in memory if that write fails), which
the open's ``refresh_profile_hooks`` then registers. A bypass launch has no profile hooks to
consent to, so the flag is a no-op there rather than a refusal. Allowlist I/O: off the loop.

name: refresh_profile_hooks
doc:
Bring this owner's shell hooks in step with the profile on every local session open
(create and resume): hooks added to ``config.yaml`` or approved since the gateway started
register, removed or revoked ones stop firing, as each new CLI process did on main. Reads the
owner home's LIVE config (as session creation does), never the session's frozen copy: the
registry is shared by every session and surface of this profile. Consent comes from the
allowlist (the launching client's TTY prompt, or ``accept_launch_hooks``) or an opt-in in force
on the gateway itself; this never prompts. A bypass launch registers nothing (main's safe mode
registered none). Config read + allowlist I/O: run off the loop.

name: register_worker_hooks
doc:
Worker side of the same contract: tools run in the managed child, so its own plugin
manager needs the session's shell hooks and outbound webhooks, registered from the frozen
config with the launch's consent (a Kanban attempt always consents), as the classic one-shot
CLI registered both at startup. Bypass sessions register nothing (the safe policy also
refuses inside both registrars).

name: bind_launch_key
arguments: authority, session_id, policy, api_key, *, config_secrets=None, owner_key=False, client_request=None
doc:
CLI keys live only in this authority lifetime, never its durable receipt.

Restart deliberately revokes them. History remains readable; inference must
report launch_credentials_unavailable, never select a profile fallback key.
An ``owner_key`` (an alias's, expanded by the owner) of the same create request as the attempt
holding the slot (``same_create_retry``, its ``client_env`` in ``client_request``) takes the held
key: a ``.env`` rotation between overlapping attempts is not a changed request, and the policy
then fingerprints the key it runs with.

name: _key_slot
doc: The in-memory slot of a durable credential ref (``<instance>:<epoch>:<sid>[#<fingerprint>]``).

name: rebind_launch_key
doc:
``session.resume`` re-supplying a launch-only key after an owner restart revoked it
(call after authorizing *session*, a SessionRef).

Only a session launched with a key can take one, and only that same key (its durable
fingerprint); anything else is an override of the frozen route and is refused. Like the
original, the key lives in this authority's memory only.

name: _secret_refs
doc: The launch-key slots and config-secret references the live LOCAL policies of *session_ids* name.

name: release_launch_secrets
doc:
Drop retired sessions' launch keys, frozen config secrets and editor MCP servers.

They live only in this authority's memory for the session's lifetime; a deleted session can
never run again, so keeping them would hold its credentials until the process exits. A branch's
policy names its parent's slots, so a slot named after a retired session stays while a live
policy references it, and then until restart, which revokes every launch secret anyway. Only
slots named after *session_ids* are released, so the set never exceeds release by name: no later
sweep, and a binding not yet published always sits under its own live session's name. Call
before the retired sessions leave ``authority.sessions``.

name: route_launch_key
doc:
The launch key a turn on *config* (the route it runs, a followed profile's included) sends.
A launch key authenticates the frozen route it was bound with: once the followed profile
supersedes that pick and moves to another endpoint, the key stays behind with its route.

name: restore_policy
doc: Reject incomplete private policy rather than rebuilding from current defaults.

name: _valid_client_env
doc: A stored client map (names to strings) or its rules (``kind=list``: rule names to string lists).

name: policy_turn_toolsets
doc:
A local turn's toolsets: the policy's current set, plus ``onboarding`` for an onboarding chat
(``agent.onboarding_session.onboarding_chat_toolsets``).

name: local_desktop_turn
doc:
*scope* (the profile scope a turn enters), also marked as work for the local Desktop when the
turn belongs to a Desktop chat its creator's connection declared local (``stage_local_session``);
any other turn gets *scope* untouched. Read from the live policy without raising: a cold policy
is restored, or refused, by the turn.

name: workspace_ready
doc:
Readiness, not structure: a removed workspace keeps the chat readable and movable, but no
turn runs in a missing directory.

name: workspace_unavailable_result
doc:
A failed, never-run turn for a session whose frozen working directory is gone. Nothing ran
and an unchanged resend fails the same way, so the reply names the folder and the way out
instead of the generic "something went wrong" apology.

name: bind_turn_workspace
doc:
Make the session's frozen workspace its terminal cwd override for this turn's tools (#140665).

The client's cwd (or ``--in DIR``) is frozen into the policy at admission, but the terminal tool
mounts ``resolve_task_overrides(task_id)['cwd']`` into a per-session Docker container. Before the
one-gateway runtime each ``hermes chat`` was its own process with its own ``TERMINAL_CWD``; now the
turn runs here, so register it under the turn's own task id (inside the turn's routed scope, which
qualifies the key). Docker mounting the host cwd only: the local backend already runs in the
policy's ``TERMINAL_CWD``, and ssh and the other sandboxes keep their own cwd. Re-registered only
when the workspace changed, so an agent's ``cd`` inside the session survives later turns.

name: unbind_turn_workspace
doc:
Drop the workspace override :func:`bind_turn_workspace` registered for *task_id*, and the cwd
record it seeded. Only its own entry (tagged ``workspace_key``): an ACP/TUI workspace or an RL
image override registered by someone else under the same id stays.

name: release_session_workspaces
doc:
Session teardown: drop each session's workspace binding under its owning profile's scope (the
key the turn bound it under), so the override table does not grow with every closed session.

name: profile_read_scope
doc:
Hold ONE read of a following session's profile for every resolution inside, as a turn's
``policy_scope`` does, without that scope's workspace and terminal setup (a session control
reads the route, it runs nothing).

name: active_policy
doc:
The frozen launch policy of the turn executing in this context, or ``None`` (standalone
serve / messaging turns). Consumers read it instead of re-deriving from live config.

name: effective
doc:
``(config, model)`` the next turn runs, both from ONE read of the owning profile when following
(the turn's policy scope holds that read): a route never pairs one profile's model with another's
endpoint. Explicit choices (create-time reasoning / tier / toolsets, a session ``/reasoning`` until
reset, a pick that still holds) are applied over the followed defaults; frozen secrets of followed
sections are never recovered.

name: read_profile
doc:
The owning profile's current config for a following session, else None; inside this policy's
turn scope, the turn's one read.

name: current_toolsets
doc:
The next turn's toolsets from its resolved *config*: a following session without an explicit
toolset pick runs the profile's current selection (main #124211), else the frozen launch set.

name: current_reasoning_config
doc:
The next turn's reasoning: a typed session /reasoning (the messaging handler's override), else
the profile's current effort when following, else the frozen one.

name: current_service_tier
doc: The next turn's tier: a typed session /fast, else the policy's (frozen, or the profile's when following).

name: current_model
doc: The model this session's next turn runs: the profile's current default when following.

name: yolo
doc:
`hermes chat --yolo`: this session's dangerous-command approvals are bypassed, exactly the
scope `/yolo` gives a messaging chat; never the process-wide HERMES_YOLO_MODE.

name: pass_session_id
doc: `--pass-session-id`: the session id rides the agent's system prompt.

name: checkpoints_enabled
doc: Frozen `checkpoints.enabled` (`--checkpoints` folds into it); legacy bool form accepted.

name: verbose
doc:
`hermes chat -v`: the session's agent runs with quiet_mode off, so its status lines reach the
viewer (``agent.print``) as main's in-process verbose agent printed them.

name: run_budget_seconds
doc: Frozen `agent.run_budget_seconds` (`--run-budget` folds into it); None = no budget.

name: _defined
doc: The value *root* defines at *path*, else ``_ABSENT`` when the key is simply not there.

name: _route_paths
doc:
Secret paths the session's own route authenticates with: its ``model:`` block, a direct alias's
key (``api_key_from``) and the one ``providers:`` / ``custom_providers:`` entry the runtime's own
named-provider selection routes its provider through.

name: _legacy_identities
doc:
Every whole-policy hash a gateway older than ``bound`` could have stamped for *policy*: the
current hash, plus each subset of the later fields dropped while they are at their defaults.

name: _route_owner
doc:
The config path of the ROUTE block a secret at *path* rides with, else None. Every route shape a
consumer reads: ``model:`` and its aliases (``model.aliases.<n>``, ``model_aliases.<n>``), both
fallback sections in dictionary (one route) and list form, and each ``auxiliary.<task>`` route with
its ``fallback_chain`` entries. A secret nested deeper in a route (headers, extra_body) rides with it.

name: _owner_block
doc:
The config path of the block whose endpoint the secret at *path* authenticates: a route block
(_route_owner) or a provider entry as a whole, else the secret's own parent block.

name: _resolved
doc: ``(provider_identity, url)`` the route *block* at *owner* is actually sent to.

name: _binding
doc:
Digest of the endpoint the secret at *path* authenticates in the frozen *config* (a terminal-scope
secret, ``path[0] is None``, authenticates no endpoint).

name: _check_scope
doc:
Refuse, by name, a reference from another home or profile, or a secret whose endpoint the policy
moved without re-binding it. A change to anything else in the policy (model name, reasoning, toolsets,
an unrelated provider or MCP server, a policy field a later release added) is not a credential change.

name: secrets_moved
doc:
Whether *secrets* (the private values of *sections*, as the profile has them now) differ from the ones
the durable reference *ref* froze there, by fingerprint. Unknown for an in-memory reference: False.

name: recover_config_secrets
doc:
The frozen config secrets; entries under a *skip* section are neither re-read nor checked. Every
caller of a following session skips its followed sections: the live profile supplies them, so a key
rotation there is not a revoked launch credential.

name: _current_custom_path
doc:
*path* (``custom_providers[i]...``, an index into the frozen list) re-pointed at the profile's
entry of the SAME canonical identity (``custom_provider_slug``), wherever a reorder moved it.
An entry the profile no longer declares maps to no index (absent), never to whatever entry now
sits at ``i``, unless that entry is the same endpoint renamed in place (the fingerprint then decides,
as on main). A frozen entry with no name has no identity: its index is all there is.

name: _entry_owner_path
doc: The ``providers:`` / ``custom_providers:`` entry a fallback entry authenticates through.

name: disable_dropped_secrets
doc:
Disable, in the session's effective *config*, whatever authenticated with a *dropped* frozen
secret, instead of leaving it with a null key (null means 'resolve another credential' and would
send another account's key). A fallback using it is removed from the chain; an ``auxiliary.<task>``
override using it is replaced by the session's primary route (``provider: main``). Never substitutes.

name: refreshed_policy
doc:
``(policy, secrets, replaced)``: *policy* with its config-derived fields from *live* (the profile's
config) and *terminal* (its terminal scope), or only its MCP servers (*mcp_only*); explicit picks (launch
flags, the *picked* policy edits) stay. *secrets* are the refreshed sections' private values, *replaced*
the sections (``None``: terminal) whose stored private values they supersede. *policy* itself when
nothing moved; a rotated private value alone (its redacted tree unchanged) moves it.

name: _settings
doc: Follow the config-derived settings into *config*; the toolsets they select.

name: _mcp_servers
arguments: policy, config, live, toolsets, secrets, replaced
doc:
The profile's MCP servers as this session's own selection takes them now (its explicit pick or platform
allowlist, ``no_mcp`` and disabled entries respected): their definitions into *config*, private values split
off as build_policy does (a managed worker binds this config, so it connects exactly these), and their
names into the returned toolsets. An editor-MCP session keeps its frozen servers.

name: _server_name
doc: The server a pick name selects: ``mcp-<server>`` is its bare alias unless a server has that name.

name: _prepare
doc:
Off the owner loop: the stored policy, its refresh from this profile home's files, and the generation
it was derived at. None when the session takes no refresh or nothing moved. *adopt_only*: the adoption
of a frozen Bot Chat alone, without the config-derived settings (a later open on the same attachment).

name: _rebind
arguments: authority, session_id, old, policy, fresh, replaced
doc:
Re-bind the private values like a policy mutation: policy identity covers config and terminal, and the
refreshed sections' private values are the profile's current ones (the stored ones there are neither
re-read nor checked: a rotated key is what the refresh picks up, not a revoked credential). A policy
that follows its profile from this open on keeps none of its followed sections' frozen values.

name: _pending_adoptions
doc:
Frozen Bot Chats an open found to adopt but could not commit (a turn running or queued, a concurrent
edit): the next open retries, whether or not that client is already attached.

name: refresh_settled
doc:
Wait out a refresh of *session_id* in flight. Its commit lands before its terminal cleanup (a sandbox
teardown can take 10-15 s) and its publication; an attach meanwhile would find the stored policy ahead
of the live one, which restore_local_session refuses.

name: commit_refresh
doc:
Commit an idle local session's refresh as its next policy generation: True when one was committed,
False when nothing moved. Raises the store's refusal (``session_busy`` while a turn runs or waits).
One refresh per session at a time, run to its publication even when the caller is cancelled: a second
waits for the first, then usually finds nothing moved.

name: refresh_resumed_policy
doc:
Commit the config refresh of an idle local session before it is attached. Never fails the resume:
a busy session, a revoked launch credential or an unreadable profile keeps the stored policy. Only a turn
running or queued (or admitted during the commit) is expected; anything else is a WARNING.

*attached*: this client already holds the session (Desktop's warm reopen). The settings refresh is once
per attachment, but a frozen Bot Chat whose adoption a busy open refused is adopted on any later open.

name: drop_session_terminal
doc:
The session's own cached terminal environments (keyed by its route, or its ids under per-session
isolation): the terminal tool reuses one by key whatever backend built it. A profile-shared one stays.
Its recorded cwd (keyed by its route or task id) goes too: it wins over the new binding's directory.

name: sanitize_prompt_pin
doc:
Validated durable snapshot of the exact ephemeral inputs reused by internal turns.

``redact_pii`` is the ``privacy.redact_pii`` the context bytes were rendered under; a pin
without it cannot prove which privacy policy produced them and is refused.

name: set_prompt_pin
arguments: self, session_key: str, pin: dict[str, Any], *, expected_session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Persist effective prompt inputs without letting a stale turn cross a boundary.

The candidate is durable before the in-memory entry is published. The expected session id
is the turn's launch identity: a concurrent reset or resume makes this a no-op instead of
writing the old conversation's system bytes onto the new one.

name: get_prompt_pin
doc: Return the prompt pin only while the route still owns the caller's session.

name: _interactive
doc:
The session's frozen launch source (a local session's row records it) names a local surface.
Callers hold the stream lock: one plain read per session, cached (``get_session`` flushes token
counts, a write). Under WAL it takes the lock-free reader pool, as ``_pending_rows`` does there.

significant_calls.callee: conn.execute('SELECT source FROM sessions WHERE id=?', (session_id,)).fetchone
significant_calls.expression: conn.execute('SELECT source FROM sessions WHERE id=?', (session_id,)).fetchone()
conn.execute('SELECT source FROM sessions WHERE id=?', (session_id,))

name: queued_controls
doc:
The queued-row verbs this owner serves for ``row``: a client shows only these (an older owner
lists none, so its clients show none).

name: pending_rows
doc:
The pending rows a viewer is shown, plus each queued admission in transfer to the running
claim: listed ``started`` and ``steering``, because it may still go back to its queue place, and a
client must not retire an admission it no longer sees. The caller holds the stream lock.

name: steer_transfers
doc:
``{admission_id: delivered}`` handed to this claim; the caller holds the stream lock. Read by
the claim's settlement after its execution returned, when no transfer can still be delivered.
The agent settles each one by its ticket (the admission id), never by its text: one no drain of
the turn consumed (still buffered, or dropped unread) reads undelivered and goes back to its queue.

name: _register
doc: ``{admission_id: delivered}`` for the claim ``generation``.

name: _receiving_agent
doc:
The agent the running claim adopted, while that claim still executes. None before adoption (a
latched text would be dropped if construction then failed) and for a turn with no steer seam.

name: _deliver
arguments: authority, session_id, generation, agent, admission_id, text
doc:
Hand the committed text to the claim's agent; the caller holds the stream lock. False once the
claim stopped executing (its settlement then decides the row) or its agent refused the text.

name: publish_transfers
doc:
After the claim's settlement: each admission it carried publishes the outcome it settled to
(``steered``, or ``cancelled`` for an interrupted transfer, as a turn's completion reports it).

name: replace_queued
doc:
Cancel the queued admission and admit the edit at the FIFO tail under a new identity, in one
write. The replacement is bound to the admission it retired: an exact retry (same old admission,
same new ``submission_id``) answers the same new admission; any other old admission under that
``submission_id`` is ``admission_conflict``, decided inside the admission's own transaction.

name: _write
arguments: db, target, row_id, newest_role, emoji, author

name: _origin_json
doc: ``source.to_dict()`` as JSON, or None when absent/unserializable.

name: _resolve_profile_for_key
doc:
Profile namespace for session keys: None when multiplexing is off (legacy
``agent:main``), else the pinned identity's runtime profile, ``source.profile`` or the
active profile.

name: _profile_from_session_key
doc: Extract the profile namespace encoded in a gateway session key.

name: _recovered_row_allowed_for_active_profile
arguments: self, *, requested_session_key: str, recovered: dict[str, Any]
doc:
Prevent a gateway from reviving another profile's row. Single-profile: the row's
namespace must match the ACTIVE profile. Multiplexed: it must match the requested key's
namespace (the active profile is meaningless there). Keyless rows stay adoptable.

Multiplexed: several profiles serve traffic at once, so the active profile is meaningless — the
requested key carries the profile the turn was routed to, and the recovered row must sit in the same
``agent:<ns>:`` namespace (#74285). Rows with no key namespace stay adoptable in both modes
(legacy/keyless data owned by this store).

name: _generate_session_key
doc: Session key for *source* (profile from *source*; key from *key_source* if given).

name: _legacy_slack_session_key
doc:
Pre-workspace Slack key for an explicitly scoped source. Deliberately Slack-only: an
unscoped Slack session may be claimed by only one workspace (old key cannot tell teams).

name: _claim_legacy_slack_key
doc: Atomically reserve one ambiguous legacy Slack key for migration.

name: _recovered_row_matches_source_scope
doc:
Reject recovered rows whose origin belongs to another workspace: a workspace-scoped Slack
lookup adopts a row only if its origin_json names the same scope_id; rows without a
parseable origin are rejected (an unattributable transcript is exactly the ambiguity).

name: _create_entry_from_recovered_row
arguments: self, *, row: dict[str, Any], session_key: str, source: SessionSource, now: datetime

name: _find_gateway_session_row
arguments: self, *, session_key: str, source: SessionSource, allow_peer_fallback: bool, raise_on_lookup_error: bool=False
doc:
Query one durable gateway session row. Scoped Slack lookups disable SessionDB's
platform/chat/user fallback: that tuple has no workspace id and could revive another team's
session; the caller performs one explicit exact lookup of the old unscoped key instead.

name: _peer_row
arguments: db, *, source: str, session_key: str, raise_on_lookup_error: bool=False, **peer: Any
doc:
``db.find_latest_gateway_session_for_peer`` guarded for a missing store, a SessionDB
without the finder, and a failing lookup (debug-logged -> None unless *raise_on_lookup_error*).
Extra keyword arguments (user_id/chat_id/chat_type/thread_id) pass through to the finder.

name: resolve_session_id_for_key
doc:
Resolve a gateway session key to ``(session_id, db)`` for shutdown-flush recovery.

The routing map (``peek_session_id``) is authoritative: it names the session the message
was actually routed to at shutdown. When ``sessions.json`` was pruned, fall back to the
durable row under the exact key (the peer finder keeps the reset fence: rows ended only by
recoverable reasons match; explicit boundaries do not). A row started after the flush
(``started_at > not_after``) cannot be the origin and is never adopted. Never mints a
session; None means the caller must preserve the flush file. ``db`` is the store owning
the key, so the append lands in the right profile partition. When that store cannot be
resolved (``_db_for_key`` fails closed for a profile without a reachable home) the answer
is None even if the routing map knows the id: appending to the ambient root store would
split one session identity across two physical stores (#66887/#102157).

name: _recover_session_from_db
arguments: self, *, session_key: str, source: SessionSource, now: datetime, raise_on_lookup_error: bool=False
doc: Rebuild a missing session-key mapping from a recoverable durable row.

name: _query_recoverable_session
doc:
DB-only half of _recover_session_from_db (no lock needed): a SessionEntry or None; the
caller assigns _entries[key] under lock. The row is NOT reopened here: the caller evaluates
reset policy first (an agent_close/ws_orphan row may need promotion to a real reset).

name: _query_recoverable_row
_promote_session_reset
arguments: self, session_key: str, session_id: str, reason: str, *, log
doc:
End *session_id* with *reason* via ``promote_to_session_reset`` (``end_session`` on old
SessionDBs). Promote, not plain end: a row already ended with a recoverable accidental
reason (agent_close / ws_orphan_reap) must be upgraded to the explicit boundary, or
stale-route recovery resurrects it over the reset. ``log(exc)`` reports failures.

name: _reopen_session_row
arguments: self, session_key: str, session_id: str, *, log_prefix: str=''
doc: Best-effort ``reopen_session``; failures are debug-logged only.

name: _record_gateway_session_peer
arguments: self, session_id: str, session_key: str, source: Optional[SessionSource], display_name: Optional[str]=None, include_compression_ancestors: bool=False, transport_profile: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Persist the routing peer for an existing gateway session row. ``transport_profile`` is the
entry's persisted receiving-bot profile; when the caller has no entry it is read off the
source's pinned identity (None = unknown, the column keeps whatever an earlier writer set).

name: _adopt_legacy_slack_entry
doc:
One-time migration of pre-workspace-scope Slack keys: MOVE (not copy) the legacy entry so
a second workspace with identical Slack ids cannot attach to the same transcript. Adopt when
the legacy origin names the same workspace; a scope-less DM is claimed once by the first
workspace; a scope-less channel/group is refused (channel ids collide across workspaces).

name: _finish_route_transition
arguments: self, session_key: str, *, end_session_id: Optional[str], end_reason: str, create_kwargs: Optional[dict[str, Any]], origin: Optional[SessionSource], display_name: Optional[str], during: str=''
doc:
SQLite side of a routing transition, outside ``_lock``: promote the predecessor row to an
explicit reset boundary (with the specific reason so state.db is auditable, e.g.
``suspended`` vs plain ``session_reset``), then INSERT the new row + routing
peer. Both best-effort: failures are warned and self-healed by the next peer refresh.

name: _session_create_kwargs
arguments: *, session_id, session_key, origin, source_value, display_name, parent_session_id
doc:
kwargs for ``SessionDB.create_session``. Identity (origin_json) and lineage
(parent/_reset_from) land atomically in the INSERT so a crash right after cannot strand the
row unroutable.

name: _create_session_row
arguments: self, session_key, db_create_kwargs, origin, display_name, *, log
doc:

name: close_discarded_turn
arguments: db, conn, row, notice=None, *, replace_after=None, display_metadata=None
doc:
Close a discarded ``unknown`` turn the way a failed turn is closed, on the resolution's
own transaction (``resolve_unknown_session_input(_terminal_write=...)``).

The lost input stays in the transcript for the user to resend, but an open ``user`` tail would be
merged into the follower's provider request by consecutive-user repair, re-sending the discarded
turn as context. A Hermes-authored boundary (``display_kind=failed_turn``, stripped of its type
before the wire) ends it. Its side effects are unknown, so the hedged copy. The boundary lands on
the CURRENT physical transcript (local reset/compression lineage tip), resolved on this
connection. Idempotent on the durable tail, like the gateway and core failed-turn closers.

A turn lost while parked on a tool (an approval or clarify prompt) ends on its assistant
``tool_calls`` row with no result. That tail is open too: repair prunes the unanswered call,
drops the now-empty row and merges the discarded input into the follower's user turn, so it
gets the same boundary (merged onto the call row, whose calls are then pruned).

``notice`` (an unattended automation turn settled by the owner, GW-10) replaces the hedged copy
and is written even on a closed tail: nobody resolved it, so the transcript must say why.

``replace_after`` (the claim's transcript mark, an owner-stop notice): when the tail is a
failed-turn boundary written after that mark, it is THIS turn's own (the agent's core closer
wrote "Send it again" for the interrupted turn), so the notice replaces its copy instead of
stacking a second boundary (#134889 GW-21). An earlier turn's boundary stays.

``display_metadata`` (``{error, error_surface}``) rides the boundary so a reopened chat redraws
the turn's error card from history (``agent.conversation_loop._failed_turn_display_metadata``).

name: tracked_write
doc:
Run a synchronous ledger write (``write()``) in a worker thread, off the owner loop.

A held SQLite writer (``_WRITE_PATIENCE_S``) must not freeze every session, timer, socket,
Stop and approval. The write and its loop-side follow-up (``then(result)``, sync or a
coroutine: publication, scheduling, the claim's execution stamp) are one task tracked like ``track_mutation``, so
retirement joins it, and shielded, so a cancelled caller cannot separate a commit from it.
``ordered`` writes (admissions) commit in call order, as they did on the loop: worker threads
alone would let a later input take an earlier FIFO position.

``after(result)`` (an admission's drain scheduling) runs in the CALLER's own step once the
write returns, as it did when admission was synchronous: the caller registers its delivery
waiter before any drain it scheduled can claim, settle or pause that admission. A caller
cancelled while the commit is in flight hands ``after`` to the commit's completion instead,
so a committed row is never stranded without a drain.

name: _rebuild_fts_once
doc:
Attempt FTS5 ``rebuild``, at most once per ``_FTS_REBUILD_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`` window;
True if any index was rebuilt.

A permanent one-shot flag meant a single rebuild failure (e.g. a transient WAL
split-brain guard hit) permanently disabled recovery for the life of the process, even
though later corruption on the same store could be fixable. Retrying on a cooldown lets
the store try again after the underlying condition (e.g. a foreign holder) has likely
cleared, without hammering a database that is corrupt on every write.

name: _clear_dirty_transcript
doc: Drop queued pending messages so a rewrite/rewind doesn't re-insert them.

name: has_platform_message_id
doc:
Whether a message with this platform_message_id is persisted (False without a DB).

Thin wrapper over SessionDB.has_platform_message_id(). Returns False when no DB is available
(in-memory sessions). Used by the gateway's transient-failure dedupe guard (#47237).

name: transcript_tail_role
doc:
Role of the newest live conversation row on the route ``load_transcript`` reads (``None``
when empty, no DB, or the read fails — the boundary write would fail the same way).

name: rewrite_transcript
arguments: self, session_id: str, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], active_only: bool=False, reject_active_turn_lease: bool=False
doc:
Replace a session's transcript (/retry, /compress). DESTRUCTIVE by default:
``active_only=False`` DELETEs every row incl. soft-archived compaction history (pass
``active_only=True`` for sessions that may carry archived rows). True when the write lands
or there is no DB, False on failure — callers committing a destructive change on top
(/compress repointing) must check it. ``reject_active_turn_lease`` is for user-initiated
rewrites that do not own the cross-process turn lease.

name: is_published_compression_child
doc:
True when *child_session_id* is an atomically-published compression continuation of
*parent_session_id*: ``publish_compression_child()`` wrote the handoff (plus any cloned
foreign-tail rows) in the SAME transaction that ended the parent with
``end_reason='compression'``, so the child transcript is already durable on disk.

Rewriting such a child is redundant AND destructive: the in-memory handoff lacks the rows
cloned during publication, and a failed rewrite reports a false "failed to persist
compressed transcript" over a committed compression. Fails open (False) on any DB error so
callers fall back to the rewrite.

name: persist_rotated_compression_child
arguments: self, parent_session_id: str, child_session_id: str, messages: list[dict[str, Any]]
doc:
Make a rotated compression child durable before the live entry is repointed: a published
child already is, anything else gets *messages* written by the destructive rewrite.

name: has_input_owner
load_transcript
doc:
Load all messages from a session's transcript (state.db is canonical). Reads follow the
same routing writes use — the in-memory reroute map, then the durable compression tip —
otherwise the transcript "vanishes" while every message sits under the child.

name: rewind_session
arguments: self, session_id: str, n: int=1, *, require_retryable_composite: bool=False
doc:
Back up ``n`` user turns via soft-delete (``active=0``), mirroring CLI ``/undo [N]``.
Returns ``{"rewound_count", "turns_undone", "target_text"}`` or ``None`` (no DB / no rewindable
turn / persistence failure); ``n`` clamps to the oldest user turn. ``require_retryable_composite``
is the gateway ``/retry`` guard: the selected turn must be a composite carrier whose live payload
is losslessly replayable as text — that replay-policy ``ValueError`` propagates so /retry can
explain why the carrier is unsafe.

name: _ack_head
doc: Pop the acknowledged head (retry lock held). True if queue drained.

name: _toggles
doc: key -> (display field, word -> value, flipped(display), report(value)); '' / toggle flips.

name: _words
doc: key -> (display field, accepted words).

name: _set_display
doc: One display preference on the raw config, main's semantics; returns the result extras.

name: _set_focus
doc: /focus on stashes the configured tool-progress mode and pins it off; off restores it.

name: _write_profile_config
doc:
``edit(raw_cfg)`` on the owning profile's config.yaml EXACTLY as written (no defaults or
overlay persisted); saved only when it changed. Runs off the loop.

name: _authorize_write
doc: Profile-level like ``config.get`` (a session is optional), plus the control capability.

name: _broadcast_skin
doc: Main repainted every surface of the profile: ``skin.changed`` on each attached session.

name: current_tier
doc: The tier this session's next turn runs: its /fast pin, else its policy's (or the profile's).

name: _set_fast
doc:
Session-scoped /fast like main's: validated against the session's route, never config.yaml.
The words parse through the shared tier table (``parse_exact_service_tier``, as the classic CLI's
``config.set service_tier`` does); the pin is the same per-session override the next turn reads
(``current_service_tier``). TUI-only on top: ``toggle`` / ``status`` and the route check.

name: _set_personality
doc:
Main's /personality: validated against the profile's personalities and persisted through
``hermes_cli.personality`` (the only sanctioned write). Every next turn of the profile's sessions
resolves its ephemeral prompt from that config, and the changed prompt rebuilds the cached agent.

name: _set_approval_mode
doc: ``/approvals <mode>``'s own write (``hermes_cli.approval_mode``) for this profile.

name: _set_command_setting
doc:
``config.set`` for a setting a slash command owns: the same handler code, so the picker, the
keybind and the typed command agree. ``reasoning`` is ``/reasoning`` (``scope=global`` =
``--global``; show/hide/reset/levels), ``yolo`` with ``scope=global`` is main's Shift+click zap
(``approvals.mode`` off / manual).

name: _profile_home
doc: The owning profile's home (a symbolic test-peer id falls back to the scoped home).

name: _multiplexed
doc: Every turn runs under a per-profile secret scope (``owner_scope``'s own predicate).

name: save_session
doc:
``/save``: main's ``session.save`` — the stored transcript as a ``/save json`` snapshot in the
profile's ``sessions/saved/``. Reads the conversation's CURRENT physical row (a local session's
reset/compression child), like main's ``_submit_row_target_key``.

name: export_session
doc:
``session.export``: the ``/save`` transcript rendered for the CLIENT to write (json/md/html,
optional force-redaction). Nothing is written on the gateway host, so a remote Desktop and a
local Ink both save to the user's own disk (T10/T11).

name: session_history
doc: Main's ``session.history``: the display transcript of the conversation's current physical row (compression tip or local receipt entry), ancestors included, each row with its durable ``row_id``; Desktop's edit resolves its turn by it.

name: reload_env
doc:
``/reload``: re-read the profile's ``.env`` (main's ``reload.env`` / CLI ``/reload``).

Single-profile owner: main's ``hermes_cli.config.reload_env()`` verbatim — the owner's
``os.environ`` is what its turns read, exactly as the TUI's own sidecar process was. Built agents
keep their credential pool until ``/new`` (main's documented behaviour).

Multiplexed owner: ``os.environ`` is shared by every served profile and turns never read profile
secrets from it, so it is left alone. Each turn already re-reads ``.env`` into its own scope; what
can be stale is the profile's external secret-source snapshot, which is re-pulled here. The count
is the number of keys whose value in this profile's secret scope changed.

name: pause_delegation
doc:
``/agents pause|resume`` and the overlay's ``p``: main's ``delegation.pause`` — block or
unblock NEW ``delegate_task`` spawns; running children keep going.

The gate (``tools.delegate_tool_registry``) is process-wide, as it was in main's sidecar (a
TUI's sidecar served one TUI, but its gate covered every agent in that process). On the shared
owner it therefore covers every chat this gateway runs, which is what an operator's kill switch
is for; ``delegation.status`` reports the same flag to every client.

name: rollback
doc:
``/rollback [list] | diff <n|hash> | <n|hash> [file]`` and ``/diff session``: main's ``rollback.*`` over this
session's checkpoints (the shared ``<profile>/checkpoints`` store, keyed by the frozen launch cwd).

The manager is built from the session's frozen ``checkpoints`` policy rather than read off the
resident agent (main's ``agent._checkpoint_mgr``, built from the same config): it carries no
per-session state these reads need, and a restarted owner or a just-rewound session has no
resident agent. A whole-tree restore also rewinds the transcript to before the newest user turn
(main's ``_rewind_active_session_history``) through the owner's fenced ``rewind`` mutation.

name: _session_diff
doc:
``/diff session``: main's ``session_diff`` (earliest retained checkpoint vs the tree) as data,
so the classic CLI renders it with its own terminal renderer instead of chat-sized text.

name: _wire_bytes
doc: Bytes ``text`` takes inside a frame: JSON-escaped as ``serialize_frame`` writes it, then UTF-8.

name: _fit_frame
doc:
The longest whole-line prefix of ``text`` whose wire size fits ``budget`` bytes. The caller
reports the uncut line count, so the client names the cut instead of the frame dropping the socket.

name: _rewind_last_turn
doc:
Drop the newest user turn and everything after it (main's full ``/rollback`` restore) via the
owner's revision-fenced ``rewind`` mutation; 0 when the transcript has no user turn.

name: tui_read

identity (approval key, HERMES_SESSION_ID) for the side agent's thread.

name: _side_agent

name: _spawn
arguments: authority, ref, task_id, event_type, body, extra=None, holder=None
doc:
Run ``body()`` on a daemon thread; publish its text (or ``error: <exc>``) on the session.

The thread is owner work until it unwinds: the authority's ``_side_agents`` ledger is counted by
the restart wait, the shutdown drain, the SessionDB close gate and idle exit
(``session_runtime_workers.uncounted_runtime_work``), and profile retirement interrupts
``holder[0]`` (the side agent, once built) and joins the thread.

(``agent/side_question.py``); the live history, FIFO and prompt cache stay untouched.

name: plan_gauge

from the reply headers the agent already tracks — no extra round trip, None for everyone else.

doc: The frozen ``session.usage`` / ``session.stats`` dict; zeros before the first turn built an agent.

name: carried_compression_count
doc:
Compactions of this conversation: main's agent counted them on its compressor for the
session's life. A canonical compress evicts the gateway's agent (a session boundary), so the
count rides the live session and seeds the successor (``seed_compression_count``).

name: note_compression
doc: A committed (never an exact-retried) compress: one more compaction than the evicted agent saw.

name: tui_usage
doc:
``stats`` in main's TUI ``Usage`` shape (``tui_gateway/server.py::_get_usage``): the fields its
status bar (context used/max/bar, ``◷`` latency, ``t/s``, ``cmp`` badge, cache hit) and ``/usage``
read off ``message.complete.usage``. Absent figures are omitted, never fabricated as zeros.

name: usage_frame
doc:
The ``session.usage`` event payload: BOTH views of the same counters, in one frame.

``SessionUsagePayload`` (``tui_gateway/contracts/events.py``) allows either view — the TUI
``usage`` object (``server._start_usage_ticker``) or the session-cumulative counters at the top
level — and the readers on the far end want different halves. The classic CLI
(``hermes_cli.gateway_connection.SessionState.apply_event``) keeps the top-level counters
whenever they are present and ignores the nested view; ACP (``acp_adapter.gateway_server``)
reads only the top level; a Desktop bundle older than ``usageFromTick`` reads only
``payload.usage``, so its context / cache-hit / tokens-per-second meters render their empty
placeholder for as long as the frame carries the counters alone. Publishing both serves every
viewer from one frame, and leaves the counters untouched for every existing consumer.

``usage`` is the standard status-bar projection of the embedded ticker's ``server._get_usage``
view, with two exceptions: ``dev_credits_spent_micros`` (``HERMES_DEV_CREDITS`` only) is not
carried, and ``avg_latency_s`` / ``avg_tps`` are rounded from the counters' two decimals rather
than the raw values, so they can differ by 0.1 at a rounding boundary. A Desktop bundle that
reads only ``payload.usage`` fills its meters here too. The
top-level counters on this event are deprecated: new viewers read ``usage`` (or call
``session.stats`` for the counters). Before they can be dropped, these readers must move off
them: the classic CLI's ``SessionState.apply_event`` → ``GatewayAgent.apply_session_usage``,
ACP's ``_project_usage`` (``usage_update`` / ``turn_usage``), and the flat branch of
``usageFromTick`` (Desktop and Ink).

name: publish_usage
doc:
One ``session.usage`` frame on the viewer's stream; never breaks the turn. At turn end
(``record``) the same dict rides the captured execution result, so the turn's
``message.complete`` carries main's ``usage`` (``session_settlement_recovery.completion_payload``).

Complete a pending viewer close once *session_id* has no viewer and an idle FIFO: stamp the

The drain calls this at every idle point; a viewer attaching meanwhile cancels the close.

name: _resolve_abandoned_unknown

A turn the previous owner lost (hard kill) recovers ``unknown`` and pauses the FIFO until

close is that decision, so the owner resolves it as Discard does (interrupted, never replayed,
transcript boundary written) and the drain moves on; a queued successor still runs before the
close. A viewer back first cancels the close and keeps the decision. Returns whether the
close may go on to its idle check (no ``unknown`` turn is left).

``TurnRunner``'s combined ephemeral prompt for a LOCAL turn (no platform context block):
the gateway prompt (``agent.system_prompt`` / ``display.personality`` / channel override) plus
the frozen ``-s`` skills blocks. API-time only, never part of the persisted system prefix.
A bypass session never reads the profile: only its frozen launch additions apply.

The session's ``provider_routing``: its own profile's, as of its creation (main's CLI read it
once at startup). Never the runner's daemon-start copy.
