Send or update an animated streaming-draft preview. Reuse one non-zero ``draft_id``
across a response so the platform animates (different responses need different ids). Drafts
have no message_id (no edit/reply/delete) — the final answer goes out as a regular ``send``.
Must be overridden by adapters returning True from :meth:`supports_draft_streaming`.

name: render_message_event
doc:
Render a MessageChunk / MessageStop / Commentary onto the sink (a
GatewayStreamConsumer), mapping 1:1 onto its existing primitives.

name: format_tool_event
arguments: self, event: Any, *, mode: str='all', preview_max_len: int=40

name: format_tool_preview
doc:
Platform-native formatting of a compact tool preview; rich-text adapters may use
the preview's metadata (e.g. a URL shortened for display).

name: _should_auto_tts_for_chat
doc:
Whether auto-TTS fires for ``chat_id``: explicit ``/voice on|tts`` wins,
then explicit ``/voice off``, then the global ``voice.auto_tts`` default.

Decision layers (Issue #16007): 1. Explicit ``/voice on`` or ``/voice tts`` → always fire (even if
``voice.auto_tts`` is False). 2. 3.

name: send_path_degraded
doc:
True while connect() succeeded but delivery is not confirmed.

Adapters with a separately-proven receive path override this; the
default adapter is either connected or not.

name: _mark_connected
doc:
``listener_base`` (``http://host:port``) is stamped by port-binders after a REAL bind: under the
multiplexer it is the shared listener a served profile's ``/p/<profile>/`` mirror hangs off, and
what the dashboard/Desktop report as that profile's api_server/webhook URL.

name: _mark_degraded
doc: Publish ``retrying`` for a running adapter whose delivery path is unproven.

name: _set_fatal_error
arguments: self, code: str, message: str, *, retryable: bool

name: _write_runtime_status_safe
doc: Publish runtime status; log preparation failures without disrupting the adapter.

name: _acquire_platform_lock
arguments: self, scope: str, identity: str, resource_desc: str
doc:
Acquire a scoped lock for this adapter; True on success. A live cross-HERMES_HOME
holder is replaced only when the runner armed this adapter for its initial
``--replace`` connect (the status module validates ownership and terminates).

name: _release_platform_lock
doc: Release the scoped lock acquired by _acquire_platform_lock.

name: _wire_plugin_handlers
doc:
Invoke plugin-registered native handler factories (``ctx.register_platform_handler``)
with ``(native, adapter)``; adapters call this from ``connect()`` once the native
client exists and :meth:`rewire_plugin_handlers` re-runs it for plugins loaded later.
Idempotent per native client: a factory is keyed by ``(plugin, qualname)`` and skipped once
wired on this ``native`` (a force re-discovery hands back NEW function objects for the same
plugin, so identity alone would double-register). Each factory is isolated so a bad plugin
can't block connecting.

name: rewire_plugin_handlers
doc:
Register handlers of plugins loaded AFTER ``connect()`` wired the first batch (#87770);
the gateway runner calls this on every plugin-loaded event. Safe to call repeatedly: only
factories not yet wired on the live native client run. Before ``connect()`` has wired once
there is nothing to re-wire — connect will pick everything up. Adapters with extra plugin
registries (Slack action handlers) extend this.

name: name
doc: Human-readable name for this adapter.

name: is_connected
doc: Check if adapter is currently connected.

name: set_message_handler
doc: Set the incoming-message handler (MessageEvent -> optional response str).

name: set_platform_event_handler
arguments: self, handler: Optional[Callable[[dict[str, Any], Any], Awaitable[None]]]
doc:
Install the gateway-owned normalized platform-event boundary (stable dicts + internal
``SessionSource``); the runner owns authorization and plugin dispatch: no callback = fail
closed.

name: set_topic_recovery_fn
doc:
Install a thread_id-recovery hook (Telegram DM topic mode): called with ``event.source``
before session keying; a non-None return replaces ``source.thread_id``. ``None`` clears
it.

name: _apply_topic_recovery
doc: Rewrite ``event.source.thread_id`` in place if the hook returns one.

name: set_busy_session_handler
doc: Set an optional handler for messages arriving during active sessions.

name: set_reaction_handler
doc:
Set the handler for platform-native emoji-reaction events: a normalised dict
(``platform``, ``event_name`` "reaction:added"/"reaction:removed", ``reaction``,
``user_id``, ``item_user_id``, ``channel_id``, ``message_ts``, ``event_ts``, ``raw_event``)
fanned out via ``HookRegistry.emit``.

name: set_authorization_check
arguments: self, callback: Optional[Callable[[str, Optional[str], Optional[str]], bool]]
doc:
Register ``(user_id, chat_type, chat_id) -> bool``; adapters pulling external context
(Slack thread replies) use it to flag non-allowlisted senders as unverified background.

name: _is_sender_authorized
arguments: self, user_id: Optional[str], chat_type: Optional[str]=None, chat_id: Optional[str]=None, *, is_bot: bool=False, thread_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
True/False from the registered check, or None when no check exists ("trust unknown",
legacy). ``is_bot``/``thread_id`` are forwarded as keywords only when set so legacy
three-positional callbacks keep working. Only literal booleans propagate: a truthy
non-boolean is "unknown", never an authorization that gates a credentialed side effect.

name: set_session_store
doc:
Set the session store (e.g. Slack checks for an active thread session
before handling un-mentioned replies).

name: set_owner_profile
doc:
Declare the owning multiplex profile (secondary profiles only); read by
:meth:`_session_key_profile` so adapter-level keys leave ``agent:main:``.

name: _owner_transport_profile
doc:
Transport profile for :func:`resolve_identity`: the owner name, or ``None`` = derive it
from the registry (the primary's identity then spells ``"default"`` out itself).

name: _canonicalize
doc:
Pin the source's :class:`RoutingIdentity` before anything derives a key from it. Every
ingress path (fresh event, batch merge, busy path, control command, callback) calls this
FIRST. Returns the identity, or ``None`` when it cannot be resolved (a rejected route under
multiplexing marks ``source.profile_route_rejected``; ``_drop_unresolved`` reads it) or when
no runner seam exists (hand-built adapters, restored sources: the legacy readers stay).

name: _drop_unresolved
doc:
True when *event* must be dropped: its identity could not be resolved because the route
targets an unserved profile. Same disposition as the runner's ingress gate — one WARNING,
never a fall-through to ``agent:main``.

name: _session_key_profile
doc:
Profile namespace for an adapter-derived session key. Ingress runs BEFORE the runner
stamps ``source.profile``, so without this every bot in a multiplexed gateway shares one
``agent:main:`` lane. Order: pinned ``RoutingIdentity`` → ``source.profile`` →
``_owner_profile`` → session-store resolver; getattr-guarded (object.__new__ in tests),
type-checked (no MagicMock in the key).

name: _coerce_float_extra
arguments: self, key: str, default: float, *, min_value: float=0.0, max_value: Optional[float]=None
doc: Float from ``config.extra``; NaN/Inf/negative/unparseable → ``default``; clamped to ``[min_value, max_value]``.

name: _configure_text_batch_delays
doc: Read ``text_batch_delay_seconds`` / ``text_batch_split_delay_seconds`` from ``config.extra`` at the shared cadence.

name: _event_session_key
doc: Adapter-level session key for ``event``, profile-namespaced like the agent run.

name: _text_batch_key
doc: Session-scoped key for text batching (subclasses may override).

name: _enqueue_text_event
doc: Buffer a text event (merging into a pending one) and restart the flush timer.

name: _text_batch_delay_for
doc: Quiet period before ``pending`` is dispatched; near-split chunks wait longer.

name: _pop_text_batch
doc: Remove and return the pending batch for ``key`` (adapters with side tables override).

name: _dispatch_text_batch
doc: Hand a flushed batch to the pipeline (adapters with per-chat guards override).

name: _flush_text_batch_now
doc: Dispatch the pending batch for ``key`` immediately (no quiet period).

name: _flush_text_batch
doc:
Wait for the quiet period, then dispatch the batch for ``key``.

Two races share this body. (1) ``_enqueue_text_event`` cancels the prior flush task
on each new chunk; when ``Task.cancel()`` lands after ``sleep()`` already completed,
CancelledError is delivered at the *next* await — after a superseded task would have
popped the event, so the successor finds nothing and the message is lost. The identity
check therefore runs synchronously between the sleep and the pop. (2) A cancel that
lands while the dispatch is in flight would abort the agent turn (#12444), so the
dispatch is shielded and the outer CancelledError swallowed.

name: _history_media_paths_for_session
doc:
Return media paths already delivered in prior turns of this session
(MEDIA: tags / image_generate payloads), so an echoed old tag isn't re-sent.

name: _bounded_history_media_paths_for_session
doc: Run best-effort history lookup in a bounded isolated daemon thread.

name: connect
doc:
Connect and start receiving; True on success. ``is_reconnect``: the reconnect watcher is
re-establishing a dropped platform — adapters with a server-side update queue (Telegram)
must preserve it so outage-time messages aren't discarded.

name: disconnect
doc: Disconnect from the platform.

name: send
arguments: self, chat_id: str, content: str, reply_to: Optional[str]=None, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Send ``content`` (may be markdown) to a chat; returns SendResult with message id.

name: create_handoff_thread
doc:
Create a fresh thread under ``parent_chat_id`` for a CLI→platform session handoff; its id
as str, or None when unsupported/failed (the watcher then uses ``parent_chat_id``
directly).

name: edit_message
arguments: self, chat_id: str, message_id: str, content: str, *, finalize: bool=False
doc:
Edit a sent message (optional: success=False makes callers send anew). ``finalize`` marks
the last edit of a streamed response; surfaces with a distinct "in progress" state (DingTalk
AI Cards) close the message on it and set ``REQUIRES_EDIT_FINALIZE`` so it's routed even
when content is unchanged.

name: delete_message
doc:
Delete a sent message; True on success (platforms without a deletion API return False and
callers leave it). Used by the stream consumer's fresh-final cleanup to remove stale
previews.

Used by the stream consumer's fresh-final cleanup path (see openclaw/openclaw#72038) to remove
long-lived preview messages after sending the completed reply as a fresh message so the platform's
visible timestamp reflects completion time.

name: _get_ephemeral_system_ttl_default
doc:
Default :class:`EphemeralReply` TTL from ``display.ephemeral_system_ttl``
(``0`` = no auto-delete); non-fatal if config is unreadable.

name: _schedule_ephemeral_delete
arguments: self, chat_id: str, message_id: str, ttl_seconds: int
doc:
Spawn a detached task that deletes ``message_id`` after ``ttl_seconds``; best-effort
(gateway restart, permission denied, Telegram 48h window) swallowed at debug level.

name: _truncate_preview
arguments: text: str, budget: int, suffix: str='...'
doc: Truncate ``text`` to ``budget`` chars, appending ``suffix`` when cut.

name: _ea_escape
doc: Escape hook for command preview/reason; HTML-mode platforms (Telegram) override.

name: _ea_fit
arguments: self, text: str, budget: int, suffix: str='...', escape: Optional[Callable[[str], str]]=None
doc:
``_truncate_preview`` measured after ``escape`` (default ``_ea_escape``) in
``message_len_fn`` units: the platform cap applies to the wire payload, and escaping
expands (``&`` → ``&``), so a raw-length cut can still overflow. Returns raw text (the
caller escapes); ``suffix`` rides outside ``budget`` like ``_truncate_preview``.

name: _exec_approval_cmd_budget
doc: Chars of command preview that fit; platforms with a hard message cap compute it.

name: _ea_deadline_line
doc: The "doing nothing means it will NOT run" line, with the configured approvals.timeout.

name: _format_exec_approval
arguments: self, command: str, description: Optional[str]=None, smart_denied: bool=False
doc:
Shared exec-approval prompt text: header + fenced (truncated) command + why it was
flagged + the deadline line, plus the smart-deny line. Buttons/trailing instructions stay
platform-local. ``description=None`` renders the localized default reason.

name: _exec_approval_actions
arguments: self, *, allow_permanent: bool, allow_session: bool, smart_denied: bool

name: supports_exec_approval_buttons
doc:
True when the adapter renders native approval buttons (overrides the prompt hook);
the runner otherwise sends the plain-text ``/approve`` prompt.

name: send_exec_approval
arguments: self, chat_id: str, command: str, session_key: str, description: Optional[str]=None, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, allow_permanent: bool=True, allow_session: bool=True, smart_denied: bool=False
doc:
Interactive exec-approval prompt; a press resolves via
``tools.approval.resolve_gateway_approval``. Text and choice set are shared; adapters
render them natively in ``_send_exec_approval_prompt``.

name: _send_exec_approval_prompt
doc: Render ``prompt`` with the platform's native buttons; the default has none.

name: _format_choice_page
arguments: options: list, page: int, per_page: int
doc:
Shared picker pagination: clamp ``page``, slice ``options`` -> ``(page_options, meta)``
with ``page``/``total_pages``/``start``/``end``/``total``/``page_info`` (`` (N–M of T)``,
empty for one page).

name: send_slash_confirm
arguments: self, chat_id: str, title: str, message: str, session_key: str, confirm_id: str, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Three-option slash-command confirmation (e.g. ``/reload-mcp``). Button adapters render
Approve Once / Always Approve / Cancel and MUST resolve via
``GatewayRunner._resolve_slash_confirm(confirm_id, "once"|"always"|"cancel")``. Default (not
supported) falls through to the gateway text fallback
(``/approve``/``/always``/``/cancel``).

name: send_clarify
arguments: self, chat_id: str, question: str, choices: Optional[list], clarify_id: str, session_key: str, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Clarify prompt; button-capable adapters SHOULD override. Multiple choice (``choices``):
one button per choice plus "Other"; callbacks MUST resolve via
``tools.clarify_gateway.resolve_gateway_clarify(clarify_id, response)``, "Other" calls
``mark_awaiting_text(clarify_id)``. Open-ended: send the question as text (the gateway
text-intercept resolves the next message). Default: numbered list +
``mark_awaiting_text``. Adapters whose prompt is a persistent card MAY define
``async retire_clarify_card(clarify_id, notice)``; the gateway calls it when the clarify
ends without a click (timeout, session reset, superseding free prose).

name: send_private_notice
arguments: self, chat_id: str, user_id: Optional[str], content: str, reply_to: Optional[str]=None, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Send a notice privately when the platform supports it; default is a normal send.

name: send_typing
doc: Send a typing indicator; ``metadata`` carries platform context (Slack thread_id).

name: stop_typing
doc: Stop a persistent typing indicator; override where typing runs as a loop.

name: _accepts_kwarg
arguments: fn: Callable, name: str, *, var_kw: bool, unknown: bool
doc:
Whether ``fn``'s signature takes keyword ``name`` (``var_kw``: a ``**kwargs`` also
counts); ``unknown`` when the signature can't be introspected.

name: _stop_typing_with_metadata
doc:
Stop typing, forwarding ``metadata`` only if ``stop_typing`` accepts it (Slack AI
status is per thread, so dropping metadata could clear a sibling thread; introspecting
keeps legacy ``stop_typing(chat_id)`` adapters working).

name: send_multiple_images
arguments: self, chat_id: str, images: list[tuple[str, str]], metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, human_delay: float=0.0
doc:
Send ``(url, alt)`` images (``http(s)://`` or ``file://``) one by one (GIFs via
``send_animation``, local files via ``send_image_file``); override to bundle natively
(Signal). Returns success when at least one image was delivered — the outcome
the turn-level delivery tracker records; every override must return the same
aggregate, or a media-only turn on that platform reports FAILURE (#106153).

significant_calls.expression:
sender(
                    chat_id=chat_id, **url_kw, caption=alt_text or None, metadata=metadata)

name: send_image
arguments: self, chat_id: str, image_url: str, caption: Optional[str]=None, reply_to: Optional[str]=None, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Send an image natively; default falls back to sending the URL as text.

name: send_animation
arguments: self, chat_id: str, animation_url: str, caption: Optional[str]=None, reply_to: Optional[str]=None, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Send a GIF as a native animation (auto-plays inline); default falls back to
send_image.

significant_calls.expression:
self.send_image(
            chat_id=chat_id, image_url=animation_url, caption=caption, reply_to=reply_to, metadata=metadata)

name: _is_animation_url
doc: Check if a URL points to an animated GIF (vs a static image).

name: extract_images
doc: Extract ``![alt](url)`` and ```` image URLs from a response; returns ``([(url, alt_text), ...], content with those tags removed)``.

name: send_voice
arguments: self, chat_id: str, audio_path: str, caption: Optional[str]=None, reply_to: Optional[str]=None, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, **kwargs
doc:
Send audio as a native voice message (Telegram bubble / Discord attachment).
Default: friendly failure notice.

significant_calls.expression:
self._send_media_fallback_notice(
            "send_voice", "audio", audio_path, chat_id, caption, reply_to, metadata)

name: _send_media_fallback_notice
arguments: self, method: str, kind: str, path: str, chat_id: str, caption: Optional[str], reply_to: Optional[str], metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]], *, file_name: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Shared default for send_voice/send_video/send_document/send_image_file. The local path is
logged but NEVER echoed into chat (host layout leak); only the caller's ``file_name`` is
shown.

significant_calls.expression:
self.emit_media_warning(chat_id, text, caption=caption, reply_to=reply_to, metadata=metadata,
                                             shown_metadata=metadata)

name: emit_warning
arguments: self, chat_id: str, content: str, *, reply_to=None, metadata=None, logical_platform=None
doc:
Present a classified channel diagnostic in the caller's owning scope.

None means suppressed, NOT successfully sent. Transport receipts/exceptions
pass through unchanged; logs and producer state belong outside this boundary.
Existing routing/stream metadata is preserved, never inferred from text.

name: emit_media_warning
arguments: self, chat_id: str, notice: str, *, caption=None, reply_to=None, metadata=None, shown_metadata=None
doc:
Present an optional media diagnostic without losing the requested caption.

Preserve the legacy fallback-text receipt when shown (``shown_metadata`` is the exact
metadata the legacy shown path passed; default None keeps callers that sent none
byte-identical). When hidden, preserve the media failure even if the independent
caption itself was delivered.

significant_calls.expression:
self.emit_warning(chat_id, f"{caption}\n{notice}" if caption else notice,
                                         reply_to=reply_to, metadata=shown_metadata)

name: warning_text
arguments: self, visible: str, hidden: Optional[str]='', *, logical_platform=None, chat_id=None, metadata=None
doc:
Project mixed content: the diagnostic variant when visible, else the requested remainder.

For payloads that combine a requested result (caption, answer) with an automatic
diagnostic. The requested part must be present in BOTH variants; never hide it.

name: warning_notifications_enabled
doc: Presentation policy under the caller's owning profile; old plugins inherit it.

name: prepare_tts_text
doc:
Chat Markdown -> transcript-like spoken script (reasoning blocks removed,
headings/bullets flattened, units expanded). Chunking and delivery limits are the TTS tool's
job.

name: play_tts
doc: Play auto-TTS audio; override for invisible playback (Web UI). Default: send_voice.

name: supports_streaming_tts
doc: Return True when this adapter can accept streaming PCM for *chat_id*.

name: begin_streaming_tts
arguments: self, chat_id: str, audio_format: AudioFormat, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Open a streaming-audio session; returns an opaque handle for the
write/finish/abort calls, or ``None`` to decline (whole-file fallback).

name: write_streaming_tts
doc: Write one PCM chunk to the adapter's outbound audio track.

name: finish_streaming_tts
doc: Signal normal end of the audio stream.

name: abort_streaming_tts
doc:
Abort the stream due to an error or cancellation. Must be idempotent: late producer
chunks after abort are silently dropped, not raised. Restores state to "not streaming".

name: _streaming_tts_turn_key
arguments: self, session_key: str | None, turn_marker: Any=None, *, event: Any=None

name: _mark_streaming_tts_completed_turn
arguments: self, session_key: str | None, turn_marker: Any=None, *, event: Any=None

name: _streaming_tts_turn_completed
arguments: self, session_key: str | None, turn_marker: Any=None, *, event: Any=None

name: send_video
arguments: self, chat_id: str, video_path: str, caption: Optional[str]=None, reply_to: Optional[str]=None, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, **kwargs
doc: Send a video natively (inline playable). Default: friendly failure notice.

significant_calls.expression:
self._send_media_fallback_notice(
            "send_video", "video", video_path, chat_id, caption, reply_to, metadata)

name: send_document
arguments: self, chat_id: str, file_path: str, caption: Optional[str]=None, file_name: Optional[str]=None, reply_to: Optional[str]=None, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, **kwargs
doc: Send a document/file natively. Default: friendly failure notice.

significant_calls.expression:
self._send_media_fallback_notice(
            "send_document", "file", file_path, chat_id, caption, reply_to, metadata, file_name=file_name)

name: _notify_media_delivery_failure
arguments: self, chat_id: str, media_path: str, *, is_voice: bool=False, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
User-visible notice when a MEDIA attachment upload failed: the tag was
already stripped from the text, so silence would be a silent drop.

The non-streaming dispatch loop strips ``MEDIA:`` tags before sending attachments. When the
subsequent upload returns ``success=False`` (for example Discord accepted the message but attached
nothing), the user must see a failure notice instead of a silent drop (#66797).

name: send_image_file
arguments: self, chat_id: str, image_path: str, caption: Optional[str]=None, reply_to: Optional[str]=None, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, **kwargs
doc: Send a local image file natively (send_image takes a URL). Default: friendly notice.

significant_calls.expression:
self._send_media_fallback_notice(
            "send_image_file", "image", image_path, chat_id, caption, reply_to, metadata)

name: validate_media_delivery_path
doc: Return a resolved path if it is safe for native attachment upload.

name: filter_media_delivery_paths
doc: Drop unsafe MEDIA paths and normalize accepted paths; ``dropped`` collects the rejects.

name: filter_local_delivery_paths
doc: Drop unsafe bare local file paths and normalize accepted paths.

name: _mask_protected_spans
doc:
Blank fenced code, inline code and blockquotes (length-preserving so regex offsets stay
valid) against MEDIA: false positives; backtick-quoted paths inside MEDIA: tags stay
scannable.

name: _mask_json_string_media
doc:
Blank ``MEDIA:<bare-path>`` tags inside JSON string *values* (stored tool-result text
like ``{"result": "MEDIA:/x/stale.png"}``) so they are never re-delivered. Only
value-context strings (``:,{[`` before the ``"``) and bare paths (``/``, ``~/``, ``X:\``)
count; ``MEDIA:"..."`` quoted tags and line-start/prose tags are untouched. Offsets
preserved.

Here the ``MEDIA:`` is part of stored text, not an outbound directive, but the bare-path branch of
``MEDIA_TAG_CLEANUP_RE`` would still match it and re-deliver a stale file. (Regression report
#34375.)

name: extract_media
doc:
Extract ``MEDIA:<path>`` tags and strip ``[[audio_as_voice]]`` / ``[[as_document]]`` ->
``([(path, is_voice), ...], cleaned)``. Both directives are message-global;
``[[as_document]]`` (unmodified sendDocument for large images) is detected by dispatch sites
on the ORIGINAL response and only stripped here.

name: strip_media_directives_for_display
doc:
Strip MEDIA: directives from streamed/display text. Known-extension tags are
removed unconditionally (as ``MEDIA_TAG_CLEANUP_RE``); extension-less tags only when
``validate_media_delivery_path`` accepts the path, so undeliverable paths stay visible.

name: extract_local_files
doc:
Bare local file paths (absolute, ``~/`` or drive-letter) with deliverable extensions ->
``(expanded_paths, cleaned_text)``. Candidates must exist on disk (URLs / hallucinated paths
ignored); paths inside fenced or inline code are skipped so code samples are never
mutilated. Dispatch by type lives in ``gateway/run.py``.

name: _keep_typing
arguments: self, chat_id: str, interval: float=2.0, metadata=None, stop_event: asyncio.Event | None=None
doc:
Refresh the typing indicator every ``interval`` seconds until cancelled (platform typing
state expires after ~5s). Chats in ``_typing_paused`` are skipped (approval waits — Slack's
setStatus disables the compose box). Each ``send_typing`` is bounded by a sub-interval
timeout so one slow round-trip is abandoned before the next tick, not the bubble lapsing.

name: _stop_typing_refresh
arguments: self, chat_id: str, typing_task: asyncio.Task | None=None, *, metadata=None, timeout: float=0.5, stop_attempts: int=2
doc: Stop the refresh task and platform typing state as one operation.

name: _stop_typing_quietly
doc: Best-effort platform stop_typing; adapter errors are swallowed.

name: pause_typing_for_chat
doc: Pause typing for a chat (approval waits); GIL-safe from the sync agent thread.

name: resume_typing_for_chat
doc: Resume typing indicator for a chat after approval resolves.

name: interrupt_session_activity
arguments: self, session_key: str, chat_id: str, metadata=None
doc: Signal the active session loop to stop and clear typing immediately.

name: register_post_delivery_callback
arguments: self, session_key: str, callback: Callable, *, generation: int | None=None
doc:
Register a deferred callback to fire after the main response. Same-key registrations are
chained (both fire in order, per-callback exception isolation) so independent features
coexist; ``generation`` ties it to a gateway run — stale generations never overwrite a
fresher slot.

name: _chain_callbacks
doc:
Async wrapper running ``callbacks`` in order with per-callback exception isolation;
async so coroutines returned by async hooks are awaited, not dropped.

name: pop_post_delivery_callback
arguments: self, session_key: str, *, generation: int | None=None
doc: Pop a deferred callback, optionally requiring generation ownership.

name: on_processing_start
doc: Hook called when background processing begins.

name: on_processing_complete
doc:
Hook called when background processing completes. Default: opt-in reaction ack — with
``_OK_EMOJI``/``_FAIL_EMOJI`` set and ``_add_reaction``/``_remove_reaction`` present, swap
the in-progress reaction for the outcome one. Remove-then-add is deterministic whether the
platform replaces or stacks a sender's reactions. CANCELLED leaves it unreacted.

name: _run_processing_hook
doc: Run a lifecycle hook without letting failures break message flow.

name: _is_retryable_error
doc: Return True if the error string looks like a transient network failure.

name: _is_rate_limited_error
doc:
Return True if the error string classifies as a rate limit / flood cap.

Single wrapper around :func:`classify_send_error` so the call sites in
:meth:`_send_with_retry` share one notion of "is this a rate limit" instead
of inline copies that could drift.

name: _is_timeout_error
doc:
Return True for read/write timeouts — NOT retryable and NOT a plain-text
fallback trigger, because the request may already have been delivered.

name: _unwrap_ephemeral
doc:
Unwrap a str/None/:class:`EphemeralReply` response into ``(text, ttl)``. ``ttl > 0``
means schedule ``_schedule_ephemeral_delete`` after a successful send; forced to 0 when the
adapter doesn't override ``delete_message`` so non-supporting platforms degrade to normal
sends.

name: _dispatch_inline_reply
doc:
Call the handler and send its reply inline, with retry, threading and
ephemeral deletion — no session lifecycle (active-session bypass paths).

name: _media_delivery_scope
doc:
Routed home + terminal policy for post-handler text, media and error delivery;
a no-op without a runner or outside multiplexing.

name: _final_delivery_adapter
doc:
The runner's CURRENT adapter for a new final-response send: a reconnect can swap the
registry adapter mid-task; an unsent final response belongs on the replacement transport,
while message IDs, edits and deletes stay owned by the old one (nothing is migrated).

name: _send_with_retry
arguments: self, chat_id: str, content: str, reply_to: Optional[str]=None, metadata: Any=None, max_retries: int=2, base_delay: float=2.0
doc:
Send with exponential-backoff retry on transient network errors; permanent
failures fall back to a plain-text send, exhausted retries notify the user.

name: _send_retry_is_final
doc:
True when a failed send must be returned as-is: neither a retry nor the plain-text
fallback can fix it (a structured auth/target refusal). Default: never.

name: _is_partial_delivery
doc:
True when a split payload was PARTLY delivered (``raw_response["partial_overflow"]``, the
contract Telegram's send/edit-overflow paths set and the stream consumer reads): the visible
head must never be sent again.

name: _resume_partial_send
arguments: self, chat_id: str, result: SendResult, *, reply_to: Optional[str], metadata: Any
doc:
Deliver only the remainder of a partially delivered split payload. ``None`` (the default) means
this adapter cannot resume; ``_send_with_retry`` then returns the partial failure instead of
re-sending the whole payload. Override only where non-delivery of the remainder is CERTAIN.

name: _send_plain_fallback
arguments: self, chat_id: str, content: str, *, reply_to: Optional[str], metadata: Any
doc:
Last-resort send after a non-transient failure; platforms whose markup is not the
likely culprit override it (Photon drops rich links instead of adding the banner).

significant_calls.expression:
self.send(
            chat_id=chat_id, content=self.warning_text(
                t("gateway.notify.plain_fallback_prefix", content=content[:3500]), content[:3500],
                chat_id=chat_id, metadata=metadata),
            reply_to=reply_to, metadata=metadata)

name: _merge_caption
doc:
Merge a new caption into existing text unless an identical (stripped) caption already
exists — exact match per caption, not substring ("Meeting" isn't swallowed by "Meeting
agenda").

name: _is_queue_text_debounce_candidate
doc: Return True for normal text eligible for queue-mode debounce.

name: _can_merge_text_debounce_events
doc: Return True when two text debounce events came from the same sender.

name: _text_debounce_delay
doc: Return bounded busy-text debounce delay for ``session_key``.

name: _queue_text_debounce
doc: Buffer normal queue-mode busy text and schedule a bounded flush.

name: _flush_text_debounce
doc: Timer task that flushes the debounced text buffer.

name: _flush_text_debounce_now
doc: Force-flush one debounced busy-text burst into the pending slot.

name: _discard_text_debounce
doc: Cancel and drop pending text debounce state for control commands.

name: _release_session_guard
doc:
Release the session guard; with ``guard`` given, only if the entry is still that exact
Event (an old task's unwind must not clear the guard a reset-like command swapped in).

name: _session_task_is_stale
doc:
True if the recorded owner task for ``session_key`` has exited. No owner task at all is
NOT stale (guards installed outside handle_message, as tests do, must not be healed).

name: _heal_stale_session_lock
doc:
Clear a stale session lock; True if healed. On-entry safety net: without it a split-brain
(guard held, nothing processing) traps the chat in "Interrupting..." until restart.

name: _start_session_processing
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, *, interrupt_event: Optional[asyncio.Event]=None
doc:
Spawn a background processing task under the session guard; True on success. If
``create_task`` is stubbed with a non-Task sentinel (tests), the guard is rolled back
(False).

name: _track_session_task
doc:
Record ``task`` as the session owner and track it for shutdown; False when
``create_task`` was stubbed with an unhashable sentinel (tests) — the owner entry is left
for the caller.

name: cancel_session_processing
arguments: self, session_key: str, *, release_guard: bool=True, discard_pending: bool=True
doc:
Cancel in-flight processing for one session. ``release_guard=False`` keeps the guard so
reset-like commands finish atomically; the await is bounded (5s) so a wedged finally can't
stall.

name: _drain_pending_after_session_command
doc:
Tail of /stop, /new, /reset: release the command-scoped guard, then
spawn a fresh processing task for any follow-up queued meanwhile.

name: _dispatch_active_session_command
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, cmd: str
doc:
Dispatch a reset-like bypass command (/stop, /new, /reset): keep a guard installed while
the runner handles it (follow-ups stay queued), cancel the old task AFTER the response,
drain once.

name: handle_message
doc:
Process an incoming message; returns quickly by spawning a background
task so new messages (and interrupts) can arrive while an agent runs.

name: _shared_runtime_owns_input
doc: True when a non-command input belongs to the shared runtime's session authority.

name: _pending_recovery_owners
doc:
Adapters whose pending slot may hold *event* after busy admission: this one, plus the
runner's current delivery adapter for its source when that replacement has no live guard.

name: _handle_message_while_active
doc:
Route a message that arrived while ``session_key`` is busy: bypass
commands / clarify replies dispatch inline, everything else is queued.

name: _get_human_delay
doc:
Random human-like pacing delay (s) from this adapter's ``human_delay`` config range
(ms), installed per profile by the runner (``_wire_adapter_handlers``); ``None`` = off.

name: _synthesize_auto_tts
doc:
Synthesize auto-TTS audio -> ``(existing_paths, requested_path)``; empty/None on failure
(logged, never raised). Path built platform-aware HERE: HERMES_SESSION_PLATFORM is cleared
post-handler.

name: _wants_auto_tts
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, interrupt_event: asyncio.Event, text_content: str, media_files: list
doc:
Auto-TTS on voice input (voice-first), gated by /voice or voice.auto_tts;
skipped when streaming TTS already delivered audio this turn.

name: _play_tts_file
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, text_content: str, tts_path: str, first: bool, metadata: dict[str, Any], record_delivery: Callable
doc:
Play one synthesized TTS file. Returns True when the ORIGINAL reply text rode
along as a Telegram caption (first file, ≤1024 chars) so the text send is skipped.

name: _record_delivery_obligation
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, text_content: str, delivery_adapter: 'BasePlatformAdapter', is_ephemeral_response: bool
doc:
Ledger the final response BEFORE the send so a crash before platform ACK redelivers on
next boot; best-effort, skips slash-command and ephemeral replies. Returns the obligation id
or None.

name: _finalize_delivery_obligation
arguments: self, obligation_id: str, result: Any, event: MessageEvent, delivery_adapter: 'BasePlatformAdapter'
doc:
Mark the ledger row delivered/failed (best-effort). On ``send_path_degraded`` with a
replacement adapter live, trigger another redelivery sweep (the watcher's may have run
before this failure landed; atomic claiming keeps it idempotent). On any other rejection arm
the runner's timed redelivery, so the reply goes out once the flood penalty or the retry
backoff has passed instead of waiting for the next restart (#91653).

name: _deliver_media_attachments
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, media_files: list, local_files: list, *, force_document_attachments: bool, human_delay: float, metadata: dict[str, Any], record_delivery: Callable
doc:
Deliver MEDIA-tag files and detected local files by type: images batched via
``send_multiple_images`` unless ``[[as_document]]``; otherwise audio → send_voice (MEDIA
tags only, never bare local files), video → send_video, else send_document. Every failure is
reported. Each send feeds ``record_delivery`` so media-only turns report SUCCESS.

significant_calls.expression:
self._send_image_batch(
                event, [(f"file://{_quote(p)}", "") for p in _image_paths], metadata, human_delay,
                record_delivery)

name: _send_image_batch
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, images: list, metadata: dict[str, Any], human_delay: float, record_delivery: Callable
doc:
Batch-send images; a failure is logged (never raised) so other attachments still go.
The batch result feeds ``record_delivery`` so media-only turns report their real
outcome instead of FAILURE.

name: send_final_ledgered
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, text_content: str, metadata: dict[str, Any], *, reply_to: Optional[str], is_ephemeral_response: bool=False
doc:
The delivery-ledger bracket every final text goes through, on the CURRENT transport
(a reconnect may have replaced this adapter): record the obligation before the send,
send with retry, finalize from the result — so a refused final (flood control, a dead
transport) leaves a ledger row the boot sweep / runtime redelivery can act on. ``event``
supplies the source and the ledger identity (``ledger_message_id`` or ``message_id``).
Returns the result with the adapter that sent it: that adapter owns ``result.message_id``
(an ephemeral delete must go to the same transport).

name: _release_turn_marker
doc:
Clear the crash marker handed to this delivery lifecycle only once the final reply is ledgered or
nothing more is owed (no kill leaves a persisted reply with neither), then wake the drain. Idempotent.

name: _send_final_text
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, text_content: str, metadata: dict[str, Any], is_ephemeral_response: bool, ephemeral_ttl: int, record_delivery: Callable
doc: Normal-lane final: the ledger bracket plus the message-id owner's ephemeral delete.

significant_calls.expression:
self.send_final_ledgered(
            event, session_key, text_content, metadata,
            reply_to=_reply_anchor_for_event(event), is_ephemeral_response=is_ephemeral_response)

name: _notify_turn_error
doc:
Tell the user a turn failed rather than leaving radio silence (last resort:
a failing notice is logged, never raised). Returns the thread metadata used.

name: _deliver_attachments
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, extracted: _ExtractedResponse, metadata: dict[str, Any], *, anything_sent: bool, record_delivery: Callable
doc:
Send extracted image URLs, MEDIA files and bare local files (human-paced),
then fail loudly if a non-empty response produced nothing deliverable. Attachment
results feed ``record_delivery`` so the turn outcome reflects them.

name: _start_typing_refresh
arguments: self, event: MessageEvent, interrupt_event: asyncio.Event, metadata: Optional[dict]
doc:
Spawn the typing-refresh task, or None when ``typing_indicator=False``.
``stop_event`` is passed only when the (possibly overridden) ``_keep_typing`` accepts it.

name: _extract_response_content
arguments: self, response: str, event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, *, is_ephemeral_response: bool
doc:
Split a handler response into deliverable text + attachments. Order matters: MEDIA tags →
image URLs → residual directives → bare local paths (skipped for ephemeral notices so config
paths stay text; unknown-extension MEDIA tags survive for the bare-path detector). History
dedup is bare-path only, off-loop, fail-open. An emptied non-empty response is recovered.

name: _fire_post_delivery_callback
doc:
Run the one-shot post-delivery callback (bounded, errors swallowed). The generation is
read HERE — stamped on the interrupt event DURING the handler await; an earlier snapshot
would let stale runs fire a fresher run's callbacks.

name: _finish_session_task
doc:
End-of-task guard/ownership reconciliation. A late ``_pending_messages`` arrival must not
drop: re-queue it if another task already owns the session (drain handoff), else spawn the
drain task and leave it the guard. Nothing pending: release the guard only if we still own
it.

name: _process_message_background
doc: Background task that actually processes the message.

name: _requeue_backoff_delay
arguments: self, session_key: str, pending_event: MessageEvent, dispatched_event: MessageEvent
doc:
Delay before re-dispatching the queued follow-up.

Only the event this task just dispatched coming straight back backs off: the same
``message_id``, or for an id-less event the same ``timestamp`` (rewrite-hook
``dataclasses.replace`` copies keep both; a genuine new message gets a fresh timestamp).
The handler put it back because the session is busy elsewhere, and re-dispatching it at
once hot-loops for the whole busy window (#123229). Any other follow-up resets the counter
and runs immediately. The first bounce stays immediate (restart auto-resume relies on one
self-bounce), then back off exponentially to a cap. Defers, never drops.

name: _spawn_drain_task
arguments: self, pending_event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, delay: float=0.0
doc:
Hand the session to a fresh task for a queued follow-up — never recurse (chained
follow-ups grew the C stack to SIGSEGV). Clearing (not deleting) the Event keeps the guard
live for concurrent inbound; ownership moves so stale-lock detection works. With ``delay``
the event stays in ``_pending_messages`` and the new owner task pops the slot only after
sleeping, so a cancel/discard during the back-off needs no put-back and can't drop a
newer message.

name: _drain_after
arguments: self, pending_event: MessageEvent, session_key: str, delay: float, guard: Optional[asyncio.Event]

name: _clear_session_guard
doc: Clear (not delete) the session's interrupt Event so the guard stays live for inbound.

name: _cleanup_finished_session_task
doc:
Release a finished owner task's guard, dropping its ``_session_tasks`` entry ONLY if the
guard was released: after a concurrent guard swap the done-task entry lets
``_session_task_is_stale`` heal the orphan.

Release-then-conditional-delete is the #48300 fix: when a concurrent path (reset/new command, drain
handoff) swapped ``_active_sessions[key]`` to a different guard, ``_release_session_guard`` skips on
the guard mismatch and the lock stays installed. If we deleted ``_session_tasks`` unconditionally
(the old order), ``_session_task_is_stale`` would later see no owner task and report "not stale", so
the orphaned guard would never be healed — a permanent session deadlock. Keeping the done-task entry
when the guard survives lets the on-entry self-heal detect the stale lock and clear it on the next
inbound message.

name: cancel_background_tasks
doc:
Cancel in-flight background tasks (shutdown/replacement); 5s bound each,
stragglers are untracked and left to unwind.

name: has_pending_interrupt
doc: Check if there's a pending interrupt for a session.

name: get_pending_message
doc: Get and clear any pending message for a session.

name: build_source
arguments: self, chat_id: str, chat_name: Optional[str]=None, chat_type: str='dm', user_id: Optional[str]=None, user_name: Optional[str]=None, thread_id: Optional[str]=None, chat_topic: Optional[str]=None, user_id_alt: Optional[str]=None, chat_id_alt: Optional[str]=None, is_bot: bool=False, scope_id: Optional[str]=None, guild_id: Optional[str]=None, parent_chat_id: Optional[str]=None, message_id: Optional[str]=None, role_authorized: bool=False, auto_thread_created: bool=False, auto_thread_initial_name: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Build a SessionSource; with ``gateway.profile_routes`` configured the matching
profile is stamped on ``source.profile`` for per-profile HERMES_HOME isolation.

name: get_chat_info
doc:
Get information about a chat/channel; dict with at least ``name``
and ``type`` ("dm", "group", "channel").

name: toolsets_for_source
doc:
Per-source toolset override REPLACING ``platform_toolsets.<platform>``, or None
(default); validated via ``_get_platform_tools`` (webhook adapter pins per-route).

name: format_message
doc:
Format a message for this platform (override for e.g. Telegram
MarkdownV2); default returns content as-is.

name: truncate_message
arguments: content: str, max_length: int=4096, len_fn: Optional[Callable[[str], int]]=None
doc:
Split a long message into chunks preserving code blocks: a split inside a fence closes it
at the chunk end and reopens it (same language tag) in the next; multi-chunk output gets
``(1/3)`` indicators. ``len_fn`` overrides ``len`` (``utf16_len`` for Telegram).

name: _send_again
doc:
Retry: the whole payload normally; only the undelivered remainder after a partial split
delivery (``raw_response["partial_overflow"]``). ``None`` when the adapter cannot resume — the
caller then keeps the partial failure rather than re-sending the already-visible head.

name: _send_one
arguments: path: str, *, is_voice: bool, media_tag: bool
doc:
MEDIA-tag files (``media_tag``) may route to send_voice; bare local files never
do.

name: ea_header_text
doc: Localized ``EA_HEADER_TEXT``.

name: ea_reason_label_text
doc: Localized ``EA_REASON_LABEL_TEXT``.

name: ea_smart_deny_line_text
doc: Localized smart-deny sentence (bare; adapters add their own line breaks/markup).

name: ea_default_reason_text
doc: Localized default "why it was flagged" reason when the approval carries none.

name: ea_action_labels
doc: Localized ``choice -> button label`` for the four approval tiers.

name: approval_timed_out_notice
doc: Localized ``APPROVAL_TIMED_OUT_NOTICE`` for an already-formatted ``window``.

name: approval_timeout_seconds
doc: The configured ``approvals.timeout`` (default 300s); module attribute so tests can pin it.

name: format_approval_window
doc:
Human wording for a timeout (300 → "5 minutes"); one formatter shared with the CLI notice and
the tool result's ``user_summary`` — see ``tools.approval_context.format_approval_window``.

name: format_approval_deadline_line
doc: The last line of every approval prompt: doing nothing is a safe no.

name: safe_url_for_log
doc: Return a URL string safe for logs (no query/fragment/userinfo).

name: streaming_tts_turn_key
arguments: session_key: str | None, turn_marker: Any=None, *, event: Any=None
doc:
Per-turn streaming-TTS suppression key — turn-scoped (not chat-scoped) so
overlapping turns in one chat can't suppress each other's fallback paths.
``turn_marker`` is normally the run generation, else the event's message/update id.

name: streaming_tts_should_skip_whole_file
arguments: completed_turns: set[str], session_key: str | None, turn_marker: Any=None, *, event: Any=None
doc: Pure, turn-scoped auto-TTS suppression decision (testable without the adapter stack).

name: absorb_reply_expected
doc: One turn now answers *other* too: an addressed message wins, then an unknown one.

name: _command_text
doc:
Return the message text with leading Desktop attachment refs stripped.

Desktop's buildContextText prepends ``@image:<path>``, ``@file:<path>``,
or ``@url:<url>`` tags before the user's visible text.  Stripping these
lets is_command / get_command / get_command_args work correctly even
when the payload is prefixed with one or more media refs.

name: is_command
doc: Check if this is a command message (e.g., /new, /reset).

name: get_command
doc: Extract command name if this is a command message.

name: get_command_args
doc: Get the arguments after a command.

name: carry_inbound_dedup
doc:
Seed a rebuilt adapter's dedup caches from the instance it replaces (call before connect).

The runner's reconnect path builds a NEW adapter; without this a platform replaying a recent
inbound ID after the reconnect (websocket resume, webhook retry, unacked poll batch) is
admitted and answered a second time.

name: hand_over_held_inbound
doc:
Move inbound ``source`` is holding to ``target`` (#132829, #133399).

The runner calls it at publish time (retired instance -> replacement) and after disposing a
failed reconnect candidate (candidate -> retained predecessor): a candidate that fails connect
can hold acked updates and salvage pending batches in disconnect(), which must not die with it.

name: cancel_task
doc:
Cancel *task* and wait for it to unwind. ``None``/finished tasks are no-ops; awaiting the
current task would deadlock, so a self-cancel only requests cancellation. Exceptions the task
dies with are swallowed: at teardown nobody is left to handle them.

name: bounded_put
arguments: store: MutableMapping[str, Any], key: str, value: Any, cap: int
doc:
Insert into an insertion-ordered mapping with a hard size bound, evicting the oldest keys. A
re-put moves the key to the newest position so live entries outlast stale ones.

name: _keep_link_target
doc:
``[label](https://url)`` -> ``label\nurl``.

The bare URL is the only thing a platform with its own data detection
(iMessage) can turn back into a tap target, so dropping it makes the link
unreachable rather than merely unformatted. Non-http targets (``mailto:``,
relative paths) are not auto-linked, so they keep the label-only behaviour.

name: strip_markdown
doc:
Strip markdown formatting for plain-text platforms (SMS, iMessage, etc.).

``keep_link_targets`` rewrites ``[label](https://url)`` as ``label\nurl``
instead of discarding the URL; pass it on platforms that auto-link bare URLs.

name: send_chunks
doc:
Send ``chunks`` in order through ``send_one(chunk) -> SendResult``, stopping at the first failure.

A failure after earlier chunks landed carries the ``partial_overflow`` contract that
``BasePlatformAdapter._is_partial_delivery`` reads, so no caller (send retry, plain-text
fallback, cron standalone fallback) re-sends the head the recipient already has.

name: redact_phone
doc: Redact a phone number for logging, preserving country code and last 4.

name: is_table_row
doc: Return True if *line* could plausibly be a table data row.

name: split_markdown_table_row
doc: Split a GFM table row into stripped cells (delegates to agent.markdown_tables).

name: _render_table_block
doc:
Render a GFM table as bold-heading + bullet groups (same alignment logic as Telegram's
renderer: without a row-label column the full row is data and the heading bullet is skipped).

name: convert_table_to_bullets
doc: Rewrite GFM pipe tables into bold-heading + bullet groups; fenced code is left alone.

name: compile_mention_patterns
arguments: raw, *, log_prefix: str, platform_label: str | None=None, display_label: str | None=None, defaults: list[str] | None=None, logger_: logging.Logger | None=None
doc:
Compile regex wake-word/mention patterns from config or env values.

* **Config-style** (dingtalk, telegram): pass ``platform_label``. ``raw`` must be a
  list or string (else warn + ``[]``); non-string entries skipped; info log on load.
* **Wakeword-style** (photon, bluebubbles): pass ``defaults``. ``raw`` may be None
  (defaults), a string (JSON list or comma/newline separated), a list, or a scalar.
``log_prefix`` is interpolated into every log line so per-adapter output stays
byte-identical to the historical inline implementations.

name: text_has_unclosed_fence
doc: Return True when *text* ends inside an unclosed ``` code fence.

name: text_ends_with_table_row
doc: True when the last non-empty line starts and ends with ``|``.

name: is_fence_atom
doc: True when an atomic block is a code block (starts with ```).

name: is_table_atom
doc: True when an atomic block is a table (first line is ``|...|``).

name: _cp_budget
doc:
Code-point count of the longest prefix of *text* within *budget* ``len_fn`` units
(callers guarantee ``len_fn(text) > budget``, so plain ``len`` needs no search).

name: split_at_paragraph_boundary
doc:
Split at the nearest paragraph boundary within *max_chars*; return (head, tail).

Priority: blank line → newline after sentence-ending punctuation (CJK/ASCII)
→ last newline → forced split at the window boundary. ``head + tail == text``
always holds. *len_fn* measures in custom units (e.g. UTF-16 code units).

name: split_markdown_atoms
doc:
Split markdown into indivisible atoms: fenced code blocks, tables
(consecutive ``|...|`` lines) and paragraphs. Blank lines belong to no atom.

name: infer_block_separator
doc:
``'
'`` when the boundary sits at a code fence or a continued table, else ``'

'``.

name: merge_streaming_fences
doc:
Rejoin chunks truncated mid-fence: while chunk *i* has an unclosed fence
and a successor exists, merge the successor in via :func:`infer_block_separator`.

name: balance_fences_across_chunks
doc:
Close orphaned ``` fences at each chunk boundary and reopen (with the
original language tag) on the next, so every chunk is fence-balanced alone.

name: fence_state_after
arguments: text: str, in_code: bool=False, lang: str=''
doc: Walk ``text`` line by line toggling on ``` lines; return the final (in_code, lang).

name: greedy_pack_blocks
doc:
Greedily pack *blocks* (joined with *sep*) into chunks of at most *max_length*; an
oversized block goes through *overflow(block)* (-> list of chunks) if given, else as-is.

name: split_text_fence_aware
doc:
Split markdown into chunks of at most *limit*, respecting fences.

``prefer_paragraphs=True`` (yuanbao-derived): atoms (fences, tables, paragraphs) are
greedily merged, oversized non-atomic chunks split at paragraph boundaries, small
neighbours re-merged; a single atom larger than *limit* is emitted oversize, not broken.
``prefer_paragraphs=False`` (stream_consumer-derived): newline-preferred hard splitting
with headroom reserved for fence markers. ``balance_fences=True`` closes/reopens fences
at chunk boundaries so each chunk renders standalone.

name: _chunk_markdown_paragraphs
doc: Yuanbao-derived paragraph/atom chunking pipeline (see module docs).

name: _chunk_newline_preferred
doc: Stream-consumer-derived newline-preferred splitting (no balancing).

name: is_discord_channel_obfuscated
doc:
True when a discord.py channel object is an obfuscated placeholder.

Skip these wherever guild channels are enumerated (channel directory, message
backfill): history reads and sends always fail with a permission error. Flag
first; the sentinel name is the fallback for discord.py builds that don't
expose the flag (a visible channel literally named ``___hidden___`` is then
also skipped — deliberate bias toward hiding). #90154

name: platform_http_client
doc:
``httpx.AsyncClient`` for a platform adapter: connect-time SSRF validation
(``tools.url_safety.create_ssrf_safe_async_client``), every redirect hop re-checked
(``gateway.platforms.base.ssrf_redirect_guard``, run before any caller ``response`` hooks) and the
shared keepalive pool limits (``platform_httpx_limits()``; pass ``limits=None`` for httpx's
defaults). Defaults ``timeout=30.0`` and ``follow_redirects=True``; other kwargs go to httpx.

doc: Return True if *msg_id* was already seen within the TTL window.

name: contains
doc: Return whether *msg_id* is live in the cache without inserting it.

name: discard
doc: Release a claimed message ID after cancelled/failed handoff.

name: absorb
doc: Adopt *other*'s still-live IDs (at their original seen times) into this cache.

name: _remember
doc:
Record *thread_id* in memory; ``True`` when a persist is still owed.

The in-memory half stays synchronous even for :meth:`mark_async` so that
a ``thread_id in tracker`` check immediately after marking is correct --
the mention-gating logic in the adapters depends on that.

name: mark
doc:
Mark *thread_id* as participated and persist.

Blocking: ends in ``atomic_json_write`` -> ``os.replace``.  Coroutines
must use :meth:`mark_async` instead.

name: mark_async
doc:
Off-loop form of :meth:`mark`.

``_save`` ends in ``atomic_json_write`` -> ``os.replace``, whose
duration is unbounded under filesystem pressure.  Every caller of this
tracker sits on an inbound-message coroutine in the Discord and Matrix
adapters, so the rename must not be paid inline on the event loop -- it
stalls every other adapter's polling and every in-flight turn for as
long as it runs.

Cache downloaded media bytes and return the local file path.

Picks the image / audio / document cache primitive by mime class (or explicit ``kind_hint``

doc: True for the dual-stack default (None/"") and the per-family wildcards.

doc: Profile name when *adapter* was constructed in shared-listener mode, else None.

doc: ``http://host:port`` clients use to reach a listener bound on ``host`` (wildcards → loopback).

name: shared_listener_base
doc: ``http://host:port`` of the default profile's live listener (api_server first, then webhook).

name: bind_listener
arguments: adapter: Any, app: web.Application, host: Optional[str], port: int, ingress_path: str, *, reuse_address: Optional[bool]=None, access_log: Any=...
doc:
Start *app* on ``host:port`` and return its ``AppRunner`` — or, in shared-listener mode,
publish *app* for ``/p/<profile>/`` forwarding and return None (nothing bound). ``ingress_path``
is the adapter's primary callback path, used for the log line and runtime status.

name: publish_shared_ingress
arguments: adapter: Any, app: web.Application, ingress_path: str
doc: Freeze *app* and expose it to the default listener; records the ``/p/<profile>/`` URL.

name: shared_ingress_apps
doc:
``(adapter, app)`` for every shared-listener adapter of a NAMED served profile. ``default`` and
unknown profiles yield nothing: the default's port-binders own their own ports, and a profile
without a live adapter must never fall back to another profile's.

name: dispatch_profile_ingress
arguments: runner: Any, profile: Optional[str], tail: str, request: web.Request, *, scoped: bool=False
doc:
Forward ``/p/<profile>/<tail>`` to the served profile's adapter app that routes ``/<tail>``,
under that profile's runtime scope (``scoped=True`` when the caller already entered it). 404 when
no adapter of *profile* serves the path.

name: has_live_listener
doc:
Blocking probe: True when something accepts connections on ``host:port``. Refused = nobody listens;
any other failure (timeout, unroutable) is treated as live so the caller stays exclusive.

name: start_tcp_site
arguments: runner: web.BaseRunner, host: Optional[str], port: int, *, log_tag: str
doc:
Bind ``host:port`` on ``runner`` and return the started site; raises OSError when unavailable.

SO_REUSEADDR: on macOS (BSD) two wildcard/specific sockets can silently split traffic while
both report success → disable. On Linux it only permits rebinding past TIME_WAIT (a quick
restart would otherwise fail to bind for ~60s) → keep the default.

The macOS exclusive bind also refuses the port while a server-side TIME_WAIT socket lingers
(2*MSL = 30s after the previous gateway closed a connection first — its shutdown, or any
``Connection: close`` request), so a ``/restart`` re-binding within seconds failed with
EADDRINUSE although nobody was listening. Preventing the TIME_WAIT at close time (SO_LINGER 0)
would reset in-flight senders and misses the per-request case, hence the bind-side retry: for an
explicit host, ``has_live_listener`` refused proves the address is free (the kernel still
rejects an exact duplicate even with SO_REUSEADDR, and a foreign wildcard listener answers the
probe), so one retry with reuse_address=True is safe. A wildcard host keeps the strict path: a
foreign listener on a non-loopback interface could not be probed, so it must keep winning.

name: _header_delivery_id
doc: The provider's delivery id (GitHub, Svix, Standard Webhooks, generic), else a fresh one.

name: _is_loopback_host
doc: True when `host` binds only to the local machine (falsy → non-loopback: usually a public default bind).

name: _hmac_str_equal
doc:
Timing-safe str equality tolerant of non-ASCII: ``compare_digest`` raises TypeError on non-ASCII
str and ``provided`` is an attacker-controlled header, so compare as UTF-8 bytes to fail closed.

name: _is_usable_secret
doc:
True when ``secret`` is a string with at least one non-space character.

A whitespace-only value is what an unset key looks like in config. It is
falsy to a person and truthy to ``if not secret``, so a bare falsy check
lets it through. Non-strings are rejected for the same reason.

name: _timestamp_fresh
doc:
True when integer timestamp header *raw* is within the replay window; unparseable → False,
stale → warn ``stale_msg % args`` and False.

name: _is_known_platform
doc: Cross-platform delivery target: built-in names or plugin-registered platforms.

name: check_webhook_requirements
doc: Check if webhook adapter dependencies are available.

arguments: body: bytes, secret: str, msg_id: str, timestamp: str, signature_header: str
doc: Svix-compatible signatures (AgentMail): base64 HMAC-SHA256 of "{id}.{timestamp}.{body}".

The route a delivery chat id names: decoded from a ``webhook:v2:`` token, else the legacy
``webhook:{route}:{delivery}`` spelling that admissions queued before the upgrade still carry.

name: _validate_route
doc: Startup validation: secret required; INSECURE_NO_AUTH only on loopback (crash early on a public footgun).

name: send

doc:
Deliver the agent's response to the destination stored for its opaque ``chat_id`` —
read with ``.get()``, never popped.

Drop delivery_info entries older than the idempotency TTL (bounds the dict by ``rate_limit * TTL``
even when runs never produce a final response).

name: _prune_seen_deliveries
doc: Occasionally prune expired delivery IDs without scanning every POST.

name: _record_rate_limit_hit
doc: Return True if route is still within limit after recording this hit.

name: _record_delivery_id
doc: Return True when this route/profile-qualified delivery should be processed.

name: toolsets_for_source
doc:
Per-route ``toolsets`` override (config.yaml or a manual key in webhook_subscriptions.json —
deliberately NOT settable via `hermes webhook subscribe`, so an agent-created subscription
cannot self-grant tools). Keyed on ``user_id`` (exactly ``webhook:{route}`` as authenticated), not
``chat_id``, whose caller-supplied delivery id and ``:``-bearing route names make any split ambiguous
(GHSA-2fmg-cjqm-hhrj).

name: _handle_health
doc: GET /health — simple health check.

name: _dynamic_route_allowed
doc:
Reject dynamic routes whose effective secret is missing, blank, or not a string
(_is_usable_secret); INSECURE_NO_AUTH is loopback-only.

name: _reload_dynamic_routes
doc:
Reload agent-created subscriptions when the file's stat identity changes.

Runs on every POST before auth, so it never takes the CLI writer lock: writers publish via
atomic rename, which also gives the file a new inode, so a restored mtime cannot hide a change.

name: _resolve_request_profile
doc:
Resolve + validate the /p/<profile>/ URL prefix: None (no prefix, or multiplexing off and the
prefix names this gateway's own profile), the profile name (served under multiplexing), or
``_PROFILE_REJECTED`` (unknown / not served → 404).

doc: Omitting ``profile`` binds a route to default; an explicit null/blank/non-string fails closed.

doc: Runtime scope for a resolved ``/p/<profile>/`` prefix; bare routes get a no-op.

doc: Auth-before-body: size-cap, read, then HMAC-validate. Returns ``(body, None)`` or ``(None, response)``.

doc: JSON, falling back to form-encoded; ``_UNPARSEABLE`` when neither parses.

doc:
deliver_only: the rendered prompt IS the message — skip the agent, reuse the same
auth/rate-limit/idempotency/template pipeline.

arguments: self, prompt: str, route_config: dict, route_name: str, event_type: str, delivery_id: str, profile: Optional[str]=None
doc:
cron_job: fire an EXISTING cron job on this event instead of starting a webhook agent session.
The rendered prompt is transient per-run context (same rail as ``cronjob(action='run', prompt=...)``);
the job's own prompt, skills, model and delivery apply. Same auth/rate-limit/filter/script/idempotency
pipeline as agent routes; 202 immediately, the run happens on a worker thread.

commands would be intercepted by the command parser.

arguments: self, request, route_config: dict, route_name: str, profile, payload: Any, prompt: str, event_type: str, delivery_id: str, now: float
doc: Acknowledge only after the authority commits the immutable delivery.

name: _spawn_agent_run
arguments: self, payload: Any, prompt: str, delivery_id: str, now: float, *, route_config: dict, route_name: str, profile, event_type: str, superseded=()
doc:
Coalesced-path dispatch (settled timer / disconnect flush): admit the merged event as a task
so ``WebhookCoalescer.flush`` can await the hand-off. The HTTP ack for these deliveries was
already ``coalesced``: an admission failure is logged and gives back the batch's delivery ids
(*superseded* too), so a resend of any of them is processed, not answered as a duplicate.

name: _admission_source
arguments: self, route_name: str, profile, delivery_id: str
doc:
The ``SessionSource`` admission builds for one delivery, ``profile_routes`` resolved on it.
The edge's coalesced-route check (``parked_profile_refusal``) asks this same source, so a
route rule matches there exactly when it matches at admission.

name: _admit_agent_run
arguments: self, payload: Any, prompt: str, delivery_id: str, now: float, *, route_config: dict, route_name: str, profile, event_type: str
doc:
Record delivery info and admit the run through the durable producer (shared by the immediate
and coalesced paths). ``"accepted"`` / ``"duplicate"``, or None when admission failed.

doc: Validate webhook signature (GitHub, GitLab, Svix, Standard Webhooks, Linear, generic HMAC-SHA256).

Render a prompt template with dot-notation payload access (``{pull_request.title}``);

doc: Render delivery_extra template values with payload data.

name: _direct_deliver
doc: deliver_only: dispatch *content* to the same delivery helpers agent-mode ``send()`` uses.

name: _deliver_github_comment
doc: Post agent response as a GitHub PR/issue comment via ``gh`` CLI.

name: _github_env
doc:
``gh`` environment for a delivery: a routed profile authenticates with ITS ``GH_TOKEN`` /
``GITHUB_TOKEN`` from the profile secret scope; under multiplex ``os.environ`` carries the default
profile's, so those keys are dropped when the profile has none (fail closed, ``gh`` then falls to
its own stored login). ``None`` (inherit) for bare/default-bound routes.

name: _find_adapter
doc:
The routed profile's own adapter, fail-closed. A ``/p/<profile>/`` route must never post as
another profile's bot, and a bare (default-bound) route must not borrow a platform parked only on
a secondary profile — both directions leaked before #65939.

name: _deliver_cross_platform
arguments: self, platform_name: str, content: str, delivery: dict
doc: Route response to another platform (telegram, discord, etc.).

significant_calls.expression: adapter.send(chat_id, content, metadata={"thread_id": thread_id} if thread_id else None)

name: _delivery_config
doc: Gateway config of the profile a delivery is bound to (call inside ``_profile_scope``).

name: _mirror_delivery
arguments: self, platform_name: str, chat_id: str, content: str, delivery: dict, thread_id: Optional[str]
doc:
Best-effort mirror of a delivered response into the TARGET chat's session transcript, so a
follow-up there ("so he's out?") sees what the webhook run just told the user. Without this the
text only lives in the ephemeral opaque per-delivery webhook session and the target chat's
agent has no idea it sent anything. Same path and USER-role convention as cron briefs
(``cron.scheduler_delivery._maybe_mirror_cron_delivery``, #2221): the text is not the target
session's agent speaking, and a labelled user turn merges safely on strict-alternation providers.
Opt-in per route (``mirror_to_session: true``), default off like cron's ``mirror_delivery``: the text
lands with user authority in a chat the route author may not own, and on ``deliver_only`` routes it is
the raw rendered payload. Called inside the routed profile's scope so the lookup hits THAT profile's
state.db — a DM chat_id is the user's id on every bot, so an unscoped mirror lands in another
profile's DM with the same person. Never raises — a delivered message must not be reported failed
because the mirror broke.

name: validate_coalesce_config
doc:
Startup validation of a route's ``coalesce`` block; raises ValueError so a typo'd route fails
fast instead of silently dispatching every event. Agent-mode routes only.

arguments: self, dispatch: Callable[..., Any], render: Callable[[str, dict, str, str], str]

doc: Buffer one event; False when the key did not resolve and the caller must dispatch immediately.

Dispatch every pending group now and wait until each run is handed to the runner, so an adapter
disconnect/reconnect drops nothing. A hard process kill still loses the current window's buffer.

doc: Resolve a user path, mapping ~/.hermes to the active profile home.

name: _resolve_script_path
doc: Resolve a route script; must live under HERMES_HOME/scripts.

doc: Values from an ``in_file`` list: JSON list, JSON object keys, or one value per non-blank line.

name: resolve_filter_field
arguments: self, field: Any, payload: dict, event_type: str, headers: Any
doc: Resolve a dotted filter field against payload/event/headers context; ``_MISSING`` when absent.

name: filter_matches
arguments: self, spec: Any, payload: dict, event_type: str, headers: Any
doc: Evaluate one declarative webhook filter spec (``all``/``any``/``not`` combinators, then field ops).

name: route_filters_match
arguments: self, route_config: dict, payload: dict, event_type: str, headers: Any

name: run_route_script
doc:
Run a route script and return (should_continue, transformed_payload).

Non-zero exit, empty/``[SILENT]`` stdout, or a ``[SILENT]``/``__hermes_ignore__`` flag drops the
webhook; JSON-object stdout replaces the payload, other text is attached as ``script_output``.

name: _refuse_parked
doc:
A delivery routed to a parked profile is retryable, never refused for good: a rescan serves the
profile again, so it is ``runtime_draining`` (a webhook answers 503; relay acknowledges and tells
the sender, ``parked_route_refusal``), not the permanent ``profile_mismatch`` of a route to a
profile this gateway does not serve.

name: parked_profile_refusal
doc:
A 503 for a webhook whose profile is not served right now, else None: a ``/p/<profile>/``
prefix that is parked or has no serving authority here, or a coalesced route that
``profile_routes`` sends to a profile admission would refuse (a coalesced delivery is acknowledged
before admission applies that route). A parked target is retryable (``Retry-After``); any other
rejected target gets the answer the immediate route gives when admission refuses it.
``admission_source`` returns the ``SessionSource`` admission builds for this delivery
(``WebhookAdapter._admission_source``), so ``profile_routes`` match here exactly as there. Answered
before the delivery id is recorded: coalesced, ``deliver_only`` and ``cron_job`` routes act before
(or without) an admission, so the in-memory id is their only replay guard, and a recorded id would
answer the provider's retry as a duplicate once the profile is served again.

name: _prefix_not_served
doc:
Parked, or on disk with no serving authority here (its own gateway still runs, or it is not
picked up yet): the URL prefix resolves against the profiles on disk, the registry says what is
served.

name: _coalesced_route_refusal
doc:
How admission would refuse a coalesced bare-route delivery that ``profile_routes`` sends away:
``'parked'`` (retryable), ``'refused'`` (a profile neither served here nor parked: standalone,
unknown, or without a live authority), else None. Reads the profile the admission's own source
resolved (``build_source`` asks ``GatewayRunner._profile_name_for_source`` on the same chat_id,
user_id and names), so this edge and admission give one answer: an explicit ``/p/<profile>/``
wins over ``profile_routes`` there, and routes apply only under multiplexing.

name: admit_producer
doc:
Commit a producer delivery; ``None`` when a plugin skipped or consumed it.

``pre_gateway_dispatch`` and ``post_gateway_admission`` (#129958) fire once per admission, like
``GatewayInboundMixin._handle_message``: before the commit (a skipped or consumed delivery is
never admitted, a rewrite is what gets committed; a consumer's reply rides
``event._consumer_reply`` for the caller's own reply leg), and never for a replay of an
already-committed delivery (provider retry, relay re-send) nor at execution (PLG-5).

name: _release_preparation
doc:
A delivery a plugin skipped or consumed, or one refused or cancelled after preparing, is never
admitted: release the media its preparation (``_prepared``) copied into the retained store. A path
another admission or an in-flight capture holds is kept, as for a refused admission.

name: _prepared
doc:
``(validated payload, principal)`` of this delivery. Preparing the payload runs the same
authorization as admission, so a refused sender raises here.

name: _committed
doc: The rows of this delivery's identity in the FIFO.

name: finalize_webhook
doc: End only the settled admitted generation, atomically with the epoch fence.

name: recover_webhook_finalizations
doc: Close settled original webhooks only after current route authorization succeeds.

name: render_mcp_event_prompt
arguments: adapter, route_config: dict, payload: Any, event_type: str, route_name: str
doc:
The prompt for an occurrence on an MCP event route whose template uses ``{data}``; None otherwise.
``{data}`` takes the whole payload (up to ``_MAX_EVENT_DATA_CHARS``, with a note when cut) instead of
the 2,000-character cap other placeholders get, and the JSON goes in after the rest of the template
renders, so text inside the payload is never read as a placeholder.

name: mcp_event_delivery_id
doc:
``eventId`` is the sketch's dedup key (stable across retries and redeliveries), unlike the
per-attempt ``webhook-id``.

name: _verification
arguments: adapter, route_name: str, route_config: dict, payload: dict, profile

name: _terminated
arguments: adapter, route_name: str, route_config: dict, payload: dict, profile

name: _gap
arguments: adapter, route_name: str, route_config: dict, payload: dict, profile

name: handle_mcp_event_control
arguments: adapter, route_name: str, route_config: dict, payload: Any, profile
doc:
The response for a control envelope on an MCP event route; None lets the delivery continue
as an event occurrence (whose replay cursor, when the server sends one, is remembered first).

name: _stash
arguments: pattern: str, text: str, tag: str
doc: Replace every ``pattern`` match with a ``\x00<tag><n>\x00`` placeholder.

name: _header_to_bold
doc:
``# Header`` → ``*Header*``, stripping already-bolded ``*...*`` so ``# **Title**``
doesn't render with literal asterisks.

name: resolve_whatsapp_bridge_dir
doc:
Bridge directory for CLI and adapter. A read-only install tree (e.g. Docker
/opt/hermes) is mirrored to HERMES_HOME so npm install works.

name: _sanitize_outbound_text
doc:
Strip zero-width format chars (WORD JOINER etc.) and normalize odd unicode
spaces — WhatsApp renders them as mojibake prefixes. Emoji joiners are kept.

name: _effective_reply_prefix
doc: Prefix for outgoing replies in self-chat mode (Cloud API overrides to ``""``).

name: _outgoing_chunk_limit
doc: Reserve room for the reply prefix; floor keeps space for pagination/fence repair.

name: _whatsapp_free_response_chats
doc: ``extra.free_response_chats`` (blank = unset) else the scoped env CSV.

name: _coerce_allow_list
doc: Parse allow_from / group_allow_from from config (list or JSON-list string) or env var (CSV).

name: _select_allowlist
arguments: extra: dict[str, Any], config_keys, env_keys, read_env
doc:
``(source, raw)`` by key *presence*: a config key wins (an explicit empty list stays authoritative),
then the first truthy env carrier; ``(None, None)`` when neither is set.

name: _select_dm_allowlist
arguments: self, extra: dict[str, Any], env_keys, read_env
doc:
Raw DM allowlist; records the winning source in ``_dm_allowlist_source`` so live DM checks keep
the same precedence.

name: _live_dm_allow_from
doc:
Allowlist currently enforced for DM intake / strict DM auth. Env-seeded adapters re-read
the same key so pairing approve/revoke takes effect without restart; a removed key (sole-entry
revoke) means empty, not the construction snapshot. Config-seeded adapters keep the in-memory
set (pairing revoke purges it in place) — a stale env value must not broaden access.

name: _is_broadcast_chat
doc:
Status updates (Stories) and Channel/Newsletter broadcasts — never reply
(answering a Story spams the status feed; Channel posts aren't addressable).

name: _matches_whatsapp_allowlist
doc:
Match a WhatsApp identifier against an allowlist across phone/LID forms. Inbound senders
arrive as ``<id>@lid`` while allowlists hold phone numbers (or vice versa), so resolve both
sides through the bridge's lid-mapping files via ``gateway.whatsapp_identity``.

name: _clean_bot_mention_text
arguments: self, text: str, data: dict[str, Any]

name: format_message
doc:
Convert markdown to WhatsApp syntax (*bold*, _italic_, ~strike~); fenced and
inline code are protected via placeholder substitution.

name: _positive_env
doc: ``cast(env)`` when set, parseable and > 0; else *default*.

name: platform_httpx_limits
doc: ``httpx.Limits`` tuned for persistent platform-adapter clients; ``None`` without httpx.

name: get_scoped_secret
arguments: name: str, default: Any=None, *, external_fallback: bool=False
doc:
Scope-aware credential read with the default-profile startup fallback.

An installed profile secret scope is authoritative: a scoped miss returns
``default`` (never borrow another profile's value from ``os.environ``).
The DEFAULT profile constructs and sends *unscoped* under multiplexing,
where a bare ``get_secret`` raises ``UnscopedSecretError``; there
``os.environ`` is that profile's own value, so fall back to it.

``external_fallback`` adds one rung for startup gates that run before any
scope exists: an unscoped miss consults a one-shot build of the profile's
own secret scope, so externally managed credentials (Bitwarden etc., only
``BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN`` in ``.env``) are visible to ``check_requirements``.

name: _unscoped_profile_secrets
doc: Process-cached profile secret mapping (external resolvers are slow); failures degrade to {}.

name: platform_gate_env
doc:
Allow/deny gate env read with per-profile isolation, always stripped.

With a profile secret scope installed AND multiplexing active, a scoped miss returns ``default``
