on a large store, which used to stall the prompt once a day. ``auto_prune_from_config`` owns the
config gate and the 24h marker and never raises.

name: _cancel_row
arguments: value: str='cancel', label_key: str='cli.billing.choice_cancel', desc_key: str='cli.billing.desc_do_nothing'

name: _modal_choice
doc: Run the choice modal and return the normalized choice value.

name: _block_header
doc: Blank line, ``<icon> <bold title>`` via _cprint, then (optionally) the rule via print.

name: _dim
doc: Dim ``  <icon><msg>`` line via _cprint; ``lead`` prints a blank line first.

name: _ok
doc: Dim ``✓ <msg>`` success line.

name: _print_logged_out
doc: Logged-out / fetch-failed block shared by /subscription and /topup.

name: _print_org_line
doc: Dim ``Org: <name> · <Role>`` line (skipped when there is no org).

name: _try_usage_model
doc: Shared dollar usage model (the only source with top-up dollars); None on any failure.

name: _usage_bar_lines
doc: Plan + top-up bars as lines (filled = remaining). Caller picks the print fn: ordering differs per surface.

name: _step_up_remote_spending
doc: "! One-time setup" step-up (explain → confirm → device-flow). True only when granted; refusals print.

name: _print_portal_line
doc: ``Portal: <url>`` via _cprint when the error carries a portal deep-link.

name: _open_url_in_browser
doc: The one portal opener. Refuses TTY-hijacking text browsers (w3m/lynx over SSH) via the auth guard.

name: _open_or_print_url
doc: Open ``url`` in the browser, or print it when no graphical browser can be used.

name: _print_nous_credits_block
doc:
Nous dollar balance block (two bars); True if anything printed. Shared dollar model first, then
legacy ``nous_credits_lines``. Agent-independent (TUI slash-worker has no live agent). Fail-open.

name: _print_usage_cta
doc: The `/usage` call-to-action; mirrors the TUI's ``USAGE_CTA``. Nous-account only.

name: _show_subscription
doc: `/subscription` (alias `/upgrade`). Deep-links NAS's ``/manage-subscription`` (NOT Stripe); never charges.

name: _subscription_overview
doc: Plan read block, then the action: portal hand-off (member / non-interactive), catalog (Free), change menu.

name: _subscription_free_catalog
doc: Free + admin + interactive: catalog → pick → portal deep-link ``plan=<tier_id>`` (a new sub needs a card).

name: _subscription_open_portal
doc: Open / copy the manage-subscription URL — the portal hand-off.

name: _subscription_change_menu
doc: The in-terminal change menu for a paid admin/owner (interactive).

name: _subscription_pick_tier
doc: Tier picker → preview → confirm. Paid tiers other than current (dropping to free = cancellation).

name: _subscription_preview_and_confirm
doc: Preview → effect → confirm+apply. ``allow_stepup=False`` (post-grant replay) never re-prompts a step-up.

name: _subscription_confirm_cancel
doc: Confirm, then schedule a cancellation at period end.

name: _subscription_apply
doc: Run ("upgrade"|"schedule", tier_id) / ("cancel"|"resume", None); scope denial → step-up + ONE replay, same key.

name: _subscription_handle_scope_required
doc: insufficient_scope → step-up, then replay `retry` ONCE so the user never re-runs the command.

name: _subscription_render_error
doc: Render a subscription BillingError (a lighter _billing_render_charge_error).

name: _subscription_render_upgrade_ambiguous
doc: AMBIGUOUS outcome (NAS may have charged) → steer to a re-check, never a blind retry (key isn't persisted).

name: _show_billing
doc:
`/topup` — ZERO sub-commands (argument ignored; Overview is the only route). Non-interactive never
prompts. Money is Decimal end-to-end; the terminal never collects card details.

name: _billing_portal_hint
doc: Print a portal deep-link line (the funnel for portal-only actions).

name: _billing_require_admin
doc: Admin + org kill-switch gate; portal funnel + False when blocked. ``icon`` adds a blank line + prefix.

name: _billing_overview
doc: Screen 1 — balance, bars, menu. No scope preflight (a charge 403s); a missing card does NOT gate it.

name: _billing_add_card_flow
doc: No card → add it on the portal (never in-terminal), bounded re-check loop. Refreshed state, or None.

name: _billing_buy_flow
doc: Screen 2 (presets) → Screen 3 (confirm+charge+poll). No scope preflight: react to the server's 403s.

name: _billing_confirm_and_charge
doc: Screen 3 — confirm total + consent, charge, then poll to settlement.

name: _billing_submit_and_poll
arguments: self, state, amount, key, *, missing_msg, status_msg, on_scope=None
doc: POST the charge, then poll. ``on_scope`` handles a scope denial (first submit); else it renders.

name: _billing_poll_charge
doc: Poll loop: 2s interval, 5-min cap, cancellable. settled = ledger truth.

name: _billing_render_charge_failed
doc: Poll `failed` reasons → the right copy + portal funnel.

name: _billing_render_charge_error
doc: Submit-time BillingError. Order matters: revoked/session before code lookups; Transient before scope.

name: _billing_handle_scope_required
doc: 403 insufficient_scope → reauth, then resume ``amount`` on explicit confirm, reusing the idempotency key.

name: _billing_auto_reload_flow
doc: Screen 4 — threshold + reload-to → PATCH. Prefills; validates ``reload_to > threshold``; "Turn off" if on.

name: _billing_patch_auto_top_up
doc: PATCH auto-top-up; scope denials → step-up, other errors → renderer. True on success.

name: _billing_offer_keep_going_off
doc:
Turning "Keep going on credits" off only stops spending, so an admin can still do it with
Remote Spending off (the portal and the server allow it too).

name: _billing_keep_going_on_credits_flow
doc:
Window plans: flip "Keep going on credits". Turning it on spends money later, so it asks
first; turning it off does not.

name: _billing_set_keep_going
arguments: self, state, turn_on: bool, *, allow_stepup: bool
doc:
PATCH the setting. A scope denial runs the step-up, then sends the same change ONCE (no card or
org Remote Spending check: the setting is not a charge, and turning it off must always work).

name: _billing_auto_reload_disable
doc: PATCH ``enabled:false``; the endpoint still requires threshold/topUpAmount → echo current (or 0).

name: _billing_limit_screen
doc: Screen 5 — monthly spend limit (read-only; cap is portal-only).

name: _ask_amount
doc: One amount; empty keeps `current` when editing. Decimal / kept value, or _CANCELLED (already printed).

name: _gateway_is_remote
doc:
True when this CLI attaches to an explicitly named gateway WebSocket that is not loopback
(``HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL``): Desktop's ``mode === 'remote'``.

name: gateway_browser
arguments: cli, connection, word: str, rest: str
doc:
``/browser`` on the shared gateway (#134889 CLI-9): ``browser.manage``, the verb Ink and
Desktop send. The browser tools run in the gateway, so changing this process's
``BROWSER_CDP_URL`` would change nothing the agent uses. ``connect``/``disconnect`` manage a
browser on the gateway HOST: only against a local gateway (Desktop's rule). The gateway scopes
them to this session's profile.

name: _normalize_cdp_url
doc:
Validate a /browser connect URL: ``(cdp_url, port)`` or None after printing the error.
A ``/devtools/browser/<id>`` path is kept verbatim; anything else is reduced to the origin.

name: refusal_text
doc:
The refusal as the client shows it: the reason code, plus the check that fired when the owner
named one (``invalid_params (toolsets: unknown or invalid toolset name: 'mcp-codegraph')``).

The gateway sends ``field``/``detail`` in the JSON-RPC error's ``data``
(``gateway/session_controls.py``), and ``hermes_cli.gateway_client.rpc_error`` carries the
bounded scalars onto ``GatewayRPCError.data``. A refusal from anywhere else has no ``data`` and
reads exactly as before.

name: chat_error_response
arguments: error: Exception | str, *, provider: str='', model: str='', failure_reason: str | None=None
doc:
Two-line panel text: plain sentence with the fix command, then ``Details: <raw>``.

``failure_reason`` is the verdict the turn loop already stamped on its result
(``agent/turn_failure_copy.stamp_failure``). When present it is used as-is instead of
re-classifying a summarised string (which has no status code and almost always lands on
'unknown'); for the loop's own site codes the ``error`` text is already the user-facing copy,
so it is returned verbatim rather than wrapped and demoted to a Details line.

name: agent_init_failure_message
doc:
Copy for a failed AIAgent build on first message: the user's turn was dropped.

A gateway that cannot be reached keeps its whole first line: its discovery detail is already
bounded (``DiscoveryError.bounded_detail``) and ends in the repair command, which the summary
limit would cut mid-path.

name: _sync_fallback_chain_with_config
doc:
Adopt ``fallback_providers`` edits made while this chat is open (#95066) — the same
per-turn, fail-closed contract as the Desktop/TUI and messaging gateways: a torn config.yaml
keeps the last known-good chain instead of reading as "chain removed".

name: chat
arguments: self, message, images: list | None=None, voice_input: bool=False
doc:
Run one user turn; returns the agent's response, or None on error.

Input typed while the agent runs goes to ``_interrupt_queue`` (separate from
``_pending_input`` so process_loop and the interrupt monitor never compete); an
interrupting message is re-queued as the next turn. ``voice_input`` gates the
concise voice-response prefix.

Args: message: The user's message (str or multimodal content list) images: Optional list of Path
objects for attached images voice_input: True when the message came from voice transcription (gates
the concise voice-response prefix, #65827)

name: _chat_release_turn_audio
doc: Every exit path: stop the thinking sound, send the TTS sentinel, cut TTS only if abnormal.

name: _chat_route_images
doc:
Attach images natively (vision model) or pre-describe them as text; returns the message to send.

"native" → OpenAI-style content parts (adapters translate per provider); "text" →
vision_analyze each image and prepend the description. Decision: agent/image_routing.py.

name: _chat_stage_user_message
doc: Append the staged user dict to the transcript under the agent's persist lock.

name: _chat_setup_turn_audio
doc: Arm the full-duplex listener and the streaming-TTS pipeline for this turn (voice mode only).

name: _chat_run_agent
doc: Agent-thread body: bind per-thread callbacks/approval key, prepend one-shot notes, run the turn.

name: _chat_monitor_agent_thread
doc: Poll the interrupt queue while the agent thread runs; returns the interrupting message (or None).

name: _chat_settle_turn
doc: After the agent thread ends: freeze timers, flush streams, drain TTS, sync history/session id.

name: _chat_render_turn
doc:
Post-turn display: errors, interrupt marker, reasoning/response panels, bell, re-queues.

Returns the response text.

name: _chat_resolve_interrupt
doc:
Return ``(pending_message, show_marker)``; clears a stale agent interrupt flag.

The marker is printed separately after the response Panel (history suppressed)
so a terminal redraw never duplicates it.

name: _chat_print_reasoning_box
doc: Collapsed reasoning box when show_reasoning is on and streaming did not already show it.

name: _chat_print_response_panel
doc: Response box (close TTS-drawn box / post-stream transform / Rich Panel), then billing CTA.

name: _attempt
doc: ``fn(*args, **kwargs)``, or ``_FAILED`` after printing ``  <label>: <exc>`` for ``errors``.

name: _take_flag
doc:
Pop ``flag VALUE`` out of ``parts``: ``(rest, value, ok)``; ok=False when the value is
missing (caller prints usage).

name: _summarize_paths
doc: ``a, b, c (+N more)`` for a list of paths.

name: _ellipsize
doc: ``text[:limit]`` plus ``...`` when truncated.

name: _persist_display_choice
arguments: key: str, value: str, label: str, note: str
doc: Save a /busy-style choice to config and report saved vs session-only.

name: _split_scope_flags
doc:
``(arg, explicit_global)`` for /reasoning + /fast: session scope by default, ``--global``
persists to config.yaml, ``--session`` is an explicit no-op (parity with /model).

name: _scope_outcome
doc: Parenthetical tail for a scoped setting change.

name: _toggle_target
doc:
Resolve a ``/x [on|off|status]`` argument: "status" for a status query, a bool for the
new state (bare arg toggles), or None when the argument is unrecognized.

name: _cron_api
doc: Call the cronjob model tool and decode its JSON reply.

name: _print_side_result_panel
arguments: cli, *, header_lines, body, title_suffix, empty_note, console=None
doc:
Print a worker-thread result (/bg, /btw, /login) into the scrollback: accent rules around
``header_lines``, then ``body`` in a skinned Rich panel (or ``empty_note``).
Forces a TUI refresh first so the spinner/status bar don't overlap the output.

name: _refresh_tui_before_print
doc:
Invalidate the running TUI (brief pause for the redraw) then print a blank separator, so
worker-thread output doesn't overlap the spinner/status bar.

name: _print_lightpanda_engine_status
doc:
``/browser status`` line(s) about ``browser.engine: lightpanda`` — silent unless set;
says whether it is in use or which higher-precedence setting shadows it.

name: _browser_use
doc: /browser use [off] — toggle Browser Use mode (browser.backend); resets the session.

name: _launch_default_cdp_browser
doc:
Launch a local debug browser for the default CDP URL; returns the discovered CDP url or
None (after printing what went wrong / how to launch manually).

name: _browser_connect
doc:
/browser connect [url] — validate the CDP URL, find or launch a debug browser, then
point the browser tools at it (BROWSER_CDP_URL) and tell the model.

name: _checkpoint_manager
doc: The agent's checkpoint manager, or None after printing why it is unavailable.

name: _handle_rollback_command
doc:
Handle /rollback [diff] <N> [<file>|--all] — list, diff, or restore checkpoints.
A restore also undoes the last chat turn; ``--all`` overwrites user hand-edits too.

name: _rollback_diff
arguments: self, mgr, cwd: str, target_hash: str

name: _rollback_restore
arguments: self, mgr, cwd, target_hash: str, file_path, restore_all: bool

name: _handle_diff_command
doc:
Handle /diff [working|staged|all|session] [--stat] [<path>...] — git changes in the
cwd; ``session`` is everything Hermes changed since the checkpoint baseline.

name: _print_diff_body
arguments: self, diff: str, stat_hint: str, limit: int=400, total: int=0
doc: Print a diff, capped at ``limit`` lines (of ``total`` when its sender cut it) with a pointer to the --stat form.

name: _print_session_diff
doc: Print the cumulative checkpoint-baseline diff (/diff session).

name: _print_diff_text
doc:
Render diff/stat text with color when a rich console is present; plain print otherwise
(e.g. unit tests instantiating the mixin standalone).

name: _handle_snapshot_command
doc: Handle /snapshot [list|create [label]|restore <id>|prune [N]] — state snapshots.

name: _handle_export_command
doc: Handle /export [profile] [-o path] — export a profile to a shareable .tar.gz archive.

name: _handle_import_command
doc:
Handle /import <archive.tar.gz> [--name <name>] — import a shared profile archive as a
new profile.

name: _handoff_keep
doc: Print ``lines`` and keep the CLI session (the True verdict of /handoff).

name: _handle_handoff_command
doc:
Handle ``/handoff <platform>`` — transfer this CLI session to a gateway platform.

Validate target → prepare session row → mark pending → block-poll (see ``_handoff_wait``).
Returns False only on ``completed`` (caller exits like /quit); True keeps the session.

name: _handoff_validate_target
doc:
Resolve the destination home channel via the live gateway config; None (after printing
the reason) when the platform is unknown, disabled, or has no home channel.

name: _handoff_prepare_session
doc:
Refuse mid-turn, make sure a SessionDB handle + session row exist, and return the
display title (None after printing why the handoff cannot start).

name: _handoff_wait
doc:
Two-phase 0.5s poll. PENDING (unclaimed): 60s, then CAS-fail the row so the user can
retry (a claim racing this instant wins). RUNNING (claimed): the gateway replays the
transcript via a synthetic turn (routinely >60s) — wait 15 min with heartbeats and on
timeout do NOT touch the row; failing it here was the split-brain bug.

name: _handle_resume_command
doc: Handle /resume <session_id_or_title> — switch to a previous session mid-conversation.

name: _resolve_resume_target
doc:
``(session_id, meta)`` for a numbered selection, title, or id (an empty compression-chain head
redirects to the descendant holding the transcript); None after printing why it was not resolved.

name: _handle_sessions_command
doc:
Handle /sessions [list|<id_or_title>] — bare/``list`` prints the recent-sessions table;
an explicit target delegates to /resume so both spellings behave identically.

name: _handle_branch_command
doc:
Handle /branch [name] — fork the current session into a new independent copy of the
full history so a different approach can be explored without losing the original.

name: _handle_worktree_command
doc:
Handle /worktree [new [name]|list|prune [--dry-run]] — isolated git worktrees.
``new`` moves this session into the tree (as ``hermes -w``: kept on exit only with
unpushed commits); ``prune`` never deletes tracked changes, unique commits, or in-use trees.

name: _handle_personality_command
doc:
Handle /personality [name] — list or set a predefined personality. All resolution and
persistence goes through hermes_cli.personality, the single owner of personality state.

name: _handle_pet_command
doc:
Handle /pet [toggle|list|scale <n>|off|<slug>] — the petdex mascot. Writes
``display.pet.*`` to config; pet surfaces pick it up on their next poll.

name: _handle_hatch_command
doc:
Generate ("hatch") a new petdex pet from a description: base look, one animation row
per state, spritesheet, then adopt. Progress streams inline (~a minute of image calls).
The desktop app opens a richer overlay for this command instead.

name: _handle_cron_command
doc:
Handle the /cron command to manage scheduled tasks. Only without a gateway session: on the shared
gateway every /cron form runs there (hermes_cli/gateway_setting_commands.py).

name: _handle_suggestions_command
doc:
Handle /suggestions — review/accept/dismiss suggested automations via the shared handler.
CLI origin is the local platform so an accepted job's "origin" delivery resolves to a home channel.

name: _handle_blueprint_command
doc:
Handle /blueprint — set up an automation from a blueprint template (shared handler).
Bare lists the catalog; ``<name>`` seeds the agent to ask for each value conversationally
(``agent_seed``, run as the next turn); ``<name> slot=val …`` creates the job directly.

name: _handle_curator_command
doc:
Handle /curator — delegates to hermes_cli.curator so the CLI and the `hermes curator`
subcommand share the same handler set.

name: _handle_kanban_command
doc: Handle /kanban — strip the leading ``/kanban`` and hand the rest to ``kanban.run_slash``.

name: _handle_skills_command
doc:
Handle /skills slash command — delegates to hermes_cli.skills_hub, after intercepting the
write-approval review subcommands (pending/approve/reject/diff/mode).

name: _handle_memory_command
doc: Handle /memory slash command — pending review + approval-gate toggle.

name: _save_write_approval
doc: Persist <subsystem>.write_approval to config (for /memory|/skills approval).

name: _queue_prompt_turn
arguments: self, msg: str, command: str, ack: str=''
doc:
Inject ``msg`` onto the agent's input queue as the next normal user turn (the
/learn, /plan, /init pattern: no engine, no model-tool footprint, prompt-cache safe). ``ack``
paints first on the turn's own channel (_cprint), so the turn's `────` never overtakes it.

name: _handle_learn_command
doc:
Handle /learn — distill a reusable skill from anything the user describes (a directory,
a URL, "what we just did", pasted notes). The live agent gathers the material with the
tools it already has and authors the skill via ``skill_manage``.

name: _handle_plan_command
doc:
Handle /plan — write a markdown implementation plan, no execution. The live agent
inspects the workspace read-only and saves the plan under ``.hermes/plans/``.

name: _handle_init_command
doc:
Handle /init — generate or update AGENTS.md from a project scan performed by the
live agent with its own read-only tools.

name: _handle_background_command
doc:
Handle /bg <prompt> — run a prompt in a separate background session (its own AIAgent
on a thread); the result prints here without touching the active history.

name: _start_background_worker
doc: The /bg result panel's daemon thread (``produce()`` returns the answer text).

name: _side_worker
arguments: self, produce, *, name, fail_label, header_lines, title_suffix, empty_note, bell=False, on_done=None, console=None
doc:
Daemon thread for /bg, /btw and /login: ``produce()`` returns the body to print in a side-result
panel; failures print ``fail_label`` failed; the TUI is always re-invalidated afterwards.

name: _handle_login_command
doc: Start an in-chat sign-in without blocking the input loop while approval is pending.

name: _handle_btw_command
doc:
Handle /btw <question> — answer a side question about this conversation from a
history snapshot via a one-shot auxiliary call. The live session is never touched
(no history mutation, no role-alternation risk, no cache invalidation).

name: _handle_bundles_command
doc:
In-session ``/bundles`` — show installed skill bundles (``hermes bundles list`` rendered
inside the running CLI). Bundles are loaded via ``/<bundle-name>``.

name: _handle_browser_command
doc: Handle /browser connect|disconnect|status|use — manage the live Chromium-family CDP connection.

name: _session_manager
doc:
The session-scoped manager from ``getter()``, or None after the standard dim
"<label> unavailable (no active session)." line.

name: _handle_heartbeat_command
doc:
Dispatch /heartbeat: set / status / pause / resume / clear. ``/heartbeat every 10m <prompt>``
sets the session's one recurring instruction, injected as a normal user turn when due.
Session-scoped and in-process — use `hermes cron` for durable schedules.

name: _heartbeat_set
doc: Set: ``/heartbeat every 10m <prompt>`` (also accepts ``10m <prompt>``).

name: _handle_refine_command
doc:
Dispatch /refine — run the memory/skill review fork on demand (same machinery as the
automatic post-turn ``_spawn_background_review``), with optional focus text. Background
fork; the live conversation and prompt cache are never touched.

significant_calls.expression:
agent._spawn_background_review(
                messages_snapshot=snapshot, review_memory=True,
                review_skills="skill_manage" in getattr(agent, "valid_tool_names", set()),
                focus=focus or None, explicit=True)

name: _handle_review_command
doc:
Dispatch /review — snapshot the last N messages (+ argument text as instructions) and
spawn an independent reviewer subagent via async delegation; the review re-enters this
session as a normal delegation completion.

significant_calls.expression:
dispatch_goal_command(
            mgr, _command_arg(cmd), authorize_gate=lambda: None,
            progress=lambda text: _cp(_dim_line(text)),
            last_user_message=last_user_message_content(getattr(self, "conversation_history", None)),
        )

name: _kick_goal
doc: Queue the next turn without mutating cached conversation history.

name: _handle_loop_command
doc:
Dispatch /loop — recurring in-session wakeups: ``/loop [interval] <prompt> [--times N]
[--until <cond>]`` starts one; ``status | pause | resume | stop`` control it.

name: _handle_subgoal_command
doc:
Dispatch /subgoal: bare → show, ``<text>`` → append, ``remove <n>`` (1-based), ``clear``.
Subgoals join the judge + continuation prompts at the next turn boundary (no kick).

name: _handle_skin_command
doc: Handle /skin [name] — show or change the display skin.

name: _compose_in_editor
doc:
Open ``$VISUAL``/``$EDITOR`` on a temp markdown file and return the saved buffer with
``#!`` comment lines stripped; "" if the editor failed or the buffer was left empty.
Factored out so the read-back/strip logic is unit-testable.

name: _handle_prompt_compose_command
doc:
Handle /prompt — compose the next prompt in $EDITOR (optionally seeded with the argument)
and queue it as the next agent turn via the one-shot ``_pending_agent_seed`` (as /blueprint).

name: _handle_focus_command
doc:
``/focus [on|off|status]`` — DISPLAY-ONLY reduced output. Reuses the ``/verbose``
suppression path: on stashes tool_progress_mode and snaps it to "off" (what
``agent/tool_executor.py`` gates on); off restores the stash verbatim. Never touches
history, system prompt, or request payloads.

name: _set_tool_progress_mode
doc:
Set the live tool-progress mode on both the CLI and the agent (one write path for
/focus and /verbose — the agent copy is what ``agent/tool_executor.py`` gates on).

name: _note_focus_hidden_line
doc:
Count one tool line focus view is suppressing this turn — against the mode the user had
BEFORE focus snapped to "off", so a prior ``/verbose off`` user is never told focus hid lines.

name: _emit_focus_recovery_line
doc: Print the dim post-turn recovery line and reset the counter.

name: _handle_approvals_command
doc: Show or persist the profile-wide dangerous-command approval mode.

name: _toggle_setting
arguments: self, arg: str, current: bool, *, usage: str, status_line: str, config_key: str, label: str, failed: str
doc:
Shared /footer + /timestamps flow: status query, usage error, or save + report.
Returns the new bool state when it was saved (None otherwise).

name: _handle_footer_command
doc: Toggle or inspect ``display.runtime_footer.enabled`` (``/footer [on|off|status]``).

name: _handle_timestamps_command
doc:
Toggle or inspect ``display.timestamps`` (``/timestamps [on|off|status]``). When on,
message labels carry an ``[HH:MM]`` suffix and ``/history`` prefixes stored-timestamp turns.

name: _handle_reasoning_command
doc:
Handle /reasoning [<level> [--global]|show|hide|full|clamp] — effort level (session
scope unless --global) and thinking display toggles (always saved).

name: _handle_busy_command
doc: Handle /busy [status|queue|steer|interrupt] — what Enter does while Hermes is working.

name: _handle_indicator_command
doc:
Handle /indicator [status|kaomoji|emoji|unicode|ascii] — pick the TUI busy-indicator style.
Persists to ``display.tui_status_indicator`` (the key the TUI reads) for its next render.

name: _handle_fast_command
doc:
Handle /fast — toggle fast mode (OpenAI Priority Processing / Anthropic Fast Mode).
Session-scoped by default; ``--global`` persists agent.service_tier to config.yaml
(parity with /model and /reasoning).

name: _handle_debug_command
doc:
Handle /debug [nous|local] — upload debug report + logs and print share URLs.
Default: public paste service; ``nous``: Nous-internal (staff-only); ``local``: render to
stdout, no upload. ``local`` wins if both are given (never touches the network).

name: _handle_update_command
doc:
Handle /update — exit the session and relaunch as ``hermes update``. Returns True when
confirmed (the caller exits the app; the relaunch runs on the main thread after
prompt_toolkit restores terminal modes), False when cancelled.

name: _handle_voice_command
doc: Handle /voice [on|off|tts|status] command.

name: _handle_wake_command
doc:
Handle /wake [on|off|status] — the 'Hey Hermes' hotword listener. The toggle IS the
config: on/off also writes ``wake_word.enabled`` so the choice persists; startup
auto-arm only reads it.

name: _persist_wake_word_enabled
doc: Save ``wake_word.enabled`` so the /wake toggle sticks for future sessions.

name: _settle_session_model
doc:
A completed sign-in moved this profile onto the account: the welcome host is gone and
the portal serves ``nous/welcome`` as a paid model, so a session still carrying it must
move too — the CLI counterpart of the gateway's on-``Completed`` sweep. Only the free
tier's own model is replaced; a model the user picked while the sign-in was pending
stands. Writing ``self.model`` is enough: ``chat()`` compares the turn-route signature
and rebuilds the agent on the next turn, so a turn already in flight keeps the agent it
started with. ``getattr``: tests drive this handler with minimal shells.

name: _cp
doc: ``_cprint`` each line (lazy import: cli.py imports this module).

name: _pr
doc: print() each line.

name: _save
doc: cli.save_config_value, resolved lazily (cli.py imports this module).

name: _dim
doc: Wrap ``text`` in the dim ANSI escape.

name: _dim_line
doc: Two-space indented dim line (the standard slash-command hint shape).

name: _accent
doc: Wrap ``text`` in the skin accent ANSI escape.

name: _accent_line
doc: Two-space indented accent line (the standard slash-command headline shape).

name: _t
doc: Catalog text for this module: ``cli.commands.<key>`` in the active language.

name: _tn
doc: Plural-aware ``_t``: ``<key>_one`` when ``count == 1``, else ``<key>_other``.

name: _gt
doc: A ``gateway.<key>`` catalog entry the CLI shares verbatim with the messaging gateway.

name: _lines
doc: Each line of a (possibly multi-line) catalog value prefixed with ``pad`` (blank lines kept).

name: _rollback_kept
doc: The kept / not-removed path lines of a restore result (in-process CLI and gateway client alike).

name: _probe
doc:
``<module>.<name>(*args)`` or ``default`` when the import or the call fails (optional
subsystems: browser backends, async delegations, wake word, ...).

name: _stop_background_work
doc:
``/stop``'s cleanup: kill the background processes, then interrupt the background (async)
delegations. Mid-turn it runs on a worker thread, so it prints through ``_cprint``: a plain
print() from off the input loop is buried by the prompt_toolkit redraw.

name: print_session_diff
doc:
Render a ``CheckpointManager.session_diff`` result (``/diff session``): this process's agent's,
or the gateway session's ``rollback.session_diff`` (``diff_lines``: its uncut body's line count).

name: _print_local_delegations
doc: This process's background (async) delegations — delegate_task(background=true).

name: _say_block
doc: print() the lines framed by a blank line above and below (the /browser output style).

name: _command_arg
doc: Everything after the slash-command word, stripped (optionally lowercased).

name: _shlex_args
doc: Tokens after the command word; falls back to whitespace split on unbalanced quotes.

name: _handle_stop_command
doc:
Handle /stop — kill all running background processes and background (async) delegations.
Typed while a turn runs it stops that turn first, as Ctrl+C does (the registry's
``busy_policy="interrupt_then_dispatch"``; the input loop dispatches it inline, on the UI
thread). The interrupt is immediate; the background cleanup then runs on a worker thread,
since ``kill_all`` waits out each process's stop grace period and would freeze input.

See #14602.

name: _handle_agents_command
doc:
Handle /agents — show background processes and agent status. On the gateway both run there:
the session's ``process.list`` and its usage's running-subagent count (no per-delegation rows).

name: _handle_journey_command
doc:
Handle /journey — the learning timeline (see `hermes journey`). Read-only views render
Rich color that patch_stdout would swallow, so capture with forced ANSI and re-emit via
``_cprint``; ``delete``/``edit`` are interactive and keep real stdio.

name: _handle_paste_command
doc:
Handle /paste — explicitly check clipboard for an image.

This is the reliable fallback for terminals where BracketedPaste
doesn't fire for image-only clipboard content (e.g., VSCode terminal,
Windows Terminal with WSL2).

name: _handle_copy_command
doc: Handle /copy [number] — copy assistant output to clipboard.

name: _handle_image_command
doc: Handle /image <path> — attach a local image file for the next prompt.

name: _handle_tools_command
doc:
Handle /tools [list|disable|enable]. Bare shows the tool list; ``list`` shows per-toolset
status; disable/enable save to config and reset the session so the new tool set takes
effect cleanly (no prompt-cache breakage mid-conversation).

name: _run_tools_config
doc:
Run ``tools_disable_enable_command``. Inside the interactive TUI its ANSI print() output
is captured (isatty=True so colors still render) and re-emitted through _cprint so
patch_stdout's StdoutProxy doesn't garble the escapes; standalone/tests call straight through.

name: _handle_autoprune_command
doc: /autoprune [on|off|later|status] — the low-disk auto-prune decision.

name: _handle_profile_command
doc: Display active profile name and home directory.

name: enter_new_worktree
doc:
Move *cli*'s session into the fresh tree -> True when the session's tools now run there.

A gateway refusal (e.g. ``session_busy``) moved nothing: the fresh tree is removed now instead of
sitting unlisted until quit, and an earlier active tree stays active. A chdir failure after the
gateway accepted the move leaves only this process behind, so it is reported as that.

name: _cli
doc: Late import of the ``cli`` facade: mutable CLI module state (and its test seams) lives there.

name: _load_prefill_messages
doc:
Load prefill messages (JSON array) from *file_path*; missing/empty -> [].

Relative paths resolve against *base_dir*, defaulting to the CLI's hermes home.

name: _resolve_prefill_messages_file
doc: Prefill file path: env, then top-level ``prefill_messages_file``, then legacy ``agent.*``.

name: _parse_reasoning_config
doc: Parse a reasoning effort level (string or YAML bool; ``false``/``off`` = disabled).

name: _parse_service_tier_config
doc: Parse a persisted fast-mode preference: None, "priority", "ultrafast", "auto", or "cold".

name: _mirror_config_to_env
doc: Project config.yaml values into the env vars the tool modules read (terminal/browser/auxiliary/security/sessions). Env always wins when already set.

name: _cli_config_defaults
doc: Built-in defaults for every config key the CLI reads (the file overlays these).

name: _merge_file_config
arguments: defaults: dict[str, Any], file_config: dict[str, Any]
doc: Overlay a parsed config file onto *defaults* in place (model normalization, deep merge, legacy keys).

name: load_cli_config
doc:
~/.hermes/config.yaml (else ./cli-config.yaml) over built-in defaults; env vars win.

``HERMES_IGNORE_USER_CONFIG=1`` skips the user config entirely (``.env`` still loads).

name: _init_logging_and_display_from_config
doc: Best-effort startup side effects: logging, config warnings, skin, display knobs.

name: cron_overview_lines
doc:
Bare ``/cron``: the command card, then the current jobs. Plain text (the shared gateway serves
the same lines to every local session, gateway/session_cron_commands.py).

name: cron_list_lines
doc: ``/cron list [--all]``.

name: _normalize_skills
doc: Strip, drop empties, and dedupe (order-preserving).

name: _parse_cron_flags
doc: Parse /cron flags into an opts dict (None for a bad --repeat).

name: _job_action_lines
doc: pause / resume / run / remove (aliases rm, delete) on one job id.

name: cron_command_lines
doc: ``/cron [subcommand ...]`` (the text after ``/cron``); raises ValueError on an unclosed quote.

name: toolsets_lines
doc: ``/toolsets``: every toolset, ``(*)`` on the ones *enabled* names.

name: platforms_lines
doc: ``/platforms``: the messaging platforms the profile's gateway config enables.

name: _tool_progress_label
doc: Localized ``Tool progress: MODE — detail`` line for /verbose ("" for an unknown mode).

name: _reload_mcp_choices
doc: (id, label, hint) rows for the /reload-mcp confirm modal, in the active language.

name: _ascii_box
doc: Print the kawaii ``+---+ | title | +---+`` header used by /tools and /toolsets.

name: _toolset_map
doc: tool name → toolset id, including tools of unavailable toolsets (banner snapshot).

name: banner_plan
doc:
The welcome banner's plan. The compact banner (``banner_kw`` None) is for a narrow terminal,
``display.compact``, or a gateway session with no snapshot yet.

name: _show_gateway_banner
doc:
Main's banner from the gateway session's snapshot (the TUI banner's data): the CLI
enumerates nothing. The canonical id shows as main's 8-character label (display only).

name: _print_gateway_tool_warnings
doc:
Main's ``_show_tool_availability_warnings`` lines, computed by the gateway that resolved
this session's tools.

name: show_banner
doc: Display the welcome banner in Claude Code style.

name: show_help
doc:
Display help. Bare /help shows categorized core commands with the skill list collapsed
to one line; /help skills lists all skill commands; /help <query> filters by substring.

name: show_tools
doc: Display available tools with kawaii ASCII art.

name: show_toolsets
doc: Display available toolsets with kawaii ASCII art.

name: _handle_whoami_command
doc: Display slash-command access for the local CLI surface.

name: _busy_inline_command
arguments: self, text: str, has_images: bool, names: tuple
doc:
True when ``text`` is a slash command in ``names`` typed while the agent is running.

Such commands MUST bypass the normal ``_pending_input`` → ``process_loop`` path: the loop
is blocked inside ``self.chat()`` for the whole run, so by the time the queued command is
pulled, ``_agent_running`` has flipped back to False and it would be delivered as a
next-turn message. Dispatching inline on the UI thread acts mid-run (``agent.steer()`` is
thread-safe; ``/bg`` / ``/btw`` start their side session without touching the foreground turn).

name: _should_handle_steer_command_inline
doc:
Return True when /steer or /queue should be dispatched immediately while the agent is
running. Queued raw, ``/queue <prompt>`` only re-enqueued itself after the turn and
``/queue list|rm|edit`` could not inspect the queue until it had already drained.

name: _should_handle_background_command_inline
doc:
Return True when /bg or /btw should be dispatched while the agent runs (their
``CommandDef`` entries declare ``busy_policy="dispatch"``; the classic CLI honours it here).

name: _should_handle_stop_command_inline
doc:
Return True when /stop should be dispatched while the agent runs: its ``CommandDef`` declares
``busy_policy="interrupt_then_dispatch"``, and queued it would only run after the turn it stops.

name: handle_bang_shell
doc:
Run a ``!<command>`` submission. Returns True when it was handled.

Dispatched from the input loop BEFORE slash routing and before anything is queued for the
agent, so a bang command never becomes a turn: nothing touches ``conversation_history``,
zero tokens, role alternation / prompt caching untouched by construction
(tests/hermes_cli/test_bang_shell_mode.py). Returns False when the text is not a bang command or
bang mode is disabled for this context (gateway/cron), so the caller routes normally.

name: _show_gateway_status
doc: Show status of the gateway and connected messaging platforms.

name: _print_random_tip
doc: Best-effort discovery tip (startup + /clear); never raises.

name: _toggle_verbose
doc:
Cycle tool progress mode: off → new → all → verbose → off.

Tool-progress display is INDEPENDENT of global DEBUG logging: this never changes
``self.verbose`` or the agent's ``verbose_logging`` / ``quiet_mode`` (those belong to
``-v`` and ``/verbose-logging``).

name: _handle_usage_command
doc:
Dispatch `/usage [reset [--force]]`: bare `/usage` is the classic display; `reset`
redeems one banked Codex rate-limit reset credit (refuses unless exhausted or --force).

name: _agent_or_self
doc: Provider-ish attribute from the live agent, falling back to the CLI's own value.

name: _usage_reset
doc: `/usage reset [--force]` — redeem one banked Codex reset credit.

name: _show_context_breakdown
doc:
`/context [all]` — 5×20 glyph grid (cell ≈ 1% of the window) plus an estimated
per-category table; `all` appends per-skill / per-toolset costs. Read-only: same chars/4
engine as the desktop popover (agent.context_breakdown) — no provider calls, no cache impact.

name: _show_gateway_context_breakdown
doc:
Main's ``/context`` grid and table over the gateway agent's own breakdown
(``session.context_breakdown``): the session's prompt, tools and transcript live there.

name: _show_usage
doc:
Rate limits + session token usage (when a live agent exists) + Nous credits.

The Nous credits block is agent-independent (portal fetch), so it runs even with no live
agent — the TUI's /usage slash-worker resumes the session WITHOUT building an agent.

name: _print_account_limits
doc:
Provider account limits block for `/usage`; True if anything printed.

Uses the live agent's route when present, else the CLI's own configured provider (the
TUI/Desktop slash-worker runs without an agent). Fetched off-thread with a hard timeout so
slow provider APIs don't hang the prompt; failures are non-fatal. Lazy import: pulls the
OpenAI SDK chain.

name: _show_insights
doc: Show usage insights and analytics from session history (`--days N` / `N`, `--source`).

name: _check_config_mcp_changes
doc:
Detect mcp_servers changes in config.yaml (polled from process_loop every
CONFIG_WATCH_INTERVAL seconds) and react.

Default (``mcp.auto_reload_on_config_change: true``) auto-triggers ``_reload_mcp()``.
When opted out it only notifies and points at ``/reload-mcp`` — every reload rebuilds the
tool surface and INVALIDATES the provider prompt cache (next message re-sends the full
prefix), so silent reloads are wrong when external tooling rewrites config.yaml often.

Instead it notifies the user that the config changed and that they can apply it with ``/reload-mcp``
— while warning that ``/reload-mcp`` rebuilds the tool surface and **invalidates the provider prompt
cache** (the next message re-sends the full input prefix, expensive on long-context / high-reasoning
models). See #1474.

name: _confirm_and_reload_mcp
doc:
Interactive /reload-mcp — confirm (Approve Once / Always Approve / Cancel, gated by
``approvals.mcp_reload_confirm``, default on), then reload. The config watcher's
auto-reload calls ``_reload_mcp`` directly. Reloading invalidates the provider prompt cache
(tool schemas are baked into the system prompt), hence the warning.

name: _reload_gateway_mcp
doc:
``/reload-mcp`` on the shared gateway: the gateway owns the MCP servers and the session's
agent, so it reconciles them with config and refreshes its agents (``reload.mcp``); main's
"Agent updated" line then counts the tools the gateway session now loads.

name: _reload_mcp
doc:
Reload MCP servers: disconnect all, re-read config.yaml, reconnect, then refresh the
agent's tool list so the model sees the updated tools on the next turn.

name: _reload_skills
doc:
Reload skills: rescan ~/.hermes/skills/ and queue a note for the next user turn.

Skills are invoked at runtime (``/skill-name``, ``skills_list``, ``skill_view``), not from
the system prompt, so this does NOT clear the prompt cache. If anything was added/removed
a one-shot note is prepended to the NEXT user message (``_pending_skills_reload_note``,
same pattern as ``_pending_model_switch_note``) — nothing is written to
conversation_history, so message alternation stays intact.

name: _row
arguments: cmd: str, desc: str, width: int=15

name: _section
doc: Print available/matching rows under a `── title ──` header (omitted if empty).

name: _adopt_gateway_toolsets
doc:
The profile default the gateway resolved for the opened session, when this process has no list to
show (display only), and main's "Unknown toolsets" warning as the gateway judged it against its own
plugins.

name: _gateway_launch
doc: This run's explicit launch flags as gateway ``session.create`` policy (main handed them to AIAgent).

name: _explicit_launch_skills
doc:
The `-s/--skills` names, which the gateway renders into the session once at creation (the CLI's
own prompt never reaches it). ``skills.auto_load`` names are left out: the gateway's agent loads those.

name: _record_shell_hook_consent
doc:
Main's first-use shell-hook prompt, on this terminal. The gateway that registers the hooks
has no TTY; it reads the allowlist this writes when the session opens (create or resume).
``--accept-hooks`` / ``HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS`` / ``hooks_auto_accept`` approve without asking.
A remote gateway has its own home and allowlist, and a bypass launch reads no profile hooks,
so nothing is asked for either.

name: lease_handed_over
doc:
Run a gateway attach without this CLI's own active-session lease, then re-claim it.

A row the gateway has not imported yet (a legacy / in-process session) is imported under the
active-session registry lock, which refuses (``runtime_coordination_required``) while ANY live
lease holds the id, including this process's own. The block may move ``cli.session_id`` to the
id the gateway returned: the lease is re-claimed for that id (main's exclusivity is kept), or
for the unchanged id when the block raises.

name: _init_display_options
doc: Display-related config: compact/tool-progress/focus view, bells, streaming, previews, stream buffers.

name: _init_model_routing
arguments: self, model, toolsets, provider, reasoning, api_key, base_url, max_turns, run_budget, checkpoints, pass_session_id, ignore_rules
doc: Resolve model/provider/base_url, turn limits, toolsets, checkpoints, prompt/personality, reasoning + routing config.

name: _init_model_and_provider
doc: Priority: CLI args > env vars > config file.

name: _init_turn_limits
doc: max_turns: CLI arg > config > env var > default; run budget: CLI flag > config.

name: _init_prompt_and_reasoning
doc: Ephemeral system prompt/prefill, reasoning + service tier, OpenRouter routing knobs, fallback chain.

name: _init_runtime_state
doc: Session store + all per-run mutable state (queues, overlays, pet/voice/status-bar fields).

name: _init_session_store
doc: Open the session store early (so /title works before the first message).

name: _ensure_gateway_session
doc:
Create (or resume) this CLI's gateway session and adopt the id it returns, before the banner
and the first turn. Idempotent; a store without the gateway facade (tests) is left alone.

name: _new_session_id
doc:
The id main mints for /new (``new_session_id``) and /branch (``mint_session_id``). On a gateway
store it is a session the gateway created: /new is a fresh ``session.create`` on the profile's
default model (an explicit -m was for the previous session only) with the run's other launch
flags, /branch the child of
``session.mutate branch``. Before this CLI opened its gateway session (or off the gateway) it is
main's local mint, which ``_ensure_gateway_session`` replaces on first use, as at startup.

name: _init_ui_state
doc: Per-run mutable UI state; must exist before any chat() call since -q never goes through run().

name: _fresh_start
doc: Banner line printed after /clear — resolved at call time so the active language applies.

name: _parse_queue_index
doc:
1-based queue index from one whitespace-free token, or None when it isn't one.

``str.isdigit()`` alone is not enough: it accepts characters ``int()`` rejects
(``²``, ``②``), and ``int()`` also refuses digit strings past Python's
conversion limit. A ValueError here would escape the slash handler and take
down the prompt_toolkit app, so every queue index goes through this.

name: _print_decision_message
doc: Print a manager decision's ``message`` (if any) via _cprint; True when one was printed.

name: _goal_blocks_loop_tick
doc:
``loops.goal_blocks_loop_tick`` for this loop's session: asked of the gateway when the manager
is the gateway's (it reads the goal row and its barrier where they live).

name: _pending_input_items
doc: Snapshot of queued next-turn prompts (raw items; may include ``_VoiceInputMessage``).

name: _mutate_pending_input
doc:
Apply ``mutate(items) -> items`` to the queued prompts under the queue's own mutex,
so a voice/interrupt ``put`` from another thread can't slip between snapshot and
write-back. Returns ``(before, after)``.

name: _gateway_queue_store
doc: The gateway session store when this CLI is a viewer of the gateway's session, else None.

name: _queue_items
doc:
``[(admission_id | None, item)]``: the owner's queued admissions (run first, in its FIFO
order), then the turns still waiting in ``_pending_input``.

name: _queue_gateway_call
doc: One owner verb on queued item ``index``; its refusal is printed (in its own words), never raised.

name: _cmd_queue
doc:
``/queue <prompt>`` enqueues; a leading management verb whose arguments fit
(``list``/``clear`` alone, ``edit N …``/``rm N``/``move A B``) manages the queue
instead. Anything else — ``clear the logs``, ``edit the config`` — is still a prompt;
``/queue add <prompt>`` forces enqueueing.

name: _session_bound_manager
arguments: self, attr: str, label: str, load
doc:
Return the manager cached on ``self.<attr>``, rebuilt when ``session_id`` changed
(after /new or a compression-driven session split).

``load()`` does the imports and returns a ``sid -> manager`` factory; an import
failure is logged and yields None, as does an empty session_id.

name: _automation_connection
doc:
``(gateway, connection)``: on a gateway session store the managers are the gateway's
(``hermes_cli.gateway_automation``), and none exists until the gateway session is open, so this
process never opens state.db read-write nor calls the goal judge. Off the gateway (tests, the
TUI slash worker's shadow CLI) main's in-process managers apply.

name: _mark_automation_stale
doc:
Agent thread: the gateway published this session's goal/loop state mid-turn (a tool moved it).
The dock re-reads the mirrored managers on its next spinner-thread poll (``cli_session_dock``).

name: _get_goal_manager
doc: GoalManager bound to the current session_id (see ``_session_bound_manager``).

name: _get_heartbeat_manager
doc: HeartbeatManager bound to the current session_id (see ``_session_bound_manager``).

name: _get_loop_manager
doc: LoopManager bound to the current session_id (see ``_session_bound_manager``).

name: _start_heartbeat_watchdog
doc:
Start the idle-poll daemon that injects a due heartbeat prompt into
``_pending_input`` as a normal user turn when the session is idle. Missed ticks
coalesce (the anchor resets on fire, so a busy hour yields ONE heartbeat turn).
Idempotent; safe to call on every /heartbeat set.

name: _maybe_resume_parked_goal
doc:
Idle hook run from process_loop: when a parked /goal's barrier has lifted (the process
exited, the timer elapsed, or the wait aged past its cap), queue the continuation so the
loop resumes WITHOUT waiting for an unrelated turn to re-evaluate it. The barrier used to be
checked only lazily, on the next turn; a session with nothing else arriving stayed parked
indefinitely (one run: 3 h 22 min on a grandchild's poller).

name: _maybe_fire_loop_tick
doc:
Idle hook run from process_loop: fire a due /loop wakeup.

Only while the agent is idle and nothing is queued — a real user message always
wins the idle boundary, and so does an active (non-parked) /goal, whose
judge-driven continuations own it; the loop defers to the next poll.

name: _last_assistant_response_text
doc: Text of the most recent assistant message ("" when none); multimodal parts are flattened.

name: _maybe_complete_loop_tick_after_turn
doc:
Post-turn hook: evaluate a finished /loop wakeup turn.

No-op unless the turn was a loop wakeup (``awaiting_response`` set by
``fire_tick``). Detects the LOOP_COMPLETE marker, judges --until, applies caps,
and schedules the next tick. Mirrors _maybe_continue_goal_after_turn's shape.

name: _maybe_continue_goal_after_turn
doc:
Post-turn hook: judge the goal and maybe re-queue a continuation. A real user
message already queued preempts judging (re-judged after their turn). Ctrl+C
AUTO-PAUSES instead of judging — the judge on partial output nearly always says
"continue" and would re-queue exactly what was cancelled; pausing is recoverable
via ``/goal resume``. Empty-response skip mirrors ``gateway/run.py``.

name: _approval_gate_on
doc: Read ``approvals.<key>`` (default on); any load failure keeps the prompt enabled.

name: _gated_confirm
arguments: self, command, key, *, title, detail, choices, unchanged, always_msg, once_verb=None, persist_failed_msg=None
doc:
Shared once/always/cancel confirm behind ``approvals.<key>`` (destructive slash, /reload-mcp).

Returns ``"once"`` without prompting when the gate is off; ``None`` on cancel / no input /
unrecognized answer (already reported to the user). Picking "always" persists the opt-out.
``persist_failed_msg`` is the full sentence printed when the opt-out could not be saved;
``once_verb`` is the legacy fragment spliced into the default sentence.

name: _open_external_editor
doc: Open the active input buffer in an external editor.

name: _submit_editor_buffer
doc:
Submit the draft an external editor left in ``buffer`` (Ctrl+G done-callback), mirroring
the `enter` keybinding: empty save ignored, bang/slash dispatched, else queued. Runs on the
prompt_toolkit loop, so it must stay cheap/non-blocking.

name: _inline_pastes
doc:
Replace collapsed ``[Pasted text #N -> file]`` placeholders in ``buffer`` with real text.

History recall and the external editor need the content (the file may be gone or on another
machine); inlining before ``reset(append_to_history=True)`` also lets prompt_toolkit persist
it. Sets ``_skip_paste_collapse`` so the ensuing text-change doesn't re-collapse it.

name: _reset_input_buffer
doc: Clear an input buffer after a programmatic submit (best-effort).

name: _prefill_input_buffer
doc: Place ``text`` in the active prompt_toolkit buffer, editable.

name: _prompt_text_input
doc:
Prompt for free-text input safely inside or outside prompt_toolkit.

``run_in_terminal`` only works on the main-thread loop; on the ``process_loop`` daemon
thread a bare ``input()`` would block forever on loop-owned stdin, so with an app running
off-main we cancel cleanly (None) — mirroring ``_stdin_fallback`` in the modal prompt.

Mirrors the thread-aware guard in ``_run_curses_picker``: ``run_in_terminal`` returns a coroutine
that must be awaited by the prompt_toolkit event loop, which only exists on the main thread. Slash
commands are dispatched from the ``process_loop`` daemon thread (see issue #23185), so calling
``run_in_terminal`` from there orphans the coroutine — ``_ask`` never runs, and user keystrokes leak
into the composer instead. Fall back to a direct ``input()`` when we're off the main thread.

name: _poll_modal_queue
doc:
Block until a value lands on ``response_queue`` or ``self.<deadline_attr>`` passes
(``None`` deadline = unlimited). Returns the value or ``_TIMED_OUT``.

Repaints every ``refresh`` seconds (``0`` = on every idle tick) so countdown hints stay
live; ``paint`` defaults to ``_paint_now`` — modal prompts must bypass the ``_invalidate``
throttle/resize guard or the panel can be dropped and time out unseen.

name: _prompt_text_input_modal
arguments: self, *, title: str, detail: str, choices: list[tuple[str, str, str]], timeout: float=120
doc:
Slash-command confirmation through the prompt_toolkit composer (raw input() fought
prompt_toolkit's stdin ownership: prompt above the TUI, Enter read as EOF). All platforms
drive the modal via ``self._app.loop`` + ``call_soon_threadsafe``; raw ``input()`` is kept
only for the safe cases (no app, no loop, scheduling failure) — on Windows a non-main-thread
input() deadlocks against prompt_toolkit, so that case cancels instead.

**Platform note (Windows — issue #33961):** Earlier code bypassed the modal on ``sys.platform ==
"win32"`` and fell back to a raw ``input()`` prompt. When the confirm was triggered from the
``process_loop`` daemon thread (the normal case) that ``input()`` ran off the main thread and
deadlocked against prompt_toolkit's stdin ownership — the user saw a frozen cursor and Ctrl-C was
swallowed (bare ``/reset`` froze; ``/reset now`` worked only because it skips the prompt entirely).

name: _normalize_slash_confirm_choice
arguments: self, raw: str | None, choices: list[tuple[str, str, str]]

name: _build_command_palette_entries
doc:
Flat (command, category, desc) rows for the Ctrl+P palette: the COMMAND_REGISTRY behind
/help filtered to this surface, plus installed skill commands. Selecting inserts the exact
command string — never a fuzzy resolution.

name: _open_command_palette
doc: Open the Ctrl+P fuzzy command palette modal (never stacked over another modal).

name: _command_palette_visible_entries
doc:
Rows matching the active filter, ranked command-name-first (a bare subsequence over
"cmd category desc" is uselessly permissive — "steer" would match 130+ rows via text):
0 exact command, 1 command startswith, 2 substring in command, 3 subsequence in command,
4 substring in description. Non-matches are dropped; ties keep registry order.

name: _handle_command_palette_selection
doc: Prefill the selected command into the composer — never auto-run (many take args).

name: _split_destructive_skip
doc:
Split inline-skip tokens out of a destructive slash command → ``(remainder, skip)``.

``remainder`` is the text minus the leading "/cmd" word and any skip tokens; ``skip`` is
True iff one was found: "/reset now" -> ("", True); "/reset --yes My title" ->
("My title", True); "/new My title" -> ("My title", False).

name: _confirm_destructive_slash
arguments: self, command: str, detail: str, cmd_original: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Confirm a destructive slash command (``/clear``, ``/new``/``/reset``, ``/undo``): returns
``"once"``, ``"always"`` (persists the opt-out) or ``None`` (cancelled). Gate off → "once"
silently; ``now`` / ``--yes`` / ``-y`` in ``cmd_original`` bypasses the modal (callers strip
the tokens via :meth:`_split_destructive_skip`).

Inline-skip: if ``cmd_original`` contains ``now``, ``--yes``, or ``-y`` as an argument (e.g.
``/reset now``, ``/new --yes My title``), the modal is bypassed and ``"once"`` is returned
immediately. This is an escape hatch for non-interactive use and for the degraded path where the
modal can't be marshaled onto the app loop (native Windows itself now drives the modal normally —
see #33961). Callers are responsible for stripping the skip tokens from any remaining argument
parsing (see :meth:`_split_destructive_skip`).

name: _ring_bell
arguments: self, prompt: bool=False, context: str='', detail: str=''
doc:
Terminal bell (\a) gated by ``display.bell_on_prompt`` (``prompt=True``, blocking modals)
or ``display.bell_on_complete`` (end of turn); works over SSH. The same flag also emits the
OSC 9 / Warp OSC 777 desktop notification; ``context`` is the short notification body.

name: _connection_opening_phase
doc:
The phase a target opens in. A pending install or enable waits for the user's Connect
even with no fields to fill; a pending authorize is the backend still minting the link.

name: _connection_send
doc: One card answer to the gateway, off the UI thread; its outcome arrives as connection.update.

name: _connection_set_field
doc: Save the active input row in the private draft and advance to the next row/action.

name: _connection_submit
doc: Enter action for prompt_toolkit bindings: URL open, selected action, or field advance.

name: _connection_render_lines
doc: Panel copy without exposing secret drafts; the prompt_toolkit renderer consumes these rows.

name: _clarify_batch_set_active
_clarify_batch_lock
doc:
Lock ``answer`` for the active batch question (overwriting an earlier one) and advance to
the next unanswered; ``meta`` ({"kind": "choice"|"other"|"multi", ...}) lets a re-visit
restore the cursor / prefill an "Other" edit. All answered → resolve the queue, tear down.

name: _clarify_batch_enter
doc:
Enter in batch choice mode: lock the active selection. Multi-select locks a JSON array of
checked labels (parsed by the tool core); "Other" switches to freetext, prefilled with an
earlier typed answer so Enter on an answered Other edits instead of retyping.

name: _clarify_callback
doc:
Clarify-tool platform callback (agent thread, #18450): the batch panel (A-compact) shows
all questions, one active, and blocks until the key bindings lock every answer. Returns
``{"answers": {qid: raw | None}, "outcome"}`` (None = skipped): ``submitted`` when every
question is locked, ``timed_out`` when the deadline expires, ``cancelled`` on an interrupt.

name: _withdraw_gateway_modal
doc:
The gateway withdrew the server request this CLI's modal is answering (``request.cancel``:
another viewer completed it, or its wait ended): close that modal as if cancelled locally, so
the blocked agent thread returns. Called from the gateway connection's thread.

name: _sudo_password_callback
doc:
Prompt for a sudo password through the prompt_toolkit UI (agent thread); clarify-style
state + queue answered by the Enter binding.

name: _approval_callback
arguments: self, command: str, description: str, *, allow_permanent: bool=True, allow_session: bool=True, smart_denied: bool=False
doc:
Dangerous-command approval through the prompt_toolkit UI (agent thread).

Choices: once / session / always / deny (see ``_approval_choices``), plus 'view' for long
commands. ``_approval_lock`` serializes concurrent requests (parallel delegation subtasks)
so the shared ``_approval_state`` / ``_approval_deadline`` aren't clobbered.

name: _approval_choices
arguments: self, command: str, *, allow_permanent: bool=True, allow_session: bool=True, smart_denied: bool=False
doc:
Smart-DENY overrides and re-ask-every-time gates (allow_session=False) show only
once/deny; ``allow_permanent=False`` for another reason hides only 'always'.

name: _handle_approval_selection
doc: Process the currently selected dangerous-command approval choice.

name: _vault_unlock_callback
doc:
Masked master-password prompt for an external password manager (agent thread).
Reuses the sudo panel state so rendering, Enter/ESC handling and interrupt cleanup are shared.

name: _vault_save_login_callback
doc:
Two-step "save this login" prompt (identifier shown, password masked) on the sudo panel; the
answer goes to the vault store, never to the model. None = declined.

name: _vault_code_callback
doc:
One-time-code prompt (shown as typed; a 6-digit code is not a secret worth masking and users
need to see typos) on the sudo panel. "" = declined/timed out.

name: _secret_capture_callback
arguments: self, var_name: str, prompt: str, metadata=None

name: _capture_modal_input_snapshot
doc: Temporarily clear the input buffer and save the user's in-progress draft.

name: _restore_modal_input_snapshot
doc: Restore any draft text that was present before a modal prompt opened.

name: _clear_active_overlays_for_interrupt
doc:
Drain and clear every input-blocking overlay left by an interrupted agent: the worker
thread is gone but the state dict still gates input (frozen terminal until its timeout).
Push a safe value onto each queue (approval -> "deny", others -> cancel), nil the state,
restore the draft; each step is wrapped so a dead queue can't block the others.

name: _resolve_cli_reasoning
doc:
Re-resolve the CLI-level ``reasoning_config`` for ``cli.model`` through the shared chokepoint
(per-model ``reasoning_overrides`` > global ``agent.reasoning_effort``). Startup resolves it once
for the launch model; every path that moves ``cli.model`` must call this BEFORE the agent branch,
because a lazily built agent inherits this field — an always-thinking model then goes out with
the launch model's effort and 400s (#112921, #96012). ``agent.switch_model`` re-resolves its own
copy for the live-agent path.

name: stored_session_route
doc:
The route a resumed session should run on, or ``None`` when the stored one is absent or
already current. Returns ``(model, provider, base_url, api_mode, provider_changed)``; the
canonical row reader is ``SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime`` (``model_config.gateway_runtime``,
else the TUI's top-level keys). Bare ``custom`` is healed because the CLI resolve path
hard-fails on it (the TUI gateway keeps it when a base_url exists).

name: _heal_bare_custom_provider
doc:
Bare ``custom`` is a billing class, not a routable identity: persisting/restoring it makes a
later resume hard-fail once the config default leaves the custom endpoint. Recover the durable
``custom:<name>`` menu key from the endpoint, else drop the provider (None).

name: _merge_preflight_warning
doc: Fold the context-compression preflight warning into ``result`` (fail-soft).

name: _print_switch_summary
arguments: cli, result, old_model, *, one_turn: bool, strict_context: bool
doc:
Record the next-turn switch note and print the "Model switched" block.

The note is prepended to the next user message (a mid-history system message would break
providers and prompt caching). ``strict_context``: the typed /model path lets
context-resolution errors propagate; the picker path swallows them.

name: _switch_model_from
arguments: cli, raw_input, *, is_global, explicit_provider, user_providers, custom_providers
doc: ``switch_model`` seeded with this CLI's live route.

name: _run_confirm_and_apply
doc:
Run a confirm+apply sequence off the UI thread when the TUI is live.

The expensive-model modal blocks its thread on a response queue (_prompt_text_input_modal);
on the prompt_toolkit main thread that freezes rendering, so the modal never appears and the
switch silently cancels after the 120s timeout.

name: _one_turn_selection_context
doc:
Context the owner's large-context guard would see, for a ``/model --once`` that does not mutate.

A live compressor measurement wins. Otherwise refresh ``session.stats``, then the session row's
persisted usage anchor (a resume, before this process has run a turn).

name: _ask_switch_anyway
doc: The model-guard prompt (switch anyway once, or cancel): True only on an explicit yes.

name: _picker_reasoning_rows
doc:
``(value, label)`` rows for the picker's effort step: the canonical ladder, the off state,
then a keep-current row (empty value = leave the effort alone).

name: _picker_offers_reasoning
doc:
False only when the inventory's capability map says the picked model has no reasoning
control; unknown capabilities keep the step (a no-op dial beats hiding a real one).

name: _apply_reasoning_after_switch
arguments: cli, effort: str, *, persist_global: bool, one_turn: bool=False
doc:
Apply a ``--reasoning <level>`` that rode along with a model pick. Runs AFTER the swap: the
agent's ``switch_model`` re-resolves ``reasoning_config`` from config.yaml, so an earlier write
would be clobbered. Session-scoped unless the pick itself persists (``--global``).

``one_turn`` (``--once``): the level rides the one-turn admission (``model_override.reasoning``)
and the restore snapshot puts the CLI's own level back. It is never a session pin.

name: _commit_model_switch
arguments: cli, result, *, persist_global: bool, one_turn: bool=False, picker: bool=False, reasoning_effort: str=''
doc:
Stage + swap, print the summary, persist (session row unless --once; config on --global).
``picker``: tolerate context-resolution errors and label the config write "(--global)"; the
typed path additionally records the one-turn restore snapshot. ``reasoning_effort`` (from
``--reasoning`` or the picker's effort step) is applied after the swap.

name: _show_model_picker
doc: ``/model`` with no args: open the picker, or print usage when nothing is authed.

name: _normalize_model_for_provider
doc: Normalize provider-specific model IDs and routing.

name: _persist_model_switch_to_session
doc:
Persist a session-scoped /model switch to the session DB row.

Writes the model column plus the route in both shapes readers use — nested
``gateway_runtime`` (CLI --resume) and top-level keys (TUI session.resume) — from one
or-None dict so stale keys are DELETED (``_merge_model_config_json`` only deletes on
explicit None) and the shapes never diverge.

Writes the model column plus the runtime route so ``--resume`` (CLI, reads ``gateway_runtime``) and
``session.resume`` (TUI/desktop, reads top-level ``model_config`` keys via
``_stored_session_runtime_overrides``) both restore the switched provider instead of recombining the
model with the ambient default (#79536). Mirrors the gateway's ``update_session_model()`` call.
getattr: tests drive the switch paths with ``object.__new__`` stubs.

name: _restore_session_model
doc:
Restore model/provider from the session DB row on every resume path.

Skips when no model is recorded or the CLI got an explicit ``-m`` (user intent wins).
A different stored provider gets its credentials re-resolved — the ambient ``api_key``
must not be sent to the session's endpoint; on failure the ambient credentials are kept
so the session still opens (the first turn surfaces the auth error).

name: _open_model_picker
arguments: self, providers: list, current_model: str, current_provider: str, user_provs=None, custom_provs=None
doc: Open prompt_toolkit-native /model picker modal.

name: _confirm_expensive_model_switch
doc: Ask for explicit confirmation before applying costly model switches.

name: _confirm_owner_model_switch
doc:
The gateway owner refused a guarded target (``confirmation_required``: cost, data policy,
large context; Ink/Desktop/ACP show the same ``confirm_message``): ask in the same prompt as
``_confirm_expensive_model_switch``. Only a yes re-sends with the owner's token. The identical
warning the user just confirmed for this switch is not asked twice.

name: _confirm_and_apply_model_switch_result
arguments: self, result, persist_global: bool, custom_providers=None, reasoning_effort: str=''

name: _snapshot_model_runtime
doc: Capture current CLI and agent model runtime for one-turn restore.

name: _restore_model_runtime_snapshot
doc: Restore a model runtime captured before a one-turn override.

name: _filter_model_picker_entries
_compute_model_picker_viewport
arguments: selected: int, scroll_offset: int, n: int, term_rows: int, reserved_below: int=6, panel_chrome: int=6, min_visible: int=3
doc:
Resolve (scroll_offset, visible) for the /model picker viewport. ``reserved_below``
matches the approval/clarify panels (input, status bar, separators); ``panel_chrome`` is
borders + blanks + hint row. The offset slides to keep ``selected`` on screen.

name: _stage_and_swap_model
doc:
Stage ``result`` onto the CLI fields, then swap the live agent in place.

CLI fields are snapshotted first so a failed agent swap rolls the whole CLI back —
otherwise the staged broken credentials leak into the next turn even though the agent
rolled back. Returns False after printing the failure (a failed switch is a no-op).

name: _apply_model_switch_result
arguments: self, result, persist_global: bool, custom_providers=None, reasoning_effort: str=''
doc: Picker-path commit (see _commit_model_switch).

name: _commit_picker_result
arguments: self, result, persist_global: bool, reasoning_effort: str=''
doc: Close the picker and run the confirm+apply sequence for ``result``.

name: _handle_model_switch
doc:
Handle /model command — switch model.

Supports:
  /model                              — show current model + usage hints
  /model <name>                       — switch model (this session only)
  /model <name> --once                — switch for the next turn only
  /model <name> --session             — switch for this session only (explicit)
  /model <name> --global              — switch and persist to config.yaml
  /model <name> --provider <provider> — switch provider + model
  /model <name> --reasoning <level>   — switch and set reasoning effort in one step
  /model --provider <provider>        — switch to provider, auto-detect model

Switches are session-scoped unless ``model.persist_switch_by_default`` or ``--global``.

name: _confirm_and_apply_cli_model_switch
arguments: self, result, persist_global: bool, one_turn: bool, custom_provs=None, reasoning_effort: str=''
doc:
Confirm an expensive model switch and apply it (typed /model path). Runs on a worker
thread when the TUI is active (see _run_confirm_and_apply) so the modal can render.

name: _handle_codex_runtime
doc:
Handle /codex-runtime — toggle the codex app-server runtime opt-in.

Usage:
    /codex-runtime                       — show current state
    /codex-runtime auto                  — Hermes default (chat_completions)
    /codex-runtime codex_app_server      — hand turns to codex subprocess
    /codex-runtime on / off              — synonyms for the above

name: _should_handle_model_command_inline
doc: Return True when /model should be handled immediately on the UI thread.

name: _cmd_moa
doc:
/moa one-shot: run one prompt through the default MoA preset, then restore the prior
model (a session-long MoA switch goes through the picker's virtual MoA provider).

name: _adopt
doc: Adopt ``canonical`` when it differs; ``notice(new)`` builds the warning text.

name: _adopt_with_mode
doc: Provider families that also own the wire protocol: adopt id, then sync api_mode.

name: layout_from_config
doc: True for the glyph layout (default); ``classic`` keeps the boxed transcript.

name: busy_input_mode_from_config
doc: ``display.busy_input_mode``; unset interrupts in both layouts (Tab still queues in this one).

name: _brand_glyph
doc: (glyph, name) from the skin's response label, e.g. ``" ☤ Hermes "`` → ("☤", "Hermes").

name: separator
doc:
An opening bar: accent for user messages and answers, dim for reasoning. Every caller prints
a blank line ahead of it, so it also settles a gap the previous block owes.

name: closing_separator
doc: The bar that closes a block; the blank line after it is owed to whatever prints next.

name: user_echo_markup
arguments: text: str, accent_hex: str, ts_suffix: str=''
doc: Rich markup for a submitted single-line user message: ``❯ text``.

name: answer_label
doc: The rows that open an answer: the accent bar, then the skin's brand glyph + name.

name: _full_title
doc: The reasoning's first ``**bold**`` heading, else its first sentence, whitespace-collapsed.

name: thought_title
doc: Short title for a reasoning block: its first ``**bold**`` heading, else its first sentence.

name: thought_line
doc: ``∴ Thought for 3s · Planning the change`` (dim italic), closing a reasoning block.

name: reasoning_text_line
doc: One streamed reasoning line: dim, no frame (the dim bar above opens the block).

name: thought_rows
arguments: seconds: float | None, text: str, full: bool
doc:
A reasoning block printed after the fact (no live stream): dim bar, its text (first 10
lines unless ``full``, as classic), then the ``∴ Thought for 3s`` summary.

name: completed_tool_line
arguments: cli, function_name: str, args: dict | None, duration: float, result=None, is_error: bool=False
doc: The scrollback line for a finished tool call in the active layout.

name: tool_row
arguments: function_name: str, args: dict | None, duration: float, result=None, is_error: bool=False
doc:
``📖 Read calc.py  0.2s`` / ``✗ $ pytest -q  0.4s [exit 1]`` — one row per completed call, led by
the tool's emoji (the classic ``┊`` row's), or a red ``✗`` when that entry failed. A tool in
``NEUTRAL_FAILURE_TOOLS`` keeps its emoji and shows the reason dim.

name: gutter_print
doc:
Wrap a line printer so a diff hangs under its tool row behind a dim ``│``: the ``review
diff`` header is dropped and ``a/<abs> → b/<abs>`` collapses to one cwd-relative path.

name: diff_printer
doc: ``print_fn`` with the gutter when the glyph layout is active in this process.

name: turn_footer
doc: ``─ 12.4s · read 3 files · edited 1 file +4 -0 · 7:02 AM`` closing each turn.

name: activity_text
doc: What the agent is doing: the classic spinner's text (kaomoji face or tool emoji included).

name: rule_style
doc: Composer rules are quiet chrome: the skin's session border, not the accent.

name: _no_bg
doc: The footer sits on the terminal background, not the classic status bar's fill.

name: top_rule_fragments
doc: ``── ⠹ Running tests · 14s ─────────── calc helpers ─``: live status left, session title right.

name: hint_pairs
doc: Keys that do something right now, for the footer's right half.

name: status_line_fragments
doc:
Footer under the composer: model · context gauge · cwd (branch) left, live key hints right.
An explicit ``display.status_bar.fields`` list keeps the user's chosen segments on the left.

name: _render_safely
doc: Boundary for prompt_toolkit render callbacks: a bad frame degrades to a bare line.

name: _status_line_fragments
doc:
The classic bar's segments (same fields, same width tiers, same ``display.status_bar.fields``
filter), then cwd (branch) and the live key hints when there is room.

name: modern_input_rules
doc: The composer's rules for this layout (the top one carries live status), plus Tab-to-queue.

name: print_truncated
doc:
Footer for a capped listing so a cut list never reads as the whole list.

``more`` is the exact number of hidden rows, or ``None`` when the caller only probed
one row past its cap (``LIMIT n+1``) and knows just that at least one more exists.
``hint`` names how to see the rest (``"use --limit 40 to see more"``).

name: line_input
doc:
Read non-secret text with normal cursor-editing keys on a real TTY.

Setup/model-selection commands run outside the chat's prompt_toolkit application, so a
short-lived prompt is safe here. Redirected stdin/stdout keep the built-in ``input`` used by
scripts, tests and numbered fallbacks.

name: prompt
arguments: question: str, default: str | None=None, password: bool=False
doc: Prompt for input (stripped), or ``default`` on plain Enter; "" on Ctrl-C/EOF.

name: __init__
arguments: self, border: str, box_width: int, title: str='', title_style: str=''

name: process_rows
doc:
Running processes plus those that exited within ``RETAIN_SECONDS``, newest-running first.

The classic CLI is one conversation per OS process, so every registry entry (its own
spawns and any a child handed back) belongs to this dock; gateway-hosted surfaces scope
by session key in ``tui_gateway`` instead.

name: process_activity
doc:
The trailing ``· …`` part of a dock line: elapsed + latest output while running, the exit
verdict + age once finished.

name: _owns_process_notification
doc: Whether this session owns a delegation event (pre-compression keys resolve to their continuation; fail closed).

name: _background_notifications_suppressed
doc:
Whether ``display.background_process_notifications`` is ``off`` for this CLI session.

The key gates the gateway's completion injection (#9290) but the CLI drain never consulted
it, so the documented ``off`` escape hatch silently did nothing here (#123114). Mirrors the
gateway semantics: events are still drained, claimed and acknowledged — only the
turn-starting injection is suppressed.

name: _tui_unwrap_input
doc: Unwrap ``_VoiceInputMessage`` / ``_SeededQueryMessage`` -> ``(text_or_tuple, is_voice_input, is_seeded_query)``.

name: _cli
doc: Late import of the ``cli`` facade: mutable CLI module state (and its test seams) lives there.

name: _strip_reasoning_tags
doc:
Strip reasoning blocks (closed, unterminated, orphan-close) and leaked tool-call XML from display text.

Keep in sync with ``agent.agent_runtime_helpers.strip_think_blocks`` and the stream consumer's think-tag sets.

Also strips tool-call XML blocks some open models leak into visible content (``<tool_call>``,
``<function_calls>``, Gemma-style ``<function name="…">…</function>``). Ported from
openclaw/openclaw#67318.

name: _hex_to_ansi
doc: Convert '#RRGGBB' to a true-color ANSI escape, remapping dark-tuned colors in light mode.

name: _luminance_from_hex
doc: Rec.709 luma in [0, 1] for '#RGB'/'#RRGGBB', or None when malformed.

name: _query_osc11_background
doc:
Terminal background via OSC 11 as "#RRGGBB", or None.

Fenced with a DA1 sentinel (``ESC[c``): terminals answer in order and virtually all
