answer DA1, so its reply proves our OSC 11 was processed — otherwise a late reply
leaks into prompt_toolkit's stdin as typed text. Skipped over SSH (round-trip too
slow; a late BEL reads as Ctrl+G). A 50 ms drain after TCSAFLUSH catches stragglers.

After the main read + TCSAFLUSH, a short drain window (50 ms) catches late-arriving bytes that slipped
past the flush — a race observed on VPS and container terminals under load (#40250).

name: _heal_cooked_mode_drift
doc:
Re-apply raw mode on *fd* when termios drifted back to cooked (POSIX only).

A lost ``run_in_terminal`` cooked_mode() restore makes the kernel line-buffer every
keystroke and the CLI looks dead. Mirrors prompt_toolkit's raw_mode flag surgery in
place. Returns True when healed; False when already raw or not inspectable.

name: _detect_light_mode_uncached
doc: The detection ladder documented above; may raise (caller maps errors to dark).

name: _maybe_remap_for_light_mode
doc: In light mode, remap a dark-tuned color to its higher-contrast equivalent.

name: _install_skin_light_mode_hook
doc: Wrap SkinConfig.get_color so EVERY skin color read goes through the light-mode remap. Idempotent.

name: _tty_wrap
doc: Wrap *s* in an SGR attribute when stdout is a real TTY; plain text otherwise.

name: _accent_hex
doc: Return the active skin accent color for legacy CLI output lines.

name: _rich_text_from_ansi
doc: Rich Text from ANSI output; literal ``[brackets]`` are not treated as markup.

name: _strip_markdown_syntax
doc: Best-effort markdown marker removal for plain-text display.

name: _preserve_windows_dot_segments_for_markdown
doc: Double the ``\`` before hidden dirs in Windows paths: CommonMark reads ``\.`` as an escaped dot.

name: _terminal_width_for_streaming
doc: Display cells inside the streamed response box (small margin for resize races).

name: _render_final_assistant_content
doc: Render final assistant content as markdown, stripped text, or raw text.

name: _post_stream_transform_output
doc: Text still to display after a streamed response transform: the suffix, or the whole response when replaced.

name: _painted_columns
doc: The width the terminal soft-wraps a print at right now, or ``None``.

name: _record_output_history
doc:
Record ``text`` as painted now. ``force`` skips the recording check when the caller
made it at print-request time (the print itself was deferred to the app loop).

name: _ansi_drop_cells
doc: ``line`` without its first ``cells`` visible cells; escape sequences are kept for their styling.

name: _terminal_reflows
doc:
Whether the terminal re-wraps the rows it shows when its width changes: ``True``
(tmux, GNU screen, VTE, kitty, iTerm2, Terminal.app, WezTerm, Alacritty, Windows Terminal —
a shrink pushes the rows that grew into scrollback), ``False`` (xterm, st, urxvt, mosh, the
Linux console keep every row in place, truncated) or ``None`` when nothing says (xterm or
iTerm2 over ssh both look like ``TERM=xterm-256color``).

name: _line_rows
doc: Rows ``line`` fills when the terminal soft-wraps it at ``columns``.

name: _output_tail_fitting
arguments: lines: list[str], max_rows: int, columns: int, painted: bool=True
doc:
Newest ``lines`` filling ``max_rows`` rows, soft-wrapped at ``columns`` — or, with
``painted``, at the width each was painted at, as a terminal that does not reflow still
shows it. The oldest one may only partly fit: its bottom rows are kept, the rows above
them are already in scrollback.

name: _output_history_lines
doc: The recorded output as the lines a replay paints (callable entries render now).

name: _output_history_rows
arguments: limit: int, columns: int, painted: bool
doc:
Rows the whole recorded output fills (counted as ``_output_tail_fitting`` does), or
``None`` when that is ``limit`` rows or more.

name: _pt_print_ansi
doc: ``_pt_print(ANSI(text))``, falling back to ``print`` when stdout is not a real console.

name: _hold_paints
doc:
Hold ``_cprint`` paints until ``_release_paints``, while a resize awaits its recovery.

A paint erases the prompt chrome from prompt_toolkit's cursor, which is stale once the
terminal re-wrapped the chrome to its new width: rows of the old chrome would stay in the
transcript, where the replay cannot account for them (#95375). On a terminal that does not
reflow, a paint would scroll rows it truncated into scrollback before the refill restores them.

name: _release_paints
doc: Paint, in the order they were requested, what ``_hold_paints`` held.

name: _paint_held
doc:
Queue ``paint`` (requested ``seq``-th) when paints are held — or must be, because the
terminal's width changed under ``app`` and its recovery has not run yet.

name: _cprint
doc:
Print ANSI text through prompt_toolkit's renderer (patch_stdout swallows raw ANSI).

From a background thread while an Application runs, a direct print races the input
redraw and gets buried, so those are painted on the app's loop via ``call_soon_threadsafe``.

name: _prepend_note_to_message
doc:
Prepend a one-shot note to a user message (str, or content-part list when an image is attached).

For lists the note is folded into the first text part or inserted as a leading one.
Unknown shapes are returned unchanged.

name: _pt_app_is_running
doc: Whether a prompt_toolkit Application currently owns the live terminal.

name: _cli_visible_print
doc: ``print`` unless a prompt_toolkit Application owns the terminal (patch_stdout swallows bare prints).

name: _build_compact_banner
doc: Build a compact banner that fits the current terminal width.

name: _panel_box_width
arguments: title: str, content_lines: list[str], min_width: int=46, max_width: int=76
doc: Stable TUI panel width wide enough for the title and content (incl. borders).

name: _wrap_panel_text
arguments: text: str, width: int, subsequent_indent: str='', *, keep_ws: bool=False
doc:
Wrap panel text; ``keep_ws`` preserves whitespace (command/detail previews). Each source
line wraps on its own: a newline inside a row would break the panel's right border.

name: _append_panel_line
arguments: lines, border_style: str, content_style: str, text: str, box_width: int

name: __init__
arguments: self, skin_key: str, fallback_hex: str='#FFD700', *, bold: bool=False

name: reset
doc: Clear cache so the next access re-reads the skin.

name: status
doc: No-op ``console.status`` so slash helpers don't duplicate ``_busy_command()``'s indicator.

name: sync_automation
doc:
Re-read the goal/loop managers' mirrored state once after the gateway flagged it changed mid-turn
(``_mark_automation_stale``): one ``state`` round trip per change, none while nothing moves.

name: goal_line
doc:
``GoalManager.status_line()`` for an active or paused goal, else ``''``.

Reads only the manager the CLI already holds for its current session: the dock refreshes on
the spinner thread every second and must never be the thing that opens state.db.

name: countdown
doc:
Time left until the next wakeup, rounded UP: whole minutes until the last one, then seconds.

Minute steps keep an idle prompt's dock to one repaint a minute (the spinner thread repaints only
when the dock text changes); per-second repaints of a 45-minute wait would fight terminal viewport
restoration for nothing.

name: loop_row
doc:
``(badge, line, prompt)`` for an active or paused /loop, else ``('', '', '')``.

``line`` is the expanded dock row (``↻ loop · every 5m · 2 runs · next in 4m · <prompt>``),
``badge`` the collapsed heading's count fragment (``↻ loop next in 4m``). Same rule as :func:`goal_line`:
only the manager the CLI already holds is read, never state.db.

name: queued_prompts
doc: One-line previews of the turns waiting in ``_pending_input``, oldest first.

name: _user_turn_indices
doc:
Indices of *real* user turns: excludes ephemeral scaffolding, display_kind timeline
rows and compaction handoffs — the same predicate as resume turn counting.

name: _timestamp_or
doc: ``datetime.fromtimestamp(value)`` or *default* when the value is missing/unparseable.

name: _squash
doc: Collapse whitespace and cap to *limit* cells with an ellipsis.

name: _dim_notice
doc:
Print a dim notice — raw to stderr on quiet (pre-TUI) paths. Module-level so tests can
call the resume helpers unbound against a minimal stand-in.

name: _reset_model_to_config_default
doc:
/new is a full boundary: re-derive model/provider from config.yaml so a
session-only ``/model --session`` switch never leaks into the next session.
Best-effort — an unreachable default must never block /new. Module-level helper (like
``_apply_new_session_title``): tests drive ``new_session`` unbound on a SimpleNamespace.

name: _apply_new_session_title
doc: Sanitize + persist a /new title; returns the stored title or None (untitled).

name: _print_save_refusal
doc: A gateway's ``/save`` refusal: ``not_found`` (no stored conversation yet) is main's nothing-to-save.

name: _export_on_gateway
doc:
The owner's ``/save`` rendering of its stored row (``session.export``: the snapshot ``hermes
sessions export`` writes, with title, metadata and archived rows), never this process's
in-memory history. Nothing is written on the gateway host, so a remote owner's disk is never
taken for this machine's. None when refused (printed), and also None when an older gateway
without ``session.export`` was handed to ``_save_on_older_gateway`` (which may save on the
gateway host and prints its own outcome).

name: _save_on_older_gateway
doc:
An owner without ``session.export``: its ``session.save`` writes default-named, unredacted
JSON on the gateway host, so only a plain ``/save json`` may use it (as Desktop does).

name: _write_save
doc:
Write a ``/save`` export on this machine: ``filename`` as typed (relative to the cwd), else
``sessions/saved/hermes_conversation_<ts>.<fmt>`` under this CLI's home.

name: _restore_session_cwd
doc:
Relaunch a resumed session in the directory it was started from.

Idempotent; called from every resume path. Both ``os.chdir()`` and ``TERMINAL_CWD``
are retargeted so the process and the terminal/code-exec tools agree (the local
terminal backend snapshots cwd on first use, after this). No-op when no cwd was
recorded, the directory is gone (dim warning, never a crash), or we're already there.

name: _restore_session_yolo
doc: Re-arm the session row's persisted /yolo on every resume path (``tools.approval_yolo``).

name: _render_resume_history_panel_lines
doc: Render the resume panel at the current terminal width for resize replay.

name: _resolve_checkpoint_ref
doc: Resolve a 1-indexed checkpoint number (or pass through a git hash).

name: _show_status
doc: Show compact startup status line.

name: _show_session_status
doc: Show gateway-style status for the current CLI session.

name: _list_recent_sessions
doc: Return recent CLI sessions for in-chat browsing/resume affordances.

name: _show_recent_sessions
doc:
Render recent sessions inline from the active chat TUI.

Returns True when something was shown, False if no session list was available.

name: show_history
doc: Display conversation history.

name: _notify_session_boundary
doc:
Fire a session-boundary plugin hook (on_session_finalize / on_session_reset).
Non-blocking; errors swallowed. Safe from shutdown, /new, /reset.

name: _discard_session_if_empty
doc:
Drop a just-ended session row that never gained content (quit-immediately, /new,
/clear) so it doesn't clutter ``/resume``. ``SessionDB.delete_session_if_empty`` only
removes rows with no messages, no title and no children (gemini-cli#27770 port).

name: _launch_session_boundary_memory_flush
doc:
Stage old-session memory extraction so /new stays responsive.

The context-engine ``on_session_end`` is delivered synchronously here: cheap (no LLM)
and ordering-sensitive — it must land before ``reset_session_state()`` rebinds the
engine. The memory-provider half (LLM-bound, seconds) is NOT run here: the returned
snapshot goes to ``MemoryManager.commit_session_boundary_async`` as one end→switch
task on the serialized worker, so a late ``on_session_end`` can never run after
``on_session_switch`` and misattribute the old transcript to the new session.

Returns the snapshot to queue, or ``None`` when there is nothing to extract.

name: new_session
doc: Start a fresh session with a new session ID and cleared agent state.

name: _consume_pending_resume_selection
doc:
Resolve a bare numeric reply following a bare ``/resume`` prompt.

``/resume`` (no args) arms ``self._pending_resume_sessions``; the next input gets one
chance to be a bare session number. The pending state is one-shot — cleared on the
first input regardless of outcome, so a stray later number is never hijacked.
Returns True if the input was consumed (caller must not treat it as chat).

See #34584.

name: save_conversation
doc:
Handle ``/save [json|md|html] [filename] [redact]``.

A convenience export only — every message is already persisted to the session DB, so
the live session stays resumable regardless. ``redact`` runs the force-mode secret
redaction pass before writing.

name: _publish_truncated_history
doc:
Install a rewound history and mirror it onto the agent (flush index reset so the
next turn re-flushes from the truncated head).

name: retry_last
doc:
Retry the last user message: drop the last exchange and return the text to re-send
(None when there is nothing to retry).

name: undo_last
doc:
Back up N user turns: truncate history, soft-delete on disk, prefill the composer.

Discards everything from the Nth-from-last user message onward (clamped to the oldest
turn). Rows are soft-deleted in SessionDB (``active=0``, kept for audit), memory
providers get ``on_session_switch(rewound=True)``, and the agent is patched like
/branch does. ``prefill=False`` is for programmatic callers (checkpoint rollback)
that must not touch the input buffer. Returns the number of user turns undone (None when
nothing changed).

name: _undo_content_to_text
doc: Flatten message content (str or content-part list) to plain text.

name: _write_terminal_breadcrumb
doc:
Record this terminal's live session for bare ``hermes -c``. Called whenever
``self.session_id`` is (re)assigned so a later bare ``-c`` in THIS terminal resumes
this conversation's live tip. Best-effort; no-op without a terminal identity.

name: _is_session_yolo_active
doc:
Whether YOLO bypass is on for this session: reads ``tools.approval._session_yolo``
(not a stale env var) and honors the frozen process-start ``--yolo`` flag.

name: _toggle_yolo
doc:
Toggle per-session YOLO mode (skip dangerous-command approvals).

Mirrors the gateway/TUI ``/yolo`` handlers. Deliberately does NOT touch
``HERMES_YOLO_MODE``: that env var is frozen into ``tools.approval._YOLO_MODE_FROZEN``
at import (so prompt-injected skills can't flip the bypass), making a later set a
silent no-op. ``run_conversation`` binds ``self.session_id`` as the active approval
key, so the bypass applies to the very next dangerous command.

name: _manual_compress
doc:
Manually trigger context compression.

* ``/compress [<focus>]`` — compress the whole history; an optional focus topic tells
  the summariser what to preserve while discarding the rest more aggressively.
* ``/compress here [N]`` — boundary-aware: summarize everything except the most recent
  ``N`` exchanges (default 2), kept verbatim.
* ``--preview`` reports what would happen and changes nothing.
No ``compression_enabled`` gate: that flag disables *automatic* compaction only, and
the context-overflow error path directs users here when it is off.

name: _persist_prompt_summary
arguments: self, icon: str, label: str, detail: str, outcome: str
doc:
Print a one-line scrollback summary of a resolved modal prompt (approval/clarify
panels vanish on repaint); gated by ``display.persist_prompts``.

name: _clear_terminal_on_exit
doc:
Clear screen + scrollback (``ESC[3J ESC[2J ESC[H``) so nothing is stranded above
the exit summary. Only safe after ``app.run()`` returned and prompt_toolkit restored
terminal modes. Skips when stdout isn't a console; falls back to ``clear``/``cls``.

name: _persist_active_session_before_close
doc:
Best-effort flush of the agent's live ``_session_messages`` before ``end_session()``
— a terminal close/SIGHUP can unwind the app while the agent thread still holds the
current turn only in memory.

name: _print_exit_summary
doc:
Print session resume info on exit. ``clear_screen`` (interactive TUI teardown)
wipes screen + scrollback first; single-query mode passes False to keep the answer.

Args: clear_screen: When True (default), clear the terminal screen and scrollback before printing
the summary. See #38252, #53009.

name: _end_current_session
doc:
Flush un-persisted messages, then end the current session row with ``reason``.
Best-effort on both steps (the switch proceeds even if the DB write fails).

name: _sync_agent_to_session
arguments: cli, session_id: str, *, parent_session_id: str, reason: str
doc:
Point an already-built agent at ``session_id`` after a /resume or /branch switch: reset
per-session state, re-anchor the DB flush index, and notify memory providers with
reset=False (their state stays valid and just targets the new id; parent keeps lineage).

name: _cli
doc: Late import of the ``cli`` facade: mutable CLI module state (and its test seams) lives there.

name: _sync_process_session_id
doc: Keep process-local session-id consumers aligned after CLI switches.

name: _flush_logging_and_stdio
doc: Best-effort ``logging.shutdown()`` + stdout/stderr flush before ``os._exit``.

name: _float_env
doc: ``float(os.getenv(name))``, or ``default`` when unset/unparseable.

name: _exit_watchdog_timeout
doc: ``HERMES_EXIT_WATCHDOG_S`` as a float (default 30; ``0`` disables).

name: _arm_exit_watchdog
doc:
Daemon timer that ``os._exit(0)``s after ``timeout_s`` once shutdown has begun.

Backstop for a cleanup step wedged on network I/O and for interpreter teardown
blocked joining non-daemon threads (ThreadPoolExecutor's atexit join). The daemon
timer survives ``Py_FinalizeEx``'s joins. ``HERMES_EXIT_WATCHDOG_S=0`` disables.

1. 2. Interpreter teardown blocked joining non-daemon threads — stdlib ``ThreadPoolExecutor`` workers
are joined unconditionally by ``concurrent.futures``' atexit hook even after ``shutdown(wait=False)``,
so one tool thread wedged on a socket held the process open forever (#27563 class).

name: _shutdown_agent_memory_provider
doc: Memory-provider shutdown (on_session_end + shutdown_all) at the real session boundary.

name: _gateway_owns_session_end
doc:
A gateway-backed session ends in the gateway: the viewer's ``end_session`` (``session.detach
{end_reason}``) makes the owner run finalize and the memory commit (gateway/session_viewer_close).

name: _notify_session_finalize
arguments: *, session_id: str | None, platform: str='cli', reason: str='shutdown'
doc: Fire on_session_finalize; return the plugin messages meant for the user (never raises).

name: _oneshot_agent_and_session
doc: ``(agent, session_id)`` for a one-shot run; the agent's id wins over the CLI's.

name: _invoke_interrupted_session_end
doc: Best-effort ``on_session_end`` hook for a turn cut short (never raises).

name: _emit_interrupted_session_end
doc: Best-effort on_session_end hook for interrupted non-interactive runs.

name: _flush_one_shot_session_store
doc:
Durably flush + finalize the one-shot session row before exit (idempotent, best-effort).

One-shot runs get a single turn, so nothing retries a transiently-failed transcript
flush, closes the session row, or drains token deltas the kanban ``os._exit(0)``
path skips. Handed-off sessions are left alone.

- a turn whose in-loop ``_flush_messages_to_session_db`` failed under write-lock contention (e.g. a busy
multiplex gateway sharing state.db) was silently lost — the reply reached stdout and agent.log but the
resumed session's stored history never changed (#88583); - the resumed/created titled session row was
left dangling open (``ended_at``/``end_reason`` NULL) on every one-shot exit; - queued async
token-accounting deltas relied on interpreter-exit hooks, which the kanban SIGTERM path's
``os._exit(0)`` skips entirely.
Idempotent and best-effort: ``_persist_session`` dedupes via the per-message ``_DB_PERSISTED_MARKER``
stamps (already-written turns are not re-written) and ``end_session`` no-ops on an already-ended row.
See #88234.

name: _wait_for_oneshot_background_completions
doc:
Bounded linger for notify_on_complete background processes (children write to our pipes).

Waits on the whole registry: a one-shot process hosts one agent, and task_id
filtering would skip processes registered before the session id settled.

Skipped when the quiet -Q notify-resume loop already consumed the run's linger
budget: it calls wait_for_pending_completions with a shared deadline, so a
re-wait here would double-block on the same stuck notify_on_complete child.

See #90879.

name: _finalize_single_query
doc:
Settle the session, then release its lease, then linger as a bystander.

Three phases, in this order:

1. **Session-owned settlement** — the durable flush (transcript retry, token
   drain, ``end_session``), the finalize hook, and memory-provider session
   finalization. Providers finalize THIS session's remote state at
   ``on_session_end`` (OpenViking synchronously commits ``sessions/{sid}``,
   Supermemory flushes pending turns stamped with the session id), so this
   belongs inside ownership — post-release it would run while a successor
   may already be mid-turn on the session. The flush runs first: memory
   shutdown can issue aux-LLM calls and nothing after it may fail in a way
   that loses the turn (#88583). Settlement is best-effort by design:
   failures are logged and the release still happens, because the failure
   mode to avoid is an exited process pinning the lease — a dangling open
   row is recoverable (session_recovery reaps stale rows), a wedged lease
   is not.
2. **Ownership handoff** — release the active-session lease. Every turn of
   the run (main turn, kanban goal loop, notify-completion follow-ups) has
   finished and the success path has no session-owned writes left, so a
   waiting delivery may acquire and resume the session immediately:
   releasing only at process exit let an alive-but-idle one-shot refuse
   deliveries for the whole exit linger (bounded, minutes) after its turn
   had ended (#118826 / #122770).
3. **Process-only work, lease-free** — the bounded linger for
   notify_on_complete children (pipe drain, the boundary the one-shot path
   itself declares "NOT part of the spawner's delivery", #113608) and
   resource teardown. ``_run_cleanup``'s memory-shutdown call is idempotent
   (``_memory_provider_shutdown``), so its post-release repeat is a no-op;
   neither it nor the linger touches session rows.

Releasing between settlement and the linger is what prevents the handoff race:
a successor that acquires and reopens the session can never receive this
process's stale ``cli_close`` end-stamp, because phase 1 has already run it.

name: _int_or
doc: ``int(value)``, or ``default`` when it does not parse.

name: _interrupt_agent_for_signal
doc:
Hard-interrupt ``agent`` for a shutdown signal, then sleep ``HERMES_SIGTERM_GRACE`` (1.5 s).

The grace lets the agent thread kill the tool's setsid subprocess group before the
main thread unwinds (else an orphan child). Never raises.

name: _run_kanban_goal_loop_q
arguments: cli: HermesCLI, first_response: str, run_turn=None, log=None
doc:
Drive a kanban goal_mode worker through ``goals.run_kanban_goal_loop`` after its first turn.

``run_turn`` defaults to the bare ``-Q`` turn (final answer only). The ``-q`` worker path
passes ``cli.chat`` so every follow-up turn keeps the tool activity feed that the Kanban
worker log is made of. The caller swallows all errors: a broken loop must never wedge a worker.

name: _run_kanban_goal_loop_chat
doc:
``-q`` worker variant: follow-up turns go through ``cli.chat`` (tool feed stays on stdout,
which is the Kanban worker log) and judge verdicts are printed there too, so a goal_mode card's
log reads like any other worker's instead of staying blank until the final answer.

name: _sync_cli_session_id_from_agent
doc: Keep ``cli.session_id`` in sync when mid-run compression rotated the agent's session.

name: _single_query_exit_code
doc:
Map a one-shot turn result onto a process exit code, for both `-q` and `-Q`.

0 only when the turn completed; 130 when it was interrupted; 1 when it failed, stopped
partway (`partial`, `completed: False`) or never ran at all (credentials / agent init
failed, so ``result`` is not a dict). A Kanban worker (``HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`` set) that
failed purely on a provider rate-limit / billing wall exits ``KANBAN_RATE_LIMIT_EXIT_CODE``
(EX_TEMPFAIL): the dispatcher books that run ``rate_limited`` and requeues the task
WITHOUT counting a failure, so a quota window or a provider outage cannot trip the breaker.
The same sentinel applies when credential resolution itself is a quota/rate-limit
AuthError (no turn result object is produced). One that failed on a terminal provider
error (credential revoked, model gone) exits ``KANBAN_TERMINAL_PROVIDER_EXIT_CODE``
(EX_CONFIG): the dispatcher blocks the card at once. The same code applies
before a turn when credential resolution explicitly requires re-authentication;
unknown startup failures retain exit 1.

The worker predicate is the STRIPPED ``kanban_task_id()`` (from
``agent.kanban_turn_recovery``) so a whitespace-only value is not a worker here
either — the exit mapping and the recovery gate must agree on what a worker is.

name: _run_quiet_single_query
doc:
Quiet (-Q) one-shot turn: run, print the response (stderr for errors/session_id), then sys.exit with the automation exit code.
With a ``StreamJsonEmitter`` the final answer and the exit line become the terminal ``result`` JSONL record instead.
HERMES_TURN_AUTHOR (set only by a bot-to-bot dispatcher) is consumed here so tool subprocesses do not inherit it.
Nested Bot Mode notifies bind this session's key (not the dispatcher's) and resume in-process
before stdout is printed, so a teammate reply is the quiet run's final answer rather than a
stranded receipt.

name: _route_single_query_images
doc: Attach one-shot images natively when the model supports vision, else pre-describe them as text.

name: _collect_kanban_task_images
doc: Kanban workers: image paths/URLs in the task body join the first turn's attachments.

name: _install_single_query_signal_handlers
doc:
Route SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP through agent.interrupt() before unwinding; kanban workers hard-exit.

A plain KeyboardInterrupt only unwinds the main thread, so tool worker threads
would orphan the setsid child; the interrupt + grace window lets them kill it.

name: _configure_quiet_agent
doc: Neutralize every stdout-writing callback so -Q stdout carries only the final response.

name: _run_single_query_mode
arguments: cli, query, image, quiet, oneshot, stream_json: bool=False
doc:
``-q``/``--image`` entry: seed an interactive session on a TTY, else run the one-shot turn and exit.
``stream_json`` (implies quiet) swaps the plain-text final answer for the JSONL event protocol.

significant_calls.expression:
emitter.emit_result({"failed": True, "error": "credentials or agent init failed"},
                                    session_id=cli.session_id or "", exit_code=fail_code)

name: _pause_owner
doc: Hand the profile off; True when this restore parked a satellite and must serve it again.

name: _threshold_style
doc: First ``class:status-bar-<name>`` whose ``value >= bound`` in a descending ladder.

name: _finite
doc: Drop NaN / negative / absurd provider timings (e.g. -0.8s seen in logs).

name: _cache_hit_rate
doc:
Return (cache_pct, label) or None without cache data. Prefers the baseline-delta pct
from ``_get_status_bar_snapshot`` (resets on model switch / compression, so it reflects
the *current* cache regime); falls back to the session-lifetime ratio.

name: _cache_hit_rate_style
doc: Higher is better (opposite of context %).

name: _vim_mode_label
doc:
Current vi editing mode as a short status-bar label; empty when vim mode is off
or the application is not running yet.

name: _handle_battery_command
doc:
``/battery`` toggles, ``/battery on|off`` sets, ``/battery status`` reports the
setting plus a live reading. Persisted to ``display.battery``.

name: _format_prompt_elapsed
arguments: prompt_start_time: Optional[float], prompt_duration: float, live: bool=False
doc:
Per-prompt elapsed time. Always a string (``⏲ 0s`` on fresh start); seconds stay
visible at every scale so it increments smoothly (``1m 59s → 2m → 2m 1s``). ⏱ while
live, ⏲ frozen — width-1 glyphs (no variation selector) keep the bar aligned.

name: _format_idle_since
doc:
``✓ 42s`` since the last final response; empty while a turn is live or before the
first turn completes.

name: _get_status_bar_session_title
doc: Current title, polling state.db at most every 1.5s (not on every repaint).

name: _status_bar_display_width
doc:
Terminal cell width (some glyphs render wider than one codepoint); keeps the bar
from wrapping onto a second line and leaving duplicate rows.

name: _trim_status_bar_text
doc: Trim status-bar text to a single terminal row.

name: _status_title_badge
doc:
(badge, left_width) for the far-right session-title badge, or None when it
doesn't fit (no title / bar narrower than 24 cells).

name: _right_align_status_title
arguments: cls, text: str, title: str, width: int
doc: Pin a bounded session-title badge to the far-right status-bar edge.

name: _right_align_status_title_fragments
arguments: cls, frags, title: str, width: int
doc: Styled counterpart to :meth:`_right_align_status_title`.

name: _get_tui_terminal_width
doc:
Live prompt_toolkit width (can be narrower than shutil's, esp. Termux), falling
back to ``shutil``.

name: _use_minimal_tui_chrome
doc: Hide low-value chrome on narrow/mobile terminals to preserve rows.

name: _scrollback_box_width
doc:
Full viewport width for printed scrollback box rules, floored at 32 cols so tiny
terminals never hit negative ``'─' * (w - 2)`` math. (The old 56-col clamp against
reflow-on-shrink is gone: the ``_output_screen_diff`` patch keeps chrome out of
scrollback, and reflow of already-printed borders is a cosmetic artifact.)

Previously this clamped to ``max(32, min(width, 56))`` as a defense against terminal-emulator reflow
on column-shrink (#25975, salvaging 24403). That clamp made response/reasoning borders look stubby
on any modern wide terminal. We now trust the prompt_toolkit ``_output_screen_diff`` monkey-patch
landed in #26137 (salvaging 25981) to keep chrome out of scrollback in the first place, and accept
that an aggressive column-shrink may visually reflow already printed Panel borders — that's a
cosmetic artifact of stamped scrollback history, not a live-render bug.

name: _agent_spacer_height
doc: Spacer height above the status bar while the agent runs.

name: _spinner_widget_height
doc: Visible height of the spinner/status line above the status bar.

name: _render_spinner_text
doc: The live spinner/status text exactly as rendered in the TUI.

name: _spinner_token_flow
doc: Cumulative output tokens for the running turn, for the spinner.

name: _turn_summary_is_active
doc:
Whether the per-turn summary line renders here: off for the config key, quiet /
tool-progress-off mode, and every non-interactive path (-q, -Q, gateway).

name: _turn_summary_begin
doc: Start per-turn accounting for the turn that is about to run.

name: _turn_summary_record
doc: Feed one completed tool call into the active tally.

name: _turn_summary_emit
doc: Print the post-turn accounting line, when enabled for this surface.

name: _pet_clear_runtime
doc: Drop renderer + queued Kitty state. Caller holds ``_pet_lock``.

name: _pet_resolve_config
doc:
(Re)resolve the active pet from config so ``/pet`` / ``hermes pets`` changes apply
without a restart (mirrors the TUI's steady poll). Fail-open: any problem disables.

name: _pet_flash
doc: Briefly force a transient reaction (wave/jump/failed) before resting.

name: _on_reaction
doc:
Core-detected user affection (ily / <3 / good bot): the pet's share of the vibe
signal that plays hearts on the TUI/desktop.

name: _pet_react_turn_end
doc: End-of-turn beat: failed on error, jump on a finished plan, else wave.

name: _derive_pet_state
doc:
A live transient beat wins; otherwise the shared ``agent.pet.state.derive_pet_state``
priority order so the CLI can't drift from the TUI/desktop.

name: _pet_frames_for
doc: Return (and cache) the half-block grids for one state.

name: _pet_kitty_payload_for
doc: Return and cache a Kitty virtual-placeholder payload for *state*.

name: _pet_queue_kitty_frame
doc:
Queue one virtual Kitty frame for the next prompt_toolkit render. No-op when the
pet pane was never initialized (``__new__`` fixtures, redraw on a pet-less CLI).

name: _pet_flush_kitty_frame
doc: Write a queued APC after prompt_toolkit has finished its screen diff.

name: _pet_view
doc: (state, is_kitty) for the current frame, or None when no pet shows.

name: _pet_fragments
doc: prompt_toolkit FormattedText for the current pet frame, or [].

name: _pet_widget_height
doc: Visible rows for the pet window — 0 collapses it when no pet shows.

name: _pet_anim_loop
doc: Advance the frame + invalidate on a timer while a pet is enabled.

name: _voice_record_key_label
doc:
The push-to-talk key label every voice-facing hint advertises. Cached at startup
(``set_voice_record_key_cache``) because the prompt_toolkit binding is registered once —
re-reading config per render could advertise a chord that isn't bound — and this sits on
the hot render path.

Two reasons (Copilot round-13 on 19835): See #19835.

name: set_voice_record_key_cache
doc:
Populate the voice label cache from a raw ``voice.record_key``; called after the
prompt_toolkit binding is registered so the label matches the live binding.

name: _get_voice_status_fragments
doc: Voice status bar fragments for the interactive TUI.

name: _status_bar_goal_segment
doc:
``⊙ goal 3/20`` while a goal is active, else ``""`` (paused/done goals already
print their own glyph lines in the thread).

name: _get_status_bar_field_set
doc:
Visible status-bar fields from ``display.status_bar.fields`` (module-level
``CLI_CONFIG``; no per-render YAML parse). ``None`` = not customized, show everything.

Fields: model, context_detail, context_pct, cache_hit, latency, tps, compressions,
bg_tasks, bg_processes, bg_subagents, goal, git_branch (opt-in only), duration,
prompt_elapsed, idle_since, focus, yolo, stash, battery, title, total_tokens
(opt-in only). Order is fixed; the config controls visibility only.

name: _status_bar_segments
arguments: self, snapshot, width: int, field_set, yolo_active: bool, *, styled: bool
doc:
Ordered status-bar segments for one width tier (<52 / <76 / wide), each a list of
``(style, text)`` fragments. Shared by the plain-text and prompt_toolkit renderers so
the two can never drift; ``styled`` selects the graphical context bar.

name: _build_status_bar_text
doc: Compact one-line session status string for the TUI footer.

name: _render_stash_panel
arguments: self, stash_list: list, cursor: int, width: int
doc:
prompt_toolkit fragments for the stash panel box. Every horizontal measurement uses
``_status_bar_display_width`` (display cells), not ``len()`` — 📌 is one codepoint but
two cells, and CJK previews would otherwise bleed past the right border.

name: _thinking_prefix
doc: ``  [thinking] `` — the reasoning-preview label; also measured for wrap width.

name: _on_thinking
doc: Called by agent when thinking starts/stops. Updates TUI spinner.

name: _on_notice
doc:
Queue an out-of-band AgentNotice for rendering at the next clean boundary.

Notices fire mid-turn (cold-start seed, per-turn _capture_credits); printing immediately
races the stream and buries the line behind the prompt. Flushed by _flush_credit_notices()
after run_conversation returns. Fail-soft.

name: _flush_credit_notices
doc:
Print queued credit notices as level-colored lines at turn end (after
run_conversation) where _cprint paints cleanly above the prompt.

name: _on_notice_clear
doc:
No-op for the REPL (lines are printed, no persistent slot to wipe); kept so the
agent's clear callback is bound symmetrically with the show callback.

name: _current_reasoning_callback
doc: Return the active reasoning display callback for the current mode.

name: _emit_reasoning_preview
doc: Render a buffered reasoning preview as a single [thinking] block.

name: _flush_reasoning_preview
doc:
Flush buffered reasoning text at natural boundaries.

Some providers stream reasoning in tiny word/punctuation chunks; buffering keeps the
preview path from printing one `[thinking]` line per token.

name: _format_submitted_user_message_preview
doc: Format the submitted user-message scrollback preview.

name: _expand_paste_references
doc: Expand [Pasted text #N -> file] placeholders into file contents.

name: _print_user_message_preview
doc: Render a user message using the normal chat scrollback style.

name: _stream_reasoning_delta
doc:
Stream reasoning tokens into a dim box above the response.

Opened on the first token, closed when content arrives (_emit_stream_text). Once the
response box is open further reasoning is suppressed — a late thinking block (e.g. after
an interrupt) would otherwise draw a reasoning box inside the response box.

name: _agent_status_print
doc:
``agent._print_fn`` for the interactive CLI: agent status lines (subagent completion ``✓ [set n · i/N]``,
background-process notices, spinner ``print_above`` text) arrive from other threads at any moment. While
a response or reasoning box is being streamed they are HELD and released at the box footer, so a line
never lands between two paragraphs of the reply. Outside a box they print immediately.

name: _release_held_status_lines
doc: Print status lines held while a box was open (called right after a box footer).

name: _close_reasoning_box
doc: Close the live reasoning box if it's open (renders the buffered reasoning tail).

name: _stream_delta
doc:
Line-buffered streaming callback for real-time token rendering.

Emits complete lines via _cprint (reliable under prompt_toolkit's patch_stdout);
reasoning tags are suppressed, or routed to the reasoning box when show_reasoning is on.
``None`` = intermediate turn boundary (tools about to run): flush boxes and reset state.

name: _emit_stream_line
doc: Print one response line with the skin's true-color text escape (if any).

name: _flush_stream_table_buf
doc:
Emit the held table block re-aligned as a whole. Cell-level markdown is stripped FIRST
so the realigner pads to the final visible width, not the marker-decorated width.

name: _emit_stream_text
doc: Emit filtered text to the streaming display.

name: _flush_stream
doc: Emit any remaining partial line from the stream buffer and close the box.

name: _reset_stream_state
doc: Reset streaming state before each agent invocation.

name: _slow_command_status
doc: Return a user-facing status message for slower slash commands.

name: _command_spinner_frame
doc: Return the current spinner frame for slow slash commands.

name: _busy_command
_preprocess_images_with_vision
arguments: self, text: str, images: list, *, announce: bool=True
doc:
Describe attached images via the auxiliary vision model and prepend the descriptions
to the user's text (works with non-vision models; same approach as the gateway). The
local path is included so the agent can re-examine via ``vision_analyze``.

name: _console_print
doc:
Print through the active command-safe console (prompt_toolkit-safe Rich once the
TUI is live, else the plain console).

name: _on_tool_gen_start
doc:
Model began generating tool-call arguments: close open boxes once, then print a status
line so a large payload (e.g. 45 KB write_file) doesn't look like a frozen screen.

Fires once per tool CALL, so a batch of parallel calls to the same tool printed the same
line N times (#10478); repeats within one generation batch are coalesced. The set is
cleared when a tool actually starts (``tool.started``), i.e. on the next batch.

name: _on_tool_progress
arguments: self, event_type: str, function_name: str | None=None, preview: str | None=None, function_args: dict | None=None, **kwargs
doc:
Tool lifecycle events (tool.started / tool.completed / reasoning.* / moa.*).

Drives the TUI spinner (tool.started stamps the elapsed timer); in "all"/"new"/"verbose"
progress modes tool.completed also commits a stacked scrollback line (tool history).

name: _show_tool_progress
doc:
Live MCP progress rides the spinner line: ``<tool label> · 42% · message``. The CLI has one
spinner, so progress shows only while exactly one call of that tool runs and nothing else does:
with parallel calls the label could belong to another call (tool.started carries no call id).

name: _on_tool_start
arguments: self, tool_call_id: str, function_name: str, function_args: dict
doc: Capture local before-state for write-capable tools.

name: _on_tool_complete
arguments: self, tool_call_id: str, function_name: str, function_args: dict, function_result: str
doc: Render file edits with inline diff after write-capable tools complete.

name: subagent_tail
doc:
The child's transcript tail from the monitor's backend (the gateway's is fetched and filtered by
the monitor's tick, never here: the detail view calls this every frame).

name: modal_prompt_active
doc:
A prompt owns the composer (its text is an answer or a secret, never a chat message):
every composer shortcut stays off while one is open.

name: roster
doc: Agents first, then processes — the order the dock and the full-height monitor paint.

name: subagents
doc:
The subagent backend: the gateway session's view when its children run there (CLI-12),
else this process's own registry; both answer the same ``subagent_*`` calls.

name: poll_soon
doc:
Let the spinner thread's next tick poll the gateway, instead of the caller blocking the
UI loop on it.

name: _poll_tail
doc:
Off the render path (the spinner thread's tick): refresh the gateway tail the open detail
view paints from the cache. True when the text changed.

name: _counts
doc:
Count fragment: ``2 live``, ``1 proc``, ``2 live · 3 procs``; the collapsed heading
(``session=True``) adds ``goal active|paused|parked``, the loop badge and ``N queued``.

name: _agent_activity
doc: ``last: <tool>`` while a tool runs, else the raw status id, else ``starting``.

name: run_control
doc:
Steer/stop off the UI loop: a stalled gateway call (up to its timeout) must not freeze the
monitor's repaint, Esc or Ctrl+C. The answer lands in the notice line when it arrives.

name: _cli
doc: Late import of the ``cli`` facade: mutable CLI module state (and its test seams) lives there.

name: _termux_example_image_path
doc: Return a realistic example media path for the current Termux setup.

name: _split_path_input
doc: Split a leading path token (quoted or with ``\ `` escapes) from trailing free-form text.

name: _resolve_attachment_path
doc:
Resolve a user-supplied attachment path (quotes, ``~``, env vars, ``file://``; relative to TERMINAL_CWD).

Returns ``None`` unless it resolves to an existing file.

name: _detect_file_drop
doc: Detect a dragged/pasted file path at the start of *user_input* -> ``{path, is_image, remainder}`` or None.

name: _format_image_attachment_badges
arguments: attached_images: list[Path], image_counter: int, width: int | None=None
doc: Attached-image badge row: compact summary on narrow terminals, per-image badges otherwise.

name: _should_auto_attach_clipboard_image_on_paste
doc: Auto-attach clipboard images only for image-only paste gestures.

name: _hermes_call_output_screen_diff
arguments: orig_osd, app, output, screen, current_pos, color_depth, previous_screen, last_style, is_done, full_screen, attrs_for_style_string, style_string_has_style, size, previous_width
doc:
prompt_toolkit ``_output_screen_diff`` with resize guards.

Inflates ``previous_screen.height`` when the new screen is taller so pt skips the
cursor move that stamps chrome into scrollback; on a corrupt previous paint buffer
(tmux re-attach) retries once as a first paint instead of crashing the loop.

1. 2. On AttributeError/TypeError from a corrupt previous paint buffer (classic after tmux attach with
same width), retry once with ``previous_screen=None`` so pt first-paints cleanly instead of crashing the
event loop with ``'cell' object has no attribute 'char'``. See #26137.

name: _apply_bracketed_paste_timeout_patch
doc:
Patch ``Vt100Parser.feed`` to flush a bracketed paste whose ESC[201~ end mark never arrives.

Without it a dropped end mark (SSH glitch, sleep/wake) freezes input forever. Idempotent.

name: _is_ghostty_terminal
doc:
Whether the terminal is Ghostty.

Ghostty gets ONLY modifyOtherKeys: its Kitty disambiguate mode strips Alt from
Backspace (upstream bug), breaking backward-kill-word.

Ghostty implements modifyOtherKeys correctly (it then emits ``\x1b[27;3;127~``, which the alias table
also maps). See #87630.

name: _terminal_supports_extended_enter_keys
doc: Allowlist of terminals where requesting modified-Enter reporting is safe (aligned with the Ink TUI).

name: _enable_extended_enter_keys
doc:
Ask allowlisted terminals to report modified keys distinctly.

Pushes BOTH kitty keyboard protocol and xterm modifyOtherKeys (kitty dropped the
latter; tmux/VS Code only accept it). Both re-encode modified keys as sequences
stock prompt_toolkit barely maps (Ctrl+C once arrived as ``ESC[99;5u``), so
``install_modify_other_keys_aliases()`` must have run first. Ghostty gets only
modifyOtherKeys. The exit reset pops both modes.

Under either protocol the terminal re-encodes modified keys as escape sequences — Kitty disambiguate
mode as ``ESC[<codepoint>;<mod>u`` (plus the Esc key as ``ESC[27u``), modifyOtherKeys=2 as
``ESC[27;<mod>;<codepoint>~``. Stock prompt_toolkit 3.x maps almost none of these, which is why the CSI
>1u push was temporarily removed in 87074 (Ctrl+C arrived as ``ESC[99;5u`` and died, #56684).
``install_modify_other_keys_aliases()`` (called at CLI startup from ``hermes_cli.pt_input_extras``) now
populates ``ANSI_SEQUENCES`` with the full Ctrl/Alt/Shift/multi-modifier and functional-key tables under
BOTH formats, so every existing key binding continues to fire — including Ctrl+C, which is handled by
prompt_toolkit's ``c-c`` binding (raw mode clears ISIG, so the kernel INTR path was never in play for
the CLI).
See #87630.

name: _cli_multiline_shortcuts_enabled
doc: ``display.cli_multiline_shortcuts`` (default on: Ctrl+J = newline; off restores the legacy c-j submit).

name: _is_backslash_line_continuation
doc: True when Enter should turn a trailing backslash into a newline.

name: _apply_backslash_line_continuation
doc: Replace a trailing ``\`` marker with an actual newline.

name: _preserve_ctrl_enter_newline
doc:
Environments delivering Ctrl+Enter as bare LF (Windows Terminal, WSL, SSH, Ghostty): c-j must stay newline.

See issue #22379.

name: _bind_prompt_submit_keys
doc:
Enter always submits; c-j submits only with multiline shortcuts off AND where Ctrl+Enter isn't c-j.

Even when the setting is disabled, environments where Ctrl+Enter is known to arrive as c-j (Windows,
WSL, SSH, Windows Terminal, Ghostty) keep c-j reserved for newline; otherwise Ctrl+Enter submits instead
of composing. See _preserve_ctrl_enter_newline() and issue #22379.

name: _disable_prompt_toolkit_cpr_warning
doc: Let prompt_toolkit fall back from CPR without printing into the prompt.

name: _terminal_may_leak_cpr
doc:
Suppress prompt_toolkit CPR queries (delayed replies leak into input); Windows keeps pt's default.

Delayed CPR replies (``ESC[<row>;<col>R`` / visible ``^[[<row>;<col>R``) leak into the status line and
can freeze input when the reply is slow (#13870 on SSH/slow PTYs). The same race hits local POSIX TTYs
under heavy subagent / status-line load — see ``tests/hermes_cli/test_cpr_local_leak.py``.

name: _build_cpr_disabled_output
doc:
Vt100_Output with ``enable_cpr=False`` (``from_pty()`` doesn't expose it), or None on failure.

prompt_toolkit's renderer sends ``ESC[6n`` (Device Status Report) to learn the cursor row before
painting in non-fullscreen mode; the terminal replies ``ESC[<row>;<col>R``. When that reply is delayed
it races into the display as raw ``^[[39;1R`` and can stall the renderer's pending-CPR future (#13870;
also local POSIX under heavy subagent load).

name: _select_classic_cli_pt_output
doc: CPR-disabled ``Vt100_Output`` when CPR may leak, else None (Application keeps pt's default).

name: _strip_leaked_terminal_responses_with_meta
doc: Strip leaked CPR replies and mouse-report fragments -> ``(cleaned, had_mouse_reports)``.

name: _estimate_tui_input_height
arguments: lines: list[str] | tuple[str, ...], prompt_text: str, terminal_columns: int, *, max_height: int=8
doc:
Input rows from live terminal cells; the BeforeInput prompt consumes cells only on line 0.

Never substitute a fake wide fallback: a mis-sized TextArea leaves stale cells at the bottom.

name: _status_bar_visible_from_display_config
doc: Initial status-bar visibility; both YAML ``off`` (False) and strings like ``"hidden"`` mean off.

name: _collect_query_images
arguments: query: str | None, image_arg: str | None=None
doc: Collect local image attachments for single-query CLI flows.

name: _run_on_app_loop
doc: Run *fn* on the app's asyncio loop when one exists, else inline (fail-open).

name: _write_terminal_sequence
doc: Write a raw escape *seq* via the app output (write_raw > write) or stdout.

name: _mark_terminal_io_broken
doc: Stop UI paints after the PTY/stdout becomes unusable (#81521).

name: _app_invalidate
arguments: self, app, where: str, *, swallow: bool
doc:
``app.invalidate()``: EIO freezes paints, other OSErrors re-raise, and any
other exception re-raises unless *swallow*.

name: _invalidate
doc:
Throttled UI repaint for high-frequency background updates (spinner frames,
streaming flushes): the throttle prevents blinking on slow/SSH links and the
resize-recovery guard keeps footer chrome out of scrollback mid-SIGWINCH.

NOT for user-blocking modals (approval / clarify / sudo) — use ``_paint_now``: a
throttled or resize-gated entry paint is silently dropped, so the prompt never
renders and times out unseen (#41098).

name: _paint_now
doc:
Unthrottled repaint for user-blocking modal prompts.

Bypasses the ``_invalidate`` throttle — a modal the user is waiting on must never be
dropped (#41098) — mirroring the direct ``event.app.invalidate()`` the modal key-binding
handlers use. While a width change awaits its recovery the app's redraw is gated
(``_install_resize_recovery``), so the paint waits for that recovery, which repaints the
whole app about every ``_RESIZE_HOLD_MAX`` seconds even while a drag keeps signalling.

name: _force_full_redraw
doc:
Force a clean full-screen repaint of the prompt_toolkit UI (Ctrl+L, ``/redraw``).

Recovers from terminal buffer drift caused by external redraws we can't detect
(cmux/tmux tab switches, ``clear`` from a subshell, SSH window restores): they
repaint without SIGWINCH, so prompt_toolkit's tracked ``_cursor_pos`` is stale
and the next incremental redraw stacks on old content (ghost status bars).

name: _schedule_focus_regain_redraw
doc:
Repaint after a terminal focus-in report (``CSI I``), at most once per
``min_interval`` (rapid Alt+Tab / pane-hop bursts). Emulators with focus tracking
(DECSET 1004) may coalesce hidden-tab output, so on regain the incremental diff
stacks on stale content (#60920, #25337); terminals without it never emit ``CSI I``.

name: _redraw_rebuilds_scrollback
doc:
Whether redraw/resize recovery should also clear scrollback (CSI 3J).

Some terminal/tmux stacks move prompt_toolkit's bottom chrome into scrollback on
maximize/restore; CSI 2J cannot remove those rows, so affected users opt in to 3J
followed by the bounded output-history replay.

name: _recover_terminal_after_interrupt
doc:
Recover the terminal after an interrupted agent turn (#33271): an in-flight
``CSI 6n`` reply arriving after the input parser tore down leaks as literal text
and can stall the VT100 parser mid-escape. Drain stdin, then full redraw; each step
self-guards. A dead PTY (EIO) skips the redraw (#81521 redraw storm). Never clear
output history here — the interruption marker is printed under
``_suspend_output_history``, so replay already excludes it (#60920).

name: _clear_prompt_toolkit_screen
arguments: self, app, *, rebuild_scrollback: bool=False, keep_above: bool=False
doc:
Clear the terminal and reset prompt_toolkit renderer state.

Returns the ``fit`` for the replay that follows (``_transcript_room`` plus where to
paint it). ``None`` means replay the whole history (scrollback wiped by CSI 3J). Without
3J the older transcript stays in scrollback, so the replay may only repaint what the
viewport held (#95375); the viewport is erased row by row because CSI 2J makes
scroll-on-clear terminals (tmux, VTE) copy the whole screen into scrollback first,
stacking a duplicate. With ``keep_above`` (a resize), on a terminal that keeps rows in
place, and the whole history on screen, only its rows and the chrome are erased — what
sits above them (the startup banner) was never recorded and a replay could not restore
it. Counted as painted, the replay leaves the chrome's top at a known row: the chrome is
drawn from there to the bottom (``_set_chrome_floor``), where the next count assumes it.
A clear that fails replays nothing: the history is already on screen or in scrollback.

name: _transcript_room
doc:
``(rows, columns, painted)``: the viewport rows the transcript fills above the
prompt chrome, and how to count them — at the current ``columns``, or with ``painted``
at the width each line was painted at, as a terminal that does not reflow keeps them.
Unless the terminal is known to reflow, count as painted: that replays at least what
the viewport held, never less.

The chrome is the renderer's last paint: prompt_toolkit may draw the app taller than
its preferred height (it fills the rows below the cursor it measured, or down to the
bottom row once a refill left its top at a known row).

name: _painted_row_widths
doc:
Cells each row of the renderer's last paint reaches: prompt_toolkit writes a row up to
its last cell that shows something (the blanks after it are erase-to-end-of-line).

name: _note_chrome_paint
doc:
Remember when each row of the chrome prompt_toolkit just drew was written, and how
wide — ``full``: the whole chrome was written anew (for ``_aim_erase_at_reflowed_chrome``).
A row only changes height when its width does, so only those changes are kept.

name: _aim_erase_at_reflowed_chrome
doc:
Point prompt_toolkit's erase at the top of its last paint as a reflowing terminal
re-wrapped it to ``columns`` (#95375).

``renderer.erase()`` moves up ``_cursor_pos.y`` rows — right where rows stay in place,
short of the top on a reflowing terminal, whose re-wrapped chrome rows would stay
above the new paint. A row's width, re-wrapped, is its height now — if the terminal got
the row before it narrowed. prompt_toolkit writes rows with autowrap off, so one it got
after narrowing (painted just before the width change was seen, the signal still on its
way) was clipped to one row instead, and counting it as re-wrapped would erase
transcript rows above the chrome. Rows painted within ``_RESIZE_PAINT_MARGIN`` of the
width change, or unrecorded, count as one row: a stale chrome row left above the new
paint is benign, an erased transcript row is lost for good.

name: _recover_after_resize
doc:
Recover a resized classic CLI without desynchronizing cursor state.

Never clears scrollback (the startup banner lives there and replay cannot rebuild
it) and never resets the renderer before prompt_toolkit's own ``_on_resize``,
which erases the chrome from the cached cursor position. The status bar / input
rules are suppressed while the reflow settles: on column shrink the terminal reflows
already-painted rows into scrollback first, so a fresh bar looks duplicated
(#19280, #22976). On a column shrink a reflowing terminal has re-wrapped the old
chrome into more rows than that cached cursor reaches, so the erase is aimed at the
re-wrapped top instead; the transcript above is left exactly as the terminal
re-wrapped it, never erased and replayed (a replay cannot know which rows the
terminal kept on screen and which it pushed into scrollback, #95375). A terminal that
does not reflow truncates every visible row at the new width instead and keeps it in
place, out of scrollback: the viewport is refilled as Ctrl+L does — also after a drag
that narrowed and widened back, which truncated rows all the same. When nothing says
whether the terminal reflows it is refilled too: a reflowing terminal had already
pushed some of those rows into scrollback and now shows them twice, which beats
truncating them for good.
With ``display.cli_rebuild_scrollback_on_redraw`` (3J + whole-history replay) every
width change rebuilds.
Same-width SIGWINCH (tmux attach, GNOME tab bar, focus) and the first signal
without a seeded baseline are left alone — 2J+replay against preserved scrollback
duplicates ``_OUTPUT_HISTORY`` (#65293). tmux-attach's stale previous_screen is
handled by ``_hermes_call_output_screen_diff`` (#83874). Suppression is cleared by
a debounced timer so the bar returns during idle; next-submit stays a fast path.

name: _restart_debounce_timer
arguments: self, attr: str, delay: float, fn
doc:
Cancel the daemon Timer stored on ``self.<attr>`` (if any) and start a new one.

``fn`` receives the new Timer so it can detect being superseded.

name: _schedule_status_bar_unsuppress
doc:
Clear the post-resize status-bar suppression after the reflow settles.

Debounced: a fresh resize cancels the pending timer, so a resize storm repaints
the bar only once it stops.

name: _schedule_resize_recovery
doc:
Debounce resize redraws so footer chrome is not stamped into scrollback.

The delay outwaits tmux, which re-wraps a pane on every resize but signals it at most
every 250 ms, so mid-drag the width a recovery reads is stale — also over ssh from a
tmux pane, where nothing says tmux is there (#95375). A width change also holds output
paints and redraws until its recovery; while a drag keeps signalling, a recovery still
runs ``_RESIZE_SETTLE`` after the first width change once output was held for
``_RESIZE_HOLD_MAX`` seconds, so output never freezes for the whole drag. A signal that
leaves the width alone holds nothing.

name: _install_resize_recovery
doc:
Route ``app._on_resize`` through the debounced ghost-clearing recovery
(#5474/#49120) and seed the width baseline so the FIRST SIGWINCH can tell a benign
signal from a real resize (#65293). Reads ``app.output`` directly, NOT
``_get_tui_terminal_width``: before ``app.run()`` the DummyApplication's output
reports a hardcoded 80 columns, which would make the first real signal look like a
width change. ``app.output`` is what the running resize handler measures.

name: _output_waits_for_resize
doc:
Whether output must wait for a resize recovery: one is pending, or the terminal's
width no longer matches the one the app last settled at — its SIGWINCH is not handled
yet, and a paint or chrome render now would land in geometry that no recovery accounts
for: on a terminal that does not reflow it scrolls rows the resize truncated into
scrollback before any refill (#95375). Noticing that schedules the recovery.

name: _try_attach_clipboard_image
doc: Save a clipboard image to ~/.hermes/images/ and attach it; True if attached.

name: _write_osc52_clipboard
doc:
Copy *text* to the terminal clipboard via OSC 52.

Wrapped for tmux/screen passthrough (mirrors ui-tui/src/lib/osc52.ts) — without
the DCS wrapper the multiplexer consumes the sequence and the copy is lost.

name: _recover_terminal_input_modes
doc: Best-effort reset when leaked mouse reports indicate mode drift.

name: _check_termios_drift
doc:
Idle watchdog: heal a tty that drifted back to cooked mode (a lost
``run_in_terminal`` cooked→raw restore leaves it line-buffering while prompt_toolkit
believes it owns raw mode — CLI looks dead, process is healthy). Skipped while
``run_in_terminal`` legitimately holds cooked mode, while the agent runs
(approval/sudo prompts touch the tty), and on Windows (no termios).

name: _approval_choice_label
doc: Localized label for an approval choice id; unknown ids render verbatim.

name: _tn
doc: Plural-aware lookup: ``<key>_one`` for exactly one, ``<key>_other`` otherwise.

name: _num_prefix
doc: Quick-select key label: 1-9 for items 1-9, 0 for the 10th, blank beyond.

name: _tui_input_rule_height
doc: Visible height for the top/bottom input separator rules.

name: _get_slash_confirm_display_fragments
doc: Render the /new-/clear-style confirmation panel.

name: _get_approval_display_fragments
doc:
Render the dangerous-command approval panel.

Layout priority: title + command + choices must always render, even in a short terminal
or with a long multi-paragraph description. The description sits at the bottom
and is truncated to the remaining row budget, so HSplit never clips approve/deny off-screen.

name: _get_tui_prompt_symbols
doc:
Return ``(normal_prompt, state_suffix)`` for the active skin.

``state_suffix`` is what special states (sudo/secret/approval/agent) render after their
leading icon. A non-default profile name is prepended (``coder ❯``).

name: _audio_level_bar
doc: One-char audio level indicator from the recorder's current RMS.

name: _get_tui_prompt_fragments
doc: prompt_toolkit fragments for the current interactive state.

name: _get_tui_prompt_text
doc: Visible prompt text for width calculations.

name: _build_tui_style_dict
doc:
Layer the active skin's prompt_toolkit colors over the base TUI style.

On a light terminal, hex tokens in each style string are rewritten through the light-mode
remap so the chrome stays readable on cream Terminal.app backgrounds. CRITICAL: a style
that paints its own ``bg:`` (status bar, completion menu) is left alone — its fg was tuned
for that dark bg and remapping would give dark-on-dark; the terminal's mode is irrelevant.

name: _apply_tui_skin_style
doc: Refresh prompt_toolkit styling for a running interactive TUI.

name: _get_extra_tui_widgets
doc: Extension hook: wrapper CLIs return widgets inserted between the spacer and status bar.

name: _register_extra_tui_keybindings
doc: Extension hook: wrapper CLIs add bindings to ``kb`` (``input_area`` is the main TextArea).

name: _build_tui_layout_children
arguments: self, *, sudo_widget, secret_widget, connection_widget=None, approval_widget, slash_confirm_widget=None, clarify_widget, model_picker_widget=None, command_palette_widget=None, spinner_widget=None, spacer, status_bar, input_rule_top, image_bar, input_area, input_rule_bot, voice_status_bar, completions_menu
doc:
Ordered children of the root ``HSplit``; override only for full control over ordering
(wrappers normally override ``_get_extra_tui_widgets`` instead).

name: _get_clarify_display_fragments
doc:
Batch (multi-question) clarify panel: "N questions" header, one status line per question
(✓ answered → answer / ▸ active / · pending), and the active question's numbered choices
(+ Other) expanded beneath its status line.

name: _render_scroll_list_panel
arguments: self, state, title, hint, labels, *, min_width, max_width, indent
doc:
Titled panel with a hint row and a scrolling selectable list (model picker, palette).

The panel renders into a Window with no max height, so the visible slice is limited to
the terminal rows or the bottom border and trailing items get clipped on long lists
(e.g. Ollama Cloud's 36+ models). ``state["_scroll_offset"]`` is updated in place.

name: _render_sudo_style_panel
arguments: self, title: str, body_lines: list[str], row_styles: list[str] | None=None
doc: Bordered ``sudo-*`` panel: blank, each body line, blank, body-final line, blank.

name: _tui_handle_voice_record
doc:
Toggle voice recording when voice mode is active.

Runs on prompt_toolkit's event-loop thread: any blocking call here (locks, sd.wait,
disk I/O) freezes the whole UI, so all heavy work goes to daemon threads.

name: _tui_cancel_voice_recording
doc: Cancel an active recording; True when one was cancelled (caller stops there).

name: _tui_cancel_foreground_ui
doc: Close the first active foreground UI (slash-confirm / picker / palette); True if any.

name: _tui_clear_blocking_overlays
doc:
Clear every agent-blocking overlay (approval/clarify/sudo/secret) in one shot.

Callers must NOT return on True alone: they fall through so a stale/orphaned overlay
(left by an earlier interrupt) can't swallow the press before the agent-interrupt
branch, leaving the chat frozen (#14026).

name: _tui_clear_or_exit
doc: Clear text/images like bash; exit when everything is already empty.

name: _tui_handle_ctrl_c
doc:
Ctrl+C priority: cancel voice recording → cancel foreground UI/overlay prompt or the wait for a
command on its own gateway socket (a plugin command, /cron) → clear a typed draft, even mid-run (a correction must never kill the turn)
→ interrupt the running agent → force exit (second press within 2s) → when idle and empty, exit.

name: _tui_handle_ctrl_q
doc: Ctrl+Q: like Ctrl+C minus the double-press force exit (and it leaves the palette).

name: _tui_restore_stash_payload
doc: Put a popped (text, images) payload back into the composer.

name: _tui_handle_stash_panel_delete
doc: D in the browse panel discards the highlighted draft.

name: _tui_handle_tab
doc:
Tab: accept the open completion, else the ghost auto-suggestion, else start completions.

After accepting a provider like 'anthropic:' the menu closes and complete_while_typing
doesn't fire (no keystroke); re-triggering here makes stage-2 models appear immediately.

name: _tui_handle_double_escape
doc:
Double ESC discards the draft and attached images (Claude Code / Gemini CLI gesture).

Works while the agent streams — the gap Ctrl+C leaves (it interrupts the turn and only
clears the draft when idle). The draft is appended to history first so Up recalls it,
which is what makes a reflex key safe. Single ESC is the Alt-sequence prefix
(escape+enter/g/v) so the escape-timeout keeps those distinct; modal prompts bind ESC
eagerly and are excluded so cancel still wins.

name: _tui_handle_ignored_terminal_sequence
doc:
Consume parser-level ignored terminal sequences before self-insert.

hermes_cli.pt_input_extras registers focus reports (CSI I / CSI O) as Keys.Ignore at the
VT100 parser; without this no-op binding the default self-insert would still land the
bytes in the buffer. Focus-in additionally schedules a rate-limited full repaint: while
hidden, the emulator may have coalesced output or repainted, so prompt_toolkit's
incremental diff would stack a fresh prompt chrome on the stale one (#60920, #25337).

name: _tui_handle_escape_modal
doc: ESC cancels active secret/sudo/connection/slash-confirm prompts.

name: _tui_handle_ctrl_z
doc: Ctrl+Z suspends the process (Unix only).

name: _tui_handle_ctrl_d
doc:
Ctrl+D deletes under the cursor (readline); exits only on empty input (pending images count),
like bash/zsh. Mid-turn it detaches: the gateway finishes the turn, Ctrl+C stops it (LC-6b).

name: _tui_recall_without_recollapse
doc:
Run a history move with paste-collapse suppressed.

Recalled history can hold the full text of a paste collapsed at submit time; loading it
back looks like a fresh large paste to ``_on_text_changed``. If the move didn't change the
text (plain cursor movement) the flag is cleared so a later real paste still collapses.

name: _tui_handle_alt_v
doc:
Alt+V pastes an image from the clipboard. Alt combos pass through every terminal
(ESC + key), unlike Ctrl+V which terminals intercept — reliable on WSL2/VSCode/SSH.
Silent when no image (avoid noise on accidental press).

name: _tui_handle_ctrl_v
doc:
Image paste for terminals without bracketed paste: GNOME Terminal/Konsole send raw
0x16. Terminals that intercept Ctrl+V (macOS Terminal, iTerm2, VSCode, Windows Terminal)
fire the bracketed-paste handler instead and never reach this.

name: _tui_handle_ctrl_l
doc:
Ctrl+L forces a clean repaint after terminal buffer drift (tmux/cmux tab switches,
``clear`` from a subshell, SSH restores) that prompt_toolkit can't detect.

name: _tui_insert_newline
doc:
Newline for multi-line input (Alt+Enter; Ctrl+J/Ctrl+Enter with multiline shortcuts).
Windows Terminal intercepts Alt+Enter (fullscreen) and delivers Ctrl+Enter as c-j.

name: _tui_handle_open_in_editor
doc: Ctrl+G (or Alt+G in VSCode/Cursor) opens the draft in an external editor.

name: _tui_set_filter
doc: Replace a picker/palette filter and rewind the selection + viewport.

name: _tui_model_picker_escape
doc: ESC clears an active filter first, else steps back from the effort stage, else closes.

name: _tui_handle_enter
doc:
Enter: submit input.

Modal overlays (sudo/secret/approval/slash-confirm/picker/clarify) are answered first via
``_tui_enter_overlay``. Otherwise: agent running → busy_input_mode routing (steer /
redirect / interrupt queue / next-turn queue); idle → ``_pending_input``. Slash and bang
commands always take the local-dispatch path (never steer/interrupt text to the model).

name: _tui_enter_inline_command
arguments: self, event, text: str, has_images: bool
doc:
Run /model, /steer, /bg, /btw directly on the UI thread; True when handled.

/model needs the prompt_toolkit terminal-handoff helpers of the interactive pickers.
/steer, /bg and /btw while the agent runs must not queue through _pending_input: the
process loop is blocked inside self.chat(), so they would only run after the foreground
turn — turning /steer into a next-turn message (defeating mid-run injection, #34569) and
starting the /bg side task after the turn it should run alongside (#75221). The
foreground turn is left alone: no interrupt, no steer. agent.steer() is thread-safe.

Every branch invalidates after reset: process_command() prints through patch_stdout
and never invalidates the app, so the just-cleared input area would keep showing the
submitted text (looking unsent, inviting a re-submit) until some unrelated redraw.

name: _tui_enter_while_busy
arguments: self, text: str, images: list, payload, mode: str | None=None
doc:
Route a submission typed while the agent runs, per ``busy_input_mode``.

steer → agent.steer(text) mid-run (images can't ride along; a missing/rejecting steer() falls back
to queue). interrupt → agent.redirect() when supported, else the legacy interrupt queue. queue →
next turn: text-only on the gateway's session is a ``/queue`` FIFO admission (#134889 N5).

name: _tui_enter_overlay
doc: Enter while a modal overlay is up: submit it. True when handled.

name: _tui_enter_clarify_freetext
doc: Clarify "Other": lock the typed answer; empty input skips the question.

name: _tui_enter_clarify_choice
doc:
Clarify choice mode: lock the active question's answer and advance to the next
unanswered.

name: _tui_collapse_paste
arguments: self, text: str, line_count: int, *, fallback: bool
doc: Save a large paste under ~/.hermes/pastes and return the placeholder for the buffer.

name: _tui_paste_over_threshold
arguments: self, text: str, line_count: int, threshold_key: str

name: _tui_handle_paste
_tui_on_text_changed
doc:
Fallback paste collapse for terminals without bracketed paste.

Either heuristic triggers: many characters added in one event (paste delivered in one
tick), or the newline count jumped by 4+ (terminals that feed characters individually
but batch newlines; Alt+Enter adds 1 newline per event so never trips it).

name: _tui_handle_prompt_stash
doc:
Ctrl+S: composer has content → push onto the stash and clear; empty + one stashed →
pop it back; empty + several → open the browse panel; panel open → close it.

A stack (not a single slot) is what makes repeated Ctrl+S safe: a second stash never
silently overwrites the first, both stay reachable in the panel.

name: _tui_handle_stash_panel_restore
doc: Enter in the browse panel restores the highlighted draft.

name: _tui_history_up
doc: Up: browse history when on the first line, else move the cursor up.

name: _tui_init_run_state
doc: Reset the per-run REPL state (queues, modal states, voice state, config watcher).

name: _tui_build_key_bindings
doc:
Build the prompt_toolkit KeyBindings for the REPL input area.

Registration ORDER matters: for the same key, prompt_toolkit picks the last matching
binding, so the generic handlers (Tab, history Up/Down) are registered before or after
their filtered modal overrides deliberately.

name: _tui_bind_overlay_navigation
doc: Clarify / approval / slash-confirm / model picker / command palette navigation keys.

name: _tui_voice_record_key_sequence
doc:
Resolve the push-to-talk key (voice.record_key, default Ctrl+B) to a prompt_toolkit
key sequence and cache the UI label.

Config spellings (ctrl/control/alt/option/opt) are normalized to c-x / a-x so the same
value binds identically in TUI and CLI. super/win/windows silently fall back to the
default (prompt_toolkit has no super modifier) — warn so users notice the split. The
label cache uses the same ``_raw_key`` that drives the binding, so status/placeholder/
recording-hint renders can never drift from the live key even if the config is edited
mid-session.

name: _tui_overlay_widget
doc: Wrapped, auto-sized panel shown while ``self.<state_attr>`` is not None.

name: _tui_build_layout
doc: Build the TUI widgets, Layout and Style; registers wrapper keybindings on ``kb``.

name: _tui_build_input_area
doc:
Multi-line prompt TextArea with slash completion, paste-collapse tracking and
placeholder/password processors.

name: _tui_set_base_style
doc: Populate ``self._tui_style_base`` (skin-aware defaults the style dict is built from).

name: _state_fragment
arguments: style: str, icon: str, extra: str=''

name: _tui_process_loop
doc: REPL worker thread: drain ``_pending_input``, run idle housekeeping, dispatch each input.

name: _tui_hold_step
doc:
One step of holding a local input behind this viewer's own ``/queue`` admission (#134889 N5):
``(hold or None, input to run now or None)``. A turn the owner runs now goes first; the held
input runs once that admission was taken, left the queue, or the bounded wait ran out.

name: _tui_idle_tick
doc: Idle housekeeping between inputs (agent not running).

name: _tui_dock_drop_dequeued
doc:
Re-read the live-work dock once an input has left ``_pending_input``.

The spinner thread polls the dock once a second, so without this the prompt a turn just took
(a seeded ``-q`` prompt above all) stays listed as queued while the turn starts. If the reply
prints in that window the dock shrinks only after it, leaving blank rows under the prompt.
The turn's own invalidate repaints the refreshed rows.

name: _tui_process_one_input
doc: Route one submitted input: file drop, /resume pick, ! shell, slash command, or a chat turn.

name: _tui_run_slash_input
doc: Dispatch a slash command. Returns the pending agent seed to run as a chat turn, else None.

name: _tui_after_turn
doc: Post-turn bookkeeping after chat() returns (normal, error, or interrupt).

name: _tui_signal_handler
doc:
SIGHUP/SIGTERM -> graceful shutdown.

The agent is hard-interrupted first so its daemon thread can kill the tool's
setsid subprocess group before the main thread unwinds (else an orphan child).
``logger.debug`` is guarded: logging is not reentrant-safe and a shutdown race
can raise ``KeyError`` inside the handler, bypassing prompt_toolkit's unwind.

name: _show_startup_browser_notice
doc:
Main's ``_show_browser_backend_notice``; on a gateway session the gateway computed the notice
(and its once-per-24h stamp) with the session's tools, so it is printed from the snapshot.

name: _tui_print_startup
doc: Startup output: light-mode probe, banner, advisories, resume/welcome lines, tips.

name: _tui_startup_prewarm_and_warnings
doc: Idle-window prewarms (picker cache, agent runtime imports) plus the redaction-off and OpenClaw-residue banners.

name: _tui_startup_background_maintenance
doc:
Best-effort startup passes: curator skill maintenance, personal + org skill sync.

Off the main thread: the curator's deterministic pass snapshots and prunes the whole
skills tree (a due weekly pass held the prompt for 6 minutes on a large library), and
the sync pulls can hit the network. The REPL must never wait on housekeeping.

name: _tui_build_application
doc: Construct the prompt_toolkit Application for the REPL.

name: _tui_install_signal_handlers
doc: SIGTERM/SIGHUP -> graceful shutdown; Windows absorbs SIGINT (see body).

name: _tui_stdin_usable
doc: Validate fd 0 before prompt_toolkit starts; on macOS fall back to a select() loop when kqueue can't watch it (uv-managed Python).

name: _closing_session_id
doc:
The session quit closes: the agent's, or (gateway) the session opened at the banner before
any agent was built. Main created its row lazily at the first turn, so with no agent it had none.

name: _tui_shutdown
doc: Teardown after the app exits: interrupt agent, stop voice/pet, persist + close session, cleanup, exit summary.

name: _wrap_rows
doc: ``(index, wrapped_line)`` pairs so selected styling can be re-applied per row.

name: _prefix_wrapped_rows
doc:
Wrap ``label``, then prefix the rows with ``first_prefix`` / ``indent``.

The prefix is applied *after* wrapping on purpose. Folding it into the
string handed to the wrapper charges those columns against the label's own
width budget — so a selected row wraps one line early and strands the ``❯``
cursor on a row of its own — and whitespace-trimming wrappers drop the
leading indent entirely, leaving long unselected labels flush against the
panel border, out of alignment with every other row.

name: unknown_command_lines
doc:
(lead line, pointer line) for a slash token with no handler.

``known`` holds names WITH the leading slash (``hermes_cli.commands.COMMANDS`` keys plus skill
commands). A close match (typo) becomes ``Did you mean /model?``; prefix expansion already ran
before this, so only fuzzy matches are considered here.

name: _config_section
doc:
``load_config()[name]`` coerced to a dict.

Shape-safe: a hand-edited ``voice: true`` / ``voice: cmd+b`` leaves the section as a
non-dict; return {} so callers fall back to documented defaults instead of crashing on
``.get()``. Config load failures also yield {}.

name: _numeric_or
doc:
``value`` if it is a real int/float, else ``default``.

``bool`` is excluded — it subclasses int, so a hand-edited ``silence_threshold: true``
would otherwise be forwarded as ``1`` instead of falling back.

name: _voice_invalidate
doc: Repaint the TUI (audio level indicator / status) when the app is live.

name: _voice_start_recording
doc: Start capturing audio from the microphone.

name: _voice_beep
doc: Play a record start/stop beep when enabled; never raises.

name: _voice_stt_model
doc:
STT model override from config, or None for the provider default.

For the local provider, prefer stt.local.model (default ``base``) so the CLI passes
a real model name into the local STT backend.

name: _voice_stt_provider
doc: Configured STT provider name (lowercased), or empty string.

name: _voice_restart_recording_async
doc: Restart continuous-mode recording off-thread (start() can block).

name: _voice_on_live_partial
doc: Live STT partial (``stt.streaming``): shown in the input placeholder while recording.

name: _voice_stop_and_transcribe
doc: Stop recording, transcribe via STT, and queue the transcript as input.

name: _voice_speak_response_async
doc: Schedule TTS and mark it pending before continuous recording can restart.

name: _voice_speak_response
doc: Speak the agent's response aloud using TTS (runs in background thread).
