arguments: force: bool=False, exclude_pids: set | None=None, all_profiles: bool=False
doc:
Kill running gateway processes (force-kill if ``force``); ``exclude_pids`` skips e.g. just-
restarted service PIDs. Returns count killed. ``all_profiles`` sweeps only gateways whose live home
is this install's root or one of its profiles: the process scan is account-wide, and a scratch-home
``gateway stop --all`` would otherwise SIGTERM the account's real gateway.

name: _reaper_candidate_is_supervisor_owned
doc:
True when ``pid``'s parent chain reaches ``services.exe`` (Task Scheduler-owned gateway). Windows-only
reaper backstop: ``_get_service_pids()`` is empty there, so a Scheduled-Task gateway with a stale
pidfile would look like an orphan. Fail-open once the Task's bootstrap parent exits. Not applied
on POSIX, where everything descends from PID 1 and would look supervised.

See #83683, #86098.
This check is deliberately NOT applied on POSIX: there, every process has PID 1 (launchd / init /
systemd) in its ancestry — and a genuine orphan is *reparented directly to PID 1* — so supervisor-name
ancestry carries zero signal and would spare every orphan the reaper exists to kill (#51325, 75936).
POSIX supervised gateways are already covered pidfile- independently by the ``_get_service_pids()``
exclusion.

name: _reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans
doc:
Kill no-supervisor gateway orphans the pidfile/runtime record can't see. On WSL/no-systemd hosts
the restart fallback runs the gateway in-process under a ``gateway restart`` argv; a stale pidfile
then lets a live orphan keep the webhook port while a restart stacks a duplicate. No-op where a
supervisor exists (there ``gateway restart`` is a transient command). ``extra_exclude``: already killed.

``min_age_s`` spares a candidate younger than the grace: a gateway claims
``gateway.pid``/``gateway.lock`` only after imports + runner setup, so a process
that a previous Desktop generation (or a concurrent ``gateway start``) just launched
is scan-visible but not yet record-visible, and the argv sweep cannot tell it from
a corpse. Reaping it writes a planned-stop marker it consumes seconds later — a clean
exit 0 with no supervisor to revive it (#122533). The Desktop boot sweep passes a
grace; stop/restart keep reaping at once.

name: _reaper_exclusion_pids
doc: PIDs the orphan reaper must never kill: self, caller extras, service-managed, recorded.

name: _await_gateway_exit
arguments: pids, *, pid_exists, sleep=None, grace_s: float=_ORPHAN_EXIT_GRACE_SECONDS, poll_s: float=_ORPHAN_EXIT_POLL_SECONDS
doc: Poll up to *grace_s* for *pids* to exit; return survivors. ``pid_exists``/``sleep`` injectable for tests.

name: _force_kill_survivors
doc:
SIGKILL processes that outlasted the grace period, loudly — a force-kill can tear the store, so
it must leave a trace.

name: stop_profile_gateway
doc:
Stop only this profile's gateway via its PID file; True if a process was stopped. Without a
supervisor the pidfile can be stale while a live orphan holds the webhook port, so fall back to
the orphan-aware scan rather than stacking a duplicate.

Even when the pid file is valid and points to the current gateway, older orphans may linger from prior
restarts that overwrote the pid file before the old process exited. After killing the recorded PID, also
sweep for any remaining orphans so each restart produces at most one live gateway (#75936).

name: _wsl_systemd_operational
doc: WSL2 with ``systemd=true`` in wsl.conf has working systemd; WSL1/without it does not.

name: _systemd_operational
doc: Return True when the requested systemd scope is usable.

name: _gw_windows
doc: Lazily import :mod:`hermes_cli.gateway_windows` (Windows-only service backend).

name: _windows_scheduled_task_state
doc:
Locale-independent Task Scheduler state, or None on failure.

Query the COM API directly: Get-ScheduledTask auto-loads the CIM module,
which can stall desktop backend startup for the entire ten-second timeout.
Keep the existing supervisor semantics (Ready and Queued count as owned).

name: _windows_scheduled_task_supervises
doc:
True when Task Scheduler still owns this profile's gateway (Ready counts: the task is Ready, not
Running, after bootstrap exits). Any failure returns False so callers fall back to pidfile / parent-chain.

Used to treat Task Scheduler as a gateway supervisor on Windows: the orphan-reap sweep must not kill a
gateway that a scheduled task launched and left detached. After the bootstrap exits the task is Ready,
not Running; a Running-only check still writes the planned-stop marker, the gateway exits cleanly with
code 0, and the scheduler never restarts it — silently killing A2A/messaging on every desktop-app launch
(#86098, #87001).

name: _stdin_is_tty
doc: ``sys.stdin.isatty()``; None when stdin is closed/invalid.

name: _windows_gateway_should_absorb_console_controls
doc:
True for detached Windows gateway runs that should ignore Ctrl+C (``HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED=1``
or no interactive stdin); foreground runs stay interruptible.

name: _windows_console_window_attached
doc: Return whether Windows assigned this process a console window.

name: _windows_gateway_breakaway_state
doc: Consume private spawn metadata without guessing for older launchers.

name: _profile_name_from_home
doc: Profile name when ``home`` is ``<default>/profiles/<name>`` with a service-safe name, else None.

name: _native_service_homes
doc:
The account's native default home plus, when root under sudo, the invoking user's (see
``_profile_suffix`` for why sudo matters). The ACCOUNT home, not the process HOME: the unit dir
follows the account (``user_systemd_unit_dir``), so a scratch ``HOME`` that called its own
``.hermes`` native resolved the bare name onto the account's real unit.

name: _bare_unit_pinned_home
doc:
Resolved ``HERMES_HOME`` pinned by an installed ``hermes-gateway.service``, or None. The unit is the
one naming basis that holds still across the sudo mid-command switch (see ``_profile_suffix``) and it
covers every elevated identity — ``sudo -i`` and cron included, where SUDO_USER is absent.

Root reads the system unit; an unprivileged process reads only its own user unit, never the system
one — a bare system unit pinning ``profiles/<name>`` would otherwise alias that profile onto the
user's default unit. The user unit matters for a custom root: the ``hermes-gateway-<hash>`` naming
(#105525) left a bare user unit installed before it pinning that same root, so lifecycle commands
saw "no unit", ``gateway restart`` fell through to a foreground run, and the still-enabled legacy
unit's ``Restart=always`` looped on the instance lock (#109476). A unit pinning THIS home is this
home's service, whatever it is named.

Linux-gated: a systemd unit is not an identity authority for launchd labels, Windows scheduled tasks,
or s6 slots, which share ``_profile_suffix()``. ``is_linux()`` is a plain ``sys.platform`` test;
``supports_systemd_services()`` would be wrong here, since it can shell out to ``systemctl
is-system-running`` on WSL/containers and this runs on every name resolution.

name: _home_owns_bare_service_name
doc: True for the resolved ``home`` that owns the bare service name (see ``_profile_suffix``).

name: _profile_suffix
doc:
Service-name suffix for HERMES_HOME: "" for a home that owns the bare name, the profile name for
``<root>/profiles/<name>``, else a short hash of the path.

Bare-name owners: this process's platform-native default (``~/.hermes``), under sudo the invoking
user's native default, and the home pinned by an installed ``hermes-gateway.service``. Under sudo the
naming basis moves MID-COMMAND — sudo strips HERMES_HOME and sets HOME=/root, then
``_sync_hermes_home_from_systemd_unit()`` adopts the unit's own HERMES_HOME into ``os.environ`` — so a
basis derived from the process alone names one unit before the adoption and another after it. The
unit-pinned check must precede the profile branch: ``sudo hermes gateway install --system`` resolves
the BARE name from root's default, then pins the invoking user's remapped home, so the bare unit
legitimately carries a ``<root>/profiles/<name>`` home.

The bare name is deliberately NOT tied to ``get_default_hermes_root()``: that helper treats any
HERMES_HOME outside ``~/.hermes`` (Docker ``/opt/data``, a temp dir) as "the root itself", which let a
temp-home harness resolve to the default profile's ``hermes-gateway`` unit and uninstall the
production gateway. Service names are host-wide identities; a home with no installed bare unit and
no native default keeps its own suffix.

name: _current_profile_name
doc:
Profile id relative to the profile ROOT: ``default`` for the root itself (Docker's ``/opt/data``
included), ``<name>`` for ``<root>/profiles/<name>``, else the service hash. s6 slots and the
multiplexer ask which PROFILE this is; ``_profile_suffix()`` answers which HOST SERVICE this is.

name: _profile_arg
arguments: hermes_home: str | None=None, default_root: str | Path | None=None
doc:
``--profile <name>`` for ``<root>/profiles/<name>``, else "". *hermes_home*/*default_root* let a
sudo/root process generate a unit for another user (the defaults would refer to root).

name: get_service_name
doc:
Systemd service name: ``hermes-gateway`` for default HERMES_HOME, ``hermes-gateway-<profile>``
or ``-<hash>`` otherwise.

name: user_systemd_unit_dir
doc:
``$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user`` (``~/.config`` only as the spec's default), ``~`` being the
ACCOUNT home, not the process HOME.

Hardcoding ``~/.config`` made every unit probe silently false-negative on a host that moves
XDG_CONFIG_HOME — doctor then reported no gateway unit while systemd was running ours. And
``Path.home()`` trusts a process HOME that profile isolation may point at ``{HERMES_HOME}/home`` — the
ACTIVE profile's, not even the one selected with ``-p`` — so ``gateway install`` wrote the unit under
``~/.hermes/profiles/<active>/home/.config/systemd/user/`` where ``systemctl --user`` never looks and
``enable`` failed with "Unit ... does not exist" (#98699). ``systemctl --user`` targets the login
user's session, so the unit dir follows the account home like ``get_launchd_plist_path()`` does.

name: _user_runtime_dir
doc: ``$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`` or ``/run/user/<uid>`` (regardless of existence).

name: _user_dbus_socket_path
doc: Return the expected per-user D-Bus socket path (regardless of existence).

name: _user_systemd_private_socket_path
doc: Return the per-user systemd private socket path (regardless of existence).

name: _path_exists_safe
doc:
``Path.exists()`` treating an inaccessible path as absent: a leaked ``XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`` from
another user (``/run/user/0`` is 0700) would otherwise crash the preflight with EACCES.

``Path.exists()`` only swallows a subset of ``OSError`` (ENOENT/ENOTDIR/ EBADF/ELOOP); ``EACCES`` still
propagates. When ``XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`` leaks from another user — the classic ``su``/``sudo -u`` from a
root shell case, where ``/run/user/0`` is ``0700 root:root`` — stat-ing a socket underneath it raises
``PermissionError`` that escapes the systemd preflight as a raw traceback (#86558). An unreadable path
is, for our purposes, not reachable.

name: _runtime_dir_is_ours
doc: True when *runtime_dir* exists and is owned by our uid (a leaked foreign XDG_RUNTIME_DIR must not be trusted).

name: _user_systemd_socket_ready
doc:
True when the user D-Bus socket OR the per-user systemd private socket exists (some distros
expose only the latter and ``systemctl --user`` still works). Inaccessible counts as not-ready.

name: _ensure_user_systemd_env
doc:
Set XDG_RUNTIME_DIR / DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS so ``systemctl --user`` works on headless (SSH)
hosts; an XDG_RUNTIME_DIR leaked from another user is replaced with our own ``/run/user/{uid}``.

An ``XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`` that leaked from another user (``su``/``sudo -u`` from root, where the env still
points at ``/run/user/0``) is dropped in favour of our own ``/run/user/{uid}`` so ``systemctl --user``
targets the right instance instead of an unreadable foreign socket (#86558).

name: _wait_for_user_dbus_socket
doc: Poll up to ``timeout`` s for a user systemd control socket (user@.service takes a moment after enable-linger).

name: _wait_for_target_user_bus
doc:
Poll for ``/run/user/<uid>/bus`` of ANOTHER account (the system unit's ``User=`` while root installs).
Only the D-Bus socket counts — ``systemd/private`` alone is enough for ``systemctl --user`` but not for
the ``systemd-run --user`` that restart-safe workers need. Never adopts anything into our env.

name: _loginctl_enable_linger
doc: ``loginctl enable-linger <username>`` (check=False, 30s); exceptions propagate to the caller.

name: _completed_process_detail
doc: stderr, else stdout, else ``exit <rc>`` — stripped.

name: _preflight_user_systemd
doc:
Ensure ``systemctl --user`` can reach user-scope systemd; raise UserSystemdUnavailableError otherwise.
No-op when a control socket exists; else wait briefly if linger is on, or (``auto_enable_linger``)
try ``loginctl enable-linger`` (non-root works when polkit permits).

name: _raise_user_systemd_unavailable
arguments: username: str, *, reason: str, fix_hint: str
doc: Build a user-facing error message and raise UserSystemdUnavailableError.

name: _run_systemctl
doc:
Run systemctl; raise RuntimeError (not raw FileNotFoundError) if missing, for callers bypassing
``supports_systemd_services()``.

name: _legacy_unit_search_paths
doc: ``[(is_system, base_dir), ...]`` to scan for legacy units; factored out so tests can monkeypatch.

name: _find_legacy_hermes_units
doc:
``[(unit_name, unit_path, is_system)]`` for legacy gateway units (e.g. ``hermes.service``), which
fight the current unit for the bot token (SIGTERM flap loop). Explicit name allowlist + ExecStart
marker check so profile/third-party units never match; no mutation.

Detects unit files installed by older Hermes versions that used a different service name (e.g. When both
a legacy unit and the current ``hermes-gateway.service`` are active, they fight over the same bot token
— the PR #5646 signal-recovery change turns this into a 30-second SIGTERM flap loop.

name: has_legacy_hermes_units
doc: Return True when any legacy Hermes gateway unit files exist.

name: print_legacy_unit_warning
doc: Warn about installed legacy gateway units; prints nothing when there are none.

name: remove_legacy_hermes_units
doc:
Stop, disable, and remove legacy gateway units. ``interactive=False`` skips the prompt; ``dry_run``
only lists. Returns ``(removed_count, remaining_paths)`` (remaining: e.g. system-scope when not root).

name: refuses_container_user_scope_install
doc:
True (after printing the guidance) when a fresh USER-scope unit was requested inside a container.

A systemd container passes ``supports_systemd_services()`` on purpose so ``--system`` keeps working,
but a user unit there is not container-scoped: the unit file and its ``default.target.wants`` symlink
land in ``~/.config/systemd/user`` — commonly the host's own home bind-mounted in — so the host's
``systemd --user`` enables it too and a second gateway polls the same bot token outside the container.
Callers decide between ``sys.exit(1)`` (CLI) and skipping the install (wizard).

name: get_systemd_linger_status
doc:
Linger status for *username* or the current user when omitted.

System-scope gateway installation runs as root but the service runs as a
configured target user, so querying the caller would validate the wrong
user manager.

name: get_launchd_plist_path
doc: ``~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway[-<profile>].plist`` under the real account home.

name: launchd_gateway_labels_for_install
doc:
Launchd labels for every profile of THIS install (root first, then profiles by name). Derived from
the profile layout, NOT by globbing ``~/Library/LaunchAgents``, so a sandboxed HERMES_HOME never
restarts another install's fleet. Names that can't map to a suffix are skipped.

name: legacy_launchd_labels_for_install
doc:
Launchd labels of THIS install that the profile-layout derivation can't map (#115254).

A unit whose label predates the profile-name suffix scheme (``ai.hermes.gateway-<8hex>`` from the
historical hash suffix) is invisible to ``launchd_gateway_labels_for_install()`` and therefore to
the update restart pass. This reads the account's LaunchAgents and credits a plist only when its
pinned ``HERMES_HOME`` is this install's root or one of its ``profiles/<name>`` homes — ownership
judged from the plist's content, never from label shape or directory membership — so the
derivation's boundary holds: a sandboxed HERMES_HOME (tests, side-by-side installs) never
enumerates, let alone restarts, another install's fleet (#41403).

name: _build_user_local_paths
doc: Return user-local bin dirs that exist and aren't already in *path_entries*.

name: _build_wsl_interop_paths
doc:
WSL Windows-interop PATH entries for generated units: systemd services don't inherit the
Windows PATH (``/mnt/c/WINDOWS/System32``…), so ``powershell.exe``/``cmd.exe`` break unless persisted.

Only the which()-resolved tool dirs and the hardcoded System32 family belong here. The
shell PATH is deliberately NOT scraped: WSL appends every Windows PATH entry (Desktop app,
git, node dirs under ``/mnt/``) ahead of the interop defaults, and persisting those into the
unit makes the gateway open 9p (Plan 9 interop) connections to each of them at start — enough
to exhaust the 9p server connection limit (#73163). Interop tools don't need them.

name: _remap_path_for_user
doc:
Swap the ``Path.home()`` prefix of *path* for *target_home_dir*; other paths return unchanged.
Intentionally does NOT resolve symlinks.

name: _systemd_env_line
doc:
One ``Environment="NAME=value"`` line: ``\`` and ``"`` escaped for systemd's quoting, ``%``
doubled so specifier expansion leaves the value alone.

name: _installed_unit_ld_library_path
doc: ``LD_LIBRARY_PATH`` baked into the installed unit; ``""`` when absent.

name: _ld_library_path_line
doc:
Carry the installer's LD_LIBRARY_PATH into the unit (glibc reads it only at process start, so
~/.hermes/.env is too late for CUDA libs — #14613); system units remap caller-home components.

The installed unit is the fallback source: the unit is regenerated and compared on every
start/restart/status, and a shell without the export (ssh, cron, ``sudo`` strips ``LD_*``)
must not be able to "repair" the line away.

name: _hermes_home_for_target_user
doc:
Remap the current HERMES_HOME (root's, under sudo) to the target user's equivalent:
``/root/.hermes[/profiles/x]`` → ``/home/alice/.hermes[/profiles/x]``; custom paths kept as-is.

name: _build_service_path_dirs
doc: Build PATH directory list for service units, excluding non-existent dirs.

name: _stable_service_working_dir
doc:
WorkingDirectory that won't disappear under systemd (HERMES_HOME, else PROJECT_ROOT). cwd is
irrelevant to ``-m`` resolution, and a pinned transient checkout rots: systemd fails at CHDIR
(status=200) before Python loads, so the unit self-heal never runs and Restart=always crash-loops.

name: _systemd_watchdog_seconds
doc: Resolve the managed-overlay-aware watchdog setting for a service home.

name: _pm_managed_node_dirs
doc:
Node dirs pm's installed-state records under *home*'s store, resolved
via ``Facts.env_for`` (``{{store}}`` templates against the store beside
the recorded facts). Only dirs present on disk count; a record whose
store dirs are gone vouches for nothing.

name: _append_node_dir_for_service
doc:
Append the Node dir a service unit should use.

PM's installed-state is the owner: facts.json under the target hermes
home's store records node/npm PATH entries, and those dirs — resolved via
Facts.env_for — are used verbatim. With managed Node recorded, consulting
the invoker's PATH would make a system unit depend on who ran sudo, so
lookup stops there. The legacy ``<hermes>/node`` tree is the only fallback,
for installs pm never recorded; the invoker's PATH node never is.

name: _systemd_command
doc: Quote argv for systemd, including its non-shell specifier expansion.

name: _prepare_service_launcher
doc: Publish the source command before a service definition references it.

name: _strip_optional_systemd_directives
doc: Remove systemd directives that older hosts silently drop.

name: _normalize_launchd_plist_for_comparison
doc:
Normalize plist text for staleness checks, ignoring the PATH payload: the generated PATH is
captured from the invoking shell and varies across shells.

name: _retire_hermes_replace_dropin
doc: Remove only the legacy ``--replace`` drop-in written by Hermes.

name: refresh_systemd_unit_if_needed
doc: Rewrite the installed systemd unit when the generated definition has changed.

name: _print_linger_enable_warning
arguments: username: str, detail: str | None=None, *, system: bool=False

name: _ensure_linger_enabled
doc:
Enable linger for *username* (default: the current user) when possible.

A user unit needs linger so the gateway survives logout. A system unit (``system=True``) needs
it for its ``User=`` so ``user@<uid>.service`` provides the D-Bus that ``systemd-run --user
--scope`` — every restart-safe cron/Kanban worker — connects to (#104893). Returns True only
when linger was enabled by this call.

name: _ensure_system_service_linger
doc:
Enable linger for the installed unit's ``User=`` (root included: restart-safe workers always cross
``systemd-run --user``, so a root gateway needs ``user@0.service`` just the same).

After a fresh enable, wait for the TARGET user's bus: logind starts ``user@<uid>.service``
asynchronously and ``--start-now`` boots the gateway immediately. A gateway that was already running
keeps its bus-less environment and ``systemctl start`` on an active unit is a no-op — say so rather
than let the repair silently not take.

name: _system_scope_wizard_would_need_root
doc:
True when the wizard would trigger a system-scope operation as non-root — mirrors
``_select_systemd_scope`` so the dead-end is detected BEFORE prompting.

name: _print_system_scope_remediation
doc: Print remediation when the wizard skips a system-scope action because the user isn't root.

name: _get_restart_drain_timeout
doc: Return the configured gateway restart drain timeout in seconds.

name: _agent_timeout_setting
doc: ``parse(env)`` when the env var is non-empty, else ``parse(agent.<key>)`` (None if unset).

name: _get_cron_drain_timeout
doc:
Return the configured cron and api_server (/v1) drain floor in seconds.

See #82161.

name: _get_restart_exit_wait_budget
doc: CLI wait for gateway exit after SIGUSR1 / self-restart (#77184).

name: systemd_install
arguments: force: bool=False, system: bool=False, run_as_user: str | None=None, enable_on_startup: bool=True, non_interactive: bool=False, force_unit_path: bool=False

name: _systemd_scope_preamble
arguments: action: str, system: bool, *, require_installed: bool=True, preflight_user: bool=False
doc:
Resolve the effective scope, then enforce root (system) / user D-Bus reachability (user, when
``preflight_user``) and — when ``require_installed`` — that the unit exists. Returns the scope.

name: _systemd_unit_belongs_to_current_home
doc:
False (with a warning) when the installed unit pins a HERMES_HOME other than this process's: the
service name then resolved to ANOTHER install's gateway, and stop/disable/unlink would take it down.

name: _systemd_graceful_restart_action
doc:
SIGUSR1-drain the live gateway ``pid``; return the follow-up ``systemctl`` verb (``"start"`` /
``"restart"``) the caller must still issue, or None when systemd already owns the relaunch.

name: _systemd_reset_and_run
doc:
``reset-failed`` then ``systemctl <action>``, then wait for the relaunch. Start-limit
rejection prints the wait hint instead of raising; a 90s timeout prints where to look.

name: systemd_status
arguments: deep: bool=False, system: bool=False, full: bool=False

name: _wait_for_gateway_exit
doc:
Wait up to ``timeout`` s for the gateway (by gateway.pid, not launchd labels, so multiple
HERMES_HOMEs work) to exit; SIGKILL it after ``force_after`` s of graceful waiting.

name: _wait_for_tcp_port_free
arguments: host: str, port: int, *, timeout: float=10.0
doc:
Wait until nothing accepts TCP connections on host:port.

PID exit is not enough on macOS: api_server disables SO_REUSEADDR, so a restart that wins
the race logs EADDRINUSE and keeps running with no API. Connection-refused means the
listener is gone; a timed-out connect is a live listener with a slow accept queue.

name: _wait_for_api_server_port_free
doc:
Wait for the configured api_server listen address to stop accepting.

Only when api_server is enabled: with the platform off, a foreign listener on the default
port is nobody's race and must not delay the restart.

name: _running_under_gateway_supervisor
doc:
True when this process IS the supervisor-launched gateway, so the conflict guard never wedges
the service into a respawn/refuse loop. Markers: systemd INVOCATION_ID, launchd XPC_SERVICE_NAME
(shells inherit "0"), s6 HERMES_S6_SUPERVISED_CHILD, or ``--external-supervisor``.

name: host_multiplexer_serving
doc:
The ONE live host gateway when it serves ``profile_name`` (default: the current profile).

Companion to :func:`named_profile_served_by_running_multiplexer`, which answers the narrower
"is this a SATELLITE of the default's multiplexer" and is hard-False for ``default`` — the
profile that usually owns the shared process. Every lifecycle guard built on it was therefore
blind to the host process itself. This one is true for ``default`` too, and it reports WHICH
profiles the host process serves. Returns a ``gateway.host_attach.HostGateway`` or None.

name: _served_by_another_host_gateway
doc:
The host gateway serving ``profile_name`` when it is NOT this home's own process.

The owner must never be guarded out of restarting itself: a refusal keyed on "something serves
you" would make `hermes gateway restart` impossible for the profile that launched the host
process. Guards want "ANOTHER process already serves you", which is this.

name: named_profile_served_by_running_multiplexer
doc:
True when a live default multiplexer already ticks this named profile (a satellite profile has no
gateway.pid; the multiplexer fires its jobs and serves its platforms). Defaults to the current profile.

See #97120.

name: _served_profile_needs_no_service
doc:
Print the "already served" note and return True when a setup flow must not install a standalone
service: a live multiplexing default gateway already serves this named profile, so the unit/plist it
would register can only sit dead (the start guard refuses it) or double-bind its platforms.
Shared by ``hermes setup gateway`` / ``hermes setup`` / ``hermes import`` (``ensure_gateway_service``)
and the ``hermes gateway setup`` wizard. See #111958.

name: _named_profile_refused_under_multiplexer
doc:
Print the refusal and return True when a NAMED profile must not get a gateway of its own.

One gateway per host serves every profile, so a ``<root>/profiles/<name>`` home never installs or
starts a standalone gateway: either the host gateway already serves it (a second one would
double-bind its platforms: two pollers on one token, port fights) or no host gateway runs yet and
the DEFAULT profile is where it is installed. Refusing only the served case let a host with no
multiplexer running (or one that had not rescanned yet) grow a brand-new per-profile fleet member.
``--force`` is the one escape (a fleet split across UNIX users or a ``HERMES_HOME`` outside
``profiles/``); a service it already installed stays startable without it. Shared by ``run`` and the service verbs (``start``/``install``/``restart``): a
refusal only inside ``gateway run`` leaves the service manager to discover it — systemd parks the
unit on exit 78 while the CLI prints "started"; launchd (KeepAlive, no exit-status gating)
respawns it every ThrottleInterval forever.

name: _guard_named_profile_under_multiplexer
doc: Exit-78 form of ``_named_profile_refused_under_multiplexer`` for the CLI entry points.

name: _host_decision_exit_code
doc:
Exit code for a host-attach verdict a supervisor may be watching.

``GATEWAY_FATAL_CONFIG_EXIT_CODE`` (78) is the PERMANENT refusal: systemd parks the unit on it
(``RestartPreventExitStatus``), the s6 finish script maps it to 125, launchd maps it to a
deliberate stop. That is right for a config-derived refusal and wrong for a runtime one — "some
other process serves me right now" ends the moment that process goes away, and parking the unit
on it strands the profile until a human notices. Transient verdicts therefore use
``GATEWAY_SERVICE_RESTART_EXIT_CODE`` (75, EX_TEMPFAIL), which every supervisor we generate
already retries: systemd has ``RestartForceExitStatus=75`` with ``RestartSec=5``, the s6 finish
script passes it through, and launchd relaunches a non-78 failure. Exit 0 would NOT do: s6
parks a clean exit too.

name: _attach_to_host_gateway_or_guard
doc:
``gateway run`` against the ONE host gateway: attach, rescan-then-attach, replace, or refuse.

A profile the host process already serves has nothing to run: print who serves it and exit 0
without spawning anything. Under a service supervisor the SAME situation exits 75 instead, so
the unit is RETRIED rather than parked (see :func:`_host_decision_exit_code`).

``--replace`` and ``--force`` are the two escape hatches this guard must not eat: both return
here so ``start_gateway`` can act on them (it owns the signalling and the PID claim).

name: _guard_supervised_gateway_conflict
doc:
Refuse a foreground gateway when a service manager already supervises one: a shell-launched run
becomes a second dispatcher that escapes the cgroup, survives ``systemctl restart``, and writes the
shared kanban DB concurrently (multi-writer SQLite WAL corruption). ``--force`` starts anyway.

See #35240.

name: _guard_existing_gateway_process_conflict
doc:
Cheap PID-file preflight before the expensive ``gateway.run`` import (the authoritative lock check):
supervisor loops re-running bare ``gateway run`` burned memory on plugin discovery just to fail
"already running". Same user-facing contract; never scans other HERMES_HOME roots.

name: _guard_official_docker_root_gateway
doc: Refuse gateway startup when the official Docker privilege drop was bypassed.

name: _apply_startup_watchdog_config
doc:
Idempotent backstop arming of the startup-liveness watchdog. Must run AFTER the conflict guards (a
--replace loser must not arm one). config.yaml gateway.startup_watchdog* is the user surface; env
vars bridge it because the argv fast-path arms before config loads, and explicit env wins. arm() is
idempotent, so a config timeout needs disarm+re-arm. GatewayRunner disarms once the loop is live.

name: _absorb_windows_console_controls
doc: Make a detached Windows gateway ignore console-control broadcasts from sibling CLIs.

name: _make_exit_diag
doc:
``_exit_diag(tag, **extra)`` recorder writing ``logs/gateway-exit-diag.log`` — captures every way
``asyncio.run()`` can return, for chasing silent Windows gateway deaths. HERMES_GATEWAY_EXIT_DIAG=0 opts out.

name: _respawn_storm_backoff
doc:
Portable app-level respawn-storm breaker (for supervisors without a floor). Defaults mirror
DEFAULT_CONFIG ``gateway.respawn_storm``; HERMES_GATEWAY_MAX_STARTS / HERMES_GATEWAY_START_WINDOW_S
override; max_starts <= 0 disables. Never blocks startup.

name: run_gateway
arguments: verbose: int=0, quiet: bool=False, replace: bool=False, force: bool=False, idle_exit: bool=False
doc:
Run the gateway in foreground. verbose 1=INFO/2+=DEBUG on stderr; quiet: no stderr logs; replace:
kill an existing instance first (avoids systemd restart loops); force: skip the supervised guard;
idle_exit: a client auto-started this unsupervised gateway, so it exits once idle
(``gateway.unmanaged_idle_exit_seconds``).

name: _runtime_health_lines
doc: Summarize the latest persisted gateway runtime health state.

name: _systemd_unit_installed
doc:
A unit at either scope that serves THIS home. A unit pinned to another install's home is not
ours, so stop/restart/start fall through to this home's own gateway (PID path) instead of
operating the other install's service.

name: _is_service_running
doc: Check if the gateway service is currently running.

name: _service_backend
doc:
Host service manager: ``"systemd"`` / ``"launchd"`` / ``"windows"`` / None, in the canonical
predicate order every subcommand routes on. ``windows=False`` never probes ``is_windows()``.

name: _service_call
arguments: backend: str, verb: str, system: bool | None=False
doc:
Run ``verb`` (start/stop/restart/uninstall) on ``backend``. Names resolve at call time so tests
can monkeypatch them; only systemd takes a scope, and ``system=None`` omits it (wizard restart).
Each systemd/launchd verb refuses a definition pinning another HERMES_HOME itself.

name: _dispatch_via_service_manager_if_s6
doc:
Dispatch start/stop/restart via s6 inside an s6 container; True iff dispatched (caller returns).
Profile defaults to the current one; missing slot / s6 errors become actionable CLI messages.

name: _dispatch_all_via_service_manager_if_s6
doc:
Dispatch ``--all`` stop/restart to every registered profile gateway under s6; True iff dispatched.
A bare pkill is seen by s6-supervise as a crash and restarted ~1s later; the service manager flips
``want up``/``want down`` correctly. ``start --all`` is not a CLI surface.

name: gateway_command
doc: Handle gateway subcommands.

name: _maybe_redirect_run_to_s6_supervision
doc:
Inside an s6 container, upgrade bare ``gateway run`` to the supervised s6 longrun; True iff dispatched.
``HERMES_S6_SUPERVISED_CHILD`` (set by ``S6ServiceManager._render_run_script``) marks the supervised
child, which must run in foreground or we'd recurse run → start → run; ``--no-supervise`` /
HERMES_GATEWAY_NO_SUPERVISE=1 opts out (CI smoke, debugging).

name: _block_until_terminated
doc:
Heartbeat when ``execvp("sleep")`` fails. SIGTERM exits 128+signum so ``docker stop`` is clean;
``Event().wait()`` covers platforms without ``signal.pause()``.

Fallback heartbeat for when ``os.execvp("sleep", ...)`` can't run (``sleep`` missing from PATH — issue
#36208). Installs a SIGTERM handler that exits with the conventional 128+signum code so ``docker stop``
produces a clean, expected exit, then blocks on ``signal.pause()``. Windows) — although this path only
runs inside the s6 Linux container image, the fallback keeps the helper safe to import and unit-test
anywhere.

name: _installed_service_kind_for
doc:
``"systemd"`` / ``"launchd"`` when the unit/plist exists, else ``"windows"`` iff ``windows()``
(a thunk so it runs last, like every caller's original ladder), else None.

name: _installed_service_kind
doc: Installed service kind; stricter than ``_service_backend`` (unit/plist/task must exist).

name: _stop_installed_service
doc: Stop the installed systemd/launchd/Windows service. Returns True if one was stopped.

name: _refuse_from_inside_gateway
doc: Refuse self-targeting stop/restart/uninstall from inside the gateway process (#92560).

name: _is_apt_termux_install
doc:
True when this install is a sealed ``apt-termux`` tree.

A Termux APT package is a sealed tree owned by the package manager with
no service manager behind it. Keyed on the steward stamp
(``sealed_steward``), never a platform probe, so the refusal follows the
INSTALL PROVENANCE (our apt distribution's own stamp) rather than the
ambient environment; the platform-shaped ``is_termux()`` lanes stay
for generic on-device installs. Foreground process management (stop/
status via the PID registry) is NOT gated: it works on every install.

name: _service_mgmt_blocked
doc:
Service lanes are unavailable: a Termux device (platform probe) or a
sealed apt-termux install (provenance probe). One predicate so a fourth
service gate cannot forget the disjunction.

name: _handle_no_backend
arguments: subcommand: str, *, wsl: bool, s6: bool
doc:
Fallthrough when no service backend matched. Predicate order: WSL (only when ``wsl``) ->
container (s6 slot hint only when ``s6``; ``start`` reaches here only when s6 isn't running) ->
unsupported.

name: _install_systemd_from_cli
arguments: args, *, force: bool, system: bool, run_as_user

name: _host_multiplexer_for_all_verb
doc:
The live host gateway a ``--all`` verb must target instead of sweeping every profile.

``--all`` means "the ONE host multiplexer", not "every gateway process on this box": sweeping
killed a multiplexer serving N profiles and started a single gateway in its place, so a
per-profile command caused a host-wide outage and left exactly one profile served.

name: _print_unfolded_gateway_note
doc: Detect-and-converge: name the per-profile gateways `--all` no longer sweeps, never kill them.

name: _stop_host_multiplexer
doc: SIGTERM the host gateway and nothing else; returns how many processes were signalled.

name: _cmd_migrate_legacy
doc: Stop, disable, and remove legacy Hermes gateway unit files (e.g. hermes.service).

name: _pm_runtime_venv_dir
doc:
The venv pm provisioned for this install, resolved through
``runtime_paths.selected_venv`` — the committed-environment contract —
never from interpreter state.

Under no-boot-through-venv the gateway runs the store python with the
venv's site-packages on PYTHONPATH, so ``sys.prefix`` always equals
``sys.base_prefix`` and ``VIRTUAL_ENV`` is unset in bundled installs;
prefix/env probing silently degrades. Resolution follows the committed-
environment contract: a committed selection is returned as-is, a host
with nothing committed yields nothing launchable, and a malformed
selection raises — fail closed, never a silently wrong venv.

name: _effort_word
doc: The ``session.mutate reasoning`` effort for main's ``reasoning_config`` dict (None: no override).

name: _rate_limit_state
doc: ``get_rate_limit_state()`` rebuilt from its serialized dict (None stays None).

name: review_summary_line
doc:
Main's ``display.review.summary_cli`` line for the gateway's ``review.summary`` frame: the background
review's "💾 Self-improvement review: ..." (``/refine``, the post-turn review), which the gateway
publishes to a local viewer once the turn settled. None for an empty one.

name: clarify_reply
doc:
Main's batch clarify panel (``callback(questions)``, ``HermesCLI._clarify_callback``) answering a
``clarify`` server request's whole question set: its ``ClarifyResult``.

name: __init__
arguments: self, *, session_db=None, session_id=None, model=None, provider=None, base_url=None, api_mode=None, max_iterations=90, quiet_mode=True, tool_progress_mode='all', reasoning_config=None, service_tier=None, clarify_callback=None, connection_callback=None, connection_update_callback=None, reasoning_callback=None, thinking_callback=None, tool_progress_callback=None, tool_start_callback=None, tool_complete_callback=None, stream_delta_callback=None, tool_gen_callback=None, notice_callback=None, notice_clear_callback=None, reaction_callback=None, interim_assistant_callback=None, connection=None, push_reasoning=False, model_confirm_callback=None, modal_withdraw_callback=None, one_turn=False, one_turn_reasoning=None, one_turn_alias='', **_ignored

name: tool_progress_mode
doc:
``/verbose`` / ``/focus``: ``config.set verbose`` with the explicit mode (never ``cycle``, which
could drift from the CLI's own cycle).

name: reasoning_config
doc:
/new's re-derived effort and a one-turn restore: ``session.mutate reasoning`` when it differs from
the session's effort (an inherited level stays inherited).

name: pin_reasoning
doc:
``/reasoning <level>`` (session scope; main rebuilds its agent with the new config) and a model
pick's ``--reasoning``: always ``session.mutate reasoning``, even when the session already runs that
level by inheritance, so it becomes the session's own choice. True when the owner committed it.

name: stage_turn_reasoning
doc:
``/model B --once --reasoning X``: X for the one-turn admission only (its ``model_override``).
Nothing is sent to the session.

name: restore_reasoning
doc: A one-turn restore: the level goes back on this object only. The session was never written.

name: _route_off_session
doc:
``{model, provider}`` the turn sends when the session runs another route, else None.

``alias``, the ``model_aliases`` entry the pick resolved through, is sent instead of the bare
model: two aliases may name one model at different endpoints, so the owner must not re-resolve
it. An alias makes even the session's own model a one-turn override.

name: switch_model
arguments: self, new_model, new_provider='', api_key='', base_url='', api_mode='', capabilities=None, *, once=False, restore=False, alias=''
doc:
Session-scoped ``/model`` and /resume commit ``session.mutate model``.

``once=True`` does not write the session. The next ``chat`` builds a new agent; that
constructor carries the pick, because this agent is retired when the route signature
changes. ``restore=True`` only puts the previous model back on this object and clears the
one-turn route. The admission already has its ``model_override``.

"Already on this route" is the session row, not ``self.model`` (a one-turn pick sets
``self.model`` without committing). A session switch of that same target still mutates
on the generation fence.

A guarded target the owner refuses with ``confirmation_required`` is re-sent with its token
only on the user's yes to ``model_confirm_callback``: a no returns False with nothing
written; with no prompt the refusal raises. Any refusal raises: main's callers roll their
own fields back.

name: _todo_store
doc:
Main swaps in a fresh ``TodoStore`` after /new, /resume and /branch move ``session_id`` (and the
constructor builds one): it starts with the gateway's snapshot of that session, so a resumed
plan is there before its next ``todo.updated``.

name: session_id
doc:
Main repoints ``agent.session_id`` on /new, /resume and /branch: attach this viewer to that
gateway session (idempotent) and read its state from then on.

name: reasoning_callback
doc:
Main installs a reasoning sink at construction and on ``/reasoning show|hide`` / verbose; the
sink's presence is what makes the agent ask the provider for reasoning. The gateway agent
gets the same switch: the session's ``show_reasoning`` display flag, sent on each change.

name: service_tier
doc:
Main rebuilds AIAgent(service_tier=...) after ``/fast``; the gateway agent gets the same tier
as the session's override (``config.set service_tier``), sent when it differs from the last
one sent for this session. The session's own default (None at first build) is left alone.

name: tools
doc: Tool schemas the gateway session will load (``info.tools`` {toolset: [names]}).

name: apply_session_usage
doc:
Install one session-cumulative usage dict (the ``session.usage`` event / ``session.stats``
result) on main's attributes. Plain assignments: the render thread reads them lock-free.

name: _reset_session_figures
doc: Zero the per-session figures main's bar, spinner and /usage read (context length stays).

name: reset_session_state
doc:
/new, /resume and /branch, after the ``session_id`` switch: drop the previous session's
figures, then show the gateway's for this one (``session.stats``, else its cached
``session.usage``). A brand-new session (no transcript, no usage yet) reads zero until its
first turn publishes, without a round trip.

name: interrupt
doc:
``session.interrupt`` for the running generation; ``message`` stays CLI-side (main
re-queues it as the next turn itself).

name: _correct
doc:
-> ``True`` (accepted), ``False`` (not taken: the caller queues the text), or
``"voice_stopped"`` (TUI-26: the owner took a bare stop phrase as the end of this LOCAL
session's voice chat; the text is consumed and reaches no turn, so it is never re-queued).

name: _compress_context
arguments: self, messages, system_message=None, *, approx_tokens=None, focus_topic=None, force=True, verbatim_tail=None, **_kw
doc:
Main's manual ``/compress`` seam (``compress_now``) as ``session.mutate compress``: the
gateway summarizes and commits; the returned transcript is the gateway's compacted history.
``verbatim_tail`` rows are stamped as stored, so ``compress_now`` does not rejoin them.
The gateway's own report (``summary``: flags and note (with the reason)) is kept for ``compress_now``;
a ``noop`` answer (a failed summary or nothing removable) committed nothing, so the history,
the tail and the compression count stay as they were.

name: _take_turn_route
doc:
The ``/model --once`` pick for the admission being built, consumed here: one admission carries
it, even when a later ``run_conversation`` submits while this one's ``prompt.submit`` still blocks.
A refusal that admitted nothing (``session_busy``) puts it back with ``_give_back_turn_route``.

Staging already compared the pick with the session's route (``_route_off_session``), so it is not
compared again: its ``model`` may be an alias spelled like the session's model, and the owner runs a
plain pick of the session's own route on the session's endpoint and key (``one_turn_runtime``).

name: _stage_content_parts
doc:
``[{type: text}, {type: image_url, image_url: {url: data:...}}]`` -> (text, attachments): each
image is staged on the owner with ``image.attach_bytes`` (bytes read here, locally, by main's
``build_native_content_parts``); main's ``[Image attached at: <local path>]`` hints are dropped
because the gateway names its own staged copies.

name: run_conversation
arguments: self, user_message, conversation_history=None, stream_callback=None, task_id=None, persist_user_message=None, turn_author=None, **_kw

name: _drain_stale
doc:
Frames left from an earlier turn of this viewer (a late settlement) are not this turn's. A
``/queue`` admission's start among them is remembered: that turn is painted after this one.

name: _stop
doc: The ``abandon`` of a turn's blocking reads: it lost the terminal, or Ctrl-C's settle bound passed.

name: _lost
doc:
The ``abandon`` of a turn's end-of-turn reads (its receipt, the cumulative stats): only losing the
terminal stops them. Past Ctrl-C's settle bound they still run, bounded by their own timeouts.

name: _pump
doc:
Dispatch frames until this admission's ``message.complete``; returns its payload, or the
transport error (disconnect).

name: _recover
doc:
``gateway_replay_gap``: re-attach, answer the controls the hole hid, stop painting live text. A
turn the snapshot no longer lists settles from its receipt; None waits for the live completion.

name: _close_segment
doc: A segment boundary: the ``text: None`` separator, or a later boundary when it fell in a gap.

name: _set_todos
doc: The gateway's ``{todos, revision}`` into the CLI's ``TodoStore`` (``restore``: no new revision).

name: _restore_connection_card
doc:
After a replay gap, the resume snapshot's open operation: (re)open the card from it, or
close a stale card when none remains (the gap may have eaten the request or the settle).

name: connection_respond
doc: The card's answer to the gateway's open operation (``connection.respond``); returns its result.

name: connection_retry
doc: The card's Try again on a failed or expired row: the gateway re-mints it on the open operation.

name: _answer_request
doc:
A gateway server→client request (``sudo``, ``secret``, ``clarify``): main's own modal
answers it on this (agent) thread, through the callback HermesCLI registered for the turn; the
answer travels only in the JSON-RPC response frame.

name: _on_request_withdrawn
doc:
``request.cancel`` (connection loop thread): the gateway settled or withdrew a request. When
this agent thread is parked in the modal answering it (another viewer completed the form, the
turn timed out or was interrupted), release that modal so the pump reads the turn's remaining
frames; its late reply to the already-settled request is dropped by the gateway.

name: _ask_secret
doc:
Main's masked "Skill Setup Required" panel (the CLI's registered secret-capture callback,
``hermes_cli.callbacks.prompt_for_secret``) collects the value and prints main's lines; the
gateway, not this process, saves it in the profile ``.env``, so the panel's save is captured.

name: _voice_stopped
doc:
TUI-26: the owner took a bare stop phrase typed into this LOCAL session's voice chat (turned
on by another viewer) as the end of that chat and admitted nothing, so no ``message.complete``
will come. The turn ends at once with main's typed-stop notice; the history is unchanged.

name: _failed
arguments: self, history, user_message, error, *, failure_reason=None, retryable=False
doc:
``failure_reason="gateway_connection"``: the CLI shows ``error`` as written instead of
classifying a lost gateway as a model failure ("Run /model to switch...").

name: _paint_owed
doc:
After a replay gap, the reply once (``owed_reply``): a reuse this terminal showed whole stays
the only copy; otherwise main's panel shows what streaming did not.

name: _anchor_display
doc:
Main's bar shows the anchored ``context_tokens`` by re-deriving it from
``_turn_base_usage_anchor`` over ``_session_messages`` (``anchored_context_tokens``), and marks
it ``~`` when the turn appended rows after its first response. Rebuild an anchor over this
viewer's transcript that yields the gateway's figure: rows after the first API call of a
multi-call turn are the estimated delta (main's ``~``); a single reply is covered by the anchor.

name: _refresh_stats
doc: ``session.stats`` → the same attributes ``session.usage`` sets; False when unavailable.

name: _apply_usage
doc:
Turn end: the session-cumulative ``session.stats`` (the same dict ``session.usage`` carries);
a gateway without the verb leaves the per-turn receipt figures as before.

name: dispatch_goal_command
doc:
``goal_command.dispatch_goal_command`` for the classic CLI: on a gateway manager ``/goal draft``
(its contract drafter is an auxiliary-model call) runs whole on the gateway; every other form is
main's dispatcher over the proxy, so its output strings stay main's.

name: gateway_connection
doc:
The CLI's gateway connection when its session store is the gateway's, else None (main's local
managers: tests and the TUI slash worker's shadow CLI).

name: is_waiting
doc:
Barrier check (and lazy clear) where the barrier lives: the pid / process session is the
gateway's. A state with no barrier answers locally, so the idle poll costs no round trip.

name: command
doc: The whole ``/goal <arg>`` run by the gateway (``/goal draft``: its contract drafter is a model call).

name: evaluate_after_turn
doc:
The judge runs in the gateway (``auxiliary.goal_judge``), with the gateway's background
processes and delegations; the decision dict is main's.

name: set
arguments: self, prompt, *, interval_seconds=None, times=0, until='', route=None

name: shell_client_env
doc:
This shell's allowlisted environment (``agent.session_client_env``) with the extra names of the
profile's effective config (managed layer included), as the gateway reads them. A bypass launch's
owner freezes code defaults, so it reads no profile.

name: client_env_policy
doc:
``client_env`` for a new session (main's process read these from its shell; the shared gateway
applies them to this session only), or nothing for a gateway that predates the field.

name: bypass_launch
doc:
--safe-mode / --ignore-user-config (or their env opt-ins): the owner freezes code defaults,
the client reads no profile.

name: continue_title
doc: ``-c <name>`` (classic precedence: ignored when ``--resume`` is given).

name: wants_latest
doc:
Bare ``-c`` or ``--resume latest`` (the keyword wins over a session titled "latest", which
stays reachable by id or ``-c latest``).

name: _caller_cwd
doc: The caller's working directory (``--in`` wins), resolved; filesystem work, so off the loop.

name: _workspace_key
doc: The classic CLI's workspace identity for ``-c`` (git root, else the cwd).

name: _resume
doc:
``session.resume``; ``--api-key`` re-supplies a launch-only key an owner restart revoked.
The owner binds it only to a session launched with that same key (never durable); anything
else is a route override and refused like every other creation flag on resume.

name: _resume_latest
doc:
Bare ``-c``: this terminal's breadcrumb session when the owner still has it, else (and for
``--resume latest``) the owner's most recent CLI session, this workspace first.

name: resume_policy_error
doc: The resume refusal naming each flag that differs from the session's frozen launch, and the way forward.

name: exit_on_resume_refusal
doc: A refused resume is a usage error on every classic path (interactive startup's copy): ``Error:``, exit 2.

name: _launch_flags
doc:
The creation flags the user passed. Identity, not equality: ``--max-turns 0`` (unlimited)
is a value, while ``0 == False`` would drop it to the profile default.

name: check_resume_policy
doc:
A resume may repeat the flags the session was created with (scripts re-run one command
line); anything that would CHANGE the frozen route is refused, as before.

name: _register_terminal_process
doc:
The chat client is still a terminal on this HERMES_HOME: record it in the process ledger
(purpose ``cli`` is never update-reapable) and warn once when another install shares the home.

name: _user_turns
doc:
Human-authored live user rows (``row_id`` = durable ``messages.id``), oldest first: no display-only
kind other than a typed /steer, never a compaction handoff carrier, never a row a compression
archived (shown in the snapshot's history, not a turn to rewind to).

name: _rewind
doc:
The rewound user turn's text (``/retry``: its lossless resend text), or None when there was
nothing to rewind.

name: _new
doc:
A fresh session with this one's frozen launch request (model, toolsets, cwd, ...); the old
session stays resumable by its id. A title is a separate rename so an existing title is a
conflict, never a silent attach to that other session.

name: forward
doc: Run a registry command (or a skill) on the owner; its refusal names where the command stands.

name: run_command
doc: Any slash command the view's own controls did not take.

name: _pending_preview
doc:
One terminal-safe line of a pending admission's prompt: escape sequences removed, every
other non-printable (C0/C1, bidi and zero-width format chars, newlines) folded to a space,
capped at ``_PREVIEW_CHARS``. Empty when the row carries no text.

name: _oneshot_admission
doc:
The one-shot query's admission id; None when the owner admitted nothing because the query was a
bare stop phrase that ended the session's LOCAL voice chat (TUI-26 ``{voice_stopped: true}``).

name: resume_footer
doc:
The classic single-query exit block (``_print_exit_summary``): how to continue this session.
A non-default profile needs ``-p`` because session ids are profile-scoped.

name: __init__
arguments: self, client, snapshot, *, quiet=False, emitter=None, usage_file=None

name: _reattach
doc:
The owner retired this view's subscription; its turns run on. Re-attach (a refusal fails the
view as before), show the controls the hole hid, and recover the turns in admission order.

name: _recover
doc:
Queued: it lost nothing. Running: cut until its live completion. Unknown: its completion was the
one lost, so an own turn settles as unknown now. Unlisted: it ended in the hole.

name: _read_line
doc:
The next composer line, or ``""`` once the event stream failed first (``self.failure``
is then set). The pending read is cancelled (prompt_toolkit restores the terminal) so the
caller reports the unknown outcome without waiting for a keypress.

significant_calls.callee:
{
            "message.delta": self._delta, "message.complete": self._complete,
            "tool.start": self._tool_start, "tool.complete": self._tool_complete,
            "approval.request": self._request, "clarify.request": self._request,
            "approval.settled": self._settled, "clarify.settled": self._settled,
            "session.info": self._session_info,
            "status.update": self._notice, "notification.show": self._notice,

self.emitter.on_tool_progress("tool.completed", payload.get("tool_name"), None, payload.get("args"),

name: adopt
doc: Attach this view to another session's snapshot (a branch, /new).

name: _confirm_model_switch
doc:
The owner refused a guarded model target (cost / data policy / large context): ask as
the in-process CLI does (``_confirm_expensive_model_switch``: switch anyway once, or cancel)
on this composer. Only an explicit yes applies; anything else keeps the current model.

name: _detach
doc:
One-shot cannot go on without a human: say why on stderr, exit 3, and in stream-json
mode close the protocol with a failed ``result`` (a consumer parsing stdout must never be
left without a terminal record).

name: _finite_block
_settled_result
doc:
The structured result the owner committed with this admission's settlement — the same
dict the in-process one-shot got from ``run_conversation`` (best-effort, never raises).

name: _print_exit_ids
doc:
The finite run's durable id on stderr (automation wrappers parse it; it names the
physical row a compaction may have advanced) and, for `chat -q`, main's resume block. Main's
`-z` (unattended) printed only the reply: no id line.

name: _report_silent_interrupt
doc:
A restart or stop drain settles a finite turn interrupted with no reply: say so on stderr
instead of exiting 130 silently. It is never replayed.

name: _report_no_reply
doc: `-z` exit 1 (a completed turn with no reply text): the in-process one-shot's stderr line.

name: _write_usage_file
doc: ``-z --usage-file``: the same JSON ledger the in-process one-shot wrote.

name: gateway_ws_target
doc:
``(url, subprotocols)`` for dialing the owner's canonical WebSocket with a session ticket.

The owner accepts exactly one ticket subprotocol beside ``GATEWAY_WS_PROTOCOL`` and echoes the
latter; callers check ``ws.subprotocol == GATEWAY_WS_PROTOCOL`` after the upgrade.

name: _bounded_error_data
doc:
At most 16 short keys whose values are bool/int/None, short strings or short lists of them;
anything else (nested objects, raw remote diagnostics) is dropped, never forwarded.

name: rpc_error
doc:
The ``GatewayRPCError`` for one received ``error`` member: only bounded reason codes, never
raw remote diagnostics. A free-text message (``unknown method: x``) falls back to the bounded
``data.reason`` the owner sends beside it, then to ``request_failed``.

name: put_behind
doc: Queue a local item (ACP's post-ack recovery) behind every frame read so far; never dropped.

name: _session_ticket
arguments: home: Path, endpoint, *, purpose='interactive', scope=None, subject=None

name: connect_gateway
doc:
Attach to this home's owner. ``endpoint``: an already-discovered ready owner to dial as-is
(maintenance that must never start a gateway); default ensures one, starting it if needed.
``subject``: mint the ticket for this principal (the caller's authenticated dashboard user)
rather than the socket identity; only a peer the owner already trusts may name one.

name: hold
doc: Queue *item* behind everything already read, never dropping it.

name: _read_on
doc:
Keep reading past a full queue: nothing is held, or an awaited answer may sit behind the
held frames (its waiter may be the queue's only consumer) and the overflow has room.

name: rpc
doc:
Send one request and await its answer; ``_timeout`` (seconds, never sent on the wire)
overrides ``DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT`` for a verb that legitimately takes longer (``math.inf``: no
deadline; the answer, a hang-up or the caller's cancel ends the wait).

name: run
doc: True when the gateway answered the command (the local handler must not run).

name: explain_service_failure
doc:
Lines to print for a systemd service failure escaping the gateway command, or None
when *exc* is not one this module knows how to explain (callers re-raise).

name: _resume_plain
doc:
A keyed ``session.resume`` the owner refused with ``exc``: returns when the caller resumes plain,
else raises. Only a refusal in ``_KEY_NOT_TAKEN`` resumes plain (a keyed startup alias on a Desktop/TUI
session); any other is raised, not hidden by a keyless attach whose first turn fails. ``typed`` (a typed
``--api-key`` the user resumes with) never resumes plain: ``admission_conflict`` is the thin client's
refusal.

name: lost_before
doc:
``frame`` is a transport error from a connection older than ``epoch``: a reconnect replaced it,
so it is no outcome of anything submitted on ``epoch``.

name: runs_route
doc: Whether the session runs ``model`` (and ``provider``, when both sides name one).

name: apply_usage
doc: One session-cumulative usage dict (``session.usage`` payload or ``session.stats`` result).

name: final
doc:
No call dials again: the viewer closed it, or its first connect failed. ``closed`` is also
true while the gateway is hung up, which the next ``call()``/``start()`` redials.

name: _resubscribe
doc:
A new socket is a new viewer: the gateway streams a session's frames only to connections
that resumed it. Resume each session this viewer had open; one gone meanwhile is dropped. Any
other failure fails the reconnect: ready without the subscription, every prompt is refused on a
live socket that never redials, while a failed redial is retried by the next call.

name: resume
_resume
doc:
:meth:`resume` for :meth:`_resubscribe`, awaited on this loop so a cancelled reconnect cancels
its request. A reconnect types nothing: never ``typed``.

name: reply
doc:
Answer one of the gateway's server→client requests (the ``sudo`` prompt): a JSON-RPC
response frame with the request's own id. Never raises; a lost reply times out gateway-side.

name: reattach
doc: ``session.resume`` after a replay gap; its snapshot names the subscription to detach.

name: _send
doc: ``(future, epoch)`` of one request sent on the live socket (see :meth:`call_tagged`).

name: call_until
doc:
``call`` with no answer deadline, for a verb that lasts as long as the work it runs (a plugin
command's handler), on a socket of its own to this connection's gateway: the gateway answers a
socket's requests one at a time, in arrival order (``tui_gateway/ws.py``), so a handler still
running never holds this connection's reads, prompts and interrupts. One dial and one send,
never retried. Waits for the answer or the transport's error, unless *wake* (a
``threading.Event``, set by Ctrl+C or :meth:`close`) is set first: then raises
:class:`CallStopped`; the request was sent and its work goes on, but its answer is dropped. The
socket closes on any of these, and its thread is gone before this returns.

significant_calls.expression:
spawn_context_thread(lambda: asyncio.run(self._command(method, params, wake, answer, sent)),
                                      name="hermes-gateway-command")

name: _command
arguments: self, method, params, wake, answer, sent
doc:
The command socket of :meth:`call_until`: dial, send once, settle ``answer`` with the reply or
the transport's error; a set ``wake`` without an answer cancels the dial or the wait.

name: call_tagged
doc:
``(result, epoch)``: the epoch of the socket that carried the request, so work it admitted
is tied to that gateway life even if another caller redials before this one reads ``epoch``.
``abandon`` (polled) true stops the wait with :class:`CallStopped`; the answer is dropped.

name: _default_gateway_id
doc:
``gw-<hostname>``: the gatewayId is the connector's kill-switch granularity, so default to
the host name for recognizability; override via ``--gateway-id``.

name: _resolve_connector_url
doc:
Connector base URL (no trailing slash): ``--connector-url`` > ``GATEWAY_RELAY_URL`` >
``gateway.relay_url``. The relay URL is a ``ws(s)://…/relay`` dial target; enrollment POSTs to
``http(s)://`` on the same host, so map the scheme and strip a pasted ``/relay`` suffix.

name: _post_enroll
arguments: *, connector_base_url: str, access_token: str, enrollment_token: str, gateway_id: str, timeout: float=15.0
doc:
POST to the connector's ``/relay/enroll``; return ``{secret, deliveryKey, tenant, gatewayId}``.
Raises RuntimeError with a user-facing message on any non-2xx / transport failure.

name: cmd_gateway_enroll
doc: Enroll this gateway with a relay connector; persist the auth creds to .env.

name: _warn_if_secondary_multiplex_profile
doc:
Warn when relay routing stamps landed in a secondary profile's .env that a multiplexed gateway
will never read. Returns True when the warning fired (caller suppresses the restart text).

name: _discard_dead_host_record
doc: Drop the host rendezvous record once its owner is provably gone (after a confirmed stop).

name: _forget_host_gateway_probe
doc:
Drop the memoized host-gateway probe after a stop, before the restart starts a new one.

The probe is cached for ``HOST_GATEWAY_CACHE_TTL_S`` and a stop finishes well inside it, so the
in-process ``run_gateway`` read "PID <stopped> serves this profile", printed "nothing to start"
and exited 0 with no gateway running.

name: get_launchd_label
doc: Return the launchd service label, scoped per profile.

name: _probe_launchd_domain_for_label
doc:
Launchd domain managing ``label`` (uncached): ``gui/<uid>`` (Aqua), then ``user/<uid>``
(Background/SSH), else the ``launchctl managername`` heuristic. Sibling profiles may live in
different domains, so never reuse the cached ``_launchd_domain()`` for another label.

name: _launchd_domain
doc:
Domain managing the current profile's gateway; cached per process so start/stop/restart agree.

See #40831, #23387.

name: _launchd_error_indicates_unloaded
doc: True when launchctl failed because the job isn't loaded (retry bootstrap).

name: _launchctl_domain_unsupported
doc: True when launchctl can't manage the domain even after a fresh bootstrap (macOS 26+) — degrade to detached.

name: _launchctl_bootstrap
arguments: domain: str, plist_path, label: str, *, timeout: int=30
doc:
Bootstrap a launchd job, recovering from a stale still-registered label (EIO 5). Without the
bootout + retry that case is misread as an unmanageable domain and degrades to detached, silently
losing auto-start and crash-restart.

name: _launchd_reload_log_path
doc: Path the launchd reload watchdog tails for persistent-orphan detection.

name: _append_launchd_reload_log
doc: Append a timestamped line to the launchd reload log (best-effort).

name: _launchd_reload_budget
doc:
Bootstrap retry window for a plist reload: the failure happens while the old gateway is still
draining (default 180s), so size it to the drain timeout with a 30s floor.

name: _launchctl_supervised_pid
doc:
PID launchd currently runs for ``label``, or None when it runs none. ``launchctl list`` exits 0 for
a mere registered definition (``state = not running`` on macOS 26+), so a PID — not the exit code — is
the answer. Domain-agnostic on purpose: ``launchctl print`` domain probes fail on macOS-26 per-user
domains, which is why the invoking profile verifies through this and not ``_launchd_print_service_pid``.

name: _launchctl_label_supervising_process
doc: True when launchd knows ``label`` AND runs a process for it.

name: _retry_launchctl_bootstrap_until_registered
arguments: domain: str, plist_path, label: str, *, deadline: float
doc:
Retry ``_launchctl_bootstrap`` until the label supervises a process or ``deadline`` passes. Under
load bootstrap can fail even after bootout, during a drain (default 180s) — ~10s is too short.

name: _write_launchd_unsupported_marker
doc: Persist that launchd cannot supervise the gateway on this host.

name: _clear_launchd_unsupported_marker
doc: Clear the unsupported marker when launchd bootstrap succeeds.

name: launchd_program_arguments
arguments: command: list[str], stdout_log: Path, stderr_log: Path
doc:
launchd ``ProgramArguments`` that run ``command`` with a Local Network identity macOS accepts (#71206).

macOS Local Network Privacy attributes a socket to the process launchd spawned for the job. A bare
venv Python has no application ID and is not platform-entitled, so every LAN connect from the
launchd gateway dies with ``EHOSTUNREACH`` while the same code works from Terminal (whose grant it
inherits). An ad-hoc-signed helper .app does not help: nehelper never prompts for it and denies
(#57812 dead-end table, re-verified live on macOS 26.3). ``/usr/bin/osascript`` spawning the child
makes it osascript-responsible — an Apple platform binary — so the child is exempt; ``/bin/sh -c
exec …`` and ``/usr/bin/time`` wrappers are NOT (the launchd job identity is the non-entitled first
executable).

Standard Additions' ``do shell script`` polls WindowServer for a user-cancel event while it waits.
That is appropriate for a short interactive script but, for the gateway's process lifetime, burns CPU
and keeps a WindowServer event connection busy (external-display wake stalls ~10s on macOS 27, #123595).
JXA calling libc ``system()`` waits in the kernel instead while retaining osascript as the responsible
process. The shell's ``exec`` keeps the gateway in the launchd job's process group, so ``launchctl
bootout`` / ``kickstart -k`` still deliver SIGTERM to it. stdout/stderr are appended inside the shell
command because ``system()`` otherwise inherits osascript's plist log handles. The encoded wait status
is translated back to a process exit code so KeepAlive's ``SuccessfulExit`` semantics are preserved.

name: _timestamped_stderr_gateway_command
doc:
Wrap gateway run so raw stderr lines are timestamped before file write. ``external_supervisor``
(launchd ProgramArguments only) adds ``--external-supervisor`` so ``hermes update`` hands back to
launchd, and drops ``--replace``: KeepAlive respawns would re-arm takeover, so two profiles sharing
a token would kill each other forever.

``external_supervisor=True`` is for launchd ProgramArguments only: the inner ``gateway run`` must carry
``--external-supervisor`` so ``hermes update`` sees the flag on the live grandchild argv and hands the
process back to launchd instead of starting a detached watcher (#86893 / #87005). The detached nohup
fallback stays unmarked.
Supervised starts also drop ``--replace`` (issue #79048): a launchd service is respawned by KeepAlive,
so takeover authority would be re-armed on every respawn — two profiles legitimately sharing one
platform token would each terminate the sibling, and launchd would revive the victim forever. Bounded
replacement is the lifecycle commands' job (``launchctl kickstart -k``, drain in ``launchd_restart()``,
bootout+bootstrap in install/refresh), which run before supervision resumes. Mirrors
``generate_systemd_unit``, whose ExecStart also runs ``gateway run`` without ``--replace``.

name: _spawn_detached_gateway
doc:
Launch the gateway detached (launchd fallback for macOS 26+). CLI-managed nohup equivalent:
stdout → gateway.log, timestamped stderr → gateway.error.log, PID via gateway.pid so stop/status work.

Used when launchctl can no longer bootstrap/kickstart the gateway on macOS 26+ (issue #23387). Mirrors
the `nohup hermes gateway run --replace` workaround but keeps it CLI-managed: stdout goes to
gateway.log, stderr is timestamped into gateway.error.log, and the PID is tracked via the gateway.pid
file that `run_gateway` writes, so stop/status/restart keep working.

name: _launchd_fallback_to_detached
doc:
Start the gateway detached when launchd can't manage it; on failure print the manual workaround
and (by default) exit 1.

name: _launchd_degrade_or_raise
doc:
Shared launchctl failure policy: domain unmanageable (5/125) → detached fallback; else re-raise.

A 5/125 exit is evidence about the *domain* only when launchd is not already supervising this job.
EIO (5) is ``launchctl bootstrap``'s answer for a label that is already loaded, so the ordinary
"reinstall/restart over the live gateway" case lands here with the service up and supervised.
Degrading there is not a graceful fallback: it writes the permanent launchd-unsupported marker and
starts a detached gateway *beside* the supervised one, and the marker makes
:func:`wait_for_launchd_gateway_supervision` answer True unconditionally — so no later
install/update can tell that nothing ties the gateway to launchd any more. A live supervised PID is
direct evidence this macOS does manage the job, so surface the failure instead of branding the host.

name: launchd_plist_is_current
doc: Check if the installed launchd plist matches the currently generated one.

name: _spawn_deferred_launchd_reload
arguments: *, domain: str, label: str, target: str, plist_path: Path, gateway_pid: int
doc:
Hand the bootout/bootstrap cycle to a transient ``launchctl submit`` job; True if spawned. The
helper waits for the OLD gateway to exit (bootstrap during drain fails EIO), then retries bootstrap
until ``launchctl list`` shows a positive PID or the drain budget elapses.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(
            [
                "launchctl", "submit", "-l", submit_label, "-o", str(reload_log_path), "-e", str(reload_log_path),
                "--", "/bin/bash", "-c", reload_script,
            ],
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        )

name: refresh_launchd_plist_if_needed
doc:
Rewrite the installed plist when the generated one differs, then bootout/bootstrap so launchd
re-reads it immediately.

name: launchd_install
arguments: force: bool=False, *, start_now: bool=True, force_unit_path: bool=False

name: _launchd_bootstrap_and_kickstart
doc: Bootstrap then kickstart; False after degrading to detached (domain unsupported). Other errors propagate.

name: _launchd_ok
doc: Print a launchd success line and clear the unsupported marker (an OS fix recovers automatically).

name: _launchd_kickstart
doc: ``launchctl kickstart -k domain/label``; raises so callers own per-label failure accounting.

name: _wait_for_launchd_service_pid
arguments: label: str, old_pid: int | None, timeout: float=10.0, *, domain: str
doc:
Poll ``domain/label`` (0.5s) until it runs on a fresh PID or ``timeout`` passes — KeepAlive respawn
isn't instantaneous. launchctl ``TimeoutExpired`` propagates; callers own failure accounting.

name: wait_for_launchd_gateway_supervision
arguments: *, timeout: float=LAUNCHD_SUPERVISION_VERIFY_TIMEOUT, label: str | None=None, poll_interval: float=0.5, old_pid: int | None=None
doc:
Poll launchd until it supervises a live gateway; True at once if the detached fallback is active.
``launchd_restart`` returns once the restart is *requested* (asynchronous), so it can't see a helper
dying before bootstrap or a ``launchctl bootstrap`` that exits 0 without registering.

The ``_request_gateway_self_restart`` branch hands the work to the running gateway and returns
immediately, and a plist reload is handed to a detached helper. Both are asynchronous, so a caller that
reads "returned without raising" as "the service is up" cannot see a helper that dies before its first
bootstrap (#88848) — nor a ``launchctl bootstrap`` that exits 0 without registering, which the reporter
measured on macOS 26.6.1.
Judge the outcome the way #80491 taught the helper to judge it: by a live supervised pid, never by an
exit code.  :func:`_launchctl_supervised_pid` is already that probe, so this only adds the wait.

``old_pid`` is the pid launchd ran for the label *before* the restart: a restart that leaves the same
process running is not a restart, so passing it holds the invoking profile to the same fresh-pid
contract :func:`_wait_for_launchd_service_pid` enforces for sibling labels. With ``old_pid=None``
(no pre-restart pid was observable) any supervised pid counts, as before.

name: _live_work_from_state
doc: ``active_agents`` from a fresh ``gateway_state.json`` whose writer is alive (older gateways).

name: live_work
doc:
What the gateway serving ``home`` is running now: ``{"active_agents", "active_work"}``, or None
when no gateway answers. The control socket answers live; the state file covers older gateways.
``profile`` narrows the answer to one served profile's work (the state file cannot, so it is skipped).

name: _candidate_homes
doc:
Homes whose gateway a stop/restart from here takes down, in order: the system unit's pinned home
(``sudo`` strips HERMES_HOME, so this process sees root's), this home's own gateway (a ``--force``
standalone one included), then the live host owner that serves it. Only READS the unit: a foreign
unit is skipped here and refused by the systemd verb before it adopts any home.

name: refusal_lines
arguments: verb: str, homes: list[Path], *, flag_hint: str=f'hermes gateway {{verb}} {INTERRUPT_FLAG}', profile: Optional[str]=None
doc: Refusal text for ``verb`` while the first answering gateway among ``homes`` has live work, else [].

name: _work_lines
arguments: verb: str, home: Path, work: dict[str, Any], flag_hint: str

name: refuse_while_sessions_live
arguments: verb: str, args, *, host_home: Optional[Path]=None, profile: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Exit 1 naming the live work unless ``--interrupt`` was passed; with it, say what is interrupted.
``host_home``/``profile``: a served profile's stop/restart unserves only that profile in the host,
so only its work counts.

name: _remove_verb
doc:
An s6 slot is parked down (it stays registered as the `hermes -p X gateway start` target), every
other unit is uninstalled.

name: _home_env
doc:
Run service-manager helpers as if ``home`` were the active HERMES_HOME. Both the contextvar
override (``get_hermes_home``) and ``os.environ`` (``gateway.status`` identity files, unit
generation) are switched, then restored.

The process keeps its LAUNCH identity while swapped (``pin_process_hermes_home``): ``os.environ``
still holds the launch profile's ``.env``, so a child spawned in here for ``home`` must see it as
a routed home and take only ``home``'s own secrets — with the env var swapped, the routed-home
checks read ``home`` as the launch profile and handed the launch profile's credentials to the
default gateway.

name: _live_gateway_pid
doc:
Verified PID of a gateway SERVING ``home``, else None (never raises: a probe failure must
not abort a migration plan).

Topology REPORTING, not ownership: ``live_gateway_pid_for_home`` deliberately answers with the
host multiplexer's PID for every home it serves (``gateway.status._host_gateway_serves_home``),
so "this profile is being served" reads as a live PID. Use :func:`_own_gateway_pid` for the
question this command acts on.

name: _host_gateway_owner
doc: The ONE live host gateway (``gateway.host_attach.HostGateway``) or None. Never raises.

name: _own_gateway_pid
doc:
PID of a gateway ``home`` OWNS, else None.

Ownership is what this command may stop, and the host multiplexer is not owned by the profiles
it serves: it is one process, launched from one home. Deriving ownership from
:func:`_live_gateway_pid` made every secondary on a CONVERGED host report the host gateway's
PID, so the plan called the host half-migrated and each `hermes update` SIGTERMed the only
gateway it had. The host process counts only for the home it was actually launched from; every
other profile it serves owns nothing.

name: _gateway_identity
arguments: home: Path, pid: Optional[int], services: list[tuple[str, bool]]

name: _installed_services
doc:
Every installed service for ``home``'s gateway (units / plist / scheduled task), user scope first.

Under s6 the footprint is the SLOT: the root slot always (it is what a restart goes through),
a named profile's slot only while it is UP — a registered-down slot is what the container's
boot leaves behind for every named profile and is not a gateway.

name: _windows_task_installed
doc:
Is a per-profile Windows gateway installed for the ACTIVE ``HERMES_HOME``?

``get_task_name()`` is home-suffixed, so this answers per profile exactly the way the systemd
unit path does. Either half counts: ``hermes gateway install`` falls back to a Startup-folder
