entry when it cannot register a scheduled task, and a migration that removed only the task
would leave the fallback launching a second gateway at the next logon.

name: _systemd_service_user
doc: Read ``User=`` before migration removes a system-scope unit.

name: _service_op
arguments: kind: str, system: bool, verb: str, home: Path, *, run_as_user: Optional[str]=None
doc: ``stop`` / ``uninstall`` / ``start`` / ``restart`` / ``install`` / ``enable`` on ``home``'s service.

name: _s6_slot_op
doc:
The s6 leg of :func:`_service_op`. A named profile's slot is never uninstalled: it stays
registered DOWN (``down`` file) as the target of a later ``hermes -p X gateway start``, exactly
the shape the container's boot produces. The root slot is (re)started so it re-reads its config.

name: _read_multiplex_flag
doc:
The operator's EXPLICIT opt-in only. The unset default (on) is settled by the default gateway at
boot and refused while a secondary runs its own gateway — exactly the fleet this command folds —
so the plan reads it as "not yet multiplexed" and the migration proceeds.

name: _write_multiplex_flag
doc:
Set ``gateway.multiplex_profiles`` in the DEFAULT profile's config.yaml through the config API
(same read-guard + nested-set + atomic write ``hermes config set`` uses; no raw YAML edits).

name: _profile_gateway_config
doc:
This profile's ``GatewayConfig`` read exactly the way the multiplexer reads it: under the
profile's own secret scope with multiplexing active, so a missing token stays missing instead of
borrowing the CLI process's ``os.environ`` (which holds the launch profile's ``.env``).

A PARKED profile stays in the inventory and the duplicate-credential guard (parking must not hide
a conflict), but it is inert for the host: its config is read without discovering its plugins,
whose ``register()`` would otherwise run in the live gateway on every boot (#123386). Only its
plugin-defined platforms fall out of the guard — their credentials cannot be evaluated without
importing the plugin; builtin bot tokens still collide.

name: _credential_probe
doc:
Config-shaped stand-in for ``GatewayRunner._adapter_credential_fingerprint`` (which probes
adapter attributes): token/api_key plus the id-style credentials adapters expose from ``extra``.

name: _credential_claims
doc: ``(platform, fingerprint)`` for every enabled platform with a discoverable credential.

name: _credential_key_names
doc:
Env key NAMES (never values) that make ``platform_value`` connect as a bot, e.g.
``TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN``; the platform id when no key is registered (config.yaml-only token).

name: duplicate_credential_lines
doc:
One finding per platform credential two profiles both hold, with the remedy. The SINGLE
source for the migrate preflight, ``hermes doctor`` and ``hermes gateway status``, so all three
name the same duplicates the same way: profile names + key names only, never a value or hash.

name: duplicate_credential_findings
doc:
The preflight's duplicate-credential check read straight from the local profile homes, for
diagnostics that have no migration plan (doctor, gateway status). A profile whose gateway config
does not load is skipped here — ``build_migration_plan`` reports that one as its own blocker.

name: _check_duplicate_credentials
doc:
BLOCKER: the same bot credential configured on two profiles — the multiplexer would park
the duplicate adapter, so one profile's bot would go silent after migration.

name: platform_serves_profile_prefix
doc:
True when the adapter for ``platform_value`` declares ``serves_profile_prefix`` (it answers
``/p/<profile>/...`` on the default listener). Read from the adapter CLASS — builtin table or the
plugin registry entry — never from a hand-kept list, so new ingress adapters count automatically.

name: _check_secondary_port_binders
doc:
BLOCKER when a secondary enables a port-binding platform with no ``/p/<profile>/`` ingress
(the multiplexer skips the whole profile); NOTICE (URL changes) when the ingress exists.

name: build_migration_plan
doc: Enumerate profiles + their OWN gateway footprint, then run every preflight check.

name: _signalled_gateways
doc:
Every RUNNING gateway process ``apply_migration`` will signal, in apply order.

Derived from the steps the apply actually takes, not from "secondaries that happen to expose a
PID". Two classes were silently missing and both killed live processes: a secondary with an
installed unit and no readable PID is stopped through ``_service_op`` (which SIGTERMs whatever
the supervisor is running), and the DEFAULT's own live gateway is replaced by
:func:`_restart_default`. A dry run that promises nothing will be stopped and then stops the
host's only gateway breaks the contract this block exists to keep.

name: _manifest_secondaries
doc: The manifest's secondary records, or None when the (hand-edited) manifest is malformed.

name: _recorded_services
doc:
Every service a manifest record names: ``services`` (all installed units) or, in a manifest
written before that key existed, the single ``service``.

name: _target_from_manifest
doc:
Service manager + ``User=`` the resumed default install should use, read from the recorded
footprint (the units themselves are gone by the time an interrupted apply is re-run).

name: _manifest_not_yet_served
doc:
The postcondition ``apply_migration`` waits for, re-derived from live state: a LIVE default that
recorded serving every unparked profile the manifest migrated. Anything less — no live gateway, an
installed-but-dead unit (``systemd_install`` writes the unit before the start that can still fail),
a standalone default never restarted — is a half-applied migration, not "already multiplexed".
Profiles created after the migration are not in the manifest, so they cannot flag it as interrupted.

name: _reconcile_standalone_runtime
doc: Remove only status owned by multiplexing, without re-stamping gateway identity.

name: _wait_for_served
arguments: default_home: Path, expected: set[str], timeout: float
doc: Poll the default's ``gateway_state.json`` until ``served_profiles`` covers ``expected``.

name: _restart_default
arguments: plan_default: ProfileGateway, target: Optional[tuple[str, bool]], default_home: Path, *, run_as_user: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Bring the default gateway up on the new flag value; returns a one-line description.

Boot enablement is NOT this function's job: an existing survivor unit is enabled by
:func:`_enable_default_at_boot` before the first removal, and the install branch enables
through ``systemd_install``'s own enable-on-startup.

name: _enable_default_at_boot
doc:
Make the survivor boot-startable BEFORE anything is removed. Every secondary unit the fold
uninstalls takes its boot enablement with it, and the pre-existing default unit may have been
disabled all along; ``restart`` on a disabled unit succeeds, so the old order (remove, then
restart) turned N boot-startable gateways into 0 and reported success (#124922). ``enable``
never starts the unit, so doing it first cannot double-bind a platform while secondaries run,
and an apply interrupted anywhere after it still leaves a host that comes back after a reboot.
Returns the failure line, or None: a fresh apply refuses on it (nothing has been removed yet),
a resume reports it and converges anyway (rollback could do no better).

name: _preflight_apply
arguments: plan: MigrationPlan, target: Optional[tuple[str, bool]], run_as_user: Optional[str]
doc:
A failure of the destructive phase that is knowable from the plan alone, refused BEFORE any
working per-profile gateway is stopped: rollback is the fallback for surprises, not the plan.
Mirrors the checks ``systemd_install``/``_service_call`` make on a system unit (root, resolvable
``User=``) and the config write's read-guard.

name: _resume_target
doc:
Service manager + ``User=`` an apply will use: the manifest's record wins on a resume (the
live units it describes are already gone), else what the plan can still see.

name: _resume_findings
doc:
Safety checks re-run on a RESUME and reported as findings instead of refusals.

Both halves matter. Skipping them (the resume branch used to return before ``_preflight_apply``
ran at all) let a duplicate bot credential, a ``/p/`` ingress gap or an unresolvable service
user reach the multiplexer unannounced. Enforcing them as blockers is worse: a resume runs on
a host whose secondary units are ALREADY removed, so refusing does not prevent damage — it
makes the damage permanent, which is exactly how a stranded host lost its only documented
recovery. So: run every check, name every finding, converge anyway.

name: apply_migration
doc:
Flip the flag, stop/uninstall every secondary gateway, bring up the multiplexer, verify.
Returns True when the multiplexer verifiably serves every profile.

Every step after the manifest write is fallible (a config write, a secondary's stop or its
unit's daemon-reload, a system unit that needs ``--run-as-user``, an unreachable user bus) and
runs inside ONE compensating boundary: on failure the manifest written before the first
destructive step brings ONE gateway back (:func:`rollback_migration`), so the host never ends
with nobody serving. The flag goes on first so an apply killed anywhere after it is resumable
from the manifest (flag on + manifest + no live multiplexer = interrupted).

**Resume beats preflight.** The manifest is read BEFORE the blocker gate: a manifest means an
earlier apply already removed units, so this run is a compensation, not an initiation, and a
gate that refuses it traps the host forever (no ``--standalone``, no rollback command). The
checks still run — as findings, see :func:`_resume_findings`. With no manifest nothing has been
destroyed yet and both gates refuse exactly as before.

name: _wait_for_live_gateway
doc:
Bounded wait for a gateway that is actually UP for ``home``; None on timeout.

A service-manager ``start`` that returns is not proof: systemd returns after its own start
timeout on a unit that keeps failing, and taking that for success is how the compensator
printed "✓ Restored" over a unit respawning every 5 s at ``ExecMainStatus=75``.

name: rollback_migration
doc:
COMPENSATOR for a failed apply: put ONE gateway back on this host.

Not a user-facing rollback and deliberately NOT a fleet restore. It used to reinstall and
start every recorded per-profile gateway, which the host gateway lock now forbids by
construction: this function clears the multiplex-owned served record first, so
``gateway.host_attach`` tells each secondary to "start normally" and the flock loser exits 75
into a supervisor respawn loop (observed live: a secondary won the race while the default's
unit sat at ``NRestarts=38, ExecMainStatus=75``, respawning every 5 s — ``StartLimitIntervalSec=0``
defeats the limiter). Under multiplex-only a restored fleet is not a state we want to be able
to reach, so the compensation is the one gateway the topology allows: the DEFAULT's, on the
recorded flag. The secondaries whose units this attempt already removed are named in the
output and are served by that gateway as soon as it multiplexes (``flag_was`` is either unset
or the retired ``false``; both resolve to multiplex at boot once nothing blocks it).

Returns True only when a gateway is VERIFIABLY live again; the manifest is kept otherwise so
the next ``hermes gateway migrate --multiplex`` resumes.

name: _host_supports_migration
doc:
Reason the host cannot be converged by this command, else None.

Windows IS handled (per-profile Scheduled Tasks and the Startup-folder fallback are removed
like any other unit). s6 IS handled too, in-process: a named profile's slot that is UP is
parked (``s6-svc -d`` + ``down`` file) and its autostart intent folded into the root slot the
same way the container's boot does it (``hermes_cli.gateway_multiplex_s6``). What cannot be
done from here is register a slot the boot never created — that is the one refusal left.

name: cmd_migrate
doc: ``hermes gateway migrate [--multiplex] [--dry-run] [--yes]``.

name: maybe_auto_migrate_after_update
doc:
``hermes update`` hook: with >= 2 profiles, per-profile gateways present and multiplex off,
migrate automatically when unblocked (deterministic, never prompts) or print the blocker block.
``gateway.auto_multiplex_migration: false`` on the default profile opts out; a secondary behind a
service-domain / UNIX-user / HERMES_HOME boundary blocks this path only (the explicit command decides).

name: service
doc: The unit the default gateway is (re)started through; None when nothing is installed.

name: already_multiplexed
doc:
Converged: nothing is left for this command to do.

TOPOLOGY, not the flag. A host whose flag is on while a secondary still owns a gateway
process or a supervisor unit is HALF-migrated; reporting that as "already multiplexed"
made the re-run a no-op on exactly the host that needed it most (#100896).

name: target_service_kind
doc:
Service manager the default gateway should end up on: its own, else the one the
secondaries used (so a systemd-managed fleet stays systemd-managed).

name: target_run_as_user
doc: Preserve the system unit identity that the default unit replaces.

name: eligible_for_migration
doc:
>= 2 profiles, at least one secondary with its own gateway, multiplex off, no blockers.
This is the AUTO-migration (``hermes update``) bar; the explicit command also proceeds with
zero standalone secondaries (see :func:`cmd_migrate`).

name: _pid_uid
doc: Owner uid of a live process: ``/proc`` where it exists, ``ps`` on macOS; None when unknown.

name: pid_is_other_users
doc:
True when *pid* is owned by another Unix user than this non-root caller.

Gateway process scans match argv host-wide, so without this a second account's gateway (users
isolate credentials by UID) became a ``restart --all`` SIGTERM target and "unfolded profile"
advice. Root keeps the host-wide view (``sudo … --system`` over a ``User=`` unit), as does
Windows (no ``geteuid``); an unknown owner is not called foreign.

name: _system_unit_uid
doc: uid a system unit runs as: its ``User=`` (root when absent); None when the name is unknown.

name: gateway_identity
arguments: home: Path, pid: Optional[int], services: list[tuple[str, bool]]
doc:
``(uid, runtime_home)`` of the gateway that serves ``home``.

uid: the live process owner; else, for a system unit, its ``User=`` — and ONLY that: a system
unit's principal is whatever systemd will run, so an unresolvable ``User=`` stays None rather than
borrowing the profile directory's owner (a stopped unit pinned to an absent NSS user is not the
account that owns the files). Without a system unit (user-scope systemd / launchd / detached), the
profile directory owner is the account the gateway runs as. None means unknown. runtime_home: the
HERMES_HOME an installed unit pins, which is where the gateway really runs; ``home`` otherwise.

name: _guard_service_domain
doc:
Different manager or scope than the one the fleet converges on (system vs user systemd, launchd vs
systemd). The reference is the default's own unit when it has one, else the manager
``target_service_kind()`` elects from the secondaries: a default that never had a gateway unit is not a
service domain of its own, and refusing every secondary against it left the common upgrade fleet (N
launchd profiles, unit-less default, #118097) printing blockers instead of folding. Two managers
among the secondaries still refuse — the ones not elected differ from the target. Two units on one
profile is an ambiguous topology the unattended path does not resolve either.

name: auto_migration_blockers
doc:
Every boundary a standalone secondary sits behind; empty when the fleet is one user, one service
domain, one profiles/ tree — the only shape ``hermes update`` may fold on its own.

name: masked_default_unit
doc:
The default profile's systemd unit when the operator MASKED it (``systemctl mask`` links it to
``/dev/null``), else None. A masked survivor cannot be enabled at boot, and masking is a deliberate
"never start this", so the update hook reads it as an opt-out instead of refusing (#139324).

name: auto_migration_opted_out
doc:
``gateway.auto_multiplex_migration: false`` in the DEFAULT profile's EFFECTIVE config: the same
``load_config`` the rest of the CLI reads (``DEFAULT_CONFIG`` + config.yaml + the managed overlay), so
an administrator's managed ``false`` wins over a user's ``true`` and a YAML string ``"false"`` is
false, not truthy. Only the nested key counts, there is no top-level alias.

name: explicit_multiplex_flag
doc:
The operator's explicit choice for the DEFAULT profile's gateway: a recognized
``GATEWAY_MULTIPLEX_PROFILES``, else ``gateway.multiplex_profiles`` (or the top-level alias) as
written in its config.yaml; ``None`` when neither is set. Raw read on purpose: the callers are
other processes (``hermes -p X ...`` has X's config loaded) asking about the default's file.

name: settled_explicit_flag
doc:
How boot reads an explicit ``multiplex_profiles``: ``true`` is final; the retired ``false``
settles exactly like an unset key (``None``: the boot preflight decides).

name: host_serves_named_profile
doc:
Offline twin of the boot verdict for named profile *home* under *default_home*'s gateway:
``False`` for a ``gateway.standalone: true`` secondary (``profiles_to_serve`` never serves it),
``True`` for an explicit ``true`` on the default, ``None`` when boot settles it (unset or the
retired ``false``, see :func:`resolve_multiplex_mode`).

name: default_gateway_multiplexes
doc:
Does the default profile's gateway serve every profile? For CLI/dashboard processes: the LIVE
gateway's ``served_profiles`` record when one runs (it settled the unset default itself), else
the explicit flag, else False — an unset flag is decided by the gateway at boot, never guessed
here.

The one thing that can no longer report "standalone" is an explicit ``false``: it is RETIRED
(warned about and ignored at boot, see :func:`resolve_multiplex_mode`), so answering False from
it made every CLI surface contradict the gateway that was about to multiplex anyway.

name: standalone_launcher_decision
doc: The per-profile opt-out also binds callers supplying an explicit GatewayConfig.

name: implicit_multiplex_blocker
doc:
Why THIS process must not multiplex right now, or None when it may.

Mirrors what makes ``hermes gateway migrate --multiplex`` refuse or leave a per-profile gateway
in place: hosts whose per-profile gateways the preflight cannot see (s6 slots) stay standalone;
a secondary that still runs its own gateway (live process or installed service) or a preflight
blocker (duplicate bot credential, port binder without a ``/p/<profile>/`` ingress) keeps this
gateway standalone.

Every blocker here is a TRANSIENT, fixable condition, which is why this function is now also
the whole answer for an explicit ``gateway.multiplex_profiles: false`` (see
:func:`resolve_multiplex_mode`): the host converges the moment the blocker is gone.

The launching profile's IDENTITY is deliberately not a blocker: multiplex-only means "the one
host process", whichever profile started it. Gating on ``active == 'default'`` made a host
whose only gateway runs under a named profile permanently standalone — and every lifecycle
verb built on "the default's multiplexer" blind to the process actually serving the host.

name: persist_resolved_default
doc:
Write ``gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`` into the DEFAULT profile's config.yaml so the file
reads as the gateway behaves. The key has ONE valid value right now (Teknium ruling): an unset key
is made explicit ("left unset" was read as "off"), a retired ``false`` is rewritten in place and
leaves a one-time marker for the boxed notice. Comment-preserving writer, once, and NEVER on a guard
refusal (the file must not say true while the runtime is standalone). Returns True on a write.

name: retired_opt_out_notice_lines
doc: The one-time boxed notice for a rewritten ``false`` (same box as the guard warning).

name: consume_rewritten_notice
doc: ``hermes update``'s summary: print the rewrite notice ONCE more, then clear the marker.

name: resolve_multiplex_mode
doc:
Settle ``config.multiplex_profiles`` for one gateway boot; the config is updated in place.

``gateway.multiplex_profiles: false`` is RETIRED as a topology opt-out (multiplex-only ruling).
The key still parses and still drives the runtime mode this function writes back, but an
explicit ``false`` no longer pins a per-profile fleet: it is warned about and resolved exactly
like an unset key. That is safe because the unset path is not optimistic — it refuses to
multiplex while any real blocker holds (an s6 container, a secondary that still owns a gateway,
a duplicate bot credential), so a host that genuinely cannot fold still comes up standalone and
says why, and it converges by itself once ``hermes gateway migrate --multiplex`` has run.

name: record_multiplex_decision
doc:
Persist a guard refusal into ``gateway_state.json`` so `hermes gateway status` can show why this
gateway serves one profile while the default says multiplex; any other verdict clears the field.

Only the runtime-lock owner writes that file. The decision is made while the config loads, before
the lock claim, and a pre-lock write published this process's pid as a live ``starting`` gateway:
a launch racing it read that as an owner and refused, leaving no gateway at all. Until this process
holds the lock the decision stays pending; ``publish_pending_multiplex_decision`` writes it once
the claim succeeds, and a launch that loses the claim never writes it.

name: publish_pending_multiplex_decision
doc: Write the decision held back before the runtime-lock claim (called right after the claim).

name: unserved_profiles
doc: Named profiles a standalone gateway leaves without a bot (the whole point of the warning).

name: standalone_warning_lines
doc:
The boxed warning a multi-profile host prints when a guard keeps its gateway standalone.

Empty for anything but a guard refusal on a host with other profiles to serve: a single-profile
install has nothing unserved, so there is nothing to shout about. The same box appears at
gateway start, in the ``hermes update`` summary and (as text) in the dashboard banner.

name: recorded_standalone_reason
doc:
The guard refusal a LIVE standalone gateway published in its ``gateway_state.json`` (this
home's, or *state_path*), else ``None``. A stopped, failed or dead record's reason is history.

name: recorded_standalone_warning_lines
doc:
Same box, rebuilt from the live gateway's ``gateway_state.json`` for processes that did not
make the decision (``hermes update``'s summary, ``hermes gateway status``).

name: fold_named_slot_intent
doc:
The ONE rule for folding per-profile s6 slots into the root slot.

A named slot is never booted from its own intent (a started named slot IS a second gateway on
this host); its ``running`` intent moves to the root slot, which is the process that serves it.
Without the fold an image only ever driven as ``hermes -p coder gateway start`` came up with
ZERO gateways: no root state, every named slot registered down, every action "registered".

name: running_named_slots
doc:
Named profiles whose s6 slot is UP right now — the only s6 state that is a second gateway.

A registered-down slot (what boot leaves behind) is a start target for ``hermes -p X gateway
start``, not a running gateway, and must never veto the multiplex default.

name: park_named_slot
doc:
Stop a named profile's slot and write its ``down`` file so a supervisor restart does not
revive it (``s6-svc -d`` alone is undone by the next ``s6-svscanctl -a``/container restart).

name: bring_root_slot_up
doc: Start (or restart, so it re-reads its config) the root slot; returns a one-line description.

name: live_default_gateway_pid
doc:
PID of the default profile's gateway when a VERIFIED live process owns it, else None.

``gateway.status.live_gateway_pid_for_home``: pid file + lock, then the runtime record the gateway
itself writes, each proven against the live process (start time, gateway command line, home). A
launch-service gateway can be live with no ``gateway.pid`` at all, and a stale record whose PID was
recycled by an unrelated process must not make its ``served_profiles`` authoritative. Never key this
off the record's ``updated_at``: an idle gateway never advances it.

name: recorded_served_profiles
doc:
``served_profiles`` the live default gateway recorded, or None when the key is absent (a record
from before the multiplexer recorded it, or a stopped/absent gateway). Callers fall back to config
derivation only on None: an empty list is an authoritative "serves nobody else".

name: multiplexer_served_secondaries
doc: Named profiles the live default multiplexer serves (excludes ``default``); empty when none.

name: served_profile_unserved_platforms
doc:
``{platform: reason}`` for a served profile's platforms the multiplexer deliberately does not run
(unpaired WhatsApp or Relay shared ingress; ``gateway.run_adapters`` stamps
``<profile>:<platform>`` as ``disabled`` with a reason and remedy).

name: served_profile_ingress_urls
doc:
``{profile: {platform: url}}`` for every secondary inbound-port platform the live multiplexer
serves on its shared listener (``<profile>:<platform>`` entries carrying ``ingress_url``). This is
what the user pastes into the vendor console (Twilio, LINE, Teams, ...). ``profile`` narrows the map.

name: format_ingress_url_lines
doc: One ``<indent><platform>: <url>`` line per platform, sorted.

name: notify_multiplexer_profiles_changed
doc:
Tell the live default multiplexer that ``profiles/`` changed (``profile_name`` was created or
deleted) so it hot-serves / unroutes it now instead of at its next periodic rescan. Returns the
served-profile list the gateway answered with, or None when no multiplexer answered (no live default
gateway, single-profile gateway, or a gateway predating the verb). Never raises.

name: model_refusal_text
doc: Why a guarded model target was not applied (the owner's guard text first).

name: confirmation_title
doc: The one prompt title for the owner's guard warnings (as ``combined_selection_warning``).

name: confirm_choice
doc:
``once`` / ``cancel`` (or None) for a typed answer: the choice's number or the classic
CLI's confirm aliases (y/yes/once, n/no/cancel).

name: compress_payload
doc:
Structured ``session.mutate(compress)`` payload from the raw ``/compress`` arguments.

The shared parser is the one every native surface uses, so ``--preview`` stays a read-only
flag and ``here [N]`` a boundary instead of becoming a focus topic; ``--aggressive`` has no
canonical implementation and is refused before anything reaches the authority.

name: apply
arguments: self, client, session_id, operation, payload, *, confirm=None
doc:
The owner's answer for this prepared mutation (retained across ambiguous replies).

A guarded model target answers ``status: confirmation_required`` and writes nothing.
``confirm`` (``async (refusal) -> bool``) is the surface's prompt: yes re-sends the same
retained mutation once with ``payload.confirm`` = the owner's token (under the original
key, so an ambiguous reply to the confirmed send retries that exact request); no answers
``status: cancelled``. Without a prompt (non-interactive) the refusal is an error, and a
confirmed send refused again (another switch or a turn landed first) is never re-asked.

``payload`` may be a function of the snapshot the CAS tuple is read from (a rewind names
its target row from that same transcript); returning None means "nothing to do" and is
answered ``status: nothing``. A derived payload is keyed by operation alone, so a lost-reply
retry re-presents the original target instead of re-deriving one from an already-rewound
transcript. Metadata edits (``rename``) carry no generation fence, as on Ink/Desktop.

name: retire
doc:
Only a session's very next control may be the retry of an ambiguous one: any other verb
on the session (a different control, a prompt) retires its retained identities, so a later
deliberate repeat is new work instead of replaying a stale receipt.

name: _read
doc:
Fetch the catalog's plugin commands and cache them for the session and gateway life that served
them (raises GatewayClientError, also when the gateway reports its plugin discovery failed). The
result is published only if neither moved during the call: a reply from epoch E that arrives after
a concurrent redial is never relabelled E+1 (``call_tagged``).

name: _catalog
doc:
``(commands.catalog, epoch)`` for the open gateway session, so its skills come from the session's
folder (its trusted project skills), not the gateway's. A gateway older than this CLI refuses the
``session_id`` (``invalid_params``): it is asked again without it, as before.

name: invalidate
doc:
Drop ``cli``'s copy of the gateway's catalog after a skill rescan (``/reload-skills``, ``/skills
install``): the next read asks the gateway again.

name: _hung_up
doc:
A closed connection keeps its epoch until the next call redials, maybe to another life: no
cache it labelled is served.

name: skills
doc:
``{"/key": {name, description}}`` of the session's skill commands from the gateway's catalog
(``notes``: its one-line notice instead, e.g. skills a built-in command shadows), or None off the
gateway. A failed read is printed once per input and lists none; nothing is scanned here.

name: skill_notes
doc:
``/help skills`` notes (skills a built-in command shadows): the gateway's notice on its session,
else this process's own scan.

name: run_skill
doc:
``/skill ...`` on the gateway session: the gateway resolves and loads the skill (its plugin
skills and stacked skills too) and returns the message, which is queued as main queued it; True
when answered there (False off the gateway: main's local load).

name: toolsets
doc:
``([(key, label, description)], {portable MCP server})`` the gateway's plugins provide for this
profile (``plugins.list``), or None off the gateway (this process's own registry applies). An older
gateway or a failed read gives none, never a local scan. Read once per gateway life.

name: names
doc:
``{name: description}`` of the gateway's plugin commands for completion, or None off the
gateway. A failed read degrades quietly to none; dispatch uses :func:`lookup`.

name: lookup
doc:
Whether ``/name`` is one of the gateway's plugin commands; None off the gateway. A name the
cached list lacks re-reads it once. A failed read is not evidence the name is no plugin: it is
printed and :class:`CatalogUnavailable` raised, so no skill, bundle or expansion stands in.

name: call_unbounded
doc:
``slash.exec`` of *command* with no answer deadline, on a socket of its own so the session's prompts
and interrupts never queue behind it (GatewayConnection.call_until). Ctrl+C stops waiting: the stopped
line is printed and :data:`STOPPED` returned (a KeyboardInterrupt still propagates after it).

significant_calls.callee: spawn_context_thread(_answer_choices, args=(cli, connection, wake, answering), name="hermes-command-choices").start
significant_calls.expression: spawn_context_thread(_answer_choices, args=(cli, connection, wake, answering), name="hermes-command-choices").start()
spawn_context_thread(_answer_choices, args=(cli, connection, wake, answering), name="hermes-command-choices")

name: _answer_choices
doc:
While the command runs, answer the ``clarify`` server requests its handler sends to this session
(``ctx.ask_choice``, ``gateway/plugin_command_choice.py``) with the CLI's clarify panel. No turn
pump reads the session's frames between turns, so they are taken here; every other frame stays
queued, in order, for the turn that owns it.

name: run
doc:
True when the gateway answered ``/name arg`` (the local handler must not run); :data:`GONE`
when it no longer has that plugin command and a fresh catalog read agrees (a plugin reload, e.g.
``hermes plugins disable``, dropped it in this session and gateway life, which no cache boundary
sees): nothing ran, and the caller dispatches the name again (bundle, skill, prefix).

name: _dropped
doc:
Whether the gateway's catalog, read again with the cached copy dropped, no longer lists
``name`` (a failed read: not known, so False).

name: report_gone
doc:
Print that ``/name`` is no longer a plugin command, unless one of the built-in commands or a
``known`` skill or bundle name starts with it (then prefix expansion decides); True when printed.

name: observe
doc:
Tell the gateway about a recognized command this process runs itself (``command.observe``), so
``pre_command`` fires there, in the session's profile, and never here; False off the gateway (main's
in-process hook applies). A command that ``runs`` nothing here (a refusal) is not reported. The
gateway replies before any plugin runs. One older than this CLI (no such method) gets one printed
line, and is not asked again on that connection life: local commands then reach no ``pre_command``
observer, and this process still fires none itself.

name: loaded
doc:
``{name: row}`` of the plugins the gateway loaded (tool/hook/command counts, load error) for
``/plugins``, or None off the gateway. A gateway without ``plugins.list`` on this socket (older
than this CLI) or one that can't answer gets one printed line and ``{}``: the listing then shows
no load details, and this process never loads plugins to fill them in.

name: mark_planned_stop
doc: Best-effort planned-stop marker for ``pid`` (default: the recorded gateway PID).

name: host_scope_for_all_verb
doc:
Home a ``--all`` verb acts as: the live host owner's, else the default root.

``--all`` names the ONE host gateway, whichever profile invoked the CLI — but the active home
decides the service name, the Windows task/launcher and the detached child's ``--profile``, so
with the host DOWN ``-p X gateway start|restart --all`` re-launched X's own gateway, which the
named-profile guard then refused (exit 78): the host stayed down after a Desktop update.

name: profile_lifecycle
doc: True when a named-profile command was handled (including an unconfirmed request).

name: print_parked_status
doc: A parked satellite is still installed, but is not a running gateway.

name: owned_gateway_pid
doc:
This profile's own gateway pid, only on positive, fresh ownership evidence; else None.

A served profile's runtime record carries the host multiplexer's pid (#141133), so the recorded
pid alone never authorizes a stop. Every ``find_gateway_pids()`` caller (stop, uninstall's kill,
``service_manager.is_running``, cron readiness, Windows start polls) reads it through here.

name: _pid_owned_by_home
doc:
Ownership ladder, cheapest proof first; the control socket is dialled only for the host's pid.

``gateway status`` asks once per profile and every served profile's record names the host, so the
host record (a file read plus an incarnation check) settles those without a dial.

name: _launch_record_owns
doc:
``<home>/gateway.pid`` names *pid*'s exact incarnation as launched from *home*.

A gateway writes that file once, about its own launch home (the host never writes one into a
served profile), so it pins the profile resolved at launch: a ``gateway run --force`` that relied
on the sticky ``active_profile`` stays stoppable after the sticky choice changes, which argv and
environment alone cannot prove.

name: report_profile_stop_failure
doc: Do not report absence when a live PID was refused or the probe failed.

name: _print_host_hint
doc: Name the refused pid when it is the host gateway serving this profile (#141133).

name: submit_queued
doc:
Admit ``text`` behind the running turn in the owner's FIFO; returns its admission id.

A refusal (``GatewayRPCError``) or a request never sent raises as is: nothing was queued. A lost
answer is asked once more under the SAME ``submission_id``, which the owner answers with the
admission it already holds (``admit_session_input`` keys it by principal, session and request id),
so the prompt is queued exactly once. Still no answer: :class:`QueueOutcomeUnknown`.

name: queued_rows
doc:
``[(admission_id, text)]`` still queued in the owner's FIFO, in run order.

This viewer's own admissions are read back with ``prompt.receipt`` (one it finds started or settled
is left for the idle tick to paint); other viewers' queued rows come from the last pending list the owner published.

name: published_queue
doc:
The texts the owner last published as queued, plus this viewer's admissions submitted after that
list (no RPC: the dock repaints on every tick).

The owner's published list is authoritative: an admission it no longer lists (cancelled, replaced or
steered by another client, or started) is not shown as queued, even while ``queued_inputs`` still
owes its turn a paint.

name: _own_head
doc:
This viewer's ``/queue`` admission at the head of the owner's queue, not yet adopted; None when
the head is someone else's, nothing is queued, or the FIFO is paused on an ``unknown`` row.

name: cancel
doc:
Retire one queued admission: ``"cancelled"`` when it never ran, ``"stopped"`` when the drain had
claimed it and the owner interrupted that run instead (``session_controls.cancel``), ``"started"``
when it already ran. A turn that ran is still owed a paint, so only a cancelled one leaves
``queued_inputs``.

name: replace
arguments: cli, store, admission: str, text: str
doc: ``prompt.replace_queued``: the edited prompt is a new admission at the back of the FIFO.

name: take_gateway_turn
doc:
Pop a turn the owner is running now (an adopted admission, a notification header) from the
head of ``_pending_input``: those run before the held item, typed items stay behind it.

name: pending_status
doc: ``queued``/``started`` (its completion follows live), or None (it ended in the hole).

name: settled
doc: True: terminal with its reply (cancelled/failed need none); False: still running; None: unreadable.

name: owed_reply
doc:
What is owed of ``final`` after ``shown`` of its segment was painted: the rest of an exact prefix
(ignoring the owner's leading ``"\n\n"`` and trailing whitespace), else a marker and the whole.

name: _checkpoint_rows
doc: ``rollback.list`` rows as ``format_checkpoint_list`` reads them.

name: attachable
doc:
Whether a client may attach to this discovery/ensure verdict.

``ready`` owners, plus a restart's after-turn wait (``draining``/``restart_wait``): that owner
still owns its turns and must stay reachable to answer a parked approval/clarify (#139041).
Shared by every client bootstrap (``connect_gateway`` and Ink's ``gateway_bootstrap.py``).

name: gateway_profile_home
doc:
The profile home whose gateway serves *home*: the home itself, or for a private overlay home
(a task dir mirroring a profile through symlinks, its ``gateway.lock`` among them) the profile its
lock names. A client compares the owner's ``profile_id`` with this, never the overlay path.
Not normcased: ``profile_id`` keeps the owner's own spelling (Windows).

name: _overlay_owner_home
doc: Return the owner named by a private overlay's gateway lock, if it has one.

name: _endpoint
arguments: payload: dict, home: Path, control_home: Path | None=None

name: control_home_for
doc: Home whose control socket mints tickets for *endpoint* (the multiplexer's for a served profile).

name: _starting_multiplexer_root
doc:
The root whose reservation is pending AND whose boot policy would serve *home*, else None.
A ``gateway.standalone: true`` secondary is never served by it, so a reserved (or ready) root
must not make its client wait out the deadline instead of starting the profile's own owner.
One uncached config parse plus a lock probe: call it once per ensure iteration.

name: _standalone_multiplexer_reason
doc:
A live host's reason for not serving its named profiles, if it published one.

A held root lock ordinarily means that a named profile should wait for its
multiplexer.  A host which published a guard refusal is different: it is a
standalone gateway and can never add the named profile during that boot. Read
with the same liveness rules as ``hermes gateway status``'s standalone box.

name: _parked_by_multiplexer
doc:
A secondary the multiplexer could not serve (unusable store, home owned elsewhere) is
published under ``parked_profiles`` (name -> reason). That is a terminal verdict for its
clients: waiting for a ``served_profiles`` entry that will never appear is the wrong answer.

name: _refused_owner_verdict
doc: The named refusal when the client proved the boundary from the control pipe, else None.

name: _served_by_multiplexer
doc:
A served secondary has no socket of its own: the default multiplexer's control socket
answers for it, and its ``identify`` lists the home under ``served_profiles``. Only the
multiplexer's live descriptor proves service; a held ``gateway.lock`` alone does not.

name: _owner_pid
doc:
The PID a refusal may name: one of *home*'s gateway records whose process is provably that
gateway, else None (the caller keeps the generic ``authorization``).

Proof is the shared identity chain: alive, its recorded start time known and equal to the live
one (a recycled PID differs), its recorded home not another profile's, and its live command line
(or, when that is unreadable across the elevation boundary, its record) a gateway's. A stale
``gateway.pid`` falls through to ``gateway.lock`` instead of masking it.

name: _refused
doc:
The owner's control channel refused this same-user client. On Windows (*windows*, the host
fact) name the boundary (an elevated owner, or one in another logon session) with its remedy
instead of the generic ``authorization`` that reads as a credential failure (#139845, #140252).

name: discover_gateway_endpoint
doc:
Read live control identity, preserving uncertainty instead of spawning.

A named profile served by the default multiplexer resolves to the multiplexer's endpoint
with ``profile_id`` = the profile's own home, so clients attach to it with that identity.

name: _update_fenced
doc:
True while an update owns the install, judged the way main's launchers and the Desktop
judge ``.hermes-update-in-progress``: a live (or still being written) marker, or a dead or
malformed one while the checkout lock is held (a killed update's tree still runs). A dead
marker over a free lock is a killed update: it never blocks a launch.

Read-only: a client never clears the updater's fence; the launch-time reclaim
(``update_lock.read_live_update``) and the next update remove a dead marker. A marker that
exists but cannot be read is unjudgeable and fences.

name: _fenced_verdict
doc:
What ensure answers while an update owns the install. The update's own drain
(``pause-for-update``) is a restart's after-turn wait whose owner may hold a turn parked on
approval/clarify, so it is handed out for clients to answer it (#139041). Discovery only:
nothing is started or replaced while fenced, and any other owner state stays ``update_paused``.

name: _observe_replacing_stale
arguments: home: Path, deadline: float, replaced: set[Path]
doc:
Discovery, except that a gateway an older Hermes left on this home is stopped once (like
``hermes gateway stop``) and reported as retiring; a refusal keeps ``incompatible`` + its remedy.

name: ensure_gateway_runtime
arguments: profile_home: str | Path, *, timeout: float=DEFAULT_ENSURE_TIMEOUT, idle_exit: bool=False
doc:
Ensure once; pending remains pending at deadline.

Never installs anything. The one owner it replaces is a gateway an older Hermes left running on
this install's own home (``incompatible``/``runtime_protocol``, the upgrade case): it is stopped
the way ``hermes gateway stop`` stops it, once, and the current one started like any absent
owner. Another install's or a newer Hermes's gateway stays refused, with the reason in ``detail``
(``hermes_cli.gateway_runtime_replace``).

A successful service command or Popen is not session readiness. After an
owner/start request is observed this invocation never launches another.
``idle_exit``: an unmanaged daemon this call starts ends itself once idle (client entrypoints:
chat, TUI, cron/kanban/ACP clients). A gateway that is ending that way reports ``draining``
(``idle_exit``); this call waits for it to go and starts the replacement transparently.

name: _may_have_access_acl
doc:
A Linux POSIX access ACL is present, or its absence cannot be established. Python has no
os.listxattr on macOS (whose chmod +a ACLs are separate); mode bits stay the policy there.

name: home_mode_unsafe
doc:
The profile home keeps the operator's mode (main's home policy: symlinked homes,
HERMES_HOME_MODE 0701/0750). Only write by another user lets them swap the socket; read/search
bits grant nothing against our 0600 socket, and group-write is harmless when the group is the
owner's private group (the umask-002 user-private-group default). What we create stays 0700.

name: _private_node
arguments: path: Path, *, kind: str, home: bool=False

name: _open_mode
arguments: path: Path, mode: int, expected: int

name: socket_peer_uid
doc:
Kernel-reported uid of the process on the other end of a connected AF_UNIX socket
(SO_PEERCRED on Linux, getpeereid on macOS); None where neither exists.

name: connect_private
doc:
Connected control socket for *home* whose listener runs as this user (caller closes it).
The path is validated by lstat first, but connect() follows a symlink swapped in afterwards,
so the listening process itself is authenticated. Platforms without a peer-credential API
(neither SO_PEERCRED nor getpeereid) fall back to the path checks alone.

name: query_identify
doc: Unlike diagnostic queries, retain timeout/access/protocol failures.

name: _private_lock
doc:
Validate ``gateway.lock``; narrow an upgraded same-owner lock to 0600 first.

Main created the inode with ``open(path, "a+")`` under the umask (0644), and lock inodes are
never replaced, so without this an upgraded home reads ``inaccessible`` forever and nothing
auto-starts its owner. Only the mode is touched, only on a regular single-link inode this user
owns, through a NOFOLLOW descriptor; a foreign or non-regular node still raises.

name: missing_owner_state
doc: A reservation before PID/control publication already excludes a new owner.

name: __init__
arguments: self, reason: str, detail: str | None=None, fix: str | None=None

name: bounded_detail
doc:
``detail`` within ``limit`` characters, never with a cut-off command: a repair command
that does not fit is dropped with a notice, and an overlong description is cut visibly.

name: multiplexer_root_for
doc: Default root that may multiplex *home*, when *home* is a named profile under it.

name: implied_host_root
doc:
The root whose gateway must serve named profile *home* when nothing records a verdict.

``hermes gateway run`` refuses a ``profiles/<name>`` home a gateway of its own unless it authored
``gateway.standalone: true`` (or passes ``--force``); the retired ``multiplex_profiles: false``
no longer opts out, so only a standalone profile keeps its own daemon.

name: multiplexer_serves_home
doc:
The root whose (possibly stopped) multiplexer serves *home*, else None.

``hermes_cli.gateway.named_profile_served_by_running_multiplexer`` answers the live question;
this is its offline twin for the moment no gateway runs, deciding from the boot policy
(:func:`hermes_cli.gateway_multiplex_mode.host_serves_named_profile`): a standalone secondary is
never served, an explicit ``true`` serves the rest, and an unset or retired ``false`` flag falls
back to the ``served_profiles`` the last multiplexer recorded. No evidence keeps it unanswered.

name: _identify
doc:
``(control_home, identify payload)`` of the process answering for *home*: its own socket, or
the default multiplexer's for a served named profile (the same order discovery uses).

name: _write_planned_stop
arguments: control: Path, pid: int, start_time: Any
doc:
The marker ``hermes gateway stop`` writes, in the OWNER's home (it reads its own), so the old
gateway exits as a planned stop: clean exit, ``stopped`` persisted, no supervisor revival.

name: replace_incompatible_owner
doc:
Stop the older-Hermes gateway answering for *home*; None once it is gone, else a refusal code
(see :data:`REFUSAL_DETAIL`). Never starts anything: the caller's ensure loop does that.

name: service_suffix
doc:
Host-service suffix for the REQUESTED home, never the initiating client's env.

Same rule as ``hermes_cli.gateway._profile_suffix``: only the platform-native
default home owns the bare unit name; ``<root>/profiles/<name>`` yields the
profile name; any other root (Docker, a temp harness) yields a path hash so a
custom root can never resolve to the production ``hermes-gateway`` unit.

name: _run
arguments: argv: list[str] | tuple[str, ...], deadline: float, *, encoding: str | None='utf-8'

name: _s6
doc:
Find the container gateway slot that owns ``home``.

TUI clients call ``ensure_gateway_runtime`` inside the Docker image too.
They must request that s6 starts the registered slot, rather than falling
through the Linux systemd probe and treating s6 as inaccessible.

name: _no_supervisor
doc:
Android/Termux has no service manager (main refuses `gateway install/start` there and says
"Run manually: hermes gateway"): an unmanaged detached start is its only owner. Python 3.13+
reports ``sys.platform == "android"``; older Termux interpreters report linux and reach the
systemd probe, which finds no unit and lands on the same unmanaged start.

name: start_existing_gateway_service
doc: Request start once; only live control readiness can establish success.

name: _own_store_launcher
doc:
Whether ``executable`` is the store launcher ``installation_command`` writes for THIS install
root (``<root>/.hermes/bin/hermes``, root = gateway.PROJECT_ROOT), never another checkout's.

name: _launch_module
doc:
``(module, its argv)`` for the module launches the installer persists: ``python -m``, or
``_launchers.installation_command``'s two forms for THIS install root (gateway.PROJECT_ROOT): the
store ``<root>/.hermes/bin/hermes --run-module`` launcher, or ``runtime_command``'s inline bootstrap
regenerated byte for byte. A launcher or bootstrap of another checkout is not ours. None otherwise.

name: verify_gateway_argv
arguments: argv: list[str], home: Path, *, wrapped: bool=False
doc:
``wrapped``: a launcher wrapper (the osascript Local Network wrapper) was already stripped, so
only this root's installer forms count: no legacy ``python -m``, and a ``hermes`` launcher must be
``<root>/.hermes/bin/hermes`` (``_own_store_launcher``). The stderr-timestamp wrapper holds its inner
``hermes`` to the same rule. A bare unwrapped ``hermes`` keeps verifying by name, as older
systemd/schtasks/launchd definitions persisted it (binding those is a separate change).

name: verify_systemd
arguments: props: dict[str, str], manager_env: str, home: Path, *, system: bool

name: _launchd_command
doc:
``(command, wrapped)``: the command the launchd job runs, and whether it came out of the Local
Network wrapper (gateway_launchd.launchd_program_arguments, #71206). The wrapper is accepted only when
the installer regenerates it byte for byte from the inner command and the two log paths it carries,
so no shell operator, substitution, extra JXA or foreign osascript rides along.

name: verify_launchd_loaded
arguments: output: str, home: Path, *, uid: int, username: str

name: verify_launchd_plist
arguments: definition: dict, label: str, home: Path

name: verify_windows_task
arguments: xml: str | bytes, home: Path, account: str, sid: str

name: spawn_unmanaged_gateway
arguments: profile_home: Path, *, deadline: float, idle_exit: bool=False, force: bool=False
doc:
Request a daemon, not readiness. Refuse Windows no-breakaway fallback.

No --replace, persistence, login changes, elevation, shell, or inherited stdio.
The gateway runtime's own exclusive ownership fence arbitrates racing starts.
``idle_exit``: the daemon ends itself once idle (a chat/TUI/cron client's own start; never
Desktop's ``gateway ensure``, which keeps its attached gateway for the app's lifetime).
``force``: a ``gateway restart --force --detach`` replacement keeps the ``--force`` its old owner
needed (a named profile under a multiplexer), or it exits on the run-side guard.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=root, env=env, close_fds=True,
                                    stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=output, stderr=output,
                                    **windows_detach_popen_kwargs())

name: start_detached_replacement
doc:
``gateway restart --detach`` with no service: start the stopped owner's replacement the way
``gateway ensure`` starts an absent one. In the foreground, the restarting client (Desktop's
bounded, piped call) would itself become the long-lived gateway it only meant to restart.

name: stdio_log_size
doc: Where this launch's output will start in the append-only stdio log.

name: startup_failure_report
arguments: profile_home: Path, offset: int, status: int, pid: int | None=None
doc:
What a client prints when the gateway it started died before serving: the exit status, the
redacted tail of THIS launch's stdio (the traceback lives there, written before logging is up and
before the detached-stdio redactor is installed) and the command that shows the whole log.

name: pinned_home
doc: ``HERMES_HOME`` pinned by the systemd unit or launchd plist at *definition_path*, or None.

name: service_home_for_unit
doc:
The ``HERMES_HOME`` this process acts for when it writes the systemd unit at *unit_path*.

User scope: its own home. System scope: an explicit ``HERMES_HOME`` remapped to the unit's ``User=``
account the way ``generate_systemd_unit`` pins it; with none (``sudo`` strips it, HOME=/root), the
unit's own pinned home, which is the only thing naming the install being operated on. Pure: it never
adopts the unit's home into ``os.environ``, so a check on this value compares caller and unit.

name: definition_belongs_to_home
arguments: definition_path: Path, home: Path, action: str
doc:
False (with guidance printed) when the existing definition pins a ``HERMES_HOME`` other than *home*.

A missing definition, or one that pins no home (hand-written, pre-pinning), belongs to nobody else.

name: unit_belongs_to_caller
arguments: unit_path: Path, system: bool, action: str, run_as_user: str | None=None
doc:
``definition_belongs_to_home`` for the systemd unit at *unit_path*, judged against the home this
process would pin there (``run_as_user``'s for an explicit ``--system --run-as-user`` install).

name: foreign_systemd_unit_home
doc:
``HERMES_HOME`` of the unit at this scope when it belongs to ANOTHER install, else None.

A throwaway ``HOME`` used to resolve the bare ``hermes-gateway`` name (its ``.hermes`` looked native) and
reach the account's real unit — user scope through the account-anchored unit dir, system scope
because system units are global. Naming now follows the account home, but two homes can still share
a name (a custom root's ``profiles/<name>``, a pre-pinning unit), so every systemd verb asks this.
``_sync_hermes_home_from_systemd_unit`` would adopt the unit's home and ``stop``/``restart`` would take
the live gateway down, so it must be evaluated BEFORE that sync.

Foreign means: the unit pins a home, it differs from this process's home, and this process's home
is not the account's own default root. The last clause keeps the ``sudo`` remap (#108674): root's
default home operating a unit that pins the invoking user's home is the operator, not a stranger.

name: refuse_foreign_systemd_unit
doc: Exit non-zero instead of operating another install's unit (see ``foreign_systemd_unit_home``).

name: refuse_foreign_launchd_plist
doc:
The launchd half of ``refuse_foreign_systemd_unit``: exit 1 rather than start/stop/restart/remove a
LaunchAgent pinning another HERMES_HOME. (Windows task names derive from LOCALAPPDATA, not HOME.)

name: service_definition_homes
doc:
Every HERMES_HOME a gateway service definition sets: systemd ``Environment=``, launchd
``EnvironmentVariables``, the Windows ``gateway.cmd`` ``set`` line and the ``gateway.vbs`` env item.

name: service_definition_launchers
doc:
The scripts a definition starts, by their quoted absolute paths. The Windows Startup-folder
fallback and a Scheduled Task's action name no home: they start the home's ``gateway.vbs``, which does.

name: temp_home_in_service_definition
doc:
Temp-dir HERMES_HOME baked into a systemd unit / launchd plist, or None. A temp home means a
test/E2E harness generated it; installing it leaves the gateway "running" but deaf to every platform.

name: refuse_temp_home_service_write
doc: Refuse (with guidance) when a service definition carries a temp HERMES_HOME.

name: session_label
doc:
Main's 8-character banner label for a canonical durable id (``local-`` + 64 hex); every other
id is shown as is. Display only: RPCs, /resume hints and the exit summary keep the full id.

name: _creation_policy
doc:
The explicit launch flags as ``session.create`` policy (the thin client's own mapping);
unset flags leave the gateway to resolve the profile default, as main's CLI did.

name: _classic_only_policy
doc: Main's `--run-budget` and `-v`, which the thin client refuses.

name: _check_resume_launch
doc:
Explicit launch flags on ``--resume`` / ``-c`` against the session's frozen route, as the thin
client checks them: the same flags again are fine, a different value is refused, never dropped.

name: move_cli_workspace
doc:
``/worktree new``: the session's tools run in the gateway under the cwd frozen in its policy, so
move that first (``session.mutate workspace``, Desktop's Move to project; a refusal raises before
anything moved). The moved session resumes in the tree, so it is recorded as a ``--tui -w`` tree is:
quit removes it when clean and a resume recreates it (N8). Then this process's cwd and TERMINAL_CWD
follow, so a later /new creates its session from the tree; a chdir OSError leaves both where they
were (the gateway session has moved by then).

name: create_titled_session
doc:
``chat -c <title> --create-if-missing`` for the classic CLI: the gateway's ``session.create``
with ``title`` (it resolves-or-creates under one owner lock), so this process writes no row.
Main's ``_create_titled_session`` minted the id and wrote the row itself, with no cwd stamp
(``row_cwd`` ""). Returns the id, or None when the gateway refused (the caller prints main's
"could not be created" copy).

name: close_reader
doc: Release this viewer's SQLite handles before offline maintenance; keep its RPC store.

name: _db
doc:
The read-only reader, opened on first use. No state.db yet (the gateway creates it on its
first start, after the CLI's startup maintenance probe) is retried on the next read.

name: attach
doc:
``session.resume`` once per session id this viewer uses (idempotent), carrying this CLI's launch
key as the thin client does (``GatewayConnection.resume``, the reconnect's too). A session that does
not take the key (a keyed startup alias resuming a Desktop/TUI session) attaches as is. ``typed``
(only :meth:`open_session`'s startup resume, where the user typed ``--api-key`` for that session)
refuses it instead, as the thin client does.

name: open_session
doc:
Create (or resume) the gateway session for this CLI and adopt its id. A resume target the
gateway does not know is left as is: main's own "Session not found" path reports it.

name: create
doc:
``session.create`` with the launch policy (and ``title``: the owner's resolve -> create ->
title step); adopts and returns the new session id. ``record_cwd=False`` (``/new``,
``--create-if-missing``) leaves the row's cwd empty, as main's explicit creates did.

name: client_env
doc: This shell's ``client_env`` when the gateway takes it (one ``runtime.describe`` per store).

name: branch
doc:
``session.mutate branch``: the gateway forks the whole active transcript into a child it
attaches this viewer to; returns the child id (main's /branch then switches to it).

name: rewind_user_turn
doc:
Main's ``SessionDB.rewind_user_turn`` (``/undo N``, ``/retry``) as ``session.mutate rewind``.
The user turn is located on the gateway's snapshot transcript (its rows carry ``row_id``),
checked against the CLI's warm view exactly as main checks it, then rewound by that row id.

name: set_session_yolo
doc:
Main's ``/yolo`` persist hook: the gateway session's own bypass (``config.set yolo``, persisted
on the route), since approvals run there. The CLI's in-process flag stays main's display state.

significant_calls.callee: conn.execute("SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE title = ? AND id != ?", (title, session_id)).fetchone
significant_calls.expression: conn.execute("SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE title = ? AND id != ?", (title, session_id)).fetchone()
conn.execute("SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE title = ? AND id != ?", (title, session_id))

name: _leave
doc:
Drop this viewer's subscription record and return its id. The connection's SessionState holds
the live id (a reconnect resubscribes under a new one); cleared, no later reconnect resumes it.

name: end_session
doc:
Main's ``end_session(sid, reason)``: detach this viewer with ``end_reason``; the owner ends
the idle local row with that reason once no viewer is left (``ended_at`` / ``end_reason``).

name: delete_session_if_empty
doc:
Main's quit-immediately prune, as a gateway delete: only a row with no messages, no title
and no children (checked on the read-only reader; the gateway deletes the lineage).

significant_calls.callee:
conn.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE id = ? AND title IS NULL"
                    " AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM messages WHERE messages.session_id = sessions.id)"
                    " AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sessions child WHERE child.parent_session_id = sessions.id)",
                    (session_id,)).fetchone
significant_calls.expression:

                    " AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM messages WHERE messages.session_id = sessions.id)"
                    " AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sessions child WHERE child.parent_session_id = sessions.id)",

                    (session_id,))

name: banner_inventory
doc:
The current session snapshot's banner fields (``gateway/session_local_inventory``), as
``build_welcome_banner`` kwargs; None until a session is open.

name: _has_created_source_column
doc:
Read-only opens don't migrate, so ``created_source`` may be missing. Only "present" is
cached: a lock or I/O error is not proof of absence, and another connection may add it.

name: _expand
doc:
``(live source labels, created_source labels)`` or None for a raw source filter.

Groups come from session_policy.SURFACES and STORED_AS_LOCAL: gui and desktop are one
conversation (the in-process agent is desktop, the managed worker creates with gui), acp
is stored local too, and tool/oneshot are not cli aliases. Live labels include the other
name of a gui/desktop pair, so a row that has not been peer-refreshed (``source='gui'``)
still matches ``--source desktop``.

name: _watch_reviewer
doc: /review spawns its reviewer off-turn: have the live-work dock poll for it right away.

name: _unbounded
doc:
True for a form answered only once its work is done, however long: a /cron write (``run`` runs the
job). Its reads keep the deadline, and so does an unclosed quote, which the owner refuses at once.

name: run
doc: True when the gateway answered the command (the local handler must not run).

name: wants_service_install
arguments: *, interactive: bool, install: bool=False, config: dict | None=None

name: ensure_gateway_service
arguments: context: str='setup', *, interactive: bool=False, install: bool=False, config: dict | None=None
doc:
Start existing services; install only with explicit setup consent.

Import and ordinary noninteractive callers cannot install, even with a saved
install preference. False leaves foreground/unmanaged startup to the caller.

name: _wizard_install_service
doc: Choose persistence once; start-now without persistence stays unmanaged.

name: _all_platforms
doc:
Built-in ``_PLATFORMS`` plus registry plugin platforms (same dict shape, source in
``_registry_entry``). Plugins are discovered here (idempotent) so the setup menu works without a
running gateway; user-installed ones still need ``plugins.enabled`` (untrusted code). Matrix is
hidden on Windows: python-olm has no wheel or native build (use WSL).

name: _platform_status
doc: Plain-text status string; uncolored because ANSI codes break curses menu width math.

name: _set_platform_unauthorized_dm_behavior
doc: Persist a platform-specific unauthorized-DM policy in config.yaml.

name: confirm_reconfigure
doc: False when ``label`` is already configured (all ``env_vars`` set) and the user declines.

name: offer_home_channel
arguments: home_var: str, user_id: str, what: str
doc: Offer to persist ``user_id`` as ``home_var`` (e.g. "your Telegram user ID").

name: prompt_csv
doc: Comma-separated ID prompt with whitespace stripped.

name: _prompt_unauthorized_access
doc: No allowlist was given — ask open access vs DM pairing vs decline vs skip/silent, and persist.

name: _telegram_auto_setup
doc: Offer the managed-bot QR flow. Returns (token_saved, owner_user_id).

name: _clean_discord_ids
doc: Strip common Discord prefixes (user:123, <@123>, <@!123>) from a comma-separated list.

name: _prompt_allowlist_var
doc: Allowlist prompt for one var; returns the saved value or None (open-access prompt shown).

name: _setup_standard_platform
doc: Interactive setup for Telegram, Discord, or Slack.

name: _builtin_setup_fn
doc: Resolve a built-in platform's setup function; late-bound to dodge the hermes_cli.setup cycle.

name: _configure_platform
doc:
Plugin ``setup_fn`` -> built-in by key -> ``_setup_standard_platform`` (``vars``) -> env-var hint.
Bundled plugins auto-load; user plugins must already be in ``plugins.enabled``.

name: _wizard_offer_service_action
arguments: action: str, question: str, failed_label: str, **kwargs
doc: Wizard start/restart prompt; prints remediation instead when system scope would need root.

name: _setup_service_action
arguments: action: str, *, failed_label: str, windows: bool=True, system: bool=False
doc:
Run a wizard service start/restart, printing remediation instead of raising. ``windows=False``
skips Windows (pre-platform status block never offers it); ``system`` is a fresh install's scope.

name: _wizard_service_status_block
doc: Pre-platform service status: warnings, then offer to start an installed-but-stopped service.

name: _wizard_install_service
doc:
Fresh install from the wizard: ask start-now / start-on-login once, install, then start.

The Windows installer owns its start decision (Scheduled Task and Startup-folder
paths start the gateway themselves when start_now is true, and a UAC hand-off
installs and starts in the elevated child), so the wizard forwards the answers
and returns without a second start. Each install-intent question is asked exactly
once per setup run.

name: _wizard_post_setup
doc: Offer to install/start/restart the gateway once at least one platform has progress.

name: gateway_setup
doc: Interactive setup for messaging platforms + gateway service.

name: connection_for
doc:
The CLI's gateway connection when its session is open, else None (not rewired). A hung-up
connection is returned (its next call redials); only a final one is None.

name: start
doc: Admit the side task on the owner: ``(task_id, wait)``; ``wait()`` -> the answer (raises on failure).

name: _incompatible_owner_verdict
doc:
``incompatible: <reason>`` when the gateway answering for this home is one this Hermes's clients
(TUI, Desktop, chat) refuse, e.g. an older Hermes's daemon left running across an upgrade.

name: report_incompatible_owner
doc:
Print ✗ (with the fix) when the running gateway cannot serve this Hermes; True if printed.
``pids`` names the scanned processes for the manual-run line; empty for a service-managed one.

name: print_standalone_by_config
doc:
Default-profile status: name the profiles that opted out of the host multiplexer by config,
so the served set the host gateway reports is not mistaken for the installed roster.

name: gateway_declares_external_supervisor
doc:
True when the running gateway ``pid`` was launched for an external supervisor.

The supervisor is SELF-declared by the gateway from its launch context: the control socket
``identify`` answer (any launch supervisor other than ``"manual"`` — a custom systemd unit or
launchd agent sets INVOCATION_ID / the XPC name, so the gateway answers ``systemd``/``launchd``
even though ``_installed_service_kind_for`` saw no canonical unit, and the same supervisor owns
the respawn), OR the ``--external-supervisor`` argv marker read live (same marker
``_prepare_profile_gateway_update_restart`` trusts), else the argv the gateway stamped into
``gateway_state.json`` when psutil cannot read the live command line.

name: _wait_for_supervised_gateway_replacement
arguments: old_pid: int, timeout: float | None=None, *, poll_interval: float=0.5
doc:
Poll the pidfile until the supervisor's replacement gateway registers a fresh PID.

A graceful SIGUSR1 exit only proves the old process left — an unloaded, broken, or
stopped-retrying supervisor leaves the gateway down. Custom-supervisor counterpart of
``_wait_for_launchd_service_pid``: the label is invisible to launchctl queries, so identity
comes from ``get_running_pid``'s lock+PID liveness verification and freshness from ``!= old_pid``.
Returns the fresh PID, or None once ``timeout`` passes.

name: restart_externally_supervised_gateway
doc:
Hand ``supervised_pid`` back to its supervisor (SIGUSR1 drain) and report the fresh PID.

Never falls through to SIGTERM + foreground run on either failure branch: that would
SIGTERM a KeepAlive-armed process and stamp this CLI's PID, recreating the competing-owner
wedge (#110637). A broken/unloaded supervisor surfaces as exit 1, not a success printed over
a dead gateway (the contract ``launchd_restart`` enforces via ``_wait_for_launchd_service_pid``).

name: refuse_restart_of_service_managed_gateway
doc:
Refuse the manual restart fallback when systemd owns the gateway under ANY unit name.

Canonical-unit checks miss pre-convention installs (``hermes.service``), so the fallback's
stop + in-process ``run_gateway`` SIGKILLed a live service-managed gateway and spawned an
unsupervised orphan in the caller's cgroup while the unit flapped against the stolen lock
(#126474). Reuses the dashboard's MainPID-verified lookup: a bare ``.service`` cgroup alone
(the caller itself started under some unit) never proves ownership.

name: start_restart_replacement
doc:
Start the manual fallback's replacement once the old owner is gone.

``--detach`` (Desktop's bounded, piped client; the updater's recovery call) starts it the way
``gateway ensure`` starts an absent owner. In the foreground that caller became the long-lived
gateway it only meant to restart: a child its own timeout killed, holding the app's quit open.

name: bind
doc: Called when the CLI's gateway-backed agent is built.

name: bind_session
doc:
Called when the CLI opens its gateway session, so ``/agents``, ``/stop``, the dock and the status
bar read the session's processes before the first turn (a resumed session's work keeps running).

name: process_view
doc:
The gateway-backed registry, or None when this process runs its own tools (not rewired) or
its gateway connection is final (a hang-up keeps the view; its next call redials).

name: process_registry
doc: ``tools.process_registry.process_registry`` for main's dock, status bar and ``/stop``.

name: background_counts
doc: The status bar's ``⚙ N`` processes and running background subagents (cached, no RPC).

name: session_tools
doc:
``/tools``: the gateway session's tool catalog (``tools.show``) as
``(tools, toolset_of)``: ``get_tool_definitions``-shaped rows (first description sentence) and
a name -> toolset lookup. None when the CLI is not gateway-backed.

name: reload_gateway_skills
doc:
Rescan skills in the gateway session too (its skill-command map serves this session's
``/<skill>`` and bundle invocations); the CLI's own rescan still drives main's output.

name: handle_skills_slash
doc:
Main's ``/skills`` (hub search / install / uninstall write the local skills tree), then the
gateway's rescan so an install reaches the skill map the session's turns use, and ``cli``'s copy of
the gateway's skill list is read again.

name: count_running
doc: Cached (the status bar repaints off the render thread).

name: kill_all
doc: ``/stop``: the session's own processes plus its background delegations (``process.stop``).

name: interrupt_delegations
doc: The delegation half of ``/stop`` (``kill_all`` already ran it when processes were live).

name: active_delegations
doc: Running background subagents (the gateway's ``session.usage.active_subagents``).

name: watch_subagents
doc:
Poll ``subagent.list`` for a while even with no turn running: an off-turn spawn
(``/review``) moves neither ``busy`` nor the usage count the gate below reads.

name: subagent_rows
doc:
The session's live children (``subagent.list``). Asks at most once a second, and only
while a turn runs (``busy``), children were listed last time, the gateway counts some, or
an off-turn spawn asked to be watched.

name: subagent_tail
doc:
The child's live transcript tail (``subagent.tail``); None when the gateway has none.
The detail view repaints every frame and reads only the cache; ``fetch`` (the monitor's
tick, on the spinner thread) asks the gateway at most once a second, failures included.

name: subagent_control
doc:
Steer (``subagent.steer``) or stop (``subagent.interrupt``) one child of this session, in
the shape ``delegate_tool_registry._handle_control_action`` answers: ``note`` or ``error``.

name: gateway_store
doc: The CLI's gateway session store, or None (a test double / an unavailable store).

name: queue_admitted_turn
doc:
Idle tick: find a gateway-admitted notification turn's ``message.start`` for this session and
queue main's ``TimelineNotification`` for it. Frames before it are the between-turn leftovers
``run_conversation`` would discard anyway; frames after it stay queued for the pump.

name: _adoption_waiting
doc: An adopted item is still in ``_pending_input`` (one ``/queue clear`` dropped is forgotten).

name: recover_queued
doc:
Idle tick, after the stream had no ``message.start`` for them: this viewer's ``/queue``
admissions the owner started or settled without this viewer painting the turn (a local turn's
drain or pump dropped the start, or it ran across a reconnect, which replays no frames). Read on
a new published pending list or a dropped start only, never every tick.

Still running: adopted and pumped live, its reply completed from the receipt (``recovered``).
Settled: adopted with its saved result, painted without a pump. One that never ran (cancelled,
rejected) is forgotten: the only point where ``queued_inputs`` drops a row unpainted.

name: missed_start
doc:
A frame dropped outside its turn: a ``/queue`` admission's ``message.start`` is remembered so
the idle tick paints that turn from its receipt instead of losing it.

name: _put_first
doc:
Ahead of anything already queued: the gateway is running this turn NOW (typed inputs the
post-turn path re-queued are admitted behind it), and a typed turn run first would drop it.

name: arm_adopted
doc:
The input loop took ``item``: when it is an adopted ``/queue`` admission, the next
``run_conversation`` pumps exactly that admission (``take_admitted_turn``).

name: take_admitted_turn
doc:
The admitted turn ``run_conversation(text)`` replays instead of submitting; None (and the
stale notification adoption dropped) for any other turn. A ``/queue`` admission is matched by the
id ``arm_adopted`` recorded, a notification turn by its model text.

name: _schtasks_encoding
doc:
Console encoding for ``schtasks.exe`` output: localized Windows emits the OEM/ANSI code page,
not UTF-8, and decoding with the wrong codec raised UnicodeDecodeError in subprocess' reader
threads. Prefer the locale's preferred encoding, fall back to UTF-8.

name: _windows_console_encodings
doc:
Code pages a console tool such as ``schtasks.exe`` writes to a pipe, most likely first: the
console output code page (65001 once ``configure_windows_stdio`` ran, else the OEM page), the OEM
page, then the ANSI page. Read from kernel32, so Python's UTF-8 mode cannot disguise them.

name: _decode_schtasks_output
doc:
Decode captured ``schtasks.exe`` bytes. schtasks writes the console/OEM code page even when this
process runs in UTF-8 mode (the launcher sets ``PYTHONUTF8=1``), so ``locale.getpreferredencoding``
is the wrong codec on a non-ASCII account path: ``C:\Users\方舟`` came back as ``����`` and the
Scheduled-Task drift check could never settle (#116193). Strict UTF-8 first (ASCII and genuine
UTF-8 output pass; legacy multi-byte text fails loudly), then the native code pages, then a lossy
fallback so a reader thread never raises.

name: hermes_service_roots
doc:
Directories a Hermes-owned SCM service binary lives under: the checkout (its ``venv`` included),
the running interpreter's ``Scripts`` dir (``hermes.exe`` shim) and the ``gateway-service`` launcher dir.

name: hermes_owns_windows_service
arguments: name: str, binpath: str, hermes_roots: tuple[str, ...]
doc:
Positive ownership of an SCM service: Hermes-named (``hermes*``) or its binary path starts under a
Hermes root. Pure so it is testable off-Windows. A Scheduled-Task-launched gateway descends from
``svchost.exe`` hosting ``Schedule``; without this gate the updater took Task Scheduler for the
gateway's supervisor and ``sc.exe stop Schedule`` aborted every update (#97208).

name: _preserve_hermes_home_path
doc:
Render Hermes-owned paths under the configured HERMES_HOME spelling.

``%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`` may be a symlink/junction to another drive; launcher files must not
bake in the resolved target for paths under HERMES_HOME.

name: _quote_cmd_script_arg
doc:
Quote one argument INSIDE a .cmd file for cmd.exe: split on spaces/tabs outside double quotes,
embedded quotes doubled. Line breaks are refused — they'd end the logical command line.

name: _quote_vbs_string
doc: VBScript double-quoted literal (embedded quote doubled; newline refused).

name: _exec_schtasks
doc:
Run ``schtasks.exe`` with a hard timeout. Return (code, stdout, stderr); a wedge returns
code=124 with a synthetic stderr so the fallback regex matches.

name: _is_running_as_admin
doc:
Return True when the current Windows process is elevated (the shared ``TokenElevation``
probe; ``IsUserAnAdmin`` is deprecated and answered the same question a second way).

name: _current_profile_cli_args
doc: Return CLI args that preserve the current Hermes profile.

name: _launch_elevated_gateway_command
doc:
Launch an elevated gateway subcommand via UAC and return True on handoff. The child is console
``python.exe`` with ``SW_HIDE``: it owns one hidden console its subprocesses (schtasks, taskkill)
inherit — no visible window and no per-descendant conhost flashes (the console-less pythonw.exe
alternative re-created #54220/#56747 for every descendant).

All operator decisions are already collected in the parent shell before this point. See #54220, #56747.

name: _launch_elevated_install
arguments: force: bool=False, *, start_now: bool | None=None, start_on_login: bool | None=None
doc: Launch an elevated gateway install via UAC and return True on handoff.

name: get_task_name
doc: Scheduled Task name, scoped per profile.

name: _sanitize_filename
doc: Remove characters illegal in Windows filenames.

name: get_task_script_path
doc:
The generated ``gateway.cmd`` wrapper under ``<HERMES_HOME>/gateway-service/`` (per-profile
installs stay self-contained); the VBS launcher lives beside it.
