embedded runtime gets the policy guidance instead, so users stop looping on
repair for a block repair can never lift (#63796).

name: _dashboard_prepare_runtime
doc:
Deps check, skills seed, terminal env bridge, plugins, MCP discovery.

Returns ``start_mcp_discovery_after_bind`` for start_server.

name: cmd_dashboard
doc: Start the web UI server, or (with --stop/--status) manage running ones.

name: cmd_completion
doc: Print shell completion script.

name: cmd_logs
doc: View and filter Hermes log files.

name: cmd_console
doc: Open the safe Hermes command console.

name: _first_positional_argv
doc:
First non-flag, non-flag-value token in ``sys.argv[1:]`` (skips values of known flags).

Not a full argparse simulation: an unknown ``--foo bar`` may classify
``bar`` as positional, which at worst forces a one-time plugin discovery.

name: _plugin_cli_discovery_needed
doc:
True when the CLI might be invoking a plugin-registered subcommand.

False skips plugin discovery at argparse setup (~500-650ms). An unknown
first token could be a plugin command OR a chat prompt — either way
discovery is needed; for a prompt its cost amortizes over the agent run.

name: _resolve_deferred_platform_cli_command
doc:
Materialize the deferred platform whose top-level CLI command matches.

Bundled platforms are *deferred* entries (no gateway SDK imports at
startup), so a platform's ``register_cli_command`` side effect only runs
on import; ``discover_plugins()`` alone leaves ``hermes photon`` failing
with ``invalid choice``. Importing just the matching platform keeps
startup cheap.

On the unknown-top-level-command slow path, ``discover_plugins()`` records the deferred loader but does
not import it, so the CLI registration never happens and ``hermes photon`` fails with argparse ``invalid
choice`` (issue #54678).

name: _agent_subcommand_selected
doc: True for ``cron run/tick``, ``gateway run`` (see _AGENT_SUBCOMMANDS).

name: _chat_runs_at_gateway
doc:
Every ``hermes`` / ``hermes chat`` turn (classic view, ``-q``, ``-z``, TUI) executes in the
gateway, which discovers and owns MCP servers itself. Discovery in this client only spawns a
second copy of every server and holds the cross-process discovery lock the cold-starting gateway
then waits on (measured 2.0 s with one stdio server) for tools nothing here ever calls.

name: _prepare_agent_startup
doc: Discover plugins/MCP/hooks for commands that can run an agent turn.

name: _apply_user_config_bypass
doc: Apply the explicit config bypass before any startup config reads.

name: _guard_noninteractive_user_config
doc: Fail closed before a non-interactive invocation initializes providers.

name: _set_chat_arg_defaults
doc: Fill the chat-parser attrs cmd_chat reads when chat was not parsed.

name: _run_oneshot_from_args
doc:
Top-level --oneshot / -z: single-shot mode, stdout = final response only.

Bypasses cli.py entirely; the transport launcher never returns.

name: _light_chat_parser
doc: Top-level + chat parser only (no subcommand tree); chat dispatches to cmd_chat.

name: _promote_top_level_resume
doc: Top-level --resume/--continue with no subcommand is a chat shortcut.

name: _try_fast_serve_launch
doc:
Dispatch an unambiguous built-in ``serve`` without the full CLI tree.

Desktop runs this on every cold start; building every other parser costs
thousands of filesystem-backed lookups on Windows. Unknown or global
arguments fall back to normal parsing so error reporting is unchanged.

name: _try_fast_chat_launch
doc:
Fast path for unambiguous interactive chat launches (all hosts).

Building all ~40 subcommand parsers costs ~140ms the chat path never
uses. Bails out (False) whenever the invocation is not certainly a chat
launch — subcommand positional, ``--help``, unknown flags. Mirrors
``_try_termux_fast_cli_launch`` minus the Termux deferred startup; kept
separate so phone-tuned behavior doesn't leak to desktops.

name: _try_termux_fast_cli_launch
doc: Run obvious Termux non-TUI chat/oneshot/version paths on a light parser.

name: _try_termux_fast_tui_launch
doc:
Launch obvious Termux TUI invocations before building every subparser.

`hermes --tui` is the hot path on phones and the TUI immediately execs
Node, so the full parser's command-module imports are pure waste there.

name: _advertise_agent_env
doc:
Advertise the agent harness to child processes.

``AI_AGENT`` is the cross-agent standard (huggingface_hub reads it); the
value must be our id in the public agent-harness registry
(``hermes-agent``) — matching is exact. ``HERMES_AGENT`` is the
Hermes-specific marker. setdefault: never clobber an outer harness.

``AI_AGENT`` is the emerging cross-agent standard (huggingface_hub's agent detection reads it; pi and
other agents set it — earendil-works/pi#7493) so generic tooling can attribute subprocesses to the
harness that spawned them. Hermes running inside another agent's terminal).

name: _attach_plugin_cli_command
doc: Register one plugin-provided top-level command from its descriptor.

name: _register_plugin_cli_commands
doc:
Register plugin-provided top-level commands (each plugin builds its own argparse tree).

Skipped when the invocation targets a known built-in — eagerly importing
every bundled plugin module costs 500-650ms.

name: _build_cli_parser
doc:
Build the full ``hermes`` argparse tree -> ``(parser, subparsers)``.

Registration ORDER is the ``hermes --help`` order; keep it stable. Groups
live in ``hermes_cli/subcommands/<group>.py`` with handlers injected so
those modules never import main.

name: _parse_cli_args
doc:
Parse ``argv`` with the bpo-9338 subparser-routing workaround.

On Python <3.11 argparse fails to route subcommand tokens when the parent
has nargs='?' optionals (--continue): "unrecognized arguments: model". When
argv holds a known subcommand token, set subparsers.required=True to force
routing; if that fails (``hermes -c model`` — 'model' is the session name)
fall back to the default behaviour.

name: _default_to_chat
doc: No subcommand given: run chat.

name: main
doc: Main entry point for hermes CLI.

name: cmd_acp
doc: Launch Hermes Agent as an ACP server.

name: cmd_monitoring
doc: Gateway monitoring status: health & diagnostics export posture.

name: _cmd_skills_trust
doc:
``hermes skills trust|untrust [path]`` — manage ``skills.trusted_project_dirs``.

With no path, operates on the project root enclosing the current directory
(nearest ancestor with ``.git``).

name: _probe_container
arguments: cmd: list, backend: str, via_sudo: bool=False

name: exec_in_container
doc:
Replace the current process with a command inside the managed container.

Probes whether sudo is needed (rootful containers), then os.execvp
into the container. On success the Python process is replaced entirely
and the container's exit code becomes the process exit code (OS semantics).
On failure, OSError propagates naturally.

Args:
    container_info: dict with backend, container_name, exec_user, hermes_bin
    cli_args: the original CLI arguments (everything after 'hermes')

name: _find_stale_dashboard_pids
arguments: *, exclude_pids: set[int] | None=None, scope_home: str | None=None
doc:
PIDs of running ``dashboard``/``serve`` backends the caller may stop.

*scope_home*: keep only backends whose resolved Hermes home (see
``_hermes_home_for_pid``) is this home; unreadable ownership is spared, never guessed.
``--stop`` and the post-update cleanup pass their own home so another install's or
profile's backend on the same machine is never a target (#113978).

name: _parse_dashboard_runtime
doc:
Best-effort parse of a dashboard/server cmdline into mode, host, and port.

The mode is the canonical holder subcommand, never an argv substring: this gates the launchd
backend inventory (a kill + kickstart path) and ``--status`` (#121156).

name: _dashboard_probe_host
doc: Map wildcard binds to a loopback address suitable for local probing.

name: _run_probe
doc: Captured, text-decoded ``subprocess.run`` for short local probes (systemctl, ps).

name: _restart_managed_dashboard_service
doc:
Restart a systemd-managed dashboard instead of raw-killing its PID.

True when a unit was found and handled (success or printed failure) — which
deliberately stops the caller's ``os.kill`` fallback: systemd treats a direct
SIGTERM as a clean stop, so ``Restart=on-failure`` won't bring it back.

name: _pid_unified_cgroup_entries
doc: Yield the ``0::<path>`` cgroup paths from ``/proc/<pid>/cgroup``; nothing when unreadable.

name: _get_systemd_service_for_pid
doc:
The systemd service unit that supervises *pid* (``hermes-serve.service``), or None.

A ``.service`` cgroup alone only says where the process was started: a dashboard launched by
hand from a shell that itself runs under some unit (a CI runner agent, ``cron.service``, a
tmux or IDE user service, the gateway's own terminal tool) sits in THAT unit's cgroup. The
unit owns the backend only when its live ``MainPID`` is this PID; otherwise restarting it
restarts an unrelated service and leaves the dashboard down. None when the PID isn't part of
a service, ownership can't be proved, the file is unreadable, or off Linux.

name: _unit_main_pid_is
arguments: svc_name: str, cgroup_path: str, pid: int
doc: True when *svc_name*'s live ``MainPID`` is *pid* (read-only ``systemctl show``).

name: _extract_scope_from_cgroup
doc: ``user`` / ``system`` from a cgroup path (``/user.slice/…`` vs ``/system.slice/…``), else None.

name: _get_pid_cgroup_path
doc: The unified (``0::``) cgroup path from ``/proc/<pid>/cgroup``, or None.

name: _systemd_owner_for_pid
doc:
``(unit, scope)`` of the systemd unit whose live ``MainPID`` is *pid*; ``None`` when no unit
provably owns it (see :func:`_get_systemd_service_for_pid`). Scope is ``user``/``system`` or
``None`` when the cgroup path does not say.

name: _systemd_restart_commands
doc: The command(s) that restart *unit* in its scope; both forms when the scope is unknown.

name: _format_restart_commands
doc: Join restart commands as a user-facing hint: each backticked, separated by " or ".

name: _try_restart_systemd_service
doc:
Restart *svc_name* via systemctl (``--user`` for user-scope units). True on success.

Unknown scope tries system first, then user.

name: _loaded_launchd_backend_jobs
doc:
``(domain, label, program_arguments, live_pid)`` for every LOADED launchd job whose
``ProgramArguments`` is a ``hermes dashboard`` / ``hermes serve`` backend. macOS only (empty
elsewhere). Reads the plists (unreadable/malformed ones are skipped) and asks ``launchctl print``
per candidate label — a job that is not loaded in any domain is not returned, so an operator's
stale plist never claims a process.

name: _launchd_job_owning_backend
arguments: pid: int, cmdline: list[str] | None, jobs: list[tuple[str, str, list[str], int | None]], ancestors: list[int] | tuple[int, ...]=()
doc:
``(domain, label, live_pid)`` of the loaded launchd job that owns *pid*: launchd reports *pid*
(or one of its *ancestors* — a plist may wrap the backend in ``/bin/sh -c …`` without ``exec``)
as the job's live process, OR the process runs the job's ``ProgramArguments`` — a detached copy
of a supervised backend (an earlier respawn) holds the port the job needs, and respawning it again
would only re-create that conflict. ``--no-open`` is ignored on both sides: the respawn path adds
it, so an earlier respawn's argv is the plist's plus that flag. None when no loaded job claims
the process.

name: _restart_launchd_job
arguments: domain: str, label: str, old_pid: int | None, *, timeout: float=15.0
doc:
Bring a launchd-supervised backend back after its process was stopped: ``launchctl kickstart
<domain>/<label>`` (no ``-k`` — a KeepAlive job may already have respawned it, and a kill would
take that fresh process down), then require launchd to report a live PID other than *old_pid*
within *timeout*. A kickstart that returns 0 only means "restart requested"; a job that is loaded
but never comes back on a fresh PID is a failure the operator must hear about.

name: _dashboard_cmdline_for_pid
doc:
Exact argv of a running process: ``/proc/<pid>/cmdline`` (Linux), ``ps -o command=`` + shlex
(macOS), None on Windows (no graceful taskkill window; Desktop manages its backend).

name: _respawnable_command_for_current_install
doc:
Rebuild a captured ``[<interpreter>, <hermes launcher>, ...]`` argv on this install's launcher.

A pre-PM-takeover install left ``~/.local/bin/hermes`` as a symlink to a Python console
script, so the kernel recorded a manual backend as ``[<old venv python>, <launcher>, dashboard,
...]``. The takeover then rewrote that launcher into a POSIX shell shim, and replaying the
captured argv verbatim asks the old interpreter to parse a shell script (#124778). This
checkout's own ``hermes`` entry script stays Python, so it and every other shape replay unchanged.

name: _respawn_dashboard_processes
doc:
Respawn manually-started dashboards after ``hermes update``, detached, logging to
``logs/dashboard-restart.log``; returns the argvs that failed to spawn. Callers pre-filter via
``_filter_dashboard_respawn_candidates`` (no Desktop ``--port 0`` backends, capped per profile).

See #78821.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(
                    command, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=log_f, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                    start_new_session=True, close_fds=True)

name: _install_hangup_protection
doc:
Protect ``cmd_update`` from SIGHUP (→ SIG_IGN, inherited by pip/git children) and broken pipes
(stdio wrapped in ``_UpdateOutputStream``). SIGINT/SIGTERM are left alone — legitimate cancels.
Gateway updates are already detached, but still need the log mirror for the
Desktop progress watchdog. Returns state for ``_finalize_update_output``.

name: _finalize_update_output
doc: Restore stdio and close the update.log handle opened by ``_install_hangup_protection``.

name: _report_dashboard_status
doc:
Print live listening dashboard/serve processes and return the count.

Serve-mode backends are INCLUDED: ``--stop`` kills them, so hiding them from
``--status`` let an operator kill what they couldn't see.

Ledger-registered serves (profiled launches the argv scan can't match) surface via the spawn-ledger
augmentation in _scan_dashboard_processes, and the ledger's recorded bind replaces the argv port so
``--port 0`` backends are probed on the port the OS actually gave them. See #81564.

name: _dashboard_listening
doc: True when something accepts TCP connections at host:port (even a 401 proves a dashboard is up).

name: _maybe_setup_dashboard_auth_interactively
doc:
Offer to configure dashboard auth when the gate engages and no provider exists.

``start_server`` fails closed for a non-loopback bind / ``dashboard.public_url``
without a ``DashboardAuthProvider``; prompt an interactive operator first.
No-op (fail-closed backstop stays) when the gate doesn't engage, a provider
exists, or stdin/stdout isn't a TTY.

name: _read_ssh_session_token_file
doc: Read and unlink a Desktop SSH token from its private runtime directory.

name: _is_electron_packaged_web_dist
doc:
True when *path* is an Electron-packaged renderer dist (``app.asar[.unpacked]/dist``).

A standalone ``hermes dashboard`` inheriting that ``HERMES_WEB_DIST`` would
serve the desktop frontend in the browser ("Desktop IPC bridge is unavailable").

name: _host_backend_attachment
doc:
Live host serve/dashboard record to attach to, or ``None``.

Record-based discovery replaces the old bare-TCP probe: "something accepts a connection on
this port" proved nothing about WHO answers (a foreign service, or a recycled PID's new
owner). The record carries ``(pid, createTime)`` so liveness is proved against the same
incarnation, and its token fingerprint must still match the 0600 token file the owner wrote.
The record only nominates a CANDIDATE; :func:`_attach_to_host_backend` makes it prove itself.

name: _explicit_endpoint_flags
doc:
Which of ``--host``/``--port`` the operator actually typed.

argparse defaults are indistinguishable from a typed value in ``args``, and the difference is
load-bearing: an unset ``--port`` may attach to whatever port the host owner bound, but a
typed ``--port 8899`` or ``--host 0.0.0.0`` (LAN access) must never be silently answered with
a loopback attach on some other port.

name: _endpoint_conflict
doc: Why an explicitly requested endpoint cannot be served by ``record`` ('' when it can).

name: _attach_to_host_backend
doc:
Multiplex-only: a second `hermes serve`/`dashboard` attaches to the host backend.

Exactly ONE backend runs per host and multiplexes every profile, so a second invocation —
for ANY profile, the default included — reports the live one and exits 0 instead of binding
a second port. ``--isolated`` opts out (Desktop's SSH backend proves ownership with it) and
Desktop pool backends (HERMES_DESKTOP=1) keep their own lifecycle.

Exit 0 means "the host backend answered and serves what you asked for", and nothing else:

* the owner must ANSWER on its recorded port and identify itself (a record alone cannot see a
  graceful-shutdown window or a foreign listener that inherited the port) — a supervisor or
  `hermes update` relaunch landing in that window would otherwise exit 0 with NOTHING
  listening, reporting success for a dead service;
* an explicitly typed ``--port``/``--host`` the owner cannot serve is a REFUSAL naming the
  owner, never a silent redirect. It exits 78 (EX_CONFIG), the deliberate-refusal code
  ``RestartPreventExitStatus=78`` parks on: exit 1 under ``Restart=always`` was an infinite
  restart loop with nothing listening on the ingress port (#119824);
* a `hermes dashboard` user is never handed a headless backend's URL (no SPA behind it).

Returns normally — leaving the caller to BIND — when no owner answers.

name: _route_named_profile_dashboard
doc:
Route a named-profile launch to the single MACHINE dashboard (per-request ``?profile=`` scoping
makes one server per profile pure fragmentation).

No-record fallback to :func:`_attach_to_host_backend`, which already attached (and exited)
when the host publishes a live rendezvous record: re-exec pinned to ``-p default`` (so
``_apply_profile_override`` can't re-route via the sticky active_profile file). ``--isolated``
opts out; Desktop pool backends (HERMES_DESKTOP=1) stay per-profile. Returns normally when no
routing applies.

name: _resolve_dashboard_web_dist
doc:
Build or validate the web UI dist before the server imports.

``serve`` sets HERMES_SERVE_HEADLESS so mount_spa() stays off. Otherwise build
unless HERMES_WEB_DIST / --skip-build promise a dist — then verify index.html
(else the server serves 404s). --skip-build on the default location gets ONE
recovery build; a caller-managed HERMES_WEB_DIST can't be populated.

name: missing_optional_deps_message
arguments: surface: str, what: str, extra: str

name: smart_app_control_block_message
doc:
Guidance for Windows Smart App Control / Application Control blocking the embedded
Python runtime's ``_ssl`` module, or ``None`` when *error* is not that case.

fastapi/uvicorn import ``ssl``; when the policy blocks the ``_ssl`` DLL, the import
fails with the signature ``DLL load failed ... _ssl`` — and the generic
missing-deps repair loop above can never fix it, so users looped on repair
(#63796). The desktop's embedded runtime is the usual victim; the CLI and the
gateway run on the system Python and stay unaffected.

name: _desktop_dist_exists
doc: Return True when a local desktop renderer build is present.

name: _renderer_bundle_dir
doc:
The renderer ``dist`` a launch loads: ``apps/desktop/dist`` in source mode, else the
``app.asar.unpacked/dist`` copy (the only real directory, and the one an interrupted replace tears).

name: _packaged_resources_dir
doc: The packaged app's ``resources`` dir (renderer bundle, baked ``install-stamp.json``).

name: _renderer_bundle_torn
doc:
True when ``index.html`` names hashed module chunks that aren't there.

A replace interrupted by locked files leaves index and ``assets/`` from
different generations; the app dies on its first lazy import while the
SOURCE-tree stamp still matches, so no rebuild fixes it. Conservative: an
unreadable index or one naming nothing checkable is NOT torn.

name: _packaged_node_pty_missing
doc:
True when the packaged node-pty has no native binary for this OS.

The main process requires node-pty at startup, so such a package dies
before any window opens while the source stamp still matches (#62462).
Same places node-pty's loader and stage-native-deps.mjs look. Conservative:
a package without node-pty at all is not judged here.

name: _desktop_build_needed
arguments: desktop_dir: Path, project_root: Path, *, source_mode: bool
doc: True when the desktop build output is stale, missing, torn, or built in the other mode.

name: _packaged_desktop_current_for_head
doc:
True when the packaged app was built from HEAD and none of its inputs changed since.

Freshness alone cannot answer this for an update: the baked ``install-stamp.json`` is a
desktop input that only the build itself rewrites, so after a pull that touched no other
desktop input the receipt still reads current while the app names the previous commit.
The commit the packaged app actually ships is the missing half; anything unreadable
means "build".

name: _desktop_packaged_executable
doc: Return the current platform's unpacked Electron app executable.

name: _desktop_packaged_executable_in
doc:
The unpacked Electron app executable under *release_dir* (live ``release`` or a staging dir).

*release_dir* is electron-builder's ``directories.output`` — the live ``apps/desktop/release`` or a
stage-and-swap staging dir (#86443).

name: _rename_riding_out_file_lock
doc: ``os.rename`` that retries a transient PermissionError with bounded backoff; re-raises the last one.

name: _desktop_staging_dir
doc:
Fresh staging dir ``apps/desktop/.staging-<pid>-<ts>``: a sibling of ``release/`` (same fs → the
swap is a rename) but not inside it, so ``release/*-unpacked`` globs never see it. Sweeps leftovers.

name: _desktop_unpacked_root
doc: The dir directly under *release_dir* holding *exe* (electron-builder's ``appOutDir``, swapped whole).

name: _recover_interrupted_swap
doc:
Finish a swap that died between its two renames before starting a new one: a missing
``live`` with its ``aside`` copy present means the previous app was moved out and nothing
moved in, so put it back; otherwise ``aside`` is leftover. Deleting ``aside`` first (as the
swappers used to) destroyed the only remaining copy of the app.

name: _swap_staged_desktop_app
doc:
Promote a VERIFIED staged pack over ``release/`` by two renames (live → ``.previous``, staged →
live); a failure between them rolls back. Returns the live exe or None (live app kept). Never raises.

name: _windows_user_runnable_pe_machines
doc:
PE machines this host runs in user mode via GetMachineTypeAttributes (the only API reporting
AMD64-on-ARM64 emulation); None when unavailable (pre-Win11 22000) so callers fall back.

name: _windows_native_machine
doc: Return the native Windows machine name in upper-case PE vocabulary.

name: _expected_windows_pe_machines
doc:
PE machines this Windows host can load: ``GetMachineTypeAttributes``, else by name (AMD64 → x64+x86,
ARM64 → ARM64+x64, x86 → x86). Unknown hosts get the full set so the gate can never brick launch.

name: _parse_pe_machine
doc:
COFF machine field of the PE at ``path``; ``ValueError`` with a readable reason when it is not a
structurally complete PE (bad magic, truncated header, section data past EOF). Header walk only.

name: _desktop_exe_integrity_error
doc: Why ``path`` cannot run on this Windows host, or None when it parses as a loadable PE.

name: _electron_dir
doc:
The installed Electron package dir: workspace-local ``apps/desktop/node_modules/electron`` (where
``electronDist`` points) when present, else the root hoist npm sometimes uses instead.

name: _runs_from
doc: True when *proc*'s executable lives inside *release_dir* (False when it cannot be read).

name: _desktop_ancestor_in
doc:
PID of a Desktop from this build's ``release`` tree that is one of OUR ancestors, else None.

That Desktop is running this process (its backend's launch-time update tail, or a
`hermes update` it spawned). On Windows it holds the exe lock the promotion rename
needs, and it cannot be stopped without killing this process first. Never raises.

name: _stop_desktop_processes_locking_build
doc:
Terminate a running desktop app whose exe lives INSIDE this build's ``release`` tree.

Windows needs it everywhere: the exe lock makes the pack die with ``Access is denied``.
POSIX can rename a running app's files away, so the pack itself needs no stop — but a
renderer left alive through the stage-and-swap promotion keeps fetching its OLD hashed
chunks by path after the swap and dies on the next lazy import (#109643), so the swap
point passes ``also_posix=True``. Never raises; returns the PIDs asked to stop.

name: _desktop_macos_bundle_id
doc: Return a bundle/framework CFBundleIdentifier for local macOS signing.

name: _desktop_macos_local_signing_identity
doc:
``desktop.macos_signing_identity`` — a persistent (even self-signed) code-signing cert anchors
the Designated Requirement and keeps TCC grants stable across rebuilds. Unset → ad-hoc.

name: _macos_signature_summary
doc:
Best-effort signing identity of a ``.app`` bundle: ``{team, identifier, verified}``.

``None`` when the bundle has no readable signature (``codesign -dv`` fails — e.g. an
unsigned bundle). ``team``/``identifier`` are ``None`` when the signature lacks them
(ad-hoc signatures report ``TeamIdentifier=not set``); ``verified`` is the strict
``--verify --deep --strict`` result. Never raises.

name: _macos_signing_downgrade_error
doc:
Reason to refuse swapping a publisher-signed installed app for ``rebuilt``, or None.

#123748: replacing a Developer ID (Team ID) installation with a locally signed or
ad-hoc rebuild — or any bundle whose signing identity or bundle identifier differs —
invalidates the code-hash-bound keychain ACLs the app's safeStorage credentials are
encrypted under and resets TCC grants. Ad-hoc-to-ad-hoc replacement (the local
development flow) is untouched. ``installed`` is a ``_macos_signature_summary`` dict;
``rebuilt`` is None when the rebuilt bundle has no readable signature.

name: _desktop_macos_has_valid_real_signature
doc:
True when the bundle has an intact Team-ID signature, so the fixup never clobbers a notarized
build with ad-hoc (resets TCC). A STALE real signature fails --verify → False → repairable.

name: _desktop_macos_local_codesign
arguments: app: Path, *, desktop_dir: Path, identity: str='-'
doc:
Sign a local build inside-out (Mach-O files, nested frameworks/helpers, main bundle) with the
repo's entitlements and an identifier-pinned DR when ad-hoc — a plain ``--deep --sign -`` gives
a cdhash-only DR (TCC re-prompts every rebuild) and strips the JIT/mic entitlements.
Raises on signing failure; True after strict verification.

name: _macos_legacy_adhoc_resign
doc:
Legacy deep ad-hoc re-sign; NEVER deletes the safeStorage keychain item (that would orphan every
credential under it, and there is no verified successor identity here — the "Always Allow"
prompt is recoverable, deletion is not).

name: _desktop_macos_relaunchable_fixup
arguments: desktop_dir: Path, *, publisher_signing_configured: Optional[bool]=None, release_dir: Optional[Path]=None
doc:
Re-sign a locally-built macOS app so in-place self-update doesn't reset TCC grants.

A rebuilt ad-hoc bundle (new cdhash, no stable Designated Requirement) reports
"Hermes is damaged" and loses every grant. Clear quarantine xattrs, then sign
with ``desktop.macos_signing_identity`` or identifier-pinned ad-hoc, keeping
entitlements. When a configured identity fails (#121857): over a locally-signed
install, retry identifier-pinned ad-hoc before the cdhash-only legacy sign;
over a publisher-signed (Team ID) install, refuse — the weaker signature would
orphan the keychain ACLs and TCC grants the update was asked to preserve
(#123748). No-op with a publisher identity (CSC_LINK / APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY;
callers may pass the decision so a later dotenv load can't reverse it) or an
intact Developer ID signature. ``release_dir`` signs the STAGED bundle before
promotion. Never raises.

name: _app_asar_hash
doc: Return the SHA-256 hex digest of an app bundle's app.asar, or None.

name: _swap_in_new_macos_bundle
arguments: tmp: Path, target: Path, old: Path
doc: Move a staged macOS bundle into place without losing the old bundle.

name: _running_macos_app_bundles
doc:
``.app`` bundles of every live Hermes Desktop process. A running bundle is never swapped
under: Electron loads ``app.asar`` chunks and helper apps lazily, so renaming its bundle away
and deleting the old tree crashes the live app (the detached updater waits for it to exit).

name: _stage_macos_bundle_copy
doc:
``ditto`` copies a bundle with its signature, xattrs and symlinks intact (``shutil`` drops
the resource-fork metadata codesign verifies).

name: _install_rebuilt_desktop_app
doc:
Copy the rebuilt macOS bundle into every stale or missing installed ``Hermes.app`` in
*candidates* (``_installed_desktop_apps()``) (#52339).

``hermes desktop --build-only`` (what ``hermes update`` runs) packages into
``apps/desktop/release/`` only. Finder, the Dock and Spotlight launch the copy in
``/Applications`` (or ``~/Applications``), so without this step every update leaves the
installed shell one build behind the backend it boots. The detached Desktop updater swaps
only the bundle it was launched from, so an app running from ``release/`` never refreshed
the installed copy either.

Returns ``(installed, problems)``: bundles that were (re)installed, and one user-facing line per
bundle that could not be (running, copy or swap failure). Both empty means every installed
copy was already current.

name: _refresh_installed_desktop_apps
doc:
Install the rebuilt bundle over stale or missing installed copies, report each outcome, and
record which copies this update keeps current.

name: _update_owned_macos_bundles
doc:
The existing bundles in *candidates* that only ``hermes update`` keeps current (#52339).

Ownership comes from the bundle's own ``install-stamp.json``. ``updateMechanism: self`` is a
bootstrap build (a local pack or the bootstrap download), and stamps older than the field
predate every self-updating kind. Bundled/light releases update themselves and commit builds
are external, so a local build must never be copied over them. No readable stamp, no claim.

name: _owns_installed_desktop_apps
doc:
A packaged app runs the checkout under the default Hermes home, so only that checkout (on
macOS) may build for it: a bundle from any other tree (a dev worktree) would split shell from
backend.

name: _installed_desktop_apps
doc:
Installed macOS ``Hermes.app`` bundles this checkout's update owns.

When no owned copy is left, a recorded one that has gone missing still counts: its ownership
stamp left with the bundle, and without the record nothing would ever put it back (Finder, the
Dock and Spotlight lose Hermes for good). A copy moved to the other Applications folder keeps
its stamp, so it is found instead of doubled. Hermes' GUI uninstall deletes the record.

name: _installed_desktop_launch_target
doc:
The executable ``hermes desktop`` launches: the installed app once it IS the checkout build.

Finder, the Dock and Spotlight open the installed ``Hermes.app``; launching the ``release/``
bundle beside it ran the same app from a second path while the installed copy went stale
(#52339). Refresh the installed copies, then launch the first one that matches the checkout
build. The checkout bundle stays the fallback: nothing installed, or a copy that is running
or could not be replaced.

name: _install_rebuilt_macos_bundles
arguments: rebuilt_app: Path, candidates: list[Path], *, running: set[Path]
doc:
Stage-and-swap ``rebuilt_app`` into each bundle path in ``candidates`` that is missing or
whose ``app.asar`` differs. The rebuilt bundle already carries the stable local signing identity and no
quarantine xattr (``_desktop_macos_relaunchable_fixup``); ``ditto`` preserves both, so nothing
is re-signed here and TCC grants survive. A publisher-signed (Team ID) installation is never
replaced by a locally signed build or a different signing/bundle identity — the swap is
refused and reported instead (#123748).

name: _force_adhoc_macos_signing
doc:
Force ad-hoc signing for the local packaged rebuild: with ``CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY`` on,
electron-builder grabs any personal keychain cert and stalls the sign step or clobbers a
notarized signature. No-op for source runs, off-macOS, with a real identity, or when pinned.

name: _desktop_linux_needs_no_sandbox
doc:
True when Electron should run ``--no-sandbox``: Ubuntu 23.10+ ``apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns``
breaks the userns sandbox without a root-owned 4755 helper. Deliberately NOT True for root —
Electron as root without a sandbox must stay an explicit choice.

name: _desktop_linux_userns_sandbox_available
doc:
True when the unprivileged userns sandbox works (probed with ``unshare``, fails closed) — then
the setuid ``chrome-sandbox`` helper is never consulted and no sudo prompt is needed.

name: _sandbox_helper_lstat
doc: ``(chrome-sandbox path, lstat or None)`` — lstat so a symlink is inspected, not followed.

name: _desktop_linux_sandbox_helper_is_regular_file
doc: Return True when ``chrome-sandbox`` exists as a regular file.

name: _desktop_linux_sandbox_fixup
doc: Configure Electron's Linux SUID sandbox helper when required.

name: _desktop_linux_needs_disable_setuid_sandbox
doc:
True when a present, non-setuid ``chrome-sandbox`` would make Chromium abort with
``setuid_sandbox_host`` despite a working userns sandbox (call after the fixup's userns path).

name: _detect_linux_password_store
doc:
Chromium password-store backend for this Linux session (KDE env → GNOME Keyring socket → D-Bus
ping of org.freedesktop.secrets), or None. Chromium's own detection fails under the launcher
env, and safeStorage then reports encryption unavailable.

name: _desktop_launch_options
doc:
``desktop.*`` launch options: ``(electron_flags, disable_gpu "auto"/"1"/"0", password_store,
ozone_hint "auto"/"x11"/"wayland", renderer_accessibility bool)``; unknown values and config
errors yield "auto"/[]/True so a malformed config never blocks the launch.

name: _register_linux_desktop_entry
doc:
Install the XDG desktop entry for Hermes Desktop (Linux only, best-effort).

``Exec`` and ``Icon`` are absolute so the entry works outside a login shell.
``hermes uninstall --gui`` removes it.

``defer=True`` (app-grid launch) returns a ``DeferredDesktopEntryInstall`` that writes the
entry only once the Electron window is on screen (#111906); ``None`` when nothing is
pending. Terminal, detached and ``--build-only`` launches install synchronously.

name: _promote_staged_desktop_app
arguments: desktop_dir: Path, staging_dir: Path, *, integrity_check: Optional[Callable[[Path], Optional[str]]]=None
doc: Sign and verify before swapping; the default integrity check is Windows PE validation.

name: _diagnose_esbuild_ignore_scripts
doc:
Print an actionable hint when a desktop build failed because esbuild's platform
binary was never staged (`ignore-scripts=true` skips esbuild's postinstall, so the
``@esbuild/<platform>`` optional dependency is absent) — #53082. Best-effort: only
adds context, never masks the original error.

name: build_prepared_desktop
arguments: desktop_dir: Path, *, source_mode: bool, npm: str, env: dict, icons: Path | None=None
doc: Build prepared desktop sources, then publish the verified staged app.

name: _prefer_wsl_d3d12
doc:
Under WSLg, /dev/dxg alone does not make Mesa pick the GPU: Chromium still lands on
llvmpipe unless GALLIUM_DRIVER selects d3d12, and it must be set before Electron spawns
its GPU process (setting it from JS is too late). Explicit Mesa choices win; hosts without
the driver are left alone.

name: _desktop_launch_env
doc:
Electron child env + config-supplied extra flags. ``desktop.*`` config is bridged to env vars
Electron already reads; an explicit env var wins over config (and over keychain detection).

name: _check_desktop_skip_build
arguments: desktop_dir: Path, project_root: Path, *, source_mode: bool, packaged_executable: Optional[Path]
doc: Validate the pre-built artifact ``--skip-build`` promised; exit with a hint when it's missing.

name: _packaged_desktop_launch_command
doc: ``[exe, *sandbox flags]`` after the Linux sandbox fixup; exits when the sandbox can't be configured.

name: _site_packages_install_kind
doc:
The package manager owning a non-editable install at *project_root*, or None.

A package-manager install (Homebrew, pip, distro packaging) places this
code in a ``site-packages``/``dist-packages`` tree. Such a tree ships no
``apps/desktop`` source, so the build ladder below can never run — the
caller must not treat it like a broken checkout. A Homebrew formula lives
under a ``Cellar`` directory; any other site-packages owner is reported
generically as pip.

name: _launch_installed_macos_desktop_app
doc:
Launch a separately installed ``/Applications/Hermes.app``, if present.

Returns True only when the app bundle exists and a detached launch was
started — the caller then exits without touching the build ladder.

name: cmd_gui
doc: Build and launch the native Electron desktop GUI.

name: _explicit_profile_args
doc:
``--profile <name>`` for Electron when ``-p``/``--profile`` was on argv.

Explicit flag only. A bare `hermes desktop` must not forward the sticky CLI
profile — Electron would persist it over the stored desktop one.

name: _launch_bundled_desktop
arguments: args: argparse.Namespace, env: dict, electron_flags: list[str]
doc:
Start the desktop app this CLI ships inside, then exit.

A bundled install has no source tree to build: the app is a signed,
read-only artifact and this Python is a passenger in its resources.
So the whole build ladder below is skipped and the launcher is started
DETACHED — the user ran a CLI command, and the app must outlive the
terminal it was typed into. The app's own single-instance lock turns a
second run into "focus the running window".

Never returns.

name: sign_path
arguments: path: Path, *, entitlements: Optional[Path]=None, identifier: Optional[str]=None, runtime: bool=True

name: _macos_codesigning_identity_valid
doc:
True when `identity` is among VALID (``-v``) code-signing identities — the plain listing also
shows untrusted certs codesign refuses. Idempotency probe + postcondition. Never raises.

name: _macos_create_signing_identity
arguments: openssl: str, security: str, codesign: str, keychain: str, identity: str
doc: Create a self-signed code-signing cert (10 years), import it with codesign access, trust it for codeSign.

name: _desktop_macos_setup_tcc_identity
doc:
``--setup-tcc-identity``: create/import a self-signed code-signing cert, point
``desktop.macos_signing_identity`` at it and re-sign the packaged app. TCC grants follow the
signing identity, so a certificate-anchored one is stable across rebuilds (the yabai/skhd
mechanism). Idempotent; never raises.

name: _pyproject_project
doc: ``[project]`` table of pyproject.toml, or ``None`` when absent/unreadable.

name: _pytest_owns_live_checkout
doc:
True under pytest when ``root`` is this checkout: unsandboxed update/recovery tests must
neither litter the live repo root with breadcrumbs (false-arming the developer's next launch)
nor run a real reinstall against the executing venv (cf. ``managed_scope._under_pytest``).

name: _clear_marker_file
doc: Remove an update-recovery breadcrumb. Never raises.

name: _clear_update_incomplete_marker
doc: Remove the interrupted core-install breadcrumb. Never raises.

name: _clear_lazy_refresh_incomplete_marker
doc: Remove the interrupted lazy-refresh breadcrumb. Never raises.

name: _reexec_dependency_sync_off_windows_shim
doc: Stop a mixed old-code/new-files updater at the retired sync boundary.

name: _venv_scripts_dir
doc: Return the venv Scripts directory if we're running inside the project venv.

name: _hermes_exe_shims
doc:
Entry-point shims uv may rewrite during ``pip install -e .`` — Windows .exe launchers
only; POSIX shims are plain scripts replaced atomically.

name: _filter_pending_shim_renames
doc:
Drop our ``<shim>`` -> ``<shim>.old.<stamp>`` pairs from a PendingFileRenameOperations
value (a flat REG_MULTI_SZ of (source, target) pairs shared with other installers).
Returns the entries to keep and how many pairs were dropped.

name: _cleanup_pending_shim_renames
doc:
Drop reboot renames older Hermes versions queued for our shims: ``MOVEFILE_DELAY_UNTIL_REBOOT``
fallbacks outlive the update that queued them and move away whatever sits at the shim path
at next boot — even a shim a later repair just wrote. Needs elevation; a no-op otherwise.

name: _quarantine_stamp_ms
doc:
The ``.old.<unix-ms>`` stamp in a quarantine filename; ``None`` (not ours — neither rescued
nor deleted) otherwise. Parsed from the NAME, not ``st_mtime``: ``rename`` preserves the
shim's mtime (when uv wrote it), not when it was quarantined.

name: _recover_update_debts_on_startup
doc: The startup half of a previous update, run on every launch before dispatch.

name: _cleanup_quarantined_exes
doc:
Sweep — and where necessary RESCUE — ``hermes.exe.old.*`` from updates.

Called early on every invocation. Two cases an unconditional ``unlink()`` gets wrong:
(1) orphan rescue — ``hermes.exe`` missing while ``hermes.exe.old.*`` exists means the .old
file is the ONLY surviving copy (update died between rename and uv's write); put it back via
the same retry-and-report helper the update-time restore uses. (2) concurrency — a fresh
quarantine file may belong to an update in flight in another process; leave anything inside
the grace window alone. Silent no-op on non-Windows, nothing to do, or locked/permission errors.

Deleting it converts a one-rename recovery into a full reinstall. See #75584.

name: _configured_features_missing_deps
doc:
Check configured platforms/MCP in the fresh, selected update-build child.

PM preserves recorded extras atomically, but configuration can reference an
unselected SDK. Never call this in the updater's stale import graph (#10651).
Rows are ``(label, hint, candidate extra)``: a platform's SDK is the extra named after it.

name: _install_configured_features_missing_deps
doc:
Add the extras configured features need to the dependency environment (#124228).

Recorded extras never follow config, so an enabled platform whose SDK is not
selected would come up without its adapter after the gateway restart.

name: _load_console_script_names
doc: Return ``[project.scripts]`` entry-point names from pyproject.toml.

name: _is_windows_npm_path
doc:
True if ``npm_path`` points at a Windows npm shim (WSL drive interop, ``.cmd``/``.exe``, UNC).

Callers use this only on a POSIX host — on native Windows ``npm.cmd`` is correct.

name: _resolve_node_runtime_npm
doc:
PM's npm, refused on a POSIX host when it is a Windows shim (EISDIR over WSL UNC paths, #30271).

Never re-scans the user's PATH for another npm: Hermes runs only its PM-managed toolchain.

name: _resolve_update_branch
doc: Normalize ``args.branch`` to a non-empty name (default ``main``; blank/whitespace = default).

name: _yes_no
doc: ``[y/N]`` prompt; Ctrl-C/EOF counts as "no".

name: _whatsapp_choose_mode
doc: Step 1 of ``hermes whatsapp``: ``"bot"`` / ``"self-chat"``, or None when cancelled.

name: _whatsapp_allowed_users
doc: Step 3 of ``hermes whatsapp``: show / set WHATSAPP_ALLOWED_USERS.

name: _whatsapp_install_bridge
doc: Step 4 of ``hermes whatsapp``: ``npm install`` the bridge when needed. False = stop.

name: cmd_whatsapp
doc: Set up WhatsApp: choose mode, configure, install bridge, pair via QR.

name: cmd_whatsapp_cloud
doc:
Set up WhatsApp Business Cloud API (official Meta integration) — complementary to the
``hermes whatsapp`` Baileys bridge wizard. See ``plugins/platforms/whatsapp_cloud/setup_wizard.py``.

name: cmd_slack
doc:
``hermes slack <subcommand>``; ``manifest`` prints or writes a Slack app manifest with
every gateway command registered as a first-class slash.

name: _uninstall_keeps_data
doc:
True when ``uninstall <args>`` removes no user data.

Parsed with the real ``uninstall`` subparser so abbreviations (``--dat``, ``--fu``) resolve
exactly as they will for the handler. ``--full`` wipes the default root, which also holds
every other profile under ``profiles/``, without asking, so it is refused like ``--data``.
The plain interactive menu still offers a full wipe, but only behind its own confirmations.

name: is_stale_profile_recovery_command
doc: ``profile list``, ``profile use default``, or an ``uninstall`` that keeps user data.

name: _is_profile_api_key_provider
doc:
True when *provider_id* maps to a profile with ``auth_type='api_key'`` — the catch-all
in select_provider_and_model() so plugin providers dispatch to the generic key flow.

name: _short_url
doc: ``https://host/path/`` -> ``host/path`` for menu labels.

name: _clear_stale_openai_base_url
doc:
Remove OPENAI_BASE_URL from ~/.hermes/.env unless the active provider is 'custom' — a
leftover value routes provider:auto auxiliary clients to the old custom endpoint.

name: _all_aux_tasks
doc:
Built-in aux tasks (in order) followed by plugin-registered ones
(:meth:`hermes_cli.plugins.PluginContext.register_auxiliary_task`).

name: _format_aux_current
doc: Render the current aux config for display in the task menu.

name: _aux_effort_word
doc: The stored ``reasoning_effort`` as a display word ("" = provider default; YAML False = "none").

name: _delegation_cfg_as_task
doc:
Project the top-level ``delegation`` section into aux-task shape (provider/model/
base_url/api_key); an empty provider means "inherit parent" and renders as "auto".

name: _aux_task_cfg
doc: The stored routing dict for *task* (delegation reads its top-level section).

name: _aux_task_cfg_for_display
doc:
The routing dict to *display* for *task*. A plugin task registered with ``inherit_from``
shows its resolved route (base included), so the menu never reports "auto" while the task
actually runs on the base's provider; every other task shows exactly what is stored.

name: _aux_task_display_name
doc: Display name for a task key, covering the special delegation entry.

name: _save_aux_choice
arguments: task: str, *, provider: str, model: str='', base_url: str='', api_key: str='', reasoning_effort: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Persist an aux task's four routing fields (timeout etc. untouched; main model config never
modified). ``delegation`` writes the top-level section, with "auto" stored as an empty provider.
``reasoning_effort``: a level word or "" (provider default) to write; None leaves the key alone.

name: _aux_task_takes_reasoning
doc:
Whether the task's config block honours ``reasoning_effort``. MoA slots and
``memory_query_rewrite`` omit the key by design (``config_defaults._aux``); ``review``
routes through delegation which reads ``delegation.reasoning_effort``, not its own block.

name: _prompt_aux_reasoning_effort
doc:
Effort step for an aux task: a level, "none", "" (provider default / inherit parent), or None to
keep current. The empty-value row is "Inherit parent" for delegation (a child inherits the parent's
effort; wording from #105431 by @fangliquanflq) and "Provider default" for aux tasks.

name: _reset_aux_to_auto
doc: Reset every known aux task (built-in + plugin) back to auto/empty. Returns number reset.

name: _aux_config_menu
doc: Top-level auxiliary-model picker; loops until the user picks "Back".

name: _aux_select_for_task
doc:
Pick a provider + model for one aux task and persist it. Rows come from
``build_aux_picker_rows()`` (shared substrate): only already-configured providers appear.

name: _aux_flow_provider_model
arguments: task: str, provider_slug: str, curated_models: list, current_model: str='', current_effort: str=''
doc:
Prompt for a model under an already-authenticated provider (then its reasoning effort),
save to aux.

name: _aux_flow_custom_endpoint
doc: Prompt for a direct OpenAI-compatible base_url + optional api_key/model.

name: _ask_index
arguments: prompt: str, count: int, *, echo_cancel: bool
doc:
Numbered-menu input loop: 0-based index in ``range(count)``, ``None`` on blank,
``_CANCELLED`` on Ctrl-C/EOF (*echo_cancel* prints a blank line first).

name: _prompt_provider_choice
doc:
Provider menu with curses arrow keys; numbered-list fallback when curses is unavailable
(piped stdin, non-TTY). Returns the selected index, or None if the user cancels.

name: _prompt_custom_api_mode_selection
doc: Prompt for a custom provider API mode: an explicit mode string, or None for auto-detect.

name: _auto_provider_name
doc:
Display name from a custom endpoint URL, e.g. "Local (localhost:11434)" or
"RunPod (xyz.runpod.io)" — the default offered during custom endpoint setup.

name: _custom_provider_api_key_config_value
doc: Return the value that should be persisted for a custom provider key.

name: _custom_provider_base_url_config_value
doc: Return the value that should be persisted for a custom provider URL.

name: _save_custom_provider
arguments: base_url, api_key='', model='', context_length=None, name=None, api_mode=None, key_env=''
doc:
Save a custom endpoint to ``custom_providers`` in config.yaml, deduplicated by base_url (an
existing entry gets model / context_length / api_mode updated). *key_env* set means the caller
already wrote the key to ``.env``; the entry references it instead of inlining the secret.

See #69449.

name: _remove_custom_provider
doc: Let the user remove a saved custom provider from config.yaml.

name: _prompt_reasoning_effort_selection
doc:
Prompt for a reasoning effort. Returns a level, 'none', "" (only with *default_label*: the
"use the provider default" row), or None to keep current.

name: _model_choice_save_count
doc: Snapshot taken by ``select_provider_and_model`` before a flow runs (see below).

name: _offer_reasoning_after_pick
doc:
Post-flow effort step for ``select_provider_and_model``, like the chat ``/model`` picker:
every flow persists through ``_save_model_choice``, so whenever one saved a pick (or
``model.default`` changed) offer the effort for the saved model + provider, including a
provider switch that keeps the same model ID or a re-pick of the current model. Cancel /
"No change." never prompts.

name: _prompt_main_reasoning_effort
doc:
The effort step every ``hermes model`` flow shares: after a main-model pick, offer the
model's supported levels (Copilot publishes a per-model set; everything else gets the full
ladder) and persist ``agent.reasoning_effort``. Skipped when the catalog says the route has
no reasoning control; "Skip" leaves the current value alone.

name: _main_model_reasoning_efforts
doc: Levels to offer for *model* on *provider*: None when the route has no reasoning control.

name: _prompt_api_key
arguments: pconfig, existing_key: str, provider_id: str='', existing_source: str=''
doc:
API-key entry for ``hermes setup`` / ``hermes model``: first-time entry, or [K]eep / [R]eplace /
[C]lear when a key exists (a malformed paste is recoverable without editing ``.env``).
Returns ``(resolved_key, abort)``; ``abort=True`` means the caller must ``return`` at once.

name: _infer_stepfun_region
doc: Infer the current StepFun region from the configured endpoint.

name: _run_anthropic_oauth_flow
doc: Run the Claude OAuth setup-token flow. Returns True if credentials were saved.

name: _named_custom_provider_map
doc: Saved custom providers keyed by slug, with raw ``${ENV}`` refs preserved.

name: _build_provider_picker_rows
arguments: config: dict, active: str, provider_labels: dict[str, str], custom_provider_map: dict[str, dict[str, str]]
doc:
Rows for the ``hermes model`` provider picker plus the pre-selected index. Canonical providers
fold into display groups (PROVIDER_GROUPS): a group row's ``members`` drive a sub-picker, leaf
rows have ``members == []``; saved custom providers and trailing actions stay flat. Honors
``model_catalog.excluded_providers`` (slug or alias, case-insensitive) like the gateway/TUI.

name: _clear
arguments: entry: dict, auto: str, task: str=''

name: _paste_token
doc: Manual setup-token entry: True saved, False empty, None cancelled.

name: _lookup_ref
arguments: refs: dict[tuple, str], name: str, provider_key: str, model: str

name: _read_query_file
doc:
--query-file: read the single query from a file (or stdin via '-').

Callers never have to shell-quote message bodies — this is the transport
the Bot Mode DM protocol uses; interpolating arbitrary text into a
double-quoted shell argument truncates on quotes and executes $(...)
(see tools/bot_mode_probe.py).

name: import_foreign_resume
doc: --resume @claude / @codex: import a foreign session and resume it.

name: _frozen_cwd
doc:
The cwd the owner runs *session_id*'s tools in (its local policy), or "" without one. The
row's cwd is main's stamp, which for a classic ``-w`` session is the repo root, not the tree.

name: recreate_resumed_tui_worktree
doc:
A resumed session whose frozen cwd is a ``-w`` / ``--tui -w`` tree that quit removed gets that
tree back before attaching, or the owner refuses every turn ``workspace_unavailable`` (N8).

name: _bypass_chat_launch
doc:
--safe-mode / --ignore-user-config chat: the gateway owner freezes code defaults and runs
the turn out of process, so the profile's display.interface must not pick a surface and the
client performs no discovery. Explicit --tui forwards the flags in its session.create policy.

name: _short_resume_id
doc:
The 22-char prefix of a canonical ``local-…`` id when it names only that session (``--resume``
resolves a unique prefix back); every other id, or an ambiguous prefix, prints whole.

name: _branch_lineage
doc:
*session* plus each ``/branch`` ancestor it was cut from. Main's epilogue after ``/branch`` still
named the parent and so reported the conversation's tokens; a canonical branch child is named
itself, and its copied history was billed on the ancestors.

name: _print_tui_exit_summary
doc: Print a shell-visible epilogue after TUI exits.

name: _find_bundled_tui
doc: Find a pre-built TUI entry.js bundled in the wheel.

name: _restore_tui_workspace
doc:
Best-effort ``git restore`` of a missing ``ui-tui/`` (Windows AV/NTFS filters can delete
tracked files after ``hermes update``); True when the directory exists afterwards.

On Windows an antivirus / NTFS filter driver can leave tracked ``ui-tui/`` files deleted in the working
tree after ``hermes update`` (HEAD stays intact; the files just vanish — see issue #49145). Those files
are tracked, so ``git restore`` puts them back deterministically. Best-effort: returns False (rather
than raising) when git is unavailable, this isn't a checkout, or the restore leaves the directory still
missing — the caller then prints the manual-recovery message.

name: _ensure_tui_workspace
doc:
Ensure ``ui-tui/`` exists before it is used as a subprocess cwd (else ``NotADirectoryError``
/ ``WinError 267`` with no usable message): git-restore first, then abort with recovery steps.

Without this, a missing workspace falls through to ``subprocess.run(..., cwd=<missing ui-tui>)``, which
crashes with ``NotADirectoryError`` (``WinError 267`` on Windows) instead of a usable message (#49145).
We first try to self-heal via ``git restore``; only if that can't recover the directory do we abort with
concrete manual-recovery steps.

name: _tui_node_bin
doc: Resolve the TUI runtime through PM; an explicit bundled HERMES_NODE wins.

name: _make_tui_argv
doc: TUI: --dev → tsx src; else node dist (HERMES_TUI_DIR prebuilt or esbuild).

name: _split_comma_items
doc: Flatten str / list (comma-separated) input into stripped non-empty parts.

name: _normalize_tui_toolsets
doc: Normalize argparse/Fire-style toolset input for the TUI subprocess.

name: _read_cgroup_memory_limit
doc:
Container memory limit in bytes, or None if unconstrained (v2 ``memory.max``, then v1).

V8 is NOT cgroup-aware: a flat 8GB heap grows past a smaller container limit
and the OOM-killer SIGKILLs Node with no breadcrumb (bare ``stdin EOF``).

name: _resolve_tui_heap_mb
doc:
V8 ``--max-old-space-size`` (MB) that fits the container: ``default_mb`` when unconstrained,
else 75% of the cgroup limit (headroom for non-heap RSS + the gateway child), floored at
1536MB when the container is > 2GB (below that V8 GC-thrashes).

name: _safe_tui_cwd
doc: Return a stable cwd value for the Node TUI child environment.

name: _apply_tui_python_env
doc: Seed/repair Python-related env vars shared by CLI and dashboard TUI launches.

name: _setup_tui_worktree
doc: Create the ``--worktree`` checkout for a TUI launch (prune + async pack maintenance); exits on failure.

name: _remove_idle_clean_tui_worktree
doc:
Remove the ``--tui -w`` checkout on quit when nothing still needs it (N8) -> True if gone.

Kept when the gateway has queued or started work for a session inside it (quitting only
detaches the viewer), still schedules work for one (an active loop, heartbeat or goal
continuation, or a cron job bound to it), another viewer still holds one, or another process
still works in it; and by ``_cleanup_worktree`` when it is dirty, holds unpushed commits or
something no branch keeps.

name: _require_bypass_model
arguments: env: dict, model: Optional[str], resume_session_id: Optional[str]
doc:
A --safe-mode / --ignore-user-config session reads no profile default model, so the owner
refuses its session.create without one (bare invalid_params). Say so before the TUI starts,
as classic chat does; a resume reuses the frozen route and needs none.

name: _launch_tui
arguments: resume_session_id: Optional[str]=None, tui_dev: bool=False, native_mode: Optional[bool]=None, model: Optional[str]=None, provider: Optional[str]=None, toolsets: object=None, skills: object=None, verbose: Optional[bool]=None, quiet: bool=False, query: Optional[str]=None, image: Optional[str]=None, worktree: bool=False, checkpoints: bool=False, pass_session_id: bool=False, max_turns: Optional[int]=None, accept_hooks: bool=False
doc: Replace current process with the TUI.

name: _pin_kanban_board_env
doc:
Pin the active kanban board into ``HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD`` so in-process tools and shelled-out
``hermes kanban`` calls agree even if a concurrent ``boards switch`` flips the file mid-turn.

Without this, in-process tools (``kanban_*``) and shelled-out CLI calls (``hermes kanban …``) resolve
the board on different paths: the env-pin if set, otherwise the global ``<root>/kanban/current`` file. A
concurrent ``hermes kanban boards switch`` from another session can flip the file mid-turn, so the same
chat sees its tool calls hit board A while its shell calls hit board B (#20074). Pinning at chat boot
mirrors what the dispatcher already does for spawned workers.

name: _sync_bundled_skills_quietly
doc:
Seed ``~/.hermes/skills/`` with the bundled library (idempotent, milliseconds when synced).
Failures are swallowed: skills are an enhancement, not a hard dependency.

name: _resolve_use_tui
doc:
Decide whether to launch the TUI: ``--cli`` → classic; ``--tui`` → TUI; no TTY → classic;
``HERMES_TUI=1`` → TUI; ``display.interface`` config; default classic.

The TTY gate is load-bearing: ambient preferences must never hijack a piped
``hermes chat -q`` (kanban workers, cron) — the Ink no-TTY bail-out exits 0 and
the worker dies with a protocol violation. Explicit ``--tui`` still bails out.

name: _record_bytecode_fingerprint
doc: Persist the current checkout fingerprint after a bytecode sweep. Never raises.

name: _sweep_stale_bytecode_if_checkout_changed
doc:
Clear ``__pycache__`` at launch when the checkout fingerprint changed since the last sweep.

Update-time clears can't close the stale-bytecode class: ``hermes update`` runs
the PRE-pull updater code and manual pulls never run it. Cheap file reads, no
git subprocess. Never raises.

The stale-bytecode bug class (issues #6207, #60242; Dhruv's WhatsApp ``cannot import name
'parse_model_flags_detailed'`` report) has one shared shape: the checkout's ``.py`` files change (git
pull inside ``hermes update``, a manual ``git pull``, a ZIP update, a file-sync restore) while
``__pycache__`` retains bytecode from the previous revision, and a later process trusts the stale
``.pyc`` instead of the fresh source.

name: _web_project_root
doc: Repo root for a frontend dir (``web/`` or ``apps/<name>/``).

name: _web_dist_dir
doc: Vite outputs to ``hermes_cli/web_dist/`` (vite.config.ts outDir), NOT ``web/dist/``.

name: _write_web_ui_build_stamp
doc: Historical updater entrypoint; current builders publish their own receipts.

name: _console_print
doc: print() that survives cp1252-style consoles (arrow/check glyphs) via errors="replace".

name: _run_with_idle_timeout
arguments: cmd: list[str], cwd: Path, *, idle_timeout_seconds: int=180, indent: str='    ', env: dict[str, str] | None=None
doc: Stop an old updater instead of running the retired build path.

name: _nixos_build_env
doc: Stop an old updater instead of running the retired build path.

name: _run_npm_install_deterministic
arguments: npm: str, cwd: Path, *, extra_args: tuple[str, ...]=(), capture_output: bool=True, env: dict[str, str] | None=None
doc: Stop an old updater instead of running the retired build path.

name: _build_web_ui
doc: Serialize dashboard rebuilds, checking freshness only after acquiring the lock.

name: _do_build_web_ui
doc: Build stale dashboard sources; failure is never reported as a usable build.

name: _under_pytest
doc:
True inside the test suite: ignore the system ``/etc/hermes`` so a real managed scope on a
dev/CI box can't leak policy into the suite. An explicit ``HERMES_MANAGED_DIR`` still wins.

name: get_managed_dir
doc:
Resolve the managed-scope directory, or None when no scope is present.

Priority: ``$HERMES_MANAGED_DIR`` (IT-only bootstrap override; never persisted to any .env;
honored only when non-empty AND the directory exists), then ``/etc/hermes`` when it exists.
A missing directory resolves to None — the common case, so it must be cheap + side-effect-free.

name: invalidate_managed_cache
doc: Drop cached managed config/env. For tests and post-edit reloads.

name: _cached_read
arguments: path: Path, cache: dict[str, tuple], parse
doc:
Shared stat-signature-keyed read; returns a deepcopy of the parsed value.

``None`` when the file is absent or fails to parse (fail-open). A parse failure is logged
LOUDLY — the admin needs to know their policy isn't applied — but never raises, so a malformed
managed file can't brick startup.

name: _load_managed_file
arguments: name: str, cache: dict[str, tuple], parse

name: load_managed_config
doc: Parsed managed config.yaml, or {} when absent/malformed (fail-open).

name: load_managed_env
doc: Parsed managed .env (KEY=VALUE), or {} when absent (fail-open).

name: apply_managed_overlay
doc:
Overlay administrator-pinned config values on top of an already-built dict.

``${VAR}`` refs in the managed config expand against the PROCESS env only, so a user cannot
shadow a managed literal via a ref they control; a bare root ``model: x/y`` string is promoted
to ``model.default`` so it can't clobber the dict shape callers expect; managed values
deep-merge ON TOP per leaf while sibling keys stay user-controlled. Fail-open: returns
``config`` unchanged when no scope is present or on any error. Mutates and returns ``config``.

name: managed_config_keys
doc: Dotted leaf keys pinned by the managed config (e.g. {'model.default'}).

name: is_key_managed
doc: True if the exact dotted config key is pinned by the managed layer.

name: is_env_managed
doc: True if the env var name is pinned by the managed .env layer.

name: managed_python_env
arguments: project_root: Path | None=None, *, install_dir: Path | None=None, base_env: dict[str, str] | None=None, **kwargs

name: rebuild_venv
arguments: uv_bin: str, venv_dir: Path, python_version: str='3.11', **kwargs

name: _catalog_root
doc: The optional-mcps/ dir: env-var override / packaged location, else the source checkout's.

name: _require_mapping
arguments: path: Path, key: str, raw: Any

name: _require_list
arguments: path: Path, field: str, raw: Any

name: _require_str_list
arguments: path: Path, field: str, raw: Any, *, non_empty: bool=False

name: _parse_auth
arguments: path: Path, raw: Any, name: str, http: bool

name: _validate_applications
doc: Accept bounded display labels/aliases, never paths, commands or regexes.

name: _parse_manifest
doc: Read and validate a manifest.yaml. Raise CatalogError on any problem.

name: list_catalog
doc:
Return all valid catalog entries, sorted by name.

Invalid manifests are skipped silently (CI catches them); future ``manifest_version`` ones are
skipped too but surfaced via :func:`catalog_diagnostics` so UIs can say "update Hermes".

name: catalog_diagnostics
doc:
``(entry_name, kind, message)`` tuples from the most recent :func:`list_catalog` call;
``kind`` is ``future_manifest`` (newer than this Hermes) or ``invalid`` (malformed).

name: get_entry
doc: Look up a single entry by name. ``official/<name>`` prefix accepted.

name: installed_servers
doc: Return current ``mcp_servers`` block from config.yaml.

name: server_enabled
doc: Whether the server block is on: the same reader the MCP client uses.

name: remove_server
doc: Drop ``mcp_servers.<name>`` from config.yaml (pruning an empty block). True if it existed.

name: _install_root
doc: Where git-bootstrapped MCPs are cloned. Per-user, profile-aware.

name: _run_bootstrap
doc: Execute bootstrap commands in *cwd*. Raise CatalogError on first failure.

name: _do_git_install
doc: Clone the entry's repo into ``~/.hermes/mcp-installs/<name>`` and run bootstrap. Returns the dir.

name: _prompt_env_vars
doc:
Prompt for each env spec.

Secrets persist to ~/.hermes/.env. Non-secrets are only collected and
returned — the caller inlines them into the server config (config.yaml),
since .env is secrets-only. Values already supplied by the caller
(``preloaded``, e.g. from a dashboard form) skip the prompt.

name: _inline_non_secret_value
arguments: obj: Any, name: str, value: str
doc:
Recursively replace literal ``${name}`` refs with the collected value.

Only non-secret env vars are inlined this way: secret refs stay as
``${VAR}`` so config.yaml never carries credentials (resolved from .env
at load time).

name: _build_server_config
doc: Translate a manifest into the ``mcp_servers.<name>`` block format used by hermes_cli/mcp_config.py.

name: _read_prior_tool_list
doc:
The user's prior ``tools.<key>`` (``include``/``exclude``) for *name*, if well-formed.

Read BEFORE a reinstall overwrites the entry: a prior include list pre-checks the checklist and a
user-edited exclude list survives instead of being clobbered by the manifest's ``default_excluded``.

name: _probe_tools
doc:
Connect to a freshly-configured MCP and list its tools.

``(tool_name, description)`` tuples on success, ``None`` on any failure (unreachable, OAuth not
yet completed, ...). Failures are swallowed here; :func:`_apply_tool_selection` handles them.

name: _write_tools_filter
arguments: name: str, mode: str, values: Optional[list[str]]
doc:
Persist ``mcp_servers.<name>.tools.<mode>`` (``include``/``exclude``), clearing the other
mode; ``values=None`` drops the whole tools block (no filter).

name: _apply_tool_selection
arguments: entry: CatalogEntry, *, prior_selection: Optional[list[str]], prior_exclude: Optional[list[str]]=None
doc:
Probe the server and let the user pick which tools to enable.

Probe-success: curses checklist; pre-check priority *prior_selection* (reinstall) > manifest
``tools.default_enabled`` > all; all-on clears any filter. Probe-fail: keep the prior filter,
else apply ``default_enabled``, else no filter; point the user at ``hermes mcp configure``.

name: card_install_config
doc:
The ``mcp_servers.<name>`` block a connection card installs, built in memory.

Same block :func:`install_entry` writes, minus everything a terminal owns: no prompts, no
probe, no checklist. The caller saves it only once the server accepted the connection. Tool
filter priority matches :func:`_apply_tool_selection`: a prior user selection survives a
reinstall, else the manifest's curated filter, else none.

name: record_mcp_install
arguments: source: str, name: Optional[str], outcome: str, *, failure_class: Optional[str]=None, error: Optional[BaseException]=None
doc:
One shared-metrics extension install for an MCP server (catalog entry name, or None when custom).
A failed one names its ``failure_class`` or passes the raised ``error`` (classified by its type).

name: recorded_catalog_install
doc:
Record a first install of catalog entry *name* once: failed when the body raises, else
success. A reinstall over an existing ``mcp_servers`` block is not an install.

name: install_entry
arguments: entry: CatalogEntry, *, enable: bool=True, preloaded_env: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None

name: _install_entry
arguments: entry: CatalogEntry, *, enable: bool, preloaded_env: Optional[dict[str, str]]
doc:
Install a catalog entry end-to-end.

Order: git clone + bootstrap (if any); credential prompts (``auth.env``) to .env; write
``mcp_servers.<name>`` (with the ``auth: oauth`` marker and any pre-registered ``oauth`` block); probe + tool checklist (falling back per
:func:`_apply_tool_selection`); print post_install notes.

``preloaded_env`` carries env values already supplied by the caller (e.g.
the dashboard form); they skip the interactive prompt.

name: uninstall_entry
doc: Remove a catalog-installed MCP from config and (optionally) its clone dir. True if anything removed.

name: _mask_header_field_value
doc:
Replace a credential header's complete associated value with ``***``.

A leading auth scheme word is kept for debugging; Digest parameters are
part of the field value and are not tokenized.

name: redact_mcp_probe_text
doc:
Fully redact MCP probe/display strings before they leave the process.

Recognized credential header fields (Authorization / Proxy-Authorization
and ``agent.redact._SECRET_HEADER_NAMES``) have their complete associated
value replaced with ``***``. Bare Bearer/Basic/Token/Digest spans are
covered the same way. The generic secret redactor then runs with
``force=True`` as defense in depth.

name: _header_value_is_only_env_refs
doc: True when every non-scheme span in *value* is a ``${VAR}`` reference.

name: redact_mcp_header_display
doc:
Fail-closed CLI display for a credential-shaped MCP header.

A value that is only ``${ENV}`` references (optionally with an auth scheme
word) may be shown — it carries no secret. Anything else, including opaque
API keys and mixed template+literal strings, is replaced with ``***``.
``name`` stays paired with the value so callers cannot drop the header
identity before this policy runs.

name: _redact_probe_exception
doc: Return a raise-able exception whose ``str()`` is safe to print.

name: _print_tools
arguments: tools: list[tuple[str, str]], width: int, desc_max: int

name: _get_mcp_servers
doc: Return the ``mcp_servers`` dict from config, or empty dict.

name: _tool_filters
doc:
Return the ``(include, exclude)`` tool lists from a server config; ``None`` = key absent.

An explicit ``include: []`` is a real (block-all) whitelist — the runtime registers nothing
(tools/mcp_tool_registration.py) — so it must not collapse to "no filter" here (#12865).

name: _save_mcp_server
doc:
Add or update a server entry in config.yaml.

Returns False when a high-signal exfiltration-shaped stdio command is rejected (shell+egress
payloads are blocked rather than whitelisting command families).

name: _validate_or_warn
doc: Print every suspicious-config issue as a warning; True when the entry is clean.

name: _lookup_server
arguments: name: str, servers: dict[str, dict], available_label: str='Available servers'
doc: Return the named server config, or print the not-found hint and return None.

name: _remove_mcp_server
doc: Remove a server from config.yaml.  Returns True if it existed.

name: _replace_mcp_servers
doc:
Replace the WHOLE ``mcp_servers`` map in config.yaml.

Every entry is validated up front; any suspicious entry rejects the whole save (``(False,
issues)``) so a bad paste can't be partially applied. An empty map removes the key entirely.

name: _env_key_for_server
doc: Convert server name to an env-var key like ``MCP_MYSERVER_API_KEY``.

name: _strip_bearer_prefix
doc:
Strip a leading ``Bearer `` from a pasted token.

The header template already stores ``Authorization: Bearer ${MCP_X_API_KEY}``; a token pasted
with its own prefix would send ``Bearer Bearer <jwt>`` and get a 401.

Normalize on save. (#37792)

name: _bearer_auth_headers
doc:
Build the persisted Authorization header template for a named MCP server.

The secret lives in the profile's ``.env``; CLI and Dashboard share this so they produce
byte-equivalent config.

name: _save_bearer_auth_token
doc: Persist a normalized Bearer token to ``.env`` and return the header template for config.yaml.

name: _parse_env_assignments
doc: Parse ``KEY=VALUE`` strings from CLI args into an env dict.

name: _apply_mcp_preset
arguments: name: str, *, preset_name: Optional[str], url: Optional[str], command: Optional[str], cmd_args: list[str], server_config: dict[str, Any]
doc: Apply a known MCP preset when transport details were omitted.

name: _resolve_mcp_server_config
doc:
Resolve ``${ENV}`` placeholders in a server config before connecting.

Mirrors ``_load_mcp_config()`` in ``tools/mcp_tool.py``; without it the discovery probe sent
literal placeholders in header templates and auth-requiring servers returned 401.

Mirrors ``_load_mcp_config()`` in ``tools/mcp_tool.py``: load ``~/.hermes/.env`` into ``os.environ`` and
recursively interpolate any ``${VAR}`` placeholders. The CLI builds header templates like
``Authorization: Bearer ${MCP_X_API_KEY}`` but the probe path never resolved them, so the discovery
probe sent the literal placeholder and auth-requiring servers (e.g. n8n) returned 401 — while runtime
tool loading worked because it interpolates. (#37792)

name: _probe_single_server
arguments: name: str, config: dict, connect_timeout: Optional[float]=None, *, details: Optional[dict]=None
doc:
Temporarily connect to one MCP server, list its tools, disconnect.

Returns ``(tool_name, description)`` tuples; raises on connection failure. ``details`` is an
out-param filled with ``schema_chars``/``prompts``/``resources`` so the return shape stays stable.

doc: True if an OAuth token file exists for ``name`` (a clean probe alone is not proof of auth).

doc: Ask enable-all / select / cancel; returns the enabled-tool count or None when cancelled.

doc: Add a new MCP server with discovery-first tool selection.

name: cmd_mcp_remove
doc: Remove an MCP server from config.

name: cmd_mcp_list
doc: List all configured MCP servers.

name: _probe_failure_reason
doc:
Plain reason for a failed probe: ``_format_connect_error`` unwraps ExceptionGroups and names a
missing executable; the result is redacted like every other probe string.

name: probe_failure_class
doc:
Extension-install class for a failed MCP probe, from the exception TYPE (the same tests
:func:`_probe_failure_next_step` uses), never its message. Never raises: an exception whose own
attribute hooks raise reads ``connect_failed`` instead of replacing the user's error.

name: _probe_failure_next_step
doc: The one command that fixes the common probe failures (sign-in, missing command, everything else).

name: cmd_mcp_test
doc:
Test connection to an MCP server.

Returns the process exit code so health probes and watchdogs can branch on ``$?`` instead of
parsing the output: 0 connected, 1 connection failed, 3 server not in the config (argparse
already owns 2 for usage errors, so "no such server" stays distinguishable from "bad flags").

name: _reauth_oauth_server
arguments: name: str, server_config: dict, *, flow: str | None=None
doc:
Force a fresh OAuth flow for one server. Returns True on success.

Browser login clears cached state and re-probes. Device login replaces state only after
approval. Both verify a token landed. Shared by ``login`` and ``reauth``.

name: cmd_mcp_login
doc: Run an explicit browser or device authorization for an OAuth-based MCP server.

name: cmd_mcp_reauth
doc:
Re-authenticate one OAuth MCP server, or all of them sequentially.

Serial-by-design: a human can only complete one browser OAuth flow at a time.

This is the self-service fix for the recurring stale-client ritual in GH#36767 (and avoids the startup
popup storm when several servers go stale at once).

name: _rebuild_exclude_list
arguments: name: str, exclude: list, tool_names: list[str], chosen: set, matches_name_filter
doc:
New ``tools.exclude`` for an exclude-mode entry after a checklist edit.

Stays in exclude mode rather than demoting the user's dynamic filter to a frozen include list:
newly-unchecked tools are appended as literal excludes, re-checked tools drop their literal
entries, and glob patterns are preserved (they keep excluding future vendor tools by design).

name: cmd_mcp_configure
doc: Reconfigure which tools are enabled for an existing MCP server.

doc: Main dispatcher for ``hermes mcp`` subcommands.

doc: Return catalog rows + any custom (non-catalog) MCPs found in config.

doc: Install *entry*, printing (not raising) a CatalogError. True on success.

name: _run_submenu
doc: Show a single-select of ``(label, callback)`` pairs and run the picked callback.

doc: Act on the picked row based on its current status.

name: _print_rows_text
doc: Plain-text catalog dump: `hermes mcp catalog` output and the non-curses fallback.
