arguments: self, api_key: Any, api_url: str, native_provider: str, has_explicit_models: bool, *, headers: dict | None, api_mode: str | None, discovery_allowed: bool, is_current: bool
doc:
Probe policy shared by sections 3 and 4 (returns ``(models, native_empty, probed)``):
with an api_key live /models is the source of truth (replaces the partial ``models:``
subset); without one, an allowlist-shaped ``models:`` narrows a public endpoint and skips
the probe. A dict-shaped ``models:`` is metadata, so still probe; pin with
``discover_models: false``.

name: _normalize_tier
doc:
Tier claims arrive verbatim from the JWT claim or the account payload, neither of which
strips or casefolds. Compare them normalized so casing or padding can never turn the
anonymous tier into a registered one.

name: nous_portal_billing_url
doc: Return the billing URL for a normalized Nous account snapshot.

name: nous_portal_topup_url
doc:
Portal top-up URL (``?topup=open`` auto-opens the top-up modal).

Prefers the org-pinned ``{base}/orgs/{slug}/billing`` (skips the legacy shim's multi-org
re-resolution); falls back to ``{base}/billing`` when ``org_slug`` is null — never
``/orgs/None/billing``.

name: format_usage_window_block_guidance
doc:
Next step after a usage-window 402: the credits step from :func:`agent.plan_limits.credits_action`
(turn on Keep going, add credits, or both), plus the auto top-up nudge when it is off. None for every
account not on a usage-window plan, so the credit-grant guidance is unchanged. A paused plan points
at the card, not at a top-up.

name: format_nous_portal_entitlement_message
arguments: account_info: Optional[NousPortalAccountInfo], *, capability: str='this feature', include_refresh_hint: bool=True, coverage_category: Optional[str]=None, in_chat: bool=False
doc:
User-facing guidance for a missing Nous tool-gateway entitlement; ``None`` when entitled.

Entitled = paid access OR a live free pool that covers it (normalized fields, not price:
purchased credits without a subscription count as paid, an exhausted paid subscription does
not). ``coverage_category`` scopes the check to one category; an otherwise-entitled user whose
access doesn't fund it gets a neutral billing nudge, never an "exhausted" message. The
pool-vs-paid distinction is never surfaced.

name: _no_paid_access_message
arguments: account_info: NousPortalAccountInfo, capability: str, billing_url: str, *, in_chat: bool=False

name: reset_nous_portal_account_info_cache
doc: Clear the short-lived account-info cache used by tests.

name: get_nous_portal_account_info
doc:
Normalized Nous Portal account entitlement.

A valid unexpired OAuth JWT serves as a local snapshot (UX gating only; the server stays
authoritative). ``force_fresh=True`` always calls ``/api/oauth/account`` and bypasses the cache.

name: nous_policy_present
doc:
Whether the caller's org carries a restrictive model/provider policy.

``None`` is unknown (older mint / unreadable claim) and must not be reported as "no policy".

name: cached_nous_portal_account_info
doc:
The account snapshot in the 60s cache, or None when empty/expired. Never a fresh fetch, never raises —
for UI chrome that must not add a round trip (the pickers) after a flow has already fetched the account.
``any_age`` returns the last snapshot even past the TTL, for callers that read only the plan's shape
(window or not, featured models), which rarely changes.

name: _account_identity
doc: Portal + the token's user and org (stable across a refresh); an opaque token falls back to its hash.

name: _current_account_identity
doc:
``_account_identity`` for the persisted Nous login, without a refresh or network call. None
when logged out.

name: nous_policy_notice
doc:
One-line notice for a list the org's policy narrowed, else ``""``.

Blocked models are omitted, which reads as "unsupported"; this says which it is without
enumerating them. ``removed`` must reflect whether the filter actually dropped anything — the
catalog read fails open, so the claim alone would label a full list as filtered.

name: _fresh_account_info
arguments: state: dict[str, Any], force_fresh: bool, portal_base_url: Optional[str]

Parse a Portal ``tool_access`` object (JWT claim or account API).

each coverage entry.

name: _coerced_dataclass
doc: Build ``cls`` from a payload dict (field names = payload keys), coercing by declared type.

name: _error_info
arguments: *, error: object, logged_in: bool, portal_base_url: Optional[str]=None, raw_account: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, account_tier: Optional[str]=None
doc:
A failed-lookup snapshot. ``account_tier`` is carried through when the caller still holds the
stored state, so a guest whose lookup failed still gets the "needs a Nous account" copy rather
than billing or re-login guidance.

name: _coerce_num
doc: ``cast(value)`` or None; bools and None are rejected, not coerced.

name: _coerce_str_tuple
doc: A JSON array of non-empty strings → tuple (order kept, non-strings dropped); anything else → None.

name: is_anonymous_tier
doc:
The free tier: no Nous account, so no billing, credits, or entitlement to speak of.
Compared case- and whitespace-insensitively — the claim is wire data.

name: tool_gateway_entitled
doc: Paid access OR a live free tool pool; use ``tool_gateway_entitled_for`` per category.

name: tool_gateway_entitled_for
doc: Paid users are entitled everywhere; pool users only where ``coverage[category]`` is true.

name: managed_tools_rolled_out
doc: Only a literal ``true`` from the portal counts; absent and unknown both read as out.

name: _nous_config
doc: The ``nous:`` section of config.yaml, or {} on any failure (config loader imported lazily).

name: _interval_seconds
doc:
Tick interval: explicit argument, then ``nous.keepalive_interval_seconds`` in config.yaml,
then the module default. Non-positive disables the keepalive thread (the documented way off).

name: _observed_lifetime_seconds
doc:
Server-issued lifetime (seconds) of the current Nous credentials; the shorter of the access
token and the invoke agent key governs. None when nothing usable is stored.

name: _tick_seconds
doc: Tick fast enough to refresh several times per credential lifetime.

name: _refresh_horizon_seconds
doc:
Life a credential needs to be left alone this tick: it must survive until the next tick
(nothing looks at it again before then), hence tick + skew rather than the bare skew.

name: _refresh_selected_pool_entry
doc:
Refresh the current pool entry when stale. True = usable/refreshed; False = pool exists but
no usable entry; None = no Nous pool.

name: refresh_nous_auth_keepalive_once
arguments: *, min_key_ttl_seconds: int=NOUS_INVOKE_JWT_MIN_TTL_SECONDS, min_access_ttl_seconds: Optional[int]=None, timeout_seconds: Optional[float]=None
doc: Refresh Nous auth once if credentials are configured (pool entry first, then singleton state).

name: _keepalive_loop
arguments: stop_event: threading.Event, *, interval_seconds: int, initial_delay_seconds: int, min_key_ttl_seconds: int, timeout_seconds: Optional[float]

name: start_nous_auth_keepalive
arguments: *, interval_seconds: Optional[int]=None, initial_delay_seconds: int=NOUS_AUTH_KEEPALIVE_INITIAL_DELAY_SECONDS, min_key_ttl_seconds: int=NOUS_INVOKE_JWT_MIN_TTL_SECONDS, timeout_seconds: Optional[float]=None
doc: Start the process-wide Nous auth keepalive thread (idempotent; None when disabled).

name: stop_nous_auth_keepalive
doc: Stop the keepalive thread. Intended for graceful shutdown/tests.

name: resolve_portal_base_url
doc: Resolve the portal base URL with login-time precedence: env, stored state, default.

name: _absolutize_portal_url
doc:
Resolve a (possibly relative) server portalUrl against the client's portal base.

The server emits ``portalUrl`` relative by design; absolute URLs pass through unchanged. urljoin
needs the trailing slash on the base to join an absolute path like "/billing?..." to the host.

name: invalidate_cached_token
doc:
Bust the token cache so post-step-up replays use the freshly-scoped token.

``_request`` only self-busts on a 401, not on a 403 scope denial — after a step-up grant the
cache would otherwise still hold the pre-grant unscoped token and the replay would 403 again.

name: _billing_not_logged_in
doc: Build the canonical 'not logged in' BillingAuthError (single source).

name: _resolve_token_and_base
doc: ``(access_token, portal_base_url)``, cached for ``_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`` unless ``use_cache=False``.

name: _retry_after_seconds
doc: Parse a ``Retry-After`` header (integer seconds) — None if absent/bad.

name: _raise_for_error
arguments: status: int, payload: dict[str, Any], headers: Any=None
doc:
Map an HTTP error response to the right typed :class:`BillingError` (see tables above).

Recognizes the Remote-Spending gate contract (NAS PR #481): 403 ``remote_spending_revoked`` (this
terminal's spend revoked → reconnect), 401 ``session_revoked`` (full logout → re-login), 503
``temporarily_unavailable`` (gate fail-closed → back off, NOT revoked). The business-denial codes
(``cli_billing_disabled`` + dual ``code:remote_spending_disabled``, ``role_required``,
``idempotency_conflict``, …) flow through as a generic BillingError carrying
``error``/``code``/``recovery`` for the surface to map.

name: _request
arguments: method: str, path: str, *, body: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, extra_headers: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None, timeout: float=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, _retried_auth: bool=False
doc:
Authenticated billing request -> parsed JSON dict (``{}`` for an empty 2xx body).

Raises a typed :class:`BillingError` on any non-2xx or transport failure. A 401 triggers exactly
one retry with a freshly-resolved token so a cached-but-just-expired token self-heals.

name: _require_str
arguments: value: Any, message: str, error: str
doc: Return ``value.strip()`` or raise a typed BillingError when it is not a non-blank str.

name: _post_idempotent
arguments: path: str, body: dict[str, Any], idempotency_key: str, what: str, timeout: float
doc: POST with a mandatory ``Idempotency-Key`` header (missing header is a server 400).

name: get_billing_state
doc: ``GET /api/billing/state`` — role-tiered overview (no scope required).

name: patch_auto_top_up
arguments: *, enabled: bool, threshold: float | str, top_up_amount: float | str, timeout: float=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT
doc: ``PATCH /api/billing/auto-top-up`` — configure auto-reload (scope required; strict body, JSON numbers).

name: patch_keep_going_on_credits
doc:
``PATCH /api/billing/keep-going-on-credits``: the window plan's "Keep going on credits" setting (scope
required; strict ``{enabled}`` body). Turning it off skips the spending gates.

name: post_charge
arguments: *, amount_usd: float | str, idempotency_key: str, timeout: float=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT
doc:
``POST /api/billing/charge`` — buy credits (scope required). Reuse the UUID ``idempotency_key`` on retry.

Returns ``202 {chargeId}`` — money is NOT confirmed yet; poll with :func:`get_charge_status`.

name: get_charge_status
doc:
``GET /api/billing/charge/{id}`` — poll a charge (scope required).

Returns ``{status: "pending"|"settled"|"failed", ...}``. An unknown or foreign id returns
``{status:"pending"}`` (never 404) — a ``pending`` past the 5-min cap is a *timeout*, not an error.

name: get_subscription_state
doc: ``GET /api/billing/subscription`` — current plan, tiers, usage (raw JSON; no scope).

name: post_subscription_preview
doc:
``POST /api/billing/subscription/preview`` — a chargeless effect quote.

``effect`` is ``charge_now`` (upgrade; ``amountDueNowCents`` prorated), ``scheduled``
(downgrade; ``effectiveAt`` period end), ``no_op``, or ``blocked`` (``reason`` says why).

name: put_subscription_pending_change
arguments: *, subscription_type_id: str | None=None, cancel: bool=False, timeout: float=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT
doc:
``PUT /api/billing/subscription/pending-change`` — set the single end-of-period intent.

``cancel=True`` schedules a cancellation; ``subscription_type_id`` a downgrade / same-price change.
UPGRADES are rejected here (they charge now — use :func:`post_subscription_upgrade`).

name: delete_subscription_pending_change
doc:
``DELETE /api/billing/subscription/pending-change`` — clear a scheduled downgrade/cancellation.

Chargeless, but re-enables recurring spend: needs ``billing:manage`` and honors the org kill-switch.

name: post_subscription_upgrade
arguments: *, subscription_type_id: str, idempotency_key: str, timeout: float=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT
doc:
``POST /api/billing/subscription/upgrade`` — immediate paid upgrade, the SINGLE money route.

One Stripe op prorates, charges the card on file, flips the plan. Reuse ``idempotency_key`` on retry.

engine is selected. Mirrors the local-mode tail of tools.browser_tool_install.check_browser_requirements.

tool_key -> has_direct_credentials. Env-configured keyless local backends (SearXNG, CAMOFOX_URL)

(unconfigured, has_direct, explicit_configured, already_managed) tool key lists: no credentials

doc: Store the managed selection for ``tool_keys``; returns the set of tools actually changed.

If eligible tools exist, show a per-tool checklist to route them through the Tool Gateway.
Triggered by a live free pool or paid access; explicit_configured tools (e.g. ``web.backend:
searxng``) are configured on purpose and never offered, like already_managed.

name: ensure_nous_portal_access
arguments: *, capability: str='the Nous Tool Gateway', coverage_category: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Make sure the user is entitled to the Nous Tool Gateway, logging in if needed.

Only performs the device-code OAuth (when not logged in) and refreshes entitlement — no model
or provider switch. Entitlement is paid access OR a live free pool; with ``coverage_category``
the pool must cover that category (a pool user selecting ``"fal-video"`` is denied).

doc: Y/n prompt: True on yes/blank, False on anything else, ``None`` on EOF/Ctrl-C.

name: _run_nous_portal_login_only

Run the Nous Portal device-code OAuth and persist credentials only (no model selection, no
provider switch, no Tool Gateway bulk prompt). ``False`` if the user declined or the flow failed.

doc:
Mark a boot computation as in flight (readers wait for it from now on) and return the call
that finishes it: ``finish(compute)`` runs *compute* and caches its answer, unless a writer
invalidated meanwhile or the files never held still.

name: read
arguments: compute: Callable[[], Due], *, stamp: Stamp=lambda: None, wait: float=BOOT_WAIT_SECONDS
doc:
The cached answer; a boot computation in flight is waited for (bounded), and with nothing
cached, or files moved since (*stamp*), *compute* answers live and is cached.

name: _store
arguments: value: Due, generation: int, before: Hashable, after: Hashable
doc: Cache *value*, computed between the stamps *before* and *after*; True when it was cached.

name: should_run
doc:
The root config's explicit ``onboarding.run`` (managed overlay included) when it is a bool,
else whether this machine has never used Hermes (``install_state``; *assume_fresh* is the
unpackaged desktop's ``--fresh-install`` switch).

name: latch_first_install
doc:
The desktop backend's first boot on a fresh install records the decision: ``onboarding.run:
true`` and the trial reserved. A launch that misses the run (a late answer, the app closed, the
user chatting first) then stays due until a run ends. True when it wrote them.

name: set_run
doc:
Persist ``onboarding.run`` (and, with *mark_profile_offered*, ``onboarding.seen.profile_build_offered``)
in the root ``config.yaml`` as one write, keeping every other key and comment. A failed write raises.

name: register_cli
doc: Attach the ``onepassword`` subcommand tree to a parent parser.

name: cmd_token
doc:
Rotate the service-account token: verify with ``op whoami`` (unless ``--no-verify``) and
only then persist to .env, so a bad paste never bricks the working token.

name: _op_whoami
arguments: binary: Path, account: str, *, token_value: str=''
doc:
Short identity string if op is authenticated, else None. ``token_value`` probes a candidate
token via the child's ``OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`` without touching the caller's environment.

name: _auxiliary_usage
doc: Per-task aux usage recorded for *session_id*'s lineage (``{}`` without a store / session).

name: _attach_auxiliary_usage
arguments: result: dict, session_db, before: dict[str, dict], fallback_session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Store this run's auxiliary usage on *result* as the delta against the pre-turn snapshot
(a resumed session already carries earlier runs' aux rows). Waits (bounded) for the auto-title
thread first: it bills from a daemon thread and can still be in flight when the turn returns.
Failed-turn dicts carry no ``session_id``; *fallback_session_id* keeps the delta readable then.

name: _auxiliary_report
doc: Add the ``auxiliary`` breakdown and ``total_including_auxiliary`` to the ledger.

name: _oneshot_exit_code
doc:
Map a finished ``-z`` turn onto its exit code: ``0`` only when the turn completed;
``130`` interrupted; ``2`` failed or stopped partway (``partial``, ``completed: False`` such
as the iteration budget); ``1`` a completed turn that produced no text at all.

The outcome is judged from the result, not from whether text was printed: a partial or
failed turn usually leaves an explanation on stdout, and exiting 0 for it made scripts treat
a half-done job (or a provider error summary) as success (#111770).

name: _normalize_toolsets
doc: Split repeated/comma-separated toolset flags into a clean list (``None`` when empty).

name: _normalize_skills
doc: Normalize repeated/comma-separated skill flags and preserve order.

name: _build_preloaded_skills_prompt
doc: Load requested skills using the same partial-success contract as CLI chat.

name: _configured_mcp_servers
doc: ``(enabled, disabled)`` MCP server names from config; both empty on any error.

name: _write_usage_file
arguments: path: Optional[str], result: dict, failure: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Best-effort JSON usage report for pipelines (``-z --usage-file``).

Written even on failure so callers can always account for spend. Never raises — a broken usage
write must not mask the run's own outcome.

name: run_oneshot
arguments: prompt: str, model: Optional[str]=None, provider: Optional[str]=None, toolsets: object=None, skills: object=None, usage_file: Optional[str]=None, resume: Optional[str]=None, reasoning: object=None
doc:
Execute a single prompt and print only the final content block.

Model/provider fall back to ``HERMES_INFERENCE_MODEL`` and config.yaml. ``usage_file`` gets a
JSON usage report even when the run fails. ``resume`` is a session id (already normalized by
the CLI layer: latest/title/--continue resolution) whose transcript is loaded and continued
by this turn. Returns the exit code; the caller owns process termination.

name: _create_session_db_for_oneshot
doc:
Best-effort SessionDB — oneshot bypasses ``HermesCLI._init_agent()``, so it must wire the
SQLite store itself or ``session_search`` is advertised but always unavailable. The registry
handle is the one in-process tools (delegation, goals) acquire during the run, so the process
holds one writer; ``_close_agent``'s ``close()`` releases the refcount.

name: _resolve_model_and_provider
arguments: cfg: dict, model: Optional[str], provider: Optional[str]
doc:
Effective model = arg → env → config; provider = arg → auto-detect → config/env.

Auto-detection only runs when the model was explicitly requested (arg or env var) — same
semantic as ``/model <name>`` — because the configured default provider may not host it.
Config-sourced models are the "use my defaults" path and keep the configured provider.

name: _load_resume_target
doc:
Resolve ``resume`` to ``(session_id, conversation_history, session_meta)`` for a oneshot turn.

Follows the same contract as the interactive CLI resume: compression-chain redirect via
``resolve_resume_session_id``, safe-resume guard, model-projection history with
``session_meta`` rows dropped. An unknown session raises (the user passed an explicit id;
silently starting a fresh session is the resume-dropped failure mode this exists to fix —
see #105892). An empty stored transcript still returns the resolved id: the turn replays
nothing but is recorded under the requested session — ``hermes -z "hello" -c <title>
--create-if-missing`` must fill the titled session it created, not mint a fresh id
(same contract as the interactive /resume of an empty session).

The resolved row is also reopened (best effort): the previous run stamped ``ended_at``,
the existing-row upsert never clears the end fields, and ``end_session()`` only writes
rows whose ``ended_at`` is null — so without this step the resumed turn would be recorded
under a session that stays closed and its new lifecycle boundary would be lost (same
reason the interactive resume calls ``reopen_session()`` before continuing).

name: _apply_stored_session_runtime
doc:
Run a resumed one-shot on the session's stored runtime, not the ambient config — the same
contract as the interactive ``_restore_session_model``, via the shared ``stored_session_route``.
An explicit ``--model`` keeps the ambient choice. A changed provider drops the resolved
``api_key``: it belongs to the ambient endpoint and is never persisted, so runtime resolution
re-fetches credentials for the restored provider.

name: _run_agent
arguments: prompt: str, model: Optional[str]=None, provider: Optional[str]=None, toolsets: object=None, use_config_toolsets: bool=True, skills: object=None, resume: Optional[str]=None, reasoning: object=None, ledger: bool=False
doc:
Build an AIAgent exactly like a normal CLI chat turn, run one conversation, and return
``(final_response, run_result)``. Imports are local to keep CLI startup cheap. *ledger* (set when
``--usage-file`` is requested) attaches this run's auxiliary usage to the result.

name: _quietly
doc: Run a cleanup step, logging (never raising) on failure.

name: _close_agent
doc:
Teardown mirroring gateway/run.py:_cleanup_agent_resources (NOT cli.py:_run_cleanup):
oneshot has no _active_agent_ref and the hard-exit path skips finalizers.

name: _oneshot_clarify_callback
doc: Clarify is disabled in oneshot mode — tell the agent to pick a default and proceed.

name: pairing_command
doc: Handle hermes pairing subcommands.

name: _cmd_list
doc: List all pending and approved users.

name: _cmd_approve
doc: Approve a pairing request id (from ``pairing list``) or a DM'd code.

name: _cmd_revoke
doc: Revoke a user's access.

name: _cmd_clear_pending
doc: Clear all pending pairing codes.

name: parse_partial_compress_args
doc:
Parse the argument string after ``/compress`` into ``(partial, keep_last, focus_topic)``.

``here [N]`` / ``up to here [N]`` / ``--keep N`` / ``-k N`` / ``--keep=N`` select the
boundary-aware form; anything else is a focus topic for full ``/compress <focus>``.

name: extract_compress_flags
doc:
Strip ``--preview``/``--dry-run``/``--aggressive`` (anywhere in the string) and return
``(remaining_args, preview, aggressive_requested)``.

``preview`` means report what WOULD be compressed and change nothing. No surface implements an
LLM-free hard-truncate path, so callers surface "not supported" for ``--aggressive`` instead of
treating it as a focus topic.

name: summarize_compress_preview
arguments: history: list[dict[str, Any]], partial: bool, keep_last: int, focus_topic: Optional[str], approx_tokens: int
doc:
Build the ``/compress --preview`` report — pure, no side effects.

Shared by the CLI and the gateway slash handler so both report the numbers the real run would
use. Returns ``head_count``/``tail_count``/``total``/``partial``/``lines`` (ready to print).

name: _coerce_keep
doc: Parse a keep-count token, clamping to [1, MAX_KEEP_LAST].

name: split_history_for_partial_compress
doc:
Split ``history`` into ``(head, tail)``: head is summarized, tail is the last ``keep_last``
exchanges kept verbatim.

Exchanges are counted by ``user`` messages so the tail always starts on a user turn and
``compressed_head + tail`` keeps alternation valid. Returns ``(history, [])`` when the head
would be empty (or there are no user turns), signaling the caller to fall back to full
compression rather than rotating the session for a no-op.

name: rejoin_compressed_head_and_tail
arguments: compressed_head: list[dict[str, Any]], tail: list[dict[str, Any]]
doc:
Concatenate a compressed head with the verbatim tail, defending the seam's role alternation.

The head compressor's output shape isn't contractually guaranteed (a plugin engine could end on
a user turn). If the last head message and first tail message share a user/assistant role, the
tail's first string content is folded onto the head's last message; non-string (multimodal)
content gets a minimal bridging turn instead so nothing is lost. ``tool`` messages are left
alone — consecutive tool entries are the one legal repetition (parallel results).

name: _get
arguments: cfg: Optional[dict[str, Any]], *keys: str, default: Any=None
doc: Nested dict lookup tolerant of None/non-dict intermediate nodes.

name: prompt_text
doc: Normalize config prompt values from YAML (str | list | None) to text.

name: render_personality_prompt
doc: Render a string or structured personality definition to prompt text.

name: describe_personality
doc: Short preview line for list UIs (CLI table, gateway /personality list).

name: normalize_personality_name
doc: Canonical form of a personality name ('' for any neutral spelling).

name: available_personalities
doc:
Built-ins overlaid by the user's personalities: root ``personalities`` then
``agent.personalities`` (later wins). Root entries were silently ignored (#9636).

name: resolve_personality
doc: Resolve a requested personality to ``(canonical_name, prompt_text)``.

name: active_personality_name
doc: The currently selected personality name ('' when none is active).

name: resolve_ephemeral_system_prompt
doc:
Session overlay: ``display.personality`` when it names a known personality, else the
user-owned ``agent.system_prompt``. Callers still prefer ``HERMES_EPHEMERAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT``.

name: persist_personality
doc:
Persist the selection — the ONLY sanctioned write path. Writes the canonical name (or '')
to ``display.personality`` atomically (comments/ordering preserved); never touches
``agent.system_prompt``. Returns True on success.

name: _cmd_list
doc: List gallery pets (or only installed ones with ``--installed``).

name: _cmd_scale
doc: Persist ``display.pet.scale`` — one knob resizes every surface.

name: _cmd_show
doc:
Animate the active (or named) pet in the terminal via the shared PetRenderer
(kitty/iTerm2/sixel when supported, else truecolor half-block fallback). Ctrl+C stops.

name: _cmd_doctor
doc: Report install state, active pet, config, and terminal capability.

name: _update_pet_config
doc:
Write ``display.pet.*`` keys and save config; returns whether anything was written.

With ``when_slug`` the write only happens when the configured slug equals it (remove/rename
must never disturb a different active pet).

name: set_pet_scale
doc:
Set ``display.pet.scale`` (clamped). Returns ``(applied, error)``; *error* is set (and
nothing written) only when *value* isn't a number. Single write path behind ``/pet scale``
and the desktop slider.

name: toggle_pet_display
doc: Toggle ``display.pet.enabled``.

name: print_pet_gallery
doc: Print a slice of the public petdex gallery (CLI/TUI text fallback).

name: _clear_active_if
doc: Disable + unset the active pet iff it's ``slug`` (e.g. after removal).

name: _rename_active_if
doc:
Repoint the active pet from ``old_slug`` to ``new_slug`` iff it's active (a rename moves
the dir; config must follow). Preserves ``enabled``.

name: _interactive_pick
doc: Minimal numbered picker (avoids curses dep for a tiny list).

name: register_cli
doc: Attach ``pets`` subcommands to *parent* (called by main.py).

name: platform_label
doc: Return the display label for a platform key (builtin, then plugin registry), or *default*.

name: get_all_platforms
doc: PLATFORMS plus plugin-registered platforms (appended after builtins) — use for menus.

name: _discord_add_reaction
arguments: adapter: Any, chat_id: str, message_id: str, emoji: str

name: _resolve_adapter
doc: Return ``(adapter, error_dict)``; exactly one is non-None.

name: _gate
doc: Run the shared gate chain. Returns ``(adapter, error_dict)``.

name: _run
arguments: self, verb: str, platform: str, *args: str, **required: Any
doc: Gate, dispatch *verb* to the adapter's platform implementation, audit, return.

doc: Add/set an emoji reaction on a platform message.

name: set_thread_title
arguments: self, platform: str, chat_id: str, thread_id: str, title: str
doc: Rename a thread / forum topic.

name: _audit
arguments: self, verb: str, platform: str, result: dict[str, Any]
doc: Every platform action is logged (the #64176 'all actions logged' rule).

name: get_bundled_plugins_dir
doc:
Bundled ``plugins/`` dir: ``HERMES_BUNDLED_PLUGINS`` (Nix wrapper / packaged installs, read-only
store paths) first, else the in-repo path.

name: _install_plugin_debug_handler
doc: When HERMES_PLUGINS_DEBUG is on, tee plugin logs to stderr at DEBUG (once per process).

name: _make_scoped_provider_registrar
arguments: method_name, kind, registry_mod, base_ref, label, doc, options
doc: Build one ``register_<category>_provider`` method from a ``_SCOPED_PROVIDER_REGISTRARS`` row.

name: _ignore_after_abandoned_load
doc:
Turn a registrar into a no-op once the context's load timed out: the abandoned worker thread may
still be executing register(), and a late registration would land in registries that the failure
path already swept (#108139).

name: _resolve_hook_callback_timeout
doc:
Effective hook-callback timeout from ``plugins.hook_callback_timeout`` (default 30s; ``<= 0``
disables the threaded path; clamped to ``_MAX_HOOK_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_SECS``).

``invoke_hook`` calls this once per hook invocation; ``load_config_readonly()`` serves cache hits
without ``_CONFIG_LOCK``, so this is a stat + dict lookup per call and needs no memo of its own.

name: _plugin_home_key
doc:
Resolved active Hermes home — the key for per-profile plugin managers (plugins capture the
home at registration, so a process serving several profiles cannot share one manager).

name: _clear_plugin_submodules
doc:
Purge ``sys.modules`` entries for this manager's directory plugins (package AND submodules —
otherwise a same-slug plugin in another profile reuses the previous profile's submodule state).

name: publish_gateway_message_host
doc: Remember the process gateway host and stamp managers that already exist.

name: clear_published_gateway_message_host
doc: Forget this owner's process gateway host without clobbering a newer runner.

name: _attach_published_gateway_host
doc: Give a newly resolved profile manager the live process gateway host, if any.

name: publish_tui_message_host
doc:
Remember the process TUI/desktop host and stamp managers that already exist.

Does not call ``set_gateway_message_injector``.

name: clear_published_tui_message_host
doc: Forget the process TUI host and clear it where this owner still holds the slot.

name: _attach_published_tui_host
doc: Give a newly resolved manager the process TUI host, if one is installed and the slot is empty.

name: get_plugin_manager
doc:
Return the plugin manager for the active Hermes profile/home (cached per resolved home; a
profile switch gets its own manager and plugin submodules).

name: _reset_plugin_managers_for_tests
doc: Test-only: drop every cached manager and its submodules for a fully clean slate.

name: has_enabled_agent_plugin_mcp
doc:
Whether config enables a portable package with MCP servers (manifest-only scan on a fresh
manager; imports nothing, mutates no registry).

name: discover_plugins
doc:
Discover and load all plugins (idempotent; ``force=True`` rescans). Joins an in-flight
background discovery instead of racing a second scan.

name: start_background_plugin_discovery
doc:
Run discovery in a daemon thread to overlap the rest of CLI startup (~150ms). Every
synchronous consumer joins it via :func:`discover_plugins`, so no one sees a half-loaded
registry. No-op when already done or in flight.

name: _join_background_discovery
doc:
Wait for an in-flight background discovery (no-op from its own thread or a plugin-load worker it
spawned — that worker's parent is blocked waiting on it).

name: _persist_plugin_toolset_keys
doc: Persist discovered plugin toolset keys + portable MCP names (best-effort).

name: _nowait_plugin_set
doc: Shared body of the ``*_nowait`` probes: live registry, else last launch's cache, else block.

name: get_plugin_toolset_keys_nowait
doc:
Plugin toolset keys without blocking on in-flight discovery: live registry when done, last
launch's persisted set while a background scan runs (callers only EXCLUDE these keys, so a stale
set is harmless and self-heals), else block via discover_plugins().

name: get_portable_mcp_server_names_nowait
doc: Portable MCP server names; same contract as :func:`get_plugin_toolset_keys_nowait`.

name: _delivery_manager
doc:
Active manager, lazily discovering if it never ran — delivery must not depend on WHICH
surface imported us (dashboards/TUI/cron never import model_tools). ``getattr`` default
``True`` leaves test doubles untouched.

Hook/middleware delivery must not depend on WHICH surface imported us: dashboards, TUI slash workers,
query mode, and cron delivery paths never import ``model_tools`` (whose import side-effect is the
discovery trigger on the interactive CLI path), so hooks registered by user plugins were silently dead
on those surfaces (#50776, #67597, #67890, #50937; tracking #64178 — salvaged from PR #64188).

name: invoke_hook
doc:
Invoke a lifecycle hook (lazy-discovers first); return non-``None`` callback results.

Hot-path / observer hooks in ``_HOOK_TIMEOUT_BOUNDED_HOOKS`` and the policy hook ``pre_tool_call`` are
bounded by ``plugins.hook_callback_timeout`` (default 30s). On timeout the worker is abandoned (not
joined) so we do not reintroduce the #6622 hang. Timed-out or still-running ``pre_tool_call`` callbacks
fail closed with a block directive; other bounded hooks fail open (skip).
Ensures plugins are discovered on first invocation so callers in processes that never explicitly call
``discover_plugins()`` (gateway platform events, TUI slash workers, query mode, cron) still fire
callbacks registered by user plugins (tracking #64178).

name: ainvoke_hook
doc:
:func:`invoke_hook` for callers on an event loop: ``async def`` callbacks are awaited
there instead of bridged through a helper thread (see ``PluginManager.ainvoke_hook``).

name: render_system_prompt_sections
doc: Render plugin prompt sections after idempotent plugin discovery.

name: invoke_middleware
doc:
Invoke registered middleware callbacks (lazy-discovers like :func:`invoke_hook`).

Lazy-discovers plugins on first use — same delivery-parity guarantee as :func:`invoke_hook` (tracking
#64178).

name: has_middleware
doc:
True when middleware is registered for ``kind``; lazy-discovers first since callers gate
:func:`invoke_middleware` on it.

Lazy-discovers first: callers use this as a gate before :func:`invoke_middleware`, so a pre-discovery
``False`` here would silently skip delivery on surfaces that never ran discovery (#64178).

name: has_hook
doc:
True when a loaded plugin handles a hook (lazy-discovers first, like :func:`has_middleware`).

Lazy-discovers first — same gate-before-invoke rationale as :func:`has_middleware` (tracking #64178).

name: iter_hook_callbacks
doc: Return a stable snapshot of callbacks registered for a hook.

name: fire_pre_command_hook
arguments: *, surface: str, command: str, alias_used: str, args_raw: str, session_key: Optional[str]=None, platform: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Fire the observer-only ``pre_command`` hook; never raises. Directive-shaped returns are
logged at debug so future block/rewrite adopters are discoverable.

name: set_thread_tool_whitelist
arguments: allowed: Optional[set[str]], deny_msg_fmt: str="Tool '{tool_name}' denied: not in this thread's tool whitelist"

name: _get_pre_tool_call_directive_details
arguments: tool_name: str, args: Optional[dict[str, Any]], task_id: str='', session_id: str='', tool_call_id: str='', turn_id: str='', api_request_id: str='', middleware_trace: Optional[list[dict[str, Any]]]=None
doc:
Check ``pre_tool_call`` hooks for ``{"action": "block", "message"}`` (veto; message becomes
the tool result) or ``{"action": "approve", "message", "rule_key"?}`` (escalate ANY tool to the
human-approval gate; ``rule_key`` picks the ``[a]lways`` allowlist grain). Precedence is
``block`` > ``approve`` > none, not registration order: any plugin's valid veto wins over an
earlier plugin's request for human confirmation (#87420); among approves the first valid one
wins. Irrelevant returns are ignored.

name: get_pre_tool_call_directive
arguments: tool_name: str, args: Optional[dict[str, Any]], **hook_kwargs: Any
doc:
Back-compat: ``(directive, message)`` with directive ``"block"`` / ``"approve"`` / ``None``.
``hook_kwargs`` are the observability ids of :func:`_get_pre_tool_call_directive_details`.

name: get_pre_tool_call_block_message
arguments: tool_name: str, args: Optional[dict[str, Any]], **hook_kwargs: Any
doc: Deprecated shim: only the ``block`` message (or ``None``); ``approve`` is invisible here.

name: resolve_pre_tool_block
arguments: tool_name: str, args: Optional[dict[str, Any]], **hook_kwargs: Any
doc:
Resolve the pre_tool_call directive to a final block message (or ``None`` to proceed),
running the human-approval gate for ``approve``. See :func:`_resolve_block_from_details`.

name: _resolve_block_from_details
arguments: details: _PreToolCallDirective, tool_name: str, *, turn_id: str='', tool_call_id: str='', session_id: str=''
doc:
The ONE place for the fail-closed approval logic: ``block`` blocks with its message; an
``approve`` whose gate errors, denies, or times out is blocked; anything else proceeds.

significant_calls.expression: request_tool_approval(tool_name, details.message or "", rule_key=details.rule_key or tool_name)

name: _dispatch_pre_tool_call_hooks
arguments: tool_name: str, args: Optional[dict[str, Any]], **hook_kwargs: Any
doc:
Invoke ``pre_tool_call`` hooks once; return ``(block_message, modified_args)`` — the resolved
block/approve message (``None`` to proceed) and merged ``modify`` args (``None`` if none).

name: get_pre_verify_continue_message
arguments: *, session_id: str='', platform: str='', model: str='', coding: bool=False, attempt: int=0, final_response: str='', changed_paths: Optional[list[str]]=None
doc:
Check ``pre_verify`` hooks for ``{"action": "continue", "message"}`` (or Claude-Code Stop
``{"decision": "block", "reason"}``) to keep the turn going; first non-empty message wins, any
other return lets the turn finish. ``coding``/``attempt`` let hooks scope and self-throttle.

name: get_plugin_error_classification
arguments: *, provider: str='', model: str='', status_code: Optional[int]=None, error_type: str='', error_code: str='', error_message: str='', error_body: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, error: Optional[BaseException]=None, approx_tokens: int=0, context_length: int=0, num_messages: int=0
doc:
Consult ``transform_api_error_classification`` hooks BEFORE the built-in classifier.
Run-all-then-pick-first: the first valid result in registration order wins, losing valid results
warn (conflicts visible, not shadowed). Returns a sanitized dict (``reason`` -> ``FailoverReason``,
hint flags -> bool, ``message`` capped at 500) or ``None``. Privacy: inputs may be unredacted.

A callback returns ``None`` to decline, or a dict with a required ``"reason"`` (a
:class:`agent.error_classifier.FailoverReason` member or its string name) plus optional recovery-hint
overrides. Dispatch is run-all-then-pick-first: ``invoke_hook`` runs every registered callback with
failures isolated, then the first result carrying a valid reason wins in registration order — mirroring
:func:`get_pre_tool_call_block_message`, invalid or irrelevant returns are silently ignored so a
misbehaving plugin degrades to a no-op. When more than one callback returns a valid classification, the
losing results are skipped with a runtime warning (the #64714 skipped-transform rule) so conflicting
provider plugins are visible in logs instead of silently shadowed.

name: _ensure_plugins_discovered
doc: Return the global manager after idempotent (or ``force``d) discovery.

name: get_plugin_context_engine
doc: Return the plugin-registered context engine, or None.

name: get_plugin_command_handler
doc: Return the handler for a plugin-registered slash command, or ``None``.

name: get_plugin_commands
doc: Plugin commands dict (name -> {handler, description, plugin}) after idempotent discovery.

name: get_plugin_auxiliary_tasks
doc: Plugin auxiliary-task registration dicts sorted by ``key`` (after idempotent discovery).

name: get_plugin_toolsets
doc: Plugin toolsets as ``(key, label, description)`` tuples for the ``hermes tools`` TUI.

name: _abandon_load
doc: Mark this load as timed out; every later ``register_*``/``subscribe``/``on_unload`` is ignored.

name: plugin_id
doc: Return the effective registry id used for this plugin's namespaces.

name: has_plugin
doc:
Return True when another plugin is loaded and enabled (runtime probe for advisory
``requires_plugins``, #64165). Matches on registry key or manifest name.

name: _segments
doc: Validated plugin-relative settings path (warn + re-raise on rejection).

name: get_config
doc:
Read plugin-relative ``plugins.entries.<plugin_id>.settings.<key>`` (falls back to the
legacy ``config`` subtree for migration compatibility).

name: set_config
doc: Atomically write one value in this plugin's ``settings`` subtree.

name: state
doc: This plugin's profile-scoped durable JSON state facade.

name: platform_actions
doc:
Capability-gated platform action facade (``add_reaction``, ``set_thread_title``). Every call
re-checks ``gateway.platform_actions`` (legacy ``plugins.entries.<id>.allow_platform_actions``,
default OFF) and returns ``{"ok": bool, ...}`` — verbs never raise into hook dispatch; no adapter
handles or raw SDK objects.

name: _wrong_type
arguments: self, obj: Any, base_class: type, label: str, article: str='a'
doc: Warn-and-ignore gate shared by every registrar that requires a base class.

name: _refuse
doc: ``ValueError`` for a malformed registration (``what`` completes "tried to register ...").

name: _track
arguments: self, kind: str, key: str, release: Callable[[], None], *, persistent: bool=False
doc: Record host-owned cleanup for a registration (``persistent``: see ``_track_registration``).

name: _track_replacement
arguments: self, kind: str, key: str, *, slot: tuple, current: Any, previous: Any, restore: Callable[[Any], bool]
doc: Track one generation in a replaceable manager-local registration slot.

name: _track_mapping_entry
arguments: self, kind: str, key: str, mapping: dict[str, Any], entry: Any, previous: Any=_UNSET
doc:
Store ``entry`` under ``key`` in a manager-local mapping and lease the slot; unload restores
``previous`` (default: the displaced entry, or removes the key) only while ``entry`` is still
current.

name: _register_entry
arguments: self, kind: str, key: str, mapping: dict[str, Any], entry: Any, log_fmt: str, *log_args: Any, previous: Any=_UNSET
doc: Store + lease a manager-mapping entry, then debug-log ``log_fmt % (plugin name, *log_args)``.

name: _register_scoped_provider
arguments: self, provider: Any, *, kind: str, base_class: type, registry: Any, label: str, article: str='a', normalize: Optional[Callable[[str], str]]=lambda n: n.strip(), register: Optional[Callable[..., Any]]=None, reject_message: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Shared body of the ``register_<category>_provider`` methods: type-check (warn + ignore),
register in the scope-keyed ``registry``, lease the slot so unload restores the displaced entry.
``None`` when the registry refused/replaced the provider (``ValueError`` with ``reject_message``
set, or a falsy ``register``).

name: llm
doc:
Host-owned :class:`agent.plugin_llm.PluginLlm` facade: completions on the user's active
model/auth. Overrides (model, agent id, auth profile) are fail-closed, gated by
``plugins.entries.<plugin_id>.llm.*``.

name: subagent_lifecycle
doc:
Plugin-safe subagent lifecycle service: serializable handles and immutable snapshots,
never a live agent or private registry.

name: delegation_backends
doc:
``agent.delegation_backends.DelegationBackends``: list delegation backends and switch them per session or
globally (a ``/delegation`` command); a host remote facade, so it acts on the owner process.

name: profile_name
doc:
Active profile name (``"default"``, the ``~/.hermes/profiles/<name>`` id, or ``"custom"``),
derived from ``HERMES_HOME`` — not ``_cli_ref``, which is None outside the interactive CLI —
so gateway and kanban workers get it too.

name: current_cron_execution
doc: The cron run executing now (``cron.execution_identity.CronExecution``), else ``None``.

name: on_unload
doc:
Register a cleanup callback for unload: runs in reverse acquisition order interleaved
with registration teardown; exceptions are logged, never propagated.

name: spawn_task
doc: Spawn a supervised asyncio task; unload/force reload cancels it. Needs a running loop.

name: register_approval_transport
doc:
Register a human approval transport, inactive until ``security.approval.transport:
<name>`` selects it. It receives a redacted ``ApprovalRequest`` and returns only a
correlated decision; policy and persistence stay host-owned. ``present_fn`` may be async.

name: register_tool
arguments: self, name: str, toolset: str, schema: dict, handler: Callable, check_fn: Callable | None=None, requires_env: list | None=None, is_async: bool=False, description: str='', emoji: str='', override: bool=False
doc:
Register a tool in the global registry and track it as plugin-provided. ``override=True``
replaces a same-named built-in (without it a name claimed by another toolset is rejected) and
needs operator opt-in via ``plugins.entries.<plugin_id>.allow_tool_override: true`` — otherwise
any enabled plugin could silently replace a privileged built-in like ``write_file`` (#23194).

name: has_capability
doc:
True when *capability* is live for this plugin (probe, then degrade gracefully). Bundled
plugins are trusted for ``tools.override``; otherwise granted_capabilities or the legacy
``allow_*`` key decides. Unknown ids / unreadable consent -> False (fail closed).

name: call_mcp
arguments: self, server: str, tool: str, arguments: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, timeout: float=30
doc:
Call ``tool`` on MCP ``server`` synchronously through :mod:`tools.mcp_tool`'s native client
(same trust gates, breaker, reconnect — never a parallel connection). Servers not in
``plugins.entries.<plugin_id>.mcp_allowlist`` raise ``PermissionError`` (default-deny). ``timeout``
clamps to 1–600s; results over ~64KB are truncated with a marker.

This is a per-server grant, deliberately not ambient authority over every configured server.
TODO(#64228): swap the per-server allowlist for the declared capability model once it lands
(per-tool grants, expiry, ro/rw).

name: _mcp_envelope
doc: Normalize an MCP handler result string into a stable envelope.

name: _mcp_allowlist
doc: Operator-granted MCP server allowlist; missing/unreadable -> [] (default-deny).

name: _tool_override_allowed
doc:
Whether this plugin may override built-in tools: bundled plugins are trusted (a maintainer
choice, not privilege escalation); others need ``tools.override`` via
:func:`plugin_capability_granted` (granted_capabilities OR legacy ``allow_tool_override: true``,
still honored for backward compatibility; #64228).

name: inject_message
arguments: self, content: str, role: str='user', *, session_key: str | None=None, origin: Mapping[str, Any] | None=None
doc:
Queue *content* for a session (``session_key``) or a chat in this plugin's own profile
(``origin``); ``True`` means a host accepted it. Contract: plugins_injection.py, plugin docs.

name: session_cwd
doc: The calling session's recorded cwd, never the gateway's own (``plugin_session``).

name: session_surface
doc: The calling session's client (``cli``/``tui``/``desktop``/``acp``) or messaging platform.

name: post_message
doc:
Post *text* into the session bound to this call; the handle's ``edit(text)`` updates it in
place. Never raises (``ok=False`` + ``error`` with no conversation): ``plugin_messages.py``.

name: apost_message
doc: ``post_message`` for async code on the gateway loop (edit with ``await handle.aedit``).

name: ask_choice
doc:
From a sync slash-command handler: ask its user to pick one of *choices* (``str`` or
``{value, label?, description?}``); the value, or None if unanswerable: ``plugin_choices.py``.

name: _gateway_injection_allowed
doc:
Return whether this plugin may trigger gateway session turns (read from the plugin's
own profile config, never the calling thread's ambient home).

name: register_cli_command
arguments: self, name: str, help: str, setup_fn: Callable, handler_fn: Callable | None=None, description: str=''
doc:
Register a CLI subcommand (``hermes <name> ...``). *setup_fn* receives the argparse
subparser; *handler_fn* becomes ``set_defaults(func=...)``.

name: register_command
arguments: self, name: str, handler: Callable, description: str='', args_hint: str='', argument_mode: str | None=None
doc:
Register an in-session slash command (``/name``); handler ``fn(raw_args: str) -> str | None``
(sync or async), plus the session-context keywords it declares (``plugin_command_dispatch``). ``args_hint`` (e.g. ``"<file>"``) lets adapters like Discord surface an argument
field; without it the command registers parameterless there but still accepts trailing text.

name: dispatch_tool
doc:
Dispatch a tool call through the registry with the parent agent (when available)
resolved automatically; returns the handler's JSON string. ``kwargs`` forward to dispatch.

name: register_context_engine
doc:
Register the (single) ``agent.context_engine.ContextEngine`` replacing the built-in
ContextCompressor; a second registration is rejected with a warning.

name: register_context_reference
doc:
Register a :class:`agent.context_references.ContextReferenceProvider`; ``provider.prefix``
defines ``@<prefix>:``. Built-in prefixes (diff, staged, file, folder, git, url) are
rejected.

name: register_memory_provider
doc:
Record a memory provider (inert). Activation is owned by ``plugins/memory`` via
``memory.provider``; a provider reaching here was loaded by the general manager, and
without this method its ``register()`` would fail on a missing attribute.

name: register_dashboard_auth_provider
doc:
Register a :class:`hermes_cli.dashboard_auth.DashboardAuthProvider` for the dashboard
auth gate (non-loopback bind without ``--insecure``). Wrong type / duplicate name warn and
are ignored, never raised.

name: register_platform
arguments: self, name: str, label: str, adapter_factory: Callable, check_fn: Callable, validate_config: Callable | None=None, required_env: list | None=None, install_hint: str='', **entry_kwargs: Any
doc:
Register a gateway platform adapter (``adapter_factory(PlatformConfig) -> BasePlatformAdapter``).
``check_fn`` is a PASSIVE "deps importable?" probe that must never install (status displays call
it freely); an ACTIVE installer goes in ``ensure_deps_fn`` (called from ``create_adapter()`` when
``check_fn`` is False). Extra kwargs (``setup_fn``, ``emoji``, ``allowed_users_env``,
``platform_hint``, ``ensure_deps_fn``) forward to ``PlatformEntry``; unknown keys raise TypeError.

name: register_slack_action_handler
doc:
Register a Slack Block Kit action handler, wired into ``slack_bolt.AsyncApp`` at connect.
``action_id`` is anything ``slack_bolt.App.action()`` accepts; ``callback`` is
``async def handler(ack, body, action)`` (``await ack()`` within 3s). Raises ``ValueError`` for
a non-callable callback or empty ``action_id``.

name: register_platform_handler
doc:
Register ``factory(native, adapter)``, invoked at ``connect()`` before/as the core handlers
register (``adapter`` read-only). ``native``: telegram PTB ``Application``, discord
``commands.Bot``, slack ``AsyncApp``, matrix client, teams ``App``, dingtalk
``DingTalkStreamClient``, line aiohttp ``web.Application``, others ``None``. Keep SDK imports
inside the factory; exceptions are logged and the platform still connects. Scope handlers in
first-match dispatch tables so core flows keep working. Raises ``ValueError`` when not callable
or platform is empty.

name: register_telegram_handler
doc:
``register_platform_handler("telegram", factory)``. PTB dispatches only the FIRST matching
handler per group and core registers a catch-all ``CallbackQueryHandler`` — always scope with
``pattern=`` or you swallow the core button flows.

name: register_auxiliary_task
arguments: self, key: str, *, display_name: str, description: str, defaults: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, inherit_from: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Register an auxiliary LLM task with its own ``auxiliary.<key>`` config block (picker entry,
``AUXILIARY_<KEY>_*`` env bridge, defaults merged into loaded configs). ``defaults`` may
override provider/model/base_url/api_key/timeout/extra_body (unknown keys kept verbatim).
``inherit_from`` names a built-in or already-registered auxiliary task whose effective
configuration becomes the base for this one; it is resolved at read time, so the task tracks
the base's current config instead of snapshotting it (precedence: inherited base, then
``defaults``, then user config in ``auxiliary.<key>``). An unknown or self-referential
``inherit_from`` logs a warning and registers the task without inheritance.
Raises ``ValueError`` for an empty/invalid key, a built-in key, or another plugin's key.

name: register_redaction_patterns
doc:
Additively register secret-token regexes with :mod:`agent.redact`; returns the count accepted.
Plugins can over-redact, never weaken built-ins; ``security.redact_secrets: false`` applies
equally. Each pattern must compile and start with >= 2 literal characters; invalid entries warn
and are skipped.

name: register_locale
arguments: self, lang: str, source: str | Path | Mapping[str, Any], *, endonym: Optional[str]=None, rtl: bool=False, surface: str='core'
doc:
Register a language-pack layer for ``lang`` (``pl``, ``pt-br``): ``source`` is a YAML file path or
a nested/flat mapping of ``dotted.key: text``. ``surface`` is ``core`` (Python ``t()``), ``tui`` or
``desktop`` (served to the renderers over ``i18n.catalog``). Partial catalogs are fine; the last
registration wins key by key. Resets the i18n caches; never changes ``display.language``. Raises
``ValueError`` for a malformed id/surface/file and ``FileNotFoundError`` for a missing path.

name: register_locale_dir
arguments: self, path: str | Path, *, metadata: Optional[Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]]=None
doc:
Register every ``<lang>[.tui|.desktop].yaml`` under ``path`` (a pack's ``locales/`` dir). The
loader calls this for plugins declaring ``provides_locales``; ``metadata`` maps ids to
``{endonym, rtl}``. A broken file is skipped with a warning so one typo never disables the pack.

name: register_hook
doc: Register a lifecycle hook callback (unknown names warn but are still stored).

name: register_middleware
doc:
Register behavior-changing middleware (request kinds rewrite the payload, execution kinds
wrap the callback). Unknown kinds warn but are stored.

name: _track_callback
arguments: self, kind: str, key: str, callback: Callable, mapping: dict[str, list[Callable]], valid: set[str]
doc: Append ``callback`` under ``key`` (warning on unknown ``key``) and lease its removal.

name: register_system_prompt_section
arguments: self, id: str, content: str | Callable[[Mapping[str, Any]], str], *, position: str='after_memory', max_chars: int=DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_SECTION_MAX_CHARS
doc:
Register bounded context frozen into each new session prompt. Callables receive a
read-only session-info mapping; the rendered prompt is persisted by core verbatim.

name: emit
doc:
Publish bare *event* as ``<plugin_key>:<event>`` (namespace FORCED to this plugin); return
the subscriber count scheduled. Any ``':'`` in the name (``hermes:x`` is reserved for core,
foreign namespaces forbidden) raises ``ValueError``. Delivery is fire-and-forget via a
single-worker queue: order preserved, a blocking subscriber cannot stall the emitter.

name: subscribe
doc:
Subscribe to a fully-qualified ``<plugin_key>:<event>`` name (unrestricted — only
emitting is namespace-gated). Owner-tagged so unload removes zombie callbacks.

name: has_gateway_message_injector
doc: Return whether a live gateway can accept plugin-triggered turns.

name: set_gateway_message_injector
arguments: self, owner: object, injector: Callable[..., bool]
doc: Publish a live gateway injector and its lifecycle owner.

name: clear_gateway_message_injector
doc: Clear the injector only when it still belongs to ``owner``.

name: inject_gateway_message
doc: Submit a plugin-triggered turn to the live gateway.

name: has_tui_message_injector
doc: Return whether a live Ink TUI / desktop host can accept plugin-triggered turns.

name: set_tui_message_injector
arguments: self, owner: object, injector: Callable[..., bool]
doc: Publish a live TUI/desktop injector. Does not touch the messaging-gateway slot.

name: clear_tui_message_injector
doc: Clear the TUI injector only when it still belongs to ``owner``.

name: inject_tui_message
doc: Submit a plugin-triggered turn to the live TUI/desktop host.

name: discover_and_load
doc:
Scan all plugin sources and load each plugin found; ``force`` unloads first so config
changes / new bundled backends become visible in long-lived sessions.

name: _re_register_config_hooks_after_force
doc:
Restore config-owned shell hooks/outbound webhooks after a force clear; each guarded
independently so one failing does not skip the other.

name: _refresh_secret_sources_after_discovery
doc:
If any plugin secret source is enabled (per its own ``is_enabled(cfg)``, honoring custom
activation), reset the cache and re-apply. Fail-open: never raises into discover_and_load.

name: _discover_and_load_inner
doc: The actual discovery sweep — see :meth:`discover_and_load`.

name: _gate_manifest
arguments: self, manifest: PluginManifest, disabled: set[str], enabled: Optional[set[str]]
doc:
Route one winning manifest per :func:`gate_manifest`: load now, defer, or record as
skipped (introspection-only placeholder). Returns True only for plugins that go through the
dependency-ordered load pass.

name: register_approval_transport
arguments: self, name: str, present_fn: Callable, *, plugin_id: str
doc:
Manager-level registration (public API kept for out-of-tree plugins); the PluginContext
method is the tracked path plugins normally use. Same validation, no unload tracking.

name: get_approval_transport
doc: Return a transport only inside the profile that registered it.

name: _collect_directory_manifests
doc: Directory manifests in full-discovery order (see :func:`collect_directory_manifests`).

name: has_enabled_portable_mcp
doc:
Probe enabled portable MCP packages without loading plugins (shares the full-discovery
manifest collection so precedence/gating cannot diverge).

name: _scan_directory
arguments: self, path: Path, source: str, skip_names: Optional[set[str]]=None
doc: Read manifests under *path* (see :func:`scan_directory`).

name: _scan_entry_points
doc: Read installed plugin entry points (see :func:`discover_entrypoint_manifests`).

name: get_slack_action_handlers
doc: ``(action_id, callback, plugin_name)`` tuples for the Slack adapter to wire at connect.

name: get_platform_handler_factories
doc:
``(factory, plugin_name)`` tuples for one platform; adapters call ``factory(native,
adapter)`` at connect (see :meth:`PluginContext.register_platform_handler`).

name: get_telegram_handler_factories
doc: Back-compat alias for ``get_platform_handler_factories("telegram")``.

name: list_plugins
doc: Return a list of info dicts for all discovered plugins.

name: find_plugin_skill
doc: Return the ``Path`` to a plugin skill's SKILL.md, or ``None``.

name: list_plugin_skills
doc: Return sorted bare names of all skills registered by *plugin_name*.

name: list_plugin_skill_metadata
doc: Return progressive-disclosure metadata for registered plugin skills.

name: list_automation_blueprints
doc: Plugin-registered ``AutomationBlueprint``s, sorted by key.

name: get_portable_mcp_servers
doc: Return a defensive copy of enabled portable MCP server configs.

name: remove_plugin_skill
doc: Remove a stale registry entry (silently ignores missing keys).

name: plugin_activation_summary
doc:
``{name, key, activated_now: {kind: [names]}, deferred: {kind: [names]}}`` for one loaded plugin,
read from what it actually registered (ownership ledger + handler registries), not from what its
manifest promises. Keys appear only when non-empty.

``activated_now``: ``gateway_commands`` (slash names), ``gateway_transforms`` / ``hooks`` (hook names),
``callbacks`` (platforms with a ``register_platform_handler`` factory / Slack action ids), ``locales``
(``<lang>.<surface>`` language-pack layers).
``deferred``: ``tools`` (tool names; next session), ``prompt`` (section ids; next session),
``mcp_servers`` (the plugin's mcp.json server names exactly as registered; until ``mcp.reload``).

name: activation_summaries
doc: One summary per loaded (non-deferred-platform, non-errored) plugin — the ``on_plugin_loaded`` payload.

name: find_activation
doc: The summary for ``name`` (manifest name, canonical key, or bare leaf of the key).

name: activate_plugin_now
doc:
After an install/enable/update: load the plugin in THIS process (so ``on_plugin_loaded``
subscribers here — the TUI/Desktop server — see it), connect its MCP servers and hand them plus
its skills to the open chats of this profile (:func:`load_and_go_live`), and nudge the running
gateway to load it too over its control socket so live adapters re-wire their handlers. A caller
in another process (``hermes plugins install``) passes ``in_process=False``; the running Desktop /
dashboard backend is then asked to do the in-process half (:func:`notify_serve_backend`). Never raises.

Returns ``{"gateway_reloaded": bool, "activation": summary | None, "restart_required": bool}``.
``activation.live_now`` lists what is usable in open chats now; ``activation.deferred`` what waits
for the next session. ``restart_required`` is True only when no gateway answered (old gateway, not
running).

name: reload_running_gateway
doc:
Ask the gateway serving this profile (its own socket, else the multiplexer's for a served
secondary) to force plugin re-discovery, so an enable loads and a disable unloads in the running
gateway now. The ``reload-plugins`` answer, or None when no gateway answered.

name: gateway_reload_hint
doc:
One honest sentence after disabling plugin ``name``, a change only the gateway's re-discovery
applies (an open session stops running its commands at once). Callbacks the plugin already
wired into platform adapters outlive a reload (the plugin guide), so a restart still ends those.

name: load_and_go_live
doc:
Force-rediscover plugins in THIS process under the caller's profile scope, connect ``name``'s
MCP servers and hand them (and its skills) to this profile's open chats with a turn note. Returns
the activation summary with ``live_now: {mcp_servers, skills}``; ``deferred`` then keeps only what
waits for the next session (Python ``tools``, ``prompt``). None when the plugin did not load.

name: _serve_backend_record
doc: The host-owner record, else the Desktop child's (a Desktop-only box has no host owner).

name: notify_serve_backend
doc:
Ask the running dashboard / Desktop backend (``hermes serve``, found through its host record) to
run :func:`load_and_go_live` for ``name`` in ``home``. None when no backend answers. Never raises.

significant_calls.expression:
urllib.request.Request(
            f"http://{format_url_host(hr.dial_host(record))}:{record.port}"
            "/api/dashboard/agent-plugins/activate",
            data=json.dumps({"name": name, "home": str(home)}).encode("utf-8"), method="POST",
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "X-Hermes-Session-Token": token})

name: _gateway_present
doc:
A gateway runs for this profile (its own, or the multiplexer serving it from the root), or a
gateway service is installed for it.

name: report_activation
doc:
After a CLI install/enable: load *name* where it can go live now (:func:`activate_plugin_now`)
and print :func:`activation_hint`, or nothing when there is nothing to say.

name: activation_hint
doc:
One honest sentence for CLI surfaces from an :func:`activate_plugin_now` result; empty when
there is nothing to say.

name: connect_plugin_mcp
arguments: activation: dict[str, Any], portable: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
doc:
Connect every portable MCP server ``activation`` defers, under the caller's profile scope.
``portable`` is the manager's portable server configs, read together with ``activation``.

Returns ``[{name, connected, tools, error?}]``, one row per server; a server that fails to
connect is reported, never retried. Never raises.

name: _utility_suffixes
doc:
The resource/prompt wrappers every MCP server gets (``mcp__x__list_resources``, ...): callable,
but they say nothing about what the plugin does, so they are left out of counts and listings.

name: plugin_skills
doc: ``[{name, description}]`` for the skills ``plugin_key`` registered (qualified ``<ns>:<skill>``).

name: catalog_plugin_skill
doc:
The registered name of a plugin skill written ``<catalog-name>:<skill>`` (``blender:blender``), or
None when that catalog plugin is not installed in this profile or registered no such skill. A
portable plugin's skills register under a collision-resistant namespace
(``agent-plugin-<slug>-<sha8>:<skill>``, ``hermes_cli/plugins_manifest.py``), so the readable form
is never itself a name ``skill_view`` resolves.

name: live_notice
doc:
The note an open chat gets on its next tool result or turn (``agent/plugin_live_notes.py``): the
plugin's skills and, per MCP server, its tool prefix and count or why it did not connect. Tools are
not listed one by one: the note stays in the chat's history and rides every later request, and
``tool_search`` lists them on demand. Empty when nothing of the plugin is live now.

name: _tool_prefix
doc: ``mcp__<server>__``: the start of every registered tool name of ``server``.

name: candidate_member_dirs
arguments: candidate_enabled: Iterable[str], candidate_disabled: Iterable[str]=(), *, active_plugins_dir: Optional[Path]=None, extra_dirs: Iterable[Path]=()
doc:
Shipped callers' member-list adapter; new discovery belongs to PM.

Without an active plugins dir, preserve every home's recorded selection.

name: admit_plugin_set_change
arguments: candidate_enabled: set, candidate_disabled: set, *, active_plugins_dir: Optional[Path]=None, extra_dirs: Iterable[Path]=(), expected_config: str | None=None, plugin: Optional[str]=None
doc:
PM discovers and validates the proposed union under its install lock.

No config or dependency selection is written by this application process. *plugin* names the
plugin being admitted so a resolver conflict is reported against it (:class:`DependencyConflict`).

name: build_auxiliary_task_entry
arguments: me: str, owner_id: str, key: str, *, display_name: str, description: str, defaults: Optional[dict[str, Any]], inherit_from: Optional[str], registered: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
doc:
Registry entry for a plugin auxiliary task, or ``ValueError`` for a bad key.

``me`` is the manifest name (for messages); ``owner_id`` is the canonical id ``ctx.llm`` is
bound to, so agent/plugin_llm.py can match it. ``registered`` is the manager's current
``_aux_tasks`` (re-registration by the same owner is allowed).

name: _marker_path
doc:
The last-run marker, resolved per call (tests monkeypatch
get_hermes_home). Derivation only — NO mkdir: a due-check or any
read path must not create user state.

name: _results_path
doc: The last check's per-plugin results, next to the marker (derivation only).

name: snapshot_installs
doc:
The install records an update check is about to compare against. Take it BEFORE the check runs:
a record read afterwards may already include an update that finished during the check.

name: record_check_results
doc:
Persist a completed check so surfaces that list plugins (the Desktop Plugins tab) can show an
update without a network call per listing. Each row carries the install record it was checked
against (*checked_installs*, from :func:`snapshot_installs` before the check), so a later reader
can tell whether the result still applies. Never raises.

name: _install_fingerprint
doc: The parts of an install record an update check depends on.

name: cached_git_updates
doc:
``{plugin name: what the update moves to}`` (a commit or a feed version) for git installs the last
check found behind. A result is dropped once the install it was checked against changed (updated,
reinstalled from another source, or pinned with ``--ref``), so Desktop never offers an update that
already landed or one ``update`` would refuse.

name: _markers_dir
doc: The markers dir, created on demand — WRITE paths only.

name: check_interval_hours
doc: plugins.auto_update_check_hours; 0 disables; default 24.

name: check_due
arguments: now: Optional[float]=None, interval_hours: Optional[float]=None, config_get: Callable | None=None
doc: The clock gate: last-run marker vs the interval.

name: run_scheduled_check
arguments: *, run_checks_fn: Callable[..., list], plugins_dir: Path, apply_updates_fn: Optional[Callable[[str], None]]=None, log=None, config_get: Callable | None=None, now: Optional[float]=None
doc:
One cadence tick: gate → check → receipt → (opt-in) apply.

Returns the check results, or None when not due / disabled / another
tick is already in flight. NEVER raises — a cadence failure is
logged, never fatal.

name: _run_check_locked
arguments: *, run_checks_fn: Callable[..., list], plugins_dir: Path, apply_updates_fn: Optional[Callable[[str], None]], log, config_get: Callable | None=None

name: maybe_run_gateway_check
arguments: *, run_checks_fn: Optional[Callable[..., list]]=None, apply_updates_fn: Optional[Callable[[str], None]]=None, plugins_dir: Optional[Path]=None, log=None, now: Optional[float]=None
doc:
The tick every gateway boot / housekeeping pass calls.

Fills in the REAL seams ``run_scheduled_check`` leaves injectable:
the same read-only ``plugins_updates.run_checks`` the manual
``hermes plugins check-updates`` uses (urllib feed fetch, git
ls-remote, PyPI latest), the real plugins dir, and the manual
``hermes plugins update <name>`` flow as the opt-in apply path —
auto-apply rides the identical security/consent/scan pipeline.

Returns the check results, or None when not due / disabled. Due-gated
by ``plugins.auto_update_check_hours`` (0 disables); a network error
costs one warning and a stamped marker — never an apply.

name: _resolve_git_executable
doc: Resolve a git binary for subprocess use when ``PATH`` may be minimal.

name: _console
doc: A fresh Rich console (rich is imported lazily).

name: _table
doc: A Rich ``Table(**kwargs)`` with ``(header, style)`` *columns* added in order.

name: _fail
doc: Print *message* and exit 1.

name: _ask_yes
doc: One y/N question; EOF / Ctrl-C count as "no".

name: _config_value
doc: Read ``keys`` from config.yaml; *default* on a missing key or any load failure.

name: _clone_timeout_seconds
doc: Deadline for plugin clone and pinned fetch, scoped to the active profile.

name: _config_name_set
doc: A list-valued config key as a set (empty on any failure or non-list).

name: _config_str
doc: A string config key; empty/missing/failed reads coerce to *default*.

name: _write_config_value
arguments: section: str, key: str, value: Any
doc: Persist ``config[section][key] = value`` to config.yaml (creating the section).

name: _scan_on_install_enabled
doc: Install/update-time security scanning; on by default, off via ``plugins.scan_on_install: false``.

name: _scan_plugin_tree
arguments: plugin_dir: Path, identifier: str, *, force: bool, scan_decision_cb=None, reviewed_pin: bool=False
doc:
Scan *plugin_dir* and enforce the install policy.

Verdicts: safe → proceed; caution → needs confirmation (``force=True`` or a truthy
``scan_decision_cb(result)``); dangerous → always blocked (:class:`PluginScanBlocked`).
*reviewed_pin* marks a tree checked out at a curated-catalog sha: that exact tree passed
the same scanner at admission with a human reading the caution findings, so caution is
accepted without a prompt (the Desktop has none). Dangerous still blocks — a signature
added after review is exactly the case the backstop exists for.
Returns the ScanResult, or None when scanning is disabled.

name: _preserved_files_note
doc: Scan-block text for a tree that also holds user files preserved from the installed copy.

name: _scan_merged_tree
arguments: plugin_dir: Path, identifier: str, merged: Optional[list[str]], **kwargs
doc:
:func:`_scan_plugin_tree` for a candidate that may hold carried user files (*merged*).

A block then names the findings that sit in those files, so user data does not read as a
malicious upstream revision; the original block stays chained as the cause.

name: _plugins_dir
doc: Return the user plugins directory, creating it if needed.

name: _sanitize_plugin_name
arguments: name: str, plugins_dir: Path, *, allow_subdir: bool=False
doc:
Validate a plugin name and return the safe target path inside *plugins_dir*.

Raises ``ValueError`` on traversal or a target outside the plugins directory. ``allow_subdir``
permits forward slashes so category keys like ``web/firecrawl`` can be looked up
(``..`` and backslashes stay rejected); install paths keep ``False`` — a clone lands top-level.

name: _resolve_git_url
doc:
Turn an identifier into a cloneable Git URL and optional subdirectory.

``http://`` and ``file://`` are accepted but trigger a security warning at install time.

name: _resolve_subdir_within
doc:
Resolve ``subdir`` inside ``clone_root``; ``..``, absolute paths and symlinks may not
escape the clone. Raises ``PluginOperationError`` if it escapes, is missing, or is a file.

name: _repo_name_from_url
doc: Repo name from a Git URL (last path component; ssh-style ``git@host:repo`` splits on ':').

name: _native_manifest_file
doc: ``plugin.yaml`` (or ``plugin.yml``) under *plugin_dir*, or None when neither exists.

name: _has_portable_manifest
doc: True when ``plugin.json`` exists (or is a symlink, even dangling) under *plugin_dir*.

name: _load_yaml_manifest
doc: ``yaml.safe_load`` of *manifest_file* (``{}`` when empty); raises on any read/parse error.

name: _read_manifest
doc: Read a native or portable manifest, preferring native YAML.

name: _looks_like_plugin_dir
doc: True when *target* has a native/portable manifest or a package ``__init__.py``.

name: _copy_example_files
doc:
Copy ``*.example`` files to their real names (``config.yaml.example`` -> ``config.yaml``),
never overwriting an existing file so reinstall keeps user config.

name: _missing_env_specs
doc:
``requires_env`` entries (plain names or ``{name, description, url, secret}`` dicts,
normalised to dicts; nameless entries dropped) whose variable is unset in ``~/.hermes/.env``.

name: _clone_failure_message
doc:
Plain-words clone failure: what to check (address, network, private repo), raw git text last.

The text reaches ``_fail`` -> Rich ``console.print``: escape the git output so ``[...]`` in it is
not parsed as markup.

name: _require_installed_plugin
doc: The plugin path if it exists; else exit 1 (invalid name, or a listing of installed plugins).

name: _unknown_plugin_message
doc: ``No plugin named ...`` with the exact-name rule and the two commands that resolve it.

name: _save_enabled_set
doc: Frozen old-updater import: never resurrect a raw plugin-selection write.

name: _admit_and_save_plugin_sets
arguments: enabled: set, disabled: set, *, extra_dirs=(), console=None, action: str='enable', expected_config=None, plugin: Optional[str]=None
doc:
ONE admission authority for proposed enabled/disabled sets (C13):
the candidate union is resolved against the ACTIVE environment and
the config commits inside the same worker-owned PM transaction — a refusal or a config-write failure
publishes nothing: previous config bytes AND previous environment
stay exactly in place. Raises :class:`AdmissionRefused` (UI callers
catch and surface it — admission never auto-disables to fit); a resolver
conflict raises its :class:`DependencyConflict` subclass naming *plugin*.

name: ensure_basic_auth_plugin_enabled_in_config
doc:
Drop the bundled basic dashboard-auth plugin from ``plugins.disabled`` in *cfg*.

``hermes setup`` / ``hermes plugins disable basic`` can park it there while
``dashboard.basic_auth`` is configured, and password auth then silently fails.
Returns True when modified.

name: _discard_key_and_leaf
doc:
Drop *key* and its bare leaf (``web/exa`` -> ``exa``) from *names*, so a
stale legacy bare-name entry can't keep vetoing the canonical key.

name: _plugin_aliases
doc:
Every spelling a config list may hold for *key*: the key, its bare leaf and the manifest name.
The loader matches BOTH the canonical key (``web/firecrawl``) and the manifest name
(``web-firecrawl``), so a stale entry under any form vetoes an enable ("explicit disable wins").
Pass *entries* to reuse one :func:`_discover_all_plugins` scan across several keys.

name: _activate_key
doc:
Transactionally persist canonical *key*, purging aliases from the opposing list.

False when the lists already say so (nothing written). PM owns the selection and dependency
publication together, so every CLI/dashboard activation surface goes through the same admission
transaction instead of writing ``config.yaml`` directly.

name: _forget_plugin_config
doc:
Drop every trace of a removed plugin (its :func:`_plugin_aliases`, taken BEFORE the tree went)
from config.yaml: allow/deny-list entries, ``plugins.entries.<id>`` grants and a ``memory.provider``
selection naming it. A later reinstall under the same name must start from the "Enable now?"
decision, not inherit a stale enable or grant (#54336); a dangling ``memory.provider`` would make
the next agent init re-clone the plugin from the catalog, silently undoing the uninstall.
Returns ``{"cleared_memory_provider": True}`` when the selection was reset.

name: _set_plugin_enabled
arguments: name: str, *, enable: bool, aliases=(), console=None
doc: Submit the command's delta with the version of the selection it read.

name: _apply_activation
arguments: enabled: set, disabled: set, key: str, aliases, *, enable: bool
doc: Add canonical *key* to the target list and purge it, its bare leaf and *aliases* from the other.

name: _resolve_plugin_key
doc:
Canonical registry key for a manifest name / directory name / path key, or ``None``.
The single normalization point so enable/disable write the key ``PluginManager`` gates on.

name: _catalog_installed_dir
doc:
Install dir whose installer-owned record names catalog entry *name* (``hermes-memory-wiki`` is
installed as ``plugins/memory-wiki``), else None (also when two dirs claim it). Read through
:func:`catalog_install_record` (``.install-metadata.json``), never the tree, so a URL-installed
repo cannot claim a catalog entry's name.

name: _find_plugin_entry
doc:
THE plugin name resolver for every verb (enable/disable/show/capabilities/remove/update, the
dashboard and the Desktop hub): the discovered ``(name, version, description, source, dir_path, key)``
