doc:
Register a read-only skill resolvable as ``'<plugin_name>:<name>'`` via ``skill_view()``,
listed by ``skills_list`` and in the system prompt's ``<available_skills>`` while the plugin
is enabled. Not copied into ``~/.hermes/skills/``. Raises ``ValueError`` (``':'``/invalid
chars) or ``FileNotFoundError``.

name: register_automation_blueprint
arguments: self, key: str, *, title: str, description: str, schedule_template: str, prompt_template: str, category: str='general', slots: Iterable[Any]=(), deliver_default: str='origin', skills: Iterable[str]=(), tags: Iterable[str]=()
doc:
Add an Automation Blueprint to this profile's catalog as ``'<plugin_name>:<key>'``
(``/blueprint``, the dashboard/Desktop gallery). Fields mirror
:class:`cron.blueprint_catalog.AutomationBlueprint`; ``slots`` are ``BlueprintSlot`` field
mappings. Malformed input or a duplicate key logs a warning and returns ``None``.

name: suppress_plugin_discovery
doc:
``discover_plugins()`` is a no-op inside; the scope's manager stays undiscovered, so the
first real consumer after the block still loads its plugins.

name: _select_entry_point_group
doc: Return one metadata entry-point group across supported Python APIs.

name: discover_entrypoint_manifests
doc:
Return metadata-only manifests for installed entry-point plugins. Kind comes from an import-free source
scan (memory/model providers route to their own discovery). Capabilities come from the companion
``hermes_agent.plugin_capabilities`` group (``<plugin-id>.<capability-id>`` entries pointing at the same
object), so consent works without importing plugin code. Failures are isolated per entry point.

name: _classify_entrypoint_value_kind
doc: Classify an entry-point target by import-free source scan (unresolvable -> standalone).

name: _get_disabled_plugins
doc: Read ``plugins.disabled`` — a deny-list that wins over ``plugins.enabled``.

name: _get_enabled_plugins
doc:
Read the ``plugins.enabled`` allow-list (plugins are opt-in). ``None`` = key missing/malformed ("nothing
enabled yet"; the first ``migrate_config`` run grandfathers installed user plugins); ``set()`` = explicitly
empty; else the allow-list.

name: scan_directory
arguments: path: Path, source: str, *, skip_names: Optional[set[str]]=None, prefix: str='', depth: int=0
doc:
Read manifests under *path*: flat ``<root>/<name>/plugin.yaml`` (key ``name``) or category
``<root>/<cat>/<name>/plugin.yaml`` (key ``cat/name``; a manifest-less directory recurses one level, depth
capped at two). *skip_names* ignores top-level names; portable ``plugin.json`` packages are accepted
alongside YAML manifests.

name: collect_directory_manifests
doc:
Read directory manifests in full-discovery order (bundled top-level, bundled/platforms, user, opt-in
project) without loading or mutating anything, so startup probes share the exact precedence/containment
rules of the real discovery sweep.

name: resolve_manifest_winners
doc:
Later sources win on key collision (project > user > bundled): a same-named copy under
``~/.hermes/plugins/<name>`` is the documented way to override a bundled plugin, and is logged. A flat
user/project manifest that claims a bundled key from a *differently named* directory is an impostor, not
an override (``impostor_dir/plugin.yaml`` with ``name: kanban``): it is skipped with a warning so
``hermes plugins enable kanban`` never activates unrelated code under the bundled name.

name: gate_manifest
arguments: manifest: PluginManifest, disabled: set[str], enabled: Optional[set[str]]
doc:
Decide how one winning manifest is handled. Gate order matters: legacy relay refusal, explicit disable,
category-owned kinds (exclusive / model-provider), bundled auto-loads (backend now, platform deferred),
then ``plugins.enabled`` opt-in (path-derived key or legacy bare name).

name: _scan
arguments: label: str, directory: Path, source: str, skip_names: Optional[set[str]]=None

name: _placeholder
arguments: error: Optional[str], level: int, message: str, *args, enabled: bool=False

name: _policy_error_block_directive
arguments: hook_name: str, cb: Callable, exc: BaseException
doc:
Block directive for a fail-closed hook whose callback raised: names the callback and the
error (truncated — a hook that embeds tool args in its exception must not grow the tool
result) so the operator can tell a crashing guard from a slow one.

name: is_valid_system_prompt_section_id
doc: Return whether *value* is a stable, heading-safe section identifier.

name: format_system_prompt_section
doc: Render an auditable, length-framed block recoverable from the full prompt.

name: format_system_prompt_sections
doc: Render the canonical container used for persistence recovery.

name: _hook_call_identity
doc:
Identity of the call this callback fires for, or ``None`` when the event has none.

Concurrent invocations of the same tool in one session must not collapse into one
gate key: they are different work, and treating the second as a duplicate drops the
hook as if a callback had timed out (upstream #98382). The identity is already in the
payload; nothing new is plumbed. Deliberately not ``api_request_id`` — one API request
carries many tool calls, which would re-collapse the keys.

name: _hook_uses_callback_timeout
doc: Whether *hook_name* should run under the non-blocking timeout path.

name: resolve_plugin_command_result
doc:
Resolve a plugin command result, awaiting async handlers: ``asyncio.run`` when no loop is
running, else a helper thread with its own loop (30s bound so a hung handler cannot wedge the
terminal).

name: _hook_callback_kwargs
doc:
The slice of *payload* a callback accepts: everything for ``**kwargs`` (or
un-introspectable) callbacks, only declared names for narrow legacy signatures.

name: _invoke_hook_callback
arguments: cls, callback: Callable, payload: dict[str, Any]
doc:
Invoke a hook while withholding additive fields from narrow legacy callbacks.

An ``async def`` callback returns a coroutine; resolve it the way plugin slash commands
are (loop-safe), otherwise the bare coroutine object is appended to the results and the
plugin's body never runs (#12449).

name: invoke_hook
doc:
Call all callbacks for *hook_name*; return their non-``None`` results.

Payloads evolve additively: ``**kwargs`` callbacks get everything, narrow signatures only
what they declare. Each callback is isolated. Bounded hooks and ``pre_tool_call`` run under
``plugins.hook_callback_timeout`` (worker abandoned, never joined); ``pre_tool_call`` fails
closed with a block directive, others skip. ``_HOOK_CALLER_THREAD_HOOKS`` always run on the
caller thread. ``pre_llm_call`` may return ``{"context": "..."}`` (or a str) to inject.

name: _report_hook_failure
arguments: self, hook_name: str, cb: Callable, kwargs: dict[str, Any], exc: BaseException, *, surface: str='Hook'
doc:
One WARNING per distinct (hook, callback, error); identical repeats at DEBUG.

A callback whose signature names a parameter the hook never sends (``tool_data`` instead
of ``tool_name``/``args``) fails identically on every tool call — ~1700 WARNING lines an
hour that bury real signals (#111922). The first report names the fields the hook does
provide so the plugin author can fix the signature. The key names the callback by
module/qualname (not ``id()``, which CPython recycles across plugin reloads) and
truncates the message so a hook that embeds tool args in its error cannot grow the set
per call; the set is cleared on unload alongside the timeout-suppression map.

name: _run_hook_callback_bounded
arguments: self, hook_name: str, cb: Callable, kwargs: dict[str, Any], timeout: float
doc:
Run one callback on a daemon worker with a wall-clock cap; ``_HOOK_SKIPPED`` when
suppressed, still running for this call id, over the abandoned-worker cap, timed out
(worker abandoned, never joined), or the worker could not be started. Exceptions
propagate.

name: _subscribe_event
arguments: self, owner: str, event: str, callback: Callable
doc: Add an owner-tagged event subscription in registration order.

name: _remove_plugin_subscriptions
doc:
Remove every subscription owned by *owner*; return the count. Queued envelopes re-check
membership per callback, so this also cancels already-snapshotted deliveries.

TODO(#64229): when the central plugin ownership ledger / registration handles land, route this
owner-tagged bookkeeping through that ledger so per-plugin unload cancels event subscriptions
alongside every other registration surface. This method is the integration seam.

name: _deliver_event
doc: Deliver one queued event on the host-owned worker thread.

name: _wait_for_event_dispatch
doc: Wait for the current event generation to become idle (test helper).

name: _dispatch_event
arguments: self, event: str, payload: dict[str, Any]
doc:
Queue *event* without blocking; return the subscriber count scheduled. Pending work is
bounded per generation so a blocking subscriber costs one worker and later emits drop.

name: has_hook
doc: Return True when at least one callback is registered for a hook.

name: ainvoke_hook
doc:
:meth:`invoke_hook` for callers that are already on an event loop.

Same payload narrowing, per-callback isolation and result contract. The difference is
where an ``async def`` callback runs: here it is awaited on the caller's own loop, so a
callback that awaits anything scheduled on that loop can make progress. Through the
sync path it runs on a helper thread while the caller blocks in ``done.wait()`` — on the
gateway that stalls the whole event loop for the callback's duration. Sync callbacks
run inline. Bounded hooks keep ``plugins.hook_callback_timeout`` via ``asyncio.wait_for``
(the coroutine is cancelled, not abandoned); a timed-out ``pre_tool_call`` fails closed.

name: iter_hook_callbacks
doc: Return a stable snapshot of callbacks registered for a hook.

name: render_system_prompt_sections
doc: Render all registered sections deterministically and fail open.

name: _render_prompt_section_text
doc: Evaluate one section; return its stripped text or None (with a warning) when skipped.

name: has_middleware
doc: Return True when at least one callback is registered for middleware.

name: invoke_middleware
doc:
Call middleware callbacks for *kind* (each isolated); return non-``None`` results.

Request middleware passes ``_payload_key``: a dict returned under it becomes the payload the
next callback sees, so rewrites compose, and each callback gets its own copy of the payload and
of ``original_<key>`` so an in-place edit cannot leak.

name: inject_plugin_message
arguments: ctx: Any, content: str, role: str, *, session_key: Optional[str], origin: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]]

name: _hook_source_of
doc: (plugin name, resolved ``__file__``) identity shared by the general and memory loaders.

name: active
doc: Whether this handle still owns an active registration.

name: dispose
doc: Release this registration once; repeated disposal is harmless.

name: _track_registration
arguments: self, manifest: PluginManifest, kind: str, key: str, release: Callable[[], None], *, persistent: bool=False
doc:
Record one registration under its canonical plugin key. ``persistent`` ones (process-global host
infrastructure) stay in the ownership ledger for attribution but NOT in ``_registration_order``, so a
routine unload cannot dispose them; the handle still releases on explicit ``dispose()``.

See #91701.

name: _track_scoped_registration
arguments: self, manifest: PluginManifest, kind: str, name: str, registry: Any, current: Any, previous: Any, *, finalize: Optional[Callable[[], None]]=None
doc:
Lease one ``(kind, scope, name)`` slot of a scope-keyed process-global registry. Unload calls
``registry.restore_registration(name, current, replacement, scope=...)`` — identity-conditional, so a
later generation is never removed by an earlier owner.

name: _active_persistent
doc: Live persistent registrations across every plugin in the ownership ledger.

name: _evict_stale_persistent_registrations
doc:
After re-discovery, dispose parked persistent handles whose plugin did not re-register the same
``(kind, key)``. Re-registered ones are dropped WITHOUT disposing — the same object re-registered would
pass the identity check and evict the live entry.

Persistent registrations (process-global host infrastructure such as dashboard-auth providers)
survive an unload-all by design (#91701); ``_unload_scoped`` parks their handles in
``_persistent_carryover``. After a re-discovery pass, three cases exist for each parked handle:

name: _remove_identity
doc: Remove the last exact object match from a registration list.

name: _remove_callback
arguments: self, mapping: dict[str, list[Callable]], key: str, callback: Callable

name: _restore_mapping
arguments: self, mapping: dict[str, Any], key: str, current: Any, previous: Optional[Any]
doc: Restore a manager-local mapping only when *current* is still present.

name: _restore_value
arguments: self, attribute: str, current: Any, previous: Any
doc: Restore a manager-local value only when *current* is still active.

name: _remove_name_if_unowned
arguments: self, kind: str, names: set[str], name: str
doc: Drop *name* from the manager-local name set once no active ledger entry owns it.

name: _register_fallback_hook
arguments: self, context: Any, hook_source: Optional[tuple], hook_name: str, callback: Callable
doc:
Register ``callback`` unless the same source is already live through general discovery, in
which case return an inert handle so the provider keeps its disposable-handle contract.

name: _dispose_registrations
doc: Dispose registrations in reverse acquisition order, best effort.

name: unload
arguments: self, plugin: str | PluginManifest | LoadedPlugin | None=None
doc: Unload registrations while excluding discovery/deferred loading.

name: _unload_scoped
arguments: self, plugin: str | PluginManifest | LoadedPlugin | None=None
doc:
Unload one plugin (or all when ``plugin=None``, as force rediscovery does). Every ledger registration
— including on_unload callbacks and supervised tasks — is disposed in reverse acquisition order with
identity-conditional inverses. Returns ``True`` when anything was found.

name: _unload_target_keys
doc: Resolve a targeted-unload request to canonical plugin keys (exact key, else by name).

name: _reset_after_unload_all
doc: Sweep pre-ledger global state and clear every manager-local container.

name: in_plugin_load_worker
doc: True on a deadline worker thread; re-entrant discovery from there must not block on its own parent.

name: _resolve_plugin_load_timeout
doc:
Effective per-plugin load deadline from ``plugins.load_timeout_seconds`` (default 10s; ``0`` runs
loads inline with no deadline; clamped to ``_MAX_LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECS``).

name: _reserve_abandoned_loader_slot
doc:
Drop finished abandoned loaders; refuse the load once the live cap is reached. Refusing beats
loading inline: at the cap the process already holds several hung loaders, so an inline load is the
exact startup hang this deadline exists to prevent.

name: run_with_load_deadline
arguments: plugin_key: str, ctx: PluginContext, fn: Callable[[], Any]
doc:
Run ``fn`` (a plugin's import + ``register()``) under the per-plugin deadline.

The worker inherits the caller's context (the Hermes-home override is a ContextVar). On timeout the
worker is abandoned as a daemon, ``ctx`` is marked so any registration it still attempts is ignored,
and :class:`PluginLoadTimeout` is raised on the calling thread so the usual failure path records the
reason and disposes whatever was registered before the hang.

name: _evict_modules
doc:
Drop ``module_name`` and every ``module_name.*`` submodule from ``sys.modules``.

``sys.modules`` is process-global, so any concurrent import — another profile's plugin
load, a lazy import on a worker thread — mutates it while this runs. The ``list()`` is
load-bearing, not a style choice: it is one atomic C-level copy, where iterating the live
mapping raises ``RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`` and
``PluginLoaderMixin._load_plugin_scoped`` degrades that to a warning that loses the whole
plugin. ``pop`` (not ``del``) keeps the snapshot-to-delete window tolerant of a key another
evictor already removed.

name: _serialized_replacement
doc: Make snapshot → write → lease attachment one atomic transaction.

name: _plugin_home_scope
doc: Bind discovery and loading to the manager's immutable Hermes home.

name: _load_error_text
doc: Human-readable load failure; ``sys.exit(0)`` has an empty ``str()`` so name the class and code.

name: _dist_installed
doc: Best-effort presence probe on a requirement's distribution name; ``None`` when unprobeable.

name: on_plugin_loaded
doc:
Subscribe to "a discovery sweep loaded plugins this process did not have": fires from INSIDE
:meth:`discover_and_load` (never emitted by an install RPC) with one
``{name, key, activated_now, deferred}`` summary per NEWLY loaded plugin — every plugin at boot,
just the newcomer after a mid-run ``hermes plugins install/enable``, Desktop / dashboard /
``plugins.manage`` install-enable-update, a tool-triggered force re-discovery or the gateway's
``reload-plugins`` verb (all of which run ``discover_plugins(force=True)``; a non-forced call
short-circuits on ``_discovered`` and never fires). See
:func:`hermes_cli.plugins_activation.plugin_activation_summary` for the payload: ``activated_now``
(gateway commands/transforms/hooks/callbacks, live at once) vs ``deferred`` (``tools``/``prompt``
until the next session, ``mcp_servers`` — the plugin's mcp.json server names — until ``mcp.reload``).
Listeners belong to the process (gateway runner, TUI server), not to a plugin, so ``unload()``
never clears them. Returns an unsubscribe callable. Fires on the discovering thread with the
discovery lock released; marshal onto your own loop.

name: _notify_plugin_loaded
doc:
Fire every :meth:`on_plugin_loaded` listener for the plugins this sweep added over
``loaded_before``; nothing new = no event. One raising listener never starves the rest.

name: _platform_name_from_manifest
doc:
Derive the platform name without importing the adapter: strip a trailing ``-platform`` from the
manifest name, else the directory basename (the bundled convention).

name: _register_deferred_platform
doc:
Register a lazy loader for a bundled platform: the adapter imports only when the
``platform_registry`` is first asked for it; a placeholder ``LoadedPlugin`` keeps it visible in
``hermes plugins list`` until then.

name: rearm_failed_platform
doc:
Re-lease the deferred loader of a platform plugin whose load failed, so the next registry lookup
retries the import. A failed load disposes its lease (the registry forgets the platform), so without
this a load that raised or overran its deadline at startup stays down until a forced re-discovery
(#126356). True when a loader was re-armed.

name: _lease_deferred_platform
doc: Publish the deferred loader as a ledger-owned lease; False when the registry refused it.

name: _register_deferred_platform_tools
doc:
Register a deferred platform's *client* tools without its adapter. Deferring the plugin would
otherwise defer its outbound tools too, so CLI/TUI processes (which never materialize platforms)
would miss them in ``hermes tools`` / ``platform_toolsets``. Opt-in is explicit via ``provides_tools``;
tools live in a ``tools`` submodule so ``__init__`` stays import-light.

A platform plugin can ship two independent things: an inbound adapter (heavy — it imports the
platform SDK) and outbound client tools the agent calls like any other tool. Deferring the plugin
defers both, so in a CLI/TUI process the client tools never register at all: ``resolve_toolset()``
returns ``[]``, the toolset is missing from the ``hermes tools`` checklist, and even an explicit
``platform_toolsets`` entry is dropped because the key is unknown. The same tools work in
gateway/web processes only because those materialize every platform at startup (issue #78050).
Opting in is explicit: the manifest must declare ``provides_tools`` (the field the plugin list and
web server already read to name a plugin's tools, per #78538). Keying off the mere presence of a
``tools.py`` would opt a plugin in by accident — a platform is free to put internal helpers there —
and would leave the contract invisible to anyone reading the manifest. ``tools.py`` remains where
the code is imported from; ``provides_tools`` is what asks for it. A platform that does not declare
the field is untouched and stays fully deferred.

name: _warn_python_dependencies
doc:
Report missing dependencies without installing during discovery.

Plugin admission and PM repair own dependency changes.

name: _validate_plugin_config_schema
doc:
Warn (never block) on plugins.entries.<id> settings that violate config_schema.

See #64165.

name: _load_plugin
doc: Import a plugin module and call its ``register(ctx)`` function.

name: _load_plugin_scoped
doc: Load one plugin with the manager's home bound as current.

name: _is_manifest_only_language_pack
doc:
A ``provides_locales`` plugin with no ``__init__.py`` is complete without Python — like a
manifest-only desktop plugin, it loads from its declared files alone.

name: _register_declared_locales
doc:
``provides_locales`` -> ``ctx.register_locale_dir(<plugin>/locales)``; a declared id with no file
is a warning (the pack promised a language it does not ship), never a load failure.

name: _runs_in_plugin_host
doc: ``plugins.isolation: host`` sends every non-bundled Python plugin to the profile's host.

name: _plugin_host
doc:
This manager's plugin host (one process per profile home), created on first use. Creation
is atomic, so concurrent first callers share one host (which starts its process once); a
failed creation stores nothing, and the next caller tries again.

name: _track_tool_override_policy
doc: Install the plugin's tool-override policy in tools.registry as a ledger-owned lease.

name: _attribute_registrations
arguments: self, loaded: LoadedPlugin, plugin_key: str, registration_start: int
doc: Fill ``loaded.*_registered`` from the ledger slice this plugin's register() produced.

name: _load_portable_plugin
doc: Load validated portable components without importing Python code.

name: _directory_module_name
doc:
Profile-safe import namespace for a directory plugin: the bare ``hermes_plugins.<slug>`` for the
first scope that claims it, a ``__home_<digest>`` suffix for any other scope.

name: _policy_module_name
doc: Return the module prefix whose callbacks inherit plugin policy.

name: _load_directory_module
doc:
Import a directory plugin as ``hermes_plugins.<slug>`` (slug from ``manifest.key`` so
``image_gen/openai`` cannot collide with ``tts/openai``).

name: _load_entrypoint_module
doc:
Load a pip-installed plugin via its entry-point reference: the module for a bare ``module`` target,
the referenced attribute (normally ``register``) for the ``module:function`` form.

name: _credit
doc: Attribute every tool registered since ``before`` to this plugin.

name: _import_and_register
doc: Import + register() — the part a plugin controls, so the part the deadline covers.

name: _portable_skill_namespace
doc: Return a readable, collision-resistant namespace for a portable plugin.

name: portable_mcp_server_name
doc:
Internal name of a portable plugin's MCP server: exactly the name its ``mcp.json`` gives it, the same
rule a user's own ``mcp_servers`` block in config.yaml follows. The plugin's skill namespace
(``agent-plugin-<slug>-<digest>``) is NOT prepended: it keeps plugin-data and skill names collision-free
without coordination, but here it cost ~40 chars of every ``mcp__<server>__<tool>`` name, which providers
cap at 64, so the tool verb was hash-clamped away. A duplicate is refused at load (native config first,
then first-loaded plugin) with a warning naming both owners; that beats hiding it behind a digest.

name: _display_author
doc: Normalize a manifest author value for the string PluginManifest field.

name: _manifest_field_of_type
arguments: data: Mapping, key: str, field_name: str, typ, what: str
doc: Return ``data[field_name]`` when absent or of ``typ``; warn and return None otherwise.

name: _manifest_list
arguments: data: Mapping, key: str, field_name: str, what: str, coerce: Callable, warn: str
doc: Coerce each item of list field ``field_name``; ``coerce`` returning None warns ``warn`` and skips.

name: _dependency_entry
doc: ``{id, version_range}`` from a requires_plugins item (str shorthand ok); None when malformed.

name: _manifest_int
arguments: raw: object, key: str, warn: str, fallback: Optional[int]
doc: ``int(raw)``; a non-integer warns ``warn`` (formatted with key, raw) and yields ``fallback``.

name: _config_schema_entries
doc:
``config_schema`` (key -> {type?, default?, description?, ...}) keeping only mapping entries;
warns on what it drops or cannot type-check. Shared by ``plugin.yaml`` and ``plugin.json``.

name: _parse_manifest_v2_fields
doc:
Validate/normalize manifest v2 fields into PluginManifest kwargs (warnings, never failures).

See #64165.

name: validate_config_schema
arguments: plugin_id: str, schema: Mapping, settings: Mapping
doc:
Return actionable warning strings for settings vs config_schema mismatches (never raises).

Never raises; schema mismatches must not block plugin load (#64165).

name: resolve_plugin_load_order
doc:
Return plugin keys in dependency order: B before A when A requires B; alphabetical ties. A cycle warns
and falls back to alphabetical order for all; a missing dependency warns once but never removes the
dependent plugin (loads never hard-fail on advisory deps).

See #64165.

name: _detect_kind_from_source
doc:
Kind implied by source markers (mirrors plugins/memory ``_is_memory_provider_dir`` and
plugins/cron_providers ``_is_cron_provider_dir``): memory-, cron- or computer-use-provider markers -> ``exclusive``;
``register_provider`` + ``ProviderProfile`` -> ``model-provider``; else ``None``. Keeps these kinds out
of the general manager's eager import (its PluginContext has no ``register_cron_scheduler``, #62951).

name: _read_source_from_origin
doc: First ``limit`` chars of a module's source (``.pyc`` mapped back to ``.py``); "" on failure.

name: resolve_module_origin
doc:
Return a module's source path WITHOUT importing it, or ``None``. ``find_spec`` on a dotted name imports
the parent package, so only the top-level name uses it; remaining segments are walked through
``submodule_search_locations`` by hand. Namespace/zipped/extension modules return ``None``. Shared with
``plugins/memory/__init__.py``.

name: _resolve_module_source
doc: First ``limit`` chars of a module's source without importing it ("" when unresolvable).

name: manifest_key
doc: Registry id of a manifest: the path-derived ``key`` when set, else the bare ``name``.

name: parse_provides_locales
doc:
``provides_locales`` -> (ids, metadata). Entries are ``"pl"`` or ``{id: pl, endonym: Polski, rtl: false}``;
ids are canonicalised (lowercase, ``_`` -> ``-``), invalid or duplicate ones are dropped with a warning.

name: running_hermes_version
doc: Base release version of the Hermes code that is running.

name: _version_tuple
doc:
``v1.2.3-rc1`` / ``1.2.3rc1`` / ``1.2.3.post1`` → ``(1, 2, 3)``; ``None`` when a segment has no
leading digits. PEP 440 pre/post/dev suffixes glued to a segment (``0rc1``) are dropped so an rc
*target* still gates and an rc *running* version does not disable every gate.

name: version_satisfies
doc:
``>=``/``>``/``<=``/``<``/``==``/``!=`` clauses (comma = AND; bare version = ``>=``). Unparseable
versions are permissive — no PEP 440 dependency for a one-field manifest gate.

name: requires_hermes_error
doc: Load-blocking reason when the manifest's ``requires_hermes`` rejects the running version.

name: portable_plugin_manifest
arguments: child: Path, source: str, prefix: str
doc: Build the manifest for a portable Agent Plugin directory (``plugin.json``); diagnostics warn.

name: _manifest_kind
arguments: data: Mapping, key: str, plugin_dir: Path
doc:
Normalize ``kind``; undeclared memory/model providers are auto-detected from ``__init__.py`` so they
route to their own discovery instead of the general manager.

name: parse_manifest_file
arguments: manifest_file: Path, plugin_dir: Path, source: str, prefix: str
doc: Parse one ``plugin.yaml`` into a :class:`PluginManifest`; ``None`` (warned) on failure.

name: read_sidecar_rows
doc:
The install-metadata rows for this plugins dir; {} when absent
or unreadable (manual-only installs never wrote one).

name: _git_origin_url
doc:
origin's URL from the installed .git — remote get-url on a real
repo, config-file parse as the fallback (works for partial/copy
installs where git refuses).

name: plugins_provenance
doc: Classify every plugin dir under plugins_dir per the 2x2.

name: _manifest_config_schema
doc:
``config_schema`` from ``<plugin_dir>/plugin.yaml``, or for a portable package from
``plugin.json`` ``extensions.com.nousresearch.hermes.config_schema`` (Agent Plugins v1 forbids
unknown top-level fields, so Hermes-specific keys live in the vendor namespace); ``{}`` when
absent or malformed (the loader already warned about malformed entries at load time).

name: secret_env_name
arguments: plugin_id: str, key: str, spec: Mapping[str, Any]
doc:
``.env`` variable a ``type: secret`` field is stored under: the manifest's ``env:`` or
``<PLUGIN_ID>_<KEY>`` upper-snaked (``image_gen/fal`` + ``api_key`` → ``IMAGE_GEN_FAL_API_KEY``).

name: plugin_settings_fields
doc:
Renderable settings fields for one plugin: schema + the current value of each key.

Secret fields never carry the value — only ``env`` (where it lives) and ``has_value``.

name: save_plugin_settings
arguments: plugin_id: str, plugin_dir: Optional[Path], values: Mapping[str, Any]
doc:
Write ``values`` (``{key: value}``) for the plugin's schema keys; returns the keys written.

Raises ``ValueError`` on an unknown key, a type mismatch, an enum value outside ``choices`` or a
secret (secrets go to ``.env`` through the credential route, never ``config.yaml``);
``PermissionError`` propagates from the shared writer (managed installs / managed keys).

name: _plugin_relative_segments
doc:
Validate/split a plugin-relative settings key; global paths, traversal, and core roots are rejected
before any config read.

The public API accepts only relative keys (``endpoint`` or ``retry.policy``). See #64227.

name: _nested_plugin_value
arguments: root: object, segments: tuple[str, ...], default: Any
doc: Walk ``segments`` through nested mappings; ``default`` on the first miss.

name: _nested_plugin_mapping
doc: Wrap ``value`` in nested single-key dicts, outermost first.

name: _plugin_settings_entry
doc: ``plugins.entries.<plugin_id>`` as a mapping, else ``None``.

name: save_plugin_setting
arguments: plugin_id: str, segments: tuple[str, ...], value: Any
doc:
Atomically write one value under ``plugins.entries.<plugin_id>.settings``.

THE writer for plugin settings: ``PluginContext.set_config`` (the plugin itself) and the
Desktop/TUI ``plugins.manage settings`` action both land here so managed-install and
administrator-managed-key refusals, the cross-process lock and the fail-closed raw read
are enforced once. ``segments`` must already be validated by :func:`_plugin_relative_segments`.

name: _plugin_data_namespace
doc:
Return one Windows-safe directory component for plugin-owned data. Portable Agent Plugins already
receive this exact PLUGIN_DATA path; otherwise the fixed prefix avoids Windows reserved device names and
the digest prevents fold collisions.

name: _locked_plugin_state
doc:
Serialize state read-modify-write across threads/processes (fcntl / msvcrt). The lock lives in a
sibling file because atomic replacement changes the target's inode.

name: data_dir
doc: Profile-scoped directory matching portable plugins' PLUGIN_DATA.

name: get
doc: Read a JSON value, returning *default* when the key is absent.

name: set
doc: Atomically set one JSON value without dropping concurrent updates.

name: recover_plugin_publication
arguments: project: Path, row: dict, journal: Path
doc: Recover a shipped caller's row through the stdlib boot-journal owner.

name: publish_plugin
arguments: staged: Path, target: Path, old_metadata: dict, new_metadata: dict, *, target_digest: str | None=None, require_consent: bool=False, assume_consent: bool=False
doc:
Publish *staged* into *target*. *assume_consent* is consent the caller
already holds (``--yes-deps``, or a memory-provider migration under
``security.allow_lazy_installs``): the active-replacement consent veto is
skipped, so an unattended install carries that decision instead of being
refused non-interactively.

name: _refresh_declared_dependencies
arguments: target: Path, staged: Path, manifest: dict, *, interactive: bool
doc:
Dependency changes carried by an update clear the same gates as an install.

New Python requirements install packages into the shared environment: install and
reinstall prompt for that, so an update prompts too, and an unattended one (dashboard,
``plugins.auto_apply`` from the gateway) is REFUSED rather than consented on the user's
behalf. Publication replaces the whole tree, so a Node sidecar the user accepted earlier is
rebuilt in the staged copy when its package.json/lock moved (custom pulls copy a stale
node_modules; catalog re-pins clone without one).

name: update_plugin
arguments: target: Path, *, catalog_entry=None, interactive: bool=False, force: bool=False, scan_decision_cb: Callable[[Any], bool] | None=None, carry_user_files: Callable[[Path], list[str]] | None=None
doc:
Prepare a catalog re-pin or custom Git pull without changing the live tree.

*interactive*: a terminal user is present to consent to newly declared dependencies;
the dashboard and the gateway's auto-apply pass False and get a refusal instead.
Every update is scanned: *force* accepts a caution verdict (the user already saw it), and
*scan_decision_cb(result)* may accept one by asking; a dangerous verdict always blocks.
*carry_user_files(staged)* may merge user-owned state into the staged tree before
manifest validation, example-file generation, dependency preparation and publication; it
returns the carried paths so a scan block can attribute findings to them.

significant_calls.expression:
publish_plugin(
                staged,
                new_target,
                metadata,
                {**metadata, installed_name: record},
                target_digest=before if new_target == target else None,
            )

name: _version_is_newer
doc: Invalid versions are unknown, not evidence of an update.

name: _read_manifest_field
doc: One field from the installed plugin.yaml (claims, not provenance).

name: check_local_provenance
doc: Check installed provenance without fetching remote metadata.

name: check_provenanced
arguments: prov: Provenance, *, fetch: Callable[[str], str], ls_remote: Callable[[str], str]
doc: Check local provenance before contacting its approved update source.

name: parse_feed_yml
doc:
The electron-updater-derived feed shape: version, released,
min_hermes, artifacts{git,bundle,bundle_sha256}, notes_url.

name: _owning_distribution
doc:
The name of the distribution the entry point belongs to — metadata,
never a guess derived from the import module (audit C17).

name: check_pip_plugins
arguments: *, installed_version: Callable[[str], str], pypi_latest: Callable[[str], Optional[str]], entry_points: Optional[list]=None
doc:
The pip world, stateless: entry-point dists vs PyPI. Nothing
recorded, nothing to drift.

name: https_update_url
doc:
Normalize a manifest ``update_url``; raises ValueError unless it is ``https://``.

The feed picks which commit of the trusted origin gets installed and the gateway fetches
it unattended every check interval, so a plaintext ``http://`` (MITM → an old vulnerable
commit), ``file://`` or ``ftp://`` feed is refused at install, at trust-update-url AND at
the fetch itself (rows saved before this rule existed).

name: default_fetch
doc:
The real feed fetcher: url -> text (raises on failure).

ONE implementation shared by the manual ``hermes plugins
check-updates`` and the cadence tick — callers never re-derive it.

significant_calls.expression: super().redirect_request(req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl)

name: default_ls_remote
doc:
The real git probe: source -> HEAD sha (raises on failure).

Uses the same resolved git executable the CLI path resolves. Lazily
imports plugins_cmd (which lazily imports this module) — no import
cycle at module load.

name: run_checks
arguments: plugins_dir: Path, *, fetch: Optional[Callable[[str], str]]=None, ls_remote: Optional[Callable[[str], str]]=None, include_pip: bool=True, pip_installed_version: Callable[[str], str]=importlib.metadata.version, pip_pypi_latest: Optional[Callable[[str], Optional[str]]]=None, pip_entry_points: Optional[list]=None
doc:
All checks for one plugins dir. NEVER mutates anything.

``fetch``/``ls_remote`` default to :func:`default_fetch` /
:func:`default_ls_remote` — the single shared network implementation
the manual command and the cadence tick both ride.

name: _default_pypi_latest
doc: PyPI JSON API — the real fetcher (injectable in tests).

name: redirect_request
arguments: self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl

significant_calls.expression: super().redirect_request(req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl)

name: parse_declared_capabilities
doc:
Normalize a manifest ``capabilities:`` value into known capability ids.

Unknown ids are dropped with a warning: they can never be granted by this build, so hiding
them from the consent screen is the fail-closed choice (the plugin must degrade gracefully).

name: _known
doc: Deduplicated (order-preserving) subset of *capabilities* with a registry entry.

name: capability_set_hash
doc: Deterministic sha256 over a capability set (order-insensitive).

name: _plugin_entry
doc: ``plugins.entries.<plugin_id>`` or ``{}`` — never raises (unreadable state = not granted).

name: granted_capabilities
doc: The set of capabilities the user has granted this plugin.

name: _legacy_gate_set
doc: True when the deprecated ``allow_*`` key for *spec* is truthy.

name: plugin_capability_granted
arguments: plugin_id: str, capability: str, config: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Canonical check: is *capability* live for *plugin_id*? True via ``granted_capabilities`` OR
the deprecated-but-honored legacy ``allow_*`` key. Unknown ids / unreadable state -> False.

name: _child_dict
doc: ``parent[key]`` as a dict, replacing any non-dict value in place.

name: record_consent
arguments: plugin_id: str, granted: Iterable[str], declared: Iterable[str]
doc:
Persist a consent decision: ``granted_capabilities`` (union with prior grants), the consent
record (hash of the declared set the user saw + UTC timestamp), and the legacy ``allow_*`` key
for each grant so existing enforcement sites keep working unchanged.

name: consent_hash
doc: Return the stored consent hash, or None when absent/corrupt.

name: pending_capabilities
arguments: plugin_id: str, declared: Iterable[str], config: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Declared-but-ungranted capabilities: everything at first consent, only the additions on an
update re-consent (they must be re-consented before going live).

name: declared_set_changed
arguments: plugin_id: str, declared: Iterable[str], config: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]]=None
doc: True when the declared set differs from what the user consented to (or never consented).

name: get_catalog_dir
doc: The ``plugin-catalog/`` directory shipped with this checkout.

name: entry_from_mapping
doc: Validate one entry mapping (YAML file or live-JSON element); ``None`` + warning on any failure.

name: load_catalog
doc:
Every valid ``*.yaml`` entry in the catalog dir (``removed.yaml`` excluded), sorted by file name.
Malformed entries are skipped with a warning — never raises.

name: load_removed_list
doc: ``removed.yaml``'s ``removed:`` list; missing/malformed → empty.

name: filter_entries
doc: Case-insensitive substring match over name, description and declared tools; empty query = all.

name: _normalize_repo
doc:
Canonical ``host/path`` for a repo URL: scheme, user, ``www.``, ``.git`` and trailing slashes are
spelling, not identity — the kill list must match ``git@github.com:Evil/Bad.git`` when it names
``https://github.com/evil/bad``.

name: find_removed
doc:
Match a catalog name or repo URL (``.git``/trailing-slash insensitive) against the kill list.

The in-tree list and the live-fetched list are UNIONED: a removal published after this checkout
shipped must still block, and a stale live cache must not un-block an in-tree removal.

name: resolved_removed_entries
doc:
The full kill list (in-tree UNION live) in one resolution. Callers that match many candidates
— e.g. a plugins-hub rebuild annotating every installed plugin — resolve the list once instead
of paying a live-catalog fetch per candidate.

name: cached_removed_entries
doc:
In-tree list UNION the last fetched live copy, with NO network round-trip — for the load-time and
``enable`` checks that run in every process and must never block on a dead catalog host.

name: match_removed
doc: One candidate against a pre-resolved kill list: exact name or normalized repo URL match.

name: invalidate_live_cache_for_home
doc:
Best-effort removal of the cached live catalog under *home* (any profile's home).

``hermes update`` drops it for every profile after the checkout changes: a snapshot fetched
before the bump would otherwise out-vote the newer in-tree catalog (pins the update just
changed, entries it just added) for the rest of :data:`LIVE_CATALOG_TTL_SECONDS` (#119340).
The next :func:`fetch_live_catalog` re-fetches the published doc, or falls back to the
in-tree catalog while the network is down — both newer than what was deleted. Safe when the
cache is absent (first run, other profiles that never opened the plugins hub).

name: _stale_live_cache
doc:
A previously fetched copy still beats the in-tree one when the network is down — for
:data:`LIVE_CATALOG_MAX_STALE_SECONDS`. Past that its pins may trail the checkout's own catalog
(a 90-day-old cache outranked a freshly updated in-tree pin), so the entries are dropped and the
caller falls back to in-tree; the removals are kept.

name: fetch_live_catalog
doc:
The published ``plugin-catalog.json`` (``{"entries": [...], "removed": [...]}``), cached under
``HERMES_HOME/cache`` for :data:`LIVE_CATALOG_TTL_SECONDS`. ``None`` on ANY failure — callers fall
back to the in-tree catalog. A failed network attempt is remembered for
:data:`LIVE_CATALOG_FAILURE_TTL_SECONDS` so a dead host costs one timeout per TTL window, not one
per call (``force`` bypasses both caches).

name: in_tree_catalog_time
doc:
Commit time (epoch) of the last change to this checkout's ``plugin-catalog/``, or ``None`` when
the install is not a git checkout (a release/pip install cannot be newer than the published doc).
On a git checkout whose path history is unreadable without network — the treeless ``tree:0`` layout
``hermes update`` produces — the newest checked-out catalog file's mtime stands in for it, so a
freshly updated checkout still outranks a doc fetched before the bump. Resolved once per process.

name: _catalog_worktree_mtime
doc:
Newest mtime under the checkout's ``plugin-catalog/``: a no-network freshness signal for clones
whose path history is unreachable (treeless or offline). ``None`` when nothing is checked out.

name: _prefer_in_tree_entry
arguments: tree: PluginCatalogEntry, live: PluginCatalogEntry, tree_is_newer: Optional[bool]
doc:
For one entry present in both sources with a different pin: the newer catalog wins. Newer is
decided by the checkout's catalog commit time vs the doc's ``generated_at`` when both resolve;
otherwise by the entries' ``version`` labels when both parse; otherwise the live doc wins (a release
install's in-tree copy is frozen at release time).

name: load_catalog_live
doc:
Entries from the live (or cached) catalog, else the in-tree catalog. When both name an entry at
different pins the NEWER source supplies it — right after ``hermes update`` bumps an in-tree pin,
a cache fetched before the bump must not re-install the old one (see :func:`_prefer_in_tree_entry`).
