name: _hold_refused_release
doc:
Hold an offered release `hermes update` refuses (it predates the gateway runtime these session
stores use). Covers releases off this checkout's history too, which the ancestry-only rollback
test cannot see. Apply only after caching the release facts: stores can gain runtime history,
or the only ledgered profile can be removed, between checks.

name: _resolve_channel
arguments: result: dict, channel: str, co: _Checkout, *, forward_only: bool=False
doc:
Resolve a release channel's target into ``result``; the SourceTarget, or None on error.

A target with a pinned commit is final; one without names a branch to follow instead.

name: _heal_deleted_branch
doc: Point the Desktop branch setting back at main after its branch was deleted upstream.

name: _unhealable_reason
doc:
Why a branch the remote does not advertise must keep its pin; None when healing loses nothing.

An empty ref advertisement cannot tell "merged and deleted upstream" from "never pushed":
only a branch that was once published (remote-tracking ref or configured upstream, which
survives ``fetch --prune``) and whose commits are all in main may be re-pinned to main.

name: _behind_count
doc: ``(behind, commits)`` for ``target``: local ancestry first, then the GitHub compare API.

name: _check_branch
arguments: result: dict, co: _Checkout, selected_branch: str, *, heal: Optional[tuple[Path, dict]]
doc: Compare the checkout with ``selected_branch``'s remote tip, falling back to main if it was deleted.

name: check_for_updates
arguments: *, install_root: Path | None=None, home: Path | None=None, branch: str | None=None, channel: str | None=None, cache_path: Path | None=None, branch_config_path: Path | None=None, force: bool=False, passive: bool=False, git: str='git'
doc:
Return a presentation-ready status. Omitted branch follows the current checkout.

Only the default (running installation) may use HERMES_REVISION. An explicit
target must never inherit the host process's embedded revision or stamp.

name: complete_source_checkout
arguments: root: Path, *, desktop: bool, assume_yes: bool, gateway_mode: bool=False, pre_update_snapshot_id: str | None=None, pre_update_version: str | None=None, completion_message: str | None=None, announce: str | None=None, followups: list[tuple[str, str]] | None=None, before_build=None
doc:
Publish commands, build the products, then run post-build maintenance.

``before_build`` (an update's paused-gateway restart) runs once the launchers are published:
dependencies are already synced, the long product builds have not started.

Every step runs even when an earlier one failed; each failure is printed as ``⚠``,
recorded on the open update receipt and appended to ``followups`` as ``(step, reason)``.
Returns True only when every step finished and the SQLite runtime is not unsafe.

name: _complete_locked
arguments: root: Path, *, desktop: bool, assume_yes: bool, gateway_mode: bool, pre_update_snapshot_id: str | None, pre_update_version: str | None, completion_message: str | None, announce: str | None, followups: list[tuple[str, str]] | None=None, before_build=None
doc: The completion body; callers hold the update lock already.

name: _bootstrap_command
doc: Re-enter the checkout on PM's selected interpreter with its environment.

name: source_repository
doc: GitHub forks own their releases; other origins must mirror official tags.

name: _resolve_channel
doc:
The only adapter to the validated requested/terminal records and manifest.

ChannelReader owns HTTPS, authority and digests. The source adapter below
admits its retirement constraints before any checkout operation. No legacy
GitHub fallback is allowed when a record is unavailable; the one exception
is an unpublished ``main`` record, which resolves to the main branch.

name: resolve_source_target
arguments: channel: str, git_cmd=None, cwd=None, *, repository=None, forward_only: bool=False
doc:
Resolve a subscription: stable from GitHub releases, main from the git branch,
preview channels (e.g. ``pm-preview``) through their R2 records.

``forward_only`` (an unchosen default subscription) pins a checkout that already
contains the release to its own HEAD, so the update is a no-op instead of a downgrade.

name: _probe
doc:
``git <args>`` in ``cwd``, or None when git did not answer: an unknown relation, not a claim.

Before the updater's fetch the release commit is usually absent, and git 2.43 spends 7-12 s
of CPU on a blobless clone failing to find it even with lazy fetch off (#137646).

name: _head_containing
arguments: git_cmd, cwd, commit: str, repository: str
doc:
HEAD's sha unless HEAD is PROVEN not to contain ``commit``, then None.

An unchosen default must never move a checkout backward on a guess, so an
unknown relation (shallow history, GitHub unreachable) keeps HEAD.

name: _describe_release_failure
doc: A transport failure names its cause (a rate limit is not "no release").

name: _resolve_stable
doc:
Stable IS the repository's latest published GitHub release: the tag a release
publishes (non-draft, non-prerelease, strict vX.Y.Z), verified against origin.
No R2 record or pointer is consulted; publishing the release is the only promotion.

name: _refuse_retirement_downgrade
arguments: request: dict, terminal: dict, git_cmd, cwd
doc: Qualification of preview data is not permission to roll back newer source.

name: _json
doc:
GitHub API JSON with the updater's credential ladder (token, gh, anonymous).

Anonymous api.github.com is 60 requests/hour per address, so an unauthenticated
stable lookup fails for everyone behind one office, CI or container exit.

name: _resolve_release
arguments: channel: str, git_cmd=None, cwd=None, *, repository=None, pointer: bool=True
doc: ``resolve_source_release`` that raises the failure instead of returning ``(None, None)``.

name: resolve_source_release
arguments: channel: str, git_cmd=None, cwd=None, *, repository=None, pointer: bool=True
doc:
Read published stable/canary release metadata (not channel discovery).

The source updater's ``stable`` reads it with ``pointer=False``: GitHub's latest
published release only. With ``pointer`` the R2 channel pointers outrank GitHub's
release listing. A malformed pointer,
draft, or tag/commit mismatch is not permission to select a different build.
``git_cmd`` resolves the selected tag on origin; ZIP callers omit it and
resolve the same tag through GitHub's commit endpoint.

name: write_source_stamp
doc:
Replace ``install-stamp.json`` with identity read from ``root`` itself.

*adopted* marks a boot-time adoption (``adoptedAt``): identity only, nothing
built, so it must never read as a completed install/update of this commit.

A root git cannot identify -- the ZIP update fallback runs precisely because
git is unusable -- publishes no identity: the old stamp is removed rather
than left naming the commit that was just replaced. Returns None then.

name: refresh_bootstrap_receipt
doc:
Move the installers' bootstrap receipt to the commit ``stamp`` just published.

install.sh / install.ps1 write the receipt once, at the commit they installed;
an update that moves the checkout has to move it too, or it keeps naming the
replaced release. Only an existing receipt is refreshed: its presence is what
marks a script install, so a manual clone never grows one.

name: is_sqlite_wal_reset_vulnerable
doc: Return whether *version_info* contains SQLite's WAL-reset bug.

name: isolated_interpreter_env
doc:
Copy of ``os.environ`` with conda/uv/venv/PYTHON* overrides stripped, so a child interpreter
reports its *own* runtime rather than the caller's.

name: probe_sqlite_runtime
doc: Probe SQLite in *python*, never the caller's linked SQLite.

name: _key
doc: Canonicalise a *filesystem* path for use as a registry key.

name: _canonical_db_path
doc:
The on-disk path of ``main`` as SQLite reports it (immune to ``file:`` URIs, relative paths,
symlinks). ``None`` for in-memory/unnamed databases, which cannot be byte-probed.

name: track_connection
doc:
Record that this process holds a connection to *path* (prefer :func:`connect_tracked`; this
is for callers managing their own connection objects, and for tests).

name: _track_key
doc: Adjust the live count for an already-canonical key (caller holds ``_live_lock``).

name: untrack_connection
doc: Record that one connection to *path* has been closed.

name: _live_main_key
doc:
The tracked main-database key that makes *key* live, or ``None`` (caller holds ``_live_lock``).

SQLite locks the main file and its WAL sidecars; a raw ``close()`` of any of those
inodes cancels this process's POSIX locks, but the registry is keyed by the main path.

name: has_live_connection
doc:
Whether this process holds a connection to *path* (or to the database it is a sidecar of).

Point-in-time answer: a raw open/close right after it returns ``False`` can still race a
new connection. Hold :func:`offline_file_access` across the I/O whenever possible.

name: _tracking_factory
doc:
Return *factory* augmented with untrack-on-close. Callers legitimately pass their own
``Connection`` subclasses (tests simulate FTS5-less or pragma-failing runtimes); leaving them
untracked would quietly unguard the database, so the tracking ``close()`` is mixed in.

name: connect_tracked
arguments: path: Path | str, *, tracking_path: Path | str | None=None, connect_fn=None, **kwargs
doc:
``sqlite3.connect`` that registers the connection for the lifetime of the fd (released on
``close()``). Use for any database that might be byte-probed (``state.db``, ``kanban.db``).
Open and registration happen together under ``_live_lock`` so a concurrent
:func:`read_header_bytes_preopen` cannot slip between them and cancel this connection's locks.

name: _retrofit_tracking
doc:
Give an already-open connection untrack-on-close semantics by swapping ``__class__`` for
one mixing in the tracking ``close()`` (used when an opener ignored the factory we asked for).

name: page_count_bytes
doc:
Logical database size in bytes (``page_count * page_size``, the header field at offset 28)
read via PRAGMA over *conn* so no new fd is opened. ``None`` when the pragmas cannot be read.

name: file_length_matches_header
doc:
Whether the file on disk is at least as long as the header claims ("torn extend" check),
without opening the file (PRAGMA over *conn* + ``stat()``). Advisory in WAL mode: a freshly
committed page may still live in ``-wal`` so the main file legitimately lags.

name: read_header_bytes_preopen
arguments: path: Path | str, *, length: int=100, force: bool=False
doc:
Read the first *length* bytes of *path* -- only when no connection is live. The ONLY
sanctioned byte-level read of a database file, for first-open validation (real SQLite? zeroed?
overwritten?). Check and open/read/close run together under ``_live_lock`` so a connection
cannot be opened between deciding "nothing is live" and closing this descriptor.

name: offline_file_access
doc:
Hold the connection-lifecycle lock across a raw read of a database file: checking
:func:`has_live_connection` and *then* doing raw I/O is a check/use race (a connection opened
in between loses its POSIX locks to the raw ``close()``). Held only for the raw I/O.

name: open_db
arguments: path: Path | str, *, db_label: str, busy_timeout_ms: int=5000, wal: bool=True, foreign_keys: bool=False, synchronous_full: bool=False, row_factory=sqlite3.Row, check_same_thread: bool=True, wal_lock_retries: int=1, initialize: Callable[[sqlite3.Connection], None] | None=None
doc:
Open ``path`` (parent created), apply the PRAGMA set, run ``initialize``; closed if anything raises.

``busy_timeout_ms`` is the single busy knob: it is passed as ``connect(timeout=)`` AND set as the
explicit PRAGMA so it is observable. ``wal=True`` goes through ``apply_wal_with_fallback`` — the
only journal-mode setter that carries the WAL-reset-bug gate, the network-FS silent-refusal
fallback and the never-live-downgrade invariant; a raw ``PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`` bypasses all
three. Only the transient ``database is locked`` from that pragma is retried (``wal_lock_retries``):
a first opener initializing a shared DB can make it ignore the busy timeout, notably on Windows.

name: transaction
doc: Commit on success, roll back on error, and ALWAYS close ``conn`` (see the module docstring).

name: add_column_if_missing
arguments: conn: sqlite3.Connection, table: str, column: str, ddl: str
doc:
``ALTER TABLE <table> ADD COLUMN <ddl>``, idempotent across races: True when this call added
it, False on the ``duplicate column name`` a concurrent migrator caused.

``column`` is the human-readable name for the call site; ``ddl`` carries the actual definition. See
#21708.

name: write_txn
doc:
An IMMEDIATE write transaction on a long-lived connection (stays open). The explicit ROLLBACK is
guarded so a SQLite auto-rollback (no transaction left under EIO / contention / corruption) cannot
shadow the original error.

name: get_ssh_workspace_fs
doc: Return a cached adapter when this profile selects the SSH backend.

name: _section
doc: Print a blank line followed by a bold cyan ``◆`` section heading.

name: _row

doc: Print one ``name  ✓/✗ text`` status row.

name: _detail
doc: Print an indented ``label: value`` detail line under a status row.

name: _kv

doc: Print a ``  Label:        value`` line (label padded to the 14-col status layout).

name: _kv_flag
arguments: label: str, ok, on: str, off: str
doc: ``_kv`` with a ✓/✗ mark followed by ``on`` or ``off`` text.

name: _first_env_value
doc: Return the first non-empty env value among ``names`` (a str or tuple of names).

name: _configured_model_label
doc: Return the configured default model from config.yaml.

name: _effective_provider_label
doc: Return the provider label matching current CLI runtime resolution.

name: _estop_status_line
doc: One-line pause banner for `hermes status`, or None when not paused.

name: _banner
doc: Blank line, then each line in ``styles``.

name: _load_ctx_config
doc: Load config.yaml into the shared context (fail-soft).

name: _render_platforms
doc: One row per platform, judged by the gateway (same verdict as the summary's Platforms line).

name: _cron_summary
doc: ``N active, M total`` jobs line, shared by the full and short status renderers.

name: _connected_platforms
doc: Platforms the gateway would start (``GatewayConfig.get_connected_platforms``).

name: _authenticated_provider_names
doc: The providers the /model picker offers: cached catalogs only, no endpoint probes.

name: _summary_row
doc: One summary row; a failing probe degrades only its own row.

name: _render_summary
doc: Default ``hermes status``: one line per component; ``--full`` prints every section.

name: show_status
doc: One-screen summary by default; ``--full``/``--deep`` print every section.

name: _format_iso_timestamp
doc: Format ISO timestamps for status output, converting to local timezone.

name: _oauth_block
arguments: name: str, status: dict, hint: str, rows
doc:
Print an OAuth provider row plus its conditional detail lines.

``rows`` are ``(label, status_key, formatter, gate)``: a detail prints when the raw value is
truthy and ``gate`` is None or equals the logged-in state (False = only while logged out).

name: _resolve_git_dir
doc: Nearest enclosing git dir for ``start``, following worktree pointer files.

name: current_git_branch
doc:
Branch name for ``cwd`` (defaults to the process cwd); ``""`` outside a repo.

A detached HEAD renders as the abbreviated commit (``a1b2c3d…``). Results are
cached ~5s per directory so per-repaint calls never re-walk the tree.

name: timestamp_or
doc: ``datetime.fromtimestamp(value)`` or *default* when the value is missing/unparseable.

name: session_timestamps
doc: ``(created, last_activity)`` from a SessionDB row; last activity falls back to created.

name: build_status_fields
arguments: session_id: str, agent: Any, meta: dict | None, *, title: str | None=None, model: str | None=None, provider: str | None=None, created: datetime | None=None, last_activity: datetime | None=None, created_fallback: datetime | None=None, tokens: int | None=None, agent_running: bool=False, home: str | Path | None=None
doc:
Common ``/status`` facts, pre-formatted for display.

``agent`` wins for model / provider / tokens; the keyword values are the surface's fallback
(CLI ``self.model``, TUI metadata mirror, gateway's resolved route) and are also what a
surface passes when it has no live agent. ``created`` / ``last_activity`` override the
``meta`` row scan for surfaces whose session store is authoritative (gateway SessionEntry).
``home`` is an explicit owning-profile path for multiplexed surfaces; omitted callers keep
the process/current-profile lookup.

name: status_lines
doc:
``Label: value`` lines for *keys* in order (English surfaces). An empty title is skipped;
an unresolved model/provider shows a placeholder rather than an empty parenthesis.

name: timestamp
doc: Local time in logging.Formatter's default ``%(asctime)s`` shape, which ``hermes logs --since`` parses.

name: stamp_line
doc: *line* with a leading :func:`timestamp` (kept as-is if it already has one) and one ``\n``.

name: _is_hermes_gateway_run_argv
doc:
True for Hermes ``gateway run`` argv this wrapper is allowed to upgrade.

The wrapper is generic. Only historical/current Hermes gateway shapes get ``--external-
supervisor``; an arbitrary launchd child must not be marked as gateway-supervised (#87005).

name: _child_launchd_label_env
doc:
Env vars that carry this wrapper's launchd identity to the grandchild.

launchd stamps ``XPC_SERVICE_NAME=<job label>`` only on this wrapper (its direct child; an
interactive shell has none, the grandchild sees ``XPC_SERVICE_NAME=0``). Re-exporting the
label lets the gateway resolve its job without it (the stop-drain cap reading the live
``ExitTimeOut``, the exit-75 restart route, the control-socket supervisor declaration — all
via ``gateway.restart.launchd_job_label``). Only ``ai.hermes.*`` labels are exported;
app-coalition labels are meaningless as a job identity.

name: _prepare_child_command
arguments: command: Sequence[str], environ: Mapping[str, str] | None=None
doc:
Return the argv to exec, upgrading stale launchd-wrapped gateway commands.

launchd stamps ``XPC_SERVICE_NAME=<job label>`` only on this wrapper (its direct child; an
interactive shell has none, the grandchild sees ``XPC_SERVICE_NAME=0``). Newly generated
plists put ``--external-supervisor`` on the inner ``gateway run`` so ``hermes update`` can see
the flag on the live process argv.

name: _child_returncode_for_supervisor
doc:
Exit status the launchd wrapper reports for *returncode* from *command*.

Signal deaths stay 128+N. Gateway EX_CONFIG (78) becomes 0 so
``KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false`` parks the job instead of crash-looping;
a non-gateway child that happens to exit 78 is left alone.

name: is_windows
doc: Return True iff running on native Windows (not WSL).

name: _flip_console_code_page_to_utf8
doc:
``SetConsoleCP``/``SetConsoleOutputCP`` to CP_UTF8 (65001). Silent on failure: without an
attached console (redirected stdout, service, PTY-less CI) the calls return 0 and we move on.

name: _reconfigure_stream
doc:
Reconfigure a text stream to UTF-8 in place; skips streams without ``reconfigure`` (e.g. an
``io.StringIO`` substituted during tests).

name: configure_windows_stdio
doc:
Force UTF-8 stdio on Windows. No-op elsewhere.

Idempotent; returns ``True`` only when something actually changed. Set
``HERMES_DISABLE_WINDOWS_UTF8=1`` to opt out (forces the old cp1252 path for diagnosing
encoding bugs). Also sets a default ``EDITOR`` on Windows if none is set.

name: _default_windows_editor
_augment_path_with_known_tools
doc:
Prepend Hermes-managed tool directories to ``PATH`` (no-op on POSIX / missing dirs).

install.ps1 adds entries like ``%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\git\bin`` to the User PATH via
``SetEnvironmentVariable``, but already-running shells never see that broadcast, so a hermes
launched from the install session would not find rg / bash / grep. Prepending the known dirs
at startup closes that first-launch gap.

name: steward_update_message
doc: The `hermes update` refusal text for a sealed tree.

name: steward_uninstall_message
doc: The uninstall refusal text for a sealed tree.

name: read_install_stamp
doc:
The build stamp of ``project_root``, or ``{}``.

Tolerant by design: steward classification must not crash a refusal
path on a malformed stamp — a tree we cannot prove is ours still
refuses (see :func:`sealed_steward`), so garbage degrades safely.

name: is_bundled_payload
doc:
True when ``project_root`` is a bundled desktop payload's ``repo/``.

THE shape predicate for the sealed-bundle branch, and a mirror of the
Electron shell's ``installShape() === 'bundled'``: the build stamp is
the authority, so filesystem coincidences (a sibling ``bin/``, a
surviving ``apps/desktop/package.json``) can never promote a checkout
into it. A missing, foreign, or unreadable stamp means NOT bundled.

name: sealed_steward
doc:
The steward owning the sealed tree at ``project_root``, or ``None``.

``None`` means the tree is a git checkout (``.git`` present — a
directory, or a worktree/submodule gitfile) and is ours to mutate.
Everything else is sealed: the stamp's ``distribution`` names the
steward, and a missing or unreadable stamp gives ``"unknown"`` —
a tree we cannot prove is ours is not ours to remove.

name: classify_install
doc:
(steward, code_removal_allowed) for the tree at ``project_root``.

A git checkout reports ``("git", True)``; a sealed tree reports its
steward and ``False``. Used by ``gui_install_summary`` so the desktop
UI can gate its destructive options on the same ladder the CLI uses.

name: stream_json_requested
doc:
True when ``--format stream-json`` was passed; exits 2 on the combinations the protocol forbids
(no query to answer, or the interactive TUI transport) and forces quiet mode on ``args``.

name: attach
doc:
Route the agent's streaming/tool callbacks into this emitter (``init`` was already written at
construction, before credentials/agent init, so a failed start still yields init + result).

name: bind_session
doc:
Record the id the gateway assigned after ``init`` was written, so an interrupted or failed
run still reports which session holds the accepted work.

name: on_tool_progress
arguments: self, event_type: str, tool_name: str | None=None, preview: Any=None, args: Any=None, **kwargs: Any
doc:
``tool.started`` → ``tool_use`` (with ``input`` when the args are a dict); ``tool.completed`` →
``tool_result``. Other progress events (reasoning, output risk) are not part of the protocol.

significant_calls.expression:
self._emit({"type": "tool_result", "name": name,
                        **({"tool_call_id": kwargs["tool_call_id"]} if kwargs.get("tool_call_id") else {}),
                        "output": output if len(output) <= _TOOL_OUTPUT_CAP else output[:_TOOL_OUTPUT_CAP] + "...",
                        "duration_ms": int(float(duration) * 1000), "is_error": bool(kwargs.get("is_error", False))})

name: emit_result
arguments: self, result: Any, session_id: str='', exit_code: int=0
doc: Write the terminal ``result`` record (once) and return the process exit code it reports.

name: _resolve_origin
doc:
Best-effort current-chat origin from session env (cron's ``_origin_from_env``, which also
withholds non-push surfaces such as api_server) so an accepted job delivers back to the
accepting chat; None lets create_job use the home channel.

name: _accept
arguments: store, rest: str, origin, surface: str

name: _dismiss
arguments: store, rest: str, origin, surface: str

name: _catalog
arguments: store, rest: str, origin, surface: str

name: _clear
arguments: store, rest: str, origin, surface: str

name: handle_suggestions_command
arguments: args: str, *, origin: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, surface: str='cli'
doc:
Dispatch a ``/suggestions`` invocation (``args`` = text after the command word); returns
text to show the user. ``origin`` defaults to the session environment's chat.

name: _api_url
doc: Resolve the onboarding API URL, honoring the PoC env override.

name: is_valid_telegram_bot_token
doc: Return True when *token* has Telegram's bot-token shape.

name: render_qr_terminal
doc: Render a URL as a QR code string suitable for terminal output.

name: print_qr_code
doc: Print a QR code to stdout, with URL fallback if qrcode is missing.

name: create_pairing
arguments: api_url: str | None=None, bot_name: str=DEFAULT_BOT_NAME, timeout: float=10.0
doc: POST a pairing; the returned poll token is only used as a bearer credential while polling.

name: poll_pairing_result_once
arguments: api_url: str | None, pairing: TelegramPairing, timeout: float=10.0
doc: Poll the onboarding service once. Returns setup metadata when ready.

name: poll_for_setup_result
arguments: api_url: str | None, pairing: TelegramPairing, timeout: float=DEFAULT_POLL_TIMEOUT, interval: float=POLL_INTERVAL, on_tick=None
doc:
Poll the pairing API until setup metadata is available or timeout. ``on_tick(elapsed_s)``
runs before each attempt (progress display).

name: auto_setup_telegram_bot_result
arguments: api_url: str | None=None, manager_bot: str='HermesSetupBot', profile_name: Optional[str]=None, poll_timeout: float=DEFAULT_POLL_TIMEOUT
doc: Run the full automatic Telegram bot creation flow.

name: _sanitize
doc: Make an id safe to use as a filename (``/dev/pts/3`` -> ``dev-pts-3``).

name: get_terminal_id
doc:
Stable identity for this terminal: the tty device path (stdin, then stdout), else the first
present multiplexer/emulator env var; ``None`` when neither exists (callers skip breadcrumbs).

name: is_enabled
doc: Config gate: ``session.terminal_continue`` (default true).

name: _prune_stale
doc: Best-effort removal of breadcrumbs older than the staleness window.

name: write_breadcrumb
doc:
Record that this terminal's live session is ``session_id``. Never raises; no-op when the
feature is disabled, the session id is empty, or no terminal identity exists.

name: read_breadcrumb
doc: This terminal's breadcrumb payload, or ``None`` (missing, corrupt, or stale). Never raises.

name: resolve_breadcrumb_session
doc:
Resolve a bare ``-c`` for this terminal, or ``None`` to fall back. The breadcrumb's session
id counts only if it still exists in the DB, projected through the compression chain so the
resume lands on the live tip (same projection as ``main._resolve_session_by_name_or_id``).

name: write_tty
doc: Write raw escapes to /dev/tty, falling back to sys.stdout. Never raises.

name: osc9
doc: OSC 9 sequence with C0 controls and DEL stripped from the body.

name: warp_supported
doc: True when running in a Warp build that can render OSC 777 agent payloads.

name: warp_osc777
arguments: event: str, detail: str, session_id: str=''
doc: OSC 777 ``warp://cli-agent`` notification; ``event`` is ``stop`` or ``permission_request``.

name: notification_sequence
arguments: context: str, *, prompt: bool, session_id: str='', detail: str=''
doc: OSC 9 (plus Warp OSC 777 when supported) for a blocking prompt or turn end.

name: coerce_epoch
arguments: value: Any, *, session_id: Optional[str]=None, field: str='timestamp'
doc:
A stored timestamp cell as float epoch seconds, or ``None`` when it cannot be trusted.

Numbers, numeric strings and ``datetime`` are accepted; anything else, non-finite values and
values outside ``EPOCH_MIN..EPOCH_MAX`` return ``None`` after a WARNING naming the session so
the corrupt row can be found. ``None``/``""`` mean "unset" and stay silent. Every reader that
renders a row timestamp goes through here (a bad row degrades to one ``?`` cell, never a dead
command) and every writer uses it to refuse persisting a new bad row.

name: relative_time
doc: Format a timestamp as relative time (e.g., '2h ago', 'yesterday'); ``?`` when unset or corrupt.

name: _configured_timeout
arguments: provider_id: str, model: str | None, model_key: str, provider_key: str
doc: Per-model ``providers.<id>.models.<model>.<model_key>`` wins over ``providers.<id>.<provider_key>``.

name: get_provider_request_timeout
doc: Return a configured provider request timeout in seconds, if any.

name: get_provider_stale_timeout
doc: Return a configured non-stream stale timeout in seconds, if any.

name: _get_model_config
arguments: provider_config: dict[str, object], model: str | None

name: _catalog_keys
doc:
Contiguous ``<prefix><NN…>`` keys present in the English catalog, cached per prefix.

Counted against English (the parity baseline) so a partial translation never shrinks the
pool: a missing translated key falls back to English inside ``t()``. The count only changes
when the bundled catalog changes, i.e. on a code change, so a process-lifetime cache is safe.

name: reset_tips_cache
doc: Forget the probed key lists (tests that swap the locales dir call this).

name: tip_keys
doc: Catalog keys of every startup tip, in catalog order.

name: composer_placeholder_keys
doc: Catalog keys of every empty-composer example prompt, in catalog order.

name: get_random_tip
doc: Return a random tip string in the active language ("" if the catalog has none).

name: get_random_composer_placeholder
doc:
Return a rotating task-oriented placeholder for the empty composer, in the active language.

Kept generic — Hermes is not a coding-only agent, so the prompts must fit any project or none.

name: toolset_allowed_for_platform
doc: Return whether ``ts_key`` is available on ``platform``.

name: parse_platform_toolsets_value
doc:
The toolset list a saved ``platform_toolsets.<platform>`` value encodes, or None.

Older ``hermes config set`` builds stored a bare ``[...]`` argument as a plain string, so an
explicit selection like ``'["browser", "terminal"]'`` parses as str, not list (#115866).
Every reader and writer of the section goes through this one parser so the runtime,
``hermes doctor`` and ``hermes plugins enable`` agree on what the user configured. Any other
shape (null, scalar, unparseable string) is None: the caller decides how to report it.

name: _platform_default_is_valid
arguments: platform: object, default_toolset: str, is_valid_toolset: Callable[[str], bool], is_allowed_for_platform: Callable[[str, str], bool]

name: saved_toolset_resolver
doc:
``is_valid_toolset`` for a saved ``platform_toolsets`` list, mirroring what
``tools_config._get_platform_tools`` lets through: registered toolsets, any configured MCP server by
its ``mcp-<server>`` toolset name or bare alias (neither is registered before MCP discovery; a
disabled server is inactive, not a typo), ``hermes-<platform>`` plugin-platform bundles and the
``no_mcp`` sentinel. The manifest scan and the plugin lookup (which may run plugin discovery)
happen only for a name the cheaper checks cannot place.

name: validate_platform_toolsets
arguments: platform_toolsets: object, is_valid_toolset: Callable[[str], bool], is_allowed_for_platform: Callable[[str, str], bool]=toolset_allowed_for_platform
doc:
Return human-readable warnings for a ``platform_toolsets`` mapping.
Reports: a toolset name ``is_valid_toolset`` rejects (suggesting ``hermes-<platform>`` when that
would have been valid); a non-empty mapping resolving to zero valid toolsets (agent would start with
no tools); a platform with no valid toolsets, checked per-platform because the global net is
suppressed once any platform is valid; and non-list platform values, which fall back to the platform
default. ``is_valid_toolset`` is injected so this does no registry imports or I/O.

name: _pip_install
arguments: args: list[str], *, timeout: int=300, capture_output: bool=True

name: gui_toolset_label
doc:
Strip the leading ``<emoji>`` from a toolset title for GUI surfaces (plugins prefix ``🔌``).
CLI/TUI keeps the raw label — only HTTP APIs call this.

name: _xai_credentials_present
doc:
Cheap offline check for xAI credentials (auth store + env only); the runtime ``check_fn`` still gates
schema registration if creds expire. Also used by ``provider_readiness_status`` for ``xai_grok`` rows.

name: _toolset_configuration_platform
doc:
Platform a platform-less configuration UI should target: a toolset restricted away from ``default``
must be configured on a supported platform, else the save helper drops it and the UI reports a no-op.

name: _get_effective_configurable_toolsets
doc: CONFIGURABLE_TOOLSETS + plugin toolsets (appended after built-ins; a plugin key already built-in is skipped).

name: _get_plugin_toolset_keys
doc: Return the set of toolset keys provided by plugins.

name: _checklist_toolset_keys
doc:
Toolset keys the ``hermes tools`` checklist offers for ``platform`` (mirrors ``_prompt_toolset_checklist``);
read-time-resolved toolsets (recovered composites, MCP names) are NOT here.

name: _platform_default_toolset
doc: Composite toolset a platform falls back to (plugin platforms derive ``hermes-<platform>``).

name: _cfg_section
doc: Return ``config[key]`` as a dict, replacing a missing or non-dict value with ``{}``.

name: _is_configurable
doc: True when the toolset has provider options or simple env-var requirements to prompt for.

name: _toolset_label
doc: Display label for a toolset key (built-in or plugin), falling back to the key itself.

name: _key
arguments: key: str, prompt: str, url: str='', **extra
doc: One ``env_vars`` entry for a provider row (key order matters for the GUI JSON).

name: _row
arguments: name: str, badge: str='', tag: str='', env_vars: list=(), **markers
doc: One TOOL_CATEGORIES provider row; ``markers`` are the ``*_provider`` / ``post_setup`` / Nous keys.

name: _get_enabled_platforms
doc: Return platform keys that are configured (have tokens or are CLI).

name: _platform_toolset_summary
doc: Enabled toolsets per platform (``platforms`` defaults to ``_get_enabled_platforms()``).

name: _parse_enabled_flag
doc: Parse bool-like config values used by tool/platform settings.

name: enabled_mcp_server_names
doc:
MCP servers globally enabled in config.yaml or by a plugin (shared by platform + cron resolvers). Enabled
unless ``enabled`` is explicitly falsey; portable-plugin servers (in-memory) count — enabling the plugin is
the opt-in.

name: _enable_recently_shipped_toolsets
arguments: enabled_toolsets: set[str], config: dict, platform: str
doc:
Turn on toolsets that shipped after this platform's saved list (mutates ``enabled_toolsets``). Both "no"s
outlive this: unchecking records ``known_builtin_toolsets`` (declined), and ``agent.disabled_toolsets`` is
subtracted last in :func:`_get_platform_tools`.

name: _configurable_subset_of
doc:
Configurable toolsets whose STATIC membership is within ``tool_names`` (``include_registry=False``: a
runtime-registered tool the composite never listed must not drop the whole toolset).

name: _default_off_toolsets
doc:
Toolsets to strip from an implicit (composite-derived) enable set. A platform named after a default-off
toolset keeps it, except platform-restricted ones (``discord`` on discord stays OFF).
Platform-native default-off toolsets (``discord`` on discord) are off for unconfigured platforms as a
security opt-in — an explicitly saved list IS that opt-in and lets them through.

name: _explicit_toolsets
arguments: toolset_names: list[str], explicit_known_keys: set[str], config: dict, platform: str, explicitly_configured: bool
doc:
Enabled set when the saved list names configurable/plugin keys directly (subset inference over
``hermes-cli`` would re-enable disabled toolsets). A mixed list (``[hermes-cli, discord]``) still expands the
composite; _DEFAULT_OFF_TOOLSETS applies to that implicit expansion only.

name: _composite_toolsets
arguments: toolset_names: list[str], platform: str, explicitly_configured: bool
doc:
Enabled set inferred from composite names by reverse-mapping tool names (only while no explicit list is
saved). ``x_search`` is not in any composite, so inject it when xAI creds exist and exempt it from default-off.

name: _enabled_plugin_toolsets
arguments: config: dict, platform: str, toolset_names: list[str], plugin_ts_keys: set[str]
doc:
Plugin toolsets: on by default unless default-off (catalog spotify) or "known" for this platform
(``known_plugin_toolsets``, written on every save) and absent from the saved list.

name: _coerce_platform_toolsets_value
doc:
Read a list-literal string saved for ``platform_toolsets.<platform>`` as the list it encodes.

The parser is shared with ``hermes doctor`` and ``hermes plugins`` (``toolset_validation``
``parse_platform_toolsets_value``) so every surface agrees on the user's selection (#115866).
Any other non-list value is warned about once (naming the expected shape) and left as-is, so
the default fallback below is loud rather than silent.

name: _platform_toolsets_explicitly_saved
doc:
True when ``platform_toolsets.<platform>`` holds an explicitly saved LIST (even ``[]``).

``_get_platform_tools``'s ``explicitly_configured`` flag without re-running the resolver
(post-coercion, so a list-literal string counts too): an unset key or a non-list value
falls back to the platform default. Callers use this to tell an explicit zero-tool
selection (fail closed, #82010) from an absent one ("no restriction").

name: _get_platform_tools
arguments: config: dict, platform: str, *, include_default_mcp_servers: bool=True
doc: Resolve which individual toolset names are enabled for a platform.

name: _prune_toolsets_stripped_by_disabled
doc:
Drop disabled names AND every toolset whose tools the runtime would strip anyway.

The agent subtracts ``agent.disabled_toolsets`` at TOOL granularity (``model_tools._select_tool_names``),
so disabling a composite like ``debugging`` removes the terminal/web/file tools even though those names
never appear in the list. A name-only subtraction here left inspection surfaces (``hermes tools
--summary``, banner, ``/tools``) showing toolsets as enabled that no session could call (#97015).
Passthrough entries (MCP server names) and toolsets with no static tools (``context_engine``) are kept.

name: _recover_platform_native_toolsets
arguments: enabled_toolsets: set[str], platform: str, *, skip: set[str]
doc:
Add non-configurable platform toolsets (discord, feishu_*) in place: in the default composite but not in
CONFIGURABLE_TOOLSETS, so never in a checklist or saved list. Runs for BOTH ``_get_platform_tools`` branches.

name: _merge_mcp_servers
arguments: config: dict, toolset_names: list[str], explicit_passthrough: set[str], include_default_mcp_servers: bool
doc:
Explicit passthrough entries plus this platform's MCP servers: listed names form an allowlist, else every
globally enabled server (when ``include_default_mcp_servers``); the ``no_mcp`` sentinel disables all.

name: _warn_all_invalid_platform_toolsets
doc:
Warn once when an explicit platform list has only invalid names (``hermes`` for ``hermes-cli`` → no
native tools), at session tool resolution rather than only in update/doctor.

name: _save_platform_tools
arguments: config: dict, platform: str, enabled_toolset_keys: set[str]
doc: Save the selected toolset keys for a platform to config.

name: _provider_env_ready
doc: True when every env var a provider row declares is set (trivially true for no-key rows).

name: _toolset_has_keys
arguments: ts_key: str, config: dict | None=None, *, force_fresh: bool=False, features: Optional[NousSubscriptionFeatures]=None
doc: Check if a toolset's required API keys are configured.

name: _prompt_choice
arguments: question: str, choices: list, default: int=0
doc: Single-select menu (arrow keys). Delegates to curses_radiolist.

name: _estimate_tool_tokens
doc:
tiktoken (cl100k_base) tokens per tool name from the serialised OpenAI schema; cached per process and
registry generation, {} if tiktoken/registry unavailable.

name: _prompt_toolset_checklist
arguments: platform_label: str, enabled: set[str], platform: str='cli', *, force_fresh: bool=True
doc: Multi-select checklist of toolsets. Returns set of selected toolset keys.

name: _configure_toolset
arguments: ts_key: str, config: dict, *, force_fresh: bool=True, reconfigure: bool=False
doc: Configure a toolset: provider selection + API keys (TOOL_CATEGORIES), else simple env-var prompts.

name: _reconfigure_tool
doc: Let user reconfigure an existing tool's provider or API key.

name: _toolset_enabled_for_reconfigure
doc: True if the toolset is enabled on any platform, so reconfigure covers enabled-but-unconfigured ones.

name: _shared_metrics_state
doc: Return (collection_enabled, send_enabled) from a config dict.

name: _shared_metrics_menu_label
doc:
Menu row for shared metrics. Collect-only is an answer the offer no longer has; a profile
that chose it earlier keeps it, and the row names it rather than reading "off" while it collects.

name: _configure_shared_metrics_interactive
doc: Toggle shared-metrics collection/sending via the setup wizard prompt (single home for the consent rules).

name: _print_toolset_diff
arguments: added: set[str], removed: set[str], *, indent: str='  '
doc: Print ``+ label`` / ``- label`` lines for a checklist change.

name: _toolsets_needing_setup
doc: Selected toolsets still missing provider/API-key setup, sorted (opened even when the selection is unchanged).

name: _configure_newly_added
arguments: added: set[str], already: set[str], config: dict
doc: Configure newly enabled toolsets that need keys, skipping those already handled.

name: _print_tools_summary
doc: ``hermes tools --summary``: enabled toolsets per platform, non-interactive.

name: _configure_list
arguments: to_configure: list[str], config: dict, *, selected: bool=True
doc: Announce then configure each toolset in ``to_configure``.

name: _checklist_diff
arguments: new_enabled: set[str], prev: set[str], platform: str
doc:
``(added, removed)`` scoped to the checklist universe, so read-time toolsets (MCP names) the user never
saw a checkbox for don't print as spurious removals.

name: _first_install_flow
doc: Fresh install: one checklist per platform, no menu, keys prompted for every enabled tool.

name: _apply_platform_checklist
arguments: config: dict, pkey: str, new_enabled: set[str], prev: set[str], already: set[str], *, indent: str='  ', header: bool=False
doc:
Print the diff, configure newly added toolsets not in ``already``, and write the platform list.
Keys for newly enabled tools not already handled by the selected-tool pass, so a tool enabled globally
but lacking provider config doesn't drop the user back to the main menu.

name: _configure_platforms
arguments: config: dict, platform_keys: list[str], *, all_platforms: bool=False
doc:
Checklist + key setup + save for one platform, or for every platform at once (the 'Configure all
platforms (global)' menu entry). Returns True when config was saved.

name: tools_command
arguments: args=None, first_install: bool=False, config: dict | None=None
doc:
Entry point for `hermes tools` / `hermes setup tools`. ``first_install`` skips the menu (checklist + key
prompts); a wizard-passed ``config`` receives platform_toolsets so its final save_config() keeps them.

name: status_fn
doc: Deduplicated token cost of the selected toolsets.

name: _run_text
doc: Run a text subprocess with consistent decoding.

name: _post_setup_no_window_flags
doc: Hide Windows children unless their output is going to a real console.

name: _cua_version_summary
doc: Bound an external binary's potentially multiline version banner.

name: _cua_driver_contract_status
doc: Cache the runtime manifest check by binary identity for UI polling.

name: install_cua_driver
doc:
Prepare the PM pin and host setup for an explicit install/upgrade command.

Both CLI modes reconcile the same pin; neither discovers a vendor release.
A configured override is validated, never replaced or acquired by PM.
Unattended callers should use PM ensure directly, without interactive host setup.

name: _cua_driver_autostart_registered_windows
doc: A task targeting a previous PM version is not a ready registration.

name: _cua_autostart_opt_in
doc:
``computer_use.autostart`` — opt IN to the Windows per-boot ``cua-driver-serve`` logon
task. The default (absent/False) is on-demand (#97389): Computer Use starts the driver per
session exactly as macOS and Linux do, install/enable flows register no scheduled task, and
a missing task is not a repair condition. True registers (or repairs) the logon task at
install/enable time — needed when driving Windows over SSH (Session 0 has no interactive
desktop). Unreadable config fails closed to the on-demand default.

name: _cua_autostart_registration_ps_command
doc:
PowerShell body for the elevated registration: Start-Process with a STRUCTURED
``-FilePath`` / ``-ArgumentList`` (older install.ps1 builds interpolated the binary path
into a command string, which split at the first space) and ``-Verb RunAs -Wait -PassThru``
so the exit code propagates.

name: _repair_cua_driver_autostart_windows
doc:
Register autostart using structured arguments, including paths with spaces.

Only registers when the user opted into the per-boot task via
``computer_use.autostart`` (#97389): the on-demand default registers
nothing, silently — returning True (nothing to repair) keeps callers from
printing "auto-start was not registered" warnings for an intentional
absence.

name: _print_cua_platform_notes
arguments: is_windows: bool, is_linux: bool, *, fresh_install: bool

name: _mcp_match_filter
doc:
Runtime name-filter matcher (exact names or fnmatch globs), with a literal fallback.
Must use the SAME semantics as tools/mcp_tool.py registration — a literal ``in`` check renders glob
excludes (e.g. ``*team_member*`` from catalog default_excluded manifests) as if nothing were
excluded.

name: _mcp_preselected
doc: Indices of tools currently enabled: include mode, exclude mode, or all when unfiltered.

name: _apply_mcp_checklist
arguments: server_name: str, tools_cfg: dict, tool_names: list[str], chosen: set[int], include_set, exclude_set, match
doc: Write a checklist result back as ``tools.include`` / ``tools.exclude``.

name: _configure_mcp_tools_interactive
doc:
Probe each MCP server for its tools, show a per-server curses checklist, and write the result
back as ``tools.exclude`` / ``tools.include`` entries in config.yaml.

name: _apply_toolset_change
arguments: config: dict, platform: str, toolset_names: list[str], action: str
doc: Add or remove built-in toolsets for a platform.

name: _apply_mcp_change
arguments: config: dict, targets: list[str], action: str
doc: Add or remove specific MCP tools from a server's exclude list.

name: _print_tools_list
arguments: enabled_toolsets: set, mcp_servers: dict, platform: str='cli'
doc: Print a summary of enabled/disabled toolsets and MCP tool filters.

name: _known_tool_platforms
doc:
Return built-in plus discovered plugin platform names. Plugin platforms register at runtime, not
in the static CLI display registry, and must be recognized so an active plugin platform can audit
its authority.

name: tools_disable_enable_command
doc: Enable, disable, or list tools for a platform.

name: _info_lines
doc: Print each line as a 4-space-indented info row.

name: _ensure_browser_use_cli
doc:
Confirm the Browser Use CLI engine is runnable. It is browser-harness, a core dependency of
Hermes's own venv, so there is nothing to download; a miss means the venv needs a re-sync.
Primary driver engine for EVERY browser backend except Camofox (Firefox-based, no CDP surface).

name: _post_setup_agent_browser
doc: PM owns the driver and Chromium; Termux and Docker own their native payloads.

name: _python_hook
arguments: module, extra, label, installing, on_install=(), always=()

name: _post_setup_python
doc: Enable one Python provider through the application dependency transaction.

name: _post_setup_xai_grok
doc:
Shared xAI credential bootstrap for any picker row that talks to xAI (TTS, STT, Video Gen, x_search
…). Accepts a SuperGrok-tier OAuth token (preferred — billed to the existing subscription) or a raw
XAI_API_KEY; the rows declare empty env_vars so the auth UX lives here.

name: _codex_credentials_present
doc: Cheap offline check for Codex/ChatGPT OAuth credentials (auth store + pool only).

name: _post_setup_openai_codex
doc:
Shared Codex/ChatGPT OAuth bootstrap for any picker row that talks to Codex without an API key
(image gen today). The rows declare empty env_vars so the sign-in UX lives here. Saves tokens only —
never rewrites ``model.provider``: the user picked an image backend, not a chat model (#102144).

name: _run_post_setup
doc: Run post-setup hooks for tools that need extra installation steps.

name: valid_post_setup_keys
doc:
Return the set of post-setup keys declared by any visible provider (``TOOL_CATEGORIES`` plus
plugin-registered providers). This is the allowlist ``post-setup`` and the dashboard endpoint
validate against, so a caller cannot drive ``_run_post_setup`` with an arbitrary key.

name: run_post_setup_command
doc:
``hermes tools post-setup <key>`` — non-interactive runner the dashboard spawns so the GUI can drive
backend setup without re-implementing install logic. Exit code: 0 ok, 2 unknown key.

name: _post_setup_already_installed
doc: Return True when the post_setup install side-effect is satisfied (or no check is registered).

name: _module_installed
doc: Cheap importable-without-importing check (no heavy side effects).

name: _agent_browser_installed
doc:
True when everything ``_run_post_setup("agent_browser")`` installs is present: the agent-browser CLI
*and* the Chromium build it drives (or the Lightpanda engine, which needs no Chromium), so "Run
setup" flips to installed only when re-running it would be a no-op.

name: _camofox_installed
doc: Readiness belongs to the configured external server, not root node_modules.

name: _lightpanda_installed
doc: True when a lightpanda binary is on PATH or in a known install dir.

name: _cloud_agent_browser_installed
doc:
Installed-check for the ``browserbase`` hook: cloud providers host their own Chromium, so
presence of the agent-browser CLI is the whole contract.

name: _plugin_registry
doc: Import a plugin registry module after plugin discovery; ``None`` on any failure.

name: _plugin_provider_rows
arguments: registry_module: str, marker_keys: tuple[str, ...], *, require_name: bool=True, skip_builtin: bool=False, flatten_variants: bool=False
doc:
Picker-row dicts (TOOL_CATEGORIES-shaped) for a plugin registry's providers.
``marker_keys`` are all set to the registry name so downstream config/model-picker code routes
through the registry. ``skip_builtin`` drops names shadowing ``_BUILTIN_NAMES``;
``flatten_variants`` expands a schema's tier ``variants`` into separate rows sharing one backend
name, distinguished by ``web_tier``.

name: _plugin_rows_for
doc: Picker rows for the plugin-registered providers of one ``_PLUGIN_PROVIDER_ROW_SPECS`` category.

name: web_provider_capabilities
doc:
Capabilities (``search`` / ``extract``) a web backend supports, per the registry provider instance.
Lets the Capabilities GUI offer ``web.search_backend`` / ``web.extract_backend`` only where it makes
sense (ddgs and brave-free are search-only). Unknown backend or registry failure -> both.

name: _computer_use_provider_rows
doc:
Rows for installed computer-use providers other than the built-in ``cua`` (hand-written row with its
install post-setup). Read from plugin.yaml without importing: an unselected provider stays dormant.

name: _visible_providers
arguments: cat: dict, config: dict, *, force_fresh: bool=False, features: Optional[NousSubscriptionFeatures]=None
doc:
Provider entries visible for the current auth/config state.
Nous-managed rows (``managed_nous_feature``) are always shown, even logged-out/unentitled, to
advertise the capability.

name: provider_readiness_status
arguments: provider: dict, config: dict, *, features=None, is_active: Optional[bool]=None
doc:
Honest readiness state for a provider picker row.
``features`` avoids re-fetching portal state per row. ``is_active`` is the completed-setup fallback
for post_setup hooks with no registered installed-check (selecting a row runs its hook).

name: _web_registry_readiness
doc:
Keyless, untiered web rows are ready only when their registry provider is available: the only such
row's ``is_available()`` is an account login (OpenAI Native = openai-codex), hence ``needs_auth``.
Free-tier rows are exempt: they run on the public keyless ring, which ``is_available()`` ignores.

name: _toolset_needs_configuration_prompt
arguments: ts_key: str, config: dict, *, force_fresh: bool=False
doc: Return True when enabling this toolset should open provider setup.

name: _any_plugin_provider_available
doc: True when any provider in the plugin registry reports ``is_available()``.

name: _configure_tool_category
arguments: ts_key: str, cat: dict, config: dict, *, force_fresh: bool=True, reconfigure: bool=False
doc:
Provider selection for a tool category, then API-key setup for the chosen row.
``reconfigure`` ("Reconfigure an existing tool"): no setup note / skip row / Nous marker, and the
chosen provider goes through the key-update prompts instead of the new-enable prompts.

name: _web_tier_matches
doc:
True when a web picker row's tier matches the configured tier (``web.provider_tier.<backend>``).
Tiered rows (Exa/Parallel Free vs Paid) share one ``web_backend`` and differ only in ``web_tier``.
No ``web_tier`` on the row → matches; configured tier set → must equal the row's tier; unset →
"auto": paid when the row's key is present, free otherwise (highlight the row the runtime would
actually use).

name: _web_serving_backends
doc:
Backend names serving web search / extract as configured: each capability's own
``web.<cap>_backend`` override first, else the shared ``web.backend`` (``tools/web_tools.py``
dispatch order; legacy ``use_gateway: true`` reads as the managed ``nous`` selection).
Lower-cased and stripped like the dispatchers.

name: _web_backend_active
doc:
True when a web row's ``web_backend`` serves either capability as configured: a vendor serving
one capability through its override is in use even when the shared key names a different one,
and a shared vendor shadowed by both overrides serves nothing. Managed Nous rows never reach
here — they answer in ``_managed_provider_active``.

name: _has_marker
doc:
``browser_provider`` is a membership test (a local row carries ``browser_provider: ""``); every other
marker is a truthiness test.

name: _managed_provider_active
arguments: provider: dict, config: dict, managed_feature: str, force_fresh: bool
doc:
Active check for a Nous-managed row: the feature must be managed AND the category's selected
provider must be the row's vendor or ``nous``.

name: _browser_use_default_active
doc:
``browser.backend`` unset: Browser Use mode is the default, so the row is active whenever the
effective mode resolves on (legacy direct-API cloud config, or CLI runnable and no Camofox).

name: _browser_backend
doc: ``browser.backend`` as a string; ``""`` when unset or empty (YAML 1.1 parses an unquoted ``off`` as False).

name: _is_provider_active
arguments: provider: dict, config: dict, *, force_fresh: bool=False
doc: Check if a provider entry matches the currently active config.

name: _detect_active_provider_index
arguments: providers: list, config: dict, *, force_fresh: bool=False
doc: Return the index of the currently active provider, or 0.

name: _fal_model_catalog
doc: Lazy-load the FAL model catalog.

name: _managed_image_catalog
doc:
The managed row's union catalog (FAL + Krea + Portal), minus the gateways this account cannot use.

A free-pool account is funded for FAL only, so its picker never offers a Krea or Portal model it
would be denied at generation time; a logged-out or paid account sees everything.

name: _plugin_model_catalog
doc:
``(catalog_dict, default_model_id)`` for a plugin provider; ``catalog_dict`` is shaped like the legacy
``FAL_MODELS`` table so the picker path is shared. ``({}, None)`` if unregistered or no models.

name: _pick_model_from_catalog
arguments: catalog: dict, default_model, cfg_key: str, display: str, config: dict, *, row_indent: str=''
doc:
Column-aligned model picker shared by the FAL, plugin image gen and video gen flows.
Writes the choice to ``config[cfg_key]["model"]``. The current model is listed first so the cursor
lands on it; a saved model belonging to another provider (shared config key) or a drifted catalog
default never indexes the catalog. Safe when stdin is not a TTY — curses_radiolist keeps the current
selection.

name: _configure_imagegen_model
doc: Prompt for a model of an in-tree imagegen backend (``IMAGEGEN_BACKENDS``).

name: _configure_gen_model_for_plugin
arguments: section: str, plugin_name: str, config: dict
doc:
Prompt for a model from a plugin-registered image/video gen catalog (video rows keep their historical
two-space indent).

name: _configure_xai_imagine_storage
doc: Prompt for xAI Imagine stored public URL behavior.

name: _select_into
arguments: config: dict, section: str, key: str, vendor, managed
doc:
Write ``config[section][key] = vendor`` (``nous`` for a managed pick) and drop any legacy ``use_gateway``
key so the old read-time shim cannot override the new choice. Returns the section dict.

name: _select_plugin_gen_provider
arguments: section: str, plugin_name: str, config: dict, *, use_gateway: bool=False
doc:
Persist a plugin-backed image/video gen provider selection (``nous`` for a Nous-managed pick, else the
plugin name) and run its model picker.

name: _configure_stt_model
doc: Prompt for the STT model after a provider pick (static catalog, or DeepInfra's live one).

name: _write_provider_config
doc:
Persist the provider/backend config keys for a selected provider.
Pure, non-interactive core of :func:`_configure_provider` (no env prompts, post-setup hooks, Nous
auth gating or model pickers) shared by the CLI and the GUI ``PUT .../provider`` endpoint. Each pick
writes exactly ONE provider string per category (``nous`` for managed rows) and removes any legacy
``use_gateway`` key so the read-time shim cannot override the new choice.

name: apply_provider_selection
arguments: ts_key: str, provider_name: str, config: dict
doc:
Non-interactively persist a provider selection for a toolset (config keys only — API keys, post-setup
hooks, auth gating and model pickers are separate GUI endpoints). ``provider_name`` is resolved among
:func:`_visible_providers` rows; raises ``KeyError`` for an unknown toolset or provider.

name: _nous_provider_gate
arguments: provider: dict, config: dict, managed_feature, *, force_fresh: bool
doc:
Return False (after printing why) when a Nous-gated row cannot be selected.
Managed Tool Gateway rows are always listed but only *activate* with paid Nous Portal access —
selecting one runs an inline Portal login (auth + entitlement only, no inference-provider switch).
Pure pre-auth UX rows (``requires_nous_auth`` without a managed feature) keep the older logged-in +
entitled gate.

name: _finish_provider_selection
doc: Model pickers that follow a provider pick: plugin image/video gen, in-tree FAL, STT.

name: _print_provider_selection
doc: Status lines announcing which backend/provider keys a pick writes.

name: _show_portal_hint
arguments: provider: dict, config: dict, managed_feature, force_fresh: bool
doc:
True when a BYOK row shares its category with a Nous-managed sibling and the user is not authed to
Nous — a single dim hint tells them the key is avoidable via a Portal subscription.

name: _prompt_secret
arguments: key: str, label: str, url: str, default_val: str, *, reconfigure: bool, url_label: str, strip: bool=False
doc:
One env-var prompt; True unless the new-enable flow skipped the key.
Reconfigure mode shows the current value and re-prompts ("Enter to keep current"); the new-enable
flow prompts with ``default_val`` visible when one exists, else as a password, and ``strip`` decides
whether whitespace is trimmed (and whitespace-only counts as skipped).

name: _prompt_env_vars
doc:
Prompt for a provider's env vars; True when every key ended up configured.
Reconfigure mode re-prompts every key and always returns True; the new-enable flow keeps already-set
keys without asking and reports False on any skipped key.

name: _configure_provider
arguments: provider: dict, config: dict, *, force_fresh: bool=True, reconfigure: bool=False
doc:
Configure a single provider - prompt for API keys and set config.
``reconfigure=False`` (new-enable): already-set keys are kept without asking and the post-setup hook
only runs when every key was provided. ``reconfigure=True`` re-prompts every key and always runs the
hook.

name: _reconfigure_provider
arguments: provider: dict, config: dict, *, force_fresh: bool=True
doc: Reconfigure a provider - update API keys.

name: _configure_vision_backend
doc:
Interactive vision-backend configuration (``auxiliary.vision.{provider,model,base_url}``).
Offers any authenticated provider + model (same surface as ``hermes model``) or a custom endpoint
rather than forcing OpenRouter. "Auto" leaves the keys empty so the resolver uses the main-model
fallback chain.

name: _configure_vision_provider_model
doc:
Provider + model picker for vision, mirroring the ``/model`` surface.
Rows come from ``build_aux_picker_rows()`` so this lists exactly what the ``hermes model`` aux-task
picker lists, including user-defined ``providers:`` / ``custom_providers:`` endpoints. Persists
``auxiliary.vision.provider`` + ``.model``.

name: _configure_simple_requirements
doc:
Fallback for toolsets that just need env vars (no provider selection).
Vision has its own provider/model picker — run it directly so neither flow falls back to the generic
single-key prompt (which would re-ask for OPENROUTER_API_KEY).

name: filter_to_enabled_toolsets
arguments: unavailable: list[dict], enabled: Iterable[str], resolve: Callable[[str], Iterable[str]]
doc:
Keep only the *unavailable* entries this session would actually load.

``enabled`` is the CLI's toolset selection as configured — on a default install that is a
composite bundle such as ``["hermes-cli"]``, never the individual names ``check_tool_availability``
reports — so each entry is expanded to tool names through ``resolve`` (``toolsets.resolve_toolset``)
and an unavailable toolset counts as enabled when its name is listed directly or any of its tools
is inside the expansion. An empty selection means "everything", so nothing is filtered.

name: current_terminal_backend
doc: The terminal backend selected for this process (``terminal.backend`` / TERMINAL_ENV), e.g. 'docker'.

name: tool_availability_warning_lines
arguments: unavailable: list[dict], *, terminal_reason: Optional[str], terminal_backend: str='local'
doc:
Rich-markup lines to print at CLI startup for *unavailable* toolsets; ``[]`` when there is nothing
worth saying. ``terminal_reason`` is ``terminal_backend_unavailable_reason()`` (None when unknown).

name: record_tui_worktree
doc:
Remember a tree the ``-w`` / ``--tui -w`` launcher created, or a classic ``/worktree new``
moved its gateway session into. Never raises.

name: _recorded_tree_for
doc: The launcher's record of the missing tree *cwd* is (or is inside), or None.

name: recreate_tui_worktree
doc:
Recreate the launcher-made tree a resumed session's missing *cwd* names -> its path, or None.

Reuses the branch when it survived (its commits come back), else makes it again from the repo's
current HEAD. The tree is locked for the session so the stale-tree prune keeps it. Never raises.

name: turn_exit_code
arguments: result, *, kanban_worker: bool, credentials_rate_limited: bool=False, credentials_terminal: bool=False, transient_reasons=TRANSIENT_PROVIDER_REASONS, terminal_reasons=TERMINAL_PROVIDER_REASONS
doc: Preserve completion, interruption and retryable/terminal provider outcomes.

name: credential_failure_flags
doc:
``turn_exit_code`` credential kwargs for an exception raised before any turn result exists.

Same predicates as the one-shot CLI's ``_ensure_runtime_credentials``: a quota/rate-limit
``AuthError`` is transient, only an explicit re-authentication requirement is terminal. The
cause chain is walked because agent construction wraps the resolver's error.

name: _print_box
doc: Print the 3-line framed heading used by the uninstall screens.

name: _prompt
doc: ``input(text).strip().lower()``; None (after printing "Cancelled.") on Ctrl-C/EOF.

name: _confirm_yes
doc: Ask the user to type ``yes``; False (after the cancel line, unless Ctrl-C/EOF) otherwise.

name: _remove_each
doc:
Run ``remove(path)`` per candidate, collecting the ones it reports removed; failures become
the shared ``Could not remove <path>: <err>`` warning.

name: get_project_root
doc: Get the project installation directory.

name: code_removal_refusal
doc:
Why the uninstaller must not remove this tree's code, or ``None``.

A git checkout (the install.sh / install.ps1 / `hermes desktop` layout)
is ours to remove. A sealed tree (no ``.git``) belongs to a steward —
the Nix store, the bundled desktop app, a Docker image — and only the
steward removes it. Returns the user-facing refusal text for sealed
trees; the text always points at ``hermes uninstall --data`` for the
user-data cleanup that IS allowed everywhere.

name: _refuse_if_steward_owned
doc: Exit with the steward's instructions when code removal is forbidden.

name: find_shell_configs
doc: Find shell configuration files that might have PATH entries.

name: remove_path_from_shell_configs
doc: Remove Hermes PATH entries from shell configuration files.

name: remove_wrapper_script
doc: Remove the hermes wrapper script if it exists.

name: _node_symlink_candidate_dirs
doc: Directories where the installer may have placed node/npm/npx symlinks.

name: remove_node_symlinks
doc:
Remove the node/npm/npx symlinks the installer placed on PATH.

Historical POSIX installs (``scripts/install.sh`` before pm owned the
Node runtime) symlinked node/npm/npx into the same directory as the
``hermes`` command:

- ``/usr/local/bin/`` on root FHS installs (Linux, uid 0)
- ``~/.local/bin/`` otherwise (the common non-root case)

We check all candidate directories so that uninstall works regardless of
how the install was done (e.g. a root FHS install that placed links in
``/usr/local/bin``, or an older install that used ``~/.local/bin`` before
the FHS fix).  Only symlinks that resolve into this Hermes home's ``node``
directory are removed — links the user has repointed elsewhere (nvm, fnm,
etc.) are left untouched.

name: uninstall_gateway_service
doc:
Stop and uninstall the gateway service (systemd, launchd, Windows
Scheduled Task / Startup folder) and kill any standalone gateway processes.

Delegates to the gateway module which handles:
- Linux: user + system systemd services (with proper DBUS env setup)
- macOS: launchd plists
- Windows: Scheduled Task + Startup-folder fallback, via ``gateway_windows``
- All platforms: standalone ``hermes gateway run`` processes

name: _remove_systemd_gateway
doc: Linux: uninstall systemd services (both user and system scopes).

name: _launchd_gateway_plists
doc: Every gateway LaunchAgent plist on disk, under the real account home.

name: _remove_launchd_gateway
doc:
macOS: boot out and uninstall every gateway LaunchAgent plist.

Sweeps BOTH label patterns (see ``_LAUNCHD_GATEWAY_PLIST_PATTERNS``):
uninstalling only the current label's plist left older-label agents
registered, and launchd kept respawning the gateway after removal.
``bootout`` (both Aqua and per-user domains, whichever holds the job) plus
the legacy ``unload`` run before the unlink so launchd never respawns a
job whose plist is gone.

name: _remove_windows_gateway
doc:
Windows: uninstall Scheduled Task + Startup-folder entry via ``gateway_windows`` (it owns
schtasks /Delete, the .cmd unlink and stopping the detached pythonw gateway).

name: _hermes_path_markers
doc:
Prefixes identifying Hermes-owned User-PATH entries (prefix match sweeps git\cmd, git\bin,
node...). ``include_managed_bin`` adds ``<root>\bin`` (launchers + managed uv) — only when that
dir is about to be deleted, so a keep-data uninstall keeps the working uv resolvable.

name: remove_path_from_windows_registry
doc: Strip Hermes-owned entries from User-scope PATH in the registry (see ``_hermes_path_markers``).

name: remove_hermes_env_vars_windows
doc: Delete HERMES_HOME and HERMES_GIT_BASH_PATH from User-scope env vars.

name: _edit_user_environment
doc:
Open HKCU\Environment read/write and run ``edit(winreg, key, removed)``. Returns what
``edit`` appended to ``removed`` even if a later registry call raised (callers report exactly
what was touched); ``[]`` off-Windows (no ``winreg``).

name: remove_portable_tooling_windows
doc:
Delete the PortableGit / Node / gateway-service dirs the Windows installer created under
``hermes_home`` (isolated from any system Git / Node, so nothing else breaks).

name: _xdg_leftover_paths
doc:
The XDG cache/data dirs an install scatters outside HERMES_HOME.

Returns (removable, data_preserved): the cache dir is always removable;
the XDG data dir is user data, so it is only removed on a full uninstall
and otherwise reported as intentionally preserved.

name: remove_desktop_app_leftovers
doc:
Remove per-user app leftovers that live outside HERMES_HOME and the
checkout, which earlier uninstallers left behind (#62209): the macOS
Library caches/logs/browser-store/state entries the packaged app and
Electron scatter, and the XDG cache dir on every platform. On a full
uninstall the XDG data dir (``~/.local/share/hermes``) goes too.

Only well-known Hermes-named entries are touched — never a glob of the
whole Library.

name: remove_legacy_runtime_trees
doc:
Delete managed-runtime trees a PRE-SPLIT install left in HERMES_HOME.

Runtime artifacts are install-scoped now, so the current locations go
away with ``rmtree(project_root)``. But a checkout OUTSIDE the home
(the common case: ``~/src/hermes-agent``) used to put its node/uv
under ``$HERMES_HOME`` — that tree survives removing the checkout and
survives "keep my data" uninstalls, because it is not data.

Only the exact managed layout is removed: ``node/`` (a tree the
installer owned wholesale) and ``bin/uv`` (the single binary, NOT the
whole ``bin/`` dir — a user's own scripts can live there). Profile
state is never touched.

name: remove_windows_bin_launchers
doc:
Delete the managed binary dir (the default Hermes root's ``bin``).

The dir holds only hermes-owned launcher copies (the relocatable venv's
console scripts, staged onto PATH by first-run repair) — pm keeps uv in
its own store entry, so nothing shared lives here and the whole dir goes.
Every uninstall mode deletes the code checkout, so a surviving launcher
would dangle: ``hermes`` in a new terminal resolves and then errors on
its missing venv target, which reads worse than command-not-found.

A launcher that IS this process's own trampoline is mandatory-locked
against deletion but not rename, so removal falls back to renaming it
aside with a non-executable suffix.

*windows* is an injectable platform verdict for tests (same pattern as
``_install_repair.ensure_windows_bin_launchers``).

name: _is_default_hermes_home
doc: Return True when ``hermes_home`` points at the default (non-profile) root.

name: _discover_named_profiles
doc: ``ProfileInfo`` for every non-default profile; ``[]`` when profile support is unavailable.

name: _uninstall_profile
doc:
Fully uninstall a named profile: stop its gateway, remove its alias, wipe its home. Shells
out to ``hermes -p <name> gateway stop|uninstall`` because service names / unit paths derive
from the current HERMES_HOME and can't be switched in-process.

name: run_data_uninstall
doc: Erase this home's data, preserving installed runtimes and sibling profiles.

name: run_gui_uninstall
doc:
GUI-only uninstall: remove the Chat GUI, leave the agent + data intact.

Mirrors ``hermes uninstall --gui``. Removes the desktop app's built
artifacts, the packaged app bundle (best-effort), and the Electron
userData dir — nothing under ``$HERMES_HOME`` config/sessions/.env, and
never the Python agent or its venv.

name: run_uninstall
doc:
Run the uninstall process.

Options:
- Full uninstall: removes code + ~/.hermes/ (configs, data, logs)
- Keep data: removes code but keeps ~/.hermes/ for future reinstall

name: _print_uninstall_dry_run
arguments: *, project_root: Path, hermes_home: Path, full_uninstall: bool
doc: Print the uninstall plan without stopping services or deleting files.

name: _remove_step
arguments: label: str, remove, success_fmt: str, none_msg: str
doc: Announce ``label``, run ``remove()``, log one success line per removed item (or ``none_msg``).

name: _rmtree_step
arguments: path: Path, *, indent: str='', fully: bool=True
doc: Best-effort ``rmtree`` with the shared success/warning lines.

name: _macos_cache_leftover_dirs
doc:
Cache dirs Electron/Chromium and the setup binary write OUTSIDE HERMES_HOME on
macOS. Chromium splits the desktop app's HTTP/script caches under ``~/Library/Caches``
keyed by both the product name and the app id, and the Tauri setup binary does the
same under its own pair of identifiers. ``gui_uninstall`` removes the userData dir
(``Application Support/Hermes``) but never these (#62209).

name: _rmtree_if_exists
doc: ``_remove_each`` remover: True (after removing) when *path* exists, else False.

name: remove_dashboard_launchd_jobs
doc:
macOS: boot out and delete every launchd job whose ``ProgramArguments`` runs a
``hermes dashboard`` / ``hermes serve`` backend, returning the removed plist paths.

The gateway uninstall only reaches the gateway label, so a dashboard/serve
LaunchAgent survives a full uninstall and launchd keeps respawning its backend.
Mirrors the enumeration ``hermes_cli.main_dashboard`` uses to find those jobs
(``_launchd_plist_dirs`` + ``_parse_dashboard_runtime``): read each plist, match the
arguments, ``launchctl bootout`` the job's domains (launchd takes the process down;
booting out an already-unloaded job is fine and never checked), then delete the
plist — a stale, not-loaded plist is still Hermes-created and still goes. A missing,
unreadable, or malformed plist is skipped, never fatal. macOS only (empty list
elsewhere).

name: _perform_uninstall
arguments: *, project_root: Path, hermes_home: Path, full_uninstall: bool, remove_profiles: bool, named_profiles: list
doc:
The uninstall steps shared by the interactive and ``--yes`` paths: stop gateway -> strip PATH
(rc files + Windows registry) -> wrapper/launchers/node symlinks -> Chat GUI artifacts -> delete
the checkout -> (Windows) PortableGit/Node -> optionally ``$HERMES_HOME`` and named profiles.

name: main
doc:
Module entrypoint: ``python -m hermes_cli.uninstall --mode <gui|lite|full|data>``.

Exists so the desktop app can run the uninstall under a Python interpreter
OUTSIDE the venv being deleted. On Windows, ``lite``/``full`` rmtree the
venv that contains the running ``python.exe`` — and a running .exe is
mandatory-locked, so doing that from the venv's own interpreter half-fails.
The desktop launches this with the system Python + ``PYTHONPATH=<agentRoot>``
so ``import hermes_cli`` resolves from source while the venv is torn down.

``data`` removes user data only (no code) and is the one mode allowed on
steward-owned installs (Nix, the bundled desktop app, Docker); the
code-removing modes hard-fail there with the steward's instructions.

Data-only mode keeps the runtime installed and uses its dependencies to
coordinate live writers. Code-removing modes can still run outside the
environment being removed.

name: __init__
arguments: self, *, mode: str, desktop_userdata: Path | None=None

name: _serve_unit_recovery_available
doc: Can a fresh process restart ``hermes-serve*``/``hermes-dashboard*`` units on this host?

name: _surviving_pre_update_serve_runtimes
doc:
Pre-update serve/dashboard runtimes that are STILL the same process — i.e. live on the
pre-update code generation. Identity is the incarnation ``(pid, create_time)``, never the PID
alone: ``ledger_entries()`` prunes dead entries, but a correctly restarted serve can come back
on the same number. Fail closed on missing evidence (unreadable ledger, no incarnation on either
side): the runtime counts as surviving.

name: _qualified_serve_skips
doc:
Scope-qualify the units the aborted phase already settled: ``<scope>/<unit>`` because
``hermes-serve.service`` can exist in BOTH the user and system manager (two processes).

name: _run_fresh_recovery_process
arguments: profiles, candidates, *, gateway_mode: bool, recover_serve: bool, skip_units
doc:
Spawn ``hermes_cli.update_restart_recovery --stdin`` detached from this process; None when it
could not run (no systemd-run in gateway mode, OSError, timeout) — the caller fails closed.

name: _parse_serve_units
doc:
Validate the child's ``serve_units`` block; an unreadable block is not "nothing to do" when
serve recovery was requested (those units may still serve the pre-update generation).

name: _recover_gateway_restart_after_abort
arguments: plan, *, gateway_mode: bool, skip_profiles: set[str] | None=None, skip_units: set[str] | None=None
doc:
Retry supervised gateway restarts from a clean Python process. Only inventory-classified
supervisor-owned profiles.

``skip_units`` names the units the aborted phase already settled, as ``<scope>/<unit>``. The scope is
part of the identity, not decoration: ``hermes-serve.service`` can exist in both the user and the system
manager as two different processes, and an unqualified token would let a settled one suppress recovery
of a stale one (review on #96235).

name: _warn_stale_serve_runtimes
doc:
Name the serve/dashboard processes still on pre-update code: ``hermes serve`` hosts
``tui_gateway.server``, and an un-restarted unit keeps the pre-pull ``sys.modules`` graph so
every chat turn fails with an ``ImportError`` no gateway row explains.

name: _owed_stale_serve_rows
doc:
Survivors the updater itself owes a restart for. A Desktop-supervised serve is excluded: the
recovery pass is forbidden to restart it (it hosts the live Desktop chats), so counting it would
end every update with the Desktop open as incomplete/exit 1. It is still named by
:func:`_warn_stale_serve_runtimes` and recorded in the receipt. See #111494. (The
fleet-restart-pending marker draws the same boundary for its own inventory, so a supervisor-owned
serve row no longer keeps that warning armed either.)

name: _abort_recovery_is_complete
doc:
May a fresh-process recovery clear the incomplete flag? Only when EVERY inventoried runtime
family is accounted for. Empty ``planned_gateway_profiles`` is deliberately NOT completeness:
with no gateway leg to prove, ``_restart_phase_failure_is_incomplete`` + the stale rows decide.

name: is_canary_tag
doc: True for a canonical canary source identity.

name: canary_timestamp
doc: Return the UTC receipt stamp from a canonical canary tag.

name: canary_tag_for_date
doc:
Return ``v<stable>+canary.<full UTC timestamp>``.

The stable core is unchanged. The suffix is build metadata, so the source
identity compares equal to the stable and only the R2 channel head moves a
canary subscriber.

name: install_id
doc:
The sha16 id of the install at ``project_root`` (default: this one).

Same identity as the ``installs/<sha16>/`` state folder key.

name: _read_stamp
doc: The install stamp of ``root``, or ``{}`` (tolerant, like steward.py).

name: channel_record
doc: This install's ``{path, channel}`` record from config, or ``{}``.

name: default_channel
doc:
The channel an unconfigured install tracks.

A source checkout of the official repository follows the latest published
stable release. Forks, mirrors and checkout-less trees keep following main.
``electron-updater`` and ``app-installer`` bundles report their artifact
channel: a canary artifact tracks canary, every other bundle
