name: _fs_path
arguments: raw_path: str, *, cwd: str | None=None, decode_fallback: bool=True

name: _translate_agent_path
doc:
One translation attempt under whatever scope is bound; None off the docker backend.

The gate keeps a local-backend gateway with leftover ``docker_volumes`` from serving
mount sources in place of real host files. Quiet: fs callers also see ordinary host
paths, which are not MEDIA misses worth a warning.

name: _agent_path_scope
doc:
Bind the profile whose sandbox a container path names: its home and its terminal policy.

A requested ``profile_home`` other than the current home binds that home and its complete
terminal policy, as MEDIA delivery does (#109024). A home already bound by the caller (a
native profile ticket's override) gets its own terminal policy when no scope is bound, so
translation never reads the launch profile's ambient ``TERMINAL_DOCKER_VOLUMES``. An
override naming the launch home keeps the ambient env, which may carry env-only policy.
Translation and the unmapped-path classification both run inside this scope, so they
agree about the backend.

name: _agent_container_path
doc:
Map an agent-visible container path to its host bind mount, or None.

Docker agents emit container paths (``/workspace/...``, ``/root/...``) in
transcripts and MEDIA tags, while the dashboard fs routes stat the gateway
HOST filesystem (#85238). Reuse the gateway's MEDIA volume translator inside
``_agent_path_scope(profile_home)``. When no terminal scope is bound even
then (``serve --isolated`` after a failed early bridge), retry once under the
current profile's complete terminal policy, never replacing an already-bound
scope or refusal (retry from #104992).

Runs on the raw string, before host normalization: on a Windows gateway
``Path("/workspace/x").resolve()`` anchors to the current drive and the
container path is gone before translation sees it. ``..`` segments are never
translated, so the managed routes keep refusing them.

name: _agent_fs_path
arguments: raw_path: str, *, cwd: str | None=None, profile_home: Path | None=None
doc:
``_fs_path`` for agent-facing reads; container paths resolve to their host
mount, so callers' boundary guards see the real host target.

POSIX: a readable host path wins, and translation only runs when the host
lookup misses, so a root-run gateway can still browse its own ``/root``.
Windows: a container-shaped path never names a host file (it would anchor to
the current drive), so a translation miss is a 404 rather than a drive lookup.

name: _is_unmapped_container_path
doc:
A docker-backend container path (``/workspace``, ``/root`` or a configured
volume target) rather than a host path or a typo elsewhere on the host. Reads
the backend and volumes in the same profile scope translation used.

name: _dashboard_local_update_managed_externally
doc:
True when the dashboard should not offer ``hermes update``.

Containerized dashboards are updated by the outer launcher/image — except a
``git`` install (bind-mounted checkout, e.g. the hermes-webui image), where
the update button is the correct path. pip stays blocked in containers: its
apply path mutates the running container filesystem.

name: _resolve_managed_path
arguments: raw_path: str | None, request: Request, *, for_write: bool=False, for_agent_read: bool=False

name: _hosted_fs_read_guard
doc:
Preview and Git reads share managed-file restrictions on locked deployments.

``request`` is unused (the policy is env/home driven) and optional so the
route functions stay callable directly, e.g. from agent-side tests.

name: _managed_file_entry
arguments: policy: ManagedFilesPolicy, target: Path, *, skip_missing: bool=False
doc: Describe an entry; listings may skip vanished files, while writes stay strict.

name: _read_dashboard_json_response
doc: Read a JSON HTTP response body with a hard size cap (issue #54808).

name: _probe_gateway_health
doc:
Probe the gateway's HTTP health endpoint (cross-container). Blocking — run in an executor.

DEPRECATED: driven by the ``GATEWAY_HEALTH_URL`` / ``GATEWAY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT`` env vars,
to be replaced by a dashboard config key; do not add callers. Accepts a base URL or an
explicit ``/health`` / ``/health/detailed`` path; tries ``/health/detailed`` first.

name: _profile_platform_ports
doc:
Best-effort ``platform -> host TCP port`` for one profile's live gateway.

Ports come from the profile's own config.yaml (``gateway.platforms`` then top-level
``platforms`` — later wins, matching load_gateway_config precedence), falling back to the
adapter default. Env-var overrides (e.g. WEBHOOK_PORT in that profile's .env) are not resolved.

name: _profile_gateway_writer_identity
doc:
``(pid, start_time)`` of the profile's LIVE gateway, or None.

Uses the same validated-liveness helper and the same ``_get_process_start_time`` that stamped
the record, so equality is exact (no unit/clock-source mismatch).

name: _owned_profile_platforms
doc:
Keep only platform entries stamped by the profile's CURRENT gateway process.

Gateway startup preserves plain platform entries in gateway_state.json across restarts, so the
raw map can carry fatal state for platforms since disabled/removed. Cross-profile aggregation
has no config context to filter against, so it demands exact ``(pid, start_time)`` writer
identity instead. Fail closed: legacy entries without identity, or no live process, yield {} —
a false "degraded forever" is the worse failure mode.

name: _collect_profile_gateway_topology
doc:
Enumerate profiles and the gateways serving them for ``/api/status``.

Returns ``profiles`` (all profile names via the cheap ``profiles_to_serve(True)`` chokepoint),
``gateways`` (one ``{"profile", "ports", "served_profiles"?}`` per LIVE gateway; liveness via
``_check_gateway_running`` so it agrees with the sidebar), ``gateway_mode``
(multiplex / single / multiple / none) and ``profile_platforms`` — ownership-filtered runtime
platform maps per live gateway, an internal aggregation input never exposed directly.

name: _load_configured_gateway_platforms
doc:
Connected platform names; synchronous by design — the first ``load_gateway_config()`` does
platform discovery and can outlast Desktop's WS connect timeout on Windows, so ``get_status``
runs this in Starlette's worker pool.

name: _windows_build_number
doc: Extract the Windows NT build number from stdlib platform strings.

name: _display_system_platform
arguments: *, system: str, release: str, version: str, platform_label: str
doc: Host OS fields for display; Windows 10 builds >= 22000 are relabelled Windows 11.

name: _terminate_desktop_managed_gateway
doc: Stop a live gateway restart child when its Desktop backend shuts down.

name: _named_profile_from_action
doc:
Return the named-profile selector that :func:`_profile_cli_args` puts in front of an action.

Deliberately inspects only the leading selector: values after the real subcommand may
legitimately contain ``-p`` / ``--profile`` for a nested process (``mcp add --args ...``).

name: _is_host_gateway_spawn
doc:
True when *subcommand* starts the host multiplexer, not a named profile's own gateway.

``hermes gateway restart`` and ``hermes -p default gateway restart`` are the host.
``hermes -p coder gateway stop`` is not.

name: _profile_action_environment
doc:
Environment for a detached ``hermes <subcommand>`` action.

The dashboard loads its own profile's ``.env`` into process-global ``os.environ``. Copying
that mapping verbatim into ``hermes -p <other> ...`` lets the named child see the dashboard
profile's platform credentials and ports *before* its own dotenv loads (``load_hermes_dotenv``
does not override keys already present): a supposedly A2A-only profile then claims the default
Discord token and binds the default API/BlueBubbles ports.

Named-profile actions therefore start from Hermes' standard scrubbed subprocess env, then drop
the profile-managed keys plus every key declared by the dashboard/default profile dotenv files
and their hydrated secret sources, and pin ``HERMES_HOME`` to the target profile. The child's
normal startup then loads that profile's own ``.env``. A host-gateway verb (bare ``gateway``
or ``-p default gateway``) starts from ``host_gateway_child_env`` so a named-profile dashboard
cannot donate its dotenv to the multiplexer. Other actions without a profile selector keep
the historical environment exactly.

name: _action_targets_system_gateway
doc:
True when *subcommand* is a gateway lifecycle verb that resolves to the SYSTEM unit.

Scope is decided by the CLI's own picker (``_select_systemd_scope``) evaluated for the profile
the action addresses, not by "a system unit exists": a host carrying both units resolves to the
user unit, which the dashboard user operates unelevated. Same root/sudo posture as the
``hermes update`` fleet restart (``update_cmd_fleet._needs_sudo`` / ``_sudo_noninteractive_ok``).

name: _spawn_hermes_action
arguments: subcommand: list[str], name: str, *, env_overrides: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None
doc: Spawn ``hermes <subcommand>`` detached (via ``hermes_cli.main``) and record the handle.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(
            cmd, cwd=str(PROJECT_ROOT), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=log_file, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            env=action_env, **detach,
        )

significant_calls.expression: f"{name}: breakaway spawn refused ({exc}); retrying without CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB\n".encode()

name: _own_profile_selector
doc:
The profile a lifecycle verb addresses: the explicit selector, else the process's own
profile (a pooled Desktop ``hermes --profile X serve`` answers ``/api/gateway/*`` without
``?profile=``; an unscoped verb there is about X). The default home resolves to the literal
``"default"`` selector, never to a bare argv: a selector-less child re-reads the sticky
``active_profile`` and would act on another profile's gateway (and skips the named-target
env scrub). ``None`` is reserved for a home that is not a profile home at all.

name: _gateway_subcommand
doc:
``hermes [-p X] gateway <verb>`` argv for a dashboard lifecycle action. A profile served by the
live default multiplexer has no gateway of its own: ``restart`` targets the multiplexer (the process
that actually serves X — a ``-p X gateway restart`` child only exits 78 into the action log while the
UI reports "restarted"); ``start``/``stop`` are refused by the caller (``multiplexed_profile_refusal``).
The multiplexer is addressed as ``-p default`` explicitly: a bare ``gateway restart`` spawned from a
pooled ``--profile X serve`` would inherit X's ``HERMES_HOME`` and hit the same exit-78 refusal. The
selector is explicit for the default home too: a bare child re-reads the sticky ``active_profile``
and would restart another profile's gateway.

name: _has_own_gateway
doc:
A live gateway of the profile's OWN (a ``--force``-started separate one), not the multiplexer that
serves it. Gateway liveness reports a served profile as running on the multiplexer's PID (#97120),
so reading liveness alone made every served profile look self-hosted and the refusal below never
fired while a multiplexer was live, which is the only time it is needed.

name: multiplexed_profile_refusal
doc:
Refusal text for ``gateway start``/``stop`` on a named profile with no gateway of its own (a
``--force``-started separate one is managed normally), else None. A profile the live host
multiplexer serves is parked by ``stop`` and a parked one is unparked by ``start`` (the spawned
``hermes -p X gateway <verb>`` runs ``gateway_profile_lifecycle``), so neither is refused;
``start`` on an unparked named profile is — one host gateway serves every profile, so a new
per-profile gateway is never the answer (the CLI twin ``_named_profile_refused_under_multiplexer``
exits 78 into an action log nobody reads while the UI shows the verb as done).

name: live_session_refusal
doc:
Refusal text when the gateway ``verb`` would act on has live sessions, else None. Asked before
spawning: the child refuses the same way, but into an action log the UI never reads.

name: _restart_gateway_after
arguments: profile: Optional[str], *, what: str, label: str
doc:
Best-effort gateway restart after a config change. The save stays authoritative: a failed
spawn is reported (``restart_started: False`` + ``restart_error``) so the UI can fall back to
its manual restart banner instead of failing the request. Live sessions refuse it the same way.

name: _split_text_for_speak_stream
doc:
Split *text* into provider-cap-sized pieces on sentence boundaries.

Deliberately NOT unified with gateway.platforms.helpers' split_text_fence_aware: this
reflows whitespace (sentences re-joined with single spaces) and has no fence semantics.

            env=action_env, **detach,

name: wrap_asgi_with_ws_tracking
doc:
Count WebSocket sessions at the ASGI boundary: open on the ``websocket.accept`` send, close
when the scope ends. Handlers stay untouched, so a new WS route is tracked automatically.

name: busy_ledger
doc:
Name the ledger that holds work — ``"retirement_admission"``, ``"session:<id>"``,
``"delegation"``, ``"cron:<job ids>"`` — ``""`` when every ledger is empty, ``None`` when one
cannot be read. The Desktop's idle probe reports this so a backend that will not retire says
WHICH work it is protecting, instead of an opaque "turn in flight".

Session work lives on ``tui_gateway.server`` (the voice mixin's helper is bound into that
namespace). Cron runs live outside that table (``cron.scheduler.get_running_job_ids``, the same
ledger the gateway shutdown drain reads): without it a daily job mid-run reported "no turn" and
the exit killed it (#107485). None keeps the backend alive forever, so the cause is logged once —
a silent never-exits would be the original bug with a new face.

name: turn_in_flight
doc:
Bool view of :func:`busy_ledger`, kept so ``should_exit_idle`` / the idle watchdog and injected
test probes keep their ``Optional[bool]`` contract; None when the ledgers cannot be read.

name: should_exit_idle
arguments: tracker: IdleClientTracker, grace_s: float, probe: Callable[[], Optional[bool]]=turn_in_flight
doc:
Exit only when no client has been connected for ``grace_s`` AND no turn is provably running.
A probe that cannot answer keeps the process (fail closed).

name: start_idle_watchdog
arguments: server, tracker: IdleClientTracker, *, grace_s: float=DEFAULT_IDLE_GRACE_S, poll_s: float=15.0, probe: Callable[[], Optional[bool]]=turn_in_flight
doc: Daemon thread that sets ``server.should_exit`` once :func:`should_exit_idle` holds.

name: pending_human_input
doc:
Count of prompts waiting on a human (clarify/approval/sudo/secret requests plus queued
gateway approvals); ``None`` when a ledger cannot be read.

name: idle_proof
arguments: turn_probe: Callable[[], bool | str | None]=busy_ledger, input_probe: Callable[[], Optional[int]]=pending_human_input
doc:
``{"idle": True | False | None, "reason": str | None}`` plus ``"detail"`` naming the busy ledger.

``True`` only when no turn is in flight (session table AND cron ledger) and nothing is waiting
on a human. ``None`` whenever either probe is indeterminate — the caller treats it exactly like
busy. ``turn_probe`` may answer with a bool or with :func:`busy_ledger`'s name; the name is
surfaced as ``detail`` so a backend that refuses to retire says which work it is protecting.

name: _process_start_marker
doc:
Return a cross-runtime marker for the current incarnation of ``pid``.

``ProcessLookupError`` means the process is absent; other failures stay
distinct so callers fail safe rather than killing a healthy backend.

name: _parent_start_marker_mismatch_is_conclusive
doc:
Whether a marker mismatch proves the Desktop parent was replaced.

``linux:`` jiffies and ``win:``/``winms:`` FILETIME markers are machine
values; a mismatch there is PID-reuse evidence. The POSIX fallback (macOS
has no ``/proc``) is ``ps -o lstart=`` -- a wall-clock string rendered in
the current TZ/locale. Electron caches it once per app lifetime while the
backend re-renders it per spawn, so a timezone change (or DST, or column
padding) makes the SAME instant differ byte-for-byte. Any ``ps:`` mismatch
is therefore inconclusive (#95693, #93958).

name: _parent_start_markers_match
doc:
Compare parent markers across Desktop generations.

Old Windows Desktop sends .NET ticks (``win:``); new builds send Electron's
creation time in Unix ms (``winms:``) to avoid launching PowerShell. The
backend reads the exact FILETIME and normalizes only for ``winms``.

name: _warm_gateway_module
doc:
Pre-import heavy modules so the event loop is not stalled on first use.

Cold Windows installs pay .pyc compilation + Defender scans (15-30s) on
these chains; the first WS RPC burst (setup.status, setup.runtime_check,
gateway.ready→resolve_skin, model.options) pulled them in on the loop
thread (#60800). Warm them all off-loop while the socket is already open.

name: _eager_reconcile_own_session_db
doc:
Bring this process's own state.db schema current at startup — read-only first.

The dashboard is a view layer; the gateway owns the writer. A healthy store
must never see a second writable ``SessionDB`` from this process (its
close-time checkpoint and a possible FTS rebuild in ``_init_fts`` are the
two-writer corruption vector, #107688 / #100896). Access-mode semantics
(no bootstrap of a missing store; one additive catch-up of a store that lags
SCHEMA_SQL, only while no gateway owns it, #79531 / #140315) live in the routers' own-store opener,
:func:`hermes_cli.web_server_sessions._open_session_db_at_path`. Never
raises: an unfixable store still gets the per-poll read-probe heal.

name: _read_bound_port
doc: Read the OS-assigned port from the live uvicorn socket (ephemeral port-0 discovery).

name: _write_dashboard_ready_file
doc:
Publish the port through an atomic ready file when ``HERMES_DESKTOP_READY_FILE`` is set.

Windows Desktop launches via ``pythonw.exe`` (no console flash) cannot use
stdout for the port announcement, so Electron waits for this JSON instead.

name: _maybe_open_browser
arguments: host: str, actual_port: int, open_browser: bool, initial_profile: str
doc:
Open the dashboard URL in the user's browser if appropriate.

Skips headless Linux (no DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY) so a TUI browser can't
SIGHUP the server; maps ``0.0.0.0``/``::`` binds to ``127.0.0.1``.

name: _is_serve_orphaned
arguments: desktop_pid: int, expected_start_marker: Optional[str]=None, *, pid_exists=None, process_start_marker=None
doc:
True when the exact Desktop process that owns this backend is gone.

``HERMES_PARENT_PID`` is the Electron PID, not necessarily our PPID (the
Windows ``hermes.exe`` launcher adds shims), so never compare getppid().
The start marker (newer Desktops) defeats PID recycling; PID-only probing
stays for older ones. Any inconclusive failure keeps serving (fail-safe).

name: _request_orphan_shutdown
doc:
Ask this backend to shut itself down, with a hard-exit backstop.

``os._exit`` here skipped the flush-on-kill handlers this same process
installs before serving (#96095, ``install_exit_flush_signal_handlers``)
and every ``atexit`` hook, so an unclean desktop exit dropped the in-memory
transcripts that a SIGTERM from a live desktop persists to ``state.db``.
Raise SIGTERM instead, and keep the reap guaranteed the way ``cli.py``'s
``_arm_exit_watchdog`` does: a daemon timer that ``os._exit``\ s if the
unwind stalls (it survives ``Py_FinalizeEx``'s non-daemon thread joins).
``raise_signal`` reaches Python's handler on Windows too, where
``os.kill(pid, SIGTERM)`` would terminate the process without running it.

Returns the armed ceiling timer.

name: _start_parent_death_watchdog
doc:
Exit when the exact desktop parent that spawned this backend dies.

Desktop passes its PID and, in newer versions, a start marker (defeats PID
reuse) plus a per-spawn nonce (makes mixed-version plumbing fail safe:
marker without nonce or vice versa disables the watchdog).

name: _is_addr_in_use_error
doc: True when ``exc`` is the platform's address-in-use bind failure.

name: _port_bind_conflict
doc:
Probe whether binding ``host:port`` would fail with EADDRINUSE.

``port == 0`` (ephemeral) never conflicts, so it is skipped. Any probe
error other than address-in-use returns ``False`` so uvicorn surfaces it
with its normal diagnostics (bad host, EACCES, …).

name: _write_machine_sentinel_line
doc:

name: _uvicorn_console_logging
doc:
uvicorn's default console logging, without its ``dictConfig``.

``uvicorn.Config``'s default ``log_config`` runs ``dictConfig``, which calls
``logging.shutdown()`` on every live handler: a multiplexed gateway's profile log routers are
already installed when its listener is built, and a closed router stays closed. The listeners
pass ``log_config=None`` and get uvicorn's handlers here instead: ``uvicorn`` to stderr,
``uvicorn.access`` to stdout, neither propagating into the Hermes log files.

name: build_listener_server
arguments: served_app, host: str, port: int, *, auth_required: bool, ws_ping: Optional[tuple[float, float]]=None, timeout_graceful_shutdown: Optional[float]=3, lifespan: str='auto'
doc:
uvicorn ``Config`` + ``Server`` for a dashboard or gateway-session listener (FastAPI-free, so
the gateway can build its session listener without importing the dashboard app).

WS keepalive ping runs ON the agent event loop; a GIL-holding worker call can starve it for
minutes, so uvicorn misses the pong and drops a healthy local socket (#53773/#48445/#50005).
The ping only detects half-open connections (proxy 524, dropped tunnels), impossible on
loopback where a dead client sends a real FIN/RST -> WebSocketDisconnect. So: no ping on
loopback; non-loopback sits behind a Cloudflare Tunnel (~100s idle) and keeps a config-driven
cadence (dashboard.ws_ping_interval/_timeout, #79635) defaulting to 20/20. *ws_ping* overrides
both (SSH-isolated Desktop backends).

name: _profile_scope
doc:
Scope config + skill-directory resolution to ``profile`` for one request.

Two seams: (1) ``load_config``/``save_config`` resolve ``get_hermes_home()`` at call
time, so the contextvar override reaches them; (2) ``tools.skills_tool`` /
``tools.skill_manager_tool`` bind ``SKILLS_DIR`` at import time, so both are retargeted
under a lock and restored after. For the dashboard's own profile config resolution is
untouched, but the skill-module globals are still retargeted to the *current*
``get_hermes_home()`` so writes land in the live home even when the import-time binding
is stale (test isolation, late HERMES_HOME override). Yields the profile dir for a named
profile, None for the current one.

``tools.skills_sync`` (reset/diff/list-modified/opt-in/opt-out/ repair-official) needs NO retargeting:
since #65828 its directory lookups resolve at call time through the same contextvar override set in step
1.

name: _config_profile_scope
doc:
Await-safe profile scope: the task-local HERMES_HOME contextvar PLUS the profile's secret
scope, never the process-global skills-module attributes ``_profile_scope`` swaps (holding
those across an ``await`` lets a concurrent request restore THIS request's dir on its
``finally``). None/""/"current" = no override.

Home alone left ``get_secret`` on the dashboard process's ``os.environ`` - the DEFAULT
profile's values - so ``GET /api/config?profile=B`` expanded B's ``${VAR}`` refs to the default
profile's plaintext credentials and ``load_gateway_config()`` under B's home bridged B's YAML
settings into the shared process env (``yaml_env_setter`` skips only under a secret scope).
A request for another profile's home also flips this process to fail-closed multi-profile
hosting (``tui_gateway/launch_profile_policy.py``), so any remaining unscoped read raises
instead of borrowing; the dashboard's own profile then runs under its frozen-launch-env scope.

Explicit names resolving to the process home retain current-profile semantics.
Still enter the requested home so a nested scope cannot retain another profile.
None/""/"current" mean the request's EFFECTIVE home: a task-local override (a secondary
profile's native ticket, ``native_profile_scope``) is that profile, so it gets that profile's
secret scope rather than the launch profile's.

See #23270.

db._conn.execute("""
            SELECT u.model,
                   u.task,
                   u.billing_provider,
                   SUM(u.input_tokens) as input_tokens,
                   SUM(u.output_tokens) as output_tokens,
                   SUM(u.cache_read_tokens) as cache_read_tokens,
                   SUM(u.reasoning_tokens) as reasoning_tokens,
                   COALESCE(SUM(u.estimated_cost_usd), 0) as estimated_cost,
                   COUNT(DISTINCT u.session_id) as sessions,
                   SUM(COALESCE(u.api_call_count, 0)) as api_calls,
                   MAX(u.last_seen) as last_used_at
            FROM session_model_usage u
            JOIN sessions s ON s.id = u.session_id
            WHERE s.started_at > ? AND u.task != ''
            GROUP BY u.model, u.task, u.billing_provider
            ORDER BY SUM(u.input_tokens) + SUM(u.output_tokens) DESC
        """, (cutoff,))

name: _mutate_via_gateway_owner
doc:
Forward a standalone dashboard mutation to the live gateway owner.

While a gateway serves the same home, a separately launched ``hermes
dashboard`` is not the store owner, so the offline path's
exclusive-maintenance reservation can never win and every write action
dies on a bare 409 (#138915). The owner exposes the same revision-fenced
verb over the control socket; with no discoverable owner return None so the
caller falls back to the offline store.

A dial, mint or RPC that dies on an endpoint discovery just identified is
not owner-less (a slow first dial, or an owner restart between discovery
and mint): the offline reservation would only lose to that same owner and
answer with the bare 409 this forward exists to remove, so every transport
failure surfaces a retryable 503. Only the owner's refusal frame
(``GatewayRPCError``) is passed on as a verdict.

The ticket is minted for the dashboard's authenticated principal, not the
socket UID: ``authorize_history`` compares the actor subject against the
row's stored owner, so a cold row owned by a dashboard account only takes
the mutation when the forward acts as that account.

configured provider. One walk of the provider ladder answers both halves.

name: claim_blocker
doc:
Why the trial cannot be claimed here, or None when it can. *assume_fresh* is the unpackaged
desktop's ``--fresh-install`` switch: it skips only the machine check. *configured* is a
``provider_configured()`` answer the caller already has, so the ladder is not walked twice.

name: claim_desktop_free_tier
doc:
Claim the trial when nothing blocks it: mint the guest, stamp the claim, mark the machine.
Returns the claimed state, or None when the trial is not available here. A failed mint raises
the coded ``AuthError`` from :func:`anon_auth.ensure_portal_identity` (memoised with its cooldown;
*force* is the user's own retry). Held under the OS user's claim lock from the checks to the
marker write, so two installs starting together claim once.

name: settle_interrupted_claim
doc:
A claim cut off between its guest write and its marker write leaves the reservation behind.
The stamped guest is the claim, so the reservation goes: kept, it would let a second trial through
once that guest is reaped or deleted. Runs before every claim and at serve boot; True when it did.

name: _win32
doc:
Namespace of the pywin32 modules (ntsecuritycon, pywintypes, win32api, win32con, win32file,
win32security); import is deferred so the module imports on non-Windows hosts.

name: _check
arguments: pattern: re.Pattern, value: str, message: str

name: _open
arguments: path: Path, access: int, creation: int, flags: int, share: int=0

name: _open_existing
arguments: path: Path, access: int, extra_flags: int=0, share: int=0
doc: ``_open`` an existing file (FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL | reparse guard); None when it is missing.

name: _read_shared
arguments: path: Path, limit: int, share: int
doc: Read up to ``limit`` bytes of ``path`` opened read-only with ``share``; None when missing.

name: _write_new
arguments: path: Path, data: bytes, share: int=0
doc: Create ``path`` (CREATE_NEW), write ``data`` and flush.

name: write_private_file
doc:
Create/replace ``path`` with an owner+SYSTEM-only protected DACL (Windows only).

The repo's writer for any credential landing on a Windows disk: ``os.open(..., 0o600)`` sets
no ACLs there at all, so a token written that way inherits whatever the parent directory
grants. CreateFile ignores the security descriptor when the file already exists, so an
existing file is removed first rather than re-opened — which also avoids ``os.replace``
failing against a reader that still holds the old file open.

name: upload_token
arguments: ownership_id: str, spawn_nonce: str, token: bytes

name: process_state
arguments: pid: int, creation_time_ns: int, hermes_path: str, spawn_nonce: str

name: terminate_owned
arguments: pid: int, creation_time_ns: int, hermes_path: str, spawn_nonce: str

name: _resolve_direct_command
doc:
Ask the configured installation for its direct, boot-selecting command.

The port owner must be the process we lock, not a console-launcher child.
No assumption about python.exe beside an external bin launcher is valid.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=log_stream, stderr=log_stream,
                                   close_fds=True, creationflags=0x00000008 | 0x00000200 | 0x01000000, env=env)

name: perform
doc: Use the same update objects for the query and the requested operation.

name: _wait
doc: Keep the STA responsive while Store displays consent and progress UI.

name: spawn
arguments: cls, argv: Sequence[str], *, cwd: Optional[str]=None, env: Optional[dict]=None, cols: int=80, rows: int=24

name: read
doc: Up to 64 KiB of child output.

name: write
doc:
Write off-loop and tear down ConPTY when its input pipe wedges.

``wait_for(to_thread(...))`` alone only cancels the asyncio wrapper;
the worker remains blocked inside pywinpty. Keep the worker future,
force-close the ConPTY on timeout, and wait briefly for that close to
release the blocked write before returning.

Cancellation (the owning socket went away mid-write) is not evidence
of a wedged child: the PTY outlives its socket by design, so give the
in-flight write the grace window and only terminate if it never lands.

name: _settle_or_stop_write
doc: Let a cancelled write finish within the grace window; terminate only if it stalls.

name: _stop_stalled_write
doc: Close ConPTY and reap the worker that was blocked in ``write``.

name: _run
arguments: args, cwd, env, timeout: float=300, stdin_text: Optional[str]=None

name: _raw_attrs
doc:
Run a content-converting command with attributes read from the empty tree (git >= 2.40);
older git lacks ``--attr-source`` and falls back to the checkout's own attributes.

name: _run_bytes
arguments: args, cwd, env, data: bytes, timeout: float=300

name: _regular_entries
doc: ``(mode, sha, path)`` for every regular-file entry of the index ``env`` points at.

name: _rehash_raw
doc:
Replace every regular-file blob in the temporary index with the file's exact bytes.

``add`` runs content conversion from every attribute source, and ``--attr-source`` only
replaces ``.gitattributes``: ``info/attributes`` and ``core.attributesFile`` still apply.
``hash-object --no-filters`` skips all of it.

name: _write_raw
doc: Overwrite every regular file of the index with its blob's exact bytes (no smudge/eol).

name: ref_safe
doc: A tree name as a single valid ref component.

name: submodule_work
doc:
Why a submodule keeps *wt_path*, or None. Read-only.

An archive records a submodule only as its ``160000`` gitlink, and removing the tree deletes
its per-worktree ``modules/`` repositories (kept by ``git submodule deinit``, private branches
included). Until submodules are archived recursively: no tree with a gitlink is archived
(*gitlinks*), and no tree whose ``modules/`` holds a repository or whose gitlink is checked out
is removed at all.

name: staged_state
doc:
Digest of the semantic staged entries (mode, blob id, stage, path) of *wt_path*.

A stat-only index refresh (``git status``) leaves it unchanged; any ``git add``/``apply
--cached``/``rm --cached`` changes it. Raises :class:`ArchiveError` when git fails.

name: archive_preflight
doc:
``(keep-action, reason)`` when archiving and removing *wt_path* would lose something
(``worktree_retention.removal_blocker``: submodule, embedded repository, per-worktree ref,
an untracked file over the size cap), else None. Read-only.

name: _split_oversized
arguments: wt: Path, untracked: list[str], max_mb: float

name: _create_ref
arguments: repo_root: str, name: str, sha: str, env

name: snapshot_worktree
arguments: repo_root: str, wt_path, *, reason: str, max_untracked_mb: float=50
doc:
Archive the full working state of *wt_path*; raises :class:`ArchiveError` on any failure.

Never writes the tree's real index or working files (temporary ``GIT_INDEX_FILE`` only).

name: list_archives
doc: Every archive in *repo_root*, newest first. Read-only; [] when git fails.

name: find_archive
doc: Exact archive name/ref first, else the newest archive of the tree called *name*.

name: prune_expired_archives
arguments: repo_root: str, retention_days: float, *, now: Optional[float]=None, dry_run: bool=False
doc: Delete archive refs older than *retention_days* (0 keeps them forever).

name: _add_args
arguments: repo_root: str, dest: Path, branch: Optional[str], head: str, env
doc: ``worktree add`` argv restoring *branch* when that is safe -> (argv, detached).

name: restore_archive
doc: Recreate the archived tree at its original path (or *target*); raises ArchiveError.

name: _sweep
arguments: repo_root: str, dry_run: bool, older_than: Optional[float]=None
doc:
The automatic sweep's plan for this repo (applied unless *dry_run*) -> (plan, actions).
*older_than* (days) bounds what the plan may archive or remove before anything runs.

name: _attended_records
doc:
The attended reclaim's records minus trees the sweep already decided (archived, removed,
kanban) and minus any tree a live process works in: those are never touched here either.

name: worktree_state
doc: ``"dirty"``, ``"unpushed"`` or None (clean and pushed / gone).

name: _still_in_use
doc:
Whether a live process (other than this one) still works in *path* after a short grace:
the TUI's own backend (``tui_gateway``) takes a moment to exit after the Ink UI closes.

name: ask_exit_choice
doc: Ask what to do with a dirty/unpushed tree; records the answer in ``info["exit_choice"]``.

name: apply_exit_choice
doc:
Carry out an Archive/Discard answer once -> True when the tree was handled (removed or a
message printed). Keep (or no answer) -> False: the caller's default keep path runs.

name: _run
arguments: cmd: list, timeout: int, cwd: Optional[str]=None, env: Optional[dict]=None

name: _git
arguments: args: list, cwd: str, timeout: int=15
doc:
Run git, translating timeouts into returncode 124. Every verdict fails safe toward "keep"
on nonzero, so a slow ``git cherry`` on a huge repo degrades to keep instead of aborting the
audit mid-list. :func:`noninteractive_repo_git_env` because ``status`` executes the repo's
``core.fsmonitor`` and clean filters (GHSA-7x36-8jrh-v4pw).

name: _tree_size_mb
doc: Cheap directory size via ``du -sm`` — best-effort, None on failure.

name: _dirty_split
doc: (has_tracked_modifications, untracked_paths) — tracked = real work, untracked = archivable.

name: _archive_untracked
doc: Copy untracked files out of a doomed tree; None on any failure (caller must then keep).

name: _classify_tree
arguments: _ops, repo_root: str, entry: Path, merge_cache, remote_heads
doc: Return (verdict, reason, untracked) for one tree under ``.worktrees/``.

name: audit_external_trees
doc:
List linked worktrees registered OUTSIDE ``.worktrees/``.

``hermes -w`` scratch trees all live under ``<repo>/.worktrees/``, but
``git worktree list --porcelain`` also knows about trees the user (or
another tool) registered elsewhere. Those are someone else's state, so
the reclaim paths never touch them — but hiding them entirely makes the
audit lie about what the repo is carrying. Report them read-only, and
flag registrations whose directory has vanished (safe to
``git worktree prune``).

name: prune_missing_registrations
doc:
Drop registrations whose directory no longer exists (any location).

The equivalent of a targeted ``git worktree prune``: purely
metadata-level, never removes files, so it is safe even for external
trees — a missing directory means there is nothing left to protect.

name: audit_worktrees
arguments: repo_root: str, *, with_sizes: bool=True, older_than_days: Optional[float]=None
doc:
Classify every tree under ``.worktrees/`` without mutating anything.

``older_than_days`` only ever RESTRICTS: a reapable tree younger than the threshold is kept
("too recent"). It never widens eligibility — age alone can't doom a tree carrying unmerged work.

name: reclaim_worktrees
arguments: repo_root: str, *, dry_run: bool=False, records: Optional[list[TreeRecord]]=None
doc:
Remove every reap-verdict tree from a frozen audit list — never re-globs inside the
destructive loop, so trees created by concurrent sessions after the audit are out of scope.

name: audit_branches
doc:
Classify EVERY local branch: deletable when fully merged OR every commit is patch-equivalent
upstream (``git cherry``) and not checked out. The gate is content reachability, not name.

name: reclaim_branches
arguments: repo_root: str, *, dry_run: bool=False, records: Optional[list[BranchRecord]]=None
doc: Delete every delete-verdict branch from a frozen audit list.

name: worktrees_summary
doc: (tree_count, total_size_mb) for the escalation notice; size is best-effort with a timeout.

name: _git
doc: Run ``git *args`` in *cwd* capturing UTF-8 text; raises like ``subprocess.run``.

name: _git_out
doc: ``_git`` returning stripped stdout, or None on a non-zero exit. Raises like ``_git``.

name: _git_quiet
arguments: args, cwd, timeout: float=10, log: str | None=None, **kwargs
doc: Fail-soft ``_git``: swallow every error, optionally logging it at DEBUG with *log* as prefix.

name: _normalize_git_bash_path
doc: Translate a Git Bash path (``/c/..``, ``/cygdrive/c/..``, ``/mnt/c/..``) to ``C:\..`` on Windows.

name: _git_repo_root
doc: Return the git repo root for CWD (Git-Bash-normalized), or None if not in a repo.

name: _path_is_within_root
doc: Return True when a resolved path stays within the expected root.

name: release_lsp_clients
doc:
Shut down this process's language servers for ``wt_path`` before ``git worktree remove``.

A gateway outlives the sessions it runs, so without this the ``(server, root)`` client for the
removed tree stays registered (tsserver heaps of several GiB pointed at a deleted worktree).
Best-effort: LSP trouble must never block worktree removal.

name: _cleanup_failed_worktree_add
arguments: repo_root: str, wt_path: Path, branch_name: str
doc:
Sweep the leftovers of a failed/timed-out ``git worktree add`` (fail-soft).

``worktree add`` is not transactional: killed mid-checkout it leaves the partial dir, a
LOCKED admin entry naming the *live* pid (immune to the pruner's dead-pid unlock) and
sometimes the branch, so any retry of the same name fails.

name: _claim_repack_slot
doc:
Exactly one process per clone gets to repack per ``_REPACK_MIN_INTERVAL``.

The lock file's mtime is the stamp: younger than the interval means another launch is
repacking (or just tried and timed out) — skip. A stale lock is taken over by ``replace``,
which only one of N racing processes can win; the O_EXCL create then serializes against a
process that found no lock at all.

name: _run_bounded_repack
doc:
Incremental geometric repack whose whole process tree dies with the timeout or with us.

``repack`` forks ``pack-objects``; ``subprocess.run(timeout=)`` killed only the parent and
left the grandchild packing for days, and a daemon thread's child outlived the CLI the same
way. A new session/process group + ``atexit`` reaps both cases.

name: _maintain_pack_health
doc:
Repack the object store when pack files sprawl (background thread, fail-soft).

``gc --auto`` only fires at 50 packs; past a few dozen, every object lookup scans every
pack index and worktree creation can blow its timeout under concurrent load.

name: _resolve_worktree_base
arguments: repo_root: str, fetch_timeout: float=5, freshness_window: float=300
doc:
Resolve the freshest base ref to branch a new worktree from -> ``(base_ref, banner_label)``.

Local ``HEAD`` can lag the remote by hundreds of commits, so try in order: (1) the current
branch's upstream, refreshed; (2) the remote default branch (``origin/HEAD``), refreshed;
(3) local ``HEAD``. The fetch is skipped when ``FETCH_HEAD`` is younger than
*freshness_window* s, capped at *fetch_timeout*, and never retried: on failure the cached
remote-tracking ref is used (the pre-push stale-base gate backstops genuine staleness).

name: _ensure_worktrees_gitignored
doc: Append ``.worktrees/`` to the repo's .gitignore when missing (fail-soft).

name: _worktreeinclude_entries
doc:
Non-blank, non-comment entries of *repo_root*/``.worktreeinclude`` (``[]`` when absent).

utf-8-sig, not the locale default: a cp1251/GBK locale would mojibake or raise on a UTF-8
list, and a Notepad BOM would glue to the first entry.

name: _copy_worktree_includes
doc: Copy/symlink the entries listed in ``.worktreeinclude`` (gitignored files the agent needs).

name: _worktree_add
arguments: repo_root: str, wt_path: Path, branch_name: str, base_ref: str, base_label: str
doc:
``git worktree add`` with a local-HEAD retry -> ``(base_ref, base_label)``, or None on failure.

Every failed attempt is swept with ``_cleanup_failed_worktree_add`` so the retry is not poisoned.

name: _setup_worktree
arguments: repo_root: str | None=None, sync_base: bool=True, name: Optional[str]=None, retain_db=None
doc:
Create an isolated git worktree -> ``{path, branch, repo_root, base}``, or None on failure.

*sync_base* branches from the fetched remote tip (``_resolve_worktree_base``), else local
HEAD. *name* replaces the random ``hermes-<id>``; named trees lack the ``hermes-`` prefix so
the pruner ages them on its slower schedule. *retain_db* (``-w``, ``--tui -w``) records the tree
for resume and names the profile store in the lock. A ``--tui -w`` tree outlives its launcher
while a session there can resume in it; a classic ``-w`` row's cwd is the repo root, so its
reaped clean tree is recreated on resume instead.

Set ``worktree_sync: false`` in config to branch from local ``HEAD`` (the pre-#10760-followup behavior).

name: _worktree_local_trunk
doc:
Local trunk of a repo with NO remote-tracking refs: ``main``/``master``, else the branch
checked out in the main worktree. None = no baseline at all; callers must preserve.

Nothing in such a repo was ever pushed, so "merged into the local trunk" is the only fact
that can tell redundant scratch work from unique commits. May raise like ``_git``.

name: _worktree_merge_base_ref
doc:
Ref merged work is judged against: ``origin/HEAD``/``origin/main``/``origin/master``, or the
local trunk when the repo has no remote-tracking refs at all. None = nothing to compare
against -> every consumer must preserve. May raise like ``_git``.

name: _worktree_has_unpushed_commits
doc:
Whether a worktree has commits unreachable from any remote branch. Fails SAFE toward True.

No remote-tracking refs = nothing was ever pushed, so the tree is compared against the local
trunk instead (``_worktree_local_trunk``); no trunk either -> True. A shallow boundary can
disconnect an older HEAD from origin/* so public commits look unpushed;
``_deepen_shallow_repo`` first if affordable.

name: _include_symlink_paths
doc:
Relative paths in *worktree_path* that are ``.worktreeinclude`` directory symlinks.

``_copy_worktree_includes`` symlinks included directories back to the main checkout
(*repo_root*). A trailing-slash gitignore pattern
(``node_modules/``) never matches a symlink, so git reports each one as untracked. Only a
symlink at a listed entry that resolves to that same entry in the main repo qualifies —
anything else is real user state.

name: _worktree_is_dirty
doc:
Whether a worktree has staged/unstaged/untracked changes. Fails SAFE toward True.

Untracked ``.worktreeinclude`` directory symlinks back to the main checkout *repo_root* are
ignored: they are our own scaffolding, and counting them would keep every worktree of such a
repo forever. ``status.showUntrackedFiles=no`` is overridden (it would hide new files), and
skip-worktree / assume-unchanged files whose bytes differ from the index count as changes
(``git status`` trusts both flags).

name: _repo_is_shallow
doc:
Whether *repo_path* is a shallow clone (installer default). Fails toward False on unknown state.

Shallowness poisons connectivity verdicts: an old worktree HEAD misreports as unpushed forever.

name: _deepen_shallow_repo
doc:
Blobless unshallow so history verdicts are correct -> whether the repo is non-shallow afterwards.

Falls back to a plain ``--unshallow`` if the server rejects filters. Background paths only.

name: _worktree_merge_cache_path
doc: Path of the patch-equivalence verdict cache (profile-aware).

name: _load_worktree_merge_cache
doc: Load the ``git cherry`` verdict cache. Missing/corrupt cache = empty.

name: _save_worktree_merge_cache
doc: Atomically persist the newest ``_WORKTREE_MERGE_CACHE_MAX`` verdicts. Never raises.

name: _worktree_commits_all_merged_upstream
arguments: worktree_path: str, timeout: int=30, max_ahead: int=20, cache: Optional[dict[str, bool]]=None
doc:
Whether every local-only commit is patch-equivalent (``git cherry``) to upstream. Fails SAFE -> False.

Catches squash-merged/cherry-picked PRs whose remote branch was deleted (commits unreachable
from ``refs/remotes/*`` forever). Upstream is ``_worktree_merge_base_ref`` (the local trunk in
a repo without remotes). More than *max_ahead* ahead = stale-base tree -> False.
*cache* memoizes on ``(base_sha, head_sha, max_ahead)``, exactly what ``git cherry`` consumes.

name: _worktree_current_branch
doc: Checked-out branch name, or None when detached/git fails. May raise on subprocess errors.

name: _worktree_branch_pr_merged
arguments: worktree_path: str, timeout: int=15, cache: Optional[dict[str, bool]]=None
doc:
Whether the branch's PR is MERGED on GitHub (``gh pr list``). Fails SAFE toward False.

Catches rebase-merges whose altered diff defeats ``git cherry``. Memoized on
``(branch, head_sha)``; only True is cached since the PR may merge later without new commits.

name: _fetch_remote_branch_heads
doc:
``{branch: sha}`` for every branch on origin (one ``ls-remote``), or None = cannot verify, preserve.

Managed installs fetch a single-branch refspec, so pushed PR branches have no
remote-tracking ref and would read as unpushed forever.

name: _worktree_branch_pushed_exact
arguments: worktree_path: str, remote_heads: Optional[dict[str, str]], timeout: int=10
doc:
Whether the branch head is EXACTLY what origin holds (tree redundant; reap it, keep the branch).

Equality is deliberately the only True case: ahead/diverged heads have commits origin lacks
and ancestry can't be proven cheaply without remote-tracking refs -> fail SAFE toward preserve.

name: _retain_worktree_for_session
arguments: repo_root: str, worktree_path: str, session_id: str, db_path
doc:
Re-lock a ``--tui -w`` tree its exiting launcher retains, naming the session that uses it.

The tree stays live while any resumable session of that store works inside it
(``_retained_tree_is_live``), not only the named one: ``/new`` leaves the older session's
history in the same checkout.

name: _inside_tree
doc:
``inside(path) -> 0/1``: *path* is the tree or under it (native path identity: Windows is
case-insensitive, either separator; the tree's own spelling and its resolved one).

name: _tree_still_served
doc:
Why the gateway still needs a ``--tui -w`` tree the launcher is about to remove, or None.

Beyond pending admissions (``_retained_tree_is_live(pending_only=True)``): scheduled work for a
session inside it (an active loop, heartbeat or goal continuation), another viewer still holding
such a session (its row was not ended by the quit), or an enabled cron job that runs in the tree
(``workdir``) or is bound to such a session's local chat. Reads only; unreadable fails SAFE.

significant_calls.expression:
conn.execute(
                    "SELECT chat_id FROM sessions WHERE hermes_inside_tree(cwd) AND chat_id IS NOT NULL")

name: _cron_bound_to_tree
_retained_tree_is_live
arguments: db_path: str, worktree_path: str, *, pending_only: bool=False
doc:
Whether a session that can still be resumed has its frozen cwd inside the retained tree:
a row with history or pending gateway work (*pending_only*: pending work alone, the exiting
``--tui -w`` launcher's "is the gateway still using it" check). A missing store means the
profile is gone; unreadable fails SAFE (live).

significant_calls.callee:
conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM sessions s WHERE hermes_inside_tree(s.cwd) AND ("
                + ("" if pending_only else "s.message_count>0 OR ")
                + "EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM session_admissions a WHERE a.target_session_id=s.id "
                "AND a.status!='terminal')) LIMIT 1").fetchone
significant_calls.expression:
conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM sessions s WHERE hermes_inside_tree(s.cwd) AND ("
                + ("" if pending_only else "s.message_count>0 OR ")
                + "EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM session_admissions a WHERE a.target_session_id=s.id "
                "AND a.status!='terminal')) LIMIT 1").fetchone()

conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM sessions s WHERE hermes_inside_tree(s.cwd) AND ("
                + ("" if pending_only else "s.message_count>0 OR ")
                + "EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM session_admissions a WHERE a.target_session_id=s.id "
                "AND a.status!='terminal')) LIMIT 1")

name: _worktree_lock_reason
arguments: repo_root: str, worktree_path: str, timeout: int
doc:
``(found, reason)`` from the tree's admin dir (``gitdir:`` of its ``.git`` file, under
``<common-dir>/worktrees/``); reason is ``None`` when unlocked and ``""`` for a bare lock.
Read raw and trimmed, as git does: ``list --porcelain -z`` needs git 2.36. Raises when git
or the admin dir cannot be read.

name: _worktree_lock_is_live
arguments: repo_root: str, worktree_path: str, timeout: int=10
doc:
Lock state: ``"live"`` (owning pid runs / a resumable session works in the tree),
``"dead"`` (pid and sessions gone / non-hermes reason), None (unlocked).

A Hermes tree locks with reason ``hermes pid=<pid>``; ``worktree remove --force`` refuses
locked trees, so a crashed session's lock would keep its tree forever. A ``-w`` tree
also names its profile's ``state.db`` from creation, so a ``--tui -w`` launcher killed with
its terminal (SIGHUP skips the exit re-lock) still keeps the tree while a resumable session's
row cwd is inside it. A classic ``-w`` row's cwd is the repo root: its tree is only recorded,
and a reaped clean one is recreated on resume. Fails SAFE toward "live", including a
``hermes`` reason this version cannot parse.

name: prune_tier_hours
doc:
Idle hours before a tree may be reclaimed: *max_age_hours* for Hermes-made trees
(``hermes-*``, ``subagent-*``), 3x for deliberately named ones.

name: _prune_candidates
arguments: worktrees_dir: Path, max_age_hours: int, now: float
doc:
Phase 1, stat-only age filter -> ``[(entry, mtime, force)]`` for trees past their soft cutoff.

Kanban trees (``t_<hex>``) belong to the kanban gc. Hermes-made trees age on *max_age_hours*,
deliberately named trees at 3x (``prune_tier_hours``); *force* marks the hard (3x) tier.

name: _classify_prune_candidates
doc:
Phase 2, parallel read-only classification -> ``[(entry, mtime, force, verdict, lock_state)]``.

verdict in ``dirty`` / ``unpushed`` / ``locked-live`` / ``reap`` / ``reap-keep-branch``. Each
check is a read-only query on a distinct worktree (no repo-wide lock), so a bounded pool is
safe; mutation stays serial. ``git cherry`` verdicts are memoized on disk.

name: removal_blocked
doc:
``(keep-action, reason)`` when deleting the clean tree at *path* would lose something no
branch holds (``worktree_retention.removal_blocker``: a checked-out submodule, an embedded
repository, a per-worktree ref); unverifiable counts as blocked.

name: _reap_prune_verdicts
arguments: repo_root: str, verdicts: list, stale_work_cutoff: float
doc:
Phase 3, serial unlock / remove / branch -D -> ``(preserved_stale, kept_branches)``.

*kept_branches* must survive the orphaned-branch pass. Branch deletion is gated on
``worktree remove`` succeeding so a failed removal never orphans reachable commits.

name: _prune_stale_worktrees
doc:
Remove stale worktrees and orphaned branches on startup.

Default (``worktrees.archive_dirty: true``): ``worktree_sweep.run_sweep`` — an idle dirty or
unpushed tree past its tier is archived to ``refs/hermes/archive/<tree>`` and then removed;
live trees (lock owner or any process inside) and Kanban trees are never touched.
``archive_dirty: false`` (no size budget) runs the classic pass below: dirty trees are never
removed; unpushed commits are never removed UNLESS patch-equivalent to upstream, the PR is
MERGED on GitHub, or the head EXACTLY matches origin (tree reaped, branch kept). Live-locked
trees are skipped; dead locks are unlocked first. Phases: ``_prune_candidates`` ->
``_classify_prune_candidates`` -> ``_reap_prune_verdicts`` -> ``_prune_orphaned_branches``.

name: _reclaim_orphan_install_states
doc:
Trees removed by any path (the prune pass, `git worktree remove` by hand, `rm -rf` of a
scratch clone) leave their ~200 MB dependency state under <home>/installs/; reclaim it on
every pass, including the early returns where no tree is old enough to prune. Startup
maintenance must never block a launch; the traceback goes to the debug log.

name: _warn_worktree_footprint
doc: The startup pass can leave trees it may not reclaim; say so once per launch.

name: _prune_orphaned_branches
doc: Delete local ``hermes/hermes-*`` and ``pr-*`` branches with no worktree, except *protect*.

name: _refresh
arguments: remote: str, branch: str, ref: str
doc: (ref, label) after one best-effort fetch; never raises.

name: registered_repos
doc: Registered repo roots that still exist (read-only; never creates the file).

name: record_worktree_repo
doc: Remember *repo_root* as a repo with Hermes-made worktrees. Never raises.

name: _git
arguments: args, wt: Path, env, timeout: float=120

name: _walk
doc: Below ignored *rel_dir*: record nested ``.git`` entries. Symlinks are not followed.

name: _ignored_entries
scan_tree
doc:
Embedded repositories of *wt_path*, ignored or not. Read-only.

Untracked non-ignored repositories are reported by ``ls-files`` itself (``dir/``); ignored
ones hide inside collapsed ignored directories, so those are walked (bounded; dependency
stores are never descended). Raises ``ArchiveError`` when git fails.

name: hidden_index_edits
doc:
Skip-worktree / assume-unchanged paths whose disk state differs from the index.

``git status`` trusts both flags and reports nothing. A skip-worktree file missing from disk
is a sparse checkout, not an edit; a missing assume-unchanged file is a deletion. Raises
``ArchiveError`` when git fails.

name: _hash
arguments: wt: Path, env, data: bytes, rel: str, *, raw: bool

name: private_worktree_refs
doc:
Per-worktree refs of *wt_path* holding commits no branch, tag, remote or archive reaches.

They live in the tree's admin dir and vanish with it. Raises ``ArchiveError`` when git fails.

name: removal_blocker
doc:
``(keep-action, reason)`` when removing *wt_path* would lose something, else None.

*skipped* is the snapshot's ``skipped_untracked`` list (or the oversize files a preflight
would skip). *gitlinks* refuses any submodule (archive paths); without it only a checked-out
or retained module repository blocks. Any failure to verify blocks. Read-only.

name: sweep_settings
doc: ``worktrees.*`` from the active profile's config (defaults on any read failure).

name: classic_mode
doc: True when the sweep must behave exactly like the pre-archive pruner.

name: live_process_pids
_last_activity
doc:
Newest mtime among the tree's HEAD/reflog, every changed or untracked file, and the
directory holding each changed path.

The tree dir's own mtime only moves when a top-level entry is created or removed, so a lane
editing files deep inside for days still looks idle by it. A deleted file has no mtime; its
nearest surviving parent directory was stamped by the unlink. The index is not a signal:
the classifier's own ``git status`` may rewrite it. ``GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`` keeps this probe from refreshing (and re-stamping) the index.

name: _plan_survivor
arguments: repo_root: str, entry: Path, verdict: str, lock_state, settings: dict, tier_hours: float, now: float
doc: (action, reason, lock_state, last_activity) for a dirty/unpushed tree past its tier.

name: _apply_budget
arguments: decisions: list[Decision], max_total_gb: float, max_file_mb: float=50
doc:
Evict the oldest idle kept trees (archive first) until they fit *max_total_gb*.

Only idle past-tier trees count or move; live, young and kanban trees are invisible here.

name: plan_sweep
arguments: repo_root: str, max_age_hours: int=24, settings: Optional[dict]=None, now: Optional[float]=None, older_than_days: Optional[float]=None
doc:
Read-only decision for every tree under ``<repo>/.worktrees`` (kanban/young included).

*older_than_days* (``hermes worktree prune --older-than``) only restricts: a tree idle for
less than that is never archived or removed, whatever its tier.

name: _branch_published
arguments: repo_root: str, branch: str, remote_heads: Optional[dict]
doc:
Whether *branch* exists on a remote. Unknown (``ls-remote`` failed) counts as published:
deleting a branch is never needed for safety, so doubt keeps it.

name: _in_use_since
doc:
Why *path* must not be removed now: a live process works in it, or a file/ref in it
changed at or after *since*. None = still idle.

name: _index_moved
doc:
Why the staged state of *path* no longer matches the archive (``git add``/``apply
--cached`` after the capture: the index is not a file-mtime signal), or None. A stat-only
refresh by ``git status`` does not count. Unreadable index = moved (keep the tree).

name: archive_then_remove
arguments: repo_root: str, path: str, *, reason: str, max_untracked_mb: float, unlock: bool, remote_heads_fn=None, keep_branch: bool=False, exclude_pids=()
doc:
Snapshot *path*, then remove it -> ``(archive_ref, kept_branch, removed, why_kept)``.

Raises ``ArchiveError`` (tree untouched) when the snapshot fails. Right after the snapshot the
tree is checked again: a process (other than *exclude_pids*) now working in it, any edit
made while the snapshot ran, staged entries that differ from the captured index, or anything
the archive does not hold (``worktree_retention.removal_blocker``: a file the snapshot skipped
for size, an embedded repository, a per-worktree ref, a submodule) keep the tree (``removed`` False, *why_kept* says why; the archive stays). The branch
survives when it is protected or published on a remote (an open PR may still need it);
otherwise the archive ref anchors its commits and the local branch is deleted.

name: _recheck
doc:
Fresh gate for ONE planned tree, run immediately before it is touched -> (why_keep,
lock_state). Earlier trees in the batch can take minutes to archive; a user may have entered
this one meanwhile.

name: execute_plan
arguments: repo_root: str, plan: list[Decision], settings: dict
doc:
Apply a frozen plan -> ``(preserved_stale, kept_branches, [(archive_ref, removed, why_kept)])``.
Each tree is re-gated (lock, live process, fresh activity) right before it is archived or
removed; ``removed`` is False when the archive was saved but the tree was kept (*why_kept*).

name: run_sweep
arguments: repo_root: str, max_age_hours: int, settings: dict
doc: Plan + execute + archive retention for one repo (the archive-mode pruner).

name: handle_pending_subcommand
arguments: subsystem: str, args: list[str], *, memory_store=None, set_mode_fn=None
doc:
Dispatch a /memory or /skills write-approval subcommand.

``memory_store`` applies approved memory writes (CLI passes its live store; gateway a freshly
loaded one); ``set_mode_fn`` persists the write_approval boolean. Returns text for the user,
or None when the args are not a write-approval subcommand so the caller falls through to its
other handling (e.g. /skills search).

name: _changed_entries
doc: Full text of every entry a memory write changed, single-op or batch shape.

name: _matched_entries
doc:
The full entry each staged memory replace/remove is pinned to: the summary shows only
the old_text search string, and approval applies to this entry, not to that search.

name: _apply_one
doc: ``(ok, error, result)`` — *result* is the applier's full payload (empty on exceptions).

name: _set_approval
doc: Turn the approval gate on/off for a subsystem.

name: _normalize
doc: Strip provider prefix (``x-ai/grok-4`` → ``grok-4``) and lowercase.

name: find_retired_xai_refs
doc:
Walk all model slots in a Hermes config and return retirement issues.

Slots scanned: ``principal.model``, ``auxiliary.<any>.model`` (introspective, covers future
aux slots), ``delegation.model``, ``tts.xai.model``, ``plugins.image_gen.xai.model``.

name: format_issue
doc: One-line human-readable rendering of a retirement issue.

name: _walk_to_parent
doc: Resolve a dotted slot path to (parent_mapping, leaf_key).

name: apply_migration
arguments: config_path: Path, issues: list[RetirementIssue], backup: bool=True
doc:
Rewrite ``config_path`` in place (ruamel round-trip: comments, order, type literals kept).

Unless ``backup=False`` a copy goes to ``backups/config/`` (reason ``pre-migrate-xai``).

name: restore_quarantined_shims
arguments: moved: list[tuple[Path, Path]], *, stream=None, backoff_ms: tuple[int, ...]=QUARANTINE_RESTORE_BACKOFF_MS
doc:
Rename quarantined shims back, retrying a lock instead of giving up.

A pair is not a failure when ``original`` already exists or ``quarantined`` has gone: the
installer wrote a fresh shim, or a concurrent sweep won the race. Both are silent, so two
processes sweeping the same orphan cannot produce a spurious error.

name: _should_skip_external_secret_sources
doc:
True inside any ``hermes update`` process (and its import probes).

Every dotenv load in the process — ``hermes_cli.main``, ``run_agent``, ``cli`` — consults
this, so the updater never resolves external secret sources: on Windows they map
``cryptography._rust.pyd`` into the process replacing that venv, and everywhere a slow
``op``/``bws``/command helper (up to 120s per source) would run inside the updater's
120s critical-module import probe and be reported as an import-health timeout.
Profile flags are stripped before ``hermes_cli.main`` loads dotenv, so ``argv[1]`` is
the authoritative subcommand.

name: _read_marker_attempts
doc: Attempt counter from a marker's opportunistic JSON body; corrupt/missing → 0.

name: _process_state
doc:
Single-letter process state (``ps`` style), or ``None`` when unknowable.

``os.kill(pid, 0)`` also succeeds for a ZOMBIE — a process that exited but
whose parent has not reaped it yet. Reading the state lets callers treat a
zombie as dead, so a crashed update stage lingering under an un-reaping
parent cannot keep a stale update marker "live" for the whole age ceiling
(#77259, #120635, #125932). Best-effort and stdlib-only: on any failure the
answer is ``None`` and callers keep their signal-0 verdict.

name: _pid_is_running
doc:
Best-effort stdlib-only process liveness probe.

``os.kill(pid, 0)`` is not a no-op on Windows, so use the Win32 process handle API there. An
access-denied result counts as live: racing an elevated updater is worse than postponing
recovery for one launch. A zombie (exited, un-reaped) counts as dead — see
:func:`_process_state`.

name: _marker_owner_is_live
doc: True when a legacy update marker names a process still running.

name: git_operation_in_progress
doc: Return the active Git operation currently controlling *root*, if any.

name: _git_dir
doc: ``root``'s git dir: ``.git`` itself, or where a linked worktree's ``.git`` file points.

name: blob_id
doc: Git's object id of a blob holding ``data``, in ``like``'s object format (SHA-1 or SHA-256).

name: recovery_closure_verified
doc: Every closure file present with exactly the bytes its manifest names, and nothing missing.

name: _git_executable
doc:
The git ``hermes update`` runs (``_subprocess_compat.expose_pm_git``), without installing it.

The absolute git the killed updater recorded in its marker first: finding PM's copy needs
``pm``, which imports ``hermes_constants``, and a merge killed while writing that module (or
anything else ``pm`` imports) leaves only this path to the repair. Then PATH's git. A Windows install whose only git is the one install.ps1 staged in PM's store
has none on PATH until the updater exposes it, so this falls back to that copy: PM's recorded
entry, or the lockfile's pinned entry the installer extracted without recording it. A bare
``git`` there dies with WinError 2 and the torn tree this repair exists for stays torn.

name: _is_git
doc:
``path`` still runs as git: ``--version`` exits 0 and says ``git version`` (m5). A recorded
git that decayed into anything else (gone executable, a stub that exits 0 silently) must not
answer the repair's questions: its empty ``rev-parse`` would read as "HEAD moved".

name: _trees_git_could_write
doc:
The trees the killed git was moving the checkout to, and the paths whose new content is unknowable.

A fast-forward or ``reset --hard`` writes ``target``. On a custom branch the updater runs
``git merge``, whose files are the merge of both sides: ``merge-tree`` computes the same tree. A
conflicted path (its markers carry other labels) and, on git < 2.38 (no ``--write-tree``), every
path both sides changed count as git's whatever their content.

name: _hash_worktree
doc: Blob ids of the checkout's files, through the repo's clean filters, like ``git add`` would store.

name: _modes_git_wrote
arguments: git, root: Path, entries: dict, links: set[str]
doc:
Paths whose new entry keeps the ``pre`` blob under another mode, already in that mode.

Equal bytes cannot tell a regular file holding ``original`` from a symlink to ``original`` (one
blob id), nor 644 from 755: only the entry's mode can (review N07). The worktree shows a link
(lstat), except under ``core.symlinks=false`` where git checks a link out as a plain file holding
its target, and the executable bit, except on Windows. The index shows the mode git staged where
the worktree cannot; git writes it after the files, so it covers a git killed after a whole tree.

name: _paths_git_wrote
arguments: git, root: Path, pre: str, target: str
doc:
Paths the killed git already touched on the way to ``target``: (restore from HEAD, remove as added,
directories git may have created for its added files, the added ones to keep aside, not delete).

Git rewrites a file as unlink, create, write, so a kill leaves it missing, empty or cut short:
all of those count as git's, like the full new blob. Content that matches neither side and is not
the start of a new blob is the user's own edit (e.g. a re-applied stash) and is left alone. An
added path holding less than a whole new blob may equally be the user's own file created there
after the kill (a ``touch``, a first line): it leaves the tree, but renamed aside, never deleted.
``None``: git no longer knows ``target``.

name: _lock_fd
doc:
False only while another launch holds the claim.

A filesystem that cannot lock at all (ENOLCK on NFS without lockd, EOPNOTSUPP/EINVAL on some SMB
shares) proceeds unguarded like a read-only git dir: counting it as "held" would stop every launch
from ever repairing a checkout the restore handled fine before claims existed.

name: _restore_claim
doc: Yields True while this launch holds the restore claim, False when another held it past the wait.

name: _git_program
doc:
``git`` or ``git-<sub>`` when ``arg0`` (an argv[0], a comm, a psutil name) runs git, else None.

Any directory (``/usr/lib/git-core/git-commit``), either separator, ``.exe`` and case folded:
Windows runs ``git.exe`` and ``git-commit.exe``.

name: _git_subcommand_of
doc:
The subcommand a git argv runs: ``commit`` for ``git -C x -c k=v commit`` and for a dashed
``/usr/lib/git-core/git-commit`` (``git-commit.exe``); None when argv[0] is not git or names none.

name: _checkout_places
doc: The checkout's own paths as given AND resolved, so another process's path need not be resolved.

name: _path_within
doc:
``path`` is one of ``places`` or under it, by PATH COMPONENTS (``/x/hermes-backup`` is not in ``/x/hermes``).

Lexical: another process's cwd is already the kernel's resolved path, and resolving a stranger's
path would touch whatever it names.

name: git_works_in
arguments: args: list[str], cwd: str | None, env: dict[str, str] | None, places: tuple[str, ...]
doc:
A git with this argv/cwd/environment works in ``places``: its cwd, a path argument (absolute,
or relative to its cwd, ``--opt=<path>`` too) or a ``GIT_DIR``-style variable is inside one.

name: _could_write
doc: A process running as ``uid`` may write ``git_dir`` (root, its owner, or a group/world-writable dir).

name: _held_open
arguments: path: Path, root: Path | None=None, *, any_git: bool=False
doc:
Whether a running process may still own ``path`` (a git lock): the holder, False, or None (unknowable).

The holder is a truthy :class:`_Holder` naming it (``pid 4242 (git commit)``). False is proof, not
a guess: Linux reads every process's fds through /proc and, with ``root``, also counts any live git
working in the checkout (cwd, a path argument or ``GIT_DIR``) that is not a pure reader
(:data:`_READER_GIT`; ``any_git`` counts readers too), whatever form runs it: ``git commit``
waiting in the editor has CLOSED its lock fd, and a dashed ``git-commit``, an alias or ``git.exe``
is the same git. A git that could write the git dir but whose cwd or environment cannot be read
makes the answer None. macOS/BSD ask ``lsof`` for open fds and ``ps`` for any such git (``ps``
cannot say where it works, so any counts). Without either check the answer is None and the caller
never deletes the lock. Windows needs no answer here: it refuses to unlink a file another process
has open, so the caller's unlink is the probe.

name: _exited
doc:
The process has released its memory (exiting, or a zombie) or is gone.

The kernel drops its fds before its cwd, and refuses its cwd/environ once it is exiting, so an
unreadable cwd there is not a hidden git: counting it made any git exiting anywhere on a busy
machine postpone the repair. A live process keeps a non-empty argv.

name: _held_open_proc
arguments: path: Path, root: Path | None, any_git: bool

name: _held_open_lsof
arguments: path: Path, root: Path | None, any_git: bool

name: _lsof_cwds
doc: Each pid's cwd from ``lsof -d cwd`` (macOS has no /proc); None when lsof cannot answer.

name: _still_running
doc: POSIX only (the lsof branch never runs on Windows); stdlib, as this launch-time repair must be.

name: _ps_git_holder
arguments: lsof: str, git_dir: Path, root: Path, any_git: bool
doc:
An empty ``lsof`` is no proof: ``git commit`` waiting in the editor has closed its lock fd.
Every git (by executable name, dashed forms included) that could write ``git_dir``, is not a pure
reader, and works in the checkout (its cwd from ``lsof -d cwd``, or a path argument) keeps the
lock; one whose cwd cannot be read makes the answer None. Gits elsewhere on the machine do not
count, or any commit open in another repository would block every launch-time repair.

name: _index_lock_holder
doc: Who keeps ``index.lock`` for the user-facing message: ``pid N (name)`` when it can be named.

name: _release_dead_index_lock
arguments: git_dir: Path, root: Path | None=None, *, any_git: bool=False
doc:
Drop a killed git's ``index.lock`` (it refuses every git command) once its owner is PROVEN gone.

False while a live git may hold it, or when this platform cannot prove it dead: the caller then
keeps the interrupted-pull marker, so the next launch tries again instead of a rollback being lost.
``any_git``: every git working in ``root`` keeps it, readers included (:func:`_held_open`).

name: write_durable_text
doc:
``text`` at ``path`` as one durable record, never a half-written one.

The temp is an unpredictable name created exclusively (no-follow) beside ``path``: a pre-existing
name there is never written through (its symlink or hardlink would carry the record onto another
file) and never deleted (it may be a user's file: review Z5). fsync before the rename: an empty
record over a mixed tree is no record.

name: restore_interrupted_pull
doc:
Put back the files a killed ``hermes update`` had half-moved to the new commit.

``after_failure``: the updater itself calls this when git exited non-zero mid-move (a locked or
read-only file): same restore, and the marker stays whenever the tree is not verified whole.

Returns True when the tree changed under this process: modules it already imported may be the
half-written ones, so the caller must relaunch (``relaunch_after_restore``).

Fast path (no marker) is one or two ``stat`` calls. Acts only when the marker's owner is gone,
HEAD is still the pre-pull commit and no merge/rebase is in progress; then every path git wrote
(the target's content, or torn on the way there) returns to HEAD (the commit the venv was built
for), so the install is whole again and ``hermes update`` redoes the update from the start. Local
edits are never touched; the updater's autostash (if any) stays in ``git stash list``. Concurrent
launches take turns (``_restore_claim``); a launch that waited out another's restore relaunches.

A torn ``hermes_bootstrap.py``, ``hermes_cli/__init__.py`` or recovery/lock/custody module fails
before (or inside) the checkout's copy of this code: a minted launcher then runs the copy the
updater published beside the marker (``RECOVERY_CLOSURE``). Limits, by design: other entry points
(``python -m``, the ``hermes-agent`` hook's ``agent/__init__.py``) have no such fallback, and a
launcher minted before that fallback existed has none either. A file git also changes that the user deleted, emptied or cut to a prefix of git's version
looks exactly like git's own half-written file and is restored too, as is a user edit to a
conflicted path or, on git < 2.38, to a path both sides of a custom-branch merge changed.

name: _checkout_custody
doc:
Hold the checkout kernel lock (``hermes_cli.update_lock``) for a repair, like an updater (R2).

Yields ``""`` while this process holds or joined it (the updater's own ``after_failure``
settle and its children join), else the busy reason: a live update tree owns the checkout and
the repair leaves the tree alone. The restore's mutating git children inherit the lock (POSIX)
or join this process's kill-on-close job (Windows) through ``update_custody.run_git``, so a
launch killed mid-restore keeps the checkout locked until its git is gone.

A torn lock module cannot prove custody: an already-running updater retains its imported
copy and may still be writing this checkout. Refuse launch rather than race that writer.

name: _claim_owner_alive
doc: The updater that wrote ``marker`` is still running and the marker is fresh: hands off.

name: _resume_killed_rollback
arguments: git, fields: dict[str, str], git_dir: Path, root: Path, pre: str, rollback: str, *, after_failure: bool
doc: Redo a killed syntax rollback's HEAD move to ``pre``; the new HEAD, or None (marker kept).

name: _advise_killed_merge
arguments: git_dir: Path, root: Path, target: str, stash: str
doc: Once per process, tell the user to abort the killed updater's own unfinished merge.

name: _custody_git
doc: The restore's ``git(*args)``: the binary the updater recorded, every run under custody (``run_git``).

name: _judge_index_lock
arguments: fields: dict[str, str], marker: Path, root: Path, *, after_failure: bool
doc:
``(foreign_lock, known_foreign, index_free)`` for the git dir's ``index.lock``, before any git runs.

A killed git's lock goes first (an unresolvable or failing git would otherwise strand it, and it
refuses every later git command). Proven-dead only; after a git that EXITED (``after_failure``) a
lock now is another git's, never ours to drop.

name: _retire_unattributable
arguments: git, git_dir: Path, root: Path, marker: Path, pre: str, target: str
doc:
``target`` is gone (a gc or re-clone): nothing left to compare the tree against.

Unattributable bytes are not proof of a whole tree: only a clean tracked tree at ``pre`` retires
the record, rollback or not (review G2).

name: _restore_holding_claim
arguments: root: Path, marker: Path, *, after_failure: bool=False

name: _put_back_written
arguments: git, root: Path, marker: Path, written, pre: str, stash: str, rollback: str, *, foreign_lock: bool, after_failure: bool
doc: Return every path git wrote (``_paths_git_wrote``) to ``pre`` and retire the marker once verified.

name: _lock_identity
doc: ``inode:mtime_ns`` of a lock file, "" when there is none: a recreated lock is a new generation.

name: _lock_predates_move
doc:
``lock`` is the generation ``arm_tree_move`` saw before the move's git ran. A marker without
the record (an older updater's, hand-written) cannot say: every lock counts as foreign.

name: _remember_foreign_lock
doc: Record ``lock``'s identity in the marker (atomically: the marker is the restore's only record).

name: _redo_rollback_head
arguments: git, git_dir: Path, root: Path, pre: str, mode: str, *, after_failure: bool
doc:
Move HEAD (and the index) back to ``pre`` for a killed syntax rollback; None, or why not yet.

The killed step's ``index.lock`` is reclaimed first, and only when its git is proven gone. After a
git that exited in this very process (``after_failure``) a lock is never ours to judge.

name: _rollback_verified
arguments: git, git_dir: Path, pre: str, owned: set[str] | None=None
doc:
The rollback landed: HEAD is ``pre``, no index lock, and no tracked change among ``owned`` (the
paths the update wrote), or anywhere when they are unknown (``target`` gone).

name: _put_back_paths
arguments: git, root: Path, restore: list[str], added: list[str], kept: set[str]
doc: Return ``restore`` to HEAD and drop ``added``, renaming those in ``kept`` aside; the failed git run, or None.

name: _keep_aside
doc: Rename ``file`` to a free ``<name>.hermes-update-kept[-N]`` beside it (never importable, never clobbered).

name: relaunch_after_restore
doc:
Re-run this command from the restored tree; never returns.

Everything imported so far (this package, ``hermes_bootstrap``, ``hermes_cli.main`` itself) may
be the killed git's new files, and they would run against the restored old tree.

name: _pytest_owns_live_checkout
doc:
Keep lifecycle tests from repairing the checkout that runs the suite.

Copied installations in tmp_path remain eligible for real recovery tests.

name: _missing_environment
doc: True when PM recorded an environment whose site-packages is gone.

name: _count_failed_attempt
doc: Bump ``marker``'s attempt count in its own format so the retry limit can trip.

name: recover_if_needed
arguments: project_root: Path | None=None, argv: list[str] | None=None, *, explicit: bool=False
