doc: Yield (name, size, payload) for each member of an ar archive.

name: deb_control_fields_and_bytes
doc:
Parse a .deb's control member and return (fields, raw archive bytes).

The caller gets the raw bytes too so hashing/pool-copy need no re-read.

name: deb_control_fields
doc: Parse Package/Version/Architecture/... from a .deb's control member.

name: deb_version_key
doc: Sort key implementing dpkg version comparison for our versions.

name: existing_published
doc: (package, version) pairs already published in dists/<suite>/Packages.

name: stage
arguments: pool_dir: Path, out_dir: Path, suite: str, gpg_key_file: Path | None, pool_subdir: str=''

name: _gpg_homedir_arg
doc:
Format a homedir path for the host's gpg.

On Windows the commonly available gpg is the MSYS/Git-for-Windows build,
which rejects native ``C:\...`` paths for --homedir and needs the
``/c/...`` form. POSIX gpg (CI's ubuntu runner) needs paths untouched,
so the conversion applies only to Windows drive-letter paths.

name: _gpg_run
arguments: homedir: Path, args: list, *, stdin: bytes | None=None, passphrase: str | None=None
doc:
Run gpg with an explicit isolated homedir.

The passphrase, when the key needs one, is fed on STDIN via
``--passphrase-fd 0`` -- it is never placed in argv (visible in
/proc or error output) and never written to disk.

name: _sole_secret_key_fingerprint
doc:
Fingerprint of the ONLY signing-capable secret key in the homedir.

The homedir is a fresh temp dir into which exactly the supplied key file
was imported, so whatever is here came from the import -- never a
pre-existing unrelated key from a user keyring. If the file carried
multiple keys we fail closed rather than silently signing with the
first one.

name: _verify_signature
arguments: homedir: Path, expected_fpr: str, sig_path: Path, signed_path: Path | None
doc:
Fail-closed check that sig_path is a GOOD signature by expected_fpr.

Verified via gpg --status-fd VALIDSIG (not exit code alone), and the
fingerprint must match the key that was selected from the import.

name: sign
arguments: dists: Path, release_path: Path, gpg_key_file: Path
doc:
Sign Release as InRelease + detached Release.gpg in an ISOLATED
temp GNUPGHOME, verify the signatures fail-closed, then publish the
signing key's public half at the repo root.

Nothing here touches the invoking user's real keyring: the gpg homedir
is a throwaway temp directory whose only content is the supplied key
file, and it is removed afterwards. Real signing keys are usually
passphrase-protected; TERMUX_APT_GPG_PASSPHRASE (set only when the key
needs one) reaches gpg via stdin, never argv.

name: _cache_valid
arguments: out: Path, manifest_path: Path, table: dict
doc:
The staged merged dir is usable only when a manifest exists that
binds the exact current table to a nonempty, EXACT set of .so files
whose bytes all hash to the recorded values.

name: download_path
doc: The verified input consumed by this stager and the CI archive preflight.

name: _ensure_extracted
arguments: payload: Path, name: str, row: dict
doc: Extract fresh bytes from a digest-verified archive on every cache miss.

name: stage
arguments: payload: Path, table: dict, licenses: dict | None=None
doc:
Stage every pinned runtime lib into <payload>/runtime-libs/lib/.

Returns the merged output dir. Raises StageError on any failure; the
manifest is written only after a complete, verified build.

name: run
arguments: argv: list[str], env: dict[str, str], cwd: Path

name: tui_smoke
arguments: launcher: Path, env: dict[str, str], cwd: Path

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(
        [str(launcher), "--tui"], stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave,
        cwd=cwd, env={**env, "TERM": "xterm-256color"}, start_new_session=True,
    )

name: build_identity
arguments: repo: Path, builder: str, platform_tag: str, python_abi: str

name: write_manifest
arguments: payload: Path, identity: dict[str, str], **metadata: str

name: annotate_preview_tool
arguments: action: str='add', ref: Optional[str]=None, selector: Optional[str]=None, label: Optional[str]=None, callback: Optional[Callable]=None
doc: Put one annotation up, take one down, or clear them all.

name: strip_ansi
doc: Remove ANSI escape sequences; clean text passes through unchanged (fast path).

name: sanitize_display_text
doc:
Sanitize stored/untrusted text before echoing it to a terminal: strips ANSI
sequences AND bare control chars, keeping only newlines/tabs (CRs become newlines
so ``\r``-overwrite spoofing can't hide content). Rich's ``Text()`` does NOT
neutralize raw escape bytes, so a replayed ``/resume`` message must not be able
to clear the screen, retitle the window, or restyle UI.

Use this when re-rendering conversation history or other persisted text in a terminal UI (e.g. the
``/resume`` recap): a message that arrived with embedded escapes — pasted content, gateway-origin text,
or model output echoing injected tool results — must not be able to clear the screen, retitle the
window, move the cursor, or restyle adjacent UI when replayed. Mirrors openai/codex#31494
(``sanitize_user_text``).

name: strip_unicode_tags
doc:
Remove invisible Unicode TAG chars (a prompt-injection smuggling channel in
untrusted tool output); valid emoji tag sequences are preserved.

Returns the input unchanged (fast path) when no plane-14 tag characters are present. Ported from
block/goose#10746.

name: _get_denial_breaker_threshold
doc: ``approvals.denial_breaker_threshold``: default 3; 0 or negative disables.

name: _record_denial
doc:
Increment and return the session's consecutive guardian-denial count. Pop-and-reinsert
keeps actively-denying sessions at the most-recent end so eviction drops idle keys.

name: _reset_denials
doc: Clear the session's consecutive-denial tally (an approval happened).

name: _denial_breaker_addendum
doc:
Escalated hard-stop text once the breaker has tripped, else ''. Read-only: callers
increment via :func:`_record_denial`; the text is appended verbatim to the deny message.

name: register_gateway_notify
doc:
Register ``cb(approval_data: dict) -> None`` for sending approval requests. The callback
bridges sync→async: it runs in the agent thread and must schedule the send on the loop.

name: unregister_gateway_notify
doc:
Unregister the callback and wake ALL blocked threads for this session so
they don't hang forever (agent run finished or interrupted).

name: resolve_gateway_approval
arguments: session_key: str, choice: str, resolve_all: bool=False, reason: Optional[str]=None, request_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Unblock waiting agent thread(s) from the gateway's /approve or /deny handler.

*resolve_all* resolves every pending approval (``/approve all``); otherwise the oldest
(FIFO) or the one matching *request_id*. *reason* is the ``/deny <reason>`` free text,
relayed to the agent in the BLOCKED message. Returns the number resolved.

name: withdraw_gateway_approval
arguments: session_key: str, request_id: str, cause: str
doc:
Withdraw one pending approval nobody can answer (the only attached client cannot render it).
The waiter wakes at once with ``cancelled=cause`` — a withdrawal, never a user deny — instead of
idling for the whole approvals.timeout (#112548). False when it is no longer pending.

name: list_gateway_approvals
doc: Return replay-safe snapshots of unresolved approvals for one session.

name: register_gateway_settle
doc:
Attach ``settle(reason)`` to one pending approval; it runs once when that wait ends by any path.
False when the request is no longer pending (the surface should withdraw its prompt itself).

name: ack_gateway_approval
doc: Record that a client received a particular pending approval request.

name: has_blocking_approval
doc: Check if a session has one or more blocking gateway approvals waiting.

name: pending_gateway_approval_count
doc: Unresolved gateway approvals across every session — a backend blocked on one is not idle.

name: get_pending_gateway_approval
doc:
Copy of the oldest unresolved gateway approval, for reconnecting clients
to restore a prompt. Read-only snapshot — the queue stays authoritative.

name: submit_pending
doc: Store a pending approval request for a session.

name: approve_session
doc: Approve a pattern for this session only.

name: _release_permission_mode_dependents
doc:
Drop resources whose immutable mode derives from Hermes YOLO. Lazy import so approval-only
sessions never load computer-use; releasing on BOTH edges makes enabling YOLO replace a
standard backend and disabling it revoke a private unrestricted daemon immediately.

name: enable_session_yolo
doc: Enable YOLO bypass for a single session key.

name: disable_session_yolo
doc: Disable YOLO bypass for a single session key.

name: clear_session
doc: Remove all approval and yolo state for a given session.

name: is_session_yolo_enabled
doc: Return True when YOLO bypass is enabled for a specific session.

name: is_current_session_yolo_enabled
doc: Return True when the active approval session has YOLO bypass enabled.

name: _yolo_active
doc:
CLI ``--yolo`` (process-scoped, frozen at import) or gateway ``/yolo``
(session-scoped). Hardline / deny-rule floors run BEFORE this everywhere.

name: _permanent_set
doc:
The permanent allowlist that governs the ACTIVE profile. Unscoped (single-profile process,
or the multiplexer's own launch profile) → the module-level set tests and the CLI seed. A routed
profile (HERMES_HOME override) → its own set, lazily loaded from ITS ``command_allowlist``: the
launch profile's "always" approvals must not pre-approve commands for a secondary, nor may a
secondary's "always" choice be written back into the launch profile's config. Callers hold ``_lock``.

name: _sync_permanent_from_disk
doc:
Apply hand edits to ``command_allowlist`` made since the last sync. The gateway daemon
outlives any one session, so an entry the operator removed must stop being honoured now, not
at restart. Only the on-disk delta is applied: approvals this process made but could not save
survive. The config read is cached on the file signature. Callers hold ``_lock``.

name: is_approved
doc:
Session-scoped or permanent approval. Accepts the canonical key and the legacy
regex-derived key so existing command_allowlist entries survive key migrations.

name: _is_permanently_approved
doc: Permanent approval only, with compatibility for migrated pattern keys.

name: approve_permanent
doc: Add a pattern to the permanent allowlist.

name: load_permanent
doc: Bulk-load permanent allowlist entries from config.

name: _persist_choice
arguments: session_key: str, choice: str, keys: list[str]
doc: Persist a human ``session``/``always`` choice for each pattern key. ``once`` persists nothing.

name: _read_permanent_allowlist
doc: ``command_allowlist`` of the active profile's config as a set (empty on malformed input).

name: load_permanent_allowlist
doc:
Load ``command_allowlist`` from config and sync it into the approval state
so is_approved() honors 'always' choices from previous sessions.

name: save_permanent_allowlist
doc:
Save permanently allowed command patterns to config, reconciling with the file.

``command_allowlist`` is a file an operator edits by hand; removing an entry
there is the documented way to withdraw a standing approval. This process read
it once at import and ``load_permanent`` only ever unions, so writing the
in-memory set straight back deleted entries added on disk since import and
resurrected the ones removed. The result written is ``what is on disk now``
plus ``what this process approved since its own baseline``; revoked entries are
also dropped from the governing permanent set so ``is_approved()`` stops
honouring them (``_sync_permanent_from_disk`` does the same on every check).

``patterns`` may only ADD: an entry left out of it is not removed, because the
on-disk list wins for anything this process did not approve itself. Remove
entries by editing ``command_allowlist`` in config.yaml.

name: is_approval_bypass_active_for_session
doc:
Canonical three-source bypass check: process ``--yolo`` (frozen at import), the
session-scoped gateway ``/yolo`` toggle, ``approvals.mode: off``. Pure bypass
sub-expression only — hardline blocklist / permanent allowlist are the caller's job.

name: is_approval_bypass_active
doc: Return whether the current approval context has bypass enabled.

name: _denied
arguments: message: str, *, pattern_key: str, description: str, outcome: str, noun: str='command', **extra
doc:
Standard non-consent result: the agent must not retry or rephrase. ``user_summary`` is the
one-line human reading of the same outcome (see ``_user_summary``).

name: _blocked
arguments: message: str, *, pattern_key: str, description: str
doc: Non-interactive block (cron / -q / unattended / no-human): no consent keys.

name: _user_approved
doc:
A human approval (incl. ESCALATE-then-approve or a smart-DENY owner
override) resets the consecutive-denial tally.

name: _pending_result
arguments: spec, session_key: str, *, command: str, description: str, pattern_key: str, pattern_keys: list[str], body: str | None, smart_denied: bool
doc:
Queue an approval nobody can answer right now (no gateway notifier, no CLI panel) for
``/approve`` / ``/deny`` review. Command/code gates return the backward-compatible
``pending_approval`` shape (``pattern_keys`` + STOP text); the action gate ``approval_required``.

name: _unattended_contexts
doc:
Active unattended contexts in evaluation order: single-query first (``hermes chat -q``
exports HERMES_INTERACTIVE=1 but nobody answers); cron beats a platform marker because
cron binds the platform for delivery routing only.

name: _unattended_deny
doc: Deny-mode handling for one unattended context (cron / -q / webhook); None = allow.

name: _smart_gate
arguments: spec: _GateSpec, command: str, description: str, pattern_key: str, pattern_keys: list[str], session_key: str, *, human_present: bool
doc:
Guardian-LLM step -> ``(result, smart_denied_for_owner)``: a result ends the gate;
``smart_denied_for_owner`` means an interactive owner may still override the DENY for this
one operation (once/deny only, nothing persists).

APPROVE approves this command only — pattern-level persistence would let one benign
command suppress review of later commands in the same broad detector category. A DENY
counts toward the denial breaker even when an owner may override it. ESCALATE follows the
normal, potentially persistent manual behavior.

name: _human_decision
arguments: spec: _GateSpec, *, command: str, description: str, pattern_key: str, pattern_keys: list[str], session_key: str, approval_callback, is_cli: bool, is_gateway: bool, is_ask: bool, smart: bool=False, pending_body=None
doc:
Ask a human (after the optional guardian-LLM step) and turn the answer into the gate result.

``pattern_keys`` are what :func:`_persist_choice` stores on session/always; a smart-DENY
owner override reduces every surface to once/deny and persists nothing. ``pending_body`` is a thunk, built only once a human is
actually asked, so a smart APPROVE never pays for redacting a large script.

name: _presence
doc:
``(approval_callback, is_cli, is_gateway, is_ask)`` for the current context.

Single-query ``-q`` and cron clear the presence trio: ``hermes chat -q`` exports
HERMES_INTERACTIVE=1 for sudo prompts, and a gateway sets HERMES_EXEC_ASK=1 at startup and
passes its environ to every external cron worker (#110932) — in neither can a human answer
the card, so the gate must resolve from ``approvals.<ctx>_mode`` instead of parking on a
pending approval. Unattended *platforms* keep ``is_ask`` only while a client on the session
could actually answer: ``/v1/runs`` and streaming chat completions bridge an approval
notifier (``approval.request`` → ``POST /v1/runs/{id}/approval``), so on api_server a
registered notifier is the discriminator. webhook/msgraph_webhook turns run through the
generic TurnRunner lane, which registers a notifier for *every* turn — but those adapters
render no approval surface and the inbound lane has no reader, so there ``is_ask`` drops
regardless and the unattended branch resolves from ``approvals.unattended_mode`` instead of
parking an unanswerable card (#100532).

name: _run_approval_gate
arguments: *, pattern_key: str, description: str, display_target: str, approval_callback=None, subject: str='', noun: str='flagged actions', advice: str='Find an alternative approach that avoids this action.', cron_deny_message: str='', single_query_deny_message: str='', unattended_deny_message: str='', autoapprove_log_prefix: str, fail_closed_when_no_human: bool=False, no_human_block_message: str=''
doc:
Shared human-approval gate for a flagged action (tool call or write): decision core for
:func:`request_tool_approval` and the file-tool write gates.

Order: yolo bypass → session-cache short-circuit → interactive/gateway/unattended branch →
prompt → persistence. Input-shape checks (hardline, allowlist, pattern detection) are the
caller's job. ``fail_closed_when_no_human``: a non-interactive, non-gateway, non-cron
context without an ask bridge BLOCKS instead of auto-approving, so a plugin-flagged action
never runs ungated.
Unattended deny text is ``ctx.block_message(subject, noun, advice)`` unless the caller passes
an explicit ``*_deny_message`` (the file-tool write gates word their own).

name: _should_skip_container_guards
doc:
True when the backend is isolated enough to skip dangerous-command prompts. Docker is the
exception once host paths are bind-mounted: ``rm -rf /workspace`` then reaches host files.

name: _user_deny_block
doc:
The operator's ``approvals.deny`` rules are documented as never bypassable — not by yolo,
not by mode=off, and not by an isolated container either: they express intent about what the
agent may DO, not what it can reach, so they are evaluated before the container fast path.

name: _floor_block
doc:
Unconditional floors, BEFORE yolo / mode=off / cron approve-mode so no
session-level setting can bypass them: hardline catastrophic commands,
password-piping to ``sudo -S`` with no SUDO_PASSWORD configured (full guard
only), the user's own approvals.deny rules ("never, even under yolo"), and
deletion of the Python interpreter/venv this very runtime boots from (a
delete the agent cannot walk back — the next start fails before any tool
can run, #58748).

name: check_dangerous_command
arguments: command: str, env_type: str, approval_callback=None, has_host_access: bool=False
doc:
Detect a dangerous command and handle approval (pattern layer only). ``has_host_access``:
a Docker sandbox that bind-mounts host paths must not skip approval.
Returns ``{"approved": True/False, "message": str or None, ...}``.

name: request_tool_approval
arguments: tool_name: str, reason: str, *, rule_key: str='', approval_callback=None
doc:
Escalate an arbitrary tool call to the human-approval gate.

Entry point for a plugin ``pre_tool_call`` hook returning ``{"action": "approve", ...}``:
it asks the SAME human gate as Tier-2 dangerous shell patterns (session/permanent
allowlist, CLI prompt, gateway pending, once/session/always/deny, timeout fail-closed), so
the LLM cannot skip it. Cron honors ``approvals.cron_mode``; any OTHER non-interactive
context without an approval bridge fails CLOSED. ``rule_key`` controls the ``[a]lways``
allowlist grain; when empty it is ``tool_name`` + a hash of ``reason`` so DISTINCT reasons
on the same tool persist independently. Returns the ``check_dangerous_command`` result shape.

name: check_all_command_guards
arguments: command: str, env_type: str, approval_callback=None, has_host_access: bool=False
doc:
Run all pre-exec security checks and return a single approval decision. Plugins that
want to veto or escalate a command do it from ``pre_tool_call``.
``has_host_access``: a Docker sandbox with bind-mounted host paths takes the normal flow.

name: _is_local_viewer_turn
doc:
A local session's turn its viewer submitted, with that viewer there to answer: its frozen launch policy is
local-interactive, the admission is the viewer's own prompt (not a plugin injection or another producer
admission) and a viewer holding ``session:approve`` is attached now, it is not a delegate_task child (sync or
async; they inherit the parent's policy), and the turn's approval notifier is registered under the bound
session key. The notifier is registered for every session turn, so it only tells side tasks (their own task
key, none registered) apart; it does not show anyone is attached.

name: check_execute_code_guard
arguments: code: str, env_type: str, has_host_access: bool=False
doc:
Approve an execute_code script before its child process is spawned.

The script can call ``subprocess``/``os.system``/``ctypes`` directly, none of which pass
through ``terminal()`` / ``DANGEROUS_PATTERNS``; in gateway/ask contexts we fail closed by
approving the script as a whole. Same dict contract as ``check_all_command_guards``.
Documented limitation: a purely local non-interactive non-gateway session returns approved
(the terminal auto-approve contract); the hardline floor still blocks catastrophic
``terminal()`` commands the script issues.

See #30882.
The hardline floor still blocks catastrophic ``terminal()`` commands the script issues; running
arbitrary code headlessly without any approval surface is trusted-by-config (set a gateway/ask surface
or ``approvals.cron_mode`` to require approval). See #30882.

name: block_message
arguments: self, subject: str, *, noun: str, advice: str

name: set_hermes_interactive_context
doc: Bind interactive mode for the current context instead of mutating os.environ.

name: reset_hermes_interactive_context
doc: Restore the prior value from :func:`set_hermes_interactive_context`.

name: _is_interactive_cli
doc: True for an interactive CLI/ACP session (contextvar first, env fallback).

name: _fire_approval_hook
doc:
Invoke a plugin lifecycle hook (pre_approval_request / post_approval_response).

Lazy-imports the plugin manager (approval.py is imported long before plugins
are discovered). Never raises: approval flow is safety-critical, plugin
observability is not.

name: gateway_approval_surface
doc:
Surface a gateway-rendered approval reports: ``cli`` for a classic CLI session's turn (main
prompted those in the CLI process), else ``gateway``.

name: is_local_interactive_session
doc:
True for a classic CLI, TUI, Desktop or ACP session's turn, read from the launch policy the gateway
froze at ``session.create`` (never a per-turn client flag). Kanban, cron and forwarded routes keep
their own sources and stay out.

name: is_viewer_turn_with_approver
doc:
True while the executing turn is one its session's viewer submitted through ``session.submit`` (as the
gateway's FIFO drain recorded for this admission) and a viewer that can answer approvals is attached now:
a subscriber holding ``session:approve``, the only answer the gateway's approval resolver accepts. A plugin
``inject_message`` turn, a delegation completion, a background-process or watch notice, a /loop tick, a
heartbeat or a hosted-room task is never a viewer turn.

name: set_current_session_key
doc: Bind the active approval session key to the current context.

name: reset_current_session_key
doc: Restore the prior approval session key context.

name: set_current_observability_context
arguments: *, turn_id: str='', tool_call_id: str='', session_id: str=''
doc: Bind active tool correlation IDs to approval hooks.

name: reset_current_observability_context
doc: Restore prior approval hook correlation IDs.

name: get_current_session_key
doc: Return the active session key: approval contextvar → session_context → os.environ.

name: _session_env
doc:
Session-scoped env value, contextvar-first so one cron/-q job cannot taint
unrelated gateway/API/TUI turns in the same process; process env is the
fallback for CLI tests and older entrypoints.

name: _get_session_platform
doc: Return the current gateway platform from contextvars/env fallback.

name: _is_cron_approval_context
doc: True when the current approval decision is running inside cron.

name: _is_unattended_platform_approval_context
doc:
True when the session platform is a programmatic/unattended surface.

Webhook, msgraph_webhook, and api_server sessions bind ``HERMES_SESSION_PLATFORM`` like chat gateways
do, but there is no human who can resolve a pending approval. Treating them as gateway approval contexts
blocks the session for the full approval timeout (60-300s) and then fails closed anyway — the deadlock
in #37284/#87509.

name: _is_single_query_approval_context
doc:
True for a single-query (-q) session: ``hermes chat -q`` exports
``HERMES_INTERACTIVE=1`` (so sudo password prompts work) but nobody is waiting
to answer approvals; without this marker the gate would wait the full timeout,
fail closed and push the agent toward workarounds (e.g. execute_code).
``approvals.single_query_mode`` makes the path deterministic. A gateway-admitted turn
carries the same fact as the submission's ``finite`` flag (``hermes -z`` / ``chat -q``
over the daemon): the viewer detaches on the first prompt, so nobody answers there either.

name: _no_user_can_answer
doc:
True in single-query (-q), cron and unattended-platform sessions. `hermes chat -q` still registers the
CLI panel callback, so a prompt that only checks for a callback would wait the full timeout for nobody.

name: _is_gateway_approval_context
doc:
True inside a gateway/API session that can answer an approval.

Legacy integrations set HERMES_GATEWAY_SESSION; concurrent paths bind
HERMES_SESSION_PLATFORM via contextvars. Cron is NEVER a gateway approval
context even when it originated from a platform (cron binds the platform for
delivery routing): falling through would submit a pending approval with no
listener and block the job indefinitely; unattended platforms likewise.

Unattended programmatic platforms (webhook, msgraph_webhook, api_server) are excluded for the same
reason: those adapters have no ``send_exec_approval`` and no way to receive ``/approve`` replies.
Submitting a pending approval there blocks the session for the full approval timeout (60-300 s) with no
human who can resolve it (#37284, 87509). Their dangerous-command handling is governed by
``approvals.unattended_mode`` config (default deny), mirroring cron.

name: _resolve_cli_approval_callback
doc: Explicit callback, else the per-thread one from ``terminal_tool.set_approval_callback``.

name: _should_fall_through_to_cli_approval
doc:
Prefer the CLI Dangerous Command panel over a silent pending approval:
``HERMES_EXEC_ASK`` (or a platform marker) can leak into an interactive CLI
process (historically via ``import gateway.run``), and without a gateway notify
listener the ask branch used to return ``pending_approval`` immediately and
skip the panel the user can actually answer.

name: _normalize_approval_mode
doc:
Normalize approval mode values loaded from YAML/config. YAML 1.1 parses a
bare ``off`` as False, so ``mode: off`` arrives as a bool; treat it as the
intended string mode. Unknown strings (e.g. 'auto') warn and fall back to
'manual' instead of silently failing every mode check.

name: _get_approval_config
doc:
Read the approvals config block: the LIVE config-cache sub-dict
(load_config_readonly contract) — callers must not mutate it or any nested structure.

name: _get_approval_mode
doc: Return 'manual', 'smart', or 'off' (a hosted-room policy overrides config).

name: _get_approval_timeout
doc:
Read ``approvals.timeout`` (default 300s: gateway push notifications may
not be seen for minutes; 60s failed closed before Telegram taps landed).
Clamped to ``agent.deadline.MAX_SAFE_TIMEOUT_S`` (~1 year): a larger value
overflows ``time_t`` inside ``Thread.join`` / ``Lock.acquire`` on macOS and
crashed every parallel tool batch; clamping at the single config-read site
keeps every consumer platform-safe at once.

name: format_approval_window
doc:
The ONE human wording for an approval timeout window, shared by the CLI timeout notice,
the tool result's ``user_summary`` and the gateway card copy so every surface agrees:
300 → "5 minutes", 90 → "90 seconds", 7200 → "2 hours".

name: approval_timeout_notice_kwargs
doc:
``{waited, suggested}`` for the ``approval.timeout`` copy: how long we waited (``5 minutes`` /
``90 seconds``) and a tripled ``approvals.timeout`` value the user can paste into ``hermes config set``.

name: _binary_approval_mode
doc: Read ``approvals.<key>`` as 'approve' or 'deny' (default deny).

name: _get_cron_approval_mode
doc: Read the cron approval mode from config. Returns 'deny' or 'approve'.

name: _get_single_query_approval_mode
doc: Read the single-query (-q) approval mode from config. Returns 'deny' or 'approve'.

name: _get_unattended_approval_mode
doc:
Approval mode for webhook / msgraph_webhook / api_server sessions; default
deny — an unattended session never silently runs a flagged action unless the
operator explicitly trusts it.

name: _get_approval_transport_config
doc: Return explicitly selected transport and fail-closed fallback mode.

name: _contains_shell_carrier
doc: Return whether any command-position word is a shell-carrying command.

name: _mask_quoted_prose
doc:
Blank out quoted string CONTENT for positionless hardline matching (detection-only).
Quote characters stay; inside double quotes `$(...)` and backtick spans are kept RAW because
the shell really executes them. An unclosed quote masks to end-of-string, which cannot hide a
runnable command (the shell would not run it either).

Detection-only rewrite used by the quote-masked hardline rules (redirect-to-block-device, fork bomb):
text inside single or double quotes is data the shell passes as an argument, so `echo "cat f >
/dev/sda"` must not trip the unconditional floor (#93392). Unquoted text is untouched.

name: _check_sudo_stdin_guard
doc:
Detect ``sudo -S`` without configured SUDO_PASSWORD -> (is_blocked, description). When
SUDO_PASSWORD is set, ``_transform_sudo_command`` injects ``-S`` itself, so this guard only
fires when the LLM wrote it explicitly.

name: detect_hardline_command
doc: Check hardline patterns (NEVER bypassable, even in YOLO) -> (is_hardline, description).

name: _approval_key_aliases
doc:
All approval keys for this pattern: the description plus the historical regex-derived key
older allowlist/session entries may still use.

name: _normalize_command_for_detection
doc:
Normalize a command before pattern matching so ANSI escapes, null bytes, Unicode fullwidth
forms, and shell splicing tricks cannot bypass detection.

name: _lower_preserving_flags
doc:
Lowercase a detection variant for the pattern pass while keeping dash-prefixed tokens
byte-for-byte, so case-dependent flags keep their distinction. All dangerous patterns are
compiled case-insensitively, so preserved flag case is invisible to them except where a
pattern explicitly scopes a case-sensitive group. Non-flag tokens (command words, quoted
prose, paths) are lowercased exactly as before; separators and whitespace are untouched.

name: _home_prefix_fold_regex
doc:
Compile a regex matching *path* as an absolute directory prefix.
Components match with either separator so native Windows, forward-slash, and mixed forms all
fold; the caller normalizes the tail's backslashes to ``/``. A non-empty tail is required, so a
bare home is never folded. Returns ``None`` for an unset/degenerate path (fewer than two
components: ``/``, ``C:\``, ``""``) so a stray HOME cannot rewrite unrelated prefixes.

name: _fold_home_prefixes
doc:
Fold each resolved home prefix in *command* to *replacement* (no trailing separator; the tail
supplies it). Longest first so a deeper home folds before a shorter overlapping one that would clobber it.

name: _rewrite_resolved_user_home
doc: User home (expanduser / realpath / $HOME) -> ``~/``; no-op when unset, degenerate, or unresolvable.

name: _rewrite_resolved_hermes_home
doc:
Resolved HERMES_HOME (and its realpath) -> ``~/.hermes/`` so the _HERMES_CONFIG_PATH /
_HERMES_ENV_PATH rules match Docker/gateway deployments that spell the absolute path.

name: _command_parser_limit_exceeded
doc:
Bound all parser work before normalization/tokenization. Separator counting is deliberately
conservative: quoted separators over-count, but crossing the ceiling fails closed rather than
letting an uninspected suffix execute.

name: _backtick_end_from
doc: Index of the backtick closing the one opened at ``i``, or None when none follows.

name: _shell_tokens_with_spans
doc:
Return shell words as ``(value, start, end, quoted)`` or ``None`` on malformed quoting.
Deliberately small lexer that never expands shell syntax; it exists to keep source spans (which
``shlex`` does not expose) for deciding which quoted grep operand is data, not another command.

Lexing stops at the end of the simple command that begins at *start*: an unquoted ``;``, ``|``,
``&`` or newline, or the ``)`` / backtick that closes the substitution the command sits inside.
Without that, a grep nested as ``"$(grep … | cut …)"`` was lexed together with the enclosing
command's closing quote, read as unbalanced quoting, and reported as a hardline block (546
blocked turns in one run, every one a false positive; ``sed -n "$(grep -n X f | cut -d: -f1),+3p" f``
is the canonical shape).

name: _quoted_grep_pattern_spans
doc:
Structurally locate quoted grep PCRE operands -> (spans, malformed). On an ambiguous or
malformed grep parse callers fail closed and use the original command: no text is hidden on
an uncertain parse.

name: _splice
doc:
Apply sorted, non-overlapping ``(start, end, text)`` edits to *command* in one pass
(re-slicing per edit is quadratic on 10k+ segments).

name: _shell_segment_tokens
doc:
Tokenize an already-bounded command segment. ``None`` distinguishes malformed quoting from
an empty segment so callers can fail closed for a program-bearing option rather than silently
skip it.

name: _iter_top_level_shell_segments
doc: Yield top-level command segments in one left-to-right pass.

name: _interpreter_exec_flag
doc: Return an execution-bearing interpreter option, if present.

name: _bash_exec_payload
doc:
Return whether Bash ``-c`` occurs and the command string it owns.
Bash's O/o options consume the following argument even when they precede a later ``-c`` or
share its short-option bundle; the two startup-file long options own their next token.
Parsing those first prevents both missed payloads and false ``-c`` hits.

name: _read_tool_exec_flag
doc: Return (option, program) for a read-only tool's program-running flag.

name: _execution_flag_findings
doc: Yield scoped execution mechanisms and any executable payloads.

name: _scan_shell
arguments: text: str, start: int=0, end: int | None=None, *, subst: str='', brace: bool=False, stop_unterminated: bool=False, naive_backtick: bool=False, comments: bool=False
doc:
Yield ``(kind, i, j, quote)`` lexical steps over ``text[start:end]`` without expanding.

The single quote/escape state machine behind every detection scanner. ``kind`` is ``"char"``
(one char), ``"esc"`` (backslash + the char it escapes; never inside single quotes), ``"quote"``
(an opening/closing quote char) or ``"subst"`` (a ``$(...)`` / backtick / ``${...}`` span);
With *comments*, ``"comment"`` spans are skipped without interpreting their quote syntax.
``quote`` is the state the step was read in (``None``, ``'`` or ``"``). Substitutions are
recognized unquoted when ``"u"`` is in *subst*, inside double quotes when ``"q"`` is; *brace*
adds unquoted ``${...}``. An unterminated substitution falls through as plain chars unless
*stop_unterminated*, which yields ``("subst", i, None, quote)`` and ends the scan (the caller
descends to *end* itself). *naive_backtick* closes a backtick at the next backtick even if
escaped (the quoted-prose masker's historical behavior).

name: _scan_dollar_paren_end
doc: Return the offset after a balanced ``$(...)`` command substitution.

name: _read_shell_word
doc: Read one shell word without executing expansions.

name: _literal_command_substitution_output
doc: Resolve tiny literal command substitutions without executing a shell.

name: _deobfuscate_shell_word_for_detection
doc:
Approximate how shell syntax can spell a command word: collapses quoting/escaping plus
simple literal command substitutions in the word itself. Intentionally narrow and non-executing.

name: _mark_command_starts
doc:
Insert *marker* (a newline) before each real (quote-aware) command start.
``\n`` is already a ``_CMDPOS`` separator, so this exposes subshell ``(cmd)`` and brace-group
``{ cmd; }`` openers — which the flat pattern class omits — to the anchored patterns WITHOUT the
quoted-prose false positives that adding ``(`` / ``{`` to ``_CMDPOS`` would cause: starts inside
quotes are never produced, so ``--title "block (reboot)"`` is left as-is.

name: _mask_quoted_newlines
doc:
Replace raw newlines inside single/double quotes with a space (detection-only).
A quoted newline is DATA to the shell, yet the flat ``_CMDPOS`` class treats every raw ``\n``
as a command start, so multi-line quoted arguments (commit messages, heredoc text) tripped the
hardline blocklist when a data line began with e.g. ``sudo reboot``. Quote tracking mirrors
``_iter_shell_command_starts``. Unquoted newlines pass through and ``_mark_command_starts``
still re-inserts newlines at genuine starts; an unclosed quote absorbs following newlines
exactly as the shell would, so masking them cannot hide a runnable command.

name: _mask_quoted_newlines_span
arguments: command: str, start: int, end: int
doc:
``_mask_quoted_newlines`` over ``command[start:end]``. A ``$(...)`` / backtick substitution
    inside double quotes is EXECUTABLE, not data: its body is re-scanned with a fresh quote state so a
    newline that separates commands inside it survives as a command boundary. Masking it as quoted
    data turned ``"$(grep x f
reboot)"`` into ``... f reboot)``, which no later stage can tell from an
    operand; the pre-fix scanner only caught it by refusing the whole command as malformed.

name: _iter_shell_command_word_spans
doc: Yield command-position words that may be executable names.

name: _shell_command_segment
doc: Bound a candidate to its command, preserving quoted argument bytes.

name: _split_env_string
doc:
Project GNU env -S literal argv, not POSIX shell words.

Dynamic ${NAME} expansion is deliberately not evaluated: the execution
backend's environment need not be this process's environment.

name: _deny_command_variants
doc:
Add executable projections without reparsing normalized argument data.

Whole-input matching is retained for existing globs. New projections parse
the original quote state, preserve path-specific rules, and fold only the
executable basename (never arbitrary argument paths).

name: _is_verification_artifact_cleanup
doc: Return whether *command* only removes one Hermes ad-hoc temp script.

name: _is_shell_token_spliced_gateway_lifecycle
doc:
Catch gateway-lifecycle verbs spelled with quote splicing.
Backslash splicing (``kick\start``) is undone by normalization, but quote splicing is not:
``_deobfuscate_shell_word_for_detection`` is deliberately scoped to command-position words
(widening it would let quoted prose like ``git commit -m "rm -rf /"`` match), and the spliced
verb is an ARGUMENT, so ``launchctl kick"start" -k gui/501/ai.hermes.gateway`` auto-approved.
Delegates to ``cron.lifecycle_guard`` (shlex-tokenized, anchored on a hermes-gateway
identifier). Runs last so an ordinary pattern match keeps its more specific reason; this layer
only prompts — the non-bypassable block still lives in ``cron.lifecycle_guard``.

``_normalize_command_for_detection`` strips backslash escapes, so ``kick\start`` already reaches the
launchctl pattern above. See #80269.

name: detect_dangerous_command
doc: Check dangerous patterns -> (is_dangerous, pattern_key, description).

name: _match_user_deny_rule
doc:
Return the matching ``approvals.deny`` glob, or None. User-defined fnmatch
globs that block unconditionally — like the hardline floor, a match fires
BEFORE the yolo / mode=off bypass ("never let the agent run this, even under
yolo"). Case-insensitive, run over the same normalized/deobfuscated variants
the dangerous-pattern detector uses so quoting tricks (``r\m``,
``git st""atus``) can't sidestep a rule.

name: _user_deny_block_result
doc: Build the standard block result for an ``approvals.deny`` match.

name: _save_blocked_payload
doc:
Persist a parser-limit-blocked command as a runnable script. That block
fires on payload SIZE/shape, not the operation — usually a legitimate script
the model inlined. Saving it makes recovery one turn (`bash <file>`) instead
of two, and is strictly safer than the hint-only path: the file goes through
the normal execution pipeline (including the referenced-script content guard)
and nothing runs here. Returns the path, or None on any failure (hint falls
back to write_file).

name: _hardline_block_result
doc: Build the standard block result for a hardline match.

name: _sudo_stdin_block_result
doc: Build the standard block result for sudo stdin guard.

name: _has_allowlist_shell_operator
doc:
Return True when a command is too compound for the allowlist shortcut.
Quote-aware: metacharacters inside quotes or behind a backslash are literal
arguments (``cargo bench -- '^a(b|c)$'``), not shell syntax. Still
disqualifying: ``$`` or backtick inside DOUBLE quotes (expansion stays
active), and any quoted/escaped control character when the command also
carries a ``-c``/``-e``/``--command``/``--eval``-style option that would
hand the quoted text to another interpreter.

name: _command_matches_permanent_allowlist
doc:
True when command_allowlist holds this exact command text or a matching
glob. Permanent approvals historically store dangerous-pattern keys such as
``recursive delete``; manual entries are command text, possibly with
shell-style wildcards like ``podman *``.

name: _poll_event
arguments: event: threading.Event, session_key: str, *, interrupt_log: str
doc:
Wait on *event* until it fires, the turn is interrupted, or approvals.timeout
elapses; returns ``"set"`` | ``"interrupted"`` | ``"timeout"``. Polls in ~1s
slices so activity heartbeats reach the agent's inactivity tracker every ~10s —
otherwise the gateway watchdog kills the agent while the user is still
responding (mirrors ``_wait_for_process()`` cadence). The loop is recorded as
human-wait time so the concurrent batch deadline excludes it.

Any interrupt (/stop, inactivity timeout, delegation teardown) ends the wait
fail-closed: the command does not run. Who caused it is read from the
per-thread interrupt-cause channel (``get_interrupt_reason()``, a trusted fixed
category), never inferred from message text, so the caller can report a
withdrawn prompt without inventing a user refusal.

name: _cancel_cause
doc:
Why the wait ended with nobody answering: the turn was interrupted (cause from the
per-thread channel — a user /stop or a parent's delegation teardown), the entry was
withdrawn with a stamped cause (leader interrupted, session torn down), or the turn ended
under the prompt (notifier unregistered, result never set). ``None`` for a real answer
or a plain timeout.

name: _finish
arguments: payload: dict, resolved: bool, choice: str | None, reason, **extra
doc:
Fire the post hook and build the decision dict. Unresolved (timeout) and
a None choice both mean the user never answered; ``cancelled`` carries the
cause when the prompt was withdrawn rather than answered.

name: _hook_choice
arguments: resolved: bool, choice: str | None, extra: dict
doc: Observer-facing outcome of a wait: the choice, else ``cancelled`` / ``timeout``.

name: _await_coalesced_leader
doc:
Wait on an already-pending identical approval instead of re-prompting.
Adopts the leader's decision: ``session``/``always`` → approval (same dict
shape as a direct resolution; persistence stays the caller's and is
idempotent across leader and followers); ``deny`` → denial carrying the
leader's reason; leader timeout / our own deadline → unresolved. ``once``
returns ``None``: single-use consent covers only the leader's execution,
so the caller must issue a fresh prompt. Hooks fire with ``coalesced=True``
so observers see the follower's lifecycle without a duplicate prompt.

name: _await_gateway_decision
arguments: session_key: str, notify_cb, approval_data: dict, *, surface: str='gateway'
doc:
Enqueue *approval_data*, notify the user, and block until resolved or timed
out. Shared by the terminal command guard, the execute_code guard, the plugin
escalation gate, and MCP elicitation. Returns ``{"resolved", "choice",
"reason"}`` or ``{"resolved": False, "choice": None, "notify_failed": True}``
when the notify callback raised. Persisting the choice and building the
tool-facing result stay with the caller.

Identical concurrent approvals (same command text + pattern-key set) are
coalesced: parallel tool calls would otherwise fire N identical prompts
the user must /approve N times while the agent sits wedged. Followers adopt
the leader's ``session``/``always``/``deny``/timeout; a ``once`` covers only
the leader, so the followers fall through to ONE fresh prompt they coalesce on.

name: _drop_entry
doc:
Leave the queue and return the choice committed so far. Reading ``entry.result`` and
removing the entry are one critical section under the approval lock: ``resolve_gateway_approval``
commits under the same lock, so a choice that landed after the deadline check but before this
removal is still ours to honour, and one arriving later finds no entry (the client is told
nothing was pending instead of being acked "ok" while the agent denies).

name: human_wait_ceiling
doc:
Max seconds a single window may contribute: approvals.timeout + margin.
Every legitimate human wait self-terminates at ``approvals.timeout`` (the CLI
prompt join and the gateway poll loop both enforce it), so a window that
overstays this ceiling is itself wedged and must not keep extending a batch
deadline. Also the bound on the authorization gate's serialization-lock
acquire in agent/tool_executor.py, so the two cannot drift. Never call while
holding ``_human_wait_lock`` — it reads the config cache.
``_get_approval_timeout`` caps at ``agent.deadline.MAX_SAFE_TIMEOUT_S`` so the
value is always safe for ``Lock.acquire(timeout=...)`` / ``Thread.join(timeout=...)``.

name: _clamped_window_seconds
arguments: started: float, now: float, ceiling: float
doc:
Seconds an open window contributes: elapsed, floored at 0, capped. Shared
by the close-time accrual and the open-window read so the two clamps stay
identical by construction.

name: _human_wait_state
doc:
Return (creating if needed) the wait state for *session_key*. Caller must
hold ``_human_wait_lock``. Evicts idle entries (no pending waiter)
insertion-order-first until the table is under the cap so an army of
short-lived session keys cannot grow it without bound. Entries with an open
window are never evicted (that would corrupt live accounting), so the cap is
best-effort under 256+ concurrently-pending sessions.

name: activity_heartbeat
doc:
Callable that pings the agent's inactivity tracker (at most every ~10s)
while a human wait is parked, so the gateway watchdog does not kill the agent
while the user is still answering. No-op in minimal tool-only environments.

name: human_wait_window
doc:
Mark the enclosed block as time spent blocked on a human prompt. Wrap ONLY
code that is genuinely parked waiting for a user's answer (the CLI approval
prompt, the gateway approval poll loop). The concurrent tool batch deadline
excludes this time; wrapping anything else re-creates the hang where
arbitrary wedged code pushes the deadline out forever. Overlapping windows
for the same session coalesce (pending counter), so two serialized approval
prompts don't double-count the same wall clock.

See #79719.

name: human_wait_seconds
doc:
Return total human-wait seconds recorded for the session: completed windows
plus the currently open one (if any). Monotonically non-decreasing for the
life of the process — except when an idle session's entry is evicted under
cap pressure, which can only shrink a consumer's baseline delta to zero (the
safe direction: the deadline fires sooner). Deadline consumers snapshot a
baseline at batch start and use the delta. Each window's contribution is
clamped to :func:`human_wait_ceiling` (belt-and-braces against the
wedged-window hang).

Each window's contribution is clamped to :func:`human_wait_ceiling`: every legitimate human wait
self-terminates at ``approvals.timeout`` (both the CLI prompt join and the gateway poll loop enforce
it), so a window that overstays that bound is itself wedged and must not keep extending a batch deadline
(belt-and-braces for #79719).

name: prompt_dangerous_approval
arguments: command: str, description: str, timeout_seconds: int | None=None, allow_permanent: bool=True, approval_callback=None, *, allow_session: bool=True, smart_denied: bool=False, title: str | None=None
doc:
Prompt the user to approve a dangerous command (CLI only).

allow_permanent=False hides [a]lways. allow_session=False hides
[s]ession too — the caller grants one operation and re-asks next time (the
protected agent-instruction gate in ``tools/file_tools.py``); offering a scope
the caller discards makes every later write re-prompt and reads as broken.
smart_denied: owner override of a Smart DENY, offer only once/deny.
title: header for the plain-input prompt when the question is not a dangerous command
("Save to memory?", "<server> is asking"); the default header stays the dangerous-command one.
approval_callback: CLI prompt_toolkit callback ``(command, description, *,
allow_permanent=True, allow_session=True, smart_denied=False) -> str``; legacy
signatures keep working while both keywords hold their defaults.

Returns 'once', 'session', 'always', 'deny', 'timeout', or 'cancelled'. 'timeout'
means no user response — still blocked (fail-closed), but callers report "no
response" rather than an explicit denial. 'cancelled' is an :class:`Unanswered`
sentinel: the prompt never reached a human (callback raised, no callback under
prompt_toolkit, interrupted read) and ``.cause`` says why (#22992).

See #81887.

name: _read_choice
doc: Read one answer on a daemon thread; None when the user never answered.

name: callback_accepts
doc:
True when *callback* takes ``keyword`` (or ``**kwargs``); approval callbacks predate ``title``
and a TypeError inside the callback would read as a deny.

name: _ask_human
arguments: command: str, description: str, timeout_seconds: int, allow_permanent: bool, approval_callback, allow_session: bool, smart_denied: bool, title: str | None=None

name: get_plugin_manager
doc: Lazy plugin-manager seam used by tests and early tool-only imports.

name: _attempt
doc: Result shape of :func:`_present_with_selected_transport` once a transport is selected.

name: _present_with_selected_transport
arguments: *, command: str, description: str, pattern_key: str, pattern_keys: list[str], session_key: str, surface: str, allow_session: bool, allow_permanent: bool
doc:
Present through an explicitly selected plugin transport, if any. A selected
transport replaces every built-in prompt surface; detection, allowed scopes,
persistence, timeout, and final authorization stay host-owned. A failed
transport reaches a built-in surface only under the explicit
``transport_fallback: builtin`` opt-in.

name: _transport_choice
arguments: attempt: dict, *, pattern_key: str, description: str
doc:
Interpret a ``_present_with_selected_transport`` attempt into
``(choice, denied_result)``: both None when the built-in surfaces should run
(no transport selected, or a failure with the explicit builtin fallback); a
denied result for any other failure; else the user's choice.

name: _consent
doc: Map an approval choice to an elicitation verdict; *unresolved* is the no-answer outcome.

name: request_elicitation_consent
arguments: message: str, description: str, *, timeout_seconds: int | None=None, surface: str='mcp-elicitation', title: str='Confirm this action?'
doc:
Route an MCP elicitation request to the surface owning the active session:
gateway sessions through ``_await_gateway_decision``, CLI/TUI through
``prompt_dangerous_approval``. Always fails closed: a missing notify_cb in a
gateway session, timeouts, and exceptions map to ``"decline"`` so a server
treats them as "user did not approve" rather than retrying or hanging.
Returns ``"accept" | "decline" | "cancel"``.

name: _strip_line_comment
doc:
Remove a trailing ``# comment`` from one shell line, quote-aware
(``echo "hello # world"`` survives).

name: _strip_shell_comments
doc:
Strip unquoted ``# ...`` comments before LLM assessment. Not a POSIX parser
— quoted ``#`` and heredoc bodies are preserved by a simple state machine; the
goal is removing the low-hanging injection surface, not full shell parsing.

name: _get_smart_policy
doc: Operator rules (``approvals.smart_policy``) appended to the guardian's system prompt.

name: _verdict_reasoning
doc:
Thinking off for the verdict, unless the operator set reasoning for the approval task
(``auxiliary.approval.reasoning_effort`` or ``extra_body.reasoning``). A one-word verdict needs
no thinking, and a reasoning model otherwise spends the whole 16-token budget thinking and
returns nothing (a local Qwen 27B: 45 of 45 verdicts came back empty).

name: _smart_approve
doc:
Ask the auxiliary LLM; return 'approve', 'deny', or 'escalate' (uncertain/failed).

Inspired by OpenAI Codex's Smart Approvals guardian subagent (openai/codex#13860).

name: _smart_verdict
arguments: command: str, description: str, pattern_key: str, pattern_keys: list[str], session_key: str
doc:
Run the guardian LLM with observer hooks; 'approve' | 'deny' | 'escalate'.
Redaction is observer-payload preparation, not approval policy: if it fails,
skip observability rather than leak raw data or block the LLM decision.

name: _persist
arguments: persist: Persist, enabled: bool, session_key: str

name: toggle_session_yolo
arguments: session_key: str, enabled: Optional[bool]=None, *, persisted: bool=False, persist: Persist=None
doc:
Flip (``enabled=None``) or set the bypass for *session_key*; returns the new state.

*persisted* is the stored flag: after a restart only it is set and the user still sees ON, so a toggle
turns it OFF. The write runs BEFORE the live flip, so a turn restoring in between never revives a
bypass that is being switched off.

name: restore_session_yolo
doc:
Re-arm a persisted bypass in a fresh process; True when this call turned it on.

Key it on the id approvals are checked under (the stored session id / routing key), never a
transport-local id. Skipped under the frozen process ``--yolo``, which already bypasses everything.

name: apply_launch_yolo
doc:
Seed a gateway-owned session's launch ``--yolo`` policy once per session boundary.

Called every turn of such a route; only the first call (or the first after ``clear_session``) arms it,
so a later ``/yolo`` off sticks instead of lasting one turn. Skipped under the frozen process ``--yolo``.

name: restore_gateway_yolo
arguments: session_key: str, persisted: Optional[bool], *, launch: bool=False
doc:
Restore the authoritative routing value, including OFF, before frozen launch seeding.

``persisted`` None means nobody toggled this route: the ``--yolo`` launch policy (*launch*) is seeded
once per boundary instead, so an untouched entry never reads as a revocation.

name: transfer_session_yolo
doc:
Move the live bypass when the conversation continues under a new id (compression rotation, /branch).
The new row records it at creation (``with_session_yolo``), so nothing is written here. Every
continuation site calls this, so it also moves the chat's MCP spend total: a rotation must not hand a
chat that spent its limit a fresh budget.

name: with_session_yolo
doc:
``model_config`` for a session row being created, carrying a live bypass. Rows are created lazily on
the first turn, so this is where a toggle made before the row existed gets recorded.

name: coerce_tool_args
doc: Coerce string-typed args to their JSON-Schema types; originals kept on failure.

name: _schema_accepts_kind
arguments: schema: Any, kind: str, root_schema: Any=None, seen_schema_ids: frozenset[int]=frozenset()
doc: True when *schema* permits JSON type *kind* via ``type`` or any anyOf/oneOf/allOf branch.

name: _normalize_json_strings_for_schema
arguments: value: Any, schema: Any, root_schema: Any=None
doc:
Recursively parse JSON-encoded strings where the schema expects array/object.

Schema-guided: a string is only parsed when its schema position expects a
container, so legitimate JSON-looking ``type: string`` fields survive.

name: restore_undelivered_completions
doc:
Enqueue durable pending completions as fresh turns after process start.
Restored events are stamped ``restored=True`` in memory only: they came from a PREVIOUS
process, so drains without an ownership filter must leave them for a consumer that can
prove ownership. Rows older than ``_MAX_COMPLETION_REPLAY_AGE_S`` are terminally dropped
instead of replaying a turn nobody is waiting on.

Every restored event is stamped ``restored=True`` (in-memory only — the stamp is added after the durable
payload is deserialized and is never persisted). Restored events originate from a *previous* process, so
no consumer in THIS process implicitly owns them: drain paths that run without an ownership filter (the
legacy single-session behavior) must leave them queued for a consumer that can positively prove
ownership, otherwise a brand-new session adopts a dead session's delegation results seconds after boot
(#64484).

name: sweep_orphaned_completions
doc:
Offer this home's completions whose owner died after THIS process started (#97202).

Startup replay (``restore_undelivered_completions``) covers owners that died before the process
started; this covers the rest while it runs. Abandoned in-flight rows are first classified by
``recover_abandoned_delegations``. A terminal row qualifies when it is pending with an event, idle
past ``_ORPHAN_STALE_S``, not under a live delivery claim, and its owner fails the shared liveness
check. A row is offered once per live in-memory copy: a consumer that discards the copy with the row
still pending hands it back for the next sweep. The consumer's ``claim_completion_delivery`` stays
the atomic cross-process gate, so two processes offering one row never both deliver it. Rows past
the delivery budget or the replay age converge to ``dropped``. Reads the current profile's ledger:
callers bind the owning profile first.

arguments: delegation_id: str, result: Any, status: str
doc:

``result`` is a dict or a callable receiving the record snapshot (stall path). The record
stays active ("finalizing") until durable persistence and queue publication finish; otherwise
process shutdown can kill this daemon worker after status flips but before SQLite commits.
A second call for the same id (late runner return after a forced stall) is a no-op.

doc:

(``is_batch``) carry the per-task ``results`` list (plus live transcript paths, the
full-fidelity record of each child's run) instead of a single summary. Best-effort: failure
must not crash the worker, but it WOULD mean a silently-lost result, so we log loudly.

The queued event is the parent's in-process copy and honours ``security.redact_secrets: false``;
``_persist_completion`` re-scrubs with force for the durable row (and the worker IPC).

Surface ONE failed child of a still-running detached batch to the parent now, instead of
when the slowest sibling finishes. In a 1,393-agent run every wave-1 child died in a 401 storm
at 08:29 and the parent learned of it at 09:36, when the batch's "unknown outcome" block finally
arrived: 66 minutes of a dead wave with nothing running. The notice rides the same
``type="async_delegation"`` event shape as the batch result (so every drain/route/format path
treats it identically) with ``task_failure_notice=True`` and a single-entry ``results`` list; the
batch record is NOT finalized and its consolidated result still arrives as before. In-process
queue only (never persisted), so the parent's copy honours ``security.redact_secrets: false``.

name: _ensure_stale_monitor
doc:
Start (once) the stale-delegation monitor thread. One daemon thread serves
every dispatch; it exits when no monitorable records remain and is restarted
by the next dispatch with a ``progress_fn``.

name: _sweep_stale_locked
doc:
One monitor pass over ``_records``; caller holds ``_records_lock``. Returns
``(stalled, expired, any_monitorable)``: newly-stalling ``(delegation_id, quiet_for, in_tool)``
tuples, stalling ids past the grace window, and whether anything is left to monitor.

name: _call_interrupt
doc: Invoke an ``interrupt_fn``; True on success, else debug-log ``msg`` (+ exc).

name: _stale_monitor_loop
doc:
Sweep running delegations for stalled progress. A changed progress token refreshes the
record's timestamp; a frozen token past the idle/in-tool threshold marks the record
``stalling`` and calls ``interrupt_fn``; a ``stalling`` record still unreturned after the
grace window is force-finalized with a terminal ``stalled`` event.

name: _stalled_error_text
doc:
Human wording for a force-finalized stall. This string reaches the user (CLI timeline, Desktop
async-result card), so it names the task, how long it was silent, and what to do — no issue
numbers or worker internals (those stay in the log line and the stall_* metadata).

name: _stalled_result
doc: Synthetic terminal result for a stalling delegation whose runner never returned.

name: _children_activity_from_token
list_async_delegations
doc:
Snapshot of async delegations (running + recently completed) without callables or private
monitor bookkeeping; adds computed live fields for UIs (``seconds_since_progress``,
``children_activity``/``in_tool`` sampled from ``progress_fn``) and stall context once tripped.

Safe to call from any thread. See #51690.

name: _interrupt_records
arguments: targets: list[dict[str, Any]], caller: str, reason: str, msg: str
doc: Call ``interrupt_fn`` on each record; log ``msg`` once; returns how many succeeded.

name: interrupt_all
doc:
Signal every running async delegation to stop (``/stop``, shutdown). Returns how
many. The child still emits a completion event (status='interrupted') via the
normal finalize path.

name: interrupt_for_session
arguments: session_key: str='', origin_ui_session_id: str='', parent_session_id: str='', reason: str='session_end'
doc:
Signal running async delegations owned by ONE ending session to stop (any
selector matches, see ``_session_records``). Returns how many.

name: refuse_for_session
doc:
Refuse new dispatches for ONE closing session (any selector matches) until ``allow_for_session``.
Set before ``interrupt_for_session``: a dispatch registered first is interrupted, a later one refused.

name: allow_for_session
doc: Lift ONE session's refusal: a viewer attached again, or the owner retired its live state.

name: _unfence
doc: Drop *token*'s refusal; caller holds ``_records_lock``.

name: _reset_for_tests
doc: Test-only: clear all state and tear down the executor + monitor.

name: transcript_tail
arguments: path: str, *, lines: int=TAIL_LINES, chars: int=TAIL_CHARS
doc: Last ``lines`` lines (at most ``chars`` characters) of a live transcript; None when unreadable.

name: git_state_hint
doc: ``branch @ sha (N uncommitted file(s))`` for the owner's cwd; None when not a git checkout.

name: sniff_container
doc: Return a CONTAINER_TO_EXT key from magic bytes, or ``None`` when unknown.

name: sniff_audio_ext
doc:
Return a container-matching extension, or ``fallback_ext`` when unknown.
Callers *claim* audio, so generic MP4 maps to ``.m4a`` (payload is AAC regardless
of brand; STT accepts both but voice-bubble routing keys off audio extensions).

name: _lower_suffix
doc: Lower-cased final ``.suffix`` of ``path`` ("" when there is no dot).

name: _strip_sidecar_marker
doc:
Return the database suffix a lower-cased sidecar suffix hangs off
(``.db-wal`` -> ``.db``), or None when ``suffix`` is not a SQLite sidecar.

name: _has_extension_in
doc:
Case-insensitive check on the final ``.suffix``; pure string, no I/O.
A SQLite sidecar counts as its database's extension (only SQLite suffixes
are stripped, so ``x.docx-wal`` stays unrecognised).

name: is_sqlite_sidecar
doc:
True for ``x.db-wal`` / ``x.sqlite3-shm`` / ``x.db-journal`` paths.
Pure string, no I/O — a sidecar path is never a legitimate text target
even when no sidecar exists on disk (a checkpointed db has none).

name: _split_frontmatter
doc: Return the parsed YAML frontmatter mapping, or None if absent/invalid.

name: parse_blueprint
doc:
Extract a BlueprintSpec from a SKILL.md string, or None if not a blueprint.

A skill is a blueprint iff ``metadata.hermes.blueprint`` is a mapping with a
non-empty ``schedule``. Raises BlueprintError if the block exists but is
structurally invalid (so a typo surfaces instead of silently no-op'ing).

name: blueprint_spec_for_installed
doc:
Find ``<skill_name>/SKILL.md`` anywhere in the skills tree and parse its
blueprint block; None when not found or not a blueprint.

name: blueprint_to_job_spec
doc:
``cron.jobs.create_job`` kwargs for a spec — the single translation used by
both ``create_blueprint_job`` and the suggestion path so they never drift.

name: create_blueprint_job
arguments: spec: BlueprintSpec, *, origin: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, name: Optional[str]=None
doc: Create the cron job for a spec (skill preloaded via ``skills=[name]``); returns the job dict.

name: register_blueprint_suggestion
doc:
Register an installed blueprint as a Suggested Cron Job (never auto-scheduled;
the user accepts or dismisses it). None when skipped (seen/dismissed/backlog full).

name: export_blueprint
arguments: job: dict[str, Any], body: str, *, blueprint_name: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Inverse of ``create_blueprint_job``: render a cron job as a SKILL.md (with a
``metadata.hermes.blueprint`` block) ready for ``hermes skills publish``.
``body`` becomes the SKILL.md body; its first line is the description.

name: _schedule_to_string
doc: Best-effort render of a parsed schedule dict back to a string.

name: retry_action
doc: Map a failure reason to the bot-turn retry action (see policy above).

name: turn_failure_text
arguments: stdout: str | None, stderr: str | None
doc:
The error text of a failed ``hermes … -Q`` delivery turn: both streams, in the order the CLI
writes them. The provider prose is the turn's final_response and lands on STDOUT; stderr carries
session bookkeeping (``session_id: …``) on every run, so ``stderr or stdout`` only ever saw the
banner and every transient failure classified as ``unknown``.

The in-process lanes hand over the same two pieces of prose as an agent result dict
(``error`` + ``failure_reason``); ``result_retry_action`` joins them here too, so one classifier
sees every lane's failure text.

name: result_retry_action
doc:
The retry action for a finished IN-PROCESS turn (an ``_run_agent`` result dict).

The transport-agnostic twin of the child-process lanes' ``retry_action(classify_agent_error(
turn_failure_text(stdout, stderr)))``: same policy, the failure text just arrives as result fields
instead of two streams — ``error`` carries the raw provider summary (status codes included) and
``failure_reason`` the turn loop's own typed verdict, which is what names an overflow the copy only
describes in prose. ``RETRY_NONE`` for anything that did not fail (and for a non-dict result), so a
successful turn whose text happens to mention 429 is never re-run.

name: classify_agent_error
doc: Map raw agent/provider error text to a closed reason code (``unknown`` when unmatched/empty).

name: delivery_failure_reason
doc:
The typed reason for a delivery refusal, kept inside the documented vocabulary.

An exception's own ``reason`` is trusted only when it names a real code: ``TurnBusyError``
carries ``target_busy``, but ``reason`` is also a stdlib attribute on ``ssl.SSLError`` and
``urllib.error.URLError``, and forwarding one of those would put free text where consumers
expect a closed set. Anything else is classified like every other failure. Shared by the
relay lane (``bot_relay.deliver``) and the local runner (``bot_mode_dm --run-delivery``).

name: _bot_chat_tip
doc: Current Bot Chat tip id, or None when the profile has no store or no Bot Chat yet.

name: find_canonical_live_owner
doc:
Discover the profile authority and its exact Bot Chat without acquiring a lease.

``session_id`` is the current Bot Chat tip, or ``''`` when the profile has none yet: the
authority's deliver door creates it on first delivery (main's ``--create-if-missing``),
so a missing chat is not a refusal. None only when the profile has no store at all.

name: authority_delivery
doc: Call only this home's already-running authority; never start a fallback.

name: authority_settle
doc:
The same authority's ``bot_relay.settle``: the delivery id settled as never sent, or its
existing receipt (``gateway/session_bot.py:_settle``).

name: _owner
arguments: home: Path | str, owner: dict[str, Any]

name: has_mailbox
doc:
Whether any delivery was ever admitted for this profile (the mailbox directory is created on
first admission only). A cheap pre-check for pollers: no mailbox means nothing to claim, so the
owner lookup — a state.db open plus the exclusive active-session registry lock — can be skipped.

name: _dir_owner
doc: Best-effort owner name for the log line; never raises (an ACL that hides it is the reported case).

name: _prepare
doc: Create/harden the mailbox dir and its ``.lock`` file; returns the lock path.

name: _locked
doc:
Hold the mailbox dir lock. A dir this token cannot use raises ``MailboxUnusable``
(logged once per dir with its owner and the remedy); errors inside the body pass through.

name: _read
doc: Exact-id read: absent → None; unreadable or not a JSON object → raises (callers fail closed).

name: _ticket_shape_error
doc:
Why a parsed ticket is unusable by the scans, or None when it is well-formed.

A ticket that parses as JSON but lost a field (truncated rewrite, foreign
writer, hand edit) used to raise KeyError/TypeError out of the sequence
scan and the claim sweep — wedging admission and delivery for the whole
profile exactly like corrupt JSON did before ``_scan_read`` existed.

name: _scan_read
doc:
Bulk-scan variant: one unreadable or malformed ticket must not wedge the whole dir.

Directory scans (sequence high-water mark, queued-claim sweep) may only
treat a file as absent when it is provably absent; an unreadable ticket
degrades to "that one delivery is uninspectable" with a warning.
Exact-id reads (admission idempotency, completion, result lookup) keep
using _read so a permission error still fails closed instead of
licensing an overwrite of a possibly-live receipt.

name: _next_sequence
doc:
Allocate the next admission sequence under the dir lock.

The high-water mark lives in a counter file beside the tickets, so a ticket
the scan cannot read does not drop its sequence and hand a later admission
a duplicate or lower one. Readable tickets still bootstrap dirs written
before the counter existed. Wall time can roll back; sequences never do.

name: deliver_to_live_owner
arguments: profile_home: Path | str, owner: dict[str, Any], message: str, *, delivery_id: str | None=None, author: dict[str, Any] | None=None, notification_category: str='result'
doc:
Return durable admission immediately, without waiting for the owner.

Retry with the same id AND pinned owner/message to inspect the existing
state. Reusing an id with a different payload is an error, never an overwrite.

name: settle_held_delivery
arguments: profile_home: Path | str, owner: dict[str, Any], message: str, *, delivery_id: str, author: dict[str, Any] | None=None
doc:
Finalize a refusal marked ``admitted: false`` under the same identity: the owner's terminal
not-sent receipt (``refused``), or the receipt of an attempt that admitted the id meanwhile.

name: _door
arguments: call: Callable[[Path, dict], dict], profile_home, owner, message, *, delivery_id=None, author=None, notification_category='result'

name: owner_holds_delivery
doc:
Whether the profile authority still holds ``record`` (main's bounded DM wait asks this).

An admission lives in the authority's durable FIFO, so it is held while the authority is
reachable; an unreachable one raises (outcome unknown, never cancelled). Only an unadmitted
legacy record whose profile has no store is provably ownerless.

name: claim_pending_delivery
doc:
Retired UI poller: only session_bot may migrate and admit queued records.

Keep this refusal until the legacy notification poller's call site is removed.
A previously claimed record can still publish its terminal receipt below.

name: complete_delivery
arguments: profile_home: Path | str, delivery_id: str, *, status: str, reply: str='', error: str='', reason: str=''
doc: Persist an immutable terminal receipt; duplicate identical completion is safe.

name: cancel_queued_delivery
arguments: profile_home: Path | str, delivery_id: str, *, error: str, reason: str
doc:
Cancel an ownerless queued receipt without racing a consumer's claim.

A claim or terminal result that won the mailbox lock is returned unchanged.

name: read_delivery_result
doc: Read admission/claim/terminal state without waiting or deleting its receipt.

name: _poll_receipt
doc:
A waiter's read: the receipt file the owner republishes when the admission settles (and on
restart recovery). Never an authority RPC: a wait outlives owner restarts, and replaying the
envelope (``read_delivery_result``) is for producers re-confirming their admission.

name: await_delivery
arguments: profile_home: Path | str, delivery_id: str, timeout: float | None, *, should_stop: Callable[[], bool] | None=None
doc:
Poll a receipt until the owner settles it, ``timeout`` lapses, or ``should_stop`` says so.

Every transport that hands a turn to a live Bot Chat owner (local ``message_agent``, the
Desktop relay, ``hermes peer dm`` and ``hermes peer run``) waits on the same receipt; keeping
the loop here is what stops the lanes drifting (one lane returned a receipt sentence instead
of the reply, two never waited at all). Returns the last record read — still pending when the
budget lapsed, None when the receipt was never readable. Polls the local receipt file only, so
an owner restart mid-wait is just a longer pending stretch.

name: await_delivery_async
arguments: profile_home: Path | str, delivery_id: str, timeout: float | None, *, should_stop: Callable[[], bool] | None=None
doc: ``await_delivery`` for an event loop: never blocks a worker thread for the whole budget.

name: message_agent_tool_schema
doc: OpenAI-format schema for ``message_agent`` (injected, not registered).

name: message_agent_authorized
doc:
The ``message_agent`` gate: a protocol-enabled agent whose session is a managed
Bot-Mode canonical Bot Chat. Session-stable, so it is prompt-cache safe to re-evaluate
on every tool-snapshot rebuild. Never raises.

name: ensure_message_agent_tool
doc:
Inject the ``message_agent`` schema into a Bot Chat agent's tool list (once per turn).
Idempotent and deterministic for the session's life (the gate is stable from the
first turn), so the tool list is byte-identical across turns — prompt-cache safe. Never raises.

name: _resolve_local_name
arguments: target: str, roster: list[str], root: Path | None=None
doc:
Map a target to a local profile FOLDER id: 'hermes' → 'default'; an exact folder id
(case-insensitive); else — when ``root`` is given — a friendly name or its Desktop @-slug
(profile.yaml ``display_name`` / Bot Mode title: 'Scribe', '@scribe', 'Dr. Foo' → 'foo').
Ambiguous friendly names resolve to None so a DM never lands on the wrong bot (#100671).

name: _err
arguments: message: str, *, roster: list[str] | None=None, peers: list[str] | None=None

name: message_agent_tool
arguments: target: str='', message: str='', task_id: Optional[str]=None, agent: Any=None
doc:
Deliver ``message`` to ``target``'s Bot Chat. Returns a JSON ack/error.
``agent`` is the calling AIAgent — used for the Bot Chat gate and sender identity.

name: _try_relay_delivery
arguments: root: Path, raw_target: str, content: str, me: str, *, task_id: Optional[str], agent: Any
doc:
Cross-connection delivery via the Desktop relay; None when the target doesn't
resolve against the relay roster. The envelope is queued on disk for the Desktop
to drain; a background waiter is spawned immediately so the relayed reply wakes
the sender through the standard completion-notification path.

name: cleanup_bot_dm_cache
_write_dm_file
doc: The message rides a temp file — never inline shell text.

name: _delivery_lock
doc:
Per-profile turn lock for a LOCAL teammate delivery: local and relay deliveries
into one profile both run a Bot Chat turn here, so the turn window is serialized on
``tools.bot_relay``'s cross-process lock. Peer transports (stdin mode) are locked
on the remote gateway by its own deliver path.

See #93091.

name: _live_intent_file
doc: The pinned live-delivery intent beside a DM file (the cache sweep globs ``*.live.json``).

name: _dm_delivery_id
doc:
One delivery id per DM file: the dispatch ack, the live-owner intent and every retry
of the runner derive it the same way, so the sender can correlate all of them.

name: _settled_no_send
doc:
The answer to a definite no-send, for both the tool and its runner: first the payload and
any pinned intent go, so nothing local can rebuild or replay the delivery. A file that is still
there is not settlement: the answer is then the unknown outcome, never "safe to resend".

name: _held_disposition
doc:
The owner's terminal not-sent receipt for a delivery refused while another writer held the
chat (``gateway/session_bot.py:_not_sent_record``).

name: _admit_live_dm
arguments: profile_home: Path | None, dm_file: str, author: Optional[dict]=None
doc: Pin intent before admission; retries may inspect, never change transport.

name: _wait_live_dm
arguments: home: str, delivery_id: str, *, dm_file: str | os.PathLike | None=None

name: _live_outcome_unknown
doc: The runner's stdout when a live admission may have happened but its outcome is unknown.

name: _runner_argv
doc:
Split ``--run-delivery [--author <json>] <mode> <dm_file> <argv…>`` into
``(author_json, mode, dm_file, argv)``; None when malformed. Stdlib only: the boot-failure
report runs it when no Hermes import is available.

name: _run_delivery
arguments: argv: list[str], dm_file: str, *, stdin_file: bool, profile_home: Path | None=None, author: Optional[dict]=None
doc:
Admit local DMs only through the profile authority; retain uncertain intent.

The optional peer stdin transport remains an explicit remote route, never a
fallback after local admission. Background processes wait for delivery only.

name: _delivery_command
arguments: argv: list[str], dm_file: str, *, stdin_file: bool, profile_home: Path | None=None, author: Optional[dict]=None
doc:
Build an argv-safe command for the cleanup-owning background runner:
``--run-delivery [--author <json>] <mode> <dm_file> [--profile-home <path>] <argv...>``.

name: _start_delivery
arguments: argv: list[str], content: str, label: str, *, stdin_file: bool, task_id: Optional[str], agent: Any, profile_home: Path | None=None, author: Optional[dict]=None
doc: Create a DM file and transfer its cleanup ownership to the runner.

name: _spawn_delivery
arguments: command: str, label: str, *, dm_file: Optional[str]=None, delivery_id: Optional[str]=None, task_id: Optional[str], agent: Any
doc:
Launch the cleanup-owning runner and transfer file ownership on ack. ``dm_file``
