is None for relay deliveries (the waiter watches a reply file; envelope artifacts
are owned/swept by ``tools/bot_relay.py``), which pass the envelope id as ``delivery_id``
instead. The ack is ``queued`` + ``delivery_id`` like the live-owner branch: hand-off
to a background process, never a delivery receipt.

name: _persist_reply_when_done
doc:
#101142 durable leg. A non-push sender (api_server, one-shot runner) gets no completion
notification, so once the tracked runner exits its stdout — the recipient's reply or the
delivery failure — is appended to the sender's session transcript as a DELIVERY row
(``display_kind="process_complete"``, the shape push surfaces persist for the same
completion; mirrors gateway.wake.persist_delegation_delivery). A sender that already read
the outcome via process(action='wait'/'log') is not told twice. Returns False (nothing
armed) when the sender has no session transcript or the process is not tracked here.

name: _wait_reply_main
arguments: reply_path: str, label: str, budget_seconds: str
doc:
The relay reply waiter (``tools/bot_relay.waiter_command``): block until the sender-side
reply file exists, print it as the completion notification the sender wakes on, exit 1 on a
delivery error or when the budget runs out. Stdlib only: this runs as a background process
from any bot turn, and the sender's completion notification is exactly its stdout.

name: _delivery_main
doc:
Runner entry for the argv ``_delivery_command`` and ``bot_relay.waiter_command`` build.
Malformed argv exits 2 without touching the DM file.

name: _agent_home
doc: The calling agent's OWN home (session-db derived), not ambient env.

name: strip_legacy_protocol
doc: SOUL text without the plugin-era "## Messaging other agents" section (idempotent).

name: _default_home
doc: Ambient process HERMES_HOME (env, else the platform default) as a string.

name: _swallow
doc: ``fn()`` or ``default`` on any exception — the probe must never crash a prompt build.

name: _hermes_root
doc: Root ~/.hermes for both the default profile and named profiles.

name: _roster
doc:
(name, dir) for the default profile + every live named profile, sorted. Same identity
predicate as ``profile list``: infra dirs (``sessions/``, ``logs/``) and tombstones are not
teammates (#99392), and neither is a marker-carrying dir whose name is not a profile id —
a parked backup or staging dir must never become a ``message_agent`` target (#116905).

name: _read_yaml_dict
doc:
YAML mapping at ``path``, or None when missing / not a mapping / unreadable. ``needle``:
cheap substring precheck that skips the YAML parse on the dominant (unmanaged) path.

name: _bots_meta
doc: The ``ui_meta['hermes-bots']`` block of a parsed profile.yaml, if a dict.

name: is_bot_mode_managed
doc:
True when ANY profile on this install is Bot-Mode-managed. Never raises. The
``message_agent`` injection gate — deliberately independent of the protocol section's
emptiness: a SOUL.md carrying the legacy protocol gets an empty section but still gets the tool.

name: _role_line
doc: 'title — description' from the non-empty parts (either may be absent).

name: _bullet
doc: Roster line: '- `handle`' plus ' — part' for each non-empty part.

name: _profile_role
doc:
Teammate role line: Bot Mode title — profile description; tells a teammate
WHO to message for a job. A friendly ``display_name`` (``hermes profile rename``) that
differs from both the folder id and the title leads the line, so an untagged
"talk to Scribe" maps to the folder handle without a disk search (#100671).
Single-line, ≤160 chars, "" when nothing. Never raises.

name: _friendly_names
doc: (Bot Mode title, profile.yaml ``display_name``) for a profile, "" when unset. Never raises.

name: _display_name
doc:
Human-facing sender name, in the Desktop's ``botFriendlyNames`` order: Bot Mode title,
then profile.yaml ``display_name`` (``hermes profile rename``), else the @handle — the
renamed primary signs as ``Maia (@hermes)``, not ``hermes (@hermes)`` (#89720).

name: alias_forms
doc:
Lower-cased mention forms of a friendly name, mirroring the Desktop's
``mentionNameForms``: slugified (``"Dr. Foo"`` → ``dr-foo``, what autocomplete inserts)
and collapsed (``drfoo``). Reserved tokens and empty forms are dropped.

name: local_alias_map
doc:
``alias form → {folder ids}`` for every local profile's friendly names (profile.yaml
``display_name`` and the Bot Mode title). Folder ids themselves are not aliases: the
caller matches those first, so a target that is an exact folder id always addresses that
folder — a friendly name colliding with ANOTHER folder id never steals it. Ambiguity
(one alias form shared by several profiles) surfaces as a multi-id set. Never raises.

name: _peers
doc:
Registered peer gateway names (``hermes peer``) from config.yaml, read
directly (no config-loader import; the section is absent on most installs). Never raises.

name: _remote_roster
doc: Desktop relay roster (``tools/bot_relay.py``); [] on any failure.

name: local_taken_forms
doc:
Bare forms this gateway's own profiles answer to (handles + friendly-name slugs); a remote
row must not be offered under any of them, since local resolution wins (``_resolve_local_name``).

name: _remote_paragraph
doc: Addendum for agents on OTHER connected machines; only when the relay roster is non-empty.

name: _peer_paragraph
doc: Addendum for cross-machine DMs — only when peers exist.

name: get_bot_mode_protocol_section
arguments: home: str | os.PathLike | None=None, *, force_refresh: bool=False
doc:
Cached probe entry point — one filesystem pass per (process, home). ``home`` should be
the AGENT'S OWN resolved home (session-db derived), not ambient HERMES_HOME — build threads
can lose the ContextVar override and the env var would then name the wrong profile.

name: _model_prompt_capability_surface
doc:
``model.*`` overrides whose flip changes a rebuilt prompt, coerced like their consumers.

``supports_vision`` uses image routing's strict bool so YAML ``yes`` and ``true`` share
one epoch. ``context_length`` is the cap ``build_system_prompt_parts`` uses to truncate
context files. Routing keys (provider, default, base_url) are identity lines, not this
surface — and no model id is special-cased.

name: capability_fingerprint
doc:
12-hex digest of the capability surface for ``home``'s profile: disabled skills +
enabled toolsets + MCP config, model capability overrides that change the prompt
(``supports_vision``, ``context_length``), SOUL.md bytes, installed skill names, the
Bot-Mode roster (+ roles), peers and the relay roster. Deliberately NOT cached — the
point is detecting on-disk drift against a stored prompt's epoch. Never raises
("unavailable" on failure).

name: epoch_line
doc: The epoch stamp appended to a Bot Chat prompt.

name: stored_prompt_capability_stale
arguments: stored_prompt: str, home: str | os.PathLike | None=None
doc:
True when ``stored_prompt`` is a Bot Chat prompt whose embedded epoch no
longer matches disk. Unstamped prompts are never stale. Fails closed to
"not stale" — a broken probe must not become a rebuild-every-turn cache burner.

name: stored_bot_chat_prompt_needs_upgrade
arguments: stored_prompt: str, home: str | os.PathLike | None=None
doc:
True when a Bot Chat session's stored prompt PREDATES the epoch mechanism (no stamp —
including SOUL-era prompts whose frozen roster rode in from SOUL.md). The caller must only
ask for sessions titled "Bot Chat"; we rebuild only when the probe would actually emit a
section, and every rebuilt prompt is stamped so this fires once. Fails closed.

name: _atomic_write_json
arguments: target: Path, payload: Any, *, sort_keys: bool=False

name: _bot_mode_cfg
doc:
``bot_mode.<key>`` from config, read lazily (tools/ must not import CLI
config at import time); None when absent or the config is unreadable.

name: _normalize_roster_row
doc:
Validated, minimal roster row or None. Rows come from the Desktop over
RPC — treat as untrusted input.

name: write_remote_roster
doc: Atomically persist the Desktop-pushed remote roster. Returns count.

name: read_remote_roster
doc: The current remote roster (possibly empty). Never raises.

name: _target_ids
doc: Lower-cased routing ids of a roster row: its @handle and profile folder id.

name: _target_aliases
doc:
Every lower-cased bare form that addresses ``row``: routing ids plus the Bot Mode title's
mention slugs (``"CoS Bot"`` → ``cos-bot``/``cosbot``, what the Desktop picker inserts). A remote
``default`` is ``@hermes`` on every gateway, so its title is the only bare form that can single it out.

name: resolve_remote_target
doc:
Matched row for a bare handle/profile/title slug (unique across connections) or
``<handle|profile|title-slug>@<connection-id>``; ``"ambiguous"`` for a bare form on several
connections; None otherwise. An exact handle/profile match beats a title slug, so a title
colliding with another row's handle never steals it.

name: _title_slug
doc:
The Bot Mode title's slug form (``"CoS Bot"`` → ``cos-bot``, what the picker inserts); "" when the
title is empty, reserved (a bot titled "Hermes") or not a valid handle.

name: remote_target_forms
doc:
One unambiguous target string per row, shortest first: the bare handle when no other remote
row and no LOCAL profile (``local_taken``: this gateway's handles and friendly-name slugs) answers
to it; else the title slug under the same test (a remote ``default`` titled "CoS Bot" is
``@cos-bot``, since bare ``@hermes`` is always this gateway's own default); else
``handle@connection``. Mirrors ``resolve_remote_target``.

name: qualify_sender_stamp
arguments: message: str, from_handle: Any, from_connection: Any, roster: list[dict], local_taken: set[str] | frozenset[str]=frozenset()
doc:
Rewrite a relayed DM's ``Message from 🤖 <name> (@<handle>):`` stamp so the handle is the
form THIS gateway can reply to: the sender's row in the local relay roster as
``remote_target_forms`` renders it, else ``handle@connection``. A relayed ``@hermes`` is another
machine's default — left bare, a reply lands on the recipient's own default (#103731).

name: _envelope_ttl_seconds
doc:
Configured drain TTL (``bot_mode.envelope_ttl_seconds``), read per-drain.
``0`` (or negative) disables expiry.

name: _target_liveness
doc:
Tri-state liveness: True / False / None (unknown → callers fail open). Offline =
explicit ``online: false`` or ABSENT from a *fresh* roster; a missing, unreadable,
empty or stale roster proves nothing → None. Never raises.

name: enqueue_envelope
arguments: root: Path | str, *, target: dict, message: str, sender_profile: str, sender_handle: str
doc:
Queue a cross-connection DM for the Desktop relay; returns the envelope. Raises
``EnvelopeRefusedError`` ('runtime_offline') without writing when the target is
definitively offline; unknown liveness enqueues (fail-open).

name: _expire_if_stale
arguments: root: Path | str, path: Path, ttl: float, now: float
doc:
True when the outbox envelope is older than ``ttl``; writes the 'queued_expired'
reply so the sender's waiter resolves (best effort). Unreadable envelopes are left for the claim.

name: _queued_at
doc:
Claim order for one outbox entry: oldest first. ``mtime`` is what ``_sweep_stale`` already
treats as an envelope's age, and unlike the whole-second ``created_at`` field it separates two
DMs sent in the same second. The name only breaks ties.

name: claim_pending_envelopes
doc:
Drain the outbox (rename → claimed/ so a second drain can't double-deliver).
TTL-expired envelopes get a 'queued_expired' reply and are removed instead.

Envelopes older than ``bot_mode.envelope_ttl_seconds`` are NOT delivered: each gets an error reply
(reason ``'queued_expired'``) so the sender's waiter resolves, and its outbox file is removed (#93091
item 2).

name: _replay_unanswered
arguments: root: Path | str, base: Path, seen: set, now: float
doc:
``claimed/`` canonical envelopes whose reply has not landed yet, replayed on EVERY drain.

A drained envelope is not "delivered": its stable id is handed out again until the target's
terminal reply is written under that id, so a Desktop that disconnects between ``outbox.drain``
and ``bot_relay.deliver`` (#111021, #111207) or loses the drain result cannot drop the DM. The
replay is safe because ``bot_relay.deliver`` forwards the SAME id to the target profile's
authority, which admits one turn per id and answers a retry with the existing record — never a
second turn. Once ``created_at + REPLY_WAIT_SECONDS`` passes with no reply the waiter is gone
(or about to be): a ``delivery_timeout`` reply is written so it learns, and the envelope is
never handed out again. Each envelope comes back with its ``_queued_at`` enqueue key so the
drain can merge it with fresh outbox rows in send order.

name: _settle_pre_upgrade_claim
arguments: root: Path | str, path: Path, env_id: str, label: str, now: float
doc:
A ``claimed/`` envelope from before canonical delivery (no ``canonical_delivery_v1``) is never
replayed: its old lane ran a CLI turn the authority has no record of, so re-admitting the id could
run the DM twice. Left alone, though, its sender's waiter watched a reply that never came. Once the
old drain's own re-offer point passes (``REOFFER_AFTER_SECONDS`` after its claim — the claim mtime
— by which time a live delivery has posted the Desktop's timeout reply) the outcome is settled as
``unknown``: the waiter resolves, the envelope is never offered again, and nothing auto-resends.

name: write_reply
arguments: root: Path | str, envelope_id: str, *, reply: str='', error: str='', reason: str=''
doc:
Persist the relayed reply (or delivery error) for the waiter. ``reason`` (typed
code, ``tools.bot_failure_reasons``) is classified from ``error`` when omitted.

Idempotent by envelope id — the first settled reply stands, error or not. That is safe because
a replayed envelope (``_replay_unanswered``) carries the SAME id into the target authority,
which admits one turn per id, so a later write is a duplicate or a bookkeeping timeout, never
a truer answer.

name: unlink_files_older_than
arguments: directory: Path, pattern: str, cutoff: float
doc: Unlink regular files matching ``pattern`` with mtime before ``cutoff``; returns count. Never raises.

name: cleanup_bot_relay_artifacts
doc:
Hourly sweep of stale relay artifacts (DM plaintext; ``_sweep_stale`` otherwise runs
only on Desktop drains). ``max_age_hours`` is for ``cleanup_*_cache`` signature parity only.

name: waiter_command
doc:
Shell command that blocks until the reply file appears, then prints it; spawned
via ``terminal_tool(background=True, notify_on_complete=True)`` so its stdout arrives
as the same completion notification local DMs use.

A ``tools/bot_mode_dm.py --wait-reply`` entrypoint, like the local delivery runner — not
``python -c``. The approval gate flags inline interpreter code ("script execution via -e/-c
flag"), and ``approvals.single_query_mode`` defaults to ``deny`` for the one-shot ``-Q`` turn a
bot replies from, so the reply waiter was refused exactly when a bot answered a teammate: the
message was delivered, the reply never woke the sender. Roster fields ride as argv (``shlex``
quoted), never as source text, so a hostile handle or connection id stays data.

name: _hermes_cli
doc:
Prefer this install's published launcher, then interpreter/PATH fallbacks.

A long-lived caller can still run in an older dependency generation. Its
sibling console script pins that generation, whereas the published launcher
selects current dependencies at child start. Keep the historical fallbacks
for external/developer installs that have no published launcher (#93590).

name: delivery_turn_author
arguments: from_profile: Any, from_handle: Any, from_connection: Any=None
doc:
The author of a relayed DM's recipient turn, built from the sender fields as the relaying client reports
them. A relayed DM always comes from another gateway, so the id carries the Desktop's id for the sender's
connection (``local`` included) and only the recipient's own profiles are bare ``bot:<profile>``. None when
the envelope names no sender.

name: _delivery_child_session_env_names
doc:
Session-bound env names to strip from a delivery child, from ``gateway.session_context``.

Synced with the session binding surface as vars are added; deliberately NOT a
``HERMES_SESSION_*`` prefix match, which would also strip non-identity knobs
(e.g. ``HERMES_SESSION_STALL_TIMEOUT``).

name: relaying_principal_author
doc:
The author of a relayed DM whose sender fields cannot be trusted: a logged-in client named them.

Server-derived and unspoofable — the id is built from the caller's minted identity digest, never from
anything the client sent — and still a BOT author, because the recipient's memory routes on that:
Honcho writes a bot-authored turn into the bot's own a2a session and refuses conclusion / profile /
mirror writes for it, while an unattributed turn is treated as the human's (#107598 review). The
human-facing signature stays in the message text the sender composed.

name: delivery_env
arguments: author: Optional[dict], profile_home: str | Path | None=None
doc:
Environment for one delivery turn's ``hermes -p <profile>`` child. The dispatcher's own
HERMES_TURN_AUTHOR is dropped first so a delivery without an author never inherits the author of the turn
that sent it. Dispatcher session identity (the canonical ``gateway.session_context`` session env names) is
dropped too: a nested recipient that ``message_agent``s onward must not stamp that grandchild
notify with the grandparent's key, or the live recipient never resumes. The child runs the target
profile's Bot Chat turn, so it starts from THAT profile's env (``served_profile_child_env``: launch
profile ``.env`` / TERMINAL_* residue dropped, target secrets overlaid), never the multiplexer's raw
``os.environ``; ``-p`` alone only pinned HERMES_HOME. ``profile_home`` is the target's home when the
caller knows it (relay RPC, roster); otherwise the active override, and under multiplex the launch
home.

name: turn_wait_seconds
doc: Wait budget for a queued delivery turn (config, lazily read).

name: turn_lock_path
doc: Per-profile lockfile path (short — safe on macOS temp roots).

name: acquire_turn_lock
arguments: root: Path | str, profile: str, timeout_seconds: float | None=None
doc:
Hold ``profile``'s cross-process turn lock for the ``with`` body: non-blocking
flock probe + short-sleep retry up to the budget (``bot_mode.turn_wait_seconds``
unless ``timeout_seconds``); raises :class:`TurnBusyError` when exhausted. No
ordering among waiters, but every waiter is bounded. Without ``fcntl`` (Windows)
the lock is a no-op — those installs never had this race path.

name: _get_command_timeout
doc: ``browser.command_timeout`` (floor 5s, default 30s), cached per profile home after first read.

name: _auth_headers
doc: Return Authorization header when CAMOFOX_API_KEY is set.

name: get_camofox_url
doc: Return the configured Camofox server URL, or empty string.

name: _config_cdp_url
doc:
Persistent ``browser.cdp_url`` from config.yaml, or "" (read here, not via
``browser_tool_cdp._get_cdp_override`` — circular import).

name: is_camofox_mode
doc:
True when the Camofox backend is selected and no CDP override is active.

Selection is ``browser.cloud_provider: camofox``; ``CAMOFOX_URL`` is only the address
and never overrides a different stored selection (legacy: with no selection ever
written, a set ``CAMOFOX_URL`` still activates Camofox). A CDP override (``BROWSER_CDP_URL``
env or ``browser.cdp_url``, same precedence as ``browser_tool_cdp._get_cdp_override()``) wins.

name: check_camofox_available
doc: Verify the Camofox server is reachable (and cache its VNC URL once).

name: get_vnc_url
doc: Return the VNC URL if the Camofox server exposes one, or None.

name: _get_camofox_config
doc: Return the ``browser.camofox`` config block, or an empty dict.

name: _managed_persistence_enabled
doc: ``browser.camofox.managed_persistence``: stable profile-scoped userId vs random per session.

name: _env_or_cfg
arguments: env_name: str, camofox_cfg: dict[str, Any], cfg_key: str, *, secret: bool=False
doc: Env/secret-scope value first, then the ``browser.camofox`` config key, else "".

name: _camofox_identity_override
doc:
Externally configured identity (integrations owning the visible Camofox browser
share a user ID so Hermes uses the same profile), or None.

name: _flag
arguments: env_name: str, camofox_cfg: dict[str, Any], cfg_key: str
doc: Boolean toggle: env var wins when set to a valid value, else config key.

name: _rewrite_loopback_url_for_camofox
doc:
Rewrite loopback page URLs for Docker-hosted Camofox, if configured.

``CAMOFOX_URL`` may point at a host-published Docker port, but page URLs are opened by
the browser *inside* the container, where loopback is the container, not the host.
Opt-in (``CAMOFOX_REWRITE_LOOPBACK_URLS`` / config) because non-Docker installs run the
browser on the host. Returns ``(rewritten_url, metadata)``; ``metadata`` is present only
when a rewrite happened so the tool result can disclose the change to the model.

name: _adopt_existing_tab
doc:
Rehydrate tab_id from an already-open managed tab: gateway restarts empty the
in-memory cache while Camofox still holds the integration-owned tab.

name: _get_session
doc:
Get or create the task's session. Identity precedence: external override
(CAMOFOX_USER_ID / config) → profile-scoped identity when managed persistence
is on → random ephemeral userId.

name: _ensure_tab
doc: Ensure a tab exists for the session, creating one if needed.

name: _drop_session
doc: Remove and return session info.

name: camofox_soft_cleanup
doc:
Drop only the local tracking entry (``True``) for managed profiles, which must
survive across agent tasks; ``False`` for ephemeral sessions so the caller falls back
to :func:`camofox_close`.

name: _request
arguments: method: str, path: str, timeout: Optional[int]=None, **kwargs: Any
doc: Issue an authenticated request to camofox and return the raised-for-status response.

significant_calls.expression:
getattr(requests, method)(f"{get_camofox_url()}{path}", headers=_auth_headers(),
                                     timeout=_get_command_timeout() if timeout is None else timeout, **kwargs)

name: _post
arguments: path: str, body: dict, timeout: Optional[int]=None

name: _get
arguments: path: str, params: dict | None=None, timeout: Optional[int]=None

name: _get_raw
arguments: path: str, params: dict | None=None, timeout: Optional[int]=None
doc: GET and return the raw response (for binary data).

name: _delete
arguments: path: str, body: dict | None=None, timeout: Optional[int]=None

name: _parse_snapshot_images
doc:
Images from an accessibility snapshot: ``img "alt" [eN]`` entries with the URL on
the following ``/url:`` line (Camofox has no /images endpoint).

name: _fetch_snapshot
doc:
``(snapshot_text, refs_count)`` truncated like the main browser tool (line boundaries,
full tree stored to cache/web, read_file pointer appended). Lazy import: ``browser_tool``
imports this module.

name: _navigate_tab
doc:
Open ``browser_url`` in the task's tab (creating it if missing) and return
``(session, navigate_response)``. A 404 on the existing tab means the server
garbage-collected it — recreate instead of failing.

name: camofox_navigate
doc: Navigate to a URL via Camofox.

name: _camofox_private_page_block
arguments: session: dict[str, Any], task_id: Optional[str], action: str
doc:
Blocked payload when the current page is private/internal, else None.

Mirrors the ``_camofox_eval`` guard in browser_tool.py: page-state reads on a non-local
backend can leak an intranet/metadata page the terminal can't reach. Only active when
the SSRF guard applies (non-local backend, not a local sidecar, ``allow_private_urls``
unset); fail-open on probe failure like sibling guards. Lazy import (cycle).

name: _require_tab
doc: Return ``(session, error_payload)``: error when no tab exists or, if ``action`` given, the page is private.

name: _with_tab
arguments: task_id: Optional[str], guard_action: Optional[str], body: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], str]
doc:
Require a tab (+ private-page guard when ``guard_action`` is set), then run ``body(session)``;
any exception becomes a ``tool_error``.

name: _tab_action
arguments: task_id: Optional[str], guard_action: Optional[str], suffix: str, body: dict[str, Any], result: Callable[[dict], dict]
doc: Simple tab action: POST ``body`` to ``/tabs/<id>/<suffix>``, build the result.

name: camofox_snapshot
arguments: full: bool=False, task_id: Optional[str]=None, user_task: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Accessibility tree snapshot. ``user_task`` is deprecated and ignored —
oversized snapshots always truncate-and-store (no LLM summarization).

name: camofox_click
doc: Click an element by ref via Camofox.

name: camofox_type
arguments: ref: str, text: str, task_id: Optional[str]=None
doc: Type text into an element by ref via Camofox.

name: camofox_scroll
doc: Scroll the page via Camofox.

name: camofox_back
doc: Navigate back via Camofox.

name: camofox_press
doc: Press a keyboard key via Camofox.

name: camofox_close
doc: Close the browser session via Camofox.

name: camofox_get_images
doc: Get images on the current page via Camofox (parsed from the snapshot).

name: _vision_llm_settings
doc: ``auxiliary.vision`` ``(timeout, temperature)``; defaults 120s / 0.1 on any config error.

name: _save_screenshot
doc: Write PNG bytes under ``$HERMES_HOME/browser_screenshots`` and return the path.

name: camofox_vision
arguments: question: str, annotate: bool=False, task_id: Optional[str]=None
doc: Take a screenshot and analyze it with vision AI via Camofox.

name: camofox_console
doc: Console output is not exposed by the Camofox REST API; return an empty result with a note.

name: get_camofox_state_dir
doc: Return the profile-scoped root directory for Camofox persistence.

name: get_camofox_identity
doc:
Stable Hermes-managed Camofox identity: userId is profile-scoped, session key is
scoped to the logical browser task so new tabs in the same profile reuse it.

name: _redact_cdp_output
arguments: value: Any, *, always_paths: tuple=(), flagged_paths: tuple=(), _depth: int=0
doc:
Redact browser-originated CDP result text; opaque bytes stay byte-identical.

Exemptions come ONLY from the calling method's spec as exact result paths. Path
suffixes propagate only into the matching subtree, so ``base64Encoded`` is honored
solely as a sibling on the trusted carrier object — never as ambient trust a
``Runtime.evaluate`` by-value object could spoof.

``_depth`` stops a page-controlled tree from raising RecursionError. The
unread remainder is replaced, not returned raw.

See #94138, #94142.

name: _run_async
doc: Run an async coroutine from a sync handler, safe inside or outside a loop.

name: _resolve_cdp_endpoint
doc: Normalized CDP WebSocket URL via ``browser_tool_cdp._get_cdp_override``, or "".

name: _navigate_private_target
doc: Blocked URL literal for ``Page.navigate`` params, else ``None``.

name: _browser_cdp_private_guard
arguments: *, task_id: str, method: str, params: dict[str, Any]
doc:
Apply the browser SSRF/private-page guard to raw CDP calls.

Raw CDP shares the cloud/private-network boundary of ``browser_snapshot`` /
``browser_console`` / ``browser_eval`` and must not become their bypass. Probes are
best-effort; a probe failure never breaks local/custom CDP workflows.

name: _cdp_call
arguments: ws_url: str, method: str, params: dict[str, Any], target_id: Optional[str], timeout: float
doc:
Make a single CDP call. With ``target_id``, ``Target.attachToTarget(flatten=True)`` multiplexes a
page-level session over the browser-level WebSocket; without it ``method`` runs at browser level.

name: _browser_cdp_via_supervisor
arguments: task_id: str, frame_id: str, method: str, params: Optional[dict[str, Any]], timeout: float
doc: Route a CDP call through the live supervisor session for an OOPIF frame.

name: browser_cdp
arguments: method: str, params: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, target_id: Optional[str]=None, frame_id: Optional[str]=None, timeout: float=30.0, task_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Send a raw CDP command (see ``CDP_DOCS_URL``). ``target_id`` attaches a fresh stateless connection
to a tab; ``frame_id`` (OOPIF from ``browser_snapshot.frame_tree``) routes through the supervisor's live
WebSocket instead — the only reliable way to evaluate inside an iframe where fresh per-call connections
hit signed-URL expiry (Browserbase). Both paths share the same private-page/SSRF guard. Returns JSON
``{"success": True, "method", "result"}`` or ``{"error": ...}``.

name: _browser_cdp_check
doc:
Availability check: offered only when a static CDP URL is set (Camofox is REST-only;
the default local agent-browser hides its CDP port; cloud per-session ``cdp_url`` isn't
surfaced). Raw (no-I/O) gate: check_fns run at every startup, and resolving the endpoint
over HTTP here would block launch on a stale endpoint.

name: browser_dialog
arguments: action: str, prompt_text: Optional[str]=None, dialog_id: Optional[str]=None, task_id: Optional[str]=None
doc: Respond to a pending dialog on the active task's CDP supervisor.

name: _browser_dialog_check
doc: Gate: same as ``browser_cdp`` so the two tools appear/disappear together.

name: _bound_identity
doc: (session_id, principal_id, transport_family) from the session context.

name: extension_controller_available
route_browser_tool
arguments: action: str, args: dict[str, Any], *, fallback: Callable[[], Any], broker: Any, enabled: bool, session_id: Optional[str]=None, task_id: Optional[str]=None, principal_id: Optional[str]=None, transport_family: Optional[str]=None, tool_call_id: Optional[str]=''
doc:
Route one browser action through the extension-control broker.

``broker`` exposes ``scope_for_session(**identity)``, ``select(scope, cap)``
and ``dispatch(scope, *, action, arguments, tool_call_id)``. ``fallback`` is
called exactly once when the feature is off or no server-bound identity
exists; once a controller is selected its result/exception is final.

name: current_tool_call_id
doc: Active tool_call_id bound by the agent executor, or ``""`` when none.

name: routed_browser_handler
arguments: action: str, args: dict[str, Any], *, fallback: Callable[[], Any], task_id: Optional[str]=None, session_id: Optional[str]=None, principal_id: Optional[str]=None, transport_family: Optional[str]=None, tool_call_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Lazy registry-handler route wrapper for ``browser_*`` tools.
Feature off (or gateway unimportable) ⇒ the legacy handler runs unchanged.

name: daemon_identity
doc: ``(*HARNESS_DIR_KEYS values, BU_NAME)`` of the daemon a call with ``env`` drives.

name: daemon_env
doc: ``env`` re-pointed at the daemon ``identity`` names (its own dirs and BU_NAME).

name: socket_dir_budget
doc:
The runtime-dir byte budget on ``platform`` (a ``sys.platform`` value) where the harness binds
AF_UNIX sockets, else None.

name: fits_socket_budget
doc:
Whether a 64-character session's socket under ``resolved_dir`` (the absolute, symlink-resolved
path the harness binds) fits ``budget``; no budget means no sun_path limit.

name: namespace_harness_dirs
doc:
Give served profile ``tag`` its own harness runtime and tmp dirs in the child ``env``. An empty
``tag`` (outside a served-profile scope) leaves ``env`` unchanged.

name: socket_fit_runtime_dir
arguments: runtime: str, base: str, tag: str
doc:
``runtime`` unless the socket the harness binds under it would be too long for a 64-character
session. The harness binds ``Path(BH_RUNTIME_DIR).expanduser().resolve()``, so the length is
judged on that path (a short relative or symlinked spelling can still resolve deep); a dir that
fits is returned as given. Otherwise the served profile gets a private dir under the short socket
temp root (``hbh-<12 hex>``), keyed by uid, base and profile; if none fits or can be claimed safely
the long path stays (shorter names only).

name: claim_private_dir
doc:
Create ``path`` 0700, or accept an existing one only when it is a real directory (not a
symlink) owned by this uid and closed to group/other: the temp root is world-writable, and the
harness resolves symlinks and only chmods a dir it created itself.

name: find_lightpanda_binary
doc:
Return the lightpanda executable, or None. Order: PATH (with agent-browser's Homebrew/managed-node
fallbacks), then installer/agent-browser locations, then ``$HERMES_HOME/bin``. No Windows build.

name: _http_cache_dir
doc:
Filesystem HTTP cache shared by every Lightpanda this Hermes spawns.

Shared rather than per-session so a cached asset survives session churn.
Lightpanda holds it in sqlite (WAL) with a best-effort write path, and
``--http-cache-entry-limit`` (upstream default 1000, not passed here)
bounds it without Hermes managing eviction.

name: _binary_supports_http_cache
doc:
True if ``lightpanda serve`` accepts ``--http-cache-dir``.

The flag landed upstream in 0.3.x; older binaries fatally reject it
("unknown argument"), which would break every launch. Probing ``help``
output keeps working across future flag additions without parsing
versions, and the lru_cache keeps it once per binary per process.

name: _read_log_tail
doc: Last non-empty line of the child's stderr log ('' when unreadable).

name: _terminate
doc: poll -> terminate -> wait(5) -> kill; shared with the real-profile Chrome cleanup.

name: _tree_kill
doc: Tree-kill ``pid`` via ProcessRegistry, verifying its start time first.

name: launch_lightpanda
doc:
Start ``lightpanda serve`` on a free loopback port; ``(server, None)`` once ``/json/version`` answers,
else ``(None, error)``. stderr goes to ``<state_dir>/<session>.log`` so a chatty child never blocks on a pipe.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(argv, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                    stderr=log_file, env=_browser_env(), start_new_session=True)

name: stop_lightpanda
doc: Stop the server for ``session_name`` (tree-kill, plain terminate on failure) and drop its record.

name: stop_all_lightpanda
doc: Stop every server this process started. Idempotent; safe from atexit.

name: _is_lightpanda_process
doc: True only when ``pid`` is verifiably the ``lightpanda serve`` we recorded.

name: reap_orphaned_lightpanda
doc:
Kill ``lightpanda serve`` processes whose owning Hermes is gone; return the count. A live owner is
never touched; a PID is only signalled after psutil confirms it is still ``lightpanda serve`` on the recorded port.

name: _redact_cdp_error_text
doc:
Redact CDP endpoint credentials from an exception's (or URL's) string form.
``websockets`` bakes the raw URL (``?token=`` / ``user:pass@``) into its exception
messages, so every egress point turning one into log/re-raise text MUST route through
here; falls back to a fixed sentinel if redaction itself raises (err toward masking).

name: _schedule
doc: Run ``coro`` on the supervisor loop from a sync caller and wait for its result.

name: to_dict
doc: Serialize for inclusion in ``browser_snapshot`` output.

name: __init__
arguments: self, task_id: str, cdp_url: str, *, dialog_policy: str=DEFAULT_DIALOG_POLICY, dialog_timeout_s: float=DEFAULT_DIALOG_TIMEOUT_S

name: start
doc: Launch the background loop and block until attachment completes; raises what attach failed with (redacted).

name: stop
doc: Cancel the supervisor task and join the thread.

name: snapshot
doc: Return an immutable snapshot of current state.

name: respond_to_dialog
arguments: self, action: str, *, prompt_text: Optional[str]=None, dialog_id: Optional[str]=None, timeout: float=10.0
doc:
Accept/dismiss a pending dialog (sync bridge onto the supervisor loop). Returns
``{"ok": True, "dialog"}`` or ``{"ok": False, "error"}`` for recoverable errors.

name: evaluate_runtime
arguments: self, expression: str, *, return_by_value: bool=True, await_promise: bool=True, timeout: float=10.0
doc:
Evaluate ``expression`` in the page's Runtime context over the live WS.
Returns ``{"ok": True, "result", "result_type"}`` or ``{"ok": False, "error"}``.
``return_by_value=True`` JSON-serializes the result (DevTools-console
semantics); non-serializable objects come back as a description string.

name: focus_page
arguments: self, origin: str, *, accept: Optional[str]=None, timeout: float=10.0
doc:
Re-attach the supervisor's page session to an open page target on ``origin``
(``scheme://host[:port]``). The initial attach picks the FIRST page target, but tools
that open their own tabs (browser_exec) put the login form somewhere else. With
``accept`` (a JS expression) the first same-origin tab where it evaluates truthy wins,
so a login and a checkout tab on one site resolve to the right one. Returns
``{"ok": True, "url"}`` or ``{"ok": False, "error"}``; on failure the previous session stays.

name: _thread_main
doc: Entry point for the supervisor's dedicated thread.

name: _fail_start
doc: Propagate ``e`` to ``start()`` if we never got ready; True if it was consumed.

name: _close_ws
doc: Detach and close the current WebSocket, swallowing close errors.

name: _reconnect_budget_spent
doc:
True once ``failures`` consecutive post-attach reconnects failed: log ONE final line
and drop this supervisor from the registry so a dead endpoint (its Chrome exited with
the task) leaves neither a retrying thread nor a stale registry entry behind. A later
browser call for the task starts a fresh supervisor via ``get_or_start``.

name: _run
doc:
Top-level reconnecting supervisor coroutine. Browserbase tears down the CDP
socket whenever a short-lived client (agent-browser's per-command CDP client)
disconnects, so on drop we reset per-session ids, re-attach, and keep going.
A failure before the first successful attach is fatal for ``start()``.

name: _attach_initial_page
doc: Find (or create) a page target, attach flattened, enable domains, install dialog bridge.

name: _cdp
arguments: self, method: str, params: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, *, session_id: Optional[str]=None, timeout: Optional[float]=10.0
doc: Send a CDP command and await its response.

name: _read_loop
doc: Continuously dispatch incoming CDP frames (responses → futures, events → handlers).

name: capture
doc:
Public CDP seam for trusted in-process plugins: a handle pinned to this task's
current connection and default page session (``tools.browser_supervisor_capture``).

name: get_or_start
arguments: self, task_id: str, cdp_url: str, *, dialog_policy: str=DEFAULT_DIALOG_POLICY, dialog_timeout_s: float=DEFAULT_DIALOG_TIMEOUT_S, start_timeout: float=15.0
doc:
Idempotently ensure a supervisor runs for ``(task_id, cdp_url)``; one bound to a
different ``cdp_url`` or unhealthy (dead thread / stopped loop) is stopped and replaced.

name: stop_home
doc: Stop the supervisors one profile home started (``/browser connect`` on a multiplexed gateway).

name: stop_all
doc: Stop every running supervisor. For shutdown / test teardown.

name: capture
doc: Pin the running supervisor for ``task_id``; never starts, reconnects or refocuses one.

name: is_valid
doc: True while the captured connection is still the supervisor's live one.

name: _send
arguments: self, method: str, params: Optional[dict[str, Any]], session_id: Optional[str], timeout: Optional[float], deadline: Optional[float], before_send: Optional[Callable[[], None]]

name: call
arguments: self, method: str, params: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, *, session_id: Optional[str]=None, timeout: Optional[float]=10.0, before_send: Optional[Callable[[], None]]=None
doc:
Send ``method`` on the captured connection and return the raw CDP reply
(``{"id", "result"}``). ``session_id=None`` targets the browser endpoint;
pass ``page_session_id`` (or a session you attached) for page domains.

Raises ``CapturedCDPInvalid`` when the connection is gone, ``TimeoutError`` when no
reply arrives in ``timeout`` seconds, ``RuntimeError`` for a CDP error reply.
Blocks the calling thread; never call it from the supervisor's own loop.

A finite timeout also fences send admission while this call waits in the
supervisor queue. ``timeout=None`` deliberately retains a reply until
the connection closes: use it only in a consumer-owned worker when a
late reply (for example an attachment session ID) must not be lost.
Keep the consumer's own wait/issuance deadline finite and retain cleanup
responsibility after it expires.

``before_send`` is a trusted synchronous nonblocking validation callback
run on the supervisor loop immediately before CDP dispatch. It may raise
to refuse a cancelled/expired operation. It must not call a blocking
capture/CDP API. This is not origin or target-ownership authorization.

significant_calls.expression: self._send(method, params, session_id, timeout, deadline, before_send)

name: _redact_supervisor_text
doc: Redact page-originated text before exposing supervisor snapshots.

name: _trim_ring
doc: Cap a ring buffer at ``keep`` entries once it overflows to 2x (slack reduces churn).

name: _dialog_dict
doc: Snapshot dict of ``keys`` with page-originated text fields redacted.

name: _cdp_quiet
arguments: self, method: str, params: dict[str, Any], *, session_id: Optional[str], timeout: float, what: str
doc: Best-effort CDP call: failures are logged at debug and swallowed.

name: _install_dialog_bridge
doc:
Install the dialog-bridge init script + Fetch interceptor on a session. Idempotent at
the CDP level (Chromium de-dupes identical add-script calls; Fetch.enable replaces prior
patterns); the final Runtime.evaluate injects into the already-loaded document so
existing pages pick up the override on reconnect.

name: _on_dialog_opening
arguments: self, params: dict[str, Any], session_id: Optional[str]

name: _on_fetch_paused
arguments: self, params: dict[str, Any], session_id: Optional[str]

name: _admit_dialog
arguments: self, *, type: str, message: str, default_prompt: str, session_id: Optional[str], frame_id: Optional[str], bridge_request_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Create the dialog and apply the policy: auto-respond, or queue + arm the watchdog.
Auto policies archive FIRST (tagged ``auto_policy``) so the ``closed`` event that
follows our own response isn't re-archived as ``remote``.

name: _respond
arguments: self, dialog: PendingDialog, *, accept: bool, prompt_text: Optional[str]
doc:
Bridge-fulfill for XHR-captured dialogs (swallows failures so the page
unblocks), else native CDP — ``promptText`` only for prompt dialogs when
given; raises on CDP failure.

name: _respond_quiet
arguments: self, dialog: PendingDialog, *, accept: bool, prompt_text: Optional[str]
doc: Auto-policy / watchdog response (already archived by the caller); failures logged only.

name: _handle_dialog_cdp
arguments: self, dialog: PendingDialog, *, accept: bool, prompt_text: str
doc:
Agent response path. The dialog is retired regardless of outcome — a CDP
error usually means it already closed (browser auto-dismissed after navigation).

name: _retire_dialog
doc: Remove a pending dialog (archiving it with ``closed_by``) and cancel its watchdog.

name: _archive_dialog_locked
doc: Move a pending dialog to the recent_dialogs ring buffer. Must hold state_lock.

name: _on_dialog_closed
arguments: self, params: dict[str, Any], session_id: Optional[str]

name: _enable_page_domains
doc: Page.enable + Runtime.enable + nested auto-attach on one session.

name: _on_frame_attached
arguments: self, params: dict[str, Any], session_id: Optional[str]

name: _on_frame_navigated
arguments: self, params: dict[str, Any], session_id: Optional[str]

name: _on_frame_detached
arguments: self, params: dict[str, Any], session_id: Optional[str]
doc:
Drop a frame only when it's truly gone. ``reason="swap"`` = migrating processes
(e.g. promoted to an OOPIF) — dropping would hide the iframe. Even with ``remove``
the parent only knows the child left ITS process; a live child session means it's
still alive, so keep it until Target.detached + a later frameDetached clear it.

name: _on_target_attached
arguments: self, params: dict[str, Any], session_id: Optional[str]=None

name: _enable_child_domains
doc: Enable Page+Runtime (+nested setAutoAttach) and the dialog bridge on a child session.

name: _on_target_detached
arguments: self, params: dict[str, Any], session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Clear the session binding of frames on a detached child session. Frames are
deliberately NOT dropped: Browserbase fires transient detaches during page transitions
while the iframe is still visible; ``Page.frameDetached`` cleans up if it truly goes away.

name: _build_frame_tree_locked
doc:
Capped frame_tree payload (must hold state lock). Top frame = one with
no parent, preferring oopif=False; BFS from it, capped by
FRAME_TREE_MAX_ENTRIES and FRAME_TREE_MAX_OOPIF_DEPTH for OOPIF branches.

name: warm_agent_browser_npx_cache
doc:
Frozen old-updater surface (tests/compat/old_updater_surface.json): a pre-PM ``hermes update``
still running mid-swap imports this from the NEW tree. Nothing is warmed — PM owns the browser
runtime — and the permanent definition must live here, not behind the revert-scheduled compat
pointer.

name: _build_browser_env
doc:
Credential-scrubbed env for an agent-browser subprocess (deferred import: test
harnesses stub the ``tools`` package). The passthrough keys are re-added from the active
profile's secret scope, never ``os.environ``: under multiplex that holds the LAUNCH profile's
Browserbase/Firecrawl keys, and a served profile's browser must run on its own (or none).

name: _browser_cfg
arguments: key: str, default, parse, log_label: str
doc:
``parse(browser.<key>)`` from the RAW profile config (loader warnings must not
leak into tool JSON); ``default`` when absent, not a mapping, or on any error.

name: _cached_browser_cfg
arguments: cache_name: str, flag_name: str, key: str, default, parse, log_label: str
doc:
Process-cached ``_browser_cfg`` read, one slot per profile home (cleared by
``cleanup_all_browsers``). The value is stored BEFORE the resolved flag flips so a
concurrent reader never sees ``resolved=True`` with an empty cache.

name: _get_command_timeout
doc: ``browser.command_timeout`` (floored at 5s; default 30s).

name: _safe_command_timeout
doc:
``_get_command_timeout`` guaranteed non-None (cache reset mid-flight); ``is not
None`` rather than ``or`` so a configured ``0`` is preserved.

name: get_browser_snapshot_threshold
doc: ``browser.snapshot_threshold`` (floored at MIN_SNAPSHOT_THRESHOLD).

name: _get_open_command_timeout
doc: Timeout for agent-browser ``open`` (navigation / daemon cold start).

name: _get_vision_model
doc: Model for browser_vision (screenshot analysis — multimodal).

name: _url_is_private
doc:
True when the URL's host is (or resolves to) a private/LAN/loopback/CGNAT address.
Routing oracle only: DNS failures are NOT private (the configured backend surfaces the
error); obvious names short-circuit the DNS hop. A local proxy's declared fake-ip sentinel
(``security.fake_ip_ranges``) is not private: the name is public, the cloud browser resolves
it itself, so routing it to the local sidecar would send every URL local on such a host.

name: _hybrid_routes_locally
doc:
True when ``url`` belongs on the hybrid LOCAL sidecar instead of the cloud provider: a cloud provider
configured, ``browser.auto_local_for_private_urls`` on, a private URL, no CDP override (it owns the
whole session), Camofox off (already local-only). Shared by browser_navigate and browser_exec.

name: _navigation_session_key
doc:
Session key that should handle ``url`` for ``task_id``: ``f"{task_id}::local"`` (hybrid
local sidecar while the cloud session keeps serving public URLs) when
``_hybrid_routes_locally`` holds for ``url``.

name: _session_info_owned_by_task
arguments: session_info: dict[str, Any], task_id: str, session_key: str
doc:
Ownership check; entries without metadata (older in-memory / hot-reload) pass,
any explicit mismatch fails before a non-nav tool can act on the wrong session.

name: _last_session_key
doc:
Session key a non-nav tool must use: the one that served the task's last navigation.
If it was cleaned up or ownership no longer matches, fail closed by dropping the stale
binding rather than recreating or mutating the wrong browser.

name: _socket_safe_tmpdir
doc:
Temp root short enough for the agent-browser socket dir and Chrome's SingletonSocket
(``hermes_constants.socket_safe_tmpdir``).

name: _secret_url_error
doc:
Refuse URLs embedding an API key/token (raw and URL-decoded, catching ``%2D``
tricks) — a prompt injection could otherwise exfiltrate secrets via the URL.

name: _url_policy_error
doc:
Backend-aware URL checks on an already-normalized URL; None if allowed. Ordered floors:
(1) cloud metadata / IMDS refused UNCONDITIONALLY (a local Chromium on a cloud VM still
reaches the host IMDS); (2) private addresses refused unless local, sidecar-routed, or
``browser.allow_private_urls``; (3) website policy allow/deny lists.

Credential-NAMED query params (``?token=``, ``?signature=``) are deliberately NOT a floor:
magic links, OAuth callbacks and signed CDN assets are how the agent signs in and browses, and
a cloud browser already sees every cookie and typed password of the session — refusing the
URL protects nothing. Hermes' own secrets leaking into a URL are caught by ``_secret_url_error``.

name: _secret_url_error_normalized
doc: Secret check on the raw URL, then again on the normalized one; returns ``(url, error)``.

name: evaluate_url_safety
doc:
Run URL safety checks; None if safe, else an error dict. ``auto_local`` (the URL is served by the
hybrid local sidecar) relaxes only the private-address floor, never the cloud-metadata one.

name: _post_redirect_block
arguments: nav_session_key: str, url: str, final_url: str, auto_local_this_nav: bool
doc:
Post-redirect SSRF check; blocked JSON payload or None. The page is moved to about:blank
first so later snapshots can't read the internal content. The metadata floor fires for
every backend; the private-address check is skipped for local, the sidecar, and
``browser.allow_private_urls``.

name: _snapshot_fields
doc:
``snapshot`` + ``element_count`` fields from a successful snapshot result; oversized
snapshots truncate at line boundaries with the full tree stored for read_file paging.

name: _merge_fallback_warning
arguments: response: dict[str, Any], result: dict[str, Any]
doc: Copy a secondary result's fallback warning only if the response has none yet.

name: _attach_auto_snapshot
doc: Add a compact snapshot to a navigate response so the model can act without browser_snapshot.

name: browser_navigate
doc:
Navigate to ``url``; JSON with title, compact snapshot and, on first nav, stealth features.
Hybrid routing decides BEFORE the safety checks whether this URL goes to a local sidecar
(the cloud provider never sees it then, so the private-address checks are relaxed).

name: _add_navigate_warnings
arguments: response: dict[str, Any], title: str, first_nav_session: Optional[dict[str, Any]]
doc: Bot-detection hint from the page title; on first navigation, the session's stealth features.

name: browser_snapshot
arguments: full: bool=False, task_id: Optional[str]=None, user_task: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Text snapshot of the page's accessibility tree (compact unless ``full``).
``user_task`` is deprecated and unused (oversized snapshots always truncate-and-store).

name: _json_with_fallback
arguments: response: dict[str, Any], result: dict[str, Any]
doc: ``json.dumps`` of ``response`` with the Lightpanda fallback metadata copied from ``result``.

name: _tool_response
arguments: result: dict[str, Any], ok: dict[str, Any], default_error: str
doc: ``{"success": True, **ok}`` or ``{"success": False, "error": result.error or default}``, plus fallback metadata.

name: _camofox
doc: Call ``tools.browser_camofox.<func_name>(*args)`` (Camofox mode delegation).

name: _guarded_action
arguments: task_id: Optional[str], action: str, command: str, args: list, ok: dict[str, Any], err: str
doc: Input action on the task's current page, refused when the SSRF guard flags the page.

name: browser_click
doc: Click the element ``ref`` (e.g. "@e5").

name: browser_type
arguments: ref: str, text: str, task_id: Optional[str]=None
doc: Type ``text`` into the element ``ref`` (fill: clears, then types).

name: browser_scroll
doc: Scroll the page ``direction`` ("up"/"down") by about half a viewport.

name: browser_back
doc: Navigate back in browser history.

name: browser_press
doc: Press a keyboard key (e.g. "Enter", "Tab").

name: _blocked_private_page_json
doc: Refusal payload for a page whose URL targets a private/internal address.

name: _blocked_private_page
doc:
Blocked payload when the SSRF guard is active and the current page is private, else
None. Fail-open on probe failure (see ``_current_page_private_url``).

name: _blocked_private_page_action
doc: Blocked payload when an unsafe cloud page would receive input.

name: _blocked_private_page_content
doc:
Content-returning tools (snapshot/vision/eval/get_images): after an eval that may
have moved ``location.href`` to a private address, returning content would expose it.

name: browser_console
arguments: clear: bool=False, expression: Optional[str]=None, task_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Console messages + uncaught JS errors (optionally ``clear``ing the buffers),
or — when ``expression`` is given — evaluate JS in the page like the DevTools console.

name: _parse_eval_value
doc: Eval returns the JS value as a string; parse valid JSON so the model gets structured data.

name: _eval_result_or_blocked
arguments: effective_task_id: str, parsed: Any, result: dict[str, Any], **extra
doc:
Eval tool JSON, unless the post-eval page-URL recheck finds an eval navigated the
page to a private address — then the result is withheld.

name: _eval_supervisor_fast_path
doc:
``Runtime.evaluate`` on the CDP supervisor's persistent WebSocket (no subprocess cost).
Tool JSON when the supervisor gave a definitive answer (value, blocked page, or a real
JS-side exception — NOT retried via subprocess, that would just reproduce it slower);
None to fall through to the subprocess path.

name: _eval_failure_response
doc: Tool JSON for a failed ``agent-browser eval``, with actionable rewrites of known errors.

name: _browser_eval
doc:
Evaluate JS in the page context. Private-network guard in two halves: the literal
pre-scan closes direct fetches (they never update ``location.href``); the post-eval
page-URL recheck closes navigate-then-read.

name: _camofox_eval
doc: Evaluate JS via Camofox's /tabs/{tab_id}/evaluate endpoint (if available).

name: _maybe_start_recording
doc: Start recording if browser.record_sessions is enabled in config.

name: _maybe_stop_recording
doc: Stop recording if one is active for this session.

name: browser_get_images
doc: List the page's images (src, alt, natural size), excluding data: URIs.

name: _capture_vision_screenshot
arguments: effective_task_id: str, annotate: bool, screenshot_path: Path, lp_prerouted: bool
doc: Take (or adopt the pre-routed) screenshot; returns ``(result, path, error_json_or_None)``.

name: browser_vision
arguments: question: str, annotate: bool=False, task_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Screenshot the current page for visual inspection. Native-vision models get the image
attached to the conversation; otherwise the auxiliary vision model returns a text
analysis. The file is kept and its path returned (MEDIA:<path>).

name: check_browser_routed_requirements
doc: Availability gate for tools that can use either browser backend.

name: _fallback_call
arguments: fn_name: str, arg_defaults: dict[str, Any], extra_kw: tuple=()
doc:
Adapter from the registry's ``(args, kw)`` to ``<fn_name>(**schema_args, task_id=...)``;
the function is looked up in module globals at call time so monkeypatching works.

name: _routed_check_fn
doc: Per-action availability gate (a named function, as the registry expects).

name: mark_suspect
doc: MUST stay cheap and lock-free (runs inline on the timed-out caller's thread).

name: ensure_healthy
doc:
Recycle the session when a prior timeout marked it suspect; False after teardown.
The flag is popped BEFORE teardown: ``close`` re-enters ``_get_session_info``
and must not recurse into another recycle.

name: _resolve_cdp_override
doc:
Normalize a user-supplied CDP endpoint into a concrete websocket URL.

Full ``ws://.../devtools/browser/...`` endpoints pass through; HTTP discovery roots and bare ``ws://host:port``
resolve via ``/json/version`` → ``webSocketDebuggerUrl`` (falls back to the raw value with a warning).

name: live_cdp_override
doc:
The current profile's live ``/browser connect`` endpoint, or "".

On a multiplexed gateway a context with no profile bound (a bare ``threading.Thread`` or stdlib
executor that did not copy the caller's context) answers "" rather than the launch profile's
endpoint, the way ``get_secret`` fails closed. Single-profile processes are unchanged.

name: set_live_cdp_override
doc: Set (or with a falsy ``url`` clear) the current profile's live endpoint and bump its generation.

name: live_cdp_generation
doc: The current (or ``home_key``'s) profile's live-endpoint generation.

name: env_cdp_url
doc:
``BROWSER_CDP_URL`` from this profile's secret scope. A routed profile (multiplex, or a scope
bound for another home) reads only its own ``.env``: ``os.environ`` holds the launch profile's
value. Single-profile reads fall through to ``os.environ`` as before (``get_secret``).

name: _get_cdp_override_raw
doc:
Return the *configured* CDP override without any network I/O.

Precedence: this profile's live ``/browser connect``, then its ``BROWSER_CDP_URL`` (:func:`env_cdp_url`),
then ``browser.cdp_url``. Is-it-configured
gates (check_fns, ``_is_local_mode`` / ``_is_local_backend``, ``hermes doctor``) MUST use this, not
:func:`_get_cdp_override`: its 10s HTTP discovery against a stale ``cdp_url`` would stall every startup's
schema build with no error.

name: _get_cdp_override
doc:
Resolved CDP URL override, or "" (skips cloud AND local launch).

May perform HTTP ``/json/version`` discovery — only call on paths about to *connect*; pure gates must use
:func:`_get_cdp_override_raw`.

name: _get_dialog_policy_config
doc: Read ``browser.dialog_policy`` + ``browser.dialog_timeout_s``; supervisor defaults when absent/invalid.

name: _ensure_cdp_supervisor
doc:
Start a CDP supervisor for ``task_id`` if an endpoint is reachable.

Idempotent (``get_or_start`` skips an existing ``(task_id, cdp_url)`` and restarts on URL change), so safe on
every navigate / ``/browser connect``. URL precedence: the CDP override, then the session's own ``cdp_url``
(cloud providers, e.g. Browserbase). Swallows all errors — a failed attach must not break the session;
snapshots just lack ``pending_dialogs`` / ``frame_tree``.

name: _stop_cdp_supervisor
doc: Stop the CDP supervisor for ``task_id`` if one exists. No-op otherwise.

name: _memo
arguments: _bt, resolved_attr: str, cache_attr: str, compute: Callable[[], object]
doc:
Process-lifetime cache on ``_bt``: the resolved flag is set BEFORE computing, then the final value is stored.

Under a routed profile (HERMES_HOME override, multiplexed gateway) the slot is NOT consulted: every
``_memo`` here caches a ``browser.*`` config read, and one process-wide slot would hand the launch
profile's engine/headed/private-URL policy to every other profile (same rule as ``_allow_private_urls``).

name: _ensure_browser_plugins_loaded
doc: Idempotently trigger plugin discovery (standalone scripts/tests may never import ``model_tools``).

name: _get_cloud_provider
doc: Return the provider cached for the active Hermes profile.

name: _instantiate_explicit_cloud_provider
doc:
Build the provider named by ``browser.cloud_provider``.

Strict: an unregistered name raises ``ValueError`` (never a silent reroute to auto-detect); any
other instantiation error is logged and yields None so the next call retries.

name: _autodetect_cloud_provider
doc:
Auto-detect: Browser Use, then Browserbase; never raises.

Third-party plugins are only reachable via explicit ``browser.cloud_provider: <name>``.

name: _resolve_cloud_provider_uncached
doc:
Return the configured cloud browser provider, or None for local mode.

Pins the cache only when definitive (explicit ``local``/``camofox`` or a resolved provider); a transient None
(unreadable config, missing credentials) is NOT cached so it can self-heal. Auto-detect runs only when no
selection was ever written.

name: _is_local_mode
doc: Return True when the browser tool will use a local browser backend.

name: _is_local_backend
doc:
True when the browser runs locally AND the terminal is also local.

SSRF protection only matters when the browser can reach networks the terminal cannot (cloud backends,
containerized terminals). A CDP override is never trusted as local (that Chrome may live off-host) and MUST
be checked before the Camofox short-circuit; ``_is_local_mode`` treats overrides the same way — keep the two
in agreement.

name: browser_backend_name
doc:
Shared-metrics label for the backend legacy browser calls use in the active profile, in session-creation
precedence (CDP override > Camofox > cloud provider > local engine). Config reads only, no network I/O.

name: _get_browser_engine
doc:
Return the browser engine: ``auto`` (no ``--engine`` flag), ``lightpanda`` or ``chrome``.

``browser.engine`` first, then ``AGENT_BROWSER_ENGINE``, then ``auto``; cached. Lightpanda is faster on
navigation but has no graphical renderer (no screenshots).

name: _is_headed_mode
doc: True when the browser should launch headed: ``browser.headed``, else ``AGENT_BROWSER_HEADED``; cached.

name: _should_inject_engine
doc: True when ``--engine`` should be added: explicit (non-``auto``) engine on a non-cloud, non-camofox local session.

name: _auto_local_for_private_urls
doc: ``browser.auto_local_for_private_urls`` (default True), cached: route private/LAN URLs to a local sidecar even with a cloud provider.

name: _use_real_profile
doc:
Whether the user consented to real-profile local browsing.

Read on EVERY call: it is a consent switch (flipping it off must not need a restart) and each multiplexed
profile must decide for itself. One YAML load per local session creation, so no hot-path cost.

name: _allow_private_urls
doc:
Whether the browser may navigate to private/internal addresses (default False: SSRF protection on).

Single-profile calls cache for the process lifetime; multiplexed profile turns (ContextVar-scoped config)
resolve on every call so one profile's opt-out is never reused by another.

name: _resolve_allow_private_urls
doc: Read the browser private-URL toggle from the active config scope.

name: _eval_ssrf_guard_active
doc:
Return True when eval-driven private-network access must be guarded.

Same gating as ``browser_navigate`` / ``browser_snapshot`` / ``browser_vision``: the SSRF guard
only matters for non-local backends (cloud browser, or a containerized terminal whose
browser-on-host reaches networks the terminal can't); skipped for local sidecars / ``allow_private_urls``.

name: _url_blocked
doc: True when ``url`` hits the always-blocked cloud-metadata floor or fails the SSRF guard.

name: _expression_targets_private_url
doc: Return the first private/always-blocked ``http(s)://`` literal in a JS expression (best-effort), else None.

name: _current_page_private_url
doc:
Return the current page URL when it targets a private/internal address (e.g. after a prior
``location.href = '...'`` eval). Fail-open on probe failure, matching the snapshot/vision guards.

name: _browser_eval_flag
doc: Read boolean ``browser.<key>`` (default False) through the origin's config reader.

name: _allow_unsafe_browser_evaluate
doc: Whether sensitive browser JS evaluation is explicitly allowed (overrides ``restrict_evaluate``).

name: _restrict_browser_evaluate
doc:
Whether the sensitive-primitive eval denylist is enabled (off by default).

It blocks the *names* of common primitives (``fetch``, ``cookie``, ``querySelector(...input...)``),
not actual exfiltration, so it also blocks much legitimate DOM extraction; egress is still gated
by the SSRF/private-URL guards in ``_browser_eval`` regardless. Opt in via
``browser.restrict_evaluate: true`` (e.g. hostile pages with a logged-in profile).

name: _decode_js_string_literal
doc: Best-effort decode of a JS string literal (not a parser): normalizes escapes like ``"co\x6fkie"``.

name: _sensitive_browser_eval_token_reason
doc:
Risk reason for direct or quoted sensitive primitives: direct spellings alone miss
``document["cookie"]`` / ``globalThis["fetch"]``, so tokens are also matched inside the decoded,
concatenated string literals (catches ``document["coo" + "kie"]``).

name: _risky_browser_eval_reason
doc: Return a human-readable reason if a JS expression uses risky primitives.

name: _enforce_browser_eval_policy
doc:
Block sensitive browser JS evaluation when the opt-in denylist is on (opt-in because it gates on
primitive *names*; private-address egress is enforced separately in ``_browser_eval``).

name: _camofox_current_page_private_url
doc:
Camofox analogue of ``_current_page_private_url`` (evaluate endpoint instead of the CLI). Fail-open
on probe failure, matching the snapshot/vision guards — do not make fail-closed without the sibling.

name: _discover_homebrew_node_dirs
doc: Homebrew versioned Node bin dirs (node@20, ...) that ``brew`` may not link into /opt/homebrew/bin.

name: _browser_candidate_path_dirs
doc: System PATH fallbacks for externally owned browser helpers.

name: _merge_browser_path
doc: Prepend browser-specific PATH fallbacks without reordering existing entries.

name: _find_agent_browser
doc:
Select PM's exact binary, then an external PATH/Homebrew installation.

Termux owns its browser installation. Elsewhere PM may acquire a missing
CLI at execution time, subject to its lazy-install policy. Readiness checks
(``validate=False``) never execute or install anything. Selection is not
cached: a new PM fact or profile must be visible immediately.

name: warm_agent_browser_npx_cache
doc:
Frozen old-updater surface names this module too (the extraction-era home); tools.browser_tool
carries the permanent definition. No npx work is performed; relaunch instead.

name: _chromium_installed
doc: An explicit browser executable or PM's selected full Chromium exists.

name: _maybe_autoinstall_chromium
doc:
Install only PM's pinned full Chromium, never the upstream browser pair.

Docker supplies the binary. Other installs require lazy-install consent.

name: _running_in_docker
doc: Best-effort detection of whether we're inside a Docker container.

name: check_browser_requirements
check_browser_vision_requirements
doc:
Advertise ``browser_vision`` only with BOTH a working browser AND a vision backend.

Without the vision check, the tool stays in the model's tool list even when no vision provider is
configured, then fails at call time with a cryptic provider-side error like ``unknown variant
`image_url`, expected `text``` (issue #31179).

name: _session_expiry_timestamp
doc:
Provider-authoritative session expiry as epoch seconds; None when absent or
malformed (cloud providers may omit ``expires_at``; local browsers never have one).

name: _session_has_expired
doc: Whether a cached browser session crossed its provider deadline.

name: _best_effort
doc: Run ``fn()``; log (debug) and swallow any exception — teardown must never abort.

name: _emergency_cleanup_all_sessions
doc:
atexit: close this process's sessions, then sweep orphans left by crashed
hermes processes — every clean exit reaps accumulated orphans, not only
processes that used the browser tool.

name: _session_owner_scope
doc:
Run under the Hermes home + secret scope owning ``task_id``'s session (no-op if unrecorded).

The janitor thread is process-global, so each teardown must re-enter its OWN
profile's scope rather than inherit the spawning profile's; never falls
through to ``os.environ``.

name: _forget_session_tracking
arguments: task_id: str, *, activity: bool=True, session: bool=False
doc: Drop the janitor's bookkeeping (and optionally the session entry) for ``task_id``.

name: _cleanup_inactive_browser_sessions
doc:
Close sessions inactive longer than the timeout (cleanup thread).

Each teardown runs under its owner profile's scope. A session whose cleanup
keeps failing is force-reaped after MAX_INACTIVITY_CLEANUP_FAILURES attempts;
only a successful cleanup clears its failure count.

See #100738, #86402.

name: _human_holds_shared_browser
doc: Lease check for the janitor, under the owner's profile scope (the lease is per profile).

name: _write_owner_pid
doc:
Record this hermes PID in ``<socket_dir>/<session>.owner_pid`` so the orphan
reaper can tell live-owner daemons from crashed-owner ones. Best-effort: an
OSError falls back to the legacy ``tracked_names`` heuristic.

name: _argv_token_is_path
doc: True when ``token`` (or its ``--flag=VALUE`` value) names exactly ``path``.

name: _verify_reapable_browser_daemon
arguments: daemon_pid: int, socket_dir: str, session_name: str
doc:
Confirm a live PID is genuinely *this* session's agent-browser daemon (fail-closed).

The ``.pid`` file sits in a world-writable temp dir: a planted or recycled PID
would turn the tree-kill into an arbitrary-process DoS. Both must pass:
(1) identity — ``agent-browser`` in name/cmdline; (2) binding — the socket dir in
the cmdline or ``AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR`` in its environ (the real spoof defense).

name: _socket_dir_idle_seconds
doc:
Seconds since anything in ``socket_dir`` was last written; None if unknown (fail safe).
Every command rewrites ``_stdout_<cmd>`` there — a restart-proof activity marker — and
rewriting doesn't touch the dir mtime, so entries are scanned too.

name: _read_pid_file
doc: Integer PID from ``path``; None when missing or corrupt.

name: _owner_pid_alive
doc: Read ``<session>.owner_pid`` and report ``(pid, alive)``; ``(None, None)`` when missing/corrupt.

name: _terminate_verified_daemon
doc:
Tree-kill ``daemon_pid`` if it has a start-time fingerprint (so a PID swapped
between check and kill is refused); False (logged via ``log``) when no fingerprint.
Raises on OS errors.

name: _reap_socket_dir
arguments: socket_dir: str, session_name: str, tracked_names: set
doc:
Reap one ``agent-browser-<session>`` dir if orphaned; True when a daemon was killed.

A live ``owner_pid`` means another hermes process owns it — leave it UNLESS untracked
here and idle past ``BROWSER_ORPHAN_GRACE_SECONDS`` (owner-alive alone made leaked
daemons immortal); no owner_pid (legacy) falls back to this process's tracking. A
pidless dir is only stale after the grace period (deleting it immediately races the
creator's first stdout open). The PID is identity-verified before any tree-kill.

name: _reap_orphaned_browser_sessions
doc:
Kill agent-browser daemons whose owning hermes process is gone (an unclean exit loses
``_active_sessions`` but node + Chromium keep running). Scans the tmp dir for
``agent-browser-*`` socket dirs; safe from any context.

name: _browser_cleanup_thread_worker
doc:
Every 30s: close sessions idle past BROWSER_SESSION_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT; reap
orphans on startup AND every BROWSER_ORPHAN_REAP_INTERVAL seconds.

name: _start_browser_cleanup_thread
doc: Start the background cleanup thread if not already running.

name: _stop_browser_cleanup_thread
doc: Stop the background cleanup thread.

name: _update_session_activity
doc:
Touch the activity timestamp and record the owning Hermes home on first sight (the
janitor tears down under the owner's scope). Does NOT reset ``_cleanup_failures``.

See #86402.

name: _kill_process_tree
doc:
Best-effort kill of *proc* and every descendant; never raises.

``Popen.kill()`` only signals the direct child; npm/npx helpers and the detached
daemon grandchild keep a capture pipe open so ``communicate()`` never sees EOF, so
the whole tree must go (no grace: the caller already burned its timeout). Delegates
to :func:`agent.deadline.kill_process_tree`, falling back to the legacy kill.

``Popen.kill()`` only signals the direct child PID. npm/npx routinely fork further processes
(registry-fetch helpers, npm's own lifecycle runner, agent-browser's own detached daemon grandchild)
that can survive a plain ``kill()`` of the top-level PID and keep a ``capture_output``-style pipe open,
hanging the caller's ``communicate()`` past the nominal timeout — the same orphaned-pipe hazard already
hit in production on POSIX (see ``tools/process_registry.py``'s ``_reader_loop``, issue 68915: a
backgrounded grandchild inheriting a pipe's write end kept it from ever reaching EOF). That hazard is
cross-platform, not Windows-specific; what *is* Windows-specific is the lack of a remedy other than
killing the tree — anonymous pipes there don't support overlapped I/O, so there's no ``select()``-style
non-blocking read to poll around a stuck grandchild the way POSIX can. Killing the whole process
group/tree the child was launched into reaches those descendants on both platforms. See #68915.

name: _legacy_kill_process_tree
doc:
Local tree-kill (fallback when agent.deadline is unavailable; tests pin
the signal sequence). A child leading its own group gets SIGTERM then
SIGKILL via killpg; a shared-group child can never be killpg'd (that is OUR
group), so it and its psutil-snapshotted descendants are killed
individually.

name: _pid_exists
doc: Best-effort 'is this PID alive' (cross-platform via gateway.status; zombies count as dead).

name: _unlink_older_than
arguments: directory: Path, pattern: str, max_age_hours: float, label: str
doc: Delete ``directory/pattern`` files older than ``max_age_hours``; never raises.

name: _cleanup_old_screenshots
doc: Prune old browser screenshots; throttled to once per hour per directory.

name: _cleanup_old_recordings
doc: Prune old browser recordings.

name: _drop_last_active_binding
doc:
Drop stale last-active ownership after cleaning ``task_id``: a bare task always, a
sidecar only if it was still the recorded owner (a later click must not resurrect a
cleaned sidecar while a primary-session binding is preserved).

name: cleanup_browser
doc:
Clean up browser session(s) for a task: a bare task id reaps BOTH the primary
session and any hybrid local sidecar; a ``::local`` key reaps only that one.

name: _kill_verified_daemon
doc:
Tree-kill the daemon in ``<socket_dir>/<session>.pid`` if verifiably ours; True when
a kill was issued. Never raises.

name: _release_session_resources
doc:
Untrack ``task_id``, close its cloud provider session, kill its daemon — the
unconditional tail of a teardown, and the whole of the janitor's force-reap path.

The unconditional tail of ``_cleanup_single_browser_session``; also the whole of the janitor's
force-reap path (#100738), which skips the polite agent-browser/Camofox ``close`` that kept failing but
must still release the cloud session and the local Chromium.

name: _release_session_backend
doc:
Close ``session_info``'s cloud provider session and kill its daemon, by object: no shared
session map is read or written (an unpublished session releases through this alone).

name: _force_reap_browser_session
doc:
Janitor last resort: skip the failing ``close`` round-trips, release resources directly.

Janitor last resort after repeated cleanup failures (#100738).

name: _cleanup_single_browser_session
doc: Reap a single browser session by its exact session key.

name: cleanup_profile_browsers
doc:
Close one profile home's browser sessions, CDP supervisors and harness daemons, and drop its
cached config slots (``/browser connect`` on a multiplexed gateway). Other profiles' browsers stay.

name: cleanup_all_browsers
doc: Clean up all active browser sessions (shutdown) and reset cached lookups.

name: _using_lightpanda_engine
doc: Return True when local browser commands are configured for Lightpanda.

name: lightpanda_engine_status
doc:
Whether ``browser.engine: lightpanda`` is actually in effect, and why.

``(False, "")`` when the engine isn't lightpanda; else the reason names the setting shadowing
it or the driver running it. Mirrors ``_should_inject_engine`` / ``_resolve_backend_cdp``
precedence with config-only gates (no network I/O) for ``/browser status`` / ``hermes doctor``.

name: _lightpanda_fallback_reason
arguments: engine: str, command: str, result: dict[str, Any]
doc: User-visible reason a Lightpanda result needs the Chrome fallback (copied into the result), or None.

name: _needs_lightpanda_fallback
arguments: engine: str, command: str, result: dict[str, Any]
doc: Check if a Lightpanda result should trigger an automatic Chrome fallback.

name: _annotate_lightpanda_fallback
doc: Add a user-visible Chrome fallback warning to a browser command result.

name: _copy_fallback_warning
arguments: target: dict[str, Any], result: dict[str, Any]
doc: Copy browser fallback metadata from an internal result into a tool response.

name: _run_chrome_fallback_command
arguments: task_id: str, command: str, args: list[str], timeout: int
doc:
Run a browser command in a temporary Chrome session at the current URL.

agent-browser locks the engine when a named daemon starts, so ``--engine chrome`` on the
Lightpanda session is ignored: fresh temp Chrome session -> same URL -> ``command`` -> tear down.

name: _chrome_fallback_screenshot
arguments: task_id: str, args: list[str], timeout: int
doc: Take a screenshot using a temporary Chrome session.

name: _module_for_globals
doc: The module object whose namespace is ``g`` (or a live view over it).

name: origin_module
doc:
The ``tools.browser_tool`` instance the *calling* moved function belongs to, mirroring
what in-file code would see: (1) the nearest enclosing frame executing origin code (the
exact module copy, even after a test purged/reloaded ``sys.modules``); (2) an origin
module referenced from a calling frame's globals; (3) ``sys.modules`` / ``tools``
package attribute / fresh import. ``_depth`` is the frame of the moved function's caller.

name: _terminate_real_profile_chrome
doc:
Terminate real-browser processes launched for real-profile sessions (idempotent, atexit-safe);
agent-browser only ATTACHED to them, so its own session cleanup never kills them.

name: _cdp_http_ready
doc: True when an ``http://host:port`` CDP discovery root answers.

name: _real_profile_daemon_env
doc:
Reaper-visible socket dir + ``owner_pid`` claim like every other lane (agent-browser's
default dir is invisible to the reaper — #100855). The daemon-side idle timeout is dropped:
Chrome is launched by Hermes, not the daemon, so a self-exiting daemon would leave Chrome
holding the copy dir under the next snapshot overlay. Returns ``(env, socket_dir)``.

name: _capture_agent_browser_cli
arguments: argv: list, timeout: float, tag: str
doc:
Run an agent-browser CLI argv once, capturing output through temp files (not pipes).

The CLI forks a resident daemon that inherits its stdio and outlives the CLI, so with
pipe capture the CLI can exit while its output never reaches EOF: POSIX burns the whole
timeout draining pipes on every call, and Windows' ``TimeoutExpired`` cleanup re-drains
with no timeout, blocking past the outer tool deadline (#96731). Same pattern as
``_popen_agent_browser``: wait for the CLI alone — a grandchild holding the inherited
file handles is harmless. Raises ``TimeoutExpired`` after killing the CLI.

name: _agent_browser_session_cmd
doc: Run ``agent-browser --session <name> <cmd...>``; None when agent-browser is missing or the run fails.

name: _agent_browser_get_cdp
doc: HTTP CDP discovery root of an agent-browser session (from its ``ws://`` cdp-url), or None.

name: _read_devtools_port
doc: First line of Chrome's ``DevToolsActivePort`` in ``data_dir`` (None when unreadable).

name: _surviving_chrome_cdp
doc:
