arguments: results: list[dict[str, Any]], task_list: list[dict[str, Any]], children: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any], Any]], parent_agent
doc: Apply host-owned summary, memory, hook, and cost contracts once.

name: _run_child_lifecycle
arguments: task_index: int, goal: str, child=None, parent_agent=None
doc: Run one child and apply the same host lifecycle used by delegate_task.

name: _declared_parameters
doc: The provider's per-task parameters, minus anything malformed or reserved (warned).

name: schema_extension
doc:
``(extra task properties, description addendum)`` for the active provider (none for the
default strategy, whose schema is the base one).

name: _param_error
arguments: index: int, name: str, value: Any, schema: Mapping[str, Any]

name: _clean_route
doc:
The route keys of a provider's answer. Other keys are dropped silently: returning the whole
``delegation`` section (``dict(config)``, the default route) legitimately carries lifecycle knobs.

name: delegated_profile_scope
doc:
Run the block as profile ``home``: HERMES_HOME override, that profile's secret scope,
multiplex semantics when it is not this process's own profile, and its terminal policy - the
binding a multiplexed gateway applies to a routed turn (gateway/AGENTS.md § Profile scope).
A no-op for anything but a path (``None``: no profile route) and for the home already in effect.

name: child_profile_scope
doc:
The profile scope a built child's own work runs in (its startup credential lease, every conversation turn
incl. the output_schema retry); a no-op for children without a profile route. Parent bookkeeping (registry,
heartbeat, progress, result assembly) stays outside it.

name: _profile_model_request
doc:
``resolve_runtime_provider`` kwargs for a profile's primary model, decoded by the same owner CLI startup
uses (``resolve_startup_model_route``): a ``model.default`` alias takes the alias's model, endpoint and key.

name: _refuse_under_worker_snapshot
doc:
A managed worker (kanban, safe mode, managed sessions) runs on the session config frozen at creation:
every config reader returns that snapshot and the process never opens profile files, so another profile's
config.yaml is unreachable here. Refuse rather than pair the launch profile's model with the target's keys.

name: _profile_route
doc:
The profile's own primary route, resolved inside its scope (its config.yaml + secrets). The
child never borrows the launching profile's key, pool, fallback chain or reasoning level.

name: _with_inherited_fallback
arguments: route: dict[str, Any], config: Mapping[str, Any]
doc:
A route without a fallback chain of its own takes ``delegation.fallback_providers`` (an explicit ``[]`` on the
route still disables fallback). A profile route keeps its profile's own chain.

name: _resolve_route
arguments: route: dict[str, Any], parent_agent: Any, backend: str

name: _route_to_task_route
arguments: route: dict[str, Any], parent_agent: Any, cache: dict[str, TaskRoute], config: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]]=None, backend: str='default'

name: _check_backend_effort
arguments: index: int, route: Mapping[str, Any], config: Mapping[str, Any]
doc:
A backend's ``reasoning_effort`` must be a known level: a typo is a tool error, never the parent's level.
The ``delegation`` section's own value (the default route, ``dict(config)``) keeps its warn-and-inherit rule.

name: _undeclared_error
arguments: provider: DelegationProvider, index: int, names: list[str], config: Mapping[str, Any], saved: str
doc:
Why a task carrying parameters the session's backend does not declare is refused. The schema follows
config.yaml for the whole session (cached prompt), so after a ``/delegation`` switch the model can still send
the previous backend's parameters; dropping them would run the task on this backend's default route.
``/new`` starts on the saved backend (``saved``), so the fix persists the session's pick first or names it.

name: _route_one
arguments: provider: DelegationProvider, declared: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], index: int, task: Mapping[str, Any], config: Mapping[str, Any], saved: str

name: resolve_task_routes
arguments: task_list: list[dict[str, Any]], config: Mapping[str, Any], parent_agent: Any
doc:
One :class:`TaskRoute` per task from the session's backend (its ``/delegation`` override, else
``delegation.backend``), or ``([], error)`` when that backend cannot run (fails closed, never another
backend). A task the backend cannot route gets a route with ``error`` set; its siblings are unaffected.
Identical routes resolve credentials once per call (the default backend resolves exactly once).

name: route_for_config
doc:
The route an internal caller's explicit config block describes (``/review`` ->
``auxiliary.review``); bypasses the provider, as those callers own their route.

name: report
doc: The ``route`` a backend-routed task's result carries (None for the default backend's unlabelled route).

name: refused_entry
doc: Result entry for a task this route refused: no child was built for it.

name: _recover_tasks_from_json_string
doc: ``(parsed_list, None)`` for a JSON-array string, ``(None, error)`` for a bad string, ``(None, None)`` otherwise.

name: _validate_batch_tasks
doc:
Batch-only quality gate beyond per-task goal presence; actionable error or None. No minimum count: a one-entry
array is the canonical single-task shape (legacy top-level `goal` is wrapped into one). Duplicate goals are
deliberately NOT rejected — identical-goal fan-outs (best-of-N / ensemble sampling) are legitimate and blocking
them broke real workflows. The too-short check applies only to multi-task fan-outs (terse goals there are
usually unexpanded templates); a SINGLE task legitimately uses short goals ("Fix the tests").

See #81141.

name: _normalize_task_list
arguments: goal, context, tasks, output_schema, top_role: str, max_children: int
doc: ``(task_list, None)`` from ``tasks=[...]`` or the legacy single ``goal``, else ``(None, error)``.

name: _coerce_task_schemas
arguments: task_list: list[dict[str, Any]], output_schema: Optional[dict[str, Any]]
doc:
Per-task coerced output schemas. A malformed output_schema fails the whole call before any child spawns;
schema-less tasks resolve to None and take no new code paths downstream.

name: _normalize_task_images
doc:
``(cleaned_list_or_None, None)`` for a task's optional ``images`` (local paths, http(s) or data: URLs), else
``(None, error)``. A bare string is wrapped into a one-entry list (small models emit scalars for arrays).

name: _coerce_task_images
doc:
Per-task validated image lists; a malformed list fails the whole call before any child spawns. The legacy
top-level ``images`` applies to a single task only, like ``output_schema``.

name: _is_mcp_toolset_name
doc: Return True for canonical MCP toolsets and their registered aliases.

name: _expand_parent_toolsets
doc:
Add every toolset whose tools are a subset of the parent's tools: a parent on a composite like ``hermes-cli``
must still let a child request ``web``/``terminal``; bare name intersection would reject them. Both sides use
the RESOLVED static surface: a composite's ``includes`` (``debugging`` -> ``web``/``file``, ``safe``) are tools
the parent genuinely holds, and the child never gains a tool the parent lacks.

name: _strip_blocked_tools
doc:
Remove toolsets whose tools are ALL blocked (derived from DELEGATE_BLOCKED_TOOLS so the two can't drift) plus
composite toolsets children must never get (``delegation``, ``kanban``).

name: _blocked_toolsets_for_role
doc:
One-tool deny toolsets for the role; passed as ``disabled_toolsets`` so
blocked names inside mixed bundles are subtracted AFTER composite expansion.

name: _resolve_child_toolsets
doc:
``(enabled_toolsets, disabled_toolsets)`` for a child. Children never gain tools the parent lacks: explicit
``toolsets`` are intersected with the parent's (composite-expanded) set, else the parent's enabled set is
inherited. Blocked tools are stripped twice — whole blocked toolsets here, and exact one-tool deny toolsets via
``disabled_toolsets`` so blocked names inside mixed bundles (hermes-cli) are subtracted AFTER composite
expansion and survive registry refreshes. Orchestrators get ``delegation`` re-added unconditionally
(role-granted, not inherited).

name: without_service_tier
doc: Deep copy of *overrides* without a speed-tier key, at the top level or inside ``extra_body``.

name: _offered_tier_overrides
arguments: tier: str, model: Any, provider: Any, base_url: Any, access_token: Any=None
doc:
Request overrides for *tier* on this route, or None when the route (or, for ultrafast, the route's own Codex
account, ``access_token``) does not offer it. The same gates as ``/fast``.

name: task_service_tier
arguments: word: str, creds: dict[str, Any], parent_agent
doc:
Creds keys for a per-task speed tier on the child's resolved route; a tier the route can't serve raises.
``task_tier_overrides`` is re-applied to the built child by :func:`pin_child_service_tier`.

name: pin_child_service_tier
doc:
Re-apply a task's speed tier to the built child: construction can merge a custom provider's ``extra_body``
(and its tier) back into ``request_overrides``. No-op for tasks that set no tier.

name: live_transcript_root
doc:
Root directory for live transcripts (profile-safe, never ~/.hermes).

Pass ``home`` when the caller holds stable parent-owned profile state
(e.g. the parent agent's SessionDB path). Ambient ``get_hermes_home()``
consults a ContextVar that raw ``threading.Thread`` boundaries drop, so
in a multi-profile process an ambient resolve can land transcripts under
whatever profile the process-wide ``HERMES_HOME`` names at that moment
(#91996).

name: _best_effort
doc: Swallow and debug-log any failure: nothing here may reach the agent loop.

name: _one_line
doc: Collapse to a single line and truncate with an elided-chars note.

name: _redact
doc:
Mask credentials (``force=True``: safety boundary, even when the global
toggle is off); if the redactor is unavailable, withhold rather than leak.

name: wrap_progress_callback
doc:
Wrap a child's tool_progress_callback (may be None) so events also land in
the log; writer failures never propagate. Preserves the ``_flush`` contract.

name: create_live_transcripts
arguments: task_list: list[dict[str, Any]], context: Optional[str]=None, delegation_id: Optional[str]=None, model: Optional[str]=None, provider: Optional[str]=None, home: Optional[Path]=None
doc:
One pre-headered writer per task + a manifest.json; prunes stale dirs.
Returns ``(delegation_id, writers, paths)``; on any top-level failure
``(None, [None]*n, [])`` so delegation proceeds untouched.

``home`` pins every transcript and the manifest to one explicit profile
home instead of an ambient resolve that raw thread boundaries can strip
of its ContextVar override (#91996). Retention pruning runs against the
same resolved root, so pinned homes clean their own stale dirs.

name: _write_manifest
arguments: delegation_id: str, task_list: list[dict[str, Any]], paths: list[str], model: Optional[str]=None, provider: Optional[str]=None, home: Optional[Path]=None

name: update_manifest_statuses
arguments: delegation_id: Optional[str], results: list[dict[str, Any]], home: Optional[Path]=None, *, completed: bool=True
doc:
Best-effort per-task status update once the batch has aggregated (``completed=False``: tasks settled
before the batch ran, e.g. ones their backend refused, while the rest still run).

name: prune_stale_live_dirs
doc:
Remove live/<delegation_id> dirs older than the retention window. Best-effort.

``root`` defaults to the ambient resolve; callers that pin transcripts to an
explicit home pass the same root so the prune sweeps where the writes actually
land (stale dirs under other profiles' roots stay those profiles' business).

name: __init__
arguments: self, delegation_id: str, task_index: int, goal: str, context: Optional[str]=None, root: Optional[Path]=None

name: event
doc:
Append one ``HH:MM:SS role | text`` line. Single choke point: every typed
helper funnels through here so one redaction covers everything.

name: _line
arguments: self, role: str, text: str, limit: int

name: tool_result
arguments: self, name: str, result: Any=None, duration: Any=None, is_error: bool=False

name: marker
doc: Lifecycle marker: start / final / error / interrupt / budget.

name: add_stream_delta
doc: Buffer streamed assistant reply text; flushed as one line.

name: observe
arguments: self, event_type: Any, tool_name: Any=None, preview: Any=None, args: Any=None, **kwargs: Any
doc:
Map a child tool_progress_callback event onto transcript lines.
Unknown events are ignored. Never raises (event() swallows I/O).

name: finalize
doc: Terminal marker with exit-reason detail subagent.complete lacks.

name: coerce_output_schema
doc:
``(schema, None)`` when usable, ``(None, error)`` when not; ``None`` input
passes through as ``(None, None)`` (no schema requested).

name: append_output_contract
doc: Append the explicit output contract block to a child's context.

name: extract_json_candidate
doc: Strip markdown fences and prose around the outermost ``{...}``/``[...]``.

name: validate_output
doc: ``(True, [])`` or ``(False, errors)`` with strings suitable for the retry turn.

name: build_retry_message
doc: Single bounded retry turn: errors verbatim, schema deliberately NOT re-pasted.

name: parent_copy
doc: ``text`` for the parent, remembering ``forced`` for persistent sinks (plain str when equal).

name: redact_child_text
doc: Scrub one child-produced string. ``force=False`` honours the user's opt-out.

name: _redact_field
arguments: key: str, value: str, force: bool
doc:
Redact a string value with its key as context: once a JSON summary is parsed apart, the
key-gated ``"api_key": "<opaque>"`` rule no longer sees the key, so credential-named fields
get that pass on a one-field document. Fails closed for those fields only.

name: redact_child_value
doc: Copy JSON-shaped child data; unsupported or excessively deep values are withheld.

name: redact_summary
arguments: summary: Any, structured: bool, force: bool
doc:
Structured (schema) summaries are redacted per value and re-serialized: a text
pass can eat JSON delimiters (``KEY=***`` swallowing the closing quote and comma)
and break an answer that was valid. The JSON is located with the validator's own
extraction grammar (code fence / surrounding prose), so every wrapper the validator
accepts stays accepted; the wrapper text gets the text pass. Unchanged output keeps
its original formatting; anything without a parseable candidate gets the text pass.

name: redact_child_result
arguments: result: dict[str, Any], output_schema=None, *, force: bool=True
doc:
Project a result or batch, preserving accounting and host-owned model/task identity.

Revalidation here is only for a summary changed by redaction. General schema
revalidation after annotations/truncation belongs to the output-schema owner.
Old durable entries do not retain the schema, so their previous positive verdict
cannot certify a newly redacted summary.

name: redact_completion_event
doc: Scrub output while leaving parent instructions and routing outside the projection.

name: set_emitter
doc: Install (or clear) the renderer-event sink. Called by the desktop gateway.

name: available
doc: True when running under the desktop app (an emitter is wired).

name: user_enabled
doc:
Read a desktop Appearance switch from ``display.<setting>``. The renderer mirrors
these toggles onto the CONNECTED gateway's config, so this is the user's real answer
for local/SSH/URL/cloud gateways alike; ``check_fn``s use it to withdraw a tool from
the schema. Unreadable config -> ``default`` so a shipped-on feature does not vanish
on a transient read error.

name: emit
doc: Route ``event`` to the window owning the current turn; False when no emitter.

name: emit_or_error
arguments: event: str, payload: dict, fail_prefix: str, desktop_only: str, result: dict
doc:
Emit ``event``; ``tool_error`` text on failure (``fail_prefix`` + exception, or
``desktop_only`` when no emitter), else ``result`` as JSON. Calls ``emit`` via the
module attribute so tests can patch it.

name: passthrough_json
doc: Desktop answers with a JSON object; pass it through, else wrap the raw text.

name: _read_limited_response_body
arguments: source: Any, limit: int, *, label: str

name: _get_bot_token
doc: Resolve the Discord bot token under the active profile secret scope.

name: _discord_request
arguments: method: str, path: str, token: str, params: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None, body: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, timeout: int=15
doc: Make a request to the Discord REST API.

significant_calls.expression:
urllib.request.Request(
        url, data=None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8"), method=method,
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bot {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "User-Agent": "Hermes-Agent (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)"})

name: _token_cache_key
doc: Stable non-reversible cache key for a bot token.

name: _read_caps_file
doc: Disk cache contents ({token_key: {"caps", "ts"}}); {} when missing/corrupt.

name: _load_caps_from_disk
doc: Return fresh disk-cached capabilities for *token*, or None.

name: _detect_capabilities_nonblocking
doc:
Schema-build lookup: in-process cache → fresh disk cache → permissive default plus a
fire-and-forget background detection that fills the disk cache for the NEXT process
(the ~2-5s blocking HTTPS call must stay off the cold-start critical path).

name: _fetch_capabilities
doc:
Fetch capabilities from GET /applications/@me. Pure network fetch — never touches
the in-process cache (background detection must not mutate schemas mid-process).
Detection failure is permissive.

name: _detect_capabilities
doc:
Blocking detection via GET /applications/@me, cached per token (the warm-up path;
schema builds use the non-blocking variant). ``force`` re-fetches.

name: _reset_capability_cache
doc: Test hook: clear the detection cache.

name: _member_summary
doc:
Member row; ``full`` adds the avatar/join fields member_info exposes
(key order is part of the result text, so the two shapes stay explicit).

name: _limit_param
doc: Discord caps list endpoints at 100 per page.

name: _list_channels

name: _get_allowed
doc: Get the process-wide skill passthrough allowlist.

name: _is_hermes_provider_credential
doc:
True if ``name`` is a Hermes-managed provider credential per
``_HERMES_PROVIDER_ENV_BLOCKLIST`` or a dynamic Hermes-internal secret
(AUXILIARY_*_API_KEY / _BASE_URL, GATEWAY_RELAY_*). Skill-declared
``required_environment_variables`` must not override this — that was the
GHSA-rhgp-j443-p4rf bypass (a skill registered ``OPENAI_API_KEY`` and received it
in the ``execute_code`` child); non-Hermes keys (TENOR_API_KEY, …) stay
registerable. Fails closed when the blocklist cannot be imported.

name: register_env_passthrough
doc:
Register env var names as allowed in sandboxed environments (typically a
skill's ``required_environment_variables``). Hermes-managed provider credentials
are rejected (GHSA-rhgp-j443-p4rf) — such skills should use the main-process tools
(web_search, web_extract, …); third-party keys pass normally.

name: _accepted
doc:
Yield non-empty *names* that are not Hermes provider credentials; refused
names are logged with *refusal_msg* (``%r`` = name).

name: _load_config_passthrough
doc:
Load ``tools.env_passthrough`` from config.yaml (cached). Same credential
filter as register_env_passthrough: operator config must not tunnel provider
credentials into sandbox children either (GHSA-rhgp-j443-p4rf).

name: is_env_passthrough
doc:
True if *var_name* was registered by a skill or listed in config and is not a
Hermes-managed credential NOW. Ownership changes after acceptance (a platform plugin
registered later declares the name in its ``required_env`` or manifest), so the refusal applied at registration
is re-applied here, where every child builder consumes the allowlist.

name: get_all_passthrough
doc:
Return the union of skill-registered and config-based passthrough vars, minus names
that have become Hermes-managed credentials since they were accepted.

name: resolve_passthrough_value
doc:
Resolve an allowlisted variable without crossing profile boundaries. ``fallback``
is what the caller would have forwarded before secret scopes existed (a snapshot of
``os.environ`` / the profile ``.env``). An active multiplex scope is authoritative:
a missing key returns ``None``, never the process-global env, and an unscoped read
raises the fail-closed ``UnscopedSecretError``. Outside multiplexing an installed
scope keeps overlay semantics and an unscoped caller keeps its fallback.

name: scoped_passthrough_additions
doc:
Declared passthrough names the bound profile secret scope supplies but the env being
filtered (*present*) lacks. A routed profile's ``.env`` and hydrated sources never enter
``os.environ`` (``load_hermes_dotenv`` skips the process-global load for a routed home), so a
name-by-name filter over the process env can only forward a declared name the LAUNCH profile
also happens to define — the served profile's own value has no way in (#114209). Reads the
bound scope alone: never ``os.environ``, never another profile. Empty without a scope, so
single-profile spawns are byte-identical.

name: clear_env_passthrough
doc:
Reset the skill-registered allowlist (e.g. on session reset).

Clears the process-wide set; a later ``skill_view`` re-registers its
vars on demand, so recovery is a single skill load.

name: _plugin_backend_is_remote
doc: Whether a plugin-registered terminal backend is remote (fail-soft).

name: _run
doc:
Run a short subprocess -> (returncode, stdout, stderr); failures (binary
missing, timeout, OSError) return (-1, "", "<reason>"). Output goes through temp
files, not pipes, so ``timeout`` bounds the *whole* call even on native Windows: a
console-script launcher (``pip.exe``) can spawn a descendant that inherits the
captured handles and outlives its parent; with OS pipes ``communicate()``'s reader
threads block until that grandchild closes the write end (a warm probe could hang
~28 min holding ``_CACHE_LOCK``). Temp files make ``wait()`` cover only the child.

name: _py_out
doc: stdout of ``<binary> *args`` when the binary is on PATH and exits 0, else None.

name: _python_version_of
doc: Return a short version string like ``3.12.4`` for ``binary``, or None.

name: _has_pip_module
doc: True if ``<binary> -m pip --version`` succeeds.

name: _detect_pep668
doc:
True when ``<binary>`` is PEP-668 externally-managed (``EXTERNALLY-MANAGED``
marker next to the stdlib, as Debian/Ubuntu ship).

name: _pip_python_version
doc:
If ``pip`` is on PATH, the Python version it's bound to — the trailing
``(python X.Y)`` of ``pip --version`` (e.g. ``"3.12"``), else None.

name: _resolve_terminal_backend
doc: Scope-aware terminal backend name (``local`` when unresolvable).

name: _build_probe_line
doc:
Build the one-liner; "" when nothing notable is detected — the goal is to
save the model from an avoidable wall, not narrate a healthy environment.

name: get_environment_probe_line
doc:
Return the cached probe line (building it on first call); "" when the
environment is clean, so the prompt assembler drops the section. Waits at most
``_PROBE_WAIT_TIMEOUT`` on the single worker, then fails open with "".
``force_refresh`` is for tests.

A wedged probe subprocess (#67964) therefore can never block system-prompt construction — at worst the
toolchain line is absent from prompts built while the probe is stuck.

name: _probe_worker
doc: Body of the single probe thread — computes and publishes the line.

name: _ensure_probe_started
doc: Start the probe worker if it isn't running and hasn't finished.

name: warm_environment_probe_async
_reset_cache_for_tests
doc: Test helper — clear the cache between probe scenarios.

name: _halve_backslash_runs
doc: Replace every maximal run of backslashes with half its length.

name: maybe_correct_backslash_doubling
arguments: old_string: str, new_string: str, content: str
doc:
Halve a verified doubled anchor only when the replacement has no backslashes.

Every old_string run must be even and its halved form must occur in the file.
Replacement backslashes are ambiguous regardless of run length, so raise
``AmbiguousEscapeDriftError`` rather than let fuzzy matching apply them.

name: _strip_spurious_quote_escapes
doc: Un-escape a spurious backslash before a quote character: ``\'`` -> ``'``, ``\"`` -> ``"``.

name: _quote_escapes_all_spurious
doc:
True when every escaped quote in ``strings`` is attributable to the wire artifact.

The artifact escapes quotes mechanically, so a quote kind it touched is escaped at EVERY
occurrence across the whole call, by exactly one backslash. A backslash the model meant
(``"say \"hi\""`` in new code) went through the same extra escape and therefore arrives
as two or more backslashes before the quote, never one. So for each kind that appears as
``\q`` anywhere: every ``q`` in every string must be preceded by exactly one backslash.
A bare ``q`` beside a ``\q`` (the kind was not drifted, so the ``\q`` is real) or a longer
run (an intended escape) cannot be told apart from the artifact, so it refuses.

name: maybe_correct_quote_escaping
arguments: old_string: str, new_string: str, content: str
doc:
Return a corrected ``(old_string, new_string)`` if a spurious backslash-before-quote wire
artifact is detected AND verified against the file's actual content; otherwise unchanged.

Mirrors ``_detect_escape_drift``'s quote-suspect check: ``\'`` or ``\"`` present in BOTH
old_string and new_string is the signature of an apostrophe/quote that picked up a spurious
backslash in transit, not a literal escape the model intended. The stripped old_string must
appear verbatim in content, which verifies old_string (and rules out a file that really
contains ``\'``/``\"``). new_string's added code is not in the file, so it is only
stripped when ``_quote_escapes_all_spurious`` holds for the whole call; otherwise the call
is left unchanged for the existing reject-and-ask guard. Raises ``AmbiguousEscapeDriftError``
when new_string escapes a quote kind that old_string does not.

name: maybe_correct_escape_drift
arguments: old_string: str, new_string: str, content: str
doc:
Apply whichever escape-drift auto-correction (if any) is verified against the file's
actual content and report which one fired.

Tries quote escaping, then backslash correction of the anchor only. Raises
``AmbiguousEscapeDriftError`` for a verified doubled anchor whose replacement
contains backslashes, or a verified quote correction whose replacement escapes a
quote kind the anchor does not; the caller must return an error without matching.

Returns ``(corrected_old, corrected_new, note)``: ``note`` is a human-readable description
of the correction that was applied, or ``None`` if neither fired. The caller attaches
``note`` to the successful result (e.g. ``PatchResult.note``) so a corrected call stays
distinguishable from one whose arguments never needed correction.

name: wait_fal_queue_result
doc:
``handle.get()`` without the SDK's 0.1 s status poll: drain ``iter_events`` at ``interval``,
then ``get()`` sees Completed on its first status check and fetches the result.

name: import_fal_client
doc:
Import ``fal_client`` (via ``pm`` when available) and return
the module reference.

Callers cache the result on their own module global so tests can monkeypatch it.

name: _extract_http_status
doc: HTTP status from httpx (``.response.status_code``) or fal_client (``.status_code``) exceptions, else None.

name: _managed_fal_billing_error
doc:
Human-readable tail for a Nous managed-gateway ``BILLING_ERROR`` response, else None.

``what`` names the rejected thing ("model", "endpoint"); the wording is shared by the image
and video callers so the two surfaces never drift.

name: _managed_fal_retry_after_seconds
doc:
Seconds the managed gateway asked us to wait after a 429: the ``Retry-After`` header,
else the body's ``error.retryAfter``; None when the status is not 429 or neither is present.

name: _managed_fal_rate_limit_message
arguments: what: str, name: str, retry_after: Optional[float]

name: submit_managed_fal_with_rate_limit_retry
arguments: submit: Callable[[dict[str, str]], Any], *, what: str, name: str
doc:
Call ``submit(headers)`` with a fresh ``x-idempotency-key``; on a 429 whose Retry-After
fits the cap, wait it out (interrupt-aware) and resubmit ONCE under a new key.

A second 429, or one with an unknown/too-long Retry-After, raises ValueError naming the
rate limit — it must never fall through to the callers' "model may not be enabled" 4xx text,
which sends agents off to switch models. Every other exception propagates untouched.

name: __init__
arguments: self, fal_client: Any, *, key: str, queue_run_origin: str

name: submit
arguments: self, application: str, arguments: dict[str, Any], *, path: str='', hint: Optional[str]=None, webhook_url: Optional[str]=None, priority: Any=None, headers: Optional[dict[str, str]]=None, start_timeout: Optional[int | float]=None

significant_calls.expression:
self._request_handle_class(
            request_id=data["request_id"], response_url=data["response_url"],
            status_url=data["status_url"], cancel_url=data["cancel_url"], client=self._http_client)

name: _comment_op
arguments: keys, missing_msg, label, method, uri, queries=None, body=None, flag_success=False
doc:
Handler factory: client check, then required ``keys`` (stripped) → lark_call → result.

All keys except ``content`` are URI path params. ``queries(args)`` / ``body(args, values)``
build the request pieces; ``flag_success`` adds ``success=True`` to the result (writes).

name: _paged_queries
doc: Query params shared by the listing endpoints; page_token goes last (after any extra).

name: set_client
doc: Store a lark client for the current thread (called by feishu_comment).

name: get_client
doc: Return the lark client for the current thread, or None.

name: build_request
doc: Build a tenant-token BaseRequest. Raises ImportError if lark_oapi is missing.

name: lark_call
arguments: client, method, uri, paths=None, queries=None, body=None
doc:
Build + execute a BaseRequest; returns (code, msg, data_dict).

Tool handlers run synchronously in a worker thread (no running event loop), so the
blocking lark client is called directly.

name: raw_body
doc: Parsed JSON object of the raw HTTP body, or None when absent/unparseable/not a dict.

name: response_data
doc: ``data`` of a lark response: prefer the raw JSON body, fall back to typed .data.

name: identify_binary_bytes
doc:
Best-effort human name for binary content from its magic bytes; never raises.
The ISO-media entry additionally requires ``ftyp`` at offset 4 (three leading
NULs alone are too weak a signature).

name: describe_binary_file
doc:
One-line binary-file refusal naming the TYPE ("PNG image data, 4.1 KB"), so the
model gets what-is-this in one read instead of hunting for tools it may lack.

name: _new_sentinel
doc:
Per-call separator line for a compound shell probe. 128 random bits make a
collision with file content negligible; the underscores keep the token outside
the base64 alphabet, so a sentinel leaking into a sample segment fails base64
validation instead of decoding into bytes.

name: _split_segments
doc:
Split compound-probe stdout on its sentinel lines. Every producer (``wc``,
    ``base64``, ``cut``) newline-terminates or prints nothing, so the separator is
    always ``sentinel + "
"`` on its own line; the text after the final sentinel
    is the status segment.

name: _json_nonstandard_constant
doc:
First NaN/Infinity/-Infinity in ``text`` when it is otherwise valid JSON,
else None. ``json.loads`` accepts these JavaScript extensions by default.

name: _refuse_introduced_json_constant
arguments: path: str, content: str, pre_content: Optional[str]
doc:
Refuse a JSON write that INTRODUCES a nonstandard constant (strict JSON
consumers reject them). A file that already holds one keeps accepting
unrelated edits, which is why the lenient syntax gate can't do this check.

name: read_file
arguments: self, path: str, offset: int=1, limit: int=2000
doc: Read a file with pagination support.

name: read_file_raw
doc: Whole file as a plain string: no pagination, line numbers or clamping.

name: write_file
arguments: self, path: str, content: str, pre_content: Optional[str]=None
doc: Write content to a file, creating directories as needed.

name: patch_replace
arguments: self, path: str, old_string: str, new_string: str, replace_all: bool=False
doc: Replace text in a file using fuzzy matching.

name: patch_v4a
doc: Apply a V4A format patch.

name: delete_file
doc: Delete a file. Returns WriteResult with .error set on failure.

name: move_file
doc: Move/rename a file. Returns WriteResult with .error set on failure.

name: search
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str='.', target: str='content', file_glob: Optional[str]=None, limit: int=50, offset: int=0, output_mode: str='content', context: int=0, order: str='discovery'
doc: Search for content or files.

name: _exec
arguments: self, command: str, cwd: str | None=None, timeout: int | None=None, stdin_data: str | None=None
doc:
Run ``command`` on the backend. cwd: explicit arg → live ``env.cwd`` →
init-time ``self.cwd``. ``stdin_data`` is piped (bypasses ARG_MAX).

name: _has_command
doc:
Check if a command exists in the environment (cached); rg goes through
the resolver so a mid-session install becomes visible.

name: _cat
doc: ``cat`` the file with stderr silenced (missing file → non-zero exit).

name: _run_python_snippet
doc:
Run ``snippet`` via the backend's ``python3``, retrying with ``python``
when only that name exists (Windows / older systems).

name: _fenced_read
doc:
Run BODY, then each of MORE, each in its own sentinel-delimited segment; return (those
segments, BODY's exit status, reply).

The transport merges the backend's own stdout with the command's, and every caller here
decodes a segment into file bytes, so the payload has to be delimited rather than taken to
be the whole reply: a remote shell announcing ``TERM`` is four base64 characters that would
otherwise join the payload and decode to ``b"LDL"`` at the head of it. The fence drops noise
OUTSIDE it only; output emitted while BODY runs (a ``BASH_ENV`` DEBUG hook) lands inside the
payload, so a caller that writes the bytes back must verify them independently (MORE). The
status rides in its own trailing segment so a failed BODY is still told apart from an empty
file. ``(None, None, reply)`` when no fenced reply came back — the command never ran as
written.

name: _matches_size
doc:
Whether DATA is exactly as long as the file's own ``wc -c``. Noise inside the payload
only ever ADDS text, and any addition that still decodes adds bytes, so equal length is
the check; noise in the size segment breaks its single-integer shape instead.

name: _sample_file_bytes
doc:
First ``length`` raw bytes, base64-wrapped so they survive the terminal
transport (which decodes stdout with ``errors="replace"`` and manufactures
U+FFFD for every undecodable byte, including a multibyte char cut in half
by ``head -c``). None when no clean base64 came back (no ``base64`` binary);
callers then fall back to the text heuristic.

Wrapping the sample in base64 lets the original bytes survive the transport, so binary detection can
happen at the byte layer where it is well-defined (#80308 and friends). Fenced like the
byte-exact read below: this sample is the binary-admission gate in FRONT of that read, so
backend noise decoded into it decides whether a file is editable at all.

name: _read_exact_bytes
doc:
The file's bytes exactly, for the edit paths that write back every line they did not touch.

The text transport cannot carry them: it decodes with errors="replace", so a byte UTF-8 cannot
decode comes back as U+FFFD and the edit then persists it. A native read on the local POSIX host,
else base64 over the transport; ``(None, result)`` hands back the failed shell read for the
caller's message. Only a regular file gets a native open (a FIFO would block this thread); the
rest take the shell path and its timeout, as before.

name: _failed_read
arguments: path: str, payload: str, read_rc: int
doc: The backend's own diagnostic for a read that ran and failed, else a bare exit status.

name: _read_exact_bytes_hex
doc:
``od`` fallback for a backend without ``base64``, fenced the same way.

``read_file_raw`` is the edit paths' source read AND, through ``_apply_add``, their
existence check, so a transport that simply is not installed must not read as "no such
file" — that clobbers the file the Add was refusing to overwrite. ``od`` is POSIX and
present in busybox; when it is missing too the caller gets a transport error, never a
not-found.

name: _decode_base64_sample
doc:
Decode one ``base64`` transport reply (a ``head -c N`` sample or a whole file). Whitespace-joins
the whole text first (``base64`` wraps at 76 columns), so callers hand over exactly one
segment; anything else fails validation → None.

name: _is_likely_binary_bytes
doc:
Byte-layer binary detection: text iff valid UTF-8, allowing one incomplete
multibyte sequence at the very end (artifact of the byte-boundary cut).
NUL bytes or mid-stream invalid UTF-8 stay read-only so a read→edit→write
round-trip never rewrites undecodable bytes as U+FFFD; a file that
legitimately CONTAINS U+FFFD is valid UTF-8 and reads as text.

See #80308.

name: _is_likely_binary
arguments: self, path: str, content_sample: str | None=None
doc: Legacy text-layer binary check: extension, else >30% non-printable chars.

name: _add_line_numbers
doc:
Prefix each line with a compact ``<n>|`` gutter, clamping long lines. Not
fixed-width: padding cost ~16% more tokens per line for no accuracy gain in
A/B, while dropping numbers regressed line-referencing.

name: _expand_path
doc:
Expand ``~`` / ``~user`` via the backend's shell (its HOME, not the
host's). A host path under the configured workspace mount is rewritten
to that container path first, so a Windows drive path is readable
inside Docker. Must run BEFORE shell escaping — ~ doesn't expand in quotes.

name: _escape_shell_arg
doc:
Escape a string for safe use in shell commands.

On Windows native drive paths (``C:\Users\x`` / ``C:/Users/x``)
and mixed MSYS leftovers (``/c/Users\x``) are rewritten to the
Git Bash ``/c/Users/x`` form via ``_bash_safe_path``: bash eats
backslashes and MSYS otherwise mangles drive paths into the
``Directory \drivers\etc does not exist`` failure class. Reuses
the env-layer translator so shell file ops and the terminal ``cd``
agree on the path form. No-op off Windows and for plain POSIX paths.

``translate_path=False`` skips that translation for non-path values
such as regex patterns. Backslash compensation applies only to the
local Windows argv transport. Serialized shell text stays literal.

name: _escape_native_tool_arg
doc:
Quote a path for a NATIVE Windows binary (rg, node, git ...): those don't
understand the MSYS ``/c/...`` form and Hermes disables MSYS argument
conversion, so nothing translates it back (→ ``os error 3``). ``C:/Users/x``
is accepted by every layer. Identical to ``_escape_shell_arg`` off Windows.

name: _atomic_write
doc:
Write ``content`` atomically: stdin → temp file in the SAME directory →
``mv -f`` (same-FS rename; cross-device ``mv`` is copy+unlink, NOT atomic).
``mkdir -p`` folded in. Exit 0 = swap happened; non-zero = original intact.

Symlink targets are resolved first (replacing the link would orphan the
target) and the temp dir recomputed from the RESOLVED target. Existing
target: mode copied via ``stat`` (GNU ``-c%a`` / BSD ``-f%Lp``) + ``chmod``
(``chmod --reference`` is GNU-only). New target: ``chmod "=rw"`` AFTER cat
gives umask-default perms instead of mktemp's 0600 — not ``$(umask)``
arithmetic (zsh parses leading-zero constants as decimal), quoted so zsh
doesn't =word-expand. ``trap ... EXIT`` removes the temp on every failure.
The local POSIX backend does the same in-process (``tools.file_operations_native``).

name: _file_has_bom
doc:
Whether the on-disk file starts with a UTF-8 BOM. ALWAYS probes disk:
``pre_content`` usually comes from ``read_file_raw``, which strips BOMs, so
trusting it would silently drop the marker on rewrite. Missing → False.

name: _unified_diff
arguments: self, old_content: str, new_content: str, filename: str

name: _not_regular_error
doc: Error for a path that exists but would block if read.

name: _probe_regular_file
doc:
Byte size of a REGULAR file: ``(file_size, status)`` with status ``"ok"``,
``"missing"``, ``"not_regular"``, ``"bad_size"`` (unparseable ``wc``),
``"env_unavailable"``, or the named working-directory error when the exec
wrapper itself failed (``_env_unavailable_error`` surfaces it verbatim).
``wc -c <`` on a writer-less FIFO/socket//dev/zero blocks forever and a
name-based blocklist can't cover a FIFO (a file TYPE at any path); ``[ -f ]``
is a stat (symlinks followed) so it answers without touching content. A dangling
symlink is ``not_regular``, never ``missing``: the entry exists, and a writer
told the path is free would follow the link and create its target.

name: _detect_binary
doc:
``(is_binary, sample_bytes)`` — byte-layer detection when the transport
allows (base64 sample), else the legacy text heuristic (sample is None).

name: _python_interpreter_cmd
doc:
Return a shell-safe Python interpreter for the terminal backend.

On the local backend ``sys.executable`` is always a working
interpreter — and on Windows it dodges the Microsoft Store
``python``/``python3`` alias stub (exit 49, "Python was not
found") that otherwise breaks inline ``-c`` snippets. Remote
backends (docker/ssh/...) don't have the agent's interpreter, so
they fall back to ``python3`` on their own PATH (the ``python``
fallback is handled at the call site).

name: _exec_python_snippet
arguments: self, snippet: str, py: str | None=None
doc:
Run a Python ``snippet`` in the terminal backend's interpreter.

Base64-encodes the snippet so it survives every shell/quoting layer
as pure ASCII: Windows ``subprocess`` list-arg quoting and ``bash``
double-quote processing both eat backslashes, which otherwise
corrupts Windows paths (``C:\Users\x``) and byte literals
(``b'\xfe\xff'``) embedded in a ``-c`` program. ``exec`` decodes
and runs it unchanged.

name: _try_read_utf16
arguments: self, path: str, offset: int, limit: int, file_size: int
doc:
Read ``path`` as UTF-16 transcoded to UTF-8, or None (caller falls back
to the binary-file error). Skips known-binary extensions and files over
10 MiB. ``path`` must already be expanded.

name: read_file
arguments: self, path: str, offset: int=1, limit: int=2000
doc:
Read a file with pagination, binary detection, and line numbers.

``offset`` is 1-indexed; ``limit`` is clamped by ``normalize_read_pagination``.
One shell round-trip answers every question the read needs (existence, size,
binary sample, page, line count, trailing newline; see ``_read_probe_cmd``).
An unparseable reply falls back to ``_read_file_sequential`` (one probe per
question), so an exotic shell can never do worse than before. On a local
POSIX environment the read never touches the shell (``_read_file_native``).

name: _native_read_enabled
doc:
Whether ``read_file`` and ``search_files`` may bypass the shell: only POSIX + ``LocalEnvironment``
(file is on this host, path already native; Windows keeps the shell path since
file_operations holds Git-Bash-style paths there). ``HERMES_NATIVE_FILE_READ=0``
turns the fast path off.

name: _native_path
doc: ``path`` resolved the way the shell resolves it: against the live backend cwd.

name: _read_file_native
arguments: self, path: str, offset: int, limit: int
doc:
``read_file`` without a shell — same contract as the shell path, byte for
byte. ``os.stat`` is the ``[ -f ]`` guard (a stat, never an open, so FIFOs and
devices are refused before anything touches them); the first 1000 bytes drive
the byte-layer binary check; the page is produced exactly as
``sed -n 'a,bp' | cut -b1-N`` prints it (each line clamped to N bytes and
newline-terminated) then decoded with errors="replace" like the transport.
One chunked pass counts lines and collects the page, so neither the file nor
a pathological line is ever held whole. ``path`` is already expanded; any
unexpected OSError hands over to the shell path.

name: _read_probe_cmd
arguments: self, path: str, offset: int, end_line: int, line_clamp_bytes: int, sentinel: str
doc:
One shell command answering every question ``read_file`` asks: six
segments each closed by a ``sentinel`` line — byte size, base64 of the first
1000 bytes, the ``sed | cut`` page, ``wc -l``, whether the last byte is a
newline, then the base64 and page pipeline statuses. Probes run only inside
``[ -f ]`` (stat-not-open, like ``_probe_regular_file``) so a FIFO/device never
reaches ``head``/``sed``. A missing path echoes ``MISSING_SENTINEL`` (a compound
command only reports its last status). Every stage silences stderr: the local
backend merges stderr into stdout and a stray diagnostic would land inside a
segment. The byte clamp is ``4 * max_line_length + 1``; see ``_read_file_sequential``.

name: _read_file_missing
arguments: self, path: str, offset: int, limit: int
doc:
Not-found recovery shared by every read path. Unicode-equivalent spellings
(NFC/NFD, confusable spaces/quotes) render identically, so the model can never
discover the byte mismatch by retyping — retrying is the tool's job. No
equivalent spelling → suggest similar files.

name: _read_binary_file
arguments: self, path: str, offset: int, limit: int, file_size: int, sample_bytes: Optional[bytes]
doc:
Binary branch shared by every read path: UTF-16 text (Notepad, PowerShell
``>``) trips the binary guard; transcode it, else refuse with the type name.

UTF-16 rescue (ported from MoonshotAI/kimi-code#2647): the terminal env decodes stdout as UTF-8 with
errors="replace", so a UTF-16 text file (Windows Notepad .txt, PowerShell `>` redirects) arrives
mangled with U+FFFD and trips the binary guard. Probe the raw bytes via the backend's Python and
transcode to UTF-8 when a BOM or the zero-byte parity heuristic identifies UTF-16.

name: _read_file_sequential
arguments: self, path: str, offset: int, limit: int
doc:
One-probe-per-call read: the pre-compound form, kept as fallback for
image / known-binary extensions and unparseable compound replies. ``path`` is
already expanded and ``offset``/``limit`` normalized.

name: _assemble_read_result
arguments: self, read_output: str, *, offset: int, end_line: int, total_lines: int, file_size: int, file_ends_with_newline: Optional[bool]
doc:
Turn a raw ``sed | cut`` page into the final ``ReadResult``. Shared by every
read path so the BOM strip, pagination hint, ``cut`` newline-artifact fix and
the ambiguous-silence guards never drift apart. ``file_ends_with_newline`` is
None when the caller could not tell (artifact left alone, as before).

name: _unicode_variant_match
doc:
On-disk spelling of a file whose name is unicode-equivalent to ``path``
(NFC/NFD, confusable spaces/quotes). Returns the entry only when EXACTLY one
matches — several candidates = homoglyph collision, guessing would read the
wrong file.

name: _suggest_similar_files
doc: "File not found" result listing up to 5 similar names from the same directory.

name: read_file_raw
doc: Whole file as a plain string (no pagination/line numbers/clamping).

name: read_file_bytes
doc: Read binary-safe bytes (as base64) from any shell-backed environment.

name: delete_file
doc:
Delete a single file (directories rejected) via the backend's ``python -c``
so one code path works on local/docker/ssh AND Windows shells (no ``rm``).

name: _reject_unencodable
doc:
Refuse content with a lone surrogate BEFORE any subprocess: letting it
reach the pipe spawns a child that hangs or truncates the target via
empty-stdin ``cat``. A regex scan needs no encode.

name: _fail_closed_syntax_error
arguments: path: str, ext: str, content: str
doc:
Fail-closed pre-write gate for ``_FAIL_CLOSED_INPROC_EXTS`` (JSON/YAML/TOML):
a structured-format write that doesn't parse is a corrupt write, so refuse
before any bytes touch disk. Checked against the RAW content, before the
BOM/CRLF shims (post-shim linting would false-positive on a BOM-marked file).

name: _write_probe_cmd
arguments: self, path: str, sentinel: str, body: Optional[str]
doc:
One shell command for the on-disk questions ``write_file`` asks. Two
segments closed by a ``sentinel`` line: base64 of the first three bytes (BOM
detection at the byte layer, same on-disk truth as ``_file_has_bom``), then
``body``: ``"cat"`` for the full text when pre-content is wanted, ``"sample"``
for the 4 KB line-ending sample, or None for nothing. Gated on ``[ -f ]`` so a
FIFO/device never reaches ``head``/``cat``; a missing path echoes ``MISSING_SENTINEL``.

name: _probe_write_target
arguments: self, path: str, pre_content: Optional[str], want_pre: bool
doc:
``(has_bom, pre_content, original_line_ending)`` for ``path`` in ONE
round-trip (replaces ``cat`` when pre-content is wanted, a ``head -c 4096``
line-ending sample and a ``head -c 3`` BOM check). Semantics unchanged:
pre-content is read only when wanted and not supplied; the line ending comes
from pre-content when there is any, else from the sample; the BOM always comes
from disk. An unparseable reply falls back to the separate probes.

name: _probe_write_target_sequential
arguments: self, path: str, pre_content: Optional[str], want_pre: bool
doc:
Pre-compound form of ``_probe_write_target``: one exec per question. A
failed ``cat`` leaves pre_content None so the lint-delta and LSP consumers
degrade gracefully.

name: _verify_written_hash
doc:
Compare the on-disk sha256 to the intended bytes: ``(verified, error)``.
The explicit flag saves the model a confirming re-read; a mismatch is a hard
error. ``verified`` is None when the hash could not be taken.

name: write_file
arguments: self, path: str, content: str, pre_content: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Write content atomically, creating parent directories as needed.

Order: deny list → lone-surrogate refusal → fail-closed syntax gate on the
CANDIDATE content (JSON/YAML/TOML) → one compound on-disk probe
(pre-content when wanted, CRLF, BOM; see ``_probe_write_target``) →
JSON NaN/Infinity refusal when the write introduces one → CRLF/BOM
preservation → atomic write (content rides stdin: no ARG_MAX limit) →
sha256 verification → lint delta → LSP check when syntax is clean
(non-blocking; the pre-edit content is its baseline, see ``_maybe_lsp_diagnostics``). ``pre_content``: pre-edit content the
caller already has (skips the read); BOM detection always probes disk.

name: _no_match_result
arguments: self, path: str, content: str, old_string: str, new_string: str, match_count: int, error: Optional[str]
doc:
PatchResult for a failed fuzzy match. Already-applied detection first: the
most common production failure is a re-send of an edit that already landed,
and a success-shaped no-op stops the model burning turns on re-reads.
Otherwise attach a best-effort "Did you mean?" snippet to the error.

name: _verify_patch_persisted
doc:
Re-read ``path`` and confirm the intended bytes landed; error result or None.
Catches silent persistence failures (FS oddities, races, truncated pipe).
Line endings are normalized first (Windows text-mode ``open()`` writes LF as
CRLF) and the re-read's BOM stripped (``new_content`` is the BOM-less
string we matched against).

name: patch_replace
arguments: self, path: str, old_string: str, new_string: str, replace_all: bool=False
doc:
Replace text in a file using fuzzy matching (``old_string`` must be
unique unless ``replace_all``). Returns a PatchResult with diff + lint.

name: patch_v4a
doc:
Apply a V4A format patch (``*** Begin Patch`` / ``*** Update File:`` /
``@@ hint @@`` hunks / ``*** End Patch``).

name: search
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str='.', target: str='content', file_glob: Optional[str]=None, limit: int=50, offset: int=0, output_mode: str='content', context: int=0, order: str='discovery'
doc:
Search for content (regex, ``target="content"``) or files (glob,
``target="files"``). ``output_mode``: "content", "files_only" or "count";
``context``: lines of context around matches; ``order``: file-search
ordering — fast "discovery" or exact "modified" time.

significant_calls.expression:
self._dispatch_search(pattern, path, target, file_glob, limit, offset,
                                       output_mode, context, order)

name: count_conflict_blocks
doc:
Unresolved git merge-conflict blocks in a ``LINE|CONTENT`` read; 0 when the page has no
balanced ``<<<<<<< `` / ``>>>>>>> `` pair (a lone marker in prose or a test fixture is not a
conflict). Reported on read so the model resolves the conflict instead of editing around it.

name: _strip_terminal_fence_leaks
doc:
Strip leaked terminal fence wrappers (OSC sequences, fence markers) from
command output; drops lines that were nothing but wrapper.

name: _detect_line_ending
doc:
Dominant line ending of ``sample`` (``\r\n`` if any CRLF in the first 4KB,
else ``\n``), or None for empty/single-line content. Preserves a file's
endings across write_file/patch: bare-LF tool args would otherwise silently
normalize CRLF files, and patch would produce mixed endings.

name: _normalize_line_endings
doc:
Convert every line ending (CRLF, lone CR, LF) in ``text`` to ``target``.
Idempotent. Collapses to LF first — separate replacements would
double-convert CRLF → LFLF.

name: _strip_bom
doc:
Return (text-without-leading-BOM, had_bom). Only a leading BOM is
stripped; mid-content U+FEFF is legitimate data.

name: _has_bom
doc: True if ``text`` begins with a UTF-8 BOM.

name: _coerce_int
doc: Best-effort integer coercion for tool pagination inputs.

name: normalize_read_pagination
doc:
Clamp read_file pagination so invalid values can never reach a sed range
like ``0,-1p`` (schemas declare bounds, but not every caller enforces them).
The ``limit`` ceiling is ``tool_output.max_lines`` from config.yaml.

name: normalize_search_pagination
doc: Return safe search pagination bounds for shell head/tail pipelines.

name: _densify_matches
doc:
Lossless path-grouped text block: path once, then ``  <line>: <content>``
rows. Relies on rg/grep emitting a file's hits consecutively. None when
too few matches to be worth it.

name: _looks_like_linter_unusable
doc: True iff ``output`` from ``base_cmd`` (first word of the linter cmd) says the tool itself couldn't run.

name: _lint_json_inproc
doc: In-process JSON syntax check. Returns (ok, error_message).

name: _lint_yaml_inproc
doc:
In-process YAML syntax check; ``__SKIP__`` when ruamel.yaml is missing. Syntax-only
(``YAML.parse``), NOT ``safe_load``: loading rejects valid multi-doc streams and
app tags (``!Sub``, ``!vault``), and this is a fail-closed WRITE gate.

name: _lint_toml_inproc
doc: In-process TOML syntax check (stdlib tomllib).

name: _lint_python_inproc
doc:
In-process Python syntax check via ast.parse (py_compile's scope, no subprocess). Parses the
bytes, as py_compile does, so a legacy ``coding:`` cookie is honoured for a file the edit paths
read with surrogateescape.

name: _post_deferred
arguments: owner: str, abs_path: str, future, carry, token
doc:
Done-callback (LSP loop thread): queue a late verdict for the session that made the edit, then
release a turn end waiting on it (``agent.lsp.deferred.settle_for_agent``).

name: _queue_late_verdict
arguments: owner: str, abs_path: str, future, carry
doc:
A superseded check posts nothing: the newer check owns its verdict AND the notes it carried.
No verdict hands back only what the check still holds (``result.carry``), never the caller's copy.

name: _check_lint
doc:
Syntax-check ``path``: in-process linter when one matches the
extension (``content`` avoids a re-read), else the shell linter table.

name: _run_managed_node_linter
doc: Run the ``ext`` Node linter on the host under PM's Node; None when PM has none.

name: _check_lint_delta
arguments: self, path: str, pre_content: Optional[str], post_content: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Post-write lint; when it fails and ``pre_content`` is known, report only
errors this edit introduced (pre-existing lines filtered out). Semantic
(LSP) diagnostics are a separate channel — see ``_maybe_lsp_diagnostics``.

name: _lsp_local_only
doc:
True iff wired to a local backend. LSP servers run on the host and
can't see files inside Docker/Modal/SSH/Daytona sandboxes.

name: _local_workspace_untrusted
doc:
True iff on a local backend the linter's cwd lies outside every trusted workspace
(``workspace.is_trusted_workspace``): ``npx`` and rustup resolve the toolchain from there, not
from the linted file's directory.  Sandboxed backends answer False: their toolchain is not the host's.

name: _lsp_service
doc:
The active LSPService, or None on a non-local backend / any failure.
LSP is an enrichment layer and must never break a write.

name: _lsp_handles_extension
doc:
True iff the active service (config-declared servers included) or, without one,
the static registry claims ``ext``. Decides whether pre-write content is worth
capturing for the line-shift map.

name: _has_ancestor_tsconfig
doc:
True iff a tsconfig.json exists in ``path``'s directory or any ancestor.
Host-side walk, local backend only: on a remote backend this answers False so
the shell linter still runs — never suppress lint on a probe that couldn't answer.

name: _lsp_call
arguments: self, method: str, path: str, default
doc:
``svc.<method>(path)`` on the active service; ``default`` when there is
no service or the call raises (LSP never breaks a write).

name: _lsp_will_handle
doc:
True iff the LSP service is active AND ``enabled_for(path)`` (workspace
detection, disabled-server set, broken-pair short-circuit). Any failure →
False so the shell linter still runs.

name: _maybe_lsp_diagnostics
arguments: self, path: str, *, pre_content: Optional[str]=None, post_content: Optional[str]=None, started: Optional[float]=None
doc:
Formatted LSP diagnostics this edit introduced, or "" when LSP is unavailable/disabled/clean
OR the verdict is not ready yet.  Never blocks the write on the language server: the check
(``agent.lsp.edit_check``) diagnoses ``post_content`` (the bytes this write produced) against
``pre_content`` (None = new file) on the LSP loop: those snapshots, not a later read of the
file, which another session may already have rewritten.  The write waits for the verdict only until ``inline_deadline(started)`` (what is
left of the write's latency budget; ``started`` = ``time.monotonic()`` at write entry); a slower
verdict reaches the model with a later tool result of the same session (``agent.lsp.deferred``).

name: _open_regular
doc:
fd of ``path`` when it is a regular file; None when missing; raises ``_NotRegular`` otherwise.
One lookup with O_NONBLOCK, judged by fstat: a FIFO swapped in never blocks this thread.

name: probe
doc:
``(has_bom, body)`` for a write target: ``body`` is the whole file when ``want_text`` else its
first 4 KB (the line-ending sample); ``(False, None)`` when the file is missing; None = ask the shell.

name: atomic_write
doc:
Replace ``path`` with ``data`` atomically; None on success, else an error message.

Same contract as the shell script: a symlink target is written through (the link survives),
parent directories are created, the temp file lives in the target's directory so the rename is
atomic, an existing target's mode is kept and a new one gets the umask default (``O_CREAT`` with
0o666 applies the process umask itself), and the temp is removed on every failure.

The temp holds its final mode before the first byte lands: an existing target's temp is created
0o600 and ``fchmod``-ed to the target's mode, so a private file's new contents are never readable
through a wider temp (the shell script's ``mktemp`` 0600 temp gave the same guarantee).

name: sha256_of
doc: Hex sha256 of the regular file at ``path``; None when it cannot be read natively.

name: _macos_protected_search_exclusions
arguments: path: str, *, cwd: Optional[str]=None, home: Optional[str]=None, platform: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Protected home dirs (relative to ``path``) below a broad macOS search root.

Only an ANCESTOR search (``$HOME``, ``/Users``) gets exclusions, so recursive
tools never trigger unattended TCC prompts; a search rooted inside a
protected dir stays allowed.

name: _normalized_filename_search_root
arguments: env: Any, root: str, fallback_cwd: str
doc: Normalize a filename-walk root without resolving remote paths locally.

name: _filename_search_root_keys
arguments: env: Any, roots: list[str], fallback_cwd: str
doc: Unique backend/root admission keys in deterministic order.

name: _acquire_filename_search_roots
doc: Atomically claim every key, polling for thread-scoped interruption.

name: _release_filename_search_roots
doc: Release a completed walk and leave no idle per-root state behind.

name: _search_stdout_and_limit
doc: Return stdout cleaned for parsing and a limit reason for search timeouts.

name: _bundled_rg
doc: Hermes's pinned ripgrep, forward-slashed for the shell transports, or None.

name: _split_tool_diagnostics
doc:
Separate rg/grep diagnostic lines from real match output → ``(diagnostics, payload)``.
``_exec`` merges stderr into stdout; classifying by SHAPE lets the exit-2 guard
tell a pure failure (no payload) from a partial one (one unreadable file, others
matched) and guarantees error text is never parsed as a match.

name: _parse_search_context_line
doc:
Parse a ``path-line-content`` context line using the RIGHTMOST numeric
separator (filenames may contain ``-<digits>-`` segments):
``dir/file-12-name.py-8-context`` → (``dir/file-12-name.py``, 8, ``context``).

name: _pattern_has_regex_newline
doc:
True when a content regex wants to match a newline: a literal newline or a
``\n`` escape with an ODD number of backslashes (``\\n`` is a literal
backslash+n and must not count).

name: _is_line_oriented_newline_error
doc: Return True for rg's hard error when multiline mode is required.

name: _maybe_warn_line_oriented_newline_pattern
doc: Attach a newline-regex warning only when search found no usable results.

name: _parse_search_output
arguments: result, output_mode: str, limit: int, offset: int, context: int, warning: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Parse rg/grep ``| head`` output into a SearchResult (shared by both engines).
Exit codes: 0=matches, 1=none, 2=error — but both tools return 2 on PARTIAL
errors (one unreadable file), so an error is surfaced only when exit==2 AND no
usable payload remains. ``warning`` is attached to files_only/content results.

name: _posix_roots
doc: Darwin-only: every root is POSIX-shaped (no drive letter / backslash).

name: _find_literal_path_expressions
doc:
Escape each search root for find's ``-path`` test, which matches its PATTERN
(glob) against the path find echoes — the operand verbatim. The operand reaches
the shell already single-quoted; ``-path`` must compare literally, so ``*?[]``
in a root's own name need escaping (a directory literally named ``a[1]`` must
be excluded by identity, not treated as a character class). Backslashes are
left alone: find does not read them as escapes inside a bracket-free pattern,
and doubling them would break matching on backslash-shaped roots.

name: _resolve_command
doc:
Resolve an executable in the command host's namespace. Ordinary commands
keep the bool hit/miss cache; rg alone caches successful resolved paths and
re-probes misses so a mid-session install becomes visible (with off-PATH
Windows candidates: cargo, scoop, winget).

name: _modified_rg_capability_error
doc: Cached actionable error unless rg can sort exactly (full SemVer, >= 14).

name: _run_rg_native
arguments: self, argv: list[str], fetch_limit: int, timeout: int, merge_stderr: bool=False
doc:
Run ``argv`` (shell-quoted rg words) natively and stop reading after
``fetch_limit`` lines — the ``| head -n`` of the shell pipeline without the
two bash spawns. ``shlex.split`` undoes the escaping the builders apply for
the shell path, so both transports see identical arguments. Exit code and
stdout follow the shell contract (rg 0/1/2; 124 on timeout with partial
output; 130 on interrupt), so ``_parse_search_output`` is shared. Once the
bound is reached rg is killed like ``head`` closing the pipe would.
``merge_stderr`` mirrors the shell path's stderr handling: merged for content
search (diagnostics feed the error message), discarded (``2>/dev/null``) for
file lists and probes.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(
                args, cwd=cwd, env=_make_run_env(self.env.env), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT if merge_stderr else subprocess.DEVNULL,
                start_new_session=True)

name: _run_rg_bounded
arguments: self, words: list[str], fetch_limit: int, timeout: int, *, merge_stderr: bool=False, native_ok: bool=True, shell_prefix: str=''
doc:
Run an rg command (shell-quoted words) and keep the first ``fetch_limit``
       lines: natively on a local POSIX host, else through the backend shell as
       ``<prefix><words> | head -n N``. ``native_ok=False`` keeps a form the native
lane cannot express (the multi-root ``cd`` prefix); ``shell_prefix`` is shell-only.

name: _quote_executable
doc: Quote an executable without leaking controller path semantics.

name: _macos_search_exclusions
doc:
Protected descendants to prune for this search root, if any. Gated on
``env.is_local``: ``sys.platform``/``_HOME`` describe the CONTROLLER, but the
search runs on ``env``'s host. Envs without the flag default to local
semantics; pruning is a warning-carrying skip, never data loss.

name: _protected_prune_paths
doc: Absolute-ish protected paths for find's ``-path ... -prune``.

name: _effective_macos_search_exclusions
doc:
Unique ``(root, relative, absolute)`` exclusions across ``roots``, never
pruning a root the caller chose explicitly.

name: _hidden_prune_expr
doc:
find clause pruning hidden dirs while keeping an explicitly selected dot-named root
(dir or single file) — find echoes each start point as given, so ``! -path`` matches it.

name: _prune_expr
doc: find ``\( -path A -o -path B \) -prune`` clause for the protected dirs.

name: _root_under_hidden_dir
doc: True when the search root or any ancestor is dot-named (``~/.hermes/skills``).

name: _rg_exclusion_globs
doc: ``--glob '!<dir>/**'`` pairs excluding protected dirs from an rg run.

name: _path_exists_probe
doc:
Existence probe; stdout contains "exists" or "not_found" (or the probe's
``cwd_error`` when the exec wrapper itself failed).

name: _dispatch_search
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str, target: str, file_glob: Optional[str], limit: int, offset: int, output_mode: str, context: int, order: str='discovery'

name: _path_not_found_result
doc: Error result for a missing search root, with nearby-entry suggestions.

name: _try_multi_path_search
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str, target: str, file_glob: Optional[str], limit: int, offset: int, output_mode: str, context: int, order: str='discovery'
doc:
Recover a not-found ``path`` that is really several paths in one string.
Commas explicitly delimit paths (internal spaces preserved); without commas
split on whitespace. Search every existing part, merge, and note skipped
parts. None when it doesn't look like a multi-path string.

name: _search_prune_glob_args
doc:
rg globs pruning known heavyweight recursive subtrees. Both forms are
needed: globs are relative to each rg root, so ``**/name/**`` alone misses an
explicitly selected ``name/`` root. Names come from the shared scan policy —
no second search-only list.

name: _zero_match_probe
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str, file_glob: Optional[str]
doc:
Steering hint for a 0-match content search, or None: a bare zero gives the
model nothing to act on, so run cheap count-only rg probes (case-insensitive,
hidden/ignored, fixed-string) and report the first that hits.

name: _is_broad_local_search_root
doc:
Whether a no-rg LOCAL root (filesystem root, $HOME or an ancestor of it) is
unsafe for recursive find. Controller paths never classify remotes.

name: _filter_hidden_descendants
doc: Drop hidden descendants while allowing an explicit hidden search root.

name: _filter_gitignored_paths
doc: Drop paths ignored by git when *root* is inside a git worktree.

name: _sort_paths_by_mtime
doc: Sort paths newest-first using metadata from the active backend.

name: _search_directories_with_find
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str, fetch_limit: int
doc:
Return matching descendant directories using find, if available.

``rg --files`` and ``find -type f`` both enumerate files only, so
directories — especially empty ones — are invisible (#54347). rg stays
authoritative for which *files* survive ignore processing; this adds
the matching directory entries so the tool honours its documented
ls-replacement contract.

name: _search_files
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str | list[str], limit: int, offset: int, order: str='discovery'
doc:
Search for files by name (glob-like) across one or more roots: rg --files,
else a bounded find. ``order``: "discovery" (fast, bounded) or "modified"
(exact global newest-first; needs rg 14+ or GNU find).

name: _search_files_rg
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str | list[str], limit: int, offset: int, order: str='discovery', rg_executable: Optional[str]=None
doc:
File-name search via ``rg --files`` (respects .gitignore, skips hidden dirs,
parallel walk). Discovery order stays bounded and fast; exact modification-time
ordering is explicit because it scans globally.

name: _search_content
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str, file_glob: Optional[str], limit: int, offset: int, output_mode: str, context: int
doc: Content search: rg, else grep; attaches zero-match steering hints.

name: _run_search_pipeline
arguments: self, cmd_parts: list[str], output_mode: str, limit: int, offset: int, context: int, warning: Optional[str]=None, line_cap: bool=False
doc:
Run ``cmd_parts | head -n <fetch_limit>`` under pipefail and parse. Extra
rows report the true total (context mode also emits "--" separators, so
grab 200 more). pipefail keeps the engine's exit 2 alive across ``| head``
(a truncating head makes rg exit 0 / grep 141, which the ==2 guard ignores).
``line_cap`` appends ``| cut -c1-2000`` for engines without --max-columns
(grep): bounds giant single-line matches at the pipe layer; skipped for
files_only/count where lines are paths/counts.

name: _search_with_rg
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str, file_glob: Optional[str], limit: int, offset: int, output_mode: str, context: int, rg_executable: Optional[str]=None
doc: Search using ripgrep.

name: _grep_cmd
arguments: self, head: list[str], pattern: str, output_mode: str, context: int, file_glob: Optional[str]=None
doc: ``head`` + context/include/mode flags + quoted pattern (argument order is fixed).

name: _search_with_grep
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str, file_glob: Optional[str], limit: int, offset: int, output_mode: str, context: int
doc: Fallback search using grep.

name: _search_with_grep_pruned
arguments: self, pattern: str, path: str, file_glob: Optional[str], limit: int, offset: int, output_mode: str, context: int, protected_paths: list[str]
doc:
grep fallback via ``find ... -prune -exec grep {} +``, used when the root needs
path-scoped pruning (macOS protected dirs) or is itself under a dot-directory
(#18473: grep's ``--exclude-dir='.*'`` would drop the root). Trade-off: find folds
grep's exit code, so a hard grep error surfaces as an empty result.

name: guard_disabled
doc:
True when the user switched the read-before-write guard off; the file
tools then warn instead of refusing stale/unread write_file overwrites.

name: _evict_oldest
doc:
Pop entries until *container* is within *cap* (sets: arbitrary; dicts: oldest
by insertion order). An eviction only costs one redundant re-send or staleness check.

name: record_read
arguments: task_id: str, resolved_or_path: str | Path, *, partial: bool=False

name: writes_since
arguments: exclude_task_id: str, since_ts: float, paths: Iterable[str | Path]

name: lock_path
doc:
Per-path lock: threads on the same path serialize, different paths proceed.
The lock entry is dropped once the last holder/waiter exits.

name: _stamp
arguments: self, task_id: str, resolved: str, mtime: float, now: float, partial: bool
doc: Caller holds ``_state_lock``.

name: record_read
arguments: self, task_id: str, resolved: str, *, partial: bool=False, mtime: Optional[float]=None

name: note_write
arguments: self, task_id: str, resolved: str, *, mtime: Optional[float]=None
doc:
Record a successful write: global last-writer AND this agent's own
read stamp (a write is an implicit read of the current content).

name: check_stale
doc:
Model-facing warning if this write would be stale, else ``None``. Severity
order: sibling wrote after our read > mtime drift / partial read > never read.

name: writes_since
arguments: self, exclude_task_id: str, since_ts: float, paths: Iterable[str]
doc:
``{writer_task_id: [paths]}`` for writes after ``since_ts`` by agents
other than ``exclude_task_id`` (delegate_task's "subagent modified files
you previously read" reminder).

name: known_reads
doc: Resolved paths this agent has read.

name: forget_task
doc:
Release read stamps and writer claims owned by a task after its lifecycle ends.

A finished task is not a concurrent sibling: leaving its writer claims behind makes
the next run of the same job (a fresh ``cron:<job>:<uuid>`` id) refuse to write the
same scratch path as "modified by sibling subagent" hours after the writer exited.

name: clear
doc: Reset all state. Intended for tests only.

name: _get_max_read_chars
doc:
Return ``file_read_max_chars`` from config.yaml (default on missing/invalid). No module
cache: ``load_config_readonly`` is already mtime+path cached, and a process-lifetime slot
would pin the launch profile's value under the multiplexed gateway.

name: _truncate_to_char_budget
doc:
Trim line-numbered ``read_file`` content to the last COMPLETE line within *max_chars*.

Returns ``(kept_text, lines_kept, truncated)`` so the caller can offer a
``next_offset`` instead of rejecting the read. If not even the first line
fits it is clamped mid-line so the read is never empty and the cursor advances.

Ported in spirit from nearai/ironclaw#5029 (dual line/byte cap on ``read_file``). Where hermes
previously hard-rejected an oversized read (forcing the model to guess a smaller ``limit`` and burn a
round-trip returning nothing), this trims the content to the last *complete line* that fits within
``max_chars`` and reports how many lines were kept so the caller can offer a ``next_offset``
continuation.

name: _apply_char_budget
arguments: result_dict: dict, content: str, offset: int, total_lines, max_chars: int
doc:
Trim *content* to the char budget, annotate *result_dict* with the
continuation hint, and return the trimmed text.

name: _file_ops_uses_host_paths
doc:
True when *file_ops* targets the host filesystem (only then may we stat paths
or rewrite V4A headers to host-absolute paths; sandboxes have their own namespace).

name: _rewrite_v4a_patch_paths_for_host
arguments: patch: str, path_to_resolved: dict, path_to_entry: dict, file_ops
doc:
Rewrite V4A file headers to the resolved host paths (host backends only).

The shell layer must patch the SAME files ``patch_tool`` resolved for
locking/staleness, not re-resolve a relative header against its own cwd
(which can differ — the git-worktree cwd bug). Delete and Move headers take
``path_to_entry``: they act on a symlink itself, never on its target.

name: _is_blocked_device_path
doc: Return True for concrete device/fd/proc paths that can hang reads or leak process state.

name: _is_blocked_device
arguments: filepath: str, base_dir: str | Path | None=None

name: _resolved_match_path
doc:
Best-effort task-cwd resolution of a search hit's path.

Search backends may return cwd-relative paths while the process cwd differs, so both the
read-block filter and the redaction classifier must resolve against the task cwd. An
unresolvable path is used as-is (the raw path is still worth classifying).

name: _filter_read_blocked_search_results
doc:
Remove credential/cache/env paths from a SearchResult in-place; return the omitted count.

Each path is resolved against the task cwd first (search backends may
return cwd-relative paths; the process cwd can differ).

name: _is_expected_write_exception
doc: Return True for expected write denials that should not hit error logs.

name: _create_terminal_env_for_file_ops
doc:
Build the terminal environment for *task_id* via the shared ``_create_configured_env``,
so a file tool that runs before any terminal command still gets the configured backend.

name: _get_file_ops
doc:
Get or create ShellFileOperations for the task's terminal environment.

Uses terminal_tool's per-task creation locks (no duplicate sandboxes).
Subagent task_ids collapse to "default" (``_resolve_container_task_id``) so
delegate_task children share the parent's container; RL/benchmark task_ids
with a registered env override keep their isolation.

name: clear_file_ops_cache
doc: Clear file-operation state for a finished task, or all tasks.

name: _special_file_kind
doc:
Human name for a non-regular file type that would hang a read, else None.

Stat-based sibling of ``_is_blocked_device``: a FIFO/socket in a workspace
hangs like ``/dev/zero`` but has no recognizable name. Host filesystems
only; unstattable paths return None and flow to the normal read path.

name: _read_extracted_document
arguments: path: str, _resolved, offset: int, limit: int, task_id: str
doc:
Render an extractable document (.docx/.xlsx/.pdf/...) as paginated text.

Returns the JSON result, a tool_error for an actionable extraction failure
(size cap, encrypted, malformed), or ``None`` to fall through to the normal
read path. Runs BEFORE the binary-extension guard.

name: _dedup_stub_or_block
arguments: task_data: dict, dedup_key: tuple, path: str
doc:
Return the "unchanged" stub for a repeated identical read, escalating to a
hard BLOCK after 2 stubs so weak tool-followers don't loop forever.

name: _record_successful_read
arguments: task_data: dict, task_id: str, path: str, resolved_str: str, offset: int, limit: int, dedup_key: tuple, *, partial: bool, redacted: bool=False, end_line: int | None=None, total_lines=None, version_before=None, snapshot=None
doc:
Bookkeeping after a real (non-stub) read; returns the consecutive-read count.

Per-task tracker under the lock (stub counter, history, consecutive count,
mtime for dedup + staleness, page coverage, and the write_file baseline once
the task has seen every line UNREDACTED — in one page or by paging
contiguously through a file too big for one; a redacted page returned a
non-round-trippable ``«redacted:…»`` sentinel, so it must not bless an
overwrite that would persist the sentinel into a credential file). Then
OUTSIDE our lock (no nested locking): the cross-agent registry, and the
background-review read-mark (a FULL read of a skill file counts like
skill_view so a follow-up skill_manage(patch) is accepted).

name: read_file_tool
arguments: path: str, offset: int=1, limit: int=DEFAULT_READ_LIMIT, task_id: str='default'
doc:
Read a file with pagination and line numbers.

Guard order: NT/device-namespace prefix (raw string, no resolution) →
device-path blocklist (no I/O) → stat-based special-file guard (host only)
→ Hermes internal denylist → document extraction → binary-extension guard
