doc: One ``~/.hermes/<segments>/<leaf>`` operand, optionally quoted (quote tracked by *group*).

name: _exec_first_arg_literal_spans
doc: Literal spans that sit as the direct first argument of an exec call (``open('<lit>')``).

name: is_inert_fixture_line
arguments: finding: Finding, line: str, is_code: bool, rel_path: str=''
doc:
The finding's text is quoted test data that nothing on the line runs: every hit is inside a
string literal, and no such literal is the direct first argument of an exec call. A literal passed
as a later argument / nested in a dict to a test dispatcher (``call(x, "/etc/passwd")``) is data;
``open('/etc/passwd')`` — the literal as open's first arg — executes and is not inert.

name: is_base64_media
doc: The line's first long base64 run decodes to a recognised media/document header.

name: is_base64_archive_roundtrip
doc:
A ``base64_decode_pipe`` line that both CREATES an archive (``tar c``) and does a base64
encode→decode round-trip — a transport, not an opaque embedded payload.

name: _is_alternation_member
arguments: line: str, start: int, end: int

name: _is_whole_literal
arguments: line: str, start: int, end: int, span: tuple[int, int]
doc: The token is the entire quoted content of the literal it sits in (``"printenv"``).

name: is_regex_alternation_token
doc:
Every occurrence of the finding's token sits inside a literal as an alternation member
or as the whole literal (a list entry) on a line that executes nothing.

name: _sudo_in_safety_clause
doc:
A negation word governs this ``sudo`` — anywhere earlier in the sentence, or in the
short clause right after it (``no permissions, xattrs, sudo``).

name: is_sudo_inert
arguments: finding: Finding, line: str, rel_path: str
doc:
Every ``sudo`` on the line is an advisory install/admin HINT inside a non-executing string
literal, or is governed by a safety negation. A bare ``sudo <cmd>`` command string (``"sudo id"``,
a ``["sudo", "id"]`` args element) is not an admin hint and is not demoted — on JSON data files
those are handled (and kept at severity) by ``is_json_prose_value``.

name: is_env_dump_in_safety_clause
doc: Every ``dump_all_env`` hit on the line is governed by a safety negation (a "never/do not" rule).

name: is_quoted_injection_phrase
doc: The finding's injection phrase sits entirely inside a quoted/backtick span on the line.

name: is_repo_root_traversal
doc: Every ``../../..`` run on the line climbs to an ancestor dir, with no sensitive leaf after it.

name: is_benign_lazy_os_import
doc:
Every ``__import__("os").<attr>`` on the line reads a benign os member, with no dangerous os
call and no exec marker on the line.

name: is_disclosed_config_note
doc:
A prose-intent config-mod finding on an install-doc surface (README-like ``.md`` or
``after-install.md``); the mechanical shell-write tier is excluded by pattern id.

name: is_authorized_keys_prose
arguments: finding: Finding, line: str, is_doc: bool
doc:
An ``ssh_backdoor`` (``authorized_keys``) mention where the token sits inside a string literal
(a UI label) and no write/append action is on the line. Agent-facing doc PROSE is not covered:
``is_doc`` is accepted for signature symmetry but an imperative README instruction keeps severity.

name: is_loopback_only
doc: Every ``hardcoded_ip_port`` hit on the line is a 127.0.0.0/8 address.

name: is_pip_install_in_prose_literal
doc:
Every ``pip install`` on a code line sits mid-sentence inside a string literal, and the
line executes nothing.

name: is_hex_in_char_class
doc: Every ``\xHH`` on the line is inside a ``[...]`` regex character class.

name: logical_line
doc: ``lines[index]`` joined with the lines a trailing backslash continues onto (max 8).

name: is_loopback_continuation
arguments: finding: Finding, line: str, joined: str
doc:
The line continues with ``\``, the finding's own pattern stops matching on the logical
line, and every ``http(s)://`` host on it is loopback.

name: is_json_prose_value
arguments: finding: Finding, rel_path: str, line: str
doc:
Every hit sits mid-sentence inside the key or value of a ``"key": "string"`` pair (or a bare
string list element) in a ``.json`` data file, under a key that does not name something executed.

name: _is_standalone_coin_name
arguments: line: str, start: int, end: int

name: is_coin_name_only
doc:
Every ``crypto_mining`` hit on the line is the standalone word ``monero`` and nothing on
the line names mining software, a pool or the act of mining.

name: is_google_installed_app_secret
doc: A ``hardcoded_secret`` hit whose literal is a Google installed-app OAuth client secret.

significant_calls.expression:
desktop_ui.emit_or_error(
        "preview.close",
        {"url": target},
        "Failed to close the preview: ",
        "The preview pane is only available in the Hermes desktop app.",
        {"success": True, "closed": target or "all"},
    )

name: _handle_preview
doc: Non-read actions only: action=read is dispatched at the agent level.

name: _checkpoint_path
doc:
Active profile's checkpoint file at call time: the patched ``CHECKPOINT_PATH`` when a test
changed it, else live profile-scoped HERMES_HOME — the multiplexed gateway serves every
profile from one process, so the import-time constant would pin every profile's process
checkpoint to the launch home.

name: _worker_memory_max_bytes
doc:
Finite per-worker cgroup limit that can never widen host risk.
``TERMINAL_LOCAL_MEMORY_MAX_MB`` is honored only when it *tightens* the safe
bound (min of the gateway's cgroup-v2 ``memory.max`` and half of physical RAM,
capped at 4 GiB), so an oversized override cannot exceed the enclosing slice.

The proposed local-memory-guard environment override is honored when it tightens the safe bound, so this
isolation composes with PR #57121 instead of inventing a second knob.

name: _systemd_scope_argv
doc:
``systemd-run --user --scope`` argv shared by the probe and real spawns.
``--collect`` self-cleans the scope after exit; ``--unit`` names it for systemctl.
No ``OOMPolicy=``: transient scopes reject it on systemd <253 (#102486).
``--expand-environment=no`` keeps the command byte-identical (#132385).

name: _default_user_runtime_dir
doc: ``/run/user/<uid>``; a function so tests can point it at a temp dir with a real socket.

name: _secure_user_runtime_dir
doc: Accept only an absolute, owned, non-writable real directory.

name: systemd_user_bus_env
doc:
Build an environment that can reach this user's lingering systemd manager.

System-level gateway units run as an unprivileged ``User=`` but normally do
not inherit login-session variables.  When the conventional runtime
directory is owned by this uid and its bus exists, derive the two standard
variables.  Derived fresh on every call rather than adopted once at boot:
linger may be enabled after the gateway started (existing installs), so
the bus can appear later and the probe's failure TTL must be able to
recover (#104893).
The returned copy is passed explicitly to the probe and every scoped spawn;
``os.environ`` is left unchanged.

name: _systemd_scope_cached
doc: Cached probe verdict, or None when a (re)probe is due.

name: _systemd_run_user_scope_available
doc:
True if ``systemd-run --user --scope`` can create a cgroup.
``shutil.which`` alone is insufficient: system services and containers may lack
the user D-Bus bus even with the binary on PATH (every spawn would fail with
``Failed to connect to user bus``), so a cheap probe is run and cached.

Use ``/bin/sh -c 'exit 0'``: NixOS provides ``/bin/sh`` but not ``/bin/true``
(#105365), regardless of the gateway service's PATH.

name: _is_supervised_gateway_process
doc:
Whether this process is the live, supervised Hermes gateway itself.
Supervisor markers and ``_HERMES_GATEWAY`` are inherited by every descendant (and
importing ``gateway.run`` sets the latter), so also require ownership of the live
gateway PID file — scopes are for the gateway, not terminal children or CLIs.
Reads the launch marker (``HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD`` included), not the restart-route
probe: a Windows Scheduled-Task gateway sets only that marker, and the self-kill guards
gated here must protect it too (#113667).

name: _build_systemd_scope_argv
doc:
Wrap *shell_argv* in a ``systemd-run --user --scope`` invocation with its own
memory accounting, so an OOM in the worker cannot kill the gateway cgroup.

``--collect`` makes the transient scope self-clean after exit; ``--unit`` gives it a recognisable name
for ``systemctl --user status`` / journalctl. See #70716.

name: _warn_scope_degraded_once
doc:
Warn once per process: the condition is host-level and the probe verdict
is cached, so this would otherwise fire on every cron dispatch.

name: scoped_spawn_lost_user_bus
doc:
After a ``systemd-run --user --scope`` wrapper exits before its child could start: True
when the user bus is gone (:func:`systemd_user_bus_env` derives nothing), in which case the
cached True verdict is replaced so the next dispatch re-probes and degrades instead of
consuming another occurrence on the same dead wrapper (#110803).

*spawn_env* is the environment the wrapper was launched with: re-deriving from it (minus the
bus address it carried) honours a configured ``XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`` exactly as the spawn did, so
an unrelated wrapper exit on a host whose bus lives outside ``/run/user/<uid>`` is not
misread as a lost bus.

name: restart_safe_gateway_child_argv
arguments: command: list[str], *, unit_suffix: str, require_restart_safe_scope: bool, outlives_parent: bool=False
doc:
Place a managed-systemd gateway child outside the gateway cgroup.

A systemd-supervised gateway restart kills every process in the service
cgroup, so children that must survive it run in a transient user scope.
Hosts with no user systemd session (containers, LXCs without linger) cannot
create one; hard-failing there is a silent cron outage, so callers state the
policy: ``require_restart_safe_scope=True`` raises
:class:`RestartSafeScopeUnavailable` (kanban's long-lived workers), ``False``
degrades to a direct external subprocess with a once-per-process warning
(cron, behind ``cron.require_restart_safe_scope``).

``outlives_parent=True`` (fire-and-forget kanban workers): any *other*
systemd unit — a ``Type=oneshot`` dispatch timer, an operator's sequencer
service — tears its cgroup down when it exits, so the child is scope-wrapped
there too (#113612). Whether that unit actually kills its children
(``KillMode``, lifetime) is not knowable here, so without a user bus it
degrades with a loud warning instead of refusing: a long-lived
``Type=simple`` sequencer without linger keeps working. A cron job blocks its
caller until it finishes and never needs this.

name: _stop_systemd_unit
doc:
Stop a transient systemd user scope by unit name.
Reaps the *entire* cgroup — catching double-forked descendants reparented to init
inside the scope that survive a plain PID signal (SIGTERM all, SIGKILL after
``TimeoutStopSec``). True if stopped or already gone; False if ``systemctl`` is
unavailable or the stop failed.

See #70716.

name: _output_tail
doc: Last *n* chars of the session output with ANSI sequences stripped.

name: _completion_output
doc:
``output`` sized by the session's ``completion_output_chars`` plus ``output_cut`` when trimmed.

Shared by the completion notification AND the wait/poll/kill snapshots: a bot in an api_server
or one-shot session cannot receive notifications and polls instead, so the polled result must
carry the same whole reply and the same cut marker (#115334).

name: transform_process_output
arguments: output: str, *, command: str, returncode: Optional[int], task_id: str=''
doc:
``transform_terminal_output`` seam for background-process output — the poll/wait/log/kill
results and the completion/heartbeat/watch notifications — so a plugin that rewrites terminal
output sees the same command output whether it ran in the foreground or not (#70760).
Same helper as the foreground path; callers redact AFTER it, never before, so a replacement
the plugin returns is still masked. ``returncode`` is None while the process is running and
``env_type`` is not recorded per process, so it is passed empty.

name: _redact_process_result
doc:
Transform, then redact secrets from background-process output before it reaches the
model, session.db and CLI, mirroring the foreground ``terminal`` pipeline (hook first,
redaction after) so the two surfaces can't diverge. Respects ``security.redact_secrets``;
``redact_terminal_output`` picks ``code_file`` from the recorded command.

The command string itself is also redacted in case it carried an inline credential. See #43025.

name: _handoff_process
arguments: session_id: str, args: dict, task_id: Optional[str]
doc:
Subagent-only: transfer a running background process to the parent agent so its completion is delivered THERE
(child-owned process notices are suppressed and child teardown kills what it owns). Validated against the live spawn
tree: the caller must be a registered child and must own the process; anything else is an error, never a silent
no-op, so a PID mentioned in prose can't masquerade as a transfer.

name: append_output
doc: Append to the rolling output buffer under the session lock, keeping the tail.

name: append_output_if_running
doc:
Append unless the session has exited. Decided under the lock a kill holds while it
snapshots the output and sets ``exited``, so a chunk is either in the kill's receipt or
dropped, never added after it.

name: mark_exited
arguments: self, exit_code, reason: str='exited', source: str=''
doc:
Record an exit. A kill that raced the observer already recorded its own
exit_code/reason; never overwrite it.

name: arm_heartbeat
doc: Enable periodic heartbeat events for ``session``; returns the effective interval.

name: _heartbeat_loop
doc:
One daemon thread for every heartbeat session: reader threads block on the pipe and
cannot keep time, and a per-process timer would leak one thread per job.

name: _emit_heartbeat
doc:
Queue a heartbeat carrying the output since the last one. A tick with nothing new is
skipped outright: every queued event costs the owner a full model turn, and "still running,
no output" is already visible on the process surfaces (status stack, /agents dock).

name: _clean_shell_noise
doc: Strip shell startup warnings from the beginning of output.

name: _emit_output
doc: Forward a chunk to the live-output sink; called from reader threads, never raises.

name: _check_watch_patterns
doc:
Scan a freshly-read chunk for watch patterns and queue notifications.
Per-session rate limiting (see WATCH_* constants): one match per cooldown
window, a match inside the window is one strike, WATCH_STRIKE_LIMIT consecutive
strikes or WATCH_LIFETIME_MAX_HITS total deliveries disable watching and
promote the session to notify_on_complete.

significant_calls.expression:
self._emit_watch_disabled(
                    session, session._watch_suppressed,
                    f"{WATCH_STRIKE_LIMIT} consecutive rate-limit windows triggered "
                    f"(min spacing {WATCH_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS}s). ")

name: _emit_watch_disabled
arguments: self, session: ProcessSession, suppressed: int, why: str
doc: Queue the one-shot watch_disabled summary (strike-limit or lifetime-cap path).

name: _watch_event_base
doc: Session identity + watcher routing fields shared by every watch event.

name: _global_watch_event
doc: Unaddressed (all-sessions) watch breaker event.

name: _global_watch_admit
doc:
True if this watch_match may pass the global breaker.
In cooldown: drop and count. Otherwise slide the rolling window; exceeding
the cap trips the breaker for WATCH_GLOBAL_COOLDOWN_SECONDS with ONE
"tripped" summary, and the cooldown's end emits ONE "released" summary.

name: _is_host_pid_alive
doc: Best-effort liveness check for host-visible PIDs.

name: _safe_host_start_time
doc: Kernel start ticks for a host PID, or None when unavailable.

name: _host_pid_is_ours
doc:
True only if ``pid`` is alive AND still the process we spawned.
The kernel recycles PIDs, so a stored number can later name an unrelated
process (seen in the wild: a browser's session leader tree-killed). The kernel
start time captured at spawn must match the live one; with no baseline
(legacy checkpoints, no ``/proc``) degrade to a bare liveness check.

name: _detached_host_fate
doc:
How a recovered host PID should be supervised.

``running`` — alive and still ours (start time matches, no baseline, or
the start-time probe could not be read). Re-attach; do not invent an exit.
``reused`` — alive, and the start time positively differs. The number
belongs to someone else; close our entry and never signal that PID.
``gone`` — the PID is not alive. Prune it; no exit status was collected.

name: _refresh_detached_session
doc:
Re-attach, close, or prune a recovered host-PID session.

A completion is not queued here: recovery has no waitable handle, so it
never collected an exit status.

name: _close_reused_detached
doc:
Close an entry whose PID was recycled onto another process.

The stranger is not signalled, and no completion is queued: we never
collected an exit status for the process we spawned.

name: _prune_uncollected_detached
doc:
Drop a recovered entry whose PID is gone, without inventing an exit.

An owned systemd scope stays reachable so kill can still reap it. A
scope-less entry is removed: poll/list must not report a collected exit.

name: _uncollected_gone
doc:
True when a detached entry was closed without a collected exit status
and the PID is no longer alive. List/poll must not report that as exited.

name: _config_value
doc:
``config.yaml`` value for ``section.key``, else the DEFAULT_CONFIG value.
Raises if config is unreadable; callers wrap with their own hard fallback so
registry code paths never crash on a broken config file.

name: _config_seconds
doc: ``terminal.<key>`` as a non-negative float (0 disables); *fallback* if unreadable.

name: _daemon_term_grace_seconds
doc: Grace (s) between SIGTERM and escalated SIGKILL; 0 disables escalation.

name: _env_temp_dir
doc: Return the writable sandbox temp dir for env-backed background tasks.

name: _scope_argv
arguments: self, session: ProcessSession, safe_command: str, unit_suffix: str, label: str
doc:
Login-shell argv for *safe_command* (parity with LocalEnvironment: rc files
sourced, user tools on PATH), wrapped in a transient systemd scope when we are
the supervised gateway (own cgroup: an OOM kills only the worker, not the
gateway and its messaging control plane).

name: _spawn_env
doc: Sanitized child env from the session's client toolchain; PYTHONUNBUFFERED so poll sees progress.

name: _track_started
arguments: self, session: ProcessSession, reader_target, reader_name: str, extra_args=()
doc: Register before the reader can publish completion, even for an exited child.

name: _spawn_local_pty
arguments: self, session: ProcessSession, safe_command: str, env_vars: dict
doc:
PTY spawn for interactive CLI tools (Codex, Claude Code, REPLs).
Raises ImportError when no PTY backend is installed and re-raises any spawn
failure; ``spawn_local`` falls back to pipe mode in both cases.

name: spawn_local
arguments: self, command: str, cwd: str | None=None, task_id: str='', session_key: str='', env_vars: dict | None=None, use_pty: bool=False, owner_task_id: str='', persist_on_release: bool=False
doc:
Spawn a background process locally (TERMINAL_ENV=local; other backends use
spawn_via_env()). ``use_pty`` requests a pseudo-terminal via ptyprocess/pywinpty
for interactive CLIs, falling back to a plain pipe when unavailable or failing.
``persist_on_release`` keeps the process out of agent-lifecycle kill sweeps (#41225).

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen(
                spawn_argv, text=True, cwd=session.cwd, env=spawn_env, encoding="utf-8",
                errors="replace", stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                start_new_session=True, **_popen_kwargs)

name: _reap_untracked
doc:
Post-Popen setup failed: kill the orphaned subprocess (and any setsid
descendants) so nothing leaks untracked.

name: adopt_local
arguments: self, proc: subprocess.Popen, *, command: str, cwd: Optional[str], task_id: str='', session_key: str='', owner_task_id: str='', output_so_far: str='', notify_on_complete: bool=True
doc:
Take over a still-running foreground Popen as a tracked background session
(yield-to-background: the user sent a message while the command was running).
The caller has stopped its own drain thread; the registry's reader continues from
the pipe's current position and ``output_so_far`` seeds the buffer so nothing
already captured is lost.

name: spawn_via_env
arguments: self, env: Any, command: str, cwd: str | None=None, task_id: str='', session_key: str='', timeout: int=10, owner_task_id: str='', persist_on_release: bool=False
doc:
Spawn a background process inside a non-local backend's sandbox.
The command is wrapped to capture its in-sandbox PID and redirect output to a
log file that later execute() calls poll. No live pipe or stdin, but it runs in
the correct sandbox context. ``persist_on_release`` keeps the process out of
agent-lifecycle kill sweeps (#41225).

name: _reader_loop
doc:
Background thread: read stdout from a local Popen process.
``buffer.read1(4096)`` not ``TextIOWrapper.read(4096)``: on pipes the latter
blocks until EOF, landing "live" output in one burst at exit. Orphaned-pipe
guard: a backgrounded grandchild (``node server.js &``) inherits our pipe's write
end so EOF never arrives while it lives, which would park this thread and never
fire ``notify_on_complete``; on POSIX we wait on an ``fd_wait`` selector (no FD_SETSIZE
cap, #94928) and stop draining shortly after the direct child exits.
Windows pipes lack select(), so the lazy ``_reconcile_local_exit`` is the net (#68915, #8340).

name: _finish_reader
arguments: self, session, decoder, append, label, wait, exit_code
doc:
Reader-thread teardown: flush the decoder (a truncated multibyte tail becomes
one U+FFFD instead of vanishing), reap the child (no zombies), record the exit.

A process may close stdout long before it exits.  The reader owns a dedicated
daemon thread, so it must keep waiting rather than publish a false completion
and discard the only ``Popen`` handle that can reap the child.

name: _env_poller_loop
arguments: self, session: ProcessSession, env: Any, log_path: str, pid_path: str, exit_path: str
doc: Background thread: poll a sandbox log file for non-local backends.

name: _pty_reader_loop
doc: Background thread: read output from a PTY process.

name: _ingest_output
arguments: self, session: ProcessSession, text: str, *, unless_exited: bool=False
doc:
Buffer a freshly-read chunk, then scan watch patterns and stream it live.
``unless_exited`` drops the chunk once the session has exited (atomically with a kill).

name: _finish_exited
arguments: self, session: ProcessSession, exit_code, reason: str='exited', source: str=''
doc:
Mark a reader-observed exit (a raced kill keeps its own code/reason) and finish.
Under the session lock, like kill_process's commit: otherwise the kill can land between
mark_exited's ``killed`` check and its writes, and the reader overwrites the kill.

name: _move_to_finished
doc:
Move a session from running to finished.
Idempotent: kill_process() and the reader thread can both call this; only
the FIRST move enqueues the completion notification, so no duplicates.
Returns True when this call is the one that persisted the session.

name: _release_finished_handles
doc:
Close a finished session's OS handles (Popen pipes / PTY master).

Best-effort and idempotent: the session may have no local Popen (env
backends, detached recovery), or the handles may already be closed by
the reader loop / kill path. Closing a Popen's stream objects does not
kill anything — the child has already exited — it only releases the
parent's pipe FDs, which is exactly the retained-resource leak.

name: _reader_finalizing
doc:
A reconcile saw the direct child exit and set ``exited``, but the reader that owns the
output is still on its final drain: the buffer is not the whole output yet, so nothing
may consume it as the completion.

name: is_completion_consumed
doc: Check if a completion notification was already consumed via wait/log.

name: is_session_waiting
doc:
Whether a goal loop (``hermes_cli.goals`` wait barrier) should stay parked on
this session: still running AND, with ``watch_patterns``, none matched yet (a
long-lived watcher unblocks on its trigger, not on exit). Unknown/exited/
already-fired sessions return False so a stale barrier can never wedge the loop.

name: wait_for_pending_completions
arguments: self, task_id: Optional[str]=None, *, timeout: float | None=None, poll_interval: float=1.0
doc:
Bounded linger for ``notify_on_complete`` background processes at one-shot exit.
A one-shot CLI run (``hermes -q/-Q/-z``) exits when its turn ends; a background
process it spawned still holds a stdout pipe owned by the dying parent and dies of
SIGPIPE seconds later (Bot Mode handoff replies were the visible casualty). Only
``notify_on_complete`` processes carry a completion contract — servers/daemons/
watchers aren't the parent's to wait for. ``task_id=None`` waits on every tracked
process; ``timeout=None`` reads ``terminal.oneshot_completion_wait_seconds`` (``<= 0``
disables). Each pass re-reconciles child state so an orphaned-pipe exit can't wedge
the linger. Returns ``{"waited", "completed", "timed_out"}`` id lists.

Bot Mode handoff REPLIES are the visible casualty (#90879): a recipient invoked as ``hermes -p <bot>
chat -Q --query-file ...`` dispatches its reply via ``message_agent`` / ``bot_relay`` exactly this
way, then exits, and the reply process is destroyed ~3s later. The sender waits forever for a reply
that was already killed.
See #17327.

name: _oneshot_completion_wait_seconds
doc: Linger (s) for one-shot exits with pending notify_on_complete processes; 0 disables.

name: _drain_should_skip
doc:
Skip a completion the CLI agent already has this turn — consumed via wait/log
or observed inline via poll(). Gateway/tui watchers check only
``is_completion_consumed`` so a read-only poll never suppresses their turn.

Skips when the agent has either truly consumed the output (wait/log → ``_completion_consumed``) or
observed the exit inline via poll() (``_poll_observed``). In both cases the CLI agent already has
the result this turn, so injecting a [SYSTEM: ...] completion would be a duplicate (#8228).

name: _surface_child_process_notifications
doc:
``delegation.surface_child_process_notifications``; False on any config
error — never crash the drain loop.

name: _owns_event
arguments: evt: dict, session_key: str, owns_event, is_async_delegation: bool
doc: Routing verdict for one drained event (see drain_notifications); False = requeue.

name: restore_completions
doc:
Rehydrate durable delegation completions from the LAUNCH profile's ledger, once per
process. Called by the first consumer that drains the queue (CLI/TUI drain, gateway boot,
TUI poller) so a mere ``import model_tools`` never touches state.db (#123265). The replay
always runs in the launch scope: the TUI poller / prompt_turn drain call this under the
session's profile binding, and a once-per-process replay taken under a secondary's scope
would leave the launch ledger unreplayed for the life of the process. Secondaries are
replayed by the gateway's ``_restore_secondary_completion_ledgers``.

name: drain_notifications
arguments: self, session_key: str='', owns_event=None, *, skip_poll_observed: bool=True
doc:
Pop all pending events and return ``(raw_event, formatted_text)`` pairs.
Skips completions per ``_drain_should_skip`` (gateway/TUI pass
``skip_poll_observed=False``). Routing (``_owns_event``): async-delegation events
always need ownership proof, ordinary events once they carry ``session_key`` or
``origin_ui_session_id``; ``owns_event(evt)`` (strongest; the TUI passes a
compression-chain-aware check) consumes ONLY on True, ``session_key`` uses plain
equality; non-owned events are re-queued for their owner. No filter consumes
everything (legacy single-session) except restored delegation payloads (fail-closed).

name: get
doc:
Session by full ID or unique prefix (``proc_4dae`` / bare ``4dae``, like git
short hashes); ambiguous or too-short prefixes resolve to None, never a guess.

name: _resolve_prefix
doc:
Resolve a unique session-ID prefix (a bare hex tail is normalized to
``proc_<tail>``); :meth:`get` tries exact first.

name: _reconcile_local_exit
doc:
Reconcile ``session.exited`` against the real child state.
The reader flips ``exited`` only at EOF; when the direct child has exited but a
descendant (e.g. a daemon from ``hermes update``) holds the pipe open, poll()
would report "running" forever. If ``Popen.poll()`` has an exit code, drain
readable bytes non-blocking and flip ``exited``. No-op for env/PTY, exited and
detached sessions.

The reader thread (`_reader_loop`) sets `session.exited = True` only in its `finally` block, which
runs when `stdout.read()` returns EOF. If the direct `Popen` child has exited but a descendant
process (e.g. a daemon spawned by `hermes update` restarting the gateway) is still holding the
stdout pipe open, the reader blocks forever and poll() keeps returning "running" indefinitely (issue
#17327 — 74 polls over 7 minutes on Feishu).

name: poll
doc: Check status and get new output for a background process.

name: read_log
arguments: self, session_id: str, offset: int | None=None, limit: int=200
doc: Read the full output log with optional pagination by lines.

name: wait
arguments: self, session_id: str, timeout: int | None=None
doc:
Block until the process exits, the timeout elapses, the user interrupts, or a
mid-turn user message (steer/redirect → ``request_yield``) releases the wait.
``timeout`` defaults to (and is clamped by) TERMINAL_TIMEOUT. Returns a dict
with status exited|timeout|interrupted|not_found|error and an output snapshot.

name: _exit_snapshot
doc: Result dict for an exited session: exit metadata + the completion-sized output tail.

name: kill_process
arguments: self, session_id: str, *, source: str='process.kill', consume_output: bool=True
doc:
Kill a background process and return its output snapshot.
``consume_output`` is true for explicit tool/RPC kills (the caller sees the
output). Bulk cleanup passes false so it doesn't suppress an autonomous
completion notification — except abandoned-turn reaping (``kill_started_since``),
which passes true so a killed abandoned process can't revive stopped work.

name: _stop_scope
doc:
Stop the session's systemd scope: True when it has none or the stop worked. Every kill
path stops the scope through here, so a failed stop always leaves it marked for retry.

name: _signal_kill
arguments: self, session: ProcessSession, session_id: str, consume_output: bool
doc:
Deliver the kill via PTY, local Popen tree, sandbox exec or recovered host
PID. Returns a final result dict when the kill cannot proceed (recycled/dead
recovered PID, or no runtime handle), else None.

name: _stdin_op
arguments: self, session_id: str, pty_op, pipe_op, ok: dict
doc:
Run a stdin operation on a running session — ``pty_op(pty)`` under PTY mode,
else ``pipe_op(stdin)`` on the Popen pipe — and return *ok* on success.

name: write_stdin
doc: Send raw data to a running process's stdin (no newline appended).

name: submit_stdin
doc:
Send data + newline to stdin (like pressing Enter).
On a Windows PTY, Enter is a carriage return: ConPTY treats ``\r`` as
end-of-line and a bare ``\n`` through pywinpty is NOT a line terminator — the
child's blocking line read (``readline()``, Go ``bufio.Scanner``) never returns
and the process hangs looking healthy. ``\r\n`` gives it both; POSIX keeps ``\n``.

name: request_close_terminal
doc:
Ask the desktop GUI to close this process's read-only terminal tab. Does NOT
kill the process — output keeps buffering and the tab can be reopened from the
status stack. Errors when no UI close sink is wired.

name: close_stdin
doc: Close a running process's stdin / send EOF without killing the process.

name: count_running
doc: O(1) running count for status-bar polling; dict ``len()`` is atomic, no lock.

name: list_sessions
arguments: self, task_id: str | None=None, session_key: str | None=None, *, include_retained: bool=False
doc:
Running and recently-finished processes for ``task_id`` and/or ``session_key``;
cross-task entries sharing the gateway session (a forgotten preview server
blocking session reset) are flagged ``"session_scoped": true``.

When ``task_id`` is given, processes that task spawned (its ``owner_task_id``) are included. When
``session_key`` is also given, session-scoped background processes (``background: true``) registered
under that gateway session are surfaced too, even if they belong to a different task — so the agent
can discover a forgotten preview server that is blocking session reset (#29177).

name: _any_running
doc:
True if any still-running session satisfies *predicate*, after refreshing
detached sessions so a finished-but-unreaped process reads as inactive.

name: has_active_processes
doc:
Whether any process for ``task_id`` is still running. Ownership is
``owner_task_id`` (the raw spawning id) like the other task-scoped queries:
``task_id`` on a session is the collapsed container key, shared across
turns and delegate children, so a container-key match alone would miss a
delegate child's own background work (#120546).

name: running_owned_by
doc: Running processes whose RAW spawning owner is ``owner_task_id``.

name: unread_completions_owned_by
doc:
Exited ``notify_on_complete`` processes of ``owner_task_id`` whose result nobody read (no wait/log/poll).
A child's completion notice is suppressed in the parent, so an unread exit is otherwise lost silently.

name: transfer_ownership
arguments: self, session_id: str, *, from_owner: str, to_owner: str, to_task_id: str, to_session_key: str, note: str=''
doc:
Move a RUNNING process from one owner to another under the registry lock. Ownership is the ``owner_task_id``
field: completion notices are stamped from it at exit time and teardown kills by it, so flipping it here is the
whole transfer. Returns the session, or None when it is unknown, already exited, or not owned by ``from_owner``
(the caller must not report a transfer that did not happen).

name: has_active_for_session
doc:
Active processes for a gateway session key. Processes older than
``max_active_age`` seconds are ignored as stale so a forgotten ``http.server``
can't freeze session idle/daily reset forever; ``None`` keeps legacy behaviour
(any running process blocks).

name: has_any_active
doc:
Whether ANY background process is running — scale-to-zero must not
suspend a gateway with live background work or the process is lost.

name: snapshot_running_ids
doc:
Running IDs owned by ``task_id`` — a turn-boundary marker: on timeout
only processes absent from the starting snapshot belong to the abandoned
turn; older ones intentionally span turns and must survive. Ownership is
``owner_task_id``: ``task_id`` is the container key (``session:<key>``,
``default``), shared across turns and sessions, not the turn's id.

name: kill_started_since
arguments: self, task_id: str, baseline_ids, *, source: str
doc:
Kill ``task_id`` processes created after ``baseline_ids``. Output is
consumed so an abandoned turn can't enqueue a follow-up reviving work the
timeout deliberately stopped.

name: kill_all
arguments: self, task_id: Optional[str]=None, *, exclude_ids: frozenset=frozenset(), source: str='kill_all', consume_output: bool=False
doc:
Kill all running processes, optionally only those ``task_id`` spawned (its ``owner_task_id``).
Returns how many it stopped. A session whose systemd scope did not stop is not counted
(its descendants may live on), and a later sweep retries it even after it finished.

Sessions with ``persist_on_release=True`` are skipped when ``source`` is an
agent-lifecycle sweep (the default ``kill_all`` release path, a gateway turn
timeout, or ``agent_close``): an explicitly persisted background job must survive
session end / compression / error recovery (#41225). An explicit operator stop
(``process.kill`` via process_manage, CLI /stop) passes its own source and still
reaches them, so the user can always stop a persisted process on purpose.

name: _prune_if_needed
doc: Drop expired, then oldest-over-cap finished sessions (hold _lock); keep pending scope stops and unpublished notices.

name: _read_once
doc: One 4 KiB read: decoded text ('' for a partial multibyte tail), None at EOF.

name: take_ready
doc:
Dequeue everything queued (waiting up to ``timeout`` for the first event) and hold each event's owner in the
same critical section, so no reaper check can observe an event as neither queued nor held. The caller MUST pass
the result to ``release`` once routing returns.

name: release
doc: End the in-flight hold ``take_ready`` took for ``events`` (after any requeue, so coverage is continuous).

name: drained_for
doc:
Dequeue everything queued for a caller that consumes only the events ``owns`` accepts (the TUI's post-turn
safety net). Every dequeued event's owner is held — foreign ones too — until the rejected events are back on
the queue and the accepted ones (yielded) have been routed, so no owner is ever between queue and hold.

name: retained_for_delivery
doc:
A finished entry whose completion is not yet published: pruning it would erase the only record that a notice
is coming, so the registry keeps it until publication.

name: awaits_notification
doc:
Whether a process spawned by one of ``owner_task_ids`` still has a notice on its way. Keyed on the RAW
spawning owner, the same field agent close kills by, so it survives compression rotating the session key.

name: _detached_host_fate
doc: Subclass supplies the live PID decision. See ProcessRegistry.

name: _write_checkpoint
doc: Write running process metadata to the checkpoint file atomically.

name: _foreign_handoffs
doc:
On-disk worker handoffs this registry never tracked whose log still decides an outcome:
the process is alive (same start time) or its recorded exit is waiting to be read.

name: recover_from_checkpoint
doc:
On gateway startup, probe PIDs from the checkpoint file; returns how many
were recovered as detached sessions.

name: log_delta_command
doc:
Shell command that reads only the log bytes written since ``offset``
(``cat``-ing the whole file every poll re-sends all output over docker/SSH).

Prints one header line ``"<size> <offset>"`` then the bytes in [offset, size).
The size is read first and the tail cut at that same size, so a growing file
never sends a byte twice; a file that shrank was rotated/truncated, so the
offset drops to 0 and the reader starts over. The window end is pulled back
to a UTF-8 character boundary (the backend decodes each ``execute()`` result
on its own, so a straddling multibyte char would become U+FFFD and break watch
patterns at the seam): up to 3 trailing continuation bytes are held for the
next poll and the header reports the trimmed size.

name: group_process_notifications
doc: Group consecutive completions only; watches and delegations are barriers.

name: is_child_process_notification
doc: Raw child process noise, not a delegation or work-closeout deliverable.

name: should_surface_notification
doc: Shared policy; callers must first enter the event's owning profile scope.

name: _format_age
doc: Human-friendly elapsed string ('18m', '2h3m', '45s').

name: _model_not_found_patterns
doc:
Model-not-found phrases from ``agent.error_classifier`` (the failover path's
own list, so nothing drifts); a minimal built-in set if the import fails.

Imported from ``agent.error_classifier`` so the batch renderer applies the SAME classification the
failover path consumes — no hand-copied pattern list to drift. Fails open to a minimal built-in set so a
classifier import problem never hides the per-task blocks. See #97667.

name: _delegation_config
doc: Active delegation config; ``{}`` on any error. Lazy: delegate_tool is heavy.

name: _delegation_model_not_found
doc:
True when a result reflects a config-level model_not_found rejection: needs a
model-not-found phrase AND the currently-configured model name in the same text,
so a stale task failing on a removed model is not mis-attributed to the config.

name: _delegation_model_not_found_notice
doc: Config-level model_not_found notice lines, or None (fail-open) — once per batch.

name: _notice_lines
doc: Blank + model_not_found notice block, or [] when the notice does not apply.

name: _preamble
arguments: evt: dict, title: str, intro: str, completed_at: float, *, with_goal: bool
doc: Shared preamble: title, intro, blank, dispatch time, [goal], context/toolsets, role+model.

name: _format_task_failure_notice
doc: One child of a still-running fan-out failed: say which, why, and that the batch goes on.

name: _recovery_lines
doc:
Owner-died recovery diagnostics (``recover_abandoned_delegations``): last persisted
status, per-task transcript paths, their verbatim tails and the owner's git state.

name: _format_batch_delegation
arguments: evt: dict, deleg_id: str, completed_at: float
doc: Consolidated block for a delegate_task fan-out that finished as one unit.

name: _process_accounting_lines
doc:
Runtime-truth lines about a child's background processes: what it handed to you (you own it now, its
completion lands here) and what it left running (terminated at teardown — never trust a child's "watcher running").

name: _format_async_delegation
doc:
Self-contained re-injection for an async-delegation completion: the FULL
original task source (goal, context, toolsets, role, model), dispatch time, status
and result, so an agent deep in unrelated context can act on it or re-dispatch.

name: async_delegation_display_text
doc: Compact UI title; the separate model notification retains all task evidence.

name: process_completion_display_text
doc: Compact UI title for one or more process completions; the model text keeps the full output.

name: heartbeat_output_tail
doc:
A tick's output capped to its newest characters (a long job's latest lines are what matter),
and the count of characters cut before it. ``omitted`` counts characters already cut before
``output``. The count rides the tick as its own field (``omitted``): text a job printed is never
read back as a cut marker.

name: join_heartbeat_outputs
doc:
Two consecutive ticks' ``output``/``omitted`` as one tick's, capped the same way, counting
every character either cut. A later tick that was itself cut leaves none of the earlier output.

name: heartbeat_output_text
doc: A tick's output as the agent reads it: the cut marker, rendered here only, then the tail.

name: heartbeat_display_text
doc: One-line CLI receipt for a heartbeat wake; the row itself is hidden (``HEARTBEAT_DISPLAY_KIND``).

name: _delegation_attribution_line
doc:
One-line provenance for a subagent-owned process event, else None. Such a process
outlives the child and lands in the PARENT conversation, which would otherwise see an
anonymous output wall. Keyed on ``owner_task_id`` — ``task_id`` may be the session key.

name: format_process_notification
doc: Format a completion_queue event into an ``[IMPORTANT: ...]`` message.

name: __new__
arguments: cls, text: str, display_text: str, display_kind: str, notification_category: str='result'

name: worker_output_log
doc: The log a worker-spawned process writes to; None outside a registered worker.

name: adoptable_log
doc: A checkpointed log path, only when it names this profile's output directory.

name: open_output_log
doc: Owner-only append descriptor for the child's stdout+stderr (the parent closes its copy).

name: record_exit_command
doc:
Prefix ``command`` so the shell writes its exit status beside the log: an interpreter
that adopts the process after the spawner exited has no Popen to wait on.

name: _log_reader_loop
doc:
Tail ``session.output_log`` until its process ends. The spawner decides the exit from
its Popen; an adopter (no Popen) from the recorded status, else ``lost`` (-1).

name: _result_paths
doc: Prune by completion time, not start time (jobs can take days).

name: load_completed_results
doc: Restore read-only snapshots; no process handles, watchers, or queue events.

name: _proc_alive
doc: True if a psutil.Process is running and not a zombie (already dead, just unreaped).

name: _terminate_host_pid
doc:
Terminate a host-visible PID and its descendants.
``expected_start`` (kernel start time at spawn) is re-validated first: a mismatch
or dead PID means the number was recycled onto a stranger and we refuse to touch
it — a leaked orphan beats tree-killing someone's browser. POSIX: snapshot descendants,
SIGTERM the parent alone so it can perform an orderly shutdown, then clean up snapshot
descendants that survive its grace window. Survivors are SIGKILLed after a second
``terminal.daemon_term_grace_seconds`` window. Windows:
``taskkill /T /F`` (psutil's stale PPID links miss orphans there); ``os.kill``
is the fallback.

name: _live_descendants
doc: PIDs of living non-zombie descendants of host PID ``pid`` (best-effort).

name: _post_kill_survivors
doc:
Host PIDs still alive once the kill signals have had time to land (#115490).

Fail-closed: anything unverifiable counts as a survivor, so a kill
that leaves a live tree can never write a killed receipt. Sandbox
(env) sessions have no host-visible tree and are unverifiable by
design — they return no survivors, preserving existing behavior.

name: _effective_config
doc:
The profile's effective user config (managed overlay, ``${VAR}`` expansion): the same reader the
completion consumers use (``gateway.run._load_gateway_config``, ``tui_gateway.server._load_cfg``), so
an admin-managed or env-expanded value decides promotion exactly as it decides delivery.

name: _enabled
doc: ``terminal.process_wait_auto_notify`` (default true); true when config is unreadable.

name: _count_unchanged
doc: Record one still-running wait/poll observation; return the consecutive no-new-output count.

name: _can_deliver_completion
doc:
Whether a completion notice for this session can reach the agent that is waiting.

Finite turns (non-interactive ``hermes chat -q`` / ``-z``, as ``delegate_task`` decides inline execution) end
the run when the turn ends, so a promised notice would never arrive.

name: _caller_receives_completion
doc:
Whether the completion this process would publish is routed to the CALLER, judged by the
consumers' own predicates: ``ProcessRegistry._owns_event`` (session-key routing; another session's
process stays with its owner) and ``should_surface_notification`` (a subagent-owned process is
suppressed unless handed off or ``delegation.surface_child_process_notifications`` is on). Fails
closed: an unbound caller cannot prove ownership of a keyed process.

name: _claim_notify_if_running
doc:
Set ``notify_on_complete`` unless the exit already won; False means it did.

``_move_to_finished`` claims the finish under ``registry._lock`` and reads the flag afterwards to
decide whether to queue the completion, so flipping it under the same lock while the session is
still in ``_running`` guarantees the exit publication sees it.

name: _promote
doc:
Wire completion delivery for a process just claimed by ``_claim_notify_if_running``.

CLI, TUI/Desktop and ``hermes chat -q`` drain ``completion_queue``, which the exit path fills
whenever the flag is set. The messaging gateway delivers only through a per-process watcher, so a
process started silently also needs the chat routing stamped and a watcher armed.

name: apply_wait_poll_policy
arguments: action: str, session_id: str, result: dict
doc: Post-process one ``process_manage`` session action result (see module docstring).

name: _is_wsl_launcher_command
doc:
True when *command* routes through a ``wsl[.exe]`` launcher chain (#120546).

The host PID recorded for such a spawn belongs to the short-lived launcher;
grandchildren inside the VM outlive it, so the entry must say so instead of
letting host-side hunting fail silently.

name: _moves_session
doc: True when a live GUI session's workspace will follow the project — ``_apply_workspace``'s gate.

name: _apply_workspace
arguments: task_id: Optional[str], path: Optional[str], name: str

name: _calling_session_project_id
doc:
``(scoped, project_id)`` for the calling session. The GUI gateway registers each session's
workspace (``cwd_source``) in the terminal override table; a caller it never registered (CLI,
scripts) is unscoped and falls back to the profile-global pointer.

name: project_create
arguments: name: str, path: Optional[str]=None, task_id: Optional[str]=None

name: process
doc: Scan ``data``; return ``(output_bytes, response_bytes)``.

name: flush
doc: Return any incomplete trailing sequence held back by the scanner.

name: _open_session_db
doc: Open the SessionDB for the profile owning this turn, or ``None``.

name: react_to_message_tool
doc: Attach (or with an empty ``emoji`` retract) the agent's reaction.

name: check_react_requirements
doc: Opt-in flag (Settings → Appearance); ``desktop_ui`` already restricts to GUI sessions.

name: _anydoc
doc:
Lazily import the optional anydoc converter (None when unavailable; failures retried after
ANYDOC_RETRY_SECONDS so one transient pip/network blip does not stick).

name: _temp_copy
doc: Materialize backend bytes in a private host temp file; removed even when parsing fails.

name: extract_document_bytes
doc: Extract a document already fetched across a file backend boundary.

name: _anydoc_missing_error
doc:
Teaching text for anydoc-gated formats (not in the schema: only sessions hitting one pay).

Response-time hint (#95681 pattern): the schema no longer lists the anydoc-gated formats or the
availability caveat — a session that never touches a .doc/.odt/.epub never pays for the explanation, and
one that does gets the full story here, with the fix.

name: _hosted_ocr_config
doc:
(enabled, api_key, api_url); never raises, no network. Maintainer decision: the ONLY route
is a direct ``FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`` (anydoc defaults api_url); the Nous gateway's Parse proxy
live-probed broken, so it is NOT used. ``file_tools.hosted_ocr: false`` disables even with a
key. The key is a profile credential: read through the secret scope so a multiplexed
secondary never spends (or reveals its documents to) the default profile's Firecrawl key.

name: hosted_ocr_available
doc: Probe for read_file's schema line; a key failing at conversion time surfaces in NEEDS-OCR.

name: _needs_ocr_warning
doc:
NeedsOcrError result when hosted OCR is off/failed; hints at CHECKING for an OCR skill
(never names one) and never advertises the hosted_ocr knob.

name: _finalize_anydoc_text
arguments: text: Any, path: str, pdf_note: Callable[[], str]
doc:
Normalize converter output; PDFs get the coverage note PREPENDED (read_file paginates, so a
footer may never be fetched) — this covers PARTIAL scan gaps that raise no NeedsOcrError.

name: _ocr_scanned_pdf
arguments: mod: Any, path: str, exc: BaseException
doc: anydoc >= 0.2 scanned-pages signal: hosted OCR when a route exists, else teach recovery.

name: _pdf_page_texts
doc: Per-page extracted text, or None when undeterminable.

name: _gap_map
arguments: counts: list[int], texts: list[str], empty: list[int]
doc: Per-gap breakdown labeled with the text before each gap, so the agent picks which to OCR.

name: _pdf_coverage_note
doc:
Warning header when many pages yielded no text, else ''. ``display_path`` (default ``path``,
which may be a host temp file) is what the recovery command shows.

name: _pdf_coverage_note_from_bytes
doc: Coverage note for backend PDF bytes via a host temp copy (pdftotext needs a path).

name: _joined
doc: Join extracted lines with a single trailing newline; raise when nothing non-blank.

name: _source_text
doc: Notebook source/text fields are a str or a list of str fragments.

name: _base64_bytes
doc: Approximate decoded size of a base64 payload (whitespace ignored).

name: _clean_stream_text
doc: Strip ANSI escapes; keep only the final ``\r`` frame of each line (tqdm redraws).

name: _notebook_output_text
doc:
One notebook output as compact text: stream/traceback/textual results kept; token-heavy
payloads (images, HTML, widgets) become sized placeholders. Handles v4 and legacy v3 shapes.

name: _notebook_outputs
arguments: cell: dict, jq_pointer: str='', filename: str=''

name: _open_zip
doc: Open an OOXML package; bad-zip/OS failures (body included) become ExtractionError.

name: _zip_xml
arguments: zf: zipfile.ZipFile, name: str, optional: bool=False
doc: Parse a package part; ``optional`` parts yield an empty element when absent or malformed.

name: _xlsx_string_text
doc: Base text of an si/is, excluding rPh phonetic annotations.

name: _col_index
doc: 0-based column of a cell ref: ``A1`` -> 0, ``AB7`` -> 27 (bijective base-26 letters).

name: _cell_value
arguments: cell: ET.Element, shared: list[str], s: str

name: _extract_sqlite
doc:
Render a SQLite file as a schema overview: per table the CREATE statement, row count and the
first rows. A ``.db`` that is not SQLite raises ExtractionError so read_file reports the real type.

name: read_preview_tool
arguments: start: Optional[int]=None, count: Optional[int]=None, callback: Optional[Callable]=None
doc: Return the active preview tab's contents (+ metadata) as a JSON string.

name: read_pane
doc:
Shared body of the read_terminal / read_preview / read_window bridges. ``window`` is
``((key, value, floor), ...)`` (None omitted, else int-coerced and floored); ``errors`` =
(not_desktop, not_integers, fail_prefix, empty).

name: read_terminal_tool
arguments: start_line: Optional[int]=None, count: Optional[int]=None, callback: Optional[Callable]=None
doc: Return the in-app terminal's contents (+ line metadata) as a JSON string.

name: read_window_below_tool
doc: Return the window underneath the Hermes window as a JSON string.

name: session_tool_scope
doc: Execution-owned overlay, additive to the existing profile registry.

name: _session_slot_key
doc:
The overlay slot key for the current session scope: writes go through ``normalize_scope``
(``register``/``deregister``), so reads must key the same way or the overlay is invisible.

name: _bound_error_text
doc: Bound an error body destined for model context; logs keep a longer prefix.

name: _bound_json_error_result
doc:
Trim an oversized ``error`` field in a JSON string result: handlers that
``json.dumps({"error": str(exc)})`` directly bypass ``tool_error``'s cap, so this runs
at the dispatch boundary to stop unbounded errors stacking across retries.

name: _is_registry_register_call
doc: True when *node* is a ``registry.register(...)`` call expression.

name: _module_registers_tools
_tool_module_candidates
doc:
Flat ``tools/*.py`` modules plus the package entry point ``tools/<pkg>/tool.py``, in one
sorted list. Only ``tool.py`` is scanned in a package, so every other file in it is a library
by construction. Sorted after merging: ``register()`` lets a same-name, same-toolset duplicate
overwrite silently, so the import order must not depend on file depth.

name: discover_builtin_tools
doc:
Import built-in self-registering tool modules and return their module names. The
per-file AST scan costs ~145 ms over ~100 files, so verdicts are memoized on disk keyed
by ``(mtime_ns, size)``; a mismatch or corrupt cache re-scans that file. The write is
best-effort and atomic, so concurrent processes race harmlessly.

name: _discovery_cache_path
doc: Path of the tool-discovery verdict cache, or None if unresolvable.

name: _load_discovery_cache
doc: Read the discovery cache; any error → empty dict (full scan).

name: _save_discovery_cache
doc: Best-effort atomic write of the discovery cache. Never raises.

name: no_cache_check_fn
doc: Mark a local, config-backed availability check as uncached.

name: _prune_check_fn_caches
doc: Expire stale entries and cap profile-dimensional cache growth. Caller holds the lock.

name: check_fn_cache_scope
doc:
Return the active profile key when availability is profile-scoped. Browser-controller
availability is request-bound (changes on every attach/detach), so a fully bound
browser-control request bypasses this cache AND model_tools' outer definition cache (same
sentinel) — one Browser session's live tools must not leak into another. Single-profile
processes keep the process-wide cache; a multiplex gateway installs a Hermes-home override
per profile turn, so the canonical profile key is the boundary.

name: _run_check_fn_uncached
doc: Run an availability check without cache/grace handling.

name: _check_fn_cached
doc: Return bool(fn()), TTL-cached across calls.

name: _core_tools_gated_by
doc: Names of ``_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS`` members whose registered ``check_fn`` is *fn*.

name: _memo_check
doc: Per-pass memo on top of the TTL cache: one probe per distinct check_fn.

name: invalidate_check_fn_cache
doc: Drop all cached ``check_fn`` results (after config changes like ``hermes tools enable``).

name: get_cached_check_fn_result
doc:
Cached verdict for *fn* if its TTL is still valid, else None. NEVER runs the probe:
for read-only surfaces (dashboard panels) that must not do network/auth/SDK work.

name: _unique_env
doc: Union of ``requires_env`` across *entries*, first-seen order, no duplicates.

name: tool_error
doc:
``'{"error": "<message>", **extra}'`` — the error body is bounded so a raw
exception can't bloat history across retries.

name: tool_result
doc: JSON-encode a dict positional arg *or* keyword arguments (not both).

name: _kwargs_accepted_by
doc:

True when at least one tool in *toolset* would be exposed. Mirrors
:meth:`get_definitions` per-tool filtering so doctor/banners agree with runtime:
mixed toolsets (``terminal`` + desktop-only ``read_terminal``) must not be gated

doc: CAS-restore policy state while retaining durable scope attribution.

name: _plugin_owner_of
doc:
Plugin namespace that DEFINED *handler* (None for built-in/MCP handlers). Bound to
``handler.__globals__["__name__"]``, fixed at definition time so it cannot drift with
call site/thread/timing; lambdas and nested functions inherit it, so a plugin cannot
launder an override via a callback.

doc:
Best-effort module name of the registry method's caller (two frames up).
``deregister()`` takes only a tool name — no handler for ``_plugin_owner_of`` —
so frame inspection is the only way to know who is asking.

name: register
arguments: self, name: str, toolset: str, schema: dict, handler: Callable, check_fn: Callable | None=None, requires_env: list | None=None, is_async: bool=False, description: str='', emoji: str='', max_result_size_chars: float | None=None, dynamic_schema_overrides: Callable | None=None, override: bool=False, scope: Optional[str]=None, execution_timeout: float | None=None
doc:
Register a tool (called at import time by each tool file). ``override=True`` is an
explicit opt-in for plugins replacing a built-in implementation (e.g. a headed-Chrome
browser backend); without it, cross-toolset shadowing is rejected.

name: deregister
doc:
Remove a tool; drops the toolset check/aliases if it was the last in its toolset.

``scope`` selects a profile overlay explicitly (multiplexed MCP tools live in the
owning profile's overlay); plugin callers may not name another scope, non-plugin
callers default to the process-global map. Gated by the same opt-in as
``register(override=True)``, else a plugin could deregister a tool it doesn't own
and re-register over the empty slot (the override check only runs when an entry
exists). ``mcp-*`` toolsets are exempt — discovery repaves its own tools per refresh.

name: move_to_scope
doc:
Move process-global registrations into *scope*'s overlay (a single-profile process that
starts multiplexing hands its launch profile's MCP tools to that profile's own scope).

name: restore_registration
arguments: self, name: str, current: ToolEntry, previous: Optional[ToolEntry], *, scope: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Restore a host-owned registration if it is still current (plugin ownership ledger).
The identity check is deliberate: another plugin (or ``PluginManager`` in a
multi-profile process) may have registered a newer entry under the same name, and
unloading this entry must leave that newer one untouched.

name: get_definitions

OpenAI-format schemas for the requested tools whose ``check_fn`` passes (or is
absent). Probes use the ~30 s TTL cache so ``hermes tools enable`` lands quickly.

name: _normalize_handler_result
doc:
Results must be a string or the multimodal envelope; anything else becomes a
string error so logging/hooks/budgeting/persistence never receive values they
cannot slice or size.

name: dispatch
arguments: self, name: str, args: dict, *, scope: Optional[str]=None, **kwargs
doc:
Execute a tool handler by name: async handlers bridged via ``_run_async()``,
results normalized, every exception returned as ``{"error": ...}``.

arguments: self, name: str, default: float | None=None
doc: Return per-tool max result size, or *default* (or global default).

name: get_schema
doc: Raw schema dict, bypassing check_fn filtering (token estimates, introspection).

name: get_emoji
doc: Return the emoji for a tool, or *default* if unset.

name: is_toolset_available
doc: True when a toolset has at least one exposable tool (never raises).

name: get_available_toolsets
doc: Return toolset metadata for UI display.

name: get_toolset_requirements
doc: Build a TOOLSET_REQUIREMENTS-compatible dict for backward compat.

name: check_tool_availability
doc: Return (available_toolsets, unavailable_info) like the old function.

name: _rewrite
doc: Bottom-up map over a schema tree: lists/dicts recurse, then *fn* sees each dict.

name: sanitize_property_key
doc: Deterministically map an arbitrary property key to a conforming one.

name: _rename_property_keys
doc:
{original_key: conforming_key} for one properties dict (identity entries omitted).
Deterministic (insertion order, numeric suffixes on collision) so the model-visible schema
and the dispatch-time reverse map from the registry's original schema agree.

name: resolve_local_schema_ref
arguments: schema: Any, root_schema: Any, seen_refs: set[str] | None=None
doc:
Follow a document-local ``$ref`` in *schema* against *root_schema*, for dispatch-time
decisions (argument coercion, key unrenaming). Remote, malformed or dangling refs come back
unchanged; sibling keywords are kept, and the referenced schema wins where they conflict.

name: unrename_tool_args
arguments: params_schema: Any, args: Any, root_schema: Any=None
doc:
Map sanitized keys in model-emitted args back to wire names. ``params_schema`` is the
ORIGINAL registry schema; recurses into objects/array items, following local ``$ref``s
(the sanitizer renames keys inside ``$defs`` too); unknown keys pass through.

name: sanitize_tool_schemas
doc: Deep-copied ``tools`` (OpenAI format) with sanitized parameter schemas; safe to mutate.

name: _strip_ref_siblings
doc: Recursively drop forbidden siblings of ``$ref`` (Fireworks rejects ``default`` there).

name: _strip_top_level_combinators
doc:
Drop combinators from the TOP level only (Codex rejects them there). They are usually
conditional-required hints, so validity is unchanged (handlers re-validate); nested ones
stay.

name: _carry_union_meta
arguments: outer: dict, replacement: dict, *, skip_default_on_ref: bool
doc:
Copy outer-union metadata onto *replacement* where absent (``default`` is illegal beside
``$ref`` on strict backends, hence ``skip_default_on_ref``).

name: strip_nullable_unions
doc:
Collapse ``anyOf``/``oneOf`` nullable unions (MCP/Pydantic optional fields) to the single
non-null branch: Anthropic rejects the null branch and optionality already lives in the parent's
``required``. Only when a null branch was dropped AND exactly one non-null branch survives.
``keep_nullable_hint`` sets ``nullable: true`` for runtime ``"null"`` → ``None`` coercion.

name: _const_branch_type
doc:
Primitive JSON-Schema type of a pure ``const`` branch (declared ``type``, if any, must match;
only ``title``/``description`` may accompany it), else None.

name: collapse_const_unions
doc:
Collapse ``anyOf``/``oneOf`` unions of same-typed consts (Rust/TS MCP servers emit
``{"anyOf": [{"const": "red"}, {"const": "green"}]}``) to ``enum``; ported from block/goose
``tool_schema_normalize.rs`` (Apache-2.0). Only when EVERY non-null branch is a pure ``const``
of one primitive type (``bool`` never merges with ``integer``); one ``{"type": "null"}`` branch
is tolerated as ``nullable: true``. Branch order kept; outer metadata carried; input never
mutated.

name: _normalize_type_array
doc:
Normalize a ``type: [...]`` array into *out* (llama.cpp and Gemini-via-OpenAI reject arrays).
Per AI-SDK: one non-null type → ``type: X`` (+ ``nullable`` if ``null`` present); several →
``anyOf`` of single-type schemas so EVERY branch survives; none → ``null``/object fallback.

name: _sanitize_node
doc:
Recursively sanitize a JSON-Schema fragment: bare-string schemas → ``{"type": <value>}``
(unknown strings → permissive object); object nodes gain ``properties: {}``; ``type`` arrays
are normalized; property keys are renamed to the provider-safe pattern and ``required``
follows, with entries missing from ``properties`` pruned.

- Normalizes ``type: [X, "null"]`` arrays to single ``type: X`` (keeping ``nullable: true`` as a hint),
and multi-type arrays like ``["number", "string"]`` to an ``anyOf`` of single-type schemas so no branch
is dropped (ported from anomalyco/opencode#31877). - Recurses into ``properties``, ``items``,
``additionalProperties``, ``anyOf``, ``oneOf``, ``allOf``, and ``$defs`` / ``definitions``.

name: _dict_nodes
doc: Pre-order walk over every dict node (yielded before its values, so it may be mutated).

name: _reactive_strip
arguments: tools: list[dict], strip_node: Callable[[dict], int], log_msg: str
doc:
Apply *strip_node* (-> keywords removed) to every dict node of each tool's parameters, in
place; OpenAI (``{"function": {"parameters"}}``) and Responses (``{"parameters"}``) formats.

name: strip_pattern_and_format
doc:
Strip ``pattern``/``format`` in place — reactive, only after llama.cpp's grammar converter
rejected a schema (its regex engine is a small ECMAScript subset); cloud providers use these as
prompting hints. Only beside ``type``/combinators, so a property *named* ``pattern`` stays.

name: strip_slash_enum
doc:
Strip ``enum`` keywords whose string values contain ``/``, in place: xAI's grammar compiler
rejects them (HTTP 400 before any token) — typically MCP enums of HuggingFace model IDs.

name: get_running_source_root
doc: The source checkout backing this process, if there is one.

name: _shell_words_at
doc:
Deobfuscated words of the simple command at ``start`` (stops at a newline, a redirection
or a trailing ``# comment``; max 64). The fd prefix of ``2>/dev/null`` / ``2>&1`` belongs to
the redirection, not to the command's operands.

name: _consume_options
arguments: words: list[str], start: int, options_with_arg: frozenset[str]=_NO_OPTIONS
doc: Index of the first positional at/after ``start`` (``--`` ends options).

name: _command_parts
doc: Split leading VAR=value assignments and wrappers off -> (env, executable, args).

name: _scope_keys
doc: Map each command start to the tuple of enclosing ``(``/``$(``/backtick openers.

name: _operator_before
doc: The list/grouping operator (or newline) immediately preceding a command start.

name: _cd_target
arguments: executable: str, args: list[str], cwd: Path
doc: Directory a ``cd``/``pushd`` would land in (existing dirs only), else None.

name: _shell_script_arg
doc:
Script string owned by a shell's ``-c``, if present. ``_bash_exec_payload`` parses bash's
real option grammar (``-o pipefail -c '<script>'``); when it finds no ``-c``, fall back to a
permissive scan: zsh/dash/ksh letters (``zsh -yc``) would otherwise fail this guard open.

name: _executes_heredoc_body
doc: A bare shell (no ``-c`` script, no script operand) executes whatever it reads on stdin.

name: _group_token
doc: ``{`` / ``}`` at ``index`` is a brace-group delimiter (its own word), not ``${x}``/``a{b,c}``.

name: _pipeline_end
doc:
Offset where the pipeline carrying a heredoc ends: the first ``;``/``&&``/``||``/``&`` or
bare newline at top level. Newlines right after ``|`` continue the pipeline (the consumer may
follow the terminator line). Inside a group the walk runs on until the group closes, then a
pipe after the closer continues it (``(cat <<EOF; echo) | bash``) and anything else ends it.

name: _shell_consumes_heredoc
arguments: masked: str, starts: list[int], scopes: dict[int, tuple[int, ...]], opener: int
doc:
Whether a bare shell reads the heredoc body: the command owning the ``<<`` or anything
downstream in its pipeline. Pipe-joined segments, and the groups or substitutions inside them,
all inherit the pipe as stdin (``| tee f | bash``, ``| (bash)``, ``| { echo; bash; }``).

name: _heredoc_specs
doc: Heredoc openers on one command line, with their ``<<`` offsets.

name: _join_continued_line
doc:
Physical line ``index`` plus every line a trailing ``\`` joins onto it -> (line, next).
The shell removes backslash-newline before it reads anything else, so the heredoc body only
starts after the joined line: ``cat <<EOF | \`` + ``bash`` pipes the body into bash. The pair
is blanked (offsets preserved) so the joined text reads as one command line.

name: _mask_heredocs
doc:
Blank heredoc bodies -> (masked command, heredocs with their bodies). Unterminated heredocs
run to end of input and are still reported.

name: _record_alias
doc: Record an inline ``-c alias.<name>=<value>`` git config override.

doc: Parse git's global options -> (target dir, subcommand, sub args, inline aliases).

arguments: executable: str, args: list[str], current_dir: Path, env: dict[str, str], root: Path, depth: int

Windows-only: NTFS locks loaded .py/.pyd files, so overwriting the live checkout can
corrupt the running process. On POSIX open handles keep the old inode alive; the mixed-module
hazard is limited to later lazy imports — not worth blocking every git workflow for.

doc: -> (blocked, message): whether a command would rewrite the live source checkout.

Single chokepoint deciding whether text rides on the media bubble as its caption:
``(caption, "")`` only for exactly one captionable file (not a voice/audio note) whose
text fits ``max_caption_len``, else ``(None, text)`` — multi-file caption→file association
is ambiguous. Length is codepoints (never under-counts Telegram's UTF-16 units for BMP
text); the Telegram sender re-checks the *formatted* caption since escaping inflates it.

Retry delay in seconds, or None when final: honours ``retry_after``; timeouts are
never retried (the send may have gone through); 5xx/429 back off exponentially.

(issue #27012).

name: _live_adapter
doc:
``(runner, adapter)`` for the in-process gateway; ``(None, None)`` standalone (cron);
``(runner, None)`` when the lookup fails — logged when a warning is given, never silently
swallowed (a silent fall-through could recreate a reconnect storm).

Multiplex: the adapter is the ACTIVE PROFILE's (``_profile_adapters[profile]``), never a bare
``runner.adapters`` hit — that map holds the default profile's bots, so a secondary profile's turn
would post/react with the default bot's identity. A profile with no adapter for the platform
yields ``None`` (fail closed → the caller's scoped standalone sender or an error), never the
default bot. Same resolver shape as ``hermes_cli/platform_actions.py::_resolve_adapter``.

name: _plugin_standalone_sender
doc:
``(standalone_sender_fn, None)`` for a registered plugin or ``(None, error_dict)``;
``discover`` runs the idempotent plugin scan first.

name: _registry_standalone_send
doc: One-shot text send through a plugin's ``standalone_sender_fn``.

name: _resolve_slack_user_target
doc:
Resolve ``user:U...`` / ``user_name:<handle>`` to a D... DM conversation (chat.postMessage
needs a conversation ID); ``user_name:`` goes through users.list first (stable handle match
only); other ids pass through. ``(chat_id, None)`` or ``(None, error_dict)``.

name: _send_matrix_via_adapter
doc:
Matrix adapter send (native media preserved). Prefer the live gateway adapter's persistent
olm/megolm session: ephemeral per-send connects re-init E2EE and claim one-time keys, which
under bursts exhausts recipient OTKs and silently drops messages — ephemeral is cron-only.

When a live gateway adapter is available (i.e. the tool runs inside a running gateway), the persistent
connection is reused — one olm/megolm session for all sends. This avoids per-message E2EE re-init storms
that exhaust recipient OTKs and silently drop messages (issue #46310).

name: _matrix_send_core
doc: Core send logic shared by live and ephemeral Matrix adapters.

name: _target_syntax_fn
doc:
The plugin's declared native target syntax, or None. A fresh CLI/cron process can parse a
target before plugin discovery registered the platform, so discover first when the name is
unknown (idempotent manifest scan; only this platform's adapter is materialized).

name: _parse_target_ref
doc:
(chat_id, thread_id, explicit): the plugin's ``target_ref_syntax_fn`` first, then in order
E.164 phone numbers (keeping the '+'), bare numeric ids, Matrix ``!room``/``@user``, XMPP JIDs.
Anything else goes to channel-directory resolution.

name: resolve_send_target
arguments: platform_name: str, target_ref: str, *, pass_unresolved_references: bool=False
returns: tuple[str | None, str | None, str | None]
doc:
Resolve one send target the same way for every caller (model tool, CLI, cron).
Channel-directory IDs are trusted; plugin parsers are the authority on native syntax. By
default an unresolvable target is an error the model can act on. ``pass_unresolved_references``
(no model in the loop: cron, react/unreact on native ids) hands an unresolvable target on a
built-in platform, or a plugin platform without a parser, to the adapter as written; a plugin
WITH a parser stays strict. The optional validator has the final say over every returned id.

name: _validated
doc: ``(chat_id, thread_id, None)`` when the plugin validator (if any) accepts, else an error.

name: prepare_send_message_platforms
doc: Load enabled standalone plugins before tool schemas/cache keys are built.

name: send_message_tool
doc: Handle cross-channel send_message tool calls.

name: _resolve_tool_target
doc:
``(platform_name, chat_id, thread_id, error)``; ``chat_id`` is None when no ref was given
(caller falls back to the home channel).

name: _authorize_relay_target
doc:
Relay egress-authorization guard (P5a); None when the send may proceed.

Thin delegate to ``gateway.relay.egress`` so the tool keeps working in
environments where the gateway package can't be imported.

THE TWO FAILURES ARE NOT THE SAME, and conflating them disabled the
boundary. A missing gateway module means there is no relay egress to
authorize, so proceeding is correct. A fault INSIDE the guard means
authorization did not happen — and returning None there means "authorized",
so a single runtime bug in the guard silently switched the whole P5(a)
boundary off. Review found this by making the guard raise and watching the
send go through.

So: the import is tolerated, the CALL is not. A guard that cannot answer
refuses, which is the only safe polarity for an authorization check.

doc:
Await ``make_coro()`` on the gateway's loop: adapter.send() uses queues/tasks bound to it,

name: _send_via_adapter
arguments: platform, pconfig, chat_id, chunk, *, thread_id=None, media_files=None, force_document=False
doc:
Live in-process gateway adapter first, else the plugin's ``standalone_sender_fn`` (cron),
else an error naming both; media uses the adapter's native media APIs under the same rules.

significant_calls.expression:
sender(pconfig, chat_id, chunk, thread_id=thread_id, media_files=media_files,
                              force_document=force_document)

_dispatch_on_gateway_loop(
                runner, make_coro, f"send_message: failed to schedule{' media send' if media_files else ''} on gateway loop")

AGENTS.md") misses; the verb→file gap forbids commas so enumerations ("Write skills, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md") miss.

scan verbatim. Fence state is ``(marker_char, opener_length)`` rather than a bool so a

Ordering by ``sorted(rglob(...))`` diverged from the bundle side on Windows: Path comparison is
case-insensitive there (normcase), while ``bundle_content_hash`` sorts plain strings — the same skill
hashed to different digests and every installed skill reported ``update_available`` forever (#62310).

doc:
GitHub answered 401 Bad credentials to *token*: stop sending it, so the next method and
finally anonymous are tried. A revoked GITHUB_TOKEN in .env otherwise shadows a working
`gh auth login` (and anonymous access to public repos) for the whole process.

name: search
arguments: self, query: str, limit: int=10, *, provider_filter: str=''
doc:
Substring-match taps, skip taps outside a provider filter, then dedupe by identifier
preferring higher trust and limit.

name: fetch
doc: Download a skill; identifier format: "owner/repo/path/to/skill-dir".

name: current_revision
doc:
Tree sha the default branch currently resolves to — one cached tree lookup per repo,
no blob downloads — so an update check can skip refetching unchanged skills.

name: _add_support_file
arguments: self, repo: str, item_path: str, rel_path: str, files: dict, shown: str, **kw
doc:
Fetch one support file into ``files``; a failed fetch warns (naming ``shown``), is skipped, and
returns False.

name: _collect_tree_files
arguments: self, repo: str, skill_path: str, entries: list[dict], ref: Optional[str], referenced: set, files: dict[str, str | bytes]
doc:
Download the FULL skill directory from the pinned tree into ``files``. Link-driven fetching
silently dropped support files under non-canonical dirs (``reference/``, ``agents/``, root
LICENSE); everything still goes through quarantine + scan, and the scanner sees MORE this way.
Returns None (bundle rejected) on an unsafe path or a SKILL.md-linked path that exists in the
tree as a symlink/non-blob — that shape is an escape attempt. A linked path that is simply absent
is a dangling link (repo-only dev tool, prose over-match): warn and install without it. Returns
False when a blob fetch failed (installed with a gap the next update check must be able to fill).
An empty ``skill_path`` is the repo-root skill layout, so the whole repo root is its directory.

name: inspect
doc: Fetch just the SKILL.md metadata for preview.

name: _list_skills_in_repo
arguments: self, repo: str, path: str, bucket: Optional[str]=None
doc:
List skill directories in a GitHub repo path, using cached index. ``bucket`` labels every
skill from a tap whose repo ships no ``skills.sh.json`` grouping, so several repos can share one
hub category (e.g. "science"); a sidecar grouping still wins when present.

name: _get_repo_tree
doc:
Cached ``(default_branch, tree_entries)`` for a repo, or None. One install may need the tree
several times; caching saves the ``GET /repos/{repo}`` + ``GET .../git/trees/{branch}`` pair each
time (~12 of the 60/hr unauthenticated budget before).

name: _github_json
doc: Decoded JSON body of a 200 ``_github_get`` (which flags rate-limit exhaustion), else None.

name: _github_get
arguments: self, url: str, *, params: Optional[dict]=None, headers: Optional[dict]=None, timeout: float=15.0, max_retries: int=3
doc:
GET against the GitHub API with retry/backoff on transient failures. Returns the final
response (caller inspects status) or None when every attempt raised a transport error.
