Retries rate-limit 403/429 (waiting until ``Retry-After`` / ``X-RateLimit-Reset`` when present,
capped 60s — one shared limit zeroes every GitHub tap at once during an index build), 5xx, and
transport errors with exponential backoff. Terminal rate-limit exhaustion flags the instance so
an index build fails loud instead of silently shipping zero GitHub skills.

name: _find_skill_in_repo_tree
doc: Locate ``<skill_name>/SKILL.md`` anywhere in the repo tree (one API call); full identifier or None.

name: _find_repo_root_skill
doc:
Identifier for a single-skill repo whose ``SKILL.md`` sits at the repo ROOT (no skill
directory) — e.g. ``orzcls/win-disk-cleaner``. The empty path segment (``owner/repo/``)
denotes the skill directory being the repo root. Only repos with EXACTLY ONE SKILL.md in
the whole tree qualify, so a categorized multi-skill repo never resolves here.

name: _fetch_file_content
arguments: self, repo: str, path: str, ref: Optional[str]=None
doc: Fetch a single text file from GitHub (None on miss or non-UTF-8).

name: _fetch_file_bytes
arguments: self, repo: str, path: str, ref: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Fetch exact file bytes. ``ref`` pins to a tree SHA (see ``fetch`` on
the TOCTOU); None keeps the legacy unpinned behavior. A pinned file comes from
raw.githubusercontent.com first: the same bytes at the same commit, outside the REST rate
limit. Through the Contents API every file in a skill folder cost one call, so an anonymous
user (60/h) could never install a skill with more than ~58 files. A private repo or a raw
miss falls back to the API. A transport failure (DNS-poisoned or NXDOMAIN raw host surfaces as
SSRFConnectionBlocked, a dropping firewall as a 15 s timeout) also falls back, and marks raw
unusable for the rest of this source's flow.

name: _get_skillsh_groupings
doc:
Repo-root ``skills.sh.json`` groupings flattened to ``{skill_name: title}``. ``skills.sh.json``
is a cross-ecosystem standard (``$schema: https://skills.sh/schemas/skills.sh.schema.json``); any
tap shipping it gets category pills for free. None when absent/unparsable; cached per repo.

name: _parse_skillsh_groupings
doc: Flatten ``{"groupings": [{"title", "skills": [...]}]}``; None if not usable.

name: _is_path_redirect
doc:
True when ``path`` is a symlink or (on Windows) a directory junction —
either lets a writer in ``skills/`` redirect a later ``rmtree`` outside it.
``is_junction`` only exists on Python 3.12+ Windows; gate with ``hasattr``.

name: _resolve_lock_install_path
doc:
Resolve a lock-file install path without allowing escapes from ``SKILLS_DIR``.

Walks component-by-component refusing symlink/junction redirects (which
``Path.resolve`` would silently follow), then rejects both escape-out and
``resolved == SKILLS_DIR`` — an empty/``"."`` install_path resolves to the
skills root and ``rmtree`` there would wipe every installed skill.

name: quarantine_bundle
doc: Write a skill bundle to the quarantine directory for scanning.

name: _category_skill_dirs
doc:
Names of non-hidden child dirs holding at least one active SKILL.md
anywhere below (nested layouts like ``mlops/training/<skill>`` count).

Vendored/cache/progressive-disclosure paths are pruned via
:func:`is_excluded_skill_path` so a lone ``node_modules`` or
``references/pkg/SKILL.md`` does not make the directory a category.
Shared with ``hermes_cli.skills_hub._existing_categories``.

name: _check_install_target
doc:
Raise ValueError when installing at ``install_dir`` would destroy other skills.

- Nesting inside an existing skill dir (``--category <existing-skill>``)
  would make a later update/uninstall of the outer skill rmtree the inner one.
- A stray regular file at the target: rmtree would raise NotADirectoryError.
- A category bucket (dir without SKILL.md that holds other skills) must never
  be silently wiped; a dir that directly contains SKILL.md is an existing
  install and stays overwritable (hub installs are lock-guarded in do_install).

name: install_from_quarantine
arguments: quarantine_path: Path, skill_name: str, category: str, bundle: SkillBundle, scan_result: ScanResult, scan_provenance: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Move a scanned skill from quarantine into the skills directory.

name: uninstall_skill
doc: Remove a hub-installed skill. Refuses to remove builtins.

name: bundle_content_hash
doc:
Deterministic hash of an in-memory bundle.

MUST stay symmetric with ``tools.skills_guard.content_hash`` (same skill
from disk), which keys files by POSIX relative path. Windows bundle keys
carry backslashes, which changed both bytes and sort order and made every
skill report ``update_available`` forever — normalize before hashing. The
path is hashed too so swapping contents between two files changes the hash.

That function keys files by ``relative_to(...).as_posix()`` — forward slashes on every OS. See #62310.

name: _current_revision_or_empty
doc: A probe failure must degrade one row to the full-fetch path, not abort the whole check.

name: check_for_skill_updates
arguments: name: Optional[str]=None, *, lock: Optional[HubLockFile]=None, sources: Optional[list[SkillSource]]=None, auth: Optional[GitHubAuth]=None
doc:
Check installed hub skills for upstream changes.

Each entry is fetched ONLY from adapters matching its recorded source.
Falling back to all sources let a same-named skill in a different registry
satisfy the fetch and silently reassign provenance (names are not
namespaced across registries), so a missing adapter reports "unavailable".

name: hub
doc:
``tools.skills_hub`` resolved at call time: its cache / HTTP / index helpers are the test-patch targets
(``patch("tools.skills_hub._read_index_cache")`` ...), so adapters look them up on every call, not at import.

name: _cached_metas
doc: SkillMeta list from the shared index cache, or None on miss/expiry.

name: _memo_json
arguments: key: str, compute: Callable[[], Any], valid: Callable[[Any], bool]=lambda c: c is not None
doc:
Shared-index-cache memo: a cached value passing ``valid`` is returned as-is; otherwise ``compute()``
runs and a non-None result is written back.

name: _get_json
doc: Plain (unguarded) GET + JSON decode; None on non-200 or transport/decode error.

name: _get_text
doc: Plain (unguarded) GET; body text on 200, None on any other status or transport error.

name: _matches_query
doc: Case-insensitive substring match against joined fields (lists space-joined; empty query matches all).

name: _first_matching
arguments: query_lower: str, items: Iterable[Any], fields_of: Callable[[Any], tuple], to_meta: Callable[[Any], Optional[SkillMeta]], limit: int
doc: Substring-search ``items`` in order, converting hits with ``to_meta`` until ``limit``.

name: _dedupe_by_trust
doc:
Dedupe by identifier, keeping the higher-trust copy (first wins on ties). identifier is unique per
skill; name is not — two taps can publish same-named skills, and browse-sh reuses task names across sites.

name: _parse_frontmatter
doc: Parse YAML frontmatter from SKILL.md content ({} when absent/invalid).

name: _hermes_tags
doc: ``metadata.hermes.tags`` from parsed frontmatter, or ``[]`` (unvalidated type).

name: source_url_for_bundle
doc: Best available human-facing immutable-source provenance URL.

name: _normalize_bundle_path
arguments: path_value: str, *, field_name: str, allow_nested: bool
doc: Normalize and validate bundle-controlled paths before touching disk.

name: _normalize_lock_install_path
doc:
Validate a lock-file ``install_path`` (the ``uninstall_skill`` rmtree target).

Must be relative, traversal-free, and end with ``<skill_name>`` — nested official skills legitimately
live at ``mlops/training/<skill_name>``; an empty/``"."``/absolute/mismatched entry could point rmtree
at the whole ``skills/`` tree or outside it.

name: _query_is_concrete
doc:
Whether a URL query is real URL syntax rather than glob prose.

A non-empty ``key=value`` part is always concrete. Valueless flags are accepted only when RFC 3986
unreserved-token shaped (percent escapes ok); ``.``, brackets and extra ``?`` are excluded because
``?x.md`` / ``?.md`` is indistinguishable from a single-char glob finishing a filename in prose.

name: _referenced_support_paths
doc: Extract safe referenced paths; return None on a traversal attempt (fail closed).

name: search
doc: Search for skills matching a query string.

name: fetch
doc: Download a skill bundle by identifier.

name: inspect
doc: Fetch metadata for a skill without downloading all files.

name: current_revision
doc:
Upstream revision the skill would be fetched at; "" when the registry has no cheap
revision probe, which keeps update checks on the full-fetch path.

name: _clean_rel_parts
doc: Split a relative path, dropping ``.``/empty parts; None on traversal or empty.

name: _entry_provider
doc: Normalized ``extra.provider`` label of a raw index entry.

name: _meta
arguments: self, rel_dir: str, name: str, description: str, tags: list

name: _remote_meta
doc: Placeholder meta for a skill that exists on live main but not locally.

name: _bundle
arguments: rel_id: str, files: dict[str, str | bytes], **kwargs

name: list_local
doc:
Every optional skill in the local checkout, with frontmatter metadata
(backs the dashboard/desktop "built-in optional skills" catalog).

name: _fetch_from_live_repo
doc:
Fetch an optional skill straight from the live default branch. Local installs lag
``main``; rather than demanding ``hermes update`` first, resolve against the live repo.
``rel`` is ``category/skill`` (used verbatim) or a bare skill name (located via the repo tree).

name: _list_remote_skill_dirs
doc:
``category/skill`` dirs under optional-skills/ on live main. One repo-tree call (cached
per-process by GitHubSource + the on-disk index cache). {} when the network/API is
unavailable — callers degrade to local-only.

name: _upstream_pointer_from_content
doc:
Parse ``metadata.hermes.upstream: {repo: owner/name, path: ...}`` out of SKILL.md content
(a catalog stub); None for vendored skills.

name: _fetch_from_upstream
arguments: self, upstream: dict[str, str], rel_id: str
doc:
Fetch an upstream-maintained optional skill via GitHubSource.fetch() (full-tree download,
symlink/unsafe-path rejection, quarantine + scan downstream) and re-label it as an official
catalog entry.

name: _find_skill_dir
doc: Find a skill directory by name anywhere in optional-skills/.

name: _scan_all
doc: Enumerate all optional skills with metadata.

name: is_available
doc: Whether the index is loaded and has skills.

name: search
arguments: self, query: str, limit: int=10, *, provider_filter: str=''
doc:
Search the cached index (zero API calls). Matches name, description, tags, identifier and
``extra.provider`` (so ``nvidia`` finds ``NVIDIA/skills/...`` entries stored as source
"github"). Ranked exact name > name prefix > provider > whole-word > name substring > other,
index order as tiebreaker — a raw break-at-limit slice buried the most relevant skills.
Provider filters narrow the catalog before ranking and limiting.

name: fetch
doc:
Fetch via the index's ``resolved_github_id`` (skipping the whole
candidate/discovery chain), falling back to ``repo/path``.

name: inspect
doc: Return metadata from the index (zero API calls).

name: _find_entry
doc: Exact identifier match first, then match with source prefixes stripped.

name: _load_hermes_index
doc:
Fetch the centralized skills index (docs site, rebuilt daily), cached
locally for HERMES_INDEX_TTL; on any failure serve the stale cache.

Brotli is deliberately NOT negotiated: the index is tens of MB and httpx's
streaming Brotli decoder (brotlicffi, pinned for Discord attachments) raises
DecodingError on payloads this size — which surfaced as a silently empty
Skills Hub. gzip/deflate first; the identity retry covers proxies that
ignore the header and return Brotli anyway.

name: _load_stale_index_cache
doc: Fall back to the cache regardless of age when the network fetch fails.

name: create_source_router
doc: All configured source adapters, in priority order.

name: _search_one_source
arguments: src: SkillSource, query: str, limit: int, provider_filter: str=''
doc: Search a single source.  Runs in a thread for parallelism.

name: _select_active_sources
doc:
Sources to query for ``source_filter``.

A provider filter (nvidia/openai/...) is not a source id — the data lives
in the index/github source under ``extra.provider`` — so it selects like
"all". Mixed-provider sources narrow before their top-N cut; the walker
cuts every source's results. "official" is always queried alongside an
explicit source filter.

name: _index_miss_fallback_sources
arguments: sources: list[SkillSource], active: list[SkillSource], query: str, source_counts: dict[str, int], provider_filter: str=''
doc:
Registries to consult after the index stood in for them and found nothing.

Empty for a browse (no query), when the index was not consulted (no skip
happened), when it returned matches, or when it did not answer at all
(timed out: no budget is left and the registries would only be blamed as
late without being asked). Also empty under a provider filter
(``--source nvidia``): the fallback registries carry no ``extra.provider``,
so their results would all be cut and the calls would only burn budget.

name: _fan_out
arguments: active: list[SkillSource], query: str, per_source_limits: dict[str, int], provider_filter: str, deadline: float, on_source_done: Optional[Any], all_results: list[SkillMeta], source_counts: dict[str, int], timed_out_ids: list[str]
doc: Query ``active`` in parallel until ``deadline`` (monotonic), merging into the accumulators.

name: parallel_search_sources
arguments: sources: list[SkillSource], query: str='', per_source_limits: Optional[dict[str, int]]=None, source_filter: str='all', overall_timeout: float=30, on_source_done: Optional[Any]=None
doc:
Search all sources in parallel with an overall timeout.

Returns ``(all_results, source_counts, timed_out_ids)``. *on_source_done*
is an optional ``(source_id, count) -> None`` progress callback. Under a
provider filter every source's results are narrowed before they are
counted and merged, so callers need no provider logic of their own.

When the centralized index stood in for the external registries and found
nothing for a non-empty query, those registries are queried within the
same ``overall_timeout`` — capped at ``_INDEX_MISS_FALLBACK_BUDGET`` so a
slow registry cannot turn an instant index miss into a 30 s stall — so
every caller (CLI, TUI gateway, dashboard) still finds skills the index
has not picked up yet.

name: unified_search
arguments: query: str, sources: list[SkillSource], source_filter: str='all', limit: int=10
doc: Search all sources (in parallel) and merge results.

name: _meta
arguments: self, canonical: str, *, name: str, description: str, path: str, extra: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None

name: _sitemap_catalog
doc:
Enumerate the full catalog via the sitemap (cached for the index TTL —
~2 MB of XML). Falls back to ``_featured_skills`` when unreachable/empty.

name: _finalize_inspect_meta
arguments: self, meta: SkillMeta, canonical: str, detail: Optional[dict]

name: _meta
arguments: self, parsed: dict, skill_name: str, description: str, files: Any, **extra

name: _matches
doc:
Claim bare HTTP(S) URLs ending in ``.md``; leave wrapped identifiers
and ``/.well-known/skills/`` URLs to their own adapters.

name: _load
doc: ``(url, text, frontmatter, resolved name)`` for a claimed identifier, else None.

name: _resolve_skill_name
doc:
Frontmatter ``name:`` when valid, else a URL-slug candidate (``.../<name>/SKILL.md`` -> ``<name>``,
``.../<name>.md`` -> ``<name>``). None when nothing usable — the CLI then prompts or refuses rather
than auto-naming something like ``SKILL``.

name: _agent_meta
arguments: agent: dict, name: str, description: str

name: _convert_to_skill_md
doc: Convert a LobeHub agent JSON into SKILL.md format.

name: _resolve_skill_md_url
doc: ``skillMdUrl`` from ``/api/skills/{slug}``; fallback to a ``raw.githubusercontent.com`` ``sourceUrl``.

name: _slug_from_identifier
doc: 'browse-sh/airbnb.com/search-listings-abc' -> 'airbnb.com/search-listings-abc'.

name: _live
doc: The patched module global if it changed since import, else the live value.

name: _iter_skill_mds
doc: Yield every non-excluded SKILL.md under ``root`` (nothing when it does not exist).

name: _iter_active_skill_mds
doc: Yield every non-excluded SKILL.md in the user's skills tree.

name: _build_external_skill_index
doc:
Names (directory and frontmatter) of every skill provided by external_dirs,
so sync_skills never shadows an externally-delegated skill.

name: _read_manifest
doc: ``{skill_name: origin_hash}``; v1 plain-name lines get an empty hash (migrates next sync).

name: _read_suppressed_names
doc:
Built-in skills the curator pruned — must NOT be re-seeded on sync.

Delegates to ``tools.skill_usage`` (single source of truth) and falls back
to reading ``~/.hermes/skills/.curator_suppressed`` directly if that import
is unavailable in a packaged/update context.

name: _write_manifest
doc: Atomic v2 write, preserving an existing file's mode/owner (not mkstemp's 0600).

name: _discover_bundled_skills
doc:
``(skill_name, skill_dir)`` per SKILL.md under the bundled dir. Exclusions are evaluated
relative to the bundled tree: the install prefix itself may contain ``venv``/``site-packages``
(which once made wheel installs discover zero skills).

name: _compute_relative_dest
doc: Destination preserving category structure (bundled/mlops/axolotl -> skills/mlops/axolotl).

name: dir_hash
doc:
MD5 of package paths/content, excluding generated runtime state.

The legacy option is only for proving an exact pre-filter origin match.
Keep the original path encoding so clean existing manifests remain valid.

name: _matches_origin_hash
arguments: directory: Path, origin_hash: str, user_hash: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Prove unchanged package ownership against a clean OR exact legacy hash.

Never re-baseline a differing package merely because it contains a cache:
if legacy cached bytes changed/disappeared, the old origin cannot be proven.
A genuinely edited package must remain protected in that case.

name: _recover_renamed_skill
doc:
Move a bundled skill's stale copy to its new canonical path after an upstream RENAME /
RECATEGORIZATION (else it is misread as user-deleted and stranded forever). Only a copy
byte-identical to the origin hash — proof *we* placed it — moves. Returns rel source path.

name: _recover_orphan_backup
doc:
If an interrupted update left the user's only copy in ``dest.bak`` with dest gone, move it
back so the skill isn't misread as user-deleted.

name: _defer_to_external
arguments: st: _SyncState, skill_name: str, dest: Path, bundled_hash: str
doc:
An external_dirs source provides this skill; a local copy would be a name collision the
loader refuses. Defer for ALL manifest states; remove a stale local shadow from an earlier
sync only when byte-identical (a user's own skill differs).

name: _install_new_skill
arguments: st: _SyncState, skill_name: str, skill_src: Path, dest: Path, bundled_hash: str
doc: Handle a skill never offered before (not in manifest).

name: _replace_skill_dir
doc: Replace ``dest`` with a fresh copy of ``skill_src`` via a .bak sibling; restore on failure.

name: _update_existing_skill
arguments: st: _SyncState, skill_name: str, skill_src: Path, dest: Path, bundled_hash: str
doc: Handle a skill that is in the manifest AND on disk.

name: _seed_category_descriptions
doc:
Copy category DESCRIPTION.md files not already present; ``only_dirs`` restricts
seeding to the essential skills' categories on opted-out profiles.

name: sync_skills
doc:
Sync bundled skills into ~/.hermes/skills/ using the manifest; returns the per-category
result dict. Opted-out profiles seed ONLY ESSENTIAL_SKILLS (the system prompt always
points at ``hermes-agent``).

name: _rmtree_writable
doc:
rmtree that first makes read-only entries writable (Nix/deb/rpm keep r-x dirs; unlinking
a child needs a writable parent, so chmod both). Scope guard: refuses anything not a STRICT
child of the active skills root (bad join / missing HERMES_HOME / malicious manifest entry).

Handles immutable package sources (Nix store, deb/rpm installs) that preserve read-only permissions on
copied files *and* directories (``r-xr-xr-x``). Removing a child requires write permission on its parent
directory, so the retry handler makes the failing path **and its parent** writable before re-attempting.
See #34860, #34972.

name: _bundled_state
doc: ``(skills_sync, manifest, bundled_dir, {skill_name: bundled_src})`` — shared op preamble.

name: reset_bundled_skill
doc:
Reset a bundled skill's manifest tracking so future syncs work normally. An edited bundled
skill stays ``user_modified`` forever because the manifest holds the OLD origin hash; clearing
the entry breaks that loop. ``restore`` also deletes the user's copy so the next sync re-copies
bundled. Returns ``{ok, action, message, synced}``; action is manifest_cleared / restored /
not_in_manifest / bundled_missing / not_reset.

name: bundled_skill_for_install
doc:
Bundled skill name an install identifier means, else None: a bare bundled name, or this
repo's own copy of one (``NousResearch/hermes-agent/skills/<cat>/<name>``, which the Skills Hub
site hands out for built-ins, or its ``skills-sh/nousresearch/hermes-agent/<name>`` mirror).
Fetched from GitHub, that copy is scanned as a community skill and refused — every time.

name: ensure_bundled_skill
doc:
Make bundled ``name`` active: ``{ok, action, path, message}``, action ``present`` (any active
copy, user edits included, is left alone), ``restored`` (copied from the bundled source and
re-tracked, so an opt-out, curator prune or manual delete no longer hides it), or
``hub_shadowed`` (a hub install owns the name; it is the user's to remove, never overwritten).
A restore into a leftover dir only adds the missing files (a user file is never overwritten) and
the manifest records the bundled hash, so a dest that kept user files reads as user-modified and
``hermes update`` leaves it alone: intended, the user's data wins.

name: list_user_modified_bundled_skills
doc:
Bundled skills ``hermes update`` keeps because the user edited them (same test the sync
loop uses). Name-sorted ``{"name", "dest", "bundled_src"}`` dicts.

name: _read_for_diff
doc: ``(raw_bytes, text)`` for diffing; ``text=None`` for binary, ``(None, None)`` if unreadable.

name: diff_bundled_skill
doc:
Diff a user's copy of a bundled skill against stock. Returns ``{ok, name, found, modified,
message, diffs}``; each diff is ``{"path", "status", "diff"}`` with status modified / added
(only in user copy) / removed (only in bundled) / binary.

name: set_bundled_skills_opt_out
doc:
Toggle the .no-bundled-skills marker (on-disk half of ``hermes skills opt-out`` / ``opt-in``;
removing present skills is ``remove_pristine_bundled_skills``).

name: remove_pristine_bundled_skills
doc:
Delete bundled skills that are manifest-tracked, still in the bundled source AND
byte-identical to the origin hash; everything else lands in ``skipped``. Removed skills lose
their manifest entry so a later opt-in re-seed treats them as new.
Returns ``{ok, removed, skipped: [{name, reason}], dry_run, message}``.

name: _ss
doc: Live ``tools.skills_sync`` module (imported lazily: it imports helpers from this module).

name: _content_hash
doc: Hub-lock hash style; provenance metadata only, so fall back to local MD5 sans guard deps.

name: _safe_rel_install_path
doc: Normalized relative POSIX path; rejects traversal/absolute paths.

name: _is_runtime_cache
doc:
Whether a skill-relative path is disposable Python/tool runtime state.

Install prefixes may themselves contain a cache directory name. Legacy
sibling bytecode is ignored only alongside its source; source-less .pyc
files can be deliberately shipped or user-owned content.

name: _ignore_runtime_cache
doc: copytree callback: don't seed generated caches into managed packages.

name: _skill_file_list
doc: List package files for provenance/diff, excluding generated runtime caches.

name: _load_hub_lock
doc: Parse the skills-hub lock; None when missing or unreadable.

name: _read_hub_install_paths
doc:
Hub-lock install paths as POSIX strings. Hub-installed skills are owned by the hub: rename
recovery must not move them even when content matches a bundled origin hash (dangling lock).

name: _iter_optional_skills
doc: Yield ``(skill_md, src, install_path)`` for every safe official optional skill.

name: _optional_skill_index
doc:
Official optional skills keyed by BOTH folder name and frontmatter name (hub-lock slug or
user-facing name). Values are ``(folder_name, install_path, source_dir)``.

name: _move_to_restore_backup
doc: Move an existing skill directory into a restore backup, preserving rel path.

name: restore_official_optional_skill
doc:
Restore one or all official optional skills from repo source. ``restore=False`` only
backfills exact-match provenance; ``restore=True`` also backs up matching active copies
and copies the official source into its canonical path.

name: _index_installed_skill_dirs_by_name
doc:
Installed skills by directory name in one active-tree scan, skipping anything that
resolves outside the skills tree (symlinks/external).

name: _relocated_dest
doc:
``(dest, install_path)`` of a UNIQUE same-directory-name match, else None: the active
tree may hold a skill under a DIFFERENT category than the repo (upstream reorganized,
installed copy kept its place); ambiguity gives no basis to pick.

name: _backfill_optional_provenance
doc:
Mark already-present official optional skills as hub-installed: formerly bundled (or
hand-copied) skills now under optional-skills/ get official provenance when byte-identical
to the source; modified/local skills are left alone.

name: clear_skills_cache
doc: Drop the scanned catalog so the next listing re-scans (explicit reloads must not wait out the TTL).

name: _dir_tree_signature
doc:
Append ``(dir, mtime_ns, child dir names)`` for *root* and the dirs below it the catalog walks
(``iter_skill_index_files``: no excluded dirs, no support dirs of a skill), depth-bounded. The child
names, not only mtimes: an install and an uninstall inside one coarse mtime tick (1-2 s on some
filesystems) leave every mtime equal, and the change must still show. ~1 ms for 170 dirs.

name: _skills_scan_signature
doc:
Stat-based change signature over every directory the catalog walks; platform is read via
``agent.skill_utils.sys`` so test patches are honored.

name: _skills_dir
doc:
Active profile's skills dir at call time: the patched ``SKILLS_DIR`` when a patcher changed
it, else live profile-scoped HERMES_HOME (long-lived runtimes may import before profile set).

name: skill_lookup_path_error
doc:
Error if lookup *name* could escape the search roots it is joined onto. Windows drive
paths are rejected too: their ``:`` would be misread as a plugin namespace separator.

name: load_env
doc:
Snapshot of HERMES_HOME/.env for the post-skill secret-capture diff (same tokenizer that
installs the profile scope, so a captured value never differs from the served one). A frozen-policy
worker never opens the profile ``.env``: ``hermes_cli.config.load_env`` owns that short-circuit.

name: _skill_utils_delegate
doc: Lazy call-time delegate to ``agent.skill_utils.<attr>`` (re-export; patches honored).

name: _get_category_from_path
doc:
``~/.hermes/skills/mlops/axolotl/SKILL.md`` -> ``"mlops"``; active profile dir first
(respects test monkeypatching), then skills.external_dirs.

name: _parse_tags
doc: Tags from frontmatter: a parsed list, "[a, b]", or "a, b".

name: _is_skill_disabled
doc:
Any of *names* disabled in config (one config load)? Platform precedence: explicit arg,
``HERMES_PLATFORM``, session ``HERMES_SESSION_PLATFORM``. A globally-disabled skill stays disabled on every platform
(keep in sync with agent.skill_utils.get_disabled_skill_names).

name: skill_search_dirs
doc:
(``(tier, dir)`` roots in precedence order, active_skills_dir) — the shared
``agent.skill_utils.get_skill_search_roots`` order with the live profile dir (dropped if absent).

name: _skill_catalog
doc:
Every scanned skill resolved by ``agent.skill_utils.resolve_skill_catalog`` (status /
load_name / tier / path), visible ones only unless *include_hidden*; cached per session.
Resolution runs over ALL files first — skill_view ignores platform/disabled gates when
collecting candidates, so it asks for hidden rows too.

name: find_all_skills
doc:
Loadable skills (name, description, category): ``name`` is what skill_view() accepts —
the declared name, or the exact relative path for a same-tier duplicate. Shadowed and
unloadable copies are left out. ``skip_disabled=True`` ignores disabled state (config UI).

name: sort_skills
doc: Keep every skill listing path ordered the same way.

name: skills_list
arguments: category: str | None=None, task_id: str | None=None
doc: Tier 1 listing: name + description (+ category) only; ``task_id`` is handler parity.

name: _resolve_plugin_skill
doc:
``plugin:skill`` dispatch: ``(result_json, None)`` when answered, else ``(None,
local_category_name)`` to fall through to the flat-tree scan — categorized local skills also use
``category:skill`` in config/gateway prompts, so the on-disk ``category/skill`` form returns.

name: _under_any
doc: True when ``path`` (resolved where possible) lives under one of ``dirs``.

name: _is_package_owned_markdown
doc: True when a legacy Markdown candidate belongs to an ancestor directory skill.

name: _collect_skill_candidates
doc:
ALL (skill_dir, skill_md) candidates across every dir and lookup strategy (direct path,
recursive by dir / frontmatter name, legacy flat <name>.md), deduped by resolved path.
Every copy is returned so the caller resolves them via ``agent.skill_utils.pick_skill_candidate``
(cross-tier precedence; a same-tier tie of different skills is refused, never guessed).

name: _skill_linked_files
doc: references/templates/assets/scripts of a directory skill (empty groups dropped).

name: _skill_readiness
doc:
Resolve required env vars / credential files (prompting for secrets where the surface
allows) and register what's available for sandboxes. Returns ``(fields, extras)``: fields go
before the readiness extras in the skill_view result — key order is tool output.

name: _owning_search_dir
doc:
Most specific search dir containing *skill_md*, compared lexically: a symlinked entry
belongs to the root that exposes it, not to the root its target lives in.

name: locate_skill
doc:
Unique on-disk skill for *name* over ``(tier, dir)`` *roots*: cross-tier precedence
(project > local > create_dir > external, shadowed copies logged), same-tier collision refusal,
same-root identical-copy ranking, quarantine gate, not-found listing. ``(error_json, skill_dir,
skill_md)``; skill_md set iff no error.

name: _owned_relative
doc: Exact load path of a candidate: its skill dir (or flat ``.md`` stem) relative to its root.

name: _log_security_warnings
arguments: name: str, skill_md: Path, content: str, all_dirs, active_skills_dir
doc:
Warn (never block) when loaded from outside the trusted dirs (project + local + external)
and/or when common prompt-injection patterns appear. The check is on the RESOLVED path:
every candidate is built as ``<search_dir>/...`` so a lexical test can never fire, and a
SKILL.md symlinked to a file outside every root is exactly what this guards against.

name: skill_view
arguments: name: str, file_path: str | None=None, task_id: str | None=None, preprocess: bool=True
doc:
View a skill (SKILL.md) or a file within its directory, as JSON. ``name`` is a skill name
or path ("axolotl", "03-fine-tuning/axolotl"); "plugin:skill" resolves plugin-provided
skills. ``preprocess`` applies the configured SKILL.md template / inline shell rendering;
slash/preload callers render the message themselves.

name: _skill_view_with_bump
doc:
Invoke skill_view, then bump view_count/use on success (best-effort). Repeat-view dedup
mirrors read_file's unchanged-stub: a result byte-identical to one already served for the
same skill file in this session returns a short stub (cache cleared on context compression).

name: dedup_skill_view
arguments: task_id, name, file_path, payload: dict, result: str
doc:
The "unchanged" stub when this task was already served exactly ``result`` for this skill
file; otherwise record ``result``'s digest and return None (serve the full result).

name: reset_skill_view_dedup
doc: Clear the dedup cache (all tasks when task_id is None); called on context compression.

name: _read_skill_text
doc:
utf-8-sig + errors="replace": user-authored SKILL.md may carry a Notepad BOM or stray
bytes; pinning UTF-8 keeps skill_view deterministic across host locales.

name: _safe_frontmatter
arguments: path: Path | None=None, *, content: str | None=None
doc:
Frontmatter of *path* (or of *content*), ``{}`` on any read/parse failure.
Parses via ``tools.skills_tool._parse_frontmatter`` so test patches are honored.

name: _available_skill_files
doc:
Non-SKILL.md files grouped by support dir (+ "other" for known source extensions
elsewhere); empty groups dropped.

name: _serve_skill_file
arguments: skill_root: Path, file_path: str, label: str, *, hint: str | None=None, list_available: bool=False, read_error_prefix: bool=False, mark_read: bool=False
doc:
Serve one linked file from a skill directory as a skill_view JSON result. ``hint``
decorates traversal/containment errors; ``list_available`` adds the available-files listing
on not-found (local); ``read_error_prefix`` wraps non-decode read errors (plugin) instead
of propagating to the caller's handler.

name: _preprocess_skill
arguments: content: str, skill_dir, session_id, debug_msg: str, *args
doc: Apply the configured SKILL.md preprocessing; on failure log and serve raw.

name: _serve_plugin_skill
arguments: skill_md: Path, namespace: str, bare: str, file_path: str | None=None, *, preprocess: bool=True, session_id: str | None=None
doc: Read a plugin-provided skill, apply guards, return JSON.

name: _is_remote_env_backend
doc: Built-in remote backends plus plugin backends declaring is_remote.

name: _as_dict_list
doc: Accept a single mapping or a list; anything else is treated as empty.

name: _clean_str
doc: Stripped string when *value* is a non-blank str, else None.

name: _get_required_environment_variables
doc:
Merge required_environment_variables, setup.collect_secrets and legacy
prerequisites.env_vars into one deduped, validated list (first entry wins).

name: _capture_required_environment_variables
doc: Prompt for missing secrets via the registered capture callback (if any).

name: _is_env_var_persisted
doc:
Return whether a requirement is present in this profile's secret sources.

The snapshot keeps the existing ``.env`` precedence.  A miss must use
``get_secret`` rather than reading ``os.environ`` directly so an active
multiplex worker can see its hydrated external secrets without seeing a
different profile's process environment.

name: _build_setup_note
arguments: readiness_status: SkillReadinessStatus, missing: list[str], setup_help: str | None=None

name: set_ledger_actor
doc: Bind an explicit actor for this context; reset_ledger_actor(token) in a finally.

name: derive_actor
doc: Explicit override, else background-review provenance -> curator, else agent.

name: _ledger_lock
doc:
Exclusive cross-process lock on the ledger file, held across an append AND the maintenance
sweep, and across the CLI compact/GC path. Without it a concurrent appender's O_APPEND write can
land on the inode ``compact_ledger``/``_trim_oldest`` are about to ``os.replace`` — the row is
silently lost and ``gc_blobs`` then deletes its blobs. Same idiom as ``_skill_mutation_lock``:
``<skills>/.locks/ledger.lock``, thread-re-entrant, no-op where neither fcntl nor msvcrt exists.

name: _skills_cfg
doc:
``skills.<key>`` from the read-only merged config (no deepcopy), or *default* when the
read fails. Lazy import keeps this module importable without the CLI.

name: ledger_enabled
doc: Config gate ``skills.ledger`` (default True).

name: _max_ledger_bytes
doc:
Config ``skills.ledger_max_bytes`` (default 5 MB, 0 disables): above it the
next append triggers the maintenance sweep instead of growing the file forever.

name: _rel_posix
doc: POSIX path of ``path`` relative to ``root`` (both normalized), or None when outside.

name: _is_within
doc: True when *path* (normalized, no symlink resolution) sits under *root*.

name: _store_blob
doc: Write *data* keyed by sha256 (existing blob left alone). Returns the hash.

name: read_blob
doc: Return blob content or None when missing/invalid.

name: snapshot_paths
doc:
{path, sha256} for every file under *root*, each stored as a blob; [] when root is
None/missing. Transient local artifacts (venvs, node_modules, caches, .git) are
excluded wherever they appear under *root*. Raises on I/O failure — callers decide
whether that is fatal (rollback safety capture) or swallowed (telemetry).
``complete_package`` unions in the newest curator tarball's files (disk hashes win).

name: _package_rel
doc:
Relative POSIX path of a skill dir under ``skills/``; None when outside it
or under backup/hub/archive metadata roots (never a package).

name: package_prefixes
arguments: root: Optional[Path]=None, skill: Optional[str]=None, before: Optional[list[dict[str, str]]]=None
doc:
Tar member prefixes of this skill's package: live location under ``skills/``,
the package parent from the before-state SKILL.md path (rollback fills where
*root* is gone), the bare skill name, and the name minus an archive suffix.

name: _read_package_files_from_latest_backup
doc:
``{posix-relpath: bytes}`` under *prefixes* in the newest ``skills/.curator_backups/*/
skills.tar.gz``; malicious member names (absolute, ``..`` traversal) are rejected.

name: fill_snapshot_from_curator_backup
arguments: root: Optional[Path], existing: Optional[list[dict[str, str]]]=None, *, skill: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Union missing skill-package files from the newest curator snapshot. Completeness fill, not
a gate: failures return *existing* unchanged, and only ABSENT paths are filled. Fill targets go
where rollback must restore them: under *root* when known (for purge that is
``.archive/<name>/``, NOT the live tree), else the live skills dir; the tar's leading
package-dir segment is stripped when *root* already names the package. Every target must stay
under ``skills/`` and HERMES_HOME.

name: _delta
arguments: before: list[dict[str, str]], after: list[dict[str, str]]
doc:
Drop paths whose hash is identical on both sides. ``rollback_entry`` writes every *before*
path and removes *after*-only paths, so unchanged files are dead weight there — and a full
package manifest per edit made a 4,000-file skill cost 1.5 MB of ledger per patch (650 MB
over one summer). Deletions/creations are preserved: a path present on one side only stays.

name: append_entry
arguments: action: str, skill: str, before: Optional[list[dict[str, str]]]=None, after: Optional[list[dict[str, str]]]=None, actor: Optional[str]=None, evidence: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc: Append one entry -> id, or None when disabled / write failed (never raises).

name: _read_ledger
doc:
Raw ledger bytes, or ``None`` (after a warning) when the file cannot be read or is not UTF-8.
``quiet_missing`` keeps a merely absent ledger silent — normal for a fresh install.

name: _maintain_size
doc:
Keep the ledger bounded: once it crosses ``skills.ledger_max_bytes`` run the
delta-dedup rewrite, and if genuinely-divergent entries still exceed the cap,
drop the oldest ones until it fits. Best-effort telemetry, never a gate: any
failure is logged and the just-appended entry stays on disk.

Trimming stops at a LOW-WATER mark (``_TRIM_LOW_WATER`` of the cap), not at the
cap itself: a ledger trimmed to exactly the cap is over it again on the very next
append, so every append would pay compact + trim + blob GC. ``gc_blobs`` only
runs when the trim actually dropped rows — that is the only way a blob can
become orphaned here.

name: _rewrite_ledger
arguments: path: Path, lines: list[bytes], op: str
doc:
Atomically replace the ledger at *path* with *lines* (one physical row each, no
terminators): write ``<name>.<op>.tmp`` fully, then ``os.replace`` it over the ledger.
Returns the bytes written so callers can report the new size.

name: _trim_oldest
doc:
Rewrite the ledger without its oldest lines until it is at most *max_bytes*;
the newest entry always survives. Lines in the retained tail are never rewritten
or parsed — malformed lines there survive verbatim; trimming drops the oldest
lines regardless of shape. Returns the number of lines dropped (0 = untouched).

name: compact_ledger
doc:
Rewrite the ledger with every entry's unchanged paths dropped (see ``_delta``); ids, order and
rollback semantics are preserved. Returns ``(entries, bytes_before, bytes_after)``. Atomic: the
new file replaces the old only once fully written. Malformed lines are kept verbatim. Follow with
``gc_blobs()``: dropped references leave blobs nothing can restore.

name: gc_blobs
doc:
Delete blobs no ledger entry references; returns ``(deleted, bytes_freed)``. The store was
write-only: on one install 98.9% of 47k blobs (1.18 GB) were unreachable after a venv walk
(#107539). Malformed ledger lines, or an unreadable/undecodable ledger, abort the sweep
(blobs are kept) — an entry we cannot read may still hold references. Blobs newer than
``_BLOB_GC_GRACE_SECS`` are kept too: ``snapshot_paths`` stores them before the referencing row.

name: record_mutation
arguments: action: str, skill: str, before_root: Optional[Path]=None, before: Optional[list[dict[str, str]]]=None, after_root: Optional[Path]=None, actor: Optional[str]=None, evidence: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
Mutation hook: after-state from *after_root* (before = pre-captured list or captured from
*before_root*), then append. NEVER raises. delete/archive/purge capture a COMPLETE package
(filled from the newest curator backup) so rollback never restores a shell.

name: capture_before
arguments: root: Optional[Path], *, complete_package: bool=False, skill: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Best-effort pre-mutation capture; None on failure/disabled (pass straight to
record_mutation). ``complete_package=True`` for delete/archive/purge.

name: list_entries
doc: Read the ledger, newest first. Malformed lines are skipped.

name: _validate_entry_paths
doc:
Every entry path must be under HERMES_HOME — a hand-edited ledger must not
become a write-anywhere primitive.

name: rollback_entry
doc:
Restore the before-state of mutation *entry_id*. Fail-closed (mirrors
agent/curator_backup.rollback): every before-blob must exist BEFORE any change, and a
pre-rollback safety entry of every touched path's CURRENT state is appended first.

1. 2. See #63366.

name: _strip_code_blocks
doc: Remove fenced code blocks so prose-only checks don't fire on examples.

name: lint_content
doc:
Lint raw SKILL.md *content*.

``skill_dir`` enables on-disk checks (name/dir match, dangling links, POSIX
gating, forbidden files); without it only content checks run, which is what
the create path needs before the file exists.

name: lint_skill
doc: Lint a SKILL.md file on disk, with all on-disk checks enabled.

name: _misplaced_text_hint
doc: Sentence naming the text-slot key(s) this op carries that ``action`` never reads, or ''.

name: _op_shape_error
doc:
Argument-shape error text for one op, or None. Only shape misses carry the misplaced-text
hint: a patch whose real problem is an unmatched old_string must not be steered to a full
rewrite. Pure function so the batch can reject a misfiled op BEFORE any sibling is applied.

name: _validate_batch_ops
doc: Shape checks with no side effects. Returns (names, None) or (None, error_json).

name: _snapshot_skills
doc:
Copy every touched skill aside. Returns (snapshots, None) or (None, error_text).

``create_targets`` maps a name with no skill yet to the dir its ``create`` op will use.
An EMPTY pre-existing dir there has no SKILL.md to snapshot, yet create adopts it (see
``_create_skill``): record that it pre-dated the batch so rollback never rmtree()s it.

name: _rollback
doc:
Restore every snapshot. ``results`` are the ops applied so far (their name/file_path
tell an adopted dir's rollback which files were the batch's). Returns (note, failed).

name: _skill_manage_batch
arguments: operations, default_name: str | None=None, task_id: str | None=None, session_id: str | None=None
doc:
Apply operations atomically: every touched skill is snapshotted first and any
failure rolls ALL of them back (batch-created skills are removed). ``delete`` is
only legal as the SOLE op (its recoverable-archive path doesn't compose with
rollback) and routes to the single-op handler. ``default_name`` is the legacy
top-level ``name`` fallback (staged replay).

name: _is_background_review
doc: True inside the autonomous curator review fork; False on any lookup failure.

name: mark_background_review_skill_read
doc:
Record that the active background-review fork has read a skill file. The fork must not
patch content it only inferred from the transcript: skill_view/read_file call this, and
the write guards require the mark.

name: _reset_background_review_read_marks
doc: Start a fresh, isolated read set for the current review context.

name: _resolved_roots
doc: ``(resolved skill_path, [(root, resolved_root), ...])`` over every resolvable skills root.

name: _containing_skills_root
doc: Skills root (local or external_dirs) containing ``skill_path``; local dir if none match.

name: _is_path_redirect
doc: Symlink or (Windows 3.12+) junction — either lets a poisoned tree redirect rmtree outside.

name: _validate_delete_target
doc:
Last-line guard before rmtree: even a poisoned tree must never delete (1) a path outside
every known skills root, (2) a skills root itself, (3) a symlink/junction (rmtree follows it).

``_find_skill`` already restricts ``skill_dir`` to a real ``SKILL.md`` parent discovered by walking the
skills roots, so the agent cannot inject an arbitrary path the way Kilo Code's HTTP endpoint could
(their issue 11227: a built-in-skill sentinel resolved to the server cwd and a recursive delete wiped
the user's entire working directory). This is the matching defense-in-depth for our agent-facing
``skill_manage`` delete path: even if discovery or a poisoned tree hands us a bad directory, never
recursively delete See #11227.

name: _is_pinned
doc: skill_usage pinned flag; None (logged at debug) when the record is unreadable.

name: _pinned_guard
_background_review_delete_guard
doc:
Refuse autonomous deletes of anything but curator-owned sediment. Content writes are not
gated by ownership: the review fork exists to improve every skill it learns from, and every
write is ledgered and reversible, while an archive removes a skill the user relies on.

name: _background_review_read_before_write_guard
arguments: name: str, target: Path, action: str, file_label: str
doc: Require review forks to load the exact target before mutating it.

name: _curator_consolidation_delete_guard
doc:
Fail closed on unverified deletes during the curator consolidation pass. The fork's only
legitimate delete is a consolidation declared via ``absorbed_into=<umbrella>`` (existence
validated in ``_delete_skill``); the deterministic inactivity prune never calls skill_manage,
so a bare delete here can only be the LLM pass pruning without evidence.

A delete with no forwarding target — ``absorbed_into`` omitted (``None``) or empty (``""``) — is the
fail-open behavior reported in #29912: the consolidation pass archived whole clusters of active skills
with zero verified consolidations (``consolidated_this_run == 0``), leaving active automations pointing
at names that no longer resolve. Refuse it; keep the skill active.

name: _guard_agent_created_enabled
doc: skills.guard_agent_created (default False): opt-in — terminal() runs the same code ungated.

name: _security_scan_skill
doc:
Post-write scan (opt-in); error string if blocked, else None. An "ask" verdict
(dangerous findings) is surfaced as an error so the agent can retry without them.

name: _skills_dir
doc:
Active profile's skills dir at call time (multi-profile runtimes rebind per session).
An explicitly patched module-level ``SKILLS_DIR`` (tests) wins over the live HERMES_HOME.

Long-lived multi-profile runtimes (Dashboard/TUI/Desktop backend, cron, kanban workers) import this
module once under the launch HERMES_HOME and later bind a different profile per session (#40677).

name: _skill_lock_path
doc:
Per-skill lock file under ``<skills>/.locks/`` (same idiom as the usage ledger's
``.usage.json.lock``), never inside the skill dir so delete/recreate cannot unlink it under a
waiting writer. Keyed by a digest of the basename so ``foo`` and ``category/foo`` share one
lock and no name can hit a filesystem limit (callers validate the basename first).

name: _skill_mutation_lock
doc: Exclusive lock held across one skill's whole read-modify-write; thread-re-entrant.

name: _skill_mutation_locks
doc: Every lock of an atomic batch, acquired in one stable path order (deadlock-free across batches).

name: _check_identifier
arguments: value: str, label: str, invalid: str

name: _validate_frontmatter
doc:
Validate frontmatter (name + description) and a non-empty body. ``new_skill`` (create
only) also enforces SKILL_PROMPT_DESC_LIMIT so new skills never lose routing signal to
index truncation; edit/patch skip it so existing over-limit skills stay maintainable.

name: _description_preview
doc: First 120 chars of the frontmatter description; '' on any failure.

name: _resolve_skill_dir
doc: New-skill dir; honors ``skills.create_dir`` (e.g. a shared fleet dir).

name: _read_frontmatter_name
doc:
Read a SKILL.md's frontmatter ``name:`` — the name skills_list displays.

Fail-quiet on unreadable files: the fallback lookup in ``_find_skill``
must never break the directory-name match, and an unreadable SKILL.md
simply has no second name to offer. The value is truncated with the
same ``MAX_NAME_LENGTH`` budget skills_list applies when displaying it.

name: _find_skill
doc:
Find a skill (local skills dir, then skills.external_dirs) -> ``{"path": Path}`` | None.

Accepts the bare dir name (``axolotl``; matches category-nested skills too) and the
categorized relative path (``mlops/axolotl``) — the two forms skill_view resolves. The
categorized form matches RELATIVE to the local root only (relative_to raises for external dirs).

As a last resort the frontmatter ``name:`` is matched too, so the name ``skills list``
and the dashboard display (frontmatter name wins over the directory name there)
resolves everywhere instead of failing with a misleading "not found in active
profile" error when the two names diverge. Directory-name matches keep priority —
a frontmatter match is only considered after the whole scan found no
directory/categorized match, so one skill's frontmatter cannot shadow another
skill's directory. A display name held by two or more distinct skills resolves to
nothing: like skill_view's same-tier collision refusal, refusing to guess beats
silently mutating the wrong skill; the directory name still resolves.

name: _find_skill_in_other_profiles
doc:
``(profile, skill_dir)`` pairs for OTHER profiles holding ``name`` (so the not-found
error can explain a wrong-profile mistake). Fail-quiet.

name: _skill_not_found_error
doc: Not-found error naming other profiles that hold the skill, plus ``suffix``.

name: _validate_file_path
doc: Validate a write_file/remove_file path: under an allowed subdir, no escape.

name: _resolve_supporting_file
doc:
Validate ``file_path`` and resolve it inside ``skill_dir``
-> ``(target, None)`` | ``(None, error_dict)``.

name: _locate_for_write
arguments: name: str, action: str, not_found_suffix: str=''
doc:
Find the skill; a delete also runs the background-review delete guard -> ``(skill_dir, None)``
| ``(None, error_dict)``.

name: _guarded_write
arguments: name: str, skill_dir: Path, target: Path, action: str, label: str, content: str
doc:
Read-before-write guard (existing targets only), atomic write, then the security scan;
a blocked scan restores the original (or unlinks a new file). Error dict or None.

name: _attach_lint_findings
arguments: result: dict[str, Any], skill_md: Path, before: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Attach ADVISORY authoring findings (hard rejects already ran in _validate_frontmatter).
With ``before`` (the pre-write content) only rules the write INTRODUCED are attached, so a
patch reports the line it crossed rather than re-listing the skill's standing findings.

name: _clip
arguments: text: str, n: int, ellipsis: str

name: _create_skill
arguments: name: str, content: str, category: str | None=None

name: _edit_skill
doc: Replace the SKILL.md of any existing skill (full rewrite).

name: _patch_skill
arguments: name: str, old_string: str, new_string: str, file_path: str | None=None, replace_all: bool=False
doc: Targeted find-and-replace in SKILL.md (default) or a supporting file; unique match unless replace_all.

name: _delete_skill
doc:
Delete a skill. ``absorbed_into``: None = undeclared (legacy, accepted); "" = explicit prune;
"<skill>" = absorbed into that umbrella, which must exist (so the model can't claim one).

name: _write_file
arguments: name: str, file_path: str, file_content: str
doc: Add or overwrite a supporting file within any skill directory.

name: _remove_file
doc: Remove a supporting file from any skill directory.

name: _run_write_gate
doc:
Shared write gate: None to proceed, else a JSON tool result (blocked/staged).
``build_staging(wa) -> (payload, gist)`` runs only when staging. Fails open if
write_approval cannot be imported.

name: _apply_skill_write_gate
doc: Flat-shape gate: stage the full kwargs so approval can replay them; bypassed during replay.

name: _skill_manage_from
doc: Call ``skill_manage`` with the flat-shape fields (and absorbed_into/operations) of ``payload``.

name: apply_skill_pending
doc: Replay a staged skill write, bypassing the gate (the /skills approve handler).

name: _act_patch
doc:
Two shapes: old_string/new_string = targeted replacement (validated in _patch_skill so the
tool and the helper give the same guidance); content alone = full rewrite (the old 'edit').

name: _record_success
arguments: action, name, result, *, file_path, absorbed_into, task_id, session_id, ledger_before
doc:
Best-effort post-mutation side effects (never break the tool): ledger, prompt-cache
clear, curator telemetry (which fires ``on_skill_lifecycle`` for plugins).

name: skill_manage
arguments: action: str, name: str, content: str | None=None, category: str | None=None, file_path: str | None=None, file_content: str | None=None, old_string: str | None=None, new_string: str | None=None, replace_all: bool=False, absorbed_into: str | None=None, task_id: str | None=None, session_id: str | None=None, operations=None
doc:
Dispatch to the action handler -> JSON string. ``operations`` (atomic batch shape,
see _skill_manage_batch) overrides the flat fields.

name: _op_schema
arguments: action: str, props: dict, required: tuple
doc:
One self-contained per-action op shape. ``additionalProperties: false`` is what lets a
grammar-constrained backend refuse another action's text slot outright.

name: get_current_write_origin
doc: "foreground" for any regular agent (CLI, gateway, cron, subagent); "background_review" for the review fork.

name: skill_file_lock
doc:
Exclusive cross-process lock on ``lock_path`` held across a read-modify-write cycle.
Re-entrant within one thread (a nested acquire of the same path just runs); a no-op
where neither fcntl nor msvcrt exists.

name: _usage_file_lock
doc: Serialize .usage.json read-modify-write cycles across processes.

name: _read_lines
doc: Stripped, non-empty lines of a small metadata file ([] if missing/unreadable).

name: latest_activity_at
doc: Newest use/view/patch timestamp; ``created_at`` is excluded so never-active skills stay distinguishable.

name: activity_count
doc: Total observed use+view+patch events.

name: _read_bundled_names
doc:
Built-in names: ``.bundled_manifest`` ("name:hash" per line) plus the curator suppression list, which
only ever records built-ins; a pruned built-in whose manifest entry an older sync cleaned after the
catalog dropped it is still not agent-authored (#95415). Empty if both are missing/unreadable.

name: _read_hub_installed_names
doc: Hub-installed names (``.hub/lock.json``) plus the frontmatter name of each in-tree ``install_path``.

name: _prune_builtins_enabled
doc: ``curator.prune_builtins`` (default False); lazy config import keeps this module importable during update/sync.

name: read_suppressed_names
doc: Built-ins the curator pruned (``.curator_suppressed``); the update-time re-seeder must leave these archived.

name: _toggle_suppressed_name
doc: Add (built-in pruned) or drop (restored) *skill_name* in the suppression list; no-op when unchanged.

name: _iter_skill_mds
doc:
``(frontmatter name, SKILL.md)`` under *base* minus metadata/VCS/venv/cache dirs; *local_only* also skips
external skill dirs mounted below the tree (curation must not touch them).

name: _scan_local_skills
arguments: keep: Callable[[str, Path, set[str], dict[str, Any]], bool]
doc: Sorted local skill names passing *keep(name, skill_md, bundled, usage)*; hub/protected names never reach it.

name: list_agent_created_skill_names
doc:
Curator-manageable skills: ``created_by: agent`` records plus, with ``curator.prune_builtins``, bundled
built-ins (which never carry a managed record, so the record gate applies only to local skills). Never hub.

name: list_archived_skill_names
doc: Skills in ``.archive/`` — flat layout (``archive_skill`` flattens), so dir name == skill name.

name: read_skill_name
doc: The frontmatter ``name:`` field of a SKILL.md (first 4000 chars), else *fallback*.

name: is_agent_created
doc: Neither bundled nor hub-installed (and not only present in an external dir).

name: is_curation_eligible
doc:
Agent-created: yes. Bundled: only with ``curator.prune_builtins``. Hub / external-dir / protected built-ins:
never (external owner).

name: _is_curator_managed_record
doc:
``created_by`` is a curator-management OPT-IN flag, not proof of authorship (``curator adopt`` flips it);
the key name is kept because it lives in every user's ``.usage.json``.

NAMING (issue #67140): the on-disk field is ``created_by``, which reads like provenance but is consumed
as a **curator-management opt-in policy flag**. The two are not the same question:

name: list_unmanaged_skill_names
doc:
Curation-ELIGIBLE skills without a provenance marker (pre-``created_by`` records, or foreground creates that
belong to the user). Invisible to ``curated_report()`` and auto transitions; only ``curator adopt`` hands
them over — provenance is declared, never inferred from activity.

name: unmanaged_report
doc:
Rows for :func:`list_unmanaged_skill_names`; ``has_provenance_key`` (False = pre-dates ``created_by``) explains
WHY, it is not a signal to adopt on.

name: adopt_skill
doc:
User-declared handover: writes the ``created_by: agent`` marker (inactivity clock NOT reset). Refuses hub,
external, bundled and protected skills. Returns (ok, message).

name: _backfilled
doc: *rec* with every missing default key appended (a fresh record when not a dict).

name: load_usage
doc: The whole .usage.json map (non-dict values dropped); {} on missing/corrupt.

name: save_usage
doc: Write the usage map atomically; True when it committed.

name: get_record
doc: The (backfilled) record for *skill_name*; fresh defaults if missing.

name: _locked_update
arguments: skill_name: str, op: Callable[[dict[str, dict[str, Any]]], tuple[Any, bool]], fail_log: str, guard: Optional[Callable[[], bool]]=None
doc:
*op(data) -> (result, dirty)* under the file lock, saving only when dirty; *guard* runs before locking.
None when the guard failed, the save did not land, or anything raised (DEBUG-logged via *fail_log*).

name: seed_record_if_missing
doc: Baseline record for a curation-eligible skill so its inactivity clock starts at first sight, not epoch.

name: reanchor_clock
doc:
Start a skill's inactivity clock NOW, once. Telemetry writes a record the moment a bundled skill is
seeded, so by the curator's first sight ``created_at`` can be months old and every never-used built-in
goes stale on that first pass (#79295); ``first_seen_at`` marks the clock as anchored so later runs age
it normally. A record the bug already marked stale is reactivated — the staleness was the artifact.

name: _mutate
doc:
Load, apply *mutator(record)* in place, save; the mutator result (None if nothing landed). Telemetry is
recorded for ANY skill; lifecycle mutators pass ``require_curation_eligible=True`` (never write onto unmanaged).

name: _set_field
arguments: skill_name: str, key: str, value: Any
doc: Curation-gated single-field write; True only when the write landed.

name: _bump
arguments: rec: dict[str, Any], count_key: str, ts_key: str

name: telemetry_provenance
doc: Bounded provenance label for shared skill metrics.

name: _emit_skill_lifecycle
arguments: skill_name: str, action: str, *, record: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None, task_id: Optional[str]=None, session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc: Best-effort lifecycle hook after an authoritative state change; facts absent from *record* go as None.

name: _mutate_and_emit
arguments: skill_name: str, action: str, mutator: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, Any]], **hook_kwargs: Any
doc: ``_mutate`` then emit *action* with the mutator's facts as the record — only if the write landed.

name: bump_use
arguments: skill_name: str, *, task_id: Optional[str]=None, session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc: Skill actively used (loaded into the prompt path / referenced from an assistant turn).

name: bump_patch
arguments: skill_name: str, *, action: str='patch', task_id: Optional[str]=None, session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc: Called from skill_manage (patch/edit).

name: record_created
arguments: skill_name: str, *, agent_created: bool, task_id: Optional[str]=None, session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Persist creation provenance and emit a create fact; the record is reset (a create is a new logical skill).

Foreground creates (``agent_created=False`` — e.g. ``/learn`` at the user's request) are stamped
``created_by="learn"``: a learning-signal marker, NOT the curator-management opt-in (``"agent"``),
so /journey can show user-taught skills without handing them to autonomous curation.

name: record_installed
doc: Record a successful Skills Hub install without exporting its name.

name: mark_agent_created
doc: Opt a skill into curator management — the only thing that makes it eligible for automatic curation.

name: set_state
doc: Set lifecycle state (no-op if invalid / unmanageable). Emits archived/stale/restored; active<-stale is silent.

name: set_pinned
doc:
False when the write did not land (not curation-eligible).

(skill not curation-eligible), True on success — so callers can report failure instead of a false
success (issue #92993).

name: _relocate
arguments: src: Path, dest: Path, skill_name: str, action: str, **capture_kwargs: Any
doc:
Move *src* to *dest* for *action* ("archive" | "restore") inside a best-effort audit-ledger entry, then apply
suppression + state side effects; rename falls back to shutil.move across devices.

name: archive_skill
doc:
Move a curator-eligible skill dir to ``.archive/`` (flattened; timestamp suffix on collision). Never hub;
bundled built-ins only with ``curator.prune_builtins`` (and then suppressed from re-seeding).

name: restore_skill
doc:
Move an archived skill back to the flat layout (nesting NOT reconstructed). Refuses a name now colliding with
a hub skill, or a bundled built-in unless ``curator.prune_builtins`` is on (restoring lifts a prune).

name: _find_skill_dir
doc: Skill dir by frontmatter ``name`` (flat or nested).

name: _find_external_skill_dir
doc: Skill dir under configured external dirs by frontmatter name.

name: curated_report
doc:
One backfilled row per curator-managed skill with ``provenance`` and ``_persisted`` (real record exists; fresh
backfills get their inactivity clock seeded instead of counting as ancient).

name: is_external_only
doc:
Present under ``skills.external_dirs`` and NOT in the local store (the local copy wins on
name clashes, mirroring ``is_agent_created``'s external exclusion). An external-only skill is
externally authored: it was mounted, not learned.

name: _external_skill_names
doc:
Frontmatter names of all skills under configured external dirs (one scan per call; the
router's set-based provenance uses this instead of a per-skill dir lookup).

name: provenance
doc:
'hub' | 'bundled' | 'external' | 'agent'.

'external' covers skills mounted from ``skills.external_dirs`` and absent from the local
store — externally authored, not learned from the user (#108032). 'agent' keeps covering
agent-authored AND local hand-made skills — the ones the user may edit/delete from the UI
(external skills stay foreground-editable in place by design, commit 8c8fc6c1ec; the label
split is about origin, not mutability).

name: usage_report
doc: Usage rows for EVERY skill on disk (built-ins and hub included); ``curated_report()`` is the managed subset.

name: register
arguments: session_key: str, confirm_id: str, command: str, handler: Callable[[str], Awaitable[Optional[str]]]
doc: Register a pending confirm, superseding any prior one for the session.

name: get_pending
doc: Return a copy of the pending confirm dict for a session, or None.

name: clear
doc: Drop the pending confirm for ``session_key`` without running it.

name: clear_if_stale
doc: Drop the pending confirm if older than ``timeout`` seconds; True if dropped.

name: resolve
arguments: session_key: str, confirm_id: str, choice: str, timeout: float=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
doc:
Run the pending handler with ``choice`` ("once" / "always" / "cancel").

Returns the handler's output string, or None if the confirm was stale, already resolved,
or the confirm_id doesn't match (superseded prompt).

name: ensure_spill_dir
doc:
Create ``path`` (and parents) as a directory, refusing symlinks. ``private=True``
creates the leaf ``0o700`` and tightens an existing leaf. Raises ``OSError`` if the leaf
is not a real directory.

name: open_exclusive
arguments: path: Path, *, private: bool=True, overwrite: bool=False, encoding: str='utf-8', errors: str='strict'
doc:
Open ``path`` for writing via exclusive create; never follows a link. ``overwrite=True``
first unlinks an existing path (``lstat``-checked, so only the link itself is removed and
directories are refused), then creates exclusively — the overwrite path cannot be
redirected through a symlink either.

name: write_text_exclusive
arguments: path: Path, text: str, *, private: bool=True, overwrite: bool=False, encoding: str='utf-8', errors: str='strict'
doc: ``Path.write_text`` equivalent that refuses to follow symlinks.

name: warm_stt_provider
doc:
Pre-load the configured STT engine so the next transcription starts hot.

Blocking; never raises. Only the ``local`` (faster-whisper) provider has
anything resident: it fills the same cache slot ``_transcribe_local``
reads (including first-use download and lazy install). ``local_command``
shells out to an external binary and cloud providers are remote, so both
are ``action: "noop"``. The result carries ``provider`` / ``warmed`` /
``action`` / ``error``.

name: acquire_stt_lease
doc:
Register ``lease`` (e.g. ``"desktop:voice-input:abcd1234"``) and warm the engine.

Re-acquiring is idempotent but still re-warms (cheap on a cache hit; heals
a cache the idle-unload watcher cleared meanwhile).

name: release_stt_lease
doc:
Drop ``lease``. A never-acquired lease is a no-op (still reports the
holder count) so surfaces can call this unconditionally. Never unloads the
model — see the module docstring for why this diverges from TTS leases.

name: stt_lease_holders
doc: Snapshot of live lease names (diagnostics / tests).

name: _run_git
arguments: args, cwd: str, timeout: int=_GIT_TIMEOUT, env=None
doc:
Run git capturing output; never raises on non-zero exit.

:func:`noninteractive_git_env` (GHSA-7x36-8jrh-v4pw): this runs unattended against whatever
repo the parent sits in and ``worktree add`` runs hooks, so a malicious ``.git/config`` must
not execute.

name: local_backend_active
doc: True when the terminal backend is local (worktrees visible to tools).

name: resolve_repo_root
doc: Return the git toplevel for *path*, or None when not in a work tree.

name: _ensure_gitignore_entry
doc: Best-effort: keep ``.worktrees/`` out of git status.

name: create_subagent_worktree
doc: Create an isolated worktree for one child; None (silent downgrade) outside git/on failure.

name: _base_payload
doc: Result-entry schema the parent expects (no creation-side internals).

name: mark_worktree_payload_unproven
arguments: payload: dict[str, Any], reason: str, *, unmeasured: str='commits/dirty'
doc:
Flag a worktree result payload as un-inspected, in place.

The parent only sees this dict, so the uncertainty must travel in it or "0 commits, clean"
reads as "the child produced nothing". *unmeasured* names only the fields actually left
unproven (one probe can succeed while the other fails).

See #88113.

name: unproven_worktree_payload
doc: Complete un-inspected payload for ``delegate_tool`` when finalize raises.

name: finalize_subagent_worktree
doc:
Inspect (and possibly prune) a child worktree after the child finishes.

Prunes only when *prune*, commits==0, clean tree AND both git probes succeeded; otherwise
keeps it with ``inspection_failed`` + ``note`` (``commits``/``dirty`` then are defaults).

name: _archive_finished_worktree
arguments: info: dict[str, str], payload: dict[str, Any]
doc:
A finished child left commits or edits: snapshot them, then remove the tree.

The branch is kept (the parent reviews and merges it); the archive also covers uncommitted
edits. ``worktrees.archive_dirty: false`` or a failed snapshot keeps the tree as before.

name: build_worktree_context_note
doc: Context block telling the child to work inside its isolated worktree.

name: _regex_hint
arguments: pattern: str, message: str | Callable[[str], str], flags: int=0
doc: Hint firing when ``pattern`` matches; ``{0}`` = first group, or ``message(group1)``.

name: _first_token
doc: Basename of the command head, skipping leading env-var assignments.

name: annotate_masked_success
doc: Warning note when an exit-0 result likely masks a failure (caller gates on exit 0).

name: annotate_failure
arguments: command: str, exit_code: int, output: str
doc: Return one short recovery hint for a failed command, or None (exit 0).

name: set_terminal_scope
doc: Install *mapping* as the current context's terminal policy.

name: get_terminal_scope
doc: The active scope mapping/refusal, or ``None`` when no scope is bound.

name: enforce_no_refusal
doc:
Raise when the active scope is a refusal scope (fail closed).

Execution paths (terminal tool, execute_code) call this before spawning anything: under a refusal scope
the profile's terminal policy could not be resolved, and running with the launch process's ambient
policy is exactly the authority leak this module closes (#68559 requires refusal, not fallback).
Non-scoped and policy-scoped contexts pass silently.

name: terminal_env
doc:
Authoritative read of a ``TERMINAL_*`` variable.

No scope: process env, then *default*. Refusal scope: raise. Policy scope: ONLY the
policy; a missing key yields *default*, never os.environ.

name: _apply_terminal_mapping
arguments: scope: dict[str, str], mapping: dict[str, Any]

name: default_terminal_scope
doc:
Code-default ``TERMINAL_*`` policy: what a profile-bypassing session freezes instead of
reading ``.env``/``config.yaml``. Total like the profile projection, minus the profile.

name: build_profile_terminal_scope
doc:
Build the COMPLETE effective ``TERMINAL_*`` policy for a profile home.

Projection: ``DEFAULT_CONFIG['terminal']`` <- profile ``.env`` TERMINAL_* <- *env_overlay*
<- profile ``config.yaml`` ``terminal:``. Total by construction, so a bound scope never
widens back to ambient authority. Raises :class:`TerminalPolicyUnavailable` if a present
file is unreadable.

*env_overlay* is a TRUSTED ``TERMINAL_*`` mapping captured from the launch process before
multiplexing began (``tui_gateway/launch_profile_policy.py``): the launch profile's
env-only policy (``TERMINAL_ENV=ssh`` from systemd, ``op run``, a launcher bridge) has no
file to rebuild it from, and reading live ``os.environ`` here is the leak this module
closes. It sits where the process env sits in the standalone bridge — explicit YAML keys
still win (``apply_terminal_config_to_env``).

name: _resolve_scope_cwd_placeholder
doc:
Give a scope with no explicit ``terminal.cwd`` the same resolved ``TERMINAL_CWD`` a standalone
gateway computes at import (``gateway/run.py``: local backend → ``$HOME``; docker with the
workspace mount → the host cwd signal; other backends → unset). Without it a routed turn's
``resolve_agent_cwd()`` falls back to the multiplexer PROCESS cwd (wherever ``hermes gateway``
was launched), so the system prompt, context-file discovery and the local terminal all run in
a directory the profile's standalone gateway would never have used.

name: install_profile_terminal_scope
doc: Build AND install a profile's policy; on failure install the refusal scope. Never raises.

name: install_and_reset_profile_terminal_scope
doc: Install the profile's terminal policy for a bounded turn/fire. Never raises.

name: _redact_terminal_error_text
doc: Force-redact text before serializing a terminal error envelope.

name: _safe_parse_import_env
arguments: name: str, default: Any, converter, type_label: str
doc:
Parse a module-level numeric env var; a malformed value must never make
the module unloadable at import time (CLI, ACP, tests, tool discovery).

name: set_sudo_password_callback
doc: Register the CLI's sudo password prompt callback (per-thread slot).

name: set_approval_callback
doc: Register the dangerous-command approval prompt callback (per-thread slot).

name: _current_session_key
doc:
Active gateway/WebUI session key, or "" outside sessions (ContextVar with
the ``get_session_env`` os.environ fallback for CLI/cron/tests).

name: _current_session_profile
doc:
Active session's Hermes profile name, or "" (same lookup discipline as
:func:`_current_session_key`).

name: _container_profile
doc:
Profile whose persistent container a session-bound command uses: the bound home's profile when it is not
the session's own (a profile-routed subagent runs in its target's home while the session, and the delivery
identity HERMES_SESSION_PROFILE carries, stay the parent's; that target may be the launch profile, reached
from a routed profile's chat), else the session's. A session with no profile name is the launch profile's,
so the launch home's own work keeps the session's key whatever the launch profile is named.

name: _docker_volume_uses_host_path
doc: Return True when a docker volume spec bind-mounts a host path.

name: _docker_has_host_access
doc: Return True when a Docker sandbox exposes host paths through bind mounts.

name: _check_all_guards
arguments: command: str, env_type: str, has_host_access: bool=False
doc: Delegate to the consolidated command guard with the CLI callback.

name: _maybe_reap_docker_orphans
doc:
Run the docker orphan reaper once per process, if enabled.

Sweeps Exited containers labeled ``hermes-agent=1`` for the current
profile — leftovers of Hermes processes that died without firing
``atexit`` (SIGKILL, OOM, closed terminal). Conservative: only containers
older than ``2 × lifetime_seconds``, profile-scoped. Gates:
``terminal.docker_orphan_reaper: false`` (operator opt-out, e.g. several
Hermes processes sharing a profile) and the once-per-interpreter flag so
parallel subagent / RL-rollout calls don't re-sweep.

name: record_session_cwd
doc:
Record *cwd* as *session_key*'s working directory (after a completed
command, or on workspace-override registration). None/empty keys collapse
to ``"default"``; non-string / empty cwds are ignored. Keys are routed-profile
qualified (:func:`_qualify_task_key`); the read/clear side qualifies identically.

name: get_session_cwd
doc:
Recorded cwd for *session_key*, or None. No fallback chain on purpose:
callers decide what an absent record means. None/empty keys read ``"default"``.

name: clear_session_cwd
doc: Drop a session's cwd record (session teardown).

name: _sanitize_cwd_for_live_env
doc:
Cwd to write into a LIVE cached env, or None to leave it untouched.

On container backends a raw host path (a desktop/TUI session registering its
workspace, e.g. ``C:\Users\me`` or ``/Users/me/workspace``) cannot be the
in-sandbox workdir: every file-tools ``_exec`` wrapper does
``builtin cd -- <env.cwd> || exit 126``, so a host cwd poisons all later
file operations with an unrelated ``cd:`` error. Prefix-shaped host paths
are already rejected on the creation paths. This write classifies the
directory mounted at ``/workspace`` as unusable before that prefix
heuristic, then remaps the match (or a child of it) to its container mount
instead of storing the host path. SSH maps the Hermes subprocess home onto
the peer's home, as environment creation already does. Other backends apply
the override verbatim (ACP project-root switching must keep working).

name: register_task_env_overrides
doc:
Register per-task sandbox overrides (``docker_image``/``modal_image``/
``daytona_image`` or a plugin backend's ``<backend>_image``, ``env_type``,
``cwd``) before the agent loop runs.

A ``cwd`` override takes effect immediately: it becomes the session's
recorded cwd (until a ``cd`` changes it) and any live env's cwd is updated
too, so env-side seeding stays consistent (ACP switching project root
mid-session via ``session/load``). The session record keeps the RAW path
(host workspaces are tracked there on purpose); only the live-env write is
sanitized, since a host cwd can never be a container workdir.

Keyed like ``_session_cwd`` — routed-profile qualified (:func:`_qualify_task_key`) — so two
profiles registering the same task id never read each other's image/cwd (#123989).

name: clear_task_env_overrides
doc: Drop a task's overrides, cwd record and container alias (rollout cleanup).

name: register_container_alias
doc:
Make *child_task_id* resolve to *parent_task_id*'s container (called at
delegate_task spawn). A missing parent id aliases to ``"default"``.

name: _resolve_container_alias
doc: Follow the child→parent alias chain (cycle-safe) for *task_id*.

name: _is_isolation_override_key
doc: An image (``docker_image``, a plugin backend's ``<backend>_image``) or ``env_type`` override.

name: _has_isolation_overrides
doc:
True when *task_id* registered image/env_type overrides — the single
"isolated RL/benchmark rollout" predicate shared by key resolution and
container creation so the two can't drift.

name: _session_scope
doc: Bridge config → env once, then snapshot the backend scope for this call.

name: _docker_session_isolation_enabled
doc: See :attr:`_SessionScope.docker_session_isolated` (used by the docker builder).

name: _routed_home_task_key
doc:
Key for a session-less task serving a routed (non-launch) profile home, else None.

A multiplexed host runs every profile's cron jobs without a session key; collapsing them all onto
``"default"`` made profile B's cron tool calls reuse the environment the launch profile's job
created (its ``.env`` residue, its bridged ``TERMINAL_*``, its shell), so B ran with A's settings.
