doc:
Run a driver verb and parse its stdout as a JSON object; None on spawn failure, empty stdout (older drivers
print usage to stderr), unparseable or non-object output, or a non-zero exit.

name: _json_object
doc: ``json.loads`` that yields a dict or None (unparseable / non-object).

name: _valid_mcp_args
doc: ``mcp_invocation.args`` when it is a list of strings (possibly empty), else None.

name: _wsl_windows_path_to_posix
doc:
Translate a Windows absolute manifest command to its DrvFS ``/mnt/<drive>/...`` form when Hermes runs in WSL
(a Windows cua-driver manifest can report ``C:\...`` while Hermes spawns via POSIX). Non-Windows paths and
non-WSL hosts are returned unchanged.

name: resolve_cua_driver_cmd
doc: Read PM's selected binary without installing; never replace an explicit override.

name: cua_driver_binary_available
doc: True if PM or an explicit override selects a local driver.

name: _mcp_args_with_overlay_flag
doc: Return *args* with ``--no-overlay`` appended when configured and supported.

name: _cua_driver_supports_no_overlay
doc:
True if ``<driver> --help`` mentions ``--no-overlay`` (probed once); older drivers reject unknown flags, which
would crash the MCP spawn.

name: _resolve_mcp_invocation
doc:
``(command, args)`` that spawn cua-driver's stdio MCP server, asked of the driver itself via ``cua-driver
manifest`` (``mcp_invocation``) so a subcommand rename keeps working. Falls back to ``(driver_cmd, ["mcp"])``
on older drivers or any discovery failure — the wrapper must not refuse to start over a failed discovery hop.
``--no-overlay`` appended when allowed.

Surface 8 of NousResearch/hermes-agent#47072: instead of hardcoding ``["mcp"]`` we ask the driver itself
via ``cua-driver manifest`` (trycua/cua#1961). The manifest carries a stable ``mcp_invocation`` pointer
with both ``command`` and ``args``, so a future cua-driver that renames or relocates the subcommand
keeps working without a Hermes patch.
When ``computer_use.no_overlay`` is enabled (or auto-detected — macOS, headless/WSL2/X11 Linux),
``--no-overlay`` is appended to suppress the cursor overlay rendering loop that can consume CPU
indefinitely when idle (#28152, #47032). Older drivers that don't recognise the flag will reject it;
callers should fall back to the no-overlay invocation on spawn failure.

name: _manifest_contract_reason
doc:
Why a parsed manifest fails the 0.20 contract, or ``""`` when it passes (version floor, MCP launch
command, then the ``"<verb> <flag>"`` entries the advertised subcommands lack).

name: cua_driver_runtime_contract_status
doc: Report whether a local driver can host Hermes' 0.20 integration.

name: cua_driver_update_check
doc: Historical import: upstream release polling is retired; PM owns the pin.

name: _target_args
doc: ``(refusal, base args)`` for an input action against the sticky target.

name: _pointer_args
arguments: self, tool: str, args: dict[str, Any], variants: Sequence[_Variant], missing_msg: Optional[str]
doc:
Fill *args* from the first supplied addressing variant (element or coordinates) plus ``window_id``; refuse
when the target has a pid but no window_id yet. No variant -> refuse with *missing_msg* (None = bare window).

name: _apply_delivery
arguments: self, action: str, args: dict[str, Any], delivery_mode: Optional[str]
doc:
Attach delivery_mode to an input-action args dict. Background is the default and needs no flag.
Foreground is only sent when the live action schema accepts it; on an older driver we refuse with
``foreground_unsupported`` instead of silently downgrading to background (which would land input
where the model didn't expect).

Returns an ActionResult to short-circuit on refusal, or None to proceed. See
NousResearch/hermes-agent#67052 phase B.

name: _run_input_action
arguments: self, action: str, args: dict[str, Any], delivery_mode: Optional[str], bring_to_front: bool
doc:
Apply one delivery rung, optionally focusing via its own tool. ``bring_to_front`` is never an
input-action property: when requested, the separately approved standalone focus action runs first,
then the original foreground input runs unchanged.

name: click
arguments: self, *, element: Optional[int]=None, x: Optional[int]=None, y: Optional[int]=None, button: str='left', click_count: int=1, modifiers: Optional[list[str]]=None, delivery_mode: Optional[str]=None, bring_to_front: bool=False

name: drag
arguments: self, *, from_element: Optional[int]=None, to_element: Optional[int]=None, from_xy: Optional[tuple[int, int]]=None, to_xy: Optional[tuple[int, int]]=None, button: str='left', modifiers: Optional[list[str]]=None, delivery_mode: Optional[str]=None, bring_to_front: bool=False

name: scroll
arguments: self, *, direction: str, amount: int=3, element: Optional[int]=None, x: Optional[int]=None, y: Optional[int]=None, modifiers: Optional[list[str]]=None, delivery_mode: Optional[str]=None, bring_to_front: bool=False

name: type_text
arguments: self, text: str, *, delivery_mode: Optional[str]=None, bring_to_front: bool=False

name: key
arguments: self, keys: str, *, delivery_mode: Optional[str]=None, bring_to_front: bool=False

name: set_value
doc: Set a value on an element. Handles AXPopUpButton selects natively.

name: _mcp_field
arguments: obj, snake: str, camel: str, default=None
doc:
Read an MCP model field across the 1.x -> 2.x rename: mcp 2.0 exposes snake_case attributes and keeps
camelCase only as a serialization alias, so ``getattr(result, "isError", False)`` is False for every 2.x result
and a denied call looks like success. Deliberately duplicated from ``tools.mcp_tool.mcp_field`` so computer_use
never loads the much larger config-driven MCP client module.

name: _action_result_from
arguments: name: str, ok: bool, message: str, meta: dict[str, Any], structured: dict[str, Any], *, requested_delivery: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Build an ActionResult, lifting cua-driver's structured verdict. structuredContent is canonical, the flattened
``meta`` copy the fallback. Every structured field is additive: a driver that omits one leaves the attribute
``None`` so old drivers see unchanged behavior.

See the action response shape in cua-driver's mcp-tool-notes and NousResearch/hermes-agent#67052.

name: _z_index_uninformative
doc: True when every window shares the same z_index (common on Linux/X11).

name: _parse_xprop_net_active_window
doc:
Parse ``xprop -root _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW`` stdout into a window id: the ``window id # 0x...`` form, falling
back to the first hex token.

name: _is_real_app_window
doc: Return False for desktop/shell helper windows that capture as empty.

name: _parse_elements_from_tree
doc:
Parse UIElements from get_window_state AX-tree markdown — last-resort fallback for drivers without
``structuredContent.elements``. Bounds are always ``(0, 0, 0, 0)`` (the markdown carries none), fine for
element-index clicks since the driver resolves the frame.

Last-resort fallback for cua-driver builds that don't carry the canonical ``structuredContent.elements``
array (see ``_parse_elements_from_structured`` — Surface 2 of #47072 prefers that path).

name: _parse_elements_from_structured
doc:
Read the canonical ``structuredContent.elements`` array: ``element_index``, ``role``, ``label`` and, when
AT-SPI / AXFrame returned usable bounds, ``frame`` ``{x, y, w, h}`` — so real pixel bounds survive (the
markdown path loses them). Malformed entries are skipped.

Surface 2 of NousResearch/hermes-agent#47072: read the canonical ``structuredContent.elements`` array
cua-driver-rs emits on every ``get_window_state`` response (trycua/cua#1961).

name: _image_dimensions_from_bytes
doc: Best-effort PNG/JPEG dimension sniff; ``(0, 0)`` when unreadable or non-positive.

name: _split_tree_text
doc: Split get_window_state text into (summary_line, tree_markdown).

name: _parse_key_combo
doc: Parse 'cmd+s' / 'ctrl-alt-t' into (key, modifiers); last non-modifier wins.

name: _tool_envelope
arguments: data: Any, images: list[str], structured: Any, is_error: bool, image_mime_types: Optional[list[str]]=None
doc:
The normalised tool-result dict every transport emits: ``{data, images, [image_mime_types,] structuredContent,
isError}``. ``image_mime_types`` is only present when the transport can report it (MCP image parts).

name: _extract_tool_result
doc:
Flatten an mcp CallToolResult into ``{data, images, image_mime_types, structuredContent, isError}``. ``data``
is the joined text parts (parsed as JSON when it looks like JSON); ``image_mime_types`` is parallel to
``images`` with ``""`` where the part carried no mimeType (older drivers — callers then sniff the base64 prefix).

`image_mime_types` is the explicit `mimeType` cua-driver emits on every image part as of trycua/cua#1961
(Surface 7 of NousResearch/hermes-agent#47072). Each entry corresponds index-for-index with `images`; an
empty string entry signals the part carried no mimeType (older cua-driver build), and the caller should
fall back to base64-prefix sniffing.

name: _image_from_tool_result
_int_or_none
doc: ``int(value)`` for int/numeric-str inputs; None for bools, other types and malformed strings.

name: _positive_int
doc: Return a positive integer, rejecting booleans and malformed values.

name: _is_placeholder_id
doc:
True when *value* is a schema-filler id (``0`` / negative) rather than a target: some providers zero-fill
every optional integer, and treating that as targeting would drop the caller's ``app=``. Non-numeric values
are NOT placeholders — they still reach validation.

name: _ingest_windows
doc:
Normalise cua-driver ``list_windows`` entries, dropping unusable ones. Every downstream call needs integer
``pid`` and ``window_id``; on X11 the PID comes from the optional ``_NET_WM_PID`` property, so root/panel/popup
windows report ``pid: null`` — skip those instead of aborting the enumeration. ``z_index``: higher = closer to
front; Wayland's null (undefined stacking) sorts lowest so real windows stay above the desktop.

name: _windows_from_tool_result
doc:
Return list_windows payloads across cua-driver result shapes: structuredContent.windows, then ``windows`` /
``_legacy_windows`` in the text payload, then on the envelope itself.

name: _outcome_unknown
arguments: name: str, exc: Exception, code: str
doc: Fail-closed ``isError`` result for *code* (see ``_UNKNOWN_OUTCOME_MESSAGES``).

name: _tool_field
doc: ``_mcp_field`` plus the ``model_extra`` fallback some MCP SDKs (Pydantic v2) forward custom fields via.

name: _cli_run_json
arguments: cmd: list[str], env: dict[str, str], name: str, timeout: float
doc:
Run ``cua-driver call`` with backoff until it prints JSON; return the parsed value. "daemon is not running"
is PERMANENT for this invocation (the CLI needs the machine-wide daemon socket, which Linux installs typically
never start) -> fail fast, no ~3.5s backoff.

name: _cli_result
doc: Remap a ``cua-driver call`` JSON body into the ``_extract_tool_result`` shape (no ``image_mime_types`` key).

name: _logical_error_text
doc: Flatten a logical MCP error into text for narrow classification.

name: _is_ended_session_result
doc: Recognise cua-driver's explicit recoverable ended-session result.

name: _lifecycle_coro
doc: Owns the stdio MCP contexts: open, signal ready, block on shutdown, clean up — all in one task.

name: _populate_capabilities
doc:
Cache per-tool capability sets, input schemas and capability_version from tools/list. Soft
prerequisite: on failure the map stays empty (capability False).

name: _start_lifecycle_locked
doc: Spawn the lifecycle owner and wait for ready. Caller holds self._lock.

name: set_transport_reset_callback
doc: Register a synchronous cache invalidation hook for transport swaps.

name: _signal_shutdown_locked
doc: Set the asyncio shutdown event from the caller's thread.

arguments: self, name: str, args: dict[str, Any]

doc:
Driver advertises *capability* for *tool* (or ANY tool). False before start.

capability token (trycua/cua#1961 capability vocabulary).

name: _has_tool
doc:
``tools/list`` advertised *name*. Routes capture() (PNG capture moved into ``get_window_state``).
False before discovery — callers treat that as "unknown".

name: supports_input_property
doc: Live tools/list schema accepts *property_name* (fails closed; no version guessing).

name: capabilities_discovered
doc: tools/list populated the map; when False ``_has_tool`` is untrustworthy.

name: capability_version
doc: Driver-advertised capability vocabulary version ("" on old builds).

name: _is_closed_session_error
doc: True for MCP/stdio failures that are recoverable by reconnecting.

name: _is_transient_daemon_error
doc:
Daemon-proxy EAGAIN congestion: on macOS the ``cua-driver mcp`` bridge uses a non-blocking unix socket
and heavy ops (``get_window_state``) fail with ``os error 35`` when its buffer is full. A retry succeeds,
so back off / fall back instead of surfacing an empty 0x0 capture.

name: _redeclare_session
doc: start_session with the declared id; log *failure_msg* and return False on rejection.

name: _recreate_session
arguments: self, name: str, timeout: float, log_msg: str, *, restart: bool=True, clear_timeout_suspect: bool=False

name: _call_tool_via_cli
arguments: self, name: str, args: dict[str, Any], timeout: float
doc:
Fallback transport: ``cua-driver call <tool> <json>`` subprocess. The MCP stdio bridge can persistently
fail heavy calls (``get_window_state``) with EAGAIN while the plain CLI, on its own daemon socket, keeps
working. Output is remapped to the ``_extract_tool_result`` shape. ``get_window_state`` routes its
screenshot to a temp file (``screenshot_out_file``) so the daemon returns a tiny JSON body, not the
multi-megabyte base64 blob that congests the socket; ``_cli_result`` reads it back.

name: call_tool
arguments: self, name: str, args: dict[str, Any], timeout: float=30.0

name: _run_cli
doc: Run ``<binary> args`` with UTF-8 capture + sanitized env (raises on failure).

name: _cli_text
arguments: binary: str, *args: str, timeout: float, exc_types: tuple[type, ...]=_IO_EXC
doc: ``_run_cli`` that returns (not raises) any exception in *exc_types*.

name: _read_cli_version
doc: First line of ``--version`` or None; health_report's ``driver_version`` can disagree (seen on Windows).

name: _cli_driver_version
doc: (status, version_or_message) from ``cua-driver --version``.

name: _cli_doctor_snippet
doc: Optional one-shot ``cua-driver doctor`` text (best-effort, never fatal).

name: _build_identity
doc: Hermes-side identity block comparing resolved binary vs health_report.

name: _extract_health_report_from_result
doc:
Report from a tools/call result. ``HealthReportUnavailable`` when the tool denied the call (isError) or the
payload is not a real report (0.10's ``{"exit_code": 1}``); ``RuntimeError`` when it carries no content.

name: _open_mcp
doc: Spawn ``<binary> mcp``; pin UTF-8 — cua-driver emits emoji/arbitrary paths and Windows' cp1252 would raise.

significant_calls.expression:
subprocess.Popen([binary, "mcp"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                            text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", bufsize=1, creationflags=windows_hide_flags(),
                            env=_sanitized_cua_env())

name: _mcp_rpc
arguments: proc: subprocess.Popen, msg_id: int, method: str, params: Any=None
doc: Write one JSON-RPC request and read one response line.

name: _call_tool
arguments: proc: subprocess.Popen, msg_id: int, name: str, arguments: Any=None
doc: tools/call *name* → raw ``result`` value (``{}`` when absent).

name: _mcp_session
doc: Spawn ``<binary> mcp`` and always close stdin / wait / kill it on exit.

name: _drive_health_report
arguments: binary: str, *, include: Sequence[str]=(), skip: Sequence[str]=(), timeout: float=12.0
doc: Handshake + `health_report` → report; HealthReportUnavailable (caller falls back) or RuntimeError.

name: _probe_tool
arguments: proc: subprocess.Popen, msg_id: int, name: str
doc: ``(result, None)`` on success; ``(None, error_text)`` on isError or RPC failure.

name: _drive_fallback_probes
doc: One MCP session: initialize serverInfo version + check_permissions + list_apps probe results.

name: _tcc_row
arguments: field: str, label: str, platform_bound: bool, ctx: Report
doc: tcc_* row for one check_permissions boolean *field* (Accessibility / Screen Recording).

name: _ax_capability_row
doc: ax_capability — inferred from list_apps success or the accessibility grant.

name: _overall_from
doc: failed if binary missing/bad; ok if accessibility fine and nothing failed; else degraded.

name: _compose_fallback_report
arguments: binary: str, *, reason: str='', timeout: float=12.0
doc: schema_version=1 report from CLI + MCP probes (``_FALLBACK_PROBES``) when health_report is denied (0.10).

name: _apply_stale_tcc_guard
doc:
Append the stale-row recovery to every failed ``tcc_*`` check. Applied at the report seam so the driver's
own health_report rows (0.22+) get it too, not only the 0.10 fallback probes — the users hit by a stale row
are on current drivers (trycua/cua#3170).

name: _apply_display_count_guard
doc:
Fail an 'ok' screen_capture_capability with ``display_count=0``: macOS ScreenCaptureKit reports 0 on headless
/ asleep panels — TCC fine, health_report ok, yet every capture is 0x0. Turns a silent failure actionable; applied
at the report seam so the real and the fallback path both get it.

Composed from PR #52949 (sujeet111) and PR #67259 (webtecnica).

name: cua_daemon_units
doc:
(kind, unit, exec_target, runs_serve, --socket path or None) for every systemd user unit / XDG autostart
entry whose Exec runs cua-driver — the hand-written daemon units Linux relies on (there is no managed
autostart). ``%h`` is expanded in the socket path so it can be probed; the exec target is left as written.

name: _stale_cua_exec_references
doc:
(kind, unit, target) for daemon units whose cua-driver Exec points at a pruned ``packages/releases/<version>/``
directory. The installer prunes all but the last five, so a versioned reference crash-loops with 203/EXEC after
every upgrade while every binary-level check stays green (#114748). ``packages/current`` and still-present
release dirs are healthy by construction and never reported.

name: _apply_daemon_liveness_guard
doc:
Append one check per configured daemon unit whose ``cua-driver serve`` is not answering on its socket
(pass when it is). Only configured daemons are probed: on Linux the MCP runtime needs no daemon, so an
unconfigured, silent socket is not a finding. Unknown probe results add nothing (#114748).

name: _apply_stale_unit_guard
doc:
Append a fail check per hand-written unit/autostart entry whose cua-driver Exec target was pruned — the
daemon can crash-loop (203/EXEC) for days while every binary-level check stays green (#114748). Binary-level
repair (`install`) cannot fix a stale unit reference, so doctor is the only surface that can name it.

name: _wayland_environment_context
doc: Linux+Wayland only: doctor probes the CLI process's environment, not the gateway's.

name: _print_text_report
arguments: report: Report, color: bool, *, identity: Optional[Report]=None, environment: Optional[Report]=None
doc:
Render like `cua-driver call health_report`: header (CLI --version preferred over health_report's stale
``driver_version``), identity block, environment note, one line per check + indented hint/``data`` rows
(support staff need them).

name: run_doctor
arguments: driver_cmd: Optional[str]=None, *, include: Sequence[str]=(), skip: Sequence[str]=(), json_output: bool=False, color: Optional[bool]=None
doc:
Resolve the binary via the shared runtime resolver (diagnose what `computer_use` actually invokes), call
`health_report`, render; on 0.10.x (denied) a report is synthesized from probes.

name: stale_tcc_grant_hint
doc:
Recovery text for grants the daemon reports missing while System Settings shows the CuaDriver toggle ON.

TCC keys each row to the app's code-signing requirement, so a row written for an earlier CuaDriver build can
stop matching after a driver update: the toggle stays ON, the daemon is denied, and flipping the toggle does
not rewrite the requirement (trycua/cua#3170). Only a reset + re-grant recovers it, so the hint names the
exact rows for the *missing* status fields.

name: _child_env
doc:
cua-driver child env (telemetry policy + provider secrets stripped); ``os.environ`` on import error.

cua-driver is a third-party binary — it must never inherit provider API keys (#53503/#55709/#58889
lineage). Each layer degrades gracefully so permission probes never break on a helper import error.

name: _json_out
doc: Run ``binary args`` and parse stdout as JSON (``None`` on empty output).

name: _doctor
doc: ``cua-driver doctor --json`` → ``{ok, checks:[{label,status,message}]}`` (None on any failure).

name: _mac_permissions
doc: Fold ``cua-driver permissions status --json`` booleans (+ ``source``) into ``out``.

name: computer_use_status
doc:
OS-aware readiness for the desktop card; key order is an API payload contract. ``ready`` is the single signal the
UI keys off: macOS = both TCC grants, elsewhere = driver health (no TCC model); ``None`` = unknown (binary missing /
probe failed). ``can_grant`` is macOS-only.

name: request_permissions_grant
doc:
Run ``cua-driver permissions grant`` (macOS), streaming its output. Returns the driver's exit code (0 ok), 2 if
the binary is missing, 64 on a non-macOS platform (no TCC model to grant).

name: get_computer_use_schema
doc: Return the generic OpenAI function-calling schema.

name: _reject_unsafe
doc: JSON error for hard-blocked input, else None. Runs BEFORE the approval prompt.

name: _input_target_mismatch
doc:
Current sticky-target app when it provably differs from *requested_app*: both known and neither a substring
of the other ('Google-chrome' vs 'chrome'). Unknown target -> None (fail open; the verify ladder catches it).

name: _screenshot_dedup_check
arguments: session_id: str, digest: str, target: tuple[str, str]
doc:
True when this capture should be delivered WITHOUT its image: the previous frame for this session had identical
bytes for the same target and the omission streak is below _SCREENSHOT_DEDUP_MAX_STREAK. Any miss (new pixels,
new target, streak exhausted, first capture) resets the stored state to this digest so the image goes out.

name: _reset_screenshot_dedup
doc: Forget dedup state (all sessions, or one scoped key).

name: reset_screenshot_dedup
doc:
Compaction boundary hook (mirrors ``reset_file_dedup``): the summary may have dropped the frame an
"unchanged" note would point at, so the next capture of this session must deliver pixels again.

name: _cua_permission_mode
doc:
Map Hermes's approval bypass onto Cua's immutable mode; fails closed. Both identity namespaces are consulted
(DB ``session_id`` and gateway ``session_key`` contextvar) or a gateway ``/yolo`` would be invisible here.
Warns once per session that ``-z``/``--yolo`` swapped the driver onto a private ``unrestricted`` daemon, dropping
the configured ceiling: deliberate (``unrestricted`` is not a config value) but easy to trigger by accident.

name: _install_backend
arguments: sid: str, backend: ComputerUseBackend, permission_mode: str
doc:
Record a backend in the session caches (the empty session also mirrors it onto the ``_backend`` hook).
Caller holds ``_backend_lock``.

name: _detach_locked
doc:
Remove one session's cache entries, plus the ``_backend`` injection hook when it aliases the empty session
(older callers/tests may populate only the hook). Caller holds ``_backend_lock``.

name: _stop_backend
arguments: backend: ComputerUseBackend, call_lock: Optional[threading.RLock], on_error: Callable[[Exception], None]
doc:
Stop under the session call lock (if any) so an in-flight action finishes first. Never called under
``_backend_lock`` (unrelated sessions stay free). ``on_error`` absorbs the failure (never raises).

name: _scoped_sid
doc:
Cache key for one Hermes session's backend. Outside a served-profile scope it is the bare id
(legacy keys byte-identical); under a multiplexed turn the routed profile's home key is appended
so two profiles that share a session id (or a DISPLAY) never share one cua-driver (#110032).
Every cache path — lookup, install, release — goes through this, so release finds what lookup made.

name: _backend_for_call
doc:
Hold a live backend through dispatch, retrying admission but never an action.

A display/mode change or release can retire a backend before lock lookup or
while a caller waits. Revalidate AFTER acquiring its profile-scoped call
lock; teardown needs that same lock. Never wait under the global cache lock.

name: release_computer_use_session
doc:
Release one session-owned backend (lifecycle seam for hosts/plugins); idempotent, True iff one was released.
Cache entries are removed BEFORE stopping so new lookups cannot retain the stale target/ref namespace. Approval
grants are not touched here: they live in the shared store and die with ``tools.approval.clear_session``.

name: _shutdown_backend_atexit
doc:
Stop all cached backends so cua-driver subprocesses don't outlive us. atexit only, no signal handlers: a
``SystemExit`` from a prompt_toolkit key binding corrupts its coroutine state and makes the process unkillable.
Never raises. Drops the global lock before stop(): teardown budgets 5s and must not block spawns.

Each session backend holds a long-lived ``cua-driver`` subprocess, so without this a driver can survive
the Hermes process that spawned it (#28152 item 3). #69903 kept the orphan from burning a core by
disabling the cursor overlay; the process itself still lingered.

name: handle_computer_use
doc:
Main entry point (tools.registry): a JSON string (text-only) or a dict marked `_multimodal`. Order: hard
blocks (_reject_unsafe) -> approval scopes (destructive action, then 'bring_to_front' — persistent focus is a
separate visible side effect with its own scope) -> backend -> dispatch under the session call lock.

significant_calls.expression: _dispatch(backend, action, args, fence=_fence, session_id=session_id or None)

name: _request_approval
doc:
None if approved, else a JSON error string. The decision (yolo bypass, session/permanent grants, CLI prompt,
gateway pending, cron/unattended policy, fail-closed with nobody to ask) is ``tools.approval``'s shared gate,
so a computer_use grant is one store entry like any terminal pattern. Scope key ``cua:<action>:<mode>``:
foreground delivery is a visible focus change, so a background ``session`` grant must NOT cover it (#67052).

name: _xy
doc: Click semantics: a coordinate only counts when its x is set (a bare y is not a point).

name: _scroll_xy
doc: Scroll semantics: axes are independent — ``coordinate=[null, 100]`` scrolls at y=100 with x unset.

name: _do_capture
arguments: backend, action, args, fence=lambda: None, session_id=None, **_

name: _summarize_click
arguments: action: str, args: dict[str, Any], fg: str

name: _dispatch
arguments: backend: ComputerUseBackend, action: str, args: dict[str, Any], fence: Callable[[], None]=lambda: None, session_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
``fence`` raises when the screen lease moved since admission; capture paths call it as soon as the
frame is in hand, before anything derived from it leaves the process (including the screenshot dedup
cache keyed by ``session_id``).

name: _classify_action_result
doc:
Next ladder step from semantic evidence, in precedence order. Escalation is advisory: it never overrides
a confirmed effect nor licenses repeating input.

name: _bounds_hints
arguments: elements: list[UIElement], image_width: int, image_height: int
doc:
(scale, note) when element bounds live in a different coordinate space than the screenshot, else (None, None).
On HiDPI displays AX bounds are native while the screenshot is downscaled, so coordinate= clicks read off the
screenshot miss by the scale factor. 5% slack: window chrome can hang a few px past the captured frame without
implying a different space. Scale heuristic: larger axis ratio wins.

name: _capture_view
doc:
One capture's derived facts, computed once for every response branch: ``visible`` is the capped element list,
``dims_omitted`` an image below the provider minimum.

name: _capture_summary_lines
doc:
Human-readable capture summary; line ORDER is contract. Lists only what `elements` surfaces, otherwise the
summary names indices the model can't find.

name: _text_capture_payload
arguments: v: SimpleNamespace, summary: str, extra: Optional[dict[str, Any]]=None
doc:
JSON text payload shared by the AX, vision-unavailable and aux-vision branches. Key order is contract:
fixed fields, ``extra`` branch markers, then set optionals.

name: _capture_response
arguments: cap: CaptureResult, max_elements: int=_DEFAULT_MAX_ELEMENTS, session_id: Optional[str]=None

name: _maybe_follow_capture
arguments: backend: ComputerUseBackend, res: ActionResult, do_capture: bool, fence: Callable[[], None]=lambda: None, session_id: Optional[str]=None

name: _secure_dir_policy
doc:
Create/reconcile a Hermes media-cache dir owner-only (0700), except managed.

A capture is as sensitive as the screen it came from — an open password
manager, a private chat, a bank tab. The umask-derived 0755 these dirs
used to get made every local account able to list (and read) those
frames whenever ``HERMES_HOME`` itself is traversable, which is exactly
what the documented ``HERMES_HOME_MODE=0701`` web-server escape hatch
arranges. Delegates to the same house policy as every Hermes secret dir —
``hermes_cli.config._secure_dir`` — with the mode passed to ``mkdir`` so
there is no window between mkdir and chmod; managed/NixOS installs keep
their group-share design (the mode is left to the configured umask/setgid
because these lazily-created dirs are not covered by the module's
``systemd.tmpfiles`` rules). Best-effort; never breaks a capture.

name: _write_private_bytes
doc:
Write ``data`` to ``path`` with owner-only (0600) permissions.

``Path.write_bytes`` would land 0644 under a default umask. POSIX mode
bits are advisory on Windows (``os.chmod`` there only toggles the
read-only flag), so this is a best-effort narrowing that falls back to a
plain write rather than failing the capture.

name: _cache_file
arguments: subdir: str, legacy: str, name: str, pattern: str='', cap: int=0
doc:
Path for a new file under ``$HERMES_HOME/<subdir>`` (dir created owner-only, per #77579).
With ``pattern``/``cap``, first unlinks the oldest matching files so at most ``cap - 1`` remain
(best-effort).

name: _write_cache_file
arguments: what: str, subdir: str, legacy: str, name: str, pattern: str, cap: int, write: Callable[[Any], None]
doc:
Bounded cache write via ``write(path)``; the path, or None on any failure — an unwritable cache must never
break control (a capture keeps working without its spill/screenshot copy).

name: _persist_capture_image
doc: Copy of the capture in Hermes' media cache so attachment surfaces can deliver it (None without an image).

name: _spill_elements_to_file
doc: FULL element tree (untruncated labels) in a cache file — the read_file/search_files escape hatch for capped text.

name: _shrink_capture_for_vision
arguments: raw: bytes, ext: str, max_dim: int=_MAX_VISION_DIM
doc:
Downscale encoded image bytes so the longest side is <= max_dim -> ``(bytes, scale_note)``. note is None when
unchanged (fits, or Pillow unavailable/failed), else it tells the vision model the factor so reported
coordinates map back to the real screen instead of being silently wrong.

name: _should_route_through_aux_vision
doc:
True when ``_capture_response`` should hand the PNG to aux vision. Any failure returns False (fail open) so a
broken config never silently drops the screenshot for vision-capable main models. Decided per capture (the
config read is the signature-cached ``load_config_readonly``), so ``/model``, a profile switch or an
``image_input_mode`` edit applies to the next screenshot instead of a stale verdict.

name: _capture_after_mode
doc: Mode for ``capture_after`` follow-ups. Default ``som`` (screenshot).

name: _route_capture_through_aux_vision
arguments: cap: CaptureResult, summary: str, *, visible_elements: Optional[list[UIElement]]=None, truncated_elements: int=0, elements_file: Optional[str]=None, screenshot_path: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Pre-analyse the capture via ``vision_analyze_tool`` (temp file under ``$HERMES_HOME/cache/vision/``) and merge
the description with the AX/SOM summary into one text payload. JSON, or None on any failure.

name: check_computer_use_requirements
doc:
The selected ``computer_use.backend``'s ``is_available()``. An unregistered name stays True so the call
surfaces the "not registered (available: ...)" error instead of the tool silently vanishing.

name: _matching_open_operation
arguments: names: list[str], *, alias: str | None, repair_id: str | None, profile_home: str | None

name: find_or_start_operation
arguments: names: list[str], *, action: str, profile_home: str | None, alias: str | None=None, repair_id: str | None=None, initiator: str | None=None
doc:
``alias`` names the one account of ``names[0]`` to connect; ``repair_id`` names the existing
account a reconnect repairs. The caller passes one name with either. ``initiator`` goes on the
connect request; none leaves the gateway to record it as unknown.

name: _run
arguments: start: AccountOperationStart, action: str, initiator: str | None

name: target_scope
doc:
Bind the profile at *home*: its home, secrets and terminal policy, the way an RPC for that
profile does. The install writes its tree, config and ``.env`` there. The home override is
bound for the launch profile too: the calling thread may carry another profile's override, and
an unbound launch scope would leave it in place.

name: _named_home
doc: The home of the profile the Advanced modal named; raises for one that does not exist.

name: _installed_row
doc:
The connected row's fields (the drawn row plus what went live, as facts the card words) and
the same notes in one English line for the model.

name: apply_answer
doc:
The card's ``connection.respond`` for a catalog operation: skip, approve (with the Advanced
values or null for defaults), approve again on a failed row (Try again), and Continue.

name: refuse
doc: Raise with the installer's own text when the catalog would refuse this entry here.

name: install_plugin
arguments: self, name: str, *, force: bool, enable: bool, ref: Optional[str], on_step: Callable[[InstallPhase], None]

name: skill_meta
doc: The first hub source that knows the identifier; metadata only, no bundle download.

name: install_skill
doc:
Install headless; ``{name, already_installed}``. ``do_install`` reports only by printing, so
success is read from the hub lock file and failure from its last line. A skill that is already
installed (force off) is left as it is and reported so.

name: approve
arguments: self, operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, env: Optional[dict[str, str]]

name: _check_answer
arguments: self, target: Target, env: dict[str, str]

name: _spawn
arguments: self, operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, env: dict[str, str], options: dict[str, Any]

name: _install
arguments: self, target: Target, env: dict[str, str], options: dict[str, Any], step: Callable[[InstallPhase], None]

name: manage_catalog
arguments: args: dict[str, Any], *, session_id: Optional[str]=None, tool_call_id: Optional[str]=None, connection_callback: Optional[Callable[[dict[str, Any]], Optional[str]]]=None, card_surface: bool=False, installer: Any=None
doc: ``card_surface``: the session is a desktop chat, the one surface that draws catalog rows.

name: install
arguments: items: list[dict[str, str]], *, session_id: Optional[str], tool_call_id: Optional[str], connection_callback: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], Optional[str]], installer: Any=None

name: search
arguments: query: str, kind: Optional[str], *, installer: Any=None
doc:
Runs on the tool call's thread, in this chat's profile scope, so ``installed`` is this
chat's profile's.

name: allowed
arguments: kind: str, current: TargetState, to: TargetState

name: record_data_use
doc: No-op outside an agent dispatch (execute_code RPC, MCP serve): no message is built there.

name: dispatch_connector_batch
arguments: calls, ids, *, user_task, enabled_tools, middleware_trace, enabled_toolsets, disabled_toolsets

name: _result
arguments: client: Any, before: set[str], operation: DisplayOperation

name: run_display
arguments: client: Any, suggested: list[str], *, session_key: str, tool_call_id: Optional[str], connection_callback: Callback, call: Optional[Any]=None
doc: Draw the card and hold the tool thread until it settles.

name: _profile_key
doc:
A session record names its profile home only for a non-default profile; the tool thread sees
the same home through its turn override, and the default profile through the process home.

name: get
arguments: session_key: str, op_id: str, *, profile_home: Optional[str]=None

name: find_target
arguments: name: str, *, alias: Optional[str]=None, repair_id: Optional[str]=None, profile_home: Optional[str]=None
doc:
The open operation connecting this account: the connector ``name`` and the same ``alias`` and
repaired account id, so an open operation for one account is never reused for another of the same app.

name: managed_client
arguments: *, creates_guest: bool, initiator: Optional[str]=AGENT_TOOL, call: Optional[Any]=None
doc:
The real gateway client for a user action. ``creates_guest`` is the caller's declaration that
it may create the guest identity when the user has none (a connect, an explicit list); a page
read passes False and holds a token already. ``initiator`` names who asked, so every link the
client mints is attributed.

name: managed_kind
arguments: client: Any, action: str, force: bool

name: _note_connected
doc: Each app that connects counts once toward the connector sign-in offer.

name: _status_by_slug
doc:
The toolkit list, by slug. Only the reconnect repair check reads it: it answers "is this app
already connected" before any account exists for the watcher to read.

name: mint
arguments: client: Any, operation: ConnectionOperation, names: list[str], *, reinitiate: bool, actor: Actor, connection_id: Optional[str]=None
doc:
Mint links for ``names`` and apply the gateway's per-app answer to the operation. ``actor`` is
the watcher on the first mint and the user on Try again. The operation id rides along so the
vendor's done page can name it on the way back to the desktop. ``connection_id`` names the one
existing account a repair restarts; the gateway then needs no alias to find it. A repair without
one (Try again) reuses the account the named target already minted, so a rename in between
cannot point the retry at another login.

name: _status_for
arguments: client: Any, target: Target, *, timeout: float
doc:
The one route the watcher reads: that target's own account row. ``None`` means "nothing to
apply this tick" — no account to read, a rate-limit still in force, an account the gateway does
not know yet (404 until the deadline), or a read that failed. A 429 is raised to the tick: its
budget is the principal's, so it is not this one target's to wait out.

name: _apply_read
arguments: operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, status: str, reason: str
doc:
Apply one account read to one target. The RPC thread can move the row while the read is in
flight — a Skip resolves it, a Continue freezes the whole result — and the read then has no
live row to move: it is dropped, not raised into the tool result (that would end the watch
with the operation still open and no card to answer it). Any other refusal is a real
contract violation.

name: _live
doc:
Only a live attempt (pending, initiated) can be advanced by a gateway read; a failed or
expired link waits for the user, and a resolved row is done.

name: _park
doc: A 429 is per principal, not per account: every live target waits out the same Retry-After.

name: _observe
doc:
One account read per live target per tick, sequential: this is the only thread reading them.
A 429 ends the tick: the next read would spend the same refused budget.

name: _mark_unknown
doc:
The gateway refuses a slug it does not list as a policy block. The model guesses a slug from the
app's name (granola for granola_mcp), so the row names the listed slug instead.

name: _prepare
arguments: client: Any, action: str, force: bool

name: _alias_status
doc:
``{slug: {"connected": bool, "connection_id": str | None}}`` for an aliased target, read from
that account's own row (``connection_id`` is None when no account has that name yet); ``None``
when no target is aliased. A failed read raises: guessing "not connected" would send the user
through a new login for an account that may be healthy.

name: _no_card_result
arguments: client: Any, action: str, targets: list[HostedTarget], force: bool, session_id: str

name: _display_result
arguments: client: Any, suggested: list[str], *, session_id: Optional[str], tool_call_id: Optional[str], connection_callback: Optional[Callable[[dict[str, Any]], Optional[str]]], call: Any
doc: The desktop card when one can draw; elsewhere the status list and where to connect.

name: _rename_result
doc:
Rename the one account of ``target.name`` called ``target.alias`` (or, when unnamed, labelled
so) to ``target.to``. Synchronous: no operation and no card.

name: run_managed_action
arguments: action: str, targets: list[HostedTarget], args: dict[str, Any], *, client_factory: Optional[Callable[[], Any]]=None, session_id: Optional[str]=None, tool_call_id: Optional[str]=None, turn_id: Optional[str]=None, connection_callback: Optional[Callable[[dict[str, Any]], Optional[str]]]=None, connectors_available: Optional[Callable[[], bool]]=None, card_surface: bool=False

name: _check_declared
arguments: name: str, entry: Any, env: dict[str, str]
doc:
Configuring one MCP is not a general env-writing primitive: refuse the whole map before the
first write if any key is undeclared or unwritable.

name: _late_key
doc:
The ``(profile, session)`` pairing ``live.open`` keys an operation by. ``profile_key``
is stamped there; the detached no-card path never opens, so fall back to the calling
thread's home — ``close`` runs on the tool thread under the turn's profile scope.

name: adopt_late_connections
doc:
Register the servers whose authorization committed after their card had closed, and add
them to the agent's toolset selection. Runs between turns, so the result that said "not
connected" is followed by a turn in which the tools are there.

name: open_runner
doc:
The runner for one MCP operation. ``prepare`` binds it to the operation, so the card's
answer and its Try again — both of which arrive on another thread — find the same work.

name: _detail
doc:
The user-facing text of a failure. Every value the card submitted for this target is
replaced by exact match before the pattern redactor runs: an opaque credential has no
recognizable shape, so only the runner knows what to remove.

name: _catalog_instructions
doc: The manifest's ``post_install`` text for a catalog name; a custom configured server has none.

name: _move
arguments: operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, to: TargetState, actor: Actor, **fields: Any
doc:
Move one target from the prepare, worker-outcome or observe path.

Continue on the RPC thread can settle the operation between any read of the target's state and
this call. A settled operation has a frozen result, so the lost move is dropped rather than
raised into the tool result; anything else is a real contract violation.

name: _fail
arguments: operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, detail: str
doc:
Report a failure, whatever the row was doing: a repeated failure has no state change to
emit, only newer text.

name: _register_connected
doc: Register one committed server in the current profile scope and report its callable names.

name: _registered_tool_names
doc:
The server's callable names, read from the registry once its registration has finished.

Registration is a no-op for a server the process already holds, and that includes one another
task is still connecting: saving the configuration wakes the config watcher, which starts its
own connect, so a large server (hundreds of tools) was reported with no tools three seconds
before they were registered. A server that failed discovery earlier is parked with no tools
and is woken once. A server that finished registering with no tools is a valid empty list.

name: _connect
arguments: operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, tools: list[str], discovery_error: str=''

name: _actor
doc: Try again is the user's move; a first attempt is the backend's.

name: _start_oauth
arguments: runner: _Runner, operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, env: dict[str, str]

name: _declare_env
arguments: runner: _Runner, operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, env: dict[str, str]
doc: The install row waits pending; the card draws a field per credential it still needs.

name: _missing_required
arguments: runner: _Runner, target: Target, env: dict[str, str]
doc:
The declared credentials that still have no value. The install runs on a worker thread,
where ``install_entry``'s prompt for a missing credential would block on stdin forever.

name: _start_install
arguments: runner: _Runner, operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, env: dict[str, str]

name: _start_install_oauth
arguments: runner: _Runner, operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, env: dict[str, str]
doc:
The row is already ``initiated``; publish the authorization link onto it. The same
``initiated`` + ``connect_url`` pair is what every card reads as its URL step.

name: _fail_install
arguments: runner: _Runner, operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, error: Any
doc:
A failed install asks for its fields again, so the card can reopen the form over the draft
it kept. Nothing was saved, so every declared field is still missing.

name: _do_enable
arguments: runner: _Runner, operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, env: dict[str, str]

name: _install_now
arguments: runner: _Runner, operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, env: dict[str, str]
doc: Off the desktop nobody can fill a credential in, so a missing one is the answer.

name: _observe_install
doc: An install is an OAuth attempt for an OAuth entry and a worker for every other one.

name: _nothing
arguments: runner: _Runner, operation: ConnectionOperation, target: Target, env: dict[str, str]
doc: Authorize needs no approval: the row's verb opens the link the flow already minted.

name: apply_answer
doc:
Fold the card's ``connection.respond`` payload into the operation: a skip, an approval that
starts the backend's work, and Continue. The card never reports an outcome, so any other claim
moves nothing.

name: _cancel_attempt
doc:
Stop the target's OAuth attempt so a late reply cannot be adopted. Returns the note for a
cancel that lost the race: the attempt had committed, and a completed authorization stays.

name: retry
doc:
Re-run the named MCP targets on the open operation (the card's Try again): a fresh OAuth
flow, a fresh install, a fresh enable. Returns an error message when the operation is not one
this module is running.

name: _no_card_result
arguments: runner: _Runner, names: list[str], action: str, session_key: str

name: run_mcp_operation
arguments: names: list[str], action: str, *, connection_callback: Optional[Callable[[dict[str, Any]], Optional[str]]], session_id: Optional[str], tool_call_id: Optional[str]=None, backend: Any=None

name: required_env
doc: The credentials the catalog entry declares that have no value yet.

name: installs_with_oauth
doc:
A catalog entry whose own OAuth the card must run. Provider-mediated OAuth is not one:
its token comes from ``hermes auth <provider>``, so the plain probe covers it.

name: start_install_oauth
arguments: self, name: str, env: dict[str, str]
doc:
Install an OAuth entry through the card's flow. The configuration is built in memory and
lands, together with the setup values, only when ``initialize`` accepts the token.

name: install

doc:

(``PUT /api/mcp/servers/{name}/enabled``): the two read-modify-write paths run in one
process, so an unserialised write here drops whichever landed first.

name: _prepare_together
doc:
Start every OAuth flow at once and wait for the URLs once. Each flow blocks until its
provider publishes an authorization URL, so a sequential prepare would keep the card empty
for one wait per target.

The wait bounds how long prepare blocks, not how long a provider may take: a row still
pending afterwards is left to its own thread, which is the only writer of that row and
ends with the URL or the flow's own failure. Failing it here as well would make two
writers of one row, and a URL that arrives a moment later would have no row to land on.

Each thread runs in its own copy of the calling thread's context: a named-profile turn
binds its home through a contextvar, and the flow resolves ``mcp_servers`` and stores the
token by that home.

name: close
doc:
The operation is over. An attempt still waiting on the browser is stopped when the user
ended the turn, and otherwise left to finish: the card closed, not the authorization. What
it commits is picked up before the session's next turn (``adopt_late_connections``).

values there, so they land with the authorization and never before it.

Retrying discovery for a server that is authorized must not ask the user to sign in again, and
must not delete the working grant first. Any failure here falls through to the interactive
flow, which replaces the grant.

so the configuration can reference them before anything is saved. ``reuse_saved`` is the

session surface keeps it off, because its caller waits for an authorization URL.
